Fistula.title: Fistula
Fistula.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Fistula is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] in the Cellar.

• [Repentance] in the Caves and the Flooded Caves. [end edition note] 

The large Fistula has 60 HP, the medium forms have 15 HP, and the small forms have 8 HP.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Moves around the room slowly, bouncing off the walls.

• When enough health is depleted, the one large Fistula breaks into four medium Fistulas.

• Medium forms behave identically but move slightly faster and can bounce off other enemies.

• Each of the four medium Fistulas breaks into two small Fistulas.

• Small forms behave identically but move very fast.

• Each of the smallest Fistulas spawns a Charger with 15 health points on defeat unless they are over a pit or other obstacle.

• Altogether, the pieces have a combined total of 184 HP (304 HP if including the 8 Chargers).

• All stages of Fistula deal a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 2] : 15% larger with 25% more HP (75). Spawns Boom Fly with 15 health points instead of Chargers unless the smallest Fistula piece is over a pit or other obstacle. Each piece travels much slower and splits into three medium Fistulas as opposed to the original's four, similar to Teratoma.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Fistula appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• A fistula is an abnormal connection between organs, intestines, and other tissues.

• Fistula’s splittings after taking enough damage is a reference to the game Asteroids, where asteroids would float in different directions and split after taking enough damage. This was confirmed by Edmund McMillen.

• [Before Repentance] Fistula used to be a Caves / Catacombs boss in the original The Binding of Isaac, but as of Rebirth, it was a Cellar boss.

• [Repentance] It has been moved back into the Caves.

• Teratoma is the posthumous version of Fistula.

• Unlike the original The Binding of Isaac, Fistula doesn't bounce off of rocks.

• Fistula was inspired by a boss of the same name in another Edmund McMillen game, C-Word.

• Fistuloid is an enemy variant of this boss combined with what looks to be a Charger or Spitty.

• The Matriarch is a boss added in Booster Pack #5 that is simultaneously based off of a Fistuloid, Chub, and this boss. The Matriarch will also spawn small Fistulas throughout the battle.

• [Repentance] Fistula is one of four bosses that can be spawned by It Lives!, the other three being Chub, Polycephalus and Teratoma.

• [Repentance] In Repentance, Fistula's sprite resembles that from the original Binding of Isaac.

Fistuloid.title: Fistuloid
Fistuloid.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Fistuloid flies towards Isaac in an erratic waving motion. When it gets close to Isaac, it fires a blood shot at him and propels itself in the opposite direction. Upon death, it fires a maggot that flies off-screen. The maggot is fired in the cardinal direction closest to Isaac and will do a full heart of damage if touched.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Fistuloids were added in Booster Pack #4.

• Fistuloids appear to be small Fistula with a Chubber charger stuck inside.

• The Matriarch, added in the Booster Pack after which this enemy was added, is designed in a way that resembles a larger version of a Fistuloid.

Flat File.title: Flat File
Flat File.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Makes all spikes retract, preventing them from dealing damage.

• Most spikes leave behind holes or a visual cue showing where they would normally be.

• The spikes around Curse Room doors are removed, allowing them to be entered and exited without taking damage.

• Retracts damaging spikes from Spiked Rocks and Spiked Chests/Mimic Chests.

• Removes the spikes from Poky, Slides, and Wall Huggers.

• • Pokies, Slides, and Wall Huggers don't immediately stop moving once they are despiked, and are still able to push Isaac without dealing damage.

• • Has no effect on Grudges, neither retracting their spikes nor despawning them.

• Causes Spikeballs to despawn.

• • Doesn't despawn or retract the spikes on Ball and Chains.

• • Doesn't cause the moveable spike balls in Singe's boss room to despawn or despike.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Flat File is dropped in a room with spikes, the spikes will not extend again unless the room is left and re-entered.

• Spiked Rocks will not re-extend their spikes.

• Mimic Chests won't change their contents when Isaac is up close to them (visible with Guppy's Eye) if opened under the effect of Flat File.

• Flat File also retracts the spikes in the center of Sacrifice Rooms, making them unusable while the trinket is held. The spikes reappear after dropping the trinket and re-entering the room.

• If Flat File is gulped, Isaac cannot use Sacrifice rooms for the rest of the run.

• Flat File does not prevent The Pile or Mama Gurdy from using their spike attacks.

• Also removes spikes from doors in the Cursed! challenge, making it significantly easier.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Bosses spike attacks, Grudge, and Ball and Chain have their spikes retracted

• A Pound of Flesh: Doesn't retract spikes placed around consumables in shops.

• Sanguine Bond: Retracts the spikes, making the item useless.

fields.description: Causes most spikes to retract, making them harmless. This includes the door to Curse Rooms, Spiked Chests, Poky and their variants.

• [Repentance] Humbleing Bundle: All normal Keys spawned by the trinket get a 50% chance to turn into Key Rings. [end edition note] 

• Tainted Keeper: The trinket works with the temporary coins spawned from defeating enemies, effectively turning it into an infinite Key generator.

Flat Stone.title: Flat Stone
Flat Stone.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Tears bounce off the floor as they travel. Whenever a tear bounces, it creates a small splash that deals 25% of Isaac's tear damage to enemies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The bounces increase effective range without affecting the stat, usually by around one third.

• Indirectly acquiring Rubber Cement through starting an Eden run or the D4 and D100 counts towards unlocking the item.

• [Repentance] Dropping Rubber Cement as Tainted Isaac and picking it back up counts towards unlocking the item. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Should be avoided when going for The Beast fight, as tears will fall straight to the ground during the final fight. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Should be avoided when going for Mother, as encountering Rotgut's 2nd & 3rd phases becomes near impossible to hit: tears DO NOT bounce on the floor. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Bob's Rotten Head: Will now bounce once, causing two explosions and two gas clouds to appear.

• Compound Fracture: Bone tears will bounce normally, and bone shards will only bounce once.

• Cricket's Body / Haemolacria / The Parasite: Tears release smaller tears every time they bounce.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs bounce, dealing damage to nearby enemies when they bounce.

• The Forgotten: The bone club bounces when thrown. Works even with Tech X .

• Ipecac: The explosive shot bounces, poisoning and dealing high damage to nearby enemies every time it bounces.

• The Ludovico Technique: The tear constantly bounces.

• With Compound Fracture, bone shards burst on every bounce.

• With Ipecac, the tear causes a poisonous explosion when it bounces. The first bounce when entering a room does not explode, allowing moving the tear with less risk of self-damage.

• With Jacob's Ladder, electricity sparks on every bounce.

• Mom's Knife: The knife bounces as it flies away from Isaac. Each bounce splashes, dealing the current damage of Isaac's tears.

• Monstro's Lung: All tears bounce simultaneously, greatly increasing reach of the burst.

• Mysterious Liquid: Tears leave a pool of creep with each bounce.

• Pop!: Eyeball tears bounce repeatedly against the floor when they are about to disappear, but can be knocked by other tears to reset their range, meaning tears can be kept in the air forever as long as they are hit when they are bouncing against the floor.

• Lead Pencil: Tears fired by Lead Penicl also bounce, greatly increasing their range.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone/Epic Fetus/Tech X/Technology: Overrides Flat Stone.

• Compound Fracture: No split tears on bounces.

• Dead Eye: Each time the tear touches the ground, there is a chance for the damage bonus to reset, making it nearly impossible to stack or keep it.

• Incubus: The effective range of Incubus' tears is roughly doubled, with a single bounce in the middle of the flight.

• Jacob's Ladder: No electricity on bounces.

• Kidney Stone: The stone fired by Kidney Stone doesn't bounce.

• Lachryphagy: Initial tears will act as normal for Lachryphagy but tears from burst will bounce.

• Technology Zero: Only the last two tears will connect via electricity.

• Trisagion: Beams continually shrink and grow. Shrunken beams do roughly 75% of normal beams' damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Flat Stone is based on this Steam Workshop item by Maddogs and Joe, originally known as Hydrophobicity.

• It seems as though originally, the lasers produced by the Technology items (Technology, Technology 2, and Tech.5) and Brimstone were meant to synergize, as seen in the concept art of Flat Stone.

fields.description: Tears bounce off the floor, creating splashes. Splashes deal 25% of Isaac's tear damage to all enemies in a small area.

Flip.title: Flip
Flip.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: It is the starting item for Tainted Lazarus.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• While holding Flip, when Isaac enters a new room containing an item (Treasure Room, Shop, etc.), the item pedestal will have a second "ghostly" item behind it.

• The real item can be interacted with normally, while the ghostly item cannot.

• The ghostly item will vanish if there is no real item on the pedestal and Isaac leaves the room.

• Upon use, flips all real / ghostly items around on pedestals, allowing Isaac to collect the ghostly items. Does not affect pedestals that do not contain a ghostly item.

• As long as Isaac does not exit the room, empty pedestals can be flipped, meaning both the original item and the flipped ghostly item can be collected.

• If playing as Tainted Lazarus, activating it also flips between them and Dead Tainted Lazarus.

• [Repentance+] Tainted Lazarus' Flip also only requires 4 charges.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Flip has no effect on item pedestals that do not generate upon the creation of the room (i.e. Boss items, items from chests / beggars, etc.).

• Buying a real item, such as from a Shop or Devil Room, will also buy the ghostly version for free, although it can still only be obtained using Flip.

• Flipping an unbought item will update the price to the ghostly item's. 

• Ghostly items do not count as seen or collected before they have been flipped into existence.

• Once a ghostly item has been chosen for a pedestal by encountering it, it will stay even if collected elsewhere before flipping.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a small white Isaac head wisp in the middle ring with high health. If you are playing Tainted Lazarus, the wisp is given to the form that isn't holding Book of Virtues. A wisp is also granted when Flip is automatically used by clearing the room as Tainted Lazarus.

• Eternal D6: When Eternal D6 makes an item disappear, the ghostly item behind it will not be gone and can be taken after using Flip.

• Upon using Flip, the new item will be free to take, even if the original item had to be purchased with money or health.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tainted Isaac / Glitched Crown: The cycling effect only gets applied to the primary item; the ghostly item does not cycle. Using Flip on a cycling item pedestal will cause the currently visible item to switch places with the ghostly one, after which neither item will cycle.

• The D6 / Perthro / Dice Shard, etc.: Only rerolls visible item. Ghostly items remain unchanged.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Damocles: Additional pedestals will not have ghostly items.

• Void: Ghostly items no longer appear when absorbed by Void, rendering Flip useless.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Flip's icons are the alchemy symbols for death and life, respectively.

• Prior to patch V1.7.6, Flip's pickup quote was "Life and death".

• Prior to patch V1.7.6, using Flip as a character other than Tainted Lazarus after having previously used Esau Jr. would switch between Esau Jr. and the base character. This was most likely a bug, as Flip was not yet obtainable for other characters besides using Death Certificate or as a starting item for Eden.

fields.description: Item pedestals have a second un-interactable "ghostly" item behind them. Activating will flip the real and ghostly items around. If playing as Tainted Lazarus, also flips between them and Dead Tainted Lazarus.

Flush!.title: Flush!
Flush!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Turns all non-boss monsters in the room into Poop.

• [Afterbirth onward] Floods the whole room with water (same effect as seen in Flooded Caves).

• Floods the room with blood if used in Womb and its alts. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth onward] Instantly kills most poop-themed bosses (Dingle, Dangle, Brownie, Clog, and Turdlings). [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Extinguishes all Normal and Red Fire Places in the room.

• [Repentance] Turns lava-filled pits in the Mines into solid rock, allowing them to be walked over. [end edition note] 

• Contributes to the Oh Crap transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Clog. [end edition note] 

• Poops created by this item are not tiles, but entities. As such, they are not grid-aligned, and behave differently:

• The poops vanish if the room is left and then returned to.

• Things that automatically target enemies, such as Monstro's Tooth and II - The High Priestess, will also target the poops.

• The poops can be slowly moved by pushing them.

• The poops cannot create a bridge if they are bombed near a pit.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The poops will flash red when hit, similar to damaging monsters.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The poops will crumble when hit, identically to regular poops.

• [Afterbirth onward] Instead of being turned into poop, poop-themed enemies like Dip and Squirt are flushed away without leaving a poop behind. [end edition note] 

• Enemies that are turned into poop do not count towards on kill effects such as health regeneration from Charm of the Vampire or [Repentance] the damage increase from Lusty Blood [end edition note] .

• If the Fear effect is applied, the poop will stay a dark red.

• Does not work against any of the following:

• Lil' Haunts when fighting The Haunt.

• • [Rebirth only] The first Lil' Haunt can be flushed, but this softlocks the game.

• Mom's Hand.

• Enemies in an intangible state, such as invisible Wizoobs.

• [edition anr+] Turdlings, Colostomia, and Turdlet, despite them being poop-themed.

• Mini-bosses.

• Using it against the Champion version of a monster will forfeit the chance to get the champion's drop.

• [Afterbirth onward] When used inside a Crawl Space, the ladders will be covered in water but the walls will not.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] 120 Volt / Jacob's Ladder: Since Flush! floods the room with water, it is now considered a wet environment, which significantly increases the arcing distance of the electricity created by these items. [end edition note] 

• Blood Puppy: Instantly tames a hostile Blood Puppy and leaves behind a poop.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns brown wisps in the middle ring. An additional wisp is spawned for each enemy turned into Poop.

• Butt Penny/Petrified Poop: Grants poops made from enemies a chance to drop pickups.

• Death's List: Enemies that die by being turned into poop do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into poop still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.

• Dirty Mind: Enemies that are turned into poop generate double the normal amount of Dips.

• Midas' Touch: Touching poops made from enemies turns them into Golden Poops just before being destroyed dropping the normal Golden Poop pickups including Counterfeit Penny.

• Oh Crap: Isaac can heal by destroying poops created from enemies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Bob's Brain: Bob's Brain will explode upon hitting an enemy that has been turned into poop.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Butt Penny/Petrified Poop: Poops made from enemies still do not drop pickups.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Oh Crap: Destroying poops created from enemies do not heal Isaac.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] A rare 2x1 tall room behaving like a closet exists in Mines with Flush! as a guaranteed item. If Isaac has already found Flush!, the item in the closet does not change. [end edition note] 

• This item is used in High Brow.

• The item sprite is a toilet handle.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Flush! works against Lil Haunts but it can softlock the game.

fields.description: Turns all non-boss monsters in the room into Poop. [Afterbirth onward] Instantly kills poop-themed bosses. Floods the current room.

Fly.title: Fly
Fly.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the fly enemies] 

Flies are enemies that buzz around the room randomly, but slowly hover towards Isaac. They cannot damage Isaac at all, even by touch, making them completely harmless. However, they can turn into Pooters if they fly around Poop for too long.

Along with monsters like the Gapers and Spiders, Flies are one of the most commonly-encountered monsters and appear in numerous different types.

sections.heading: Attack Fly
sections.text:
Attack Flies are red and black flashing flies that will chase Isaac, dealing contact damage.

Weirdly, while they can easily hit Isaac from the left or right, they have great difficulty hitting him from the top or bottom.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Attack Flies turn into regular Flies if Isaac has Skatole. However, they take a small amount of time to convert into Flies, so it is possible for Isaac to be damaged if the player is not careful.

• Hives can spit out attack flies that die upon touching Isaac, but the ones spawned upon the monster's death do not.

• The Duke of Flies can spit out normal and larger versions of Attack Flies that have 10 base HP. Both of these Attack Flies die upon touching Isaac, but the ones spawned upon the boss's death do not.

• The Husk can spit out attack flies that die upon touching Isaac, but the ones spawned upon the boss's death do not. 

• Gurdy can spawn weaker versions of Attack Flies that only have 3 base HP and die upon touching Isaac.

sections.heading: Ring Fly
sections.text: Ring Flies are a new addition to Rebirth. They are pink flies that, upon entering the room, will cluster together into a circular formation and orbit rapidly while moving towards Isaac. They will hold formation even as flies are destroyed. The maximum amount of flies per formation is 10.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Ring Flies are not affected by Strange Attractor and will continue to stay within their current circular formation.

sections.heading: Moter
sections.text:
Moters appear as two conjoined Attack Flies. They behave similarly to regular Attack Flies, but split into two Attack Flies upon being killed. The directions the Attack Flies will split off is parallel to Isaac (vertical if Isaac is to either side, and horizontal if he is above or below).

Alternatively, if a Moter's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (i.e., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If Isaac has Skatole, it will not split into two Attack Flies on death.

sections.heading: Eternal Fly
sections.text:
The Eternal Fly is a white-colored fly that can be found on any floor in the game. They usually circle Corny Poop or enemies like Holy Leeches and Hangers, and will not stop circling them until their hosts are destroyed. Before that, they will deal damage to Isaac if he touches them, and they are completely immune to all forms of damage. When their hosts are destroyed, they convert into a modified version of an Attack Fly that regenerates health and can be killed if walked into.
Eternal Flies circling Corn Poop do not need to be killed to clear a room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Eternal Flies can be killed by Chaos Card, Little Horn, and Euthanasia.

• Their bestiary entry states that they have 300 HP.

sections.heading: Dart Fly
sections.text: Dart Flies are similar to regular Attack Flies, but attempt to predict Isaac's movements and cut him off. If surrounded or otherwise in a tricky situation, moving toward these can buy some time or keep an escape route open, as they will stop their advance toward Isaac and instead start moving away from him for a moment.

sections.heading: Swarm
sections.text: Swarms are similar to regular Attack Flies, but appear in tightly-packed clusters.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If a Swarm is somehow separated from its group, it quickly moves back to its group when it is able to.

sections.heading: Hush Fly
sections.text:
Hush Flies are mainly spawned by Hush and behave somewhat similar to Ring Flies, but do not fly towards Isaac and remain in a fixed path. Unlike Ring Flies, Hush Flies can form other shapes such as polygons. When spawned by Hush they can also orbit it, form a pattern and travel in a straight path, or form a pattern and chase after Isaac.

Hush Flies have a brief period of invincibility when Hush spawns them, making them appear to have more health than they actually have.

[Afterbirth+ onward] Hush Flies can also spawn outside of the Hush fight in some rare rooms. When encountered in these rooms they will continuously orbit in a fixed path.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Hush Flies are not affected by the Beelzebub transformation.

• [Repentance] They can also appear in ??? with the use of Red Key. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Army Fly
sections.text: Army Flies chase Isaac, moving in the cardinal directions as they do so. If there are other Army Flies in the room, they will form a single-file line while chasing Isaac.

sections.heading: Willo
sections.text: Willos circle a set distance around Isaac, moving with him perfectly, and firing shots inwards towards him; only one can fire at a time, and the one about to fire telegraphs this by flashing rapidly just beforehand. They circle quickly at even intervals, and can be hard to hit. If there is a Fire Place within the room, they can be guided into it; making this an efficient method of tackling this enemy. They do not deal contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Min-Min can spawn these; some of them behave normally, while some pop out of the ground, launch a volley of shots at Isaac, and disappear back into the ground.

• Mullighouls spawn these occasionally, and spawn 2 more when they die.

sections.heading: Ultra Famine Fly
sections.text: Ultra Famine Flies are flies spawned by Ultra Famine that charge at Isaac on a delay. They come in 3 sizes- small, medium and large.

sections.heading: Ultra Pestilence Fly
sections.text: Ultra Pestilence Flies are flies spawned by Ultra Pestilence that swarm around him, blocking shots and dealing contact damage. They also can be spawned by the Ultra Pestilence Fly Ball in Ultra Pestilence's 2nd phase. They come in 3 sizes- small, medium and large.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Black Fly has the lowest health of any enemy in the game, tied with the Corn.

• Eternal Flies were first added to the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original Binding of Isaac game.

• Before Rebirth, Eternal Flies simply became vulnerable and chased the player rather than turning into an Attack Fly.

• There is a variant of Moters in the Eternal Edition of the original The Binding of Isaac that resembles a ball of 4 Attack Flies, or 2 Moters stuck to each other. This enemy does not appear in Rebirth, likely due to being added in said Eternal Edition update that was added a while after the release of Rebirth.

• In a Q&A Reddit thread by Edmund McMillen, Edmund confirmed that the species of flies in The Binding of Isaac are house flies and botflies.

• [Repentance] The Willo originates from the Antibirth mod.

• The name Willo might be a reference to Will'o the Wisps, atmospheric ghost lights seen at night, especially over bogs, swamps or marshes.

• Although Army Flies were known to be revealed during Repentance's first PAX session, it was in fact first revealed in the latest blog of a now-canceled update for the Antibirth mod back in December 21, 2017.

Fly Bomb.title: Fly Bomb
Fly Bomb.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the fly enemy; other uses; Fly (Disambiguation)] 

Fly Bombs are enemies added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. They are characterized by their appearance of a small Bomb with wings.

They chase Isaac, attempting to circle around him as they do so. Upon death, they turn into a tiny Bomb that explodes shorty after. Running into a Fly Bomb causes it to explode instantly. The instant explosion deals a Half Red Heart of damage to Isaac and 40 damage to monsters unlike the tiny bomb's explosion which deals a Red Heart to Isaac and 100 damage to monsters.

sections.heading: Eternal Fly Bomb
sections.text: Eternal Fly Bombs are variants to Fly Bombs that exclusively spawn in a group of 3 and orbit Boom Fly spawned by The Horny Boys. Similar to Eternal Fly, they are immune to all damage until their respective Boom Fly dies. Then, they turn into tiny Bombs that explode shortly after. While generally immune to damage they can still be ran into and will explode like regular Fly Bombs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The [Repentance] Fly Bomb first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

Fly Trap.title: Fly Trap
Fly Trap.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Fly Traps are enemies added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

Floats slowly towards Isaac, orbited by 3 Attack Fly that spawn with it. It will, along the way, either cough to spawn an additional Attack Fly to orbit it or release a cloud of gas that pushes the flies outwards before they group back together and continue to orbit the Fly Trap. The Fly Trap will only fart if it has at least 3 Attack Flies in orbit and will continuously spawn flies until it has the minimum amount. The maximum amount of flies orbiting the Fly Trap is 6 and it will use the spawning attack less often the closer it reaches this threshold.

Upon death any orbiting Attack Flies will chase Isaac as usual.

Forever alone.title: Forever alone
Forever alone.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a blue attack fly that orbits a long distance from Isaac and deals 2 damage per tick or 30 damage per second on contact.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] This item can drop from killing Super Envy. [Before Repentance] Super Envy can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Solar System.

• The name of this item is a reference to the Forever Alone meme.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, this item had the same instant-kill property on contact with Fly and Pooter variants that an item like Halo of Flies has. This effect is removed in Rebirth.

fields.description: Spawns an attack fly that orbits a long distance from Isaac, dealing 30 damage per second.

Death's Head.title: Death's Head
Death's Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Death's Heads are invulnerable, flying enemies that move diagonally around the room and deal contact damage. They will bounce off of Isaac, walls, and each other, generally causing chaos in a room. They immediately die when the room is cleared.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• They can be killed if hit with the Chaos Card, Little Horn, or Euthanasia.

• [Repentance+] Death's Head and Brimstone Death's Head are destroyed by Hagalaz, leaving behind a Flesh Death's Head (all others are unaffected). [end edition note]

sections.heading: Dank Death's Head
sections.text: Dank Death's Heads behave the same as regular Death's Heads, but are vulnerable and must be killed to clear a room.

sections.heading: Flesh Death's Head
sections.text: Flesh Death's Heads are vulnerable, but do not need to be killed to clear a room. They release six blood shots upon death or upon clearing the room.

sections.heading: Cursed Death's Head
sections.text: Cursed Death's Heads behave the same as regular Death's Heads but have a purple aura around them. If Isaac enters the aura, he will be inflicted with the fear status effect for around two seconds. While feared, Isaac is unable to fire tears nor perform any other actions except moving for the duration of the effect.

sections.heading: Brimstone Death's Head
sections.text: Brimstone Death's Heads behave the same as regular Death's Heads in terms of movement. When Isaac passes close to them horizontally or vertically, they will pause in place and aim a faint red indicator beam in that direction, before following it up with a Brimstone laser.

sections.heading: Dusty Death's Head
sections.text: Dusty Death's Heads behave uniquely to other Death's Heads. They continuously travel horizontally across the screen, oscillating up and down, going off-screen and reentering on the opposite side. They are invulnerable and are destroyed once the room is cleared.

sections.heading: Redskull
sections.text: Redskulls move similar to Death's Heads, however if Isaac gets too close they will pause in place and release out a ring of fire. This ring can ignite certain enemies like the Rock Spider. Like Flesh Death's Heads, they can be killed, but will also die when the room is cleared.

sections.heading: Ultra Death Head
sections.text: Ultra Death Heads behave uniquely to other Death's Heads and more similarly to Dusty Death Heads, oscillating up and down in large wave-like patterns, going off-screen and reentering on the opposite side. They are summoned in a horde as a part of one of Ultra Death's attacks and are invulnerable, only being destroyed at the end of the attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Death's Head, [Afterbirth onward] Flesh Death's Head, Stoney, Cross Stoney, and Eggy are the only non-boss enemies with a death animation.

• [Afterbirth onward] In the game's files, the Dank Death's Head has a death animation that is impossible to see because it needs to be killed to clear a room.

• The Death's Head is based on the Bubble from The Legend of Zelda on the NES, as they are both skulls that are usually invulnerable which maneuver by bouncing off of walls.

• [Repentance] The Dusty Death's Head is based on the Medusa Head, as both fly in a wave-like pattern that is intended to be difficult to dodge.

• [Afterbirth onward] In a closet room in Womb, there is a room with 1 Red Poop, 4 Blood Donation Machines, and 4 Flesh Death's Heads. When entering the room, they appear to die quickly since no other enemies in the room exist there.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] If a Death's Head is permanently charmed by charming a Portal in Chapter 3, it cannot interact with enemies or enemy tears and will simply fly around the room.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Prior to Booster Pack #5, if Death Heads were in the process of dying, they could still damage Isaac.

• [Repentance] In Antibirth, Cursed Death's Heads were called Smokys. They could also spawn in the Chest.

• [Repentance] Cursed Death's Heads resemble The Heretic.

• [Repentance] Redskulls have a stray pixel on the top-right of their sprite which does appear in-game, and is animated similar to their fire.

Fatty.title: Fatty
Fatty.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the monster; the boss; Mega Fatty] 

Fatties walk slowly toward Isaac, occasionally stopping to fart, which pushes Isaac away without dealing damage if he is too close. This will also push away adjacent enemies to a lesser degree.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The Pale Fatty, Fat Sack, Blubber, and the Conjoined Fatty will not spawn anything on death if their HP is dropped to -25 or below in one instance (i.e., by using a Bomb).

sections.heading: Pale Fatty
sections.text: Pale Fatties behave like Fatties, but will also spit out 6 blood shots in all directions when farting. When killed, they have a chance to become a Blubber.

sections.heading: Flaming Fatty
sections.text:
Flaming Fatties behave identically to regular Fatties but have a chance to leave behind a damaging flame upon death. [Repentance] They can also spawn a damaging flame by farting.

Unlike other flaming enemies, they are not immune to damage from fire sources, and regular Fatties will not turn into Flaming Fatties upon contact with any source of fire.

sections.heading: Fat Sack
sections.text: Fat Sacks walk slowly towards Isaac and can leap offscreen and attempt to land on Isaac, shooting 6 bullets in all directions and leaving a puddle of Red Creep behind when it lands. Like Pale Fatties, they have a chance to turn into a Blubber when killed. These monsters behave very similar to Leapers.

sections.heading: Blubber
sections.text: Blubbers walk aimlessly around the room, randomly spewing a cluster of blood shots in all directions. When killed, there is a chance for it to become a Half Sack.

sections.heading: Half Sack
sections.text: Half Sacks walk aimlessly around the room and leave behind a trail of Red Creep.

sections.heading: Conjoined Fatty
sections.text:
Conjoined Fatties slowly walk towards Isaac and occasionally pause to fart out a line of damaging Green Creep. There is a chance that upon death, it will turn into a regular Fatty.

If killed while farting, the Creep line won't grow to its full length. It will instead stop spreading the instant the Conjoined Fatty is killed.

sections.heading: Blue Conjoined Fatty
sections.text: Blue Conjoined Fatties slowly walk towards Isaac and occasionally fart out a homing Ipecac shot at Isaac. Unlike normal Conjoined Fatties, they won't turn into any kind of Fatty upon death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] They only appear in normal mode.

• D10 can be used to reroll non-boss enemies in Chest and in The Void into Blue Conjoined Fatties even on Hard mode.

• [Repentance] They can also appear in ??? with the use of Red Key or by entering Treasure Rooms with the Blue Key. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Blue Conjoined Fatties now have a new appearance, resembling that of Hush. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Peeping Fatty
sections.text:
Peeping Fatties slowly walk towards Isaac and occasionally fart out 6 blood shots in all directions. They are unique in that they have two indestructible Peeping Fatty Eyes that float around them that are out of their sockets and attached by muscles.

Each eye generally prioritizes its focus on Isaac, but will occasionally become interested in something else, which could be an enemy, obstacle, or a collectible. The Peeping Fatty will sometimes begin pursuing whatever one or both of his eyes have become fascinated with, but will also prioritize chasing Isaac if he is in view.

If both eyes are destroyed (using Euthanasia, for example), the Fatty will become blind and wander around randomly.

sections.heading: Peeping Fatty Eye
sections.text:
Peeping Fatty Eyes spawn in pairs and behave differently from similar enemies, as they are attached by muscle-like cords to a Peeping Fatty. Peeping Fatty Eyes each have their individual object of focus which directs the Peeping Fatty's movements. They can still float over obstacles like their variants while the Peeping Fatty cannot. They will be destroyed once their correlating Peeping Fatty dies.

Each eye generally prioritizes its focus on Isaac, but will occasionally become interested in something else, which could be an enemy, obstacle, or a collectible. The Peeping Fatty will sometimes begin pursuing whatever one or both of his eyes have become fascinated with, but will also prioritize chasing Isaac if he is in view.

sections.heading: Bloaty
sections.text: Bloaties, unlike other Fatties, seem to be blind and do not chase Isaac nor target him. They lumber in random directions and periodically spit out a line of Green Creep and arcing projectiles in the direction they are facing or to its either side, horizontally or diagonally. The initial creep shot can hit Isaac even if he has flight. Upon death, they leave a small puddle of green creep.

sections.heading: Bubbles
sections.text: Bubbles slowly walk towards Isaac like regular Fatties and will occasionally fart, sending out a burst of short range projectiles in all directions. Hitting a Bubbles will cause it to shoot a projectile in a random direction. Upon death, they will burst into a geyser of projectiles that rain down in a large radius.

sections.heading: Shady
sections.text:
Shadies follow Isaac at a faster pace than regular Fatties and have two attacks which they perform:

• They can shoot a large black and red projectile towards Isaac which releases accelerating shots perpendicular to itself while traveling. Upon colliding with a wall, the large projectile creates a ring of shots that spread outward.

• They can jump in place, creating lines of explosions in the cardinal directions upon landing which span the length of the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Shadies are one of the few enemies which utilize Damage Scaling, making their unimpressive HP total misleading. Their armor is quite high and allows them to take massive amounts of punishment before being taken down, comparable even to some bosses.

sections.heading: Quakey
sections.text: Quakeys walk slowly towards Isaac and occasionally attempt to jump on Isaac, shooting out 8 rock shots when they hit the ground and causing rocks to fall from the ceiling. Isaac will take knockback if he is standing too close to a Quakey's zone of impact.

sections.heading: Big Bony
sections.text: Big Bonies walk towards towards Isaac, and occasionally fire a large bone projectile that bounces off of objects and can be destroyed.

sections.heading: Vis Fatty
sections.text:
Vis Fatties spawn with a Fetal Demon attached to their slit abdomens. The Fatty will slowly walk towards the player while the Fetal Demon occasionally lunges towards Isaac if he gets too close. As it is tethered, the Demon has a limited range of movement. Occasionally, the Vis Fatty will fart, which briefly pushes the Fetal Demon away, giving it a substantial increase in range, as well as creating puddles of damaging Red Creep around the Fatty, the Demon, and the cord that attaches them.

If the Fatty is killed first, the Demon will be broken free and continuously chase down the player similar to Gemini Suture. If the Demon is killed first, the Vis Fatty unleashes a Brimstone laser in the closest diagonal direction to Isaac. It will then fly backwards around the room diagonally, bumping off of walls and tall blocks, all while continuously shooting Brimstone behind it.

sections.heading: Fetal Demon
sections.text: Fetal Demons usually spawn tethered to a Vis Fatty's slit abdomen and occasionally makes short lunges towards Isaac if he gets close. They can also be propelled a longer distance when the Vis Fatty farts. If the Vis Fatty is killed, they will chase Isaac, similarly to Gemini Suture. The only other place where they can be encountered is in the Mom fight in Mausoleum / Gehenna, and is the only place where they are encountered alone.

sections.heading: Gutted Fatty
sections.text:
Gutted Fatties lumber around the room aimlessly and occasionally shoot out a pile of Festering Guts downwards leaving a trail of Red Creep. They can spawn a maximum of 3.

Every time a third of the Gutted Fatty's health is depleted, it spawns a Gutted Fatty Eye. These eyes normally float around the Gutted Fatty they emerged from and block shots. Whenever Isaac walks too close to one of these eyes, they will abandon their position and begin slowly chasing him instead. The eyes will return to defending the Gutted Fatty if Isaac walks far enough away from them. The eyes only die when the Gutted Fatty dies.

Upon death, the Gutted Fatty explodes into a massive shower of blood projectiles, similar to that of Bubbles.

sections.heading: Gutted Fatty Eye
sections.text:
Gutted Fatty Eyes spawn in pairs, but do not bounce around the room erratically like similar enemies. They are spawned by a Gutted Fatty as it takes damage, one at 66% HP and a second at 33% HP. When spawned, they will hover around their correlating Gutted Fatty blocking tears. They will be destroyed once their correlating Gutted Fatty dies.

Whenever Isaac walks too close to one of these eyes, they will abandon their position and begin slowly chasing him instead, moving in wave-like patterns. If both eyes are chasing Isaac, they will maintain a distance between the two as they move in order to cover more area. They will return to defending the Gutted Fatty if Isaac walks far enough away from them.

sections.heading: Stoney
sections.text: Stoneys walk towards Isaac while blocking his shots. They stop and catch their breath after chasing Isaac for a few seconds. They do not do contact damage but will often push Isaac around. They are invincible, but die when the room is cleared, similar to the Death's Head enemies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Stoneys aren't unlocked yet, they will be replaced by Fatties in Normal mode, or Conjoined Fatties in Hard Mode.

• Spectral tears and [Before Repentance] piercing tears will pierce through Stoneys.

• [Before Repentance] If they are poisoned with The Virus, upon clearing the room, they have a chance to drop a Black Heart despite not taking damage.

• Stoneys are immune to all status effects.

• Stoneys are destroyed by Chaos Card, Euthanasia, and Little Horn.

• [Repentance+] Also destroyed by Hagalaz.

• Stoneys were nerfed in update v1.06.0188 by making them pause periodically to catch their breath while following the player. Before that, Stoneys would continually chase the player.

sections.heading: Cross Stoney
sections.text:
A Cross Stoney is a type of Stoney added in Booster Pack #5. These new enemies act like a hybridization of a Stoney and a Cross Stone Shooter; they constantly chase the player like a Stoney but will shoot 4 shots outwards vertically and diagonally like a Cross Grimace.

Cross Stoneys only appear in challenge #32 (Aprils Fool) as replacements to regular Stoneys.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Cross Stoneys are destroyed by Chaos Card, Euthanasia, and Little Horn.

• [Repentance+] Also destroyed by Hagalaz.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Death's Head, Flesh Death's Head, Stonies, Cross Stonies, and Eggy are the only non-boss enemies with a death animation.

• Conjoined Fatties and Bloaties are one of five enemies (four without Repentance, three without Afterbirth+) in the game that use Creep as projectiles, the others are Ultra Pride, Meatballs and The Thing.

• Blubbers appear to be headless Pale Fatties or, more accurately, headless Fat Sacks.

• Similarly, Half Sacks appear to be the lower portions of Pale Fatties or, more accurately, the lower portions of Fat Sacks.

• [Afterbirth onward] Conjoined Fatties and Blue Conjoined Fatties suffer the condition of polycephaly, having more than one head.

• [Afterbirth only] Conjoined Fatties and Blue Conjoined Fatties make the same high-pitched growling noises as Gapers instead of the lower-pitched ones used by other Fatties.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Stoneys make the sounds of a pitched-down Gaper.

• [Repentance] Stoneys make the sounds of a pitched-down Fatty.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Antibirth developer Kilburn first revealed Cross Stoneys on the 1st of April for Booster Pack #5.

• It was revealed on the 1st of April, and Cross Stoneys are exclusive to the Aprils Fool Challenge.

• [Repentance] Bubbles, Quakies, and Big Bonies originate from the Antibirth mod.

• In Antibirth, Quakies have a different face.

• The Big Bony's bone attack is also different from Antibirth, where the bone was instead a lobbed projectile that created shockwaves in the place of its impact. Big Bonies also used to spawn in Mausoleum.

• [Repentance] Vis Fatties look very similar to Exorcists.

• [Repentance] Bloaty's name and design is somewhat a reminiscent to the human corpse's bloating stage, which causes the corpse to swell up and bear swollen lips and eyeballs due to gas.

• [Repentance] Shadies are inspired by the Shadow Ninja enemy from the Shadow Warrior game series.

Gaper.title: Gaper
Gaper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Gapers walk towards Isaac by the most direct route possible. They will actively path around obstacles and other enemies that block their path to Isaac. Upon death, there is a 50% chance they leave behind a Pacer or a Gusher; if this check succeeds, there is a 33% chance it leaves behind a Gusher, otherwise it leaves behind a Pacer (in other words, 1 in 3 Gapers leave behind a Pacer on death, and 1/6 leave behind a Gusher; 50% of them will leave nothing).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: All Gaper variations will never leave behind an enemy on death if their HP is dropped to -25 or less in one instance (i.e., by using a Bomb). The Level 2 Gaper is an exception and will do so regardless.

sections.heading: Frowning Gaper
sections.text: Frowning Gapers walk slowly toward Isaac (though faster than Gapers) and deal contact damage. They start out with their eyes closed, and when they have line of sight with Isaac, they will open their eyes and gain extra permanent speed. Upon death, they will usually transform into a Pacer or Gusher.

sections.heading: Flaming Gaper
sections.text: Flaming Gapers walk slowly toward Isaac (slightly faster than Gapers) and deal contact damage. Upon death, they have a 50% chance to leave behind a Pacer or a Gusher.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Unlike other flaming enemies, they are not immune to damage from fire sources and regular Gapers will not turn into Flaming Gapers upon contact with any source of fire.

sections.heading: Nulls
sections.text: Nulls walk slowly toward Isaac (similarly to Frowning Gapers) and deal contact damage. They start out with their eyes closed, and when they have line of sight with Isaac, they will open their eyes, though without a speed increase. They periodically fade into and out of visibility.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• White Champion Nulls may not be able to turn invisible while invincible.

• They are referred to as "Nulls", which goes both for its singular and plural usage.

• [Afterbirth onward] The health bar that Spider Mod adds to enemies will not appear under a Nulls while it is invisible.

sections.heading: Cyclopia
sections.text: Cyclopias walk toward Isaac (slightly slower than Gapers), dealing contact damage and leaving behind a short-lasting trail of damaging Red Creep. Occasionally shoots a blood shot towards Isaac.

sections.heading: Gurgle
sections.text: Gurgles walk towards Isaac (significantly faster than Gapers), dealing contact damage and periodically firing Ipecac shots at him. These shots can kill other enemies caught in their blast radius, but Gurgles themselves are immune to their own shots as well as Ipecac shots, bombs, and [Repentance] fireballs from other monsters. They can turn into a Splasher upon death.

sections.heading: Crackle
sections.text: Crackles walk towards Isaac at the same speed as a Gurgle, dealing contact damage and periodically shooting a fireball which releases 4 lines of fire in the cardinal directions when it touches the ground. These lines of fire span the length and height of a normal sized room. Like the Gurgle, they are immune to fireballs, Ipecac shots, and bombs from other monsters.

sections.heading: Blue Gaper
sections.text: Blue Gapers walk towards Isaac slightly faster than Gapers, and deal contact damage. They are mainly spawned by Hush.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• They can rarely appear in Dirty Bedrooms and I AM ERROR rooms.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] They can rarely appear in a closet on most floors before Chapter 4.

• [Repentance] Blue Gapers can also be found in the unique rooms created by Blue Key and in Red Rooms created on ???. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Greed Gaper
sections.text:
Greed Gapers walk toward Isaac, dealing contact damage. They are mainly spawned during the Ultra Greed boss fight.

[Repentance] If they deal contact damage to Isaac, they will force Isaac to drop or lose some coins, similar to Keepers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• They have 4 different appearances, though this is purely cosmetic.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] 2 Greed Gapers may rarely replace the Shopkeeper in Shops.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] 2-4 Greed Gapers have a chance to appear in Treasure Rooms.

• [Repentance] Greed Gapers no longer appear in Treasure Rooms; layouts that used to contain them now contain Bulbs. They can, however, appear in Ultra Secret Rooms. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Deep Gaper
sections.text: Deep Gapers are initially hidden and emerge from the floor once all initial enemies in the room have been killed. Deep Gapers walk towards Isaac slightly faster than Gapers after emerging and deal contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • This enemy has 14 design variants, 7 for Downpour and 7 for Dross. These variants are purely cosmetic with the exception of one that has a Small Leech stuck to its head, which will detach from it and chase Isaac when the Deep Gaper is killed.

sections.heading: Blurb
sections.text:
Blurbs walk slowly towards Isaac, dealing contact damage. After taking some damage or getting close to Isaac, they fire a chaotic burst of tears at him and chases Isaac at the speed of Frowning Gapers, attempting to deal contact damage. They have a high chance to turn into Pacers or Gushers upon death.

They will still spit out their projectiles if killed in an instant with high damage, firing towards Isaac even if he is not within targeting range.

sections.heading: Wraith
sections.text: Wraiths walk towards Isaac slightly faster than Gapers, dealing contact damage. They are invisible and can only be seen through the reflection they cast in the water, or the ripples they make as they walk. The occasional lightning strikes in Downpour will also make them briefly visible.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • They are visible in the Mirrored World, but their reflections will be invisible instead, appearing when lightning strikes.

sections.heading: Rotten Gaper
sections.text:
Rotten Gapers chase Isaac but have different behaviors depending on their appearance, and each has a different subtype (10.3.x).

| ID | Image | Specifications

| 10.3.1 | | Fairly high speed, same as a Frowning Gaper.

| 10.3.2 | | Significantly higher speed, slightly less than a Gazing Globin.

| 10.3.3 | | Moderate speed; spawns a Small Maggot every 2 seconds, but no more than 6 at a time.

| 10.3.4 | | Moderate speed, same as a Gaper.

| 10.3.5 | | Moves similarly to Lust, gradually gaining momentum, and moves very fast. Doesn't try to run into Isaac, instead tries to 'orbit' around him.

sections.heading: Dead Isaac
sections.text: Dead Isaacs are enemies exclusively spawned by Mother as part of one of her attacks. They are summoned from the bottom of the arena and will walk directly upward (ignoring Isaac completely), dealing contact damage. Once they reach Mother, she swipes at them, killing them, releasing a burst of blood shots, and launching their corpses towards Isaac. After a while, she ends this attack by slamming down both hands, which causes a small rock wave to appear beneath any remaining Dead Isaacs, launching them up into the air.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Due to Dead Isaac only being encountered via one attack, it is possible to go multiple runs without finding them. They are required in order to complete the Bestiary.

sections.heading: Twitchy
sections.text: Twitchies are a Gaper/Trite hybrid that alternate between chasing Isaac and rapidly leaping at him, dealing contact damage. They leap at Isaac 1-3 times before returning to chasing him on foot, and their leaps can target him from almost across an entire normal-sized room. They can leap to Isaac's current position, or where Isaac is heading, and can also leap away to dodge incoming fire.

sections.heading: Level 2 Gaper
sections.text: Level 2 Gapers walk toward Isaac (faster than Gapers but slower than Frowning Gapers), dealing a full Heart of contact damage. They split into a Level 2 Horf and Level 2 Gusher upon death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] When Head of the Keeper is picked up as Keeper, he will look similar to the Greed Gaper. [end edition note] 

• The appearance of Cyclopias is reminiscent of the fatal birth defect of the same name, which is characterized by the failure of the embryonic prosencephalon to properly divide the orbit of the eyes into two cavities.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] A Stoney makes the same sound as a Large Champion Gaper. [end edition note] 

• Frowning Gapers and Nulls don't make noises until they open their eyes.

• [Afterbirth onward] Greed Gapers are also known as Greedlings, a name given by a card of it from The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls, although it's seldom referred to as a "Greedling" by players.

• Gapers have among the most variations of any 'family' of monster.

• [Repentance] Blurbs spawned outside of Downpour will be skin-toned. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Wraiths spawned in rooms without water will appear translucent.

• [Repentance] Blurbs, Deep Gapers, Wraiths, Rotten Gapers, and Twitchies originate from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Deep Gapers were referred to as Tidal Gapers.

• [Repentance] Despite being a hybrid with a Trite, Twitchies aren't affected by Bursting Sack due to being categorized as a Gaper variant. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] 34 Dead Isaacs are specifically spawned in Mother's attack, referencing the 34 playable characters, implying that they are all dead. This makes sense, as all characters really are Isaac himself, whom we see suffocating in a chest in Ending 20. [end edition note] 

• A Frowning Gaper figure can be seen in a screenshot for the player's house in Mewgenics, another game from Edmund McMillen.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If a Dark-Red champion Frowning Gaper does not become a Pacer or Gusher and regenerates, the head won't appear until it sees Isaac. The same goes for a Gaper, however the head won't appear at all.
Bug note: If an Explosivo tear is stuck to a Nulls when it becomes invisible, the tear will fall to the ground.
Bug note: The Explosivo tear will instakill a Nulls when it becomes invisible.
Bug note: If a Champion Gaper is killed and it turns into a Pacer or Gusher, it will no longer be a champion.
Bug note: Cyclopias become unable to shoot while slowed, either through attacks that cause the slow status or global effects like Stop Watch.

Hopper.title: Hopper
Hopper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
A Hopper jumps around the room, doing contact damage to Isaac. They jump slowly around the room until Isaac gets close to them, at which point they start chasing Isaac. They can jump across rocks and gaps.

Hoppers transform into Flaming Hoppers after touching a Fire Place, fire spawned from Fire Mind or [Repentance] Red Candle, or if they touch a Hot Bombs bomb.

sections.heading: Flaming Hopper
sections.text:
Flaming Hoppers behave similarly to normal Hoppers in that they will randomly hop around the room, following Isaac only when within a certain range. Unlike normal Hoppers, Flaming Hoppers have a larger range of detection and can hop both further and faster.

Flaming Hoppers will still take damage from the burning status effect.

sections.heading: Leaper
sections.text: Leapers behave similarly to Hoppers, hopping around the room and chasing Isaac when he gets close but can also jump into the air and land on Isaac's position, firing four blood projectiles in the cardinal directions upon landing.

sections.heading: Sticky Leaper
sections.text: Sticky Leapers behave like normal Leapers but spawn a pool of Black Creep and spew several tar shots around themselves upon landing.

sections.heading: Eggy
sections.text: Eggies behave similarly to Hopper jumping around the room and chasing Isaac, spawning white creep wherever it jumps. When it takes enough damage, it spawns a group of Swarm Spiders. After dying its body remains for a few seconds where it can delay the room from being completed.

sections.heading: Tainted Hopper
sections.text:
Tainted Hoppers are much stronger versions of Hoppers. They jump and twirl consecutively around the room, shooting 4 rings of projectiles, each increasing in size compared to the last. The first ring has 4 projectiles, the second has 6, the third has 8, and the last has 12.

They are exclusive to the Ascent to Home.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Hoppers share similar movement patterns with Tektites from The Legend Of Zelda.

• Death's Head, Flesh Death's Head, Stoney, Cross Stoney, and Eggies are the only non-boss enemies with a death animation.

Host.title: Host
Host.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the enemy; the challenge; The Host] 

Hosts are immobile skulls. When lowered down, which is their normal state, they are invincible to every source of damage except status effects such as poison, burning, being knocked into a wall by Hemoptysis, or Knockout Drops' knockback. Occasionally, they will pop up and shoot three spread shots towards Isaac, revealing a fleshy stem that can be damaged. Attacking a Host while it is lowered will increase the delay before it pops up: if it takes what would be a large amount of damage at once they will grimace.

Hosts deal no contact damage either when closed or open.

[Repentance+] Hagalaz has special interactions with these enemies when used:

• Host - Destroys and leaves behind a Red Host

• Hard Host - Destroys and leaves behind a Red Host

• Mobile Host - Destroys and leaves behind a Flesh Mobile Host

• Floast - Destroys and does not leave behind anything [end edition note]

sections.heading: Red Host
sections.text: Red Hosts can replace regular Hosts in any area. Their skull is replaced by a vulnerable red fleshlike material. Unlike normal Hosts, they can still take damage when lowered down, but they will fire 5 blood shots instead of 3.

sections.heading: Hard Host
sections.text: Hard Hosts behave similarly to regular Hosts, however instead of firing any shots when they lift their skull, they slam down and fire a tremor towards Isaac. The tremor will destroy most obstacles and damage most monsters in its path. They also deal damage on contact. If Isaac is too close to a Hard Host when it slams down he will be knocked back.

sections.heading: Mobile Host
sections.text: Mobile Hosts function the same as the original hosts but now do contact damage and slowly approach Isaac. They also have a more random delay between the times they open up, unlike the immobile Host which opens up instantly if it has a line of sight to Isaac and has been closed for a set amount of time without being shot.

sections.heading: Flesh Mobile Host
sections.text: Flesh Mobile Hosts are like Mobile Hosts, but can be damaged at any time and will fire 5 blood shots instead of 3.

sections.heading: Floast
sections.text: Floasts bounce around diagonally, occasionally opening up to shoot a triple shot like regular Hosts. Unlike regular Hosts, they deal contact damage and resemble Mobile Hosts more in that sense.

sections.heading: Mushroom
sections.text:
Mushrooms appear exclusively in Chapter 2 and have a 20% chance to replace Hosts.

Mushrooms start by hiding inside of their cap. While inside, they take only 25% damage. Occasionally, they pop out for a few seconds, shooting 4 red shots in either the cardinal or diagonal directions. Unlike Hosts, Mushrooms deal contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Mushrooms will not resist damage while petrified.

• If Mushrooms aren't unlocked yet, they are replaced by Hosts.

• [Repentance] The rock waves spawned by Hard Hosts can open Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Hosts originated from a multiplayer flash game created by Edmund McMillen called HOST.

• Hosts are very similar to the Met enemies from the Mega Man series. Both are immune to any kind of damage when they are lowered down, and when they pop up, they become vulnerable and shoot three shots.

• Additionally, Mobile Hosts behave like the Neo Met, a version of the Met that walks after shooting.

• The Gate physically resembles a giant Host.

• [edition anr] In the game's files, Red Hosts and their walking variations have grimace animations that are impossible to see in-game because they are always vulnerable.

• [Repentance] When Mom's Bracelet is used on a Host/Mobile Host, the resulting Red Host/Flesh Mobile Host will use its respective grimace animation.

• [Repentance] Using Mom's Bracelet on a Host/Mobile Host will transform it into a Red Host/Flesh Mobile Host.

• A Mobile Host's body won't change color when transformed. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Floasts and Hard Hosts originate from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Floasts used be to called Floating Hosts.

• [Repentance] The Floast's name is a reference to a monster of the same name from The End is Nigh.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Hosts or Mobile Hosts are affected by fear, [Afterbirth onward] shrink, or stunned, then if the effect wears off at the same time as they try to attack you, they sometimes attack without the corresponding animation.
Bug note: Little Horn effect cannot be triggered on Mobile Hosts.
Bug note: If two Mobile Hosts are affected by permenant Charm (on the C0CKFGHT seed), they do not become vulnerable when touching eachother, meaning they cannot attack eachother or be damaged by isaac, softlocking the game

Knight.title: Knight
Knight.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Knights are enemies that can normally only be damaged from their exposed brains on the backs of their heads. However, explosions, attacks that pierce enemies (Brimstone, Cupid's Arrow, etc.), or melee attacks (Spirit Sword, Mom's Knife, etc.), will deal damage from any direction. The Knight normally walks around in random directions and will dash at Isaac if he is within line of sight.

sections.heading: Selfless Knight
sections.text: Selfless Knights are considerably faster than regular Knights but otherwise function the same. Rather than an exposed brain, they have Isaac's face on the backs of their heads.

sections.heading: Floating Knight
sections.text: Floating Knights are similar to ordinary Knights but are slightly slower and can fly over obstacles.

sections.heading: Bone Knight
sections.text: Bone Knights are similar to ordinary Knights but leaves behind a short-lasting trail of damaging Red Creep. They charge faster than an ordinary Knight, but not as fast as the Selfless Knight. [Before Repentance] Bone Knights are the only variant of Knights that are susceptible to knockback both from the front and from the back.

sections.heading: Loose Knight
sections.text: Loose Knights are similar to ordinary Knights, but move slower and separates into a Brainless Knight and Pon when killed.

sections.heading: Brainless Knight
sections.text: Brainless Knights are a variant of Knight created when a Loose Knight dies. They alternate between running around the room along the cardinal directions and aimlessly walking in circles, charging at Isaac when he gets in line of sight. It dies when its corresponding Pon dies; otherwise, they are invincible.

sections.heading: Black Knight
sections.text: Black Knights are a variant of Knight that have slightly higher health and will walk erratically around the room, charging at Isaac if he is within line of sight. When charging, they accelerate rapidly, sending waves of fire in the cardinal directions and becoming stunned momentarily after colliding with a wall or obstacle. A Black Knight's mask will also reflect any of Isaac's tears that come in contact with it. They are almost immune to knockback and other forced-movement (such as Black Hole).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] Hagalaz has the following interactions with the Knight and its variations:

• Knight, Floating Knight, Bone Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Brain

• Selfless Knight - Notably, no effect

• Loose Knight, Black Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Pon

• Brainless Knight - Destroys and leaves nothing
[end edition note] 

• The Knight is a monster in two segments: an invisible, invincible "shield" segment that leads the way and the visible "body" that follows close behind. The shield takes no damage and partially covers the body, stopping shots that would damage it.

• Sometimes, when a Knight changes directions, it appears to pause for a moment; this is because the shield segment is moving past the body segment, and the body won't move until the shield moves away from it, the same way the trailing segments of Larry Jr. or Buttlicker chains behave.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Prior to Booster Pack #5, the Knight and its variants were briefly invulnerable when they spawned, or when Isaac entered the room they are in. They would become vulnerable when they started moving.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, Knights were completely vulnerable when they spawned; the shield segment did not cover the Knight's front until it started moving, so Isaac could shoot it in the face for damage as soon as it appeared.

• Items that provide a fear effect (like Dark Matter) work remarkably well because they run away from Isaac, exposing their weak side.

• Items that have a damage-over-time effect (such as Fire Mind or Scorpio) also work well, since hitting them on the shield portion will still inflict the effect and mitigate the need to hit them from behind.

• The name of the monster is a reference to the Darknut (also known as Tartnuc) enemy from The Legend of Zelda who, similar to Knights, cannot be harmed from their front.

• Floating Knights cannot fly over key blocks.

• If Isaac charms a Knight and it is the only enemy in the room, the Knight will chase Isaac but will not charge, making the Knight more difficult to damage until the effect is gone.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Black Knight, Brainless Knight, and Loose Knight first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• In Antibirth, Brainless Knights were referred to as Empty Knights.

• Black Knights had a slightly different appearance in Antibirth and would spawn in the Mausoleum.

• Knights and their variants first appear in Chapter 2 (Caves,Catacombs,Flooded Caves), but become much more common in Chapter 3 (Depths,Necropolis,Dank Depths).

• [Repentance] The functionality of Black Knights and their ability to deflect Isaac's tears from the front is similar to that of Eternal Knight champions in the original flash version of the Binding of Isaac: Eternal Edition.

• [Repentance+] Bone Knight is the only Knight variant that does not play sound effects.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The hitbox of Dark Red Champion Knights (and their variants) do not change when they crumble into goo, and they must be shot from the back to damage them.
