Level Generation.title: Level Generation
Level Generation.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Level generation is the process the game uses to create each floor. Each floor has its own requirements of size, special rooms, and dead ends that must be met.

sections.heading: Process
sections.text:
First, the game determines how many rooms will generate on the floor. Later floors have more rooms, and [cu: Labyrinth] makes the floor much larger.

• If the floor is not XL or The Void:

• NumberOfRooms = 3.33 × FloorDepth + 5-6 (maximum of 20)

• If the floor is an XL floor:

• NumberOfRooms = 1.8 × (3.33 × FloorDepth + 5-6) (maximum of 45)

• If the floor is The Void:

• NumberOfRooms = 50-59

• 2-3 more rooms are added if playing on Hard Mode

• 4 more rooms are added if the floor has Curse of the Lost.

Then the minimum number of dead ends the floor must generate is set.

• All floors have at least 5 dead ends:

• 1 dead end is added to all floors except the first floor.

• 1 dead end is added to XL floors.

• 2 dead ends are added to The Void.

• [Repentance] 1 dead end is added if Isaac has Voodoo Head. [end edition note] 

Next, special rooms are generated in dead ends.

• Special rooms are placed in order from the dead end farthest from the starting room to the closest.

• If all dead ends on a floor become occupied by special rooms, no more special rooms can generate.

• Chest, Dark Room, and The Void only generate Boss Rooms and Secret Rooms/Super Secret Rooms (and a Grave Room in the Dark Room).

Special rooms generate in the following order:

• Boss Room (guaranteed).

• If it is an XL floor, two boss rooms will be generated back to back.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Multiple Boss Rooms are generated in The Void. [end edition note] 

• Super Secret Room (guaranteed).

• [Repentance] Two Super Secret Rooms will be generated if Isaac has Luna. [end edition note] 

• Shop (guaranteed for the first 3 Chapters).

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Also guaranteed in Chapter 4 if Isaac has Silver Dollar [end edition note] .

• [Repentance] Also guaranteed in Chapter 5 if Isaac has Holy Crown or Wicked Crown). [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Will not be generated on the third and subsequent Victory Laps. [end edition note] 

• Treasure Room (guaranteed for the first 3 Chapters).

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Also guaranteed in Chapter 4 if Isaac has Bloody Crown. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Also guaranteed in Chapter 5 if Isaac has Holy Crown or Wicked Crown). [end edition note] 

• If it is an XL floor, two Treasure Rooms will be generated.

• Planetarium (base 1% chance to be generated in Chapter 1 through Chapter 3, but will not be generated in later chapters; skipping Treasure Rooms, and obtaining one of a number of items and trinkets will modify this chance).

• Dice Room or Sacrifice Room (1/7 (~14%) base chance, plus a second 1/4 chance for a total of 5/14 (~36%) if Isaac’s total health is equal to or greater than his total Heart Containers).

• If a Sacrifice Room is successfully generated, it has a 1/50 base chance to become a Dice Room instead, plus a second 1/5 chance for a total of 27/125 (~22%) if Isaac has 2 or more Keys.

• Library (1/20 chance).

• [Before Repentance] The code specifically checks for a flag that is supposed to increase Library generation rate if a book was touched, but the flag is never set. That code was removed in Repentance.

• Curse Room ( [Before Repentance] 1/7 chance [Repentance] 1/4 chance).

• [Before Repentance] The code specifically checks for a flag that is supposed to increase Curse room generation rate if Devil Room was visited this run, but the flag is never set. That code was removed in Repentance.

• [Repentance] An additional Curse Room is generated on each floor if Isaac has Voodoo Head; an extra dead end is also generated to accommodate it. [end edition note] 

• Mini-Boss Room (1/4 chance, plus a second 1/3 chance for a total of 1/2 (50%) if it is the first floor).

• Challenge Room (guaranteed if Isaac’s total health is equal to or greater than his total heart containers; will not be generated otherwise).

• Will not be generated on the first floor, and has a 50% chance on the second floor.

• Will always be a Boss Challenge Room on the second floor of a chapter, and a normal Challenge Room otherwise.

• Vault or Arcade (guaranteed if Isaac has 5 or more Coins and it’s the second floor of a Chapter; will not be generated otherwise).

• If an Arcade is successfully generated, it has a 1/10 chance to be a Vault instead, plus a second 1/3 chance for a total of 2/5 (40%) if Isaac has 2 or more Keys.

• [Repentance] If Isaac has 2 or more Keys but less than 5 Coins, a Vault can still be generated. If Isaac has 5 or more Coins but less than 2 Keys, and if the 1/10 chance to become a Vault passes, then neither an Arcade or a Vault will be generated. [end edition note] 

• Clean Bedroom or Dirty Bedroom (1/50 chance, plus a second 1/5 chance for a total of 27/125 (~22%) if Isaac has 1/2 or fewer Red Hearts and no Soul Hearts, or 1 or fewer Soul Hearts and no Red/Bone Hearts).

• Equal chance to be a Clean or Dirty Bedroom.

• Will only be generated in the first 3 Chapters.

• Secret Room (guaranteed).

• Each location candidate is given a starting weight of 10-14, reduced by 3 if it has only 2 neighboring rooms, and reduced by 6 if it has only 1 neighboring room. The highest weight candidate is picked.

• • In practice, this means a Secret Room will be extremely likely to have at least 2 rooms adjacent to it, unless it's the very first floor, where occasionally one will be placed at a dead end for lack of anywhere else to put it.

• Will not be placed next to a Boss Room, Super Secret Room, another Secret Room, or the starting room if it's The Chest or Dark Room.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] An additional Secret Room will be generated if Isaac has Fragmented Card. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] An additional Secret Room will be generated if Isaac has Luna, three if he also has Fragmented Card. [end edition note] 

• Ultra Secret Room (guaranteed).

• [Afterbirth+ onward] A Grave Room is placed if the floor is Dark Room. [end edition note] 

• Normal Room layouts are chosen.

• Each room has a set difficulty number, which is chosen based on the current floor of the chapter and if it's Hard Mode or not.

• • Normal Mode floor 1: 1-5

• • Normal Mode floor 2: 5-10

• • Hard Mode floor 1: [Before Repentance] 5 only / [Repentance] 1-10 (1 and 10 are less common)

• • Hard Mode floor 2: [Before Afterbirth+] 10 / [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] 10-15 / [Repentance] 5-15 (5 is less common)

• • XL Floors count as [Before Repentance] floor 1 / [Repentance] both floors

• • Chapters 5 and 6 count as [Before Repentance] floor 1 / [Repentance] floor 2

• • The Void on Normal Mode: 5-10 ( [Repentance] and 20)

• • The Void on Hard Mode: 5-15 / [Repentance] 5-20

sections.heading: Pseudo-Code
sections.text:
Some parts of the level generation are based on the following pseudo-code:

--Pseudo lua code for getting the number of rooms for a floor.

NumberOfRooms = Min(20, Rand(0, 1) + 5 + Floor(StageId * 10 / 3))
if CurseOfTheLabyrinth then
NumberOfRooms = Min(45, Floor(NumberOfRooms * 1.8))
elseif CurseOfTheLost then
NumberOfRooms += 4
end
if StageId == 12 then --The Void
NumberOfRooms = 50 + (Rand() % 10)
end
if IsHardDifficulty then
NumberOfRooms += 2 + Rand(0, 1)
end

--Pseudo lua code for getting the number of deadends a floor must have.

MinDeadEnds = 5
if StageId ~= 1 then
MinDeadEnds += 1
end
if CurseOfTheLabyrinth then
MinDeadEnds += 1
end
if StageId == 12 then
MinDeadEnds += 2
end

-Deadends are sorted by distance from the starting room descending.
--e.g. Boss room is placed in the farthest deadend, super secret is placed in the next farthest deadend

--DequeueDeadend also resizes the deadend. This is important to note because that means most deadends get changed to a 1x1 by the end of this.

PlaceRoom(ROOM_BOSS, DequeueDeadend())
--Super Secret
PlaceRoom(ROOM_SUPERSECRET, DequeueDeadend())
--Shop
if StageId < 7 or (StageId < 9 and HasTrinket(SilverDollar)) and VictoryLap < 3 then
PlaceRoom(ROOM_SHOP, DequeueDeadend())
end
--Treasure
if StageId < 7 or (StageId < 9 and HasTrinket(BloodyCrown)) then
PlaceRoom(ROOM_TREASURE, DequeueDeadend())
end
--Dice and Sacrifice
if StageId < 12 then
local deadend = DequeueDeadend() --resizes the room :(
if deadend ~= nil then
local roomType = nil
if Rng() % 50 == 0 or (Rng() % 5 == 0 and GetNumKeys() > 1) then
roomType = ROOM_DICE
else
roomType = ROOM_SACRIFICE
end
if Rng() % 7 == 0 or (Rng() & 3 == 0 and GetHearts() + GetSoulHearts() >= GetMaxHearts()) then
PlaceRoom(roomType)
else
QueueDeadend(deadend)
end
end
end
--Library
local deadend = DequeueDeadend()
if deadend ~= nil then
if Rng() % 20 == 0 or (Rng() & 3 == 0 and GetStateFlag(STATE_BOOK_PICKED_UP)) then
PlaceRoom(ROOM_LIBRARY, deadend)
else
QueueDeadend(deadend)
end
end
--Curse
local deadend = DequeueDeadend()
if deadend ~= nil then
if Rng() & 1 == 0 or (Rng() & 3 == 0 and GetStateFlag(STATE_DEVILROOM_VISITED)) then
PlaceRoom(ROOM_CURSE, deadend)
else
QueueDeadend(deadend)
end
end
--MiniBoss
local boss = GetMiniBossRoom() --mini boss is picked based on floor, STATE_ULTRAPRIDE_SPAWNED and rng
local deadend = DequeueDeadend()
if deadend ~= nil then
if Rng() & 3 == 0 or (Rng() & 2 == 0 and StageId == 1) then
PlaceRoom(boss, deadend)
else
QueueDeadend(deadend)
end
end
--Challenge
local deadend = DequeueDeadend()
if deadend ~= nil then
if (Rng() & 1 == 0 or StageId > 2) and GetHearts() + GetSoulHearts() >= GetMaxHearts() and StageId > 1 then
PlaceRoom(boss, deadend)
else
QueueDeadend(deadend)
end
end
--Chest and Arcade
local deadend = DequeueDeadend()
if deadend ~= nil then
local roomType = nil
if Rng() % 10 == 0 or (Rng() % 3 == 0 and GetNumKeys() > 1) then
roomType = ROOM_CHEST
else
roomType = ROOM_ARCADE
end
if GetNumCoins() >= 5 and (StageId == 2 or StageId == 4 or StageId == 6 or StageId == 8) then
PlaceRoom(roomType)
else
QueueDeadend(deadend)
end
end
--Bedroom
if StageId < 7 then
local deadend = DequeueDeadend()
if deadend ~= nil then
local roomType = nil
if Rng() & 1 == 0 then
roomType = ROOM_ISAACS
else
roomType = ROOM_BARREN
end

local maxHearts = nil
if GetPlayerType() == PLAYER_THELOST or GetPlayerType() == PLAYER_XXX or GetPlayerType() == PLAYER_THESOUL then
maxHearts = GetMaxHearts()
else
maxHearts = GetMaxHearts() + GetBoneHearts() * 2
end

local second = false
if (GetHearts() < 2 and GetSoulHearts() <= 0) or (maxHearts <= 0 and GetSoulHearts() <= 2) then
second = true
end

if Rng() % 50 == 0 or (Rng() % 5 == 0 and second) then
PlaceRoom(roomType)
else
QueueDeadend(deadend)
end
end
end
--Secret
TryPlacingSecret()
if HasTrinket(TRINKET_FRAGMENTED_CARD) or HasItem(ITEM_LUNA) then
TryPlacingSecret()
end
-- Grave Room
if StageId == 11 and StageType == 0 then --Dark Room
PlaceGrave(DequeueDeadend())
end

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The algorithm is from Blade's GitHub Gist, also known as blcd / Will. He reverse engineered the game using a disassembler in order to create the pseudo-code.

• The second chances for certain types of rooms are separate, independent rolls: the probabilities are not added together directly.

Whipper.title: Whipper
Whipper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Whippers are fiendish enemies added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

They wield long fleshy whip-like tendrils, which they use for a short-range melee attack. They wander around the room in straight lines and charge at Isaac if he lines up with them, during which they open their mouths wide. If Isaac gets too close, they will slash their whips at him, causing damage and deflecting nearby tears. Whippers will also whip at placed Bombs.

In Gehenna, their appearance changes to resemble a bondage suit.

sections.heading: Snapper
sections.text: Snappers are much more dangerous versions of the Whipper. They possess a much longer, fleshy whip that can extend across the room, at the minor cost of decreased attack width. They behave similarly to normal Whippers in that they'll charge towards Isaac if he's far enough but in their sights (their eyes turn redder to signify such) but will snap their whips at Isaac if he lines up with them at a moderate or close distance. Similar to the Whippers, their appearance resembles a bondage suit in Gehenna.

sections.heading: Flagellant
sections.text: Flagellants are even more mutilated versions of the Whipper. They wander around the room in straight lines, charging at Isaac relentlessly if he lines up with them. However, they constantly swipe their whips back and forth as they charge, damaging Isaac if he gets caught and deflecting tears much more frequently than regular Whippers. Flagellants are also more aggressive than regular Whippers and will chase Isaac for a while instead of simply charging once.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Flagellant, Snapper, and Whipper first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• Flagellant, Snapper, and Whipper's sprites were changed slightly in Repentance.

• Flagellants were formerly called "Lunatics" in the Antibirth mod and could appear in Corpse.

• Snapper in Antibirth would only appear in Mausoleum.

• The names of the Whipper and Snapper enemies are a joke to the term "whippersnapper", which is the name for a young and inexperienced person who is considered to be presumptuous or overconfident.

MemBrain.title: MemBrain
MemBrain.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: MemBrains are much larger Brains that slowly move around the room and occasionally hop to fire 8 blood shots in all directions. They have a large amount of health and will split into two Brains upon death. Membrains deal a whole heart of damage with contact and projectiles.

sections.heading: Mama Guts
sections.text: Mama Guts are large versions of the regular Guts. They slowly move around the room, occasionally hopping and firing 8 large blood shots in all directions. Upon death, it splits into 2 Guts.

sections.heading: Dead Meat
sections.text: Dead Meats are bigger versions of the Cysts that move around the room slowly, occasionally hopping which fires 8 large blood shots in all directions that bounce off the walls like Rubber Cement. Upon death, they split into 2 Cysts.

sections.heading: Dinga
sections.text: Dingas are large Dips that behave similarly to MemBrains. Dingas slide around the room aimlessly and occasionally hop, spawning Dips or shooting poop shots in 8 directions. Splits into two Squirts when killed.

sections.heading: Mega Clotty
sections.text: Mega Clotties slowly move around the room, occasionally hopping. When one hops, it will usually fire six blood shots around itself, but it can also alternatively leave a puddle of Red Creep near itself. Even more rarely, the hop may spawn a Clotty or a collapsed Globin. Upon death, it’ll split into two Clotty. Even though the sprite shows three conjoined Clotties, it always creates two upon death, and will never spawn three.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • All monsters listed on this page deal one whole heart of contact damage except for Mega Clotty which deals half a heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• MemBrain is a pun on the word membrane, which means a thin, flexible layer of body tissue.

• Mama Guts slightly resembles a digestive system.

• [Afterbirth onward] The Mega Clotty’s behavior coincidentally bears some resemblance to a fan idea of a boss called “Mega Clotty,” as, besides its name, this 2012 idea mentions that its behavior would be jumping up to shoot out blood shots as well as spawning one Clotty. However, the Mega Clotty is implemented as an enemy, not a boss, and some of its conceptual behaviors on the ideas wiki were never implemented for the fact that it’s purely coincidental. [end edition note]

fields.behavior: Slowly moves around the room, occasionally hopping and either firing 6 blood shots in all directions, leaving a puddle of Red Creep, or spawning a Clotty or a collapsed Globin. Splits into two Clotty upon death.

Member Card.title: Member Card
Member Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a trapdoor in each Shop that leads to an additional underground shop that can sell 2-5 of the following:

• A Trinket for 15 cents.

• An Item for 15-30 cents. Items will be from the Secret Room, Shop, Devil/Angel Room, or Boss Room items; there can be multiple items from different item pools, but items will stay to their chosen item pool if rerolled.

• • Devil/Angel room items can cost up to 50 cents, and Secret Room items can cost up to 99 cents.

• A Card/Rune/Soul Stone for 6-8 cents.

• A Black Heart/Bone Heart for 8 cents.

• An Eternal Heart for 15 cents.

• A Rotten Heart for 5 cents.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The trapdoor spawns even if the shop was replaced by Greed or Super Greed, in which case it won't open until Greed has been defeated.

• Similar to Crawl Spaces, there is only one secret shop per floor. The trapdoors in extra shops created by Red Key will lead to the same secret shop.

• If the Member Card was removed from the player's inventory (for example, by playing Tainted Isaac and replacing it with a different item), the trapdoor will still remain open once it has been spawned, even after leaving and reentering the shop.

• The trapdoor will appear in the Mirrored World version of the shop. Despite the shop itself being empty, the trapdoor will lead to the same secret shop where the items are still for sale. Buying from the secret shop in the Mirrored World will thus remove the bought item from both worlds.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Eden's Soul/Magic Skin/Mystery Gift: Only shop pool items are created if used in the underground shop.

• Restock: Items bought in the underground shop will also be restocked.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Member Card is from the Antibirth mod.

• It is likely a reference to the Member Card from the Fire Emblem series. In Fire Emblem, having a Member Card gives one access to unique and valuable items in shops, similar to the Member Card in Repentance.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using XVI - The Tower? in the underground Shop can spawn rocks under the ladder, resulting in a softlock if Isaac can't fly or doesn't have any bombs.
Bug note: Using IV - The Emperor? in the underground Shop on Mausoleum II, and getting Rotgut as the boss, will result in an infinite loop of entering and exiting the boss room and the shop, respectively.
Bug note: On Downpour II (or one of its alternate versions) :

• Don't go into the underground shop.

• Go in the mirror world, enter the underground shop's alternate mirror version. It should have nothing for sale.

• Make the game refill shop. For example by using a restock machine.

• Go to the regular underground shop in the normal non-mirror world.

• Now the underground shop contains two overlapped sets of things on sale : One from when the mirror version was restocked, and one from when you entered the "real" underground shop for the first time.
Bug note: If Isaac teleports to an I AM ERROR, Devil Room, or Angel Room from the underground Shop, and then enters a Crawl Space from that room, exiting the Crawl Space will lead Isaac to the underground Shop. From there, Isaac is unable to exit the underground Shop, and he will be permanently stuck unless he can teleport out.

fields.description: Adds a trapdoor to every Shop that leads to a second shop with a unique stock and marked-up prices.

Mercurius.title: Mercurius
Mercurius.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.4 speed.

• Opens most doors after entering a room, even in rooms with enemies, allowing Isaac to leave at any time.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• While Door Stop has a similar effect, Mercurius has the added benefit of opening the doors that Isaac did not enter through.

• Does not open the Boss Rush door.

• Does not open any Special Rooms, including those that require pickups to unlock. Doors won't be opened even if they were open already (such as Treasure Rooms and Shops on the first floor, Sacrifice Rooms, etc.) or have been entered before.

• Mini-Boss Rooms, despite looking identical to normal rooms, are considered Special and will not be opened. This makes it possible to distinguish between regular rooms and mini-boss rooms without map-revealing effects (such as The Compass).

• Does not open doors to Red Rooms if those doors are created while there are enemies inside the current room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 4.5 Volt / Jumper Cables: Provides infinite charges by clearing some enemies then leaving the room, and repeating.

• Camo Undies: Allows the player to go through rooms at a quicker pace due to the invisibility.

• Charm of the Vampire / Leech: Allows for unlimited healing.

• Gimpy / Sharp Straw: Allows the possibility to generate unlimited Hearts.

• Head of the Keeper: With enough patience, Coins can be gathered infinitely.

• Tainted Keeper: Leaving and re-entering the room allows for unlimited coin farming; however, enemies in rooms Tainted Keeper has already visited will eventually stop dropping coins.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mercurius originates from the Antibirth mod.

• Mercurius' effects reference the Roman god of travel and communication, Mercury, who wore winged shoes and a winged hat.

• Mercurius is the biggest static speed upgrade in the game.

• Despite Mercurius preventing doors from closing, the sound of doors opening can still be heard after clearing a room with enemies.

fields.description: +0.4 speed. Doors stay open after entering a room, even in rooms with enemies.

Metal Plate.title: Metal Plate
Metal Plate.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one Soul Heart.

• Enemy shots that hit Isaac have a 25% chance to be reflected.

• Isaac does not take damage from the reflected tears, but gets pushed a bit.

• The reflected tears are homing and concussive, and use Isaac's Damage and Tear effects.

• • Projectiles that create other projectiles (e.g. Shady) can harm Isaac and be reflected.

• Can reflect:

• • [Repentance] Fireballs (e.g. from Crackle), but their lines of fire harm Isaac. [end edition note] 

• • Fire projectiles (e.g. from Mega Satan).

• • [Repentance] Obstacles thrown by Polty or Kineti. [end edition note] 

• Does not reflect:

• • Explosive projectiles (e.g. from Gurgle).

• • Lasers or beams.

• • [Repentance] Lines of fire from fireballs.

• • [Repentance] Projectiles from Big Bony, Coal Boy, Danny. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• The following items that change the property of Isaac's tears affect the reflected tears:

• Eye of the Occult

• Haemolacria

• Ipecac

• Lachryphagy

• My Reflection

• Pop!

• Tiny Planet

• Trisagion

• The following items that modify Isaac's tears do not affect the reflected tears, aside from stat changes (if present):

• Brimstone

• Chocolate Milk

• C Section

• Cursed Eye

• Dr. Fetus

• Epic Fetus

• The Ludovico Technique

• Mom's Knife

• Monstro's Lung

• Neptunus

• Spirit Sword

• Technology

• Tech X

• 20/20 / Keeper and other multi-shot effects: Do not add the reflected tears.

• Anti-Gravity / Tractor Beam: Does not affect the reflected tears, aside from stat changes.

• Cone Head: Metal Plate's chance of reflecting effect is applied first.

• This leaves Isaac 40% chance to negate tears in any way.

• Dead Eye: The reflected tears grant the damage multiplier, but do not reset it even when they miss.

• Eye of Greed / Lead Pencil: The reflected tears are not counted for shots fired.

• Gnawed Leaf: Tears can be blocked while Isaac is invulnerable.

• This leaves Isaac 62.5% chance to negate tears in any way.

• Hallowed Ground: Metal Plate's chance of blocking effect is applied first.

• Infamy: Infamy's chance of blocking effect is applied first. Tears blocked by Infamy are not reflected by Metal Plate.

• This leaves Isaac 62.5% chance to negate tears in any way.

• Isaac's Heart: Tears can be blocked when hitting the heart, not Isaac.

• Holy Card / Holy Mantle: Metal Plate's chance of blocking projectiles is applied before the shield, allowing it to be saved.

• Host Hat: Host Hat's chance of blocking effect is applied first. Tears blocked by Host Hat are not reflected by Metal Plate.

• This leaves Isaac 40% chance to negate tears in any way.

• Metal Plate: Additional copies of this item, such as from Diplopia / Crooked Penny, have no effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The description of Metal Plate is a reference to Texas Chainsaw Massacre 2.

• Metal plates are sometimes surgically implanted in people's heads, typically to cover a hole in the skull.

fields.description: Grants one Soul Heart. Enemy shots have a chance to be reflected at the shooter as confusing tears.

Metronome.title: Metronome
Metronome.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Grants a random item's effect for the current room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item can trigger self-damage effects, making it not recommended for The Lost or Tainted Lost.

• Using this item multiple times in the same room will replace the previous item with a new one.

• Metronome cannot grant the effects of itself, Glowing Hourglass or Plan C.

• [Repentance] Also unable to grant Breath of Life, Clicker, or R Key. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] Also unable to grant Urn of Souls. [end edition note] 

• Metronome can grant items that haven't been unlocked yet.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: If an active item was selected, grants the same wisp as that item. If a passive item was selected, grants any random wisp.

• Rock Bottom: Isaac keeps any stat upgrades gained by a random temporary item as long as the item brings his stats over their highest value reached on that run.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Blanket / Holy Card / Holy Mantle / Wooden Cross: if Metronome is used while the shield is active, any stat changes or familiars/orbitals generated from Metronome will persist between rooms until Metronome is used again or replaced with another active item. Items that modify your stats and have other additional effects will keep the stats but the effect will be gone after leaving the room. For example, the tears down applied from The Inner Eye will persist between rooms, but Isaac will not shoot three tears at once.

• Some items behave unusually after leaving the room while the Holy Mantle shield was active:

• • Items that grant flight: Isaac's appearance is reset back to normal, but he is still able to fly.

• • 1up!: the mushroom familiar continues to follow Isaac, but doesn't grant an extra life.

• • Cupid's Arrow: the tear appearance is reset back to normal, but the tears still travel through enemies.

• • Fire Mind: the tear appearance is reset back to normal, but tears can still explode when they hit an enemy.

• • Mysterious Liquid: the tear appearance is reset back to normal, but tears will still leave green creep on the ground.

• Car Battery: Metronome is activated twice at once as expected, but the item chosen for the first activation is shown raised above Isaac's head, instead of the second one that actually remains active.

• Moreover, active item effects chosen by Metronome are only activated once.

• Bird Cage: Spawns the familiar for the current room, leaving the room it spawned in will only left the sprite over Isaac's head without doing nothing.

sections.heading: Specific Item Effects
sections.text:
• Certain items used by Metronome have permanent or limited/unusual effects, or no effect. It is not clear what is intended and what is a bug.

• Permanent effects include:

• Health, coins, bombs, or keys that are granted to Isaac directly will persist.

• Cube of Meat granted by Potato Peeler will persist.

• D8's rerolled stat multipliers will persist, D4 or D100 will reroll all items permanently and D infinity mimicking any of the previous also has the same effects.

• Damocles' activated version will permanently grant the passive version. The passive can also be chosen, which will apply only for the current room; they can be told apart by no Damocles item appearing in the collected items list.

• Dataminer's stat changes will persist.

• Forget Me Now will restart the level.

• Genesis will work as normal and will cause Metronome to disappear from the active slot.

• Heartbreak does not add broken hearts immediately, but will protect Isaac from death and grant its damage bonus. Broken hearts received from avoiding death are permanent.

• Magic Skin will give Isaac a broken heart, spawn an item, and count as an activation of Magic Skin, causing future items to have a chance of being replaced by Magic Skin.

• Vengeful Spirit wisps will persist for the rest of the stage.

• Void absorbing passives and granting stats will persist.

• Limited and unusual effects include:

• Items do not spawn pickups and consumables that they would when picked up normally.

• [Before Repentance] Items that adjust Isaac's size will not do so.

• 1up!, Ankh, Guppy's Collar, Judas' Shadow and Lazarus' Rags give no indication of extra lives, but will still work if you die in the room.

• 9 Volt will restore one tick of charge instead of fully charging.

• Abaddon will not remove red hearts or grant black hearts.

• Act of Contrition does not grant an eternal heart.

• Alabaster Box will immediately activate without requiring Soul Hearts.

• Azazel's Rage is useful only in Greed Mode or Boss Rush as the activation requires multiple room clears without actually leaving the room.

• Belly Button and Mom's Purse allow picking up two trinkets in the room, but if another one is picked up outside, one trinket disappears completely along with the extra slot.

• Birthright effects that add health, spawn items or alter level generation do not work. Eve does not go into Whore of Babylon mode.

• Black Candle only adds a black heart and does not remove curses.

• Brittle Bones and Divorce Papers do not grant bone hearts. Brittle Bones can still be used to gain permanent tears ups if bone hearts are available.

• Crown Of Light only adds soul hearts, no damage multiplier.

• Dead Cat will only restore one red heart without setting heart containers to 1.

• • [Before Repentance] Doesn't grant extra lives.

• • [Repentance] Grants only one extra life for the room.

• Eden's Blessing will not grant an extra item for the next run.

• False PHD grants a black heart, but will not identify pills. Pills are still guaranteed to be negative. Damage bonus is lost upon leaving the room.

• Fate only grants flight, no Eternal Heart.

• Little Baggy, Polydactyly, Starter Deck, and Deep Pockets allow picking up two consumables while in the room and kept outside, but using them will lose the extra slot.

• Lost Soul cannot be taken to the next stage, reducing its use to potentially blocking a single hit.

• Mega Mush stats increases and Isaac's appearance revert on changing rooms, but Isaac retains the shadow of his large size, the ability to crush rocks, and invulnerability until the 30 seconds are up.

• Mercurius only grants a speed up but does not open the doors.

• Moving Box will cause items in the room to be packed away into the box until you either find the Moving Box or Metronome gives you the Moving Box effect again.

• PHD will not identify pills, but they are still guaranteed to not be negative.

• Remote Detonator bombs placed in the room when the effect is active will not detonate. If Isaac manages to charge Metronome again, using it will detonate any placed bombs. 

• Schoolbag allows picking up two activated items while in the room and they can be kept even outside, but the extra slot and one of the items is lost if another activated item is picked up.

• Spin to Win will give Isaac two orbitals.

• Strawman: If the Keeper dies, it will instantly respawn near Isaac. The familiar does not persist between rooms.

• The Swarm will not spawn its initial flies, but will add one on room clear.

• The following items have no effect beyond possible cosmetic changes:

• Items that only spawn pickups or consumables.

• Items that trigger upon entering the next stage: Blood Oath, Card Reading, Dream Catcher, Empty Heart, Isaac's Tomb, The Stairway, Voodoo Head.

• Other items: Ankh, Battery Pack, Blue Map, Breath of Life, Broken Watch, Camo Undies, The Compass, Dad's Note, Death's List, Experimental Treatment, Holy Mantle, The Jar, Judas' Shadow, Lazarus' Rags, Luna, Marrow, Member Card, The Mind, Missing No., More Options, Poke Go, Purity, Redemption, Sanguine Bond, Spelunker Hat, Toxic Shock, Treasure Map, Vanishing Twin.

• The following items have a reduced chance of activating:

• Death Certificate (15%)

• Genesis (25%)

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The name, pickup quote, and effect of this item are a reference to the move Metronome from the Pokémon franchise.

• This item works similarly to the item Dead Sea Scrolls.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: It is possible for this item to give an indefinite Breath of Life effect that persists throughout rooms, eventually killing the player.
Bug note: Some tear effects from items will remain active between rooms. These include: Continuum, Epic Fetus, Eve's Mascara, Godhead, Ipecac, Jacob's Ladder, The Ludovico Technique, A Lump of Coal, Monstro's Lung, My Reflection, Ouija Board, Pop!, Rubber Cement, Sacred Heart, Spoon Bender, Strange Attractor, Technology Zero.
Bug note: If Urn of Souls is activated through Metronome, it won't shoot fire and Isaac could get stuck with the urn in his hands unable to shoot tears. You can fix this by exiting and continuing the run, restarting the room without the urn and without Metronome charges.

fields.name: Metronome
fields.description: Grants a random item effect for the current room.

Midas' Touch.title: Midas' Touch
Midas' Touch.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Petrifies and turns enemies into gold upon contact with Isaac.

• Enemies killed while in this state will drop 1-3 Penny.

• When held by Keeper or Tainted Keeper, enemies will drop 0-1 pennies instead.

• Enemies that make contact with Isaac take damage equal to the number of coins he has.

• [Repentance] The damage is 3.5+0.2 * the number of Isaac's coins. The damage caps at 23.30 with 99 coins and 203.3 with 999 coins.

• Damage is dealt up to twice per second per enemy.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• With Midas' Touch, some effects that create Poop may instead create Golden Poop (see Synergies for details).

• If an enemy doesn't deal contact damage, Midas' Touch can safely be used on it to create extra Pennies. Fly, Bulb, Mulligan, and Host are the most common enemies this can be applied to.

• If Isaac has 13 coins or more when using Midas' Touch on Mulligan, they will die and release flies, hurting Isaac.

• With Skatole, Hives and Swarmers will constantly spawn black flies, meaning they can create endless amounts of coins.

• [Before Repentance] As Mom's foot and Satan's feet don't deal contact damage, Midas' Touch can be used against them to great effect.

• Spawning Multiplayer Babies while the player has Midas' Touch will give the Midas' Touch effects (freeze on touch + damage) to the baby itself. This can be abused, considering the baby's invincibility frames upon spawning:

• Spawn the baby using the Enter key. It is invincible for a short period.

• During this period, stay in contact with enemies to freeze them and damage them.

• This can be used to gather 99 coins very quickly, and in turn, deal massive damage with Midas' Touch damage component.

• [Repentance] Petrified enemies that are frozen will not drop any coins on death.

• [Repentance] Midas' Touch can be a great item with Tainted Keeper, as you can run into enemies and get even more coins. Just be careful to not kill yourself.

• [Repentance] Both Midas' Touch and E. Coli affect Tainted Forgotten's body, causing enemies that touch the body to freeze and turn into poop respectively.

• [Repentance+] If a violet champion monster is killed while it is gold-petrified, the trinket it drops is guaranteed to be a golden one. Rainbow champions still drop normal trinkets. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Card Against Humanity: Spawned Poops have a great chance to turn into Golden Poops. 11% at 0 luck and 100% at 18 luck.

• Deep Pockets: Increases maximum contact damage. The damage caps at 203.3 damage with 999 coins.

• E. Coli: Enemies touched are turned into Golden Poop.

• [Before Repentance] Epic Fetus + E. Coli: Launching a rocket at Isaac will turn the rocket into a golden poop, causing the explosion to break it automatically and spawning coins, which allows health to be exchanged for money.

• Flush!: Touching poops made from enemies turns them into Golden Poops just before being destroyed dropping the normal Golden Poop pickups including Counterfeit Penny.

• The Poop: Using The Poop has a high chance to spawn Golden Poop.

• [Before Repentance] 50% at 0 luck and 100% at 5 luck.

• [Repentance] 34% at 0 luck and 100% at 6.6 luck.

• Re-Lax: Spawned Poops have a chance to turn into Golden Poops. 25% at 0 luck and 100% at 8 luck.

• Any item or card that grants Isaac temporary invincibility lets Isaac use Midas' Touch on any enemy without taking damage. This includes, but is not limited to:

• VII - The Chariot/VII - The Chariot?

• A Pony/White Pony

• Book of Shadows/Celtic Cross/Empty Vessel/Algiz/The Polaroid/Virgo

• Breath of Life

• Dull Razor

• Holy Mantle

• My Little Unicorn/Unicorn Stump/Feels like I'm walking on Sunshine!

• [Repentance] Aries (if Isaac's speed is greater than 0.85)

• The Gamekid/Power Pill!

• Ventricle Razor (briefly after exiting a portal)

• Tooth and Nail

• • The stone isaac turns into is changed to a yellowish gold with Midas' touch

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Petrified enemies that are turned into pickups don’t also drop coins from the petrification effect.

• [Repentance] Freeze Effects: Petrified enemies that are frozen don’t drop coins.

• Mine Crafter: Has a chance to petrify the TNT block when placed, damaging Isaac in the process if he touches the golden TNT Block.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is a reference to King Midas from Greek Mythology, who wished to be able to turn everything he touched with his hand into gold and ended up regretting his wish after turning his food (or in some interpretations his wife) to gold.

fields.description: Enemies that touch Isaac are temporarily petrified and turn to gold. Any enemy killed while in this state will drop Penny.

Midnight Snack.title: Midnight Snack
Midnight Snack.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one full Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Binge Eater: When Isaac picks up Midnight Snack it now grants: a permanent +1.0 Damage and +1.0 Luck, a temporary +3.6 Damage (which diminishes to 0 in 30 seconds), heals 1 additional red heart, and takes a permanent -0.03 Speed reduction.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] This item's name was changed from Moldy Bread to Midnight Snack.

• It is the only plain stat upgrade added in Afterbirth †, from release to the last Booster Pack.

fields.name: [edition alternatives: baseline: Moldy Bread; Repentance: Midnight Snack]
fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Midnight snack!; Repentance: HP up]
fields.description: Grants one full Red Heart container. [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

boxes.name: [edition alternatives: baseline: Moldy Bread; Repentance: Midnight Snack]

Milk!.title: Milk!
Milk!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a glass familiar that follows Isaac.

• [Before Repentance+] The milk spills on the floor upon taking damage. After which, Isaac gains -2 tear delay ( [Repentance] +1.0 fire rate) until leaving the room. The familiar will reappear in the next room.

• [Repentance+] The milk will block projectiles and take damage up to 10 times, after which the familiar shatters granting Isaac +1.0 fire rate for the rest of the floor. The familiar will reappear upon entering a new floor.

• • The familiar can also take damage from contact with enemies, fire places, enemy lasers and all explosions, although they are not blocked or pushed back.

• Direct tear delay reduction can break the normal soft fire rate cap.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The milk puddle is purely visual, and will stay on the ground for a few seconds before disappearing.

• [edition rnr+] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Milk! having the lowest priority at 6th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

• [Repentance+] Milk! has the third-highest priority; just behind Incubus. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Box of Friends: The milk familiar is not duplicated; instead, tear delay decreases by 2 upon use even if the player has not taken damage in the current room.

• [Repentance] No extra tear delay is granted, neither before nor after breaking.

• Rock Bottom: If activated at least once, the increased rate of fire will always be active.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • BFFS!: Familiar is bigger but no effect on tear delay.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is a reference to the phrase "Don't cry over spilled milk".

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: When the milk is spilled and becomes a puddle while Extension Cord is equipped, the electricity will fire consistently to the upper left even when the puddle disappears.
Bug note: The milk familiar has a chance to block a projectile, but not count towards breaking. This is indicated by the familiar not flashing red despite blocking a shot.
Bug note: If the run is exited and resumed when the familiar has been broken, it will reppear but only hover at the latest entrance to the current room. It can still block enemy shots and flashes red when damaged, but can't be broken again. It becomes normal again upon entering the next stage.

• The familiar can be broken again by using a fire place, this can be exploited to reach the maximum fire rate.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Dont cry over it...; Afterbirth+ onward: Don [Afterbirth+ onward] 't cry over it...]
fields.description:
[Before Repentance+] Spawns a glass familiar that follows Isaac. After Isaac takes damage, the milk spills, and he gains -2 tear delay ( [Repentance] +1.0 fire rate) until leaving the room
[Repentance+] Spawns a glass familiar that follows Isaac. The milk will block projectiles, and upon blocking 10, the milk spills, giving Isaac +1.0 fire rate for the rest of the floor.

Min-Min.title: Min-Min
Min-Min.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Min-Min is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in [Repentance] Downpour.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Min-Min floats slowly towards Isaac and performs the following attacks:

• Spits a Willo at Isaac which fires a projectile at him before returning to orbit around Min-Min. Min-Min can have a maximum of 4 orbiting her. Willos do not deal contact damage.

• This can be done multiple times in quick succession until the limit of 4 Willos has been reached.

• Willos orbiting Min-Min occasionally fire a projectile towards Isaac.

• Once Min-Min has 4 orbiting Willos, she periodically causes them to fire 3 projectiles outwards. If any Willos are killed during this attack the remaining ones perform this attack uninterrupted.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
In this phase, Min-Min burns away the husk surrounding her, and can now have a maximum of 7 Willos orbiting her. She will continue to float slowly towards Isaac and has new attacks:

• Min-Min spawns up to 4 Willos around herself and then causes all orbiting Willos to fire 3 projectiles outwards.

• Willos orbiting Min-Min still occasionally fire a projectile towards Isaac.

• Spits a Willo at Isaac which fires a projectile at him before returning to orbit around Min-Min.

• Causes the current orbiting Willos to fire 3 projectiles outwards.

• Sends her orbiting ring of Willos to chase Isaac. After a few seconds, they return.

• Disappears and creates several groups of lights on the ground. One group at a time, Willos appear from the lights, fire at Isaac, and disappear.

Upon Min-Min's defeat, all spawned Willos die alongside her.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Min-Min is confirmed to be female, as shown in this tweet.

• In her first phase, Min-Min is hiding within a drowned and bleached corpse of The Husk.

• In a way, this corpse can be seen as a posthumous version of Lil Blub.

• Min-Min may be named after Min Min lights, a light phenomenon that has often been reported in outback Australia, where remote lights appear on the horizon and appear to follow people around.

• Min-Min in her first phase is very similar to the Mullighoul monster as they both are white creatures, have a ball of light in the mouth, and shoot out Willos.

• In the files of Repentance, there is an unused Boss Portrait for a Boss called "Maid in the Mist". Unlike the other unused Bosses, there are no files for this boss. This is likely because she was early concept for what would become Min-Min in the final game, as they are both female, share a Willo theme, and were both assigned the enemy ID 913 according to their file names.

Mine Crafter.title: Mine Crafter
Mine Crafter.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, spawns a Movable TNT.

• If used a second time while the created TNT is still active, it will explode. [Before Repentance] This will consume a charge to remotely detonate the TNT instead of creating another TNT.

• [Repentance] The remote detonation can be used while the item is uncharged.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] The Movable TNT has a unique cubic appearance, but it functionally identical to a regular Movable TNT.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns one glowing green wisp that cannot take or deal damage in any way, and bounces around the room in a random direction, instead of following Isaac. If the wisp is shot by Isaac or his familiars, it explodes, dealing 100 damage to nearby enemies. The wisp does not persist between rooms. Explosions and enemy shots do not detonate it, and the wisps' explosions are unaffected by BFFS! and bomb synergies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 120 Volt: The TNT is spawned and may be instantly hit by 120 Volt's electric shock, which usually wont detonate it unless Isaac is near some enemies.

• Tainted Magdalene: Tainted Magdalene may immediately attempt to hug the TNT upon holding it up, instantly detonating it and dealing damage to her.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Car Battery: The TNT will be spawned and then instantly explode, dealing a full heart of damage.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Spawns two TNT barrels instead.

• Midas' Touch: Occasionally spawns a golden TNT barrel which turns into a regular movable TNT after 3 seconds. While in its gold state, Isaac cannot collide with the barrel nor push it, although it can be pushed by enemies. In some cases, the golden barrel will explode immediately after spawning, dealing damage to Isaac. Apart from that, it doesn't give any benefits.

• Spider Mod: The TNT can be inflicted with a random status effect if the spider comes into contact with it.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item's name is a reference to the game Minecraft created by Mojang.

• TNT is a craftable explosive block in Minecraft that is red and cubed. When lit up by the fire, fire setting objects, or certain redstone currents, it would eventually explode, damaging nearby blocks and entities. However, it doesn't share many similarities with the Mine Crafter pickup item or TNT in the Binding of Isaac.

• [Repentance] Mine Crafter also physically resembles a TNT block from Minecraft.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using this item during the Mega Satan fight will cause a soft lock since an exploded barrel counts as an enemy that needs to be defeated before the fight can continue.
Bug note: Placing the TNT under the effects of Venus or 2Spooky will tint it as if it were applied the corresponding status effect. It is purely visual and will fade after a while.

fields.description: Places a Movable TNT barrel that can be pushed and used to destroy rocks or damage enemies. If used again in the same room while the previous TNT barrel is still intact, remotely detonates the TNT.

• Unlike other size downs, the one from Mini Mush is permanent - after taking the item, Isaac's hitbox cannot be increased past 75% of its base value.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item and its effects are likely a reference to the Mini Mushroom of the Super Mario series.

• Mini Mush, along with 1up!, Magic Mushroom, Super Bandage, and Mega Mush is one of the few items that make a unique sound upon pickup.

fields.description: Decreases Isaac's size, making him less likely to be hit. [Before Repentance] +0.3 speed, +1.5 tear falling speed, -4.25 range (effective range is increased). [Repentance] +0.3 speed, +2.5 range.

Missing No..title: Missing No.
Missing No..attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Randomizes passive items and attributes on pickup and at the start of every floor.

• Regarding stats, this randomness is not dependent on the run's seed.

• Stats gain a random modifier. These modifiers do not stack between levels and are instead rerolled every time.

• • Speed -0.2, 0 or +0.2.

• • 
• [Before Repentance] Also affects maximum speed, may never exceed 2.0.

• • [Before Repentance] Range -0.5, 0 or +0.5.

• • [Repentance] Range -2.5, 0 or +2.5.

• • [Before Repentance] Tears -0.5, 0 or +0.5.

• • [Repentance] Fire rate -0.5, 0 or +0.5.

• • Shot speed -0.2, 0 or +0.2.

• • Damage flat -1, 0 or +1.

• • Luck -1, 0 or +1.

• Does not affect trinkets, cards, pills, Pretty Flies, The Polaroid / The Negative, Key Piece 1 / Key Piece 2, Knife Piece 1 / Knife Piece 2, or active items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• See D4 for more details of the rerolling process.

• Due to losing all items every level, it is beneficial to try to gain permanent stat boosts if possible. These include using pills when equipped with PHD or Virgo, [Afterbirth+ onward] sacrificing health with Potato Peeler to gain damage or Brittle Bones to gain tears, or using up Judas' Shadow.

• Like other full-reroll effects, Missing No. has a small chance to not reroll every item.

• [edition alternatives: baseline: Can cause transformations.; Repentance: Transformations are lost when rerolling out of the items that caused them.] 

• Missing No. cannot be rerolled or removed by most means after being picked up, including:

• Rerolling passive items with D4.

• • A D4-type reroll will cause the stat modifiers from Missing No. to be rerolled. 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Using Clicker to remove the last item collected.

• [Repentance] Using XVII - The Stars? to remove the last item collected.

• [Repentance] Taking damage as Tainted Eden to reroll passive items.

• [Before Repentance] This item can be used to gain more health if desperately needed, as the randomization does often include items that grant you various types of hearts.

• [Before Repentance] If the player has already obtained a large number of items (such as during a run where they have gained infinite money in greed mode), it is highly recommended to avoid this item, as it will almost always end up rerolling all the items the player has thus far collected into Breakfast.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [edition alternatives: baseline: Butter!; Repentance: Genesis] : Provide the only available methods for getting rid of Missing No.

• [Repentance] Butter! can no longer remove Missing No.

• Glowing Hourglass: Using Glowing Hourglass to go back to the previous floor will keep the rerolled items, which will allow to reroll them again.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • The Stairway: When getting the Stairway at the start of a floor, the ladder doesn't spawn. It will spawn at the start of the next floor even if rerolled.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to the infamous MissingNo. glitch occurring in the first-generation Pokémon games. The glitch would often corrupt save files, and therefore randomize various parts of the game as it would use the incomplete index values attributed to entities not included in the final release of the game. Isaac's appearance when affected by Missing No. is based on this glitch which could cause the player's sprite to become scrambled.

• The item also resembles the painting "Composition II with Red, Blue, and Yellow" by Dutch painter Piet Mondrian.

• The background color for the Missing No. achievement has the same color as all the challenge unlocks. This implies that Missing No. was originally intended to be unlocked via a challenge. (Or, perhaps, it was intended to be looked at as an error.)

• The background color for the Suicide King achievement has the same color as all the boss rush unlocks. This implies that potentially Lazarus would have unlocked Suicide King for completing the Boss Rush and Suicide King would have unlocked Missing No.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Rerolling into PHD from it will not reveal newly acquired pills.
Bug note: randomizing effect happens twice.

Missing Page 2.title: Missing Page 2
Missing Page 2.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one Black Heart.

• Activates The Necronomicon effect upon taking damage if Isaac's total health (Red Hearts, Soul Hearts, and Black Hearts) is at one heart or less afterwards.

• [Repentance] Adds +40 damage to The Necronomicon and similar effects, such as Black Hearts.

• Contributes to the Necromancer transformation.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Black Feather: Counts as an 'evil' item, granting a damage up.

• [Repentance] Blood Rights / Dry Baby / The Negative / Heartbreak / XIII - Death / Black Rune: The damage boost is applied to these items. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] A Missing Page/Missing Page 2: The damage increase from the trinket/copies of Missing Page 2 stacks, adding +40 damage per stack to The Necronomicon and similar effects. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Necronomicon, A Missing Page, and Missing Page 2 are all references to the Necronomicon and its missing pages appearing in Evil Dead.

• Which, in turn, is a reference to The Necronomicon, a fictional grimoire appearing in the works of horror writer H.P. Lovecraft.

fields.quote: Evil up. Your enemies will pay!
fields.description: Grants one Black Heart. Upon taking damage that reduces Isaac's health to one heart or less, deals damage to all enemies in the room. [Repentance] Increases the damage of Black Hearts and The Necronomicon-like effects by 40.

Missing Poster.title: Missing Poster
Missing Poster.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] If Isaac dies to a Sacrifice Room's spikes, a puzzle piece will appear on his last will.

• [Afterbirth onward] Dying in a Sacrifice Room while holding the trinket consumes it, revives Isaac as The Lost and unlocks the character.

• If The Lost is already unlocked, the trinket works outside Sacrifice Rooms as well, reviving Isaac as The Lost.

• [Repentance+] Adds a 1/3 chance to reveal a super secret room upon entering a new floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] None of the effects will occur during any Challenges.

• [Repentance+] This trinket can no longer spawn in challenges.

• [edition anr] Resurrection items activate in a set order. Missing Poster has the lowest priority of all / [Repentance] the second-lowest priority of all, with only Tainted Lost's Birthright effect being lower.

• If another resurrection item activates before Missing Poster while in the sacrifice room, then the player will not become The Lost, but The Lost will still be unlocked. Missing Poster will also not get used up by this.

• [edition anr] The Lost's intrinsic Holy Mantle is not gained when revived into this way.

• [Repentance] If unlocked, The Lost will have his intrinsic Holy Mantle when revived into this way.

• [Afterbirth onward] Dying to Sacrifice Room spikes specifically is not required to unlock The Lost, and any death within the room counts.

• If Isaac teleports out of the room before dying, i.e. is teleported by the spikes to Dark Room, The Lost will not be unlocked.

• [Repentance] Doesn't unlock The Lost in challenges.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases the chance to reveal the location of the super secret room upon entering a new floor to 2/3. Having both to 100%.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Gulp! / Marbles / Smelter: Missing Poster functions correctly after being consumed, but still disappears after activating.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Birthright: The Lost's Birthright effect will apply after respawning as him, even if Birthright was obtained prior to dying.

• Jacob and Esau: As long as one holds the poster, Isaac will be revived, regardless of which one dies. The Lost will get both characters' items.

• Tainted Lost: Revives as Tainted Lost instead of The Lost.

sections.heading: Puzzle Pieces [Rebirth only]
sections.text:
• The puzzle piece will belong to one of four jigsaw puzzles, differentiated by a grey symbol in the corner of each piece.

• The symbol can either be a pixel, a 2x2px square, a 3x3 px square, or four pixels arranged like a plus-sign.

• Each jigsaw puzzle displays an altered last will for the characters Isaac, Magdalene, Judas, or Azazel respectively.

• Each picture on the last will shows in which way Isaac has to die when playing as the respective character to unlock The Lost.

• There are many puzzle pieces and more details to be found; see here.

sections.heading: In-game Footage
sections.text: Note that this footage only applies to the Rebirth version of this trinket and does not show the changes made to it in Afterbirth.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Lost]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The first scenes in Ending 15 and Ending 17 show The Missing Poster pinned to a utility pole, with a silhouette of Isaac's mother who seems to be searching for Isaac in the background.

• There are many puzzle pieces in total. Assembling all of the jigsaw puzzles and figuring out what they meant was initially designed to be a collaborative effort of the community. As such, Edmund and Tyrone had openly expressed disappointment towards the datamining.

• The unlock pop-up of Missing Poster calls it "Lost Poster". It is unknown if this is a mistake or a hint.

• A chest always containing the Missing Poster will appear as a room clear reward from the Dogma room, although it is impossible to access it without the use of console commands.

Mitre.title: Mitre
Mitre.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants [edition alternatives: baseline: 50%; Repentance: 33%] of converting any non-specific Red Heart pickups that spawn into Soul Heart, Black Heart or Bone Heart instead.

• Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• ???, Tainted ???, Black Judas, Tainted Judas, and Tainted Forgotten: Decreases the chances of useless red heart drops, which these characters can't pick up.

• Bethany: Sacrifices potential healing for more charges. Usefulness depends on active item.

• Eve/Whore of Babylon: Decreases the chance of useless red heart drops when trying to maintain the half a heart (full heart on Eve) of red heart health required to keep Whore of Babylon's ability active.

• Tainted Bethany: Sacrifices potential blood charges for more health. Overall, still a beneficial pickup.

• Tainted Magdalene: Due to the "in your face" gameplay of Tainted Maggy, soul hearts will not be as useful up until the later floors.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Keeper/Tainted Keeper: Nearly useless, since all hearts are converted into blue flies anyway. The only use is contributing to the Seraphim transformation.

sections.heading: Trivia

Modeling Clay.title: Modeling Clay
Modeling Clay.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Has a 50% chance to mimic the effect of a random passive item from the current room’s item pool when entering a room.

• The trinket takes the shape of the mimic item.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Modeling Clay can only mimic items that have the "summonable" item tag, the same way Lemegeton selects the wisps it summons.

• The item given by Modeling Clay is seeded and based on the room Isaac is in.

• Effects that activate upon pickup will not be applied.

sections.heading: Excluded Items
sections.text: The following passive items cannot be mimicked by Modeling Clay.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Increases the chance of triggering to 100%. Having both, or stacking extra copies has no effect.

• Chaos: Removes the item pool constraint for Modeling Clay's available items.

• Rock Bottom: Permanently increases Isaac's stats when it transforms into an item that surpasses Isaac's current stats.

• Sacred Orb: Temporary items are affected by Sacred Orb.

• Sacrificial Altar: If Modeling Clay is currently mimicking a viable familiar, it will also be sacrificed and spawn an additional Devil Room item, but Modeling Clay will not be destroyed.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Modeling Clay: No effect.

• Magic Skin: Modeling Clay can turn into Magic Skin if it was used during the run. Modeling Clay has no effect if this occurs.

• TMTRAINER: Modeling Clay cannot copy glitched items; it will do nothing and not have a sprite if it tries to.

If Modeling Clay mimics the following items, they will behave in the following ways:

• 9 Volt: 1-room charge active items will not recharge over time. Other active items are affected normally.

• Belly Button / Mom's Purse: Allows Isaac to hold another trinket alongside Modeling Clay if he picks it up while Modeling Clay mimics the item, and he will continue to hold both even after Modeling Clay changes. If Isaac tries to pick up another trinket while he already has two, it will instead be destroyed and he will only be able to hold one trinket again.

• Isaac can safely exchange cards/pills/trinkets by manually dropping them, at the cost of being unable to hold two.

• Extra trinkets held this way are susceptible to not working properly, if at all.

• Black Candle: Does not remove the current floor’s curse.

• Bloody Lust / Bloody Gust / False PHD / Keeper's Sack / Rock Bottom: Stat boosts will not persist after Modeling Clay changes. If it mimics that item again, it will remember the stat boosts they gave.

• Blue Map / The Compass / The Mind / Treasure Map: Does not reveal rooms on the map.

• Candy Heart / Soul Locket: Stats granted from picking up hearts will not persist after Modeling Clay changes.

• Cambion Conception / Immaculate Conception: If Isaac can somehow meet the requirements for these items to spawn familiars, the familiars will persist for only one room after Modeling Clay changes.

• Delirious / Mr. ME!: Has no effect, even if Isaac uses his active item.

• Dog Tooth / Spelunker Hat / X-Ray Vision / YO LISTEN!: Will reveal/open neighboring Secret Rooms.

• False PHD / PHD: Pills’ effects will be changed, but they will not be identified.

• GB Bug: The familiar respawns every time Isaac re-enters the room where Modeling Clay mimicks GB Bug, allowing for the infinite transformation of pickups.

• Glitched Crown: Items that are spawned while it’s being mimicked will cycle between 5 different items, even after Modeling Clay changes.

• Missing No. / Isaac's Tomb / Voodoo Head: If Isaac can enter a trapdoor to the next floor while it’s being mimicked, they will have their normal effects.

• Other items that activate on floor transition (such as Dream Catcher, Empty Heart, or Lost Soul) will not work.

• Little Baggy / Polydactyly / Starter Deck: Allows Isaac to hold two cards and/or pills if he picks them up while Modeling Clay mimics the item, and he will continue to hold both even after Modeling Clay changes. If Isaac tries to pick up another card/pill after Modeling Clay changes, the inactive card/pill he was holding will be destroyed and he will only be able to hold one card/pill again.

• If Isaac goes to a new room while Modeling Clay mimics Starter Deck/Little Baggy, cards/pills in the new room will be converted appropriately.

• Member Card: The special trapdoor will not spawn.

• Sanguine Bond: The unique spikes will not spawn.

• Schoolbag: If Isaac picks up another active item while Modeling Clay mimics the item, the other active item is dropped after Modeling Clay changes.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
Modeling Clay can open additional advantages if a particularly helpful item is chosen for a given room. Exploring all rooms to see what effects are available may be worthwhile to gain the most value of the trinket:

• Explosive shots: Allows Isaac to destroy rocks and open Secret Room doors without spending resources.

• Damage-triggered items: To gain extra value from using Machines/Beggars that take health or Sacrifice Rooms. Note that stats given by on-hit items will not persist outside the rooms they were used in.

• Hallowed Ground can be used first to spawn a white poop next to a Machine/Beggar that takes health to give Isaac the chance to resist damage taken from using them.

• The Battery: Allows Isaac's active item to be overcharged; overcharging will persist after Modeling Clay changes.

• Cancer / The Wafer: Reduces the damage taken from Sacrifice Rooms to half a heart, allowing Isaac to use them more.

• Echo Chamber: Cards and runes’ effects will be stacked if used while it mimics the item. The game will remember what cards and runes were used if it turns into Echo Chamber in the future, even on later floors.

• Lucky Foot / PHD / Virgo: Bad pills will be their good counterparts while mimicking these items, making them much safer to use.

• Marbles: Allows trinkets to be smelted if Isaac can deal damage to himself while it mimics the item.

• Pyromaniac: Lets Isaac heal off explosions in the current room. Can be used to greater effect in rooms with TNT or Bomb Bums.

• Restock: Items will restock themselves as normal.

• Scapular: To gain a Soul Heart if at low health. This will not work if the damage source is considered "health donation", such as from a Blood Donation Machine, Devil Beggar, Confessional, or Hell Game, but it will work for Curse Rooms and Sacrifice Rooms.

• Sharp Plug: Isaac’s active item can be instantly recharged at the cost of red hearts.

• Steam Sale: Shop items and pickups will be discounted.

• Tarot Cloth: Cards will have their effects boosted.

• Notable cards are IX - The Hermit for getting rid of Greed in shops and XVII - The Stars for effectively More Options.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The trinket is a direct reference to the item of the same name in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls, which turns into another available item when used.

• In addition, the item is possibly a reference to the Self-forming Clay item from the rogue-like deckbuilder Slay the Spire.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Walking between rooms back and forward with Modeling Clay may cause the game to crash at random.
Bug note: [Before Repentance+] Normally, Modeling Clay's appearance changes to reflect what item it's imitating. This is not the case if the trinket is absorbed, e.g. through Smelter. It will appear in the Found HUD where passive items appear, like other absorbed trinkets, but will never change its appearance.
Bug note: Magic Skin's item-replacing effect can also apply to this trinket. If modeling clay replicates Magic Skin, it will have no effect.

Mole.title: Mole
Mole.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Mole is a monster added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

It chases Isaac by burrowing in the ground (characterized by small, moving rubble on the surface). When it gets near Isaac, it pokes out of the ground and fires 3 blood shots at him. It will then jump to a nearby tile leaving a Poop where it jumped.

sections.heading: Tainted Mole
sections.text:
The Tainted Mole is a stronger, distorted version of the regular mole.

It burrows through the ground, creating rockwaves in the direction it moves in. When it gets near Isaac, it pokes out of the ground, creating a ring of rock waves (similar to the Roundy) and fires 3 blood shots at him 4 times. It will then jump to a nearby tile leaving a Poop where it jumped.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Mole first appeared in the Antibirth mod where it would not create Poops upon leaping, but instead Pits.

• Moles will have their eyes open and glowing in the dark if encountered in a dark room, however this doesn't affect their behavior.

Peep Eye.title: Peep Eye
Peep Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Peep Eyes spawn in pairs and float diagonally around the room over obstacles, bouncing off of walls and other monsters and dealing contact damage to Isaac. They are completely invulnerable and can also block projectiles. The trajectory of the eyes can be deviated by bombs. They are only spawned by Peep as apart of his fight, one at 66% HP and a second at 33% HP and are destroyed once Peep is killed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Cyan champion Peep Eyes spawn detached from Peep at the beginning of the fight.

sections.heading: Bloat Eye
sections.text: Bloat Eyes spawn in pairs and behave identically to Peep Eyes but are spawned by The Bloat- both completely detached at the beginning of the fight and are destroyed once The Bloat is killed.

sections.heading: Mockulus
sections.text: Mockuli start off stationary, but start rapidly floating around the room diagonally when Isaac starts shooting. They stop moving when Isaac stops shooting. There is a minimum time that they move for before stopping. Unlike other Peep Eye variants they do not spawn with a correlating Monster and will be destroyed once the room they spawn in is cleared.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance] Mockulus is a portmanteau of "mock" (to ridicule) and "oculus" (Latin for "eye").
