fields.behavior: Invulnerable enemy that rapidly floats diagonally over obstacles and bounces off of walls, blocking tears and dealing contact damage. They can only move while Isaac is shooting.

Blood Rights.title: Blood Rights
Blood Rights.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• On use, takes a full heart of health and activates The Necronomicon's effect, dealing 40 damage to all enemies in the room.

• Blood Rights takes Red Hearts before other heart types.

• [Repentance] This bypasses damage scaling.

• [Repentance] When used more than once in the same room, damage taken is lowered to half a red heart.

• [Repentance+] Increases fire rate by +0.48 for the current room for the first use in the current stage.

• Subsequent uses in the same stage add a +0.15 to the bonus.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using this item does not affect Devil Room or Angel Room chances.

• Using Blood Rights grants immunity frames; this allows access to Curse Rooms without losing soul hearts.

• Using this item as The Lost or Tainted Lost kills The Lost, even if the protective effect from Holy Mantle is active.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Missing Page / Missing Page 2: Deals an additional +40 damage. Effects stack together and with multiple copies.

• Book of Belial interaction: Invokes the effect of Razor Blade along with its original effect.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns red wisps in the middle ring that have higher health than average and shoot red tears.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Habit + Schoolbag: Damage from Blood Rights grants a point of charge to Isaac's other held active item. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] Isaac's Heart: Blood Rights doesn't deal damage to Isaac, allowing repeated usage without penalty.

• [Before Repentance] Shield/Invulnerability: Blood Rights can be used without taking damage for the duration of the shield or invulnerability. Invincibility frames from recently taking damage will not protect against this item's damage.

• The Wafer: Reduces the damage dealt to Isaac to half a heart.

• Bloody Lust / Bloody Gust: The Blood Rights damage counts for the raise of statistics of these objects.

• Whore of Babylon: As Blood Rights takes Red Hearts before other heart types, it can be used to get the Whore of Babylon activation's condition easier.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• [Repentance] Shield/Invulnerability: Will not protect against this item's damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item itself is a straight-edge razor.

• "Blood Rights" is a term that means that the inherent has the right to certain things by way of heritage.

• This item is possibly a reference to the 2002 film Gangs of New York, which deals heavily with themes of cultural obligation passed down through heritage; shortly before his own death, the main protagonist's father entrusts his son with his straight razor after having ritualistically cut himself with it, with the admonition that "The blood stays on the blade." The protagonist then hides the razor before being incarcerated and recovers it 16 years later, effectively making it his "inheritance".

• May also be a play on words of "Blood Rites", rituals done using one's own blood, usually with the context of summoning a demon or similar otherworldly entity.

• It being unlocked by defeating Satan, being in the Devil Room pool, and Eve as a character relating to both demons and self-harm all support this.

fields.quote: Mass enemy damage at a cost
fields.description: Takes a full heart of health and deals 40 damage to all enemies in the room. [Repentance] Repeated uses in the same room only take half a heart. [Repentance+] Increases fire rate when used.

Blood of the Martyr.title: Blood of the Martyr
Blood of the Martyr.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 damage.

• Isaac's tears become red.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Blood of the Martyr, it turns into a red locust dealing double Isaac’s damage per tick.

• The Book of Belial / XV - The Devil: Applies an additional 1.5× damage multiplier.

• The ×1.5 damage multiplier does not stack with the ×1.5 damage multiplier from Magic Mushroom and Cricket's Head.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Blood of the Martyr: No further effect when multiple copies of the item are acquired.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to the book of Revelations: And I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: and when I saw her, I wondered with great admiration. -Revelation 17:6

• This item's appearance is a reference to the crown of thorns placed upon Jesus Christ's head during His crucifixion.

fields.description: +1 damage. Isaac shoots blood tears.

Bloodshot Eye.title: Bloodshot Eye
Bloodshot Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the enemy; Eye#Bloodshot EyeBloodshot Eye (Enemy)]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Summons an orbital familiar eye that deals contact damage and occasionally fires tears that deal 3.5 damage. [Repentance] It also blocks enemy shots.

• [Before Repentance] The eye deals 2 contact damage per tick or 30 contact damage per second. Tears are fired once every 2 seconds in the direction its currently facing.

• [Repentance] The eye deals 2 contact damage per tick or 20 contact damage per second. It shoots a tear once every 1/3rd of a second as long as an enemy is in its line of sight.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The orbital's tears can knock Isaac's Bombs around.

• [Before Repentance] Unlike other orbitals, the eye does not block enemy shots.

• [Before Repentance] Bloodshot Eye can override Pretty Flies without giving protection from enemy shots.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Bloodshot Eye was originally an unofficial item which was supposed to showcase the modding capabilities of Afterbirth+ in the PAX 2016 livestream. However, all items included in the demo were later added to the final game.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Spawns an orbital familiar that deals contact damage and fires a tear every 2 seconds.
[Repentance] Spawns an orbital familiar that deals contact damage, blocks shots, and fires tears at enemies in its line of sight.

Bloody Crown.title: Bloody Crown
Bloody Crown.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Treasure Rooms appear in the Womb, Utero, and Scarred Womb.

• [Repentance] Treasure Rooms also appear in the Corpse. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This trinket must already be held upon starting the Womb/Utero/Scarred Womb floor for the effect to take place, i.e., the trinket needs to be carried over from the previous floor.

• Bloody Crown only needs to be held when entering the floor. The Treasure Room will remain after dropping the trinket, even if it hasn't been explored yet.

• [curse: XL] floors will have 2 treasure rooms, like any other XL floor.

• [Repentance] The Treasure Rooms that appear in Corpse will have 2 items, one behind a [curse: blind] like the other Alt Path floors.

• This trinket does not work if held during a challenge run that impedes Treasure Rooms from spawning.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Treasure rooms in the Womb have an item choice, as if Isaac had More Options.

fields.description: Treasure Rooms appear in Chapter 4.

Bloody Gust.title: Bloody Gust
Bloody Gust.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When Isaac takes damage, he gains Speed and Fire Rate for the rest of the floor.

• Speed gained per hit is (0.04x previous hits taken) +0.07.

• Fire Rate gained per hit is (0.1x previous hits taken) + 0.25.

• • Both effects stack up to six times, for a total of +1.02 speed and +3 fire rate.

• • Fire rate bonuses can exceed the normal maximum fire rate limit.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Rights / Razor Blade / IV Bag: The damage from the item counts for the stats up.

• Bloody Lust: Bloody Gust's "rage" effect is shared with Bloody Lust, so if Isaac picks up Bloody Lust after already getting hit with Bloody Gust (or vice versa) the boosts will automatically update to that level.

• Dull Razor: Safely provides the stat boosts without needing to take damage.

fields.description: The first 6 times Isaac takes damage on a given floor, he gains Speed and Fire Rate for the rest of the floor, up to a maximum of +1.02 and +3.00, respectively.

Bloody Lust.title: Bloody Lust
Bloody Lust.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish: Lusty Blood; Bloody Gust]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Damage increases as Isaac receives damage. The damage increase stays for the whole floor, but resets upon entering a new floor.

• [Before Repentance] The first three times Isaac is hit, his damage is increased by 0.5. The next three times Isaac is hit, his damage is increased by 33%.

• • [Repentance] Damage is increased by flat amounts: +0.5 for the first hit and an additional +0.2 for each hit, until +1.5 at the sixth. The maximum total is +6.0.

• Any damage taken past the sixth hit does not further increase damage.

• Isaac becomes redder as his damage increases.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Samson starts with this item by default.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Rights / Razor Blade / IV Bag: The damage from the items count for the stats up.

• Birthright + Samson: Birthright allows him to gain 4 more damage boosts at the same +0.2 intervals, for a new maximum total of +14.0.

• Dull Razor: Safely provides the damage boost without needing to take damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bloody Lust: No effect, damage up still caps at +6 and increases at the same intervals.

• Bloody Gust: Bloody Lust's "rage" effect is shared with Bloody Gust, so if Isaac picks up Bloody Gust after already getting hit with Bloody Lust (or vice versa) the boosts will automatically update to that level.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original Binding of Isaac, Bloody Lust only lasted for one room and the damage increase was triggered by killing enemies.

• Lusty Blood now has the effect of the original Bloody Lust.

• On the character select screen, Samson's starting item is spelled as "Blood Lust".

• Even if Bloody Lust is removed, Isaac will keep the same level of "rage" for the rest of the level. This means that his boosts will automatically update to that level if he picks up another Bloody Lust or a Bloody Gust on the same level.

fields.description: Increases Isaac's damage whenever he takes damage, up to six times. The bonus resets when entering a new floor.

Bloody Penny.title: Bloody Penny
Bloody Penny.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Gives a chance to drop a Half Red Heart when money is collected.

• [Before Repentance] 50% chance.

• [Repentance] The chance is based on the coin's worth:

| Coin | Chance 
| Penny | 25.00%

| Double Penny | 43.75%

| Nickel | 76.27%

| Dime | 94.37%

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] This trinket can be found by destroying Special Shopkeepers.

• [Afterbirth onward] This trinket is very useful in Greed mode, as the coins dropped for completing a wave now provide health.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Makes the Ultra Greedier fight trivial, as many of his attacks drop coins, thus providing free health.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• IV Bag: Can chain to create a large amount of coins.

• Keeper: The trinket can be seen as a "better" version of Rotten Penny, as instead of spawning one fly per coin, it spawns multiple at the cost of it being chance-based.

• Tainted Keeper: Fly production is heavily increased as most enemies drop coins on death.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Increases the chances to:

| Coin | Chance 
| Penny | 50.00%

| Double Penny | 75.00%

| Nickel | 96.88%

| Dime | 99.90%

• Golden Trinket + Mom's Box: Increases the chances to:

| Coin | Chance 
| Penny | 75.00%

| Double Penny | 93.75%

| Nickel | 99.90%

| Dime | 99.99%

fields.description: Gives a chance to drop a Half Red Heart when a coin is collected.

Blue Cap.title: Blue Cap
Blue Cap.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one full Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals Isaac for 1 additional Red Heart.

• +0.7 tears.

• -0.16 shot speed.

• Contributes to the Fun Guy transformation.

fields.quote: HP + tears up + shot speed down
fields.description: Gives one full Red Heart container, +0.7 tears, and -0.16 shot speed. [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

Blue Key.title: Blue Key
Blue Key.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the trinket that creates Blue Womb rooms; the trinket that opens the Hush fight and empowers Pandora's Box; Strange Key]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Entering a room that requires a Key does not consume a key, but brings Isaac to a room resembling ???, which acts as an in-between of the two rooms.

• These rooms contain assortments of Blue Gapers, Blue Boils, and/or Blue Conjoined Fatty, and are always long rooms (either normal or slim). They have a chance to give a reward when cleared, like normal rooms.

• Once exited, the room cannot be re-entered.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Doors that were unlocked with the trinket have a blue hue emitting from them instead of the normal floor-dependent hue.

• The doors leading to the entrance of Downpour or Dross can be unlocked for free by Blue Key, though the blue room generated will be a dead end. Leaving the way Isaac came in will leave the door unlocked, allowing the player to continue normally.

• Rooms that require money to enter (Arcades or rooms affected by Pay To Play) can also be opened for free.

• Doors that require two keys to open, such as Vaults or Dice Rooms, will be opened instantly instead of waiting for the animation of both keys to be used.

• The door leading to Hush will also produce a blue room, despite not requiring a key.

• Isaac can unlock the rooms with Blue Key, but not enter them straight away. By exiting and re-entering the room, he can pass through the door that was unlocked with the Blue Key without having to go through the room in between.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either makes the blue rooms drop double rewards when cleared. Having both triples the rewards.

• Door Stop / Mercurius: The blue room can be exited without fighting the enemies, and the door will remain unlocked.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Broken Padlock: Doors opened via explosions will not spawn the corridor.

• Ventricle Razor: Any portals inside the hall will be deleted upon exiting. While in the hallway, any portals to the outside can still be taken.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The trinket might be a reference to SCP-860, a fictional key that acts in a near-identical manner.

• If used on the ??? floor, one might hear the mid-combat layer of the floor's theme, Nativitate, an asset which was previously unused.

• The combat layer of Nativitate can also be heard in a Crawl Space or an I AM ERROR room with enemies, or in rooms created by Red Key (or similar effects) on the ??? floor.

• This is the only trinket to be unlocked by defeating The Beast.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Opening a locked door without entering it and then leaving and re-entering the room will no longer cause the door opened by Blue Key to lead to a Blue Womb room. In other words, this removes the downside of the trinket.

fields.description: Doors can be unlocked without using Keys. Opening a door this way brings Isaac to an in-between room that resembles ???, with a few monsters.

Blue Map.title: Blue Map
Blue Map.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Reveals the locations of Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms on the map.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• When combined with The Compass and Treasure Map, the entire floor is revealed, identical to the effect of The Mind.

• [Repentance] Blue Map does not display Ultra Secret Rooms. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Secrets: Makes it easier to gain X-Ray Vision as Book of Secrets cannot give a mapping effect Isaac already has.

• Fragmented Card / Luna: Extra Secret Rooms / Super Secret Rooms are revealed as well.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Cursed!.

• In the original game, Treasure Map revealed the location of Secret Rooms as well. In Rebirth, this effect, along with the added effect of revealing of Super Secret Rooms, now belongs to this item instead.

• [Repentance] Under the minimap, The Mind's icon will override the icon of this item.

fields.description: Reveals the locations of Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms on the map.

Bob.title: Bob
Bob.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Bob is a transformation added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth, turning Isaac into Bob after picking up 3 Bob-related items.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac leaves a trail of green poisonous creep as he walks that deals [Before Repentance] 6 / [Repentance] 20 damage per second.

• [Repentance] Grants poison immunity.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.text: Pick up 3 items or trinkets from the following list ( [Repentance] with the [code: bob] tag).

sections.heading: Trinkets
sections.text:
[trinket rows: Bob's Bladder] 
|}

fields.description: Isaac leaves a trail of green poisonous creep as he walks that deals 6 damage per second.

Bob's Bladder.title: Bob's Bladder
Bob's Bladder.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Bombs leave green creep underneath themselves.

• [Repentance] The creep deals 23.3 damage per tick.

• Contributes to the Bob transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Bombs will leave a trail of creep when moved or pushed around until they explode.

• [Repentance+] The Golden Trinket or the Mom's Box combination will not count as multiple items of the transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Creep pool is slightly larger.

• If Isaac has both a golden trinket and the Box, the creep also lasts longer.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs from Dr. Fetus leave creep, allowing for extra damage.

• Remote Detonator: Bombs will continue to leave creep until they are manually detonated. Allows for maximization of creep damage, potentially dealing more damage over time to a boss than just a singular bomb.

• Rocket in a Jar: Fired Rockets leave creep.

• Scatter Bombs: Tiny bombs will also create creep, allowing for a larger area of effect.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bob's Rotten Head: No effect.

• Epic Fetus: No effect.

• Mr. Mega: Does not produce bigger creep puddles.

• Throwable Bombs from Bomb Grimaces do not leave creep.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance+] This is one of the only three trinkets that count toward a transformation, the other ones are Kid's Drawing and A Missing Page.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Bob's Bladder will not contribute to the Bob transformation despite having the item tag.

fields.description: Leaves a pool of green creep under all Bombs Isaac places, which damages enemies that walk over it.

Bob's Brain.title: Bob's Brain
Bob's Brain.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a floating brain familiar that can be fired towards enemies as a projectile.

• [Rebirth only] Bob's Brain is fired directly from where Isaac is standing.

• [Afterbirth onward] Bob's Brain is fired directly from where it is located in the chain of familiars behind Isaac, making aiming it slightly more difficult.

• If it hits an enemy, it deals 3.5 damage and explodes, further damaging and poisoning monsters.

• [Before Repentance] The explosion deals 60 damage. The poison deals double Isaac's Damage over time.

• [Repentance] The explosion deals 100 damage. The poison damage is dealt 4 times, inflicting Isaac's Damage per tick.

• [Repentance] The explosion ignores armor.

• The explosion can hurt Isaac, dealing a full heart of damage.

• This can make picking up the item a risky choice, as Bob's Brain will always fire, regardless of whether or not Isaac will be caught in the explosion.

• Once it explodes, it takes a few seconds to re-appear.

• Contributes to the Bob transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Bob's Brain is affected by most bomb modifiers.

• Bob's Brain only explodes when hitting an enemy, and does not explode upon hitting a fire, poop, or wall. It can destroy poops and fires like normal shots, however.

• Bob's Brain never launches immediately upon entering a room unless a tear-firing key is released and pressed again, or until several seconds have passed.

• If Isaac has multiple copies of Bob's Brain, only one familiar will be active at a given time, with another one firing immediately after the first has exploded or starts to return from a miss.

• [Rebirth only] Multiple copies of Bob's Brain will float in the same spot in the familiar line.

• [Afterbirth onward] Each copy takes up their spot on the familiar line, but only the first one launches out. Respawning brains may end up stacking on top of each other.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Bob's Brain having [Before Repentance+] 5th / [Repentance+] 7th priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: The impact damage is increased to 7 and the explosion deals an additional 25 damage.

• Mr. Mega: The explosion deals an additional [Before Repentance] 85/ [Repentance] 50 damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Effects applied as normal:

• Blood Bombs

• Brimstone Bombs

• Butt Bombs

• Glitter Bombs

• Hot Bombs

• Nancy Bombs

• Sad Bombs

• No effect:

• Bobby-Bomb

• Bob's Curse

• • [Repentance] The poison effect of Bob's curse is applied which deals only 2 ticks of damage, resulting in inflicting halved damage.

• Fast Bombs

• Ghost Bombs

• Rocket in a Jar

• Scatter Bombs

• Sticky Bombs

• • [Repentance] Spiders do not spawn, however the explosion leaves behind a puddle of slowing creep.

• Bomber Boy: No cross explosions. Damage from the explosion is halved against the initial target, but others caught in the blast take full damage.

• [Repentance] Explodes in a cross-shaped pattern. Damage from the main explosion deals a flat 37.5 damage, and any additional explosion deals flat 75 damage to which Bomber boy's damage reduction is not applied.

• • Bomber Boy + BFFS!: Explosion damages are increased to 1.25x, which are 46.875/93.75 each.

• • Bomber Boy + Mr. Mega: Explosion damages are increased to 1.5x, which are 56.25/112.5 each.

• • Bomber Boy + BFFS! + Mr. Mega: Explosion damages are increased to 1.75x, which are 65.625/131.25 each.

• Duct Tape: Bob's Brain stays in place relative to Isaac until it is fired.

• [Before Repentance] E. Coli / Flush!: Bob's Brain will explode upon hitting an enemy that has been turned into poop.

• [Repentance] Bob's Brain no longer explodes upon hitting poops made from enemies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] Three copies of this item are used in BRAINS!. [end edition note] 

• In a Twitter AMA, Edmund McMillen mentioned that Bob's Brain is his favorite item from The Binding of Isaac.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that charges forward when shooting tears and explodes upon contact with an enemy, damaging and poisoning them. The familiar respawns after a few seconds.

Bob's Curse.title: Bob's Curse
Bob's Curse.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants 5 Bombs.

• Grants all of Isaac's bombs a poison effect.

• [Repentance] The bombs leave a lingering green poison cloud after exploding.

• [Repentance] Gives Isaac immunity to poison effects such as those from destroying Mushrooms and Sick Boom Fly. [end edition note] 

• Contributes to the Bob transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • This item can drop from killing Super Sloth. [Before Repentance] Super Sloth can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Despite the item sprite for Bob's Curse having a fuse, the bombs placed lack them.

• The bombs placed after picking up this item resemble the head of Pestilence or Sloth. Bob is also the confirmed first name of Sloth as revealed by a QnA.

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Before Afterbirth+: Rebirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth+]
fields.description: +5 Bombs. Grants Isaac's bombs a poison effect. [Repentance] They also leave a lingering poison cloud, and Isaac becomes immune to poison.

Bob's Rotten Head.title: Bob's Rotten Head
Bob's Rotten Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac holds a poison Bomb over his head which can be thrown in the cardinal directions and explodes on impact.

• The bomb can fly across the room for 9.5 tiles before falling to the ground and exploding.

• [Before Repentance] The explosion deals a flat 50 + Isaac's tear damage and poisons affected monsters.

• [Repentance] The explosion deals a flat 185 + Isaac's tear damage and leaves behind a gas cloud that poisons affected monsters. The poison cloud deals 5 damage.

• [Rebirth only] The poison deals 6 or 8 points of damage over time.

• [Afterbirth onward] The poison deals 3 times Isaac's tear damage over time.

• Contributes to the Bob transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item can drop from killing Sloth. [Before Repentance] Sloth can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. 

• Bob's Rotten Head is affected by many tear modifiers and some bomb modifiers. Notable exceptions and precautions are listed below.

• Bob's Rotten Head passes through [machine: Beggar] s, [machine: Slot Machine] s, or [machine: Blood Donation Machine] s, but can destroy them with the blast damage if it impacts anything nearby.

• Can open open Secret Rooms, Super Secret Rooms, or destroy rocks like any other bomb.

• Certain interactions require Flat Stone to be effective or work.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bob's Bladder / Bobby-Bomb / Bomber Boy / Fast Bombs / Rocket in a Jar / Scatter Bombs / Mr. Mega: No effect.

• Bob's Curse:

• [Before Repentance] No effect.

• [Repentance] The explosion leaves behind a poison cloud.

• Blood Bombs: Bob's Rotten Head leaves a pool of red creep on the ground after each explosion.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring. The wisps shoot arcing green tears with decreased range, with a 7.5% chance of firing an explosive, poisonous tear.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Compound Fracture: Spawns 1-3 smaller heads that explodes for half the damage of the bigger one.

• Continuum:

• [edition anr] Bob's Rotten Head can now travel through walls and appear out of the opposite wall, similar to a portal-type mechanic.

• [Repentance] No longer travels through the wall; instead he bounces off it, like with Rubber Cement, and then travels for the rest of its duration at a slower speed and then explodes.

• Cricket's Body: Spawns four smaller heads that explode for half the damage of the bigger one.

• Explosivo / Sticky Bombs:

• [edition anr] If Bob's Rotten Head sticks to an enemy (sometimes with Explosivo, always with Sticky Bombs), the explosion is delayed but will deal 110 damage.

• [Repentance] No longer sticks to monsters.

• Eye of the Occult: Isaac can control the mid-flight direction of the head, however its air-time is not increased.

• Flat Stone: Will cause Bob's Rotten Head to bounce once, exploding twice and leaving two gas clouds.

• Fire Mind: Creates fire when the head lands.

• Godhead: Creates a Godhead aura around the head and applies homing effect when thrown.

• Haemolacria: When the head lands, tears are fired.

• Holy Light: Has a chance to throw a Holy Light head that spawns a damaging beam of light dealing ( [Before Repentance] 4x) [Repentance] 3x the explosion damage when it hits an enemy.

• Homing tears: Homing is applied to the thrown head as well.

• [Before Repentance] Spectral tears: The head will pass through obstacles and walls, meaning it will no longer destroy obstacles or open secret rooms on impact. They can still be opened if the user stands back far enough to let the thrown head run out of range.

• [Repentance] The head will slightly bounce off of walls with spectral tears. It still passes through obstacles.

• Lachryphagy: The head act as a tear, dividing itself if enough time has passed and interacting with other tears. The five heads coming from the main head deal half damage. Feeding a head with another increases damage by the amount of damage Isaac has. If a tear is fed with a head, the tear will gain the head's damage.

• The Parasite: Causes two smaller tears to appear that explodes for half the damage of the head. Tears do not look like the normal head.

• Rubber Cement: Causes the head to bounce off of rocks and walls.

• Tiny Planet: When used, Bob's Rotten Head will orbit the player similar to a tear.

• Trisagion:

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Not recommended as it explodes multiple times before reaching its target, dealing explosive damage and knockback to Isaac.

• [Repentance] Shoots a white blast of light instead of the head that pierces through monsters, and causing explosions when it contacts an enemy (if not killing it at the first tick), an obstacle, or when it runs out of range. One tick of the beam deals 33% of Bob's Rotten Head's damage to monsters, but the resulting explosion every tick deals full damage.

• Uranus: Monsters are frozen when dying to Bob's Rotten Head.

• Worm trinkets: Bob's Rotten Head is affected by trinkets like Hook Worm and Wiggle Worm the same way tears are.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Lil Spewer, The Parasite]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item's appearance is similar to Pestilence's head.

• Sloth's full name is Bob Sloth, revealed in a QnA. Because Sloth drops this item, it may be his head.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Although Bob's Rotten Head works normally with Butt Bombs and Bomber Boy has no effect with it, their combination drops the explosion damage by 50%.

fields.description: Isaac holds a poison Bomb which can be thrown in a cardinal direction and explodes on impact.

Bobby-Bomb.title: Bobby-Bomb
Bobby-Bomb.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants 5 Bombs.

• Grants homing bombs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • This item can make bombing out of rooms difficult, as the bombs may slide towards enemies and away from the door.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Dr. Fetus: The bombs that Isaac fires will be homing.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Doctor's Remote/Epic Fetus: Crosshair will not home in on enemies.

• Bob's Rotten Head: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is a reference to Bob-ombs, enemies from the Mario franchise who self-detonate to hurt Mario.

fields.description: +5 Bombs. Bombs gain a homing effect, slowly moving towards the nearest enemy.

Boil.title: Boil
Boil.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Boils start as small red spheres that slowly grow to full size. When at their full size, they can spurt out a cluster of blood shots at Isaac, similar to one of Monstro's attacks. Boils decrease in size when hit, but will regenerate to their full size until fully destroyed.

sections.heading: Gut
sections.text: Guts have a 5.71% chance to replace Boils and behave almost identically. Instead of disorganized blood shots, they fire singular Ipecac shots at Isaac that do not damage them.

sections.heading: Sack
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the enemy; the pickup; Sacks] 

Sacks don't shoot projectiles; instead, they periodically spawn a Spider when fully swollen. Therefore, damaging them will prevent them from spawning Spiders, making them easy to kill. They also regenerate much slower than Boils or Guts. They can commonly be found on the early floors.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Up to six spiders can be active at once.

• [Repentance] They can spawn in unique Curse Room layouts if Isaac has Voodoo Head. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Blue Boil
sections.text: Blue Boils are mainly spawned during the Hush fight. They spawn fully swollen and don't need to charge up like regular Boils. Instead of spraying clusters of blood shots, they fire either one blood shot, or three blood shots in a spread towards Isaac. They also regain their health 10x faster than regular Boils if they are damaged but not killed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Blue Boils that appear in regular rooms can be Champions.

• Blue Boils' shots deal a full heart of damage to Isaac.

• [Repentance] They can also appear in ??? with the use of Red Key or by entering doors unlocked with the Blue Key. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Gush
sections.text:
Gushes are stationary, being unable to do any form of damage. Instead, they continuously create slowing black creep around them that slowly expands infinitely in radius and can cover the entire room if left alive for long enough. Unlike other Boil variants, they do not shrink or regenerate.

Although the Black Creep is relatively harmless on its own, Tar Boys can use their special attack if Isaac is standing on the creep.

sections.heading: Pustule
sections.text: Pustules are stationary enemies that appear to grow out of the ground, unlike Boils they do not shrink when damaged and instead continuously swell in size. When destroyed at the smallest stages, they explode into a tiny puddle of red creep and don't spawn anything. When destroyed at the last 2 stages of swelling they spawn a Small Maggot and a small pool of Red Creep, and if not destroyed, they will burst into a Bloodfly and a slightly larger puddle of Red Creep.

sections.heading: Walking Boil
sections.text: Walking Boils act like Boils, but randomly wander around the room, can deal half a heart of contact damage, and don't shrink or regenerate.

sections.heading: Walking Gut
sections.text: Walking Guts act like Guts, but randomly wander around the room, can deal half a heart of contact damage, and don't shrink and regenerate.

sections.heading: Walking Sack
sections.text: Walking Sacks act like Sacks, but randomly wander around the room, can deal half a heart of contact damage, and don't shrink or regenerate.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Afterbirth+] While regular Boils can be touched without taking damage, champion forms do inflict one heart of damage on touch (like all champions).

• Champion Boils grow significantly slower but take more hits to deflate. The exception to this is gray champions, which grow faster and take fewer hits to deflate.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gushes were added in Booster Pack #4, after the initial release of the DLC.

• [Repentance] A pustule is the scientific name for a pimple.

• [Repentance] Pustules in Antibirth would burst into Small Maggots and puddles of Green Creep as opposed to the Bloodfly and Red Creep in Repentance.

Boiled Baby.title: Boiled Baby
Boiled Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and fires chaotic bursts of tears in all directions at random intervals while in a room with enemies, shooting faster the closer it is to an enemy, similarly to Boils.

• Each tear fired by Boiled Baby does either 3.5 or 5.3 damage, with no in-between.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Boiled Baby having the lowest priority at [edition alternatives: baseline: 6th; Repentance+: 8th] and thus staying the farthest away from Isaac when compared to other familiars with higher priorities.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Boiled Baby originates from the Antibirth mod.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and fires chaotic bursts of tears in all directions.

Bomb Bag.title: Bomb Bag
Bomb Bag.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that drops a Bomb every 3 rooms.

• The first drop happens after 2 rooms.

• The bomb dropped can be a Double Bomb, Troll Bomb, Mega Troll Bomb, Golden Bomb, or a Golden Troll Bomb.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Bomb Bag having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • BFFS!: The familiar drops bombs in a repeating pattern of 2, 2 then 3 rooms.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: This item is the bomb counterpart to Sack of Pennies, Rune Bag, Mystery Sack, and Sack of Sacks.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that drops a Bomb every 3 rooms.

Fire Places.title: Fire Places
Fire Places.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Deals a half-heart of damage when touched. [Repentance] This damage is considered to be from a hostile source, not self-inflicted. Pyromaniac and Hot Bombs will prevent this damage.

• Can be extinguished by tears, bombs, or explosions.

• 25% chance to drop coins (75% chance) or hearts (25% chance) when extinguished.

• [Repentance] The chance to drop a reward is reduced to 10% while playing on Hard Mode.

• Piercing tears and Explosivo shots can pierce through fire places and all of their variants. [Before Repentance] Spectral tears, however, are blocked.

• [Repentance] Spectral tears can pierce through fire places.

sections.heading: Red Fire Place
sections.text:
• Can shoot red projectiles at medium speed at Isaac.

• [Before Repentance] They do not telegraph before firing projectiles.

• [Repentance] Red Fire Places have a bounce animation before firing.

• [Repentance] They fire a projectile only once until Isaac re-enters the room.

• Shots fired from a Red Fire Place will not spawn directly on the Red Fire Place, but rather near the fire.

• If Isaac stands too close when a Red Fire Place shoots, the projectile will spawn on Isaac.

• [Before Repentance] Pyromaniac makes Isaac immune to these projectiles.

• Can be extinguished like normal Fire Places.

• 25% chance to drop coins (75% chance) or hearts (25% chance) when extinguished.

• [Repentance] The chance to drop a reward is reduced to 10% while playing on Hard Mode.

• Can rarely replace normal Fire Places.

• [Afterbirth onward] Rarely, they'll appear in a room that needs to be cleared by pressing Pressure Plates. When all are pressed, the Red Fire Places will turn into normal Fire Places.

sections.heading: Blue Fire Place
sections.text:
• 25% chance to drop a Soul Heart when extinguished.

• [Repentance] The chance to drop a Soul Heart is reduced to 10% while playing on Hard Mode.

• Can only be put out by the following:

• Bombs/explosions and rock blasts (such as from Wait What?).

• Little Horn tears.

• [Repentance] Teleporting on top of it with Stitches.

• [Repentance] Using Suplex! on it, then leaving and re-entering the room (likely a bug).

• [Repentance+] Making contact with an explosive locust made from Abyss.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Purple Fire Place
sections.text:
• Fires purple homing projectiles at Isaac.

• [Before Repentance] The homing projectiles deal a full heart of damage.

• [Repentance] They fire a projectile only once until Isaac re-enters the room.

• 25% chance to drop a Soul Heart when extinguished.

• [Repentance] The chance to drop a Soul Heart is reduced to 10% while playing on Hard Mode.

• Can only be put out the same way as Blue Fire Places.

• Can rarely replace Blue Fire Places.

• [Afterbirth onward] Rarely, they'll appear in a room that needs to be cleared by pressing Pressure Plates. When all are pressed, the Purple Fire Places will turn blue.

sections.heading: White Fire Place
sections.text:
• Only spawns in specific rooms on Downpour II or Dross II, and there will only be one of these rooms on the floor. The room may contain multiple white fire places depending on the layout.

• Red Rooms in Downpour I/II or Dross I/II also have a chance to contain white fire places.

• When Isaac touches the flame, he "dies" and becomes a ghost, which has the properties of The Lost (flight, spectral tears, no health, and the Holy Mantle).

• The ghost will not have Holy Mantle if it is not yet unlocked for The Lost.

• The ghost will not have Holy Mantle if the room has not been cleared.

• The ghost can take a devil deal for free like The Lost can.

• The ghost can collect health pickups, but these are applied to the main character once Isaac reverts to normal form.

• While a ghost, Isaac can enter the mirrored world by walking into the mirror found on Downpour/Dross II.

• Completing and exiting a hostile room outside of the mirror world will change Isaac back to normal.

• However, traveling to the next floor as the ghost will not change Isaac back until a room is cleared on that floor.

• As a ghost, the fire can be flown through as if it were an empty tile, with no other effects.

• Can be extinguished by using Chaos Card or by an explosion under the effect of Astral Projection (bug) or Suplex! (bug).

• Can also be extinguished by using Soul of Judas; quickly running to hover over the White Fire Place then shooting on the white fire place. Upon leaving and re-entering the room, the White Fire Place will be extinguished.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• All types of fire places deal 16 damage to enemies that come in contact with them.

• [Repentance] Normal and Red Fire Places are automatically extinguished in flooded rooms (including most rooms in Flooded Caves). Using Flush! will immediately put out all Normal and Red Fire Places in the room. [end edition note] 

• Unlike similar room obstacles, bombing a fire place will not create a walkable area over a pit.

• Hot Bombs makes Isaac immune to contact damage with fire places. Fire place projectiles will still deal damage.

Stone Grimace.title: Stone Grimace
Stone Grimace.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: A Stone Grimace is an invincible stationary statue with the shape of a head with a wide-open mouth and hollow eyes. Stone Grimaces will sporadically spit a Red bullet in Isaac's direction until the room is cleared by killing regular enemies, or by pressing Pressure Plates. When the room is cleared, the Stone Grimace closes its eyes and mouth.

sections.heading: Vomit Grimace
sections.text: The Vomit Grimace fires an explosive Ipecac-like shot. Like Stone Grimaces, Vomit Grimaces will stop firing at Isaac when the room is cleared.

sections.heading: Triple Grimace
sections.text: The Triple Grimace fires a triple shot. Like Stone Grimaces, Triple Grimaces will stop firing at Isaac when the room is cleared.

sections.heading: Gaping Maw
sections.text: The Gaping Maw sucks Isaac towards it, along with warping Isaac's and any enemies' bullet paths. It does not fire any shots and simply functions as an obstacle, and is often surrounded by spikes. [Afterbirth onward] They can, however, be deactivated by Pressure Plates.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If a Gaping Maw is rerolled with D10, it will always turn into a Broken Gaping Maw.

sections.heading: Broken Gaping Maw
sections.text: A broken variant of the Gaping Maw. It alternates between active and inactive every four seconds, but it has a much stronger attraction power. [Afterbirth onward] Just like regular Gaping Maws, they can be deactivated by Pressure Plates. Prior to Afterbirth+ Booster Pack 5, only one room in the game contained Broken Gaping Maws.

sections.heading: Constant Stone Shooter
sections.text: Constant Stone Shooters, sometimes referred to as Turret Grimaces, constantly fire bullets in a fixed direction, and do not stop firing even after the room is cleared. [Afterbirth onward] The exceptions are rooms with Pressure Plates, which deactivate them once they are all pressed.

sections.heading: Cross Stone Shooter
sections.text:
Cross Stone Shooters were added in Booster Pack #4.

The Cross Stone Shooter, sometimes referred to as Cross Grimace, constantly fires bullets in four directions, alternating between cardinal and diagonal directions. If the room has to be cleared, whether by killing enemies or by pressing Pressure Plates, then Cross Grimaces will deactivate upon the room's completion like a regular Grimace. However, if the room is purely trap based and does not present an objective to complete, then Cross Grimaces will continue shooting indefinitely.

sections.heading: Brimstone Head
sections.text: Found in Gehenna and Sheol, the Brimstone Head, sometimes referred to as Brimstone Grimace, periodically shoots Brimstone lasers and does not stop firing even after the room is cleared. [Afterbirth onward] The exception is pressing all Pressure Plates, which deactivates them.

sections.heading: Stone Eye
sections.text: The Stone Eye resembles the Bloodshot Eye. It constantly rotates in a clockwise circle and shoots a flickering Technology laser. It stops firing after the room is cleared. Unlike any other Stone Grimace variants, the Stone Eye appears to despawn when the room is cleared, exited, and then re-entered. [Repentance+] Stone Eyes will do an entire rotation before shooting their laser.

sections.heading: Bomb Grimace
sections.text:
The Bomb Grimace is a unique Stone Grimace in that its only purpose is to keep a single Throwable Bomb spawned. A few seconds after Isaac takes the bomb, it will spawn another.

If it is destroyed with an instant-death attack such as Euthanasia or Little Horn, it spawns 10 Throwable Bombs.

Always spawns during the battle of Tuff Twins and The Shell. It can also appear in the mineshaft in Mines/Ashpit II, where the Throwable Bombs it provides prove essential for fleeing Mother's Shadow.

sections.heading: Quake Grimace
sections.text:
The Quake Grimace fires a line of rocks in one direction upon landing every 3 seconds. In most cases, even after the room is cleared of vulnerable enemies, they will continue this behavior. However, they can be deactivated from Pressure Plates.

If a Secret Room or a Super Secret Room is placed in the path of their attack, the attack will break the wall and open the entrance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• These monsters are impassable, even with flight.

• These monsters can be destroyed using Chaos Card, Little Horn and Euthanasia, though they will respawn upon leaving and re-entering the room they were in.

• With Infestation 2, killing Stone Grimaces creates a Blue Spider, allowing blue spiders to be farmed by leaving and re-entering the room.

• Fire Mind tears that hit these monsters can still cause explosions.

• [Afterbirth onward] Hitting Grimaces increases the Dead Eye damage multiplier.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If an uncleared room has Cross Grimaces, leaving and then re-entering the room by bombing a door will make them stop shooting, making the room easier.

• [Repentance] 4 Stone Grimaces can appear in Loki's boss fight.

• [Repentance+] All variations of the Stone Grimace are destroyed when Hagalaz is used.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Afterbirth+] Stone Grimaces and their variants play their appearance animation for a second before resuming as deactivated in a cleared room if they were deactivated.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] They now no longer reuse their appear animation in a cleared room when the player re-enters it.

• If a Constant Stone Shooter is deactivated, it closes its eyes and mouth and stops crying, looking similar to Stone Grimaces upon deactivation. The difference is that deactivated Constant Stone Shooters still have a crack on top of their heads.

• If a Gaping Maw or Broken Gaping Maw is deactivated, unlike other Grimaces, it doesn't fully close its eyes. Instead, it closes its eyes only partially and makes a frown.

• Grimaces will turn green if poisoned.

• Great Gideon is the boss variant of Stone Grimaces.

• Gaping Maws were going to have fangs, as shown on the Bestiary.

• [Repentance] The Bomb Grimace and Quake Grimace first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• [Repentance] Quake Grimaces have substantially different designs compared to their original appearance in Antibirth. Most notably, they are the same size as other Stone Grimaces instead of being twice as large, and they do not have the large gash in their body.

• • Pre-release content of Repentance as well as the "death preview" shows the original version of Quake Grimaces, suggesting this change was made late in development.

• [Repentance] Bomb Grimaces are the only Grimaces who don't appear in the bestiary.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Using the D10 in a room with Stone Grimaces will turn them invisible. They will not fire, but the space they occupied will prevent Isaac from moving through it like an invisible wall.

Sucker.title: Sucker
Sucker.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Suckers fly slowly towards Isaac and, upon death, fire 4 shots in the cardinal directions.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Suckers are unaffected by Skatole.

• [Repentance] Suckers and all of its variants will not deal contact damage while Isaac holds Skatole, but can still deal damage by other means (usually by a bullet fired after death).

sections.heading: Spit
sections.text: Spits fly slowly towards Isaac and, upon death, fire an explosive Ipecac shot toward him.

sections.heading: Ink
sections.text: Inks fly slowly towards Isaac and, upon death, fire four projectiles in the ordinal directions and spawn a puddle of Black Creep.

sections.heading: Soul Sucker
sections.text: Soul Suckers float towards Isaac and, upon death, spawn a swirling red vortex, which then fires four Brimstone beams in the cardinal directions after a short delay.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Brimstone beams fired from the Soul Suckers can damage other enemies, including other Soul Suckers.

• The appearance of the vortex resembles the same vortex that appears when firing Brimstone with the effects of Anti-Gravity.

sections.heading: Mama Fly
sections.text: Mama Flies float away from Isaac and occasionally stop to plant down a Pustule. They spawn Small Maggots upon death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • After planting a Pustule, they will move directly away from Isaac, and will continue in that direction until either planting another Pustule or hitting a wall.

sections.heading: Bulb
sections.text: Bulbs fly in erratic, right-angled motions. If Isaac has an active item with any amount of charges (this includes timed recharge items), they fly towards him and drain up to 2 charges upon contact, but do not deal damage. If Isaac does not have an active item, or if his item has no charges, they simply fly around randomly and are completely harmless.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Bulbs aren't unlocked yet, each will be replaced with a Fly.

• Bethany's soul charges and Tainted Bethany's blood charges cannot be drained by them.

• Bulbs replaced Greed Gapers in any Treasure Room layouts that previously contained them in Afterbirth+.

sections.heading: Bloodfly
sections.text: Bloodflies are exclusively encountered in Corpse after a Pustule bursts. They behave very similarly to Bulbs in movement, but unlike Bulbs, don't drain charges and deal contact damage. After dying, they shoot 4 shots in the cardinal directions.

sections.heading: Tainted Sucker
sections.text:
Tainted Suckers float towards Isaac and, upon death, shoot 6 projectiles in all directions that bounce off of walls and obstacles, splitting into 6 smaller projectiles each.

They are exclusive to the Ascent to Home.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Strangely enough, they are the only Sucker variant aside from Bulbs that do not deal contact damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Suckers seem to be based on mosquitoes, midge-like flies that suck the blood of other animals, as they seem to share a small proboscis and blood sac.

• Bulbs seem to be based on fireflies, with the positioning of their bulb mirroring the bioluminescent organ of the firefly.

• [Repentance] The Sucker is tied with the Boom Fly for being the monster with the most true variants ('true variants' being monsters with ID x.1, x.2, etc.), both with 7.

• Soul Suckers were added in Booster Pack #4, after the initial release of the DLC Afterbirth †.

• [Repentance] The Ink and Mama Fly first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• The Mama Fly's AI has been changed from the mod where it would fly aimlessly rather than flying away from Isaac after planting down a Pustule.

• Bulbs have a couple odd behaviors when converted into a friendly enemy by the Beelzebub transformation:

• If the room has no hostile enemies, they will still move erratically in Isaac's general direction regardless if he has charges or not (they will not steal charges while friendly).

• If the room has hostile enemies, they will erratically fly toward enemies; they deal no contact damage to enemies either, so this is useless and only results in their deaths.

• Tainted Suckers have the lowest health out of any tainted variant.

• [Repentance] The sound that plays when a Bulb dies is the same as when an active item charge was filled in the original Flash-based Binding of Isaac.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Mama Flies are not affected by the Beelzebub transformation.
Bug note: Bulbs ignore Tainted Forgotten even when they have an active item.

sections.text:
Bombgaggers are monsters added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC and are exclusively found in Ashpit.

When near Isaac, they will begin to vomit up a Giga Bomb and proceed to run to a safe distance.

sections.heading: Notes

sections.heading: Trivia

Bumbino.title: Bumbino
Bumbino.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Bumbino is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in all environments of Chapter 2 (Caves, Catacombs, [Afterbirth onward] Flooded Caves).

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Bumbino slowly moves towards Isaac and can perform the following attacks:

• Swipes forward to clear a path to Isaac if Bumbino is obstructed by obstacles while chasing him.

• Performs two swipes, one in Isaac's direction, followed by another swipe in the opposite direction; these swipes can break obstacles. Then slams the ground, releasing 8 rock projectiles in all directions as well as 4 rock waves diagonally.

• If Bumbino hits a wall or a pit with a swipe he is momentarily stunned, interrupting this attack and causing rock projectiles to fall from the ceiling.

• His swipe attack will also deflect incoming projectiles.

• Charges in Isaac's direction when vertically aligned with him and a wall, breaking all obstacles caught in his path. Bumbino will become stunned upon impacting the wall, launching a cluster of rock projectiles in the opposite direction and causes rock projectiles to fall from the ceiling.

• If Isaac is close to the impact, he is pushed away.

• Launches a Butt Bombs Bomb in Isaac's direction.

All of Bumbino's attacks deal 1 Heart of damage.

Additionally, Bumbino attempts to pick up any dropped Coins, similar to Ultra Greed, but without the healing.

• He prioritizes picking up coins on the ground over attacking.

• He cannot pick up Sticky Nickels, but will try indefinitely if one should spawn in the room, effectively anchoring him to one spot.

• Getting hit by Bumbino's swipes may sometimes cause Isaac to drop coins.

• If Bumbino picks up at least 12 cents worth of coins, he drops an extra item from the following list and then leaves the room:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Bumbino cannot spawn copies of items that Isaac has already encountered/collected. Once Bumbino's item pool is exhausted, he will only drop The Poop.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Bumbino is based on Bumbo, an item in-game and the main character in The Legend of Bum-bo, another game developed by Edmund McMillen in 2019.

• All items dropped by Bumbino reference the gameplay symbols from The Legend of Bum-bo: Pee, Poop, Hearts, Bones, Snot, and Teeth.

• The name "Bumbino" is a portmanteau of "Bumbo" and "Bambino", the Italian word for child.

• Bumbino's slam attack may be a reference to the Wario Land games, as he slams with his shoulder forward, mimicking Wario's Shoulder Bash move.

• Bumbino's voice is noticably deeper pitched than Bumbo's from The Legend of Bum-bo, despite resembling him.

• Bumbino's ingame face resembles the Newgrounds emoticon "Agnry Faic", which is also represented as a Co-op Baby called Boss Baby.

• Taking Knockout Drops as Keeper will give him an expression resembling Bumbino.

• Bumbino does not have a sprite for his delirium form.

• Bumbino is one of only 3 bosses that can be spared, with the others being Baby Plum and Hornfel.

• Coincidentally, they all made their debut in Repentance.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Isaac will drop coins from Bumbino's swipes even if he's immune to damage through any means. This includes Tainted Forgotten's skeleton.

Chimera.title: Chimera
Chimera.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Chimera is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Corpse.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Chimera trots quickly in Isaac's direction, slowly building up speed. When fast enough, it leaves a trail of harmful green creep and makes wide turns due to its momentum. It can also perform the following attacks:

• Spits out 5 Small Maggots.

• Any Small Maggots it walks into are killed.

• Unlike its other attacks, Chimera can perform this one without interrupting its chase and its built up speed.

• Spits out a Sick Boom Fly and throws it towards Isaac.

• Jumps twice towards Isaac, shooting out a radius of 8 tears on the first landing and 4 rock waves in diagonal directions on the second landing.

• Shoots out 8 Ipecac shots towards where Isaac is predicted to move. The landing position of each projectile is marked on the ground.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Once its HP has dropped to about half, it makes a final charge towards Isaac before tripping and dividing the head and body into separate entities. It will take increasingly reduced damage as it approaches 50% HP until it transitions phases.

• The head continuously makes leaps towards Isaac and slides a distance after landing while leaving a trail of damaging red creep. It can also perform the following attacks:

• Shoots out 4 spreads of 5 projectiles in Isaac's direction.

• Performs three quick dashes, similar to Dingle, leaving Red Creep. The first 2 dashes are towards Isaac while the final dash is towards its body. After completing the final dash the body can pick the head up and throw it at Isaac, leaving a trail of projectiles as it travels and creating a burst of projectiles where the head collides with a wall.

• • If the body is performing another attack during the head's charges, the head will charge at Isaac for its third charge instead.

• If the body dies before the head, it continuously makes long charges at Isaac, bouncing off any walls while also leaving Red Creep.

• The body continues to chase Isaac like the first phase but at a slower pace. It can also perform the following attacks:

• Fires a green-hued Brimstone beam downwards if Isaac is directly above or below it. It is propelled upwards by this beam until it hits the wall.

• Runs quickly towards Isaac building momentum before leaping and rolling around the room bouncing off walls, similar to The Cage.

• If the head dies before the body, the body continuously rolls around like The Cage for the rest of the battle.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Chimera lends its name to the fact that it is a mix of three other bosses.

• It has the body of The Cage.

• It has the head of either Gurglings, Gurdy Jr., or Gurdy.

• It has the face of Monstro.

• It has behavior similar to that of all bosses stated above.

• A Chimera in Greek mythology is a monstrous creature composed of a lion, goat, and snake.

• "The term "chimera" has come to describe any mythical or fictional creature with parts taken from various animals...".

• "Chimera" is also the medical term for a human or animal that possesses more than one set of DNA.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Chimera's head will occasionally disappear once the body is killed, rendering them unbeatable unless the player exits the game and continues the run.

Clog.title: Clog
Clog.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Clog is a boss introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance and can appear in [Repentance] Dross.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Clog remains stationary in the center of the room, with the exception of a rare boss room layout where he spawns at the top center. He performs the following attacks:

• Spits out a Drip below him, repeating this attack a random number of times.

• Clog stops spitting out Drips if 4 are already alive.

• Clog alternates between spitting out Drips and performing his other attacks. If 4 Drips are alive, he skips spawning them and continuously uses his other attacks.

• Creates three lines of farts that spread across the room, knocking away Isaac and Drips. Each fart has a chance to spawn Poops.

• 1-2 Corny Poops are spawned in this attack, and no more than 3 can be up at a time.

• Shoots out 4 spiraling lines of projectiles, consisting of either slow projectiles with small gaps in between or fast projectiles with large gaps in between.

• The projectiles pass over poop for 1 second after being fired, and are blocked by poop afterward.

• The gaps between the slower projectiles are barely large enough for Isaac to move between them if he is next to the left or right wall.

• Clog spins and causes the water in the room to circulate around him clockwise or counterclockwise, catching Isaac and any Drips, Bombs, and/or Pickups in its current.

• This attack can only be used if at least 2 Drips are alive.

• Like other water-based effects in the Dross floor, Isaac is unaffected by this current if he has flight.

• Upon Clog's defeat, he and all remaining Drips are "flushed" away identical to the effect of using Flush! on them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If a Butt Bombs Bomb goes off in the same room as Clog, it heals him.

• The hitbox of poops is small enough for Isaac and the Drips spawned by Clog to move diagonally between them, even if they are undamaged.

• This happens frequently when Clog causes the water to circulate and forces them to be pressed against the poops he spawns.

• All poops created by Clog are significantly less likely to spawn pickups until Clog is defeated and Isaac re-enters the room, at which point they return to having their normal pickup drop chance.

• Flush! kills Clog instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 Dips.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Clog appears to be a boss version of a Splurt.

• A clog is a blockage in a toilet and/or its drain pipes.

• This is further referenced in Clog's death animation, where he gets flushed into the floor.

• Clog has many similarities to Brownie, though it is unknown whether or not they are truly connected.

• Clog's "voice" is the same as that of Brownie, albeit pitched down.

• Clog has buck teeth, just like Brownie.

• Clog and Brownie are both large, round balls of poop.

Clutch.title: Clutch
Clutch.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Clutch is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance (update v1.7.8) that appears in the Ashpit.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Clutch always spawns alongside 3 Clickety Clacks that it utilizes in its attacks. Phase 1 uses the following pattern:

• Randomly possesses one of the three Clickety Clacks, causing its head to spin and shoot 8 bone shots in the cardinal and ordinal directions. While possessing a Clickety Clack, Clutch is immune to all damage.

• Clutch will swap between Clickety Clacks at random intervals, or when the Clickety Clack he is possessing is killed. It can be briefly damaged when it is flying between Clickety Clacks.

• The possessed Clickety Clack will pursue Isaac and fire chains of bone projectiles at him when lined up in a cardinal direction, similar to a Bony, but will also move along a cardinal axis to stay in line with Isaac' position while shooting.

• The other non-possessed Clickety Clacks will be shielded, akin to the shield from a Bishop.

• When a Clickety Clack is killed, the bone pile it leaves behind will not regenerate. Instead, it will spawn a small purple fire that occasionally summons a bone projectile on its position before shooting it at Isaac, similarly to a Necro.

• When all three Clickety Clacks are killed, Clutch will be forcefully ejected and stunned, making it open to attack.

• After enough damage is dealt, Clutch will scream and revive all three Clickety Clacks, restarting the process.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Phase 2 begins once Clutch reaches 25% health. Clutch will scream, destroy all of the Clickety Clacks, and spawn bone orbitals that orbit Clutch and block tears.

• The bone orbitals follow Clutch loosely, dragging behind its movements.

• Indestructible purple fires will be left in the wake of the dead Clickety Clacks.
In this phase, Clutch will only perform the following attack:

• Rushes to Isaac's position in the room, stops, and shoots six volleys of six purple flames, in an alternating pattern.

• Clutch repeats this attack until its health is depleted.

• Upon death, Clutch creates a large explosion that deals 4 ticks of 80 damage to all monsters.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Eraser is used on Clickety Clacks prior to entering the boss room, the boss fight will begin directly in the second phase.

• If all the Clickety Clack bone piles are destroyed in Clutch's first phase through items such as Euthanasia or Chaos Card, it will automatically be forced into its second phase but without the purple fire places or bone orbitals.

• Clutch can be killed at 50% hp using Vade Retro.

• Vanishing Twin spawns a second Clutch in its second phase as there are not enough Clickety Clacks.

• Flush! will convert all Clickety Clacks into poop, immediately starting the second phase.

• Items like Uranus and Freezer Baby allow the Clickety Clacks to be frozen and destroyed, giving an easier time with the battle.

• The D10 will downgrade the Clickety Clacks into Globins and start the second phase.

• Using Meat Cleaver isn't recommended until the second phase of the fight, as it will also split the invulnerable Clickety Clacks.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Clutch was originally unused content in the release version of Repentance. It had unfinished behavior and could not be encountered in-game, but it could be spawned using the Debug Console and had room designs. This early version of Clutch could possess more than one Clickety Clack at a time, and the Clickety Clacks were always vulnerable to damage. In its second phase, it also shot standard blood shots instead of purple flames, and did not explode upon death. The boss was finished and added into the game properly in V1.7.8.

• Prior to release it also went by the name "The Possessor".

• On the patch notes for the V1.7.8 update, this boss was referred to as "Something Spooky."

• Clutch shares some sound effects from Polycephalus, with some seeming to be altered.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If a Clickety Clack is killed (e. g. with Euthanasia) just as Clutch decided to swap to it (and before the boss reaches it), Clutch will charge at the bone pile, seemingly trying to posess it. The boss will stay in this state until its health is reduced below 25% or all Clickety Clarks' bone piles are destroyed, including the one the boss is charging at.

Cohort.title: Cohort
Cohort.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Cohorts are enemies resembling a giant Globin in the shape of Monstro. They act similarly to Monstro, and have the following attacks:

• Hops towards Isaac.

• Spits a ball of blood at Isaac, which creates a radial burst of 8 blood shots after a moderate distance.

• Coughs up a chaotic burst of shots at Isaac. This burst contains a Globin goo pile, which will regenerate and chase Isaac if not killed. This has a chance to be a Gazing Globin goo pile.

• This attack cannot create Globins if the Cohort currently has 4 summoned Globins. Other Globins in the room do not count towards this limit.

• Upon death, splits into four Globin goo piles.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If a Globin goo pile lands over non-solid ground e.g. over a pit or between a wall and obstacles, it is killed instead of spawning.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Cohort first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• The eyeball that appears when it performs its splitting projectile attack resembles that of a Gazing Globin.

Colostomia.title: Colostomia
Colostomia.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Colostomia is a boss introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in [Repentance] Dross.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Colostomia alternates between the following attacks:

• Hops in place and then slides toward Isaac in the closest cardinal direction, firing projectiles in both perpendicular directions as she moves and leaving trails of explosive gas.

• The slide can be at a slight angle if Isaac isn't perfectly aligned with it.

• Colostomia continuously performs this attack until ~40% of the room is covered in explosive gas.

• Launches a Butt Bombs Bomb towards Isaac that ignites any gas clouds its explosion hits, causing a chain of explosions.

• This is always her first attack upon spawning.

• Unlike Isaac's Butt Bombs, these do not fog the room.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After dropping to half health, the bag containing Colostomia explodes, creating explosive clouds and leaving her adhering to the floor.

• Jumps to another nearby location, firing 8 projectiles in a radial burst and creating a puddle of harmful Brown Creep where she lands.

• Only 2 puddles of Brown Creep can persist at once.

• Spits two Butt Bombs Bombs at Isaac. The range of these bombs is dependent on how close Isaac is to her.

• Farts, creating a ring of explosive gas around her location.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Colostomia is based on a Colostomy bag, a removable, disposable bag that attaches to the exterior opening of a colostomy to permit sanitary collection and disposal of bodily wastes.

• Colostomia's 1st phase charge attack is similar to an attack from The Witness in Antibirth.

• Colostomia is confirmed female according to messages from NotYourSagittarius in the official Binding of Isaac Discord.

• Upon death, Colostomia diffuses into the water of the arena, turning it from green to a murky brown.

Cultist.title: Cultist
Cultist.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Cultists are an enemy added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

At the start of the room, they create a homing, indestructible Purple Ball (like Rag Mega's) and proceed to follow it around on a brief delay. These purple balls fade into Dark Balls after 6 seconds, which can be destroyed as normal and have 10 HP. They cannot spawn another ball as long as the one they previously spawned is still intact.

If they detect an enemy has died in the current room, it will stop following the ball it summoned, move to where the enemy died, and resurrect it with full health before going back to following its ball.

They can revive up to 5 enemies at a time and cannot revive other Cultists. They can, however, revive most bosses and mini-bosses.

sections.heading: Blood Cultist
sections.text: Blood Cultists are a variant of Cultists, but are similar only in appearance and their mobility. They wander erratically around the room and, if Isaac aligns with them horizontally, they will fire a horizontal wave of red creep and blood shots with unlimited range. They can also summon four bone traps that prevent Isaac from moving for one second when stepped on, predicting where he will be when summoning them. The bone traps cannot be destroyed in any ways other than stepping on them, and de-spawn after 3 seconds if not stepped on.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If a Blood Cultist is charmed or friendly, the bone traps it summons will petrify other enemies that step on them.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Cultist might be a reference to the Floater enemy from The Legend of Bumbo, despite there actually being a Cultist enemy in the game.

• Cultists may have replaced the Necromancer enemy from Antibirth, as they both have near identical mechanics and reside in Mausoleum.
