Mulligan.title: Mulligan
Mulligan.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the enemy; the item; The Mulligan] 

Mulligans are enemies that will actively try to avoid Isaac; their eyes widen and their speed increases when doing so. When running away, they may walk over spikes or into a fire.

Upon death, they spawn several Fly, Attack Fly and, occasionally, a Pooter. Mulligans may sometimes self-detonate. If this occurs: in addition to spawning flies as normal, it will also fire four projectiles in the cardinal directions and destroy nearby objects when doing so. Mulligans cannot deal contact damage to Isaac ( [Before Afterbirth+] unless they are Champions).

Alternatively, if a Mulligan's health is dropped to -10 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Mulligoon
sections.text: Mulligoons behave like Mulligans and will run away from Isaac, don't deal contact damage, and can self-detonate. They release 4 projectiles in ordinal directions and drop a Troll Bomb on death. If they self-detonate, they release 8 projectiles in the cardinal and ordinal directions in addition to dropping a Troll bomb.

sections.heading: Mulliboom
sections.text: Mullibooms, unlike Mulligans, will chase Isaac at a very fast pace and explode on contact, dealing half a heart of damage. They also explode immediately if they are killed.

sections.heading: Hive
sections.text:
Hives behave similarly to Mulligans, evading Isaac and spawning Fly, Attack Fly, and Pooters upon death. However, they also occasionally spit Attack Fly while running away from Isaac, and unlike Mulligans and Mulligoons, they can't self-detonate.

Alternatively, if a Hive's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Drowned Hive
sections.text:
Drowned Hives behave similarly to Hives but spit out Drowned Chargers instead of Attack Flies. Upon death, they spawn 1-2 Drowned Chargers.

Alternatively, if a Drowned Hive's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

[Repentance] Drowned Chargers spawned by Drowned Hives have half their usual health (11 HP).

sections.heading: Nest
sections.text:
Nests behave similarly to Hives, but they spit out Spider instead of Attack Fly when being chased. They spawn a Trite or a Big Spider upon death.

Unlike normal Spider, those spawned by the Nest die upon touching Isaac. This is not the case for spiders spawned from killing the Big spider.

Alternatively, if a Nest's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Leper
sections.text:
Lepers are a Mulligan variant that alternate between walking towards and running away from Isaac. For every 15 damage they take, a chunk of their head, known as a Leper Flesh, will detach and start erratically chasing Isaac. Lepers deal contact damage if they are in this state or below. Lepers can naturally be found with some head chunks missing.

After being reduced to 15 health, Lepers will chase Isaac continuously, leaving a trail of damaging Red Creep. Upon death, they leave behind one Leper Flesh and have a 50% chance to leave behind a Grey-colored Gusher.

Alternatively, if a Leper's health is dropped to -25 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will never spawn a Gusher on death, but will still spawn Leper Flesh.

sections.heading: Leper Flesh
sections.text:
Leper Fleshes are head chunks from Lepers that erratically chase Isaac and are spawned from Lepers for every 15 damage they take. Upon death, they fire a projectile at Isaac that predicts his movements.

They will die if Isaac walks into them, though he will still take contact damage.

sections.heading: Holy Mulligan
sections.text:
Holy Mulligans behave similarly to Nests and Hives; avoiding Isaac and spawning Angelic Baby (small) when chased. When killed, they leave behind 1-2 Embryos.

Alternatively, if a Holy Mulligan's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Prey
sections.text:
Preys behave similarly to Nests and Hives; avoiding Isaac and spawning Small Leeches when chased. Upon death, they spawn 2-3 Small Leeches.

Alternatively, if a Prey's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Mullighoul
sections.text:
Mullighouls behave similarly to Nests and Hives; avoiding Isaac and occasionally spawning a Willo when chased. Upon death it spawns 1-2 Willos. This variant can fly over pits.

Alternatively, if a Mullighoul's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

sections.heading: Gas Dwarf
sections.text: Gas Dwarves act similar to Mullibooms, but hock up explosive gas as they chase Isaac. Upon death, they release an explosive Ipecac shot that blows up any gas clouds it hits. If it manages to reach Isaac, however, it will explode, damaging Isaac and detonating nearby gas clouds.

sections.heading: Bouncer
sections.text:
Bouncers behave like regular Mulligans and avoid Isaac with the exception that they can still deal contact damage to Isaac in their normal state. However, after some time or when close to death, their head inflates and they start chasing Isaac. If they die or come into contact with him in this state, they explode into a large cloud of projectiles with some lingering in the air before dropping down. If they are killed before they enter this hostile state, they release 4 projectiles in the ordinal directions.

They can also occasionally reflect tears in their inflated state.

sections.heading: Tainted Mulligan
sections.text:
Tainted Mulligans are stronger versions of Mulligans that behave similarly to Hives. They walk away from Isaac and will spit several Ring Fly at him if he is near. Upon death, they spawn a plethora of fly enemies including: Fly, Attack Fly, Suckers, Spits, Inks, Boom Fly, and Red Boom Fly.

Alternatively, if a Tainted Mulligan's health is dropped to -20 or less in one instance (e.g., by using a Bomb), it will spawn nothing on death.

They are exclusive to the Ascent to Home.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Leper and Leper Flesh enemies were added in Booster Pack #5.

• The Mulligan, Mulligoon, Hive, and Swarmer are all the same monster in stages of decay and infestation.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, when a Mulligan self-detonated, the explosion would not break rocks.

• Mulligans will start running in random directions instead of directly away from Isaac if he stays close to them for long enough. This behavior also applies to Small Baby Long Legs.

• In the game's files, there is an unused Mulliboom self-detonation animation, an unused graphic of a Hive with a Mulligoon's face, and an unused graphic of the [Afterbirth onward] Drowned Hive with a blue-tinted Mulligoon's face.

• [Afterbirth onward] Drowned Hives, along with Drowned Chargers (name of Drowned Charger wasn't revealed), were revealed for Afterbirth in this official Binding of Isaac post.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] A leper is a person who suffers from leprosy, which is a contagious disease that causes discoloration and lumping on the skin plus disfigurement and deformities.

• [Repentance] Due to the Holy Mulligan leaving behind Embryos on death, it could be suggested that it transforms Embryos into the Small Angelic Babies it spawns.

• [Repentance] Holy Mulligans, Holy Bony, and Holy Eyes originated as cards from the card game The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls.

• [Repentance] Gas Dwarves used to be called Fartigans.

• [Repentance] Prey, Mullighouls, and Bouncers originate from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Mullighouls could also appear in Mausoleum and had 13 stage hp. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If a Mulligan or a Mulligoon is killed before the spawning period is finished (before they move), it will count as a self-detonation.
Bug note: If a Nest is killed in the Burning Basement, it has a chance to spawn a Flaming Hopper.
Bug note: Rarely if you kill a Drowned Hive before their spawn period is finished (before they move), it will shoot 4 projectiles in ordinal directions but the monster won't explode.

Conquest.title: Conquest
Conquest.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Conquest is a Harbinger that can appear in all environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb).

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Charges horizontally off-screen. Reappears alongside 7-8 copies of himself from the opposite end of the screen. These copies are randomly dispersed, covering a majority of the screen and will continuing charging. After all the copies have charged off-screen, the original Conquest will charge back into the room.

• He performs this attack more often if Isaac is to his left or right.

• All copies of Conquest share his health bar.

• Fires 4 homing projectiles in the cardinal directions.

• Ascends off-screen and summons 8-10 staggered Crack the Sky beams in random locations.

• Returns from the side of the screen.
Conquest deals a whole heart of contact damage, including every summoned copy during his charge.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Revelations, 7 Seals]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Conquest was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• He is an alternative of Death.

• Despite being Death's alternate version, his attacks are direct variations of War's first phase.

• • His ID and room ID also both show that he is a variation of War. 

• • In the original The Binding of Isaac, this similarity with War went comically further due to a bug where Conquest could in-fact replace War as the Chapter 3 Harbinger fight. 

• Conquest is one of the actual Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse, as opposed to Pestilence.

• The stitching on Conquest's stomach is an autopsy stitch, an incision in the shape of a Y.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Conquest can be found in The Void, even before being unlocked. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Delirium's Conquest form's horse resembles Famine's horse rather than Conquest's.

• Conquest is the only alternate boss in both the original The Binding of Isaac and Rebirth that is not a reference to one of Edmund McMillen's previous games.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Killing Conquest quickly while his clones are rushing across the screen and leaving one alive will cause the boss music to continue playing until leaving the room.

Consolation Prize.title: Consolation Prize
Consolation Prize.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac one of the following stat boosts, depending on what attribute Isaac has the least of:

• +1.0 flat damage

• +0.5 fire rate

• +0.2 speed

• +2.5 range

• Also drops either 3 Penny, 1 Bomb, or 1 Key on the ground.

• Bombs and keys are valued at 3 coins' worth. The pickup dropped will be what Isaac has the least value of, and in case of a tie one is chosen randomly.

• As Bethany and Tainted Bethany, one Soul Heart or two Red Hearts can also be dropped if they are low on charges.

• Charges are valued at 2 × Charges - 1 coins' worth. For instance having 7 charges would be valued at 13 coins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Pickups spawned can be variants of their type.

• [Before Repentance+] As Tainted ???, the game still checks the bomb count instead of the poop count. Since Tainted ??? cannot get bombs normally and bombs are turned into poop pickups or troll bombs, he will receive them every time once he has at least 3 coins and a key.

• The tears up can break the soft tears cap of 5, due to the fact that it is a fire rate modifier.

• Cards and trinkets that grant temporary stat increases will affect the stat given by Consolation Prize (e.g. using I - The Magician or carrying Tape Worm will likely prevent the item from granting a range up, VII - The Chariot or Goat Hoof - speed, and so on.)

• This can be use to force the raise of a chosen stat, if the player knows that 2 of them are tied.

• The stat up is permanent and won't go away even if the item is removed, similar to Experimental Treatment.

• Because of that, Tainted Isaac can pick it up and freely drop it without losing anything.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Consolation Prize is from the Antibirth mod.

• The sprite of the item is a reference to a "chocolate medal", an ironic medal designed for the places of a competition no medal is normally given for. As such, it is a consolation prize.

fields.description: Increases Isaac's lowest stat and drops either 3 Penny, 1 Bomb, or 1 Key depending on what Isaac has the least of.

Contagion.title: Contagion
Contagion.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Toxic Shock]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• In each room, the first enemy killed will release a gas explosion and poison nearby enemies.

• Poisoned enemies will also release gas upon death, spreading the effect.

• • Poisoned enemies do not need to die while the poison is still active to spread the effect.

• The initial gas explosion deals 5 damage, and the poison deals Isaac's tear damage per tick, for 6 ticks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The effect will also activate if a Shopkeeper is destroyed before killing any enemies.

• Re-entering a room and destroying another Shopkeeper inside it will trigger the effect for a second time.

• The gas explosion and poison can damage friendly enemies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Gigante Bean: Greatly increases the size of the gas explosions, making the poison spread much more effective.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups can't create a gas explosion.

• Dr. Fetus/Epic Fetus: Explosion damage does not apply to poison damage.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop can't create a gas explosion.

• [Repentance] Freeze effects: Enemies that are frozen are still "alive" and can create a gas explosion when they are the first ice statue broken before any other enemy in the room dies.

• Ipecac: Ipecac only applies a 2x multiplier as opposed to +40 to poison damage.

• Poison tears: No effect. Gas explosions will only be triggered by poison caused by Contagion.

• Second Hand: Poison duration is not affected.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Contagion's sprite is a recolor of Toxic Shock.

fields.description: The first enemy killed in a room releases a gas cloud that poisons nearby enemies. Affected enemies will also release gas upon death, spreading the effect.

Continuum.title: Continuum
Continuum.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants spectral tears.

• When tears travel off-screen, they loop back around through the opposite wall.

• [Before Repentance] +2.25 range.

• [Repentance] +3 range.

• [Before Repentance] +1.5 tear falling speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Mega Maw. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] When fighting The Beast tears will not loop downward identical to a Crawl Space. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Azazel / Brimstone / Revelation / Tainted Azazel / Technology: The laser continues behind Isaac and back once again, potentially hitting enemies twice in one blast.

• Bob's Rotten Head: Bob's Rotten Head can travel through walls and appear out of the opposite wall.

• [Repentance] Does not travel through the wall; instead bounces off it like with Rubber Cement.

• The Forgotten: The skeleton form's charge attack can loop through walls.

• A Lump of Coal: Tears will continually gain damage when passing through walls.

• Mom's Knife: Causes Mom's Knife to appear on the opposite wall if thrown through one. It then returns through the wall to Isaac.

• Mom's Knife + Brimstone: The barrage of knives flies across the room until it hits the wall twice.

• My Reflection: When shooting through a wall, tears speed up towards Isaac rather than returning through the original wall. With enough shot speed and range the tears can loop twice.

• Tech X: Laser rings will go through walls, extra distance depending on shot speed.

• [Before Repentance] Tech X + Incubus: Incubus's laser rings cannot go through walls. This applies to Lilith too.

• [Repentance] Tech X + Incubus: Laser rings travel through walls and continue on the other side of the room.

• Tractor Beam: Causes the tears to loop right back in front of Isaac after they go offscreen.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Brimstone: Overrides Continuum, stat effects apply.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Compound Fracture: Tears will only split when hitting obstacles or enemies but not walls. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Tears will split on contact with walls. Only one split will occur on contact with walls and objects.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs cannot go through walls, but are spectral.

• Epic Fetus / Rubber Cement: Overrides Continuum, stat effects apply.

• The Ludovico Technique: When the tear is moved offscreen, it loops back through the opposite wall.

• [Before Repentance] The Parasite: Tears will only split when hitting obstacles or enemies but not walls. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Tears will split on contact with walls. Only one split will occur on contact with walls and objects.

• Proptosis: Tears shrink while traveling through walls and often disappear before they can reappear on the other side.

• Technology Zero: Tears will travel through walls; however, the electricity will not connect the tears while they are outside the room. Once tears have passed through walls, the electric arcs connect very erratically to other tears.

• Tiny Planet: Tears that travel through walls will travel until they reach Isaac and start orbiting him again.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The tears fired by Isaac look similar to the projectiles fired during Hush's fight.

fields.description: Grants spectral tears and increases range. Tears travel through walls and appear at the opposite side of the room.

Contract From Below.title: Contract From Below
Contract From Below.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Spawns N + 1 Room Clear Awards, but has a (0.666N / 2) chance to set the number of spawned pickups to 0, where N is the number of copies of this item held.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• In practice, the effect means the overall number of pickups is increased by 1/3 over the rest of the run, on average.

• Neither effect applies to trinkets.

• Doubled Chests will not necessarily be of the same kind.

• [Afterbirth onward] Neither effect applies to Penny dropped in Greed mode. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Diplopia: Each additional Contract increases the number of room drops by one and lowers the chance of getting nothing.

• Guppy's Tail: Higher chance of double chests upon clearing a room.

• Deep Pockets: If Contract removes the reward, spawns 1-3 random coins. Allows Deep Pockets to remain useful at high luck.

• Options?: Spawns a second set of consumables. The "Options?" consumable is not guaranteed to be the same for each copy of the original consumable.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A reference to the card of the same name from Magic: the Gathering, a collectible card game Edmund McMillen played since his childhood, this is more notable in the artwork of the card in Four Souls where the words written in the contract are word for word identical to the ones written in the original contract from below card.

• Isaac's name is written at the bottom of the contract, implying that he signed the contract.

fields.description: Doubles the number of most room clear awards, but reduces the overall chance of getting one by 1/3.

Converter.title: Converter
Converter.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Converts two Soul Hearts or Black Hearts into one filled Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Converts one Soul Heart or Black Heart into one filled Red Heart container.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using this item on Black Hearts will activate the Black Heart's damaging effect.

• [Before Repentance] Must use with two full Soul Hearts to work. One and a half will not work.

• [Repentance+] Converter's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring, looking like hearts. Wisps have slightly higher health than average. Red Heart pickups can be used to restore their health.

• Book of Revelations / Satanic Bible: Allows for generation of Heart Containers. (Schoolbag required)

• 9 Volt + Habit: Allows for an easy setup to get max health as long as one has a self-damage source, such as a Blood Donation Machine or a Devil Beggar.

• Guppy's Paw:

• [Before Repentance] Allows Isaac to have 10 Heart Containers and 1 Soul Heart.

• [Repentance] Allows Isaac to attain up to 12 Red Heart Containers or any combination of Red Heart Containers and Soul Hearts.

• • Potato Peeler + Sharp Plug: Allows Isaac to generate infinite damage upgrades and Cube of Meat.

• [Repentance] ??? + Birthright: Removes one Soul Heart and grants two, effectively becoming a 3-room charge Book of Revelations.

• Tainted Eden: Heart containers gained from Converter are kept, even after rerolling.

• [Repentance] Black Judas / Tainted Judas: Converts one Black Heart into one Black Heart, keeping Judas’ health the same as before but activates The Necronomicon effect regardless.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bethany: Bethany cannot activate the Converter whether she has soul charges or not.

• Car Battery: [Repentance] Consumes 2 Soul Hearts and produces 2 Red Heart Containers.

• The Soul: Consumes Soul Hearts and produces Bone Hearts for The Forgotten. Does nothing when used by The Forgotten.

• Tainted Bethany: When used while fully charged, adds 2 Blood Charges to her pool at no cost to her Heart total. When used with no charges, consumes 3 Blood Charges and produces 2, resulting in a net loss.

• With Car Battery: Consumes 3 Blood Charges and produces 4, still at no cost to Heart total, resulting in infinite Blood Charges.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Converter is a reference to a converter, a device or system that changes the form of something.

• According to Edmund via the Four Souls Isaac lore stream, the Converter's sprite was originally supposed to be similar to an adapter that converted US-standard power plugs for UK-standard power outlets, then he "just threw some wires on it."

• The Converter can be seen as an opposite to Guppy's Paw. Where the Converter takes two Soul or Black Hearts to form a Heart container (or just one Soul or Black Heart as of Repentance), Guppy's Paw takes one Heart container to form three Soul Hearts. Additionally, their flavor texts are similar.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Converts two Soul Hearts or Black Hearts into one filled Red Heart Container.
[Repentance] Converts one Soul Heart or Black Heart into one filled Red Heart Container.

Counterfeit Penny.title: Counterfeit Penny
Counterfeit Penny.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives a chance, upon picking up a coin, to increase the value of that coin by 1.

• [Before Repentance] 50% chance.

• [Repentance] The chance is based on the coin's worth:

| Coin | Chance 
| Penny | 50.00%

| Double Penny | 75.00%

| Nickel | 96.88%

| Dime | 99.90%

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This trinket can be found from destroying Golden Poop and Special Shopkeepers.

• [Afterbirth onward] Counterfeit Penny allows the chance for Keeper / Tainted Keeper to gain the full value of a coin while healing, or to heal 2 coin hp from a single penny. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] If picked up by Jacob and Esau, only the brother holding Counterfeit Penny can trigger the effect. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either gives the chance to increase the value of collected coins by 2. Having both by 3.

Coupon.title: Coupon
Coupon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, turns a random item in the current room that costs money or hearts into a pedestal item that can be taken for free.

• While held, guarantees a random item or pickup from the Shop to be half price.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Coupon has a 1% chance to drop from destroying normal Shopkeepers.

• Using Coupon in a Devil Room and taking that free item does not affect or remove the chances for Angel Rooms.

• Using Coupon in Greed mode does not restock the taken item or consumable.

• Using Coupon in a Shop while holding Restock will not respawn a new item after taking the free one.

• [Repentance] Using Coupon as The Lost or Tainted Lost allows multiple Devil deals to be taken. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns green wisps on the middle ring. The wisps fire three tears at a time, similarly to The Inner Eye. However, all of these wisps are destroyed if Isaac buys something using money. Does not affect wisps other than ones made by this item.

• Car Battery: Makes two items free upon use.

• Satanic Bible: The Devil deal in the boss room can be acquired for free.

• Steam Sale: The discounts stack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Coupon is based on this Steam Workshop item by Plumbus, originally known as Cereal Cutout.

fields.description: While held, guarantees one item in every Shop will be on sale for half price. On use, makes a random item in the current room free.

Crack Jacks.title: Crack Jacks
Crack Jacks.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one full Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

• Spawns one random trinket.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to Cracker Jack, a snack that is well-known for containing a prize in every bag.

• Despite the item description, swallowing the trinket through Marbles or a Gulp! pill has no known additional effect.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Don't swallow the prize!; Repentance: HP up. Don't swallow the prize!]

Crack the Sky.title: Crack the Sky
Crack the Sky.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, summons five beams of light in random locations on the ground. Each beam lasts for 0.8 seconds and deals large amounts of damage to enemies that touch them. They have a hitbox in a 3×3 cross shape.

• Each beam can hit the same enemy up to 8 times, and deals Isaac's tear damage plus a flat 20 damage per hit.

• [Rebirth only] The beams tend to gravitate towards the enemies, unlike the original game.

• [Afterbirth onward] The beams have a high chance to directly target enemies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring. The wisps summon a beam of light when touched, dealing 12 damage to nearby enemies in addition to their normal contact damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Conquest and Holy Eyes uses this ability to damage Isaac.

• Isaac also uses this ability to damage Isaac, only in a pattern and in a higher quantity of beams.

fields.description: Creates five beams of light around the room, dealing high damage to any enemies that touch them.

Cracked Crown.title: Cracked Crown
Cracked Crown.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] -20% tear delay (increased rate of fire)

• Since this directly affects tear delay instead of changing the tears stat, it allows Isaac's rate of fire to go over the normal maximum rate.

• Tear delay decreases are more noticeable and are a greater increase to DPS when the tears stat is high.

• Boosts speed, range, shot speed, damage, and [Repentance] tears if they are above their base values.

• Affects stat bonuses from passive items, trinkets that are absorbed or in a second trinket slot, and permanent bonuses given by items such as Void.

• [Before Repentance] The extra stat upgrades are 33% of any final stat calculations over its base value (which is equivalent to Isaac's base stats), for example with 4.5 damage, it is 1 damage over the base 3.5, and the 1 damage gets buffed to 1.33, ending up with a total of 4.83 damage.

• [Repentance] The extra stat upgrades are 20% of any final stat calculations over its base value (which is equivalent to Isaac's base stats), for example with 4.5 damage, it is 1 damage over the base 3.5, and the 1 damage gets buffed to 1.2, ending up with a total of 4.7 damage.

• • Fire rate multipliers change what is considered to be the base value, so with Soy Milk, only tears ups above 15.00 will gain a bonus.

• • 
• The only exception is Eye Drops, which gains a bonus to its 1.2x fire rate multiplier if it's above base.

• • Direct fire rate modifiers like Mom's Perfume do not get a bonus. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The trinket does nothing for the listed boostable stats if they are at or below the base value; the boost is calculated on the total bonus, not per item.

• Luck is not affected by Cracked Crown.

• Speed will not exceed 2.0.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Mom's Box: The tear delay reduction rises to 36%, and the stat boost is increased to about 77%.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Cracked Crown: Each copy gives +20% of stat boost.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance] This achievement was initially bugged on release of Repentance and would not unlock correctly. Fixed as of V1.7.6.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Decreases Isaac's tear delay by 20%, and improves the effectiveness of his other stat upgrades by 33%.
[Repentance] Improves the effectiveness of stat upgrades by 20%.

Cracked Dice.title: Cracked Dice
Cracked Dice.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon taking damage, randomly activates one of the following dice's effect:

• The D6

• D8

• D12

• D20

• D10

• [Repentance] The chance to activate is 50%, and each of the 5 dice have an equal probability to be picked.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This trinket can be used in conjunction with the IV Bag or a Blood Donation Machine to generate unlimited pickups and items.

• [Repentance] Cracked Dice has a chance to re-roll the spike in the middle of a Sacrifice Room, making it unusable.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases the chance to activate a dice to 75%. Having both to 100%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] Cracked Dice's sprite was changed for Booster Pack #5.

fields.description: [Before Repentance] Activates [Repentance] Has a chance to activate the effect of The D6, D8, D10, D12, or D20 (chosen randomly) whenever Isaac takes damage.

Cracked Key.title: Cracked Key
Cracked Key.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Cracked Key is a consumable item added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Acts as a single-use Red Key, allowing Isaac to create new rooms by using the key next to a wall where there would be no conditions that could prevent a (secret) room from appearing there. This is indicated by walls that have red door outlines on them.

• These rooms are most commonly normal rooms, but have a chance to be various special rooms instead, including Devil Rooms, Angel Rooms, Shops, Treasure Rooms, etc. The red rooms can be connected to the floor's Ultra Secret Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Despite it not being a card, the Cracked Key is considered a special card, so it has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• Cracked Key's main purpose is to allow unlocking Tainted characters in Home without having to rely on finding the Red Key.

• To create a Cracked Key (once unlocked), drop any trinket in a Boss Room or a Treasure Room on any floor before acquiring Dad's Note, including the floor Dad's Note is in. After starting the Ascent by collecting Dad's Note, the trinket left behind will have become a Cracked Key in the corresponding room.

• • While trinkets are fairly common, there is always a chance one doesn't appear naturally. This chance can be avoided by clearing three consecutive floors without taking damage, which is guaranteed to cause Perfection to spawn.

• • Mom's Box can be helpful for creating Cracked Keys, providing extra trinkets to leave in Boss rooms or Treasure rooms for later use.

• Cracked Keys can also spawn in the same condition as any Card.

• This item cannot be mimicked by Wild Card, Blank Card or Clear Rune, and Tarot Cloth has no effect on it.

• Using the Cracked Key in Home having unlocked that character's tainted version or as a tainted character will spawn the item Inner Child in the closet where the Tainted character would normally be found, as long as Inner Child is unlocked, otherwise there will be a shopkeeper.

• [Repentance+] In Online Co-Op, each player will unlock the Tainted version of the character they are playing as, regardless of whether they are alive or not, and if they are alive, they will also see the correct character, else seeing the host's character. However, if the host is playing as a Tainted character, the room will not contain any Tainted characters even if other players have not found their respective Tainted character, and the character will not be unlocked for anyone.

• If found before the Ascent, the Cracked Key can serve as a Secret Room finder, as secret room entrances do not have red door outlines.

• Cracked Key cannot appear in greed mode.

fields.description: Creates a room adjacent to a viable wall, like Red Key.

Cracked Orb.title: Cracked Orb
Cracked Orb.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon taking damage, activates the following effects:

• Unlocks all locked doors in the room (doors that need the room to be cleared are not affected).

• Opens the Secret Room and the Super Secret Room if adjacent to the room you are in.

• Reveals a random unmapped room on the floor.

• Destroys all tinted rocks and rocks with Crawl Spaces in the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The effect is able to reveal the Ultra Secret Room.

• The unlocking effect is able to open:

• The golden door to Mega Satan;

• Doors leading to Downpour / Mines / Mausoleum;

• • Since opening the door to Mausoleum requires taking damage, Cracked Orb will immediately open it, effectively halving the cost.

• The entrance to the Mom's Heart fight in the Mausoleum and Gehenna;

• A Strange Door.

• The effect will not open the doors to:

• Challenge Room or Boss Challenge Room from inside or outside

• Regular doors in Chest / Dark Room.

• Boss Rush / ??? doors even after the fight.

• Greed mode

• Taking damage while inside a Secret Room will open all its entrances, even if they lead to Challenge Rooms and are barricaded after Greed / Super Greed encounter.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Dog Tooth / Shiny Rock / YO LISTEN!: Makes it extremely easy to destroy tinted rocks and enter Crawl Spaces.

• Dull Razor: Allows the player to benefit from the item without taking actual damage.

• Book of Secrets / The Mind / Blue Map / Treasure Map / The Compass: Having more rooms already discovered makes Cracked Orb more likely to reveal the ultra secret room.

• XIV - Temperance: Allows the player to spawn a source of damage, making it easier to access rooms such as the entrance to Mom's Heart and Mega Satan's door when lacking bombs or being immune to explosive damage.

fields.description: Unlocks doors and reveals a random room on the map when Isaac takes damage.

Credit Card.title: Credit Card
Credit Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Using the Credit Card in a Shop instantly removes the cost of all items in that shop, allowing Isaac to take all of them for free.

• Using the Credit Card in a Devil Room or Black Market allows Isaac to take all the items without any health cost.

• Taking Devil Room items with the Credit Card does not prevent Angel Rooms from appearing.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, the Credit Card has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• Free items will remain free, even if Isaac leaves the current room.

• Works with the Blank Card, allowing Isaac to purchase all items from every Shop, if used correctly.

• [Afterbirth onward] Using the Credit Card in a Shop prevents Restock from working in this Shop only. However, Shop Restock Machines will work, creating new items. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Can be used in the starting room of Dark Room, allowing all four items to be taken for free.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Credit Card is given significantly more detail in its Four Souls card, showing it to be owned by Isaac's Mom.

• The Credit Card itself is from "Heavenly Rewards", with a symbol resembling an upside-down Godhead in the bottom right corner.

• The last four digits on the Credit Card are "0109", a reference to a bug involving the Greed Donation Machine that was later incorporated in an ARG that added Keeper to the game.

fields.description: Makes all pickups and items that cost money or health in the room free.

Creep.title: Creep
Creep.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[distinguish: Wall Creep] 

Creep is a liquid created by the attacks of certain monsters and bosses, or may be spawned by Isaac. Creep appears on the ground as a glowing or "shiny" puddle or line. There are a few different kinds of Creep which can affect enemies or Isaac. Having the ability to fly or the Callus trinket or Orphan Socks item nullifies the effects of Creep.

Creep that will affect Isaac is shown flickering rapidly. When all enemies inside a room are defeated, the creep they produced will quickly disappear.

sections.heading: Red Creep
sections.text: Red Creep is the most common type of Creep in the game. It can be created by various different enemies, champions, or Isaac himself. When spawned by enemies, it damages Isaac but not other enemies in the room. When spawned by Isaac, it damages walking enemies but not Isaac himself. It deals half a heart of damage to the player. Red Creep is representative of blood.

sections.heading: Green Creep
sections.text: Green Creep is spawned by various enemies, Ultra Pride, Pestilence, green champion monsters, Dangle, and Brownie (when they are poisoned). When spawned by enemies, it is functionally equivalent to Red Creep; however, some forms spawned by Isaac deal damage at a faster rate. It can be spawned by Isaac with Bob's Bladder, Toxic Shock, Mysterious Liquid, or 7 Seals' Pestilence familiar. ( [Afterbirth onward] Notably, the Bob transformation actually generates red creep that is just colored green. [end edition note] ) Green Creep is representative of acid, bile, or poison.

sections.heading: Yellow Creep
sections.text: Yellow Creep is spawned by Peep, Lemon Mishap, Lemon Party pills, and Free Lemonade. When spawned by Peep, it deals half a heart of damage to the player. When spawned by Isaac, it continuously damages walking enemies and seems to do more damage than any other type of creep that Isaac can create. Yellow Creep is representative of urine.

sections.heading: Black Creep
sections.text: Black Creep is spawned by various enemies, Gish, [Afterbirth+ onward] the Something's Wrong... pill, Ball of Tar, and 7 Seals' Famine familiar. It slows the movement speed of affected enemies or the player. When spawned by enemies, it affects Isaac but not other enemies. When spawned by Isaac, it affects enemies but not Isaac, bypassing the status resistances of Bosses. Black Creep is likely representative of tar or oil, [Afterbirth+ onward] though in the case of the Something's Wrong... pill, it may be fecal matter with blood in it.

sections.heading: White Creep
sections.text: White Creep is functionally similar to Black Creep. White Creep is spawned by several bosses, including Widow, The Wretched, Triachnid, and The Frail, as well as Small Baby Long Legs. Isaac can spawn white creep with Juicy Sack, Large Zit, Parasitoid, and Sticky Bombs. White Creep could be representative of a liquid form of Cobweb or pus.

sections.heading: Blue Creep
sections.text:
Blue Creep is spawned by Depression, Holy Water, and Aquarius. Blue creep damages enemies that walk over it. It is likely representative of water or tears.

[Repentance] Blue creep spawned by Holy Water petrifies enemies.

[Repentance] Blue creep spawned by Aquarius synergizes with tear effects.

sections.heading: [Afterbirth onward] Dark Blue Creep
sections.text:
Dark Blue Creep is spawned by Hush during his beam attack. Blue creep spawned by Hush makes Isaac slide, and does not affect other enemies.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Grey Creep
sections.text: Grey Creep is spawned only by The Cage. It damages Isaac like Red Creep but does not affect other enemies. It may be representative of some type of rotten fluid.

sections.heading: Orange Creep
sections.text: Orange Creep is spawned only by Mama Gurdy. It slows down Isaac like Black Creep, but does not affect other enemies. Unlike other types of Creep, Orange Creep does not flicker rapidly, even though it only affects Isaac. Due to its nature, it may be representative of vomit, pus, or some other bodily liquid.

sections.heading: [Afterbirth onward] Brown Creep
sections.text:
Brown Creep is spawned by Tainted ??? and IBS's mechanics, or by bosses such as Brownie, Dangle, Turdlings, Sisters Vis, and the [Afterbirth+ onward] X-Lax pill. Hostile Brown Creep and the Creep spawned by X-Lax will make Isaac slide, affecting his ability to stop moving or change directions while moving. This kind of Brown Creep does not flicker rapidly even though it only affects Isaac. Friendly Brown Creep spawned by Tainted ??? or IBS boosts damage and tears if Isaac is standing on it, and will synergize with other kinds of poop spawned by those mechanics. It is representative of liquid poop, likely to be diarrhea.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: [Repentance] Static Creep
sections.text:
Static Creep is spawned exclusively by Dogma's first phase. It appears underneath the boss as they move. It functions the same as Red Creep, harming Isaac for half a heart. Rather than being representative of a certain type of liquid, it represents visual static, most commonly seen on televisions with no signal.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• All Creep share a single sprite base, and simply apply their colors and visual effects to it in accordance to the Creep's type.

• [Repentance] Static Creep uses the same static effect as the Dogma item and Dogma, but applied to the entire sprite, and not just the areas indicated in blue. [end edition note]

Cricket's Body.title: Cricket's Body
Cricket's Body.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When Isaac's normal tears disappear (either from hitting the ground or hitting something else), they spawn 4 smaller tears.

• Each smaller tear deals half of Isaac's normal damage.

• Split tears are scaled down by 0.6x from the main ones, ignoring damage-based size reduction.

• [Before Repentance] Tear size multiplier: 1.2x.

• [Repentance] +0.1 tear size.

• [Before Repentance] [tear delay down: 1] 

• [Repentance] +0.5 fire rate.

• [Before Repentance] -10 range.

• [Repentance] 0.8x range multiplier.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Split tears will inherit the main tear's status effect, if any.

• If Isaac has less than [Before Repentance] 10 range/ [Repentance] 10 tear height, the split tears appear but cannot cause damage before hitting the floor.

• [Before Repentance] Cain, Lazarus, and Samson have lower starting range and are particularly susceptible.

• Tear falling speed ups can't mitigate this downside.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Angelic Prism: All tears split by the prism will burst into split tears.

• Bob's Rotten Head: Bob's Rotten Head splits into four smaller heads on detonation.

• Compound Fracture: When bone tears split into bone shards after hitting an obstacle or enemy, the bone shards will split into 4 smaller bone shards after hitting the ground.

• Explosivo: The explosion results in split Explosivo shots being generated. [Before Repentance] If the target survives, they're likely to immediately stick again. [Repentance] The split tears explode when they hit an enemy or the ground.

• Haemolacria: Main tears can split as they burst upon hitting the floor, an obstacle, or an enemy. The split tears can burst, but burst tears from main tears do not split.

• Cricket's Body's x0.8 range multiplier does not stack with Haemolacria's own x0.8 range multiplier.

• Ipecac: Main tear splits into four explosive splash tears. The split tears can still damage Isaac. Having Host Hat or Pyromaniac is strongly recommended.

• [Repentance] Cricket's Body's x0.8 range multiplier does not stack with Ipecac's own x0.8 range multiplier.

• Lachryphagy: Fed tears split into 12 tears.

• Lead Pencil/Monstro's Lung: All tears fired will splash after landing. Increased damage potential only noticed when firing into groups, due to the random pattern of each tear when it splashes.

• The Parasite: Eight split tears instead of four.

• Tiny Planet: The split tears orbit Isaac instead of spreading.

• Tough Love: Teeth tears will split into 4 smaller teeth.

• Tractor Beam: Main tears and split tears will travel along the beam.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Brimstone: Overrides Cricket's Body.

• [Repentance] Small red brimstone tears will fire out upon the beam hitting a wall or enemy.

• [Repentance] Brimstone + Soy Milk: Brimstone tears always fire out at the end of the beam.

• Dead Onion: Significantly decreases effective range, potentially preventing the split tears from causing damage.

• Diplopia: No effect.

• Dr. Fetus: Reduces range, bombs do not split.

• [edition anr] Reduces range, the bombs fired by Dr. Fetus will split into smaller bombs, much like Scatter Bombs.

• [Repentance] Increases range, the bombs fired by Dr. Fetus will split into smaller bombs, much like Scatter Bombs.

• Epic Fetus: Only tear stat change applies.

• Euthanasia: Needle tears will split into 4 small needle tears upon hitting the ground or an enemy. Split tears produced have a chance to deal triple damage but will not cause tear bursts.

• Fire Mind: Main tear splits into four explosive splash tears. Having Host Hat or Pyromaniac is strongly recommended.

• Flat Stone: Tears will usually only bounce twice, unless Isaac has high range, and spawn burst tears when they bounce.

• Hook Worm: Split tears gain a significant range increase, allowing them to potentially hit farther targets

• Kidney Stone: Drastically decreases range, potentially preventing the split tears from causing damage. The stone will not split.

• The Ludovico Technique: Overrides Cricket's Body except for stat effects which apply.

• Mom's Knife: Range of the knife is significantly decreased.

• Number One: Tears disappear very quickly after being fired, and split tears barely travel at all.

• [Repentance] Not recommended. Unlike other similar items, Cricket's Body's x0.8 range multiplier does stack with Number One's own x0.8 range multiplier, thus drastically reducing range.

• Piercing tears: Tears will only split after landing on the ground.

• Spectral tears: Tears will only split after landing on the ground.

• [Before Repentance] Technology/Tech X: Overrides Cricket's Body. Stat effects still apply.

• [Repentance] Cricket's Body tear splitting effect applies when lasers hit something.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Cricket's Body is named after Edmund's former cat, Cricket.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Splash damage; Repentance: Bursting shots] + tears up
fields.description: When tears hit an object or deplete their range, they spawn 4 smaller tears, whose range and damage scale with Isaac's. [Before Repentance] Grants -1 tear delay and reduces range. [Repentance] Grants +0.5 fire rate and reduces range.

Cricket's Head.title: Cricket's Head
Cricket's Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.5 Damage.

• ×1.5 Damage multiplier.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The ×1.5 damage multiplier does not stack with the ×1.5 damage multiplier from Magic Mushroom, from the combination of The Book of Belial and Blood of the Martyr, or itself (by using an item such as Diplopia, for example). However, it will stack with any other multipliers, such as Sacred Heart.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Cricket's Head, it turns into a larger red locust dealing [edition rnr+] triple / [Repentance+] double Isaac’s damage per tick.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Parasite]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original Binding of Isaac, this item was known as "Max's Head". Max was a non-existing animal named after the rabbit of Edmund McMillen's sister.

• [Before Repentance] The filename for the item icon in the game files still refers to it as "Max's Head".

• According to Edmund's first post-Repentance Lore Stream, the reason for the name change is due to the fact that it 'bugged him' to name an item after an animal that did not exist in a game that was written around his life.

• Cricket's Head is named after one of Ed's former cats who is now rehomed, Cricket.

• According to Edmund's first post-Repentance Lore Stream, the reason for re-homing Cricket was that Cricket became increasingly moody after the death of one of Edmund's other cats named Guppy, which involved getting into fights with Tammy.

• Although Cricket's Body and Cricket's Head are presumed to be from the same animal, Cricket's Body has darker fur color and spots than Cricket's Head.

fields.description: Increases Damage by 0.5, and increases damage multiplier by ×1.5.

Cricket Leg.title: Cricket Leg
Cricket Leg.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Has a 1/6 chance to spawn a random locust when killing an enemy.

• Up to 4 White Locusts can be spawned from a single enemy.

• The trinket is not affected by luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box/ Cricket Leg: The chance to spawn a locust increases to 1/3.

• Multiple copies of the trinket increase the chance by 1/6 per copy. At 6 copies, enemies are guaranteed to spawn locusts on death.

• Bomber Boy: Red locusts explode in a small horizontal cross-shape pattern.

• Brimstone Bombs: Red locusts will shoot out four brimstone beams in a + formation after hitting an enemy.

• Glitter Bombs: Red locust explosions have a chance to spawn pickups or trinkets.

• Hive Mind: Increases locusts' size and doubles their damage.

• Red locusts’ impact damage is doubled and the explosion damage is increased to 85.

• Sad Bombs: Red locusts fire a ring of ten tears outward upon detonation, which are affected by Isaac's tear modifiers, and deal damage equal to 15 + 0.6x, where x is Isaac's Damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups don’t spawn locusts.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop don't spawn locusts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Despite this trinket's name, as well as the locusts' in-game appearance, real life locusts are "the swarming phase of certain species of short-horned grasshoppers".

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again) will duplicate the locusts.

fields.description: Adds a 1/6 chance to spawn a random locust when killing an enemy.

Dip.title: Dip
Dip.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Dips move by making small dashes in random directions and are commonly found on most floors. They can also be spawned by some bosses, like Dingle and Mega Fatty, as well as enemies like Squirts and Dingas.

sections.heading: Corn
sections.text: Like Dips, Corns dash in random directions. Their dashes are faster and longer, but they have less health.

sections.heading: Brownie Corn
sections.text: A Brownie Corn is an alternate version of the Corn mainly spawned by the Turdlings, Dangle and Brownie, though they can also rarely be found in some rooms. Despite the different appearance, they behave exactly like normal Corns.

sections.heading: Big Corn
sections.text: A Big Corn is an alternate version of the Dip with twice as much HP that can also travel over flooded pits. When it dies, it launches the corn lodged in its head toward Isaac, predicting his movements and aiming for where he is moving.

sections.heading: Drip
sections.text: A Drip is an alternate version of the Dip that rolls around in diagonal directions and can travel over flooded pits. They are also spawned by Splurts upon death and by Clog during battle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Dirty Mind will convert all Dips to Dip Familiars. Dips, Corns and Brownie Corns are turned into their respective familiar counterparts while Drips are converted into regular Dip familiars and Big Corns into Corny Dip familiars.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] The Corn has the lowest health of any enemy in the game, tied with the Fly.

• Dips are likely a reference to Gels, enemies from The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, as they have nearly the same movement patterns.

• The name of the Dips is a pun on the term "dipshit", due to their names (Dips) and the fact that they are living fecal matter.

Gurdy Jr..title: Gurdy Jr.
Gurdy Jr..attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Gurdy Jr. is a boss that can appear in all environments of Chapter 2 (Caves, Catacombs, Flooded Caves).

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
• Spawns a Pooter.

• Jumps and shoots a radial of 8 tears in all directions on landing.

• Charges towards Isaac at high speeds, sliding while bouncing off obstacles and walls, She gradually loses speed before coming to a full stop.

• Any Pooters caught in her charge will be killed.

• The course of her charge can be affected by Tear knockback

• If Gurdy Jr. charges into an active bomb, she is slowed down tremendously.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: • When she has less than 50% health, she uses her charge attack continuously.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 7] : Instead of one Gurdy Jr., there will be two 42% smaller ones. This version has 45% less HP than the original (137.5) and only uses the charging attack. It drops a Soul Heart upon death.
[bc: 12] : 15% larger than the regular, with 25% more HP (312.5). She spawns Super Pooters instead of regular Pooters. Does not shoot projectiles of any sort.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Slowing Gurdy Jr. will, for the most part, render her charge attack useless.

• [Before Repentance] Piercing tears lack knockback and cannot be used to divert or stop Gurdy Jr.'s charge attack.

• If Gurdy Jr. is feared/stunned during her charge attack after the effect wears off, she will immediately charge at Isaac.

• Gurdy Jr's charge attack has no telegraphing, making it very dangerous to stay close due to the lack of a warning.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gurdy Jr. was added in the Wrath of The Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• Gurdy Jr. from Wrath of the Lamb is larger than Gurdy Jr. in Rebirth.

• In the original game, Gurdy Jr. could be encountered in the Cellar.

• • Also in the original game, in Chapter 2, Gurdy Jr. could only be encountered in The Catacombs, while in Rebirth, she can be encountered in all environments of Chapter 2 (in The Caves, The Catacombs, and The Flooded Caves).

• Gurdy Jr. appears to be the second stage of the "Gurdy" boss line, with the first stage as Gurglings, third as Gurdy, and final as Mama Gurdy.

• Gurdy Jr. is female.

• Edmund McMillen has referred to the double Gurdy Jr. champion room in an interview as "double Gurditration".

Gurgling (Enemy).title: Gurgling (Enemy)
Gurgling (Enemy).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the enemy; the boss; Gurglings] 

Gurglings are ordinary enemies that behave slightly differently from their boss counterparts. They have significantly less HP, leave a constant trail of Red Creep, and after dashing, shoot out six blood projectiles instead of spawning Attack Flies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gurglings appear to be the first stage of the "Gurdy" boss line, with the second stage as Gurdy Jr., third as Gurdy, and final as Mama Gurdy.

• If the Gurglings audio is slowed down or if one spawns as a large champion, the audio reveals that it is a little kid saying "Rawr!"

• In the game files, a Gurgling's feet are called hands.

Gurglings.title: Gurglings
Gurglings.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the enemy; Gurgling (Enemy)] 

Gurglings are a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] Only in the Basement.

• [Repentance] In the Basement and the Burning Basement. [end edition note] 
They each have [Rebirth only] 90 HP / [Afterbirth onward] 60 HP.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Gurglings spawn as a pair and wander around the room. Each individual Gurgling has one attack in total which is performed independently of the other:

• Rushes towards the player when aligned in any cardinal direction, leaving behind damaging Red Creep until they have run into a wall.

• After rushing into a wall, they pause for a brief moment, and then spawn 0-2 Attack Fly.

• Their dash can be interrupted if they run into an Attack Fly.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 18] : Gurglings spawn Troll Bombs at regular intervals instead of Red Creep when rushing towards the player. They take only 5 damage from their own bombs. They don't spawn any Attack Flies.

• While petrified, the Gurglings take full damage from their own bombs.
[bc: 12] : Three Gurglings will appear instead of two. They are faster but do not leave any Creep. They don't spawn any Attack Flies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gurglings appear to be the first stage of the "Gurdy" boss line, with the second stage as Gurdy Jr., the third as Gurdy, and the final as Mama Gurdy.

• With the Turdlings, the Gurdy boss series has a total of five bosses, the second most out of any boss in the game after the Harbingers and the most out of floor-specific bosses.

• The Gurglings and [Afterbirth onward] their poop-themed variant, the Turdlings [end edition note] , spawn in groups of three during the Boss Rush.

• If the Gurglings' audio is slowed down, the audio reveals that it is a little kid saying "Rawr!"

• Unlike the regular Gurgling, boss Gurglings have a one-second death animation.

• In the game files, the Gurglings' feet are called hands.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If the player stays close to walls, the Gurglings will not charge.
Bug note: If both Gurglings charge at once, only one of the Gurgling's grunting noise file will play.
Bug note: When fought in the Boss Challenge Room, they will appear in their enemy form rather than their boss form, making them much weaker and lacking a health bar.
Bug note: When the Gurglings are slowed and attempt to charge Isaac, they can't move and constantly spawn Attack Flies. Similarly, the "mini-boss" Gurglings attempting the same attack will constantly shoot 6 blood tears.

Guts.title: Guts
Guts.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Guts is a monster that attaches itself to a wall or obstacle, such as a rock, rolling around the contour of the terrain.
If the obstacle it is attached to is destroyed, then it will continue rolling in the direction it was previously traveling until it meets another wall or obstacle.

They make up for their limited movement by being very fast, and in numbers they can tighten movement space (especially in layouts containing narrow passages). Two of them are spawned by Mama Guts upon death.

sections.heading: Scarred Guts
sections.text: Scarred Guts are paler versions of the regular Guts. They have a 50% chance of replacing normal Guts in the Scarred Womb. They behave identically to regular Guts but leave behind a trail of damaging Red Creep and move slightly faster than their regular counterparts.

sections.heading: Slog
sections.text: Slogs are much darker than Guts and bear a yellow eye in their center that follows Isaac's position. Initially, they behave identically to Guts while moving slightly slower and leaving behind a trail of slowing Black Creep. However, when Isaac cardinally aligns with them, they charge at him until colliding with a wall or obstacle, where they will then resume their previous behavior. Slogs are exclusive to the Dank Depths.

sections.heading: Cyst
sections.text:
Cysts behave like normal Guts but they will occasionally shoot 1 blood shot towards Isaac if he is close enough.

Two of them will be spawned if a Dead Meat is killed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Guts and their variants are immune to Strange Attractor's effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Cyst first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• Cysts in real life are abnormal growths, usually non-cancerous, filled with fluid or other semi-solid substances. Some even develop in organs or contain pores.

Gyro.title: Gyro
Gyro.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Gyros were introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. They look like a piece of meat with a bone right through the middle.

They move themselves by rolling — similar to how a wheel moves. When Isaac is in their line of sight, they will charge at him quickly and can rotate to continue pursuing him for a short time. Afterward, the Gyro will briefly quit chasing Isaac and slowly roll around as if in exhaustion before resuming its normal behavior. Gyros will convert into Grilled Gyros, if in contact with fire.

sections.heading: Grilled Gyro
sections.text: Grilled Gyros function relatively the same to normal Gyros, but they move at a faster pace and leave some damaging flames in its trail, but only when chasing Isaac.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Both Gyro variants first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

• Edmund has expressed that this enemy doesn't fit in the game because it does not have a face like the other enemies.
