Habit.title: Habit
Habit.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • When Isaac is hit, his active item gains 1 room's worth of charge.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Rights/Razor Blade + Schoolbag: Damage from the item grants a point of charge to Isaac's other held active item.

• 9 Volt + Yum Heart: Isaac could potentially become invincible on early floors or with The Wafer, losing only half a heart per three hits taken.

• The Battery + [Repentance] Sharp Plug: Isaac gains one charge from Habit for every half-heart of damage that Sharp Plug deals, effectively granting double the charges when using Sharp Plug.

• Dull Razor + Schoolbag: Using the Dull Razor activates the Habit, but this does not restore its charge, only that of the item in the Schoolbag.

• Dull Razor + Car Battery + The Battery: Using Dull Razor activates the Habit, fully recharging Dull Razor, allowing for infinite uses of the Dull Razor, infinite invincibility frames, and infinite proccing of on-hit effects.

• Larynx: Both on-hit charge effects stack, granting Larynx 2 charges per hit.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Glass Cannon: Upon taking damage, Broken Glass Cannon will be half-charged. However, taking damage before the last charge will break the cannon again.

• Habit Duplicates: Doesn't stack; will still yield one charge per hit.

• Eraser: Taking damage with Eraser in your active item slot will not charge Eraser.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Habit was significantly nerfed from the previous game. In the original game, it would restore half of Isaac's item's required charge rather than just one room's worth of charge. This could essentially make Isaac unkillable if it was used in conjunction with Yum Heart, The Nail, or Book of Revelations and The Wafer for The Womb and beyond.

• This item is used in When Life Gives You Lemons.

fields.description: When Isaac is hit, his active item gains 1 room's worth of charge.

Haemolacria.title: Haemolacria
Haemolacria.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Turns Isaac's tears into large blood tears fired in an arc. Upon hitting the floor, an obstacle, or an enemy, they burst into smaller tears in all directions.

• The number of burst tears is random between 6-11 and they have an equal chance of occurring.

• The scattered tears deal random damage that is 50-83.33% of the main tear. On average, they deal 66% damage.

• [Before Repentance] Tear Delay × 2 + 10

• [Repentance] Tear Delay × 2 + 11

• The tear delay adjustment is applied after additive fire rate modifiers (e.g. Cancer) and multipliers less than 1 (e.g. Polyphemus), and before fire rate multipliers greater than 1 (e.g. Soy Milk).

• I.e. calculate tear delay from tears, then fire rate from tear delay, then apply additive modifiers and multipliers less than 1, then recalculate tear delay from fire rate, then multiply by 2 and add 11, then recalculate fire rate from tear delay, then apply fire rate multipliers greater than 1.

• [Before Repentance] 1.31~× damage multiplier.

• [Repentance] +1 damage and 1.5× damage multiplier.

• [Repentance] Range down: 0.8× range multiplier.

• The main tear has a roughly 1.71× size multiplier.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Higher shot speed lowers the arc of the main shot, whereas lower speed heightens it, resulting in a very minor change in effective range.

• The split tears are affected normally by shot speed.

• [Before Repentance] The tear falling speed stat is entirely ignored for both the main shot and the split tears.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Bob's Rotten Head: When the head lands, tears are fired.

• Brimstone: Haemolacria has priority. +20 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Brimstone tears down. The main tears burst into 4-7 brimstone beams instead of smaller tears. The beams deal 100% damage per tick.

• This does not apply to Azazel/Tainted Azazel's default brimstone beam, which is overridden but with no special effects.

• [Repentance] If the powered-up version is acquired through another Brimstone or through Sulfur, the 1.2× damage multiplier is overridden by Haemolacria's own 1.5× damage multiplier. The beams' width doubles.

• Brimstone + Chocolate Milk: The brimstone beams deal 100% damage regardless the charge. Chocolate Milk allows for rapid firing of Haemolacria tears, giving Isaac the ability to flood the room with Brimstone lasers.

• [Repentance] Brimstone + Technology: The lasers coil the beams, which is purely visual, and Technology does not grant 1.5× damage multiplier.

• Dangerous when combined with Ipecac.

• Berserk! / The Forgotten / Tainted Forgotten: Burst effect occurs on each enemy hit. It also increases the size of the club, similar to Polyphemus. The throw is unaffected and does not scatter blood tears.

• The Soul uses Haemolacria as normal.

• Chocolate Milk: Completely charged shots and their burst tears are larger and deal higher damage than normal. Chocolate Milk also allows low-damage Haemolacria shots to be fired rapidly.

• [Before Repentance] Increased tear delay.

• Compound Fracture / The Parasite: The main tears can split as they burst upon hitting an obstacle, or an enemy, but not upon hitting the floor. The split tears can burst, but burst tears from the main tears do not split.

• Cricket's Body: Main tears can split as they burst upon hitting the floor, an obstacle, or an enemy. The split tears can burst, but burst tears from the main tears do not split.

• [Repentance] Haemolacria's ×0.8 range multiplier does not stack with Cricket's Body's own ×0.8 range multiplier.

• Dead Eye: Both the main tear and the burst tears can increase the damage bonus, but missing the burst tears won't reset it.

• Dr. Fetus: Haemolacria has priority. +10 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Dr. Fetus tears down. The main tear is reminiscent of a bomb and scatters into 3-5 bombs that explode simultaneously. The split bombs deal half of Dr. Fetus' damage calculation based on the main tear's damage.

• [Repentance] Double Dr. Fetus: Isaac fires one additional Haemolacria tear, essentially a multi-shot effect, without stat change.

• Dr. Fetus + Sad Bombs: Sad bombs from Haemolacria tears shoot 10 Haemolacria tears, which then scatter into bombs without Sad Bombs' property.

• Ipecac: Tear delay is increased by 1/3 compared to either of the items on their own, but Isaac now fires Ipecac shots that release poisonous, high-damage but non-explosive split tears on impact.

• [Repentance] Haemolacria's ×0.8 range multiplier does not stack with Ipecac's own ×0.8 range multiplier. Can be dangerous when combined with Brimstone.

• Lachryphagy: Main tears can feed on other main tears or burst tears while burst tears cannot feed. The main tears will burst into 8 tears that have Haemolacria's burst effect upon impact or being fed enough. If they impact too soon after being fired or hit an enemy, they will burst into Haemolacria's burst tears. Lachryphagy's burst tears do not benefit from Haemolacria's synergies with other items, such as Brimstone or Tech X.

• Lead Pencil: Fires 12 Haemolacria tears, all of which will burst.

• Mom's Knife: Haemolacria tears fire while Mom's Knife is charging.

• [Repentance] Overridden by Mom's Knife. Stat changes still apply; however, the tears down is instead a +10 Tear Delay.

• Monstro's Lung: Monstro's Lung has priority. Fire rate is reduced. Fires 8 Haemolacria tears, all of which will burst.

• My Reflection: Range becomes extremely high, making Haemolacria tears follow Isaac for a long time before hitting the ground. Burst tears do not have a boomerang effect.

• Proptosis: Effects combine to create large tears that bounce off each other and burst into smaller, standard tears that are not affected by Proptosis.

• Technology: Haemolacria has priority. Fires arcing tears that release Technology lasers upon bursting. The lasers deal 100% of Isaac's Damage.

• [Repentance] Double Technology: Isaac fires one additional Haemolacria tear, essentially a multi-shot effect.

• Tech X: Haemolacria has priority. The tears burst into 3-5 Tech X rings on impact. The sizes of the rings are various, but they deal 100% of Isaac's Damage.

• [Repentance] Double Tech X: Isaac fires one additional Haemolacria tear, essentially a multi-shot effect.

• Trisagion: Both Trisagion and Haemolacria fire at the same time, Haemolacria does not keep spectral tears despite its tears sprite change but the arced tear keeps piercing.

• [Repentance] Haemolacria becomes one big Trisagion beam that splits into more beams when it reaches its max range.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Azazel: Haemolacria overrides Azazel's Brimstone.

• The Book of Belial + Blood of the Martyr/Cricket's Head/Magic Mushroom: Haemolacria's 1.5× damage multiplier stacks with these items' own 1.5× damage multipliers as expected.

• C Section: C Section has priority. +4 Tear Delay, instead of Haemolacria tears down. Fetuses explode into a burst of tears when they hit the ground.

• Epic Fetus: Epic Fetus has priority. +10 Tear Delay, instead of Haemolacria tears down.

• Flat Stone: At the base range, the main tear bounces once, releasing burst tears [Before Repentance] which do not bounce, and then burst normally. At a high range, the main tear can bounce multiple times.

• [Repentance] Burst tears also bounce.

• Godhead: The main tear retains all effects, but burst tears do not.

• [Repentance] The main tear has the damaging aura as well as the burst tears.

• Haemolacria: Additional copy of this item, such as from Diplopia / Crooked Penny, grants +1 damage instead of normal stat changes.

• Holy Light: The main tear can be a holy tear and bursts normally in addition to the light beam. Burst tears have an independent chance of being holy tears.

• [Repentance] The burst tears inherit the effect from the main tear. They do not have an independent chance.

• Kidney Stone: Overridden by Haemolacria. Only stat changes apply.

• [Repentance] Works as expected. The kidney stone also bursts when it reaches its max range.

• The Ludovico Technique: Overridden by Haemolacria, provides piercing.

• Mysterious Liquid: Only the main tear will leave creep.

• [Repentance] Both main and burst tears spawn creep.

• Number One: Not recommended. Unlike other similar items, Haemolacria's ×0.8 range multiplier does stack with Number One's own ×0.8 range multiplier, thus drastically reducing range.

• Piercing tears / Spectral tears: The main tear gains these effects, but the burst tears don't inherit them.

• [Repentance] Burst tears inherit these effects.

• Polyphemus: Stat changes applied as normal. The main tear gains the semi-piercing ability and may not burst when hitting a weaker enemy. Burst tears do not semi-pierce.

• [Repentance] Burst tears do semi-pierce.

• Pop!: Tears no longer arc, but will still burst when hitting an obstacle or stopping and falling to the ground. Burst tears do not bounce off of each other.

• Sharp Key: Split tears from thrown keys are normal tears.

• Sinus Infection: If the main tear is a booger, it will get stuck and not burst on hitting an enemy. Split tears have an independent chance of being booger tears.

• [Repentance] The burst tears inherit the effect from the main tear. They do not have an independent chance.

• Spirit Sword: Spirit Sword has priority. +10 Tear Delay, instead of Haemolacria tears down. The projectiles from the sword arc and burst.

• Technology Zero: Only main tears can be connected.

• [Repentance] Main tears and bursts can be connected via electricity.

• Tractor Beam: The main tear follows the beam, but the burst spreads normally.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Haemolacria is based on this Steam Workshop item by HiHowAreYou, originally known as Water Balloon.

• Haemolacria is a rare condition that causes people to produce tears that are composed of blood.

• When Tainted ??? uses Haemolacria, the tears will be black instead of red. This is purely cosmetic, and is probably a reference to how stools containing dried blood are often black.

• [Repentance] Haemolacria is one of the few items that still modify tear delay instead of fire rate.

• When playing as Tainted Isaac, if your inventory is full, you can drop Blood Clot and pick it up again. Doing this would increment the amount of Blood Clot pick ups by 1 regardless of how many times you do this. By using this exploit, you could easily unlock Haemolacria without much difficulty.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: When using The Forgotten's melee attack with both Jacob's Ladder and Haemolacria, the sparks caused by splattered tears will hurt the player. (Video clip)
Bug note: Using Mom's Knife and Marked with Haemolacria will cause it to only fire towards the center of the room; using the fire buttons will barely move the Marked icon, while Mom's Knife will be unusable and locked to the right.

fields.description: Turns Isaac's tears into large blood tears fired in an arc. Upon hitting the floor, an obstacle, or an enemy, they burst into many smaller tears in all directions. Increases tear delay.

Hagalaz.title: Hagalaz
Hagalaz.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Destroys all breakable obstacles in the room.

• Does not affect Key Blocks.

• [Afterbirth onward] Does not destroy Movable TNTs (though it does destroy TNTs). [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] Kills all of the following stone-themed enemies:
[end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] Has special interactions with the following stone-themed enemies:

• Host - Destroys and leaves behind a Red Host

• Hard Host - Destroys and leaves behind a Red Host

• Mobile Host - Destroys and leaves behind a Flesh Mobile Host

• Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Brain

• Loose Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Pon

• Black Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Pon

• Floating Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Brain

• Bone Knight - Destroys and leaves behind a Brain

• Rock Spider - Destroys and leaves behind a Spider

• Tinted Rock Spider - Destroys and leaves behind a Soul Heart

• Coal Spider - Destroys and leaves behind a hot coal

• Death's Head - Destroys and leaves behind a Flesh Death's Head

• Brimstone Death's Head - Destroys and leaves behind a Flesh Death's Head

• Hardy - Destroys and leaves behind a Dip

• Tuff Twins - Removes their armor plating

• The Shell - Removes their armor plating, minus the head
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Hagalaz cannot create bridges.

• [Repentance+] Hosts revealed from skulls will start out with their armor destroyed, as Red Hosts.

• [Repentance+] Enemies with no interactions that are notable exceptions: 

• Danny

• Coal Boy

• Selfless Knight

• Mask + Heart

• Mask II + 1/2 Heart

• Quakey

• Cursed Death's Head

• Dusty Death's Head

• Redskull

• Ultra Death Head

• Wall Hugger

• Carrion Queen

• Great Gideon

• Mask of Infamy

• The Visage
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • Hagalaz is best used in a room with special rock obstacles, including mushrooms, urns, skulls, or polyps, as they often drop useful pickups and items. All of these are potentially hazardous when destroyed (mushrooms can explode, polyps can fire bullets in all directions ( [Repentance] or in Corpse, scatter Maggots) [end edition note] , urns can scatter Spiders, and skulls can leave behind a Host/Red Host, all with roughly a 20% chance), so give them a wide berth before doing so to avoid damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Hagalaz will open Secret Room doors in L-shaped rooms.
Bug note: Hagalaz has no effect on Wall Huggers despite destroying the other 3 variants of this enemy, which is almost certainly unintended as there's no apparent reason for this.

fields.name: Hagalaz
fields.description: Destroys all breakable obstacles in the room. Does not affect Key Blocks. [Repentance+] Also destroys or removes the armor of most stone-themed and/or invulnerable enemies, such as Hosts, Stone Grimaces, and Knights, among many others.

Hairpin.title: Hairpin
Hairpin.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Fully recharges Isaac's active item upon entering an unexplored Boss Room.

• This effect only occurs the first time a Boss Room is entered; leaving and re-entering the Boss Room will not result in more recharges.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If there are multiple Boss rooms on the same floor ( [cu: XL] , The Void), the trinket's effect will trigger once for each and every Boss Room.

• The trinket's effect also triggers during the stronger Mom's Heart fight at the end of Mausoleum/Gehenna. This allows Isaac to effectively skip both fights if he is holding the The Bible.

• In Greed Mode, grants a full charge only for the two boss fights on the final level.

• [Repentance] Cannot appear in Greed Mode, though will function the same if accessed through the Debug Console.

• [Repentance] Recharges twice on Corpse II: 1st time happens when entering the boss room, 2nd time happens when entering the Mother fight. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Does not fully recharge between Dogma and The Beast. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Active item will be overcharged.

• Jacob's Ladder: Increases arcing distance of sparks.

• IV - The Emperor?: The currently held active item is fully charged the first time the extra boss room is teleported to. The normal boss room also charges the active item.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• The Battery: If the item doesn't have a full first charge level, it will be filled. If the first level is full, the second charge level will be filled.

• [Repentance] The item will gain both its charges.

• Mega Blast: Mega Blast gains only 3 charge units, unlike all other 12 room recharge items, which are fully charged.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Hairpin is based on this Steam Workshop trinket by zarat.us.

• Hairpin's original description was "Poke that power outlet! Bosses charge you".

fields.description: Fully recharges Isaac's active item upon entering a boss fight.

Hallowed Ground.title: Hallowed Ground
Hallowed Ground.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Spawns a white poop familiar which turns into a White Poop when Isaac is hurt.

• White Poop has an aura that multiplies both fire rate and tear delay by x2.5 and has a 50% chance to ignore damage similarly to Cone Head, except the chance is higher.

• [Repentance] White Poop has similar durability to Golden Poop. The aura additionally increases damage by 20% and gives Isaac's tears a homing effect.

• Hallowed Ground will not activate if the player negates the source of damage through items such as Holy Mantle.

• The familiar will respawn after Isaac leaves the room.

• [Repentance] This item belongs to the Oh Crap set. Collecting three items from this set will transform Isaac into a walking pile of poop.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Aligning a white poop to drop next to a Devil Beggar, a Blood Donation Machine or a Confessional is a great way to save on health, as the aura will allow for frequent free plays.

• Damage from Sacrifice Room spikes can be blocked by Hallowed Ground, but no payout is rewarded.

• White Poop is impervious to enemy shots and charging attacks.

• White Poop is not immune to explosive damage or stomping attacks.

• Chubber attacks cannot destroy White Poop, but can still harm Isaac.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Hallowed Ground having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

• [Repentance] This item does not produce White Poop in The Beast's boss arena.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Card Against Humanity / Re-Lax pill: The poops created have a 33% chance to become white.

• Blood Rights/IV Bag/Kamikaze!/Razor Blade: The aura has a chance to block the damage inflicted, but the effects will still occur.

• Dirty Mind: Destroying the White Poop will spawn friendly white Dips which give off a small version of the aura.

• Everything Jar: Using the first charge will always spawn a white poop.

• Barring Everything Jar is only used at its first charge, when used along with items that grant active item charges, white poop can be spawned more than once in the same room, making this item much more powerful. If used with Habit, allows white poop to be spawned indefinitely rather than only on the first hit.

• The Poop: Using The Poop will always spawn a white poop.

• When used along with items that grant active item charges, white poop can be spawned more than once in the same room, making this item much more powerful. If used with Habit, allows white poop to be spawned indefinitely rather than only on the first hit.

• Rock Bottom: Isaac will keep the stat upgrades even after leaving the aura. However, it won't keep the homing effect outside of the aura.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Increases familiar's size but otherwise has no effect.

• Box of Friends: All poop familiars turn into white poop at the same time, and their affects are accumulative. A new poop familiar appears even if the previous poops have been used up.

• D12: Does not increase the chance for rerolled obstacles to become White Poop.

• Holy Mantle / The Lost: Breaking the holy mantle shield does not count as damage taken, so the white poop will not drop.

• Immaculate Heart: The damage multiplier does not stack with that from a white poop.

• Star of Bethlehem: The star's aura does not stack with the poop's aura.

• Mom's Eye / Loki's Horns: Not recommended. Backwards/cross shots from these items make it very easy to destroy the white poop by accident.

• Meconium: Although Meconium cannot replace the poop Hallowed Ground spawns with, Black Poop has a chance to replace White Poops that would have been created by other items which have synergies with Hallowed Ground.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is likely a pun on the phrase "holy shit" or "holy crap".

• "Hallowed Ground" was also the name of the Downpour OST back in Antibirth.

• Hallowed ground is another way of calling The Holy Land.

• As such, people thought the soil from Jerusalem and Bethlehem to be holy and brought them to sanctify the land by sprinkling it, like the famous cemetery Sedlec Ossuary, which explains why it's unlocked byThe Forgotten.

fields.description: Spawns a white poop familiar, which turns into a White Poop when Isaac is hurt. White poop has an aura that increases tear fire rate and can block enemy shots. [Repentance] The aura also increases damage by 20% and gives homing.

Halo of Flies.title: Halo of Flies
Halo of Flies.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns two Pretty Flies that block enemy shots.

• Pretty flies kill some fly enemies upon contact.

• The orbital limit of three flies cannot be surpassed with this item, reducing its effectiveness if Isaac has two or more orbitals.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Duke of Flies. [end edition note] 

• Orbital flies can also be obtained by other means, such as Slot Machines and Pretty Fly pills.

• The following types of flies are instantly killed when they come in contact with the orbitals:

• Army Fly

• Attack Fly

• Dart Fly

• Fly

• Hush Fly

• Moter

• Pooter

• Ring Fly

• Super Pooter

• Swarm

• Having multiple copies of Halo of Flies, (such as by Diplopia) does not increase the fly cap of 3, unlike The Swarm.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Halo of Flies two gray locusts are created dealing half of Isaac’s damage per tick each.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • D4: This item can't be rerolled by the D4 or other items that reroll passive items.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Solar System.

• This item is a reference to Halo of Flies, by Alice Cooper.

• Halo of Flies was the first orbital item that Edmund McMillen ever implemented into The Binding of Isaac.

• Halo of Flies shares its name with a level from Edmund's previous game Super Meat Boy.

fields.description: Spawns two Pretty Flies that block enemy shots and deal contact damage to flies.

Hanger.title: Hanger
Hanger.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Hangers are dead Shopkeepers that are hostile. They can shoot 3 projectiles at the player that will steal coins on hit (similar to Greed and Keepers). The Hanger is very slow and can float over obstacles. The best strategy is to be constantly moving. They always have an Eternal Fly circling them, which will become an Attack Fly once the Hanger is dead.

Harbingers (Bosses).title: Harbingers (Bosses)
Harbingers (Bosses).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Harbingers are a group of hobbyhorse riding bosses that are unlocked by defeating Mom for the first time.

sections.heading: [Repentance] The Ultra Harbingers
sections.text:
The Ultra Harbingers are a team of stronger forms of The Harbingers. The team comprises of the main four harbingers without the alternatives of Conquest, or Headless Horseman. They are fought one at a time prior to fighting The Beast.

| | | | 
| Ultra Famine | Ultra Pestilence | Ultra War | Ultra Death

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Each of the Harbingers, excluding Conquest, have a unique transition to phase 2/final phase of their fight which is shared by their Ultra versions (Except for Death & Ultra Death). Everything except Famine's head is lost, Pestilence only loses their head, War loses their horse and Death dismounts their horse to fight alongside them.

• Ultra Death does not dismount, instead upon defeat they lose their scythe and begin descending with the horse while exploding like the other Ultra Harbingers.

Harlequin Baby.title: Harlequin Baby
Harlequin Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar who follows Isaac around and fires two tears at once in a V-shape pattern [edition alternatives: baseline: once per second; Repentance: 1.36 times a second] that each do 4 damage.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Mr. Fred. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Harlequin Baby having [edition alternatives: baseline: 5th; Repentance+: 7th] priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Mongo Baby: Will copy Harlequin Baby’s spread double shot effect.

• Tainted Forgotten: The momentum from the skeleton being tossed makes Harlequin Baby's tears launch at an abnormally high shot speed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item refers to a condition called Harlequin Ichthyosis, which is a rare skin condition from birth, which on babies gives puffy red eyes, green or red crackled/scaly skin, and stretched out lips.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and fires two tears at once in a V-pattern.

Head of Krampus.title: Head of Krampus
Head of Krampus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, fires a powerful Brimstone beam in the four cardinal directions, similar to that of the attack used by The Fallen and Krampus.

• [Afterbirth only] Has a 50% chance to rotate all beams around Isaac 90 degrees, similar to Krampus' second Brimstone attack.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Head of Krampus is one of two items that can drop by defeating Krampus. The other one is A Lump of Coal.

• This is the only way to get this item normally.

• [Before Repentance] Each beam deals 22 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 440 damage per use.

• [Repentance] Each beam deals 10 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 200 damage per use.

• Damaging enemies with the effect of this item as Guppy will spawn multiple Blue Flies.

• By standing really close to large enemies such as bosses, it's possible to hit them with multiple beams at once, dealing significantly more damage than a single beam.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns red wisps in the middle ring. The wisps fire small Brimstone lasers in the cardinal directions when destroyed. The lasers deal the wisps' tear damage per tick, and can hit up to 20 times. BFFS! will not increase this damage, despite it scaling with the wisps' tear damage.

• Car Battery: Doubles the damage the brimstone beams deal, but not their durations.

• [Before Repentance] Each beam now deals 44 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 880 damage per use.

• [Repentance] Each beam now deals 20 damage per tick, ticking a total of 20 times, dealing a total of 400 damage per use.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item was originally planned to appear as a Halloween Update in the original The Binding of Isaac, but was scrapped.

• A scrapped item in the original game called Pumpkin Mask was very similar in effect to Head of Krampus.

fields.description: Fires a powerful Brimstone beam in four cardinal directions. [Afterbirth only] Has a 50% chance to rotate all beams around Isaac 90 degrees.

Hard mode.title: Hard mode
Hard mode.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Hard mode changes the gameplay compared to Normal in some ways to make it more difficult.
When playing in Hard mode, a small red pentagram ( [mode: hard] ) appears on the HUD, below the pickups.

sections.heading: Differences
sections.text:
• 2-3 more rooms generate each floor.

• [Before Repentance] Standard rooms with a difficulty of "1" cannot generate.

• [Repentance] Standard rooms with a difficulty of "1" have a reduced chance of appearing.

• Most rooms with this difficulty are very easy, making difficult rooms more common.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Rooms with a difficulty of "15" are able to generate on the second floor of chapters 1-4.

• [Repentance] Additionally, they can always spawn on single floor chapters.

• [Before Repentance] Enemies have a base 20% chance to become Champions instead of only 5%.

• Champion enemies only award pickups 33% of the time instead of 100%.

• [Before Repentance] 66% of Heart drops from completing rooms are removed and replaced with nothing.

• [Repentance] 34% of Heart drops from completing rooms are removed and replaced with nothing.

• [Before Repentance] Only champion bosses will drop hearts; normal bosses will not.

• Floors are more likely to have curses.

• Slot Machines are half as likely to pay out.

• Fortune Telling Machines have an 85% chance to give a fortune, instead of 65%.

• Confessionals only have a 25% chance to pay out, instead of 30%.

• Blood Donation Machines only give out one coin per use.

• [Repentance] Also applies to IV Bag.

• Beggars require a minimum of 6 donations before paying out.

• [Repentance] This doesn't apply to Bomb Bums or Key Masters. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The Shop has a 50% chance of becoming a lower level, regardless of having store upgrades unlocked.

• [Repentance] The drop rate of Soul Hearts from Blue Fire Places and Purple Fire Places is decreased to 10%, instead of 25%.

• [Repentance] The drop rate of Double Hearts is decreased to 2%, instead of 5%.

• [Repentance] The chance of a Micro Battery spawning in place of other types of Batteries is increased to 83.33%, instead of 66.67%.

• [Repentance] Tinted rocks have a 50% lower chance of appearing.

• [Repentance] Certain enemies and bosses have increased shot and movement speed.

• The Harbingers have increased charge attack speeds where applicable.

• Dogma does not provide the effect of The Wafer.

• Most Hard mode unlocks are co-op babies, with the notable exceptions of Godhead, Smelter, Marrow, Mega Mush, Death Certificate and the character Bethany.

• Godhead's unlock requirements were extended in later DLCs due to the addition of more completion marks, but it can still be unlocked in the base game using the same method.

• [Repentance] The Repentance chances for max level shops and tinted rocks were initially much more sparse. These chances were increased in update v1.06.J791 a few days later.

• [Repentance] None of the tainted characters have unlocks tied to getting all completion marks, apart from Death Certificate. [end edition note]

Pacer.title: Pacer
Pacer.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Pacers wander around the room aimlessly and can be spawned when a Gaper, a Flaming Gaper or a Frowning Gaper is killed.

sections.heading: Gusher
sections.text: Gushers wander around a room aimlessly, similar to Pacers, but will occasionally shoot a short ranged slow-moving, blood shot in whichever direction they happen to be moving in. They can be spawned from all the same sources as the Pacer with the addition of Lepers which will always spawn a grey-colored Gusher upon death.

sections.heading: Notes

They can be spawned when a Gurgle is killed.

Squirt.title: Squirt
Squirt.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Squirt is a medium-sized poop enemy that does contact damage to Isaac by periodically dashing to him. Two Squirts spawn from Dingas when killed. It splits into two Dips when killed.

sections.heading: Dank Squirt
sections.text: Dank Squirts dash towards Isaac, leaving a trail of slowing Black Creep. Upon death, they spawn two Clots.

sections.heading: Splurt
sections.text: Splurts are a variant of Squirts that dash twice towards Isaac rather than just once and can travel over flooded pits. Upon death, they spawn two Drips.

sections.heading: Hardy
sections.text:
Hardies are a rocky variant of Squirts. Upon death, it spawns a Dip.

They charge at Isaac, and if they run into an obstacle/wall, a piece of them breaks off and rock projectiles are fired outwards. A Hardy will destroy most breakable obstacles on collision and is also able to reveal secret rooms if it hits the entrance of one. After running into rocks/walls three times, a Hardy will die.

• First collision: 8 rock projectiles are fired out in a radius.

• Second collision: 8 rock projectiles are fired out in a radius and a cluster of rock projectiles is launched in Isaac's direction.

• Third collision: A cluster of small and large rock projectiles is launched in Isaac's direction. The small rock projectiles have shorter range and will spawn 2-3 Rock Spiders and the large rock projectiles each shoot out a small cross of 4 smaller rock projectiles upon landing.

In the uncommon event that it charges but doesn't hit a wall or obstacle, it will slow down like a normal Squirt without sustaining damage.

[Repentance+] Destroyed by Hagalaz on use, leaving behind a Dip. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Hardy first appeared in the Antibirth mod where its third impact with an obstacle would cause the same effects as its first and second impact but also create rocks to fall from the ceiling.

• Squirts are likely a reference to Zols, big Gels that split into two Gels upon death.

The Haunt.title: The Haunt
The Haunt.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the item; Lil Haunt; the enemy; Lil' Haunt] 

The Haunt is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In the Cellar and the Burning Basement.

• [Repentance] Only in the Cellar.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Phase 1:
The battle begins with three Lil' Haunts circling The Haunt, who floats around the room and is invulnerable. The Haunt and its Lil' Haunts can still do contact damage to Isaac while incorporeal.

• One Lil' Haunt becomes corporeal and chases Isaac. Once the first one is dead, the other two take up the chase.

• Once all three Lil' Haunts are dead, Phase 2 begins.

Phase 2:
The Haunt, now vulnerable, quickly flies to the upper wall of the room and begins to move left and right along the wall while periodically performing the following attacks:

• Fires a straight Brimstone laser downwards.

• Fires five blood shots in a spread downwards.

• If Isaac is close to the upper wall, The Haunt will quickly dash toward his position.
During The Haunt's transition to this phase, it can deal contact damage during the dash to the upper wall.

The Haunt attacks based on its location and distance. If it cannot make it to a certain position, it gets stuck attempting to reach it and will not attack until it can resume moving.

During both phases, The Haunt deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 18] : Only two Lil' Haunts circle The Haunt in the first phase. In the second phase, The Haunt spawns 1-2 Spiders instead of firing a Brimstone laser.
[bc: 20] : Only one Lil' Haunt circles The Haunt in the first phase. In the second phase, The Haunt has 50% less HP (100). The Haunt's laser is replaced with two diagonal Brimstone lasers that reflect once off of walls. The Haunt's blood-shot attack is changed to 8 shots and is aimed towards Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Although The Haunt can fly over rocks and most other obstacles, its movement in the second phase can be completely stopped by dropping a bomb in its path.

• [edition anr] In Afterbirth and Afterbirth †, the Haunt is no longer stopped by bombs and can move over them.

• Lil' Haunts are immune to the effects of E. Coli, Flush!, D10 and [Repentance] Ace cards.

• Inflicting fear or confusion on The Haunt during Phase 2 can be dangerous, as it will sometimes start sliding back and forth rapidly.

• The Haunt can be damaged in phase 1 using Dark Arts and The Boomerang.

• The Haunt can be instantly killed with Vade Retro if it is at 50% health or below.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It is the boss version of the Lil' Haunts.

• The Forsaken is the posthumous version of it.

• The Haunt's design may be a reference to Paunchy Chops, a boss from the game Gish, also developed by Edmund McMillen. They function similarly in that they are both ghosts that can phase in and out of corporeality, and they bear similar facial expressions.

• [Repentance] The Haunt has a resurrected variation known as The Heretic.

• Black Champion Haunt in its second phase resembles Tainted Lost.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: When you kill the Lil' Haunts spawned by The Black Champion Haunt, there is a chance that the music will end as if you defeated the boss.
Bug note: If phase 2 starts at the same time as Isaac inflicts a status effect on The Haunt, after the effect is gone, The Haunt will be permanently tinted with that status effect's color until it dies.

Keeper's Bargain.title: Keeper's Bargain
Keeper's Bargain.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a 50% chance for Devil Deals, Black Markets, and A Pound of Flesh Shop items to cost money instead of health.

• Items that would normally cost 1 heart container will cost 15 coins, while items that would normally cost 2 heart containers will cost 30 coins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The effects of this trinket are inherent to Keeper and Tainted Keeper, rendering the trinket useless for them.

• Items affected by Keeper's Bargain may occasionally be discounted (30 coin item down to 15 coins, or 15 coins to 7), just like items are in a regular shop.

• Dropping this trinket while in the room disables its effect.

• Purchasing a Devil Deal with this trinket's effect will still prevent Angel Rooms from appearing.

• If an item that costs health is rerolled (via The D6 or similar methods), the new item can cost coins instead. The reverse is also true.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: The chance for deals to cost money is 100%. Having both makes the deals have an increased chance to be on sale.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Judas' Tongue: Does not provide any discount.

• The Lost/Tainted Lost/Soul of the Lost: Purchasing items affected by this trinket will not cause the other items in the room to disappear.

fields.description: Adds a chance for Devil Deals to cost money instead of health.

Keeper's Box.title: Keeper's Box
Keeper's Box.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, spawns a random pickup or item, which must be bought for its normal Shop price.

• Items generated will always be shop items and pickups will only be those that can appear for sale in shops.

• • The only exception to this is Black Sacks, which can replace Grab Bags despite not being able to do so in shops.

• There is an an equal ~11.1% chance to spawn a card, pill, bomb, key, battery, item, soul heart, red heart, or sack.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The pickup/item will be surrounded by spikes/cost hearts if the box is used in a Devil Room, a Black Market, if Isaac has A Pound of Flesh or is in a boss room after using Satanic Bible.

• While playing as Tainted Lost /The Lost pickups that would cost health are free.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns glowing coin wisps on the middle ring. Enemies killed by the wisps' tears have a 20% chance to drop a random coin.

• Coupon / Mr. ME! / Crooked Penny + Schoolbag: Spawned pickups/items can be made free.

• D20 + Schoolbag: Rerolled pickups have a chance to reroll into an item from the current room's item pool.

• Keeper's Sack: Stat upgrades from the spawned pickups/items can be gained even when shops become unavailable (Floors after the Mom fight excluding ???).

• Restock: Buying spawned pickup or item in Shop will always restock into the same thing as what's being sold in the upper left of the shop and their prices will never increase. This still works even if the top left slot was already bought before having Restock. This does not work outside of the shop. It also works in Greed and Greedier modes, respawning them as Keys (since the leftmost pickup is always a key).

• Steam Sale: Spawned pickups/items will be on sale.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Adoption Papers: Does not affect Keeper's Box items, meaning both familiars and shop items can be purchased in tandem over the course of a run.

• Chaos / Sacred Orb / TMTRAINER: Affects items spawned by the box.

• Glitched Crown / Tainted Isaac: The alternate item(s) will be from the pool of the room it is used in.

• Store Credit: Cannot be used on consumables or items spawned by Keeper's Box outside of the Shop.

• Shop Restock Machine: Using a Restock Machine in a Shop will remove every spawned pickup/item. Using the machine outside of the shop will only reroll items.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Keeper's Box has a similar shape to Pandora's Box, along with a keyhole in the same position.

• This item is similar to Portable Slot, and the pickup quote (Portable shop) may be a reference to it.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Keeper's Box can spawn hearts for sale when playing as Keeper/Tainted Keeper.

fields.description: Spawns a random Shop item or pickup which can be bought for its normal price.

Keeper's Kin.title: Keeper's Kin
Keeper's Kin.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• If Isaac is in a room with enemies, rocks and rock-like obstacles will occasionally spawn blue spiders.

• Causes all rocks to spawn 0-2 blue spiders when destroyed.

• Contributes to the Spider Baby transformation.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Compost : Will double the current amount of blue spiders.

• D12: Due to the high tendency of replacing rocks with TNT, it allows for easy destruction of nearby rocks, resulting in lots of blue spiders.

• Leo / Mega Mush / Notched Axe / Stompy / Sulfuric Acid / Terra / Thunder Thighs: As Isaac can break all reachable rocks, he can amass a lot of blue spiders.

• Mega Mush : When Isaac destroys blocks it will produce blue spiders.

fields.description: Rocks and other Obstacles spawn blue spiders over time while in a room with enemies, and spawn two blue spiders when destroyed.

Keeper's Sack.title: Keeper's Sack
Keeper's Sack.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns 3 random coins and a Key on the floor when picked up.

• Every 3 coins spent on items and pickups grants in a cycle: +0.5 damage, then +0.25 range, then +0.03 speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The coins and key spawned on pickup can be any of their variants.

• Keeper's Sack works with anything that costs coins, including Devil deals/Black Markets as Keeper / affected by Keeper's Bargain or A Pound of Flesh, items or pickups created by Keeper's Box, the Angel shop created by The Stairway, and the second shop created by Member Card.

• The stat upgrades are tied to Keeper's Sack; losing Keeper's Sack (for instance, using D4, crossing a 1-pip or 6-pip Dice Room, or using XVII - The Stars?) will result in the loss of all obtained stats.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bag of Crafting: Purchasing a pickup by swinging the Bag of Crafting at it will still give the stat upgrades from Keeper's Sack.

• Diplopia/Crooked Penny: Extra copies of Keeper's Sack do not grant any more stats from purchasing items.

• Steam Sale: As items/pickups cost less money, Isaac will gain fewer stats for making the same purchases.

• Store Credit: Anything bought will not give stats.

• Tainted Keeper: Every Devil Room, Treasure Room, Angel Room etc. will give stat ups, as long as the items are bought.

fields.description: Gives range, speed, or damage when buying things from a shop. Spawns three coins and a Key on pickup.

Key Bum.title: Key Bum
Key Bum.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and collects Keys, dropping random Chests in return.

• Spawns almost exclusively Chests, Red Chests, and Locked Chests, with a very slim chance to spawn another type of chest or a Grab Bag.

• Contributes to the Super Bum transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Key Bum will not pick up Golden Keys.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Key Bum will pick up Charged Key without additional benefit.

• [Repentance] Key Bum will leave a Lil' Battery behind when picking up Charged Key.

• [Before Repentance] From a scoring perspective, Keys that Key Bum picks up count towards your Schwag bonus on daily runs.

• Key Bum does not join the line of familiars that follow behind Isaac.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Familiar is bigger and drops chests more often.

• Flat Penny: Chests frequently contain pennies, which have a chance of spawning more keys for Key Bum to pick up, possibly lead to a loop.

• King Baby / RC Remote: No effect.

• Gilded Key / The Left Hand: Works as expected.

• Guppy's Eye: Allows Isaac to choose which Locked Chests are worth opening and which to pass, thus saving keys. Great for min-maxing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is the Key Master counterpart of Bum Friend and Dark Bum.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Credit Card is used in a Shop with Keys, Key Bum will not be able to pick up the free keys. This can be fixed if Isaac leaves and re-enters the shop.
Bug note: Charged Keys do not increment Key Bum's key count when picked up.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac and collects Keys for himself, giving random Chests in return.

Key Piece 1.title: Key Piece 1
Key Piece 1.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Combined with Key Piece 2, unlocks the golden gate in the starting room of Chest and Dark Room to fight Mega Satan.

• Increases the chance of finding an Angel Room.

• Grants a 2.5% chance of converting Red Heart pickups into Eternal Hearts.

• This effect stacks with Key Piece 2.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item is a guaranteed drop from Uriel if not already in possession.

• This item, along with Key Piece 2, can be rerolled into any item from the Angel Room pool.

• This item also counts as a familiar, meaning it takes up a familiar slot.

• Unlocking the Golden Gate with the combined key pieces and then restarting the floor with Forget Me Now or an I AM ERROR room will waste the key, which will not respawn.

• Will not be rerolled by D4, D100, or Dice Room effects.

• Will not be doubled by Box of Friends

• Picking up two copies with Diplopia will not double itsEternal Heart effect.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Key Piece 1 having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Unlockable achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Dad's Key, The Family Man, Filigree Feather]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in I RULE! and Ultra Hard.

• Key Piece 1 is tied with Key Piece 2 and Card Reading for the item with the most item tags at 6.

Kid's Drawing.title: Kid's Drawing
Kid's Drawing.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• While held, acts as one of the three items needed for Guppy.

• The effect is lost if Kid's Drawing is dropped.

• This includes instantly losing the transformation if dropping the trinket results in having only 2 out of 3 Guppy items required for the transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If multiple copies of the trinket are obtained, they will each count as a Guppy item.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket: Counts as holding 2 Guppy items.

• Mom's Box: No effect, even with Golden Trinket.

• [Repentance+] The Internal Item Description claims otherwise. See bugs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Unlike Guppy items, this trinket doesn't have the "Guppy" tag (in items_metadata.xml) and seems to be hard-coded to count toward the total. This may have to do with how trinkets in general, with or without an applicable tag, don't count toward transformations or unlock requirements.

• This is the only trinket ( [Repentance+] one of the only three trinkets) that counts toward a transformation, [Repentance+] the other ones are Bob's Bladder and A Missing Page.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: • Bug note: Although the trinket is supposed to count as 2 Guppy items with Mom's Box according to internal item descriptions, it still counts only as one.

fields.description: While held, counts as one of three items needed to transform into Guppy.

Kidney Bean.title: Kidney Bean
Kidney Bean.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac farts, charming all nearby enemies.

• [Before Repentance] The cloud deals 5 damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Bird's Eye/Ghost Pepper: Whenever the player creates a charming fart, a fire will be shot in a random direction.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns purple wisps on the middle ring. The wisps charm nearby enemies when destroyed.

• Second Hand: Doubles charm duration.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: Spawns two charming farts on top of each other [Before Repentance] and the cloud deals double damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The charm effect this item gives may be a reference to the fact that Kidney Beans are one of the most nutritious / healthy type of bean to eat, or the fact that it resembles a heart.

• The sprite for Kidney Bean was much larger prior to Repentance. It was resprited to be similar in size to Butter Bean, The Black Bean, and The Bean.

fields.description: Isaac farts, charming all nearby enemies.

Kidney Stone.title: Kidney Stone
Kidney Stone.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] -0.2 speed and maximum speed.

• [Before Afterbirth+] -15 range.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] -17 range.

• [Before Repentance] +2.0 tear falling speed.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The increased tear falling speed and decreased range results in slightly increased firing distance.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The increased tear falling speed and decreased range results in nearly identical firing distance.

• Occasionally, Isaac will become unable to fire tears. He must charge an attack, indicated by his head turning red, that launches a piercing, spectral kidney stone when released, followed by a rapid, inaccurate spray of tears.

• This effect occurs approximately every 25 seconds.

• [Before Repentance] The kidney stone does 5x Isaac's damage and has approximately twice the range of normal tears.

• [Repentance] The kidney stone does 10x Isaac's damage and has approximately twice the range of normal tears.

• The barrage grants a decaying 6x fire rate multiplier that can exceed the normal cap and forces Isaac to fire for the duration.

• The barrage will continue for its full length between rooms, as will the state of charging the attack.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tints tears red. This is only a cosmetic change.

• The kidney stone can still be fired by blindfolded characters, but not the tear barrage. This includes Lilith.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Incubus: Fire tears normally while Isaac is charging, and copies the barrage but not the stone. The barrage from the Incubus will be in a straight line instead of an inaccurate burst.

• Maw Of The Void: Whenever the kidney stone is fired, the tear barrage will continuously charge and activate Maw Of The Void until Isaac can fire normally.

• Montezuma's Revenge/Revelation: Whenever the kidney stone is fired, the tear barrage will continuously charge and activate these items' effects until Isaac can fire normally.

• Rock Bottom: The temporary tears up from the kidney stone burst becomes a permanent x6 fire rate multiplier.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 20/20/The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider: Only fires one stone.

• Anti-Gravity: The stone will not hover and will travel regardless.

• Azazel/Brimstone: Overrides Kidney Stone. [Before Repentance] Speed and range downs still apply.

• Chocolate Milk: When Kidney Stone activates, it fires one kidney stone and then no more tears until tears stat is under a certain value (unknown).

• Cursed Eye: Charging the barrage pauses the Cursed Eye charge bar - if the bar is not full and Isaac is hurt, he will teleport. Firing during the barrage will neither fire tears, nor show the charge bar, but will still charge Cursed Eye. Being hit while the invisible charge bar is not full will teleport Isaac.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: The stone cannot split into smaller stones.

• Dr. Fetus: Overrides Kidney Stone. [Before Repentance] Speed and range downs still apply.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Kidney Stone. [Before Repentance] Speed and range downs still apply.

• The Forgotten: The Forgotten will swing his club rapidly instead of shooting the burst of tears (The Forgotten still fires the stone normally).

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Haemolacria: Overridden by Haemolacria. Only stat changes apply. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Fires a barrage of Haemolacria tears upon activation

• Jacob's Ladder: The stone will only spawn sparks when hitting enemies.

• Libra: Stats are greatly increased during the barrage. [Before Repentance] The harsh speed and range down make Libra a large stats down.

• The Ludovico Technique: Overrides Kidney Stone.

• A Lump of Coal: The stone will not grow bigger as it travels, but it will increase in damage.

• Marked: Occasionally, Isaac will stop automatically firing, and an attack key must be held to release the kidney stone and continued firing.

• Mom's Knife: Overrides Kidney Stone. [Before Repentance] Speed and range downs still apply.

• Monstro's Lung: Overrides Kidney Stone. [Before Repentance] Speed and range downs still apply.

• [Repentance] Monstro's Lung + Technology: Kidney Stone can activate, but the barrage does not work correctly (see bugs).

• Number One: Number One's range down overrides Kidney Stone, for an additional -0.62. The stone is not affected by the range decrease.

• Spirit Sword: Overrides Kidney Stone.

• Tainted Lilith: Kidney Stone has no effect.

• Technology: Overrides Kidney Stone.

• [Repentance] Fires the stone like normal, followed by a barrage of Technology lasers.

• Tech X: Overrides Kidney Stone.

• Urn of Souls: Firing the urn counts as fire time but the urn must be put away for Isaac to charge and shoot the kidney shot. Switching to the urn while auto-firing from Kidney Stone forces the urn to fire as well.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• "Matt" refers to Matt Kap, a pixel artist for The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, who has once been afflicted with a kidney stone.

• A kidney stone is a hard deposit made of minerals and salts that form inside kidneys. It will usually pass through the urethra, which is often a very painful process.

• When Isaac enters a room with half a heart and holding this item, he will leave a small puddle of blood rather than pee.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Kidney Stone activates while a charged tear effect such as Tech X or Chocolate Milk is currently charging, the charge will get stuck, unable to fire for a somewhat-short period of time, before eventually having the Kidney stone be released as normal. Tears will then occasionally charge, even if a fire button isn't held down anymore.
Bug note: [Repentance] With Monstro's Lung and Technology, the stone can be launched but the barrage will not charge Monstro's Lung enough to fire, preventing Isaac from firing at all during the barrage.

fields.description: Isaac is occasionally forced to stop firing and charge an attack that launches a massive piercing, spectral kidney stone and a barrage of tears. [Before Repentance] -0.2 speed, decreases range. [end edition note]

King Baby.title: King Baby
King Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a familiar that follows Isaac and always appears first in the familiar chain.

• While firing tears, King Baby stops moving and glows white.

• When Isaac stops firing tears, King Baby moves rapidly back towards Isaac.

• While King Baby is stationary, other familiars remain stationary as well. [Repentance] This affects every familiar that has priority in how closely it follows behind Isaac.

• [Before Repentance] Shooting familiars will fire tears in the direction Isaac is firing, while Throwable familiars ignore King Baby.

• [Repentance] Shooting familiars fire at nearby enemies automatically and throwable familiars launch themselves at nearby enemies automatically.

• • Familiars that have charged attacks will operate on similar rules to Marked: they will immediately fire at full charge, and variable-charged attacks will be released earlier the closer that King Baby is to the target.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• King Baby will move back towards Isaac even if Isaac is still holding a fire button, if he enters a state that overrides his animation or prevents him from firing (i.e.: picking up an item, getting hurt, using most activated collectibles)

• Abel will still reflect Isaac's movements, and not King Baby's.

• Lil Delirium's behavior depends on which familiar form it takes.

• Duplicate King Babies, such as those granted from Box of Friends, will cause familiars to follow the last King Baby added.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with King Baby having 1st priority and thus being closer to Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

• [Repentance] Has no effect on Tainted Eve's/Sumptorium clots. [end edition note] 

• Familiars unaffected by King Baby include:

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Isaac's Heart: Isaac can fire tears and leave King Baby and the heart behind, and run into a group of enemies without being damaged.

• Lil Brimstone: Can fire in full 360 degrees and will fire as soon as he's fully charged, making him extremely effective.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Increases King Baby's size. No other effect.

• Child Leash: Familiars stay closer to King Baby while Isaac is firing.

• Cain's Other Eye: Cain's Other Eye will attempt to fire directly at enemies but only when they are on the same side as the random direction it is firing in.

• Duct Tape: King Baby will stay in place relative to Isaac until Isaac starts firing tears. Then King Baby will remain stationary until Isaac has stopped firing and will rapidly move back to him.

• Friendship Necklace: Familiars will orbit King Baby at all times instead of Isaac, even while not firing. King Baby itself is unaffected.

• GB Bug: GB Bug will only throw itself at nearby enemies automatically if a fire button is double tapped while King Baby's effect is active.

• Gemini: Suture will rest near King Baby as long as there are no enemies near Isaac. When Isaac gets near enemies, Suture will rapidly snap from King Baby toward the enemy. Functionally, King Baby has no real effect on Gemini.

• Visually, this can result in the umbilical between Isaac and Suture getting stretched to a long length.

• Jaw Bone: After being thrown, Jaw Bone will return to Isaac and then reappear behind King Baby.

• RC Remote: Overrides King Baby's halting; familiars will mimic Isaac's movements even while firing. King Baby's auto-targeting remains active.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• King Baby references the official Binding of Isaac tarot card set, in which ??? represents the Emperor.

• The Steam achievement description for unlocking King Baby says "Unlocked a new co-player baby," despite it being an item.

• [Repentance] King Baby's pickup quote is a reference to the film Army of Darkness, where the protagonist Ash says "Hail to the king, baby!". The same quote also appears in Duke Nukem 3D.

fields.name: King Baby
fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Lord of the dead!; Repentance: Hail to the king baby]
fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac and makes other familiars follow it. While firing tears, other familiars stop moving.

Knife Piece 1.title: Knife Piece 1
Knife Piece 1.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Spawns a knife handle familiar that follows Isaac.

• Generates a room in Mines / Ashpit II for Knife Piece 2 to spawn in.

• Combines with Knife Piece 2 to form a knife familiar that launches itself in the direction Isaac shoots, dealing 25 damage to and piercing enemies it hits.

• Launching it at the red door at the end of Mausoleum/Gehenna II will open the door, destroying the knife in the process.

sections.heading: How to Acquire
sections.text:
• A white fire place will be present in Downpour / Dross II. Touching the white fire place temporarily transforms Isaac into The Lost. Another room on the floor has a mirror, which Isaac can enter while a ghost. Walking through the mirror will teleport Isaac to the Mirrored World. The Knife Piece is in the Mirrored World's Treasure Room. After acquiring it, Isaac can return to the normal floor by walking through the mirror again.

• The mirror floor is technically a separate area to the normal floor with an identical layout, meaning all rooms will not be cleared, and that destroying obstacles in one area has no effect on the other.

• No other items or pickups naturally spawn in the mirror floor, although they can still be generated or awarded for clearing a room.

• If the character is The Lost, Tainted Lost, Tainted Jacob in his Lost form, Tainted Forgotten's Soul, or any character upon using Soul of the Lost, the mirror can be entered without interacting with the white campfire.

• • Since Tainted Forgotten does not need to interact with the white fire to enter the mirror, their normal health remains intact.

• • Despite the Soul of the Lost only lasting for one room in most circumstances, when used to enter the mirror, the Lost form will be kept until Isaac leaves the mirror world, meaning Isaac cannot keep his health on his way to obtain the Knife Piece.

• Should the player use a Forget Me Now on this floor, it's possible (though useless) to acquire two separate Knife Piece 1s.

• • However, the spare Knife Piece can be rerolled just like any other pedestal item.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Isaac will remain as The Lost until after he has cleared a room of enemies; it does not matter whether this room is in the mirror world. His normal form will be restored upon entering any room outside the mirror world. This effect can extend to the next floor.

• If you don't have Holy Mantle unlocked on The Lost, you don't get Holy Mantle while in ghost form.

• The red door can alternatively be opened using Cracked Orb, Sharp Key, or Soul of Cain.

• The knife piece can be rerolled, in the event that Mother is not the desired completion mark.

• Knife Piece 1 takes 6th priority on the line of following familiars while the knife familiar created from both knife pieces takes 5th priority.

• It's possible to see the Knife Piece 1 multiple times by using Forget Me Now or R Key, allowing you to use the The D6 or Void on one of the duplicates while still collecting the other.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Knife Piece 1 is from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Isaac would acquire Knife Piece 1 by bombing open a hidden stone chest instead of entering the Mirrored World. Once bombed, the stone chest would remain open on subsequent runs.

• Knife Piece 1 was also one of 3 knife pieces which needed to be combined to make the knife familiar instead of 2.

fields.description: Combined with Knife Piece 2, creates a knife familiar that damages enemies and can open the door to the Corpse.

Knife Piece 2.title: Knife Piece 2
Knife Piece 2.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Combines with Knife Piece 1 to form a knife familiar that launches itself in the direction Isaac shoots, dealing 25 damage to and piercing enemies it hits.

• Launching it at the red door at the end of Mausoleum/Gehenna II will open the door, destroying the knife in the process.

sections.heading: How to Acquire
sections.text: • In Mines/Ashpit II, if Isaac has Knife Piece 1, there is a tall room with a broken minecart track. Scattered across the floor are three yellow buttons that will repair pieces of the track. Once all buttons have been pressed, the minecart becomes rideable, which will take Isaac to an abandoned area, with Knife Piece 2 at the end. Picking up the Knife Piece will trigger a chase sequence in which Mother's Shadow will pursue Isaac through the corridor. Getting to the end of the area will seal it off.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Obtaining Knife Piece 2 without Knife Piece 1 will spawn a knife blade familiar that follows Isaac but has no other effect.

• The door to the abandoned area can be opened with two explosions or items like Dad's Key; however, Isaac will not be able to reach the door unless he has flight or all three buttons have been pressed anyway. If the door is already open, the minecart cannot be ridden but the path can be walked along.

• While in the abandoned area, all of Isaac's items and consumables are removed. Extra Life items will not activate despite still visually appearing beside the health bar. However, any items with reroll protection will still function as normal. (This includes Knife Piece 1 itself.)

• If a character has inherent flight, they will retain it in the abandoned area, making it significantly easier.

• This room, as well as the buttons to reach it, will only be generated if Knife Piece 1 was already collected.

• The buttons can be bypassed with flight and 2 bombs to destroy the door. Upon exiting the room, the rail pathway will be built in order to prevent softlocks from using temporary flight methods such as The Bible.

• The red door can alternatively be opened using Cracked Orb, Sharp Key, or Soul of Cain.

• If Isaac takes Knife Piece 2 and is somehow able to immediately leave the room before Mother's Shadow fully activates (usually by using Mama Mega! earlier in the floor), the rest of the sub-area will not have reset, and the doors leading to the exit will all be locked. This forces the player to re-enter the Knife Piece 2 room, which triggers another activation of Mother's Shadow, causing two instances of Mother's Shadow to pursue the player during the escape sequence.

• It is possible to find a Crawl Space as normal in this area, which will be the same crawlspace as any other generated on the normal floor. Entering the crawlspace will allow Isaac to use his normal items and consumables, but Mother's Shadow will also be present. Using any teleport card or item will teleport Isaac to a random room on the abandoned area map. Any items obtained while in this crawlspace will remain upon leaving the area, but will not be able to be used while in the abandoned area.

• It is possible to softlock the run by entering a crawlspace with the key needed to escape the room. Upon leaving the crawlspace, the key will be gone.

• The Black Market or I AM ERROR room can potentially be entered from the crawlspace. Going through the trapdoor there will end the pursuit and lead to Depths II (or alternatives). Isaac will keep all his items, including those bought in the market.

• The knife familiar created from both knife pieces takes 5th priority on the line of following familiars.

• Knife Piece 2 takes 6th priority on the line of following familiars while the knife familiar created from both knife pieces takes 5th priority.

• It's possible (though useless) to acquire another Knife Piece 2 using Forget Me Now or R Key.

• Tainted Eve retains her ability to create clots, but loses access to Sumptorium. Caution should be used if entering with low health as clots cannot be reabsorbed until exiting.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Knife Piece 2 is from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Isaac would acquire Knife Piece 2 by pressing the right sequence of buttons in a special room instead of entering the abandoned area and being chased by Mother’s Shadow. Once the sequence was solved, Knife Piece 2 would always automatically appear in the center of the special room on subsequent runs.

• Knife Piece 2 was also not the final piece, with 3 knife pieces being needed to be combined to make the knife familiar. Moreover, the sprites for Knife Piece 2 was only the left half of the blade, with the 3rd knife piece being the right half.

fields.description: Combined with Knife Piece 1, creates a knife familiar that damages enemies and can open the door to the Corpse.

Knockout Drops.title: Knockout Drops
Knockout Drops.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a chance to shoot red fist-shaped tears that deal extreme knockback and cause confusion for 2 seconds.

• Enemies will take 10 + 2 * (floor - 1) damage when they are knocked into a wall/obstacle or when hit by another knocked back enemy.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The chance to fire fist tears depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 10 - \left \lceil \mathit{Luck} \right \rceil}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 100% at 8.01 luck.

• Bosses are also affected by all of Knockout Drops' effects.

• Fist tears play a unique punch sound effect when they hit enemies.

• Knockout Drops can be dangerous in The Beast battle, as the Ultra Harbingers may get knocked so far off the screen they become hard to damage further and their attacks cannot be seen properly.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Aquarius: The trail of tears has a chance to knockback enemies.

• Brimstone: Gives the lasers high knockback.

• Jacob's Ladder: Enemies that are shocked by a knockback tear will also be knocked back.

• The Ludovico Technique: Hovering tear alternates between a normal tear and a fist.

• Technology: Laser receives knockback effect as with normal tears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Knockout Drops is from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, enemies would not take extra damage from being knocked into something else but still deal damage to enemies they are knocked into.

• Taking this item as Keeper will give him the expression of Bum-Bo the Brave, and by extension, Bumbino.

sections.heading: References
sections.text: • The Binding of Isaac Item Trigger Testing

fields.description: Adds a chance to shoot a fist tear that has extremely high knockback and confuses enemies.

Krampus.title: Krampus
Krampus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Krampus is a mini-boss that can occasionally appear inside of a Devil Room.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Krampus moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:

• Stops and fires Brimstone lasers in all 4 cardinal [Afterbirth+ onward] or diagonal directions.

• [Afterbirth onward] The lasers can sometimes rotate 90 degrees in either direction after being shot.

• • [Afterbirth+ onward] Krampus signals rotating Brimstone lasers by growling and quickly dashing towards Isaac before performing this attack.

• Fires 3 projectiles in a spread followed by 4 projectiles in a spread in succession towards Isaac.
Krampus deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Encountering Krampus replaces both the statue of Satan as well as any deals in regular Devil Rooms.

• Krampus can drop A Lump of Coal even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. However, he can only drop Head of Krampus once, and any other kills will only drop copies of A Lump of Coal.

• [Afterbirth onward] Krampus can spawn in Greed Mode without needing to be unlocked.

• Defeating Krampus when encountered here still unlocks Head of Krampus even if Krampus himself has not yet been unlocked.

• Chaos will not change the items dropped from Krampus.

• [Repentance] Krampus can never appear in the first Devil Room entered on a run.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Head of Krampus]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• His name and appearance are based on Krampus, an alpine folkloric figure. It supposedly acts as a antithesis to Saint Nicholas, punishing children who misbehave near Christmas time.

• This is most likely why A Lump of Coal is in his item pool.

• Krampus is both visually and behaviorally similar to The Fallen.

• Krampus is tied with The Fallen as having the highest Stage HP among all entities in the game.

• In an AMA subreddit thread for Edmund McMillen, a user questioned why Krampus got "worse with every update." Edmund McMillen jokingly responded, "he's the new bloat."; referencing the general hatred some fans have towards The Bloat.

• [Repentance] Despite Krampus receiving a redesign in Repentance, Delirium's Krampus appearance has yet to be updated.

• [Repentance] Red Mini-Boss Rooms created by Red Key (etc.) can contain a battle against Krampus. [end edition note]
