Lachryphagy.title: Lachryphagy
Lachryphagy.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac's tears decelerate as they travel. Upon stopping or hitting an obstacle, they burst into tears that fly in all directions. Hitting an enemy will not cause them to burst.

• [Before Repentance] They burst into 8 tears.

• [Repentance] They burst into 5-8 tears, depending on tear size.

• Tears can be fired into other tears to feed them, increasing their damage and the damage of the burst tears.

• If one tear is fed 5 other tears, it will immediately burst.

• The tears will have their damage added together, with the first consumed tear giving additional damage.

• Tears in the burst will deal half the damage the main tear would have.

• This also applies to Familiar tears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Certain items that cause tears to split and feed each other, when combined, can cause the resulting tear to become so large that the game will crash.

• Tears can also burst from shot size. With sufficiently high damage or several tear-size increasing items, the tears will burst almost immediately after firing.

• The distance burst tears fly depends on tear height and not range.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20 / The Inner Eye / Mutant Spider: Tears tend to clump together soon after firing for high damage shots. It may take more than 5 tears in total to cause a burst.

• Akeldama: Akeldama tears can feed and be fed by the Lachryphagy tears. Fed Akeldama tears will gain increased damage but will not burst, and will cap at 5 tears fed each.

• Bob's Rotten Head: The head act as a tear, dividing itself if enough time has passed and interacting with other tears. The five heads coming from the main head deal half damage. Feeding a head with another increases damage by the amount of damage Isaac has. If a tear is fed with a head, the tear will gain the head's damage.

• Book of Virtues / Jar of Wisps: Wisps' tears can feed the Lachryphagy tears.

• [Repentance] Brimstone: Brimstone's range is now limited, but piercing Lachryphagy tears will quickly form at the end of the beam.

• Azazel: Lachryphagy effectively leaves Azazel's brimstone unchanged given it already has limited range.

• Rubber Cement: Reflected brimstone will still have its full range.

• Compound Fracture: Bone tears split into a random spread of fractured tears and bone tears.

• Cricket's Body / The Parasite: Fed tears split into 12 tears.

• Dead Eye Firing into the floating tear won't reset the multiplier as long as that tear doesn't hit a wall. The burst tears will never reset the multiplier.

• Euthanasia: Needle shots will allow the tears to burst at least twice.

• Eye of Belial: Tear burst retains Eye of Belial's effect, greatly increasing the effectiveness of the tear burst due to the piercing, spectral, and increased tear damage. By proxy, piercing, spectral, and continuum tears all improve the value of Lachyphagy.

• Evil Eye: can compound tears with Lachryphagy.

• Haemolacria: Tears look like Haemolacria. They can be fed and will burst into 8 tears that have Haemolacria's burst effect upon hitting obstacles or enemies.

• [Repentance] Haemolacria + Brimstone / Tech X / Technology: The tears behave like Lachryphagy tears. On hitting enemies, they always burst into respective Lachryphagy-synergized lasers (if available), but on hitting a wall or an obstacle, slower-moving shots burst into normal shots and faster ones into lasers.

• Kidney Stone: When a barrage of tears is fired, tears clump together and burst at a high rate. The stone also behaves as a Lachryphagy tear. Because of the tear height decrease, burst tears cover much shorter distance before falling, making the combination less effective.

• Lost Contact: Both the original tear and the burst tears can block enemy shots. The tears' size is increased, so it is easier to feed them.

• A Lump of Coal: Tears continually grow in size without being fed other tears, but they will still only deal bonus damage based strictly on how far they travel. Burst tears will still grow in size and damage as they travel.

• Monstro's Lung / Lead Pencil: The tears clump together soon after firing, causing potentially up to 20x tear damage on a direct hit on an enemy.

• My Reflection: Causes tears to float back towards Isaac and clump together with any tears they come along.

• Pulse Worm: The fluctuating hitboxes of the tears causes them to clump together at a faster rate.

• Revelation: The beam's range is now limited, but piercing Lachryphagy tears will form at the end of it.

• Sinus Infection: Boogers will always burst into more boogers, though some of the boogers may incorrectly appear to be normal tears. When a booger sticks to an enemy, it will burst into 8 boogers which have a high chance of sticking again to the same enemy.

• [Repentance] Technology: Technology's range is now limited, but piercing Lachryphagy tears will form at the end of the beam.

• [Repentance] Technology 2: Significantly shortens the range of the laser. A piercing Lachryphagy tear spawns at the end of the laser every tick, rapidly feeding off of each other and bursting when standing still. This is an extremely powerful combo that alone can provide enough damage output to challenge any boss in the game.

• A fire rate reduction such as from The Inner Eye or a few Tears Down pills makes the combo even stronger, as tears will grow even larger before bursting.

• Tiny Planet: [Before Repentance] Tears will orbit until they are behind the character. Tears will burst into 8 tears that follow the orbit in 2 close groups of 4. One group travels clockwise and the other travels counterclockwise.

• [Repentance] Tears orbit the player without slowing down, and can be fed as normal. When a tear bursts, the created tears orbit the place of burst.

• Tractor Beam: All split tears will travel along the beam.

• [Repentance] Trisagion: Trisagion tears will fade faster, but will constantly spit out more piercing Lachryphagy tears while they are active. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone: Lachryphagy does not affect regular Brimstone beams, but tears from other sources such as Isaac's Tears or Fate's Reward will burst into 8 Brimstone beams. Lachryphagy affects Chocolate Milk + Brimstone.

• Chaos Card: Counts as a tear and will be wasted if thrown into another tear.

• Dr. Fetus: Overrides Lachryphagy.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Lachryphagy.

• Flat Stone: Overridden by Lachryphagy.

• Ipecac: Lachryphagy tears will burst into ipecac shots and explode. The Ipecac tear burst will travel like a normal tear instead of an arc. Due to tear slowdown effect it becomes hard to hit enemies without standing in the explosion radius.

• The Ludovico Technique: Overrides Lachryphagy.

• Mom's Knife: No effect.

• Pop!: Tears behave erratically, with freshly fired tears usually behaving like Lachryphagy and burst tears like Pop!.

• Saturnus: Orbiting tears are Lachryphagy tears, including enemy tears caught in orbit. Tears will still burst after a set duration, greatly the reducing the amount of time the tears orbit for. Burst tears will remain in an orbital path instead of spreading out.

• Stop Watch / Broken Watch / Era Walk: Tears are slowed/sped up along with enemies.

• Tech X: Overrides Lachryphagy.

• Technology: Overrides Lachryphagy.

• Technology Zero: Tears will generate arcs of electricity until they burst. As the tears will hang in the air for several seconds, this significantly increases the uptime of electricity arcs. Burst tears are similarly connected to each other by electricity. 

• Trisagion: Tears will split but cannot be grown by feeding tears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Lachryphagy is based on this Steam Workshop item by KittyK47, originally known as Hungry Tears.

• Lachryphagy refers to the insect practice of drinking tears or eye secretions from other creatures.

• Isaac's appearance (his eyes being replaced by gaping mouths) is similar to the Corinthian from Neil Gaiman's "The Sandman".

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: In the battle with The Beast and the Ultra Harbingers, outputting high amounts of Lachryphagy tears can cause the damage from all the tears offscreen to be instantly applied to each entity the moment they arrive to fight Isaac.
Bug note: Rubber Cement causes all tears on screen to have their damage applied to any enemy that gets hit by a tear.

fields.description: Isaac's tears decelerate as they travel. Upon stopping or hitting an obstacle, they burst into 8 tears in all directions. Tears can be fired into other tears to feed them, increasing their damage.

Large Zit.title: Large Zit
Large Zit.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• While firing, Isaac has a chance to fire an additional creep shot that deals double damage, slows enemies, and leaves a short trail of white creep that also slows enemies.

• The chance is not affected by luck.

• The creep shots don't take on any tear effects.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The creep shots are affected by range and shot speed.

• • [Repentance] The creep shots are not affected by range but affected by shot speed, which determines their effective range.

• Their tear sizes are not affected by their damage. They always retain their small size.

• The creep shots can be fired diagonally.

• A creep shot will also be fired in a random direction when taking damage.

• Large Zit does not fire when

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brimstone / Chocolate Milk / Epic Fetus / Mom's Knife / Monstro's Lung / Tech X: Creep shots will still be fired occasionally while holding the fire button.

• Dr. Fetus: Creep shots will occasionally be fired along with bombs.

• Ipecac: High tear damage from Ipecac is doubled, causing very powerful creep shots.

• Multidimensional Baby: Creep shots can be duplicated.

• Polyphemus: High tear damage from Polyphemus is doubled.

• Technology Zero: Creep shots will be connected to other tears via electricity.

• Urn of Souls: Creep shots still shoot as normal while using the urn.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 20/20 / The Inner Eye / Mutant Spider: Isaac will still fire one creep shot.

• Bird's Eye / Ghost Pepper: Firing creep shots does not spawn the fires.

• Compound Fracture / Cricket's Body / The Parasite: Creep shots will not burst into split tears.

• Dead Eye: Creep shots do not grant or reset the damage multiplier, although their damage still benefit from the multiplier.

• Eye of Belial: Creep shots are not affected.

• Eye of Greed / Lead Pencil: Creep shots are not counted for shots fired.

• Eye of the Occult: Creep shots are not controlled. Creep shots will only fire in cardinal or diagonal directions unless there is a cross-hair, in which case creep shots will fire directly toward it.

• Incubus / Twisted Pair: The familiars does not fire creep shots.

• Immaculate Heart: Firing creep shots does not spawn the orbiting tear.

• Lachryphagy: Creep shots are not affected from Lachryphagy, but Lachryphagy tears can feed on them.

• The Ludovico Technique: Movable tear behaves as normal. Isaac will occasionally fire a creep shot while moving the tear, and creep shots will only fire in cardinal or diagonal directions.

• A Lump of Coal: Creep shots are not affected.

• My Reflection / Tiny Planet / Tractor Beam: Creep shots are not affected by the trajectory altering effect. Stat changes are applied as normal.

• Pop!: Creep shots are not affected. Pop! tears do not bounce off of creep shots.

• Proptosis: Creep shots are not affected.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Large Zit was originally an unofficial item which was supposed to showcase the modding capabilities of Afterbirth+ in the PAX 2016 livestream. However, all items included in the demo were later added to the final game.

fields.description: Adds a chance to fire a creep shot that deals double damage and leaves a trail of slowing white creep.

Larry Jr..title: Larry Jr.
Larry Jr..attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Larry Jr. is a boss that can appear in the Basement and the Burning Basement.

He has 22 HP per segment.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The number of individual Larry Jr. bodies that can spawn each fight can vary from 1-4. The most common encounter with Larry Jr. is with 2 bodies.

• Randomly moves around the room in the cardinal directions, turning when colliding with walls or obstacles.

• Larry Jr. can change direction if one of his segments is destroyed.

• Randomly spawns Poop while moving.

• Colliding with a Poop destroys the Poop and causes Larry Jr. to turn.

• Larry Jr. segments can be split into smaller copies of the boss as long as the new Larry Jr. segments are longer than 2 pieces.
There is a chance that a Grub can spawn alongside a shorter Larry Jr. (basically replacing a second Larry Jr.) due to its patterns being very similar to the boss.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 7] : Is 15% larger and has 45% more HP (31.9), but moves more slowly and does not leave poop behind. Has shared health between his body segments, meaning that dealing damage to one segment will deal a percentage of the damage to the other segments. This version always drops a Soul Heart when defeated.
[bc: 5] : Will occasionally shoot a projectile in the direction he's facing, pausing momentarily as he does so.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Poop spawned by Larry Jr. will never drop pickups, even when in possession of Petrified Poop.

• [Repentance] Poops spawned by Larry Jr. have an incredibly low chance to spawn pickups. This chance is not affected by Petrified Poop.

• Leaving the room and returning will make the poop generate pickups normally.

• [Before Repentance] The D12 doesn't reroll Larry Jr.'s poop.

• Destroying Larry Jr.'s poop with Brown Cap will cause it to explode.

• Piercing tears make fighting Larry Jr. much easier, as each tear can damage multiple segments.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Larry Jr. appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• The Hollow is the posthumous version of him.

• Larry Jr. is an allusion to Larries' Lament, the name for a group of bosses in Edmund McMillen's game, Super Meat Boy.

• Not only do they look similar but smaller Larries came from a dead Larry in the Super Meat Boy credits. This is a strong indication that those smaller Larries and Larry Jr. are the same.

• In battle, Larry Jr. seems to be crying and has blood on the lower belly of his body, unlike the splash screen before the fight.

• Larry Jr. might be a reference to the centipede enemies from the 1980 arcade game Centipede.

Larynx.title: Larynx
Larynx.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac shouts, damaging and pushing away nearby enemies. The item can be used when not fully charged, and deals more damage and has increased range the more charges it has when used.

• The initial shout deals 20 damage + 28 per charge and destroys enemy shots, obstacles, Shopkeepers, Beggars, and machines, and opens bombable doors in range.

• A number of extra pulses are released equal to half the charges used (rounded up) that deal 2.5 damage + 3.5 per charge.

• Larynx gains 1 charge whenever Isaac takes damage, as well as through normal means.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Larynx only has 1 charge when initially picked up.

• Larynx will gain charges if Isaac is hit during the Mother's Shadow escape sequence.

• Obstacles destroyed by the shout don't bridge gaps.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns red wisps on the middle ring. The wisps deals contact damage equal to 30% of Isaac's damage * Charges Used. Charges Used equals the number of charges Larynx had at the time it was used. Health 1 * Charges Used. Tear Damage 1.5 * Charges Used.

• Habit: Both on-hit charge effects stack, charging 2 points per hit.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 9 Volt: The first bar gains an automatic timed recharge, but the further bars will not be affected.

• The Battery: Larynx can hold up to two full charges. Only up to 12 charges will be used at a time.

• Void: If Larynx is absorbed, its effect is only replicated at 1 charge.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Larynx is the medical term for the voice box, the organ that holds the vocal cords in mammals.

• Larynx, Everything Jar, Notched Axe, and Spin to Win are the only activated items that can be used when not fully charged.

• Larynx, Alabaster Box, Berserk!, Eden's Soul, and Everything Jar are the only activated items that are not fully charged on first pickup.

fields.description: Isaac shouts, damaging and pushing away nearby enemies. The shout gets stronger the more charges the item has. Larynx gains 1 charge whenever Isaac takes damage, in addition to charging normally.

Latch Key.title: Latch Key
Latch Key.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants 1 Soul Heart.

• +1 luck.

• Spawns 2 Keys.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• There is a chance a Golden Key gets spawned instead of regular Keys.

• [Repentance] Latch Key's Quality is considered 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting.

• This item can be crafted from Bag of Crafting with eight Keys.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The name of the item refers to latchkey kids, children who return from school to an empty home because one or both of their parents are at work, or who are otherwise often left at home with little parental supervision.

fields.description: Grants 1 Soul Heart and +1 luck. Spawns 2 Keys.

Lazarus' Rags.title: Lazarus' Rags
Lazarus' Rags.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Upon dying, resurrect as Lazarus Risen in the current room with one Red Heart container and Anemic.

• [Repentance] Upon dying, resurrect as Lazarus Risen in the current room with one less Red Heart container (but no less than 1), Anemic, and a permanent +0.5 Damage up.

• Going to the next floor reverts him back into Lazarus, with his inherent extra life effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Resurrection items activate in a set order. Lazarus' Rags is [Before Repentance] 5th / [Repentance] 7th in this order after Soul of Lazarus, 1up!, Dead Cat, Lazarus' inherent extra life ( [Repentance] swap the order of the previous two), Inner Child, and Guppy's Collar.

• Completion marks earned after being revived by this item will go toward Lazarus, regardless of who the original character was.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Tainted Lazarus / Dead Tainted Lazarus: Revived as Tainted Lazarus / Dead Tainted Lazarus correspondingly instead of Lazarus Risen.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Birthright: Dying and reviving as any character will not give Lazarus Risen a damage boost; however, picking up Birthright as him will.

• [Before Repentance+] Plan C: Isaac can use Plan C on end-game bosses (e.g. Hush, Delirium) and survive, although, if going for unlocks, he will get Lazarus's post-it notes instead.

• [Repentance+] Plan C Takes longer to kill the player character, effectively allowing Delirium to fully die to get the achievement, before changing character to Lazarus Risen.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] When Tainted Forgotten dies and respawns using this item, the resulting Lazarus Risen appears as a skin-colored pile of bones with Lazarus' head on top. This is purely visual and Lazarus Risen is still able to move and shoot as normal. This was originally a bug, but was left in because the developer Kilburn found it funny. [end edition note] 

• All characters, except Azazel, The Lost, and Tainted Lost, have this bone-pile form. They can be seen if Clicker is used as bone-pile Lazarus to turn into another character.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Upon dying, resurrect as Lazarus Risen in the current room with one Red Heart container and Anemic.
[Repentance] Upon dying, resurrect as Lazarus Risen in the current room with one less Red Heart container, Anemic, and +0.5 Damage. Transform into Lazarus when reaching the next floor.

Lazy Worm.title: Lazy Worm
Lazy Worm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• -0.5 shot speed.

• [Repentance+] +0.5 damage.

• [Before Repentance] +4.0 range.

• [Before Repentance] +2.0 tear falling speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance+] This trinket has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Pin, Larry Jr., The Hollow or Scolex. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Lazy Worm: Each copy decrease shot speed by 0.5.

• [Repentance+] Each copy also increases damage by 0.5. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Godhead: Tears will take longer to hit enemies, increasing the damage dealt by the aura.

• The Ludovico Technique: Decreased shot speed makes it harder to keep the tear on enemies.

• Trisagion: Because Trisagion can hit the same enemy multiple times, lower shot speed results in a substantial DPS increase.

• [Before Repentance] My Reflection / Pop! / Lachryphagy: Decreases effective range.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] Lazy Worm's sprite was changed for Booster Pack #5.

fields.name: Lazy Worm
fields.description: Decreases shot speed by 0.5. [Before Repentance] Increases range by 4. [Repentance+] Increases damage by 0.5.

Lead Pencil.title: Lead Pencil
Lead Pencil.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• After every 15 tears fired, Isaac will fire a low range burst of 12 tears at once, in a similar fashion to Monstro's Lung.

• Tears in the barrage inherit the majority of Isaac's tear effects.

• [Before Repentance] Tears in the barrage deal double damage.

• Tears will fire only from Isaac's right eye.

• [Repentance] Fired tears have a 50% chance to be colored red.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Lead Pencil gives characters other than Cain the same special properties that he has when it comes to one-eye items like Blood Clot.

• [Before Repentance] Tears fired from items that cause multiple tears to be fired at once e.g. 20/20, Mutant Spider, etc. are counted.

• [Repentance] Each tear fired from Monstro's Lung still count towards triggering the barrage, but only if Isaac does not have any tear modifying items, such as Technology.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Clot: The tears from the barrage will always have the bonus damage from Blood Clot.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: All tears from the barrage split.

• Haemolacria: Fires a barrage of Haemolacria tears, all of which will burst.

• Lachryphagy: Tears tend to clump together, becoming one giant tear which splits into 8 large tears. When tears burst, they can also spawn barrages of tears that can be fed.

• Pop!: Causes burst tears to remain in the room for much longer, forming a soft barrier of sorts, which enemies must survive through to reach Isaac.

• Torn Card: Decreases shot requirement by 1. Lead Pencil will fire every 14th shot, with Torn Card quickly following at 15th.

• Trisagion: Fires a barrage of beams.

• The Scooper: All tears benefit from the damage bonus granted by The Scooper.

• Sprinkler: Sprinkler tears count for activation of the Lead Pencil effect. The tear burst may fire from the sprinkler or Isaac.

• Flat Stone: Tears fired by Lead Pencil will bounce, greatly increasing their range.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone: Overrides Lead Pencil.

• [Repentance] The Lead Pencil tears fire alongside the beam every 4th blast.

• Dr. Fetus: Overrides Lead Pencil.

• [Repentance] The Lead Pencil tears fire alongside the bombs. The tears are likely to hit the most recent bomb, launching it unpredictably.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Lead Pencil.

• [Repentance] The Lead Pencil tears fire towards the cursor, locked to cardinal directions, after every 3rd missile launch.

• [Before Repentance] Lilith: No effect, as Lilith is inherently Blindfolded.

• [Repentance] Firing with Incubus will now activate Lead Pencil.

• Loki's Horns: Lead Pencil can fire in any of the cardinal directions if it fires at the same time as Loki's Horns.

• [Before Repentance] The Ludovico Technique: The tear blinks red, but the effect is entirely cosmetic.

• [Repentance] The Lead Pencil tears fire towards the Ludovico tear, locked to cardinal directions, every 15th damage tick.

• Incubus: Fires red tears like Blood Clot with Cain, but without increased damage.

• [Repentance] Incubus is capable of firing the barrage of tears like Isaac.

• [Before Repentance] Mom's Knife: Overrides Lead Pencil.

• [Repentance] The Lead Pencil tears fire alongside the knife, every 15th throw.

• Spirit Sword: The effect from Lead Pencil fires separately to Spirit Sword slashes.

• Sprinkler: No effect.

• Stye: The tears from the barrage will never have the bonus damage from Stye.

• [Before Repentance] Technology: Overrides Lead Pencil.

• [Repentance] A barrage of tears is fired alongside Technology every 15 shots.

• [Before Repentance] Technology 2: Overrides Lead Pencil and disables normal tears entirely, even if not playing as Cain.

• [Repentance] Replaces tears with lasers similar to Technology. These are shot from the eye that shoots Technology 2, dealing damage alongside the Technology 2 beam.

• Tech X: Overrides Lead Pencil.

• [Repentance] Every 15th laser ring fired also shoots a cluster of tears.

• Tiny Planet: The burst follows Tiny Planet's circular trajectory with minimal range, hitting the ground almost immediately.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Though the pencil is in Isaac's right eye, it blocks tears from firing out of his left eye.

fields.description: After every 15 tears fired, Isaac will fire a high-damage cluster of tears.

Leech.title: Leech
Leech.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the monster; Leech (Enemy)]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Spawns a crawling Leech familiar that follows Isaac. If an enemy comes near, the Leech will attack and chase it, doing 1.5 damage per tick or about 3.2 damage per second. If an enemy is killed by the Leech, Isaac will be healed by a Half Red Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] This item can rarely drop from destroying buckets in Downpour. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Wormwood. [end edition note] 

• The Leech's healing effect does not affect characters that do not have Heart containers.

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper will be healed by The Leech.

• Enemies that turn into flesh piles and regenerate when killed such as Globins and some dark red champions regenerate quicker than the Leech can kill them. Isaac will gain half a heart each time the enemies collapse, granting an easy way to regenerate all Red Hearts. This can also open up many powerful synergies with any item that provides a benefit or resource when Isaac takes damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Arcades: The player can let the Leech eat Fly from the Shell Game and use the resulting health to gamble on the Blood Donation Machine.

• BFFS!: Leech grows bigger and does double damage. Still only heals for a Half Red Heart.

• E. Coli: Enemies can be turned into Poop at the cost of a Half Red Heart, then consumed by the leech to regain health. Utilization of temporary immunity when hit can allow multiple enemies to be turned into poop, resulting in a net gain of health. However, when combined with Gnawed Leaf (see below), the player can simply stand still and let Leech do the dirty work.

• Flush!: The leech still can attack the enemies turned into poop and gain health.

• Gnawed Leaf: The player can stand still and allow the Leech to clear a room, granting simple clears and easy health.

• Tainted Bethany: The leech can grant blood charges by killing enemies.

• Tainted Magdalene: Leech restores a full Red Heart.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop are now treated as regular poop and can't be damaged by Leech.

• Maggy's Bow: No effect on healing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This familiar is notorious for having bad tracking AI.

Leech (Enemy).title: Leech (Enemy)
Leech (Enemy).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the monster; the item; Leech] 

Leeches are flying monsters introduced in the vanilla content of The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth.

Similar to Chargers, if Isaac lines up with a Leech horizontally or vertically, the Leech will quickly charge towards him. Leeches do a full heart of contact damage.

[Repentance] Leeches and their variants are immune to knockback.

sections.heading: Kamikaze Leech
sections.text:
Kamikaze Leeches are a unique type of Leech with an eye in their mouth. They are introduced in the vanilla content of The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth and commonly found in Sheol but can appear elsewhere such as Necropolis and Dark Room.

These behave similarly to normal Leeches, but explode upon death. They can be spawned by a couple of bosses, such as Satan's second form; as well, two of these will also appear to either side of The Fallen during the first phase of this battle.

sections.heading: Holy Leech
sections.text:
Holy Leeches are white-colored variants of the Kamikaze Leech commonly found in the Cathedral, but can occasionally appear in Utero.

These behave similarly to Kamikaze Leeches, but have an Eternal Fly circling them. Because the Holy Leech explodes upon death, the Eternal Fly will die instantly and only serves to block projectiles.

sections.heading: Small Leech
sections.text:
Small Leeches are small, juvenile versions of the Leech added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC.

They are quite similar to normal Leeches and make the same sound effect (albeit higher-pitched), but they have no knockback immunity, and continuously chase Isaac rather than only pursuing him if Isaac lines up with one horizontally or vertically. They are also very small in size and can swim over flooded gaps.

Primarily spawned by Prey and Lil Blub, and can be found in Buckets. They will also spawn during Wormwood's boss fight, after Wormwood charges out from the wall.

When in a room without water, Small Leeches make small, short hops towards Isaac.

sections.heading: Adult Leech
sections.text:
Adult Leeches are bigger and stronger versions of the Leech added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC.

They are characterized by their large size and much higher amount of health in comparison to typical Leeches. They behave like Leeches but will only charge horizontally and release a ring of 12 blood shots in all directions upon colliding with a wall. Upon taking a certain amount of damage, they burrow underground then reappear by attempting to crash into Isaac from above (a sound cue will play prior to it crashing down) and sending out a ring of 10 blood shots in all directions on impact, which only occurs once per Adult Leech.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Kamikaze Leech was first added in the Halloween update for the original Flash version of The Binding of Isaac.

• Holy Leech was first added in the original Flash game's Wrath of the Lamb DLC.

• The Leech's charging sound effect is, in reality, a man saying "EHHH" sped up. This can be revealed by listening to the attack sound of a Large Champion Leech.

• [Repentance] The Small Leech and Adult Leech first appeared in the fan DLC Antibirth.

• The Adult Leech's design is from a mockup for a Corpse altfloor by artist NotYourSagittarius created in February 2015.

Lemegeton.title: Lemegeton
Lemegeton.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: It is the starting item for Tainted Bethany.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Lemegeton will grant a random passive item as an orbital familiar. The item summoned has a 25% chance to be from the current room's Item Pool, or from a random item pool otherwise. The item must have the 'summonable' item tag in order to be generated.

• These familiars can block up to 4 shots and/or get hit by 2 explosions before being destroyed. When the familiar is destroyed, the item it granted is lost.

• • If Isaac is shielded or invulnerable, his familiars are also immune to damage.

• Familiars also deal contact damage to enemies equal to 2× Isaac's damage per tick (4× Isaac's damage per second). They take contact damage.

• Isaac can have up to 26 familiars: an inner counterclockwise ring of 6, a middle clockwise ring with 8, and an outer counterclockwise ring of 12.

• • Using Lemegeton while Isaac already has 26 causes the oldest one to be replaced.

• Contributes to the Bookworm transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tainted Bethany starts with this item in the consumable slot.

• When playing as Tainted Bethany, picking up 4.5 Volt will cause Lemegeton to no longer gain charges as long as her normal active item has empty charges.

• Items given by Lemegeton are separate from the normal item pools and Isaac's current collection of items. This has the following effects:

• Isaac can still normally find items that were previously summoned by Lemegeton.

• Isaac can have multiple wisps of the same item.

• Wisps cannot be rerolled by Missing No. or the D4 / D100.

• Wisps do not count towards transformations.

• • Super Bum is an exception and can be gotten from wisps.

• Summoned items do not count towards the Collection Page.

• Items that would normally add or remove hearts/consumables (such as Boom!, Breakfast, Abaddon, etc.) do not do so if given by Lemegeton.

• Summoning a Birthright wisp grants Tainted Lost infinite lives until the wisp is destroyed.

• Wisps of mapping items only activate upon entering the next floor.

• [Repentance+] Wisps of mapping items' effect are applied immediately.

sections.heading: Random pool choices
sections.text:
When Lemegeton chooses an item pool different than the current room's, the chances are as follows. In Greed Mode, the mode's own pools are used except for the Planetarium. Probabilities are rounded to nearest 0.1%, so the totals may not be exactly 100%. 

| Item pool | Normal Mode probability | Greed Mode probability

| Treasure | 57.5% | 52.6%

| Boss | 17.2% | 15.8%

| Shop | 17.2% | 26.3%

| Angel | 2.3% | 2.1%

| Devil | 2.3% | 2.1%

| Curse | 1.1% | 0%

| Secret | 1.1% | 0%

| Planetarium | 1.1% | 1.1%

sections.heading: Excluded Items
sections.text: The following passive items cannot be spawned by Lemegeton.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Doubles the damage of Wisps.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Lets Lemegeton's wisps shoot homing tears once per second that deal 3 damage.

• Also applies to Tainted Bethany's Lemegeton, despite not being visually shown.

• Rock Bottom: Stat increases remain even after its wisp has been destroyed.

• Satanic Bible: Using Lemegeton in a Boss Room after activating the Satanic Bible on that floor will pull from the Devil Room item pool, even if the boss wouldn't normally drop an item after defeat.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Box of Friends: Does not double the wisps spawned by Lemegeton.

• Car Battery: Two wisps are created on use, only the name of the second item is displayed. If a Car Battery wisp is created, another wisp is summoned immediately.

• Chaos: Item wisps will be selected from random pools, regardless of the room Isaac is in.

• Magic Skin: Can be spawned by Lemegeton if it has been used in the current run.

• Sacred Orb: Generated wisps are affected by Sacred Orb.

• Sacrificial Altar: Every wisp will be converted to a Half Soul Heart. Familiars created by Lemegeton are sacrificed normally.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Lemegeton is another name for the Lesser Key of Solomon, an anonymous grimoire focused on demonology that was compiled in the 17th century.

• The symbol on the cover of Lemegeton may be the Seal of Solomon.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: After using Genesis, Isaac keeps the passive effects of each wisp until the next use of Lemegeton, which erases all lingering wisp effects.
Bug note: If a run is exited and resumed while Isaac has item wisps generated from Lemegeton, all wisps will be condensed into the middle clockwise ring, even if this would result in more wisps on that ring than normally allowed. This also allows further wisps to be generated on the inner and outer rings.
Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again) will duplicate the wisps. Creating wisps in this way allows Isaac to exceed the item's wisp limit.

fields.description: Spawns a destructible orbital familiar representing a random passive item, which blocks shots and deals contact damage. While the wisp is alive, Isaac gains that item's effects.

Polty.title: Polty
Polty.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Polty is an enemy added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

Unlike normal enemies, Polties appear from inside Buckets or Urns in the current room. They then pick up the obstacle they were under, fly towards Isaac, and then throw it at him. For the rest of the room, it will fly around the room, stopping to pick up more rocks, props, poops, and other obstacles and throw them at Isaac. Thrown obstacles have the same chance to release pickups or enemies as if they had been destroyed normally. Once there are no more rocks to throw at Isaac, they will leave the room.

Polties prefer to pick up Buckets and TNT over normal rocks, with the exception of Metal Blocks and Spiked Rocks, which they cannot pick up. If there's a Tinted Rock, it will avoid picking it up until there's no other rocks left to throw. When it finally does pick it up, it will fly offscreen with it instead of throwing it at Isaac. If the Polty is killed before it successfully runs away with the rock, it will give its contents like normal.

Destroying the Bucket or Urn which a Polty is hiding beneath will cause it to spawn and then behave normally.

Once Haunted Chests are unlocked, Polties may be encountered anywhere. After being spawned by approaching the chest, they grab it and throw it at Isaac, then act normally.

sections.heading: Kineti
sections.text:
Kineti is the Mausoleum variant of a Polty and behave similarly to their counterpart, with the exception that they use telekinesis to bring obstacles toward them rather than moving towards them and picking them up manually. The obstacles can damage Isaac while being pulled towards the Kineti.

Kinetis will prioritize picking up rocks that would hit Isaac while being pulled towards itself. They are also knocked back by the force of the rock they carry once it enters their hands. If there are no more obstacles for them to pick up, similar to Polties, they will exit the room, and if they choose to pick up a Tinted Rock, they will fly offscreen with it instead of throwing it at Isaac.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Polty first appeared in the Antibirth mod where it had 20 hp and 3 stage hp.

• "Polty" is a nickname of the word "poltergeist" as it behaves quite similarly to one. In lore, poltergeists are known to be "responsible for physical disturbances, such as loud noises and objects being moved or destroyed."

• "Kineti" is a shortened version of the word "kinetic," which describes the form of energy that an object possesses due to its motion.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Petrifying Kinetis while they are pulling a rock towards them causes the rock to keep flying and can cause it to fly out of the room.

Angel Room.title: Angel Room
Angel Room.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Angel Rooms are the divine equivalent of the Devil Room. They feature an angel and 0-4 free items. Taking one of these items causes all other free items to disappear. (Tainted Keeper still needs to pay for these items, and buying any of them causes all of the others to disappear. Some of these items cost 30 pennies to buy.)

Every time the Devil Room is spawned/entered, there's a chance for it to be replaced by the Angel Room if certain conditions are met. After beating the Dark Room or Chest once, an Angel can be awoken by planting a bomb near the statue (or destroying it with Leo or similar items). This will begin an angel boss fight and allow Isaac to charge his active item and pick up Key Piece 1 or Key Piece 2. Both pieces are needed to get through the Golden Door in Chest or Dark Room to fight Mega Satan.

sections.heading: Conditions to Make Angel Rooms Appear
sections.text:
For the player to have a chance to get an Angel Room after killing a boss (or with a Joker card / Red Chest teleport), some conditions must be met:

• A Devil Room door has spawned on any previous floor.

• Teleporting to a Devil Room with a Joker card or a Red Chest doesn't count.

• [Repentance] Book of Virtues and the "You feel blessed!" fortune from Confessionals make the first deal to appear in a run to be an Angel Room. [end edition note] 

• No Deals with the Devil have been made throughout the run.

• Taking Red Chest items, using Credit Card, using Coupon, or collecting an item from Krampus do not count.

• Even though it technically doesn't cost any health, taking a Devil Deal with The Lost will still prevent Angel Rooms from appearing.

• [Repentance] Paying for Devil Room items from Boss Rooms after using Satanic Bible will still prevent Angel Rooms from spawning. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Book of Virtues and Act of Contrition allow for Angel Rooms to spawn even if a Devil Deal was taken previously, as well as allowing to take Devil Deals without being locked out of Angel Rooms. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The "You feel blessed!" fortune from Confessionals allow for Angel Rooms to spawn even if a Devil Deal was taken previously, but only for the current floor. [end edition note]

sections.heading: [Afterbirth onward] Sacrifice Room Exception
sections.text:
• On the 3rd and 5th sacrifice in a Sacrifice Room, there is a 66% chance that the player will receive the "You feel blessed!" effect. This will increase the chances of the Angel Room spawning even if the previous conditions have not been met.

• On the 6th sacrifice in a Sacrifice Room, there is a 33% chance that the player will be teleported to the Angel Room if they haven't already visited or opened the Devil Room for that floor. This will occur even if the previous conditions have not been met.

sections.heading: Angel Room Generation Chance
sections.text:
The selection between Angel Room and Devil Room is made upon opening the door after defeating the floor's boss (or upon teleporting to the room using a Joker card or a Red Chest).

The game makes a series of coin flips to determine if an Angel Room will appear or not. If one of these coin flips succeeds, an Angel Room is generated (except for the Devil beggar coin flip). If all the coin flips fail or no coin flips are done, a Devil Room is generated. Satisfying certain conditions gives additional coin flips with varying probabilities:

| Condition | Chance Bonus 
| Base chance | 50%

| Donating 10 coins to the Donation Machine on the current floor | 50%

| Holding Key Piece 1 | 25%

| Holding Key Piece 2 | 25%

| [Before Repentance+] Killing a Devil Beggar on the current floor **

• [Rebirth only] Killing Key Masters and Shell Game Beggars also applies the bonus. | 25%

| Donating to a Beggar until it pays out with an item on the current floor **

• Making a [Before Repentance+] Key Master, [edition anr+] Bomb Bum [end edition note] , or Shell Game pay out does not apply the bonus. | 25%
[Afterbirth onward] 10%

| Donating to a Devil Beggar until it pays out with an item on the current floor **

• [Afterbirth onward] If this coin flip succeeds, a Devil Room will be generated regardless of the above coin flips. | -25%
[Afterbirth onward] -10%

| [Afterbirth onward] "You feel blessed!" fortune in the Sacrifice Room of the current floor

• If the "You feel blessed!" fortune appeared on the 3rd sacrifice, the chance will be 15%.

• If the "You feel blessed!" fortune appeared on the 5th sacrifice, the chance will be 50%.

• If both "You feel blessed!" fortunes appeared, the chance will be 65%. | 15/50/65%

| [Repentance] "You feel blessed" fortune from Confessionals on the current floor

• The bonus is additive and goes up to 100% with 10 activations. [end edition note] | 10%

| Holding Rosary Bead | [Before Repentance+] 50%
[Repentance+] Guaranteed

| [Repentance] Holding Book of Virtues [end edition note] 

• While held, The Book guarantees the first encountered Devil/Angel Room to be an Angel Room. | 12.5%
Guaranteed

| [Afterbirth+ onward] Having Eucharist [end edition note] | Guaranteed

| [Repentance] First successful generation after seeing but not entering the first Devil Room of a run | Guaranteed

** These conditions share the same "coin flip chance" in Rebirth.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.text:
If Isaac meets the prerequisites and has Key Piece 1 with him, the game will make two coin flips to determine if he gets an Angel Room or not. The first coin flip has a 50% success chance and the second one has a 25% success chance. Isaac will only get a Devil Room if both coin flips fail, and he will get an Angel Room if one of the coin flips succeeds. The chance of failure is 0.5 * 0.75 = 0.375, which means the chance of success is 1 - 0.375 = 0.625. Thus, Isaac has a 62.5% chance to get an Angel Room—take note that the result is not simply the sum of the coin flip probabilities 50% + 25% for 75%.

If Isaac meets the prerequisites, has Key Piece 1, and a Beggar paid on the current floor, the chance to fail all coin flips (and get a Devil Room) become 0.5 * 0.75 * 0.75 = 0.28125, which means that the chance of success is 1 - 0.28125 = 0.71875. Thus, Isaac has a 71.875% chance to get an Angel Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The highest Angel Room chance is 95.25% in Rebirth and 98.34% in Afterbirth (with the Sacrifice Room blessings).

• If an Angel Room spawns after the player defeats Mom's Heart or It Lives!, instead of items or pickups, a beam of light will appear. Touching this beam of light will take the player to the Cathedral. The Angel can still be awoken by destroying the statue in this room. The beam of light will disappear for the duration of the fight.

• [Afterbirth onward] Angel Rooms that spawn after Isaac defeats It Lives! will be normal Angel Rooms with items or pickups.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The rock behind the Angel statue can rarely be a Tinted Rock.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Two angel statues can appear in the same room, allowing Isaac to fight both Uriel and Gabriel. It is possible to get both Key Pieces if Isaac awakes and fights each of them one by one; however, fighting both at once will only spawn one Key Piece corresponding to the last defeated angel.

• [Repentance] Both angels can be fought at once, and will drop their corresponding Key Pieces as they die.

• Contrary to popular belief, the Bible Tract doesn't allow Angel Rooms to appear after paying for a Devil Deal.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The Found HUD will incorrectly display the angel room chance as 100% if either of the "Blessed" messages appear. The percentages listed in this page are however correct.

Arcade.title: Arcade
Arcade.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
An Arcade is a special room that can only spawn on an even-numbered floor (Basement II, Caves II, Depths II, Womb II) if you have 5 coins or more when you leave the previous floor. Arcades require one coin to be opened. They can be replaced with a Vault if Isaac is carrying two keys or more.

• Arcades cannot spawn on XL floors.

• [Repentance] Unless it is on an alt path floor.

• [Repentance] Arcades can spawn on the first floor of the alternate chapters (Downpour I, Mines I, Mausoleum I, Corpse I). [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The posters that can appear on the arcade's walls are pictures of games that Edmund McMillen has worked on, such as Gish, Super Meat Boy, and Time Fcuk.

Ascent.title: Ascent
Ascent.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Ascent is a special sequence begun by obtaining Dad's Note from the special versions of the Mausoleum/Gehenna II. These floors can be accessed by opening the special door in the starting room of the Depths II or its variants. This door appears once Isaac has defeated Mother at least once. It involves going back up through abbreviated versions of every floor previously seen through beams of light. Much like the Backasswards challenge, Isaac begins in the boss room of each floor and must find the beam of light, located in the corresponding starting room.

These abbreviated versions contain the same Treasure Rooms and Boss Rooms as they did previously, in almost the same condition.

• Any trinkets left behind in these rooms, however, will each be transformed into a Cracked Key.

All the other special rooms do not spawn.

• Special Red Rooms still have the normal chance to be generated.

Monsters not normally found on the current floor will appear, as well as unique room layouts and new monsters not found anywhere else in the game.

After leaving the Mausoleum II, Isaac will begin taking full heart damage, as would otherwise occur on entering any variant of the Womb or the Corpse.

Entering the Basement I's light beam will take Isaac to Home.

sections.heading: Unique Monsters
sections.text: This table lists all of the unique monsters that only spawn during the ascent. These enemies are based on normal enemies from the individual pre-ascent chapters they are seen in, but are far tougher.

sections.heading: Regular Monsters
sections.text:
When the game makes a small mock floor to take the place of each original floor/chapter Isaac descended through before the ascent, it populates each new floor mostly with its pre-ascent chapter-specific enemies. However, the Ascent enemy pools are altered to allow enemies from later floors.

These are the tables of enemies the game spawns to populate its specific ascent mock chapters.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If any variant floors were encountered during descent, all floors of the Ascent will still be the original ones. For example, if the second floor on a run was the Cellar II or the Burning Basement II, during the Ascent, it will be replaced by the Basement II regardless. This includes alternate chapters, such as the Downpour, and so on.

• However, it's still possible to access them through the use of Debug Console.

• Isaac won't encounter any curses during the Ascent, except [cu: Labyrinth] if it was on the original floor.

• When encountering [cu: Blind] , it may be a good idea to skip boss and treasure room items, as they will be revealed during the Ascent.

• XL floors in the Ascent will contain both Treasure Rooms from the original floor.

• Red Treasure Rooms found through the Red Key during the original run will automatically show up during the Ascent, and will be adjacent to normal rooms. These doors do not require keys to open.

• Any unopened Treasure Rooms on previous floors will still be locked during the Ascent.

• If these skipped Treasure Rooms are entered during the ascent, they will contain different items. This is best viewed with the effect of Dream Catcher.

• This also means a strategy is to skip Treasure Rooms early in a run to spawn a Planetarium, and then get the skipped Treasure Room items during the Ascent. However, there's no need to keep doing it after encountering a Planetarium, since the probability to encounter it will stay at 1%.

• Angel Rooms and Devil Rooms will have different contents than on the original path.

• Since the Boss Rooms have already been cleared during descent, Devil Rooms and Angel Rooms won't open during the Ascent, and can only be accessed with teleport effects.

• The special Angel Room Shops generated by The Stairway will also have different contents.

• During the Ascent, both items in a double item Treasure Room are visible.

• Items and trinkets that activate on entering the floor, such as Maggy's Faith, will trigger each time Isaac ascends a floor.

• If pickups were transported to another floor from the Treasure or Boss Room by Myosotis, their copies will remain in those rooms and can be encountered during the Ascent. Affected trinkets still transform into Cracked Keys, potentially allowing you to gain large amounts of Cracked Keys.

• Myosotis will work on the Ascent, and can be used to bring an additional pickup if holding a Cracked Key.

• In each floor, after exploring all normal rooms, using Teleport 2.0 will teleport Isaac to the Angel Room/Devil Room, since Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms will not spawn.

• If a floor is restarted, which can be accomplished through using Forget Me Now or by finding a Red 5-pip Dice Room, the following effects will happen:

• No dream animations will be shown when restarting.

• The regenerated floor will still be an Ascent floor, not a descent floor.

• If the floor was an XL one, the regenerated floor will also be XL.

• If the Treasure Room was skipped during descent, and during the Ascent its contents were seen, after restarting it will contain different items.

• All Cracked Keys in either the Boss Room or the Treasure Room will remain there, even if they were used before restarting.

• The I AM ERROR room can be reached during the ascent. I AM ERROR rooms will mimic the layout that they had corresponding to the floor. Rather than containing a trapdoor, they will contain a beam of light leading up to the next floor.

• Entering an I AM ERROR room in Gehenna II (before the Ascent) takes Isaac to the starting room of the floor.

• No consumable voice lines will be spoken during the Ascent.

• Jacob and Esau will overlap one other when ascending to a new floor. This effect stops upon pressing the Swap key or entering a new room.

• During the descent, it is recommended to leave any abandoned Trinkets in Treasure Rooms or Boss Rooms, so that the resulting Cracked Keys can be used during the Ascent, which could potentially create special rooms containing items or other useful pickups.

• If the Boss Music would play, it plays the Boss Music for the alternate path rather than the Boss Music for the main path. One way to make Boss Music play is to find an Angel Room by using a Red Key/Cracked Key.

• If a Boss is not fought during the descent (e.g. if it was skipped using We Need To Go Deeper!), the Boss Room will still be empty during the Ascent.

• Portals to The Void that spawn after the Mom fight will still appear in the boss room during Ascent, however they will be permanently closed.

sections.heading: Dialogue
sections.text:
At various points during the Ascent, arguments between Isaac's parents can be heard, shedding some light on the fractured state of Isaac's family.

| Stage | Dialogue | Audio 
| At the start of the Mausoleum II | • Dad: "I spent it, it's gone. Just get over it!"

• Mom: "What do you mean, what do you mean it's gone? How could you have spent our savings?!" |

| At the start of the Depths I / Mines II | • Mom: "He's self-destructive and disturbed, just like his father! Look at who he has to look up to! ...And you're drunk again, aren't you?"

• Dad: "Shut up, Maggy! SHUT! UP! You just keep pushing me like this, I'm leaving!"

• Mom: "Good! LEAVE! We'll be fine without you! Abandon us like you abandoned yourself..." |

| At the start of the Caves I / Downpour II | • Mom: "You need to repent. You need to confess your sins, and become saved! Let His light inside you! CLEANSE YOUR SOU-"

• Dad: "You. Are. INSANE. You are taking this too far. Can't you hear how you sound!?"

• Mom: "Pray with me... Pray for your salvation! Come, pray with us, Isaac..." |

| At the start of the Basement I | • (The sound of a door opening and footsteps are heard)

• Mom: "Where are you going?! Wait! We need you! Your son NEEDS you!"

• Dad: "I'm doing more harm than good. I just can't do this anymore, I'm sorry."

• Mom: "PLEASE! PLEASE DON'T LEAVE US...!!"

• Dad: "I'm sorry, Isaac..." |

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Ascent is referred to as "backwards" in the sequence's rooms file.

• According to an interview with _Kilburn, the tainted enemies were designed with inspiration from eternal champion monsters in The Binding of Isaac: Eternal Edition.

• Great Gideon can be seen in its boss room during the Ascent. However, since he was already defeated on the way down, he will be deactivated.

• Even if he was encountered in the Ashpit during the normal descent, he will still appear in the Mines during the Ascent.

• He can still be destroyed by using the Chaos Card, to reveal the unique 1x2 Crawl Space.

• If he was previously destroyed with the Chaos Card before the ascent, he will be missing during the ascent.

• What sounds like a reversed version of Genesis Retake Light can be heard playing during the Ascent, and as the ascent progresses, more instruments are added to it based on the floors Isaac ascends through.

• The Mausoleum adds a crunchy, electric bass line.

• The Depths adds occasional guitar riffs and a unique composition.

• The Mines adds a drum line and metal clanking sounds.

• The Caves adds a standard bass line.

• The Downpour adds a fuller guitar line with an echo effect.

• The Basement adds a full drum line.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Dropping a trinket in the exact same spot as an obstacle may despawn Cracked Key further down the road during Ascension.

Ashpit.title: Ashpit
Ashpit.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Ashpit is an alternative floor to the Mines and is unlocked by defeating all of the bosses inside the Mines. The floor can be accessed by using bombs on the Exit Door of the Caves/Catacombs/Flooded Caves I or II, or at the end of Downpour/Dross. Ashpit's theme is centered around a dry, crumbling wasteland, with an abundance of skeleton enemies and brutal-looking foes.

The Ashpit is significantly more difficult than their standard counterparts, filled with stone and bone-themed enemies that boast greater health and aggression. Most obstacles are rocks or Spiked Rocks, and Poops are almost non-existent. Tinted Rocks have a high chance of spawning Tinted Rock Spiders. Travelling through it is only advised if you have already acquired Knife Piece 1 in Downpour and intend to access the Corpse.

After defeating the Mines II's boss, a door leading to the next alternate chapter - Mausoleum - appears. It requires 2 full hearts to open. The damage taken ignores almost every form of damage reduction, including The Wafer and invincibility. Unlike other methods of health donation, red hearts will not be prioritized over more valuable hearts.

sections.heading: Knife Piece
sections.text:
If you have Knife Piece 1, a special double-sized room will spawn in Ashpit II containing a minecart and a broken length of rail track leading to a boarded up door, just like those that lead to a Bedroom. Behind this door lies the area in which Knife Piece 2 can be acquired. There are two methods for accessing this area:

• If you have flight and 2 Bombs, you can simply fly over to the boarded up door and blow it open. It is also accessible with flight and an item with an effect that opens doors such as Dad's Key, Soul of Cain, Cracked Orb, etc.

• Otherwise, you can repair the track. There are three Rail Plates spread throughout the floor. One will be in the same room as the broken rail track, but the other two are randomly placed. Once all three buttons are pressed, the rail track will be repaired and you can touch the minecart to access the area.

Upon entering this area, all passive and active items will be rendered inactive, and your Bombs, Penny, and Keys will be set to zero. New pickups can still be obtained, however, and will persist after Isaac leaves the area. You will pass through several empty rooms before reaching a room with the Knife Piece 2. Once you pick it up, Mother's Shadow will spawn and your race back to the entrance begins. This enemy cannot be defeated by any means, and escape is your only option.

Unlike your initial trip to reach the Knife Piece 2, the path back will be obstructed by rocks and Poops. While flying characters can handle all of this with ease, walking characters will have a significantly harder time. Using your tears and the conveniently located Throwable Bombs, you will need to break through the obstructions, press buttons, and grab keys for Key Blocks to make it back to the main dungeon. Making it out taking little or no damage is possible, particularly if you are fast and accustomed to dodging the shadow's attacks. Once you escape, all your items will be reactivated, and the shadow will end its pursuit.

• It is possible for the floor's Crawl Space to appear on your escape path. Upon entry, your items will temporarily be reactivated, and you will be able to pick up any items/consumables available. Items will become inactive again after exiting. Mother's Shadow will still appear in the crawl space, and the enclosed area makes the dodging of her attacks very difficult. Furthermore, if a key is required to complete an obstacle on the way back, and it is picked up before entering the crawl space, it will be lost and could make the obstacle impossible.

• The Black Market can also appear in a crawlspace. Entering the trapdoor will complete the escape sequence.

sections.heading: Music
sections.text: • The music for the Ashpit is called Absentia. Absentia is the Latin word for absence, likely because a "ashpit" is generally what remains after everything has burned away in a wildfire.

Basement.title: Basement
Basement.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Basement is one of the environments in Chapter 1. Unlocked at the beginning of the game, it is considered the easiest of the environments in the game. The theme of the Basement is flies and poop.

The Basement's harder unlockable variants are the Cellar and the Burning Basement.

[Repentance] After A Secret Exit is unlocked, a locked door similar to the one leading to a Treasure Room will appear in this floor's Boss Room upon defeating the boss, which leads to Downpour / Dross. Like a Treasure Room, this door requires a key to be unlocked. Unlike Angel Rooms and Devil Rooms, this door never disappears. [end edition note]

Black Market.title: Black Market
Black Market.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Black Markets are unique shops that can be accessed through a Crawl Space. Black Markets are 2 rooms wide. The left side of the Black Market contains a door back to the crawlspace and a trapdoor or beam of light to the next floor (including the Dark Room or Chest, even if they haven't been unlocked yet). The center of the room contains several items from the Shop pool that can all be bought for 1 Red Heart container. [Before Repentance] Although these will not be Devil Room items, they still count as Devil deals for Angel Room generation and unlocking Azazel. [Repentance] This is no longer the case, and Isaac can buy items from the Black Market without affecting the spawn chances of Angel rooms. The rest of the room will be strewn about with Shopkeepers, pickups, and various Beggars and machines.

Telepills, Undefined, and [Repentance+] Cursed Penny [end edition note] have a very small chance to teleport you to the Black Market, but there will be no door exiting back to a Crawl Space. This means that without another way to teleport, the player will be forced to proceed to the next level, like in an I AM ERROR Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] Exiting the Black Market through the beam of light in Chest or Dark Room causes the floor to restart (in a similar fashion to Forget Me Now), as there are no floors further than these two. This can come in handy to gather a lot of items. The same applies to I AM ERROR.

• [Afterbirth onward] Black Markets and I AM ERROR can no longer be accessed in Chest or Dark Room.

• • [Repentance] I AM ERROR rooms can be accessed by exiting a Crawl Space in an unintended direction.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Black Markets and I AM ERROR can be found in The Void. Using the trapdoor causes the floor to restart (in a similar fashion to Forget Me Now). [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Players can no longer access the Black Market through the wall glitch. However, it is still possible to access the Black Market using the glitch via special circumstances including having Ipecac and The Inner Eye.

• The Lost can take items from the Black Market for free, just like with regular devil deals.

• [Repentance] The Lost can take only one item from each selection of items. When an item is taken, the others disappear.

• [Repentance] If a Black Market is found in the Mirrored World and is populated using a Shop Restock Machine, it will follow the rules of the non-mirrored character. Despite playing as The Lost in this area, multiple items can be purchased, and health will be deducted from the non-mirrored character, possibly resulting in death.

• [Repentance] When playing as Keeper, the items are sold for money instead, making it no different from a regular Shop.

• [Repentance] When two crawl spaces lead to a Black Market in the same floor, they lead to the same Black Market.

• [Repentance] During the Ascent, crawlspaces with Black Markets lead to an I AM ERROR room instead.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • In the game files, every Black Market room is named "# - The Black Market (Racist Placeholder) (copy)", which can be seen with the "Debug 5" command.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Creating and entering a trapdoor which also leads to a Black Market (for example by We Need To Go Deeper! or an Ehwaz rune) results in not being able to escape the Black Market other than going to the next floor.
Bug note: Using Telepills or Undefined to enter a black market in the mirrored world on Downpour II and Dross II will generate a black market with no items and no exits. Without any other means of teleporting, this will softlock a run.

Blighted Ovum.title: Blighted Ovum
Blighted Ovum.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Blighted Ovum is a boss that can appear in the Cellar.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Blighted Ovum starts separated into two parts.

• Suture, now a ghost, is invincible and slowly floats towards Isaac, firing a horizontal Brimstone shot whenever Isaac is to his left or right. Suture cannot be killed and will die once Contusion does.

• Contusion constantly chases Isaac while leaving behind a trail of Red Creep, and he periodically charges and gains speed. Unlike Gemini, he will not stop for a breath but slows down to his regular speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Suture can be killed by Little Horn. [end edition note] 

• If encountered in a Double Trouble boss fight, Suture's Brimstone laser can damage the other boss.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Blighted Ovum was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original game, Blighted Ovum could also be encountered in the Catacombs.

• They are the posthumous version of Gemini.

• In medicine, a blighted ovum is a pregnancy in which the early pregnancy appears normal on an ultrasound scan, but later no visible embryo develops.

• [Before Repentance] Contusion has skin on his body in the boss art, but he doesn't in-game.

• Blighted Ovum is the only boss in chapter 1 that is a posthumous version of another boss.

• Gemini also shows up in chapter 1, which makes it one of only four bosses to have its posthumous version in the same chapter, the other cases being Polycephalus and Chub having The Stain and Carrion Queen, respectively, in chapter 2; [Repentance] and the Tuff Twins having The Shell in Chapter 2.5. [end edition note] 

• In Wrath of The Lamb, when Blighted Ovum was killed, Contusion would shoot 8 extremely fast tears in the cardinal and ordinal directions, and after a short delay, would be followed up by Suture, who would explode similarly.

• In the Bestiary, Suture is referred to as "The Blighted Ovum Baby".

• [Repentance] Blighted Ovum, Big Horn, Triachnid, Isaac, and ??? are the only bosses whose portraits were completely changed in Repentance (beyond simply adding more detail). Of these, only Triachnid, Isaac, and ??? didn't receive new sprites. [end edition note] 

• In Rebirth, the older boss portrait had Suture smiling in it, which was the 2nd time he had a smile.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: [Before Afterbirth+] The D10 can reroll the Suture half of Blighted Ovum.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Burning Basement is one of the environments in chapter 1 added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth. The theme of the Burning Basement is fire, and most enemies are replaced with burning versions. There are relatively few flying or shooting enemies; most of the enemies are ground-based and rely on contact damage. [Before Repentance] Rocks have a chance to be replaced with Fire Places.

The Burning Basement's alternate floors are the Basement and the Cellar.

[Afterbirth+ onward] The Burning Basement is unlocked by defeating Mom's Heart 11 times.

[Repentance] After A Secret Exit is unlocked, a locked door similar to the one leading to a Treasure Room will appear in this floor's Boss Room upon defeating the boss leading to Downpour / Dross. Like a Treasure Room, this door requires a key to be unlocked. Unlike Angel Room and Devil Rooms, this door never disappears. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Cathedral is one of two floors following the Womb / Utero / Scarred Womb, the other being Sheol. After defeating Mom's Heart, depending on Isaac's deal chance, an Angel Room may spawn which will only contain a beam of light leading upwards to the Cathedral. Other methods to enter the deal room such as Joker or Red Chests will work too. It's also possible to enter Cathedral via the beam of light in I AM ERROR Rooms. Unlocking and defeating It Lives! will always spawn a beam of light leading to the Cathedral, as well as a trapdoor leading to Sheol.

The Cathedral has only one floor, featuring mostly undead and/or holy enemies, and the boss is always Isaac.

Blue Fire Places are far more common in this floor than normally.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] Some rooms contain Angel Statues that can be bombed to summon the Angels and [Before Repentance] acquire key pieces.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original Binding of Isaac, the windows along the walls were much larger and had different patterns resembling Isaac and a crucifix.

• The floor's theme, Everlasting Hymn, is one of the few tracks, together with Morning Star, Living in the Light and Revelations 13-1, that contains actual lyrics: Dei, quod reliquum est, Nolite metuere, Et ossa tua liberabit, Exspectans.

• Even though the Latin in the song likely contains a few mistakes (like dei, which can only mean "of god" or "the gods" as subject of the sentence, or the inconsistency between the singular vocative "expectans" and the plural verb "nolite metuere"), the more accurate translation would be: "O thou who await, ye shan't fear what is left of God, and He will set thy bones free." Considering the fact that Isaac believes that killing himself is the morally correct thing to do (as he sees himself as being sinful or corrupted), the lyrics are encouraging Isaac to stay in the box and suffocate as his body panics for air.

• The theme of Cathedral (Everlasting Hymn) is noticeably shorter than other floor themed soundtracks. The second layer of the theme (for when entering a room with enemies and bosses with a high HP count) wasn't added in the official OST, with the in-game second track being barely noticeable chants. The Dark Room's theme (Devoid) is also shorter, but actually lacks the second, intense part of the track.

• [Repentance] Interestingly, Cathedral was the only non-final level with no unique enemies. This was why it was given some enemies exclusive to the floor in Repentance (those being Holy Mulligans, Holy Eyes, and Holy Bony).

• Holy Eyes, Holy Bonies, and Holy Mulligans were first seen in cards from the card game The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls. [end edition note]

Challenge Room.title: Challenge Room
Challenge Room.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: A Challenge Room is a special room that allows Isaac to fight enemies for extra rewards. They will only spawn on a floor if, upon entering the floor, Isaac's total health is greater than or equal to his number of heart containers. There are two kinds of challenge rooms: Normal Challenge Rooms, which appear on the first floor of a chapter or on [cu: Labyrinth] floors, and Boss Challenge Rooms, which appear on the second floor of a chapter. Challenge rooms do not appear in chapter 6.

sections.heading: Normal Challenge Room
sections.text:
Normal Challenge Rooms can only be entered via their doors if Isaac's total health (Red, Black, and Soul Hearts) is greater than or equal to his number of heart containers. Picking up its contents will cause three waves of enemies to spawn. While in chapter 4 (Womb/Utero/Scarred Womb), 3 waves of bosses will be spawned, typically from Chapters 1 or 2.

[Afterbirth+ onward] Each wave cleared will charge Isaac's active item by 1.

sections.heading: [Before Repentance] Waves
sections.text:
The enemies that spawn depend on the current chapter, and each chapter has two different possible sets of enemies:

| Floor | Wave 1 | Wave 2 | Wave 3 
| Basement | 3 Hoppers | 3 Horfs | 2 Clotty

| 5 Attack Fly | 5 Pooters | 4 Gapers

sections.heading: Boss Challenge Room
sections.text:
Boss Challenge Rooms will only spawn if Isaac has full health upon entering the second floor of a chapter, and can also only be entered via their doors if he has one or fewer hearts of health. Picking up its contents will cause two waves of bosses to spawn. Starting on Chapter 4, they use the same waves of bosses as Normal Challenge Rooms.

[Afterbirth+ onward] Each wave cleared will charge Isaac's active item by 1.

[Before Repentance] The Boss Challenge Room door only counts Red Hearts in determining whether Isaac is allowed to enter. Soul Hearts are ignored.

[Repentance] Boss Challenge Rooms require one or fewer hearts total to enter, counting Soul Hearts. Boss Challenge Rooms will always contain an item from the Boss.

The bosses that spawn depend on the current chapter. Alternate floors have two possible sets of bosses that could spawn:
