sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Temporary Tattoo will cause an additional chest to spawn after a normal Challenge Room is completed as well as cause an additional item from the Boss to spawn after completing a Boss Challenge Room.

• [Afterbirth onward] The waves appear in random orders rather than the orders listed above.

• If Isaac has some way to teleport out of the room, the contents of the Challenge Room can be taken without fighting the enemies.

• If a trigger to start a challenge room is left in the room after teleporting out (such as a chest or active item) or an item is spawned in the room and collected (such as rewards from Beggars or Blood Donation Machines), the challenge room will start over when it is picked up/opened.

• If a Secret Room is next to a Challenge Room, it can be entered by using a bomb in the Secret Room on the wall separating the two rooms. However, the entrance to the Secret Room from the Challenge Room will be closed when waves are active, meaning Isaac cannot escape through the Secret Room entrance.

• If Spiders spawn from a Red Chest before or during a wave, the Spiders have to be killed in order for the waves to start/continue.

• If Spiders spawn from a Red Chest after the challenge room is cleared, Isaac can leave the room without fighting them.

• Because of the health requirements, both types of Challenge Room will always be open for The Lost, Tainted Lost [Before Repentance] and ???.

• [Repentance] As Boss Challenge Rooms now take soul hearts into account, Soul Heart characters are now also forced to be at one heart before being allowed access.

• Doors to challenge rooms can be opened regardless of health with Dad's Key, Get out of Jail Free Card, Mr. ME!, or Soul of Cain.

• Boss Challenge Room doors do not count Bone Hearts as long as they are not filled with Red Hearts, so picking up an item like Brittle Bones will allow entry, despite the player technically having more than one heart of health.

• [Repentance] Using Glowing Hourglass will re-roll the enemies involved in both variations. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] In cases in which there are multiple characters on screen (such as when playing Co-op, being Jacob and Esau, etc.), all characters must meet the requirement for the door to open. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If the game crashes or you close it before you finish the challenge room it will crash every time you try to continue that run.
Bug note: If Isaac encounters Greed or Super Greed in a Secret Room next to a boss challenge room, the path to the boss challenge room is boarded up from the mini-boss fight. Defeating Greed or Super Greed does not remove the boards, despite the room no longer being active.

Corpse.title: Corpse
Corpse.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Corpse is a new floor added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance, which acts as the Womb's alternative Chapter. It features a desolate and dreary atmosphere with enemies that carry the theme of death and advanced rot. The Corpse is one of five final levels in The Binding of Isaac, alongside the Chest, the Dark Room, [Afterbirth+ onward] The Void, and [Repentance] Home. Like in the Womb and its alternate floors, floors in Corpse do not naturally generate item rooms or shops, and all damage taken will do a full heart of damage to Isaac's HP (unless he has The Wafer), regardless of the source.

To access The Corpse, the player must first open the flesh door at the end of the Mausoleum/Gehenna II after defeating the Mausoleum version of Mom by doing one of the following:

• Collect Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2, which are obtained via puzzles inside Downpour and the Mines, to build the knife familiar, and stab the door with it.

• Sacrifice one key and open the door by using Sharp Key.

• Cracked Orb can also open the door while simultaneously letting you keep the knife familiar.

• Using a Soul of Cain.

• If Isaac exits the Boss Rush room in Gehenna after 25 minutes have passed, there is a chance that the flesh door will change positions to the wall where the boss rush door was, causing Isaac to "come out" of the flesh door and leaving it open, allowing entry without the knife.

On the other side of the flesh door, the player will fight the Mausoleum version of Mom's Heart, after which the entrance to the Womb will turn into the Corpse entrance, which will take the player into the Corpse floor.

The boss of Corpse II is always Mother.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Mama Mega! can not be used to open the Flesh Door.

• We Need To Go Deeper! and Ehwaz cannot generate trapdoors in Corpse II.
An I AM ERROR room can only be visited in Corpse II via clipping out of a Crawl Space; such an I AM ERROR room will contain a passageway which leads back to the starting room of the floor.

• If the game is exited after defeating Mother and rejoined, there will be a door in the room allowing the player to leave the room. This can be used to go to a Sacrifice Room and then warp to the Dark Room, letting the run continue further.

• [Repentance+] If the player has previously defeated Mother, beating her again will cause a portal leading to The Void to spawn, allowing the player to continue their run without the need for a sacrifice room.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Corpse is the only Alternative Chapter to not have any alternative floors.

• An unused floor named Mortis, presumably as an alternative to the Corpse, exists in the game files.

• In Antibirth, the hole to the Mother battle had 4 Locked Chests next to it that always contained items, similar to chests in Chest.

• If a room's floor is filled with blood, there will be a huge blood stain on the floor upon entering any room adjacent to it.

sections.heading: Music
sections.text:
• The music for Corpse is titled Carrion.

• The term "carrion" refers to the decaying flesh of dead animals.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Curse Rooms feature teeth-like spikes on the door that hurt Isaac when entering and exiting the room.

Curse rooms can appear from Chapter 1 to 5.

[Repentance] Taking damage from the spikes doesn't reduce the odds of getting a Devil or Angel room.

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Items that grant flight allow Isaac to avoid damage taken upon entering a Curse Room, but do not prevent damage taken upon leaving.

• Any item that gives Isaac a shield or invulnerability will prevent damage taken when passing through a Curse Room Door, including Holy Mantle.

• If a Secret Room is next to a Curse Room, it can be entered without taking any damage by bombing the wall between these rooms from the Secret Room.

• The damage done by the Curse Room's door is applied when touching the door. This means that Isaac can be damaged by it without actually going through the door, and any effects that occur upon taking damage will occur in the current room and not the room that the door leads to.

• During Cursed!, all doors except for special types turn into this type of door.

• Damage taken from entering a Curse Room doesn't count for the purposes of score calculation.

• [Repentance] Holding Flat File will remove the spikes from Curse Room doors, allowing them to be entered without taking damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Curse Room's icon is similar to the icon of Whore of Babylon.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: [Before Repentance] Isaac can pass through Curse Room doors without taking damage even when he should. This usually requires 2.0 speed, a long running start and careful positioning to cross the door before its damage effect kicks in, or alternatively several size downs and very careful nudging along the door's edge.

Dank Depths.title: Dank Depths
Dank Depths.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Dank Depths is one of the environments in chapter 3 added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth. The theme of the Dank Depths is tar, which can be found dripping from the ceiling and bubbling in pits. [Before Repentance] Rocks have a chance to be replaced with spikes.

The Dank Depths' alternate floors are the Depths and Necropolis. The boss of the Dank Depths II is always Mom.

[Repentance] After A Secret Exit is unlocked, a door will appear in Dank Depths I's Boss Room upon defeating the boss, leading to the Mausoleum / Gehenna. This door requires two hearts to be opened (except on Lost characters). Unlike Angel Rooms and Devil Rooms, this door never disappears. Also after this achievement is unlocked, a Strange Door in the starting room of Dank Depths II will appear. This door leads to Mausoleum / Gehenna II before entering the Ascent.
[end edition note] 

[Afterbirth+ onward] The Dank Depths are unlocked by defeating It Lives! 21 times.

• Killing Dogma and The Beast also increases this tally, as does Mausoleum's version of Mom's Heart.

Dark Room.title: Dark Room
Dark Room.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Dark Room is one of five final levels in The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, alongside the Chest, The Void, the Corpse, and Home. The Dark Room is unlocked by defeating Satan 5 times, after which it can be accessed by touching the chest dropped by Satan with The Negative equipped. Entrance to the Dark Room can also be achieved via the I AM ERROR room in Sheol, even without The Negative, as well as through the Black Market in Sheol, and through a trapdoor spawned by a button. After completing this level or the Chest for the first time, the Dark Room will always contain a large golden door in the first room, which can be unlocked with either the Key Pieces (combination of Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2), Dad's Key, Get out of Jail Free Card, or Mr. ME!.

[Afterbirth onward] The Dark Room can also be accessed by repeatedly using a Sacrifice Room. After using the spikes for the 12th time, continuing to use the Sacrifice Room will have a 50% chance to teleport Isaac directly to the Dark Room, regardless of what floor he was previously on.

[Afterbirth+ onward] The Dark Room is home to the Grave Room, which will contain a Dirt Patch, which can be dug up using Mom's Shovel. Doing so for the first time will unlock The Forgotten. On subsequent runs, multiple Dirt Patches can be found, and digging them up using We Need To Go Deeper!, Ehwaz, or Mom's Shovel will spawn a random type of chest. [end edition note] 

Like Sheol before it, the Dark Room consists of only one floor. In the Dark Room, it is not possible to bomb doors open to skip rooms. The Dark Room's rooms are usually devoid of Rocks and other obstacles; but are mainly filled with bosses and mini-bosses. The boss of the floor is always The Lamb.

The first room the player spawn in will automatically contain 4 Red Chests that [Before Repentance] function normally or [Repentance] contain random Devil Deals. Rerolling these items will produce new items that are from the Treasure Room item pool. As well, all other types of chests spawned in the Dark Room will always contain Treasure Room items. [Before Repentance] Destroying [machine: Slot Machine] s, [machine: Fortune Telling Machine] s, and all types of [machine: Beggar] s with the exception of [machine: Shell Game] will also spawn items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance+] If Isaac gets Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2, the key will open the golden gate to fight Mega Satan, but if Isaac uses Forget Me Now, the floor will reset and Isaac won't get both Key Pieces back, making it so that the golden gate won't open again.

• [Repentance+] Golden gate to Mega Satan will stay opened after using Forget Me Now.

• [Repentance] When playing as The Lost or Tainted Lost, it is advised to open all the devil deal chests in the starting room, as only one of the four items can be taken and all the other chests will disappear.

• [Repentance] Taking the devil deals generated by the chests will NOT prevent Angel Rooms from appearing.

• [Repentance] If Jera is used in the initial room with the devil deal chests, the newly spawned chests will contain four additional and distinct devil deals.

• [Afterbirth onward] The I AM ERROR room cannot be reached by any method in Chest and the Dark Room.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Dark Room is the only floor in the game which is original to the initial release of Rebirth. All the other floors included in Rebirth at its launch were from the original The Binding of Isaac and its DLC Wrath of the Lamb.

• The Dark Room is also the name of a room which, like its name suggests, is plunged into complete darkness, for the notable purpose of processing photos. The fact that access to this floor is granted by touching the chest in Sheol while holding The Negative, which is the name given to a photo that has not been processed yet and whose colors and hues are inverted, might be a nod to this.

• The layout to The Chest and the Dark Room are identical for a given seed.

• [Rebirth only] One of the Super Secret Room layouts is of the Dark Room and a Black Heart. The sprite for the door is a portal rather than a gray door, however, since bombed-out entrances in the Dark Room appear as portals.

• This secret room appears floating in a black void on most floors, but in the Dark Room, it appears in a purple misty void instead, just like all the other rooms.

• [Afterbirth onward] This secret room takes the appearance of a Library instead.

• One possible room in the Dark Room contains only a Bony and a Lil' Haunt. These possibly represent The Forgotten and The Soul.

• On the 6/2/2021 Kickstarter livestream, Edmund McMillen confirmed that the Dark Room represents the closet that Isaac was locked inside in Ending 21.

• The theme of Dark Room (Devoid) is noticeably shorter than other floor themed soundtracks. This is because a floor theme is comprised of 2 parts. The 1st part is the normal theme, and the 2nd part is for the more intense version of the track when an enemy room with a combined high health count is entered. There is no "Intense" theme for when a high health room in Dark Room is entered. The Cathedral's theme (Everlasting Hymn) is also shorter than other tracks, but does have a barely noticeable secondary intense part of the track.

sections.heading: Music
sections.text: • The music for the Dark Room is titled Devoid, which means "empty".

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Depths is one of the levels in Chapter 3. It features a dark environment, filled with skulls. Common enemies in the Depths include Knights, Guts, and Vis.

The Depths' unlockable variants are Necropolis and the Dank Depths, which can be unlocked after defeating every boss from the Depths (not necessarily in the Depths), and after killing It Lives! 26 times.

The boss of The Depths II is always Mom.

[Repentance] After A Secret Exit is unlocked, a door will appear in Depths I's Boss Room upon defeating the boss, leading to the Mausoleum / Gehenna. This door requires two hearts to be opened (except on Lost characters). Unlike Angel Rooms and Devil Rooms, this door never disappears. Also after this achievement is unlocked, a Strange Door in the starting room of Depths II will appear. This door leads to Mausoleum / Gehenna II before entering the Ascent.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Devil Rooms primarily allow Isaac to make Deals with the Devil, but they can also contain a variety of enemies, pickups, or even a boss battle against Krampus. A Devil Room has a chance to appear in a Boss Room after the boss occupying it has been defeated. If certain criteria are met, a Devil Room can be replaced by an Angel Room.

[Afterbirth onward] In Greed Mode, Devil Rooms are guaranteed to appear upon completing the optional 11th / [Afterbirth+ onward] 12th (in Greedier Mode) wave of a floor.

sections.heading: Deals with the Devil
sections.text:
A Devil Room has a high chance of spawning items that will be put up for sale. Unlike Shops, where Isaac pays with money, to make Deals with the Devil Isaac has to trade Red Heart Containers as payment. All items normally cost either 1 or 2 Red Heart Containers, and their prices roughly correspond to their power.

When playing as Keeper, the character's coin heart containers are used to trade for Devil Deal items, with items costing the same number of coin heart containers as red heart containers with a different character.

• [Repentance] Instead of coin heart containers, Devil Deal items must be bought using coins. One-heart and two-heart deals cost 15 and 30 cents, respectively. Paying cents for Devil Deals will still remove the Angel room appearance chance in the same way when other characters pay with heart containers.

• The same cost for deals are applied with any character who collected A Pound of Flesh.

See the Devil Room for a comprehensive list of items offered and their health price. 

[Repentance+] Additionally, Devil Deal items with the devilsacrifice item tag will have a sacrifice spike cost instead of a Red Heart Container cost. There is a 50% chance to award the item on the first play and 100% chance on the second. Picking up an item from the pedestal spawned this way counts as taking a regular deal and will prevent Angel Rooms from spawning naturally.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Isaac does not have Red Heart Containers upon entering a Devil Room, all items will cost 3 Soul Hearts.

• [Afterbirth onward] If Isaac is presented with 2+ items to buy, but only has enough Red Hearts to buy one, the price of the other(s) will change to 3 Soul Hearts upon spending your Red Hearts.

• [Repentance] Additionally, if Isaac only has one Red Heart, deals that normally cost 2 Hearts will change to one Red Heart and two Soul Hearts.

• • If Isaac does not have enough Soul Hearts for this type, he will still be able to take the Deal. However, if Isaac has no health at all (e. g. he is defying death with Berserk!), he will not be able to take the Deals.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] If Isaac has less than 3 Soul Hearts, but at least one Bone Heart, he can take a three-Soul-Heart Deal and stay alive because of the bone hearts. [end edition note] 

• • [Repentance] Bone hearts are considered Heart Containers. Having at least one bone heart will change the price of a Deal to at least one red heart.

• Two-heart deals can be taken even if Isaac does not have enough Red Hearts to afford them, as long as he has one Red Heart to spend.

• Spending all of his Heart Containers will not kill Isaac as long as he has Soul Hearts, Black Hearts, or Bone Hearts remaining.

• If taking a Deal leaves Isaac with no health remaining, he can still survive if he picks up a Soul Heart, Black Heart, or Bone Heart while holding the item in the air. Also, if he has an active item that grants Soul/Black Hearts, he can take a Deal and then use the active item, leaving him alive with whatever the item gave him. The same is true for consumables that give hearts (e. g. Dagaz).

• • [Afterbirth onward] If Isaac takes a Deal for an item that grants an Eternal Heart through the use of Chaos, it will not keep him alive. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] The temporary heart container granted by XI - Strength cannot be used to purchase a devil deal. However, if Isaac has no other heart containers to spend, then it can be used this way. This also works if the devil deal costs 2 hearts, but Isaac only has 0 or 1 before activating the Strength card.

• [Repentance] Temporary heart containers can be used for devil deals with no restrictions.

• [Repentance] Some items may cost Soul Hearts even if Isaac still has Red Hearts.

• An item's price may change from Red Hearts to Soul Hearts if Isaac visits the Devil Room before obtaining enough Soul Hearts and returning to the Devil Room.

sections.heading: Angel Rooms
sections.text:
• Refusing to make Deals with the Devil will give Isaac the chance of an Angel Room replacing the Devil Room on subsequent floors. If any Deal with the Devil is taken, Angel Rooms will not spawn for the remainder of the run.

• [Before Repentance] Trading Heart Containers for items in a Black Market counts as taking a Deal with the Devil for Angel Room generation purposes.

• Only the act of paying health (Red Hearts or Soul Hearts) for an item in a Devil Room counts as a Deal with the Devil. Taking Black Hearts, opening Red Chests, and taking items that weren't paid for (such as those obtained from Red Chests, Krampus, Beggars, Pandora's Box, or made free by using Credit Card) do not count as Deals taken, allowing Isaac to still see Angel Rooms.

• [Repentance] If the first offered Devil Room is not entered at all, the next offer is guaranteed to be an Angel Room. If the player uses the Joker it will take you to the Angel Room without removing the guarantee.

sections.heading: Conditions to Make Devil Rooms Appear
sections.text:
A Devil Room can only open on floors between the second floor of Chapter 1 and Chapter 4.

There is only a 1% base chance for the Devil Room door to open. This chance can be modified in various ways:

| Condition | Chance 
| [Repentance] Having Sausage | +6.9% [end edition note]

| Blowing up at least one Shopkeeper on the current floor | +10%

| Having Pentagram | [Rebirth only] +20%
[Afterbirth onward] +10%

| Having a second Pentagram | [Rebirth only] +10%
[Afterbirth onward] +5%

| Having Black Candle | [Rebirth only] +30%
[Afterbirth onward] +15%

| Holding Book of Revelations | [Rebirth only] +35%
[Afterbirth onward] +17.5%

| Blowing up at least one Beggar, Rotten Beggar, Battery Bum, [Repentance+] Devil Beggar or [Repentance+] Key Master on the current floor | +35%

| Taking no Red Heart damage against the boss | +35%

| Taking no Red Heart damage for the entire floor | +99%

| [Repentance] Having Act of Contrition and taking Red Heart damage | +40% [end edition note]

| [Repentance] Having Act of Contrition and taking Red Heart damage in the Boss Room | +15% [end edition note]

| [Repentance] Having Satanic Bible wisps | +10%, up to +80% [end edition note]

| Holding The Book of Belial | [Rebirth only] +2500%
[Afterbirth onward] +12.5%

| Having Goat Head | Guaranteed

| [Afterbirth+ onward] Having Eucharist [end edition note] | Guaranteed
(always Angel Room)

| Previous Devil Room door seen two floors ago | x0.5

| Previous Devil Room door seen less than two floors ago | x0.25

For example, if Isaac has avoided taking Red Heart damage and has blown up a Shopkeeper, he will have a (1+35+99+10)% = 145% base Deal with the Devil chance which will be displayed 100%, which will then go down to 36.25% once he sees the Devil Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If the player enters a Devil Room without the entrance door appearing (by teleporting in), the chance to receive a Devil Room will not be reduced. Because of this, if a Devil Room is seen this way and the player does not want to enter it again, intentionally taking red heart damage will reduce the chance of seeing it after the boss fight, which can prevent the penalty from seeing the Devil Room door from applying to the next floor.

• The chance that the Devil Room or Angel Room door will remain open after re-entering the Boss Room is based on the current Deal with the Devil chance, which gains the x0.25 multiplier from seeing the Devil Room door less than two floors ago. Due to its high chance of disappearing, it is recommended to go directly into the Devil Room when offered, [Repentance] unless it's the first time one is seen and the player wants to get a guaranteed Angel deal.

• Once a Devil Room door closes for the floor, it cannot be re-opened without picking up Goat Head or Eucharist.

• On XL floors, the Devil Room door can only appear after completing the second Boss Room.

• On XL floors, not seeing a Devil Room will count as not seeing a Devil Room for two floors, and seeing it will count as not seeing a Devil Room for one floor.

• Taking Soul Heart, Black Heart, Eternal Heart, Bone Heart, or Rotten Heart damage does not decrease the chance to open a Devil Room; only Red Hearts count.

• Taking red heart damage from a Devil Beggar, Blood Donation Machine, IV Bag, Blood Rights, Razor Blade, Shard of Glass or Sharp Plug does not decrease the chance to open a Devil Room.

• • [Repentance] Sacrifice Rooms also count as self-damage and do not lower the Devil Room chance.

• • [Before Repentance] The Bad Trip pill effect or damage from Curse Room doors still counts as Red Heart damage.

• • [Afterbirth+ onward] Losing a Bone Heart container as The Forgotten counts as Red Heart damage.

• Tainted Magdalene's leaking Red Hearts being damaged does not count as Red Heart damage, regardless of the damage source.

• There are additional ways to enter a Devil Room on any floor:

• Red Chests have a chance of teleporting Isaac into the Devil Room upon being opened.

• Using Joker will teleport Isaac into the room.

• [Afterbirth onward] Using Teleport 2.0 after all other rooms on the floor (excluding the I AM ERROR room) have been visited. [end edition note] 

• Teleport!, Undefined, and Telepills cannot transport Isaac to the Devil Room.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If a deal would deal lethal damage to The Soul, quickly switching to The Forgotten will keep him alive. This can even be done to take 3-heart deals for one soul heart.

• If The Soul has no Hearts, switching to The Soul is disabled until another Soul or Black Heart is acquired. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The same can be done "in reverse" - take a deal as The Forgotten and quickly switch to The Soul. However, this will usually cause a softlock unless Birthright is obtained since switching to The Forgotten will be disabled while he has no Hearts, and The Soul is chained to The Forgotten and thus is incapable of traversing rooms.

• [Before Repentance] The Lost can take all Deals with the Devil for free.

• [Repentance] The Lost, Tainted Lost, and Tainted Jacob in ghost form are allowed to take one of the offered Deals for free; the others will vanish afterward.

• • The same applies to any character turned into ghost form via Soul of the Lost or by touching a White Fire Place. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] ??? pays for Devil Deals with Soul Hearts for prices equal to their Red heart equivalent; ie, one or two Soul Hearts depending on the item, rather than the normal three. No other character has this effect, including Tainted ???. [end edition note] 

• [Before Afterbirth+] The rock behind the Devil can rarely be a Tinted Rock.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] An Angel statue can rarely substitute the Satan statue and can be awoken with an explosion as usual.

• Angels spawned in this way do not drop Key Pieces, however.

• The highest possible Devil Room chance without Goat Head is 204% in Afterbirth, or 326.9% in Repentance.

• [Repentance] It is possible to have a guaranteed Deal Chance without Goat Head or Eucharist if enough Satanic Bible wisps are produced and all chance-increasing effects take place. However, this is extremely difficult to achieve since only up to 8 Satanic Bible wisps can exist simultaneously (certain items such as Jar of Wisps ignore this). [end edition note] 

• Teleporting into a deal without beating the floor boss can generate a different deal than the one you'd receive after beating it. This can be observed by having a Red Chest teleport or using a Joker while holding on to a Glowing Hourglass, using it to undo the teleport and then accessing the deal after defeating the floor boss, even if the deal door does not open by itself.

• This can be observed even in the starting floor of the game. It however no longer happens after Womb 2.

• Once a deal has been generated in any manner, it can not be changed or influenced.

• For example collecting Eucharist after a Devil Deal door had opened, will not result into changing the current floor deal to an Angel Deal even if the Devil Deal was not visited.

• It is possible to "undo" a deal door opening after beating the floor boss with Glowing Hourglass (provided the natural chance for the deal was not 100%) by entering the deal door and using the hourglass inside the room. If that happens, the game considers the current deal as not having opened at all, and will not apply a deal chance penalty for the next floor. This can be useful if the deal did not offer anything the player wanted.

• This can be repeated as many times as necessary until the door closes by itself, and as long as Isaac directly visits the deal and does not leave it himself but only by using the hourglass.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, the Devil Rooms were somewhat less forgiving; if Isaac had an Eternal Heart, taking a Devil Deal would remove it.

• Furthermore, if Isaac has at least one Soul Heart and one Red Heart Container, and he takes a Devil Deal, Isaac would die. Isaac's last will will show a pentagram or a goat head as a result.

• Purchasing something worth two Red Heart Containers with one Red Heart Container and at least one Soul Heart will also remove the Soul Heart. Strangely, this will not kill Isaac, but the next hit he takes will, similar to The Lost.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Once item pedestal spawned in devil room is rolled into an item with devilsacrifice tag, all further rolls for this pedestal are restricted to items with the devilsacrifice tag. Additionally, this bug breaks item exclusion mechanic on Tainted Lost, Birthright on The Lost (self-harm items appear when they're not supposed to) and Spindown Dice.

Dice Room.title: Dice Room
Dice Room.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[Before Repentance] [Repentance] 

Dice Rooms are special rooms that can randomize many elements of the run. Dice Rooms require two Keys to be opened, unlike most other special rooms. For a Dice Room to spawn, two things must happen;

• First, the game must decide that a Sacrifice Room will spawn that floor. This normally has a 1/7 (~14%) chance of happening each floor, but increases to 5/14 (~36%) if Isaac’s total health (filled red and soul hearts) is equal to or greater than his total Red Heart Containers (including Bone Hearts).

• Once the game determines a Sacrifice Room will spawn, a Dice Room has a 1/50 (2%) chance to replace it. This chance increases to 27/125 (~22%) if Isaac has two or more keys.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
In addition to whatever else the room holds, there will always be a symbol of one of the sides of a six-sided die in the 5x5 center of the room. The amount of pips shown will be between one to six, chosen randomly. When Isaac crosses the die, a certain effect will occur that randomizes a certain aspect of the run, dependent on how many pips were on the die face shown. Any given Dice Room can only give this effect once.

The die numbers and effects are:

• ⚀ 1 pip - [Before Afterbirth+] Rerolls Isaac's currently held collectibles into items from the Treasure Room, like the D4 would. Activated collectibles can be changed into passive ones, but passive collectibles cannot turn into activated ones.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Rerolls each of Isaac's passive items into a random item from the pool of the room where it was acquired.

• [Repentance] Rerolls both Isaac's active and passive items.

• [Repentance] Only rerolls the items of the character that stepped onto the dice in co-op.

• • Meaning that Tainted Forgotten has to be thrown on the button in order to take effect.

• ⚁ 2 pips - Rerolls all pickups in the room, like the D20 would.

• ⚂ 3 pips - Rerolls all pickups and trinkets on the entire floor. This includes Shop pickups. Does not reroll pickups or trinkets in the Devil Room, Angel Room, Black Market, or Crawl Space.

• Pickups rerolled in shops by this effect have a chance to turn into items. If these are active items, they will have no charges when picked up.

• ⚃ 4 pips - Rerolls any item pedestals on the floor, like The D6 would. Does not reroll item pedestals in the Devil Room, Angel Room, Library, Black Market, or Crawl Space.

• ⚄ 5 pips - Rerolls and restarts the current floor, which is the same effect as Forget Me Now.

• ⚅ 6 pips - Combines the effects of the 1-, 3-, and 4-pip rooms. (Rerolls all held items (including active), pickups, trinkets, and pedestal items like the D100.)

• [Repentance] Rerolls all held items for all characters in co-op.

sections.heading: Layouts
sections.text:
The following room maps were made using Basement Renovator for cleaner viewing. Note that any pickups in the 5×5 center of the room will be on the die symbol, requiring Isaac to activate the room in order to obtain them unless he knocks them away with explosions of some kind. Given how hazardous some dice room effects can be, this may be the preferred way of retrieving them.

All rooms have a weight of 1.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Dad's Key, Get out of Jail Free Card, Mr. ME!, and Sharp Key open Dice Rooms in one use.

• Due to how Dice Room generation works, a floor cannot have both a Dice Room and Sacrifice Room; they are mutually exclusive.

• If a floor has two special rooms that require two keys to enter, the one closer to the start room will be a Vault, and the one further away from it will be a Dice Room.

• It is possible to re-roll a floor into another that has a 5-pip Dice Room. Getting a 5-pip dice room in Womb / Utero II can allow the player to defeat Mom's Heart (or It Lives!) multiple times in one run. This can be used to quickly gain progress tied to the number of Mom's Heart kills.

• It is possible to unlock Samson by finishing the first floor and using a 5-pip Dice Room.

• A 5-pip dice room on an XL floor sends Isaac to the first floor of the chapter.

• When shop pickups are re-rolled via a 3- or 6-pip room, the original prices will remain in place.

• 3- or 6-pip Dice Rooms can reroll chests in Challenge Rooms or Boss Challenge Rooms into collectibles. And since those rooms detect whether a chest is open or an item picked up, there won't be any monsters.

• 3-pip room can re-roll shop pickups into items.

• Using items such as The D6 in the room without buying the item can cause the item to revert to a pickup.

• There is a small chance that 1- and 6-pip rooms will not reroll every item Isaac has in his possession.

• [Afterbirth onward] Dice Rooms don't re-roll starter challenge items or remove blindfold on challenges.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Dice Rooms have a small marker indicating the effect that will be activated when the room is used. This was inspired by this Steam Workshop mod by Wofsauge.

• [Repentance] If Jacob and Esau activate a 6-pip room, the items held by both characters will be rerolled, but only the items of the character that step on a 1-pip room will be rerolled. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Any rooms generated by Red Key that contain an item pedestal will not be affected by a 4-pip room. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] In the Mirrored World, the second Dice Room may be different.

• [Repentance] If Tainted Lazarus activates a 1-pip room, only the state that activated the room will have the items rerolled, leaving the other form's items untouched. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: The 1-pip room may reroll your active item into a "passive" item. The 1-pip room always empties your active item slot. However 1-pip room may fail to find a replacement item which results in Isaac still having the collectible. This is because the D4 will try 3 times to get a non-active item from the item pool before giving up replacing the item.
Bug note: The 1-pip room will reroll your secondary active collectible without emptying the slot. This means you will keep the active ability but lose some passive abilities. For example, you will lose Mom's Box passive of doubling trinkets but you keep the speed boost from A Pony.

Downpour.title: Downpour
Downpour.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Downpour is the first new environment added in Repentance. The theme of Downpour is flooded, haunted storm drains with many supernatural enemies and elements. Though there is some overlap with the Flooded Caves due to both featuring water flooding, the Flooded Caves' unique enemies are almost exclusively 'drowned' or 'bloated' as opposed to Downpour's more haunted theme.

Treasure rooms in Downpour always have two items to choose from. One of the items will always be unknown; however, this can be circumvented with the Dream Catcher.

After A Secret Exit is unlocked, a locked door to Downpour I or II will appear upon completing the Basement / Cellar / Burning Basement I or II, respectively. The locked door requires a key to enter.

sections.heading: Unique Elements
sections.text:
• Flooded Rooms - A layer of water covers all rooms in the floor, allowing certain enemies such as Small Leech and Striders to swim over flooded pits. Deep Gapers can hide beneath the water and emerge when all other enemies in the room have been killed. The reflection visible in the water is also utilized by Wraiths, which are always visible in the reflection when they are otherwise invisible. 

• Lightning Flashes - Lightning will occasionally strike, briefly brightening the room and revealing any Wraiths.

sections.heading: Knife Piece
sections.text:
Downpour II (or Dross II) contains the Mirrored World in which Isaac can acquire the Knife Piece 1, one of the quest items used to access Corpse. 

To access this area, Isaac can find the White Fire Place which spawns in a single room on the floor. Touching it converts Isaac into a ghostly form, resembling The Lost. Clearing any room will return Isaac to normal.

• The ghost form will hold the Holy Mantle if it is unlocked as a starting item for The Lost. The Holy Mantle will not be active until Isaac leaves the room.

• Interacting with Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars in the ghost form will kill Isaac despite having health in his normal form.

While in the ghost form, Isaac can then enter the mirror in the 1×1 room with a mirror on the icon, which leads Isaac to the Mirrored World, where he can find Knife Piece 1.

• The mirror can be entered normally when playing as The Lost, Tainted Lost, Tainted Soul, or Tainted Jacob in his ghost form after being hit by Dark Esau. 

Once Isaac has cleared one room, has obtained the Knife Piece, and returns through the mirror back to the real world, he will be converted back to the original character. After acquiring the first Knife Piece, Knife Piece 2 will now be accessible in Mines / Ashpit II.

For further notes and details, see the Mirrored World page.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Downpour is referred to on Isaac's Last Will as "Some Sewer".

• Antibirth used to have a different method of obtaining the first Knife Piece. Somewhere on the floor, there was a seemingly empty dead-end room with a minimap icon that indicated the room had a chest. Bombing the center of the room would open a hidden stone chest containing Knife Piece 1.

• In Antibirth, The Haunt could spawn as a boss.

• In Boss Challenge Rooms in Downpour, The Haunt is one of the possible spawns, which is a nod to this.

• Gapers and Frowning Gapers are tinted blue if encountered. As well, Clotty that spawn in the floor will appear wet and shiny.

• Almost any Spiders that spawn on this floor are replaced with Striders, including those spawned from Red Chests and Shopkeepers. The ones that spawn from a Big Spider are still normal spiders.

sections.heading: Music
sections.text:
• The music for the Downpour is called River of Despair.

• An early version of this song was revealed during the pre-release of Repentance, where it was titled "River of Despare".

• River of Despair features heavy use of a theremin, an instrument commonly associated with the paranormal.

Dross.title: Dross
Dross.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Dross is one of the environments of chapter 1.5, added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

Dross is an alternative floor to Downpour, differentiating itself from Downpour by having more poop and sewage-themed enemies. Just like in Downpour, Knife Piece 1 can be found on Dross II. Some rooms in this green brick sewage recess have a thin layer of dirtied reflective water on the ground.

Along with the watery floor, many visual effects are employed on this floor, such as:

• Random walls might have animated pipes pumping brown sewage onto the floor.

• Wet rooms have water distorted light reflections on the walls.

• Random water shower points consistently dropping water on the floor in small areas.

• Small water droplets randomly fall from the sky, leaving small wet marks that dry over in dry rooms, and don't really visually affect the floor of wet rooms.

• The floor underneath the water can be tiled, solid concrete, or grated.

• Overhead, light is blocked in 3-4 bar grate, multi-pipe, and diagonal pipe patterns, the remaining light hitting the floor and coloring it a little more yellow.

• Downpour Buckets also show up here as well, with the full variant of the bucket being full of poop, instead of full of water.

In Dross, some Rooms may have grates on the walls, expelling a strong water flow. The water flow pushes Isaac and everything else in the Room in one specific direction, usually towards the wall opposing the grates. The flow will hamper your speed if you move against it and speed you up if you move with it.

In addition, Dross floors have the rare chance to spawn Giant Poops, Big Poops that take up 4× the space as regular Poops.

sections.heading: Knife Piece 1
sections.text:
Dross II (or Downpour) contains a special area in which Isaac can acquire the Knife Piece 1, one of the key items for accessing the Corpse. Two unique features can be found here:

• A White Fire Place that cannot be extinguished. Touching it separates Isaac's body and soul, converting Isaac into The Lost (with Holy Mantle if you have unlocked it as a starting item, as well as your current items) for a brief time. After a room is cleared, the player returns to normal.

• Be warned that even if it has been unlocked for The Lost, the Holy Mantle will not be active until Isaac leaves the room. Taking damage in the same room after touching the white fireplace will be fatal.

• When playing as The Forgotten, The Lost still fights with the bone club, and turning into The Soul is still possible.

• When playing as Azazel, The Lost keeps Azazel's mini-Brimstone attack.

• A 1×1 room with a mirror on the icon. There is always a mirror that can't be accessed normally.

The mirror can only be entered as the Lost (or Tainted Forgotten (but not non-tainted The Soul) or Dark Esau-stricken Tainted Jacob, the former of which is allowed to retain their [functional] health), after which it leads Isaac to the Mirrored World, where he can find the Knife Piece 1.

• No items or pickups other than Knife Piece 1 will spawn there via level generation (i.e. be present upon the room being loaded/entered). However, the player can still get rewards for clearing rooms or destroying objects.

• Beating the boss room will spawn an item from the boss pool.

• While shops do not usually have items or pickups in them, using or destroying a restock machine will spawn items and pickups from the shop pool to buy.

Once Isaac has the Knife Piece and returns through the mirror back to the real world, he will be converted back to the original character. To acquire Knife Piece 2 and complete the process, be sure to head to the Mines/Ashpit II next.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Dross may be a reference to the Sewers of Dross from Gish, one of Edmund McMillen's previous games.

• It may also be a reference to Sewers of Dross from The Legend of Bum-bo. Though, this stage might also just be a reference to Gish as well.

• Like the Downpour, the Dross has unique recolors of certain enemies. Tube Worms, Blurbs, Sub Horfs, Gapers, Frowning Gapers, Pacers, Gushers, and Small Leeches are recolored to fit the floor, Preys and Bubbles are altered to focus on poop, and Deep Gapers and Wraiths get a different texture entirely.

• Lil Blub and Wormwood are also recolored green to match this floor.

• Occasionally, player can find a rare room that only contains Henry. He will smile at Isaac, then get flushed, instantly getting killed.

• "Dross", other than a synonym for rubbish and feces, is the residue of smelting of precious metals, frequently mentioned in the Bible as a metaphor for impurity and worthlessness.

sections.heading: Music
sections.text:
• The music for the Dross is called Night Soil.

• Night Soil is a historical euphemism for human waste, which used to be collected at night from cesspools and eventually made into a fertilizer.

Familiar.title: Familiar
Familiar.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Familiars are small companions, usually generated by passive items, that follow and assist Isaac. Effects of familiars include (but are not limited to) pickup generation, shooting familiars that fire their own tears at enemies, and orbitals that act as projectile shields and/or deal contact damage.

Many of these familiars (especially pickup generation and shooting familiars) follow behind Isaac. When Isaac picks up multiple of these following familiars, they form a line behind him from oldest to newest (with closest familiar behind Isaac being the oldest one picked up) rather than constantly overlapping one another on the same spot behind Isaac.

• [Repentance] In addition to being chronologically ordered, certain familiars on the line take priority over others in how close their position is to Isaac. There are the following priorities, in order:

• King Baby, making it always the closest familiar to Isaac.

• Incubus.

• Milk!.

• Lil Portal.

• Lil Brimstone and Lil Monstro.

• Censer, Dry Baby, Lil Abaddon, and Mongo Baby.

• Most shooting familiars and some throwable familiars.

• Most pickup generation familiars and "quest item" familiars such as Key Piece 1. Boiled Baby also takes this priority.
[end edition note] 
Isaac cannot have more than 64 total familiars at once. This includes blue spiders and flies, familiar items such as Dry Baby, Tainted Eve's blood clots, etc. Gaining more than this will result in familiars being destroyed, with blue spiders and flies being destroyed first.

sections.heading: Blue Flies
sections.text:
Blue Flies are familiars that will orbit around Isaac and rush towards nearby enemies, dealing damage and dying in the process. Blue Flies deal double Isaac's current tear damage.

[collectible rows: Compost, Everything Jar, Guppy's Head, Jar of Flies] 
[collectible rows: Mom's Pad] 
|}

[collectible rows: Infestation, Lil Portal, The Mulligan, Parasitoid, Rotten Baby, The Swarm] 
[collectible rows: Mom's Underwear] 
[collectible rows: Sticky Bombs] 
|}

[pickup rows: Black Rune] 
[pickup rows: Berkano] 
|}

Other sources of Blue Flies

• Red Chest: Has a chance to spawn 3 Blue Flies.

• Dark blue champion: Will create 3 Blue Flies when defeated.

• [Before Repentance] Guppy: Isaac will create Blue Flies whenever his tears or his familiars' tears hit enemies.

• [Repentance] Guppy: Isaac's tears have a 66% chance to create Blue Flies whenever they hit enemies.

• Beelzebub: Some types of enemy flies become Blue Flies.

• [Afterbirth onward] Friends Till The End! pill: Spawns 3 Blue Flies.

• As Keeper or Tainted Keeper, all heart pickups turn into Blue Flies.

• Rotten Heart: After clearing a room, a maximum of 2 Blue Flies spawn for each Rotten Heart in Isaac's life bar.

• [Repentance] Corny Poops created by Tainted ??? or IBS spawn a Blue Fly every two seconds, up to a maximum of 3. [end edition note] 

• Rotten Beggars can spawn Blue Flies as a reward.

sections.heading: Locusts [Afterbirth+ onward]
sections.text:
Locusts are variants of Blue Flies that are spawned by Locust trinkets and 7 Seals. They behave like regular Blue Flies but have additional special effects. Red Locusts explode on contact with an enemy, dealing an extra 60 damage in the radius ( [Repentance] explosions are affected by certain bomb modifiers). Green Locusts poison the enemy. Yellow Locusts slow the enemy. Black Locusts deal quadruple Isaac's damage instead of double. White Locusts are identical to Blue Flies, but are generally spawned in high quantities.

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Blue Spiders
sections.text:
Blue Spiders are familiars similar to Blue Flies that crawl erratically and rush towards nearby enemies, dealing damage and dying in the process.

[Before Repentance] Blue Spiders deal 2.5 times Isaac's current tear damage.
[Repentance] Blue Spiders deal twice Isaac's current tear damage.

Unlike Blue Flies, Blue Spiders cannot attack over obstacles such as rocks and pits.
Bug note: Exiting the game and re-entering will cause all Blue Spiders to disappear.

[pickup rows: Black Rune] 
[pickup rows: Berkano] 
|}

Other sources of Blue Spiders

• [Afterbirth onward] Infested? pill: Spawns Blue Spiders equal to the number of enemies in the room.

• [Afterbirth onward] Infested! pill: Spawns a Blue Spider under Isaac and every pile of poop in the room.

• Rotten Beggars and Hell Games can spawn Blue Spiders as a reward.

• Red Chest: Has a chance to spawn 3 Blue Spiders.

sections.heading: Dips [Repentance]
sections.text:
Dips are temporary familiars that are spawned when destroying poops. They move erratically around the room and behave similarly to their hostile counterpart, dealing contact damage to enemies and blocking projectiles. There are a variety of Dips with unique effects that correlate to the different types of Poop.

Other sources of Dips

• Destroying a Charming Poop spawns a few Dip Familiars.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Wisps [Repentance]
sections.text:
Wisps are temporary orbital familiars that are mostly associated with Bethany. By default, they orbit Isaac, blocking shots and dealing contact damage. They also fire spectral tears that deal 1.6-2.4 damage. Normal wisps have 2 health. There are many variants of wisps, most of which can be spawned randomly or through combinations with Book of Virtues. See here for a full list of wisps.

Other unique variants of wisps include item wisps from Lemegeton which only mimic the effects of passive items while alive, and red wisps from Vengeful Spirit, which are invulnerable, but disappear upon entering a new floor.

Other sources of Wisps

• Picking up Birthright as Tainted Bethany spawns 4 item wisps with increased health.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Ghosts [Repentance]
sections.text:
Ghosts are temporary familiars that are summoned by various items. Most ghosts (except those created by Vade Retro) will automatically attack enemies after being summoned, quickly homing in on nearby enemies. All ghosts attack enemies by exploding, though some also deal contact damage shortly before doing so. Explosions from ghosts do not damage terrain or hurt Isaac. Unlike other temporary familiars, ghosts do not persist across rooms.

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Chasing Familiars
sections.text:
Familiars in this category actively chase enemies, dealing contact damage to them.

[trinket rows: Eve's Bird Foot] 
[trinket rows: Umbilical Cord] 
|}

Note: Only third and fourth stage Cube of Meat and Ball of Bandages chase enemies.

Note: [Afterbirth onward] Only fourth stage Bumbo chases enemies. [end edition note] 

Note: [Afterbirth+ onward] Only War and Death in 7 Seals chase enemies. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Orbital Familiars
sections.text:
Familiars that orbit Isaac, absorbing enemy projectiles and/or dealing contact damage. Despite their different apparent sizes, most of them have the same effective size with regard of blocking shots or damaging enemies.

Pills / Slot Machine

| Name | Description 
| [anchor: Pretty Fly] | Grants 1 fly orbital that circles the player, blocking projectiles and damaging fly-type enemies on touch.

Pretty Fly

• A maximum of three Pretty Flies can orbit around Isaac.

• Cube of Meat, Ball of Bandages, Sworn Protector, Guardian Angel, Smart Fly, Sacrificial Dagger, and Slipped Rib take up a Pretty Fly slot. These familiars are not affected by the Pretty Fly cap of 3.

• If Isaac has three Pretty Flies and picks up a Cube of Meat, the Cube of Meat will replace one of the flies.

• The amount of Pretty Flies Isaac has is stored. If a Pretty Fly is replaced by a Cube of Meat but then that Cube of Meat is removed, the replaced Pretty Fly will return. If Isaac has more than 3 Pretty Flies and one of his current Pretty Flies is removed through Sacrificial Altar, then another will replace it.

Orbital Rings

• There are set orbit rings that have specific rotations and distance from Isaac.

• [Afterbirth onward] If two orbitals share a same orbit ring they will be positioned opposite each other (three will cause them to fly 120 degrees apart, four will fly at 90 degrees etc.). [end edition note] 

• Ring 1 flies counter-clockwise and is the closest to Isaac.

• It consists of Pretty Flies and familiars that can replace Pretty Flies.

• • Guardian Angel will increase the rotation speed of all familiars in this ring.

• Ring 2 flies counter-clockwise and is second closest.

• It consists of Bloodshot Eye, Big Fan, Guillotine, Leprosy, and Mom's Razor

• • Big Fan will decrease the rotation speed of all familiars in this ring and ring 1. It will also override Guardian Angel's speed boost.

• • [Repentance] A Pretty Fly Horse Pill will spawn a unique Big Fan that will not orbit slower or affect the speed of other orbitals.

• Ring 3 flies counter-clockwise and orbits slightly slower than ring 2.

• It consists of Psy Fly and Tinytoma.

• Ring 4 flies clockwise at the speed of ring 3.

• It consists of Distant Admiration and Bot Fly.

• Ring 5 flies counter-clockwise even slower than ring 4.

• It consists of Friend Zone and Angelic Prism.

• Ring 6 flies counter-clockwise at the speed of ring 5.

• It consists of Forever alone and Best Bud.

• • Best Bud will orbit much faster than Forever alone but not affect the speed of the ring. However it will impact the orbiting position of other Forever alones.

• The Swarm has a unique orbit ring between 2 and 3, it orbits counter-clockwise much slower.

• Angry Fly has a unique orbit ring between 3 and 4, it orbits clockwise much faster.

• Familiars affected by Friendship Necklace have a unique orbit ring just around ring 3. Its familiars orbit clockwise faster.

sections.heading: Pickup Generation Familiars
sections.text:
Familiars that generate pickups when certain conditions are met.

Note: [Afterbirth onward] Only the second, third, and fourth stages of Bumbo generate pickups. [end edition note] 

Note: [Repentance] Only the second and third stages of Blood Puppy generate pickups. [end edition note] 

Note: For many of these familiars that generate pickups every n rooms, the first pickup will be dropped after n-1 rooms, where n is the amount of rooms required to normally spawn a pickup and for all drops but the first time. For instance, Acid Baby drops pills ever 7 cleared rooms, but the first pill is dropped after 6 rooms (7-1).

sections.heading: Shooting Familiars
sections.text:
Familiars that attack with their own tears or other ranged effects. Most shooting familiars only shoot as long as Isaac is attacking or charging a shot, though there are others that target and fire automatically.

[collectible rows: Abel, Ball of Bandages, Boiled Baby, Bot Fly, Brother Bobby, Buddy in a Box, Bumbo, Cain's Other Eye, Cube of Meat, Demon Baby, Fate's Reward, Freezer Baby, Ghost Baby, Giant Cell, Harlequin Baby, Incubus, Lil Brimstone, Lil Abaddon, Lil Loki, Lil Monstro, Lil Spewer, Little Gish, Little Steven, Mongo Baby, Papa Fly, Quints, Rainbow Baby, Robo-Baby, Robo-Baby 2.0, Rotten Baby, Seraphim, Sister Maggy, The Intruder, Twisted Pair] 
[collectible rows: Isaac's Heart] 
[collectible rows: Hushy] 
|}

Note: Only second stage Cube of Meat and Ball of Bandages shoot tears.

Note: [Afterbirth onward] Only third stage Bumbo fires tears. [end edition note] 

[Repentance] Note: Most shooting familiars that follow Isaac take 5th priority along the familiar line. This is the second to last priority with the last being non-combat familiars. There are some exceptions such as Incubus which has 2nd priority, Lil Brimstone and Lil Monstro which have 3rd priority, and Boiled Baby which has 6th priority. [end edition note] 

[Repentance] Note: Using five or more different copies of Esau Jr. will destroy the item and spawn a familiar that behaves the same way as Abel. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Wandering Familiars
sections.text:
Familiars that move around the room sporadically.

Note: [Afterbirth+ onward] The Spider Baby transformation grants a familiar nearly identical to Spider Mod with the only difference being the lack of ability to see enemy HP bars. [end edition note] 

Note: [Afterbirth+ onward] Only Famine, Pestilence, and Conquest in 7 Seals wander randomly. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bouncing Familiars
sections.text:
Familiars that bounce around the room in a zig-zag pattern, changing directions when hitting a wall.

[collectible rows: BBF, Hushy, The Peeper, Succubus] 
[collectible rows: Cain's Other Eye] 
[collectible rows: GB Bug] 
|}

sections.heading: Mimicking Familiars [Afterbirth onward]
sections.text:
Familiars that copy Isaac's movements after a certain delay.

[collectible rows: Multidimensional Baby, Obsessed Fan, Papa Fly, Shade] 
[collectible rows: My Shadow] 
|}
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Throwable Familiars
sections.text:
Familiars that are thrown by Isaac by shooting and can return to him after awhile.

[collectible rows: Big Chubby, Bob's Brain, Jaw Bone, Knife Piece 1, Knife Piece 2, Lil Portal, Little Chubby] 
[collectible rows: GB Bug, Holy Water] 
|}

[pickup rows: Berkano] 
|}
Note: [Repentance] Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2 are only throwable when combined. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Controlled Familiars
sections.text: Familiars that move in the direction Isaac is shooting.

sections.heading: Others
sections.text: Familiars that don't fit into any of the above categories or that produce multiple effects.

??? (Floor).title: ??? (Floor)
??? (Floor).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the chapter] 

???, referred to as Blue Womb or Dead Womb in the OST, is a chapter added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth. It is unlocked by defeating Mom's Heart for the 10th time.

It is accessed by defeating Mom's Heart or It Lives! within 30 minutes. Leaving and re-entering the Boss Room after the timer has reached 30 minutes will make the entrance to ??? disappear.
If the player is fast enough, both Boss Rush and ??? can be completed in a single run.

It contains the following:

• Four Locked Chests in the main room.

• Unlike the ones in the Chest, these are just regular golden chests and don't guarantee an item drop.

• Two locked Treasure Rooms, both of them offering two choices of items as if More Options was active.

• A Shop that always contains 6 goods for sale, even if Shop Upgrade Lvl. 4 has not been unlocked.

• A 2×2 boss room that contains Hush.

• The door leading to the boss room is unique and appears to be part of the wall until it is touched.

It is advised to only enter ??? with very powerful items and/or a set of good dodging skills because Hush ranks amongst the most difficult bosses of the entire game.

After Hush is defeated, one of two things will happen:

• If this is the first time Hush has been defeated, a giant golden chest will appear in the middle of the room. Jumping into it ends the run and gives ending 17.

• If Hush has been defeated before, a trapdoor and a beam of light leading to Sheol or the Cathedral will appear.

• If Hush has been defeated before but Sheol and the Cathedral have not been unlocked, the giant golden chest will appear instead.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Additionally, an exit will spawn in the corner of the room, containing a portal leading to The Void. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Boss
sections.text:
| 
| Hush

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This floor cannot be skipped with We Need To Go Deeper! or Ehwaz; neither will work.

• The floor can be skipped if a Black Market or I AM ERROR room is found, [Repentance] or a trapdoor is created with D12. This will always take the player to Sheol.

• • [Repentance] I AM ERROR room can contain a beam of light that takes Isaac to Cathedral.

• Genesis will skip the floor, and always take the player to Cathedral.

• ??? has its own Devil Room/Angel Room which can be reached via a Red Chest or a Joker.

• ??? doesn't have Secret Rooms, a Super Secret Room, or an Ultra Secret Room.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Using Mama Mega!, Mega Bean or holding Strange Key will open the entrance even if the time limit has expired. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] When Suplex! is used while a Berserk! effect is ending, Isaac lands with an explosion similar to Mama Mega!. This explosion can open the entrance after the time limit has expired. [end edition note] 

• Rocks contained in ??? have a significantly increased chance of spawning a Crawl Space when destroyed.

• Red Key creates exclusive room layouts that contain the following enemies:

• Blue Boil

• Hush Fly

• Blue Gaper

• Blue Conjoined Fatty

• [Repentance] Despite red rooms being able to be created, no Ultra Secret Rooms appear, even when using XVIII - The Moon?. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Music
sections.text:
• The stage's music is called Mater Prope or Nativitate.

• These names are in Latin and could be translated to "Almost Mother" and "With Birth" / "Due to Birth" / "At the Time of Birth" respectively.

• Nativitate has a combat layer which can only be heard in rooms with enemies. Since enemies do not spawn on ??? normally, the only way to hear the combat layer is to encounter enemies in I AM ERROR rooms, Crawl Spaces, rooms created by Blue Key, or Red Rooms. Spawning enemies via Reward Plates, however, will not change the music to the combat layer.

• • The layer can also be heard while playing DELETE THIS if the music is replaced with this floor's music track.

• The tracks that play during the battle against Hush are called Ascension (the ??? boss fight music; played during Hush's first phase, which is similar to the ??? boss) and Morituros (during the second phase).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The displayed name of the chapter is ???, but the chapter is referred to as Blue Womb by the achievement, using the same logic as the character ???.

• The character ??? and the chapter ??? have the same unlock requirements.

• ??? is unique as the only chapter that can be optionally done between mandatory chapters.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] It is mandatory, however, to complete this chapter to unlock The Void. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] It is also mandatory to complete three times to unlock Downpour, as well as the rest of the alternative chapters. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] ??? is the smallest chapter, only containing 6 normally accessible rooms.

• Home ties with ??? in terms of having 6 normally accessible rooms.

• In Isaac's last will, ??? is referred to as "some barren place".

• This may be a reference to the fact that infertile women were historically referred to as "barren".

• ???'s icon on the progress bar is actually a recolor of the Womb's.

• Similarly, the trapdoor leading to ??? is a recolor of the trapdoor leading to the first and second floor of Chapter 4.

• [Repentance] There is an unused version of ???, which uses the textures for the Basement and has the filter seen in The Ascent, with the song for The Void. The sound played after defeating Hush normally is replaced by a sound that plays after defeating an alt-path boss. Entering the trapdoor to Sheol or the beam of light to Cathedral after defeating Hush will send Isaac to Home. It can be accessed by typing stage 9c in the Debug Console. The void portal in this version of ??? is replaced by a cobweb. [end edition note] 

• The 30-minute limit of reaching Blue Womb could signify how long it took Isaac to suffocate, hence the floor's theming and Hush's presence.

• The Hush boss door's texture is larger than is depicted ingame. When the door sprite sheet is opened in a photo editor, it is revealed to actually be a archlike gateway, rather than the "garage door" like door it is seen as ingame.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Attempting to open the door leading to Hush's room while holding a Golden Key will cause Isaac to walk through the door without opening it, immediately beginning the Hush fight.
Bug note: Mama Mega! cannot be used to open the door to ???.

Bony.title: Bony
Bony.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Bonies are skeleton enemies which wander around the room and quickly throw bone projectiles at Isaac when he lines up with them.

sections.heading: Black Bony
sections.text: Black Bonies are harder versions of Bonies that behave identically to regular Bonies, but fire three bones in a row and explode upon death. The first bone will be fired when Isaac lines up, but the second and third one may be fired at an angle towards him.

sections.heading: Revenant
sections.text: Revenants are variants of Bonies that appear in the Mausoleum and Gehenna. Revenants wander around the room randomly, occasionally stopping to shoot a stream of flames at Isaac. These flames have limited range, and are blocked by obstacles.

sections.heading: Quad Revenant
sections.text: Quad Revenants act similarly to normal Revenants, but they shoot a 4-way flamethrower that rotates slowly.

sections.heading: Maze Roamer
sections.text: Maze Roamers are Gehenna-exclusive variants of Bonies that shoot eyeballs at Isaac when lined up. They always spawn in pairs, with their movements and attacks being mirrored between each other. When one dies, the other becomes angry and begins directly pursuing Isaac. The opposite Maze Roamer can be determined by its blood stained rags and mirrored eye socket.

sections.heading: Holy Bony
sections.text: Holy Bonies are larger and tougher versions of Bonies that were introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. Its bone projectiles travel in an arc and create a blue flame at its landing spot that blocks shots, deals contact damage, and despawns after some time.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] Despite Bonies being made entirely of bones, they leave bloodstains behind upon death.

• [Afterbirth onward] They only leave behind bones when killed.

• Bonies are one of a few enemies in-game to have their own unique projectile type.

• Bonies were confirmed to be the first enemy not designed by Edmund McMillen. He also confirmed that it was designed by Matt, the lead artist for The Binding Of Isaac: Rebirth, and that Edmund loved the simplicity of the AI, fitting "perfectly into the Isaac world."

• [Afterbirth onward] Bonies are spawned by The Forsaken, and Black Bonies are spawned by its Black Champion version. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Holy Bonies, Holy Mulligans, and Holy Eyes originated as cards from the card game The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls. [end edition note] 

• Holy Bonies have the highest Stage HP among regular Monsters in the game.

• If a Maze Roamer spawns as a Champion, its counterpart will be a Champion of the same type.

• The Maze Roamer's tactic of spawning in groups, lining up with Isaac, and mirroring the other Maze Roamer's movements are similar to the cut enemy Strifer, which appeared in Antibirth. The Strifer also appeared in Mausoleum, the alternate level to Gehenna.

• [Repentance] The Revenant first appeared in the Antibirth mod where it also had 2.4 stage hp.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the objects called chests; the floor; Chest (Floor)] 

Chests are objects that contain other objects, items, trinkets, pickups, enemies, other chests, and more. There are eleven types of chests.

sections.heading: Chest
sections.text:
Normal chests have no requirements to open. When opened, they will contain one of the following:

• Pickups: If a chest spawns pickups, 2-3 of the following batches of pickups will spawn. The same batch can be chosen multiple times. If Isaac has Mom's Key, an additional batch of 2-3 pickups spawns, up to a total of 4-6.

• 1-3 random coins

• 1 random Bomb

• 1 random Key

• 1 random Heart

• A trinket

• A pill

• A smaller Chest

| 1 Rune | 5% | ~5.95%

| 1 Trinket | 5% | ~5.95%

| 1 Lil' Battery | 5% | ~5.95%

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Red Chest
sections.text:
Red Chests are most commonly found in Curse Rooms and Devil Rooms, but can also occasionally replace normal chests. If Isaac is holding The Left Hand trinket, all chests will turn into Red Chests. They can contain the following:

• 2 Troll Bombs

• 1 Mega Troll Bomb

• 2 Spiders [Repentance] or 2 Striders in Downpour/Dross [end edition note] 

• 1-2 Soul Hearts

• A Red Chest pool item

• 1-2 pills

• Teleport to the Devil Room or Angel Room

• If the Devil/Angel Room has not been encountered normally on the floor yet, it will actually change what's in the deal.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Red Chests inside a Devil Room cannot teleport the player to the Devil Room.

• 1-3 Blue Flies

• 1-3 Blue Spiders

Having the Daemon's Tail trinket changes the chances to get various rewards from a Red Chest.

[Repentance] Reward Chances

| Reward | Base % + [Before Repentance] in Devil/Angel Room | In a Devil/Angel Room | Daemon's Tail | In a Devil/Angel Room & Daemon's Tail

| Red Chest Item | 10% | 10.5% | 11.3% | 12%

| Teleport to Devil/Angel Room | 5% | 0% | 5.5% | 0%

| 2 Spiders/Striders | 13% | 13.6% | 14.7% | 15.6%

| Mega Troll Bomb | 13% | 13.6% | 14.7% | 15.6%

| 3 Blue Flies | 7% | 7.3% | 7.9% | 8.4%

| 3 Blue Spiders | 7% | 7.3% | 7.9% | 8.4%

| 1 Soul Heart | 7.5% | 7.8% | 3% | 3.3%

| 2 Soul Hearts | 7.5% | 7.8% | 0.3% | 0.3%

| 2 Troll Bombs | 15% | 15.7% | 17% | 18%

| 2 Pills | 15% | 15.7% | 17% | 18%

[Before Afterbirth+] Red Chests have the same stats inside of a Devil/Angel Room as they can teleport players into the room despite being inside it.

sections.heading: Bomb Chest
sections.text: Bomb Chests (or alternatively Stone Chests) are grey chests that have an appearance similar to stone. They are unique in that they will only open if hit by an explosion. They give the same rewards as Golden Chests. Bomb Chests are most commonly found in Challenge Rooms, Curse Rooms, and Vaults, and they will occasionally replace normal chests.

sections.heading: Eternal Chest
sections.text:
Eternal Chests are similar in appearance to Golden Chests, except that they are a bright blue instead of gold and emit a pale glow. They have the same requirements to unlock and rewards as locked chests, but with an additional feature: the chest will close itself after a few seconds, at which point it can be opened again for more rewards at the cost of another key. However, there is a 25% chance that the chest will give nothing when opened, and if the chest contains nothing or an item, it will not reclose and cannot give any more rewards. They can be found in Angel Rooms, Vaults, and I AM ERROR rooms, and will very rarely replace normal chests and locked chests.

[Repentance] Eternal Chests are guaranteed to pay out at least once.

sections.heading: Spiked Chest
sections.text:
Spiked Chests are brown-colored chests with spikes protruding from them. Opening the chest will deal half a heart of damage to Isaac unless he has a way to resist the damage, such as with invulnerability effects or Holy Mantle. The Forgotten can also open spiked chests without taking damage by swinging their bone club. They give the same rewards as normal Chests. They can be rarely found upon completing a room or in Greed mode Shops.

[Repentance] Spiked Chests can also be opened without any damage being taken when using Magneto or holding Flat File.

[Before Afterbirth+] Unlike other chests, they do not appear on the minimap.

sections.heading: Mimic Chest
sections.text:
Mimic Chests appear similar to normal Chests (both for the sprite and the mini-map icon) until Isaac gets close to them, at which point they sprout spikes and act the same as a Spiked Chest.

[Before Repentance] They can be distinguished from normal Chests by their darker, brown coloring, the grayish spots on each side of the latch where the spikes will sprout from, and a tiny bloodstain.

[Repentance] Mimic Chests can be identified through a bloodstain on their bottom-right edge. Damage from this chest is considered self-damage.

The contents inside mimic chests will change whenever their spikes pop out, [Repentance] which can be observed with Guppy's Eye. [end edition note] The only way to get the original drops is to open it with Flat File, Magneto, or a melee swing attack such as The Forgotten's bone club or Spirit Sword.

sections.heading: Old Chest
sections.text:
Old Chests are similar in shape to Golden Chests, but have the color of a normal Chest and a worn-down appearance. They have the same requirements as locked chests. When opened, they contain one of the following:

• 1-3 Soul Hearts (43% chance)

• 3 trinkets (42% chance)

• An Old Chest item (10% chance)

• An Angel Room item (5% chance)

Old Chests can be found through the effects of Isaac's Tomb and inside I AM ERROR rooms.

sections.heading: Wooden Chest
sections.text:
Wooden Chests appear similar to normal Chests, but have a wooden texture. When opened, they contain one of the following:

• 2 cards or runes (45% chance)

• 2-3 pills (45% chance)

• A Wooden Chest item (10% chance)

Wooden Chests have a chance to replace regular chests, and can additionally be found in one Secret Room layout, as well as one Super Secret Room layout. Before they are unlocked, Wooden Chests are replaced by random regular Chests or Grab Bags (Spiked Chests and Locked Chests cannot replace the regular chest).

sections.heading: Mega Chest
sections.text:
Mega Chests appear similar to Golden Chests but are larger in appearance. They require 1-7 keys to open. When opened, they have an equal chance to contain one of the following:

• 2 Treasure Room Items

• Pickups equivalent to 5 Locked Chests, including trinkets, cards, and runes.

Mega Chests have a 0.8328% chance to replace any golden chest, and appears in one super secret room layout next to 2 keys, and one vault room layout. Before they are unlocked, Mega Chests are replaced by Locked Chests.

sections.heading: Haunted Chest
sections.text:
Haunted Chests appear nearly identical to normal Chests, but are slightly lighter in color and are haunted by a Polty. A haunted chest deals collision damage while the Polty is inside it. When Isaac gets close enough to a Haunted Chest, the Polty will emerge and throw the chest at him, breaking it open and dealing half a heart of damage if it hits. The Polty then acts normally.

• If the player leaves the room while the chest is in the air, it will disappear.

• If Polty have been permanently destroyed by Eraser, approaching the chest makes it pop open with a pink puff of smoke.

• Using Pause at a time when Polty has not yet picked it up, the chest will be impossible to open in any way until Polty unfreezes or dies. If you try to push Haunted Chest away from Polty, the ghost will appear immediately at the current chest after unfreezing.

sections.heading: Mom's Chest
sections.text:
Mom's Chest appears in Home. Mom's Chest has no requirements to open. It contains a Red Key upon the first visit (used to access the hidden closet), and on later encounters, an item from the Mom's Chest item pool.

• Can't be copied by D1.

• Can't be duplicated with Jera or Diplopia.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Normal chests cannot contain cards or items.

• Consider opening adjacent Red Chests before Stone Chests; Red Chests often contain Troll Bombs, which can blast Stone Chests open.

• Stone Chests can also be pushed to any position in the room, which can be used to save bombs by hitting multiple targets with one blast.

• Opening any chest (except for red chests) while on Chest or Dark Room will spawn an item.

• Chests of all types are considered pickups and will be doubled by Jera.

• [Repentance] Mom's Chest cannot be doubled.

• Mom's Key cannot change the contents of a chest; it only causes the chest to spawn more pickups if it normally would.

• Whenever a chest contains another chest, the smaller chest may also contain another chest. This can repeat as many times as the chance allows, but that chance is very slim by default. The smaller chest will have no different rewards than one of the same size.

• If these smaller chests contain an item, they will appear as tiny items.

• When using the Debug Console, a Golden Chest is referred to as a "Locked Chest" and a Stone Chest is referred to as a "Bomb Chest".

• [Before Afterbirth+] All of the icons for the items in the Golden Chest pool are heads or, as is the case for Bob's Brain and Infamy, head-related.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The Golden Chest pool also includes bags, such as IV Bag or Sack of Pennies.

• [Before Repentance] Empty opened chests may be rerolled into other pickups by using items such as the D20, but this must be done immediately, as opened chests will disappear upon leaving the room.

• [Repentance] Opened chests cannot be rerolled.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Prior to update v1.06.0182, Mimic Chests looked identical to normal Chests.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Mr. ME!, Red Key]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Mimic Chests share the same name with a recurring Chest enemy that has appeared in Dungeons and Dragons and eventually in various video games. Mimic Chests in the games act as a chest but attempt to catch players off guard and attack them. The Mimic Chests in The Binding of Isaac, although not a living entity, may have mostly been inspired by the Mimic Chest's ability to act like chests and catch players off guard, which explains its nature.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If a smaller chest is present in a room, re-entering the room will make the chest appear in a regular size.
Bug note: Unless the player has enough keys, flight, or any form of teleportation, the Mega Chest can block the way of a narrow passage way and may even deny access to many other rooms such as the Boss Room, possibly softlocking your run.
