fields.image name: [edition alternatives: baseline: Mimic Chest; Repentance: Mimic Chest Repentance]

Tainted Jacob.title: Tainted Jacob
Tainted Jacob.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Tainted Jacob is a character added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. He is the alternate version of Jacob. Tainted Jacob is unlocked by reaching Home and using the Red Key, Cracked Key, or Soul of Cain to access a special room in one of the walls while playing as Jacob & Esau.

Tainted Jacob spawns with 3 red heart containers and Anima Sola in his consumable slot, which freezes the nearest enemy for 5 seconds. However, he is pursued through the entire game by Dark Esau, who will try to charge into and kill Tainted Jacob. Anima Sola always affects Dark Esau if he is on screen.

If Dark Esau touches Tainted Jacob, Tainted Jacob "dies" and becomes functionally identical to The Lost but will not have Holy Mantle. While in this form, having an Eternal Heart in his last heart slot will block the next hit like a Holy Card.

Upon reaching a new floor, Tainted Jacob will return to his living state.

sections.heading: Dark Esau
sections.text:
Dark Esau is a hostile mini-boss version of Esau.
Dark Esau spawns 20 to 40 seconds after Tainted Jacob enters a new floor, emerging from a crack in the ground, in his wake creating a circle of damaging flames around him.

Dark Esau continuously pursues Tainted Jacob by floating towards him, speeding up when further away and slowing down to a near standstill when within a fixed distance. If Tainted Jacob remains within that fixed distance for a short period of time, Dark Esau will perform a fiery charge attack in which he will pause for a brief moment with a sound cue before rushing towards him, damaging any enemies in his path.

Anima Sola's targeting always prioritizes Dark Esau. When released, Dark Esau immediately charges towards Tainted Jacob's current position.

Using Anima Sola in a room with no enemies will immediately spawn Dark Esau without exhausting the item's charge, bypassing the usual wait period before spawning.

Dark Esau's position at all times is determined by his position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning he persists in the same location even when Tainted Jacob moves through rooms. Entering a new room cancels Esau's charge if he was preparing one or frees him if he was bound by Anima Sola.

Dark Esau is impervious to damage and cannot be killed, but can block enemy projectiles.

Dark Esau is able to damage enemies as well as Tainted Jacob in the following ways:

• Creates 12 rings of 8 flames when spawning, each dealing 6 damage to enemies they hit, dealing anywhere between 6-576 damage depending on how close they are to him. These flames can be blocked by obstacles.

• Deals 30 contact damage per tick to enemies and pushes them (60 damage per second).

• Deals an extra 10 damage per tick to enemies and inflicts Burning on them when leaving a flame trail while charging at Tainted Jacob (300 damage per second).

• Dark Esau's charge also ignores Boss Armor.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
Throughout the majority of a run, Tainted Jacob is harassed by Dark Esau with no intended way of permanently getting rid of him. Because of this, playing as Tainted Jacob requires the player to manage both the playable Jacob and his vengeful brother Esau.

• Using Anima Sola is key to success for Tainted Jacob, as it can help prevent damage from Dark Esau or turn him into a powerful weapon against enemies.

• In the Mines, Tainted Jacob can intentionally run into Dark Esau in order to abuse the mechanics of The Lost form (specifically Flight in an area which normally removes any previous sources of flight you may have attained) to quickly and easily acquire the Knife Piece 2 with a rapid and flight-assisted escape if you are attempting to reach the Corpse to defeat Mother.

• Typically, the escape path would become excessively difficult due to both Mother's Shadow and Dark Esau attempting to charge at you in intervals which are typically out of sync, making it very difficult to escape without taking damage or potentially dying.

• By remaining in The Lost form, this also allows you bypass the damage which would normally be required to enter the door in order to advance to Mausoleum / Gehenna.

• It is recommended to fully clear the floor first, as Tainted Jacob remains in The Lost form until the next floor is reached.

• While in his Lost form, Tainted Jacob can take Devil Deals in the same way as the Lost. At the end of each floor with a Devil Deal spawn, it is possible to intentionally have Dark Esau turn Tainted Jacob into The Lost form in order to receive free Devil Deals.

• Items and transformations that give you flight (Guppy, Beelzebub, Seraphim, and Leviathan) to be able to more easily dodge Dark Esau in rooms with pits and rocks, and/or spectral tears (quicker room clears with obstacles plus can cheese obstacle mechanics with Dark Esau) can help quickly clear rooms and avoid the brother's attacks.

• Perfection is not lost upon getting hit by Dark Esau.

• It can actually be quite risky to take Birthright. Each Dark Esau can charge in a different direction than the other, which ultimately increases your chances of getting hit by one of them.

sections.heading: Defense
sections.text:
Dark Esau himself should be respected. Being touched a single time by Dark Esau has a high chance of leading to a run's end by putting Jacob in his fragile Lost state for the remainder of a floor.

• Dark Esau deals no contact damage to Jacob while chained down with Anima Sola.

• Dark Esau's touch effect can be avoided while shielded, invulnerable, or otherwise immune to damage (such as with Holy Mantle or Gnawed Leaf).

• Dark Esau keeps a consistent distance from Jacob, and will only charge if he is within this distance. Dark Esau will never actually be able to touch Jacob unless he starts his charge animation, charges, or Jacob runs into him.

• As such, running from and maintaining enough distance from Dark Esau will prevent him from charging.

• In some cases such as being next to an obstacle, Dark Esau will stop moving within the prop and will be unable to charge until Jacob moves away from it.

• Dark Esau will only charge at Jacob once he enters his cardinal line of sight. Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he is positioned diagonally from him, even if Jacob is standing still.

• Dark Esau's position at all times is determined by his position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning he persists in the same location even when Tainted Jacob moves through rooms. Entering a new room cancels Esau's charge if he was preparing one or frees him if he was bound by Anima Sola.

• Caution should be taken when moving between rooms where Dark Esau is near the doorway, as this may lead to a situation where Tainted Jacob immediately runs into Dark Esau.

• Teleporting a great distance or traveling quickly through rooms with the help of special items or a high speed stat makes it harder for Dark Esau to catch up to Jacob.

• If Dark Esau is in the process of traveling between rooms, it is possible to use Anima Sola to chain him outside of the current area Tainted Jacob is in.

• As Dark Esau takes time to respawn after entering a new floor, the first few seconds on every floor can be used to explore rooms freely.

• Dark Esau will not charge at Jacob if he eats a Paralysis Pill.

sections.heading: Offense
sections.text:
Considering the damage Dark Esau can deal to enemies and the fact that Anima Sola can be canceled early by using it a second time, Dark Esau can become a powerful, albeit dangerous weapon to use against enemies by positioning Tainted Jacob in ways that manipulate him into charging into enemies. This is further compounded, as his charge attack ignores Boss Armor.

• Anima Sola can be used in an empty room to instantly summon Dark Esau in order to use him advantageously.

• Dark Esau's charge is able to single-handedly kill most early bosses in one or two hits. He can also be held in place with Anima Sola to bait chasing enemies, as Jacob can stand behind Dark Esau and cause them to run into him.

• In Greed Mode, Anima Sola will always be charged at the beginning of a new wave. This can be taken advantage of by binding Dark Esau before a new wave begins and then letting him charge into a freshly spawned enemy group or a priority enemy like a champion. Since releasing Dark Esau manually does not consume the item charge, the item will still be available to restrict him again immediately afterwards.

• Dark Esau's charge will extinguish Fire Places.

• Dark Esau cannot damage friendly enemies.

• When Dark Esau charges while in fear, he charges away from Tainted Jacob.

sections.heading: Co-Op Mode
sections.text:
• Dark Esau cannot affect other players and ignores them completely.

• [Before Repentance+] If multiple players are playing Tainted Jacob, then any Tainted Jacob who touches any Dark Esau will still be turned into a ghost or die. Tainted Jacob players will only be able to use Anima Sola on their own Dark Esau, and if one of the Tainted Jacobs is completely killed, both Dark Esaus will begin to target the one that is still living.

• [Before Repentance+] When Tainted Jacob completely dies and is turned into a small ghost baby as a Co-Op partner, Dark Esau will still follow the ghost of Tainted Jacob if no other Tainted Jacob players are in the match, allowing them to still use him as a high damage weapon to help their teammates.

• [Repentance+] Dark Esau will no longer deal damage to enemies or charge at the ghost of Tainted Jacob until he is revived.

• If Tainted Jacob was turned into his ghostly form by Dark Esau, then dying and being revived upon completion of the boss will have him revive as his ghostly form.

• [Before Repentance+] If Tainted Jacob is dead at the start of a floor, Dark Esau will still spawn, but will target one of the living players instead. Unless they are also playing Tainted Jacob, he will never hurt them outside his spawning animation.

• [Repentance+] If Tainted Jacob is dead at the end of a floor, he will respawn at the start of the next floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Dark Esau is considered a boss.

• Like every other "boss", Dark Esau can be spawned with debug commands. However, if playing as someone other than Tainted Jacob, the player will be immune to his attacks.

• • Jacob, even in his normal non-tainted form, is an exception. When touched by Dark Esau, he will take damage, but will not turn into a ghost. Esau, like most characters, is still immune to Dark Esau.

• When the console command "restart 39" is loaded, the player will be spawned as a ghostly version of Tainted Jacob. The only differences is that Dark Esau never seems to spawn and that this version of Tainted Jacob has the health of The Lost.

sections.heading: Item Interactions
sections.text:
• Birthright: Dark Esau splits into two. Both Esaus will always charge at the same time, and one will not charge if the other is not in position. Using Anima Sola chains both Dark Esaus at once and forces them together into one spot. Subsequent uses of Anima Sola release each Dark Esau one at a time. Anima Sola's recharge time is reduced to 10 seconds, and chain duration is increased to 6.67 seconds.

• Health Ups (eg; Breakfast): Tainted Jacob will still receive the additional health, even in his Lost form.

• This also applies to health down items as well, such as Dead Cat.

• However, Health Down pills turn into Health Up pills while in Lost form.

• Items that grant broken heart containers such as Magic Skin, VI - The Lovers?, or Heartbreak will still add a broken heart container as normal, even while Jacob is in the Lost's form.

• Dead Cat: If Tainted Jacob dies in the Lost form with this item, he will not regain the body back.

• Homing and most other targeting effects will not target Dark Esau despite him being an enemy. On-kill effect items will also activate if Dark Esau kills enemies.

• Cube Baby: Dark Esau can also "kick" the baby into enemies.

• Strawman: Dark Esau ignores and does no harm to Strawman. Strawman can also walk through Dark Esau.

• Angry Fly: Will chase only Dark Esau whenever possible.

• Car Battery: Anima Sola will spawn 2 sets of chains. The second set will either tie up another enemy or if no other enemies are present it will tie up Dark Esau for twice as long. Using it again will unchain whichever enemy is closer to Tainted Jacob first, adding another factor to keep track of if using Dark Esau offensively.

sections.heading: Favored Items
sections.text:
• 9 Volt: Reduces the charge time of Anima Sola by half, giving the player much better control of Dark Esau.

• In addition, Gello will be very useful in this case since it will fully charge after clearing the room and can be used in each room; allowing you to focus more on dodging rather than aiming.

• Athame /Vasculitis /Bone Spurs: Killing enemies with Dark Esau also triggers the effect.

• The Battery: Anima Sola will hold an extra charge making it available for use more often.

• Belly Jelly /Infamy: The chance to avoid damage still applies to Dark Esau, potentially saving Jacob from death/being turned into the Lost.

• Glowing Hourglass: Returns Jacob to his regular form if he was turned into the Lost in the actual room.

• Gnawed Leaf: Allows Jacob to stand still and let Dark Esau do all of the work for him.

• Holy Mantle: Block attacks from Dark Esau and also protects Tainted Jacob in his Lost form.

• How to Jump: Can be used to jump over Dark Esau.

• Pause: Stopping time while Dark Esau is charging through an enemy will cause him to constantly damage it via contact until the effect wears off.

• Punching Bag: When Dark Esau spawns, he will aggro to the closest of Punching Bag or Jacob. So long as Anima Sola is not used, he will never re-target Jacob, making him endlessly attempt to kill the Punching Bag until the next floor, where he will target whomever is closest upon spawning.

• Satanic Bible/Devil's Crown: Allows Jacob to intentionally turn into his Lost form to receive free Devil Room items every floor.

• Sigil of Baphomet: Kills made by Dark Esau will also trigger a temporary shield.

• Stop Watch: Dark Esau is slowed by this item, making him easier to dodge and outrun.

• Unicorn Stump: Provides temporary invincible each room, which also provides a chance to use Anima Sola in offensive way safely.

• Ventricle Razor: Entering portals created by this item while Dark Esau is charging will immediately interrupt the charge.

• Book of Shadows: Makes Jacob immune to Dark Esau attacks for the duration of the shield.
Any items part of a transformation that grants flight, like Guppy, Beelzebub, Seraphim, and Leviathan, and any items that give flight in general, like Fate, Dead Dove, or Lord of the Pit. This will make it easier to dodge and reduces chances of being stuck on restrictive paths.

sections.heading: Disfavored Items
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues: The wisps generated from Anima Sola will target Dark Esau, despite his invincibility.

• Vasculitis: Enemies killed by Dark Esau release fire tears which can explode and deal accidental damage to Jacob.

• Epiphora: Jacob will have to be constantly moving because of Dark Esau, making it near impossible to stay and fire in one direction for the increased tears.

• Isaac's Heart: Dark Esau no longer kills Jacob if he touches his body, but contact with the heart will. This makes it far easier to die since both Isaac's Heart and Dark Esau's default positions are behind Jacob, causing them to collide very frequently.

• Lost Soul: The soul can be killed by Dark Esau, making it very difficult to keep it alive.

• This can be somewhat mitigated with BFFS!, which grants the Lost Soul a shield.

sections.heading: Unlockable Items
sections.text: [achievement text: RC Remote, The Sun and the Moon, Soul of Jacob and Esau, Golden Trinket, Anima Sola, Found Soul, Esau Jr.]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Dark Esau may be based on a story in the Book of Genesis, in which Esau attempts to kill Jacob after both Jacob and their mother tricked their father Isaac into giving Jacob a blessing intended for Esau, resulting in Jacob fleeing from Esau's wrath.

• This is also further backed up by Tainted Jacob's unlock achievement name, "The Deserter."

• This is also supported by Tainted Jacob's Birthright effect, which benefits Dark Esau more than Jacob himself. The Birthright was originally intended for Esau.

• Tainted Jacob unlocks both XIX - The Sun? and XVIII - The Moon?, this is a reversal of Jacob and Esau as his radiance disappears along with Esau's misery for no longer being Jacob's slave, as now Esau is the eternal tormentor of Jacob, Jacob fulfills both the misery of the reverse Sun and the instability and terror of the reverse Moon.

• Dark Esau is referred to as "The Revenant" in his Four Souls card.

• A Revenant is a spirit that has come back from the dead to enact their revenge on somebody that has wronged them. This fits as Dark Esau is a demon trying to kill Jacob for stealing his birthright and blessing from their father Isaac.

• Anima Sola targeting Dark Esau may be referring to Genesis 27:40 where Isaac tells Esau that he will live by the sword and serve his brother, but throwing his yoke from his neck when grown restless.

• The item description which appears when obtaining Birthright as Tainted Jacob may be a reference to a story in Genesis, where Esau sells Jacob his birthright for stew.

• Dark Esau's behavior is similar to that of Mother's Shadow.

• Prior to v1.7.5, Dark Esau had a health bar. Upon death, he would be dragged into a pit by Big Horn and create a Mama Mega!-like explosion that would turn Tainted Jacob into his Lost form.

• He can now only be killed via the Debug Console and will have the effect, but this won't turn Jacob into his Lost form.

• Dark Esau still shows that he has 250 Hp in the bestiary despite after v1.7.5 he is invulnerable and does not have any health.

fields.name: Dark Esau
fields.behavior: Charges at Tainted Jacob. Upon collision, transforms him into The Lost for the remainder of the floor

Pluto.title: Pluto
Pluto.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.7 tears

• Significantly shrinks Isaac, allowing him to squeeze between objects and makes some enemy shots pass over him.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• With enough speed and the correct angle or being pushed by an explosion, it is possible to cross pits and pass through obstacles, allowing Isaac to reach places he usually isn't able to reach.

• Pluto can stack with other size reduction effects.

• May allow Isaac to squeeze through the walls and floors in Crawl Spaces and 2nd/3rd phase of Rotgut. Passing through the outermost wall in an unintended direction leads to the I AM ERROR room.

• The decrease in size makes dodging certain tear effects easier, most notably Hush's continuum tears, and Dogma's feather attacks from their respective second phases.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Cricket's Body: Split tears' range is dropped drastically. Range ups do not mitigate the effect.

• Dr. Fetus: Drops the bombs' range drastically despite no change in the range stat, greatly increasing chance of self-damage. Range ups do not mitigate the effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Pluto originates from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, it would also give a range down.

• Pluto's effects reference the planetoid Pluto's nature as a dwarf planet.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: It is possible to throw a shrunken Tainted Forgotten exactly into the room corner, making it impossible to pick him up.

fields.description: +0.7 tears. Significantly shrinks Isaac, allowing him to squeeze between objects and makes some enemy shots pass over him.

Pointy Rib.title: Pointy Rib
Pointy Rib.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a bone familiar that can be aimed with the fire buttons in all directions and does contact damage.

• The familiar will continuously hover back and forth in the direction that it is pointing in.

• The damage is equal to Isaac's tear damage and is dealt 6 times per second.

• The damage increases when Isaac is moving on the direction the familiar is pointing in based on Isaac's current speed, up to twice of its base damage.

• The familiar will damage Poops and Fire Places.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Proptosis: Triples the contact damage. Has no penalty with range.

• Spin to Win: As Spin to Win allows moving faster than the normal limit, the bonus damage from jabbing can also be over 100%.

• Spirit Sword: When doing a spin attack, the familiar will spin with the sword.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • BFFS!: Doubles the base contact damage, but not the bonus damage granted from Isaac's movement.

fields.name: Pointy Rib
fields.description: Spawns a bone familiar that hovers back and forth in front of Isaac, dealing damage equal to Isaac's damage.

Poke Go.title: Poke Go
Poke Go.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Adds a 20% chance to spawn a friendly enemy upon entering a room with enemies in it. The following enemies can spawn from Poke Go:

• Attack Fly

• Fat Bat

• Frowning Gaper

• One Tooth

• Pooter

• Vis

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance+] The effect is not activated upon entering the main room of Greed Mode, neither when fighting the waves, making it nearly useless.

• Multiple friendly enemies can spawn at the same time.

• For enemies that spawn other enemies, the spawned enemies will also be friendly.

• Enemy variants may spawn.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Friendly monsters are still affected by Ace Cards.

• Blood Puppy: Either angry version of Blood Puppy will target friendly enemies as well and can drag them along with it when it charges them. Blood Puppy cannot damage friendly enemies however friendly enemies can damage Blood Puppy despite not targeting it outright.

• Broken Modem: Broken Modem also affects friendly enemies and projectiles created by them.

• Eraser: Enemies erased via Eraser will never spawn again. This can be a detriment if Vises are erased, as it greatly reduces the usefulness of Poke Go.

• [Repentance] Ghost Bombs / Hungry Soul / Purgatory / Vade Retro: Explosions from ghosts can kill friendly enemies. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item is a reference to Pokémon GO: an augmented reality mobile game in which Pokémon are generated around the player as they walk around in real life.

• The pickup quote is a shortened version of "Gotta catch 'em all!", one of the series' marketing slogans.

• "A charmed (enemy) appears!" is a reference to the phrase "A wild Pokémon appears!" from the games.

• Poke Go was originally an unofficial item which was supposed to showcase the modding capabilities of Afterbirth+ in the PAX 2016 livestream. However, all items included in the demo were later added to the final game.

• Since Poke Go is simply part of Isaac's imagination, Edmund McMillen confirmed that Isaac therefore technically knew about Pokémon Go.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room than the one he is currently in ( [Before Repentance] such as the starting room of a new floor) will duplicate friendly enemies.

fields.name: Poke Go
fields.description: Upon entering a room with enemies in it, has a chance to spawn a random friendly enemy that persists across rooms.

Poker Chip.title: Poker Chip
Poker Chip.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• If a Chest would contain Red Heart, Penny, Bombs, or Keys and pills, cards, or runes (for Wooden Chests), it has a 50/50 chance to either drop extra consumables or replace all of its contents with an Attack Fly.

• The affected chests include:

• • Chests

• • Locked Chests

• • Bomb Chests

• • Eternal Chests

• • Spiked Chests

• • Mimic Chests

• • Mega Chests

• • Haunted Chests

• • Wooden Chests

• This excludes:

• • Red Chests

• • Old Chests

• • Mom's Chest

• Consequently, Poker Chip has no effect in Chest or Dark Room.

• [Repentance] If opening a Mega Chest yields pickups, it can spawn 1-2 Attack Flies alongside the pickups.

• [Repentance+] If the chest would contain an item of quality 0-2, it is rechosen to get a +1 quality bonus.

• If there are no suitable replacement items remaining in the Golden Chest pool, the Treasure Room pool can be used instead.

• The quality improvement is not applied in Chest or Dark Room.

• [Repentance+] Slightly increases the payout chance from Slot Machines, Fortune Telling Machines, Crane Games, Shell Games and Shop Restock Machines.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The effect of Poker Chip does not trigger when it's picked up, nor does it deactivate when it's dropped. Rather, Isaac must leave and re-enter a room for a chest's contents to update.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either doubles gambling payouts. Having both triples them.

• Guppy's Eye: Provided that the Poker Chip is not smelted, it can be used in conjunction with the eye to open all chests with extra pickups, while dropping the chip for any chests containing flies, nullifying the downside of the trinket.

• Sharp Key: Enemies killed by keys have a 50/50 chance to spawn extra pickups or an Attack Fly; the attack fly will be instantly killed by the thrown key.

fields.description: Chests have a 50% chance of paying out with extra pickups and a 50% chance of replacing all of its contents with an Attack Fly. [Repentance+] If the chest would contain an item of quality 0-2, it is rechosen to get a +1 quality bonus. Slightly increases the payout chance from Slot Machines, Fortune Telling Machines, Crane Games, Shell Games and Shop Restock Machines.

Poky.title: Poky
Poky.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Pokies are invulnerable enemies that slide around the room aimlessly in cardinal directions, dealing contact damage. They may move slightly faster towards Isaac if he gets in their sight. When the enemies or [Afterbirth onward] Pressure Plates are cleared from the room, the Poky stops moving and no longer does contact damage.

sections.heading: Slide
sections.text: Slides will remain stationary in their positions and have their spikes drawn out, dealing contact damage. Should Isaac get in their sight in a cardinal direction, Slides will move towards Isaac's direction, then move back to their previous position after hitting a wall or obstacle. They have a short cooldown after charging towards Isaac before being able to move again. They will not stop moving even after enemies in the room are cleared. [Afterbirth onward] They can, however, be deactivated by Pressure Plates and retract their spikes as a result, meaning that they'll stop dealing contact damage and also stop moving towards Isaac.

sections.heading: Wall Hugger
sections.text: Wall Huggers move around walls and obstacles endlessly. A couple of seconds after Isaac enters a room with them, their spikes will be drawn out, dealing contact damage. They cannot be shut down, even if enemies are cleared from the room. [Afterbirth onward] They can, however, be deactivated by Pressure Plates, retracting its spikes, meaning that it'll no longer move and do contact damage. Their paths can also be stopped should a Fire Place or static enemy be in their way.

sections.heading: Grudge
sections.text:
Grudges are exclusive to Mausoleum and Gehenna and are characterized by the eye in the center and two spikes on each side instead of three. Very briefly after Isaac enters a room, their spikes will be drawn out. They remain stationary until there's an uninterrupted path between it and Isaac in a cardinal direction, at which point it will quickly slide towards him, dealing a full heart of damage if it hits. They will not return to their original position after moving. They also have unique interactions with other stage elements.

• If it runs into an enemy, it will be pushed along with it, instantly killing it if they're caught between the Grudge and a wall/obstacle.

• Even bosses are prone to this instant kill effect. However, the only method to witness this happening is to get a TMTRAINER effect with summoning friendly Grudges.

• If it runs over a button, it will be pressed. Many rooms use this to create puzzles where Isaac has to manipulate the Grudge into pressing buttons.

• If it runs into a Bomb, it will be pushed along with it, causing it to instantly explode if it gets caught between the Grudge and a wall/obstacle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• A Poky can appear in a Loki boss fight.

• These monsters can be destroyed using Chaos Card, Little Horn and Euthanasia. However, Grudges will re-spawn upon re-entering the room.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Two Pokies can appear in a Super Pride miniboss fight.

• [Afterbirth onward] In Greed mode, if a Slide is spawned and all waves are cleared, the Slide will still try to harm Isaac. Leaving and re-entering the room will make the Slide disappear.

• [Repentance] All Pokies except for Grudges will retract their spikes if Isaac holds Flat File.

• [Repentance+] Golden Trinket / Mom's Box + Flat File: Grudges are also affected, retracting their spikes. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] The Poky, Slide, and Grudge are destroyed by Hagalaz on use.

• Strangely, it has no effect on the Wall Hugger. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The three original variants are similar to Blade Traps, hazards found in The Legend of Zelda, with each trap imitating the different behaviors of them between games.

• Pokies imitate the Blade Traps from Phantom Hourglass and Spirit Tracks, being traps that move freely around the room.

• Slides imitate the traditional Blade Traps from the original The Legend of Zelda, charging towards Isaac whenever he is in their line of detection.

• Wall Huggers imitate the Blade Traps from Twilight Princess, moving around the room's walls and obstacles.

• Grudges are very similar to Crush Traps from Spelunky, having a similar design with an eye in the center, the same movement pattern, and the same quirk of instantly killing enemies it traps between itself and a wall or obstacle.

• [Repentance] Isaac has a unique death animation if he dies to a Grudge. He bursts into gibs like any other enemy, and his body is invisible (aside from his ghost arising from it).

• This is a reference to the death sequence caused by crush traps, from the game Spelunky, which behave exactly like a Grudge.

• [Repentance] Grudge's eyes will stare at and follow Isaac as he moves.

Polycephalus.title: Polycephalus
Polycephalus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Polycephalus is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In the Catacombs and the Flooded Caves.

• [Repentance] Only in the Catacombs.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Polycephalus burrows underground when Isaac is not within range. While burrowed he becomes invincible and follows Isaac's movements. When close to Isaac, he pops out and performs one of the following attacks:

• Sprays out a cluster of projectiles towards Isaac, similar to Monstro, but more drawn out.

• Fires a spread of 3 projectiles at Isaac.

• Shoots out 8 projectiles in all directions.

• Summons a Round Worm.
He will stay vulnerable for a few moments after performing an attack before quickly burrowing underground again.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 1] : Summons Para-Bites instead of Round Worms. All projectile attacks are replaced with a ring of six projectiles.
[bc: 20] : Two Polycephaluses, each with 50% HP (100), replace the normal Polycephalus. They do not spawn Round Worms.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Stain is his posthumous version, who also shows up in Chapter 2. Polycephalus is one of four bosses to have their posthumous version in the same chapter, the others being Gemini having Blighted Ovum in Chapter 1, Chub having Carrion Queen in Chapter 2 and the Tuff Twins having The Shell in Chapter 2.5.

• [Before Repentance] However, Polycephalus is the only one of them to have their posthumous version in the same environments as well, sharing both the Catacombs and the Flooded Caves with The Stain. The only difference is that The Stain can appear in Caves as well, where Polycephalus cannot.

• • [Repentance] This is no longer the case as of Repentance, since Polycephalus no longer appears in the Flooded Caves while The Stain no longer appears in The Catacombs.

• • 
• This makes Polycephalus the only boss whose posthumous variation is more likely to be encountered than its normal variation, since it can only be encountered in the Catacombs, whereas the Stain can be encountered in the Caves and Flooded Caves.

• Polycephaly is the condition of having more than one head.

• Polycephalus shares his name with a cactus.

• Polycephalus is one of the four bosses that can be spawned by It Lives!, the other three being Chub, [Repentance] Fistula and Teratoma.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Prior to Booster Pack #5, Red Champion Polycephalus could spawn Scarred Para-Bites if he was fought in the Scarred Womb. [end edition note]

Polyphemus.title: Polyphemus
Polyphemus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
Notes
sections.text: • [Before Repentance] Polyphemus is a special item.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20: Damage is reduced and tear rate is increased.

• Abyss: When Polyphemus is picked up instead of being converted into a locust, it grants all of Abyss's locusts the high damage up without suffering the tears down allowing Isaac to increase his damage rate substantially the more items he uses Abyss on.

• Dr. Fetus: Increases tear delay, and after the first bomb explodes, a second bomb appears where the first one exploded, doing roughly half the damage of the first.

• The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider/C Section: The tear rate is not lowered further, but the effect on damage becomes a flat +5 bonus instead.

• The Forgotten: The Forgotten's bone club becomes massive. It deals very high damage but has a very low swing rate.

• Rock Bottom: Allows Isaac to keep his previous fire rate in addition to the massive damage boost.

• Shard of Glass: The rapidly spawning red tears do full damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Haemolacria: The main tear retains the semi-piercing ability and may not burst when hitting a weaker enemy. Split tears do not semi-pierce.

• Lachryphagy: Greatly increases how big the fed tear can grow.

• Lost Contact: Isaac's tears will block enemy shots and continue, but lose 10 damage. If the tear had less than 10 damage left, it disappears.

• Piercing tears: Semi-piercing is replaced by proper piercing, with no loss of damage on any enemy contact.

• Polyphemus: No further effect when multiple copies are acquired.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Much like other eye-altering passive items, Polyphemus has a unique appearance on The Forgotten, appearing as an empty eye socket.

• Polyphemus, ancient Greek for "The much vaunted", is a Cyclops. He is the son of Poseidon and the sea nymph Thoosa. This item is a reference to the cyclops named Polyphemus from the poem by Homer called "The Odyssey"

• This item is used in Slow Roll.

fields.description: Isaac fires huge tears that deal massive damage, but fire rate is greatly decreased. If a tear kills an enemy, it travels on with any leftover damage.

Poot Mine.title: Poot Mine
Poot Mine.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Poot Mines are an enemy added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. They are encountered only in Dross.

Poot Mines float in place, producing lingering gas clouds and propelling themselves away from Isaac when they take damage non-consecutively. On death, they explode, causing all of the gas clouds they created to explode in a chain reaction.

Pooter.title: Pooter
Pooter.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Pooter wanders very slowly around the room to the point where they stay put, and they shoot one bullet at Isaac. Pooters will not shoot if Isaac wears Skatole. A Fly can turn into a Pooter if it stays near Poop for long enough.

sections.heading: Super Pooter
sections.text: The Super Pooter behaves like the Pooter, except that it shoots two bullets in a V-shaped pattern. Just like the Pooter, it also does not shoot Isaac with Skatole.

sections.heading: Tainted Pooter
sections.text:
Tainted Pooters are corrupt and much tankier versions of Pooters. They move the same as Pooters, slowly drifting towards Isaac, however instead of firing just one blood shot at him, they shoot 4 big shots that become 2 smaller ones when in contact with a wall or obstacle.

They are exclusive to the Ascent to Home.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Prior to Afterbirth †, Super Pooters were called Fat Flies.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If a Pooter or a Super Pooter is stunned at the same time that it tries to shoot Isaac after the effect wears off, their shot will be fired without its corresponding animation.
Bug note: If a Pooter or a Super Pooter is stunned or feared at the same time that it tries to shoot Isaac, its sound effect will repeat continuously until the effect is gone.

Pop!.title: Pop!
Pop!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Replaces Isaac's tears with eyeballs that can bounce off of each other.

• Isaac's tears are no longer limited by range, and will instead dissipate when they stop moving or when hitting an enemy or obstacle.

• [Repentance] Eyeball tears will start to fall to the ground after bouncing off of each other 8 times.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Anti-Gravity: Tears will force each other out of the way if placed on top of another tear. Releasing the trigger button propels the tears in the direction Isaac was firing at the time before slowing down to a stop.

• Azazel/Brimstone/Tainted Azazel/Technology 2: Fires out multiple Pop! tears at the end of the laser, which is dramatically shortened.

• Brimstone + Tainted Azazel: The beam is shortened to around double the range of Azazel's, while a constant stream of red eyeballs come out of the end.

• Continuum: The tears will bump into each other, increasing in speed as they go through the room until they dissipate or hit an enemy.

• Tractor Beam + Continuum: Occasionally, some tears will glitch out of their position for a short while. Contact with an enemy while a glitched tear is on-screen will fling Isaac to a corner of the room. This can potentially cause a softlock if Isaac is blocked by obstacles and does not have How to Jump or flight to escape. Bombs will not work either, as the explosion will not trigger despite the sound of one playing once the bomb sets off.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body: Split tears can also be knocked around.

• Eye of the Occult: Tears will continuously try to follow the crosshair, virtually extending their lifespan ad infinitum until they hit an enemy or obstacle. This can cause tears to quickly fill the room.

• Godhead: Tears gain a damaging aura and become damaging aura fields.

• Godhead + A Lump of Coal: Tears will quickly fill up the screen and increase in damage, easily killing any enemy.

• Haemolacria: Tears fire a burst of smaller tears in random directions when hitting an obstacle or stopping and falling to the ground.

• Immaculate Heart: Tears that orbit Isaac will be constantly moving and therefore will never disappear until they hit an enemy or Isaac leaves the room. Filling the orbit with enough tears can potentially cause a chaotic, vibrating ring of eyeballs enveloping Isaac as the tears constantly collide with one another.

• Ipecac: Tears do not arc and will instead shoot straight. They retain their explosive abilities on impact with enemies or obstacles, or when they eventually fall. Tears also do not explode when bouncing off of each other, which can be used to propel the high-powered tears to other enemies.

• Lead Pencil/Monstro's Lung: Removes the arcing effect from the tears, greatly increasing air time. The tight cluster the tears are shot in will cause unpredictable spread, however.

• A Lump of Coal: Tears will increase their damage and size as they travel, and they are not limited by range.

• My Reflection: Tears constantly swarm around Isaac, quickly filling the room.

• The Parasite: When tears hit an enemy, obstacle, or wall, they split into many smaller tears that have the same behavior as eyeball tears.

• Rubber Cement: Allows tears to never disappear when hitting enemies and objects, increasing the uptime of tears greatly.

• Rubber Cement + A Lump Of Coal: Tears continuously increase in size and damage as they bounce endlessly around the room. Eventually the damage can be enough to kill bosses in a single frame.

• [Repentance] Tech.5/Technology/Technology 2: The laser's range is drastically reduced, and an eyeball is created at the end of the laser each shot.

• [Repentance] Technology + Monstro's Lung Lung will fire laser beams as normal, but Pop eyeballs will appaear at the tail end of every shot, including obstacles hit by the beams.

• [Repentance] Tiny Planet: With enough tears and/or fire rate, the Pop! tears can constantly collide with each other, causing them to orbit Isaac indefinitely.

• Trisagion: Every damage tick will shoot out a Pop! tear making this synergy a potent combination. Trisagion shots will also hover in the air longer than normal.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Angelic Prism: The Prism will split eyeballs that it passes over.

• [Before Repentance] Azazel/Brimstone/Technology: Lasers override Pop!.

• C Section: Fetuses' movements do not extend their lifespan, it is still limited by Range. Fetuses do not fall after bouncing off of each other 8 times.

• Dr. Fetus/Epic Fetus/Mom's Knife/Tech X: Overrides Pop!.

• Immaculate Heart: Tears will be blocked by orbiting the eyeballs, severely reducing damage output.

• Flat Stone: Eyeball tears bounce repeatedly against the floor when they're about to disappear.

• The Ludovico Technique: Overridden by The Ludovico Technique, though the tear looks like an eyeball.

• Lachryphagy: Chance of tears to bounce off each other when the first tear is eaten or the tear bursting.

• Sinus Infection: Boogers that are stuck to enemies will cause other tears to bounce off them, making the enemy unable to be hit from that side until the boogers dissipate.

• [Before Repentance] Tech.5/Technology 2: The laser is unaffected by Pop!.

• Tractor Beam: Tears can now only knock each other forward.

• Trisagion: Tears will remain floating but will not bump each other.

• (Not Recommended) Any kind of piercing shots (i.e. Cupid's Arrow) except for Trisagion (which can damage the same enemy more than once) will gradually fill the room up with 'expired' shots that do no damage to enemies. This can greatly reduce the overall damage output rate in longer boss fights.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Pop! is based on this Steam Workshop item by Ashkait and Scayze, originally known as Bank Shot and themed about billiard balls.

fields.description: Replaces Isaac's tears with eyeballs that can bounce off of each other. The eyeballs are not limited by range, and will instead dissipate when they stop moving or when hitting an enemy or obstacle.

• [Repentance] The item only costs 10 coins when found in a Shop.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Gives the wisps of the following items depending on the reward:

• Fly: Nothing.

• Bomb: Mr. Boom wisp.

• Penny: Coin wisp for each coin dropped.

• Red Heart: Yum Heart wisp.

• Key: Dad's Key wisp.

• Pill: Mom's Bottle of Pills wisp.

• Pretty Fly: 2-4 Guppy's Head wisps.

• Equality!: Allows Isaac to get rid of coins and potentially spawn bombs and keys, making it easier to keep the number of pickups the same.

• IV Bag: Can be alternated between to gain ridiculous amounts of pickups from only a few initial coins or hearts.

• Keeper: Can be used to spawn coins in the room to heal Keeper.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Portable Slot could be used to spawn an enemy Fly after defeating the boss in a Boss Room, which would enable Isaac to leave the room and come back, facing another boss battle and obtaining another item.

• Also, hearts spawned from Portable Slot were affected by what room it was used in, such as Eternal Hearts spawning when used in Cathedral.

fields.name: Portable Slot
fields.description: Consumes one Penny and has a chance to drop a random pickup, like a Slot Machine.

Portal.title: Portal
Portal.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the enemy; the item; Lil Portal; the chapter; The Void] 

Portals are enigmatic entities that appear [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] on many floors/ [Repentance] only in The Void [end edition note] . They continuously spawn enemies until they are destroyed or spawn a certain number of enemies.

Portals spawn different enemies depending on the floor they appear on.

In The Void, Portals spawn enemies based on the theme of the room they are in.

sections.heading: Lil Portal
sections.text: Lil Portals are entities that only appear in Mausoleum and Gehenna. They continuously spawn fly and spider enemies until they are destroyed. There can be a max of 4 spawned monsters alive at once. Monsters they can spawn include:

sections.heading: Lil Portal (Flies Only)
sections.text: There is a variant of the Lil Portal with the ID 306.1.1 that looks and behaves identically to regular Lil Portals but will only spawn Fly related monsters from its regular pool.

sections.heading: Entrance Portal
sections.text:
A special version of the Portal (dubbed the "Entrance Portal" to avoid confusion) serves as the entrance to The Void. It is found in ???, but can also be found after defeating Mom, Mom's Heart / It Lives!, Isaac / Satan, ??? / The Lamb, Mega Satan, or Mother.
The Entrance Portal room in ??? gets darker the closer the player is to the portal.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Black Hole]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Charming a Portal with Mom's Eyeshadow or similar items will cause the Portal to spawn permanently charmed enemies similar to the Friendly Ball.

• As a result, a permanently charmed Death's Head can spawn from charmed Portals on Chapter 3 and remain permanently invulnerable. This is the only known method of charming an invulnerable enemy.

• If a portal is spawned in ???, Chest, Dark Room or Home via [Afterbirth+ onward] Debug Console, the Portal will despawn a few seconds before spawning any monster.

• If Portals aren't unlocked, certain enemies will spawn in their rooms instead, depending on the floor the room is in. For instance, Frowning Gapers spawn as Portal placeholders on Chapter 1 floors, whereas Vises spawn as Portal placeholders on Chapter 4 floors.

• It is often wise to instantly run into portals with orbitals after entering the room, if possible. Catching the small window timeframe for this almost always results in their instant death without any consequences.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Before v1.06.0185, portals continually spawned enemies until they were defeated.

• Portals were able to spawn Bosses such as The Haunt on floors such as the Cathedral. This was later removed.

• As of Booster Pack #5, Portals will now leave a Purple "blood" splatter when killed by the player. This effect is only for aesthetic purposes. Formerly, they left the generic Red blood splatter.

• [Repentance] Lil Portals resemble Warp Zones from Super Meat Boy.

Potato Peeler.title: Potato Peeler
Potato Peeler.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• On use:

• Removes one Red Heart Container.

• Increases damage by a flat +0.2.

• Grants one Cube of Meat.

• • [Repentance] The Cube of Meat is not added as a real item in Isaac's inventory.

• [Repentance+] If Isaac has Ball of Bandages, Potato Peeler will give additional copies of that instead.

• Grants an active Anemic effect for the current room.

• [Repentance] Counts as self-damage for the purposes of damage-triggered items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• It is possible for Isaac to kill himself by removing his final heart container.

• It is possible to generate multiple Meat Boys.

• Cubes of Meat given by this item do not remove any Cubes of Meat from Greed Mode item pools.

• [Repentance] The Cube of Meat gained through this item will persist in the escape sequence of Mines II. [end edition note] 

• This item cannot normally be used on Soul Hearts, Black Hearts, Bone Hearts, or Eternal Hearts.

• Thus, this item does not work with The Lost, ???, Black Judas, The Forgotten, Tainted ???, Tainted Judas, Tainted Bethany, Tainted Lost or Tainted Forgotten. Using it will not hurt them, nor produce any Cubes of Meat.

• [Before Repentance+] If Isaac has Ball of Bandages, Cubes of Meat will be added regardless.

• Harbingers will preferentially drop Cubes of Meat if Isaac has both types of orbitals.

• [Repentance] In Repentance Co-Op the Cube of Meat gained through this item will persist when a player dies allowing them to have a powerful damage output while in ghost form.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Each use grants a permanent +0.5 normal damage up in addition to a +0.2 flat damage up.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns an indestructible wisp. The wisps do not orbit Isaac, block shots, or deal contact damage. Instead, they chase and constantly shoot at nearby enemies.

• D4: Every Cube of Meat produced using Potato Peeler counts as an item for rerolling. Because health usually is not removed when rerolling items, this is useful to increase the number of items at the expense of the item pool.

• Cubes of Meat created by Potato Peeler will always reroll into Treasure Room, regardless of where Potato Peeler was obtained or the rooms it was used in.

• III - The Empress?/XI - Strength: The temporary hearts granted by the cards can be used to create a Cube of Meat.

• Tainted Eden: The Cube of Meat is not re-rolled when Tainted Eden takes damage, but the loss of a heart container is permanent.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Box of Friends: The Cubes of Meat from Potato Peeler cannot be duplicated by Box of Friends.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Car Battery + Book of Virtues: Summons 2 wisps and one Cube of Meat upon use.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In earlier versions of Repentance, this item used to kill any characters with red hearts when used while they were turned into The Lost.

• The description on this item matches the name of the item A Pound of Flesh.

• The pickup quote "A pound of flesh" is a reference to Shakespeare's The Merchant of Venice.

• This item might be a reference of the infamous suicide of Petunia from Happy Tree Friends' episode Wishy Washy (content warning: extreme cartoon gore).

Prayer Card.title: Prayer Card
Prayer Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Gives an Eternal Heart upon activation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If used after clearing a floor, before proceeding to the next one, it guarantees a new Heart Container every floor.

• Since it adds the eternal heart directly to the health bar instead of spawning it on the floor, the item is useless for Keeper and Tainted Keeper.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns white, heart-shaped wisps in the inner ring. Wisps' tears have 0.75 shot speed. The wisps' tears effectively act as though they have Sacred Heart.

• Car Battery: Grants one full Heart Container upon use.

• Tainted Eden: Health ups granted by eternal hearts are not rerolled when Tainted Eden takes damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tainted Magdalene: Doesn't benefit from her passive ability, giving only 1 Eternal Heart as usual.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the Christian tradition, holy cards or prayer cards are small, devotional pictures mass-produced for the use of the faithful. They usually depict a religious scene or a saint in an image about the size of a playing card. The opposite side typically contains a prayer, some of which promise an indulgence for its recitation.

• The design on the Prayer Card appears to be of the painting Our Lady of Guadalupe.

fields.description: Gives Isaac an Eternal Heart.

Pride.title: Pride
Pride.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Pride is a mini-boss based on one of the Seven Deadly Sins.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Pride wanders randomly around the room and performs one of two attacks:

• Spawns 4 Troll Bombs in random sections of the room.

• Pride is immune to damage from his own Troll Bombs.

• Fires 4 wave-like lasers from himself in an X-pattern.
Pride deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Pride can drop Anarchist Cookbook even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

• Pride is not immune to damage from his own Troll Bombs while under the effect of Anima Sola.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Sin]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Pride's grayscale color, simple design, and the wavy scribble-like appearance of his lasers make him resemble Isaac's drawings as seen in the game's menus and cutscenes, possibly meaning he represents the pride Isaac takes in his creations.

• Pride's expressions during its attacks are a reference to "rage comic" memes, he briefly resembles troll face before spawning Troll Bombs and assumes a forever alone before firing lasers.

• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived.

• Pride is the personification of one of the Seven Deadly Sins. Pride is the excessive belief in one’s own importance, and can be thought of as narcissism, entitlement, or egotism. Pride can lead to other sins such as excessive desires for fame/attention, selfish desires for power, disobedience, discord, hypocrisy, and vanity. Pride is also believed by many to be the root of all sins.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Pride is feared, only his head will be colored purple when he is facing the back wall of the room.
Bug note: If Pride is slowed during his attack animation, he will not play the full animation.

Proptosis.title: Proptosis
Proptosis.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Proptosis is a passive item.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Doubles Isaac's damage stat.

• [Repentance] +0.5 damage.

• Tear size multiplier: 2x.

• [Before Repentance] The tears shrink and lose damage the farther they travel.

• [Repentance] The tears shrink and lose damage the more time they stay airborne, starting at 3x damage at point blank range. After 0.8 seconds, they deal no damage at all.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Effective range of Isaac's tears now also depends on the damage, as they can shrink out of existence before their air time runs out.

• [Repentance] Since tears run out of damage after 0.8 seconds (48 frames), shot speed is the only stat that determines the effective range of Isaac's tears. Damage and range don't affect the travel distance at all.

• [Repentance] Approximately 2.08% damage is lost per frame. This means at approximately 0.53 seconds (32 frames) Isaac's tears will deal the normal amount of damage.

• [Before Repentance] Tear size increasing items also increase the maximum distance before its disappearance, but the damage dealt can go below original at the extreme.

• [Before Repentance] The damage decrease does not affect Azazel's short-ranged Brimstone unless the range stat is extremely high.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Anti-Gravity: The tears will not decrease in size or damage until they start moving, making this excellent against enemies that chase Isaac.

• Anti-Gravity + Eye of the Occult: Lets Isaac maintain the full 3× damage multiplier while controlling his tears.

• Anti-Gravity + Spoon Bender: Tears will move towards enemies while maintaining the full 3× damage multiplier, negating both the need to release tears and the power decrease with distance.

• Brimstone: Retains the double damage effect without losing damage over range.

• [Afterbirth onward] Damage is doubled again for a total of 4x next to Isaac, but quickly drops further along the beam, at about 0.8x per tile of distance, reaching its minimum of 0.1 per tick roughly at 8 tiles.

• [Repentance] The beam does 6x damage at point blank range. 

• C Section: Fetuses deal triple their usual damage (2.25× Isaac's damage) at point blank, but shrink and deal less damage over time.

• C Section + Mom's Knife: The knives shrink along with the fetuses, but they retain their tripled damage.

• C Section + Tech X: The rings shrink along with the fetuses, but they retain their tripled damage.

• C Section + Technology: Although the laser's damage diminishes along with the fetus, it does not lose its damage over range.

• Dr. Fetus/Epic Fetus: [Before Repentance] Doubles damage with no penalty for distance.

• [Repentance] Triples/quadruples damage respectively.

• Godhead: The damaging halo shrinks with the tears.

• A Lump of Coal: Proptosis scales with Isaac's damage while the Lump of Coal does not. At base damage, the Lump of Coal will approximately negate the damage lost over distance, but with increased damage, tears still do more damage up close.

• A Lump of Coal + The Ludovico Technique: The controlled tear has full Proptosis damage buff, [Before Repentance] no matter how far it is from Isaac. [Repentance] Very slightly decreases damage from far away.

• [Repentance] If the damage stat is extremely low through methods such as combining Soy Milk with 20/20, it can cause the tear to gain Proptosis's triple damage while still having the tear grow from A Lump of Coal's effects.

• Mom's Knife: The Knife damage is [Before Repentance] doubled ( [Repentance] tripled), regardless of range.

• Polyphemus: Tears do massive damage and carry with leftover damage while still shrinking.

• Technology/Technology 2: Doubles damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] The beam decreases in damage and width the farther it travels. Tears become virtually powerless across large rooms like the Boss Rush and the Hush fight, reaching its minimum of 0.1 roughly at 8 tiles.

• [Repentance] The beams do 6x damage at point blank range.

• Tech X: Ring size and damage is substantially increased, but decreases as the ring travels further from Isaac.

• Trisagion: Base damage is doubled and beam damage is boosted to about 65%. Blasts lose no power as they travel further, though the tips of the blasts deal very slightly less damage.

• [Repentance] Damage slightly increased, beam damage is doubled. Blasts lose no power with distance.

• Bird's Eye: Size and damage of fires is increased, but does not decrease with range.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Athame/Maw Of The Void: The ring is much larger and deals 1.5× damage.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The ring deals normal damage.

• [Repentance] The ring is now normal size.

• [Repentance] Broken Watch: The speedup effect applies to tears and increases the effective range.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: Tears will often disappear before they can burst. Tears created from bursts will also shrink, but due to their already low range, the difference may not be noticeable.

• [Repentance] Era Walk card/I'm Drowsy... pill/Stop Watch: The slowdown effect applies to tears and reduces the effective range of Proptosis.

• Flat Stone: At base range and tear size, tears will bounce twice against the floor and then disappear.

• Immaculate Heart: Tears that appear around Isaac disappear quickly.

• Ipecac: Tears almost disappear completely but are still able to do massive damage.

• [Repentance] Tears no longer deal massive damage at the end of the arch. Damage decreases rapidly with range.

• Isaac's Heart is a very good item to have, as you can run up to most enemies to deal maximum damage to them with little downside.

• Lachryphagy: Tears disappear too quickly to be fed.

• The Ludovico Technique: The closer the tear floats to Isaac, the larger it is. The farther away, the smaller it becomes.

• Monstro's Lung/Lead Pencil: Tears will disappear at different distances depending on how big they were when fired.

• My Reflection: Tears disappear before they can return to Isaac.

• Pop!: Tears will disappear extremely quickly after being fired.

• Saturnus The ring tears from Saturnus disappear nearly instantly upon entering a room.

• Soy Milk: Very poor combination. Tears disappear nearly instantly in front of Isaac, decreasing his range and damage to nearly nothing.

• [Repentance] Tears no longer disappear instantly. Range is only minimally shorter.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Eye proptosis is a condition resulting in forward displacement and entrapment of the eye from behind by the eyelids. The condition is also known as eye dislocation and eye luxation.

fields.description: Tears start out massive with high damage, and then shrink down and become weaker over a short range.

Psy Fly.title: Psy Fly
Psy Fly.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Obsessed Fan]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a fly orbital familiar that chases and blocks enemy shots.

• After a certain amount of shots are blocked, it enters a short cooldown period where it still blocks shots, but does not actively chase them.

• Psy Fly also deals 1 contact damage to enemies per tick (15 per second).

• Instantly kills some Fly enemies upon contact.

• Flies affected include: Army Fly, Attack Fly, Fly, Ring Fly, Swarm, and Willo.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• While Psy Fly is an effective means of projectile protection, it is not immunity, and recklessly wading into a barrage of shots can easily result in taking damage.

• Psy Fly will block most types of projectiles, not just red bullets. This includes the fires from Mega Satan phase 2, the bone projectiles Bony throw, Ipecac shots from Gurgles and similar enemies, or even the rocks that the Kineti throws at you.

• Ipecac shots still explode if blocked by Psy Fly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item originates from the Antibirth mod, but it was unobtainable due to a bug. It also had two scrapped abilities that made Attack Flies turn into Blue Flies when encountered and blocked tears home in on enemies. Psy Fly was originally unlocked by completing Isaac's Awakening.

fields.name: Psy Fly
fields.description: Spawns a fly orbital familiar that seeks out incoming enemy shots and destroys them.

Brain.title: Brain
Brain.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Brains slide around the room erratically in the cardinal directions, leaving a trail of red creep, they deal a whole heart of contact damage. When Isaac is within line of sight they will charge in his direction until they collide with an obstacle or another enemy similar to Knights.

sections.heading: Poison Mind
sections.text:
Poison Minds behave like regular Brains, but they slide diagonally and leave a trail of green creep.

[Repentance] Poison Minds float, passing over obstacles, and explode when killed.

sections.heading: Black Globin's Head
sections.text: Black Globin's Heads behave like Brains, but they target Isaac directly, chasing him.

sections.heading: Festering Guts
sections.text: Festering Guts are spawned exclusively by Gutted Fatty. They travel around the room randomly in cardinal directions and occasionally spawn a Charger.

sections.heading: Pon
sections.text:
Pons hop around erratically leaving red creep wherever they land. If close to Isaac then they will hop towards Isaac chasing him similarly to Hoppers.

They can spawn with a paired Brainless Knight in which killing them is required to kill their corresponding Brainless Knight. A Pon and a Brainless Knight pair will always spawn when Loose Knight is killed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] If Poison Minds aren't unlocked yet, they are replaced by Brains.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Pon first appeared in the Antibirth mod where it could also appear in Depths.

• [Repentance] The name of Pon is likely a pun in reference to the homophonic pronunciation of the Pons region of the brain and pawns from chess.

Pills.title: Pills
Pills.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Pills are pickups that can provide useful or inhibiting effects. They take up the same slot as cards and runes.

At the start of each run, an effect is randomly assigned to each color of pill. The pill effect for each color will remain constant throughout the run. (However, it is possible for PHD, Virgo, False PHD, or [Repentance] Lucky Foot to reassign some of the effects, such that 2 different colored pills will have the same effect.) Pills start the game unidentified (unless the player is holding PHD or False PHD); their effect is shown as "???" when picked up. Upon using a particular pill for the first time, its effect will be revealed and all subsequent pills with the same color will have their effect shown as well. The set of pill effects for any given run is usually known as the pill pool.

• [Afterbirth onward] The pill pool for each run has increased from 9 to 13.

sections.heading: [Repentance] Pill Classes
sections.text:
Repentance introduces the mechanic of pill classes. Internally, pills are given a class from 0 to 3 and a polarity that reflects their influence:

Pills in class 0 have little to no impact on a run overall, while pills in higher classes are correspondingly more influential, class 3 pills having effects as significant as permanent stat changes.
Classes that end with + or - denote a positive or negative effect, otherwise considered neutral.

Polarity is used by certain items to determine which pills to convert.

Five class 3, two class 2, two class 1, and one class 0 pill effects are guaranteed to be chosen in each run. The remaining three pill effects have random classes. Consequently, the average run is expected to draw, in total: 

• ~5.84 positive pills

• ~4.15 negative pills

• ~3.01 neutral pills

Polarity is not considered when drawing pill effects; it is therefore possible that only bad pill effects are chosen over this entire process, at an astronomically low chance of 1 in 5,799,273,480. With average luck, slightly less than one third of your pills should be bad ones.

During a [mode: greed] Greed Mode run, the Amnesia, ???, and Telepills effects cannot be chosen; otherwise, it uses the same system as above.

[end edition note]

sections.heading: [Repentance] Gold Pills
sections.text:
Repentance introduces Gold Pills (or Golden Pills). Using one gives a random pill effect. Gold pills are unique in that they can be used multiple times, with each use only having a 10% chance to remove the pill. This often allows many uses before they finally disappear.

• Unlocked by: [achievement unlock: Gold Pill] .

• The possible effects are all effects that aren't in the run's pill pool, which means if you see an effect from a normal pill, you will never see it from a gold pill.

• Items such as PHD or Lucky Foot which alter pill effects also work on the effects of this pill, allowing many beneficial effects to be stacked with little risk. Effects altered by these items may overlap with the effects in the run's pill pool; for example, a run might have Tears Up in the pill pool and Tears Down outside of the pill pool, which will be turned into Tears Up due to the effects of the item.

• Gold Pills have an ID of 5.70.14.

• A Gold Pill can also be a Horse Pill. Gold Horse Pills use the Horse Pill effect on every use.

• Gold horse pills are most likely the rarest pickup in the game with a 0.06% chance of spawning instead of a normal pill.

• If a Gold Pill uses the 'Vurp' effect, and no other pill was used prior, another gold pill will drop.

[end edition note]

sections.heading: [Repentance] Horse Pills
sections.text:
Repentance introduces Horse Pills. These are larger versions of the standard pills with a more powerful effect, but only appear very rarely. Unique sound effects can be heard when they are used, and the narrator's normal spoken voice lines are instead shouted using a different voice.

• Unlocked by: [achievement unlock: Horse Pill] .

• All items that work with pills work identically with horse pills.

• A horse pill with a given effect has the same color as the normal pill does.

• Horse pills have an ID of the normal ID + 2048 (i.e. 1 << 11). For example, a white-blue pill has an ID of 2, so the horse pill version would have an ID of 5.70.2050.

• It is also possible to have a golden horse pill. (It has an ID of 5.70.2062.)
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Probabilities
sections.text:
Pills that spawn with a sub-type of 0 (i.e. a random pill) will have the following probabilities:

• Random normal pill - 97.86%

• Specific normal pill - 7.53%

• Gold pill - 0.7%

• Random horse pill - 1.43%

• Specific horse pill - 0.11%

• Gold horse pill - 0.01%

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Among the attribute-modifying pill effects, only five of the seven visible attributes are covered: health, range, tears, speed, and luck. Both shot speed and damage can't be altered by pills.

• [Repentance] Shot speed can now be altered with pills. Damage can now also be altered with pills with False PHD.

• If a "Health Up" pill is used while Isaac has 11 empty red hearts and one non-red heart, the non-red heart will be replaced with an empty container, killing Isaac.

• Having Midas' Touch, Meconium, or Hallowed Ground and using a "Re-Lax" pill has a chance to spawn Golden Poop, Black Poop, or White Poop, respectively.

• If the item PHD is picked up and then lost in any way, such as rerolling by the D4 or a Dice Room, or dropping it as Tainted Isaac, pills will remain fully identified for the rest of the run, but negative pills will not be converted.

• [Afterbirth onward] Pill effects have a chance to be narrated upon use, as do cards and runes.

• [Afterbirth onward] Currently, the "Retro Vision" pill effect can crash the game on some machines, resulting in restarting the current floor when the game is continued.

• [Afterbirth onward] The "Addicted!" pill will have no effect if Isaac has The Wafer.

• Despite this, if Isaac takes both the "Addicted!" pill with "Percs!" in the same room, a full heart of damage will be taken from all sources.

• [Afterbirth onward] Using an "Infested!" pill on Red Poop will spawn blue spiders and the Red Poop will regenerate.

• [Afterbirth onward] If a Tiny or Large Champion monster drops a "One Makes You Smaller"/"Larger" pill and either pill is not in the current pill pool, an existing pill will be overwritten. If the chosen pill was already identified, the new pill will also be.

• [Afterbirth onward] "R U A Wizard" does not affect Lilith's Incubus. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth onward] Isaac's hitbox can be reduced to 30% of original, which is achieved after 6 One Makes You Small pills. Further pills will only make him visually smaller, with no additional benefit.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Using a "Gulp!" pill while holding two trinkets (with Belly Button or Mom's Purse) will cause both trinkets to be absorbed.

• Magdalene's starting pill will override one of the pills in the current run's pill set if it doesn't exist in it ("Speed Up" for Afterbirth+, or "Full Health" in Repentance). The pill that is converted is dependent on the run's seed.

• This only applies if the run is started as Magdalene, not if Isaac turns into Magdalene using Clicker.

• [Repentance] All golden pills in the run have a shared sequence of effects they activate, so reversing the effects of one golden pill through Glowing Hourglass and consuming another golden pill will activate the same effects.

• [Repentance] If a "Vurp!" effect is activated by a golden pill, it will spawn the last non-golden pill taken by Isaac, or a golden pill if no non-golden pills have been taken by Isaac in the run.

• A normal "Vurp!" pill will also ignore previous effects granted by gold pills.

• [Repentance] If a Marked Skull is destroyed while Isaac is holding Little Baggy, it will spawn a "Telepill" instead of 0 - The Fool. If "Telepills" doesn't exist in the current run's pill set, an existing pill will be overwritten. The pill that is converted is dependent on the run's seed.

• [Repentance] While transformed into The Lost form (for example, by a White Fire Place), "Health Down" pills turn into "Health Up" pills, and "Bad Trip" pills become "Full Health", regardless of Isaac's health. [end edition note] 

• "Telepills" is unobtainable in Greed Mode.

• [Repentance+] The "Amnesia" and "???" pills are also unobtainable in Greed Mode.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• [Repentance] There are 24 good effects, 14 neutral (sometimes good/sometimes bad) effects, and 12 negative effects. This means that taking mystery pills is usually beneficial.

• Use of unidentified pills is recommended for outside of combat as Hematemesis, R U a Wizard?, Paralysis, [Afterbirth onward] Addicted!, [Afterbirth+ onward] X-Lax, and [Afterbirth+ onward] I'm Excited!!! can be detrimental mid-fight. However, [Afterbirth+ onward] I'm Drowsy..., [Afterbirth+ onward] Something's wrong..., Lemon Party, Bad Gas, and Pheromones are useless outside of combat.

• [Afterbirth onward] Percs! can be used in the Sacrifice Room to reduce the damage Isaac takes, potentially allowing him to do more sacrifices. However, if Isaac is teleported to the Devil/Angel room, he loses the effect.

• [Afterbirth onward] The invincibility effect from Power Pill and [Afterbirth+ onward] Feels like I'm walking on sunshine! can be utilized to get into Curse Rooms, play [machine: Blood Donation Machine] s and [machine: Confessional] s, or use [machine: Devil Beggar] s and [machine: Hell Game] s without taking any damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] Percs! can be used to reduce damage from these from chapter 4 onward.

• [Repentance] Endless Nameless can be used to effectively generate infinite golden pills, as the trinket's ability to respawn collectibles applies with every use.

• [Repentance] Taking only golden pills in a run can allow for infinite golden pill generation by repeatedly activating the Vurp! effect.

• [Repentance+] ??? can be distinguished from unidentified pills more easily by enabling item descriptions in the Options menu. They will display as "???" instead of "Unidentified Pill" when approached.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Vurp! pill is a portmanteau of the words vomit and burp.

• [Afterbirth onward] Power Pills activating the Gamekid effect is a reference to Pac-Man, in which the "Super-Pac" powerup is obtained by eating a Power Pellet.

• "I Found Pills (and Ate Them)," "R U a Wizard?," and "I can see Forever" are all image macro memes.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Feels like I'm walking on sunshine! pill is a reference to the 80s song Walking on Sunshine.

• Furthermore, creator Edmund McMillen made in 2010 a video with the same name, although it doesn't feature the actual Walking on Sunshine song.

• Balls of Steel is a reference to Duke Nukem; it is one of Duke's more famous quotes.

• Explosive Diarrhea is extremely loud and forceful diarrhea. In the original game, the message that displayed when the pill was activated was "Oh No!". The pill name and effect are likely a reference to Atomic Bomberman where a pickup of the same name would cause the player to drop bombs behind them uncontrollably for a short duration.

• Shot speed effects were introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Eternal Edition, after the release of Rebirth. They were finally added to Rebirth in the Repentance DLC.

• Hematemesis is a medical term for vomiting blood.

• Lemon Party is a reference to internet shock site featuring a group of elderly men performing oral sex, peeing on each other.

• "Puberty" having a negative sound effect is a tongue in cheek connotation to how unpleasant that period in life can be.

• [Afterbirth onward] Friends Till the End! was originally in the Wrath of the Lamb but removed in Rebirth, then put back into Afterbirth.

• [Afterbirth only] Friends Till The End! is the only non-narrated pill.

• 48 Hour Energy is a reference to the drink 5 Hour Energy.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] X-Lax is a reference to the anti-constipation medicine Ex-Lax.

• [Afterbirth onward] "One makes you larger" and "One makes you small" are references to Alice in Wonderland, and the specific wording is a reference to the song White Rabbit by Jefferson Airplane.

• [Afterbirth onward] "Percs" is a reference to a street name for the prescription drug Percocet, which is more generically known as Oxycodone. This drug is meant to be used to treat pain, but it is often abused for recreational purposes.

• [Afterbirth onward] The "???" is the only pill that has 3 different narrated voice lines.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] "I'm Drowsy..." and "I'm Excited!!!" are references to benzodiazepines and stimulants respectively. From the pill themed Mom items, it's implied that Mom is a drug addict, and therefore keeps narcotics around the home and in her coin purse.

• [Repentance] "Horse pills" is a slang term used to refer to large, hard to swallow pills, hence their sprites being larger than those of regular pills.
