sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Any blue flies and blue spiders created by pill effects can be multiplied when Glowing Hourglass teleports Isaac in a way that does not move him to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again). [end edition note]
Bug note: After shrinking significantly from "One makes you smaller", Isaac is able to run past the hit detection of solid objects, allowing him to run past gaps in the floor and metal blocks.

Tumor.title: Tumor
Tumor.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Tumors are enemies that slowly float across the room diagonally bouncing off walls. They occasionally fire 6 blood shots in all directions, and fire even more quickly when attacked.

sections.heading: Psy Tumor
sections.text: Psy Tumors behave exactly like regular Tumors, but fire homing shots instead of blood shots.

sections.heading: Camillo Jr.
sections.text: Camillo Jr. behave exactly like Tumors, but fire Technology lasers at Isaac. Their lasers may also hit enemies for 8 damage.

sections.heading: Planetoid
sections.text: Planetoids are a variant of Tumor that move faster than their variants and fire blood shots that orbit them, similar to effect of Tiny Planet. When they take damage, they fire shots more frequently and have a chance to fart, releasing their orbiting projectiles out of orbit and let them fly off while starting a new ring.

sections.heading: Poofer
sections.text:
Poofers, unlike other Tumors, slowly float towards Isaac. However, if Isaac is shooting, they will target a position in front of where he is facing instead of targeting him directly, to try and intercept his projectiles.

Each time they take damage, they swell up and fire 6 blood shots in a fixed, radial spread. They can swell up a total of 4 times, becoming slower the more swollen they are. Upon death, they explode, forcibly pushing Isaac, destroying nearby grids, healing nearby enemies for 15 HP, and leaving a large puddle of damaging Red Creep.

Their health also doesn't deplete until they are hit by a total of at least 40 damage, giving them an effective health of 60 and a unique form of one-shot protection.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Tumors are a reference to abnormal growth of tissues of the same name, caused by genetic mutations.

• Camillo Jr.'s name is a reference to Kracko Jr., a recurring enemy from the Kirby series. In appearance he bears resemblance to Kracko, the mature version of Kracko Jr.

• [Repentance] Poofer is a reference to the enemy from The Legend of Bumbo with the same name.

• [Repentance] A Planetoid is an astronomical object that is neither a planet nor a comet.

Crooked Penny.title: Crooked Penny
Crooked Penny.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, has a 50% chance to double all items, pickups, trinkets, and Chest in the current room.

• If the effect fails, the items, pickups, and chests disappear, and a Penny is spawned.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If used in a Shop or Devil Room, the duplicated items and pickups can be taken for free.

• If the effect fails in a shop that contains a Shop Restock Machine, then the Restock Machine can be used to refresh the Shop, bringing back new items and pickups.

• [Before Repentance] If used in the Boss Rush room, it can duplicate the items, and all of them can be taken without affecting the originals. Successfully duplicating the items will trigger Boss Rush, and failing to duplicate them will not.

• [Before Repentance] If used on The Polaroid and The Negative after defeating Mom, it can duplicate them, and they can both be taken without affecting the originals.

• The 50% chance is predetermined after each use of Crooked Penny. By force quitting or using Glowing Hourglass after each failure, this can be exploited to generate large numbers of copies of useful items — if the penny is going to fail, then use it in a different room, recharge it, and try again.

• [Repentance] The outcome of Crooked Penny is determined on a per-room basis, meaning that it will succeed in certain rooms and fail in others respecting the 50/50 chance. Using Crooked Penny will still advance an RNG step, however, and re-roll the outcome of the other rooms.

• If used in Boss Rush and the items disappear, the boss rush cannot be started.

• If Crooked Penny is used right after taking an item from a choice pedestal (such as those created by More Options), it is possible to double the other item(s) as they disappear. The copies of items will not disappear and will act normally.

• Unlike Diplopia, Crooked Penny can be used to duplicate trinkets.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
See Diplopia#Synergies for info about stacking duplicate items.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a coin wisp on the middle ring. The wisps have a 50/50 chance to duplicate all their copies or destroy all their copies when one takes damage. Does not affect wisps other than ones made by this item. Using Crooked Penny always spawns one wisp, with no chance to affect the others.

• [Before Repentance] Void: Void's item-absorbing effect activates before Crooked Penny's effect, but Crooked Penny nonetheless has a chance of doubling the absorbed items, leaving behind copies of them. Missing with Crooked Penny still results in the item being absorbed, but one penny also appears.

• [Repentance] Void does not absorb the item if Crooked Penny fails, but one penny still appears. Void absorbs only the original item if Crooked Penny succeeds, leaving behind a copy.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Car Battery: Activates the item twice, quadrupling all items/drops in the room at a 25% chance. However, if the first activation fails, and the second activation succeeds, a copy of the item will be created as the original disappears, and the new copy will have no cost if it were in a Shop or Devil Room. This has a 25% chance as well, leaving the overall failure chance at 50% (a success followed by a fail will have the same effect as two fails).

• [Repentance] Activates the item twice, quadrupling all items/drops in the room at a 25% chance but having a combined 75% chance to fail. A failure followed by a success generates 2 pennies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item's effect, if the coin flip succeeds, is almost identical to Diplopia's.

• Diplopia can be copied by this item.

• Before Booster Pack #1, it could be used on empty item pedestals to cause another item to appear.

• This item was originally suggested by Reddit User /u/CultOfTheHelixFossil in a fan item suggestion thread made by Edmund McMillen.

• According to the original post, the name "crooked" refers to that the item "can't be fully trusted" and is meant to differentiate it from other coin items.

• This item was inspired in part by the playstyle of YouTuber Northernlion, and his tendency toward Risk vs Reward items. (citation needed)

Crow Heart.title: Crow Heart
Crow Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Red Heart damage will be taken before Soul Heart, Black Heart, and Rotten Heart damage.

• With Bone Hearts, Red Hearts contained within the Bone Hearts will be taken before regular Red Heart damage.

• If Isaac [Before Repentance] only has half a Red Heart left / [Repentance] has no Red Hearts left, Soul and Black Heart damage will be taken, and Bone Hearts can be destroyed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] This is useful for getting into Boss Challenge Rooms while maintaining Soul/Black Hearts.

• [Repentance] No longer works as Boss Challenge Rooms now require one heart in total.

• Red Heart damage taken via the trinket affects Devil Room/Angel Room chances normally.

• This can be used to voluntarily decrease the Angel / Devil room chance if it has already been accessed in favor of increased chance next floor.

• If Isaac has at least one Rotten Heart, he does not lose deal chance from taking any red heart damage, despite rotten hearts not being taken first.

• • This means having just a single rotten heart can be a great strategy for removing the majority of the downside of this trinket.

• Although Gold Hearts are in front of the HP bar, they will shatter when red heart damage is taken through the trinket.

• This trinket is useful when playing as The Forgotten, as it will preserve his Bone Hearts (and Devil/Angel Room chance) until all of his Bone Hearts are empty.

• This trinket does nothing while controlling The Soul.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Adds a 25% chance that taking damage does not reduce Devil room chances. Having both brings the chance to avoid reduction to 50%.

sections.text:
• Grants 2 Soul Hearts.

• Replaces normal tears with blue diamond tears while all of Isaac's Red Heart containers and Bone Hearts (if any) are full.

• This includes whenever Isaac has zero Red Heart containers.

• Containers can be filled with Rotten Hearts and still activate the effect.

• The coin health containers of Keeper and Tainted Keeper count as red heart containers for the purposes of this item.

• While the effect is active, grants the following stats:

• 2x damage.

• [Before Repentance] +5.25 range.

• [Before Repentance] +0.5 tear falling speed.

• -0.30 shot speed.

• The crown will glow blue while active; if inactive, it will appear grey.

• The effect will deactivate for the rest of the current room when damage is taken, regardless of Isaac's health.

• Fighting waves in Greed mode won't reactivate the crown.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Because the effect occurs if Isaac has no Red Heart containers at all, this is an extremely beneficial item for ???, Tainted ???, The Lost, Tainted Lost, Black Judas, Tainted Judas, Tainted Bethany and Tainted Forgotten.

• Due to the fact that they will be at full health a larger portion of the time than most characters, this item is also very powerful for Keeper and Tainted Keeper.

• If the damage is lost with Tainted Isaac, he can pick up another item in the same room and then swap it back to refresh the effect. Holding onto pedestal generation like Mystery Gift will allow him to place an item inside a difficult boss room and regain the bonus damage after being hit.

• Using XI - Strength when already at a maximum 12 hearts, but having taken damage (hence visually having full maximum health) will not reactivate the item.

• Additional copies of the item will grant 2 Soul Hearts upon pickup, but no change in stats.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Holy Mantle: This will block damage and keep Crown Of Light active.

• Rock Bottom: While the diamond tear effect will disappear when Isaac is hit, the damage up will not be reverted.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] This item is the angelic counterpart to the Dark Prince's Crown. [end edition note] 

• Although this item is normally only available in the Angel Room, it can be found as one of the Nintendo-themed Treasure Room items in the 6th of December's Daily Run, which is an homage to the late CEO of Nintendo, Satoru Iwata.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If Isaac picks up a Bone Heart while the crown is glowing blue and leaves the current room, the crown will continue to glow blue even though the damage boost is inactive due to the Bone Heart container being empty. Taking any damage won't make the crown turn gray until Isaac fills all of his Red Heart containers and leaves the current room to reset the effect.

fields.description: +2 Soul Hearts. While Isaac has no empty red hearts, grants 2x damage, -0.3 shot speed, [Before Repentance] and increased range. Regardless of health, the crown deactivates for the current room when Isaac takes damage.

Crystal Ball.title: Crystal Ball
Crystal Ball.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, reveals the floor layout and all special rooms except the Super Secret Room and Ultra Secret Room and drops either a Soul Heart or a random card or rune. (50% chance of either)

• [Repentance] While held, increases the chance of finding a Planetarium by 15%, or 100% if a treasure room has been skipped. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Crystal Ball can be obtained by playing a Fortune Telling Machine.

• It's possible to get more than one Crystal Ball from Fortune Telling Machines on a single run.

• The map revealing effect will not work if the [cu: Lost] is active.

• [Repentance] The Planetarium bonus guarantees the level generation to attempt placing one, but the level layout may not have enough room. Read the article on Planetariums for further details. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Wisps have much greater health than normal wisps. Tears that are fired from the wisps will auto aim towards nearby enemies, similar to Demon Baby.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Daemon's Tail: The chance to drop cards or runes will change to 90%/10% in favor of Soul Heart.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Planetarium]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The reflection of a face can be seen on the crystal ball's surface. It is easier to make out on the 3DS lower screen icon.

fields.description: Reveals the map (except the Super Secret Room and Ultra Secret Room) and drops a Soul Heart or random card or rune. [Repentance] While held, increases the chance of finding a Planetarium. [end edition note]

Crystal Key.title: Crystal Key
Crystal Key.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Whenever Isaac clears a room, has a chance to open a neighboring Red Room.

• This effect can occur while Isaac is inside a Red Room, but the chance is smaller.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• It's possible to increase the chance of a Red Room unlocking if multiple Crystal Keys are held, e.g. from absorbing using Smelter, holding Mom's Box, having a golden Crystal Key. The chance for a Red Room door to unlock depends on the number of Crystal Keys held and if the room cleared is normal or Red.

| Crystal Key Count | Normal Room | Red room

| 1 | 33.3% | 12.5%

| 2 | 50% | 16.6%

| 3 | 100% | 25%

| 4 | 100% | 50%

| 5 | 100% | 100%

• Each cleared wave of a Challenge Room has a chance to generate an adjacent Red Room.

• Rooms that are re-fought using the D7 have a chance to generate additional Red Rooms.

• Doors do not have to open to an actual valid Red Room, and can lead outside the map and into an I AM ERROR Room.

fields.description: Whenever Isaac clears a room, has a chance to open a neighboring Red Room.

Cube Baby.title: Cube Baby
Cube Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish: Ice Cube; Freezer Baby]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns an ice cube familiar. It cannot move on its own, but slides around when Isaac walks into it, uses a melee attack on it, or when Isaac or enemies shoot at it.

• The familiar damages and slows enemies it touches while moving. It can deal up to 17.5 damage when it collides with enemies, depending on how fast it's moving.

• Monsters killed by Cube Baby are frozen.

• Frozen monsters will follow the same physics as Cube Baby, and will shatter on impact creating ice shards that are capable of freezing other monsters

• Cube Baby can block enemy projectiles.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Killing enemies by freezing them does not however count as a "kill" for the purposes of activating the on kill effects of certain items and trinkets. Because of this, only enemies killed by icicles from statues, bombs, familiars and other sources will count towards the on kill effects, rendering them quite difficult to use. These items and trinkets are: Bat Wing, Berserk!, Charm of the Vampire, Eve's Bird Foot, Jumper Cables, Lusty Blood, Red Stew, Samson's Lock, Sigil of Baphomet, Toxic Shock, and Vasculitis.

• If a non-boss enemy dies within 10 ticks (0.33 seconds) after being hit by Cube Baby, it will be frozen regardless of what killed it.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Mom's Bracelet: Cube Baby can be picked up and thrown. It will then slide at maximum speed in the direction it's thrown at and leave a trail of damaging white creep until it slows down.

• BFFS!: Increases the size and doubles the damage dealt.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Pushing Cube Baby directly into a hole in a way that it cannot slide sideways will cause it to shake until it starts to "float" over the hole, acting as if it were on the ground. It returns to normal if it leaves that hole.
Bug note: If a Cube Baby is picked up by multiple characters using Mom's Bracelet at the same time, it seems that they are all holding one, but trying to throw "them" at the same time will make Cube Baby disappear, only leaving a trail of creep.

fields.description: Spawns an ice cube familiar that slides around when walked into. It slows and deals contact damage, freezing monsters it kills.

Cube of Meat.title: Cube of Meat
Cube of Meat.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns an orbital familiar around Isaac which blocks shots and deals [edition alternatives: baseline: 105; Repentance: 52.5] contact damage per second.

• Each subsequent Cube of Meat obtained is combined with the first one (increasing its 'level'), changing its characteristics:

• Level 2: Gives the orbital the ability to shoot tears that deal 3.5 damage once every [edition alternatives: baseline: second; Repentance: 0.73 seconds] .

• Level 3: Changes it from an orbital to a Meat Boy that chases nearby enemies dealing [edition alternatives: baseline: 8.75; Repentance: 12.5] contact damage per second.

• Level 4: Increases the size of the Meat Boy and increases its damage to [edition alternatives: baseline: 13.75; Repentance: 25] contact damage per second.

• The fifth Cube of Meat will create a new Level 1 cube, and start the cycle again.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Multiple Cubes of Meat can be collected in a single run.

• [Repentance] The orbital orbits Isaac significantly faster.

• Famine, Pestilence, War, and Death will always drop either a Ball of Bandages or Cube of Meat. After the first one drops, further Harbingers will only drop that same one and never the other for the duration of the run.

• The ticking rate for Meat Boys' contact damage causes them to often deal damage twice once they touch an enemy, making their first second of DPS up to 1.5x higher than normal.

• The following types of flies are instantly killed when they come in contact with the familiar, at any level:

• Army Fly

• Attack Fly

• Dart Fly

• Fly

• Hush Fly

• Moter

• Pooter

• Ring Fly

• Super Pooter

• Swarm

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Invulnerability and shields are very useful with orbitals like Cube of Meat.

• This is even more useful with invulnerability items which doesn't allow to do contact damages, like Unicorn Stump.

• Book of Revelations: Ensures that Harbingers that haven't already been defeated will replace their respective floor's boss, making it drastically easier to collect multiple Cubes of Meat.

• Box of Friends / Monster Manual: Additional copies of Cube of Meat combine with the first, increasing its level as normal.

• Potato Peeler: Consumes 1 Red Heart container in return for creating 1 Cube of Meat and increasing damage a little.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Duct Tape: Familiar will stay in place relative to Isaac at levels 1 and 2. No effect at levels 3 and 4.

• Pretty Fly: Cube of Meat will replace one if Isaac already has 3 Pretty Flies. If the Cube of Meat reaches level 3 or 4, the Pretty Fly will come back until another Cube of Meat orbital is obtained.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Super Meat Boy]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Cube of Meat is a reference to the game Super Meat Boy, developed by Edmund McMillen, creator of The Binding of Isaac.

• The pickup quote is a reference to the Pokémon series catchphrase "Gotta catch 'em all."

• [Before Repentance] Cube of Meat is found in 9 item pools, the highest count amongst all items, due to the fact that it appears in all of Greed mode's item pools.

• Cube of Meat's 3rd and 4th stage form is referred to as "Ultra Flesh Kid!" in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls, Edmund's card game.

fields.description: Creates an orbital familiar. Collecting additional copies gives it the ability to shoot tears, then chase enemies to deal contact damage, then deal even more contact damage.

Cupid's Arrow.title: Cupid's Arrow
Cupid's Arrow.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants piercing tears that travel through enemies (but not obstacles) instead of breaking on impact with them.

• [Before Repentance] Also pierces through Poop and Fire Places.

• [Before Repentance] Tears no longer apply knockback to enemies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 8 Inch Nails/Blister/Pisces: Tears can now knock enemies back again, but the knockback effectiveness of these items is reduced.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs travel through enemies. When combined with Ipecac, bombs do not explode upon hitting enemies.

• [Repentance] Bombs also deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.

• Fire Mind: Tears will continue to pierce enemies while retaining the explosion chance.

• [Before Repentance] Ipecac: Pierces through Poop and Fire Places, but not enemies.

• [Repentance] Doesn't pierce through Poop, Fire Places, or enemies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Slow Roll and Pong.

• The item name is a reference to Valentine's Day and Cupid shooting an arrow into people's hearts to make them fall in love with someone.

• Despite its name, it does not charm enemies.

• The costume for this item is a reference to the headbands worn by both military and ceremonial leaders of Native American tribes.

fields.description: Grants Isaac triangular piercing tears that travel through enemies (but not obstacles) instead of breaking on impact with them.

Curse of the Tower.title: Curse of the Tower
Curse of the Tower.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Upon taking damage, spawns six Troll Bombs around the room, similar to the effect of XVI - The Tower.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Despite appearing as Troll Bombs, the bombs are mechanically identical to player-placed bombs and will benefit from Isaac's bomb-enhancing items.

• These bombs hurt the player as well as enemies.

• Taking damage from the Troll Bombs spawned by Curse of the Tower or any other type of bomb, including Isaac's bombs, will not re-activate the effect.

• [Before Repentance] Picking up this item will make all health transactions more difficult. Devil Beggars and Blood Donation Machines will be almost impossible to use because they will very likely be destroyed by bombs.

• [Repentance] Taking damage from Devil Beggars and Blood Donation Machines does not trigger the effect. IV Bag, however, does trigger the effect.

• The bombs prefer to spawn near the center of the room.

• The 6 Troll Bombs are difficult to dodge in small rooms.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blasting Cap: Spawned Troll Bombs can drop extra bomb pickups.

• Glitter Bombs: Each troll bomb has a chance to spawn a pickup or a trinket including hearts for repeated use.

• The Polaroid: If Isaac is damaged when he has half a Red Heart or less, the shield will activate and protect him from the Troll Bombs.

• Pyromaniac: Troll Bombs will heal Isaac instead, allowing for essentially infinite health with proper usage.

• [Repentance] Due to Pyromaniac being weakened to healing half a heart per explosion in Repentance, this synergy requires The Wafer to continue being effective past Chapter 3/Chapter 3.5.

• Remote Detonator: The Troll Bombs generated will not explode until Remote Detonator is activated, unlike regular Troll Bombs.

• Safety Scissors: The Troll Bombs generated will be converted into bomb pickups rather than exploding.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Blind Rage: Normally, the invincibility frames will end before most of the explosions take place. However, if Isaac takes a full heart of damage (e. g. from a champion), the invincibility will protect him from all spawned Troll Bombs.

• Damage sources that scale up from half a heart of damage to a full heart of damage starting on Chapter 4 don't provide enough invincibility frames to ignore the explosions.

• Blood Oath: Not recommended. Spawns 6 Troll Bombs for each Half Red Heart removed, making death highly likely if Isaac does not leave the room immediately after being stabbed by Blood Oath, and leaving the starting room unsafe.

• Sharp Plug: Not recommended. Spawns 6 Troll Bombs for each Half Red Heart removed, making extra damage highly likely if Isaac does not leave the room immediately after using Sharp Plug.

• Bomber Boy: Not recommended. The cross pattern explosion makes it very hard to avoid taking damage.

• Mr. Mega: No effect.

• Scatter Bombs: Not recommended. Each Troll Bomb will spawn several smaller bombs upon exploding, making it very hard to avoid taking damage.

• [Repentance] No visual change can be seen with the Troll Bombs, but the smaller bombs have the sprite of the smaller normal bombs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The item image appears to be an XVI - The Tower card that has been burnt.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: You feel cursed...; Repentance: Embrace chaos]
fields.description: Upon taking damage, spawns six Troll Bombs around the room, similar to the effect of XVI - The Tower.

Cursed Eye.title: Cursed Eye
Cursed Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Mom's Pearl]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants charged tears which fires a tight burst of tears. Firing mid-charge will shoot fewer tears depending on the charge time.

• [Before Repentance] The full burst size is four tears.

• [Repentance] The full burst size is five tears.

• [Before Repentance] Quickly tapping the fire key will result in no tears being fired.

• Charging while a burst is currently firing will prevent the rest of the shots from being fired.

• Taking damage while mid-charge (holding fire, but not fully charged) will teleport Isaac into another room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item can be counterproductive, especially while fighting bosses, as getting hit while charging a shot will reset the fight.

• The teleport effect only occurs when taking damage while in the middle of charging, before the shot is fully charged. Having a high tears stat for faster charging will decrease the window where Isaac is vulnerable to teleporting.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The teleporting and charge-up effects do not apply to Lilith. Her Incubus will fire three projectiles with each shot without needing to charge, tripling her damage output with no downside.

• The color of Isaac's cursed eye will indicate what state it currently is in:

• White: Inactive

• Black: Charging up

• Flashing black and white: Fully charged

• Having multiple instances of Cursed Eye grants no additional effect.

• [Repentance] When fighting The Beast, Isaac will teleport to a different part of the screen if hit while charging tears instead of leaving the room. This essentially eliminates the Cursed Eye's main drawback during the fight.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Black Candle: Teleport effect is removed.

• Holy Mantle: Losing Holy Mantle while charging Cursed Eye will not teleport Isaac.

• Incubus:

• [Before Repentance] Incubus fires 3 tears for each one that normally would be fired, with no change in delay.

• [Repentance] Incubus has the same charge shots as most characters would. Getting hit while charging will have the chance to teleport, as usual. [end edition note] 

• Marked: Tears are charged and automatically fired to varying levels depending on the distance between Isaac and the reticule. The firing rate is greatly increased without affecting the tears stat, even beyond normal maximum fire rate. The teleport effect is removed.

• Technology: Becomes a quick charging laser that shoots multiple lasers on release.

• Epiphora: Epiphora's tear rate multiplier affects the number of tears in a burst for a total of ten shots with a full Epiphora charge.

• Technology 2: Laser fires while charging Cursed Eye. Tear delay for the charge is unaffected by Tech 2. Allows Cain to fire normal tears.

• [Repentance] Tears are replaced with lasers, fired from the same eye of Tech 2. Conjoined transformation removes the synergy.

• Mutant Spider / The Inner Eye / 20/20 / The Wiz / Conjoined: Isaac shoots multiple tears from each eye, the amount is item-dependent.

• The Lost/Tainted Lost: Since The Lost dies in one hit, it is effectively immune to its teleportation effects, making this item much safer to use.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Almond Milk/Kidney Stone (when the barrage of tears is fired)/Soy Milk: Cursed Eye is automatically charged and fired when the fire key is held. The charge bar of Cursed Eye becomes invisible. The teleport effect remains.

• Having a tears stat of 30 or higher will trigger this effect as well, the above items will trigger this effect regardless of Isaac's tears stat.

• Lilith + Kidney Stone: When the kidney stone is shot, Incubus is unable to shoot for the duration of the effect, making this a anti-synergy.

• Anti-Gravity: Anti-Gravity effect cannot be used, as releasing a tear fire button also releases the Anti-Gravity Effect.

• Azazel/Brimstone/Dr. Fetus/Epic Fetus/The Ludovico Technique/Mom's Knife/Monstro's Lung: Overrides Cursed Eye.

• With Tainted Samson/The Forgotten/Berserk!: While charging your bone you will be teleported if hit.

• C Section/Neptunus/Spirit Sword/Tainted Azazel: Overrides Cursed Eye.

• With Tainted Samson/The Forgotten/Berserk!: While charging your bone you will be teleported if hit.

• Chocolate Milk: Charged tear is followed by up to 3 minimum-power tears, depending on Cursed Eye's charge.

• [Repentance] Cursed Eye takes longer to charge, but low damage shots can be fired rapidly. If fully charged, Isaac fires five Chocolate Milk shots.

• Eye of the Occult: The tears stack on top of each other, and only move forward when holding a direction afterwards.

• The Forgotten: The skeleton form's charge attack becomes a rapid barrage of hits; the amount depends on how full the charge is, up to 4.

• Ipecac: At full charge, quick bursts of ipecac shots are fired.

• Neptunus: Overrides Cursed Eye.

• Sprinkler: Overrides Cursed Eye.

• Tainted Lilith: The fetus gains the effect of Cursed Eye and the teleportation effect does not happen.

• Technology: Overrides Cursed Eye.

• Tech X: Overrides Cursed Eye.

• Urn of Souls: Opening the urn while charging will hold the charge until the urn is closed. As such, the teleport effect will always occur when hit with the opened urn.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• In most cases effects that override cursed eye will remove the teleporting effect. 

• Tainted Samson/The Forgotten/Berserk!: While in their melee form, getting hit while charging a shot will cause the teleport effect regardless of items that normally override the effect.

• The damage per second increase is dependent on Isaac's current tears stat, with lower tears showing a larger increase. Ranging from a ~90% increase at a tear stat of 0.96 to becoming a damage loss at tear stat of ~23 or above. 

• Having a high Tears stat around 10 or above without forms of auto firing such as Soy Milk or Marked can make it difficult to properly time charge shots, potentially leading to a damage loss.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item may be a reference to Edgar Allan Poe's "The Tell-Tale Heart" where the narrator talks about murdering an old man because of his "evil eye", which is described to look like The Cursed Eye.

• The concept of unluckiness brought about by someone's evil eye is not unique, and also appears across many different cultures.

• [Before Repentance] When Keeper charges up his shots his eye is reminiscent of a dollar sign. This is a pure coincidence, as he has no specific costume for Cursed Eye.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: In Greed mode, taking Red Heart damage while charging will decrease the displayed Devil Room chance on the Found HUD to 0%. It returns to 100% if the button is pressed again.

fields.description: Grants charged tears that can be fired in a tight burst. Getting hit while charging will teleport Isaac to another room.

Cursed Penny.title: Cursed Penny
Cursed Penny.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Teleports Isaac to a random room upon picking up a coin.

• [Repentance+] The type of the coin picked up affects the teleport destination:

• Penny: 50% chance for an unexplored combat room.

• Double Penny: 50% chance for Dice Room, Vault, Clean Bedroom or Dirty Bedroom.

• Nickel: 50% chance for Treasure Room, Shop, Library, Arcade, Challenge Room or Boss Challenge Room.

• Dime: 25% chance for Angel Room or Devil Room. This ignores Isaac's current devil/angel deal chances and picks at random.

• Lucky Penny: 50% chance for Secret Room or Super Secret Room.

• Golden Penny: 10% chance for I AM ERROR room.

• Sticky Nickel: 100% chance for Boss Room or Curse Room. This is only for the still-stuck version and the coin is still not actually picked up.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The effect can teleport Isaac to any room aside from an undiscovered Ultra Secret Room.

• [Repentance+] The trinket has a small chance to teleport Isaac to Black Market if the I AM ERROR room should have been the target. In this case, there will be no door exiting back to a Crawl Space.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: The odds for landing in a special room are increased.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Black Candle: Prevents the teleport effect from triggering for all coins except the still-stuck Sticky Nickel.

• [Before Repentance+] Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: No effect.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The effect can teleport Isaac to the tall room with a broken minecart track in Mines/Ashpit II, if the player hasn't pressed all the yellow buttons and doesn't have a way to destroy the wooden door, the player can't do anything rendering the game softlocked.

fields.description: Picking up coins teleports Isaac to a random room. [Repentance+] The type of the coin picked up affects the teleport destination.

Cursed Skull.title: Cursed Skull
Cursed Skull.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• If Isaac has less than one full Red Heart after taking damage, he will be immediately teleported to a random room.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The teleportation happens only at half a heart or less left, regardless of health type. Empty Bone Hearts are not counted as health even if they can absorb a hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Does not affect The Lost, as being hit with Holy Mantle does not count as taking damage.

• [Repentance] It will affect Isaac with Spirit Shackles, teleporting the player out of the room and restoring the Holy Mantle charge. [end edition note] 

• It is not recommended to have this item equipped during a boss fight as the boss's health will be restored to 100% if the player is teleported out of the room and returns, placing the player at a disadvantage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either teleports Isaac to a random special room instead. Having both activates if Isaac has 1 full heart or less after taking damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Scapular: Provided Scapular can always trigger, grants effective immortality, as the soul heart is always given before the teleport takes place.

• +The Wafer: Grants true immortality, plus one hit on the soul heart, allowing the player to get hit once before teleporting.

fields.description: If Isaac has less than one full Red Heart after taking damage, he will be immediately teleported to a random room.

Curved Horn.title: Curved Horn
Curved Horn.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • +2 flat damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Since Curved Horn grants flat damage, it is not affected by the damage up formula, which normally gives diminishing returns for each new damage up.

• Curved Horn is affected by most damage multipliers, excluding Polyphemus, Mega Mush, and character multipliers (such as Azazel's 1.5x damage multiplier).

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases Damage by 4. Having both by 6.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This trinket is a curved ram horn, similar to those granted by Aries or shown on The Lamb.

fields.description: +2 flat damage.

D1.title: D1
D1.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, duplicates one random pickup in the current room, including Cards, Runes, Chests, and trinkets.

• [Repentance] Duplicated pickups may not be identical to the original; for example, a duplicated card may be a different one than the original.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• It is possible to duplicate Shop pickups that have not been purchased yet.

• [Before Repentance] Jera can not be duplicated.

• [Before Repentance] Mimic Chests will not be duplicated until their spikes are exposed.

• [Before Repentance] Opened chests will be duplicated into an unopened copy.

• [Before Repentance] A normal Chest may be duplicated into a Red Chest or a Mimic Chest.

• [Before Repentance] A duplicated trinket is mostly useless, as you cannot pick up two of the same trinket even with Mom's Purse, Belly Button, or Smelter.

• However, with "consumable" trinkets such as Store Credit or Bag Lunch, it can be extremely powerful.

• [Before Repentance] In combination with a 48 Hour Energy pill and Paper Clip, the initial Locked Chests on Chest can be infinitely duplicated and opened.

• [Before Repentance] In Greed mode, if a Lil' Battery appears in the Shop and a 2 of Diamonds is acquired, infinite money can be gained by duplicating the Two of Diamonds.

• [Before Repentance] By dropping a card, rune, or pill in a room with no other pickups, then using D1, this item can function similarly to Blank Card and Placebo.

• [Repentance] By dropping a card, pill, or trinket in a room with no other pickups, then using D1, this item can function similarly to Deck of Cards, Mom's Bottle of Pills, or Mom's Box (But without the luck up or doubled trinket effects).

• [Repentance] A duplicated card has a very rare chance to turn into a Dice Shard, Cracked Key, or Emergency Contact; however, these will always duplicate as themselves instead of duplicating as a card.

• [Repentance] A duplicated Golden Pill will turn into a random Pill chosen from the Pill Pool.

• When duplicating any type of chest, the contents of the original chest will be invisibly rerolled.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Car Battery: Generates two pickups instead of just one. 

• Car Battery + Lil' Battery: Allows for infinite generation of Lil' Batteries. [Repentance] While it's still possible to generate infinite batteries with this synergy, it is slow to do so since mostly Micro Batteries will spawn. The occasional Lil' Battery or other battery spawn is needed to build up the battery pile.

• • [Before Repentance] An endless supply of Lil' Batteries allows for endless duplication of all pickups, chests, and trinkets on the floor.

• • [Repentance] An endless supply of Lil' Batteries allows for an endless supply of every kind of unlocked pickups, chests, and trinkets, as long as there is at least one of the initial pickup type on the floor.

• • 
• Card: Allows for an infinite supply of every kind of unlocked card.

• • 
• Pill: Allows for an infinite supply of every kind of pill in the current run's pill pool.

• • 
• Pill + PHD: Allows for an infinite supply of beneficial pills.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a white six-sided die wisp on the middle ring. An extra wisp spawns if no pickups are duplicated.

• Tainted Lost: Duplicated cards have an increased chance to be Holy Cards.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Guppy's Eye: Guppy's Eye can be used to see what changed when duplicating a chest. It will not immediately show the new contents, but leaving the room and returning will reveal the changes. This essentially allows rerolling the rewards within them, especially useful in Chest and Dark Room.

• [Repentance+] The contents are immediately updated upon reroll.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] D1 is the only die item that doesn't re-roll anything.

• [Repentance] The D1 now creates randomized pickups, meaning that the description is more accurate to the item's effect.

• [Repentance] As an exception, Spindown Dice and D10, although they technically do re-roll items/enemies, have a controlled and consistent result. [end edition note] 

• D1 is the only standard die item that doesn't have the respective number of sides as outcomes, but rather, just a D6 with all sides having singular pips. Rather, an actual D1 would be more accurately pictured as a Mobius strip, a sphere or an actual real-word “denary die” similar in form to a cyllindric object with slanted top and bottom.

fields.description: Duplicates a random pickup in the room. [Repentance] The new pickup may be different than the original (i.e. a different card, etc).

D10.title: D10
D10.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Upon use, rerolls all monsters in the room.

• [Repentance] Upon use, replaces all monsters in the room with weaker monsters. Each monster type has a specific weaker monster it will transform into. If the monster is already at its weakest level, it usually transforms it into a background critter or kills it outright.

• Some enemies can be transformed into obstacles or pickups instead.

• Transforming an enemy with a D10 does not necessarily make it objectively easier to kill. For example, Globin gets transformed into Clotty, which although has less health, may be harder to fight due to the tears it fires. Other prominent examples include Evis transforming into Double Vis, Holy Eye transforming into Eye, and Wall Creep transforming into Big Spider.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Rerolling a monster will replace it with an entirely new one from any floor, making it dangerous to use early on in the game (as Isaac could get monsters from Depths or later).

• [Before Repentance] The D10 will not reroll Bosses but can reroll monsters spawned by bosses.

• [Repentance] The D10 will not reroll friendly enemies.

• Using this item can cause some rooms to become impossible to clear. Jumping or flying monsters may become trapped behind rocks after being rerolled, and therefore become unbeatable.

• Sealed doors open after 2 minutes, though there are situations that can prevent this failsafe from triggering.

• [edition anr] Flying monsters will only be rerolled into other flying monsters, and ground monsters can only be rerolled into ground monsters. (Horfs are classified as ground monsters by the D10).

• [Repentance] Some invincible enemies will be rerolled, while others (including most Grimace variants) are completely unaffected.

• Using this item in a room with Mom's Hand can be very dangerous, as unless they have already landed, they will be directly on top of Isaac, resulting in the new monsters spawning directly on top of Isaac, instantly dealing contact damage.

• Using this item, then exiting the room, such as by teleporting or a bombed door, will cause the enemies to be in their original forms upon Isaac's return.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns orange wisps in the middle ring. Tears shot from these wisps have a 10% chance to replace enemies with their weaker variants.

• Car Battery: Weakens affected enemies twice.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Broken Remote: Using D10 while holding this will first teleport Isaac, and then reroll the enemies in the new room.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Despite being a dice item, D10 is not an unlock.

• [Afterbirth onward] This trait is shared with D7 and Dice Shard. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] D10 was voted the worst quality 0 item in the game in a poll on the Binding of Isaac subreddit, resulting in its consequent rework and upgrade to quality 1.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: The D10 can reroll the Suture half of Blighted Ovum.
Bug note: Using this item on any monster with several pieces will reroll every piece into a monster. Mr. Maw and Gemini's cord dots are considered pieces, each turning into a new monster.
Bug note: Rarely, a monster can be rerolled into the mask half of the Mask + Heart enemy, and the mask will die instantly.
Bug note: The Attack Fly, Swarm, and Camillo Jr. enemy can't be rerolled (even though monsters can be rerolled into them).
Bug note: Using this item in a room with Stone Grimaces will turn them invisible. They will not fire, but the space they occupied will prevent Isaac from moving through it like an invisible wall.
Bug note: D10 and items related to it can reroll frozen enemies into alive ones, effectively bringing them back to life.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Rerolls all monsters in the room.
[Repentance] Replaces all monsters in the room with weaker monsters.

D100.title: D100
D100.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Upon use, it:

• Rerolls all passive items on Isaac (like the D4).

• Rerolls all pedestal items in the room (like The D6).

• Rerolls all pickups in the room (like the D20).

• [Repentance] Restarts the room and respawns all enemies (like the D7). [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Rerolls Isaac's damage, tears, range and speed (like the D8). [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Rerolls all enemies in the room into weaker ones (like the D10).

• Doesn't go into effect in rooms the D7 works in. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Rerolls all rocks in the room (like the D12). [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Duplicates 1 random pickup in the current room (like the D1). [end edition note] 

• The pickup is rerolled by the D20 before being duplicated, essentially just granting a random extra pickup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] D100 is a special item.

• [Before Repentance] See the D4, The D6, and the D20 to learn more about the respective individual effects.

• [Repentance] See the D1, D4, The D6, D7, D8, D10, D12, and the D20 to learn more about the respective individual effects.

• If Missing No. is given to the player, it will activate and remove the D100, preventing further rerolls.

• Note that Missing No. can be rerolled into, but can't be rerolled out of.

• [Repentance+] D100's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Rerolls all of Isaac's wisps and gives him one random wisp. Book of Virtues will not be rerolled in the process.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Unlike the base game sprite, the D100 sprite on the lower part of the 3DS screen appears to have no edges and is a perfect sphere, which would make it more akin to the D infinity.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The D100 can reroll Angel Room passive items into the Book of Virtues. Upon further use, the Book of Virtues will not be rerolled.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Activates the combined effects of D4, The D6, and D20.
[Repentance] Activates the combined effects of D1, D4, The D6, D7, D8, D10, D12, and D20. [end edition note]

D12.title: D12
D12.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Re-rolls obstacles in the current room into other random obstacles.

• [Before Repentance] Poops, TNT, Fire Places and Key Blocks cannot be re-rolled.

• Obstacles can reroll into: Rocks, Tinted rocks, Cobwebs, Chapter-specific obstacles (Urns, Mushrooms, Skulls, and Polyps), Metal Blocks, Trap doors, Crawl Spaces, TNT, White Poop, [Repentance] Fool's Gold Rocks, Reward Plates and Killswitches [end edition note] .

• [Repentance] Rerolled obstacles will only reroll into another one in this group: Poops, Retractable Spikes, Normal and Red Fire Places, both types of TNT, and Cobwebs.

• Rerolled obstacles can also reroll into Reward Plates and Killswitches, but will not reroll any further. They can not roll into Trap doors or Crawl Spaces. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Destroyed obstacles will not be rerolled.

• Rainbow Poop, Golden Poop, Tinted Rocks, Trap Doors, Crawl Spaces, [Repentance] Fool's Gold and Killswitches are much less likely to be created by the D12 than all other obstacles.

• [Repentance] It is possible to reroll the spikes in a Sacrifice Room and render the room unusable.

• Newly created spikes (but not retractable spikes) in Sacrifice Rooms use separate reward counters, allowing you to get more rewards in one room.

• Each re-roll is seeded and will produce the same result for each room that the D12 is used in.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Lucky Rock, Meconium, Petrified Poop, and Stud Finder can provide extra value in conjunction with their associated obstacles.

• Leo / Mega Mush / Notched Axe / Pyro / Stompy / Sulfuric Acid / Terra / Thunder Thighs can provide Isaac a way to destroy the re-rolled obstacles.

• [Repentance] Car Battery: Re-rolls have a higher chance of entering the looping pool and creating obstacles that can't reroll (Reward Plates, Killswitches, Trap doors and Crawl Spaces)

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns blue die wisps on the middle ring. Wisps' tears have a 5% chance to reroll obstacles they hit. Poops, TNT barrels and metal blocks cannot be rerolled.

• [Repentance] XVI - The Tower? / A Card Against Humanity: Created obstacles can be rerolled into more useful objects such as Rainbow Poop or Golden Poop. Rocks created from XVI - The Tower? will have a larger pool to pick from. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • [Before Repentance] Car Battery: Re-rolls twice instantly without any benefits.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] The D12 is the only way in the game to remove metal blocks.

• [Repentance] Metal blocks can also be destroyed with Mega Mush. [end edition note] 

• The original Antibirth mod had its own D12 that functioned similarly to this item. For obvious reasons, that item wasn't added in Repentance, although the D12's effect was updated in V1.7.8 to be more similar to the Antibirth version.

• In Antibirth, the pick up quote was Reroll your playground.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If D12 creates a trap door in The Void, Chest, Dark Room or Home it will restart the floor when entered.
Bug note: If D12 creates a Reward Plate in the boss room on the floor where an alt door is allowed to appear (After A Secret Exit is unlocked), activating the button to create enemies and kill will create another one, up to 4 doors (depending on the size of the room). Exiting the boss room will leave only the original alt door. By entering a copy of the door, you can go to the alt floor and if you exit, the original door will also be open, even if you did not open it.
Bug note: When rerolling obstacles while Isaac has 2Spooky; any Movable TNT or Fire Places spawned in the fear radius has a chance of being spawned momentarily feared with only the purple tint to indicate the status effect. This effect lasts even on the remains of either object after it's destroyed before the fear effect ends. Corn poops created in the radius are unaffected; however, the Eternal Fly may also become temporarily feared. Venus has the same bug with the only difference being that it is charming obstacles and Eternal Fly and turning them pink.
Bug note: If Isaac has Car Battery and uses D12 two times or more in a quick succession (possible with The Battery), some obstacles may become stacked (there will be two or more obstacles in the same spot).

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Re-rolls all Rocks and Metal Blocks in the current room into other random obstacles.
[Repentance] Re-rolls most types of obstacles in the current room into other random obstacles.

D20.title: D20
D20.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Upon use, re-rolls all pickups, chests, and trinkets in the current room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Chests are more likely to be re-rolled into other chests.

• [Before Repentance] The empty chest object that is left behind after opening any kind of chest can be re-rolled into another pickup. As empty chests disappear after leaving a room, it's better to wait until D20 is fully charged before opening chests.

• [Before Repentance] D20 cannot re-roll pickups into Lil' Battery, but can re-roll pickups into Grab Bags which can contain Lil' Batteries.

• [Repentance] D20 can re-roll pickups into Lil' Battery and other battery pickups, and can re-roll pickups into Grab Bags which can contain Lil' Batteries.

• D20 can re-roll pickups into chests or trinkets and vice versa.

• On Chest and Dark Room, the re-rolled chests will always contain items unless they are a Red Chest or a Wooden Chest.

• Re-rolls create trinkets far less often than pickups and chests.

• It can re-roll pickups sold in the Shop.

• [Repentance] When used to reroll pickups in any shops, pickups may be rerolled into items instead.

• Rerolling pickups duplicated by Jera, Diplopia and Crooked Penny will result on both the original item and the duplicate being rerolled into the exact same pickup.

• Golden Trinkets rerolled by D20 will cause the resulting pickup to have the golden effect applied to it. If the trinket is rerolled into another trinket, it will lose the golden effect and act like a normal trinket, otherwise the gold effect will do nothing and will disappear upon leaving and reentering the room.

• Additionally, items spawned by chests with the gold effect applied will be golden as well, however other pickups dropped by chests will not be.

• [Repentance] Can reroll coins dropped by Tainted Keeper into other pickups, but they will still disappear if not picked up quickly.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] In Greed mode, the D20 is a one-item game breaker as long as the Shop has a Lil' Battery available. Leave behind as many coins and pickups in the arena as possible. After using the D20, avoid opening chests until the item has been recharged. Avoid collecting things that do not spawn pickups, help buy Lil' Batteries, or help open chests. This can often be repeated indefinitely, leading to collecting coins, bombs, and many pedestal items.

• [Repentance] Due to how the D20 interacts with the Book of Virtues, this strategy will not work with Bethany, as using the D20 while playing as her will destroy all pickups in the room.

• • However, this can be avoided by removing Book of Virtues using Butter! [end edition note] 

• D infinity can be used for this strategy if it is found.

• • D infinity in D20 mode will also destroy all pickups while also having the Book of Virtues. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Safety Scissors: Bombing a Bomb Bum while possessing this trinket will convert the Troll Bombs he spawns into regular Bombs. This process can be repeated indefinitely for unlimited Bomb pickups. These Bomb pickups can then be rerolled with the D20.'[end edition note] 

Interactions

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring. In addition to summoning its specific wisp, instead of rerolling pickups, it will destroy all the pickups in the room and has a chance to give a random wisp for each pickup destroyed.

• Car Battery: Re-rolls twice instantly without any benefits.

• [Repentance] Slightly increases the probability to re-roll into chests.

• Options?: Can re-roll both items created by Options?, but only one can still be taken.

Trivia

• In the originalThe Binding of Isaac, the D20 was unlocked by beating Isaac as Isaac.

fields.description: Re-rolls all pickups, chests, and trinkets in the current room.

D4.title: D4
D4.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, rerolls each of Isaac's passive items into new ones.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The new items will be drawn from the Treasure Room item pool.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The new items will be drawn from the item pool where the original item was acquired.

• [Repentance] If health upgrade items are removed by a reroll, the health they granted is subtracted.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The D4 does not reroll Dead Cat, Halo of Flies, Key Piece 1, Key Piece 2, Missing No., The Negative, The Polaroid, or Tonsil.

• [Repentance] The D4 can reroll Dead Cat and Halo of Flies, but will not reroll Dad's Note, Damocles, Dogma, Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2, and glitched items, in addition to the above. [end edition note] 

• Note that Missing No. can be rerolled into, but not rerolled out of.

• The D4 does not remove traits or abilities inherent to a character, such as Azazel's Brimstone-like attack, Lilith's Incubus, or The Forgotten's bone attack.

• Starting items from Challenges will also not be rerolled.

• [Repentance] The Lost's Holy Mantle is included.

• [Repentance+] Characters' starting passive items (except Eden's and Tainted Eden's) are now inherent to them and will also not be rerolled.

• Items that grant pickups (like Pyro or A Dollar) do not remove their bonuses when rerolled.

• These same items also do not grant pickups when another item is rerolled into them.

• The D4 can grant items that have not yet been unlocked.

• The items gained by the D4 count towards the collection page.

• Multiple copies of the same item (as generated by Diplopia, the Debug Console, or gathering them from multiple item pools (e.g. Steam Sale from both the Shop and Greed) will each be rerolled into a different item, [Before Repentance] even though the duplicates are not present on the pause screen.

• There is a small chance that D4 will not reroll every item: the game makes a number of attempts to reroll each item, but if they all fail to produce a new item that is available and applicable, the original remains unchanged.

• Smelted/Swallowed trinkets (via Marbles, Smelter or Gulp!) will not be rerolled.

• Will reroll Eden's starting item(s).

• [Before Repentance] Items rerolled away don't return to circulation and can't be encountered again.

• [Repentance] Items rerolled away return to circulation and can be encountered again.

• [Before Repentance] D4 doesn't remove transformation progress, meaning that he will keep a transformation or gain one if he gets a transformation item while having two points of this transformation before rerolling.

• [Repentance] D4 removes transformation progress.

• [Before Repentance] If it is unlocked, The Lost starts with this item along with spectral tears and flight. Using it will reroll Holy Mantle.

• [Repentance] The D4 does not give hearts that would be otherwise gained from item pickups, but will remove previously collected health upgrade items.

• [Repentance] If used while playing as Jacob and Esau or Tainted Lazarus, it will only reroll the items on the character that used it.

• Tainted Isaac can avoid having their health subtracted form rerolling health up items by dropping health items for full inventory before rerolling.

• [Repentance+] D4's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Abyss: Locusts created by Abyss are not rerolled.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Removes all of Isaac's wisps and gives him one random wisp for every two items rerolled. Book of Virtues will not be rerolled in the process.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: Instantly rerolls Isaac's items twice, which doubles the speed at which the item pools are exhausted and transformations are achieved.

• Potato Peeler: Every Cube of Meat produced counts as an item available to reroll. Because health usually is not removed when using the D4, this is useful to increase the number of items at the expense of the item pool.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The image of the D4 that appears on activation is incorrect; it shows the numbers 9, 7, and 8 on the right face of the die, when it should depict numbers consistent with the left face (i.e. 1 at the top, 3 at the front, and 4 at the right).

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Previously held items are not removed from the pause menu, which makes it difficult to determine which items Isaac currently has if they're too many to appear on the HUD.
Bug note: When D4 is used with a co-op baby present, the baby's sprite will turn into a glitched sprite of Isaac.
Bug note: If Isaac rerolls Schoolbag, he will keep both active items, but if he picks up a new active item it will swap with the one currently selected and the other will disappear.
Bug note: When Schoolbag is rerolled away while another active item is held along D4, the other active item will be dropped on a pedestal. Activating D4 after the other active item is dropped will then reroll D4 itself.
Bug note: An item picked up is assigned the pool of the most recently generated item; usually this has correct results but a difference can be seen, for instance, by killing a boss, entering a Devil Deal that has items and collecting the boss reward after seeing the Devil items. The boss item will be rerolled to a Devil pool item with D4. Items with no item pool (starting items, fixed drops etc.) will always use the item pool of the most recently generated item from an item pool as a result; if no items from item pools were encountered yet, the treasure room pool is used.
Bug note: If Isaac uses D4 in a room with an item before taking it, that item is assigned the pool of the most recently collected item. For example, if Isaac takes a Devil item, then uses D4 in a Treasure Room with an item before taking it, the latter will reroll into Devil items on subsequent uses of D4.
Bug note: Items that are rerolled are assigned the pool of the item with the highest item ID. This means one reroll with the D4 will probably go as expected, but further rerolls will be proliferated by items from the pool that had the highest ID before the first reroll.

fields.description: Rerolls all of Isaac's passive items.

D7.title: D7
D7.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Upon use, it restarts the room and respawns all monsters. Normal room clear awards are generated.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• No effect in:

• Rooms with no naturally placed enemies. This includes "trap rooms" with Poky-type enemies, though deactivated pokies will spawn in their original location.

• • Challenge Rooms and Boss Challenge Rooms.

• • Greed Mode main arena room.

• • Enemies spawned by pressing buttons, destroying Shopkeepers, obstacles or Angel statues do not count as naturally placed.

• [Repentance] Boss Rooms.

• The Mega Satan fight.

• [Repentance] The Mother fight.

• [Repentance] The Beast fight.

• [Before Repentance] Teleports Isaac in the starting room if used in Boss Rooms, Angel Rooms or Devil Rooms.

• [Before Repentance] Converts Secret Rooms and Shops that had a Greed or Super Greed fight into regular Secret Rooms and Shops.

• [Repentance] Krampus can be fought again in the Devil Room, like other Mini-bosses.

• [Before Repentance] Respawned Mini-Bosses will always have the same drop.

• When used in a room with a Champion enemy, the enemy will not respawn as a Champion.

• Enemies respawn exactly where they first spawned, even if that's where Isaac is standing, in which case Isaac will take damage immediately upon use of the D7. Right next to doors is usually a safe place to use it.

• [Repentance] If used in the Mirrored World of Downpour or Dross II, the rooms will not only have their enemies respawn, but all the normal non-mirrored contents such as pickups are restored. Using it in the Shop causes it to be stocked normally, and additional uses will restock the Shop's contents, unlike normal Shops. Using it in the mirrored treasure room that does not have the knife piece in Downpour XL / Dross XL will spawn an item. [end edition note] Using it in the mirrored Curse Room has a chance to spawn an item from its pool.

• [Repentance] In Mines or Ashpit, the D7 cannot regenerate minecarts. Any monsters that were riding a minecart on room entry will respawn on foot. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] As Tainted Keeper, enemies respawned by the D7 will drop the same type of coins as they had before using the D7. This can be used to quickly generate money from enemies that dropped high-value coins or greatly increase Luck if an enemy dropped a Lucky Penny. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Enemies respawned by the D7 don't drop loot when killed if they were champions and don't grant score in daily runs. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 4.5 Volt: Depending on the enemies in the room, some rooms can grant enough charge to be rerolled indefinitely.

• 9 Volt/AAA Battery: Quadruple-sized or L-shaped rooms can be rerolled indefinitely. With both of them, even normal sized rooms can be rerolled indefinitely.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a grey six-sided die wisp on the middle ring. The wisps start gray; if the wisps get hit while they’re gray, they invoke the effect of the D7 in the current room and turn blue. Damage that turns the wisps from gray to blue is negated.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: Doubles the amount of enemies summoned, but does not give double rewards.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Despite being a dice item, D7 is not an unlock.

• This trait is shared with D10 and Dice Shard.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If used in a non-Boss Room containing Chubs, C.H.A.D.s, or Carrion Queens, each segment of the boss(es) will be revived as an entire clone, tripling their number.
Bug note: If used in a "trap room" with Grudges after all Pressure Plates were pressed, all Grudges will respawn and will remain active if the room is left and re-entered.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Reroll Rewards!; Repentance: Roll again]
fields.description: Restarts the current room and respawns all monsters, allowing more rewards to be acquired by completing the room.

D infinity.title: D infinity
D infinity.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Upon use, grants a random die item that transforms into a different random die item.

• Each die item has a 2 room charge.

• D infinity is able to use all the available effects, regardless of whether the individual die mimicked by this item has been unlocked prior or not.

• [Repentance] Upon use, acts as any die item except for Spindown Dice, and can be cycled through by pressing the drop key.

• The charge time when picked up is 4, but changes to that of the last used die. Cycling does not change the charge time.

• The table below shows charges and effects.

| Name | Icon | Charge | Effect 
| D1 | | 4 | Duplicate 1 random pickup / trinket / chest

| D4 | | 6 | Reroll all of Isaac's items

| The D6 | | 6 | Reroll all items in the room

| Eternal D6 | | 2 | Reroll all items in the room. 25% chance for items to disappear

| D7 | | 3 | Restart room and respawn all monsters

| D8 | | 4 | Reroll stats (tears, damage, range, speed)

| D10 | | 2 | Replace enemies into weaker versions

| D12 | | 3 | Reroll obstacles (rocks etc.)

| D20 | | 6 | Reroll all pickups, chests and trinkets

| D100 | | 6 | Activates every dice effect (except Eternal D6 and Spindown)

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The icon of the D infinity will change to resemble the corresponding die while being held. Putting it back on a pedestal will change its icon back to normal.

• [Repentance] When in possession of more than one active item with the Schoolbag, all dice must be cycled through before the other active item can be used.

• When playing as Tainted Isaac and holding D infinity as well as another active item via Schoolbag, if Schoolbag is replaced by another passive item in its slot while the other active item is held, D infinity will be dropped on the ground, reset to its original state. This could allow the player to use any dice item with only a 2-pip charge. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] This item can be crafted from Bag of Crafting with eight Dice Shard. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a normal wisp in addition to having an extra effect based on the current die selected.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: Activates 2 dice. [Before Repentance] The second activation die cannot be predicted.

• [Repentance] The second activation die is determined by the seed and never changes.

• Void: When absorbed and Void is used, replicates the effect of a random die item.

• [Repentance] Acts as a copy of one of the 10 dice D infinity can replicate. This die is randomly chosen and does not change.

• ? Card: Activates the selected die, updating the charge time and keeping the charges stored.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance] When transformed into another die, the D infinity looks similar to Delirium. In its regular form that it appears as on item pedestals, the item resembles one of Delirium's eyes.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Has the effect of a random die item that changes each use.
[Repentance] Replicates the effect of a selected die item (except Spindown Dice), and can be cycled through by pressing the drop key.

Globin.title: Globin
Globin.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Globins chase after Isaac, similar to Gapers but are much faster. Instead of dying, they will collapse into goo and then regenerate after a few moments unless destroyed in their goo form. Each time a Globin is turned into goo form, it will have its total health decreased. Globins will do 1 full heart of damage on contact.

sections.heading: Gazing Globin
sections.text: Gazing Globins are an alternate version of the Globin which have a 9.49% chance to replace regular Globins. Gazing Globins run towards Isaac with increased speed and slide away when they collapse into goo, but otherwise function identically to regular Globins.

sections.heading: Dank Globin
sections.text: Dank Globins behave identically to regular Globins. Each time they collapse, they leave behind a puddle of slowing Black Creep and spawn a Spider. They spawn another puddle of Black Creep when finished off.

sections.heading: Cursed Globin
sections.text:
Cursed Globins are a variant of Globin that chase Isaac at a pace similar to a Gazing Globin. However, they will split into two piles of goo instead of one, and unless killed in this goo form, they will regenerate quickly into two Cursed Globins.

There is a maximum number of times the Cursed Globin can split.

Champion Cursed Globins will split into non-champion enemies.

sections.heading: Black Globin
sections.text: Black Globins walk towards Isaac, launching Spiders towards Isaac every time it takes damage. Upon death, they spawn another spider and split into a Black Globin's Head and a Black Globin's Body. This makes them the only Globin variant that doesn't have a goo form.

sections.heading: Clickety Clack
sections.text: Clickety Clacks are a bony version of Globins that alternate between chasing Isaac and wandering around the room. They turn into a pile of bones that can block Isaac's tears when killed, and will eventually regenerate if any other Clickety Clacks in the room are still alive. Only when all Clickety Clacks in the room are dead will the piles of bone disappear.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Dark Red Champion Globins will turn into goo twice.

• [Repentance] To prevent softlocks, Clickety Clacks cannot spawn as White Champions.

• [Repentance] 3 Clickety Clacks spawn at the beginning of the Clutch boss fight [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Sloth is a recolored Globin.

• Super Sloth is a recolored Gazing Globin with a large head.

• The name of the monster is a type of protein and is also similar to a goblin.

• Globins appear to be based on the Red Skeletons from the Castlevania series since they reform from their pile of bones after being killed. They can only be killed using a special weapon or spell.

• [Repentance] Clickety Clacks seem to be based on Dry Bones, a Mario enemy that has a similar mechanic.

• [Repentance] The Cursed Globins first appeared in the Antibirth mod where they regenerated at a slower rate.

• [Repentance] Cursed Globins act similarly to Cursed Crystal Spiders from Nuclear Throne.

Baby-Bender.title: Baby-Bender
Baby-Bender.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Grants Isaac's familiars homing shots.

• This includes the shots fired by Lilith and Tainted Lilith's attached familiar.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Using I - The Magician with Tarot Cloth will unlock this item.

• [Repentance] Tarot Cloth with the card has a unique effect and does not count as two uses for unlocking purposes.

• Using Telepathy For Dummies twice in the same room will unlock this item.

• Using it once with Car Battery will work.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either makes familiar tears gain the Brain Worm effect. Having both makes familiars gain the Tape Worm effect on top.

• The Intruder: Baby-Bender applies to The Intruder's projectiles while it is still in Isaac's head.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Baby-Bender is based on this Steam Workshop item by Ink Toodles and ajudadoraAustera.
