[end edition note] 
[Afterbirth+ onward] 

| Chance | Payout 
| 32.33% | Nothing

| 32.33% | 2 random Coins

| 32.33% | 2 Spiders

| 1% | Steam Sale

| 1% | Head of the Keeper

| 1% | Coupon (if unlocked)

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth onward] If Isaac already has Steam Sale, Head of the Keeper, and Coupon, shopkeepers will not drop any further pedestal items.

sections.heading: Special Shopkeeper
sections.text: When unlocked by donating coins to the Greed Donation Machine, special shopkeepers have a chance to replace regular shopkeepers. Special hanging shopkeepers require 14 coins, while grounded ones require 234 coins.

sections.heading: Possible Rewards
sections.text:
| Chance | Payout 
| 66% | Nickel / Sticky Nickel

| ~30.09% | Nothing

| 3.125% | Bloody Penny / Butt Penny / Counterfeit Penny / Flat Penny / Swallowed Penny / Burnt Penny

| ~0.78% | Greed

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Greed appears after destroying a special shopkeeper, the doors will be locked.

• Special shopkeepers can spawn in some specific room layouts even while not unlocked.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Shopkeepers have 5 hit points, but most attacks capable of hitting them deal more damage than that.

• Aside from explosives, shopkeepers can be damaged through other means.

| Items and other effects that can destroy shopkeepers 
| Flames spawned by The Candle, Red Candle, Ghost Pepper and Bird's Eye

| Light beams spawned by Crack the Sky, White Pony and Holy Light

| Monstro and Mom's foot when summoned with Monstro's Tooth, Mom's Toenail and II - The High Priestess

| The Boomerang

| When dashing into a shopkeeper with A Pony, , White Pony or Mars

| [Repentance] Blast from Camo Undies and Dark Arts (the slicing attack will not hit; an extra target is required to destroy a shopkeeper with Dark Arts) [end edition note]

| [Repentance] Collision damage from Mega Mush [end edition note]

| [Repentance] Fire waves generated by enemies such as Crackles, or by Mars when colliding with an obstacle [end edition note]

| [Repentance] When grabbed with or hit by the shockwaves of Suplex! [end edition note]

| [Repentance] When teleporting into a shopkeeper with Stitches [end edition note]

• Shopkeepers will be directly targeted by Monstro's Tooth and II - The High Priestess.

• Destroying a shopkeeper triggers the effects of specific items and trinkets, such as Charm of the Vampire, Infestation 2, Samson's Lock, Lusty Blood, Jumper Cables, Bat Wing, Athame and Sigil of Baphomet. Shopkeepers also count as enemies for the purposes of Jar of Flies and Book of the Dead.

• The effects of Gimpy, Infestation 2, Vade Retro, Vasculitis, Quints, Hungry Soul and Cricket Leg cannot be triggered by destroying shopkeepers. Destroying shopkeepers also does not provide soul charges for Urn of Souls.

• Using the PAC1 F1SM Seed makes shopkeepers invincible too.

• [Repentance] Charmed Cultists can resurrect destroyed shopkeepers (which will also charmed, though their behavior will be unchanged), which is not especially useful but demonstrates that shopkeepers are, by the game's logic, enemies like any other.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Lucky Toe]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The shopkeepers' faces occasionally take on the appearance of certain popular Internet memes, such as "Forever Alone".

• [Repentance] The Dummy looks identical to shopkeepers, though unlike real shopkeepers, it always bears the same appearance when spawned.

• Edmund has confirmed that all shopkeepers (and, by extension, Keeper) are mummified versions of Isaac from previous runs.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Greeds spawned by blowing up Shopkeepers will play the incorrect boss music.

Short Fuse.title: Short Fuse
Short Fuse.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Bombs placed by Isaac explode in 0.66 seconds instead of 1.5 seconds.

• [Repentance+] Bombs deal +15 damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If Isaac leaves and re-enters a room after placing a bomb, its explosion timer would not be affected by the trinket.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Bombs: Bombs placed by using health will explode while Isaac is still invincible.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Isaac's bombs deal +30 damage. If Isaac has both the golden trinket and the Box, the increase is +50.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Anarchist Cookbook / Best Friend / Bob's Brain / Epic Fetus / Kamikaze!: No effect.

• Bomber Boy / Scatter Bombs: The +15 bonus is applied prior to the bomb damage multipliers.

• Book of Virtues: None of the bomb-spawning wisps are affected.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs from Dr. Fetus also explode more quickly.

• [Repentance+] Damage is not increased. The bonus is applied only to manually placed bombs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This trinket originated in Antibirth, where it was originally called Exploded Firecracker.

fields.description: Bombs placed by Isaac explode quicker. [Repentance+] Bombs also deal +15 more damage.

Shot Speed.title: Shot Speed
Shot Speed.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Shot Speed is the attribute that governs how quickly an individual tear travels and is represented by a speeding ball.

[Before Repentance] Shot Speed also affects the effective range of the tears. As the range stat determines how long tears will stay in the air (and not distance traveled), a lesser shot speed reduces effective range.

Shot speed measures the velocity of each tear in contrast to the Tears stat, which measures tear frequency.

A tear traveling at 1.0 shot speed crosses one tile in 4 ticks (8 frames, or 0.133 seconds), giving a velocity of 7.5 tiles per second. Higher and lower values of the attribute scale the velocity linearly.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• All characters start with the same shot speed except for Samson, who has 1.31 shot speed, Jacob, who has 1.15 shot speed, Esau, who has 0.85 shot speed, and Eden, whose shot speed can be anywhere between 0.75 and 1.25.

• A higher shot speed will increase the directional knockback of enemies hit by the tears.

• Having a high shot speed is not always desirable. While a high shot speed means enemies are easier to aim at, [Before Repentance] and effective range is increased , it also means more knockback, which can make enemies move in unpredictable ways, potentially damaging Isaac and making it harder to land consecutive shots. Some items will also directly benefit from low shot speed, such as Tech X and Trisagion, and particularly items that grant homing tears, such as Godhead and Spoon Bender.

• Items that reduce shot speed cannot lower it past 0.6.

sections.heading: Other
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] In co-op, Long Baby will occasionally briefly increase range, shot speed, and tear falling speed. Dark Baby will occasionally briefly increase all stats, including shot speed.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Era Walk card decreases shot speed and increases speed for the current room. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Absorbing an item using Black Rune can increase shot speed by 0.2.

• [Repentance] Shot Speed Up pills increase shot speed by 0.15, and Shot Speed Down pills lower it by 0.15.

Sigil of Baphomet.title: Sigil of Baphomet
Sigil of Baphomet.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Shields Isaac for 1 second after killing an enemy.

• If another enemy is killed while Isaac is shielded, another second is added to the shield's duration.

• Up to 5 seconds of invincibility can be accumulated.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Isaac is in range of an enemy that explodes on death, the shield will not come up before Isaac takes damage from the explosion. Other on-death effects, like firing shots, are still guarded against.

• [Before Repentance+] In Arcades, [machine: Blood Donation Machine] s or [machine: Devil Beggar] s can be used without losing health by killing the red flies from [machine: Shell Game] s and gaining a shield.

• Additionally, losing in a [machine: Hell Game] always spawns a red spider, the shield generated from killing it guarantees a payout for each half-heart.

• During the fight against Ultra Greed, destroying Ultra Greed Coin (Spinner) will not grant a shield, despite being considered enemies.

• Destroyed Shopkeepers also grant a shield.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increase the shield duration to 1.5 second and 7.5 seconds of invincibility can be accumulated. Having both increase the shield duration to 2 seconds and 10 seconds of invincibility can be accumulated.

• Kamikaze!: Isaac can chain-kill enemies without taking explosion damage while the shield is active.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups don’t activate the shield or extend its duration.

• E. Coli / Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop don’t activate the shield or extend its duration.

• Freeze Effects: Enemies that are frozen don't activate the shield or extend its duration.

• Because of this interaction, when Isaac has Uranus, only enemies killed by icicles from statues, bombs, familiars and other sources will activate Sigil of Baphomet's effects, thus rendering the trinket quite difficult to use.

• [Repentance+] Frozen enemies do activate the shield and can extend its duration.

• Friendly Enemies: When friendly enemies spawned by items die, they activate the shield or extend its duration.

fields.description: Grants an invulnerability shield for 1 second after killing an enemy.

Silver Dollar.title: Silver Dollar
Silver Dollar.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Shops appear in the Womb, Utero, and Scarred Womb.

• [Repentance] Also spawns Shops in the Corpse. [end edition note] 

• Golden Trinket: An upgraded Shop will appear instead

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Cannot appear in Greed Mode.

• This trinket must already be held upon starting the Womb/Utero/Scarred Womb/Corpse floor for the effect to take place, i.e. the trinket needs to be carried over from the previous floor.

• Silver Dollar only needs to be held when entering the floor. The Shop will remain after dropping the trinket, even if it hasn't been explored yet.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: The shop will be upgraded.

fields.name: Silver Dollar
fields.description: Shops appear in Chapter 4.

Singe.title: Singe
Singe.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Singe is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Ashpit.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Singe always spawns with 4 damaging Singe's Balls that can be pushed around; these play an important role in his attacks. Any spiked rock caught up in an explosion launches rapidly across the room, bouncing when colliding into obstacles, walls, and each other.

• Farts, leaving a cloud of explosive gas.

• Spiked rocks caught in this attack will be propelled slowly.

• Runs erratically towards Isaac or a spiked rock and creates an explosion at the end of the run.

• If close to Isaac at the end of the run, Singe can also perform a short jump in Isaac's direction to gain extra distance, creating an explosion on landing.

• Charges up before releasing a large explosion, launching Singe into the air and creating a small cross-shaped pit in his wake; after a few moments he lands on top of Isaac's position. This attack spawns an additional spiked rock that lands down alongside him. This attack only occurs twice during the fight and only after Singe has reached a certain amount of HP.

• Spiked rocks are able to be launched into the pit that Singe creates. This temporarily removes it until Singe generates another explosion, which spawns it again from the ceiling.

• Multiple spiked rocks can be removed at a time, but Singe only spawns one back at a time per each explosion.

• After performing his second large explosion, Singe gains a new attack where he lights a match and places it in front of his butt, farting to produce a large stream of fire that follows Isaac's movement.

• Singe's explosion upon death can also damage Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance+] Singe's Balls can be destroyed by Hagalaz, greatly simplifying this fight.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A singe is a superficial burn.

• Along with The Beast, this is Edmund's favorite boss in Repentance.

• According to a Twitter AMA on April 4th 2021, the reason why Singe is so gassy is because he "eats farts". Why this is remains a mystery.

• The bestiary features a unique dancing animation that doesn't play during Singe's fight.

• The animation is referred to as "yeehaw" in the .anm2 file.

• Singe's matchstick attack is a possible reference to the Pyro's Gas Blast taunt in Team Fortress 2.

Sinus Infection.title: Sinus Infection
Sinus Infection.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a 20% chance to fire a booger tear that stick to the first enemy that they come in contact with and deals damage over time.

• Each booger deals damage equal to Isaac's tear damage every second.

• [Before Repentance] The booger lasts for 60 seconds or until the enemy dies.

• [Repentance] The booger lasts 10 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] This item can be spawned by Bumbino if he picks up 12 cents. [end edition note] 

• The booger tear chance is not affected by Luck.

• Boogers tears cannot pierce through enemies.

• Multiple boogers can stick to one enemy to deal extra damage.

• Booger tears pass through fireplaces and bombs even without piercing shots.

• Boogers cannot inflict status effects, even if the booger's appearance changes.

• The booger falls off the enemy after they die. If it hits another enemy before it touches the ground, it will stick to them and deal damage.

• Sinus Infection is extremely effective against bosses. If each booger tear lasts for the full 10 seconds, this item effectively triples Isaac's DPS against bosses.

• Jumping enemies or bosses like Monstro and Leapers and burrowing enemies like Round Worms and Lumps can get rid of the booger when they leap or burrow.

• Bosses like The Harbingers or Dark One, or enemies like Oob that have dash attacks do not lose the booger when they go off-screen.

• The tear-sticking effect is similar to Explosivo and Mucormycosis's.

• The Nose Goblin trinket's effect is almost identical to Sinus Infection, with an added homing bonus but half the activation chance.

• When Isaac is holding both Nose Goblin and Sinus Infection each booger tear created by the item has a 50% chance to also have homing.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brimstone/The Ludovico Technique/Tech X/Trisagion: Every tick of damage Isaac’s tears deal have a chance to attach a separate booger tear on a hit enemy.

• Cricket's Body: Booger tears will split into split booger tears that can attach to enemies.

• Explosivo: Explosivo tears can also be booger tears which damage the enemy over time while stuck to them before exploding.

• Godhead: Shots retain their aura while stuck to an enemy, but the aura can damage only enemies other than the booger victim. If the enemy dies before the booger’s maximum duration, it will resume homing and will often stick to a second enemy.

• Guppy: Damage instances from boogers attached to enemies have a 100% ( [Repentance] 50%) chance to spawn a Blue Fly.

• Lachryphagy: All tears have a chance to burst into boogers. Boogers will always burst into more boogers, though some of the boogers may incorrectly appear to be normal tears. When a booger sticks to an enemy, it will burst into 8 boogers which have a high chance of sticking again to the same enemy.

• Lost Contact: Boogers that stick to enemies will block shots, and will not be destroyed in the process.

• Polyphemus: Booger shots lose the Polyphemus pierce effect, but stick to enemies while dealing the full damage of the Polyphemus shot. Damage does not degrade.

• Spirit Sword: Swings and projectiles have a chance to apply boogers on enemies.

• Tech.5: The laser also has a chance to apply boogers on enemies.

• Technology: Hit enemies have a chance for a booger to be applied to them.

• Technology 2: The laser can also apply boogers with the laser’s chance to apply boogers being determined rapidly every tick.

• Technology Zero: Boogers can be connected with electricity while being attached dealing large amounts of damage to the booger victim.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone/Technology/Tech X/Trisagion/Ipecac: Overrides Sinus Infection.

• Ipecac: Booger tears will still appear, but will act identically to other Ipecac shots.

• Compound Fracture/The Parasite: Booger tears will not split after killing enemies.

• Dr. Fetus/Epic Fetus/Mom's Knife: Overrides Sinus Infection.

• Holy Light: Holy light strikes do not activate on booger shots.

• Immaculate Heart/Saturnus: Orbiting tears that stick to an enemy will return to the ring if the enemy cannot be stuck to anymore before the tear's duration ends.

• Jacob's Ladder: Lightning strikes do not activate on booger shots.

• C Section: Some Fetuses stick to enemies. However, they only do the Sinus Infection damage ticking and often result in dealing much less damage. 

• [Before Repentance] Tech.5/Technology 2: The laser is unaffected by Sinus Infection.

• [Before Repentance] The Ludovico Technique: The large tear has a chance to stick to enemies. The tear cannot be controlled while it is stuck to an enemy, and cannot be removed until the enemy has died.

fields.description: Adds a chance to fire a booger that sticks to enemies and deals damage over time.

Siren Minion.title: Siren Minion
Siren Minion.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Siren Minions are spawned by The Siren as one of her attacks and shoot projectiles towards Isaac while orbiting the boss. They are only spawned if Siren does not have 3 follower/orbital familiars stolen from Isaac. Technically classified as familiars and not enemies, their enemy status and HP is determined by the Siren Helper enemy that controls them. They behave identically to a charmed Brother Bobby.

sections.heading: Siren Helper
sections.text: Siren Helper has no appearance itself and instead controls and takes on the appearance of all of The Siren's charmed familiars. It also acts as the hitbox of each familiar and determines their HP. When it takes control of a familiar stolen from Isaac, the familiar will have a red hue. Siren Minions it controls have no change to their appearance.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• If spawned by other means than The Siren's attack, e.g. by console commands or modded effects, the Siren Minion follows Isaac and acts identically to Brother Bobby. If such a copy is charmed by The Siren, it will be destroyed like the ones summoned by The Siren herself instead of uncharmed when defeated.

• The Siren Helper appears as a Fly if forcibly spawned, but it will not take control of Isaac's familiars whether The Siren is present or not. It simply disappears immediately.

Boom Fly.title: Boom Fly
Boom Fly.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Boom Flies fly across the room in straight diagonal lines, dealing contact damage. Explodes upon death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] While Skatole is held, the Boom Fly and all of its variants will fly significantly slower and will not deal contact damage, but their other means of attacking/dealing damage will still damage Isaac as normal.

• While Isaac has the Beelzebub transformation, all Boom Fly variants will become friendly, and will not damage Isaac by any means (including explosions).

sections.heading: Red Boom Fly
sections.text: Red Boom Flies fly across the room in straight diagonal lines, dealing contact damage and releasing 6 blood shots in all directions upon death.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Red Boom Flies cannot replace Boom Flies in Dross.

sections.heading: Drowned Boom Fly
sections.text: Drowned Boom Flies fly across the room in straight diagonal lines, dealing contact damage. Upon death, they explode and release 4 blood shots in the cardinal directions, and sometimes also spawns a Drowned Charger. If a Drowned Boom Fly dies while over an obstacle or pit, the Drowned Charger will not be spawned.

sections.heading: Dragon Fly
sections.text: Dragon Flies fly across the room in straight diagonal lines, dealing contact damage. Upon death, creates four lines of fire in the cardinal directions; the fire nearly spans the length of an entire normal-sized room.

sections.heading: Dragon Fly X
sections.text: Dragon Fly X is identical to the Dragon Fly in behavior, but upon death, creates four lines of fire in the ordinal directions; the fire nearly spans the length of an entire normal-sized room. Note its X-shaped eyes to help remember its fire pattern.

sections.heading: Bone Fly
sections.text: Bone Flies fly across the room in straight diagonal lines, dealing contact damage and firing bones at Isaac if he lines up with one in a cardinal direction. Upon death, they shoot 3 evenly spaced bones (one of them aligned towards the closest cardinal direction to Isaac).

sections.heading: Sick Boom Fly
sections.text: Sick Boom Flies fly across the room in straight diagonal lines, dealing contact damage and trailing poisonous gas. Upon death, they explode into eight clouds of gas and release 6 green shots in all directions. The poison gas left behind upon death persists for much longer, but will dissipate when the room is cleared.

sections.heading: Tainted Boom Fly
sections.text:
Tainted Boom Flies fly across the room in straight diagonal lines, dealing contact damage. Upon death, they will emit a cross-shaped glow for a brief period, after which they will explode. This explosion sends 4 lines of further explosions in the cardinal directions, which span the length of the room.

They are exclusive to the Ascent to Home.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Boom Fly is tied with the Sucker for being the monster with the most true variants ('true variants' being monsters with ID x.1, x.2, etc), both with 7.

• [Repentance] Both Dragonfly types and the Sick Boom Fly first appeared in the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, instead of having any stage hp they had 20 base hp.

• Sick Boomflies would only create poison gas on death and would not shoot out six tears when dying.

Hook Worm.title: Hook Worm
Hook Worm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Tears move shifting left to right on a square-wave-like path.

• [Before Repentance] +10 Range.

• [Repentance] +1.5 Range, +0.4 Tears.

• [Repentance] Grants spectral tears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This trinket has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Pin, Larry Jr., The Hollow or Scolex. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] Effective range remains the same because the range buff only compensates for the tears tracing a longer path.

• [Repentance] Effective range is a bit lower, by about 1 tile.

• [Before Repentance] Shooting with this trinket equipped when next to a wall or block may cause the tear to travel into the wall.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: In addition to the further stats increase, the square-wave-like pattern has a bigger amplitude.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone / Tech.5 / Technology / Technology 2 / Revelation / Tainted Azazel: Effect applies to the Brimstone beam, effectively increasing the width of the beam.

• [Before Repentance] It also adds an extra tick to the Brimstone beam.

• Azazel: Azazel gains the wider beam, but no range increase.

• The Forgotten: Bone club does not get any wider or attack any further [Repentance] though he will still benefit from the tears up, making the trinket's main effect only work on The Soul.

• Tiny Planet / Tech X: No effect.

• Tractor Beam: The beam overrides the worm's tear movement effect, but keeps the +10 range.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Hookworms are parasitic worms that can enter through the skin from dirt that contains their eggs and larvae.

fields.description:

[Repentance] Tears move shifting left to right on a square-wave-like path. +0.4 Tears, +1.5 Range (effective Range is slightly lower).

Horf.title: Horf
Horf.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the enemy; the pill effect; Pills] 

Horfs are disembodied human heads with their eyes gouged out. Horfs remain immobile in one spot, firing blood shots at Isaac when he gets in their range. They will fire shots directly at Isaac when they're about ½-room width away from him, even though their shots can travel the entire room's length. This makes it possible to outrange Horfs in almost all encounters with them; even if you're in range, they have a slow rate of fire and their shots are slow-traveling as well, and can be dodged simply by moving slightly to the side.

• [Repentance] Horfs have a 1.67% chance to be replaced by Sub Horf. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Psychic Horf
sections.text: Psychic Horfs behave similar to Horfs, but they shoot homing shots instead of blood shots. Unlike a Psychic Maw, it does not possess an Eternal Fly.

sections.heading: Sub Horf
sections.text:
Sub Horfs are a variant of Horfs found in Downpour, Dross and rarely replace Horfs in other floors. Sub Horfs look like Horfs but are tinted blue in Downpour and rotten green in Dross; the random replacements in other floors are identical.

Sub Horfs will only shoot if hit first. If they are shot at, they will rotate and periodically shoot in the direction they are facing while rotating. They will also shoot upon receiving any knockback. They release 1 water shot upon death. Despite appearing to float, Sub Horfs can be pushed by the water streams in Dross.

sections.heading: Necro
sections.text: Necroes are a variant of Horfs resembling ghostly Bony. They will summon bones in a radius around them, sending them at Isaac. They can target Isaac from anywhere in the room.

sections.heading: Tainted Sub Horf
sections.text: Tainted Sub Horfs are a stronger version of the Sub Horf that behave like a Sub Horf, but fire much faster, have bigger projectiles, and slowly move towards Isaac while facing him.

sections.heading: Level 2 Horf
sections.text:
Level 2 Horfs are a variant of Horfs found in Corpse. They look like Horfs in a decaying state.

Level 2 Horfs act quite similarly to regular Horfs; however, they spit Small Maggots at Isaac instead of blood shots. Although they appear to float, they cannot get past gaps in the floor and are affected by creep.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Maws and Psychic Maws appear to be the posthumous versions of Horfs and Psychic Horfs, as their attacks and appearance are similar.

• Even though Horfs look like they are flying, they are considered grounded.

• However, they do fly in Crawl Spaces and can be hit down.

• [Repentance] Sub Horfs appeared in the Antibirth mod, where they would only fire upon receiving any knockback.

• [Repentance] Sub Horfs spawned outside of Downpour will have the same coloration as a normal Horf.

• Their bullets are also colored the same as normal horf bullets. [end edition note] 

• Horfs and Psychic Horfs use the same champion spritesheet.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If a Horf or Psychic Horf is stunned, feared, or frozen at the same time that it tries to shoot Isaac after the effect wears off, its shot will be fired without its corresponding animation.

Hornfel.title: Hornfel
Hornfel.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Hornfel is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Mines.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Hornfel appears with his own specially designed boss room: each wall has multiple boss doors with minecart tracks connecting each pair of doors. After a short delay, he appears out of a random door riding a minecart and performs one of the following attacks:

• Occasionally, when Hornfel enters the room through a door, he is accompanied by 2 Fly Bombs.

• Throws 1-2 Bombs at Isaac. Each bomb has a small chance of having the Hot Bombs or Sad Bombs effect.

• Throws 3 Brimstone Bombs that resemble mines. Each bomb has a delay and detonates after a few moments.

• Accelerates to a very high speed along one set of tracks, traveling in one direction, while frequently throwing out bombs. After multiple cycles, he slows down, gets sick, and vomits a fireball that releases fire trails in the cardinal directions upon landing.

• Sends out 1-2 decoy dummies with 4 HP on other tracks that burst into 6 Troll Bombs if killed or walked into.

• Other minecarts occasionally appear on other tracks independent of Hornfel, carrying a Fire Place, TNT, or a variety of other enemies:
Bony
Faceless
Danny
Gurgle
Quakey

Hornfel and his decoys deal a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Once Hornfel has taken enough damage, he falls out of his minecart and attempts to escape from the room via one of the doors surrounding the arena. He makes no attempt to attack Isaac, but he can still deal contact damage. In this phase, his contact damage is reduced to half a heart.

• Other minecarts carrying other monsters and objects can still appear as usual during this phase.

• If Hornfel escapes successfully, the fight ends as normal.

• If Hornfel is defeated, he unlocks Brimstone Bombs if not already unlocked, and has a 1/7 chance of dropping either Boom!, Brimstone Bombs, Hot Bombs, Remote Detonator, or Sad Bombs if it hasn't been seen or collected, otherwise he drops 3 Bombs.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Brimstone Bombs]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Hornfel will sometimes taunt Isaac by sticking out his tongue while sending out his decoy dummies.

• Hornfels is the group name for a set of contact metamorphic rocks. They are known to be very hard and durable.

• The Horny Boys are a stitched amalgamation of Hornfel and Loki.

• Hornfel and Loki are brothers.

• Hornfel is one of only 3 bosses that can be spared, with the others being Bumbino and Baby Plum.

• Coincidentally, they all made their debut in Repentance.

• These three bosses all can drop extra additional items. In [Repentance+] Repentance+, only Hornfel was given a special 1% item drop as the other two were omitted.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If Hornfel is killed off screen, the game crashes.

Host Hat.title: Host Hat
Host Hat.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Enemy shots that hit Isaac have a 20% chance to be blocked. When a shot is effectively blocked, Host Hat fires 3 projectiles similar to the Host's.

• Projectiles fired from Host Hat use Isaac's Damage and Range, and copy Isaac's Tear effects.

• • The bullets do not use Isaac's Shot Speed.

• Can block:

• • Fireballs (e.g. from Crackle), but their lines of fire harm Isaac.

• • Fire projectiles (e.g. from Mega Satan).

• • Obstacles thrown by Polty or Kineti.

• Does not block:

• • Lasers or beams.

• • Lines of fire from fireballs.

• • Projectiles from Big Bony, Coal Boy, Danny.

• Grants immunity to explosions.

• [Repentance] Grants immunity to bullets falling from above.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Gate. [end edition note] 

• Does not protect against exploding mushrooms.

• Does not protect against Hush's vertical beams in the final phase.

• [Before Repentance] Isaac becomes immune to Mom and Satan's stomp attacks, as they are considered explosions. This makes the item very valuable if trying to unlock The Forgotten, as it will protect Isaac from the effects of the Broken Shovel 1.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] This item is invaluable in Greedier Mode as nearly all of Ultra Greedier's attacks are considered explosions.

• One of only two items that grant full immunity to explosive damage, the other being Pyromaniac.

• Although Host Hat has firing animation that expose itself after it blocks a tear, it can still block tears in this state, firing bullets as it blocks.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Dr. Fetus / Epic Fetus / Ipecac: Isaac becomes immune to his explosives.

• Walnut: Walnut will only require 1-5 explosions to open. As Isaac is immune to explosions, he can safely open Walnut without taking any damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• The following items that change the property of Isaac's tears affect Host Hat's bullets:

• Eye of the Occult

• Haemolacria

• Ipecac

• Lachryphagy

• My Reflection

• Pop!

• Tiny Planet

• Trisagion

• The following items that modify Isaac's tears do not affect Host Hat's bullets, aside from stat changes (if present):

• Brimstone

• Chocolate Milk

• C Section

• Cursed Eye

• Dr. Fetus

• Epic Fetus

• The Ludovico Technique

• Mom's Knife

• Monstro's Lung

• Neptunus

• Spirit Sword

• Technology

• Tech X

• 20/20 / Keeper and other multi-shot effects: Do not add Host Hat's bullets.

• Anti-Gravity / Tractor Beam: Does not affect Host Hat's bullets, aside from stat changes.

• Cone Head: Cone Head's chance of blocking effect is applied first. Tears blocked by Cone Head do not cause Host Hat to fire.

• This leaves Isaac 40% chance to negate tears in any way.

• Dead Eye: Host Hat's bullets grant the damage multiplier, but do not reset it even when they miss.

• Eye of Greed / Lead Pencil: Host Hat's bullets are not counted for shots fired.

• Gnawed Leaf: Tears can be reflected while Isaac is invulnerable.

• Hallowed Ground: Host Hat's chance of blocking effect is applied first.

• This leaves Isaac 60% chance to negate tears in any way.

• Host Hat: Additional copies of this item, such as from Diplopia / Crooked Penny, have no effect.

• Infamy: Infamy's chance of blocking effect is applied first. Tears blocked by Infamy do not cause Host Hat to fire.

• This leaves Isaac 60% chance to negate tears in any way.

• Isaac's Heart: Tears can be reflected when hitting the heart, not Isaac.

• Holy Card / Holy Mantle: Host Hat's chance of blocking projectiles is applied before the shield, allowing it to be saved.

• Metal Plate: Host Hat's chace of reflecting effect is applied first. Tears blocked by Host Hat are not reflected by Metal Plate.

• This leaves Isaac 40% chance to negate tears in any way.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Nice hat!; Repentance: Blast resistance]
fields.description: A host familiar that sits on Isaac's head and has a 20% chance to block enemy shots and retaliate with 3 tears. Grants immunity to explosions.

Hot Bombs.title: Hot Bombs
Hot Bombs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac gains +5 Bombs on pickup.

• Placed bombs deal damage to enemies on contact and will leave behind a fire that damages enemies on contact upon exploding for 10 seconds.

• [Before Repentance] The fire does 22 damage per tick (66 damage per second).

• [Repentance] The fire can block four shots and/or deal four ticks of contact damage before expiring. It deals 23 damage at full durability, 17.25 damage after taking one hit, and 11.5 damage otherwise for a maximum damage of 63.25 damage.

• Fire from a Hot Bomb doesn't damage Isaac.

• [Before Repentance] Bombs deal 1 point of contact damage to enemies.

• [Repentance] Bombs deal 16 contact damage to enemies.

• [Repentance] Isaac can no longer take contact damage from static fires such as Fire Places or enemy fires. Fire projectiles still damage Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] This item has a 1/7 chance to drop if Hornfel is killed in his second phase. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] It also has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Hornfel. [end edition note] 

• If a Hopper touches a Hot Bomb, it will become a Flaming Hopper.

• The contact damage does not scale with Isaac's damage and is completely removed if Isaac acquires another bomb item that overrides the flaming bomb graphic such as Mr. Mega or Glitter Bombs.

• Big Horn will throw Hot Bombs at Isaac that deal contact damage.

• If eaten by a boss such as Chub, a Hot Bomb will continously deal damage to the boss until it explodes.

• [Repentance] Negates the damage from the floor of lava in The Beast's chamber, but not from its fire inhalation attack.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BBF / Best Friend / Bob's Brain / Bob's Rotten Head / Mr. Boom: These explosions are affected by Hot Bombs.

• Bomber Boy: Bombs leave behind nine fires in a cross shaped pattern.

• [Afterbirth onward] Doctor's Remote / Dr. Fetus / Epic Fetus: Bombs/missiles are affected by Hot Bombs.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Red Locusts: Red locust explosions are affected.

• Remote Detonator: Allows for maximization of contact damage, especially if an enemy gets stuck on a bomb.

• [edition anr] Scatter Bombs: Each additional explosion creates a fire.

• [Repentance] Fires from extra bombs now start with 1 less durability.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] Doctor's Remote / Dr. Fetus / Epic Fetus: Bombs/missiles are not affected by Hot Bombs.

• Ipecac: Ipecac shots are unaffected.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Orange champion Little Horn summons bombs that are identical in function, but given the Troll Bomb sprite and colored orange.

fields.description: +5 Bombs. Isaac's bombs leave behind fire that damages enemies upon contact.

How to Jump.title: How to Jump
How to Jump.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac jumps in the direction he is currently moving. The distance of the jump depends on how fast Isaac was moving and for how long he was holding the button when the item was activated. Jumping allows Isaac to travel over obstacles such as rocks and pits.

• While mid-jump, enemies, projectiles, Bombs, and spikes cannot damage Isaac. Isaac cannot interact with pickups or Chest mid-jump.

• Contributes to the Bookworm transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Standing still while jumping only grants invincibility for the first jump. Isaac has to move to regain invincibility while jumping.

• If Isaac has flight, Isaac dashes instead of jumping. This is functionally the same as jumping, but without the animation playing. Isaac will have invincibility during the dash, and the dash will only stop on terrain that can be walked on.

• While flying above a pit, the dash distance will be very short.

• This item can also be used to pass through otherwise impassible Crawl Space walls.

• Isaac can't jump through doors, which means damage from Curse Room doors cannot be avoided.

• If Isaac has a Stompy trait (from items such as Leo and Thunder Thighs), rocks won't be destroyed mid-jump.

• When jumping in an uncleared room, it is easy to land on top of an enemy, especially one that follows Isaac's position when attacking. The damage can be avoided by immediately triggering another jump, however.

• This can be repeated indefinitely, and it may be a good idea to keep jumping until you find a safe spot to land.

• [Repentance] How to Jump can be used to jump over pillars and spiked rocks safely.

• Isaac can jump over key blocks. However, if he has a key, it will be spent to open the key block.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Enemies Judas jumps through take 2 + 0.2 × floor contact damage and are set on fire. The burn deals damage equal to Judas' damage, and ticks up to 5 times.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns stationary wisps at the location jumped from which fires in the same direction as Isaac. Max of 6 wisps can be spawned at a time this way. Wisps only last for the current room.

• Broken Remote: Isaac can teleport indefinitely, but the jump will instantly be cancelled by the teleport.

• Panic Button: Makes Isaac immune to contact and projectile damage while moving.

• Familiars that orbit Isaac (such as Sacrificial Dagger, Sworn Protector, etc.) can damage enemies when Isaac jumps over them. However, items that activate on contact (e. g. Serpent's Kiss, Midas' Touch, etc.) cannot trigger during jumps.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Void: If this item is activated by Void, it is possible to get stuck in an impassable area with no ability to escape. Exiting and resuming the run will place Isaac at whichever door he entered the room through.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The cover of the How to Jump book resembles the original packaging artwork of the game Super Mario Bros., and also refers to Mario's original name, "Jumpman," in the game Donkey Kong.

• The description of the item is also a joke referring to the fact that Isaac can't jump, and that Isaac must apparently read a book with Mario in it to learn how.

• How to Jump is the only book in the Bookworm set that doesn't look like a book; every other book has white pages with a cover, while How to Jump has no distinct color for the pages, resulting in it looking more like a magazine or game cartridge.

fields.description: Isaac jumps in the direction he is currently moving, allowing travel over obstacles and enemies.

Huge Growth.title: Huge Growth
Huge Growth.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants the following effects for the current room:

• Increases Isaac's sprite size and hitbox by 60%. Hitbox cannot be increased past the standard value.

• +7 flat damage.

• [Before Repentance] +30 range.

• [Repentance] +3 range.

• Allows Isaac to walk over obstacles to destroy them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, Huge Growth has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• This effect doesn't stack if used multiple times in the same room.

• To unlock, Isaac must be 3 times bigger than his starting size.

• Isaac's total size is taken into account in unlocking Huge Growth; any size downs, such as One Makes You Small pills and Binky, will hinder progression towards the unlock.

• Liberty Cap will count towards this when the Magic Mushroom effect is active.

• Tarot Cloth causes XI - Strength to count for 2 size increases.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Huge Growth has been added in Booster Pack #1, after the initial release of the DLC.

• Huge Growth is based on this Steam Workshop mod by aeiou.

• Huge Growth is a reference to the card Giant Growth from Magic: The Gathering. The quote is a reference to the card Become Immense, which has a similar effect to Giant Growth, both making a creature larger.

fields.description: For the current room, makes Isaac larger, allows him to crush obstacles he walks on, and grants +7 flat Damage and [Before Repentance] +30 Range [Repentance] +3 Range.

Humbleing Bundle.title: Humbleing Bundle
Humbleing Bundle.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Transforms all Bombs, Keys, Penny, and Red Hearts into their respective Double versions.

• [Repentance] All Bombs, Keys, Penny, and Red Hearts have a 50% chance to be replaced by their respective Double versions.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Only works specifically on Bombs, Keys, Penny, and Red Hearts; other variants, like Nickels or Soul Hearts, etc., are not doubled.

• [Before Repentance] By bombing Donation Machines, Isaac can earn more money than is taken from the machine, giving an endless supply of coins until the machine breaks or he runs out of bombs.

• [Before Repentance] When used while fighting Greed, Hangers, or Keepers, every coin knocked out of Isaac will be worth two coins, allowing Isaac to net a profit.

• [Repentance] Coins dropped when taking damage from enemies such as Greed, Hangers, or Keepers have a chance to be doubled, allowing Isaac to potentially recover all lost money or even net a profit.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Contract From Below: Single pickup drops have a 2/3 chance to be doubled, which then become their doubled versions by Humbling Bundle.

• This results in an average increase from 1.33x more pickups to [edition alternatives: baseline: 2.67x; Repentance: 2x] more.

• IV Bag + Old Bandage + Humbleing Bundle / Maggy's Bow: The damage from IV Bag has a chance to spawn 2 hearts, which can be picked up to create further coins and possibly even heal hearts with enough Luck.

• [Repentance] Humbleing Bundle only has a 50% chance to double the hearts dropped, but Old Bandage may still drop 1 heart.

• The Jar: Allows for replicating hearts. Using the jar with 4 hearts inside it will cause 8 to drop, allowing Isaac to create an infinite amount of Red Hearts.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BOGO Bombs: No further effect.

• [Repentance] Due to Humbleing Bundle no longer guaranteeing double pickups, BOGO Bombs will always double bombs.

• Humbleing Bundle: No further effect if multiple copies are obtained.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item is a reference to Humble Bundle, collections of games and soundtracks that are sold online through a "pay what you want" system. The original The Binding of Isaac was represented in three humble bundles.

• "Humbleing" is a common misspelling of the word "humbling", and may be a further pun on the reference to Humble Bundle.

• All the files related to the object, such as graphics and animations, use the correct spelling in their names.

• The description and writing on this items graphic is a reference to picking up double bombs in the original The Binding of Isaac where the message "1+1 Free!" would pop up in the bottom right whenever picking up a double bomb.

fields.description: Transforms Bombs, Keys, Penny, and Red Hearts into their respective Double versions. [Repentance] This will occur 50% of the time.

Hungry Soul.title: Hungry Soul
Hungry Soul.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants Isaac a chance to spawn a friendly ghost upon killing an enemy, which rapidly chases down and deals contact damage to enemies.

• The chance to spawn a ghost is 33% and is not affected by luck.

• Ghosts deal contact damage equal to half of Isaac's damage, 4 times per second (2x Isaac's damage per second).

• After 7 seconds, the ghost explodes, dealing 7 flat damage to nearby enemies up to 3-4 times.

• The explosion cannot damage Isaac or the environment.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Enemies killed by ghosts are unable to spawn more ghosts, except for those killed by the ghost's final explosion.

• The ghost's explosion is capable of damaging friendly monsters, such as Bony summoned by Book of the Dead.

• Ghosts cannot be taken outside the room they spawned in.

• The ghosts are not considered to be familiars and as such aren't affected by any items that modify the behavior of familiars.

• This also means that Isaac can have more than 64 ghosts at a time and this won't override other familiars.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups can’t spawn ghosts.

• BFFS!: No effect.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop can’t spawn ghosts.

• Ipecac: The ghosts get only +1 flat damage from Ipecac, not the expected +20.

• Libra: The ghosts ignore damage modification from Libra, both positive and negative: the actual unbalanced damage value is used.

• Sacrificial Altar: Ghosts cannot be sacrificed.

fields.description: Enemies have a chance to spawn ghosts on death, which chase and deal contact damage to enemies and explode after a short time.

Hush.title: Hush
Hush.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Hush is the boss of ???, and the final boss of Ending 17.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Hush begins with a fight identical to the first phase of the ??? fight, having the same attacks and behavior but with a different appearance, half of ???'s health, and longer projectile travel distance due to being fought in a 2×2 room.

See ??? for more details.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After Hush's first form is defeated, it reveals its large true form at the top of the room, taking the form of its splash screen portrait.

• During this phase, Hush occasionally sinks into the ground, becoming non-attacking and invulnerable, and only returning once most of the projectiles onscreen have dissipated. It performs this move every time it loses around 20% HP and also in conjunction with some of its later attacks.

sections.heading: Phase 2-1 (100-80% HP)
sections.text:
Hush remains stationary in the top center of the room and performs the following attacks:

• Fires barrages of yellow, blue, and green glowing projectiles in certain patterns, combining 1-3 different patterns of projectiles. These patterns include:

• Rings of projectiles that alternate between rotating clockwise and counterclockwise as they move outwards.

• U-shaped salvos aimed at Isaac.

• Lines of projectiles aimed at Isaac that either gain (yellow), lose (blue), or maintain (green) momentum as they travel (these lines have spaces between them every 4-5 shots).

• 2-4 repeating volleys of 4 projectiles, with equal spacing between each volley (the angle these volleys are shot out at rotates as the attack continues).
The same pattern can be used multiple times in each barrage, and projectile patterns become less dense if multiple patterns are used in the same barrage.

sections.heading: Phase 2-2 (80-60% HP)
sections.text:
Hush sinks into the ground and relocates to the center of the room before resuming its attacks. It also gains the following attack patterns, in addition to attacks from the previous phase:

• Hush's projectile barrage can include two new patterns:

• A very dense ring of projectiles, with a gap aimed somewhere towards Isaac's general direction.

• 3-5 spirals of projectiles, with even spacing between each spiral (projectiles from these spirals initially lose momentum, but after a few seconds they resume their normal speed while rotating counterclockwise as they move out).

• Spawns a cluster of Hush Fly that either orbit Hush, launch towards Isaac's position and fly off-screen, or actively chase Isaac. These flies have invincibility for a short time after being spawned, and alternate between forming the shapes of a circle, triangle, square, pentagon, or a 5 or 6-pointed star.

sections.heading: Phase 2-3 (60-40% HP)
sections.text:
Hush keeps its attacks from previous phase and gains two more attacks and an extra shot pattern:

• Hush’s projectile barrage can now also include a very wide spread of projectiles that closes in on where Isaac was standing when fired.

• Hush spawns a horde of Blue Gapers, before sinking into the ground to relocate. While relocating, Hush can summon Blue Boils.

• Hush fires three rows of wavy Continuum projectiles in one of the cardinal directions, which warp over to the other side of the screen and increase in speed the longer they travel. Hush performs this attack 2-5 times before using a different one. These projectiles move in a set pattern and leave safe zones that last the entire barrage.

sections.heading: Phase 2-4 (40-20% HP)
sections.text:
Hush keeps its attacks from previous phases, gains an extra attack, and modifies its shot patterns:

• Hush sinks into the ground while firing its projectile barrages, moving in a random direction or chasing Isaac as it fires, and spawning Blue Boils as it moves. Only shot patterns from phase 2-1 can be used; the patterns added in phase 2-2 and 2-3 are lost.

• Hush creates three large red projectiles that move outward and split into 3 more projectiles multiple times. The split shots move quickly when they spawn but slow down before splitting again. Hush can start other attacks before the projectiles from this attack fully dissipate.

• [edition rnr+] From this point onward, the cooldown between each of Hush's attacks is drastically reduced due to a bug.

sections.heading: Phase 2-5 (<20% HP)
sections.text:
Hush keeps most of its attacks from previous phases, but loses its ability to spawn Hush Flies. However, it gains one more attack in this phase:

• Hush fires two laser beams upward from its eyes, which creates beams on the ground that move toward Isaac and leave trails of slippery Blue Creep. The speed at which the beams move is based on Isaac's speed stat, and are always possible to outmaneuver. While firing these lasers, Hush also releases five wavy, slow-moving lines of projectiles in all directions.

• [edition nrr+] When at <1% health, there is a greatly reduced delay between Hush's attacks.

• [Repentance] If too much time passes without damaging Hush, it will regenerate some health. This removes the effectiveness of some very slow fight strategies (such as Gnawed Leaf combined with less effective familiars) that would have been successful (if slow) in previous versions.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: New Area, Fart Baby, Purity, D12, Betrayal, Fate's Reward, Athame, Blind Rage, Maw of the Void, Empty Vessel, Eden's Blessing, Sworn Protector, Incubus, Keeper now holds... A Penny!, Hushy, Hallowed Ground, Divine Intervention, Vanishing Twin, A Secret Exit, Soul of Isaac, Soul of Magdalene, Soul of Cain, Soul of Judas, Soul of ???, Soul of Eve, Soul of Samson, Soul of Azazel, Soul of Lazarus, Soul of Eden, Soul of the Lost, Soul of Lilith, Soul of the Keeper, Soul of Apollyon, Soul of the Forgotten, Soul of Bethany, Soul of Jacob and Esau, Godhead]

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using Chaos Card only kills one of its phases.

• [Before Repentance] If it is thrown upwards during its first phase, it can kill both phases if timed correctly.

• Using the Emergency Contact on Hush's second form appears to lower its damage resistance by 50% for approximately 5 seconds.

• Upon defeating Hush, Isaac gains 2 charges for his active item.

• A Card Against Humanity works in the Hush room. This can be done after the fight is completed to farm huge amounts of health and coins. Having Sack Head or Petrified Poop makes this strategy even more effective.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] If Hush is killed for the first time and The Void is unlocked, Isaac can exit the room and come back in, and the entrance to The Void will appear without having to fight Hush again on a new run. [end edition note] 

• Successfully using Eraser on Hush's first form prevents his second from spawning.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
• Effects that cause long-lasting mass slowdown such as Stop Watch or the I'm Drowsy pill are very valuable, aiding the player's ability to dodge the complex tear patterns and deal with the massive spawns of enemies, which can happen in quick succession.

• The Broken Watch item can also cause a mass slow, but using it may not be a good idea since it also has a chance to speed up the entire room, making the fight extremely difficult.

• Night Light or Censer can apply tear slowdown on a smaller scale than the watch items, but their hard-to-control areas of effect may cause more confusion than benefit.

• [Repentance] The I'm Drowsy pill should not be used against Hush. The laser beams summoned in the final phase move at a speed based on Isaac's own base speed, but the slowdown from I'm Drowsy is not accounted for. Using it during the Hush fight will make it impossible to outrun the lasers.

• Any items that can block or deflect projectiles will be highly useful, due to the bullet-hell design of the fight. Orbital familiars, Circle of Protection, The Soul, Trinity Shield, Dry Baby, Farting Baby, Host Hat, and Infamy may greatly help mitigate damage.

• Dry Baby's The Necronomicon effect will trigger very often due to the amount of projectiles, allowing to easily wipe out the large waves of enemies Hush can spawn.

• Psy Fly is especially helpful, as it both deflects a large number of projectiles, and only has a small cooldown after deflecting multiple.

• Saturnus may help with the large amount of bullets, but the tears in the ring at the start of the room may have fallen by the time Hush's shots reach you.

• Ocular Rift can trivialize most of Hush's attacks as projectiles are pulled towards the rifts and away from Isaac. However, rifts can also disrupt the projectile patterns, making dodging significantly more difficult.

• Lost Contact may be beneficial or detrimental depending on the player's tears stat; in combination with a high tears stat, many Lost Contact tears may still reach Hush even after blocking Hush's shots, but if the player has a low tears stat, they may find all their Lost Contact tears fired being destroyed during Hush's bullet hell attacks before they can reach their target.

• When the player has piercing tears, however, Lost Contact can cause dodging most attacks to become trivial regardless of the player's tears stat, as the player's tears will destroy any enemy projectiles they come into contact with while remaining themselves intact.

• [Before Repentance] Serpent's Kiss, Maw Of The Void, Athame, or The Virus (in combination with defensive items like Algiz or Book of Shadows) will make Hush's summoned enemies occasionally drop black hearts, allowing the player to farm large quantities of health during the enemy-spawning attacks.

• [Repentance] Serpent's Kiss only generates black hearts from contact damage. Maw Of The Void, Athame, and The Virus no longer generate black hearts at all.

• Broken Modem is not recommended, as it will stop Hush's tears and close some escape routes, making it harder to dodge in some cases.

• [Repentance] Tears affected by Broken Modem will be deleted rather than frozen in place, making the fight much easier.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The combination of Mysterious Liquid and Trisagion can kill Hush extremely quickly by spawning massive amounts of creep under his large body.

• The Forgotten's ability to swap characters into The Soul is very helpful in the Hush fight. Since nearly all of Hush's attacks are projectile-based, The Soul can hide behind the skeletal body and deal damage while staying totally safe.

• [Repentance] Magnetizing Hush using Lodestone causes many of the slower bullets to not be able to go further than Hush's own hitbox, rendering the barrage ineffective.

• Cursed Eye can greatly benefit Keeper/Tainted Keeper if given the right items. They can fight Hush, and if they get damaged while charging, they teleport out of the fight and can go back to the shop area and bomb the Donation Machine to replenish health.

• Cursed Skull also works for this.

• • [Repentance] The Donation Machine can only be bombed once, after which it is destroyed for the rest of the run.

• Hush' Blue Gapers spawning attack is useful for healing when playing as Tainted Magdalene.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• According to Edmund on Twitter, Hush represents Isaac's imminent death slowly approaching towards him, which is the reason why Hush and ??? are the same thing, since ??? represents Isaac suffocating in the chest, hence the blue color of their body.

• According to Edmund on Twitter, Hush is a giant ??? pushing from the other side.

• In its first form (the replica of the ??? fight), "Ascension" plays, while in its second form, the name of the boss theme is "Morituros".

• Morituros in Latin is the accusative masculine plural for 'about to die', which roughly translates to "those who will die". This could also be interpreted as "death inevitable", since Isaac's unusual way of living was ought to have consequences at some point or another.

• Hush is one of only two bosses in the game with a Boss Room scaled in a 2x2 fashion, the other being Delirium.

• There is an unused file in the game named "boss_hush_skinless" which appears to be an unfinished sprite sheet for the unreleased third form of Hush. It resembles a red, fleshy head.

• Tyrone has stated that Hush's "skinless phase" was originally intended to be his second form, having concept art ideas based on it.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] It is possible to spawn it using console command. It moves but doesn't attack in any way.

• Hush shares his name with a level from Edmund's previous game, Super Meat Boy.

• As Hush loses health, the boss room grows gradually darker, and vein-like shadows begin to appear in the ceiling.

• When defeated, Hush screams and disappears in a flash of light. The ground where it once was becomes scorched in a shape resembling a distressed face.

• The 30-minute limit of reaching Hush's floor could be alluding to how long it took Isaac to suffocate in the chest.

• In the card game The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls, Hush's card features an original translation of Job 4:16, "It stood still, but I could not discern its appearance; a form was before my eyes; at first there was a hush, and then I heard a voice." This might be due to Job 3, a monologue where Job curses the day of his birth.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Delirious is used in phase 2 of the Hush fight and Delirium is killed, The Calm (music usually played after defeating a boss) will replace Morituros.
Bug note: Having the No Return seed enabled when going to Hush will result in no doors being available, softlocking the run.
Bug note: If Hush takes too much knockback too quickly (e.g. from Knockout Drops), the Hush Flies it spawns may teleport around the room erratically, occasionally resulting in unavoidable damage.
Bug note: Hush is not actively targeted by blue spiders

Hushy.title: Hushy
Hushy.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a Hush familiar that floats and travels diagonally around the room, bouncing on walls, and deals contact damage to enemies. While firing tears, Hushy stops moving. In this state, it will:

• Block enemy projectiles.

• [Repentance+] Fire out rings of 8 blue projectiles that deal 6 damage each, once every 1.033 seconds.

• Hushy deals 2 contact damage per tick or 30 damage per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Hushy can be pushed by explosions, both while stationary and during movement (in this case, the explosion may cause the familiar to change the direction it is moving in).

• [Repentance+] Although Hushy can float over obstacles, its projectiles are not spectral, meaning its shots will be blocked if it's positioned directly over a rock.

fields.description: Spawns a Hush familiar that bounces diagonally around the room and deals contact damage. While firing tears, it stops moving. [Repentance+] When stationary, Hushy will periodically fire out rings of projectiles.

Hypercoagulation.title: Hypercoagulation
Hypercoagulation.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• After Isaac takes damage from an enemy or donates health, he drops a Red Heart that despawns after 1.5 seconds.

• The heart dropped depends on the source: half-hearts of damage taken drop Half Red Hearts, and full hearts of damage taken drop full hearts.

• The hearts will get launched out of Isaac with momentum, making them difficult to pick up.

• If Isaac is firing tears as he gets hit, the heart will get launched in that direction.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Damage sources that scale up from half a heart of damage to a full heart of damage starting on Womb/Corpse will still only cause Hypercoagulation to spawn half a heart. However, being hit by a champion enemy will still spawn a full red heart, even though all enemies do a full heart of damage by that stage.

• Red hearts are not spawned when Isaac loses heart containers (such as through health down pills, buying Devil Room items, using Guppy's Paw, etc), with the only exception being Potato Peeler.

• Red hearts will still drop regardless of the type of heart being subtracted from damage, making the item generally useless for characters who cannot utilize red hearts.

• However if Isaac takes damage while inside a super secret room layout with specific heart spawn, he will drop a full heart of that type instead. The full heart will drop even if Isaac takes half a heart damage.

• The following damage sources will activate Hypercoagulation:

• Enemy attacks

• Normal spikes

• Spiked rocks

• Fire Places

• Explosions

• Blood Donation Machines

• Devil Beggars

• Confessionals

• Hell Games

• Razor Blade

• Blood Rights

• Dull Razor (despite it not taking health)

• Potato Peeler

• Extra damage taken from holding Glass Cannon

• The following damage sources will not activate Hypercoagulation:

• Curse Room doors

• The door to Mausoleum

• Sacrifice Room spikes

• Spiked Chests/Mimic Chests

• Bad Trip pills

• Golden Battery

• Kamikaze!

• Breath of Life

• A Pound of Flesh shop spikes

• IV Bag

• Sharp Plug

• Shard of Glass

• Blood Bombs

• Blood Oath

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Ace Cards / Diplopia / D1 / Jera: Converted/duplicated hearts will not disappear.

• Blood Rights / Razor Blade: Damage taken to use the item also spawns hearts, reducing the cost of using them. The first usage of these items each room will spawn a full red heart.

• Cancer / Percs! pill / The Wafer: Damage sources that spawn full red hearts will still spawn a full red heart despite the cost being reduced to half a heart.

• Dull Razor: Can be used to spawn full red hearts for Isaac to pick up.

• Equality!: As long as Equality is active, all hearts spawned will be doubled and never disappear. Hearts remain on the ground even after the effect is no longer active.

• Humbleing Bundle: Red Heart spawns can be converted to Double Hearts.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Cambion Conception: By intentionally taking damage with something like a fire and grabbing the half-red hearts, Isaac can easily generate powerful familiars for free.

• Candy Heart / Immaculate Conception: The hearts will count toward gaining stat boosts/familiars.

• Compost: The temporary heart will be converted into a Blue Fly/Spider.

• D20 / GB Bug: Rerolled hearts will still disappear.

• Daemon's Tail: Hearts spawned do not turn into keys but simply do not spawn 80% of the time, and the 20% that do spawn will always be Black Hearts.

• Glass Cannon: Spawns two more full red hearts when Glass Cannon breaks, regardless of how much health was lost to it.

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper: Spawns blue flies upon getting hit, essentially granting them the same effect as Infestation.

• IX - The Hermit?: The heart will not be converted to coins.

• IV Bag: Doesn't spawn hearts.

• Maggy's Bow: Doubles the healing received from the hearts spawned.

• Magneto / Super Magnet: Will immediately start pulling the dropped hearts to Isaac, breaking their momentum and making collection much easier.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Hypercoagulation (otherwise known as Thrombophilia) is a medical condition that causes blood clots to spontaneously form in a person’s blood vessels and prevents them from dissolving properly.

fields.description: After Isaac takes damage from an enemy or donates health, launches Red Hearts from Isaac that despawn after 1.5 seconds.

I - The Magician.title: I - The Magician
I - The Magician.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Grants homing tears for the current room.

• [Repentance] Grants homing tears and +3 Range for the current room. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • I - The Magician has the same effect as Telepathy For Dummies, as evidenced by the given costume.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • Since this effect only lasts for a room, it is preferably used against a boss. Homing allows to focus more on dodging.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Gives The Book of Belial effect on top of homing.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card + Car Battery : Only damage is doubled.

sections.heading: Interactions

I - The Magician?.title: I - The Magician?
I - The Magician?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants a repelling blue aura that strongly pushes projectiles and enemies away from Isaac for one minute.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • Since the effect lasts one minute, it is advised to use it on bosses that fire high amounts of projectiles such as Mega Satan, Hush, Delirium, or Mother.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Once the minute has passed, Isaac reverts back to his normal state on the spot, he does not need to change rooms to remove the effect.

• I - The Magician?'s effect is similar to the The Soul's but stronger, with a wider area of effect, and has consistent effect strength.

• As long as Isaac does not walk into a projectile or enemy himself, most projectiles will be completely repelled and enemies cannot come into contact with Isaac.

• Certain enemies can bypass the effect if they dash fast enough, such as Oobs.

• Additional uses of I - The Magician? only refresh the one minute timer.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

fields.name: I - The Magician?
fields.quote: May no harm come to you

Clotty.title: Clotty
Clotty.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Clotties are enemies that wander around the room, randomly shooting four blood shots in the cardinal directions. These can be particularly difficult to deal with early on if the player isn't careful. [Afterbirth onward] Two of them are also spawned from Mega Clotties when killed. They are immune to any fire damage and will turn into Grilled Clotties when set on fire, unless they're in a flooded room (such as those found in the Flooded Caves or a room that Flush! was used in), in which case they'll be killed as normal.

sections.heading: Clot
sections.text: A Clot is an alternate version of a Clotty that shoots four tar shots in the diagonal directions. They appear similar to Gish, who also spawns them. As they do not shoot tar shots in the cardinal directions, they are considerably easier to defeat than Clotties.

sections.heading: I.Blob
sections.text: The I.Blob is an even rarer alternate version of the Clotty. It is an Isaac-like blob that shoots 8 blood shots in all directions, combining the attacks of both the Clotty and the Clot.

sections.heading: Grilled Clotty
sections.text: The Grilled Clotty is an enemy that behaves exactly like a Clotty; however, it moves much quicker, and their shots are ever-so slightly off-kilter. Clotties transform into Grilled Clotties when set on fire.

sections.heading: Cloggy
sections.text: The Cloggy is an enemy that behaves similarly to a Clotty; however, its shots are brown and curved rather than straight. Its bullets alternate clockwise and counterclockwise with each shot.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Clots are a miniature version of Gish, from the game of the same name.

• The I in I.Blob stands for Isaac, referencing their similarities to Isaac.

• [Repentance] Grilled Clotties originate from the Antibirth mod.
