Golden Razor.title: Golden Razor
Golden Razor.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, spends 5 Penny and grants +1.2 damage for the current room.

• The effect can be stacked.

• If Isaac has fewer than 5 coins, nothing happens.

• Grants 5 pennies upon being picked up for the first time.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using the item will give Isaac's tears a golden tint that becomes more noticeable with each use, up to a maximum of three times. This effect is purely cosmetic.

• When unlocking the item, coins do not actually have to be spent, just removed. Actions such as donating to a Donation Machine or items like Magic Fingers will also count as long as the coin amount goes from 99 to 0.

• Similarly, losing coins by getting damaged by Greed or similar enemies counts as spending coins when it comes to unlocking Golden Razor.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Also invokes the effect of Magic Fingers when used, which occurs after the damage increase and deals an additional +5 damage; non-boss enemies killed by this effect also have a chance to drop 1-2 pennies.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns yellow wisps on the middle ring, looking like coins. Wisps' tears have a 15% chance of inflicting Midas' Touch effect on enemies.

• Deep Pockets: The increased money capacity can allow the Golden Razor to be used more than 10 times as much before the player runs out of money.

• Rock Bottom: The damage bonus from each use will be permanently locked at the highest achieved value in a single room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is similar to Razor Blade, the only difference being the cost in coins instead of hearts.

• The item is based on the Golden Razor Blade from The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls card game.

fields.description: Spends 5 Penny to grant +1.2 damage for the current room. Grants 5 pennies when picked up for the first time.

Golden Trinket.title: Golden Trinket
Golden Trinket.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Golden Trinkets are an unlockable type of trinket unlocked by beating Mega Satan with Tainted Jacob.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Golden trinkets have their effects either doubled or given additional effects, identical to how the trinket works with Mom's Box.

• [Repentance+] Some golden trinkets have a special effect if combined with Mom's Box.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Once unlocked, any trinket drop has a 2% chance to spawn as a golden version of itself. This includes regular room drops, opening chests, using Mom's Box, finding them in the shop in Greed Mode, etc.

• This chance is not affected by luck, Mom's Box or difficulty settings.

• Holding a golden trinket counts as the player holding 2 of the normal version.

• Only trinkets that are affected by Mom's Box or can stack with each other are affected by their golden counterparts. Others will act just like the normal ones.

• Hardcoded drops such as Mysterious Paper from Divorce Papers, The Left Hand from beating Ultra Pride, Forgotten Lullaby from bombing The Siren's skull and Perfection for beating 3 bosses without taking damage cannot spawn as golden variants.

• Eden and Tainted Eden's starting trinket can also be a golden one.

• If a violet champion monster is killed while it is gold-petrified, for instance through Midas' Touch or Eye of Greed, the trinket it drops is guaranteed to be a golden one. Rainbow champions still drop normal trinkets.

sections.heading: Notable effects
sections.text:
• Broken Remote: Triggers the Teleport 2.0 effect whenever an activated item is used.

• Crystal Key: Increases the chance of red rooms spawning.

• NO!: Prevents items with quality 0 from appearing.

• Rosary Bead: Adds 4 Rosary items to all item pools.

• Hook Worm / Ring Worm / Wiggle Worm: In addition to the further stats increase, they have an increased effect on your tear trajectory.

• In addition, the following effects are unique to the golden versions of their respective trinkets, and cannot be replicated by Mom's Box:

• Kid's Drawing: Having a golden version counts as having 2 Guppy items.

• Mysterious Candy: Spawned poops will be Golden Poops.

• Store Credit: The golden version won't be removed on a purchase. Instead, it has a chance to turn into a non-Golden Store Credit with each item purchased using it.

• Tick: In addition to the doubled effects, the golden Tick can be dropped/replaced like any other regular trinket.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The ID, or more accurately subtype, of a golden trinket is the normal ID + 32768. For example, the ID of Golden Cancer is 32807 (because it normally has an ID of 39).

• The Debug Console spawn code would in this case be 5.350.32807.

• Using the high damage debug flag, debug 4, causes all trinkets spawn as golden ones.

• [edition rnr+] Some golden trinkets do not have an effect due to them being added late in development.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Golden trinkets rerolled by D20 will cause the resulting pickup to have the golden effect applied to it. If this is a trinket, the trinket will turn into a standard trinket, otherwise the gold effect will do nothing and will disappear upon leaving and re-entering the room.

• Additionally, items spawned by chests with the gold effect applied will be golden as well, however other pickups dropped by chests will not be.

Great Gideon.title: Great Gideon
Great Gideon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Great Gideon is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Mines and the Ashpit.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Great Gideon is always fought in a vertical double-size room and has no health in a traditional sense. Instead, Isaac must battle 6 waves of monsters to beat him, similar to Greed Mode waves. Each wave begins once all enemies from the previous wave have been defeated.

He uses the following attacks during these waves:

• Creates a vacuum that affects the whole room, pulling in Isaac and all monsters and monster projectiles. It also pulls in additional rock projectiles. Touching Gideon while he is performing this attack damages Isaac.

• Spits 5 projectiles in a cone shape towards Isaac. The center projectile is larger and splits into 8 projectiles in a radial burst when it lands or hits something.

• Charges up then spits large flame projectiles down the center of the arena that can occasionally leave small fires behind.

• Some enemies caught in this attack are turned into their flaming versions: Rock Spider into Coal Spider, Clotty into Grilled Clotty and Gyro into Grilled Gyro.

• After the beginning of the 4th wave, Great Gideon charges up and releases a rock wave down the center of the room, breaking parts of the floor and leaving gaps.

• There is always at least 1 gap between the trail of holes created by this attack as to not completely trap Isaac on either end of the room.

• Gideon does not spawn the next enemy wave during the middle of any of his attacks and only progresses a wave once he has finished.
After Isaac defeats all 6 waves of monsters, Great Gideon will deactivate, similar to a regular Stone Grimace.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Great Gideon can be instantly killed with Chaos Card. Doing so reveals a unique 1x2 Crawl Space beneath him, containing two locked chests, two items and a random key.

• This can be done at any time, even if he has already been defeated, as his deactivated body still remains after returning to the room.

• Defeating Great Gideon in this way plays a unique animation in which the Chaos Card gets lodged in his forehead before he explodes.

• Pressing on a Killswitch in the room similarly kills Great Gideon, and reveals the unique 1x2 Crawl Space. This also plays the unique animation of the Chaos Card in his head. Doing so is possible with D12

• Completing waves will not charge active items.

• Vanishing Twin will duplicate Great Gideon and increase the number of waves by 2. The waves themselves contain no extra enemies.

• Great Gideon can be fought outside the Mines or the Ashpit via using a IV - The Emperor? card in Downpour or Dross. If encountered outside his regular stages, he has preset waves consisting of Frowning Gapers, Wall Creeps, Round Worms, Gurgles, and Suckers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• He is the boss version of Stone Grimaces, resembling a giant version with his left eye replaced by 7 holes arranged in a hexagonal pattern, and his left backside appears rougher with several protruding rocks.

• When performing his rock wave attack, he grows spikes resembling a Quake Grimace's.

• Great Gideon's name likely comes from Gideon, an Old Testament prophet and military leader known for winning a decisive battle against an overwhelming Midianite army with only an army of 300 Israelites — explaining the large amount of enemies the boss spawns.

• The name Gideon is said to mean “hewer” which is an individual who works in a mine breaking stone.

• Great Gideon is one of the few bosses with a unique health bar, aside from Dogma.

• The Crawl Space that opens up when using Chaos Card on Gideon is titled "Gideon's Grave" in the game's code.

• According to artist NotYourSagittarius, this is a direct reference to Scott Pilgrim, a series of graphic novels.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Spawning Great Gideon with the debug console will spawn him with a normal boss healthbar instead of a "waves" mechanic. When Great Gideon attempts to spawn a wave of enemies, the game crashes.
Bug note: Dealing enough damage quickly enough (e.g. with Soy Milk) to the monsters Great Gideon creates can cause him to spawn the next wave before all enemies in the current one are dead.

Greed.title: Greed
Greed.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the game mode; Greed Mode] 

Greed is a mini-boss and one of the Seven Deadly Sins. He can appear in Shops starting on the second floor of Chapter 2 or Secret Rooms starting on the first floor of Chapter 3.

• [Afterbirth onward] He also has a small chance to spawn when destroying aSpecial Shopkeeper.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Greed wanders randomly around the room and performs one of two attacks:

• Fires a spread of 3 projectiles in the cardinal direction closest to Isaac.

• Spawns 2 Hoppers to his either side.
If hit by Greed, Isaac loses 2-4 coins and drops 1-3 Pennies on the floor.

Greed deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If any member of the Seven Deadly Sins is defeated on the current floor, then Greed and Super Greed cannot spawn on that floor's shop.

• Therefore, exploring every room for a Mini-Boss Room and opening the Secret Room is the best way to minimize the odds of Greed appearing.

• Shops and Secret Rooms Greed is encountered in count as Mini-Boss Rooms, and cannot be bombed out of. They also prevent any other Mini-Boss Rooms from generating that floor.

• Once Greed is encountered in a Shop or Secret Room, Super Greed replaces him in subsequent Shops and Secret Rooms. After Super Greed is encountered in the same manner, they cannot spawn in Shops or Secret Rooms for the rest of the run.

• Defeating Greed in a Secret Room causes all entrances to adjacent room entrances to be opened. [Before Repentance+] The exceptions are entrances to adjacent Challenge Rooms and Boss Challenge Rooms- which will be barred and blocked off forever, unable to be opened by a bomb.

• If Isaac teleports out of the room after defeating Greed but without killing all the Hoppers he spawns, Isaac can re-fight Greed for extra coins or copies of Steam Sale.

• [Before Repentance] Greed can drop Steam Sale even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. 

• [Afterbirth onward] Greed spawned by blowing up a special shopkeeper can never spawn as Super Greed, even if another Greed was encountered before.

• [Repentance] The exact spawn chances for Greed/Super Greed are as follows:

• Base chance 33.3%

• Having more than 20 coins entering the floor: +1.66%

• Destroyed the Donation Machine on the previous floor: +3.33%

• Destroyed a Shopkeeper in the previous floor: +0.66%

• Donated money to the Donation Machine in the previous floor: -1.66% per coin, up to a maximum of -8.33% for 5 coins

• These put the minimum and maximum chances at 25% and 39% respectively.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Sin]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Greed has his own account on Twitter. This was uncovered after the community dug up a figurine of Greed covered in Sharpie marks during an ARG, which quickly led to his account. After guessing his password, and tweeting on it, the password was quickly changed and was then used to announce the arrival of Keeper.

• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived.

• Greed is a personification of one of the Seven Deadly Sins, with Greed being described as an inordinate desire to possess something, whether that be wealth, power, etc. Greed is a desire to possess something even if it means doing something immoral. Greed can lead to sins such as deception, violence, hardheartedness, and ingratitude.

Greed's Gullet.title: Greed's Gullet
Greed's Gullet.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants an extra Red Heart container for every 25 Penny Isaac has, up to a maximum of 4 hearts at 99 coins.

• Dropping below the number of coins required for a Red Heart container removes the Red Heart container.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The extra Red Heart container can exceed the maximum Coin Heart container limit of Keeper, allowing him to obtain more than [Before Repentance] 2 / [Repentance] 3 Coin Heart containers.

• Depending on the character used, this item only affects Red Heart containers, Soul Hearts (???) or Coin Heart containers (Keeper). It does not affect The Lost.

• [Before Repentance] The Red Heart container gain is not retroactive - picking it up at 99 coins will not grant 4 extra Red Heart containers.

• However, picking it up at 99 coins and then dropping below 99 coins will lose a Red Heart container, decreasing the viability of picking this item up the more coins you have.

• • The player will die if they lose their last form of health as a result of Greed's Gullet.

• • If Keeper drops to under 2 Coin Heart containers as a result of Greed's Gullet, or by any other means (Devil deal, etc.), he is unable to use an HP Up to increase his health back to 2 and has to regain the lost coins to do so.

• [Before Repentance] If Greed's Gullet is rerolled away after gaining health, the extra health will be preserved even if the player loses the coins afterward.

• • However, if this happens with Keeper, his health will drop back to 2 Coin Heart containers upon picking up an item, unless another Greed's Gullet is picked up.

• [Repentance] If Greed's Gullet is lost or re-rolled by any means (including the Mother's Shadow chase sequence), the health will be lost. This may cause Isaac to die. After returning from the Mother's Shadow chase sequence, the heart containers will be re-added, but they will be empty. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The Red Heart containers granted by Greed's Gullet are now retroactive - picking the item up at 99 coins will immediately grant 4 Red Heart containers. Consuming coins will still cause Isaac to lose Red Heart containers.

• [Repentance] This also applies in reverse; consuming Red Heart containers granted by Greed's Gullet through methods such as Devil Room items or Guppy's Paw will cause Isaac to lose an appropriate amount of coins.

• [Repentance] For Keeper specifically, Greed's Gullet in combination with Deep Pockets allows him to bypass the 12 heart container health limit, capping at 15 Coin Hearts at 999 coins.

• Works the same for Tainted Keeper but caps at 14 Coin Hearts instead.

• By using Health Up pills and Health Up items while having Deep Pockets the cap for Keeper can be raised to 54 Coin Hearts. However, additional heart containers beyond 24 will not appear on the health bar.

• • Works the same for Tainted Keeper but caps at 53 Coin Hearts instead.

• Be careful when buying items from the Shop, as it can remove Red Heart containers.

• Enemies that drain Isaac's coins (such as Keepers, Hangers, Greed, or Super Greed) can remove Red Heart containers.

• This item allows Keeper and Tainted Keeper to utilize Health Up pills and Health up items, as the Coin Hearts gained this way are kept even if the coins are lost once the coins lost are regained, and can bypass the 99-coin limit.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Deep Pockets: After exceeding 100 coins, Isaac gains an extra heart container for every 100 coins instead of every 25.

• Strawman: The assisting Keeper may also gain extra coin hearts, and in fact will retain the extra health containers even if coin loss would otherwise drop him below the threshold. However, exiting the game and then continuing thereafter will update Keeper's health.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Abaddon: Removes heart containers by removing coins in 25 cent increments.

• Dead Cat: Any extra Red Heart containers granted by Greed's Gullet will be removed upon pickup. If Isaac had more than 24 coins when picking up Dead Cat, then the remaining Red Heart container will be removed if enough coins are lost.

• A Dollar: Isaac will instantly gain the max amount of Red Heart containers.

• Eye of Greed: Coins will be lost for every 20th tear fired, risking Red Heart container loss if Isaac has more than 24 coins.

• Money Power: Isaac will gain both damage and health.

• A Quarter: Isaac will gain a Red Heart container.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: For the Keeper characters, they gain an additional Coin heart container slot, separately from the HP gaining increments, which they can fill by getting HP ups. You gain one of these every 25 coins even with Deep pockets. You can gain an additional 39 via this bug.

Greed Mode.title: Greed Mode
Greed Mode.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Greed mode is a game mode introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth.

sections.heading: Gameplay
sections.text:
In Greed mode, each floor has a Curse Room, a Devil Room/Angel Room, a double-wide Shop, and an exit room all connected to a main double-height arena room with a button in the center. A Super Secret Room is also connected to one of the rooms. Up until the penultimate floor, an already unlocked Treasure Room with a silver door frame and a normal locked Treasure Room are also available. The silver Treasure Room always gives items from the Boss pool. The sixth floor (The Shop) does not have any Treasure Rooms but does have the Shop and Curse Rooms. The final seventh floor has no waves and contains only three rooms, the largest of which contains the game mode's final boss.

When playing Greed Mode, a yellow coin ( [mode: greed] ) will appear on the HUD, below the consumables.

sections.heading: Shop
sections.text:
As there are no normal drops in Greed mode, the Shop becomes Isaac's primary source of items and pickups. Shops in Greed mode automatically restock. Shops will always have six items/pickups for sale, sometimes discounted; in order from the left side of the room to the right, these will always be:

• A Key

• A red heart

• A Shop item

• A Boss item

• Two random pickups, trinkets, or items from the Treasure Room pool.
There will also almost always be two Shopkeepers near the center of the room, as sometimes just one special shopkeeper spawns instead.

sections.heading: Arena
sections.text:
The 1x2 room in the center of all floors except the final one is the Arena, where most of the game mode's coins and enemies come from. These rooms always have a button in the center that, when pressed, bars all the doors and starts spawning waves of enemies and coins. While active, the button has a timer underneath it that counts down; when the timer runs out or all enemies in the current wave are killed, the next wave spawns. This continues until wave 8 or 10 is reached, Isaac dies, teleports out of the arena or presses the button again. Pressing the button before all the waves have spawned deals half a heart of damage to Isaac (or removes 1 penny from the next wave if playing as The Lost or Tainted Lost) and stops the timer that causes waves to spawn automatically. Once the timer stops and all remaining enemies are killed, the doors re-open. The button can then be reactivated to continue progressing through the waves. Once all waves are spawned, the button's spikes retract and cannot be pressed until all enemies are cleared. All waves except the optional "nightmare" wave must be completed for the door to the next floor to open.

For the first 8 waves, the timer will start at a set time and then increase by 1 second for subsequent waves. For Basement and Caves, the clock starts at 6 seconds. For Depths, the clock starts at 5 seconds. For Womb, the clock starts at 4 seconds. For Sheol and The Shop, the clock starts back at 6 seconds again. The first boss wave is set at 33 seconds (30 after Everything is Terrible 2!!! is unlocked) on all floors.

The enemies spawned by each wave are determined by the wave number and current floor. Each wave is as follows:

• Normal enemy waves:

• Wave 1-3: "Easy" enemy pool

• Wave 4-6: "Medium" enemy pool

• Wave 7-8: "Hard" enemy pool 

• Boss waves:

• Wave 9: "Easy boss" pool 

• Wave 10: "Medium boss" pool

• Wave 11 (optional): Nightmare boss wave - "Hard boss" pool (spawns the floor's Devil Room/Angel Room on completion).

Note that "boss" pools can include multiple (mini)bosses spread out across the room. Unlike normal mode, deal chances will only appear after doing the extra wave, and their spawn chances are not affected by taking red heart damage.

[Repentance] Enemies can spawn as Champions as normal, but will not drop pickups, with the exception of The Hollow's gold champion, which drops coins as normal. Rainbow champions drop consumables too, albeit only appear in Sheol in [mode: greed; greedier] Greedier version of the mode.

At the start of each wave, Pennies are dropped on the ground, which Isaac can use in the Shop to purchase items and pickups. Each normal wave drops 2 pennies, each boss wave drops 4 pennies along with a bonus coin after passing through 3 waves without receiving red heart damage. That means on a full hitless floor, an extra coin can be obtained on waves 4, 7 and 10, bringing the total of coins earned to 27 per floor. This extra coin mechanic explains why sometimes a coin can spawn on the 11th wave.

Each new wave counts as a new 'room' for purposes of item charges, familiars dropping items or the like. However, one-room temporary effects, such as The Book of Belial, will remain across waves, and items that activate upon entering a new room will not activate when a new wave starts.

• Taurus is an exception and will activate each time the button is pressed to start a wave.

sections.heading: Floors
sections.text:
Greed mode has seven total floors, five of which are based on floors found in the main game. These floors are Basement, Caves, Depths, Womb, Sheol, a unique floor called The Shop, and the final boss floor. Each floor will spawn enemies and bosses native to that floor in the main game, except for The Shop, which has no counterpart outside of Greed mode. Instead, The Shop spawns mostly Greed enemies, but can also spawn enemies from any floor. The Shop is the only normal floor which does not contain Treasure Rooms.

[Repentance] Greed mode floors can appear as their variants with unique waves including Burning Basement, Cellar, Flooded Caves, Catacombs, Dank Depths, Necropolis, Utero, and Scarred Womb.

sections.heading: Ultra Greed
sections.text:
The Ultra Greed floor contains only three rooms: An empty starting room, a Mini-Boss Room in which multiple Greeds, Super Greed, Wrath or Monstro will spawn, and the final Boss Room containing Ultra Greed.

After Ultra Greed has been defeated, turning him into a golden statue, a Final Boss Chest to end the level and the Greed Donation Machine will spawn. Isaac is given the chance to donate his remaining money to the Greed Machine, which will unlock several rewards including the Keeper character.

sections.heading: [Afterbirth+ onward] Greedier Mode
sections.text:
Greedier mode is a harder version of Greed mode. When playing Greedier mode, a small, red stained coin ( [mode: greedier] ) will appear on the HUD, below the consumables.

You must [achievement unlock: Greedier!] to unlock it.

Greedier mode changes gameplay in the following ways:

• An additional “hard” wave is added to the initial set of 8 waves, bringing it up to 9.

• The time the clock starts at is shorter (with the exception for Basement and Caves' mob waves).

• For Basement, the clock starts at 8 seconds. For Caves, the clock starts at 6 seconds. For Depths, the clock starts at 4 seconds. For Womb, the clock starts at 3 seconds. For Sheol and The Shop, the clock starts at 2 seconds. The first boss wave is set at 14 seconds on all floors.

• Coin drops per wave are modified to give fewer coins overall.

• Waves 1-8 drop 1 penny.

• Wave 9 drops 2 pennies. (total 10 coins from mob waves)

• The first boss wave drops 3 pennies.

• The second boss wave drops 6 pennies. (total 9 coins from boss waves)

• Plus the extra coin mechanic explained above that can give 3 additional coins, bringing the potential total to 22.

• [Before Repentance+] One enemy per wave is guaranteed to spawn as a champion, unless the wave consists solely of non-champion enemies. They will not drop pickups, unlike the regular game.

• The final boss gains a second phase.

• The Greed Donation Machine's chance to jam is greatly reduced, making it much easier to fill out.

Greedier mode unlockables were separate from Greed mode unlockables; however, as of Booster Pack #5, completing Greedier Mode with a character will also unlock the corresponding Greed mode unlockable.

Despite being a "hard" version of Greed, most hard mode rules from the vanilla gamemode don't apply. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text:
• Flight will not prevent damage from the spiked stop button unless the player is The Lost, Tainted Lost, or Tainted Forgotten.

• However, a Penny is deducted from the next round of rewards if the button is pressed as The Lost or Tainted Lost. It is possible to negate this by triggering the button and surviving until all waves have spawned before quitting out. When reloading the save, all of the coins will be on the ground. Pressing the button again will start the waves from wave 1, but will no longer spawn coins, removing the downside.

• Items with effects that only persist in the room are especially useful in Greed mode. Complete all waves in one go to maximize their efficiency. Examples of such items include Box of Friends, The Book of Belial, The Nail, Lusty Blood, The Pinking Shears, Scissors, and Sulfur.

• Being teleported by the Curse of the Maze can open the exit door without needing to complete the floor, allowing large portions of a run to be skipped.

• Only a half heart of damage is taken in floors beyond chapter 3, a feature unique to Greed mode.

• This makes items such as The Wafer substantially less useful, since there is a limited number of enemies that could cause more than a half heart of damage. However, they can still be used for the Ultra Greed boss fight, since all of his attacks deal a full heart of damage.

• Killing all the enemies before the timer resets doesn't increase the number of coins produced.

• It is also often a good idea to get rid of pickups on the ground if possible, as they can limit movement in a relatively cramped arena.

• Due to the fact that the mode presents fewer rocks, finding Crawl Spaces is much easier.

• Using keys or bombs to open golden and stone chests is almost always worth it since it's highly likely that it will return the used pickup, with the smaller possibility of an item like the A Quarter.

• Staying towards the middle of the room makes seeing most of the arena at once, as well as avoiding potential instant damage.

• It is often a good idea to press the button when the arena is flooded by invulnerable entities like Death's Heads or Poky, so that they are guaranteed to die once the waves are complete. Clearing the room before the next wave still deactivates them.

• Firing non-stop is not always the wisest thing to do as it can lead to instant damage, from something like explosions for example. Items like Cursed Eye and Chocolate Milk help avoiding that, although Cursed Eye is still a double edged sword.

• "The Shop" penultimate chapter often spawns several shopkeeper entities throughout the waves, which can be blown up for extra cash.

• The shop keepers have a very low chance of dropping Steam Sale or Counterfeit Penny and other useful pickups when bombed.

• Sometimes spending the acquired pennies may be wiser on the next floor. Certain collectible items, hearts or keys may be on sale a depth below, which saves money compared to refilling them when not yet necessary.

• Any form of homing is tremendous in this gamemode as its' effect covers a relatively large part of the arena.

• [Repentance] "Ace of" cards are very helpful to use on spawning enemies — be it to heal up or gain resources.

• Sack Head tends to replace the coins Ultra Greedier's coin explosions spawn, which can be useful forTainted Lost with a clutch Holy Card. Alternatively - it could be useful for battery drops instead.

• There are methods of achieving infinite coins/items. Although difficult to coordinate, and sometimes heavily reliant on luck, these methods can practically guarantee a successful run. These strategies can be combined with Chaos to allow stronger items to be obtained more easily.

• Method #1: Requires a 2 of Diamonds card, the Blank Card, a Shop selling Lil' Battery, and enough coins to buy one. This allows infinite coin count doubling with no drawback.

• Method #2: Requires Jera, the Blank Card, a Shop selling Lil' Battery, and enough coins to buy one. Similar to the first method, but instead of doubling Isaac's currently held coins, this method allows for infinite duplication of Pennies dropped during waves.

• • [Repentance] Since Blank Card no longer copies the ability of the runes, this method no longer works with Jera, so instead you need Clear Rune in place of Blank Card, a Shop selling Lil' Battery, and enough coins to buy two, as Clear Rune requires 12 charges to copy effect of Jera. [end edition note] 

• Method #3: Use Diplopia or the Crooked Penny on a Steam Sale. This will allow Isaac to take as many items as desired for free.

• • [Repentance] This method is no longer infinite, as stacking multiple Steam Sale uses a new algorithm.

• Method #4: Requires Swallowed Penny and a discounted red heart (2c). Use the curse door by entering and exiting right after losing only half a red heart and spawning a coin. By repeating the process long enough you can get infinite coins, Swallowed Penny being able to spawn nickels and dimes and being guaranteed 1 penny per half heart. If Mom's Box is held, this method can be performed without a discounted red heart as the number of coins spawned by Swallowed Penny will be doubled.

• The D20 can be used in tandem with Lil' Battery to re-roll all Pennies dropped during combat, some of which will become Grab Bags or chests. The process can then be repeated indefinitely.

• [Before Repentance] As the D20 re-rolls all opened chests into pickups, chests should not be opened unless the D20 is fully charged.

• [Repentance] Using the D20 in conjunction with the Book of Virtues will destroy all pickups in the room; as such, the D20 should not be picked up while playing as Bethany. [end edition note] 

• This method also works with D infinity or Clear Rune paired with a Soul of Eden.

• [Before Repentance] In Greedier mode, upon defeating Ultra Greedier, all poops, whether destroyed, damaged or intact, will be converted into Golden Poops.

• As a result, A Card Against Humanity can be used to guarantee a large source of coins for the Greed Donation Machine.

• • [Repentance] Poops spawned inside of the Ultra Greedier fight are turned into yellow colored poops, and drop normal brown poop pickups.

• Common display resolutions, such as 1920x1080 with aspect ratio 16:9, will show only part of the arena in fullscreen mode. Switching to windowed mode and then resizing the window makes it possible to keep an eye on the entire arena while playing.

sections.heading: Helpful Items
sections.text:
As mentioned above, all items that grant a temporary buff or benefit that expire once Isaac leaves the room are extremely powerful in Greed Mode, as these effects can last an entire floor's worth of waves, and some can be stacked. Items typically useful in Normal Mode that are not enhanced by Greed Mode's nature are not listed.

• Steam Sale: Reduces prices so that more items can be bought, and saves more money for the Greed Machine.

• Sack of Pennies / A Quarter / A Dollar: Provides an abundance of money.

• Mystery Sack / Sack of Sacks / Bomb Bag: Provides more pickups, especially bombs which are scarcer in Greed Mode.

• Keeper's Sack: Due to the gamemode's nature, many stats ups will be granted by this item very frequently.

• Leech / Charm of the Vampire: The large amount of enemies means more healing.

• Crooked Penny: May be used to duplicate all shop contents. If Crooked Penny fails, the shop could simply be rerolled to replenish its contents.

• Linger Bean: Any cloud created by the item stays afloat for a while & provides a consistent, wide-area effect.

• Brown Nugget: Multiple flies can be spawned in the arena before starting the waves.

• Akeldama: Slows down and damages chasing enemies, who can get overwhelming as the waves get shorter.

• Lemon Mishap / Free Lemonade: Deals great AoE damage.

• [Repentance+] Creep created by Lemon Mishap remains on the ground indefinitely, allowing Isaac to cover a large portion of the room in it.

• Sprinkler: Can be used multiple times in one arena.

• Gnawed Leaf: Allows for passive damage through familiars while staying invincible.

• Mega Blast / Mega Mush: Long lasting effects that can trivialize a floor.

• Plum Flute: Baby Plum is able to damage way more enemies as they are usually strewn about in the room.

• Star of Bethlehem: Always present in the middle of arena, allowing for great DPS increase, though it also makes accidentally pushing the button easier.

• Red Stew: The damage buff can be sustained by the constant onslaught of enemies.

• The Stairway: As long as one remains in the arena at the start of a floor, the ladder won't disappear. This allows Isaac to get richer before going into The Stairway's deal.

• Quints: Gives you a persistent source of help during all the waves.

• Jar of Flies: The high enemy count of Greed Mode causes Jar of Flies to generate stacks very quickly.

• Ocular Rift / Lodestone / Black Hole: Can suck up many enemies in large chunks garnered in close proximity.

• Hungry Soul: Very useful in a run since massive formation of enemies are ever-present throughout.

• Purgatory: Can be timed to fire a ghost right as a new wave generates.

• It Hurts: The effects stack throughout the entire arena zone.

• Azazel's Rage: Triggers every 4 waves and can easily wipe out every enemy in the arena.

• Larynx: Cleans up the enemies fast as well as preventing hits with high likelihood.

• D10: Downgrades all the enemies in the room, useful because of the low charge amount.

• Birthright + Tainted Cain: Purchasing an on-sale item over and over while having Birthright results in almost infinite consumables.

• Betrayal: Charms every enemy when hit, allowing an entire wave to be cleared at the cost of one hit.

• Betrayal: The high enemy count will cause them to harm each other more often.

• The Candle: Can be used to wipe out clusters of enemies, which helps prevent overcrowding.

• Black Candle: While most curses don't especially matter in Greed Mode, Curse of the Blind is especially devastating, making immunity to it very valuable.

• Paschal Candle: Quickly gains stacks, especially later on, due to the short wave timer.

• Midas' Touch + E. Coli: Touching enemies turns them into golden poops, making you rich.

• Cube of Meat / Ball of Bandages,Mom's Heels,The Virus,Serpent's Kiss, Aries, Little Horn, The Nail and My Shadow: Since the mode prevents telefragging for a tiny amount of time even if enemies spawn on top of you - the contact damage trait of that item becomes very useful to instantly kill those that spawn on you with no consequences, however it can turn out badly if said monsters are explosive.

• Keeper's Kin: Provides support in early floors due to the abundance of rocks.

• Glass Cannon: helps immensely with clearing waves, it's possible to even use it in advance before pressing the buttons to get use of 2 shots in a row.

• Potato Peeler: Meat boys can be created in mass due to the abundance of HP ups available in the shop. Isaac also emits damaging creep for the current room after using the item.

• Book of the Dead: Spawns bone orbitals or charmed Bony when there are killed enemies in a room. Making this item especially useful after the first 8 rounds and before the boss rounds.

• D20: The D20 is a one-item game breaker as long as the Shop has a Lil' Battery available. See the tips section above for more information.

• D infinity: Incredibly powerful in Greed Mode, as the dice can now be toggled to mimic the effects of the D1, The D6, and the D20, allowing Isaac to quickly gain consumables and reroll items.

• Dark Arts: Dark Arts can be used to press the button without taking any damage, kill many enemies with each activation, and have the item be constantly recharged with each wave.

• While playing as Tainted Judas, each enemy or projectile ran into will grant a damage buff. With the sheer amount of enemies appearing, especially in Greedier, Tainted Judas will gain an immense damage buff and can kill huge swaths of enemies with ease. Additionally, this is even more potent against Ultra Greed, as you can run through the many Greed Gapers summoned to gain even greater damage buff, as the Gapers will be clustered very closely together.

• Gello: Incredibly powerful, as it can be activated multiple times in the same room.

• Hemoptysis: Can be spammed to push into enemies into walls, which happens almost always due to the arena being somewhat secluded.

• No. 2: Can deal room-wide damage every 5 seconds, as well as giving you free bombs to blow up shopkeepers & secret room walls.

• Red Candle: Filling the room with flames before pushing the button will quickly kill all enemies and bosses.

• [Repentance] This method is no longer effective because the flames now extinguish after a set time.

• Wooden Nickel: Allows for an easy gain for a lot more money very quickly, as it can be used once per wave. If the 9 Volt is also picked up, Isaac can use activate the item once every 15 seconds to gain infinite money as long as there is an enemy left in the room.

• Liberty Cap: Can be used to repeatedly exit and re-enter the arena to force the Magic Mushroom effect.

• Mom's Lock: Can be used to repeatedly exit and re-enter the arena to force the Mom's Knife effect.

• Counterfeit Penny, Swallowed Penny and all other penny trinkets are useful due to the nature of Greed Mode. Even Cursed Penny is useful if you're trying to teleport into the exit door of the floor; Although it is wise to take all money before picking the trinket up, and only using it with 1 coin left.

• Equality!: With careful pickup management, the coins can be doubled.

• Eve's Bird Foot: The bird provides consistent help throughout waves.

• Samson's Lock: Abundance of enemies offers consistent damage increase.

• Berkano: Consistently useful in Greed Mode due to locusts lasting as long as Isaac stays withing the arena.

• Sigil of Baphomet: The wave based enemy spawns allow for constant uptime.

• Coupon: Can be used to make pickups or items free in the shop, in exchange for making them no longer restock. Can also be used to take Devil Deals for free, conserving any heart containers, which are more valuable due to red heart damage having no effect on Deal chances.

sections.heading: Unhelpful Items
sections.text:
• Blanket: Only grants a shield for the two boss fights on the final level. The shield does not activate for the regular boss waves on previous floors.

• Camo Undies: This item does almost nothing in Greed Mode, despite being able to be obtained from the Greed Mode Treasure Room.

• [Repentance] Due to its ability to destroy Shopkeepers, Camo Undies can net you some extra pennies or nickels from shops each floor. Its new effect in Repentance also nets you a risk-reward dynamic as long as you re-enter the arena. You risk by losing money but get rewarded by clearing the waves easier.

• Champion Belt:While it does provide a damage up, it also quadruples the chance for champion enemies to appear, while not being able to profit from any extra pickups dropping from champions.

• D12: Very few rocks to reroll, however, can be abused to force a hatch to the next floor.

• Eucharist: You're already guaranteed an Angel or Devil deal each floor, so all this does is ensures that it's an Angel Deal.

• Guppy's Eye: This item is substantially less useful in Greed Mode, due to the scarcity of chests.

• Guppy's Tail: This item has no effect in Greed Mode other than counting towards the Guppy Transformation.

• Holy Mantle: Only triggers once without leaving the room, however can still be useful to make use of curse rooms for free; As well as deactivating the wave button with no consequences.

• Monstro's Tooth: Only targets one enemy, virtually useless with the exception of cleaning up dead shopkeeper bodies.

• Mom's Bracelet: Very few rocks to throw.

• Mama Mega!: The explosion will only trigger once per room, making it effectively useless in Greed Mode after the first activation.

• The Mind: In Greed Mode, this item effectively becomes Blue Map. Other map-related items such as Treasure Map and The Compass are negated completely irrelevant.

• Pause: Using the item in Greed Mode will freeze all enemies but will not pause the timer. New waves of enemies will continue to spawn even while the effect is active.

• Soul of Cain: Will show red door outlines, but cannot generate normal red rooms, leaving only special rooms as a rare possibility. The red outlines can be used to find the Secret Room or leave the floor, however.

• Meat Cleaver: Virtually useless, especially considering how pretty much none of the champions drop any pickups.

• Dream Catcher Doesn't show the outcomes for the boss waves and is bugged in the way that it doesn't show the right items, making it useless outside of the half-soul heart it gives each floor.

• Deep Pockets: Doesn't actually increase the amount of money you gain, causing it to only be valuable if you had a way to generate absurd amounts of money, which you don't need Deep Pockets to do.

sections.heading: Neutral items
sections.text:
• Sulfuric Acid is both a blessing and a curse since it helps to always find secret rooms for free and destroy polyps; however it is bad for The Lost and Tainted Lost because they effectively can't hide inside rocks anymore.

• Both Head of the Keeper and Eye of Greed are very useful throughout the entire run but are a severe disadvantage during the final boss fight, as it gives Ultra Greed and Ultra Greedier a consistent way to heal themselves.

• Member Card offers more options for sale, however the items inside are still costly & indulging too much there may cause neglect of the base shop stuff.

• Magic Fingers and Golden Razor provide short-term helping hand at the cost of being less advantageous long-term.

• Money Power is a double-edged sword in the mode as it essentially forces the player to choose between buying shop items, or saving them for damage and the Greed Donation Machine.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• With the nature of the mode's arena being the place most of the time is being spent at – anything that only temporary boosts up the character for one room is significantly more useful during the lingering battlefield. Penny-Related trinkets are also very useful with the constant flood of money.

• Despite being possible to make, red rooms will only open if a generated one is a special one, or if you're on the final floor. Red Rooms on the last floor are mostly empty with no contents inside. Some red rooms on the final floor can be Curse rooms or Super Secret rooms with some pickups in them.

• The combat room before Ultra Greed boss fight doesn't grant active item charges.

• Greed Mode is the only place in the game where Match Book doesn't drop Match Stick.

• Using Glowing Hourglass at the start of the run sends Isaac into the I AM ERROR room.

• "Telepills" is unobtainable in Greed Mode.

• [Repentance+] The "Amnesia" and "???" pills are also unobtainable in Greed Mode.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Shop and Ultra Greed are [Before Repentance] two of only four/ [Repentance] the only floors to not have their own music track, as they share a song with both each other and Shops.

• [Before Repentance] The others are Womb and Utero, which share a song with each other.

• [Repentance] Utero now has its own unique music.

• Ultra Greed's theme, named “Chorus Mortis”, is a remix of the main menu theme.

• The doodles that pop-up at the start of a run are always greed-themed in this gamemode.

• Isaac doesn't have the animation of jumping inside a golden chest in the end, possibly drawing a parallel with the ending in which he gets stuck inside a cave, drying up and becoming Greed. The updated Greedier ending also shows many spiders from Isaac's body flooding up everything - drawing possible symbolism of Isaac becoming rotten to the core.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If the Super Secret Room is generated behind the locked (golden) Treasure Room, it is possible to get stuck by teleporting into before unlocking the Treasure Room. The Treasure Room doors all become unlocked when one of them is, unlike the normal game mode where a Treasure Room may have only one locked door, which results in the bombable wall between the Super Secret Room and the Treasure Room also being "locked". It cannot be bombed or opened with a key from inside the Super Secret Room, and unless another means of teleporting is available, the run is softlocked.
Bug note: The music played in chapters 1-4 have the wrong music. The music played will always be of the 2nd alt floor version of the current floor. For example, Burning Basement's track will play on Basement, and Flooded Caves's track will play on Caves.
Bug note: Using Genesis forces you down a new "Ultra Greed" floor instead of the starting room, even if the final boss is already killed.
Bug note: Dream Catcher shows the wrong items in Greed mode.
Bug note: Non-boss enemies spawned in waves will never be champions. Enemies spawned by other means (e.g. those present in the Exit room) may still be champions.
Bug note: All Bony enemies spawned by Polished Bone will be champions.

Growth Hormones.title: Growth Hormones
Growth Hormones.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:

• [Before Repentance] +0.4 speed.

sections.text: • Growth hormones are used to stimulate growth, cell reproduction, and cell regeneration. People often abuse growth hormone drugs in competitions to get physically stronger.

Grub.title: Grub
Grub.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
A Grub is a type of monster that appear infrequently in Caves and beyond. They are similar in appearance to Larry Jr. and can spawn alongside Larry Jr. or The Hollow in their respective boss rooms.

Grubs move around the room somewhat randomly until they line up with Isaac, after which they rapidly charge towards Isaac, similar to a Charger. Upon death, each of the Grub's segments will spawn a Maggot, Charger, or Spitty. Unlike Larry Jr. which requires each of its segments to be destroyed, as soon as one Grub segment is destroyed, the entire enemy will be destroyed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] Prior to Booster Pack #5, if a Grub spawned in the Flooded Caves, it had a high chance to spawn Drowned Chargers instead of Chargers. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Because of its similar movement behavior and design to that of Larry Jr. (along with the fact that Grubs can spawn in a Larry Jr. boss room), Grubs are also known as "Larry Sr." by The Binding of Isaac community.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Attempting to capture a Grub with Friendly Ball will only capture one segment of the Grub.

fields.behavior: Erratically moves around the room like Larry Jr. and charges at Isaac when he gets within its line of sight. Spawns Maggots, Chargers, or Spitty upon death, one for each of its segments.

Guardian Angel.title: Guardian Angel
Guardian Angel.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns an orbital familiar that blocks enemy shots and deals 7 damage per tick on contact.

• [Before Repentance] This deals 105 damage per second.

• [Repentance] This deals 52.5 damage per second.

• Increases the speed that all orbital familiars rotate around Isaac at.

• Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The following types of flies are instantly killed when they come in contact with the familiar:

• Army Fly

• Attack Fly

• Dart Fly

• Fly

• Hush Fly

• Moter

• Pooter

• Ring Fly

• Super Pooter

• Swarm

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Sacrificial Altar: This familiar will also reward 2 Black Hearts when sacrificed.

• Spin to Win: The two orbital speed boosts stack.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Big Fan: Overrides Guardian Angel's speed boost. If Guardian Angel was obtained first, it will retain its own increased speed. If Big Fan was obtained first, Guardian Angel will be slower.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • A guardian angel is a type of angel that is assigned to guide or protect a particular person/group.

fields.description: Spawns an orbital familiar that blocks enemy shots, deals 7 damage per tick on contact, and increases the speed of all orbital familiars.

Guillotine.title: Guillotine
Guillotine.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac's head becomes an orbital familiar that blocks shots and deals contact damage. Tears are still fired from the rotating head.

• +1 damage.

• [Before Repentance] [tear delay down: 1] 

• [Repentance] +0.5 fire rate.

• The head orbital deals 7 damage per tick or [edition alternatives: baseline: 105; Repentance: 56] damage per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Isaac's body will spew a fountain of blood like a Gusher. This is purely cosmetic.

• While Isaac's actual hitbox (his body) does not change, the position of the head can obscure the body's exact position, making things such as dodging or collecting pickups more difficult.

• Items that apply contact damage and effects (The Virus, Aries, etc.) do not apply to the head.

• The head orbital ignores the normal three orbital cap used by items such as Cube of Meat and Sacrificial Dagger.

• The orbital is larger than most other orbitals, making it easier to use both offensively and defensively.

• Despite changing size with Isaac, the orbital's hitbox does not change, which can be deceptive.

• Standing near a wall may cause the head to go inside the wall while rotating, blocking tears.

• [Repentance+] Guillotine's quality is treated as 1 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Although the head doesn't increase in size, doubles the contact damage.

• Big Fan: Slows down the head orbital.

• Diplopia: Additional copies provide the stat increase as well as an orbital head familiar that doesn't fire.

• Guardian Angel: Does not increase the head's rotation speed.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
Overrides Guillotine's firing pattern:

• Berserk!

• C Section

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Forgotten

• Mom's Knife

• Spirit Sword

• [Repentance] Tainted Forgotten

• [Repentance] Tainted Lilith

• Tractor Beam: The beam appears to move with the head, but tears are fired from the body.

Other interactions:

• Box of Friends / The Twins: Adds another rotating head, but only the original head will fire tears.

• Guillotine: Each additional copy adds another orbital and increases stats, but only the original head will fire tears.

• Duct Tape: Causes tears to be fired from far below and to the right of Isaac. This causes tears to be out of bounds unless Isaac is standing in the top-left corner of the room.

• Duct Tape: Tears are fired from whatever position the head is stuck in.

• The Pinking Shears / Transcendence: Removes Isaac's body aside from a small shadow. This can make Isaac's position more confusing.

• Sacrificial Altar: The head orbital cannot be sacrificed.

• Scissors: The head created by Scissors fires tears, while the head created by Guillotine only acts as an orbital.

• Spin to Win: Affects the head, which boosts its damage and defense properties but makes shots harder to hit.

• Tiny Planet: Tears fire from the head and orbit around the body.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • A guillotine is an execution device that kills by severing its victim's head. It gained notoriety during the French Revolution where it was used to kill 17,000 people during the period known as the "Reign of Terror."

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: An out-of-body experience; Repentance: DMG + tears up. An out-of-body experience!]
fields.description: Isaac's head becomes an orbital familiar that blocks shots and deals contact damage. Tears are still fired from the rotating head. [Before Repentance] +1 damage, -1 tear delay. [Repentance] +1 damage, +0.5 fire rate.

Guppy.title: Guppy
Guppy.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Guppy is a transformation, turning Isaac into his cat Guppy after picking up 3 Guppy-related items.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants flight.

• [Before Repentance] Spawns a Blue Fly each time a tear from Isaac or one of its familiars hits an enemy.

• [Repentance] Grants a 66% chance to spawn a Blue Fly each time a tear from Isaac or one of its familiars hits an enemy.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.text: Pick up 3 items or trinkets from the following list ( [Repentance] with the [code: guppy] tag).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Technology 2 spawns flies only very rarely.

• [edition na+r] If Isaac has transformed into Guppy, Guppy's Hairball spawns Blue Flies when it deals damage.

• [Repentance] If all the 9 extra lives have been consumed, Dead Cat is removed from Isaac's inventory. This causes the transformation to be removed.

• [Repentance] Blue flies will only spawn if Isaac has less than 30 blue flies.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Guppy's Hairball, Cat Got Your Tongue]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This transformation is a reference to Edmund's first cat, as seen in some of his early videos on his personal channel.

• Guppy the cat passed away in 2014.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Transforming into Guppy as The Forgotten will give him the appearance of a cat's skeleton.

• [Repentance] The guppy item tag determines if an item counts towards the transformation, except for Kid's Drawing which seems to be hard-coded to count as a Guppy item despite not having the tag.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Grants flight and spawns a Blue Fly each time a tear hits an enemy.
[Repentance] Grants flight and adds a 66% chance to spawn a Blue Fly when a tear hits an enemy.
fields.items: Dead Cat, Guppy's Collar, Guppy's Tail, Guppy's Hairball, Guppy's Eye, Guppy's Head, Guppy's Paw

Guppy's Collar.title: Guppy's Collar
Guppy's Collar.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a permanent 50% chance to resurrect on death.

• Resurrection leaves Isaac at half of a Red Heart, or half a Soul Heart if he had no Red Heart Containers.

• Contributes to the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Resurrection items activate in a set order. Guppy's Collar is [edition alternatives: baseline: 4th; Repentance: 6th] in this order after Soul of Lazarus, 1up!, [edition alternatives: baseline: Dead Cat, Lazarus' inherent extra life; Repentance: Lazarus' inherent extra life, Dead Cat] , and Inner Child.

• It is possible to obtain two collars by finding one in a Red Chest, without picking it up, and then finding another collar in a different Red Chest. [Before Repentance] However, this does not have any additional effects and does not count towards transforming into Guppy.

• [Repentance] Obtaining multiple copies of Guppy's Collar now grants extra lives, depending on how many copies are obtained (obtaining a second collar displays the lives count as '2?', and so on). The chance for Guppy's Collar to activate is defined with separate rolls, but increases the odds for one of the collars to revive Isaac. Additional collars also count towards the Guppy transformation.

• Resurrecting in a Curse Room may trap Isaac if he has no way of recovering health or exiting them without losing health.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Resurrecting via Guppy's Collar during a Daily Challenge will count as a death, even if the run is eventually completed.

• [Repentance] While escaping Mother's Shadow, the HUD states the revive chance is 100% (the question mark is removed). However, since all Isaac's items are removed in the area, the revive will not happen.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a tribute to Edmund McMillen's cat Guppy.

• This item may also be a reference to the Schrödinger's Cat thought experiment.

• With this item, at any given point, Isaac will on average be resurrected once more (before he is killed). This is not dependent on how many times he has been resurrected already, a property known as memorylessness.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: When the Keeper is resurrected by Guppy's Collar, there is a chance he spawns with a Half Soul Heart instead of Coin Hearts. When an HP up is obtained, Keeper will have 1 Coin Heart, as well as the Half Soul Heart he had previously. When a second HP up is obtained, Keeper will lose the Half Soul Heart and have 2 Coin Hearts, like normal.
Bug note: Guppy's Collar can be exploited to gain infinite lives. When Isaac's last will is on the screen, close the game, re-open it, and continue the run. Isaac will appear to die again, and will also have a separate chance to be resurrected.

fields.description: Grants a permanent 50% chance to respawn with 1/2 of a Red Heart after death.

Guppy's Eye.title: Guppy's Eye
Guppy's Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Shows the contents of Chests, Fire Places, Grab Bags, and Shopkeepers before they're opened/destroyed.

• Contributes to the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Guppy's Eye does not show the contents of tinted rocks, Poops, and other obstacles.

• Guppy's Eye does display enemies that can be contained within chests.

• Chests and Grab Bags can only display up to four pickups at a time. If there are more than four, higher-value pickups like Bombs, Keys, and Soul Hearts will have priority on the display.

• If a Red Chest looks like it doesn't have anything in it, it will teleport Isaac to the floor's Devil Room / Angel Room.

• Due to how Trinkets generate, if a Chest displays a trinket, all future Chests will also display/give that trinket until it spawns in some way, at which point all Chests will display a new trinket.

• This means it is worthwhile opening even chests containing undesirable trinkets so that the trinket cycle advances.

• Mimic Chests will change their contents whenever their spikes pop out. The unchanged drops can still be obtained by:

• Opening them with Flat File or Magneto.

• Using swing attacks (such as The Forgotten, Notched Axe, Spirit Sword, etc.)

• This effect works on all non-ending chests, including Mom's Chest.

• This item is substantially less useful in Greed Mode, due to the scarcity of chests.

• The contents of Sacks or Chests that haven't spawned yet will still be revealed (for example, in rooms that spawn such Chests or Sacks when Isaac pressed a hidden switch, etc.).

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• D1: When duplicating a chest with D1, the original's contents will be changed. Guppy's Eye will not immediately show the new contents, but leaving the room and returning will reveal the changes. This essentially allows rerolling the rewards within them, especially useful in Chest and Dark Room.

• [Repentance+] The contents are immediately updated upon reroll.

• Poker Chip: Guppy's Eye will show which chests contain an Attack Fly. This allows Isaac to drop the Trinket, leave the room, and return to reset the chest's contents.

• Sack Head: Sack Head rerolls pickups into Grab Bags after they are spawned, making Guppy's Eye less effective on non-Grab Bag contents.

• Guppy's Eye: Picking up a second copy of the item gives Isaac a unique costume with both eyes replaced. This is purely cosmetic, and it will otherwise have no effect.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Parasite]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Guppy's Eye is one of the few items that will give Isaac a unique costume when two copies are acquired, along with Brimstone and Glass Eye.

• This item was suggested on a Reddit post on the Binding of Isaac Subreddit.

• This item originates from the card game The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls. In it, Guppy's Eye forces all other players to play with their hands face-up on the table.

• Its pickup text is possibly a reference to the description of the Rasmus mask from Hotline Miami.

fields.description: Shows the contents of Chests, Fire Places, Grab Bags, and Shopkeepers before they're opened/destroyed.

Guppy's Hairball.title: Guppy's Hairball
Guppy's Hairball.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a hairball familiar that loosely follows behind Isaac, blocks shots, and can be swung like a flail to damage enemies.

• The ball deals 5 damage per tick, but grows, increasing damage by 2 each time it kills an enemy — up to 4 times for a maximum of 13 damage. The damage it deals per tick (each half-second) is (level × 2) + 3.

• The hairball level decreases upon entering a new floor: if level 2, it reverts to level 1. If level 3 or 4, it reverts to level 2. If level 5, it reverts to level 3.

• Contributes to the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The hairball's hitbox is the same size regardless of level.

• [edition na+r] If Isaac has transformed into Guppy, Guppy's Hairball spawns Blue Flies when it deals damage.

• If Blindfolded, the ball occasionally spawns a Blue Fly while it's damaging an enemy.

• [Repentance] The hairball will be reset to level 1 after entering and leaving the Mother's Shadow escape sequence.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Cat Got Your Tongue.

• The function and flavor text of this item might reference the idioms "no room to swing a cat" and "can't swing a dead cat without hitting...".

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Guppy's Hairball did not count towards the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Killing the Hush Flies that Hush spawns does not increase the hairball's level.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that loosely follows behind Isaac, which blocks shots and can be swung like a flail to damage enemies. Grows bigger by killing enemies.

Guppy's Head.title: Guppy's Head
Guppy's Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns 2-4 friendly Blue Flies.

• Contributes to the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Summons wisps in the outer ring instead of flies. Wisps summon Blue Flies when destroyed. One wisp contains one Blue Fly.

• Car Battery: Increases range of flies spawned to 4-8.

• Fish Tail: Doubles flies spawned.

• 9 Volt: Guppy's Head slowly gains charge while in a hostile room.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Cat Got Your Tongue.

• The item is a reference to Edmund McMillen's cat also named Guppy.

• Box of Spiders is essentially the spider equivalent to Guppy's Head.

fields.description: Spawns 2-4 friendly Blue Flies that damage enemies.

Guppy's Paw.title: Guppy's Paw
Guppy's Paw.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, converts one Red Heart Container into three Soul Hearts.

• Contributes to the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Bone Hearts cannot be converted.

• [Repentance+] Guppy's Paw's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Grants a permanent 0.5 damage up for every converted heart.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns 3 wisps in the middle ring for every Red Heart Container consumed, in addition to granting Soul Hearts. These wisps have a large amount of health.

• Broken Remote: The teleport will activate whenever Guppy's Paw is used, even if Isaac has no Red Heart Containers to trade. This can give any characters with no Red Hearts the ability to teleport any number of times for free.

• Converter:

• [Before Repentance] Allows Isaac to attain up to 10 Red Heart Containers and 1 Soul Heart.

• [Repentance] Allows Isaac to attain up to 12 Red Heart Containers or any combination of Red Heart Containers and Soul Hearts.

• • + Potato Peeler + Sharp Plug: Allows Isaac to generate infinite damage upgrades and Cube of Meat.

• Tainted Eden: Soul Hearts granted by Guppy's Paw are not rerolled when Tainted Eden takes damage.

• Dead Cat: In addition to contributing to the transformation, converting the Red Heart Container obtained after revival into three Soul Hearts effectively triples Isaac's HP.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bethany: Guppy's Paw will remove one Heart Container in exchange for Soul Heart charges. This will kill Bethany if she has no health left afterward.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Keeper: Guppy's Paw will take away one Coin Heart, but will only grant Blue Flies in return.

• XI - Strength: Converts the temporary Red Heart Container into three Soul Hearts (however, Isaac will still lose one Red Heart Container upon leaving the room if he has any left).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is the first (by item ID) to appear in The Binding of Isaac: Wrath of the Lamb DLC. The last one is Box.

• It is also a reference to Edmund McMillen's cat Guppy.

• [Repentance] This item is used in Baptism by Fire. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If Keeper uses Guppy's Paw to remove all his Coin Hearts, he will not die until he picks up an item.

fields.description: Converts one Red Heart Container into three Soul Hearts.

Guppy's Tail.title: Guppy's Tail
Guppy's Tail.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a 1/3 chance of replacing Room Clear Awards with a Chest or a Locked Chest, but also a 2/9 chance to replace it with nothing at all.

• Contributes to the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The drawback to this item is that Keys become much more scarce, while increasing the amount of Locked Chests. This makes taking Guppy's Tail a potential liability early on.

• Due to any found Chests containing items while in Chest or Dark Room, Guppy's Tail can be a good way to quickly stack up more upgrades before facing the final boss.

• [Afterbirth onward] The effect does not apply to Penny dropped in Greed Mode, meaning that this item has no effect in Greed Mode other than counting towards the Guppy Transformation.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Deep Pockets: If Guppy's Tail removes the room clear drop, it is turned into coins instead.

• Guppy's Eye: Makes Key management easier by revealing which Locked Chests are worth opening and which are not.

• The Left Hand: Turns all chests into Red Chests, allowing Isaac to get Red Chest items much more quickly. Useful when pursuing the Guppy transformation.

• Mom's Key: Increases the number of drops from Chests and counteracts the increased chance to run into Locked Chests.

• Options?: Chests may be accompanied by normal room drops or other chests of a type that's easier to open, mitigating the downsides.

• Paper Clip: The Key scarcity problem is completely prevented, since Paper Clip causes Locked Chests to be openable without Keys, making Guppy's Tail's only downside the chance to replace room clears with nothing at all.

• [Afterbirth onward] If Cain starts with the Trinket, entering Curse Rooms and opening Red Chests in hopes of finding Guppy's Tail early is a very effective strategy.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Cat Got Your Tongue.

• The item Dead Cat has Guppy's tail be completely black while Guppy's Tail has a white fur on the tip of the tail.

• In the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original game, this item had to be unlocked by beating a challenge titled "9 Deaths".

fields.description: Room Clear Awards have a 1/3 chance of being replaced with a Chest and a 2/9 chance being replaced with nothing.

Gurdy.title: Gurdy
Gurdy.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Gurdy is a boss that can appear in the Caves and the Flooded Caves.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Gurdy is completely stationary and will always appear in the upper middle of the room. She has three attacks:

• Ducks down into her body and emerges from the middle facing Isaac, firing 5 projectiles in a spread.

• She can do this below her and to her sides and will not perform this attack if Isaac is behind her.

• Spawns a Pooter near herself.

• Spawns two Attack Fly behind her.

• Spawned Attack Flies are weaker than normal, with only about 3 health and can be killed if Isaac walks into them, though they will still deal contact damage before dying.

• Summons two Boils in front of her.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 5] : 11% larger and does not use her projectile attack. Instead, she summons monsters at a faster rate.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Upon entering a room with Gurdy in it, the player will usually be teleported to the bottom center of the room regardless of which side the player entered from.

• This teleporting effect occurs when Gurdy spawns in a Boss Challenge Room as well.

• Gurdy will sometimes be accompanied by Attack Flies to the left and right of her and two Boils in the bottom corners of the room. She might also be accompanied by three Boils behind her.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gurdy appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• Gurdy was originally supposed to be a pile of dead children, but it looked too confusing, so Edmund McMillen made her body made of guts instead.

• Gurdy's name is supposedly derived from a medical condition called G.E.R.D. (gastroesophageal reflux disease), more commonly known as acid reflux.

• Gurdy appears to be the third stage of the "Gurdy" boss line, with the first stage as Gurglings, second as Gurdy Jr., and final as Mama Gurdy.

• Gurdy shares her name with a level from Edmund's previous game Super Meat Boy.

• Gurdy is female.

• [Repentance] Gurdy will perform a taunting laugh animation if Isaac takes damage.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Using A Card Against Humanity will cause Gurdy to appear to teleport onto the player. This is purely a cosmetic effect and clearing the poop from the center of the room will cause her to return to normal.
