Tiny Planet.title: Tiny Planet
Tiny Planet.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] +7 tear falling speed.

• [Repentance] +6.5 range.

• Grants spectral tears.

• Tears now revolve around Isaac at a fixed distance until they hit the ground.

• [Repentance] The tears orbit close to Isaac, offset slightly in the direction fired. Changing the firing direction will redirect all previously fired tears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tears will not hit directly in front of Isaac; aiming directly away from enemies is often effective.

• [Repentance] It is possible to control the direction of Tiny Planet with the mouse. On Windows, go to [code: C:/Users/[username]/Documents/My Games/The Binding Of Isaac [Rebirth/Afterbirth/Afterbirth+]/] and in the options.ini file, change the line that says [code: MouseControl0] to [code: MouseControl1] . Unlike normal controls, the mouse allows diagonal direction.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20: Each shot fires two tears in opposing orbital directions.

• This synergy is effectively the same for The Wiz, with the exception of 20/20's damage penalty not being applied.

• Anti-Gravity: Tears orbit around Isaac at a short range while fire button is held. When the fire button is released, tears snap to their normal range.

• Azazel: Increases Azazel's range with Brimstone, and wraps the beam around the character.

• Brain Worm: Tears will home directly towards nearby enemies in a line from the center of the orbit.

• Brimstone: The beam will wrap around the character and shoot straight forward.

• Brimstone + Mom's Knife: The knives shot after the Brimstone beam similarly wrap around the character and shoot forward.

• Cricket's Body: Tears will split into 2 close groups of 2 tears that follow the orbit. One group travels clockwise and the other travels counterclockwise.

• Euthanasia: Euthanasia's tear bursts will follow the orbit in 2 close groups of 5 tears. One group travels clockwise and the other travels counterclockwise.

• Eye of Belial: After piercing an enemy, instead of homing in on enemies, tears will continue to orbit, but each tear can pierce multiple enemies to gain more size and damage multipliers.

• Eye of the Occult: Tears struggle to move outside of the pre-set path Tiny Planet gives.

• Flat Stone: Tears will bounce and orbit around the character.

• Godhead: Tears with damaging auras orbit the character, creating a damaging barrier.

• Ipecac: Explosive tears orbit around Isaac. Host Hat or Pyromaniac is highly recommended.

• Kidney Stone: The stone and barrage of tears that follow orbit the character.

• Lachryphagy: [Before Repentance] Tears will orbit until they are behind the character. Tears will burst into 8 tears that follow the orbit in 2 close groups of 4. One group travels clockwise and the other travels counterclockwise.

• [Repentance] Tears orbit the player without slowing down, and can be fed as normal. When a tear bursts, the created tears orbit the place of burst.

• Loki's Horns: Effectively grants a great tear multiplier, as the extra tears from Loki's Horns will follow the trajectory given by the Tiny Planet.

• Lost Contact: Shielded tears will orbit Isaac, granting a partially successful 360-degree projectile protection around him. Works better with a faster fire rate or Anti-Gravity.

• A Lump of Coal: This item drastically increases the screen time of tears because it makes them orbit around Isaac for a few seconds. A Lump Of Coal adds a lot of damage to tears in "outer orbit".

• The tears do not fall during The Beast fight, allowing tears to grow bigger and bigger.

• Marked: Isaac will continuously fire orbiting tears, which allows him to not touch the attack keys and focus just on moving (with giant tears it makes it hard to see as he can't stop firing).

• [Repentance] Mom's Knife: Increases range. Causes Mom's knife to orbit around Isaac at very high speeds until it reaching it's maximum range, where it will circle back to Isaac at the same speed.

• [Repentance] My Reflection: After reaching their maximum range, the tears will circle back around to Isaac.

• Revelation: The beam of light wraps around Isaac and shoots forward at a slight angle, similar to Brimstone.

• Rubber Cement: Tears bounce off enemies then keep orbiting Isaac. Very powerful as the tears are not destroyed upon damaging an enemy. When near walls, the orbiting tears tend to get stuck against the walls until Isaac moves away.

• Spirit Sword: The sword's melee attack becomes disjointed from Isaac, hitting in an increased range in front of him but creating a blind spot where the strike used to be. Spin attacks also occur in front of Isaac instead of around him. Sword projectiles orbit around Isaac as normal.

• Tainted Eve: Blood clot familiars will each fire tears in their own individual orbits, rather than all orbiting around the character.

• Tainted Lilith: Tears orbit around the Gello instead of the character.

• Technology: A laser creates a circle around Isaac's body before being fired forward normally. The laser becomes spectral.

• [Afterbirth onward] Technology + A Lump of Coal: The extra distance covered by the laser more than doubles damage right in front of Isaac, and it increases as normal further away.

• Technology Zero: Creates moving laser fields that orbit the character.

• Varicose Veins: The ten tears that are fired when the character is hit orbit them closely.

• Tear Detonator: Makes the additional tears go around in a pattern around the location where Isaac used the Tear Detonator, making it much easier to hit enemies with it.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bob's Rotten Head: The thrown bomb orbits around Isaac, making it hard to predict where it will land.

• C Section: Fetuses will rotate around Isaac, but still home in on enemies.

• Dr. Fetus: The bombs orbit Isaac, exploding just barely far enough to cause no damage assuming he stays motionless.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Tiny Planet.

• Haemolacria: Fired tears orbit around Isaac, but burst tears do not.

• Hook Worm: Has no effect.

• The Ludovico Technique: Tear orbits around Isaac, however, the orbit can be grown or shrunken, sped up or slowed down by using the firing keys.

• [Before Repentance] Monstro's Lung: This item removes the extra tear falling speed bonus, causing the burst of tears to circle and land behind the player after only being airborne for a short time.

• [Repentance] Range isn't as significantly reduced.

• My Reflection: Tears will move to maintain their orbital positions around Isaac as he moves, making aiming much easier.

• The Parasite: Tears only split when hitting objects and enemies.

• A Lump of Coal: Tears glitch out when splitting, remaining for absurdly long times and turning the area around Isaac into an instant-death zone.

• Pop!: Tears tend to clump together behind the character and then disappear after a few seconds.

• Proptosis: At base damage, tears disappear after half an orbit.

• Ring Worm: Every single tear spins uncontrollably fast, making aiming incredibly difficult. However, with large shots (Death's Touch with high damage, for instance) this combo can fill the entire screen with projectiles almost immediately.

• Sprinkler: Tears made by Sprinkler will follow Isaac

• Tech X: Overrides Tiny Planet.

• Tractor Beam: Overrides Tiny Planet but keeps the large range increase.

• Tractor Beam + Rubber Cement: Tears will travel along the beam until they hit a wall and then orbit Isaac.

• Tractor Beam + Dr. Fetus: Tractor Beam is ignored and plain Dr. Fetus interaction applies.

• Tractor Beam + Haemolacria: Tractor Beam overrides Tiny Planet and Haemolacria Tears no longer arc.

• Wiggle Worm: The tear forcefully orbits while spiraling. The orbit amplifies the wiggle.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Tiny Planet was pitched as a cosmetic item in Team Fortress 2, alongside Skatole, tears, and Brimstone. Only Brimstone made the cut.

• This item is used in Head Trauma.

• The item is likely a reference to asteroids, or possibly dwarf planets.

fields.description: Massively increases Range and grants spectral tears. Tears orbit around Isaac at a fixed distance until they hit the ground.

Tinytoma.title: Tinytoma
Tinytoma.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a large orbital similar to Teratoma that slowly orbits Isaac.

• The orbital repels enemies that touch it and deals 3.5 contact damage to enemies, once per second.

• After blocking 3 shots and/or dealing 3 ticks of contact damage, the orbital splits into two smaller ones that orbit opposite of each other. They behave the same as the original, except they are smaller and can only take 2 hits before being destroyed, bursting into 3 blue spiders in the process.

• 5 seconds after both orbitals are destroyed, the original, full-size orbital respawns.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Teratoma. [end edition note] 

• If there is a spiked rock in the room, Isaac can destroy Tinytoma with them to spawn lots of blue spiders, as Tinytoma will respawn after being destroyed.

• This can be done until the maximum of 64 blue spiders/flies is reached.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Tinytoma is from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, destroying Polyps on the Corpse floor had a chance to drop Tinytoma and could even drop the item before it was unlocked.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again) will duplicate any smaller orbitals of Tinytoma currently orbiting Isaac.

fields.description: Gives Isaac a Teratoma orbital that blocks shots, deals contact damage, and splits into smaller versions of itself upon taking damage. The smaller versions break into blue spiders.

Tonsil.title: Tonsil
Tonsil.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• After taking [Before Repentance+] 12-20 / [Repentance+] 6-12 hits a removed tonsil familiar starts following Isaac, blocking enemy shots.

• The effect can happen twice, after which the trinket will be destroyed.

• The familiar does not deal damage to enemies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• When the familiar is generated, Isaac will gain the familiar permanently as a passive item. This allows Isaac to drop the trinket while keeping the familiar.

• [Before Repentance] The passive Tonsil item does not exist in any item pool; thus, this is the only way to find it and make it appear in the Collection Page aside from starting with it as Eden.

• • [Before Repentance] If Eden starts with the passive tonsil item and picks up the trinket, the trinket will spawn only one familiar before being consumed.

• [Repentance] The passive item form of Tonsil no longer exists; its ID has been taken by Broken Glass Cannon and no longer appears in the Collection Page, nor can it be obtained by Eden as a starting item. [end edition note] 

• Sources of self-inflicted damage, like IV Bag or Blood Donation Machines, can spawn a familiar.

• Damage that is blocked by Holy Mantle or the Holy Card does not count to the number of hits that are needed for the tonsil familiar to spawn.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Tonsil having the lowest priority at 6th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • [Repentance+] Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either can generate a 3rd tonsil before destroying the trinket. Having both can generate a 4th tonsil before destroying it.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • D4: If a passive Tonsil item is given, this item can't be rerolled by the D4 or other items that reroll passive items.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Tonsils are soft tissue located near the back of the throat which, in the event of inflammation to the point of obstructing the throat, can be removed without much noticeable difference.

• [Repentance] The passive item form of Tonsil is technically the only item to be removed from the game.

• Broken Glass Cannon has the same ID that the passive item form of Tonsil used to have. [end edition note]

fields.description: When hit, there is a small chance to spawn a permanent tonsil familiar that blocks enemy shots. This can happen twice, after which the trinket is destroyed.
Grants a familiar that follows Isaac and blocks enemy shots.

Tooth Picks.title: Tooth Picks
Tooth Picks.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.7 tears.

• +0.16 shot speed.

• Tear color becomes red.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Is functionally identical to Torn Photo.

fields.description: +0.7 tears, +0.16 shot speed.

Tooth and Nail.title: Tooth and Nail
Tooth and Nail.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Every 6 seconds, Isaac turns to stone and sprouts spikes for 1 second. While Isaac is in this state, he is immune to damage and deals 40 contact damage.

• Isaac flashes white three times before turning to stone on the fourth flash. The first three flashes are accompanied by a "ticking" sound, the final one with the spike extension sound of a mimic chest.

• Unlike Gnawed Leaf, Isaac can still move and shoot tears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Tuff Twins. [end edition note] 

• Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars will still deal damage while Tooth and Nail is active.

• With proper timing, Curse Rooms can be both entered and exited without taking damage.

• When invincible, Spiked Chests/Mimic Chests can be opened without taking damage.

• When under the effects of the Paralysis pill Isaac cannot change into a statue.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Contact damage items work great with Tooth and Nail, such as Aries / Mom's Heels / The Virus for extra damage, Serpent's Kiss for Black Heart generation, Midas' Touch for coin generation etc.

• Midas' Touch also makes the stone turn a yellowish golden while active. Purely visual, but can help remind the player that they have both items.

• Damocles: As Isaac is invincible 1/6th of the time, with some luck, Tooth and Nail may save him from the falling sword.

• Kamikaze!: Allows usage without taking damage during invincibility.

• The Lost can use this item to prevent additional damage from occurring after losing the Holy Mantle (for example, exiting a Curse Room after being hit), and it does not use up the Holy Mantle's 1-hit protection if it has not been lost.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Tooth and Nail is lost while in the statue form (e.g. through losing its Lemegeton wisp), Isaac will indefinitely remain in the statue form until he leaves the room.
Bug note: Using an active item with no cooldown repeatedly (Mom's Bracelet, Bag of Crafting, etc.) whilst in an invulnerable state will keep Isaac in that state.

fields.description: Isaac periodically turns into a spiked statue, briefly becoming invulnerable and dealing contact damage.

Torn Card.title: Torn Card
Torn Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Fragmented Card]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Every 15 shots, Isaac will shoot an Ipecac + My Reflection tear with a very high range value.

• The tear will follow Isaac until it hits an enemy or lands, where it will explode.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy reduces the number of shots required to shoot an ipecac tear by 5, with a minimum of 5 shots in between.

• Pyromaniac: Completely negates the downside of Torn Card and will heal you if the shot misses an enemy or wall and hits you instead.

• Host Hat: Completely negates the downside of Torn Card.

• Almond Milk / Soy Milk / Chocolate Milk: Unlike the normal Ipecac synergy, Torn Card shots ignore the damage down multiplier, always dealing +40 damage, significantly increasing DPS.

• Brain Worm: Brain Worm forces some tears to snap 90 degrees to target enemies that they may have missed.

• Death's Touch / Pupula Duplex: Ipecac shots get a bigger hitbox, making shots easier to hit, and from a safer distance.

• Eye of the Occult: Tear control is stronger than the reflection, although it's still present if Isaac stops shooting. Effectively negates downside.

• Fire Mind: A fire is always spawned at the place of explosion.

• Homing: The homing is stronger than the reflection, effectively negating Torn Card's downside.

• Hook Worm: Hook Worm allows tears to hit enemies more easily, while also making them easier to avoid.

• Lead Pencil: Lowers tear shot requirement by 1. Lead Pencil will always proc at the 14th shot, soon followed by Torn Card's at 15th.

• Monstro's Lung: An Ipecac shot is fired for 4 bursts consecutively, with the 5th burst lacking one, and repeat. Makes Torn Card very consistent.

• Proptosis: Ipecac tear will always explode before reflection takes effect. It's the only item that affects Torn Card's flat 40 damage.

• Spirit Sword: Swings can be spammed rapidly to create Ipecac shots.

• Tiny Planet: Ipecac shots will stick to the orbit and direction Isaac is aiming.

• Whip Worm: Increased shot speed boosts accuracy and the tear is more likely to hit walls if the enemy is missed.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 20/20 / Eye Sore / The Inner Eye / Immaculate Heart / Loki's Horns / Mom's Eye / Mutant Spider / The Wiz: Extra tears fired do not count towards Torn Card proccing.

• Anti-Gravity: Ipecac shots will follow Isaac closely until he stops firing.

• Epic Fetus: Despite replacing tears, Torn Card will still calculate shots required based on Isaac's fire rate. These shots will be fired regardless if the missile crosshair is moving or not.

• Evil Eye: Tears shot by evil eyes cannot fire Ipecac shots, nor count towards proccing.

• Fate's Reward: Cannot proc Torn Card.

• Incubus / Twisted Pair / Lil Clot / Found Soul: Has its own shot counter, independent of Isaac's. Shots not affected by its damage multiplier, always dealing +40 damage. Shots fired from the Soul will reflect back on itself, rather than Isaac. The Twisted pairs fire an Ipecac shot at the same time.

• Lachryphagy: Ipecac shots become Lachryphagy shots, allowing them to grow. Reflection is weaker due to lower momentum. The burst tears spawned from the tear will all explode.

• Marked: Ipecac shots will be fired from cardinal directions rather than aiming at the crosshair.

• Second Hand: Does not lenghthen the poison effect.

sections.heading: Detrimental items
sections.text:
• Dr. Fetus: Ipecac shots will immediately explode on contact with the bombs, unless back pedaling.

• Flat Stone: Each bounce produces an explosion. As tear height lowers on return, the explosion frequency increases.

• The Ludovico Technique: Ipecac shots are fired even when not controlling the tear. Proc rate is based on fire rate, same as with Epic Fetus.

• The Parasite: Tears split on walls will all try to home in back to Isaac.

• Tractor Beam: Tears that did not hit any enemy or wall will reflect back to Isaac with ease, thanks to the beam. If the tear gets on top of Isaac, it's very hard getting rid of it, usually resulting in self-damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This trinket is a torn Suicide King card, and its tear effect is the same combination used in the Suicide King challenge (which unlocks said card).

• The Suicide King challenge uses Lazarus as the starting character, which is also referenced by it being one of the Tainted Lazarus unlocks.

fields.description: Every 15 shots, Isaac shoots an Ipecac + My Reflection tear.

Torn Photo.title: Torn Photo
Torn Photo.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.7 tears.

• +0.16 shot speed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item sprite appears to be a picture of Isaac and his mother torn where his father is assumed to be.

• The Torn Photo can also be seen in Ending 20.

fields.description: +0.7 tears, +0.16 shot speed.

Torn Pocket.title: Torn Pocket
Torn Pocket.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon taking damage, Isaac drops 2 random Pickups from his inventory (except Hearts, Pills, or Cards).

• Pickups of higher amounts have more chance to drop.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• All pickups are subjected to standard pickup spawn rules, which means that trinket's effect won't necessarily result in a net neutral.

• Coins dropped have a chance of being replaced with a Golden Penny, Lucky Penny, Nickel, Sticky Nickel or Dime.

• Bomb dropped have a chance of being replaced with Double Bomb, Golden Bomb, Troll Bomb or Mega Troll Bomb.

• • When a dropped bomb is replaced with a Troll/Megatroll bomb, the game will still subtract that bomb from the total bomb count.

• • Giga bombs, however, can't be dropped if Isaac has them, but their count will still be retained unless the bomb count reaches 0.

• Keys dropped have a chance of being replaced with Golden Keys or Charged Keys.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy makes Isaac drop 1 more pickup from his inventory.

• Penny Trinkets : This can be used to generate extra pickups as long as one has a coin.

• BOGO Bombs: Dropped bombs will be their doubled variants.

• Humbleing Bundle: All dropped pickups have a chance to be replaced with doubled variants.

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper: Grants a chance to drop coins upon taking damage, giving back the lost health.

• Scapular: Can be used to infinitely generate pickups when down to half a Heart by re-entering a room to regenerate a Soul Heart.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Nuh Uh!: Coins and Keys will be replaced with other pickups starting from Chapter 4.

• Tainted ???: Does not drop poop nuggets after taking damage.

fields.description: Upon taking damage, Isaac drops 2 random Pickups from among those he's currently holding. Pickups of higher amounts have more chance to drop.

Tough Love.title: Tough Love
Tough Love.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Adds a chance to shoot a tooth instead of a tear, which deals x3.2 Isaac's damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The chance to fire a tooth depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 10 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 100% at 9 luck.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Apple!: With 14 Luck, overrides Tough Love. With 13 Luck, Apple and Tough Love each have about an equal chance to trigger.

• Brimstone: Overridden by Brimstone.

• [Afterbirth onward] Occasionally fires Brimstone beam with damage multiplier of Tough Love.

• Cricket's Body / Compound Fracture: Teeth will split into smaller teeth.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs explode with the increased blast damage and radius of Mr. Mega.

• [Repentance] Adds a chance for the bombs to deal increased damage. See the page for the specific damage formula.

• Fire Mind: Adds a flaming effect to the teeth, [Before Repentance] but without the chance of exploding.

• Ipecac: Teeth explode with the increased blast damage of Mr. Mega.

• Mom's Knife: Overridden by Mom's Knife.

• [Repentance] : Both damage multipliers apply, combined damage multiplier is x6.4.

• Haemolacria: Tears will not appear as teeth but may still gain the damage multiplier.

• Jawbreaker: Activation rates are individually applied to each tear, effectively allowing for higher amounts of teeth. At 9 Luck, the trinket is no longer needed, as Tough Love will already guarantee that every shot is a tooth.

• The Ludovico Technique: Tear occasionally flicks to being a tooth, which deals 3.2x Isaac's tear damage, before immediately returning to being a normal tear. The frequency at which the tear very briefly transforms into a tooth increases with Luck, permanently becoming a tooth at 9 Luck.

• The Parasite: Split tears will not turn into teeth.

• Papa Fly/Pointy Rib/Linger Bean: Can benefit the damage multiplier. 

• Spirit Sword: Both the sword and projectiles can deal increased damage.

• Technology: Damage multiplier applies occasionally.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The x3.2 damage multiplier is likely a reference to the fact that full set of adult teeth amounts to 32 teeth in total.

fields.description: Adds a chance to shoot a tooth instead of a tear, which deals x3.2 Isaac's damage.

Toxic Shock.title: Toxic Shock
Toxic Shock.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Contagion]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon entering a room, creates a green fog effect and all enemies are poisoned.

• [edition nrr+] The poison ticks 2 times.

• [edition rnr+] The poison ticks 4 times on normal enemies and 2 times on bosses (likely a bug).

• Killing enemies leaves a small, short-lasting pool of green creep on the ground.

• The creep deals 1 damage per tick or 30 damage per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• High tear damage will cause this item to become very powerful for rooms with a lot of enemies, since they can die instantly and render the room harmless.

• Enemies which spawn after the first few seconds of each room are not affected by this item, e.g. Flies spawned from a Mulligan dying.

• Enemies that spawn with some form of invulnerability such as Hosts, Wizoobs, or Needles are not affected by this item.

• The poison effect only activates upon entering a room and not at the start of a wave. In Boss Rush and most of Greed mode, the item will not poison enemies.

• If Toxic Shock is picked up in the middle of a room with enemies, the mass poison will occur immediately.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Second Hand: Extends the poison duration, allowing it to tick 6 times on normal enemies and 4 times on bosses.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Toxic Shock: Doesn't stack

• Red Stew: High damage stat makes Toxic Shock clear most rooms instantly, making Red Stew's damage up last almost indefinitely.

• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups don't leave creep.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop don't leave creep.

• [edition rnr+] Freeze Effects: Enemies that are frozen don't leave creep.

• [Repentance+] Frozen enemies do leave creep.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Contagion is a recolor of its sprite.

• Toxic Shock is a rare, but extremely serious and deadly condition caused by Staphylococcus Aureus bacteria releasing toxins in the bloodstream.

fields.description: Upon entering a room, poisons all enemies, dealing double Isaac's tear damage. Killing enemies leaves a small, short-lasting pool of green creep on the ground.

Tractor Beam.title: Tractor Beam
Tractor Beam.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac emits a beam in the direction that his head is facing. Isaac's tears travel in the path of the beam. When Isaac moves or turns his head, tears that are mid-flight will remain within the beam.

• [Before Repentance] +0.5 Tears.

• [Repentance] +1.0 Fire Rate.

• [Before Repentance] +5.25 Range.

• [Repentance] +2.5 Range.

• +0.5 Tear Falling Speed.

• +0.16 Shot Speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item prevents tears from being fired at angles using momentum.

• Isaac does not automatically aim downwards after he stops firing with this item.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20/Bookworm/Conjoined/The Inner Eye/Keeper/Mutant Spider/Tainted Keeper/The Wiz: Every extra tear will follow the beam instead of having a spread, making it easier to hit enemies with the extra tears. Essentially increases damage per second.

• Compound Fracture: All split tears will follow the beam greatly increasing effective damage.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Bone tears will not burst into bone shards when fired at obstacles, however, bone tears will burst into bone shards when fired at enemies.

• [Repentance] Bone tears burst into bone shards when fired at obstacles.

• Cricket's Body/The Parasite: All split tears will follow the beam greatly increasing effective damage.

• Continuum: The tears will re-appear directly in front of Isaac and continue their flight path after going off screen.

• Guillotine: The beam will visually follow Isaac's head as it orbits, but tears will still stay centered relative to Isaac's body making his tears easier to aim.

• Lachryphagy: Tears can still be fed and will still burst. [Before Repentance] Burst tears will travel along the beam.

• Monstro's Lung: All tears are fired along the beam but at different heights.

• Ouroboros Worm: The altered patterns tears travel in is confined to the beam allowing Isaac to benefit from the stat bonus and spectral tears granted without losing accuracy.

• Pop!: Tears stick along the tractor beam even when they slow down and collide, capable of creating a dense line of shots.

• Rainbow Worm: The altered patterns tears travel in is confined to the beam allowing Isaac to benefit from the stat bonuses granted without losing accuracy.

• [Repentance] Many of the worm trinket effects it gives now grant spectral tears as well.

• Ring Worm: The altered pattern tears travel in is confined to the beam allowing Isaac to benefit from its stat bonus and spectral tears without losing accuracy.

• Rubber Cement / Super Ball: Tears will no longer be bound to the beam after bouncing off of something.

• Sinus Infection: Once the booger falls off the enemy, Isaac can loosely control it by moving and firing in different directions, and make it stick to another enemy.

• Tear copiers like Cain's Other Eye / Incubus / Sumptorium / Twisted Pair: Tears shot by these familiars will originate from Isaac, following the beam.

• Wiggle Worm: The altered pattern tears travel in is confined to the beam allowing Isaac to benefit from its stat bonus without losing accuracy.

• [Repentance] Wiggle Worm also grants spectral tears with little downside in accuracy.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Analog Stick: Tears cannot be fired diagonally; however, stat effects apply.

• [Repentance] Tractor Beam can be angled diagonally or in any direction using an analog stick or mouse controls.

• Anti-Gravity: Tears that are still hovering can be pushed in the direction Isaac is aiming by walking into them.

• Brain Worm: Overrides Brain Worm.

• Brimstone / Epic Fetus / The Ludovico Technique / Tech X: Overridden by Brimstone. Stat effects still apply.

• C Section: Overridden by C Section. Stat effects apply.

• Dr. Fetus: After firing a bomb and moving, the bomb will have a homing-style effect towards the beam, but will not stay directly on the beam. Not recommended, as changing directions while firing will cause the bomb to reel back to Isaac at high speed, making self-damage very likely.

• Euthanasia: Needles fired will follow beam; however, burst needles will not.

• Evil Eye: Both evil eyes and tears fired by them will not be affected by the beam.

• Explosivo: Explosivo's tears will become "entangled" when sticking on an enemy, causing them to jump from the tractor beam to the enemy and vice versa every frame. The tear will explode only once regardless while attached to an enemy or bound to the beam.

• Eye of the Occult: Tears will only move forward while being fired, but control is otherwise overridden.

• Eye Sore: No effect on the extra tears.

• Haemolacria: Fired tears will travel along the beam; however, the burst tears will not.

• Homing tears: The tears will stay in the line but will slow down when near enemies.

• Hook Worm: Overridden, except for the range increase.

• [Repentance] The tears increase and spectral tears it now grants are also still in effect.

• Immaculate Heart: No effect on the extra tears.

• Incubus: The Incubus tears aren't affected by the beam, but the beam will still be there.

• Incubus + Monstro's Lung: Incubus's tear barrage will follow the beam.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Lead Pencil: Tear barrage will not follow the beam. [end edition note] 

• Loki's Horns: No effect on extra tears.

• [Before Repentance] Marked: Tears will only fire in cardinal directions.

• [Repentance] The beam will point towards the marker.

• [Before Repentance] Multidimensional Baby: The beam only affects the original tears, not the duplicated ones.

• [Repentance] The duplicated tears will follow the beam.

• Ouroboros Worm: Tears will stall at points along their path; the normal spiral pattern is negated entirely, however.

• Saturnus: No effect on orbital tears.

• Spirit Sword: Overrides Tractor Beam. Stat effects still apply.

• Sprinkler: Tears fired by the sprinkler will follow Isaac's beam.

• Tammy's Head: Tractor Beam does not affect the tears created by Tammy's Head.

• Technology: Overridden by Technology.

• [Repentance] The beam becomes unaffected by Isaac's momentum.

• Tiny Planet: The orbiting effect is overridden, but Isaac still gains the Range increase and spectral tears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is a reference to tractor beams in science fiction, often depicted as beams of energy that can be used to move objects.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Tractor Beam has unusual effects when combined with Continuum and Pop!. While shooting, tears will appear for brief moments at the back of Isaac's head, and if he hits an enemy with one of these, that enemy will be teleported to a corner of the screen for poorly understood reasons. Isaac himself can also get teleported to a corner, resulting in a potential softlock without flight or How to Jump.

fields.description: Isaac's tears are bound to a beam emitting in the direction he's firing. [Before Repentance] +0.5 Tears, +5.25 Range, +0.16 Shot Speed. [Repentance] +1 Fire Rate, +2.5 Range, +0.16 Shot Speed.

Transcendence.title: Transcendence
Transcendence.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants flight.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • The Intruder: When the effect is activated Isaac becomes invisible.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The pickup quote "We all float down here... " is a reference to the Stephen King book 'IT'.

• According to Edmund McMillen's first post-Repentance Lore Stream, the explanation behind the visuals of Transcendence (namely the lack of a noose and more importantly, a body) is simply that McMillen found the idea of a head flying around amusing.

• If Scissors are used after picking up Transcendence, Isaac will have no visible body from which to shoot tears. Only a shadow and orbitals will remain.

• [Repentance] In Repentance, however, blood gurgles will be spewing constantly from the body, making it much easier to keep track of it.

• This item is used in Solar System.

• In the original Binding Of Isaac, Transcendence was unlocked by beating Mom's Heart two times instead of three.

• The item sprite is a reference to the suicide method of one hanging themselves with a rope connected to an anchor point on top.

• This is further supported with Ending 3.

• This is the only flight granting item to not give Isaac any extra attributes, such as stats or health.

fields.name: Transcendence
fields.description: Grants flight.

Transformations.title: Transformations
Transformations.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Transformations alter Isaac's appearance and grant him special abilities.

A transformation occurs when obtaining at least three different items from a particular set of items.

These collectibles always share a particular theme that corresponds with the transformation.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.text:
• Items only need to have been acquired once in order to count.

• [Before Repentance] Duplicate items (like those acquired from Diplopia) do not count toward transformations when picked up. Only the first instance of an item Isaac owns will count.

• [Repentance] Duplicate items are all counted.

• [Repentance+] Duplicate items are not counted for the Necromancer transformation.

• Activated collectibles (e.g. Guppy's Head) can be picked up once and then swapped away with another without any loss to transformation progress.

• [Before Repentance] Rerolling items with a Dice Room, the D4, or the D100 will not remove progress towards the transformation.

• [Repentance] The transformation will be lost if the items required are rerolled or otherwise lost, eg. Sacrificial Altar.

• [Afterbirth onward] Familiars gained from Cambion Conception or Immaculate Conception do not count towards transformation progress. [end edition note] 

• Trinkets do not count toward progress for any transformation, with the exceptions of Kid's Drawing that counts for Guppy transformation, Bob's Bladder for Bob, and A Missing Page for Necromancer.

• Pills only count toward Adult and Stompy, they do not count toward progress for any other transformation.

• Characters that start with an item that counts towards a transformation do count as one of the three items needed for a transformation, such as Judas starting with The Book of Belial.

• [Repentance] Only the first character to pick up an item will gain progress towards its transformation. This applies in co-op, or when playing as Jacob and Esau or Tainted Lazarus. [end edition note] 

• Tainted Isaac will not lose a transformation nor progress towards it if he replaces an item that counts towards that transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Transformations can be combined, keeping the effects of all transformations with no effects overriding others.

• Transforming into Beelzebub for the first time will unlock the Lord of the Flies achievement and Angry Fly.

• [Afterbirth onward] As none of the Afterbirth transformations unlock an achievement or item, obtaining them is not required for 100% completion of the game in terms of achievements. However, this is only true if you unlocked Mom's Contacts on Rebirth, as the Yes Mother? transformation will happen once you collect three Mom items on Afterbirth and Afterbirth †.

• [Before Repentance] Many of the Afterbirth transformations override the charge animations of items such as Monstro's Lung and Brimstone, potentially making them more difficult to use.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] There is now an option to show a charge bar that floats above Isaac.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac flash game, the transformation into Guppy was the only one available, making it chronologically the first.

• Rebirth introduced Beelzebub as the chronologically second transformation.

• Made after Rebirth, the Eternal Edition of the original The Binding of Isaac game added another transformation that turned Isaac into an angel after gaining 7 heart containers from eternal hearts.

• The original name for the Beelzebub transformation was Lord of the Flies.

• The reason no new transformations were added to Repentance is because at the time Edmund and the dev team did not like them, as they viewed them as significant advantages gained only from being lucky enough to find specific items. This is why Guppy, the most powerful transformation, requires much more effort to get compared to a transformation like Spider Baby. If any new transformations were to be added for Repentance, they would be purely visual.

Treasure Map.title: Treasure Map
Treasure Map.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Reveals the map of each floor. It does not identify special rooms and does not reveal the locations of Secret Rooms / Super Secret Rooms.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• When combined with Blue Map and The Compass, the entire floor is revealed, identical to the effect of The Mind.

• Although not explicitly revealing it, the Boss Room can usually be found by locating the room farthest away from the starting room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Secrets: Can make it easier to gain X-Ray Vision as Book of Secrets cannot give a mapping effect Isaac already has.

• Liberty Cap: If Liberty Cap triggers the effect of The Compass, it will last for the remainder of the floor.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Treasure Map received a significant downgrade in Rebirth, as it no longer reveals Secret Rooms. That effect, along with being able to reveal Super Secret Rooms, now belongs to the Blue Map.

• This item is used in Cursed!.

• This item is likely a reference to the Legend of Zelda franchise, in which dungeon maps are commonplace.

• [Repentance] Under the minimap, The Mind's icon will override the icon of this item.

• This item can be found as one of the Nintendo-themed Treasure Room items in the 6th of December's Daily Run, which is an homage to the late CEO of Nintendo, Satoru Iwata.

fields.name: Treasure Map
fields.description: Reveals the map of each floor. It does not identify special rooms and does not reveal the locations of Secret Rooms / Super Secret Rooms.

Triachnid.title: Triachnid
Triachnid.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Triachnid is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb).

• [Repentance] Only in the Utero and the Scarred Womb. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Triachnid's head hangs down stationary and can perform the following attacks:

• Raises his head, making it invulnerable, and stomps the ground in random locations around the room 3 times in quick succession, leaving small puddles of slowing White Creep. [Repentance] One of these legs will always stomp on top of Isaac's position.

• The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.

• Lifts his head off-screen and stomps the ground 3 times at regular intervals on top of Isaac's position, leaving a small puddle of White Creep with each stomp. At the end of the stomps, he slams his head down quickly in the center, shooting 8 white projectiles in all directions and creating a large puddle of White Creep. He can only slam his head down along a horizontal plane across the center of the room and slams it down close to Isaac's position.

• Occasionally performs a fourth stomp before slamming his head down and very occasionally performs a fifth.

• Occasionally, when he slams his head down, he leaves a larger puddle of White Creep, but only shoots 4 white projectiles in the cardinal directions.

• The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.

• Spits out a Trite in Isaac's direction.

• Trites can be killed by Triachnid's stomps and head slam.
Triachnid's foot stomp and head slam deal a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Unlike all other other alternative versions of bosses, such as Dangle, C.H.A.D., and Gish, Triachnid has the same weight as his alternative boss form.

• Although they share the same weight, Triachnid is actually more common than Daddy Long Legs, since he also appears in the Scarred Womb.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Triachnid was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original game, Triachnid could be encountered in Necropolis.

• Triachnid's unlock method is possibly a reference to a bug in Wrath of the Lamb that caused Triachnid to occasionally replace Isaac in the Cathedral.

• Triachnid originated from the 2006 flash game Tri-achnid, which was created by Edmund McMillen.

• He is an alternative of Daddy Long Legs.

• Unlike the other alternate bosses (Steven, C.H.A.D., Gish, and Conquest), Triachnid does not drop a specific item.

• While Daddy Long Legs uses 4 appendages in his attacks, Triachnid is reduced to mostly only using 3; this is most likely in homage to the fact that Triachnid in his title game only had 3 appendages.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Triachnid does not have a death animation.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Triachnid can be found in The Void, even before being unlocked. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Blighted Ovum, Big Horn, Triachnid, Isaac, and ??? are the only bosses whose portraits were completely changed in Repentance (beyond simply adding more detail). Of these, only Triachnid, Isaac, and ??? didn't receive new sprites.

Trinity Shield.title: Trinity Shield
Trinity Shield.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac uses a shield to block shots.

• The shield stays in the same direction until Isaac fires in another direction.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The shield can block diagonally by holding down 2 arrow keys at once.

• Tears will be fired vertically while the shield is at an angle.

• The shield can't block beams or explosions.

• The shield can be held in any direction if you're using a joystick.

• Many items that change the color of Isaac's tears will also change the color of the shield; this effect is purely cosmetic.

• When using Tainted Forgotten, the shield goes on the bone pile and not the soul.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Marked: The shield will now face the crosshair instead of facing just four cardinal directions.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: No effect.

• Maw Of The Void: Trinity shield briefly stays fixed in place during the start of the effect.

• [Before Repentance] Notched Axe: While using this item, the shield stays in place. It returns when the effect ends.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item is a reference to the Shield of the Trinity.

• This item is used in I RULE! and Isaac's Awakening.

• Although this item is normally only available in the Angel Room, it can be found as one of the Nintendo-themed Treasure Room items in the 6th of December's Daily Run, which is an homage to the late CEO of Nintendo, Satoru Iwata.

• Its appearance in this challenge references the Hylian shield from The Legend of Zelda series.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: When Pause is used with Trinity Shield it creates a second shield that stays in place where Isaac used "Pause" which lasts for the active item's duration. Moreover both shields are flashing and can not block enemy tears for the duration.
Bug note: [Repentance] Swapping characters using Esau Jr. or as Tainted Lazarus will leave a stationary copy of the shield until Isaac leaves the room. The stationary shield still blocks tears. [end edition note]

fields.description: Isaac gains a shield that protects him from enemy shots. It aims in the direction Isaac fires from.

Trinkets.title: Trinkets
Trinkets.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Trinkets are a type of collectible with their designated slot that can provide passive bonuses. Only one trinket can be carried at a time and must be dropped if you wish to carry another. Some of these limitations can be bypassed with certain items; Mom's Purse and Belly Button allow two trinkets to be held at once, [Afterbirth+ onward] and trinkets can be absorbed by Smelter, Marbles, or Gulp!. Absorbed trinkets do not take up a trinket slot and act as permanent passive effects.

Compared to items with a similar effect, trinket effects are typically more subtle, less powerful, or less reliable. For example, the Callus only prevents damage from spikes and creep, while many items that do the same also grant Isaac flight.

The original Binding of Isaac DLC 'The Wrath of the Lamb' introduced Trinkets as a mechanic and had 33 trinkets. Rebirth has a total of 60 trinkets. Afterbirth added 29 new trinkets, for a total of 89 trinkets. Afterbirth † added 38 new trinkets, for a total of 127 trinkets. Repentance added 61 new trinkets, for a total of 188 trinkets.

[Repentance] All trinkets have a very rare 2% chance to spawn as Golden Trinkets.

• Unlocked by: [achievement unlock: Golden Trinket]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• It is possible to drop a trinket by holding down the key or button bound to the "Drop" function for three seconds. (Doing this is not possible with the Tick.)

• While held, Mom's Box doubles the effect of most trinkets.

• [Repentance] A Golden Trinket with Mom's Box will have a tripled effect.

• Trinkets appear in a set order based on the run's seed, and each trinket can usually only be encountered once.

• Trinkets which are set drops, such as Mysterious Paper from Divorce Papers and The Left Hand from Ultra Pride, can appear even if encountered previously.

• Other set drops, such as Swallowed Penny from a urn or Umbilical Cord from a polyp, will not appear if already seen.

• If enough trinkets are spawned, e.g. through Mom's Box, the cycle loops and begins spawning trinkets that were already encountered.

• [Before Repentance] If two of the same trinkets are gathered, Isaac can have both by using Gulp! on one and then picking up the other. This rarely has any useful purpose.

• [Repentance] Multiples of the same trinkets sometimes stack as expected, and two copies of the same trinket can be held simultaneously with Belly Button or Mom's Purse. However, a large number of trinkets don't stack, especially the ones that are more complicated than a simple stat up. [end edition note] 

• Trinkets cannot be duplicated with items such as Diplopia or Jera.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Activating the D1 on a trinket will duplicate the trinket. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Activating the D1 on a trinket will spawn a new, different trinket. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Polaroid was originally a trinket in the original Binding of Isaac, but it was changed into an item. It had the trinket ID 47 which is now empty.

• Wiggle Worm was an item in the original Binding of Isaac; however, in Rebirth, it was changed into a trinket. Interestingly, these changes keep the count of items and trinkets from the original game the same.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Afterbirth+'s original trinket count was 29. The Booster Packs added 9 trinkets.

• Game Squid is the only trinket from the original Binding of Isaac that wasn't implemented into Rebirth or any of its DLCs. This is likely due to it having been added in the Eternal Edition update after Rebirth's release.

• Chewed Pen, a trinket added in Repentance, has a nearly identical effect to Game Squid.

• The game has a set "order" of trinkets that will appear. So, for example, if a trinket is encountered as a room drop, then going back in time with the Glowing Hourglass, the next trinket that drops from any source will always be that same trinket. This is also why Guppy's Eye can show the same trinket in two different chests; as the next drop is technically that trinket, no matter which chest is opened. Opening that chest and getting that trinket will cause the other chest to change its drop to a different trinket.

Trisagion.title: Trisagion
Trisagion.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Tears are replaced with piercing white blasts of light.

• Blasts deal 33% of the regular tear damage, but can hit each enemy they are in contact with up to 15 times per second.

• Blasts decrease in size until disappearing.

• • Despite the blasts decreasing in size after passing through obstacles, this purely visual as the blast will only damage enemies adjacent to the obstacle.

• [Before Repentance] Blasts do not knock back enemies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Since the blasts can strike one enemy multiple times while they remain in contact, low shot speed can be very beneficial whereas high shot speed may lower effective damage.

• Walking backward while firing can allow tears to move slower, making it useful for increasing damage output.

• Items that grant a high Tears rate, such as Soy Milk, can cause the light beams to significantly obstruct visibility, which can further be exacerbated by items such as Fruit Cake causing rapid color and size change.

• With only Trisagion, Isaac with base stats will deal about 18 damage per second on an unmoving, gaper-sized enemy, which is almost double Isaac's base DPS of 9.5. 1.32 shot speed will reduce DPS of Trisagion to about 14.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 8 Inch Nails / Blister / Pisces: Adds knockback to blasts, which can not only significantly repel enemies when used correctly, it can deal a high amount of damage to enemies unable to escape the knockback.

• Chocolate Milk: Fully charged Trisagion blasts deal 4 times more damage, exceeding Isaac's normal damage.

• Cricket's Body: Original blast shoots four white tears in a cross pattern during its travel time and four blast tears in a cross pattern at the end of its range. Only the original blast splits.

• [Repentance] Euthanasia / Explosivo / Head of the Keeper / Holy Light / Nose Goblin / Sinus Infection: Beams can apply the effects on each damage tick, potentially triggering them in rapid succession.

• Evil Eye: Eyes will fire beams. Occasionally causes Trisagion beams to stay static in the air for a few seconds, dealing damage to enemies that come in contact with them.

• Godhead: Although the damaging aura isn't visible, it still exists and is not affected by Trisagion's damage reduction. Still grants homing effect and shot speed down which can be very beneficial.

• Guppy: As it hits multiple times, it spawns multiple flies per tear making it very strong.

• Haemolacria: Both Trisagion and Haemolacria fire at the same time; Isaac's tears do not keep the spectral attribute despite the sprite being changed. The tears keeps their piercing effect.

• [Repentance] Haemolacria becomes one big Trisagion beam that splits into more beams when it reaches its max range.

• Hemoptysis: Enemies hit by the sneeze will gain a curse that increases the damage the blasts deal to 0.66x and +3 flat damage (instead of just x0.33). Enemies who die to the blasts under the curse will damage and spread the curse to nearby enemies. Since the flat damage ignores the multiplier, this is a huge increase to Isaac's damage.

• Hemoptysis + Soy Milk/Almond Milk/ [Repentance] 20/20: The flat damage increase ignores the multiplier reductions, which results in a massive increase in damage.

• Homing tears: Tears slow down and stay on top of the enemy, doing continuous damage.

• Jacob's Ladder: Small electric arcs generate from the blast every tick.

• The Ludovico Technique: The beam becomes controllable, still dealing reduced damage but at a very high rate.

• Mucormycosis: The spore effect can stack multiple times on the same enemy.

• My Reflection: In addition to the usual effect, lengthens the Trisagion blasts into short flexible beams for a much larger damage-dealing area.

• Mysterious Liquid: Causes a large trail of creep. The effect stacks, which causes heavy damage (even to Hush).

• Ocular Rift: Creates multiple rifts as the projectile pierces enemies.

• Pop!: Every damage tick will shoot out a Pop! tear. Trisagion shots will also hover in the air longer than normal.

• [Before Repentance] Proptosis: Base damage is increased by the expected amount and beam damage is boosted to about 65%. Blasts lose no power as they travel further, though the tips of the blasts deal very slightly less damage.

• [Repentance] Blasts now deal 2x Isaac's damage instead of 0.33x. Damage only slightly decreases in the front of the blast.

• Spirit Sword: The sword will shoot Trisagion beams instead of energy beams, with the Trisagion beams having increased damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
Overrides Trisagion:

• Azazel

• Brimstone

• C Section

• Dr. Fetus

• Epic Fetus

• The Forgotten

• Mom's Knife

• Tainted Azazel

• Tainted Forgotten

• Tech X

• Technology

Overridden by Trisagion:

• Dead Eye

• [Before Repentance] Euthanasia

• [Before Repentance] Explosivo

• Eye of Belial

• [Before Repentance] Holy Light

• [Before Repentance] Nose Goblin

• [Before Repentance] Parasitoid

• [Before Repentance] Sinus Infection

Other interactions:

• Bob's Rotten Head: Not recommended as it explodes multiple times before reaching its target, dealing explosive damage and knockback to Isaac.

• [Repentance] Shoots a white blast of light instead of the head that pierces through enemies, and causing explosions when it contacts an enemy (if not killing it at the first tick), an obstacle, or when it runs out of range. One tick of the beam deals 33% of Bob's Rotten Head's damage to enemies, but the resulting explosion every tick deals full damage.

• Compound Fracture: Split blasts are not generated on hitting enemies, only on obstacles and walls.

• Cricket's Body: Split blasts are not generated on hitting enemies, only on obstacles, walls, and the floor.

• Fire Mind: Tears still ignite enemies, but no longer have a chance to explode.

• [Before Repentance] Flat Stone: Blasts continually disappear and reappear as they "bounce". The bounces deal 25% splash damage based on Isaac's base damage, but the blasts cannot do their damage while they're disappearing, leading to an overall reduced efficiency.

• [Repentance] Blasts no longer disappear.

• Glass Cannon / [Repentance] Isaac's Tears / Tammy's Head: Trisagion does not gain additional damage.

• Ipecac: Beams will now travel through obstacles and maintain their piercing effect dealing 33% of regular damage to enemies they come in contact with, but won't explode on hit. The Ipecac explosion will happen once the beam runs out of range or hits a wall and will deal damage equal to Isaac's damage.

• [Repentance] Keeps Ipecac's stats and shoots an exploding Trisagion beam. The beam explodes while in contact with an obstacle or an enemy that it does not kill on the first tick, resulting in an excellent synergy with Pyromaniac or Host Hat. One tick of the beam deals 33% of Ipecac's damage to enemies, but the resulting explosion every tick deals full damage.

• • Warning: In the fight with The Beast, Trisagion will lose its straight shot path and go at an extreme Ipecac arc instead, which is almost guaranteed to hit any even somewhat nearby rock spire and leading to self damage, making the fight significantly more difficult.

• Jacob's Ladder: Electric arcs are not generated on hitting enemies, only on obstacles and walls.

• Lachryphagy: The blasts will slow down and float like Lachryphagy tears and eventually burst, but can not consume each other.

• [Repentance] Blasts have greatly reduced range, but constantly generates Lachryphagy tears, with one shot alone being capable of bursting a tear.

• A Lump of Coal: Nearly no effect; increases damage by around 5% when the hit is dealt by the tip of the blast. Makes the blasts absorb light, making it difficult to see anything while [cu: Darkness] is present.

• A Lump of Coal + My Reflection: As the beam is longer, the amount of extra damage at the tip can be up to around 50%.

• Multidimensional Baby: The baby cannot duplicate Trisagion blasts.

• The Parasite: Split blasts are not generated on hitting enemies, only on obstacles and walls.

• Playdough Cookie: Rather than applying the effect to each individual tear, all beams will share the same color and change simultaneously every tick.

• Pop!: The blasts will slow down and float like Pop! tears, but will not bounce off each other.

• Sharp Key: Thrown keys become Trisagion blasts and no longer cause enemies to drop chest contents on kill.

• Technology Zero: Unless Isaac has shooting familiars, Technology Zero will not function. Familiars' tears will be connected to the blasts with electricity, however.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Trisagion is based on this Steam Workshop item by x Wyvern x and TRPG, originally known as Lightshot.

• The name is a reference to one of the oldest Christian hymns.

• The design of Trisagion appears to be that of Borromean rings, a Christian symbol of the Trinity.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Trisagion makes Lil Spewer achievement impossible to obtain via a suicide with Bob's Rotten Head or Ipecac.

fields.description: Tears are replaced with piercing white blasts of light that deal less damage but can damage the same enemy multiple times.

Tuff Twins.title: Tuff Twins
Tuff Twins.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Tuff Twins is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Mines.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Tuff Twins always spawn in a pair consisting of 5 body segments and a head segment each. They are always fought in a double-sized room.

• The Tuff Twins roam around the room randomly, like Larry Jr.

• The Tuff Twins are initially covered in rock armor that gives them immunity to all non-explosive damage, but bombs and explosives can destroy their armor, making their segments vulnerable to all damage.

• There are always at least two Bomb Grimaces that dispense Throwable Bombs for Isaac to use against the Tuff Twins to break their armor.

• All segments have damage resistance to explosives both before and after having their armor removed, taking only 25-14% damage based on how far away the explosion is from them.

• • This also applies to Isaac's tears if they have an explosive effect, such as if he has Ipecac, Dr. Fetus, etc.

• The armor absorbs up to 15 damage before breaking, and is independent of the segments' 35 HP value.

• Head segments occasionally spit Inks while protected by its rock armor.

• Vulnerable head segments spit Suckers instead.

• Head segments will not try to spawn Inks or Suckers if there are at least 4 total in the room. However, head segments can occasionally spawn multiple in succession, bypassing this limit.

• Vulnerable body segments spew bloody shots, similar to Boils.

• Tuff Twin segments can be split into smaller copies of the boss as long as the new Tuff Twin segments are longer than 2 pieces.

• The Tuff Twins become faster the more rock armor they lose.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Terra, along with any items that create rock waves like Mega Bean and Wait What? can destroy the Tuff Twins' armor.

• [Repentance+] Hagalaz will also remove their armor on use.

• Sulfuric Acid tears cannot destroy their armor. 

• Destroying all the Bomb Grimaces with effects like Little Horn and Euthanasia and then somehow wasting all of the bombs they drop when destroyed can soft-lock Isaac in this fight.

• Plan C cannot kill the Tuff Twins if they still have their armor.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• They appear to be a rocky variation of Larry Jr.

• The Shell appears to be the posthumous version of them.

• Tuff is the name of a type of rock formed from volcanic ash.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The Tuff Twins can get stuck with the Bomb Grimace in the room.

Turdlet.title: Turdlet
Turdlet.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Turdlet is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in Dross.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Turdlet consists of 5 separate segments that travel together similar to Larry Jr., and acts the following way.

• Moves around the room loosely chasing Isaac, making wide turns and bouncing on walls.

• After 7 seconds of normal movement, huddles its body together, then launches tail-first towards Isaac while straightening out. Its head end spins around its tail while bouncing against walls at high speeds before eventually decelerating to a full stop.

• Turdlet leaves a trail of slippery Brown Creep wherever it moves.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
• After dropping to 30 health or less, Turdlet splits into two parts with two segments, each continuing the same behavior.

• The health each split Turdlet has is equal to the health the original Turdlet had when it split, plus 15.

• While both parts are alive they coordinate the launch attack by huddling together.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using the Meat Cleaver on Turdlet instantly skips its first phase.

• Since the health Turdlet's split segments have scales depending on how much health the original Turdlet have when it split, if a strong attack (like a Bomb or II - The High Priestess) causes Turdlet to split, its split segments will have significantly less health.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Turdlet resembles a grounded Pin, albeit with a happier expression.

• Alternatively, it may be a Dross-specific variant of Larry Jr., seeing as how both bosses slide on the ground.

• Turdlet uses the same scream that the Gurglings and the Turdlings use.

• In the games files, there are unused enemies with the name of "Floater Turdlet" which resemble Drips with the color scheme of Turdlet. This implies that Turdlet may have had another phase or attack planned, but was ultimately scrapped.

Turdlings.title: Turdlings
Turdlings.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Turdlings are a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth that can appear in the Basement [Repentance] and the Burning Basement. [end edition note] 

They each have 50 HP.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Turdlings spawn as a pair and wander around the room. Each individual Turdling has one attack in total which is performed independently of the other:

• Rushes towards Isaac when aligned in any cardinal direction, leaving behind slippery Brown Creep until it has run into a wall.

• After rushing into a wall, it spawns 4 Brownie Corns that launch out in the cardinal directions.

• Occasionally, after rushing into a wall it will fart, knocking back Isaac and nearby Brownie Corns.

• Its dash can be interrupted if it runs into a Brownie Corn.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Turdlings are much less common than their counterparts, spawning only 1/4th as often.

• [Repentance+] Flush! kills Turdlings instantly and causes them to leave behind 6 Dips each. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• They are a corny poop-themed variant of the Gurglings.

• [Repentance] Unlike the Gurglings, their sprite was not updated for Repentence.

• The Turdlings and their regular variant, the Gurglings, spawn in groups of three during the Boss Rush.

Twisted Pair.title: Twisted Pair
Twisted Pair.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns two familiars who float by Isaac's side and fire tears that use Isaac's tears, range, shot speed, tear effects and that each deal 0.375x his damage.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Twisted Pair is very similar to the item Incubus. It provides the same total damage per second increase in the form of a familiar (familiars in this case).

• When playing as Lilith or Tainted Lilith, the demon familiars will deal 50% of Lilith's damage each.

• Holding the up/down + left/right attack buttons will make one demon go further behind and the other one in front of Isaac.

• Because the demons need time to adjust their position while firing, the left/right directional buttons can be tapped to shoot more precise, straight lines of tears.

• They don't inherit all effects and stats from the player. See Interactions below check for small oversights.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Twisted Pair's tears deal twice as much damage.

• Box of Friends/Crooked Penny/Diplopia: Each additional Twisted Pair will add two more familiars that float farther out from Isaac.

• Forgotten Lullaby: Increases the fire rate of Twisted Pair.

• Tractor Beam: Twisted Pair's tears follow the beam.

• Friendship Necklace: Causes the Twisted Pair to orbit Isaac, allowing for a more precise firing of tears.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Epic Fetus: Each familiar will fire a missile from a two additional crosshairs. Not Recommended, as the twisted pair crosshairs are not synced to Isaac's crosshair and move at a much slower rate, making self damage much more likely as the additional crosshairs will struggle to make distance from Isaac. This is likely an oversight.

• Eye Drops: The familiars do not have the staggered attack, stat bonuses still apply.

• Eye of Greed The two familiars will also fire coin tears which spend Isaac's coins. Their shot counter is independent from Isaac's.

• Sacrificial Altar: Only 1 item pedestal is spawned for their sacrifice, unless they were spawned through Cambion Conception, in which case they will count for two.

• Terra + Brimstone/Technology: While Terra + laser items like Brimstone or Technology don't open doors normally, Twisted Pair's lasers can open doors. This is likely an oversight.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • "Twisted Pair" may be a reference to Neil Breen's film of the same name, or to twisted pair cabling.

fields.description: Spawns two familiars that float on either side of Isaac and fire tears that use his tears, range, shot speed, and tear effects, and scale with damage.

Rock Spider.title: Rock Spider
Rock Spider.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Rock Spiders are small spider-legged stones and they were added to The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. They behave very closely to Spider, but they are exclusive to Mines and Ashpit and skitter at a slower speed.
Upon death, they turn into a normal Spider.

If Isaac is capable of breaking rocks by stepping on them (e. g. with Leo or Stompy), Rock Spiders will die if stepped on. This will spawn a Spider which is extremely likely to deal damage to Isaac.

[Repentance+] The Rock Spider, Tinted Rock Spider, and Coal Spider are destroyed by Hagalaz on use, leaving behind a Spider, Soul Heart, and a damaging hot coal, respectively. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Tinted Rock Spider
sections.text:
Tinted Rock Spiders are similar to Rock Spiders, however they have nearly twice as much health and move much faster. When killed, instead of transforming into a regular Spider, they drop 1 Soul Heart upon death. They are characterized by the "X" on their rock, which is similar to Tinted Rocks.

They do not spawn naturally; there is a chance that 1-2 will spawn upon destruction of a Tinted Rock while in the Mines or Ashpit.

If killed by freezing, for example, with Uranus or Freezer Baby, the spider will not drop a soul heart.

sections.heading: Coal Spider
sections.text:
Coal Spiders behave very closely to Rock Spiders, but they skitter at a faster speed due to being on fire.

Upon death, it leaves a hot rock on the ground that despawns after several seconds. They can be shot to make them despawn faster.

Rock Spiders coming into contact with a Fire Place or fire spawned by items, such as Red Candle or Bird's Eye, turn into Coal Spiders.

Unlike Rock Spiders, Coal Spiders cannot be killed by stepping on them while having a Stompy effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Rock Spider and all its variants originate from the Antibirth mod.

Round Worm.title: Round Worm
Round Worm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the monster; trinkets; :Category:Worm trinkets] 

A Round Worm is an enemy introduced in the vanilla content of The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth. They appear from Chapter 1 to Chapter 4.

It will periodically burrow into the ground and pop up in different part of the room. If Isaac is in their line of sight when that happens, it will spit a blood shot in his direction.

sections.heading: Night Crawler
sections.text: Like the Round Worm, the Night Crawler will burrow into the ground and appear somewhere else. When Isaac is within their line of sight, they will fire four short-range projectiles that spiral outwards.

sections.heading: Roundy
sections.text:
Roundy is a type of Round Worm added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth DLC.

Like the Round Worm, a Roundy will burrow into the ground and appear somewhere else. When it surfaces, it releases a small rock wave around it and fires an Ipecac shot towards Isaac.

The Roundy's rock wave and explosive projectile can kill other monsters including each other.

sections.heading: Ulcer
sections.text:
The Ulcer is an enemy added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth DLC.

Like the Round Worm, the Ulcer will burrow into the ground and appear somewhere else. When it surfaces, if Isaac is within its line of sight, it will spawn a Dart Fly, but if there are ≥6 enemies in the current room, it will start firing a blood shot instead. Ulcers burrow underground at a slightly slower rate than most other Worms, usually making them easier to attack.

sections.heading: Tube Worm
sections.text:
The Tube Worm is a unique variant of the Round Worm found in [Repentance] Chapter 1.5 and the Flooded Caves of Chapter 2. They are added in the Booster Pack #4 for The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth † DLC.

Like the Round Worm, the Tube Worm will burrow into the ground and appear somewhere else. Upon popping out of the ground, they will fire a long-ranged arcing spray of shots at Isaac, attempting to intercept Isaac's position based on his movement. Unlike standard Round Worms, they can fire at Isaac even if they do not have a line of sight.

sections.heading: Fire Worm
sections.text:
Fire Worms were introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

Like the Round Worm, the Fire Worm will burrow into the ground and appear somewhere else. If Isaac is in their line of sight, they will fire a single flame at him. They can only appear in lava-filled gaps.

sections.heading: Tainted Round Worm
sections.text:
Tainted Round Worms are much stronger and tankier versions of Round Worms. They are added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC.

Like Round Worms, they will pop out of random locations in the floor, but the Tainted Round Worm does so alongside multiple tail ends. The head and all the tail ends will shoot Isaac together when he is in sight; while the tail ends each shoot a small blood shot, the head spits a large blood shot which will split into 8 blood shots upon obstacle collision. The tail ends can be attacked to deal damage to the Tainted Round Worm.

They are only found on the Ascent to Home.

sections.heading: Tainted Tube Worm
sections.text:
Tainted Tube Worms are a stronger variant of Tube Worms only found in Downpour during the Ascent. They are added to The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC.

After popping up in a random location, they spit 4 spread-out Ipecac shots in the direction of Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Worms are immune to the effects of Strange Attractor and Black Hole.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Round Worms are parasitic creatures in real life that can be found inside cats or dogs.

• Nightcrawlers in real life could refer to earthworms, although they don't look similar to the Nightcrawlers from The Binding of Isaac.

• [Afterbirth onward] Ulcers are a reference to ulcers, breaks in bodily membranes caused by sloughing out of inflamed necrotic tissue.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Tube Worms were created by Kilburn, who later became the programmer and developer for the Repentance DLC.

• In real-life, tube worms are creatures that live underwater and anchor their tails underground, which may be where the Tube Worm from The Binding of Isaac got its name from. However, they don't resemble real-life tube worms.

• [Repentance] The Fireworm first appeared in the Antibirth mod where its name was one word instead of two.

Rainbow Baby.title: Rainbow Baby
Rainbow Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and fires tears with random effects similar to other familiars.

• [Before Repentance] Rainbow Baby shoots once per second.

• [Repentance] Rainbow Baby shoots 1.36 times a second.

• The shot types and their damage are:

• Short-range blood tear for 3 damage.

• Plain red tear for [edition alternatives: baseline: 3.5; Repentance: 6] damage.

• V-pattern double shot for 3.5 damage each.

• Charming purple tear for 3.5 damage.

• Slowing black tear for 3.5 damage.

• Spectral tear for 3.5 damage.

• Long-range homing violet tear for 3.5 damage.

• Long-range spectral and homing tear for 3.5 damage.

• Blood tear for 4 damage.

• Large blood tear for 5 damage.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Conjoined transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Rainbow Baby having [edition alternatives: baseline: 5th; Repentance+: 7th] priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Mongo Baby: Will copy Rainbow Baby’s random tears.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Rainbow Baby: The randomization of tears shot by multiple Rainbow Babies are not in sync.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in PRIDE DAY!.

• A rainbow baby is a healthy baby born to a family that had previously experienced the loss of an infant before, during, or shortly after birth.

• In the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original game, this item was unlocked by beating Isaac as ???.
