Meconium.title: Meconium
Meconium.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a 33% chance for Poop to turn into Black Poop.

• This includes Red Poop.

• Adds a 5% chance for black poops to drop a Black Heart upon being destroyed.

• The chances are not affected by luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• D12: Obstacles that are rerolled into poop have a greater chance of being Black Poop.

• A Card Against Humanity / Mysterious Candy / The Poop / Re-Lax pill / Everything Jar's 1st charge: Has chance for the poop created to be a Black Poop.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either of these effects raises the chance to 66% chance for Poop to turn into Black Poop and to 7% chance for black poops to drop a Black Heart upon being destroyed. Having both of them raises the chance to respectively 100% and 10%.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Hallowed Ground: Although Meconium cannot replace the poop Hallowed Ground spawns with, Black Poop has a chance to replace White Poops that would have been created by other items which have synergies with Hallowed Ground.

• Second Hand: The confuse duration from Black Poops is unaffected by Second Hand.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Meconium is the earliest stool of a mammalian infant.

fields.name: Meconium
fields.description: Black Poops can drop Black Heart when destroyed. Poop has a chance to turn into Black Poop.

Mega Bean.title: Mega Bean
Mega Bean.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Petrifies all enemies in the current room for about 1.5 seconds.

• Deals 5 damage and poisons any enemies near Isaac.

• The poison deals Isaac's damage per tick and lasts for 6 ticks.

• [Before Repentance+] Sends out a wave of rocks across the room in the direction Isaac is facing, dealing 10 damage to any enemies it comes in contact with.

• [Repentance] The fart deflects enemy projectiles which deal 6 damage if they would've hurt Isaac for half a heart, and 7 for a full heart.

• [Repentance+] The fart creates a Mama Mega! explosion that deals 100 damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• It can be used to open Secret Rooms.

• [Before Repentance+] The rock wave can break rocks to fill in gaps.

• [Repentance+] As Mega Bean creates a Mama Mega! explosion, it can be used to open the entrances to Boss Rush and the ??? if they are closed.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Bird's Eye/Ghost Pepper: Whenever Mega Bean is used, a fire will be shot out behind Isaac. Two flames will be shot if Isaac also has Car Battery.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns tiny magenta wisps on the middle ring. The wisps send rock waves outward when Mega Bean is used. They also petrify and poison all enemies in a large radius when destroyed.

• Car Battery: Deals double damage, but the status effect lasts for the same amount of time.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Second Hand: Doubles the petrification duration but not the poison duration.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: [Before Repentance] Kidney Bean had the same sprite as Mega Bean albeit colored red. Repentance made the sprite of Kidney Bean much smaller.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Mega Bean can be used to push The Beast and the Ultra Harbingers into the lava while they are still in the background. This has no effect on their actual fight, only on their earlier preview. Same effect can be achieved using Mama Mega!.

fields.name: Mega Bean
fields.description: Petrifies all enemies in the current room for about 1.5 seconds, poisons any enemies near Isaac. [Before Repentance+] The fart also sends a rock wave across the room in the direction Isaac is facing. [Repentance+] The fart also creates a Mama Mega! explosion. [end edition note]

Mega Blast.title: Mega Blast
Mega Blast.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac fires a giant, incredibly powerful Brimstone laser from his mouth, similar to the one used by Mega Satan, for 15 seconds.

• The laser deals Isaac's current damage multiplied by 5 per tick.

• The laser has enough power to push Isaac backward while being fired and will last between rooms, and across multiple floors.

• The laser is not locked to the cardinal directions; it can be aimed freely.

• While Mega Blast is being fired, Isaac cannot:

• • Open Chests.

• • Pick up a Lil' Battery, collectibles, pills, trinkets, or cards or runes.

• • Pick up the trophy or enter the chest that spawns after defeating a final boss.

• • Sleep in a bed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Picking up a Lil' Battery with this item will add 3 to its charge, meaning that 4 batteries are required to fully recharge the item.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] A Charged Key will only add 3 charges.

• • Lil' Battery and Charged Key add 6 charges instead of 3.

• [Repentance] Picking up a Mega Battery will fully charge it twice.

• Using a 48 Hour Energy pill with this item will fully charge it.

• Mega Blast has an 80% decreased item pool weight, making it less likely to appear than other collectibles.

• [Repentance] It is not recommended to use Mega Blast in fight with The Beast, because its laser forces you into obstacles on the level.

• This can be mitigated to a degree with Anima Sola, especially with a Car Battery which doubles the Anima Sola's length. The Beast won't be able to spawn obstacles while chained. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
All synergies and interactions pertaining to Brimstone pertain to Mega Blast, with the following exceptions and additions:

• 4.5 Volt: Item will gain charges for dealing damage, which is especially effective when fighting bosses with large health pool.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns red wisps on the middle ring that utilize a miniature Brimstone as their weapon, which requires charging and releasing as usual. Lasers can hit up to 8 times for a total of 24 damage. If Mega Blast is being used, the wisps will continuously fire their laser outward rather than in the direction Mega Blast is firing.

• Car Battery The beam lasts 50% longer, about 23 seconds.

• Tainted Azazel: Enemies hit by the sneeze will gain a curse that increases the damage the laser deals to 10x and +3 flat damage (instead of just 5x). Enemies who die to the laser under the curse will damage and spread the curse to nearby enemies.

• Hemoptysis: The sneeze can be activated while Mega Blast is firing.

• Schoolbag: laser will continue to fire when switching to another active item. Other active items can be used while the laser is firing.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Familiars which copy Isaac's tears fire normal tears while Mega Blast is in use.

• Angelic Prism: The laser does not split.

• Anti-Gravity: No effect.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Hairpin / Sol: Only grants 3 charges.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Mega Blast's collectible sprite is called 'Mega Satan's Breath' in the game files, which may be its initial name.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Quitting a run and resuming it while Mega Blast was active will retain the costume and animation of Mega Blast until the item is used again, but no laser will appear.
Bug note: If the Glowing Hourglass is used while in the room Mega Blast was used in, the Mega Blast laser will still remain, but the animation will be removed, and a full charge for Mega Blast will be reobtained.

fields.description: Isaac fires a giant blood laser for approximately 15 seconds. This laser deals massive damage, pushes Isaac backwards, and persists between rooms and floors.

Mega Fatty.title: Mega Fatty
Mega Fatty.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Mega Fatty is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] Only in the Caves.

• [Repentance] In the Caves and the Flooded Caves.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Leaps off-screen and tries to land on Isaac's position, leaving a large puddle of Red Creep upon landing.

• Slides briefly towards Isaac and performs a short-range jump, also leaving Red Creep when he lands.

• Inhales, drawing in Isaac and any monsters towards him, before then vomiting upwards, unleashing a barrage of projectiles into the air. The projectiles will rain down for a short duration, following Isaac's movements.

• Farts, which can damage Isaac if he's too close, and will either:

• Summon 1-3 Dips.

• Unleash a cluster of either small or big projectiles behind him, similar to Monstro.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 23] : Has 15% more HP (690). He will not use his vomit attack and sends out rock waves instead of leaving Red Creep upon landing when performing the long-range jump, similar to The Cage.
[bc: 1] : 33% smaller and has 10% less HP (540). Shoots 6 bullets instead of leaving Red Creep upon landing. Creates Red Poop instead of Dips. Vomit attack sends out four projectile stream attacks in a pattern similar to Mom's Heart/It Lives!. [Before Repentance+] Due to the high tear height of the vomit attack projectiles, it is nearly impossible to get hit by them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Lost Contact will still block all incoming projectiles from his barrage, even if they happen to go high enough to be offscreen.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• He is the boss version of the Fatty.

• The Cage is the posthumous version of Mega Fatty.

• The picture of Mega Fatty on Isaac's last will closely resembles the unused variant.

Mega Maw.title: Mega Maw
Mega Maw.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Mega Maw is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] Only in the Caves.

• [Repentance] In the Caves and the Flooded Caves.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Mega Maw is stationary and will perform the following attacks:

• Fires red projectiles at Isaac in disorganized bursts, similar to Monstro.

• Releases 2 rings of 5 flames which expand outwards and rotate in opposite directions.

• Releases one large ring of 9 flames that expands outwards.

• Releases one large ring of 9 flames that can rotate in either direction while expanding outwards.

• Gradually spits out a Hopper directly below it.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 18] : Spits 1-2 Spiders instead of Hoppers. The Spiders will be tossed directly towards Isaac instead of landing below Mega Maw. It does not use flame attacks.
[bc: 1] : Doesn't shoot any flames or spawn monsters and has a completely different set of blood-shot attacks:
Fires a ring of 9 blood shots that spiral outward.
Fires 4-5 lines of 4 curving blood shots.
Fires 4 lines of 7 waving blood shots.
Fires 10 lines of 4 blood shots in all directions.
All the attacks of the Red version do 1 heart of damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It is the boss version of the Maws.

• The Gate is the posthumous version of it.

• Despite its name, it behaves and looks more like a Horf, or a Psychic Horf than a Maw.

• Its fire attack could be a reference to Mega Man's leaf shield/attack.

• [Repentance] The visual appearance of the Red Champion version may be a reference to the 2Spooky item.

Mega Mush.title: Mega Mush
Mega Mush.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, gigantifies Isaac for 30 seconds, persisting between rooms and floors. While gigantic, Isaac gains the following effects:

• A 4x damage multiplier, +2 range, and -1.9 tears.

• Cannot take damage for the duration of the effect.

• Can destroy Objects, Obstacles, and Pitfalls when walking over them. This includes Metal Blocks and Key Blocks without using keys.

• Can break through normal doors, Secret Rooms, and any doors that require Bombs such as Clean Bedrooms, by walking into them.

• • Cannot break through Challenge Rooms, Boss Rooms, Mini-Boss Rooms, Curse Rooms, Sacrifice Rooms, or any doors that require Keys such as Shops. Bedrooms also cannot be broken back into if they are closed but no longer boarded up.

• Deals extremely heavy contact damage to enemies (80 per tick, or 2,400 per second).

• Contributes to the Fun Guy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using Mega Mush again while its effects are still active will add an additional 30 seconds to the current active time.

• Isaac's physical size, i.e. collision circle or "hitbox" is roughly doubled in radius when Mega Mush is active. This is the only item that can make Isaac tangibly larger than his starting size, as normal size ups can't increase the collision area beyond the default.

• Mega Mush will not negate the damage taken from the Mausoleum door and the Golden Battery. It is also possible to die this way.

• Non-tear based attacks such as Brimstone or Mom's Knife are overridden by normal tears while Mega Mush is active.

• The only exceptions are the melee attacks by The Forgotten, Tainted Samson and Berserk!, which have increased hitboxes.

• Isaac is unable to use the invulnerability effect to donate to Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars, since they will be destroyed on contact. Bomb Bums will also be destroyed by walking over them.

• Mega Mush can be obtained by using Spindown Dice on Knife Piece 1.

• If Isaac dies while giant, he will revive in his giant form if he has any revival items.

• Using Mega Mush as Tainted Lazarus will retain effect and time remaining upon flipping back to the form that used it.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 4.5 Volt: The contact damage dealt by Mega Mush will allow it to be recharged and used multiple times in the same room.

• Car Battery: Mega Mush's active time will be doubled to 60 seconds.

• Rock Bottom: Retains massive damage increase after Mega Mush's timer is up, though can make it nearly impossible to raise it afterwards without another use.

• Serpent's Kiss: Enemies killed with contact damage will frequently drop hearts.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues: Spawns a basic wisp.

• Keeper's Kin: Destroying rocks and blocks will allow Isaac to amass a lot of blue spiders.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mega Mush is based off of the Mega Mushroom from New Super Mario Bros., which would turn Mario giant, grant invulnerability, and allow him to defeat almost anything he touches.

• Originally in Antibirth, Mega Mush didn't gain charges while active, and was unlocked by defeating Mother (then known as The Witness) as every character on Hard Mode.

• Entering the Big chest in Mega Mush form triggers the credits 0.5 seconds faster than normal (tested by entering the Big Chest going from the same position to the beginning of credits and timed with scripts)

• The Mega Mush form makes Isaac's face look similar to Flash Isaac.

• Mega Mush, along with 1up!, Mini Mush, Magic Mushroom, and Super Bandage is one of the few items that make a unique sound upon pickup.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Activating Mega Mush before entering the Knife Piece 2 area will keep the effect active inside the chase area but Isaac will have his normal sized, followed with a huge shadow and will continuously stomp the ground, breaking everything in his way, even pushing away Mother's Shadow.
Bug note: If Isaac walks over a Teleport Pitfall while Mega Mush is active a visual bug will occur where the pitfall is destroyed and can no longer harm Isaac however its sprites still remain in the room. When Isaac reenters the room or exits and continues the run, the teleport pitfall works normally again.
Bug note: Using Mega Mush in combination with Suplex! makes you grab enemies and move them around until you leave the room. Doing this on any of the Ultra Harbingers or The Beast will make the enemy disappear and render you unable to move at all.
Bug note: Activating Mega Mush through Void will cause Isaac to visually revert to normal after leaving the room while still under the item's effects. If Isaac does not have flight, a stomping sound will play and the screen will shake constantly even if he is not moving.
Bug note: When Mega Mush times out and Isaac returns to normal size, he may occasionally appear to have no head. Isaac is unable to fire tears in this form and cannot interact with enemies or objects or pick up items. He also cannot interact with trap doors or Crawl Space entrances, causing softlocks. Going into an animation (e. g. by taking damage, using a pill, etc.), or exiting and continuing the run fixes this issue.

fields.description: Gigantifies Isaac for 30 seconds, increasing damage and range while lowering tears, granting invulnerability, and allowing Isaac to crush enemies and obstacles he walks on. The effect persists between rooms.

Mega Satan.title: Mega Satan
Mega Satan.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Mega Satan is a boss that appears in Chapter 6 (Chest, Dark Room), and is the final boss of Ending 16.

sections.heading: Unlock
sections.text:
Mega Satan is located behind the Golden Gate at the starting room of the Chest and the Dark Room. To unlock Mega Satan, the following criteria must be fulfilled:

• ??? or The Lamb must have been defeated once for the Golden Gate to spawn. Once that is done, the achievement "The Angels Await" will appear.

• Reaching the Dark Room to fight The Lamb or Mega Satan without having unlocked The Negative can be achieved by either:

• Taking the trapdoor in a Black Market from Sheol if one shows up.

• Taking the trapdoor in an I AM ERROR room while in Sheol.

• [Afterbirth onward] Taking a trapdoor that has a small chance to spawn from pressing a Reward Plate in a Secret Room in Sheol if it shows up.

• [Afterbirth onward] Using a Sacrifice Room 12 or more times.

• Once unlocked, the Golden Gate can be opened using one of the following methods:

• Defeating Uriel and Gabriel to obtain Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2, respectively. Collecting both pieces turns them into the Golden Key, which automatically opens the Golden Gate upon entering Chapter 6.

• • The Angels can be summoned by bombing an Angel Statue.

• • [Afterbirth onward] Sacrifice Rooms summon Uriel and Gabriel after stepping on the spikes for the 9th and 11th time, respectively.

• Using Dad's Key in the starting room.

• [Afterbirth onward] Using a Get out of Jail Free Card in the starting room. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Instructing Mr. ME! to unlock the door. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Using Sharp Key on the door. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Using a Soul of Cain in the starting room. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Activating Cracked Orb in the starting room. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Wisps generated by Book of Virtues + Mr. ME! opening the door on their own. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Wisps generated by Book of Virtues + Book of Secrets when destroyed in the starting room. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text: Passing through the Golden Gate and stepping onto the pentagram initiates the Mega Satan fight.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Mega Satan is accompanied by two hands, which serve as a barrier to protect him and an avenue for him to attack. His hands spread apart if Isaac gets close to him, and move together if Isaac moves away from him. Each hand has 600 HP, and destroying a hand deals 100 damage to Mega Satan. Each hand respawns 30 seconds after it’s destroyed.

Mega Satan has the following attacks:

• Closes his eyes and then fires one of several projectile patterns, including:

• 3-5 lines of blood projectiles. The angle these shots are fired at alternates between rotating clockwise and counterclockwise. The less lines of projectiles there are, the faster they travel and rotate.

• Spreads of brown projectiles that split into 4 smaller projectiles after traveling far enough, similarly to Cricket's Body.

• 2 spirals of blood projectiles that very rapidly rotate clockwise, creating semi-circular waves of projectiles.

• Rings of blood projectiles, fired in rapid bursts of 3.

• 2 spirals of blood projectiles that rotate clockwise at different speeds.

• 3 lines of blood projectiles that alternate between slowly curving right and left with every shot fired. The angle these lines of projectiles are fired out at alternates between slightly rotating clockwise and counterclockwise.

• Closes his eyes and then fires a Mega Blast laser straight down. His hands always fully spread apart while charging the laser, regardless of Isaac's position.

• The growl that telegraphs this attack is louder than usual, distinguishing it from his other attacks.

• Slams his head into the platforms 1-3 times, creating chaotic bursts of projectiles in all directions.

• Holds up one hand, then slams it at Isaac, creating a circular rock wave on impact. This attack can’t be used if both hands are currently destroyed.

• Slams both hands 3 times, alternating back and forth, creating rock waves that move towards the bottom of the screen. This attack can’t be used if either hand is currently destroyed.

• Destroying a hand during this attack prevents it from creating more rock waves.

• Mega Satan also spawns sets of mini-bosses to attack Isaac alongside him. These sets can be:

• Gluttony and Envy

• Sloth and Pride

• Wrath and Greed

• Lust

• The Hollow

• • These mini-bosses can be damaged by Mega Satan’s attacks. His laser deals 36 damage per tick, while all others deal 10 damage per hit.

• After taking enough damage, Mega Satan and his hands withdraw into the darkness behind him and become invulnerable. During this time, he spawns a wave of bosses or mini-bosses, which must be killed in order to make Mega Satan vulnerable again. The first waves of bosses begins after Mega Satan takes 750 damage, the second after 1,500 damage, and the third after 2,250 damage. He will withdraw but not spawn these waves if there are any remaining previously spawned bosses left. Only when the room is cleared does he spawn the following:

• Wave 1.1: Famine and Pestilence

• Wave 1.2: War and Death

• • There is a chance for all Horsemen to appear as their champion forms.

• Wave 2.1: Super Envy

• Wave 2.2: Super Lust and Super Wrath

• Wave 2.3: Super Sloth, Super Gluttony, Super Pride, and Super Greed

• Wave 3.1: Fallen Uriel

• Wave 3.2: Fallen Gabriel

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After taking 3,000 damage, Mega Satan sinks into the darkness and rises in his final phase as a skull. He no longer has his hands, nor does he spawn bosses; instead, he fires complex projectile patterns. Possible patterns include the ones from the first phase (with increased shot speed), plus:

• 2 spirals of projectiles that slowly rotate counterclockwise. The shots zig-zag as they travel outward.

• 2 lines of projectiles that alternate between curving left and right. These lines combine to create curving lines with a safe space that moves from the left of the arena to the right.

• Rings of projectiles, with every other wave fluctuating in speed as it travels.

• Many lines of projectiles that slowly curve to the left (if black) and right (if red); these lines create safe spaces to maneuver in that slowly shift to the right.

• Several lines of projectiles that slowly wiggle as they travel, similarly to Wiggle Worm. The angle these shots are fired at either rotates clockwise or alternates between rotating clockwise and counterclockwise.

• Many lines of projectiles that wiggle as they travel and slowly curve to the left (if black) and right (if red); these lines create unmoving safe spaces between them.

• Many lines of projectiles that spin as they travel, similarly to Ring Worm. The angle these shots are fired at constantly randomizes.

• These projectiles don’t travel far enough to reach the corners of the arena if Mega Satan isn’t close to that corner.

• Dense rings of projectiles that wiggle as they travel.

• Several lines of projectiles that make large zig-zags as they travel.

• Six lines of projectiles, half of which slowly curve to the left (if black) and right (if red). These lines create safe spaces that slowly move towards Mega Satan.

• Rings of projectiles that rotate clockwise (if red) and counterclockwise (if black) simultaneously.

• Several lines of projectiles that continuously converge onto each other.

• The projectiles used in these patterns can be colored black, red, brown, or silver, depending on which one is used. For some attacks, they instead appear as red or yellow fire.

As Mega Satan takes damage during this phase, his skull begins to crack before eventually shattering. After this final phase is defeated, the game ends and Ending 16 plays.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If The Void is unlocked, there is a [edition alternatives: baseline: 50%; Repentance+: 100%] chance that the game does not immediately end, and Mega Satan instead drops an ending chest along with a portal. Entering the chest ends the game and plays the cutscene, while entering the portal takes Isaac to The Void. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text:
These achievements don't exist in Rebirth.
[achievement text: Apollyon, Cry Baby, Red Baby, Green Baby, Brown Baby, Blue Baby, Lil' Baby, Rage Baby, Black Baby, Long Baby, Yellow Baby, White Baby, Big Baby, Noose Baby, Mort Baby, Bound Baby, Glowing Baby, Illusion Baby, Mega, Mega Chest, Queen of Hearts, Gold Pill, Black Sack, Charming Poop, Horse Pill, Crane Game, Hell Game, Wooden Chest, Wild Card, Haunted Chest, Fool's Gold, Golden Penny, Rotten Beggar, Golden Battery, Confessional, Golden Trinket]

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text:
Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to the players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

[Repentance] Damage Scaling was given to Mega Satan and his hands in Repentance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] Afterbirth added Completion Marks for defeating Mega Satan. There are no direct achievements needed for beating Mega Satan in Rebirth aside from unlocking Ending 16.

• Mega Satan does not have a health bar, making it difficult to determine how close he is to death. The other bosses that have no health bar are Mother and The Beast.

• Mega Satan is behind an invisible wall Isaac can't move past, making it impossible to inflict contact damage effects like Midas' Touch and The Virus to him, unless Isaac has an item allowing him to dash into Mega Satan's head (A Pony, Mars).

• Using Chaos Card on the first phase causes Mega Satan to go into his second phase instead of instantly killing him.

• This is because the first and second phase of the fight are actually two different enemies, and are shown as such in the bestiary.

• Mega Satan's hands count toward the mob cap total in the room, and prevent Greed, Sloth, and Fallen Gabriel from spawning enemies while they are undestroyed.

• With homing tears and The Ludovico Technique, the tear will be strongly attracted by the head even when it can't be targeted, making killing other enemies very hard.

• Unlocking the Golden Gate with the golden key and then restarting the floor with Forget Me Now or an I AM ERROR room will not cause the golden key to respawn and the Golden Gate will be closed again.

• [Repentance+] The Golden Gate will stay open after using Forget Me Now.

• [Repentance] Defeating Mega Satan will not revive dead co-op players if the portal to The Void appears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mega Satan's battle theme is titled Hericide, and is shared with regular Satan.

• Hericide means, “to kill one’s lord or master”.

• The Mega Satan room is actually a 1×2 room with only the lower half accessible.

• Mega Satan's second phase is referred to as "Mega Satan 2" in the bestiary.

• Mega Satan's second phase has unused sprites of skeletal hands.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Doing too much damage between phases will cause the game to play the normal "boss defeated" music throughout the rest of the fight.
Bug note: If Isaac has Mom's Box and Tick, Mega Satan will start the fight at 70% health, instantly starting the fight at the first wave of bosses. Afterwards, Mega Satan will be invisible the entire fight, and if Isaac moves to the upper half of the arena before Mega Satan dies, the game will softlock.

The Matriarch.title: The Matriarch
The Matriarch.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Matriarch is a boss added in Booster Pack #5 of The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth † that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb).

• [Repentance] Only in the Womb and the Scarred Womb. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
The Matriarch hops randomly around the room and performs the following attacks:

• Spawns two small Fistulas once she takes 140 damage, and 2 more every 100 damage afterward.

• She takes considerable knockback when this occurs.

• [Repentance] Reduced to 1 small Fistula for the first 2 spawns.

• Spawns a Fistuloid that chases Isaac, subsequently spawned Fistuloids orbit her. She can have up to a maximum of 4 spawned at once and does not spawn more until she has taken enough damage to release a small Fistula even if previous Fistuloids have been killed.

• Only 1 Fistuloid can chase Isaac at a time and they can occasionally swap when Isaac moves close to an orbiting Fistuloid. If the Fistuloid that chases Isaac is killed, one of the remaining ones stops orbiting the Matriarch and starts chasing Isaac.

• • The active chasing Fistuloid will not chase Isaac if he is too far away and returns to staying near the Matriarch until Isaac draws near.

• • Orbiting Fistuloids occasionally fire a projectile towards Isaac

• All Fistuloids spawned when there are 2 or more small Fistulas alive will orbit The Matriarch and one only becomes active when there is only one small Fistula left.

• [Repentance] The Matriarch loses 30 HP each time she spawns a Fistuloid. If this would cause her to change phases or spawn small Fistulas, The Matriarch is unable to create Fistuloids.

• Jumps and launches 8 Chubber projectiles in all directions, which rebound back to herself.

• Spews a large long-range blood projectile towards Isaac that leaves Red Creep on the ground, similar to Mr. Fred.

• The puddle of Creep left at the end of the projectile's path lasts longer than the Creep trail.

• This projectile can kill the chasing Fistuloid.
The Matriarch's Chubber and regular projectiles deal a whole heart of damage.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text: After taking 340 damage, the Matriarch rapidly spawns waves of glowing red Fistuloids that have 20 HP and quickly lose health, causing them to shoot their maggots almost immediately.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text: After taking enough damage, the Matriarch repeats the phase transition attack from Phase 1 to 2. During the rest of this phase The Matriarch no longer spawns Fistuloids and only uses the Chubber and projectile attacks.

sections.heading: Phase 4
sections.text:
When at low HP (after taking ~540 damage), The Matriarch's shell splits into a medium-sized Fistula, 2 small Fistulas and a Fistuloid, and she turns into a low HP Chub.

• Previously orbiting Fistuloids, including the one spawned, permanently orbit her Chub form, while previously active Fistuloids continue to chase Isaac.

• The Matriarch as Chub always spawns charging in a random direction, regardless of Isaac's position, before returning to the normal Chub pattern, similar to the Chargers spawned by Sloth.

• If the Matriarch eats a Bomb during her charge attack, she spits it back out at Isaac.

• Most bomb modifiers will still be present on the bomb, except for Bomber Boy.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Matriarch is unique in being twice as common than other Boss Room Bosses in the Scarred Womb boss pool, but only 1/4th as common as other Boss Room bosses in The Womb.

• This makes her the only boss in the game to have a boss weight higher than 1 on any floor.

• This also makes her the only boss to have a special weight which isn't an alternative variant of another boss on the same floor.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Matriarch appears to be a Chub stuck inside a Fistula. In this way, it also acts as a giant Fistuloid.

• As Chub also appears to be a grown up Charger, the Matriarch could be a Charger inside a Fistula that outgrew its capacity.

• The Matriarch is the only boss that was added in a Booster Pack.

Wooden Cross.title: Wooden Cross
Wooden Cross.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants a shield which nullifies a single hit once per floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The shield granted by Wooden Cross stacks with Holy Mantle, Blanket, and Dogma.

• [Before Repentance+] It does not, however, stack with the Holy Card; both are treated as the same shield.

• [Repentance+] Shield-type items stack in the following order:

• • Wooden Cross

• • Blanket

• • Holy Mantle

• • Holy Card

• • Dogma

• The shield of Wooden Cross has a higher priority than Holy Mantle or Blanket and will be lost first when hit.

• Entering Knife Piece 2 area with Wooden Cross gives Isaac Holy Mantle effect.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Wooden Cross: Gives Isaac two shields per floor.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Wooden Cross is based on this Steam Workshop trinket by Striped and cathery.

fields.name: Wooden Cross
fields.description: Grants a shield that negates the first damage taken once per floor.

Wooden Nickel.title: Wooden Nickel
Wooden Nickel.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, has a roughly 60% chance to drop a penny, nickel, or dime.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The exact chances are 50% for a penny, 5% for a nickel, 1% for a dime and 44% for nothing.

• [Repentance] The exact chances are 52% for a penny, 6% for a nickel, 2% for a dime and 40% for nothing.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This is a starting item for Keeper after he beats Isaac.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Sticky nickels and lucky pennies cannot be generated.

• [Repentance] The item only costs 10 coins when found in a Shop.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 9 Volt: Allows for infinite generation of coins in a room with enemies.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns tiny coin wisps in the middle ring. The wisps have a 50% chance to drop a random coin when destroyed.

• Car Battery: Two independent attempts of generating a coin, which can be of different values.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Wooden nickels are souvenir coins given out by some American banks. The adage "Don't take any wooden nickels" is a reminder to be cautious in one's dealings, since these coins have no monetary value.

• The Wooden Nickel is the name of the shop in another one of Edmund's games, The Legend of Bumbo.

fields.description: Has a roughly 50% chance to drop a Penny, Nickel, or Dime and a roughly 50% chance to do nothing.

Wooden Spoon.title: Wooden Spoon
Wooden Spoon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • +0.3 speed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In his first post-Repentance Lore Stream, Edmund McMillen revealed that the wooden spoon is inspired by the fact that during his childhood his parents would threaten to beat him with a wooden spoon.

• The Wooden Spoon granting a speed up is a nod to the act of running faster to try and escape the abuse.

• In this way, the Wooden Spoon is a counterpart to The Belt, which is also a speed-up item based on a specific object used by McMillen's parents to abuse him.

fields.description: +0.3 speed.

Worm Friend.title: Worm Friend
Worm Friend.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac a Nerve Ending familiar that burrows out of the ground to grab enemies for 4 seconds. Grabbed enemies take damage over time, are slowed, and are unable to move.

• Worm Friend deals 4 damage per tick (8 per second), for a total of 32 damage per grab.

• Worm Friend can target and restrain bosses in addition to normal enemies, even including endgame bosses such as Ultra Greed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Stain. [end edition note] 

• Enemies can avoid/escape being grabbed if they move fast enough, jump, or teleport.

• Worm friend must wait 5 seconds after losing/killing/releasing its target before it can attack another enemy.

• When playing as Tainted Lazarus / Dead Tainted Lazarus, entering a room with Worm Friend active and then using Flip to swap to the other character will keep Worm Friend active for the remainder of the room.

• When grabbing The Beast, the Beast is still able to dive down and appear on the other side, though no animation will be played for either diving down or up. This can be dangerous as there will be no warning of the Beast switching sides.

fields.description: Gives Isaac a Nerve Ending familiar that burrows out of the ground to grab and deal damage to enemies over time.

Wormwood.title: Wormwood
Wormwood.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Wormwood is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in [Repentance] Downpour and [Repentance] Dross.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Lunges from a pit towards Isaac, releasing 4 projectiles in the cardinal directions in the air. Wormwood then chases Isaac in a zig-zag pattern, before eventually returning to a pit.

• If Wormwood lunges out of a pit and lands on top of another large pit, he returns back into that pit.

• Eats any Bombs dropped in his path same as Chub while chasing Isaac, stunning him for a moment before dealing considerable damage.

• Partially emerges from a pit and fires a spray of disorganized projectiles at Isaac before re-submerging.

• At 33% health, Wormwood pierces the ground with his tail at Isaac's location with a short delay 3-6 times. Pits are created where Wormwood pierces the ground. Afterwards, Wormwood charges out from inside the left or right wall horizontal to Isaac's location while spawning 3 Small Leech. He then chases Isaac for a short duration before returning to a pit.

• Wormwood can never create a pit in a spot that would trap Isaac.

• Wormwood takes increasingly reduced damage after reaching 33% HP until he performs this attack and takes only 20% damage while performing this attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• His behavior and appearance is reminiscent to that of Pin, and is a variant of it.

• When encountered in the Dross, the color palette of Wormwood and his attacks are altered to fit the floor. Lil Blub also features this.

• His name is a reference to the Biblical Wormwood. It is a star that, according to the Book of Revelation, will fall on a third of the Earth's water, which will turn the water bitter and deadly to drink.

• In the Antibirth mod, Wormwood could be encountered as a degraded boss in the Corpse, and would take on a red color palette.

• The red color palette is still present in the files of Repentance, despite going unused.

Wrath.title: Wrath
Wrath.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Wrath is a mini-boss based on one of the Seven Deadly Sins.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Wrath wanders around the room randomly, occasionally standing still.

• Throws a Bomb towards Isaac if he is in line of sight and then attempts to run away from the bomb.

• Wrath takes only 20 damage (as opposed to the usual [Before Repentance] 60 / [Repentance] 100) from his own bombs.
Wrath deals a full heart of damage (both bombs and contact).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [edition anr] Occasionally, 2 regular Wraths appear in a Mini-Boss Room and the boss message will display "Isaac vs Super Wrath".

• Isaac's bombs and Epic Fetus missiles deal 200 damage to Wrath regardless of modifiers or damage stat.

• [Before Repentance] Wrath can drop Mr. Boom even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Sin]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Wrath's behavior, his room layouts (most of the time), and his appearance are references to the Bomberman series of games.

• The item Mr. Mega gives Isaac's head a similar appearance to Wrath's.

• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived from.

• Wrath's absence of eyes could be a reference to the expression "blind rage".

X-Ray Vision.title: X-Ray Vision
X-Ray Vision.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Opens Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms automatically.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] When in The Void, the entrances are not automatically opened if the room is not yet cleared. Re-entering the room once enemies are killed and/or Pressure Plates pressed will open the doors normally. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] When Book of Secrets is used while all mapping effects have been obtained, through book of secrets itself or another mapping effect, the X-Ray Vision effect is given.

• The flavor text "I've seen everything" could be a reference to Patrick Stewart's popular scene in the TV series "Extras".

• The cosmetic is a reference to 'X-ray Specs' sold as gag-gifts or on the back of Comic books in the 1960's and 70's.

• This item is used in Seeing Double.

fields.description: Reveals and opens all Secret Room and Super Secret Room entrances.

XIII - Death.title: XIII - Death
XIII - Death.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Deals 40 damage to all enemies in the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• XIII - Death's effect is identical to The Necronomicon's effect.

• [Afterbirth onward] Damage from the card bypasses damage scaling.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Deals 80 damage.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Deals 40 damage.

• A Missing Page / Missing Page 2: Deals +40 damage per copy.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text:
[achievement text: The Necronomicon] 

• Tarot Cloth: Reduces the number of uses to 2 to unlock.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Death is the thirteenth card of a Major Arcana set.

• Death is sometimes called the "Card with no name" with its number hidden for the bad omen it represents.

fields.name: XIII - Death
fields.quote: Lay waste to all that oppose you
fields.description: Triggers The Necronomicon effect, dealing 40 damage to all enemies in the room.

XIII - Death?.title: XIII - Death?
XIII - Death?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns one of the following for each enemy already killed in the current room:

• An orbital bone familiar (very common).

• A friendly Bony (uncommon).

• A friendly Black Bony (rare).

• A friendly Bone Fly (uncommon).

• A friendly Revenant (rare).

• A friendly Big Bony (uncommon chance only if the killed enemy has high enough HP)

• [edition rnr+] Spawning an enemy other than a Bony/Black Bony is only possible after dying at least once to said enemy on the save file.

• The chance to spawn Revenants is greatly increased in Mausoleum / Gehenna / Sheol / Dark Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• XIII - Death?'s effect is identical to that of Book of the Dead. Refer to its page to see in-depth interactions, detailed spawn chances, and notes about the bone orbitals.

• Up to 32 enemy deaths can be tracked in the room. Those locations are used as spawn points for bone orbitals and Bonies.

• If Isaac leaves the room, the points are reset. Using XIII - Death? will have no effect.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • To gain the most value out of XIII - Death?, it is recommended to leave enemies that can summon other enemies alive for longer, which will increase the number of dead enemies in one room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • XIII - Death's effect being to kill all enemies in the room, its antithetical effect is to raise them from the dead.

fields.name: XIII - Death?
fields.quote: May life spring forth from the fallen
fields.description: Creates a friendly Bony, Black Bony, Bone Fly, Revenant, Big Bony, or an orbital bone for each enemy killed in the current room.

XII - The Hanged Man.title: XII - The Hanged Man
XII - The Hanged Man.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants flight for the duration of the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] During the chase sequence following Knife Piece 2, XII - The Hanged Man may appear behind puzzle element and if reached, allows Isaac to skip an entire room by flying out of it. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • Flight can halve the cost of entering a Curse Room: entering a curse room while flying will not deal any damage. Exiting a curse room by its door will deal damage to Isaac in all cases.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Hanged Man is the twelfth card of a Major Arcana set.

• XII - The Hanged Man temporarily grants Transcendence, as evidenced by the given costume.

fields.name: XII - The Hanged Man
fields.description: Grants flight for the duration of the room.

XII - The Hanged Man?.title: XII - The Hanged Man?
XII - The Hanged Man?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac turns visually into Keeper for 30 seconds, with triple shot, -0.1 Speed and a tears multiplier of x0.51.

• Killing an enemy during the effect makes them drop a random Penny.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Once the 30 seconds are passed, Isaac reverts back to his normal state on the spot, he does not need to change rooms to remove the effect.

• Only enemies killed specifically by Isaac drop coins, those killed by Isaac's familiars, or environmental hazards such as Fire Places do not.

• Unlike many other on-kill drop resources effects, the coin drops do not suffer from diminishing returns on repeatedly spawned enemies.

• Further uses of XII - The Hanged Man? are additive, each adding 30 seconds to the effect's length.

• The card's effect persists in the Knife Piece 2 abandoned area.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • XII - The Hanged Man? is best used against enemies that spawn many weak enemies such as Eggy or The Duke of Flies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Doubles the effect's duration.

• Nuh Uh!: Slain enemies drop random pickups other than coins and Keys on Chapter 4 and beyond.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Sprinkler: Enemies killed by the sprinkler do drop coins.

fields.name: XII - The Hanged Man?
fields.quote: May your greed know no bounds
fields.description: Isaac turns visually into Keeper for 30 seconds, with triple shot and -0.1 speed. Killed enemies drop a random Penny.

XIV - Temperance.title: XIV - Temperance
XIV - Temperance.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a Blood Donation Machine near Isaac.

• In [mode: greed] Greed mode, spawns a Devil Beggar instead.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Using XIV - Temperance can, in rare cases, spawn the Blood Donation Machine directly on Isaac, forcing him to use it once. This happens more often if Isaac is against a wall and there are many more machines around him.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• Even if Isaac is short on HP to use the machines, they can still be blown up for more pickups.

• To save on bombs, it is recommended to use XIV - Temperance next to a tinted rock or a Secret Room's entrance, so that they can both be blown up by the same bomb.

• Since the machine/beggar prioritizes taking away Red Hearts, they can be placed next to a Curse Room and entered just after giving health to the machine/beggar. This halves the cost of potential Soul/Black Hearts for entering the Curse Room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Spawns 2 machines.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card + Car Battery : Spawns 4 machines.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Only spawns one machine when used with Blank Card.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Temperance is the fourteenth card of a Major Arcana set.

fields.name: XIV - Temperance
fields.quote: May you be pure in heart
fields.description: Creates a Blood Donation Machine near Isaac. [Afterbirth onward] Spawns a Devil Beggar instead in Greed mode.

XIV - Temperance?.title: XIV - Temperance?
XIV - Temperance?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Forces Isaac to eat several random pills (from the run's pill pool) in quick succession.

• Eaten pill types become identified.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Changing rooms while the pills are eaten does not stop the forced feeding of pills.

• If unlocked, Horse Pills can rarely appear in the sequence of force fed pills.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: Forces Isaac to eat 10 pills.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Acid Baby: Each eaten pill triggers Acid Baby's poison effect, dealing 10 damage per pill + extra poison damage.

• Endless Nameless: Only XIV - Temperance? itself can be copied, not the pill it generates.

• Lil Spewer: Each eaten pill changes Lil Spewer effect.

• Vurp!: Clones the last pill used.

fields.name: XIV - Temperance?
fields.description: Forces Isaac to eat 5 random pills in quick succession. Eaten pill types become identified.

XIX - The Sun.title: XIX - The Sun
XIX - The Sun.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Deals 100 damage to all enemies in the room.

• Reveals the map for the current floor, except for the Super Secret Room and Ultra Secret Room.

• Restores Isaac to full health.

• [Repentance] Removes [cu: Darkness] for the current floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance+] In multiplayer, XIX - The Sun heals all players. Similarly, Jacob and Esau both receive healing regardless of who used the card, even in singleplayer. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• XIX - The Sun is a powerful card thanks to its many effects.

• 100 damage is equivalent to a Bomb's damage and will kill most enemies.

• The revealed map allows for optimized charge management.

• The full heal can help against tough boss fights, and also to make better use of Blood Donation Machines, Devil Beggars, Sacrifice Rooms, etc.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Deals 200 damage to all enemies in the room.

• Tarot Cloth: Deals 400 damage.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Deals 200 damage when used with blank card.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Book of Secrets: The mapping provided by XIX - The Sun does not count as a mapping effect. The amount of times the Book of Secrets must be used before activating the X-Ray Vision effect remains the same.

sections.heading: Unlockable achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Blinding Baby]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Sun is the nineteenth card of a Major Arcana set.

fields.name: XIX - The Sun
fields.quote: May the light heal and enlighten you
fields.description: Restores Isaac to full health, deals 100 damage to all enemies in the room, and reveals the map for the current floor, except for the Super Secret Room and Ultra Secret Room. [Repentance] Removes [cu: Darkness] for the current floor.

XIX - The Sun?.title: XIX - The Sun?
XIX - The Sun?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• For the duration of the current floor:

• Grants Spirit of the Night and +1.5 Damage.

• Turns Isaac's red heart containers into Bone Heart.

• Causes a [cu: Darkness] that cannot be dispelled.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• When the effect reverts, all bone hearts remaining will be restored to heart containers.

• Actual bone hearts remain unchanged.

• If Isaac travels to the next floor with only empty temporary bone hearts (either by donation or with Crow Heart), he will die as his resulting health after reverting are only empty heart containers.

• The card's effect persists in the Knife Piece 2 abandoned area, allowing for easier completion of the chase sequence if flight was not acquired before.

• Picking up health-increasing items while XIX - The Sun?'s effect is active will add normal heart containers.

• Using XIX - The Sun? again will convert them into bone hearts.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• XIX - The Sun? negates the downsides of items that remove heart containers on pickup (such as Dead Cat and Brittle Bones) since it converts all heart containers into Bone Hearts.

• The bone hearts allow for more uses of the Sacrifice Room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Night Light: Curse of Darkness is not removed, regardless of whether Night Light is picked up before or after using the card. However, the visual effect is still lessened.

• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: As Tainted Lazarus, all effects of XIX - The Sun? except bone heart conversion and sprite change will disappear when flipping.
Bug note: Entering the Knife Piece 2 area while under the effects of XIX - The Sun? will cause a visual bug wherein Isaac will revert to his default appearance but still be capable of flight and spectral tears.

fields.name: XIX - The Sun?
fields.quote: May the darkness swallow all around you
fields.costume: Collectible Spirit of the Night appearance.png
fields.description: Gain Spirit of the Night and +1.5 Damage for the current floor. Turns Isaac's Red Heart into Bone Hearts, but they revert once the effect ends. Also causes [cu: Darkness] that cannot be dispelled.

XI - Strength.title: XI - Strength
XI - Strength.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants the effects of Magic Mushroom (minus the health restoration) for one room. The added Red Heart container is not removed if doing so would kill Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Using XI - Strength as ??? will give him a permanent Soul Heart instead of a temporary one.

• [edition anr] When Keeper has only one Coin Heart, he can use XI - Strength to gain a second one which is also permanent. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Both of the mentioned characters will lose the temporary health granted by XI - Strength.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• Since this effect only lasts for a room, it is preferably used against a boss.

• [Before Repentance] The heart container granted by XI - Strength cannot be used to purchase a devil deal. However, if Isaac has no other red heart containers to spend, then one granted by XI - Strength can be used this way. This also works if the devil deal costs 2 hearts, but Isaac only has 0 or 1 before activating the Strength card.

• [Repentance] The heart container granted by the card can now be spent for any purposes (e. g. devil deals, Potato Peeler, etc.) without any restrictions.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Doubles the stat increases, but the damage multiplier applies only once.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card + Car Battery : Quadruples the stat increases.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card : Does not double stat increases if used with Blank card.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text:
[achievement text: Huge Growth] 

• Tarot Cloth: The size increase is also doubled, contributing even more to Huge Growth's unlock.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Strength is the eleventh card of a Major Arcana set.

fields.name: XI - Strength
fields.description: Grants the effects of Magic Mushroom (minus the health restoration) for one room. The added Red Heart container is not removed if doing so would kill Isaac.

XI - Strength?.title: XI - Strength?
XI - Strength?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• All enemies (including bosses) in the room are weakened, becoming slightly slower, having slightly slowed projectile speed, and taking double damage from all sources for up to a minute or until the room is cleared. Afflicted enemies also have their damage reduced to half a heart.

• Causes a purple fog to cover the room; this effect is purely visual.

• The effect lasts up to one minute, or until the room is left.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Enemies spawned in later on, after Isaac has already used the card, will also be afflicted with weakness as long as the effect is active.

• Enemies' decreased damage applies even in the Womb stages and beyond.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• Addicted!: Makes Isaac take a full heart of damage even when XI - Strength? is active.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: When using XI - Strength?, any segmented bosses are able to be one-shot due to the way segmented bosses are handled.

fields.name: XI - Strength?
fields.description: All enemies in the room are weakened, becoming slightly slower and taking double damage from all sources. Affected enemies also have their damage reduced to half a heart. The effect lasts up to one minute, or until the room is left.

XVIII - The Moon.title: XVIII - The Moon
XVIII - The Moon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Teleports Isaac to the Secret Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Opens one wall inside the Secret Room, so Isaac can leave even if he doesn't have any Bombs.

• XVIII - The Moon cannot teleport Isaac to the Super Secret Room.

• Using XVIII - The Moon on a floor that doesn't have a secret room will teleport Isaac to a random room.

• When there are two secret rooms (via Fragmented Card and/or Luna), one of the two secret rooms is chosen at random to teleport Isaac into.

• XVIII - The Moon will always teleport to an unexplored secret room. If one has been explored, it will teleport to the other.

• When [curse: Maze] is active, using this card can teleport Isaac to a random room instead.

• XVIII - The Moon cannot appear in greed mode.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• XVIII - The Moon can be used to escape any room that locks down after taking its contents, like Challenge Rooms or Boss Rush, effectively "stealing" its contents without facing the imposed challenge.

• The hole in the wall created by teleportation will always be on the wall closest to Isaac when the card was used. This can be exploited to force the hole to appear between a secret room and a locked room of any kind. To do so, the target room must be between the secret room and Isaac.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Luna: Allows to access the Half Soul Heart and tears up immediately upon entering the floor, providing protection early on the floor.

• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: The Moon is the eighteenth card of a Major Arcana set.

fields.name: XVIII - The Moon
fields.quote: May you find all you have lost
fields.description: Teleports Isaac to the Secret Room.

XVIII - The Moon?.title: XVIII - The Moon?
XVIII - The Moon?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Teleports Isaac to the Ultra Secret Room.

• The pathway back to the normal rooms will be made of Red Rooms.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using XVIII - The Moon? on a floor that doesn't have an ultra secret room will teleport Isaac to a random room.

• When [curse: Maze] is active, using this card can teleport Isaac to a random room instead.

• XVIII - The Moon? cannot spawn in greed mode.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

fields.name: XVIII - The Moon?
fields.description: Teleports Isaac to the Ultra Secret Room. The pathway back to the normal rooms will be made of Red Rooms.

XVII - The Stars.title: XVII - The Stars
XVII - The Stars.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Teleports Isaac to the Treasure Room.

• [Repentance] If there is a Planetarium, teleports Isaac there instead. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] XVII - The Stars cannot appear in greed mode.

• Using XVII - The Stars on a floor that doesn't have a Treasure Room / Planetarium will teleport Isaac to a random room.

• When [cu: Labyrinth] is active, one of the two treasure rooms is chosen at random to teleport Isaac into.

• XVII - The Stars will always teleport to an unexplored treasure room. If one has been explored, it will teleport to the other.

• When [curse: Maze] is active, using this card can teleport Isaac to a random room instead.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• XVII - The Stars allows to access the Treasure Room / Planetarium without using a key.

• XVII - The Stars can be used to escape any room that locks down after taking its contents, like Challenge Rooms or Boss Rush, effectively "stealing" its contents without facing the imposed challenge.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: If the treasure room was unexplored before using XVII - The Stars, it will contain two choice item pedestals, as if More Options was active.

• It has no effect if it teleports to a planetarium.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Star is the seventeenth card of a Major Arcana set.

• This card is erroneously titled "The Stars"

fields.name: XVII - The Stars
fields.quote: May you find what you desire
fields.description: Teleports Isaac to the Treasure Room. [Repentance] If there is a Planetarium, teleports Isaac there instead. [end edition note]

XVII - The Stars?.title: XVII - The Stars?
XVII - The Stars?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Removes Isaac's oldest passive item (ignoring starting items) and creates 2 random item pedestals from the current room's item pool. Does nothing if Isaac has no items.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Removes 2 items and spawns 4.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Only removes one item and spawns two when used by Blank card.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues: Will be removed because it is also considered a passive item.

• Damocles: XVII - The Stars? does not remove the passive sword item created by Damocles.

• Eden's Blessing: Items granted by Eden's Blessing are considered starting items by the effect of XVII - The Stars?. Thus, only the first item picked up within the current run is removed.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Using XVII - The Stars? in DELETE THIS will cause the game to crash.

fields.name: XVII - The Stars?
fields.description: Removes Isaac's oldest passive item (ignoring starting items) and creates 2 random item pedestals from the current room's item pool. Does nothing if Isaac has no items.

XVI - The Tower.title: XVI - The Tower
XVI - The Tower.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Spawns 6 Troll Bombs, generally near the center of the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This card's active effect is identical to Anarchist Cookbook's.

• Although visually unchanged, all passive Bomb effect items affect the spawned Troll Bombs unless otherwise noted.

• The bombs spawn one after the other, meaning that they will also explode one after the other and can push each other around.

• If the room is exited before all bombs are spawned, the remaining bombs will not continue to spawn upon re-entering the room.

• Exiting the room will reset the troll bombs' fuses.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • By repeatedly exiting and re-entering the room, the bombs can be slowly pushed towards a tinted rock or a Secret Room's entrance.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Spawns 13 troll bombs.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Only spawns 6 troll bombs if used with blank card.

• Blasting Cap: All troll bombs have a 10% chance to drop a Bomb pickup when it explodes.

• Remote Detonator: The Troll Bombs generated will not explode until Remote Detonator is activated.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bomber Boy: Not recommended. The cross pattern explosion makes it very hard to avoid taking damage.

• Mr. Mega: No effect.

• Pyromaniac: Spawned bombs can be used for mass healing.

• Safety Scissors: Spawned troll bombs become bomb pickups.

• Scatter Bombs: Not recommended. Each Troll Bomb will spawn several smaller bombs upon exploding, making it very hard to avoid taking damage.

• [Repentance] No visual change can be seen with the Troll Bombs, but the smaller bombs have the sprite of the smaller normal bombs.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Tower is the sixteenth card of a Major Arcana set.

fields.name: XVI - The Tower
fields.description: Spawns 6 Troll Bombs randomly around the room.

XVI - The Tower?.title: XVI - The Tower?
XVI - The Tower?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Creates 7 clusters of random rocks and other obstacles. The pathways between exits can't be blocked.

• Every rock has a 3% chance to be a tinted rock.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • It is recommended to use XVI - The Tower? in a large room, as the clusters will be larger, increasing the chance of spawning tinted rocks.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: Spawns 14 rock clusters.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using XVI - The Tower? in a Boss Room may block all paths to the trap door, resulting in a softlock if no bombs or flight are available.
Bug note: Using XVI - The Tower? can also trap certain familiars over the rocks such as Lost Fly until Isaac leaves the room.

fields.name: XVI - The Tower?
fields.description: Creates 7 clusters of random rocks and other obstacles. Spawned clusters will often contain tinted rocks, with the possibility of finding more than one in the same room. The pathways between exits can't be blocked.

XV - The Devil.title: XV - The Devil
XV - The Devil.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants +2 Damage for the current room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• XV - The Devil's effect is identical to The Book of Belial.

• Unlike The Book of Belial, the card does not grant increased chances for Devil Rooms / Angel Rooms to appear after defeating a boss.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • Since this effect only lasts for a room, it is preferably used against a boss.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth / The Book of Belial / [Repentance] XV - The Devil: The effects stack, every copy of the effect gives +1 damage.

• Blood of the Martyr: Also applies a temporary x1,5 damage multiplier.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth / The Book of Belial / [Before Repentance] XV - The Devil: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Devil is the fifteenth card of a Major Arcana set.

fields.name: XV - The Devil
fields.quote: Revel in the power of darkness
fields.costume: Collectible The Book of Belial appearance.png
fields.description: Triggers The Book of Belial effect, granting +2 Damage for the current room.

XV - The Devil?.title: XV - The Devil?
XV - The Devil?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Invokes The Bible effect.

• Grants Flight and spawns a Seraphim familiar for 30 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Bible effect can kill Mom, Mom's Heart, and It Lives!. It will also kill Isaac if XV - The Devil? is used during the Satan fight.

• As such, killing Mom with XV - The Devil? can also unlock A Halo.

• The card's effect persists in the Knife Piece 2 abandoned area, allowing for easier completion of the chase sequence. However, the effect is likely to wear off before the end of the sequence.

• The Seraphim familiar disappears precisely 30 seconds after use, but the flight ability is removed only after exiting the room the 30 seconds were elapsed in.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

fields.name: XV - The Devil?
fields.quote: Bask in the light of your mercy
fields.description: Invokes The Bible (which can kill Mom). Grants Flight and spawns a Seraphim familiar for 30 seconds.

X - Wheel of Fortune.title: X - Wheel of Fortune
X - Wheel of Fortune.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a Slot Machine (75% chance) or Fortune Telling Machine (25% chance) near Isaac.

• [Repentance+] Also has a 1% chance to spawn a Crane Game. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• Even if Isaac is short on coins to use the machines, they can still be blown up for more pickups.

• To save on bombs, it is recommended to use X - Wheel of Fortune next to a tinted rock or a Secret Room's entrance, so that they can both be blown up by the same bomb.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Spawns 2 machines.

• Each machine can be any of the two types.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card + Car Battery: Spawns 4 machines.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Only spawns one machine when used with Blank Card.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Wheel of Fortune is the tenth card of a Major Arcana set.

fields.name: X - Wheel of Fortune

Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the monster; co-op babies; Co-op; items that follow Isaac; Familiar] 

Babies slowly float towards Isaac, occasionally shooting a single projectile towards him. They can also occasionally teleport to anywhere in the room.

sections.heading: Angelic Baby
sections.text: Angelic Babies are variants of Babies that fire 3 projectiles at Isaac in a spread instead of 1. They also teleport more often, usually near Isaac.

sections.heading: Small Angelic Baby
sections.text:
Small Angelic Babies behave identically to Angelic Babies but have less health and shoots only one projectile instead of three.

They are exclusively spawned by Holy Mulligans.

sections.heading: Wrinkly Baby
sections.text: Wrinkly Babies slowly move towards Isaac similar to regular Babies, but while approaching him, they may dash towards him at high speed until they hit either a wall or Isaac and then subsequently fire three projectiles in his direction once they stop dashing. If Isaac approaches them after they've performed their previous attack, they will move back from Isaac and fire three projectiles at him without dashing for as long as Isaac continues to follow them, although they will resume their chase and dashing attack if Isaac then moves far from them. They are unable to teleport.

sections.heading: Imp
sections.text: Imps slowly float towards Isaac, occasionally firing 5 projectiles at Isaac in quick succession and can also occasionally randomly teleport around the room. They move slightly to try to avoid Isaac's tears.

sections.heading: Baby Begotten
sections.text:
Baby Begottens float toward Isaac, attempting to avoid Isaac's tears as it approaches. After getting close to him, it lines itself up with him in the closest cardinal direction and fires a thin short-range Brimstone laser at him, propelling itself in the opposite direction.

Despite their namesake and visual similarities to Begottens they have no similarities in behavior.

sections.heading: Unborn
sections.text: Unborn fly towards Isaac in a circular pattern, and will periodically teleport near Isaac on another side of him.

Ultra Death.title: Ultra Death
Ultra Death.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Ultra Death is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance and is the last of the Ultra Harbingers fought before The Beast in Home.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Unlike the other Ultra Harbingers, Ultra Death has only one phase and has three attacks which he cycles through indefinitely:

• Summons a rectangle of 11 Ultra Death Scythes which close in towards Ultra Death's position and continue in the same direction until disappearing off screen. Ultra Death uses this attack 3 times in a succession.

• Flies off screen, then reappears travelling slowly while summoning waves of Ultra Death Heads which move up and down across the screen in the same direction. At the end of the attack, the skulls freeze in place and Ultra Death summons three harmless scythes which spin outwards, destroying the skulls.

• Immediately after the previous attack, the screen darkens and Ultra Death disappears into the darkness. Ultra Death appears next to Isaac and swings his Scythe before disappearing again, darkening the screen with each attack. This attack is repeated 4 times, afterwards, the screen returns to normal and Ultra Death reappears.

• His position during this attack can be indicated by a faint glowing red eye.

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Ultra Death, like the other Ultra Harbingers is an upgraded version of his regular counterpart, Death.

• Unlike the others, he has the greatest variation in behavior from regular Death- notably the lack of a second phase where he dismounts, while each of the Ultra Harbingers share their specific second phase transiton with their regular counterpart. (Famine losing everything except his head, Pestilence only losing their head and War losing their horse)

• The visual similarity of Ultra Death's horse and a scythe, which the regular counterpart has, is made more apparent with the body of Ultra Death's horse having a curve (like farming scythes have) and sharing the same wood texture & colour as the handle of Ultra Death's scythe. 

• The violin heard in the section of Revelations 13:1 that plays during Ultra Death's fight is performed by Carla Kihlstedt, the voice actor for Mom.

• Ultra Death can be seen facepalming in the background after killing Ultra War.

• The wave of Ultra Death Heads loosely resembles one of Conquest's attack.

• This could be compensation for Conquest's lack of appearance despite his Harbinger role.

• Ultra Death's glowing eye during the darkness attack could be a reference to the Terminator series, as Ultra Death bears some resemblance to the Terminators seen in those movies.

• Ultra Death's glowing eye is actually invisible during the whole fight but active the whole time, and becomes visible when the room is darkened. Using XIX - The Sun? darkens the arena, making it visible.

• Ultra Death is male.

Ultra Famine.title: Ultra Famine
Ultra Famine.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Ultra Famine is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance and is the first of the Ultra Harbingers fought before The Beast in Home.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Ultra Famine has two attacks which it alternates between:

• Matches Isaac's vertical position and charges off screen. Appears from a random side of a screen and fires a spread of five lines of five projectiles towards Isaac that lose speed before disappearing again. This attack is repeated five times.

• Moves across the screen from one side of the screen to the other, oscillating between the top and bottom of the screen. Ultra Famine spawns a swarm of Ultra Famine Fly behind himself as he moves. Each fly charges towards Isaac when he is close and continue to move in the same direction until disappearing off screen.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After dropping to 1/3rd of his max health, Ultra Famine loses his horse and body becoming only a head. In this phase, Ultra Famine only has one attack which he performs continuously from the center of the screen:

• Continuously fires projectiles in a counter-clockwise pattern, while simultaneously firing 6 bursts of projectiles outwards with alternating orientations.

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Ultra Famine, like the other Ultra Harbingers is an upgraded version of his regular counterpart, Famine.

• Unlike his lesser counterpart, Ultra Famine has no red pupils.

• Ultra Famine is male.
