Ultra Greed.title: Ultra Greed
Ultra Greed.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Ultra Greed is the final boss of Greed Mode and Ending 18.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Ultra Greed is fought in a unique vertical double-size room with golden Boss Room doors on all 4 walls in regular positions.
When Isaac enters the boss room, Ultra Greed starts out hanging on a noose before he abruptly cuts it off and lands on the ground. Ultra Greed cannot be damaged until he drops to the ground. Ultra Greed then performs a variety of attacks in addition to wandering around the room:

• Stomps on the ground 4 times, spawning a Keeper with each stomp. Only 4 Keepers can be alive at once.

• Charges at Isaac when he is in line of sight.

• Shoots either 3-5 coin projectiles in a spread from his mouth, or a cluster of coin projectiles, similar to Monstro.

• Ultra Greed does not perform this attack if Isaac is far enough away.

• Spins around the room, firing coin projectiles in random directions.

• If Isaac is too close to Ultra Greed, he performs a spin, kicking Isaac away in the process.

• Stops moving and rotates his eyes in a slot machine manner. If both eyes land on the same symbol, he then spawns multiple Ultra Greed Coins of the same symbol.

• If the two symbols on Ultra Greed's eyes don't match, he spawns Ultra Greed Coin (Spinner).

• If there are too many monsters/coins alive at once, Ultra Greed assumes a defensive stance. While blocking, Ultra Greed takes much less damage from Isaac's attacks, and maintains this state until most of the monsters/coins have been killed.

All of Ultra Greed's attacks deal a full heart of damage and cause Isaac to drop coins on hit. If he walks over any coins on the ground, he collects them, healing him for 4.375 HP each. Doing so also makes him slightly more aggressive. Heart coins also make the boss angrier.

When Ultra Greed has low health, he turns red, which increases his attack speed and movement speed. This effect also occurs if Ultra Greed is healed by enough Heart Ultra Greed Coins, although only providing a temporary effect.

• The scaling speed increases if Everything is Terrible 2!!! has been unlocked by using the Greed Donation Machine.

When Ultra Greed's health bar is depleted, he turns into a golden statue and drops the end chest and the Greed Donation Machine. If in Greedier Mode, he instead begins his second phase.

sections.heading: Ultra Greedier
sections.text:
Greedier Mode is a mode added in Afterbirth ♰. It is unlocked by depositing 500 coins in the Greed Machine.

Playing on Greedier Mode gives Ultra Greed a second phase where his gold statue form comes to life. This phase is known as Ultra Greedier, and is the final boss of Ending 19. Additionally, he performs several new attacks:

• The coin projectiles that Ultra Greedier shoots from his first phase now explode upon contact.

• Slams his fists into the ground, creating explosions where he slams and causing golden Brimstone lasers to fire from the golden Boss Room doors that surround the room.

• They can either come out from one pair of doors at a time or from all of them at once.

• Jumps into the air towards Isaac's position, dropping exploding coins down below while travelling. Upon landing, rock waves are sent in various directions.

• Stomps on the ground four times, causing a slew of Bomb Coins to rain from the ceiling.

• These coins can spawn a single Penny when they explode, providing both healing for Ultra Greedier and extra coins for Isaac.

After defeating Ultra Greedier, he explodes, dropping a Penny and turning the entire room into solid gold. It is at this point that the end chest and the Greed Donation Machine spawn.

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to the players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• After Key Coins appear, using A Card Against Humanity causes spawned Gapers to be stuck and, as long as they're alive, Ultra Greed will not attack.

• Having E. Coli (and perhaps other contact-based collectibles) is a fast way of disabling the Bomb, Key, or Heart Coins because they don't do contact damage. However, unmarked coins do.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Except for direct contact and the Brimstone lasers, all of Ultra Greedier's attacks only do explosive damage. Therefore having Pyromaniac or Host Hat makes this phase of the fight much easier to survive.

• [Repentance] The rock waves after Ultra Greedier's jump attack are no longer considered explosive damage.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The entire room will be turned to gold when he dies. This is due to a special shader that turns on in the room when he dies, so using effects like A Card Against Humanity or XVI - The Tower? will make the grid entities spawned look golden.

• Any poop spawned in the Ultra Greedier fight, destroyed or not, will respawn as Golden Poop when Ultra Greedier dies and turns the room into gold.

• [Repentance] This effect is only visual, they act like regular Poop when destroyed despite the gold color.

• If you manage to spawn a Sticky Nickel (possibly through a D20) Ultra Greed may station himself over it and no longer move around the arena.

• Eraser can allow the Ultra Greedier phase to be skipped if you use it on Ultra Greed when he has 15 or less HP.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Ultra Greedier has an unused sprite of him hanging from the ceiling similar to Ultra Greed when first entering the room.

• This special sprite can still be seen if Ultra Greedier is summoned with console commands.

• Ultra Greed can pick up coins even after being turned into a statue.

• Ultra Greed is the second Ultra deadly sin boss to appear in the game, behind Ultra Pride, but is the first to appear as a final boss.

• Teleporting out of the boss room after defeating Ultra Greed will cause the statue to disappear.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The name "Ultra Greedier" comes from the bestiary.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] In Greedier Mode, when Ultra Greed is defeated for the first time, he will stay as a gold statue for 10 seconds before he begins to break out and turn into Ultra Greedier. On future runs, he will begin to break out immediately instead.

• Prior to Booster Pack #5, Ultra Greed could spawn Blisters along with Keepers.

• There is an unused form of Ultra Greed in the game's sprite sheets, with a goatee style beard and a less fit body build. He was supposed to be a boss that represented Tyrone Rodriguez, similar to how Ultra Pride represents Edmund McMillen and Florian Himsl. This spritesheet can be found in the file folder "delirium forms".

• The Korean version of the game still has some images with the beard used in the game.

• According to Edmund in a twitter AMA, the other deadly sins were supposed to have ultra forms as well, but were scrapped for unknown reasons.

• The prevalence of greed and money as a theme could represent how Isaac's Dad's poor spending habits, as heard in the dialogue of the Ascent, have affected Isaac.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Ultra Greed is defeated at the bottom of the room, the ending chest will spawn incorrectly, causing it to be unreachable.
Bug note: If Ultra Greed is hit by a Chaos Card after being turned into gold, his death animation will replay and cause a lot of gut splatter.
Bug note: If the player dies and respawns outside of the room while Ultra Greed is rolling his eyes like a slot machine, the slot machine sound will play continuously until the game is paused.

Ultra Pestilence.title: Ultra Pestilence
Ultra Pestilence.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Ultra Pestilence is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance and is the second of the Ultra Harbingers fought before The Beast in Home.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Ultra Pestilence spawns with a swarm of Ultra Pestilence Fly that hover around himself for the entire duration of the fight. He has two attacks which he alternates between:

• Launches a large Ipecac projectile at Isaac's position. Upon landing in the lava below, it creates a pillar of poisonous cloud, creates a burst of projectiles that shoot upwards from the lava, and creates 3 additional projectiles that shoot upwards from the lava on both sides of the pillar. This attack is repeated 3 times.

• Fires a large maggot from his eye which flies across the screen, wrapping around three times. Before it completes a fourth wrap, it reverses direction, wrapping around three more times before re-entering Ultra Pestilence's eye. Where the Maggot comes from depends on how many screen wraps it has done:

• After the first screen wrap, the maggot aims at the top third of the arena.

• After the second, third, and fourth screen wrap (the maggot reverses directions after the third), it aims at Isaac.

• After the fifth screen wrap, it aims at the top third of the arena again.

• After the sixth and final screen wrap, it aims at Ultra Pestilence, re-entering his eye when he hits them.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After dropping to 40% health, Ultra Pestilence loses his head, begins to periodically spawn Ultra Pestilence Flies around himself, and uses two attacks:

• At the start of this phase, Ultra Pestilence's steed spawns an Ultra Pestilence Fly Ball which follows Isaac. Attacking this ball of flies spawns additional flies. Ultra Pestilence performs this attack one more time after dropping to 20% health.

• Fires a spray of projectiles from his empty neck, which rain down on the area in front of it.

sections.text:
• Little Horn or Euthanasia can kill the maggot projectile.

• Friendly Ball can be used on the maggot projectile.

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Ultra Pestilence, like the other Ultra Harbingers is an upgraded version of its regular counterpart, Pestilence.

• Upon death, Ultra Pestilence explodes into Small Maggots that rain down harmlessly into the lava.

• Ultra Pestilence is the only Ultra Harbinger with less than 2000 health, instead having 1800.

• However, the Ultra Pestilence Fly Ball he summons (which has 200 HP) equates his total health to 2000.

Ultra Pride.title: Ultra Pride
Ultra Pride.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Ultra Pride is a mini-boss and one of the Ultra Sins. Ultra Pride resembles Edmund McMillen, while the Ultra Pride Baby resembles Florian Himsl.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Ultra Pride differs from its normal counterparts by having attacks more similar to Super Sloth and a Baby than Pride. They perform attacks independently of each other.

Edmund wanders randomly around the room and performs one of two attacks:

• Shoots out 3 arcing homing projectiles.

• Throws out a horizontal line of Green Creep if Isaac is to his left or right.

• The line is cone-shaped and will always be wider to the right end, no matter which direction it was sent from.
Ultra Pride Edmund deals a whole heart of contact damage.

Florian slowly floats towards Isaac and can randomly teleport around the room.

• If Isaac is close, he periodically shoots out a homing projectile that deals one full heart of damage.

• Florian has [Before Repentance] 25 HP / [Repentance] 30 HP.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Edmund is defeated last, Ultra Pride drops The Left Hand, regardless of whether or not it has already appeared during that run. If this is the first time it is defeated, the Left Hand achievement is also unlocked.

• If Florian is defeated last, there is a 25% chance to spawn [Before Repentance] a A Treasure Room item / [Repentance] the Eternal D6 if it has been unlocked.

• [Before Repentance] Florian is treated as an ordinary Baby by the game, so it still has a chance to spawn as an Angelic Baby. This will override its unique appearance.

• [Afterbirth onward] In one room, two Edmunds can spawn instead of one of each.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Left Hand]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• They are randomly encountered as an alternate version of Pride.

• Despite this, Edmund's attacks mirror Super Sloth's more than Pride's.

• • This is supported by both Edmund and Super Sloth having the same entity ID of 46.

• Ultra Pride may be a reference to the book Frankenstein, in which Victor Frankenstein creates a living being he deems a monster. The creation of life is often considered the ultimate act of pride. In this case, Florian takes the place of Frankenstein and Edmund takes the place of the monster.

• It might also be a reference to the fact that inserting yourself into your own video-game is often seen as narcissistic.

• Ultra Pride's first appearance was in the final update to the flash version of The Binding of Isaac and was believed by fans to symbolize Edmund's "Ultimate Pride" at both the success of, and the fact he had finally finished development on The Binding of Isaac.

• Florian Himsl was the programmer of the first The Binding of Isaac game.

• Ultra Pride (Edmund) is one of five enemies (four without Repentance, three without Afterbirth+) in the game that uses Creep as projectiles, the others are Conjoined Fatty, Bloaty, Meatball, and The Thing.

• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived from.

• [Repentance] Florian dropping the Eternal D6 is a reference to the Eternal Edition of the original game, which was a free update developed by Florian.

• According to Edmund in a twitter AMA, the other deadly sins were supposed to have ultra forms as well, however they were scrapped for unknown reasons. [end edition note] 

• Edmund dropping/unlocking the Left Hand trinket may be a reference to how Edmund is left handed in real life.

Ultra War.title: Ultra War
Ultra War.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Ultra War is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance and is the third of the Ultra Harbingers fought before The Beast in Home.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Ultra War charges in from the side of the screen and has two attacks which he alternates between:

• Throws a large, Giga Bomb that deals contact-damage and explodes mid-air in a cross pattern that spreads across the entire screen, similar to Bomber Boy Bombs. The Bomb also releases a burst of 12 lines of 4 projectiles outward when it explodes. This attack is repeated 3 times.

• Charges off-screen, then wraps around the bottom of the screen 3 times, creating 4 to 6 pillars of harmless light in alternating positions across the screen, from which large lava projectiles launch upwards with staggered timing.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Ultra War dismounts from his hobby-horse and has two new attacks which it alternates between:

• Chases Isaac, then lunges diagonally downwards in Isaac's direction. After, Ultra War releases 4 streams of fire in the cardinal directions as well as a small burst of slower moving fires in all directions. This attack is repeated 2 times.

• Lunges diagonally downwards while holding a large bomb which explodes in a cross pattern that spreads across the entire screen. Ultra War then bounces across the sides of the screen 3 times while moving upwards before plummeting into the lava below. When Ultra War emerges, he creates 4 to 6 large lava projectiles that launch upwards with staggered timing.

• Upon death, Ultra War explodes, which can damage Isaac at close range.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Isaac has the Safety Scissors, the Giga Bombs Ultra War throws will be defused and fail to explode, after which they can be picked up or left to fall into the lava.

• Ultra War's Giga Bombs can be killed by Euthanasia shots.

• The lava projectiles can be slowed and knocked down with certain slowing items such as Censer and high knockback tears.

sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Ultra War, like the other Ultra Harbingers is an upgraded version of his regular counterpart, War.

Umbilical Cord.title: Umbilical Cord
Umbilical Cord.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] When Isaac's health is brought down to half a red heart and no soul hearts, a Little Steven familiar spawns for the current room.

• [Repentance] When Isaac enters a room and has half a red heart or less, a Little Steven familiar spawns and will remain until red health is restored to above a Half Red Heart, disappearing after entering another room.

• Characters which cannot acquire red heart containers in any way will always have a Little Steven.

• [Repentance] When Isaac takes damage, there is a chance to spawn a Gemini familiar for the current room. This effect is stackable.

• The chance to spawn the familiar depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: 30% + \mathit{Luck} \times 2%.

• • At 0 luck the chance is 30%, maxing out at 100% at 35 luck.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • This trinket has a chance to drop from destroying polyps (outside of Corpse).

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either spawns the Little Steven familiar if Isaac enters a room with a red heart or less. Having both spawns it if Isaac has 1 and a half red heart or less.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • An umbilical cord is a tube that is connected to a fetus via the placenta and is used to give nutrients, blood, and oxygen to the growing child.

fields.name: Umbilical Cord
fields.description: When brought down to only a Half Red Heart, spawns a Little Steven familiar for the current room. [Repentance] Adds a high chance to spawn a Gemini familiar for the current room after taking damage.

Mom's Underwear.title: Mom's Underwear
Mom's Underwear.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] +5.25 range.

• [Repentance] +2.5 range.

• [Before Repentance] +0.5 tear falling speed.

• [Repentance] Spawns 3-6 Blue Flies when picked up.

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] This item has a 1% chance to spawn when bombing Mom's Dressing Table. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method. [end edition note]

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] +5.25 range, +0.5 tear falling speed.
[Repentance] +2.5 range. Spawns 3-6 Blue Flies on pickup.

Mom's Wig.title: Mom's Wig
Mom's Wig.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac now spawns friendly Blue Spiders when firing tears.

• Heals Isaac for 1 Red Heart upon pickup.

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] This item has a 1% chance to spawn when bombing Mom's Dressing Table. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method. [end edition note] 

• The blue spider spawning chance depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac{1}{20 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 2 \right \rfloor}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 5%, maxing out at 100% at 9.5 luck.

• The spiders are spawned when Isaac is shooting, and up to 5 spiders can be spawned at the same time. More spiders can be spawned if the previous ones died.

• [Before Repentance] This item does not work for Lilith since Incubus tears do not count as her tears.

• Spiders can still be spawned in rooms without enemies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Before Afterbirth+] Brimstone / Chocolate Milk / Cursed Eye / Mom's Knife / Monstro's Lung / Tech X: Charging an attack spawns spiders in rapid succession.

• Epic Fetus / The Ludovico Technique / Marked: Moving the tear/crosshair around will spawn spiders rapidly.

• Fish Tail: Doubles the total amount of spiders that can be spawned at the same time, up to a total of 10.

• Hive Mind: Doubles the limit to 10 spiders, in addition to boosting the damage of spiders per the item's base effect.

fields.description: Adds a chance to spawn Blue Spiders when firing tears. Restores 1 Red Heart.

Money = Power.title: Money = Power
Money = Power.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds 0.04 damage for every Penny Isaac has.

• The damage caps at +3.96 Damage at 99 coins.

• Though Isaac can still collect coins if he already has 99, he will not gain any damage bonus from them.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Deep Pockets: Increases maximum damage bonus from Money = Power. The damage caps at +39.96 Damage at 999 coins. [end edition note] 

• A Dollar: Immediately maxes out damage bonus.

• A Quarter: Increases damage by 1 per 25 coins.

• Greed's Gullet: Isaac will gain health and damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Diplopia: Damage bonus doesn't stack.

• Spindown Dice: Turns into The Wafer when rerolled.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The name of the item is a reference to the popular saying "Money is power".

• This item is used in PAY TO PLAY.

• For a few weeks, a hidden message under Money = Power's icon in the game's files read "where are you".

• The message was part of an alternate reality game and could be seen on the collection page, representing Isaac asking for his father.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Money = Power was unlocked by beating Mom's Heart eight times.

fields.description: Increases damage by 0.04 for every Penny Isaac has, up to +3.96 damage at 99 coins.

Mongo Baby.title: Mongo Baby
Mongo Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar who follows Isaac around and cycles between the tears of Isaac's other familiars.

• If no familiars are present, Mongo Baby will fire normal tears that each do 3.5 damage.

• [Before Repentance] Mongo Baby shoots once every half second.

• [Repentance] Mongo Baby shoots at the same rate as Isaac at base tears, 2.73 tears per second.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Mongo Baby can only copy the familiars listed below:

• Brother Bobby

• Demon Baby

• Freezer Baby

• Ghost Baby

• Harlequin Baby

• Little Gish

• Little Steven

• Rainbow Baby

• Robo-Baby

• Rotten Baby

• Sister Maggy

• Mongo Baby will not copy familiars spawned by Cambion Conception or Monster Manual.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Mongo Baby having [edition alternatives: baseline: 4th; Repentance+: 6th] priority.

• Despite bearing similarity to previously mentioned familiars, Mongo Baby will not copy the effects of:

• Seraphim

• Buddy in a Box

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Demon Baby: Mongo Baby behaves like Demon Baby, and will no longer shoot its regular tears unless Isaac has another compatible familiar. If Isaac has other familiars that Mongo Baby can mimic, its behavior alternates between Demon Baby’s and the other familiars’.

• Lil Loki: Mongo Baby's tears will become red, but Mongo Baby will not fire in four directions.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • According to Edmund, this item is a bunch of babies cut up and put back together to create the "mongoest" baby.

fields.name: Mongo Baby
fields.description: Spawns a familiar who follows Isaac around and cycles between the tears of Isaac's other familiars.

Monkey Paw.title: Monkey Paw
Monkey Paw.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish: The Left Hand]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• If Isaac has half a heart or less after taking damage, this trinket drops a Black Heart.

• The effect can trigger up to three times, after which the trinket will disappear.

• The fingers stuck out by the paw will change to display the number of triggers left.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The effect can trigger more than once in the same room.

• The effect does not trigger when picked up at half a heart or less.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If Gulped or smelted, its effect still only triggers 3 times, then disappears.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy allows Monkey Paw to drop an extra black heart.

• Scapular: If Scapular's effect is triggered, the Soul Heart awarded will not cancel the effect of Monkey Paw.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is a reference to the supernatural short story The Monkey's Paw by W.W Jacobs. The title artifact could grant three wishes, but they frequently carried a most unpleasant price.

fields.name: Monkey Paw
fields.description: If Isaac has half a heart after taking damage, drops a Black Heart. The effect can trigger up to three times, after which the trinket will disappear.

Monster Manual.title: Monster Manual
Monster Manual.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
When used, a random familiar will be spawned from the following:

• [Before Repentance] Familiars spawned by Monster Manual last for the current room.

• [Repentance] Familiars spawned by Monster Manual last for the rest of the floor.

• Familiars generated by Monster Manual do not contribute toward transformations.

• Contributes to the Bookworm transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• It can spawn familiars not yet unlocked.

• If Cube of Meat or Ball of Bandages are spawned and Isaac already has either of those items, the level of these items will increase while the effect is active.

• Using Monster Manual is a good method to unlock achievements related to Super Meat Boy and Super Bandage Girl.

• Using Monster Manual and enough Lil' Battery, Super Meat Boy and Super Bandage Girl can both be achieved in the same run.

• If Isaac does not already have the Cube of Meat or Ball of Bandages, Monster Manual can spawn a level 2 Cube of Meat or Ball of Bandages in one use.

• Mongo Baby will not copy familiars spawned by Monster Manual.

• Familiars spawned by Monster Manual cannot be rerolled into other items by D4 or D100.

• Box of Friends will not duplicate familiars spawned by Monster Manual.

• Tinytoma orbitals will persist between floors until they are all destroyed. They will not respawn outside of the floor they were generated in.

• [Repentance] The familiars summoned by Monster Manual are items with a monstermanual item tag.

• Tainted Lazarus: If dead Tainted Lazarus has used Monster Manual, but living Tainted Lazarus progresses to the next floor (or vice versa), familiars from the previous floor are not removed. Upon exiting the game, or moving to the next floor as either character, any familiars retained this way are lost, meaning familiars cant be kept at most 1 extra floor.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the inner ring. The given wisps function similarly to familiars given by Buddy in a Box.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Sacrificial Altar: Summoned familiars can be sacrificed since they persist for the entire floor, even if Monster Manual isn't currently being held.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, due to a typing error this item was called "Monster Manuel". This has been corrected for Rebirth.

• [Repentance] Monster Manual may sometimes display the misspelled name when picked up.

• Monster Manual is a direct reference to Dungeons & Dragons. Its appearance in the game closely resembles the Advanced Dungeons & Dragons First Edition Monster Manual.

• [Repentance] The item being in the Devil Room pool is likely a reference to the moral panic surrounding the game in the 1980s.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: [edition rnr+] Monster Manual will fail to spawn a familiar if it attempts to spawn Halo of Flies.

Monsters.title: Monsters
Monsters.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Monsters refers to the many antagonistic creatures and entities Isaac can encounter throughout the game.

Most monsters (with few exceptions) damage Isaac by either touching him or shooting him with projectiles. Less frequently, monsters spawn additional, lesser monsters, spread creep, or attempt to affect Isaac's movement. Some monsters have scaled health depending on which floor they're encountered. Along with the more common variety of monsters, champion versions can be found lurking about; these monsters are often like their common counterparts, but have a color tint or size change, more health, and drop basic pickups on death. There are also champion versions of most bosses.

There are 336 naturally spawning monsters in total. 40 of them were added in Afterbirth, 21 were added in Afterbirth † (13 were added in Booster Packs) and 140 were added in Repentance. Almost all of these naturally spawning entities are featured in the [Afterbirth+ onward] Afterbirth+ Bestiary or [Repentance] Repentance Bestiary.

Monstrance.title: Monstrance
Monstrance.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac a large pulsing aura around him that deals damage to enemies inside of it.

• The aura deals more damage the closer enemies are to Isaac, ranging from 0.4 on the edge up to 3.9 + 0.3 * floor damage.

• The aura deals damage up to 7.5 times per second.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Camo Undies: Enemies won't target Isaac, thus he can safely damage enemies while standing near them. However, this won't work with bosses.

• Isaac's Heart: Monstrance becomes much safer to use offensively as Isaac's body no longer takes damage.

• Items granting invulnerability or a shield: Monstrance damages enemies while Isaac is invincible.

• This includes Gnawed Leaf / VII - The Chariot? allowing Isaac to clear most rooms without moving.

• Dark Arts: Enemies will still be damaged while Dark Arts' effect is active, allowing Isaac to safely deal damage while invulnerable in this way.

• Pause: Monstrance will not stop the pause effect allowing Isaac to kill or chip bosses easily by standing near them for the duration of the pause effect.

• Tainted Forgotten: The aura surrounds Tainted Forgotten allowing Tainted Soul to damage enemies from a safe distance.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Monstrance is from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Monstrance would also increase Soul Heart drop chances.

• A monstrance is a vessel used in many Christian practices to display another religious artifact such as the Eucharist. In other words, it is generally used as a display piece.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: When Pause is used with Monstrance it creates a second aura of light that stays in place where Isaac used "Pause" which lasts for the active item's duration. The second aura is a visual glitch and does not deal damage to enemies. Moreover, both auras are flashing for the duration.

fields.description: Isaac gains an aura that deals damage to enemies inside it.

Monstro.title: Monstro
Monstro.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the posthumous version; Monstro II; the enemy; Ministro; the item; Lil Monstro] 

Monstro is a boss that can appear in the Basement and the Burning Basement.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Hops towards Isaac.

• Coughs up a large number of disorganized projectiles towards Isaac.

• Jumps off-screen, aiming to land on top of Isaac. Create a burst of disorganized projectiles in all directions on landing.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 2] : 15% larger and has 25% more HP (312.5). Uses projectile volleys much more often and is unable to jump off-screen.
[bc: 1] : Two 20% smaller Monstros, each with 55% less HP than the original one (112.5), replace the normal Monstro.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• In the boss room, Monstro can be paired with Fly, Attack Fly, Gapers, Hoppers, Frowning Gapers, Mulligans, Cyclopias, or Ministros.

• When Monstro jumps off-screen, he is cured of all status effects.

• [Before Repentance] Monstro can't hop over Obstacles.

• Larger Tears that Monstro shoots deal 1 Heart of damage, while the smaller Tears only deal half a Heart of damage.

• If Isaac is somewhere that Monstro cannot reach, Monstro will jump in place.

• If Isaac has flight and is over an obstacle, Monstro will essentially be unable to perform any attacks.

• • While Monstro can hit Isaac with his tear barrage because of its tear height, it is very unlikely.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Monstro can rarely spawn in a room with two Blood Donation Machines.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Monstro appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• He is the boss version of the Ministros.

• Monstro appears to be missing a tooth which appears as the item, Monstro's Tooth.

• Monstro also has a cleft lip.

• Monstro is Monster in Portuguese.

• "Monstro" is a somewhat common mispronunciation of the Spanish word monstruo.

• Monstro is also the name of The Terrible Dogfish, a fish with a large mouth and many teeth from the book The Adventures of Pinocchio.

Monstro's Lung.title: Monstro's Lung
Monstro's Lung.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a charged shot that fires 14 tears in the same fashion as Monstro.

• The attack can be released only when fully charged.

• Each tear deals 100% Isaac's damage.

• Each tear has a random size multiplier between 0.9x to 1.33x, but there is no effect on damage.

• Tears down: [Before Repentance] Tear Delay × 4.3 / [Repentance] Fire Rate ÷ 4.3 (roughly 0.23x).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Monstro II. [end edition note] 

• Charge time can be found with the following equation:
\text{time} = \frac{1}{30}(Roundup(\text{Tear Delay)}) \approx \frac{1}{\text{Fire Rate}}

• Each tear has independant chance to have Tear Effects.

• Tear falling speed ups will slightly reduce the effective range of Monstro's Lung.

• [edition rnr+] Since range ups always add to tear falling speed, every range up reduces effective range.

• [Repentance] Multi-shot effects such as 20/20 or Keeper adds 2.4 tears to the barrage per tear they normally grant. The resulting amount is rounded, and is capped at 50.

• [Repentance] Reaching above 30 fire rate will release the charge automatically when full. Since this is nearly instant, it results in a constant spray of tears.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20 / The Inner Eye / Mutant Spider:

• [Before Repentance] Adds 2, 5 or 7 tears to the barrage respectively. For the latter two, greatly slows down the charge.

• [Repentance] Adds 2.4 extra tears to the barrage per extra tear added by the item, rounded down to the nearest whole number. For the latter two, greatly slows down the charge.

• Almond Milk / Soy Milk: Fires automatically upon reaching full charge, regardless of fire rate.

• Anti-Gravity: Hover effect is overidden, but tear delay down still applies, which greatly reduces the charge time.

• Blood Clot: All tears are larger, with increased damage (as opposed to every 2nd tear like Blood Clot alone).

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Tears have a 50% chance to be Blood Clot tears.

• Brimstone: Brimstone has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. Fires 3-5 additional beams in random directions around Isaac. This effect also applies to Azazel and Tainted Azazel's versions of Brimstone.

• Brimstone + Eye Sore: Overrides this synergy with a chance to shoot 1-3 additional beams in random directions.

• Chocolate Milk: Reduces Isaac's tear delay by 20%, and each tear from Monstro's Lung is a charged Chocolate Milk shot, massively increasing fire rate and damage.

• This does not apply to Lilith's Incubus; picking up Chocolate Milk will significantly reduce damage and increase charge time.

• [Repentance] The tear damage and the barrage size scale with charge amount. At 50% charge, the tear damage is 100%, the barrage size reaches 100% and is capped there. At 100% charge, the tear damage is 200%.

• • \text{Charge Time (s)} = \frac{1}{30}(Roundup(\text{Tear Delay} \times \frac{5}{2} + 1)) \approx \frac{5}{2 \times \text{Fire Rate}}

• • 
• This makes damage per second drop to 80%.

• Dr. Fetus: Monstro's Lung has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. Fires 6 bombs which detonate simultaneously.

• [Repentance] Monstro's Lung has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. Fires 6 mini-bombs which detonate at different times. Multi-shot effects add 1 bomb to the barrage, up to 21 bombs.

• Epic Fetus: Epic Fetus has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. 2-4 extra cursors rotate around the main cursor before the missiles land.

• Eye Sore: Adds a chance to fire 1-3 additional barrages in random directions.

• The Forgotten: Melee swing is unaffected, but the throw attack is replaced by the burst attack with small bones instead of tears. Each additional copy of Monstro's lung adds 5 bone clubs in his melee attack, up to a limit of 16. The Soul behaves normally, including the tears down.

• Flat Stone: All tears bounce simultaneously; the effective range is greatly increased.

• Haemolacria: Monstro's Lung has priority. Applies +43 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Monstro's Lung tears down. The barrage size is reduced to 4/7 (roughly 0.57), tears of which all burst.

• The barrage size is 8 without any multi-shot effect. The resulting amount is rounded, and is capped at 29.

• Immaculate Heart: Fires a large number of extra tears alongside the burst that begin orbiting Isaac once they reach the orbit range.

• Ipecac: Fires Ipecac tears, with no increase in charge time.

• [Repentance] Applies Ipecac's tears down.

• Technology: Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. Grants a charged shot, fires 12 lasers in 30° spread that arc 3-4 times. A laser can hit an enemy multiple times between their arcings.

• \text{Charge Time (s)} = \frac{1}{30}(Roundup(\frac{43}{10} (\text{Tear Delay} + 1))) \approx \frac{43}{10 \times \text{Fire Rate}}

• • This is equivalent of applying Monstro's Lung's tears down and its charge time, without actually altering tear delay.

• Multi-shot effects add 12 lasers to the barrage, up to 128 lasers total.

• Technology + Mysterious Liquid: The lasers leave creep each time they arc, resulting in a massive amount of creep.

• Technology + Proptosis: The 6x damage is recovered each time they arc, nearly nullifying the distance penalty.

• Tech X: Fires 3-5 extra rings in 30° spread. Extra rings deal from 50% to 100% damage of the main ring.

• Additional copy of Monstro's Lung adds 3-5 more rings.

• [Before Repentance] Increases Tear Delay.

• [Repentance] Fire Rate is divided by 3.1.

• The Ludovico Technique: The Ludovico Technique has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. A cluster of variably sized tears orbit the main tear.

• Mom's Knife: Mom's Knife has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. Fires additional knives depending on charge amount, each dealing 2x tear damage. Fires 3-5 knives at maximum charge.

• Mom's Wig: Charging an attack spawns spiders in rapid succession.

• [Repentance] Spawns spiders upon firing, not charging. The amount of spiders spawned is dependent on luck.

• Monstro's Lung: Additional copies of this item, such as from Diplopia / Crooked Penny, add [Before Repentance] 10/ [Repentance] 12 tears to the barrage.

• This effects is equivalent of adding [Before Repentance] 4/ [Repentance] 5 multi-shot effects. The items which have priority over Monstro's Lung or override it (e.g. Brimstone/C Section) benefit from this multi-shot effect.

• My Reflection: Tears stay in the air much longer and consistently, allowing better reach and more focused blasts before the tears returning to Isaac.

• Tractor Beam: All the tears follow the beam at different heights without spreading out, making it much easier for multiple tears to hit a target.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Chemical Peel: Overridden by Monstro's Lung.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Tears have a 50% chance to be Chemical Peel tears.

• C Section: Overrides Monstro's Lung.

• Cursed Eye: Overridden by Monstro's Lung.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Monstro's Lung.

• Epiphora: Tears stat is increased properly but firing cancels the effect.

• Isaac's Tears / Sad Bombs / Tammy's Head: Fires 8 normal tears.

• Kidney Stone: If Monstro's Lung is picked up while Kidney Stone is ready to fire, charge time for Monstro's Lung will be significantly decreased.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Only stat effects from Kidney Stone apply.

• Kiney Stone will work if technology has been picked up.

• Lachryphagy: The tears merge into one giant tears a while after being fired, and instantly burst. Without piercing, most of the damage is often wasted. Without spectral, the tears often collide against obstacles due to their size.

• Loki's Horns / Mom's Eye: Adds a chance to fire single tears in the other direction(s).

• [Repentance] Adds a chance to fire barrages in the other direction(s).

• The Ludovico Technique: Overrides Monstro's Lung.

• Marked: Only stat effects from Marked apply.

• [Repentance] Works as expected. Fires automatically upon reaching full charge.

• Neptunus: Overridden by Monstro's Lung.

• Pop!: The tears still fall after being fired.

• Spirit Sword: Overrides Monstro's Lung.

• Strange Attractor: Due to the high concentration of tears enemies will be pulled into Isaac at great force, in certain cases enough force to pull enemies through rocks.

• Tech.5: Occasionally fires a linear laser while charging.

• Technology: If picked up after Technology, Monstro's Lung has no effect. Technology will override Monstro's Lung with a very low firerate.

• [edition anr] Technology has priority. Does not apply Monstro's Lung's tears down. Fires extra lasers in random directions.

• Technology 2: Fires a linear laser while charging.

• Ipecac + Dr. Fetus: Removes explosion immunity.

• The Wiz: 7-8 tears are fired at each diagonal direction instead of a full burst.

• [Repentance] Adds a multi-shot effect (see Notes section). Full-sized barrage on each diagonal direction.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Charged attack; Repentance: Charged burst attack]
fields.description: Replaces normal tears with a charged shot that fires 14 tears in the same fashion as Monstro.

Monstro's Tooth.title: Monstro's Tooth
Monstro's Tooth.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Upon use, a friendly Monstro jumps on a random enemy, dealing 120 damage while destroying nearby obstacles like rocks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] This item can be spawned by Bumbino if he picks up 12 cents. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Monstro. [end edition note] 

• This item will target Isaac if it is used in a room without monsters and can cause damage (a full heart).

• Monstro can be dodged depending on Isaac's Speed and his movement.

• Monstro can open Secret Rooms or destroy tinted rocks without hurting Isaac, if timed correctly.

• Monstro will target Shopkeepers. 

• [Before Repentance] Like Mom and Satan's stomp attacks, this attack is treated as an explosion, so Pyromaniac and Host Hat will be activated if Monstro falls on Isaac.

• [Rebirth only] This item does not affect the Monstro boss.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring, looking like teeth. These wisps shoot 50% slower than the average wisp, but deal 12 damage per shot.

• Car Battery: Monstro deals double damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The tooth can be seen missing in Monstro/Monstro II's mouth.

• This item is similar to II - The High Priestess, but deals less damage.

• Judging by the sprites of Monstro/Monstro II, it can be assumed that the missing tooth is an incisor tooth or canine tooth. The item physically resembles a molar tooth however.

• This item's unlock is the most common steam achievement in the game.

fields.description: A friendly Monstro jumps on a random enemy, dealing 120 damage in an area. Targets Isaac if used in a room without enemies.

Monstro II.title: Monstro II
Monstro II.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Monstro II is a boss that can appear in the Depths and the Dank Depths.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Hops towards Isaac, similar to Monstro.

• If Isaac is standing to the left or right side of Monstro II, he will shoot a horizontal Brimstone laser.

• Jumps off-screen and lands on Isaac's position two times in a row.

• Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions on his first landing. Each projectile deals a full heart of damage.

• Spawns 4 Suckers on his second landing.

• • Suckers caught in Monstro II's hops, as well as his jump and his Brimstone attack, are killed.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 1] : 20% smaller. Moves and attacks much faster, but only spawns 2 Suckers when landing. [Repentance] Has 10% less HP (569.25).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Monstro II can often be seen with 2 Attack Fly to its left and right sides.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Monstro II appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• He is the posthumous version of Monstro.

• Gish is his alternate version.

• A spinal cord can be seen attached to Monstro II in his Versus image, implying that Monstro had a lower body at one point. The spine can also be seen when he fires a Brimstone laser.

• Monstro II is missing a tooth, most likely a reference to Monstro's Tooth.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Monstro II was the very first posthumous boss prior to the Wrath of the Lamb DLC.

• He is Edmund McMillen's least favorite boss solely due to his name.

Montezuma's Revenge.title: Montezuma's Revenge
Montezuma's Revenge.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Continuously shooting for 2.35 seconds allows Isaac to fire a short-ranged brown Brimstone laser and corn shots behind himself when he stops shooting.

• The laser deals Isaac's damage per tick (15x Isaac's damage per second), ticks up to 19 times and lasts ~1.28 seconds (77 frames).

• Corn shots deal 6 damage, and a random amount are created each blast.

• Contributes to the Oh Crap transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Dangle. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Montezuma's Revenge, No. 2, Maw Of The Void and Revelation all have the same charge time, allowing Isaac to easily utilize them at same time.

• Brain Worm: Can cause the poop beam to hook to a target anywhere in the room, potentially hitting a target far outside of its usual range.

• Dark Arts: The corn Isaac poops out can be sliced, giving Isaac an insane damage up in seconds.

• Hemoptysis: Enemies hit by the sneeze will gain a curse that increases the damage the poop beam deals to 2x and +3 flat damage. Enemies who die to the poop beam under the curse will damage and spread the curse to nearby enemies.

• Ipecac: The poop beam gets only a +2 flat damage bonus instead of +40. The beam explodes 10 times, either on the first enemy or obstacle it hits or at the very end otherwise, dealing 10 + twice of the beam's damage.

• Jacob's Ladder: The brown laser Isaac fires will produce random arcs of electricity at the end of the laser. The corn Isaac poops out does not interact with the electricity.

• Lachryphagy: Spawns a large amount of tears at the end of the poop beam, heavily increasing Isaac's damage output.

• My Reflection: Causes the poop beam range behind Isaac to become significantly increased as well as having a short range similar to Azazel's beam in front of him. This greatly eases the use of this item allowing for high DPS.

• The Parasite: The poop beam splits into two horizontal beams meaning less risk for Isaac and a bigger area for enemies to be hit.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Censer: The corn shots are slowed by the aura.

• Eye of the Occult: No effect.

• Eye of the Occult + Brimstone/Technology: The poop beam also automatically fires at the crosshair and becomes a lasso. The loop starts where the beam would normally end and extends out to the cross-hair.

• Libra: The poop beam ignores damage modification from Libra, both positive and negative: the actual unbalanced damage value is used.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Montezuma's Revenge is a colloquial term for Traveler's Diarrhea, an intestinal infection caused by ingesting contaminated food or water. Montezuma II was the last Aztec ruler before the Spanish conquest of the Aztec civilization, and the sickness is seen as a curse afflicting tourists visiting Mexico as revenge for the Aztec massacre.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: When playing as Tainted Forgotten, the charge attack will always come out of the left of the body regardless of the direction it or the Soul is facing.
Bug note: When combined with Chocolate Milk, Cursed Eye, Monstro's Lung or Tech X, releasing a Montezuma's Revenge attack may prevent a charged shot from firing at the same time as expected. The charged shot is delayed by about ~0.5 seconds. Holding a full charge for a longer time makes the delay more likely to happen.

fields.description: While firing, Isaac charges up a short-ranged Brimstone-like diarrhea beam that shoots behind him.

More Options.title: More Options
More Options.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: an item affecting Treasure Rooms; a similar item affecting Boss rewards; There's Options; a similar item affecting room clear rewards; Options?]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Two item pedestals are presented in every Treasure Room. Only one can be taken; the other will disappear.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Small Treasure Rooms only present one item, nullifying this item's effect.

• Having multiple copies of More Options will not have any extra effect.

• If the Treasure Room has already been entered and the item was not taken, then picking up More Options later on the same floor will not retroactively add a second item to the room.

• If the Treasure Room has not been entered on the same floor More Options was picked up, then it will contain two items.

• The very rare Treasure Rooms that have either no item or two items that can both be picked up will be replaced with a one-out-of-two choice room, like other Treasure Rooms. In the latter case, this is a downgrade.

• [Repentance] In the alternative path, Treasure Rooms will have two known items and one unknown item, instead of the usual one known and one unknown. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] In Downpour II / Dross II, The Mirrored world's treasure room will not contain a second item. [end edition note] 

• More Options will work for Treasure Rooms during the Ascent as long as those rooms were never originally entered.

• Neither of the items in the modified Treasure Room are guaranteed to be the same as the original item, effectively rerolling the original item while also offering a second choice.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Crooked Penny / Diplopia: Both items are copied, allowing Isaac to take both copied items without the other disappearing. The original pedestals will function as normal, disappearing the other if one is collected. [end edition note] 

• Devil's Crown: Both items can be taken, although they must be paid for with hearts.

• Glowing Hourglass: Entering an unexplored More Options Treasure Room and then using Glowing Hourglass can cause the room's layout to change rerolling the offered items. The reroll is not always guaranteed as Glowing Hourglass is causing the Treasure Room to alternate between a set number of different More Options room layouts on a given floor with repeat layouts offering the same items.

• Jacob and Esau: Both brothers can take one item each if they are lined up properly.

• Pay to Win: Treasure Rooms will always contain a Shop Restock Machine in addition to the two choice items.

• [Repentance] In Downpour, Dross, and Mines, Pay to Win by itself can sometimes spawn the combined Treasure Rooms, even without More Options. Having both doesn't guarantee the combined effect.

• • For Ashpit, Mausoleum, Gehenna, and Corpse, this combination does work correctly for normal-sized Treasure Rooms, but not thin ones. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance] There's Options' description is "More options". For this item, it's the other way around.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: There are even more options!; Repentance: There's options]
fields.description: Two item pedestals are presented in every Treasure Room. Only one can be taken; the other will disappear.

Morningstar.title: Morningstar
Morningstar.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Morningstars are enemies that float towards Isaac only when Isaac is moving. They get faster as they move, eventually reaching a point where Isaac cannot outrun them unless he has a high speed stat. When Isaac stops moving, their speed resets and they stop in place. They deal a full heart of contact damage.

They have 2 different appearances though this is purely visual as they behave the same.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The name Morningstar comes from "Morning Star" which is one of the meanings of the name "Lucifer"- a common name for Satan.

• Morningstars resemble the end of a morning star, a medieval club-like weapon.

• Morningstars closely resemble Ferals, enemies from Edmund's game The End is Nigh. Both are sharp-toothed spiked balls that float in the air and pursue the player, attached to the ground by a chain.

• "Morning Star" is the name of the track that plays while in Gehenna.

fields.environment: Gehenna /
fields.behavior: Floats toward Isaac to deal contact damage while Isaac is moving, gaining speed the longer Isaac continues moving. Stops moving when Isaac stops moving.

Mother.title: Mother
Mother.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the final boss of Corpse; the boss of chapter 3 and chapter 3.5; Mom] 

Mother is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance and the only boss of the second floor of the Corpse, as well as the final boss of Ending 21.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text: Upon entering the boss room in Corpse II, the room is empty except for a hole in its center. Walking into it drops Isaac down into the arena where Mother is fought.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Mother begins the fight attached to the top of the room and is stationary, similar to Mega Satan. Her face and hands can all be attacked to deal damage to her, and she uses them separately in her attacks:

• One of Mother's hands grabs a knife and throws it directly downwards. The knife emits projectiles horizontally while travelling and a burst of many projectile lines in a radius upon impacting the back wall. This attack has two variations in terms of the projectiles' paths.

• One of Mother's arms releases trails of projectiles that move across the arena in a wave pattern, eventually homing in on Isaac.

• One of Mother's hands slams the ground, releasing streams of projectiles in a radius and spawning Small Maggots.

• Small Maggots that land on top of Mother's hitbox do not spawn.

• Occasionally, Mother spits out a unique Fistula at Isaac that bounces off walls. Mother swipes the Fistula towards Isaac whenever it travels close to one of her hands and releases 6 lines of 2 projectiles when it collides with the bottom wall. Mother repeats this several times, causing the Fistula to gradually gain speed, before slamming a hand down on the mass, crushing it and sending 3 medium Fistulas outwards. Each medium Fistula flies until it collides with a wall, sending out 2-3 small Fistulas and being destroyed in the process. These small Fistulas travel a short distance before bursting and spawning a Small Maggot.

• This Fistula can be reflected back towards Mother through the use of a variety of melee-based attacks, each reflect causing the Fistula to glow brighter. Successfully reflecting the Fistula 6 times will cause it to be destroyed upon contact with Mother, dealing damage to and briefly stunning her. It will also burst into 8 medium Fistulas in a radius that disappear quickly, six of which deal damage to Mother; each of these can also deal damage to Isaac. Abilities that can cause this interaction include:

• • Spirit Sword's spin attack.

• • The Forgotten/Tainted Forgotten/Soul of the Forgotten's bone swing.

• • Tainted Samson/Soul of Samson/Berserk!'s donkey jawbone swing.

• • Bag of Crafting's swipe.

• • Tainted Magdalene's hug attack, though it cannot be triggered by the Fistula.

• Occasionally, Mother retreats upwards, becoming invulnerable, and summons a horde of 34 Dead Isaacs at the bottom of the arena that walk up towards Mother. If any are left alive to reach Mother, she swipes with a hand, killing any that are caught in the swipe, releasing a tiny burst of red projectiles, and launching their corpses towards Isaac. After a while, she ends this attack by slamming down both hands, which causes a small rock wave to appear beneath any remaining Dead Isaacs, killing them, and launching their corpses up into the air.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After losing 2222 HP, Mother retracts her head and arms into her body before releasing a green Mega Blast laser down the middle of the arena, destroying the lower wall and expanding the area of the room to be 1x2. She then separates from the top wall, launching her head into the center of the room. From this point on, she slides slowly towards Isaac when she isn't performing one of her attacks:

• Spins around in place, shooting out strings of wavy projectiles in all directions.

• Inhales and draws Isaac to her as projectiles appear behind Isaac as he moves. After that, she shoots a massive ball of projectiles towards Isaac that splits into many smaller clusters when hitting a wall, which each then send out lines of projectiles when they collide with a wall or Mother.

• Leaps upwards off-screen before charging vertically across the half of the room which Isaac is located within, then across the other half in the opposite direction. The half she charges across first is telegraphed by a splat at the top or bottom of the room. After this, she slams down in the middle of the room, sending rock waves and small strings of projectiles in all directions.

• Faint white lines appear at set intervals along a random arena wall before a line of projectiles quickly shoots out of the wall along each line; these projectiles hover for a moment before dropping. One line of projectiles is always lined up with Isaac's position. This attack is repeated five times and follows a pattern: vertical lines, then horizontal, vertical, horizontal, horizontal (or vice versa).

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: A Strange Door, Jacob and Esau, Seeing Double, Isaac's Awakening, Meat Cleaver, Yuck Heart, Guppy's Eye, Akeldama, Eternal D6, Bird Cage, Bloody Gust, Devil's Crown, Tinytoma, 'M, Lost Soul, Blood Puppy, Keeper's Sack, Lil Portal, Bone Spurs, Revelation, Magic Skin, Dice Bag, Mother's Kiss, Lucky Sack, Number Magnet, Ring Cap, Lil Clot, Swallowed M80, Azazel's Stump, Torn Card, Modeling Clay, Crystal Key, Adoption Papers, Cursed Penny, Apollyon's Best Friend, Hollow Heart, Beth's Essence, Found Soul, Godhead]

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance+] Using Plan C will kill Mother in time if you have an extra life. Even though Isaac dies well before the animation is complete, the game over screen will pop up almost immediately after the animation ends. If Isaac has an extra life item that revives him outside the room, he will be able to enter the Final Boss Chest without fighting Mother again.

• [Before Repentance+] Killing Mother in this way will not reward the completion mark for the current character if they don't have an extra life.

• [Before Repentance+] Killing Mother in this way will not work for The Lost, Tainted Lost, The Forgotten (if used as The Soul), and Tainted Forgotten if the revival transports them to the previous room since their death animations are shorter than those of normal characters.

• [Repentance+] Using Plan C in Mother's room will now kill Isaac in 11.5 seconds, which is enough time to let Mother's death animation finish and reward the completion mark for the current character before Isaac's Last Will pops up.

• Rotten Tomato or any items that inflict Charm can cause Mother's wavy projectiles during the first phase and second phase to target herself.

• The ball of splitting projectiles in Mother's second phase can also collide with Mother. The player can therefore move to the opposite side of Mother after she fires to more easily dodge the attack.

• Unlike most other bosses, Mother has no visible health bar in either of her phases, so it is impossible to tell how much damage you are dealing to her without Spider Mod.

• Suplex! works on Mother, but in Mother's first phase, Isaac can pick up only one of her parts at a time, either her head or one of her arms, and give it a suplex.

• II - The High Priestess will damage Mother even though it can be considered another form of Mom.

• Using Black Hole will not stop Mother's wavy projectiles from proceeding once the black hole has diminished.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
• Chaos Card works on Mother, but only kills one of her phases. If you are holding a Chaos Card, it is recommended to use it in Phase 2, since Mother's attacks are much more dangerous.

• Curse of the Tower can be very useful, since Troll Bombs will attempt to spawn near Mother, and bombs in Repentance will deal 100 damage and ignore the armor. Around 43 bombs would be able to kill her, which corresponds to about 6~7 times of damage. This will be affordable if you have more than 10 hearts in total.

• Similarly, using Anarchist Cookbook, XVI - The Tower, or your own Bombs will also help.

• Her charging attack in Phase 2 can be greatly stalled by placing a bomb in front of her path, while also dealing damage to her in the process.

• In phase 2, if the player has Gnawed Leaf, they can bring Mother to a complete standstill while she's charging if they enter statue form in front of her.

• Pair this with at least one offensive familiar and the fight becomes a joke for all characters.

• Using Ace of Hearts during the Dead Isaac attack will spawn 10 hearts on average, which should keep any red heart characters alive for quite some time. Using it during the hand slam attack that spawns Small Maggots will usually spawn 3-5.

• Using Eraser on Mother's first phase allows phase 2 to be skipped as long she has 15 health or less.

• With proper timing, Soul of Judas can one-shot Mother's second phase even with base damage. The best attack for this is the spinning attack, but it is also possible to do this right after Mother spits out the ball of projectiles. Be aware that the boss can dodge the damage by performing the charge attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Ending following this fight reveals Mother to be a grotesque, undead representation of Mom imagined by Isaac before the events of the game.

• This boss originates from the Antibirth mod, and was originally named "The Witness".

• The Witness itself was first designed as a boss mockup by the name of "Ur-Gurdy". The Ur-Gurdy was a speculative posthumous version of Mama Gurdy which was rumored to rarely replace Satan in Sheol.

• Between her original appearance in Antibirth and Repentance, Mother’s boss fight was changed drastically, including the arena being shrunken dramatically, the replacement of several attacks with new ones, the boss theme being changed, and the boss's death animation being changed, along with the addition of Mom’s voice lines during the battle.

• Because of how she died in Antibirth (turning to stone), it was possible to softlock the game by killing The Witness where the ending chest spawned.

• In Antibirth, the Corpse II boss room contained four golden chests with items (similar to the starting room in Chest). In Repentance, the boss room is completely empty except for the hole leading to the fight against Mother.

• Mother's boss theme is called "Morticide". "Morti-" stems from Latin "Mors" which means "death" or "corpse", while "-cide" means "an act of killing", so the track name effectively means "Killing the dead".

• The back wall of the fight is actually part of Mother's model; attempting to summon her via the console will change the bottom wall of the current floor to a Corpse wall.

• Unlike Mom, Mom's Heart, and It Lives!, Mother is not instantly killed by using The Bible.

• Mother is one of only three bosses that don't have a visible health bar of their own. The others are Mega Satan and The Beast.

• Faint translucent Chubber projectiles can be seen leading the lines of projectiles in Mother's second phase white line attack.

• In Antibirth, The Witness was immune to Status Effects.

• The interaction of Spirit Sword to the Fistula attack is likely a reference to the "Dead Man's Volley" commonly seen during boss fights in The Legend of Zelda.

• According to _Kilburn, the mega Brimstone laser when starting phase 2 is a reference to The Nuclear Throne, a boss from the game Nuclear Throne.

• Mother beating up Dead Isaacs in one of her attacks could be alluding to how Isaac gets beaten up in life after leaving his room.

• Mother spawning 34 Dead Isaacs might be a reference to there being 34 playable characters.

Mother's Kiss.title: Mother's Kiss
Mother's Kiss.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one heart container while held.

• This heart container will be filled the first time the trinket is picked up.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If the only heart container Isaac has is the one given by Mother's Kiss, the trinket will be destroyed if the heart container is traded/consumed.

• The trinket will get destroyed even if smelted via Smelter, Marbles, or a Gulp! pill.

• If Isaac drops the trinket while he only has one heart container for health, he will have no health and die instantly.

• This also means that using 0 - The Fool? card will do the same, even if he has soul hearts.

• The extra red heart container can exceed the maximum coin heart container limit of Keeper and Tainted Keeper, allowing them to obtain more than 3 or 2 coin hearts, respectively.

• The heart added is a soul heart for ??? and Tainted Bethany, and a black heart for Black Judas and Tainted Judas.

• Using The Fool? card as one of these characters while holding this trinket will kill you instantly, as it drops the trinket, removing the last half soul heart that you normally would remain with.

• The Forgotten will always get a Bone Heart regardless of whether the body or the soul picked up the trinket.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Adds 1 more heart container per copy.

• If the trinket is picked up while holding Mom's Box, 1 heart container will not be filled.

• Guppy's Paw: The trinket will be consumed, but the soul hearts from conversion are kept.

• Potato Peeler: The trinket will be consumed, but the damage and Cube of Meat is kept.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Mother's Kiss will not contribute to the Yes Mother? transformation nor unlocking Mom's Contacts despite having the item tag.
Bug note: While playing as characters who cannot have red HP, if Mother's Kiss is picked up while having 12 Soul/Black Hearts, Mother's Kiss will not trigger until damage is taken. However, if only half a heart of damage is taken, Mother's Kiss will immediately restore the health back to a full 12 but believe its effect failed due to not restoring a full heart's worth, allowing it to trigger again and again until a full heart of damage is taken, after which it will cease taking effect. If combined with The Wafer, this makes any of the aforementioned 6 characters virtually invincible as long as their health is not reduced in any way through Devil Deals, Health Down pills, etc.
Bug note: Dropping Mom's Box will not remove the second heart container until the trinket is dropped.
Bug note: Dying and respawning with Dead Cat will respawn you with only 1 heart container, meaning you will instantly die if you drop the trinket.

Flooded Caves.title: Flooded Caves
Flooded Caves.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Flooded Caves is one of the environments in chapter 2 added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth. The theme of the Flooded Caves is water; as such, most of the enemies inhabiting it are airborne, such as One Tooth and flies, and many of them shoot projectiles, while there are fewer ground-bound and contact-damage-reliant enemies. Some enemies like the Hive have a chance to be replaced with their drowned variants [Before Repentance] and rocks have a chance to be replaced with water-filled pits.

The Flooded Cave's alternate floors are the Caves and the Catacombs.

[Repentance] After A Secret Exit is unlocked, a boarded door similar to the one leading to a Bedroom will appear in this floor's Boss Room upon defeating the boss, leading to the Mines / Ashpit. This door, like a Bedroom, requires two bombs to be opened. Unlike Angel Rooms and Devil Rooms, this door never disappears. [end edition note] 

[Repentance] Though there is some overlap with Downpour due to both featuring water flooding, Downpour's unique enemies are often ghostly and supernatural in nature as opposed to the Flooded Cave's theme of drowned or bloated enemies. [end edition note] 

[Afterbirth+ onward] The Flooded Caves are unlocked by defeating It Lives! 16 times.

• [Repentance] Killing Dogma and The Beast also increases this tally, as does Mausoleum's version of Mom's Heart. [end edition note]

Gehenna.title: Gehenna
Gehenna.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Gehenna is an alternative floor to the Mausoleum and was added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

Gehenna has a demonic theme, with horned skulls, bones, and blood on the black cracked floor, while bloodied chains hang from the walls. Unique features of this stage include Teleporters, Grudges, and the Ball and Chain.

The door to the Mausoleum / Gehenna will appear after defeating the boss in The Mines II / Ashpit II or the Depths I / Necropolis I / Dank Depths I. The door will not spawn after defeating Mom. It costs two full hearts to enter, and ignores almost every form of damage reduction, including The Wafer and invincibility. Unlike other methods of health donation, red hearts will not be prioritized over more valuable hearts.

• The Lost, Tainted Lost, Tainted Jacob (In his soul form), Tainted Soul (unless he is holding Tainted Forgotten), and any character under the effect of Soul of the Lost can enter the door for free.

• Dad's Key, Get out of Jail Free Card, Mr. ME!, and Sharp Key can be used to open the door without taking damage.

• Broken Padlock can be used to open the door with one bomb.

• Cracked Orb's effect can open the door with less damage taken than needed, or with no damage with Dull Razor.

• The extra characters spawned by Strawman, Soul of the Forgotten, and Soul of Jacob and Esau can expend their health to open the door.

• Crow Heart can be used to open the door with red hearts first.

The boss of Gehenna II is always a more powerful version of Mom. After Mom is defeated, a trapdoor that leads to the Womb II, and a sealed fleshy door both appear. Stabbing the door with the knife familiar created by Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2 will cause it to open, leading to a more difficult version of Mom's Heart. Defeating Mom's Heart will cause the boss room to darken, and the trapdoor to Womb II will now lead to the Corpse.

• A Sharp Key can be used in place of the Knife.

• Cracked Orb's effect can open the flesh door, allowing Isaac to keep the knife.

• If Isaac exits the Boss Rush room after 25 minutes have passed, there is a chance that the flesh door will change positions to the wall where the boss rush door was, causing Isaac to "come out" of the flesh door and leaving it open, allowing entry without the knife.

• After this special version of Mom's Heart is defeated, any Item or Pickup that was left behind anywhere on the floor will disappear (including Shop items, Angel Room/Devil Room items, etc.): the floor will be empty.

• Therefore, make sure not to leave behind something that you might want to use after this floor. The strategy consisting in teleporting outside of Mom and Mom's Heart to retrieve something that was left behind after fighting them is not viable here.

• The Boss Rush entrance will disappear if it was previously open.

• If a Shop Restock Machine is used within the now-empty shop, it will restock the shop as normal.

• If the effect of Forget Me Now is invoked after the special version of Mom's Heart is defeated, the [cu: Darkness] -like effect will remain on the newly generated floor. Additionally, no items will naturally generate in rooms where they would have. After the player defeats Mom again, there will be no flesh door, and the trapdoor to Corpse will appear.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In Hebrew belief, Gehenna (or Gehinnom) was thought to be a small valley in Jerusalem. The name literally translated to "Valley of Hinnom" and in the Valley, Kings of Jerusalem would sacrifice their children through fire.

• Gehenna was also thought to be "the destination of the wicked" in Jewish literature. It differs from the neutral-leaning Sheol as Gehenna was considered a type of waiting room; the longest one can be there is 11 or 12 months with few exceptions.

• It was also thought to be the location of Jerusalem's garbage dump, where the city's waste and the corpses of criminals were disposed by incineration. These fires burned for most of the day, inspiring later descriptions of Hell as a place of eternal torment by fire for the wicked.

• This floor may a reference to The 7 Planes of Hehenna, a similarly named area in another of Edmund McMillen's games, Gish. This is reinforced by the numerous similarities the two share, such as the appearance of gimp-clad enemies and the visual theme of a demonic temple.

• The boss Sisters Vis was also originally the boss of this area in Gish, though that is not the case for Gehenna.

• As the Mausoleum only has 2 unique bosses, it is possible to unlock Gehenna in one run by completing a Boss Challenge room in Hard mode, as both bosses will spawn.

sections.heading: Music
sections.text:
• The music in Gehenna is titled Morning Star.

• "Morning Star", "Shining One" or "Light-Bringer" comes from ancient Greek and is used to refer to Lucifer.

• The planet Venus is considered the Morning Star and is associated with the Devil falling from heaven. This is due to it falling beneath the horizon in the morning, much like how the former angel fell to Earth. Venus and the Devil share the name Lucifer because of this.

• A morning star is also a type of weapon that consists of a spiked ball at the end of a club, an extremely brutal weapon that resembles the rotating spike balls and similarly named enemies unique to this floor.

• In the background of the track, the Latin phrase "bonum est Deus" can be heard, which can be translated to "God is good."
