Home.title: Home
Home.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Home is one of the final floors in The Binding of Isaac, alongside the Chest, the Dark Room, [Afterbirth+ onward] The Void, and the Corpse. It was added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

Home can be accessed after picking up Dad's Note and going through the ascent or by using the Glowing Hourglass in the first floor's starting room without entering any other rooms. The bosses of the floor are always Dogma, followed by a gauntlet against Ultra Famine, Ultra Pestilence, Ultra War, and Ultra Death, and finally The Beast.

sections.heading: Layout
sections.text:
The Home floor has no enemies, and is completely empty. Similar to ??? and the Greed mode floors, its layout is always the same. Home features Isaac's room, two corridors, a room with a pickup, the living room, and Mom's room.

Isaac's room is where Isaac spawns upon entering the stage. It contains a bed in the upper left corner and a carpet in the center, like a regular Clean Bedroom, as well as a Locked Chest. Isaac can sleep in his bed to recover provided he's not at full health, or to add three Soul Hearts provided he has no Red Heart containers. Triggering an explosion on the carpet will cause it to be damaged, but reveal nothing underneath.

A single door in the bottom wall leads to the narrow right corridor. Through a door in the upper side of the right wall is a small room that contains a random pickup or, rarely, an item. Further down in the left wall, there is another door leading to the house's living room.

The living room is double-sized and extends vertically downwards from the entrances at either side. It contains a large turned-off TV, placed against its northern wall, and a couch further south, as well as a red carpet located between them with a massive picture of a cross with wings. A door in the upper left side leads to another narrow corridor, which Isaac can walk north to reach Mom's room.

Mom's room contains a unique chest, a carpet, a dressing table, and Mom's bed, all of them larger than similar items found throughout the game. When the chest is opened for the first time, it will contain the Red Key, which will be permanently unlocked. In subsequent playthroughs, it draws from its own item pool of Mom-related items; the Red Key can still be found, but more rarely. The carpet and the dressing table in this room cannot be interacted with.

Sleeping in Mom's bed will cause Isaac to have a nightmare, showing the loading screen with no floor icons. In the dream, Isaac is sitting next to his mother as she watches TV. Isaac's distorted face then appears on the TV screen, as the noise of static begins to increase in volume.

After a flash of static briefly covering the entire screen, Isaac wakes up again, presumably at night since Home is considerably darker. At this point, when exiting Mom's room and walking down the left corridor, a grey light can be seen through the bottom-right door. The source of this light is the TV in the living room, which is now turned on but only emits static. Stepping on the cross in the living room's carpet will begin the battle against Home's first boss, Dogma.

Upon beating Dogma, a cutscene will play, after which the fight with The Beast will start.

sections.heading: Hidden closet
sections.text:
In the hallway leading to Mom's bedroom, using either the Red Key, Cracked Key, or Soul of Cain will open an entrance to a hidden room. This is hinted by the existence of the closet on the other side of the map, by Isaac's bedroom. There is also a barely visible glowing red outline for the hidden door when the Red Key or Cracked Key has been picked up. The closet is also the place Isaac is thrown into in ending 21.

Inside is the tainted version of the character currently being played, laying on the floor, crying. Touching them will unlock that character, which can be selected from their own menu and has their own unique mechanics and unlocks. Each playable character has a tainted version that can be unlocked this way. If the player changes the character (for example dying with Missing Poster and respawning as The Lost) and re-enters the Hidden Closet, the crying baby will not change to the corresponding character, and will stay as the first character it turned into. This means the player cannot unlock two Tainted Characters in the same run. In true co-op, the character in the closet will be the tainted version of player one's character.

If the tainted version of a character has already been unlocked, or a tainted character is being played, the closet will contain Inner Child. If Inner Child has not been unlocked, it will contain a Shopkeeper instead.

The method for obtaining a Cracked Key during the ascent is described on their respective pages, but the Red Key can also be obtained from Curse Rooms (if unlocked) or by using Pandora's Box on the Home floor.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The fact that there isn't a trap door underneath the rug in Isaac's bedroom hints towards the Final Ending, as the game is kicked off with Isaac finding and using a trap door underneath his rug in order to escape his mother and using it to reach The Basement.

• Uniquely, using Undefined in Home is impossible, despite an I AM ERROR room existing for this floor; any attempts to trigger the effect result in nothing happening.

• The Bible and Mom's Purse can be seen on top of her dresser in her room. Mom's Lipstick, Mom's Perfume, and Mom's Eyeshadow can be seen atop a dresser beneath her mirror. Various pills can be seen in the drawers reaching from her bed.

• The unique chest in Mom's room resembles a much larger version of Mom's Box.

• The drawings seen in Isaac's room reference the events of Ending 20.

• The closet created by using the Red Key resembles the one featured in the Official Art for Repentance and is most likely shown in Ending 21.

• Normally unseen, there is a crack on the door to Isaac's room referencing the events of the game's introduction cutscene where Isaac peeks through and sees his mom approaching with a knife. It can be seen by using Everything Jar and getting it to close the room's doors. The cracked door sprite is also used in bedrooms which can be seen by reward plates spawning enemies or, as mentioned before, Everything Jar

• Including the hidden room, Home's layout resembles a heart. This may be a reference to the phrase 'Home is where the heart is'.

• The golden chest in Isaac's room can spawn as a Mega Chest.

• There is an unused Combat layer for the music in Home, in which you can hear Mom yelling at Isaac, either his name or in full sentences (Although very echoey, like "Oh god, ISAAC!")

• This soundtrack can be heard via entering Crawl Space with enemies in it.

• Both Home and the Lake of Fire are referred to on Isaac's Last Will as "Some Familiar Place".

Machines.title: Machines
Machines.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Machines are objects that Isaac can interact with to gain a variety of rewards.

sections.heading: Slot Machine
sections.text:
Walking up to the Slot Machine and bumping into it will consume one penny and spin the slots. The Machine then has a chance to spawn one of its possible rewards.
Slot Machines appear naturally in Arcades, Secret Rooms, and other room layouts, and can be summoned using the X - Wheel of Fortune tarot card.

If the Slot Machine is caught in an explosion of any kind, it will be destroyed, yielding various rewards (see below). The Slot Machine also has a 2% chance to self-destruct after inserting a penny, in which case it drops several random pickups, A Dollar, or [Repentance+] Portable Slot and becomes unusable.

The D4 is unlocked when 30 Slot Machines are destroyed (via explosion or overloading) by Isaac.

[Before Repentance] When blown up in the Dark Room or Chest, it will drop a collectible from the Treasure Room item pool, much like Chests and Locked Chests.

Lucky Foot raises the odds by a multiplier of 1.4×. On hard mode, the chances of winning at the Slot Machine are halved.

sections.heading: Possible Rewards when Destroyed
sections.text:
When Isaac destroys a Slot Machine, there is a:

• 10% chance to drop a random pill

• 10% chance to drop a random trinket

• 0.8% chance to drop a Chest

• 0.792% chance to drop a Locked Chest

• 78.408% chance to drop 2-3 random pickup groupings; for each grouping, there is a

• 35% chance to drop 1-3 random Pennys

• 20% chance to drop a random heart

• • If Daemon's Tail is held, there is an 80% chance to prevent this grouping from being chosen; if prevented, another pickup grouping will be chosen instead.

• • If chosen, there is a 50% chance that this counts as 2 pickup groupings.

• 15% chance to drop a random Key

• 30% chance to drop a random Bomb

There is a 33% chance of an extra pickup grouping spawning if Isaac is holding Lucky Toe.

Furthermore, if the 78.408% chance to drop the pickup groupings is selected, there is a 33% chance for the following conditions to occur:

• If Ace of Spades is held, spawn an extra random card.

• If Safety Cap is held, spawn an extra random pill.

• If Match Stick is held, spawn an extra random Bomb.

• If Child's Heart is held, spawn an extra random heart.

• If Rusted Key is held, spawn an extra random Key.

Note that only 1 additional item can spawn from this 33% chance. In the case of having multiple matching trinkets, the conditions are checked in order.

For debugging purposes, an init seed that spawns a Slot Machine that pays out a Dollar on the first attempt is 1236239571.

sections.heading: Fortune Telling Machine
sections.text:
The Fortune Telling Machine is similar to the Slot Machine. Bumping into the Machine costs one penny, which will either display a random fortune or special seed on-screen, or cause the Machine to spawn one of its possible drops. Fortune Telling Machines appear naturally in Arcades, Secret Rooms, Super Secret Rooms, and other room layouts, and can be summoned using the X - Wheel of Fortune tarot card.
The Fortune Telling Machine also has a chance to self-destruct after inserting a penny, in which case it drops several random pickups or Crystal Ball. [Before Repentance] Like the Slot Machine, Fortune Telling Machines will also drop a random collectible item when destroyed in the Dark Room or Chest.

sections.heading: Blood Donation Machine
sections.text: Bumping into the Blood Donation Machine will damage Isaac. The machine will then pay out with 1-2 of any type of Penny (only 1 in Hard Mode) or, rarely, Child's Heart. Every donation has a 6.66% chance of causing the Blood Donation Machine to explode, giving either a Blood Bag or an IV Bag. Alternatively, it can be destroyed with a Bomb, which will cause it to drop several coin or heart pickups.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• On the floors before Womb, the Machine will take a half-heart of health from each use. From Womb and onward, the Blood Donation Machine will take one full heart instead.

• Once a Blood Donation Machine has given IV Bag, future Blood Donation Machines will never pay out with it again for the rest of the run unless Blood Bag has not been unlocked yet.

• It is possible for any number of Blood Bags to appear in the same run.

• Holy Mantle does not prevent damage from a Blood Donation Machine.

• Invulnerability and shields can be used to prevent damage from it.

• [Before Repentance] The Machine will accept Eternal Hearts first, then Red Hearts. When Isaac's health is at half a heart (or a full heart in Womb and beyond), the Machine will drain Soul Hearts and Black Hearts instead.

• [Before Repentance] While the Machine takes Red Hearts before Soul Hearts or Black Hearts, using a Blood Donation Machine will trigger Scapular once Isaac is at half a heart. Leaving the room afterward and then reentering resets Scapular, allowing for further donations using Soul Hearts. Repeating this process after every Scapular activation allows Isaac to collect coins from the Blood Donation Machine until it breaks.

• [Before Repentance] With Isaac's Heart, the Machine can be used without taking any damage.

• [Before Repentance] Invincibility frames can be used to activate a Blood Donation Machine for free.

• [Repentance] Blood Donation Machines will drain Isaac's last half Red Heart before draining Soul Hearts.

• [Repentance] The Machine will ignore Eternal Hearts if Isaac has any other heart type, unless it would deal fatal damage.

• [Repentance] If Isaac has Red and Rotten Hearts, the Machine will take Red Hearts before taking Rotten Hearts.

• [Repentance] When using Keeper or Tainted Keeper, the Machine has a chance to pay out with no coins, preventing abuse.

sections.heading: Shop Restock Machine
sections.text:
The Shop Restock Machine commonly appears in Shops in Greed Mode, and rarely in Arcades, Black Markets, Crawl Spaces, I AM ERROR rooms, Secret Rooms, and Treasure Rooms outside of Greed Mode. Shop Restock Machines also have a chance to spawn in Shops outside of Greed Mode, replacing the Donation Machine.

In Shops and Black Markets, each activation will cause the following effects:

• Rerolls every item and pickup for sale.

• Refills all empty Shop slots.

• Item pedestals in the room that are not for sale will not be rerolled.
The chance for the Shop to be restocked increases as more coins are inserted.

In all other rooms, the Shop Restock Machine will reroll any items present after donating enough pennies or blowing it up. It will not generate new items to replace the taken ones. It will reroll all items in the room even if they were not originally present (e.g. items from Beggars).

Shop Restock Machines can break after the fourth guaranteed reroll with a 50% chance for every subsequent reroll that should've been successful. This will cause them to drop a small number of coins.

[Repentance] Bombing a Shop Restock Machine breaks it immediately. 

• [Before Repentance+] When a Shop Restock Machine explodes, either through bombing or extended use, it has a chance to rapidly reroll all items a few times. With timing, any item seen briefly during the rapid reroll process can be picked up, similar to acquiring items from Glitched Crown. Saving and quitting in the middle of the reroll process will cause the items to stop rerolling upon re-entering the game.

[Repentance] Restocking the shop in the Mirrored world will make items appear in the mirrored shop. The normal shop will not be rerolled, and subsequent rerolls will not match those of the mirrored shop.

sections.heading: Mom's Dressing Table
sections.text:
Mom's Dressing Table is an object added in Booster Pack#2. [Before Repentance] If Isaac has more than 8 items, it has a 50% chance of appearing in the starting room of a floor. [end edition note] [Repentance] Mom's Dressing Tables have a high chance to spawn in Clean Bedrooms and Dirty Bedrooms. [end edition note] 

If Isaac bumps into Mom's Dressing Table, his appearance will be randomly changed such that only a few of his items are displayed.

Hitting Mom's Dressing Table with an explosive will cause it to break and drop 1-4 pills. There is a 1% chance to spawn one of the following items instead: Mom's Underwear, Mom's Heels, Mom's Lipstick, Mom's Bra, Mom's Pad, Mom's Eyeshadow, Mom's Contacts, Mom's Wig, Mom's Perfume or Mom's Pearls. Items that have already been generated and/or collected can be spawned again in this manner.

sections.heading: Crane Game
sections.text:
The Crane Game can appear in Arcades and rarely in normal rooms after being unlocked. It can also appear in the Greed Mode Shop, replacing the Shop Restock Machine. The Machine contains one visible item; after the Machine pays out, another one will be displayed. A grapple is above the items. The Machine pays out prizes from the Crane Game.

Bumping into the Machine consumes 5 cents and activates the grapple, which will attempt to grab the item in the center. If it succeeds, the item will be taken out of the Machine and appear on a pedestal.

There is a 25% chance for the Machine to pay out, so the probability of the Machine paying out after at most N tries is 1-(3/4)^N. The Machine explodes after giving 3 prizes.

Alternatively, it can be destroyed with a Bomb, which will cause it to drop several pickups.

• if the Machine is destroyed during its payout animation, it will still give the item.

The Crane Game won't change the reward item once it has been displayed, even if it was picked up elsewhere in the level. The same item can even be paid out twice in a row: the next item is determined before the first one is fully spawned, and at that point the reward is locked.

Once all items in the Crane Game item pool have been picked up, the Crane Game will only dispense Buddy in a Box.

Leaving the room while the animation is still playing after winning will cause the reward to not spawn.

[Repentance+] Crane Games have a 1% chance to appear from a X - Wheel of Fortune card.

Will be replaced with a Slot Machine if not unlocked.

sections.heading: Confessional
sections.text:
The Confessional damages Isaac with the same rules as the Blood Donation Machine in exchange for various rewards. It can be found in Super Secret Rooms or Angel Rooms, but can rarely be found in normal rooms.

The Confessional has a 30% chance on Normal Mode and 25% chance on Hard Mode to pay out. This is increased by 1.5× if Isaac has Lucky Foot.

The following are the rewards and are evaluated in the order they are listed.

• 5% chance to explode.

• 3.3% chance to explode giving an Angel Room.

• If a Deal with the Devil has been made this run, it will instead give Redemption.

• Removes a Broken Heart, if Isaac has one.

• 46.875% chance to receive a Soul Heart. Reduced to 9.375% if Isaac has Daemon's Tail.

• 3.125% chance to receive an Eternal Heart. Reduced to 0.125% if Isaac has Daemon's Tail.

• "You Feel Blessed!": Removes an active curse. For the current floor, increases Angel Room chance by 10% and allows Isaac to find an Angel Room even if he already made a Deal with the Devil. This effect stacks additively, going up to a 100% Angel Room chance at 10 activations.

• If Isaac hasn't seen any Devil Rooms or Angel Rooms before and the fortune is activated once, the deal on that floor is guaranteed to be an Angel Room.

Alternatively, it can be destroyed with a Bomb, which will cause it to drop pickups, with a chance to drop trinkets as well. Despite its appearance, destroying a Confessional does not affect Angel Room or Devil Room chance.

Will be replaced with a Soul Heart if not unlocked.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Invulnerability and shields can be used to prevent damage from it.

sections.heading: Donation Machine
sections.text: See Donation Machine.

sections.heading: [Afterbirth onward] Greed Donation Machine
sections.text: See Greed Donation Machine.

sections.heading: Revive Machine
sections.text:
The Revive Machine is used in co-op to revive players. It will always spawn in the starting room of each floor just left of the top doorway in normal and hard mode. In greed and greedier mode it will spawn somewhere in the Shop of every floor.

Bumping into the Machine costs 1 cent and lowers the number displayed on the Machine by 1. Once the counter hits 0, a single player is revived at 1 and 1/2 filled hearts (1 coin heart for Keeper and Tainted Keeper). If multiple players are dead, then the player who filled the Machine chooses who is revived. The Machine starts at a counter of 10 and increases in cost by 2 every time its requirement is reached.

Filling the Machine while there are no dead players will do nothing, but will reset the current counter.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Several messages from the Fortune Telling Machine are references to famous quotes, usually from video games:

• The message "Your princess is in another castle" is a reference to a famous quote from the 1985 NES game Super Mario Bros.

• The messages "It is dangerous to go alone" and "Go to the next room" are references to quotes from the 1986 NES game The Legend of Zelda; the former is usually followed up with "Take this".

• The message "You will die" is likely a reference to a famous quote from the Philips CDi game Zelda: The Wand of Gamelon.

• The message "I Feel Asleep!!!" is a reference to a famous quote from the 1988 NES game Metal Gear.

• The message "Look to La Luna" is a reference to a hint on how to unlock the hidden character Reptile on the 1992 game Mortal Kombat.

• The message "Come to a fork in the road - Take It" is a reference to a famous quote from baseball hall-of-famer Yogi Berra.

• The message "Steven Lives" is a reference to Time Fcuk, a previous game of Edmund McMillen's which is heavily referenced in Isaac.

• The message "Use bombs wisely" is a reference to a quote in Star Fox 64.

• The message "MARRY AND REPRODUCE" is likely a reference to one of the billboards revealed in They Live.

• The message "ASK AGAIN LATER" is one of the non-committal answers given by a Magic 8 Ball.

• Mom's Dressing Table is based on this Steam Workshop mod by Sinsthar.

sections.text:

Bug note: The Fortune Telling Machine's fortunes are broken and display as a garbled mess.

Mausoleum.title: Mausoleum
Mausoleum.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Mausoleum is the alternative floor to the Depths and was added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance.

Mausoleum is an occult-themed stage full of magic and cult material. Unique features of this stage include Teleporters and Grudges.

The door to the Mausoleum / Gehenna will appear after defeating the boss in The Mines II / Ashpit II or the Depths I / Necropolis I / Dank Depths I. The door will not spawn after defeating Mom. It costs two full hearts to enter, and ignores almost every form of damage reduction, including The Wafer and invincibility. Unlike other methods of health donation, red hearts will not be prioritized over more valuable hearts.

• The Lost, Tainted Lost, Tainted Jacob (In his soul form), Tainted Soul (unless he is holding Tainted Forgotten), and any character under the effect of Soul of the Lost can enter the door for free.

• Dad's Key, Get out of Jail Free Card, Mr. ME!, and Sharp Key can be used to open the door without taking damage.

• Broken Padlock can be used to open the door with one bomb.

• Cracked Orb's effect can open the door with less damage taken than needed, or with no damage with Dull Razor.

• The extra characters spawned by Strawman, Soul of the Forgotten, and Soul of Jacob and Esau can expend their health to open the door.

• Crow Heart can be used to open the door with red hearts first.

The boss of Mausoleum II is always a more powerful version of Mom. After Mom is defeated, a trapdoor that leads to the Womb II, and a sealed fleshy door both appear. Stabbing the door with the knife familiar created by Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2 will cause it to open, leading to a more difficult version of Mom's Heart. Defeating Mom's Heart will cause the boss room to darken, and the trapdoor to Womb II will now lead to the Corpse.

• A Sharp Key can be used in place of the Knife.

• Cracked Orb's effect can open the flesh door, allowing Isaac to keep the knife.

• If Isaac exits the Boss Rush room after 25 minutes have passed, there is a chance that the flesh door will change positions to the wall where the boss rush door was, causing Isaac to "come out" of the flesh door and leaving it open, allowing entry without the knife.

• After this special version of Mom's Heart is defeated, any Item or Pickup that was left behind anywhere on the floor will disappear (including Shop items, Angel Room/Devil Room items, etc.): the floor will be empty.

• Therefore, make sure not to leave behind something that you might want to use after this floor. The strategy consisting of teleporting outside of Mom and Mom's Heart to retrieve something that was left behind after fighting them is not viable here.

• The Boss Rush entrance will disappear if it was previously open.

• If a Shop Restock Machine is used within the now-empty shop, it will restock the shop as normal.

• If the effect of Forget Me Now is invoked after the special version of Mom's Heart is defeated, the [cu: Darkness] -like effect will remain on the newly generated floor. Additionally, no items will naturally generate in rooms where they would have. After the player defeats Mom again, there will be no flesh door, and the trapdoor to Corpse will appear.

• The alternative floor to Mausoleum is Gehenna. It is unlocked after all bosses from this floor have been defeated.

sections.heading: Unique Elements
sections.text: • Hidden Switches - Mausoleum and Gehenna commonly contain buttons hidden behind pillars which allow access to normally inaccessible areas or immediately kill all enemies in the room.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In Antibirth, fully constructing The Knife required 3 Knife Pieces, with the third appearing in Mausoleum II. For Repentance, however, the third piece was removed, and the completed knife only requires the player to obtain two pieces from Downpour and Mines.

• Also in Antibirth, there was a mechanic where somewhere on the floor, there was a special Teleporter that usually required solving a puzzle, having flight, or using pickups to access. This Teleporter led to a second section of the floor, a cluster of rooms with enemies and a few random special rooms. Since this second area was on the same map as the main part of the floor, it could also be accessed by using the Red Key enough times to reach it, or by teleporting to it with other means. Both floors of the Mausoleum had this feature, and in Mausoleum II it was required to go there to solve a puzzle in order to unlock Knife Piece 3. However, like Knife Piece 3, this mechanic was also removed in Repentance.

• The Visage was originally a Mausoleum boss in Antibirth, but it was changed in Repentance to appear on Mausoleum's alternate floor, Gehenna. Its appearance was also updated from grey and purple to black and red to reflect this.

• This might have been because of Gehenna's "torture chamber" theming, which The Visage complements more so than Mausoleum's occult theming.

• Mausoleum is referred to on Isaac's Last Will as "Some Cursed Place".

Mines.title: Mines
Mines.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Mines are the second floor of the alternate path added in Repentance. This stage can be accessed by using 2 bombs to open the boarded up door that appears after defeating the boss of the Caves / Catacombs / Flooded Caves I or II, or Downpour / Dross II. The Mines has an underground theme consisting of mostly rock and fire themed enemies and obstacles. The alternative floor of the Mines is the Ashpit, unlocked after beating every single boss from the Mines.

The Mines are significantly more difficult than their standard counterparts, filled with stone and fire-themed enemies that boast greater health, aggression and occasionally resistances to damage. Most obstacles are rocks or spiked rocks, while Poops are almost non-existent. Tinted rocks have a high chance of spawning Tinted Rock Spiders. Travelling through it is only advised if you have already acquired Knife Piece 1 in Downpour and intend to access the Corpse, however, you will still be presented with an additional, blind option in the item rooms.

After defeating the Mines II's boss, a door leading to the next alternate chapter - Mausoleum - appears. It requires 2 full hearts to open. The damage taken ignores almost every form of damage reduction, including The Wafer and invincibility. Unlike other methods of health donation, red hearts will not be prioritized over more valuable hearts.

sections.heading: Unique Elements
sections.text:
• Minecarts - Several rooms contain rail tracks with minecarts racing around on them, usually containing enemies or hazards. These enemies can be defeated as normal, and doing so will destroy the minecart.

• Throwable Bombs - Bomb Grimaces can be commonly found in various rooms which infinitely produce red, throwable bombs. Walking into one will cause Isaac to pick it up, lighting the fuse, and giving a short time window to rid of the explosive by pressing any of the fire buttons.

• Dark Rooms - Some rooms are very dark, having a more potent [cu: Darkness] effect, leaving only a small aura of light around Isaac.

sections.heading: Knife Piece
sections.text:
If Isaac has Knife Piece 1, a special double-sized room will spawn in Mines II containing a minecart and a broken length of rail track leading to a boarded-up door, resembling a Bedroom door. Behind this door lies the area in which Knife Piece 2 can be acquired. There are two methods for accessing this area:

• Three Yellow Buttons can be found in rooms throughout the floor. One will be in the same room as the broken rail track, but the other two are randomly placed. Once all three buttons are pressed, the rail track will be repaired, and once Isaac touches the minecart it will bring him into the special area.

• If Isaac has flight and 2 Bombs, he can fly to the boarded-up door and blow it open. Other effects that open doors such as Dad's Key, Soul of Cain, Cracked Orb, etc. can also be used in place of bombs.

Upon entering this area, all passive items, active items, and trinkets will be rendered inactive, and Isaac's Bombs, Penny, and Keys will be set to zero. Isaac will pass through several empty rooms before reaching a room with the Knife Piece 2. Once picked up, Mother's Shadow will spawn and chase Isaac until he reaches the entrance to the area and leaves. Once Isaac escapes, all his items will be reactivated, and Mother's Shadow will end her pursuit.

For more notes and details, see Mother's Shadow.

sections.text:

In the room, next to each button, were 1 to 4 small pebbles, indicating the order in which to press them. After all four buttons were pressed, the Knife Piece 2 would appear in the center of the room. This also wasn't the last knife piece, as there was a third piece to collect on the Mausoleum floor.

• Moles will open their eyes if encountered in a dark room, however, this doesn't change their behavior.

Necropolis.title: Necropolis
Necropolis.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Necropolis is the alternative chapter of The Depths. It is a dark environment infested with insects, with common enemies including Masks + Heart, Swarmers, and Hangers.

Necropolis is unlocked by defeating every boss from The Depths at least once.

The boss of Necropolis II is always Mom.

[Repentance] After A Secret Exit is unlocked, a door will appear in Necropolis I's Boss Room upon defeating the boss, leading to the Mausoleum / Gehenna. This door requires two hearts to be opened (except on Lost characters). Unlike Angel Rooms and Devil Rooms, this door never disappears. Also after this achievement is unlocked, a Strange Door in the starting room of Necropolis II will appear. This door leads to Mausoleum / Gehenna II before entering the Ascent.
[end edition note]

Obstacles.title: Obstacles
Obstacles.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Obstacles are objects that are meant to get in Isaac's way in rooms. Obstacles have a variety of effects, either doing nothing, acting as a gate, dealing damage to Isaac, exploding, providing loot, or slowing him down. These obstacles can be found scattered throughout rooms, with some occuring on more floors than others.

Planetarium.title: Planetarium
Planetarium.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Planetarium is an unlockable room type added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. Planetariums are similar to Treasure Rooms, in that they both require keys to enter, but always contain special Planetarium that are only available through Planetariums. Their chance for appearing increases with each Treasure Room skipped. They are unlocked by acquiring three different astrology-related items in a single run.

sections.heading: Generation Chance
sections.text:
Planetariums can only appear in chapters 1, 2, and 3 (Including their alternative floors).

• Telescope Lens allows Planetariums to generate in Womb and Corpse.

• However, Planetariums can appear in the additional Mausoleum II / Gehenna II level that is accessed through A Strange Door.
The base chance for a Planetarium to generate is 1%. This chance can be modified in various ways:

| Condition | Chance 
| Descending a floor | +20%

| Entering a Treasure Room | -20%

| Having Telescope Lens | +24%

| Having Crystal Ball | +15%
+100% if a Treasure Room has been skipped

| Having Magic 8 Ball | +15%

| Having Sausage | +6.9%

| Entering a Planetarium | Set to 1% chance and cannot be increased
Set to 10% with Telescope Lens

In other words, every Treasure Room skipped will add 20% to the generation chance. However, if additional Treasure Rooms are entered, such as those created by Forget Me Now or Red Key, then the 20% penalty for entering a Treasure Room will be taken without receiving the 20% bonus for descending a floor.

• The combined percentage from descending floors and entering Treasure Rooms will never go below 0%.

• Entering Treasure Rooms in the Mirrored World of Downpour II / Dross II will not affect the generation chance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Crystal Ball and Deck of Cards will not count towards the unlock if they are left behind after picking them up, they must be actively held.

• If Isaac loses passive items (ie: using the D4) they will not count towards the unlock. In other words, Isaac must have 3 items simultaneously.

• Planetarium items can be found before Planetariums have been unlocked in-game. To do so, use any method that ignores item pools (Chaos, Eden, etc.).

• If attempting to find a Planetarium to obtain one of its items, very careful consideration should be taken before picking up Rosary, as this will add The Bible to the Planetarium's item pool. Given the pool's small size, you will have a high chance to find it instead of a normal Planetarium item.

• A simple way to unlock Planetariums is to acquire a D20 in Greed Mode and re-roll the coins to keep buying store items (this requires a battery to recharge the D20). The item pool includes Magic 8 Ball and all Treasure Room items (which include most of the pertinent items); therefore, it can easily be unlocked.

• Acquiring the astrology-related items from the Bag of Crafting will not guarantee the Planetarium achievement.

• However, acquiring the regular Zodiac items via Bag of Crafting will grant the achievement.

• If a Planetarium has been generated, XVII - The Stars will prioritize teleporting Isaac into it over the Treasure Room.

• If a Planetarium appears on Downpour II, even if the door has been unlocked, the planetarium in the Mirrored World will be locked and will contain nothing.

• Planetariums will not be available on challenges that prevent Treasure Rooms from spawning.

• During Pica Run, a Planetarium will contain only a trinket.

• If Isaac uses Glowing Hourglass to exit a Planetarium upon first entering one, the Planetarium does not count as entered, and Planetarium chance is preserved for later floors, allowing Isaac to effectively reroll his Planetarium until a desired item is found.

• Doing a Victory Lap does not reset the entered Treasure Room count, making it very difficult to have a high chance for Planetarium generation.

• Using R Key resets the entered Treasure Room count.

• If the Planetarium layout selected was a closet-sized room, and there are no valid locations for it to spawn, then the Planetarium will not generate.

• Leaving an XL floor will count as descending 2 floors.

sections.heading: General Strategy
sections.text:
Overall, the Planetarium items are average to above-average. None of them are bad, but none of them are particularly gamebreaking either. So, given that skipping a treasure room doesn't guarantee a Planetarium showing up, it usually isn't worth skipping Treasure Rooms without a good reason to do so unless you're doing speedruns. In speedruns the global strategy is to skip everything to go to the last floor. So in that case, Terra and Mercurius are the best items and overall skipping Treasure rooms is always worth since we can have a build with only Devil or Angel deals.

Given the Ascent path takes Isaac back through previous floors, it is viable to skip item rooms on the way down to improve his chances of the Planetarium spawning and then getting the items from the rooms he skipped on the way back up. However, Planetariums can NOT generate during the Ascent, nor will skipped Planetariums "reappear".

Items such as Glowing Hourglass or Dream Catcher can be used to check the contents of a Treasure Room without negatively affecting the chances for a Planetarium to spawn.

sections.heading: Statistics
sections.text:
Without Telescope Lens, Planetarium rooms can't be found in chapter 4 and after. Since the chance to find a Planetarium depends on the number of Treasure Rooms skipped, skipping earlier ones allows for a higher cumulative chance of encountering one.

The table below presents the chances if the first Treasure Rooms are skipped. For example, if the first two are passed on, there is an 84% chance to find a Planetarium between Basement I and Depths I.

| Treasure Rooms skipped | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 
| Chapter 1-1 | 1.0% | x | x | x | x | x | x

| Chapter 1-2/1A-1 | 2.0% | 21.8% | x | x | x | x | x

| Chapter 2-1/1A-2 | 3.0% | 38.2% | 53.9% | x | x | x | x

| Chapter 2-2/2A-1 | 3.9% | 51.2% | 72.8% | 82.0% | x | x | x

| Chapter 3-1/2A-2 | 4.9% | 61.4% | 83.9% | 93.0% | 96.6% | x | x

| Chapter 3-2/3A-1 | 5.9% | 69.5% | 90.5% | 97.3% | 99.4% | 100% | x

| Chapter 3A-2 or 4-1 with Telescope Lens | 6.8% | 75.9% | 94.4% | 98.9% | 99.9% | 100% | 100%

| Chapter 4-2 with Telescope Lens | 7.7% | 81.0% | 96.7% | 99.6% | 99.98% | 100% | 100%

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Planetariums were introduced in the Antibirth mod, which forms the basis for most of Repentance's content. Their unlock method and generation mechanics remain the same in both versions.

• Their item pool in Antibirth included the Signs of the Zodiac alongside the Planetarium-exclusive items. This is not the case in Repentance.

• The original effects of most of the Planetarium-exclusive items have been unchanged from Antibirth with the item pool now having the introduction of two new items, Jupiter and Neptunus, in Repentance.

Rocks.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
• Blocks movement and projectiles unless the player has flight or spectral tears, respectively.

• Can be destroyed with explosions and certain items like the Notched Axe, The Nail, Leo, or Thunder Thighs.

• Can fill in a 1-block wide gap when pushed in the right direction by an explosion, or with one of the abilities that allows destruction by walking onto the rock.

• Note: With these items, it is important to walk in the direction of the gap.

• Small chance to reveal a Crawl Space when destroyed.

• Destroying 100 rocks will unlock the Lucky Rock trinket.

sections.heading: Tinted Rocks
sections.text:
Sometimes referred to as "Marked Rocks", they are always marked with an "X", and in some levels slightly tinted/discolored. These rocks are much less noticeable in Womb, Utero, and Scarred Womb due to them being the same color as the surrounding rocks, but can still be distinguished by the "X" on the bottom right. Only one tinted rock can spawn per room.

• Destroying 10 Tinted Rocks will unlock Mr. Mega.

• Destroying 100 Tinted Rocks will unlock The Small Rock.

• [Repentance] Multiple tinted rocks can spawn in one room by using XVI - The Tower?. [end edition note]

In Chapter 4 and Chapter 4.5, Super Special Rocks are almost identical to Tinted Rocks, making them easier to spot in these chapters.

sections.heading: Spiked Rocks [Repentance]
sections.text:
Spiked Rocks are variants of normal rocks which hurt Isaac on contact, even if he's flying.

They can fill in a 1-block wide gap like ordinary rocks, but the spikes will remain and Isaac will take damage as he steps on them. If they are located in a room with Pressure Plates, after all the plates are pressed, the spikes will retract into the interiors of the rock. If a Crawl Space is generated with the same rock used to fill a gap, the bridge will not be spiked.

Flat File will remove the spikes from the rocks.

If spiked rocks are crushed by being Stompy, having Leo or Thunder Thighs, or using The Nail, they do not always deal damage, depending on Isaac's speed, size, and the angle they are touched from.

Found in: Every stage except for Chapter 6, ??? and Home. Additionally, some layouts of Curse Rooms, Super Secret Rooms, and Boss Rush have spiked rocks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If a Spiked Rock is used to fill in a gap, stepping on the created spiked path will deal a full heart of damage. This damage is considered self-damage (it will not affect Angel/Devil Deal chances and items such as Paschal Candle). Touching Spiked Rocks, however, will not count as self-damage. [end edition note]

Sacrifice Room.title: Sacrifice Room
Sacrifice Room.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[Repentance] 

Sacrifice Rooms are special rooms that contain a set of spikes in their center.

[Rebirth only] Isaac can damage himself on the spikes for a chance to spawn a Chest or a Locked Chest. The chance is determined by the seed, meaning Isaac must damage himself on the spikes a set number of times for a Chest to spawn.

[Afterbirth onward] Sacrifice Rooms were reworked, with a wide variety of possible rewards (shown below).

[Repentance] Taking damage from the spikes doesn't reduce the odds of getting a Devil or Angel room.

The base chance of a Sacrifice Room being generated is 1/7 (~14%). If Isaac's total health is equal to or greater than his total red heart containers, an additional 1/4 chance applies for a total of 5/14 (~36%).

Sacrifice Rooms are mutually exclusive with Dice Rooms. If a Sacrifice Room is to be generated, it has a 1/50 base chance to be replaced by a Dice Room, plus an additional 1/5 chance for a total of 27/125 (~22%) if Isaac has 2 or more keys.

sections.heading: Rewards [Afterbirth onward]
sections.text:
The payouts only depend on the number of sacrifices made. The number of sacrifices is reset to 0 when Isaac goes to the next floor.

| № of sacrifices on Current Floor | Chance | Reward 
| 1st / 2nd | 50% | Nothing

| 50% | 1 Penny

| 100% [Afterbirth+ onward] | 1 Bomb (Only if the first floor boss has been defeated in less than one minute and Isaac has no bombs, to help obtain Broken Shovel 1) [end edition note]

| 3rd | 33% | Nothing

| 67% | "You feel blessed!" (increased chance to receive an Angel Room over a Devil Room for the current floor)

• Does not increase the chance of a Devil/Angel Room after defeating a boss, only the chance of getting an Angel Room over a Devil Room.

• Can cause an Angel Room to spawn even if Isaac has already taken a deal with the Devil.

• Gives a smaller bonus than the "You feel blessed!" effect below.

• [Before Repentance] A guaranteed Angel Room replacement if this occurred in a Chapter 1 XL floor.

• [Repentance] If Isaac has not yet encountered a Devil/Angel Room, guarantees the room encountered on the same floor as the sacrifice (if any) to be an Angel Room.

| 4th | 50% | Nothing

| 50% | 1 random Chest (The type of chest is governed by the same mechanic as room drops. Thus, regular chests are more likely to spawn than any other kind of chest.)

| 5th | 33% | 3 Penny (These coins do not have a chance to spawn as a nickel or a dime.)

| 67% | "You feel blessed!" (Same conditions as 3rd sacrifice but providing a stronger modifier.)

| 6th | 33% | Teleport to the Angel Room, even if past Devil Deals have been taken. If the Devil Deal on that floor has already been seen, it will sent Isaac back there instead.

| 67% | 1 random Chest (The type of chest is governed by the same mechanic as room drops. Thus, regular chests are more likely to spawn than any other kind of chest.)

| 7th | 33% | 1 random Angel Room.

| 67% | 1 Soul Heart

| 50% | [Repentance] if a Deal with the Devil was taken previously, Redemption can spawn instead if unlocked.

| 8th | 100% | [Before Repentance] 6 [Repentance] 7 Troll Bombs

| 9th | 100% | Uriel battle

| 10th | 50% | 7 Soul Hearts

| 50% | 30 Penny (individual coins may overlap)

| 11th | 100% | Gabriel battle

| 12th and onwards | 50% | Nothing

| 50% | Teleport directly to the Dark Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The sacrifice rewards are determined ahead of time, not when Isaac steps on the spikes.

• Received items/trinkets can be changed, however. If Isaac checks the items and resets (such as with the Glowing Hourglass), he can find that item on the same floor, then redo the sacrifice to force a different item to spawn.

• Resetting will reset Isaac's number of sacrifices to what it was prior to his reset unless stated otherwise.

• Spikes in a Sacrifice Room will deal damage even when flown over, so Isaac can use them even with Flight.

• Isaac must take damage on the spikes for the rewards to pay out. Invulnerability, shields, and effects that block damage (Holy Mantle, Wooden Cross, the Dog Mode Special Seed etc.) will not trigger a sacrifice.

• Temporary characters created by Strawman, Soul of the Forgotten, and Soul of Jacob and Esau can be used to make sacrifices without Isaac himself having to take damage.

• [Before Repentance] The Callus prevents the Sacrifice Room from functioning.

• Cracked Dice has a chance to re-roll the spike in the middle of a Sacrifice Room, making it unusable.

• Bone Hearts cannot be broken if filled with at least a Half Red Heart, even if a full heart of damage is taken. This can be abused to repeatedly pay a half-red heart for each use of a Sacrifice Room.

• If Redemption was already taken, 1 random Angel Room will spawn instead.

• Sacrifice Rooms do not naturally appear in the Chest, Dark Room, or The Void.

• [Repentance] They can, however, be generated in red rooms, such as those created by the Red Key.

• [Repentance] Sacrifice Rooms generated by using Red Key in the Dark Room will warp Isaac to the first room of the floor when used enough, rather than warping to a new instance of Dark Room.

• [Repentance] If more than one Sacrifice Room is created on one floor with Red Key or equivalent effects, each Sacrifice Room has its own sacrifice counter. For example, doing 3 sacrifices in one room, then 3 in another gives Isaac the 1st to 3rd effects from both rooms, instead of 1st to 3rd, then 4th to 6th. Additionally, performing more sacrifices in the first room again will count up from 4th; the count is not reset by using another room.

• [Repentance] Sacrifice Rooms won't teleport Isaac to the Dark Room during a challenge or daily challenge that does not end there, thus nothing will happen from the 12th sacrifice onward.

• [Repentance] Similarly, separate spikes even in the same sacrifice room, if spawned with the D12, have their own individual sacrifice counters. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Entering a Sacrifice Room while holding Flat File will cause the spikes to be retracted into the ground. Dropping the trinket and re-entering the room will cause the spikes to reappear.

• This room is essential for daily runs as every angel statue gives a large amount of exploration bonus without consequences of damage penalty. However, overindulging in it can make you miss Boss Rush | Hush so playing cleverly around it is a must. Something to keep in mind is that " no damage penalty " only holds true for Repentance dailies, in Afterbith and AB✞ dailies these rooms give a lot of damage penalty and aren't worthwhile unless you need a seam inside of Dark Room and / or just want to go fast.

sections.heading: [Rebirth only] Notes on Rebirth Sacrifice Rooms
sections.text:
• Only one chest can be received per Sacrifice Room.

• Taking damage down to half a red heart will always drop a chest. (Because ??? cannot have Red Heart containers, dropping down to half a heart does not guarantee a drop.)

• Dying on the spikes guarantees a chest, which can be useful if Isaac is low on health and has more lives from something like Dead Cat.

• Dying in a Sacrifice Room with the Missing Poster will reveal puzzle pieces used to unlock the The Lost.

sections.heading: [Afterbirth onward] Notes on Afterbirth Sacrifice Rooms
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Losing red hearts due to the spikes will reduce the chance for a Devil Room or Angel Room to appear.

• If Isaac receives both of the "You feel blessed!" effects, they will stack for a 65% Angel Room generation chance.

• The amount of health Isaac has left after taking a sacrifice does not affect the payout probabilities.

• Isaac's Luck stat does not affect the payout probabilities.

• If Uriel or Gabriel spawn, they can be despawned by exiting the room.

• While Uriel and Gabriel can normally fly over spikes without taking damage, they will take damage from Sacrifice Room spikes.

• Dying in a Sacrifice Room while holding Missing Poster will unlock The Lost (except during a Challenge or Victory Lap).

• Spikes in the sacrifice room normally deal one full heart of damage.

• However, if you have half a soul heart in addition to red hearts, the damage will remove the half soul heart and not deal any red heart damage.

• The Wafer, Cancer, and the [Afterbirth onward] Percs pill reduce the spikes' damage to half a heart, allowing Isaac to make more sacrifices.

• If using the BASE MENT seed, the Dark Room teleport can escape the infinite Basement floors.

• Even if The Negative isn't unlocked, Isaac can still teleport to the Dark Room.

• This allows Isaac to challenge The Lamb without facing Satan, Mom's Heart / It Lives!, or even Mom.

• Dying and respawning does not reset the number of sacrifices made, so Dead Cat can be used on low health in an attempt to acquire soul hearts.

sections.text: [achievement text: The Lost]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Found HUD will incorrectly display Angel Room generation chance at 100% when receiving either of the "You feel blessed!" effects.
Bug note: Attempting to teleport to the Dark Room via the Sacrifice Room in online multiplayer whilst having all other players be ghost babies plays the teleporting animation and locks Isaac in place, softlocking him.

Scarred Womb.title: Scarred Womb
Scarred Womb.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Scarred Womb is one of the environments in Chapter 4 added in Afterbirth. The theme of the Scarred Womb is wounded and scarred tissue, grafted skin, and early stages of decay. The floor looks much like a failed surgery, with stapled skin being plastered onto the womb's walls being this floor's alt. backdrop. Most new enemies featured in The Scarred Womb are damaged and grievously injured variations of other enemies, such as Fistuloids and Lepers. [Before Repentance] Rocks have a chance to be replaced with Red Poop.

The Scarred Womb's alternate floors are the Womb and the Utero. Similarly to these, from this floor onward, Treasure Rooms and Shops will no longer naturally generate and all damage that is taken deducts a full heart from Isaac's HP (unless he has The Wafer), regardless of the source.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Secret Rooms are rooms that are not normally visible on the map and are usually accessed by bombing a wall leading to them. Regular Secret Rooms are usually located next to 3 or 4 rooms, while Super Secret Rooms can only be next to one room; they are placed on one of the dead ends generated on the map, similar to other Special Rooms. Very rarely, the regular Secret Room may also be located next to only one room. Entrances to Secret Rooms will never have rocks or gaps in the way. Secret Rooms usually contain at least one Shopkeeper and various pickups. Items found in Secret Rooms are from the Secret Room.

Unlike the Flash version of the game, Secret Rooms stay open after bombing them.

sections.heading: [Repentance] Alt path layouts
sections.text:
Secret Rooms in alternate chapters (Downpour, Dross, Mines, Ashpit, Mausoleum, Gehenna and Corpse) differ from the standard layouts. Each alternate floor has 11 unique layouts (12 in Downpour). Regular Secret Room layouts cannot appear on these floors.

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Super Secret Rooms
sections.text:
Super Secret Rooms are only located next to one other room, and this room can't be a Special Room; in other words, it is placed on one of the floor's dead ends, like any other Special Room. Each Super Secret Room has set drops depending on the room layout, but will usually contain useful spawns such as Hearts, Chests, or Machines. Note that the visual interior of a Super Secret Room is not limited to the floor it mimics (e.g. Isaac can find a Womb-themed Super Secret Room in Caves).

Although rare, items spawned or rerolled in Super Secret Rooms still use the regular Secret Room.

Super Secret Rooms are most likely to be found either at the end of a series of rooms that lead to a dead-end, and are particularly likely to appear near the Boss Room, as they are the second room type to be placed on a map during Map Generation, and are therefore placed far away from the room Isaac starts in. Because Shops are the third type of room generated, super secret rooms are also likely to spawn near the shop, and are likely to spawn in between the shop and the Boss Room.

sections.heading: [Repentance] Ultra Secret Rooms
sections.text:
Ultra Secret Rooms are special rooms that are not connected to any other room on the map directly. They are not revealed by most mapping effects (The Mind, etc.) and can only be revealed on the map with Cracked Orb, Book of Secrets' Book of Virtues wisps, and Rune Shard. They can be accessed directly by opening Red Rooms adjacent to them using Red Key or Red Key wisps, Crystal Key, Cracked Key, and Soul of Cain: entering a Red Room next to the Ultra Secret room will reveal its position and automatically open the doorway leading into it. It can also be entered by teleporting to it using XVIII - The Moon?; when teleported into, a pathway of Red Rooms back to the rest of the level will be opened automatically. Ultra Secret rooms contain items from the Ultra Secret Room.

Ultra Secret rooms are most likely generated in spots that connect to 3+ non-red rooms through its adjacent red rooms (different squares in L rooms count as 2). They can be connected to 2 or 1 non-red rooms through its adjacent red rooms, but a specific 3+ room location is 11.5x more likely than a specific 2 room location, and 1 room locations being virtually impossible if there is a 3+ location available. If there is no 3+ room location available then a specific 2 room location is 11.5x more likely than a specific 1 room location. 

Ultra Secret Rooms can't be connected to red rooms that connect to Secret Rooms, Super Secret Rooms, or Curse Rooms, and can't be in a location where any of its adjacent red rooms are invalid, such as next to a Boss Room (Boss Rooms in The Void can have red rooms next to them, but the Ultra Secret Room will never be connected to one), next to the sides of narrow rooms, or any room that can't have a red room opened on that specific side, however locations on the 13x13 border where a red room would normally open to an I AM ERROR room are allowed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Generally, the best strategy for finding Ultra Secret Rooms is by checking a location that connects to at least 3 non-red rooms through its adjacent red rooms (in which all sides can have red rooms created, and isn't next to a Secret, Super Secret, or Curse Room), and if it's not in any 3+ locations, checking the spots connected to 2 rooms, then 1.

• When choosing which side to open from, the best way to increase your odds is to open the red room that connects to the highest number of other potential Ultra Secret Room locations.

• • However, there is also value in choosing to open a red room that connects to an otherwise hard-to-access room, such as a Boss Challenge Room.

• If the only remaining valid locations are connected to a single non-red room, it's just as likely for the Ultra Secret Room to be connected to the side of a single room as it is connected to a corner.

• The doors of the Ultra Secret Room are opened automatically only when approached from the outside. If other rooms exist adjacent to it, the doors will not open from inside the Ultra Secret Room without using the Red Key or returning from the outside.

• The Ultra Secret Room can generate north of the Mega Satan door, despite not being able to create a red room there.

• In the Mirrored World, the Ultra Secret Room will be empty, same as any Special Room.

• It's possible for the Ultra Secret Room to not generate if there are no valid locations.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Secret Rooms are found by bombing the middle of a wall in a standard size room. For larger size rooms, divide the room mentally into the size of individual rooms to figure out where to bomb.

• One easy strategy to place the bomb correctly in large rooms is to position Isaac in a corner, walk along a wall, then place the bomb at the spot where the camera starts moving.

• For closet-size rooms, Secret Rooms will never be found by bombing the sides but may be found by bombing the wall at the end of the closet.

• Rooms adjacent to Secret Rooms will always have a clear, walkable path to the middle of the wall where Isaac can place a bomb. Secret Room entrances are never found in front of gaps, obstacles, spikes, or places that enemies spawned when the room was originally entered. Each room adjacent to a Secret Room must satisfy these requirements, so if one room near a suspicious gap in the map fails these requirements, then look elsewhere.

• Secret Rooms are equally as likely to be in a valid location with 3 neighbors, as it is with 4 neighbors. 2 neighbor locations are rare but possible, even when there are locations with 3+ neighbors available. 1 neighbor locations can only happen if there are no valid 3+ neighbor locations, and are very rare. 

• X-Ray Vision opens all available entrances to both the Secret Room and the Super Secret Room. The I Can See Forever pill does the same for the floor on which the pill was used. Dog Tooth will play a howl sound effect when Isaac enters a room adjacent to a Secret Room or Super Secret Room, and YO LISTEN! will hover over Secret Room entrances.

• Teleportation items can randomly teleport Isaac into Secret Rooms, and XVIII - The Moon will always teleport Isaac to the Secret Room.

• Secret Rooms are revealed on the map with Blue Map, Book of Secrets, Crystal Ball, The Mind, Spelunker Hat, XIX - The Sun, or XXI - The World, but Isaac will still need to open their entrance.

• Red Key can be used to find Secret Rooms. The lack of Red door frame means a Secret Room could have generated on the other side.

• Star of Bethlehem sometimes reveals Secret Rooms as it can travel through them.

• If Greed or Super Greed spawn inside a Secret Room, Isaac won't be able to exit it (like a Mini-Boss Room), but once the fight ends, all the exits of the Secret Room will be accessible.

• Secret Rooms can exist next to all types of rooms except Boss Rooms, Super Secret Rooms, and other Secret Rooms; allowing certain restricted rooms to be entered.

• Even if Isaac has no Keys, it is possible to bomb into a locked Special Room should there exist an adjacent Secret Room. Leaving through the door will unlock the room without requiring a Key.

• It is possible to enter Curse Rooms without taking damage by bombing in from a Secret Room.

• It is possible to access Challenge Rooms even if Isaac doesn't meet the health requirements, but it is not possible to "steal" the items, as the hole will be blocked up as soon as the fighting stage begins.

• [Repentance] Secret Rooms of all types do not exist in the Ascent.

• [Repentance] Once Corrupted Data is achieved (beating Delirium as Tainted Eden), items that spawn in Secret Rooms have a chance to be "glitched" as if affected by TMTRAINER.

• Super Secret Rooms replace the dead-end room that would require the 2nd most rooms walked through from the start room to access, and cannot be connected to the Secret Room.

• For reference, the Boss Room takes the dead-end room that would require the most rooms walked through, and the Shop takes the room that would require the 3rd most. This means that the Super Secret Room is equally as far or further from the start room than the Shop. It also means the Super Secret Room tends to be close to the Boss Room. Loops and large rooms connected to more than one room on any given side can tamper with this logic, however.

• Sometimes, the Boss Room will not be the furthest dead-end room; usually, in these cases, the Boss Room has one side blocked off and the Super Secret Room will be connected to the furthest normal room, with the wall leading to it being on the opposite side of the blocked off side in the Boss Room.

• • For example, if the blocked off side in the Boss Room is to the north, the Super Secret Room will be to the south of the furthest normal room.

• Super Secret Rooms can have layouts with themes from floors that Isaac hasn't unlocked yet.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Secret Rooms worked differently; if the player left a room after opening a Secret Room entrance, the entrance would disappear. To access the room again for any purpose, the player needed another Bomb to reopen the entrance.

• [Before Repentance+] For some reason, Challenge Rooms and Boss Challenge Rooms still work this way.

• Prior to V1.7.5, Ultra Secret Rooms used the Angel Room. This was meant as a placeholder.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: After fighting Greed/Super Greed spawn inside a Secret Room, if there is an adjacent Challenge Room or Boss Challenge Room, the metal bars from the Greed/Super Greed fight will not disappear after the fight has ended, making it impossible to enter the Challenge/Boss Challenge room this way.
Bug note: Teleporting to the Super Secret Room in Greed or Greedier Mode, when the room is generated behind a still-locked Treasure Room, can trap Isaac inside.
Bug note: Secret rooms can be unreachable in the Dark Room. If so, they will always be diagonal to the Grave Room.
Bug note: [curse: maze] can move a room in a way that prevents creating a red room that connects to the Ultra Secret Room leading to a softlock.

Sheol.title: Sheol
Sheol.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Sheol is one of two floors following the Womb/Utero/Scarred Womb, the other being the Cathedral. After defeating Mom's Heart, depending on Isaac's deal chance, a Devil Room may spawn which will only contain a trapdoor leading down to Sheol. Other methods to enter the deal room such as Joker or Red Chests will also work. Unlocking and defeating It Lives! will always spawn a trapdoor leading to Sheol, as well as a Beam of Light leading to the Cathedral. Additionally, Sheol can be accessed using We Need To Go Deeper! or Ehwaz from The Womb II.

Sheol has only one floor, featuring undead and dark/demonic enemies, and the boss is always Satan.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In Hebrew, Sheol is translated as "place of the dead"; it is described as the common afterlife of humans in Jewish religious lore (including the Old Testament), making it the Abrahamic version of the underworld.

• Sheol is the ninth level of the game (without there being a Curse of the Labyrinth). The 14th-century novel Inferno, the first part of Dante Aligheri's famous Divine Comedy and one of the first books to describe Hell in detail, notes that the ninth and lowest layer of Hell, where those who commit the sin of betrayal are sent, is frozen. On Isaac's last will, it says he died in "a cold place" if he dies in Sheol.

• The ninth layer of Hell is said to be where Satan, who turned against God and was cast down for it, is imprisoned, indicating the reason for Satan's presence in the area.

• It's also said that the ninth layer of Hell is the prison for Judas Iscariot, the betrayer of Jesus, which may be the reason that Judas is unlocked there.

• Like in all chapters, small non-interactive objects can be found on the ground. One of these decorations is a drawing of a triangle that may be a reference to the Triforce, an iconic relic from The Legend of Zelda series.

• There is an unused version of Sheol, which uses textures for Dark Room, but with a black background. It can be accessed by typing stage 10b in the Debug Console.

sections.heading: Music
sections.text:
• The music for Sheol is titled Duress.

• The term duress means intimidation or coercion and usually denotes violence.

Shop.title: Shop
Shop.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Not to be confused with The Shop, a floor in Greed mode.

[Before Repentance] [Repentance] 

A Shop is a Special Room that sells various pickups and items in exchange for Penny. Shops require a Key to open, unless Isaac holds Store Key ( [Repentance] except on floor 1, where Shops are always initially unlocked), and appear in every Chapter prior to Womb or including The Womb if Isaac holds Silver Dollar. [Afterbirth onward] Additionally, a single Shop always spawns adjacent to the ??? starting room. [end edition note] 

Only one shop will ever appear on a floor at a time, even while under the effect of [cu: Labyrinth] .

Shops have a chance of being replaced by a Mini-Boss Room containing Greed or Super Greed once entered, starting on the second floor of Chapter 2. Once both mini-bosses has been defeated in a Shop or Secret Room, they will not appear in either for the rest of the run.

• Greed will always spawn first, followed by Super Greed.

• [Before Repentance] If any mini-boss is encountered on the floor, including Greed/Super Greed in the secret room, Greed or Super Greed will not appear in the shop on that floor.

• Rib of Greed prevents both Greed and Super Greed from appearing in Shops while held.

sections.heading: [Afterbirth onward] Greed Mode
sections.text:
In Greed Mode, Shops are twice as wide as usual and do not require a key to enter. They always contain a Key, a Red Heart, an item from the Greed Shop, an item from the Greed Boss, and two random pickups, trinkets, or items from the Greed Treasure Room. The effect of Restock is always active inside of Shops in this mode ( [Repentance] prices will not increase continuously like they normally would when Isaac has Restock).

Shops will never be replaced by Greed or Super Greed in Greed Mode.

Layouts can be found here.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Merchandise
sections.text:
• Shops can sell Red Hearts for [pennies: 3] . They can also sell Soul Hearts, Bombs, Keys, Lil' Battery, Pills, and Cards for [pennies: 5] each.

• [Repentance] Also: Grab Bags for [pennies: 7] . [end edition note] 

• Shops can sell items for [pennies: 15] , from among those found in the Shop.

• [Repentance] Certain active items are sold for [pennies: 10] .

• Any purchasable item has a chance to be discounted, which will cut its price in half.

• Discounted items have red price tags instead of white price tags.

• If a discount leaves the price of an item at a number that is not an integer, items and Grab Bags will round their price down while pickups will round their price up.

• Steam Sale will halve all prices in the Shop (and anywhere else items are bought for coins), [Before Repentance] including discounted ones.

• [edition anr] Two Steam Sales will make every item free, which can be combined with Restock to allow infinite purchasing power. This also holds true in Greed Mode.

sections.heading: Layouts
sections.text:
Shops start at level 0 and can be upgraded by donating Coins to the Donation Machine, which can be found in Shops and sometimes in Arcades, Vaults, Black Markets, rare normal/special room layouts, and from pressing [Afterbirth onward] Reward Plates. Each level increases the number of items for sale and visually fills the walls of the Shop.

[Repentance] Normal mode will always feature the highest unlocked level of Shop. In hard mode, any level of shop that has been unlocked can appear. The room has 1/256 chance to be a rare shop (layouts 5, 6, 12, 13), then the weight determines which layout will be chosen.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Shop can also be accessed through the usage of IX - The Hermit, a Golden Key, [cu: Maze] , Dad's Key, bombing an adjacent Secret Room wall, or Store Key, without spending a Key.

• [Before Repentance] The Shop has a door that is identical to a Library as well as an identical symbol on the minimap. The Shop can never appear adjacent to the starting room (with the exception of the first floor), meaning that any one-key door that spawns adjacent to the starting room is a Library and not a Shop.

• Store Key will not open Library doors, which reveals which room the locked door will lead to.

• Using a Credit Card in the shop will make everything for sale free, spawning item pedestals and removing all listed prices.

• Restock only replenishes items that are bought for a listed price (including [pennies: 0] ); therefore, Credit Card negates the effect of Restock for that Shop.

• Holding Store Credit will reduce the price of all items to [pennies: 0] . It will be consumed once an item is purchased. Unlike the Credit Card, Restock will restock the bought item.

• [edition anr] If the Store Credit effect is gained through the effects of Error, it will not be consumed upon making a purchase; this can be combined with Restock to infinitely purchase items. [end edition note] 

• • [Repentance] Only 1 item can be bought for free without losing the trinket, even if Error is dropped and picked up again.

• Diplopia and Jera function as expected in Shops, generating free pickups/items.

• The Shopkeeper that spawns in the Shop can be bombed for potential rewards.

• Special Shopkeeper can replace the regular shopkeeper at a chance, which can drop better rewards.

• [Before Repentance] A total of 9 Shops maximum can be entered during a normal run — two in Basement/etc., two in Caves/etc., two in Depths/etc., two in Womb/etc. with the Silver Dollar, and one in ???.

• [Repentance] This is increased to 10 if Isaac additionally holds Holy Crown or Wicked Crown in Cathedral or Sheol respectively, and Isaac can theoretically encounter many more Red Shops with Red Key. [end edition note] 

• Multiple different shops can also be entered in one floor through resetting effects such as Forget Me Now or R Key.

• [Repentance] Items will increase in price the more bought with Restock until maxing out at 99 cents. [end edition note]
