Void.title: Void
Void.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the item; the chapter; The Void] 

It is the starting item for Apollyon.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, destroys all pedestal items in the room. Items that require payment cannot be absorbed unless they are bought first.

• If Void destroys an activated item, it gains the activated ability of that item; whenever Void is used, it will simultaneously use all previous active items that were absorbed in the same order they were absorbed. Passive effects of absorbed active items will not apply (e.g., the passive effect of Mom's Box). The active item effects happen after the initial destruction of current pedestal items, and in the order that the active items were absorbed. 

• If Void destroys a passive item, Isaac gains 2 random stat boosts. Possible stat changes include:

• • +1 flat Damage

• • [Before Repentance] +0.5 Tears

• • [Repentance] +0.5 Fire Rate

• • +0.2 Speed

• • 
• [Before Repentance] Also affects maximum speed (may never exceed 2.0)

• • +0.2 Shot Speed

• • +1 Luck

• • [Before Repentance] +0.5 Range

• • [Repentance] +2.5 Range

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] If speed or tears are at their maximum and are chosen, there will be no visible increase.

• [Repentance] If speed is at its maximum and is chosen, there will be no visible increase.

• [Repentance] Void can exceed the normal maximum tears limit.

• Using Void to absorb items in Boss Rush or Challenge Rooms counts as taking the items and will cause waves of bosses or enemies to start spawning.

• [Before Repentance] The ability of the newly absorbed active item(s) will activate even if the item has no charge. Using any multiple-use item before absorbing it with Void will effectively allow Isaac to use the item twice.

• [Repentance] If Void is used while Isaac is holding an item above his head, it can still consume the item, allowing to immediately absorb passive items bought from Devil Rooms, Black Markets, or Shops. This also can be used to give Isaac a chance to see what an unknown item is before deciding if he wants to consume it, in the case of an active [cu: Blind] or a Treasure Room in Downpour, etc.

• This mechanic can be used to absorb familiars granted by Soul of Lilith.

• Active items can also be absorbed this way if Isaac has Schoolbag and is not carrying a second active item. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The newly absorbed active item(s) won't be used right away, but with the next usage of Void.

• [Repentance] If Isaac absorbs items from a room with choice pedestals, it will only absorb one item, and the other item vanishes as if Isaac took it.

• If Isaac finds another Void, such as during a Victory Lap where it is left behind in the previous lap, it will have the same active effects stored in it as the other Void.

• Consuming a second Void will create no effect.

• If multiple copies of an active item are absorbed, using Void will activate that effect equally many times.

• Stat boosts upon destroying passive items are determined by the seed and are tied to the number of items destroyed, not the items themselves. If Isaac runs the same seed and chooses to consume different passive items, the same stat boosts will be gained.

• [Repentance] Void's random number generation is advanced once after each usage, so using Void will change what stat boosts are gained.

• Stat boosts are permanent and are retained if Void is dropped (except when the player's build is rerolled, e.g. with D4 or D100).

• Using Void to absorb Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2 will not permanently remove them from the run. They will continue to spawn after defeating Uriel or Gabriel no matter how many times Isaac uses Void on them, as long as he does not pick them up normally.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Alabaster Box: Allows the box to be charged through normal means, rather than by absorbing soul hearts.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns the wisps of all the active items Void has absorbed. Spawns no wisps by itself. Using Void on Book of Virtues will give stat upgrades instead of its normal effect, as Book of Virtues is considered a passive item.

• Breath of Life: Immediately grants invincibility frames.

• Panic Button: Getting hit with Breath of Life stored inside Void will negate the damage.

• Crooked Penny: Using Void with the Crooked Penny absorbed will result in items in the room being absorbed as usual, but afterwards new copies of the items or one coin are spawned.

• [Repentance] If Crooked Penny deletes the contents of the room, they will not be consumed by Void.

• Eraser: Allows the Eraser to be used multiple times per floor.

• Glass Cannon: Can be used without it ever breaking or causing damage to the player.

• [Before Repentance] More Options / There's Options: Using Void will cause both items to be absorbed.

• Moving Box: Moving Box will not be added to Void; instead, it is converted into stat boosts like a passive item.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Abyss: Since consumed activated items are used before absorbing new items in a room, using Void with Abyss stored inside will destroy pedestals with Abyss' effect first, essentially overriding Void's item consumption effects. Previously consumed active items will still function as normal when using Void. Passive items can still be consumed with Void by picking them up before using Void.

• Blank Card + ? Card: Using the ? Card with an absorbed Blank Card simply activates Void. Isaac will not be teleported to the I AM ERROR room and Void will not be deleted.

• Broken Remote / Teleport! / Teleport 2.0 / Undefined / any other teleport method: Void will still consume any item pedestals in the room, after which the teleport occurs.

• [Before Repentance] The D6 / D100: If absorbed while there are other pedestal items in the room, it will reroll the items before absorbing them. Likewise, if The D6 or D100 was previously absorbed and Void is used, pedestal items will get rerolled before being absorbed.

• [Repentance] The D6 and D100 can't roll items while being absorbed since their effect isn't triggered the first time anymore but any subsequent Void uses will still roll items before absorbing them.

• Death Certificate: Only allows the consumption of one item per Death Certificate room and the consumed item is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.

• D infinity: When absorbed and Void is used, replicates the effect of a random die item.

• [Repentance] Acts as a copy of one of the 10 dice D infinity can replicate. This die is randomly chosen and does not change.

• [Before Repentance] Diplopia / Forget Me Now / Pandora's Box / Mama Mega! / Mystery Gift / any single-use active item: They are used once upon being absorbed, but their effects are not absorbed and will not activate with subsequent Void uses.

• [Repentance] Single-use items won't be used upon their absorption, instead being invoked on the next usage of the Void, which allows Isaac to use the absorbed item later when needed. Their effects will still only be invoked once.

• • Car Battery: As Void will be activated twice, single-use items are immediately used when absorbed.

• • When multiple copies of a given single-use active are in Void, only half of them will be used each time Void is activated, rounded up.

• Diplopia: On the next use, the pedestal items in the room will be consumed but another copy of the items will be spawned afterward.

• • Diplopia + Mystery Gift: If both items are absorbed in the same room, the next use of Void will only trigger Mystery Gift, with the use afterward activating Diplopia

• [Repentance] Everything Jar/Larynx: Will only replicate the 1-charge version of the effect. [end edition note] 

• Flip/Jar of Flies/The Jar/Stitches/Notched Axe/Esau Jr.: None of these items do anything when absorbed by Void.

• When playing as Tainted Lazarus, and Flip is absorbed by the void, it will still flip the character. But it is not normally possible to obtain a second Flip, and therefore not normally possible to absorb it.

• Genesis: All effects granted by absorbed items including stat ups and activated item abilities Void takes are removed without creating items to replace them. Since Void is stripped of any active item abilities it would have gained, any other Void found will also have no other active effects stored in it.

• Void's active effects are reset even if Isaac is currently not holding it.

• Glowing Hourglass: Upon using Void, Isaac is sent to the previous room and most changes are reverted, nullifying many other effects that Void may have absorbed. If the Glass is absorbed in a shop, Isaac is sent back to the previous room, but the Glass will be unused in the shop on its pedestal. This allows for an infinite shop donation circle, eliminating the need for a battery to be present in the shop.

• [Repentance] Hourglass can now be used indefinitely per floor, but every use will cost the entire charge of Void. Makes most active items and Apollyon's Birthright useless.

• How to Jump: If this item is activated by Void, it is possible to get stuck in an impassable area with no ability to escape. Exiting and resuming the run will place Isaac at whichever door he entered the room through.

• Jar of Wisps: Each use will spawn only one wisp.

• Mega Blast / Mega Mush: Allow to use it every [Before Repentance+] 6 or [Repentance+] 4 charges instead of 12. Batteries will also full charge Void, instead of giving [Before Repentance] 3 or [Repentance] 6 charges to Mega Blast.

• Remote Detonator: Absorbing it with Void does not cause bombs to remain on the ground until Void is used, but using Void explodes all player-placed bombs as usual.

• Sharp Key: Using the Void will cause Isaac to shoot a key the next time he will press the fire key. Keys are consumed as normal.

• Spin to Win: A spinning top orbital will spawn every time the Void is used. The orbitals will last until Isaac leaves the room.

• Breath of Life: Using Void with Breath of Life will immediately grant invincibility frames, then inflict damages to Isaac every second until he leaves the room.

• Urn of Souls: Although a sound effect will play, using Void will do nothing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• When this item was originally teased, it had a recharge counter of four and converted pickups into blue flies; in its release, it was nerfed to a recharge counter of six and the ability to convert pickups to flies became the item Compost.

• [Repentance+] The recharge time was changed back to four in Repentance+.

• The original effect of the item may have become a base for Void's future counterpart, Abyss.

• Before the balance patch on 5 January 2017, Void synergized with single-use items such that it would trigger them upon each use of Void; this has since been removed.

• Void is one of only five items to appear in both the Angel Room and Devil Room item pools, the others being 7 Seals, Lil Delirium, Duality and Purgatory.

• The swirl in Abyss's appearance is in the opposite direction of Void's.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Sacrificial Altar is fully absorbed, unlike other single-use active items, allowing Isaac to sacrifice familiars and obtain Devil Room items with each activation of Void.
Bug note: If Isaac has overcharge from The Battery, using absorbed items that Isaac can "put away" (e.g. Shoop da Whoop!, Bob's Rotten Head, Eraser, and Notched Axe) will use all the overcharge, even when Isaac puts away the items. In the case of Notched Axe on its own, using Void will use all charges at once.
Bug note: Pedestal items do not vanish instantly upon Void usage, allowing for an item to be obtained despite using Void on it. While the animation when using the Void prevents picking up pedestal items, this can be circumvented by cancelling the animation (e.g. using bombs or timed damage mechanisms like Shard of Glass) or by having another player.

fields.description: Consumes all pedestal items in the room. Activated items will have their effects added to Void, and passive items will grant random stat upgrades.

Voodoo Head.title: Voodoo Head
Voodoo Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns an additional Curse Room on each floor, if possible.

• Doesn't work on the Ascent.

• Curse rooms have improved layouts and rewards while Voodoo Head is held.

• A coin is guaranteed to spawn in Curse Rooms.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Has no effect in Greed Mode.

• The singular coin generated by the item in curse rooms cannot be a special coin (nickel, dime, lucky, etc).

• Does not retroactively upgrade the current floor's curse room when picked up, if one exists. Its layout won't be improved and there is no guaranteed coin.

• This item is beneficial for The Lost due to the chance of obtaining Dead Cat or Guppy's Collar in curse rooms. However, use caution as the run can easily end from being hit while fighting any enemies inside. A teleport card, such as 0 - The Fool, would be advised to prevent such situations.

• This item is also very beneficial for Tainted Judas or Tainted Forgotten, as they can enter and leave curse rooms for free.

• The coin that spawns, while minimal for most characters, is considerably useful for Keeper and Tainted Keeper, letting them partially heal from the curse room door's donation and letting Tainted Keeper leave even if there are no enemies to get coins from.

• This item causes the level generation to increase the minimum number of dead ends on each floor by 1, increasing the likelihood of curse rooms spawning.

• The level generation does not guarantee an additional curse room can be placed; there is limited space for special rooms, and other types may take priority over it.

• • If a curse room doesn't spawn, it's possible Voodoo Head still increased the dead end count, giving you an extra special room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Cursed Penny: The coin can be used to teleport out of the curse room and avoid the damage from exiting through the curse room’s door.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Voodoo Head is from the Antibirth mod where it had similar effects, except it would not improve the contents of Curse Rooms.

fields.description: Spawns an additional Curse Room on each floor. Curse Rooms have improved layouts.

Wait What?.title: Wait What?
Wait What?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac farts, knocking back enemies and their shots. It also sends out a circular rock wave around him that deal 10 damage per tick to nearby enemies and break obstacles.

• [Repentance] Shots deflected by Wait What? farts deal 6 damage if they would've hurt Isaac for half a heart, and 7 for a full heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item is identical to Butter Bean in appearance.

• [Before Repentance] Butter Bean has a 10% chance to turn into this item upon pickup.

• [Repentance] Each run has a 5% chance of replacing Butter Bean with Wait What? in item pools. Both items generally do not exist during the same run.

• One way for both items to exist in the same run is via Death Certificate or Spindown Dice. Since both items are identical in appearance, you can differentiate them by looking at the items that are next to them, Butter Bean will be between Head of Krampus and Magic Fingers while Wait What? will be between Mama Mega! and Crooked Penny.

• This item is useful for opening Secret Rooms, Super Secret Rooms, Bedrooms and the path to Mines. In Bedrooms, it can also open up the passage under the carpet.

• To break open a secret room, the wall must be hit with one of the rock waves, not the gas cloud, so Isaac needs to stand a few steps away from the wall.

• The earthquake can open Bomb Chests.

• The earthquake can destroy Shopkeepers.

• [Before Repentance] The earthquake can be used to blow up the Donation Machine or activate/blow up a Shop Restock Machine.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns white glowing wisps on the middle ring that don't shoot. The wisps invoke the effect of Wait What? when destroyed and do not persist between rooms.

• Ghost Pepper / Bird's Eye: Shoots a flame behind Isaac upon each use of Wait What. Despite Car Battery not duplicating Wait What's shockwave, the flame shot is duplicated.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item description is a reference to a brand of margarine named "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter!".

• [Before Repentance] Unlike Butter Bean, this item has no unlock condition, meaning it's possible for the player to find it right away, making the joke and reference slightly confusing.

• [Repentance] Wait What? no longer shows up naturally in any item pools, however it has a chance to replace Butter Bean in any run.

• The sprite of this item is exactly identical to that of Butter Bean, making them the two only items that are visually identical in the game.

fields.quote: I can't believe it's not butter bean!
fields.description: Isaac farts, sending out a circular rock wave that destroys obstacles and hurts enemies.

Walnut.title: Walnut
Walnut.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • While held, being hit with an explosion has a 33% chance to destroy the trinket and spawn a Penny, a Red Heart, a Key and another trinket. The pickups may be of any normal variety.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Taking damage from the explosion is not required to trigger the effect. This makes effects granting Invulnerability very useful for safely destroying the Walnut.

• Getting hit by multiple explosions simultaneously has a high chance of cracking the Walnut, as every individual explosion will have its chance to activate the effect, no matter how closely they occur.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either makes the trinket spawn 2 of each mentionned pickups. Having both makes the trinket spawn 3 of each.

• Bomber Boy: As Bomber Boy causes 9 explosions at once, laying a bomb and not moving before it explodes is almost guaranteed to trigger the trinket.

• Gnawed Leaf: Isaac will not be knocked back from the explosions, but it will count for the trinket.

• Holy Mantle: Explosions hitting the mantle still count for the trinket.

• Host Hat / Pyromaniac: Isaac becomes immune to explosions, which allows to get the effect without any risk.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Walnut: Two copies cannot be held at the same time.

fields.name: Walnut
fields.quote: That's a hard nut to crack!
fields.description: Being hit by explosions will eventually destroy the trinket and spawn various pickups.

War.title: War
War.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: War is a Harbinger that can appear in all environments of Chapter 3 (Depths, Necropolis, Dank Depths).

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
• Charges either left or right off-screen and continuing on from the opposite end of the screen. Continues until he has crossed the screen three times.

• He performs this attack more often if Isaac is to his left or right.

• Shoots eight projectiles in all directions.

• Ascends off-screen and summons 5 Troll Bombs.

• Returns from the side of the screen.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Once his health is below half, War's horse blows up, dropping War, who performs a crying animation.

• War charges quickly at Isaac gradually building speed and making more tighter turns.

• Every time War loses around 1/3rd of his remaining HP in this phase, he pauses briefly to sob before restarting this process.
War deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases and during his charge.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 2] : 15% larger with 25% more HP (625). Summons 2 Mega Troll Bombs when he ascends off-screen and summons a single Troll Bomb behind his path when he charges through the screen. When transforming into his second phase, he shoots 6 projectiles in all directions, as well as each time he stops chasing Isaac in this phase.

sections.heading: Unlockable achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Revelations, 7 Seals]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• War appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• War is one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse mentioned in the Bible.

• In many depictions of War, he is shown holding a sword vertically, corresponding with why War's battle sprite shows him holding his hobby-horse vertically.

• Although his appearance on the vs screen shows his hobby-horse as brown, it is red in-game.

• War's "horse" appears more akin to a bull.

• In the original game, War's face was round.

• [Repentance] This has been somewhat reverted.

• War can be seen wielding a Wire Coat Hanger as a weapon in one of the original game's concept arts.

• When holding Mars, Isaac strongly resembles War, referencing the Roman god of war, Mars.

Watch Battery.title: Watch Battery
Watch Battery.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Increases the chance of a Lil' Battery pickup after clearing a room by 6.67%.

• Increases the chance of random pickups being a Lil' Battery by 2%.

• Has a 5% chance to add an extra charge to Isaac's activated item upon completing a room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Watch Battery: Each copy gives one more extra charge when the 5% chance on room clear triggers. [end edition note] 

• Jacob's Ladder: Increases arcing distance of sparks.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • AAA Battery: Watch Battery triggering after clearing a room will also trigger AAA Battery, provided the activated item was missing exactly 3 charges prior to clearing the room.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Watch Battery will not contribute to unlocking Jumper Cables despite having the item tag.

fields.description: Increased chance of Lil' Battery spawning. Has a chance to add an extra charge to Isaac's activated item upon completing a room.

Wavy Cap.title: Wavy Cap
Wavy Cap.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, grants +0.75 fire rate, -0.03 speed, and distorts the screen and background music. The effects can be stacked in the same room, and the distortion becomes more pronounced with repeated use. After repeated uses, the colors begin to turn very bright and intense.

• Each use increases the recharge time, which starts at 0.5 seconds with the 1st use, and ends with 15 seconds on the 9th use. After the 10th use, it no longer recharges automatically though it can be recharged and used even more through Lil' Battery.

• Leaving the room doubles the speed penalty and multiplies the fire rate bonus by x0.4, for the uses in that room.

• Clearing a room removes one use's worth of penalties and bonuses, giving +0.06 speed and -0.3 fire rate.

• Isaac's costume will change the stronger the Item's effects get.

• Contributes to the Fun Guy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • This item can very rarely drop from destroying mushrooms in the Secret Room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Gives a damage bonus which lasts until the next floor equal to 0.2 × the maximum number of times Wavy Cap's effects have been stacked.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Creates a single mushroom wisp on the middle ring, firing 1.5 damage tears. Only one of these wisps can exist at a time.

• Rock Bottom: The distortion effect will wear off eventually, but the highest reached fire rate bonus won't. However, Wavy Cap will no longer have any positive effects until an even higher bonus is reached.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tainted Lazarus / Esau Jr.: The distortion effect will not be removed when flipping between characters.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Wavy Cap originates from the Antibirth mod, and was called Black Mushroom. By extension, it was also from the Community Remix mod for the flash version.

• In Community Remix, its effects were permanent, always had an instant recharge time, and did not have any screen distortion effects.

• Since the fire rate increase is flat, it is technically possible to reach the hard cap of 120.0 with enough uses. In practice this renders the game unplayable due to distortion.

• The distortion effect applied to Isaac is very similar to the one seen in Yoshi's Island when touching a Fuzzy.

• On final stages of the distortion, the wave effect will appear to make parts of the top of the screen on the lower screen and the lower screen on top of the screen, while bright colors dance on the screen, similar to how psychedelic trips are described.

• Wavy Cap, also known as Psilocybe cyanescens, is a species of potent psychedelic mushroom.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using the item causes the game to crash.
Bug note: If the player continues a save after maximizing the use of the Wavy Cap, they will respawn with the fire rate increase and changed appearance, but none of the screen effects. The screen effects will return at the same intensity once a room is cleared.

fields.quote: Tears up. A mind changing experience!
fields.description: Increases tears, decreases speed, and distorts the screen. All effects become more pronounced with repeated use, and wear off by clearing rooms.

| Ultra Greed | Some gems are animated. |
[end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The item may be used on the Dirt Patches in the Dark Room to dig up a random type of chest.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• All Crawl Space trapdoors on a floor lead to the same Crawl Space.

• It can be used in Depths II to access Womb even before defeating Mom and gaining the achievement which 'unlocks' the Womb.

• If used in Womb II / Utero II / Scarred Womb II, the trapdoor will always lead to Sheol.

• [Before Repentance] Has no effect in the Cathedral, Chest, Sheol, Dark Room, ??? and The Void (no trapdoors of any type will be generated).

• [Repentance] It can only create crawl space trapdoors in the Cathedral, Chest, Sheol, Dark Room, ???, The Void, Corpse II, Dad's Note floor, Home, and during the Ascent. However the chance for the crawl space trapdoor to appear does not change. [end edition note] 

• Using the item on the 3 tiles directly horizontal to a door, including Secret Room entrances, will cause the trapdoor to spawn in a random spot next to Isaac instead, making this item an indirect aid to locating Secret Rooms.

• [Repentance] If a special graphic is in these spots, the trapdoor will likely be moved to a spot that won't spawn a Crawl Space.

• Spawning enough trapdoors can cause a trapdoor to spawn in these spots.

• This item can be used to destroy rocks if used while Isaac is flying over a rock.

• If a crawlspace is spawned before activating a Challenge Room or Boss Challenge Room, the crawlspace will remain open during the fight. Entering and exiting the crawlspace skips the fights entirely.

• [Before Repentance] When used on the last floor of a challenge, a trapdoor to the next floor can spawn. If it is entered, Isaac must beat the boss of that floor to spawn the ending trophy.

• [Repentance] Trapdoors will not spawn on challenges on floors at the final destination, however certain challenges like Red Redemption may still spawn a trapdoor leading to the next floor.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a skull wisp on the middle ring that shoots bone tears.

• Lil Portal: upon entering a trap door (not a Crawl Space), inside the Lil Portal special room, Isaac will be teleported to the I AM ERROR Room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: In most cases, no extra effect. When used near the entrances to a room, the item can occasionally open 2 trapdoors at once, [Before Repentance] increasing the chance of opening a Crawl Space.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The name of this item is a reference to the movie Inception.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If a trapdoor is spawned inside of a Black Market with this item and is entered, the player is trapped in the Crawl Space unless they go to the next floor.

fields.description: Creates a trapdoor to go to the next floor. [Repentance] Once per floor, using it on tiles with special graphics will instead create a Crawl Space.

Whip Worm.title: Whip Worm
Whip Worm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Increases Shot Speed by 0.5.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance+] This trinket has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Pin, Larry Jr., The Hollow or Scolex. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy increase shot speed by 0.5.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Whipworms (Trichuris trichiura) are intestinal parasites that most commonly infect dogs and humans.

fields.name: Whip Worm
fields.description: Increases shot speed by 0.5.

White Pony.title: White Pony
White Pony.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Passively grants flight.

• If Isaac's speed is less than 1.5, passively increases his speed to 1.5.

• Upon use, Isaac charges in the direction the pony is facing, giving invincibility during the charge and damaging enemies while also creating beams of light.

• [Before Repentance] The beams of light are spaced randomly around the room and deal the same damage as those created by Crack the Sky.

• [Repentance] The beams of light deal 4 times Isaac's damage, plus a flat 10 damage and trail behind Isaac as he charges.

• [Before Repentance] The dash deals 40 flat contact damage to enemies.

• [Repentance] The dash deals 4 times Isaac's damage, plus a flat 28 damage.

• [Repentance] Isaac can dash through doors, which means that damage from Curse Room doors can be avoided.

• • Although the dash can persist between rooms, the beams of light only occur in the room it is used in.

• While not time-based, invincibility from White Pony is otherwise identical to damage immunity granted by the invulnerability effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• White Pony is only obtainable as a boss drop from Conquest, as a starting item for Eden, by using Spindown Dice on Sacred Heart, or by using Death Certificate.

• White Pony cannot be crafted with the Bag of Crafting.

• If White Pony is replaced by another activated item, Isaac will lose any passive benefits that it had granted.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Creates white pony wisps on the middle ring that fire white tears with a 10% chance to fire Holy Light tears. The beams of light the wisps' tears make deal extra damage to enemies in a small area equal to 3x the wisps' tear damage.

• Mars: Using White Pony after dashing lowers the dash cooldown to approximately 1 second.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Taurus / Thunder Thighs: The speed decreases from the items can lower Isaac's speed past 1.50 (making the new lower speed limits 1.20 and 1.10, respectively). Having both items can lower the minimum speed to 0.80.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to the White Horse, one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse described in the last book of the Bible. This is reinforced by the fact that the item is dropped by Conquest, which is a further reference to that passage of Christian theology.

• The item appears to be a stick horse.

fields.description: Passively grants flight and increases speed to 1.5. Upon use, Isaac charges in the direction the pony is facing, giving invulnerability during the charge while also creating damaging beams of light.

Whore of Babylon.title: Whore of Babylon
Whore of Babylon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants +1.5 Damage and +0.3 Speed whenever Isaac has a Half Red Heart or less.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Eve starts with this item by default, and has the following extra effects:

• The item is activated at one full Red Heart or less.

• Her damage multiplier increases from 0.75 to 1.0 when active.

• The effect is removed after leaving a room with more than half a heart (more than one full heart for Eve).

• The effect may not be immediately applied if Isaac has lost red hearts without taking damage; the effect will activate upon entering a new room.

• The effect is always active for characters without Red Heart containers, such as ??? and The Lost, though other characters can also lose their heart containers through Devil deals or items like Guppy's Paw or Abaddon.

• III - The Empress grants a similar effect to Whore of Babylon for the current room which does stack with Whore of Babylon.

• Stacking The Empress on Whore of Babylon either via multiple cards or multiple activations of Blank Card increases damage by the number of uses squared, e.g. +1.5 * 2 * 2 total damage bonus for using the card on top of activated Whore of Babylon.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Rights / Razor Blade / IV Bag / Sumptorium: As these items takes Red Hearts before other heart types, it can be use to get the Whore of Babylon activation's condition easier.

• Sharp Plug / Blood Bombs: Prioritize removing Red Hearts first although are conditional on having an applicable active item or having zero bombs. 

• Shard of Glass: Will slowly drain Isaac's red hearts upon taking damage, eventually triggering Whore of Babylon, unless Isaac has a Rotten Heart with no soul, black or bone hearts (unless playing as Eve). 

• Blood Oath: Consistently triggers Whore of Babylon at the start of each floor along with giving other bonuses. 

• Guppy's Paw / Potato Peeler: Can be used to remove red health containers to keep Whore of Babylon Active.

• Magic Skin / VI - The Lovers?: Prioritize removing red heart containers with the downside of giving a Broken Heart with each use 

• Crow Heart: Can be used to remove red hearts while keeping soul and black hearts intact.

• The Forgotten: By quickly switching to The Soul, Whore of Babylon can be triggered for the room if The Forgotten does not meet the trigger conditions.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Birthright + Eve: Whore of Babylon will be active at all times.

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper: As Keeper cannot have half of a Coin Heart, this item has no effect on him.

• Rotten Hearts: Counts as a full Red Heart for the purposes of this item, rendering it impossible to activate (except for Eve).

• Whore of Babylon: No further effect when multiple copies are acquired.

• Placenta / Charm of the Vampire / Leech / Sol: Regen effects can make triggering Whore of Babylon difficult if Isaac has empty Red Heart Containers.

• Isaac's Fork / Mom's Locket / Stem Cell: Regen effects from trinkets can be problematic in maintaining Whore of Babylon if swallowed or smelted 

• Cambion Conception / Soul of Lilith: Have a chance of granting Leech, although are likely still worth using for the chance of receiving strong familiars.

• Dogma: Is forcefully given to Isaac after defeating Dogma, which among other effects heals him up to at least 6 hearts by filling Red Heart Containers and giving Soul Hearts. Forcing Isaac out of Whore of Babylon if he has at least 1 Red Heart Container while under 5 hearts (2 Containers while under 4 hearts for Eve)

• Magneto: Can make avoiding Red Heart pickups difficult

• Bethany / Tainted Magdalene: Due to their reliance on red hearts makes Whore of Babylon much more difficult to use.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Upon obtaining the Whore of Babylon effect, a popup displaying the text "What a horrible night to have a curse" appears on-screen. This can be disabled in the game options.

• This text is a reference to Castlevania II: Simon's Quest. In the game, the text appears when the sun goes down.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Whore of Babylon gave a higher stat increase just for the room it was activated in, with +2.16 damage and +0.36 speed.

• III - The Empress was also much stronger, with +3.375 damage and +0.45 speed.

• The Whore of Babylon is an evil creature mentioned in the Book of Revelations.

• This item is used in Darkness Falls.

fields.description: Grants +1.5 Damage and +0.3 Speed whenever Isaac has a Half Red Heart or less.

Wicked Crown.title: Wicked Crown
Wicked Crown.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Causes a Treasure Room and Shop to generate in Sheol.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Cannot appear in Greed Mode.

• The spawned Treasure Room will have one of 22 unique layouts for the floor.

• Card Reading will spawn a second portal if Isaac has the trinket upon entering Sheol.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Treasure rooms in Sheol have an item choice, as if Isaac had More Options and Shops will be upgraded. Having both reveals the locations of the treasure room and the shop on the map.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This trinket has an angelic counterpart in Holy Crown.

fields.quote: Walk the path of the wicked
fields.description: A Treasure Room and Shop appear in Sheol.

Widow.title: Widow
Widow.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Widow is a boss that can appear in the Cellar.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Widow makes large leaps towards Isaac, at approximately double the distance of Monstro, and can perform the following attacks after landing:

• Leaves a puddle of White Creep and spawns a Sack.

• There is a maximum of 3 Sacks alive at once.

• Spits out a Spider.

• Widow can kill her own Spiders and Sacks if she jumps on top of them.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 18] : Spawns Big Spiders with half health instead of Sacks, Black Creep instead of White, and spits out six blood shots instead of Spiders.
[bc: 20] : Spawns Boils instead of Sacks and Attack Fly instead of Spiders. Jumps quicker. [Repentance] She is also 25% smaller and has 10% less health (117 HP).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Widow was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• She is the boss version of the Trites.

• The Wretched is the posthumous version of her.

• The name probably refers to the Latrodectus, commonly known as "black widow spider".

• [Repentance] Widow's and The Wretched's animations and behavior have been sped up to more closely resemble their Flash counterparts.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The tint for the Pink Champion Widow does not show up as pink and looks like a normal Widow, but her attacks are the same spawns as pink.

Wiggle Worm.title: Wiggle Worm
Wiggle Worm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac's tears travel in a wave-like pattern.

• +0.4 Tears up.

• [Repentance] Grants spectral tears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance+] This trinket has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Pin, Larry Jr., The Hollow or Scolex. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Soy Milk: Tears now travel in a double helix pattern.

• Tractor Beam: The altered pattern tears travel in is confined to the beam allowing Isaac to use its benefits without losing accuracy.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: In addition to further stat increases, each copy causes the path of tears to become even wigglier.

• Tech X: Rings take a star-shape, slightly increasing their area of effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Wiggle Worm was a passive item in the original Binding of Isaac. The likely reason for the change to a trinket is the situational usefulness of this shot pattern, along with the new ability to drop trinkets on demand. It took ItemID #59, which is now unused.

• [Repentance] ItemID #59 is now used by the passive The Book of Belial created by the Birthright effect from Judas/Black Judas.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The tears up is not applied until Isaac's Tears are first increased by any other method.

fields.name: Wiggle Worm
fields.description: Isaac's tears travel in a wave-like pattern. +0.4 Tears up. [Repentance] Also grants spectral tears.

Wild Card.title: Wild Card
Wild Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Copies the effect of the most recently used Pill, Card, Rune, Soul Stone, or activated item.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, the Wild Card has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• Using Jera on a Wild Card will copy the Wild Card, allowing Isaac to infinitely copy any other consumables in the room.

• Using Diplopia will copy the Wild Card and any pedestal item in the room, allowing Isaac to infinitely copy any item in the room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Plan C: Activating the Plan C effect resets Isaac's 3 second death timer, allowing for longer boss death animations to play out.

• [Repentance+] Bosses with longer death animations now make Plan C's cooldown longer, therefore making this strategy a little less useful.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Wild Card comes from Uno. In Uno, this card allows whoever played it to choose its color.

fields.description: Copies the effect of the most recently used Pill, Card, Rune, Soul Stone, or activated item.

Wire Coat Hanger.title: Wire Coat Hanger
Wire Coat Hanger.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • +0.7 tears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Is functionally identical to The Sad Onion.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In his first post-Repentance Lore Stream, Edmund McMillen revealed that the Wire Coat Hanger was a reference to the famous line "No wire hangers, ever!" from the 1981 film Mommie Dearest, as well as being a reference to a highly dangerous method of self-induced abortion in which a pregnant woman attempts to use a long implement (usually metal) such as a wire coat hanger to physically damage the uterus in a desperate bid to prevent fetal development.

• In the original flash version of The Binding of Isaac, this item was unlocked by default.

fields.description: +0.7 tears.

Wish Bone.title: Wish Bone
Wish Bone.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Taking damage has a [Before Repentance+] 2% / [Repentance+] 5% chance to destroy the trinket and spawn a random item using the item pool of the current room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Adds +5% chance to destroy the trinket upon taking damage per copy.

• Wish Bone: Two copies cannot be held at the same time.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The wishbone is the furcula of the turkey, which is eaten during Thanksgiving. It's tradition for two people to break the wishbone by holding one end each and pulling. The one that gets the bigger end gets to make a wish.

fields.name: Wish Bone
fields.description: Taking damage has a small chance to destroy the trinket and spawn a random item.

Needle.title: Needle
Needle.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Needles are monsters that resemble a miniature Pin, and added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC.

They lunge towards Isaac in an attempt to deal contact damage. Before they lunge, they are characterized by a small lump in the ground. Unlike Pin, they do not move underground relative to where they land. Instead, they teleport to a spot near Isaac before lunging. They can leap over pits and obstacles to reach Isaac if he has flight.

Needles will not leave a cloud of smoke upon spawning within a given room.

sections.heading: Pasty
sections.text: Pasties are skeletal variants and behave exactly like the Needles. However, when emerging off the ground, they will shoot 4 blood shots on the ordinal directions. The appearance of Pasty is similar to The Frail's in its second phase.

Rotgut.title: Rotgut
Rotgut.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: • Rotgut is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Corpse.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
The first phase occurs against Rotgut's "face" in its regular boss room. Rotgut is stationary in the center of the room and performs the following attacks:

• Spews a constant wave of projectiles that alternates above and below it in a fanning pattern.

• Spews out waves of fluctuating spaced-out projectiles in a disorganized pattern.

• Fires rings of 8 expanding projectiles that alternate between rotating clockwise and counter-clockwise.

• Fires three waves of projectiles in a row:

• A radial of tightly knit slow-moving tears.

• A radial of spaced out fast-moving tears.

• A burst of randomly positioned tears that hover for a moment before dropping.

• Coughs up a horizontal burst of red projectiles to the left and right side of itself.

• Vomits out projectiles, bones, as well as Globin goo, Gazing Globin goo, and Small Maggots that rain down in a large area.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Once Rotgut's first form has been defeated, it sucks Isaac, any monsters, and floating projectiles into its mouth and sends Isaac into a Crawl Space-like interior. The second phase consists of a large maggot that sits in the bottom right of the room and performs attacks depending on Isaac's position.

If Isaac is on the platform, the maggot uses its rear end:

• Launches a cluster of projectiles onto the platform and covers it in green poisonous gas.

• Launches an Ipecac shot that bursts into arcing tears.

• Shoots out 6 slow travelling tears that travel in a wave pattern across the entire room.

If Isaac is below the platform and on the ground, the maggot uses its head:

• Spits out a stream of arcing blood projectiles along with a few Attack Fly and Small Maggots.

• Shoots out a Brimstone laser.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text:
Defeating the Maggot allows passage into the next chamber, which contains Rotgut's "heart". The heart switches randomly between two modes of projectile patterns that occur for the entire duration of the fight:

• Mode 1: shoots out half-rings of 6-7 green projectiles below it with each pulse of the heart.

• Mode 2: drops 3 yellow projectiles in random locations with each beat of the heart. Each projectile splits into 2 arcing projectiles after hitting the ground.

The heart can perform additional attacks that occur independently of its two set modes:

• Retreats upwards and spawns Leech on the end of the room furthest from Isaac. These Leeches move quickly across the screen and despawn upon reaching the edge of the screen. The final Leech spawned has a chance of being an Adult Leech.

• Drops 2 large blood projectiles below it one after another. Each bursts into smaller projectiles that bounce all over the room.
After defeating this phase, Isaac is automatically ejected out of Rotgut's insides and back into the boss room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Dying with a respawn item (such as Dead Cat) in the second or final phase places Isaac in the previous phase, meaning Isaac has to fight that phase again. This does not apply to effects that revive the player in the same room such as Inner Child.

• The transitions between phases count as room changes (which means the Holy Mantle shield will re-activate after each phase, for instance).

• The chambers for second and third phases are not considered boss rooms for the purposes of items such as Blanket.

• Vanishing Twin will spawn a copy of Rotgut's first phase. When either of them is defeated, the fight can be advanced to second phase without killing the remaining boss. Second and third phases are not affected except for the fact that Vanishing Twin familiar will remain with Isaac despite having transformed into a copy of Rotgut. After Isaac defeats the third phase of the boss, the familiar will spawn another Rotgut, which will instantly die and drop an item.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Compared to Antibirth, Rotgut's 1st and 3rd phases have a new visual design.

• Rotgut's appearance change was a decision made by Edmund.

• The maggot inside of Rotgut has been nicknamed "Gus" by the developers.

• Tainted Spitty, an enemy which can appear during the Ascent to reach Home, bears a strong resemblance to Gus in both appearance and attack patterns.

• Rotgut is the informal name for a grade of moonshine that is very poor quality, being poor enough to be deadly to drink.

• Rotgut is the name of a level from Super Meat Boy, one of Edmund McMillen's earlier games.

• Rotgut's current design is supposed to be a Fatty that grew so big that it fused to the floor, according to developer _Kilburn.

• He also speculated that Rotgut could be It Lives! having grown massive instead.

• The reason for this design change was due to Edmund not liking the previous worm-like appearance.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Isaac is small enough (with Pluto for example), he can very easily clip through the ground during the Rotgut fight at phase 2 or 3 and enter I AM ERROR room, consequently skipping the fight to Corpse II.

• Dashing through the Maggot in phase 2 using items such as Mars or A Pony or standing inside of it when Dark Arts deactivates can also clip Isaac through the room, causing the same effect.

• This is also possible by using Suplex! against its second or third phase.
Bug note: If debug 10 ("quick kill") is active, Rotgut will repeat its phase 1 death animation indefinitely, preventing Isaac from accessing phases 2 and 3, thus softlocking the game.
Bug note: If Suplex! is used to kill Rotgut's first phase, the fight will fail to progress as instead of taking Isaac to the next phase touching Rotgut will hurt him.
Bug note: If Isaac has Flat Stone, the tears WILL NOT bounce on the floor in the crawspace-like rooms, forcing Isaac to shoot at very close range and making the third phase almost unbeatable.
Bug note: If The Forgotten defeats Rotgut as The Soul whilst having Birthright, once outside Rotgut's interior, switching back to The Forgotten will restart whichever phase of the fight you left the skeleton in, forcing you to redo the rest of the fight

Cut Content.title: Cut Content
Cut Content.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Cut Content refers to entities, mechanics, objects, graphics, etc. that didn't make it into the final game but are still present within the game's data.

sections.heading: Pressure Plates
sections.text:
Pressure plates can be found in the game files and could have served as another type of obstacle. They are fully functional and can do the following things:

• Nothing

• Spawn a random chest

• Spawn 6 Attack Flies

• Spawn 6 Troll Bombs

• Activate Curse of Darkness for the rest of the floor

• Spawn a random pickup

• Spawn 15 random coins

[Afterbirth onward] Buttons appear in rooms.

sections.heading: Various Half Hearts
sections.text:
Half Soul Heart and Black Heart pickups are in the game files, but they cannot be found in-game.

[Afterbirth+ onward] Half Soul Hearts are an unlockable pickup.

sections.heading: Colored Destructibles
sections.text:
There are several colored versions of certain destructibles, which could have served a purpose similar to tinted rocks.

[Repentance] Marked Skulls are an unlockable obstacle through A Secret Exit. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Sisters Vis
sections.text:
A boss version of the Vis enemy that could have appeared in Sheol. According to the unused corresponding achievement file, Sisters Vis would have been unlocked by beating Sheol 10 times. The Sisters Vis were also a boss in Gish, one of Edmund McMillen's previous games.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] This boss can be encountered, but can appear in all environments of Chapter 3, [Before Repentance] all environments of chapter 4 and requires unlocking Something wicked this way comes+!. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Unused 12 Room Charge
sections.text:
By editing the game's "items.xml" file and setting an item to maxcharges=12, it's possible to see the charge bar in-game.

• [Afterbirth onward] The bar is used for the Mega Blast item, which has a 12-room charge. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The bar is also used for the Delirious and Eden's Soul items, which have 12-room charges. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The bar is also used for Alabaster Box, Larynx, Jar of Wisps, Everything Jar, Mega Mush, and for various consumables for Blank Card, Placebo, and Clear Rune. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Keeper (Enemy) unused Animation
sections.text: A keeper enemy animation for jump from the back, jump for right and shooting from the back, shooting facing for right and left.

sections.heading: Unused Floors
sections.text: By disabling the invalid seed check, and using an invalid seed, you can continue the game after The Chest and Dark Room, up to an additional 14 floors. They use pre-existing graphics and the same layout.

sections.heading: Mega Satan's Skeleton Hand
sections.text: Originally, a skeletal version of Mega Satan's hands would have appeared for his 2nd form. Even if Mega Satan's hands were not killed, fully depleting his head's health in his 1st form will cause the hands to immediately despawn.

sections.heading: Cut Afterbirth Content
sections.text: [section dlc: a]

sections.heading: Old Man Keeper
sections.text:
Old Man Keeper was originally a second new playable character before ending up replaced by Keeper. This character, however, is playable since the DLC's initial release by using the Cheat Engine until in the later update patches, but he appears invisible with no sprites and has zero hearts.

On every April Fool's Day between 2016 and sometime after the release of Afterbirth †, Keeper was replaced by Old Man Keeper during the daily run for that day.

sections.heading: Skinless Hush
sections.text: From the files, there was an unfinished sprite sheet of Hush's flayed form. At first, Edmund stated that the file is a "red herring to the data miners". However, this scrapped form was later confirmed to be actually intentional.

sections.heading: Beta Ultra Greed
sections.text: Ultra Greed, based on his unused sprite sheet, was originally featured with a beard, along with a single tooth and a rather stout-looking body build. This old Ultra Greed design supposedly represents Tyrone Rodriguez, similar to Ultra Pride who also represents Edmund McMillen and Florian Himsl.

sections.heading: Cut Afterbirth † Content
sections.text: [section dlc: a+]

sections.heading: Unused Ultra Greedier Sprites and Animation
sections.text: Ultra Greedier has not only an unused hanging sprite like his original form but an entire unused 'waking up' animation. The animation can be seen in game by spawning him with Debug Console.

sections.heading: Big Horn's Big Bomb
sections.text: This unused bomb sprite reveals that Big Horn was intended to summon a larger bomb.

sections.heading: Unused Room Editor Sprites
sections.text: Along with modding support, several tools were included with Afterbirth † to assist new and existing modders, one of which was the Room Editor. It came with a huge number of icons it used for visualization, which included a number of pre-release enemy designs which were never used in-game. Some were simply colored differently while others looked drastically different.

sections.heading: Cut Repentance Content
sections.text: [section dlc: r]

sections.heading: Dogma's Unused Attacks
sections.text:
There are 2 unused attacks for Dogma that appear in the files and can be spawned using console commands, but neither are ever seen in-game normally.

Entity 950.10 is "Dogma Angel Baby". When spawned, it floats around for a few seconds before charging at Isaac and exploding. They were originally supposed to spawn alongside Dogma's spin attack in Phase 2, but were ultimately removed from the fight, likely for being too difficult. They are fully functional in-game, though they cannot spawn naturally. They can still be spawned in with the command "spawn 950.10".

Entity 1000.171 is "Dogma Blackhole". When spawned, it starts charging up, and after a few moments, it emits a powerful suction force and spawns damaging tears to be dragged in as well. If Isaac makes contact with the blackhole, he will also take damage. The blackhole explodes into a shower of tears after it finishes the suction attack. The Hole would also suck Isaac's own shots and even bombs. The attack pattern was cut because it was deemed to be too hard by the playtesters. The black hole can still be spawned with the debug console with the command "spawn 1000.171".

sections.heading: Unimplemented Bosses
sections.text:
Files for several bosses created for The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that were ultimately cut can be found within the game files. However, it was confirmed that some of the bosses may have a chance to be implemented in the DLC's future updates.

• Maid in the Mist, a scrapped ghost-like boss. She is an early version of Min-Min with both sharing a Willo theme:

• Raglich, a boss that appears to be a part of the Rag Man lineage. Raglich does not appear in any rooms, meaning it must be spawned with the console. It was originally intended to be encountered in Mausoleum and has confirmation from _Kilburn, one of the developers, that: "he will make it in, eventually" (though now that _Kilburn is no longer working on the game, this is rather unlikely).

• Cadavra, a pair of bosses similar in appearance to Chimera. Their walking animation gifs were first shown by Edmund McMillen on September 4, 2020, but they were never found in the DLC's final release. Unlike the previous two bosses, Cadavra does not exist as an entity and cannot be spawned in-game. It does not have a portrait nor a boss title. Edmund stated that they're "still in pieces maybe one day", implying that Cadavra would be later added in the future update patches some other time.

sections.heading: Unimplemented Enemies
sections.text:
• Tainted Mr. Maw, an enemy resembling three Maw faces stuck together. The enemy's sheet suggests that each face broke off as its health lowered. It also has sprites for a body making it akin to the original Mr. Maw.

• Floater Turdlet, a variant of Drips themed after Turdlet, likely meant to be a part of Turdlet's fight (Drips are known as Floaters in the game's assets).

• Red Fly Bomb, a red version of a Fly Bomb with small spikes protruding around it.

• Lump Corpse, a Corpse-themed version of a Lump that looks more like the Flash version, albeit green.

• Split Rage Creep, an enemy resembling Rage Creeps, but with a more gored body that shoots two Brimstone beams at 30° angles instead of one straight beam, leaving a blind spot in the middle.

• Rag Creep, a variation of a Wall Creep which spits a chain of 4 homing shots, spawned as part of Raglich's fight.

• Canary, a Gaper with what seems to be a fleshy version of the Technology costume. The name of its body sprite, along with the name of the enemy itself, indicates that it would have appeared in Mines.

• Foreigner, a Gaper with a large white eye resembling a fleshy version of the Polyphemus costume and could have been possibly a variation of a Cyclopia. Its shares a theme with the Canary and thus would have also appeared in Mines.

• Graverobber, a small enemy resembling Greed paired with a penny sack.

• Gasbag 2 and Lump Corpse 2, greyish blue hued variations of a Gasbag and the cut Lump Corpse.

sections.heading: Unimplemented Pickups
sections.text:
Several unused achievements for pickups exist.

• Illusion Hearts: Illusion Hearts appeared to function as Soul Hearts that create a clone of the player character that moves in tandem with the original, a similar mechanic to Jacob & Esau, with a copy of all of your items. When an Illusion Heart was depleted, the Isaac that got hit disappeared. This was also cut from Antibirth.

• Rune of Ingwaz

• Rune of Sowilo

sections.heading: Unimplemented Challenges
sections.text:
Several unused achievements exist that mention the following challenges being unlocked. It is unknown what the challenges would have been.

• Dimension Red; possibly an early version of Red Redemption.

• Divide and Conquer; seems to feature a Conquest-like Isaac throwing copies of himself at enemies.

• Ghost Babel; notably features the cut Nightwatch enemy (see Cut Monsters below).

• Turbo!; evidently involved Cain, with the game sped-up.

sections.heading: Unimplemented Co-op Babies
sections.text:
Several unused achievements exist for co-op babies that never made it in.

• BFF Baby

• Duplex Baby

• Lot Baby

• Pawn Baby

• Salty Baby

sections.heading: Mortis
sections.text: An unused floor which would have been an alternative version of Corpse exists as an STB file with one room and no associated assets. In the music XML file, there is also a listing labeled as "not done" after Gehenna, which uses The Womb's theme as a placeholder. Edmund McMillen has confirmed on Twitter that there are currently no plans to add Mortis to the game.

sections.heading: The Void
sections.text:
An unused floor which shares its name with The Void can be found in the game's files and contains a variety of unique unimplemented rooms, some of which feature Repentance mechanics/bosses as well as one containing Clutch/The Possessor.

• This new version of The Void may have been related to the Delirium revamp which Kilburn noted in a tweet.

sections.heading: Curse of the Giant
sections.text: A new curse from the Antibirth mod, which generates a floor with special big rooms made from combining multiple small rooms together, remains in the game files in Repentance, but as of yet cannot be encountered in-game. It was likely cut due to the number of unfair, extremely difficult, or even impossible rooms it could sometimes generate.

sections.heading: Derpy Plum
sections.text: Next to Baby Plum's animation file is a file called "908.000_derpy plum.anm2" which is missing its associated sprite sheet. There are two images of what appears to be Derpy Plum, as shared by one of the developers.

sections.heading: Beast Laugh
sections.text: During the Beast fight, any remaining Ultra Horsemen as well as the Beast herself can be seen in the background of the fight, with the former cheering on the current Horseman whenever Isaac takes damage. It seems that originally the Beast was intended to laugh when this occurred as well, since there are unused sprites and even a fully finished animation within the .anm2 file. However, this animation does not play in the final game.

sections.heading: Heretic Dabbing
sections.text: In "905.000_heretic.anm2", there is an animation called "why does this exist" showing Heretic dabbing after being defeated.

sections.heading: Cut Characters
sections.text: • Edith - An unused character from Antibirth that could only move through teleporting. It was confirmed early on by Ed that Edith would not be added, however, a statue that looks similar to Edith does appear rarely when using VII - The Chariot?. Her gameplay style was reworked and added to the game as Tainted Forgotten.

sections.heading: Cut Items
sections.text:
The following items were planned for but ultimately cut from Antibirth:

• 613 - Salt Shaker - Was Edith's active item. Edith was a planned character for Antibirth, who was cut out for gameplay reasons. (It was item ID 613, but now this ID is currently unused.)

• 630 - Lucky Seven - Was an item planned for the first Antibirth update. (It was item ID 630, but now this ID is currently unused.)

• 648 - Pill Crusher - Was an item planned for the first Antibirth update. (It was item ID 648, but now this ID is currently unused.)

sections.heading: Cut Monsters
sections.text:
Some monsters from the Antibirth mod are found in the game files but unused, while others are completely absent in Repentance. Edmund McMillen confirmed that he has no plans for the currently unused Antibirth monsters.

• It is possible to encounter these enemies along with other cut enemies with TMTRAINER or in the DELETE THIS challenge, although it is highly unlikely.

Unused monsters:

• Barfy - A variant of Fatty. Wanders around the room, and slowly follows Isaac when he's in its line of sight. Occasionally spews clusters of green shots that leaves green creep towards Isaac.

• Blind Bat - A variant of One Tooth. Starts out asleep. When Isaac gets close, it wakes up and chases Isaac, followed by a group of three more Blind Bats.

• Echo Bat - A variant of One Tooth. Flies towards Isaac and periodically fires three white orbs. If an orb hits Isaac, he becomes confused and his movement is reversed for a few seconds.

• Corpse Eater - Rapidly moves around the room erratically and charges at Isaac if he comes within its line of sight. When spawned in game, it will behave like normal but only has the front end for its sprite.

• Carrion Rider - A variant of Corpse Eater. Rapidly moves around the room erratically and charges at Isaac if he comes within its line of sight. The Bony on its back shoots at Isaac. If spawned in game, acts the same as Corpse Eater, while also having a chance to spawn a charger on death.

• Necromancer - Summons skeleton enemies such as Bonies and Big Bonies.

• Nightwatch - Invulnerable enemies. Moves in a fixed pattern or rotates in a spot. If Isaac enters its light, it will lock all doors, summon enemies, and vanish.

• Swapper - A variant of Baby. Slowly floats towards Isaac and fires purple lasers. Occasionally teleports and reappears elsewhere. Has a chance to swap positions with Isaac.

• Strifer - Walks horizontally or vertically, attempting to line up with Isaac. Frequently fires lines of four tears forwards.

• Vessel - A variant of Fatty. Walks around the room and explodes into Small Maggots upon death.

Removed monsters:

• Dumpling - Flies around and farts if Isaac is close, if it is damaged, and when it dies. Farts knock Isaac back and propel it forwards.

• Skinling - A variant of Dumpling. Their behavior is similar but their farts are poisonous.

• Scab - A variant of Dumpling. Flies towards Isaac. Upon death, farts and sends out 6 blood shots in all directions.

• Fissure - A Dumpling/Trite hybrid. Jumps towards Isaac like a Trite. When it jumps, it fires a red shot towards Isaac. Occasionally, it stands still and spews a chaotic burst of red shots.

• Screamer - Walks slowly around the room. If Isaac gets too close, it will scream, paralyzing Isaac. It will gain a slowing aura and start charging towards him.

• Coil - Creates beams of electricity to other enemies in the room. Touching the electricity damages Isaac. Cannot be killed.

• Stillborn - Slowly floats towards Isaac, occasionally firing blood shots. Cannot be killed and dies when the room is cleared.

As well, there is a cut Orange-Red champion that behaved similar to the flashing green champion, splitting once, and then having its clones split.

The Rainmaker.title: The Rainmaker
The Rainmaker.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Rainmaker is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in [Repentance] Downpour.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Rainmaker floats slowly towards Isaac and performs the following attacks:

• Creates two horizontal lines of 6 projectiles each on both sides of himself, then fires them towards Isaac at intervals starting from the far ends towards the center.

• Creates a ring of 12 projectiles around himself, then fires them towards Isaac in short staggered intervals starting from 2 opposite ends of the ring.

• Summons a large water projectile overhead, then pops it, unleashing a burst of projectiles in random directions.

• Twirls around, following Isaac's movements while summoning projectiles around himself which hover briefly before being fired towards Isaac.

• At the end of this attack, the Rainmaker releases 8 projectiles in a radial burst.
The Rainmaker deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The Rainmaker can be immediately killed with Vade Retro if he is at 50% health or below.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Rainmaker's name is a reference to the traditional ritual of rainmaking which may involve "Rain Dances".

• The Rainmaker was originally going to be omitted from Repentance, according to a Tweet from Edmund Mcmillen.

• This tweet also confirms that the Rainmaker is both male and gay.

• Defeating the Rainmaker stops the rain in the current room.

Breakfast.title: Breakfast
Breakfast.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Grants one full Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item has a 12.6% chance to spawn from paying out a Beggar in addition to being in the Beggar item pool. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method.

• If the Treasure Room Pool runs out of items, it will only contain Breakfast from that point onwards.

• Once other item pools run out of items, they will only contain Treasure Room Pool items. This means that if the Treasure Room Pool was also exhausted, that item pool will only contain Breakfast.

• • [Afterbirth onward] With Chaos, every fully depleted item pool will only contain Breakfast. [end edition note] 

• Breakfast spawned via exhausted item pools cannot be rerolled into other items with a few exceptions:

• • [Afterbirth onward] Rerolling Breakfast from an exhausted item pool while holding Chaos can reroll it into an item from another pool. [end edition note] 

• • 
• [Repentance] This also works with Soul of Eden. [end edition note] 

• • [Afterbirth onward] Dropping NO! after exhausting an item pool while holding it will allow active items to spawn on pedestals again. [end edition note] 

• • [Afterbirth+ onward] Having an item spawn from a non-exhausted pool before picking up Breakfast can allow rerolls to collected passive items (e.g. D4) to reroll Breakfast into an item from that item pool. [end edition note] 

• • [Repentance] Losing Sacred Orb after exhausting an item pool while holding it will allow low quality items to appear again. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Binge Eater: When Isaac picks up Breakfast it now grants: a permanent +0.2 Shot Speed and +2.5 Range, a temporary +3.6 Damage (which diminishes to 0 in 30 seconds), heals 1 additional red heart, and takes a permanent -0.03 Speed reduction.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In Edmund McMillen's first post-Repentance Lore Stream, he revealed that the pinkish-yellow label on the left side of the breakfast sprite is actually meant to be a portrait of Isaac, referencing the practice of advertising lost children on milk cartons that was popular in the United States during the 1980s.

• The term used by the community when an item pool is depleted is "breakfasting."

• In a Twitter Q&A, Edmund revealed that breakfasting was originally a bug.

• Breakfast’s sprites can be seen as part of Binge Eater.

Breath of Life.title: Breath of Life
Breath of Life.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Holding the active item button will deplete the charge bar. As the charge gets closer to zero, Isaac turns bluer over time.

• Once the charge bar hits zero, Isaac will become invincible to all outside sources of damage. If the button is held for an additional second after hitting zero, Isaac will take damage for every second the button is held down.

• Isaac loses invincibility once the active item button is released.

• [Repentance] If the button is released before the charge bar hits zero, a negative sound effect will play and the item will lose all of its charge.

• [Repentance] While Isaac is invincible, he deals 3.5 contact damage to enemies and beams of light will strike down enemies touching Isaac, dealing 15 damage.

• [Repentance] Blocking damage at the exact moment the invincibility activates will create a 4-way cardinal beam of light that deals 12 damage per tick for a total of 180 damage per beam.

• • If an enemy is standing in the center of all the light beams, they will take a total of 720 damage.

• The item will recharge on its own, but cannot be used again until it is fully charged (even if the charge bar wasn't fully depleted).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• While not time-based, invincibility from Breath of Life is otherwise identical to damage immunity granted by the shield effect.

• Breath of Life will prevent damage from Blood Donation Machines, Devil Beggars, Hell Games, and Confessionals, allowing them to be played infinitely for free.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Once the invincibility takes effect, Isaac starts flashing rapidly.

• [Before Repentance] Isaac will continue flashing for about a second even when invincibility has ended after releasing the active item button.

• [Repentance] Cannot be used to prevent damage from the door to the Mausoleum. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Taking damage from holding the active item button for too long is considered self-damage for the purposes of Angel/Devil Deal chances and items such as Paschal Candle.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The Battery: Adds an extra level of charge for Breath of Life, which allows Isaac to use it twice in a row. Releasing the active item button early will use up 1 full charge, and using the item before the 2nd charge is full will remove that extra charge.

• Book of Belial interaction: Judas leaves a damaging flame trail while the invincibility is active instead of creating beams of light. Blocking damage just as the invincibility begins activates The Necronomicon effect and grants Judas a temporary damage bonus.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns 4 regular wisps on the inner ring when the four-way beam is created. Only 4 of these wisps can exist at a time. No wisps are created otherwise.

• [Before Repentance] Isaac's Heart: When held down too long, Breath of Life no longer damages Isaac, resulting in infinite invincibility.

• Void: Using Void with Breath of Life will immediately grant invincibility frames.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Void: Using Void with Breath of Life will immediately grant invincibility frames, then inflict damages to Isaac every second until he leaves the room.

• ? Card/Car Battery/ [Before Repentance] Habit/Wild Card: No effect.

sections.text: [end edition note]

sections.heading: In Repentance [Repentance]
