C Section.title: C Section
C Section.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac gains a short delay charge attack that fires homing, piercing, spectral fetus tears.

• The fetus tears do 75% of Isaac's Damage, 3.75 times per second, until they run out of Range.

• The fetuses will automatically fire when Isaac is at full charge, meaning the charge cannot be held.

• Charge time is calculated based on Tear Delay.

• • \text{Fetuses per Second} = \frac{30}{Roundup(\text{Tear Delay} \times 3) + 1}

• • Fetuses per second is capped at 15.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Fetus size scales with damage.

• The fetuses slow down upon contacting enemies, making its homing effect more powerful.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Berserk!: Isaac can fire the fetuses on duration. The fetuses hold and attack with bone clubs that are identical to The Forgotten's one.

• Brimstone / Azazel: Shoots 4 fetus tears along with the brimstone beam.

• Each additional beam created from Monstro's Lung, split tears (such as The Parasite), or multi-shot effects (including Loki's Horns and Eye Sore) spawns four additional fetuses.

• Anti-Gravity: The fetuses spawn when the beam is being released. The fetuses do not spawn if Isaac is charging when the beam is being released.

• The Ludovico Technique: When combined with Brimstone, overrides C Section: fetuses no longer spawn.

• Compound Fracture: Fetuses are skeletons that shoot splitting bone fragments when in contact with an enemy.

• Cricket's Body: Fetuses drop four short-ranged tears when they hit the ground.

• Dead Eye: Damage boost is granted once a fetus hits an enemy (once per fetus) and is reset when a fetus does not hit anything before going down, using the same rule to determine whether the damage boost is reset or not.

• This makes for a great synergy since the fetuses are homing and stay up much longer than regular tears.

• Dr. Fetus: The fetuses drop small bombs when they touch an enemy. The bomb's damage follows Dr. Fetus' damage calculation, based on half of the fetuses damage. A fetus can drop only one bomb.

• The fetuses' bombs do not benefit from Isaac's bomb effects such as Hot Bombs or Bobby-Bomb. However, they do benefit from Isaac's tear effects and have the appearance of the corresponding bombs. For example, Hot Bombs from Fire Mind, Bobby-Bomb from homing tears. As such, Cricket's Body, The Parasite, and Polyphemus leave a subsequent bomb or bombs, and Mysterious Liquid leaves a creep.

• Dr. Fetus + Ipecac: The fetuses explode before dropping any bomb.

• Dr. Fetus + Haemolacria: Fetuses will both drop a bomb on touching an enemy and burst into multiple small bombs upon hitting the ground.

• Explosivo: Some Fetuses stick to enemies, expand, then explode. However, they do not inflict their contact damage while sticking.

• Explosivo + Mom's Knife: The knives from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaging tick. The explosions from a knife deal 60 + half of the fetus' damage which held it.

• Explosivo + Berserk! / Spirit Sword / The Forgotten / Tainted Forgotten: The clubs/swords from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaged enemy from their attack. The explosions from a club/sword deal 60 + the damage its attack dealt.

• Explosivo + Technology: The lasers from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaged enemy from their attack. The tears inherit the fetuses' property, including laser attacks, from which can create more tears. The tears from a laser deal 60 + the laser's damage they originated, and their lasers deal the same as the lasers they originated. Fetuses can fire lasers while sticking to an enemy and spin, while tears do not spin.

• Explosivo + Tech X: The laser rings from fetuses with Explosivo's effect create exploding tears for each damaging tick. The explosions from a ring deal 60 + the ring's damage.

• The Forgotten / Tainted Forgotten: Fetuses are skeletons that attack with bone clubs in addition to contact damage. The fetuses from Tainted Forgotten deal 80% of their normal damage.

• With Brimstone: Spawns a brimstone ball along with a fetus. Shots are fired automatically as the charge completes.

• With Mom's Knife: Fetuses hold knives instead of bone clubs and no longer perform the swing attacks.

• With Monstro's Lung Tears remain unchanged; the Forgotten will fire a burst attack alongside the fetus. No effect on the Soul.

• With Technology: Fetuses perform laser attacks and enhanced bone club attacks separately, causing more damage.

• Godhead: Fetuses have a glowing aura around them, but the aura cannot damage the enemy in contact with the fetuses.

• Haemolacria: Fetuses explode into a burst of tears when they hit the ground.

• Ipecac: The fetuses explode on impact, dealing its contact damage, which is often massively increased from the item.

• Jacob's Ladder: Fetuses zap nearby enemies.

• Luck-based tear effects (e.g. Holy Light / Knockout Drops): If a fetus has the effect, the fetus causes the effect for each damaging tick.

• Little Horn: Still only two hands can appear at once.

• Ocular Rift: The rifts spawn only once per fetus.

• Luck-based tear effects + Angelic Prism: If Isaac's speed is greater than the speed of a fetus, he can manually walk the prism through any fetus with a luck-based tear effect (or any fetus), greatly multiplying its effectiveness.

• Luck-based tear effects + Mom's Knife: If a fetus has the effect, the knife also causes the effect for each damaging tick. If not, the knife has chance to cause the effect based on Isaac's Luck for each damaging tick.

• Luck-based tear effects + Berserk! / Spirit Sword / Technology / The Forgotten / Tainted Forgotten: If a fetus has the effect, each attack also causes the effect.

• Luck-based tear effects + Tech X: If a fetus has the effect, the laser ring also causes the effect for each damaging tick.

• Mom's Knife: Fetuses hold small knives in their front, causing extra damage. The knife deals twice of Isaac's Damage, just as when it is held by Isaac, and their size scales with the fetuses' size. Any additional copy of the item causes Isaac to shoot more fetuses.

• Mom's Knife + Proptosis: The knives shrink along with the fetuses, but they retain their tripled damage.

• Mom's Knife + Brimstone: Instead of a barrage of knives, fires a normal Brimstone beam alongside knife-carrying fetuses.

• Mucormycosis: Some Fetuses stick to enemies, expand, then burst. However, they do not inflict their contact damage while sticking. Unlike normal spores, the fetuses from the burst can home into the enemy they burst from.

• Mucormycosis + Mom's Knife: The knives from fetuses with Mucormycosis' effect create spores for each damaging tick. Their knives deal twice of Isaac's Damage, same as the ones they originated.

• Mucormycosis + Berserk! / Spirit Sword / The Forgotten / Tainted Forgotten: The clubs/swords from fetuses with Mucormycosis' effect create spores for each damaged enemy from their attack. The fetuses from the burst also hold clubs/swords which are able to create another wave of spores. The damage of attacks are calculated based on half of the spores' flat 3.5 damage.

• • Berserk! / The Forgotten: Their swings deal 10.5 damage.

• • Tainted Forgotten: Their swings deal 8.4 damage.

• • Spirit Sword: Their swing attacks/spin attacks/projectiles deal 8.75/24/11 damage.

• Mucormycosis + Technology: The lasers from fetuses with Mucormycosis' effect create spores for each damaged enemy from their attack. The spores inherit the fetuses' property including laser attacks, which can create another spores. The fetuses from the burst also has laser attacks which are able to create another wave of spores. Their laser attacks deal 3.5 damage, based on the spores' flat 3.5 damage. Fetuses can fire lasers while sticking to an enemy and spin, while spores do not spin.

• Mucormycosis + Tech X: The laser rings from fetuses with Mucormycosis' effect create spores for each damaging tick. The fetuses from the burst are also surrounded by laser rings which are able to create another wave of spores. Their rings deal 1.75 damage, based on half of the spores' flat 3.5 damage.

• My Reflection: Fetuses travel a short distance, then reverse direction and return to Isaac.

• The Parasite: Fetuses fire short-ranged tears constantly while in contact with an enemy.

• Parasitoid: Parasitoid fetuses spawn spiders/flies and slowing creep with every hit on an enemy.

• Polyphemus: Grants +5 flat damage with no fire rate down.

• Sinus Infection: Some Fetuses stick to enemies. However, they only do the Sinus Infection damage ticking and often result in dealing much less damage.

• Sinus Infection + Mom's Knife: The knives from fetuses with Sinus Infection's effect create boogers for each damaging tick. The boogers from a knife deal half of the fetus' damage which held it per tick.

• Sinus Infection + Berserk! / Spirit Sword / The Forgotten / Tainted Forgotten: The clubs/swords from fetuses with Sinus Infection's effect create boogers for each damaged enemy from their attack. The boogers from a club/sword deal half of the fetus' damage which held it per tick.

• Sinus Infection + Technology: The lasers from fetuses with Sinus Infection's effect create boogers for each damaged enemy from their attack. The boogers inherit the fetuses' property including laser attacks, which can create another boogers. The boogers from a laser deal the laser's damage, so does their lasers. Fetuses can fire lasers while sticking to an enemy and spin, while boogers do not spin.

• Sinus Infection + Tech X: The laser rings from fetuses Sinus Infection's effect create boogers for each damaging tick. The boogers from a ring deal the ring's damage per tick.

• Spirit Sword: Fetuses hold small swords and repeat the swing attack and the charged spin attack as they travel. The damage calculation is based on half of the fetus' damage. On base Range, they have just enough time to perform the attacks twice. The sword's size scales with the fetus' size.

• Spirit Sword + Berserk! / Mom's Knife / The Forgotten / Tainted Forgotten: The fetuses hold swords and do not benefit from the others.

• Spirit Sword + Proptosis: Although the attacks' damages diminish along with the fetus, the projectile from the sword does not lose its damage over range.

• Tainted Azazel: Shoots 2 fetus tears along with his thin brimstone beam.

• Tech.5 / Technology 2: Both fire at the same time.

• Technology Zero: Fetuses are connected with electricity.

• Tech X: Fetuses are surrounded by a laser ring that deals half of their damage. The ring's size scales with the fetus' size.

• Tech X + Brimstone: The laser rings do not change into brimstone rings. The Brimstone has no effect unless combined with other additional items.

• Tech X + Proptosis: The rings shrink along with the fetuses, but they retain their tripled damage.

• Technology: Fetuses rapidly shoot a short-ranged laser based on their damage when facing enemies.

• Technology + Cricket's Body: Split tears created from the end of the laser inherit the effects of fetus tears including laser attacks from Technology, but they do not create another split tears.

• Technology + Lachryphagy: Fetuses can feed on either other fetuses or Lachryphagy tears which their laser attacks create. Fed fetuses shoot stronger lasers, creating powerful Lachryphagy tears.

• Technology + Pop!: Pop! tears created from the end of the laser inherit the effects of fetus tears including laser attacks from Technology, which can create another Pop! tears.

• Technology + Proptosis: Although the laser's damage diminishes along with the fetus, it does not lose its damage over range.

• Technology + Spirit Sword: Fetuses hold lightsabers and perform laser attacks and enhanced sword attacks separately, causing more damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
Overridden by C Section:

• Chocolate Milk

• Cursed Eye

• Evil Eye

• Eye of the Occult (besides stat changes)

• The Ludovico Technique

• Monstro's Lung

• Neptunus

• Tractor Beam (besides stat changes)

• Trisagion
Other interactions:

• Anti-Gravity: Fetuses will begin stuck in-place as expected, but will ignore this behavior if there are nearby enemies, in which case they will home in and chase them. Range "lifetime" is still ticking during the stuck time unlike normal tears, making them markedly harder to use and shorter lasting.

• BFFS!: No effect; fetuses are considered tears, not familiars.

• C Section: No additional effect for multiple copies of the item.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides C Section making Epic Fetus the only item in the game that can override it.

• Eye of Belial: Fetuses' appearances change into Eye of Belial tears when passing through an enemy, but they retain their effects.

• Fire Mind: The fetuses can explode and leave fires before they run out of Range, which can result in inflicting less damage.

• Flat Stone: Fetuses only bounce after going rather far or damaging enemies for long enough.

• Immaculate Heart/Saturnus: No unique interactions; regular tears are generated which orbit Isaac normally.

• Knockout Drops: Fetuses affected by it have the appearance of a fist, but they retain their effects.

• Lachryphagy: Burst tears appear to be fetuses, but they do not retain homing or piercing effect from C Section.

• Lead Pencil: low range burst of 12 non-fetus tears every 15 fetuses fired.

• Lost Contact: Fetuses collide with enemy shots, destroying them. The collisions slightly affect the fetuses' movement.

• Multidimensional Baby: Fetuses' appearances change into normal tears when passing through Multidimensional Baby, but they retain their effects.

• Pop!: Fetuses' movements do not extend their lifespan, it is still limited by Range. Fetuses do not fall after bouncing off of each other 8 times.

• Sad Bombs / Tammy's Head: Fires normal tears.

• Scissors: C Section tears are fired from the body instead of the head. This makes the head do nothing, but the item still provides a benefit as the body will fire both the C Section tears and the blood fountain from Scissors.

• Sharp Key: No effect on thrown keys.

• Tear Detonator: Fetuses split into normal tears.

sections.heading: Gallery
sections.text:
C Section has a variety of appearances for its fetus shots. It depends mostly on the color of the character's body and is influenced mostly by costumes. There are a few unique appearances for specific items/characters.

| Image | Notes 
| | Default; appearance when fired by the large majority of characters.

| | Azazel, Lilith, Tainted Azazel, Tainted Lilith, Brimstone, Ball of Tar, or any other effects that turn the character's body black.

| | ???, The Soul, Tainted ??? (albeit heavily brown tinted), Anti-Gravity, Neptunus, or any other effects that turn the character's body blue.

| | Black Judas or Tainted Judas.

| | Infestation or any other effects that turn the character's body green.

| | Keeper, Apollyon, Tainted Lost, Tainted Keeper, Tainted Apollyon, Terra, Tooth and Nail (while active), VII - The Chariot? (unless in the Edith costume; see below), or any other effects that turn the character's body grey.

| | Esau, SMB Super Fan, Razor Blade, Red Patch, or any other effects that turn the character's body red.

| | The Forgotten (not The Soul), Tainted Forgotten, or Compound Fracture.

| | The Lost, Dead Tainted Lazarus, any character in their ghost form, Uranus, the Edith costume from VII - The Chariot?, or any other effects that turn the character's body white.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A Caesarean Section, or C Section for short, is a surgical procedure by which a baby is delivered through an incision in the mother's abdomen.

• Isaac's body resembles a Vis. The fetus shots themselves resemble Unborns.

• Prior to v1.7.5, this item had no effect other than changing Isaac's appearance and appeared in no item pools. Nonetheless, obtaining it was still required in order to unlock the Dead God achievement.

• It was only obtainable via Death Certificate and Spindown Dice, or as a starting item for Eden / Tainted Eden.

• According to Edmund McMillen, C Section was a "dream item" whose mechanics and many hard-coded synergies were too complex to implement at Repentance's launch, with Kilburn "obsessively" working on the item and other parts of Repentance.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: There's no idle animation for C Section's costume, so Isaac (and every other character other than Lilith) will always appear to be walking when charging a shot, even when stationary.
Bug note: Tainted ??? does not have a costume assigned for C Section (despite ??? having one), and nonetheless always appears to be walking while charging a shot, even when stationary (see previous bug).
Bug note: While Isaac has both C Section and Incubus (including Lilith's inherent Incubus), Incubus' flying animation does not play while not firing; it floats around with no animation at all. The animation plays normally while firing.

fields.description: Replaces tears with fetuses that chase down enemies and deal contact damage. Each shot requires a brief charge up.

Caffeine Pill.title: Caffeine Pill
Caffeine Pill.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.3 speed.

• Decreases Isaac's size, making him less likely to be hit.

• Upon pickup, gives Isaac a random pill. If he is already holding a consumable, it is forcibly dropped to the ground.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Before Repentance] It will still drop a pill even if the player has Starter Deck.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Caffeine is a stimulant in coffee and other drinks, relevant to the speed boost. It was also rumored, but isn't proven, to stunt growth in children, as per Isaac's decreased size and emaciated appearance with it.

fields.description: Grants +0.3 speed, reduces Isaac's size, and gives a random pill.

Cain's Eye.title: Cain's Eye
Cain's Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Not to be confused with Cain's Other Eye.

sections.heading: Effects
Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Secrets: Can make it easier to gain X-Ray Vision as Book of Secrets cannot give a mapping effect Isaac already has.

• Glowing Hourglass: Traveling back to the previous floor and going back down may trigger the Cain's Eye if it hasn’t triggered before.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either doubles the chance to trigger The Compass effect. Having both triples the chance.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Due to the existence of Cain's Other Eye, this trinket is implied to be Cain's healthy eye.

fields.description: When starting a floor, 25% chance to gain the effect of The Compass for the duration of the floor.

Cain's Other Eye.title: Cain's Other Eye
Cain's Other Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Not to be confused with Cain's Eye, Evil Eye, or Glaucoma.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Spawns a familiar that floats slowly around the room in a zig-zag pattern similar to The Peeper and shoots normal tears in the same direction as Isaac.

• [Rebirth only] Each tear deals 3.5 damage.

• [edition anr] Each tear deals Isaac's damage.

• [Repentance] Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac and copies all of his tear modifiers/stats (like Incubus), with a 25% damage reduction. It fires randomly in the cardinal directions.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Unlike The Peeper, Cain's Other Eye does no contact damage.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Cain's Other Eye having [Before Repentance+] 5th / [Repentance+] 7th priority.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Analog Stick: The familiar will fire in completely random directions, not locked to the cardinal ones.

• Epic Fetus: Cain's Other Eye gains a crosshair and rocket similar to Isaac's but smaller. Caution is required, as the crosshair is erratic and will constantly shake, possibly making the rocket hit Isaac.

• Eye of the Occult: The familiar's tears travel a very short distance in their original direction and can be controlled afterwards.

• King Baby: Cain's Other Eye will attempt to fire directly at enemies but only when they are on the same side as the random direction it is firing in.

• Mom's Knife: The familiar will constantly swing its knife, trying to point it in the random direction it is firing in. When the fire button is released, the knife will travel in whatever direction it is pointing at the moment (it can be any direction, not necessarily a cardinal one).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is implied to be the damaged eye of Cain beneath his eyepatch.

• Rather than deciding a random input when a tear is fired, the familiar will rapidly switch the direction it's facing at all times.

• This effect is visible with The Forgotten, Tainted Forgotten, and other characters under the effects of Berserk!.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Spawns a familiar that slowly floats around the room on a zig-zag pattern and shoots normal tears in the same direction as Isaac.
[Repentance] Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac and fires tears in random cardinal directions that copy Isaac's tears and tear effects and scale with damage.

Callus.title: Callus
Callus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Prevents damage from creep and floor spikes.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Sacrifice spikes only damage Isaac for 1/2 hearts. 

• If Isaac has both Mom's Box and Golden Trinket, all damage is reduced to 1/2 hearts similar to The Wafer.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Also grants immunity to slowdown from black and white creep, but not from Cobwebs.

• Does not prevent any damage from Curse Room doors.

• [Afterbirth onward] Does not prevent damage from Spiked Chests. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth onward] Does not prevent damage from Greed mode's stop button.

• [Repentance] Does not prevent damage from Spiked Rocks.

• [Before Repentance] Prevents the use of Sacrifice Rooms, unlike flight.

• [Repentance] Can use Sacrifice Rooms now. Can also use the spikes created by Sanguine Bond.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • A callus is an area of thickened skin that forms as a response to repeated friction, pressure, or other irritation.

fields.description: Prevents damage from creep and spikes.

Cambion Conception.title: Cambion Conception
Cambion Conception.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon taking damage a certain number of times, Isaac gains a permanent demonic familiar. Possible familiars include:

• Dark Bum

• Demon Baby

• Incubus

• Leech

• Lil Brimstone

• Succubus

• Lil Abaddon

• Twisted Pair

• The first and second familiars will each spawn after taking damage 15 times. The third and fourth familiars will each spawn after taking damage 30 more times. No further familiars will spawn. As a result, after taking damage 90 times, four out of eight possible familiars will have spawned.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Isaac will look progressively more pregnant as he takes damage.

• Familiars spawned this way do not count towards transformations nor the collection page.

• Lilith starts with this item by default, even if it hasn't been unlocked. Lilith can get a second Incubus through this.

• Only one of each familiar can be spawned.

• Familiars that have yet to be unlocked can spawn, [Repentance] with the exception of Lil Abaddon and Twisted Pair, which must be unlocked before they can spawn through Cambion Conception. [end edition note] 

• Only actually getting damage counts towards the payout. For example, negating damage with the Holy Mantle will not count. Using the Blood Donation Machine or Devil Beggar counts as damage taken.

• Familiars spawned by the item do not affect item pools, so multiple copies of one familiar can be obtained. For example, a second Incubus can be purchased after Cambion Conception spawns one.

• If a familiar obtained is a copy of another one already obtained, using Box of Friends will only clone one of that familiar.

• If this item is removed in any way (such as with a XVII - The Stars?), the familiars from Cambion Conception will be removed upon updating familiars, including picking up items that don't add familiars but update its cache, such as Brimstone.

• If the item is re-obtained after being removed (e.g. by dropping the item as Tainted Isaac), the damage counter and familiar limit will be reset, allowing Isaac to obtain all eight familiars with only one Cambion Conception. If the familiars were removed, all will return once familiars are updated.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Dull Razor: Dull Razor counts towards the payout despite not removing health from Isaac.

• Hypercoagulation: By intentionally taking damage with something like a fire and grabbing the half-red hearts, Isaac can easily generate powerful familiars for free.

• Scapular: By intentionally taking damage with something like a fire to half a red heart a soul heart will be generated. Leaving the room and taking damage again will continuously allow damage to be taken.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Caffeine Pill: Makes it impossible to tell how far along the pregnancy is.

• Cambion Conception: Having a second Cambion Conception allows Isaac to get the eight familiars, but cannot give an already obtained familiar. The hit counters do not stack. Isaac has to fully pay out the first cambion before collecting the second to get all 8 familiars. Collecting a second Cambion Conception will restart the damage counter and number of familiars received even if the first one has not finished paying out yet.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is the demonic counterpart to Immaculate Conception.

• In mythology, a cambion is the offspring of a human and an incubus or succubus.

• During the development of Afterbirth, Edmund McMillen asked on Twitter what the opposite of Immaculate Conception would be called. 27 people replied with suggestions, but none of them were used.

fields.description: After taking damage a certain amount of times, a permanent demonic familiar spawns.

Camo Undies.title: Camo Undies
Camo Undies.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon entering a new room, Isaac will become camouflaged and all enemies become confused. The effect will last until Isaac presses a fire button.

• Bosses will not be confused when Isaac is camouflaged.

• [Repentance] While camouflaged, Isaac gains +0.5 Speed. When the camouflage is dropped, enemies in a short radius around Isaac take 15 damage, and he gains a temporary +10.5 Damage and +7.5 Tears up which both rapidly scale down to 0. The tears up ignores the soft tears cap.

• • If Isaac is firing tears while walking into a room, the camouflage and stat boost will not apply.

• • 
• This also applies when pressing a fire button to skip boss transition cutscenes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• List of enemies that are completely unaffected by this item:

| Name | ID
[entity row minimal: Fistuloid] 
[entity row minimal: Poky] 
[entity row minimal: Slide] 
[entity row minimal: Stone Grimace] 
[entity row minimal: Stoney]

• List of enemies partially affected by this item, all of which visually appear confused but react to Isaac's presence in some way nonetheless:

| Name | ID | Details
[entity row minimal: Black Globin's Body] | Keeps spawning Spiders that are also confused.
[entity row minimal: Blind Creep] | Their behavior is practically the same as normal.
[entity row minimal: Fat Bat] | Keeps shooting projectiles in random, ordinal directions.
[entity row minimal: Fatty] | Farts when Isaac gets too close.
[entity row minimal: Host] | Pops up very often without actually shooting.
[entity row minimal: Imp] | Fires at Isaac's current location and teleports around like normal.

• Red Fire Places & Purple Fire Places are not affected by this item.

• While bosses are not confused, monsters spawned during boss fights are confused, as long as the effect lasts.

• The item's effect can potentially cause FPS drops.

• Champion enemies become tinted the same color as regular enemies, making it difficult to distinguish them.

• A co-op baby firing will also end the camouflage effect.

• [Repentance] Shopkeepers can be destroyed by the area effect when firing tears for the first time in a room.

• [Before Repentance] This item does almost nothing in Greed mode, despite being able to be obtained from the Greed mode Treasure Room.

• [Repentance] Due to its ability to destroy Shopkeepers, Camo Undies can net you some extra Pennies or Nickels from shops and The Shop floor, should a Shopkeeper wave appear there.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Active items: May be used to deal damage without canceling the effect.

• Chasing familiars: Familiars like these can chase and damage enemies with little risk. Best ones for the task are 7 Seals and Daddy Longlegs, since they have long aggro range.

• Orbital familiars: Enemies can be damaged with little risk, as the camo effect allows Isaac to get close enough for the orbital to deal damage with low risk of taking damage in return.

• 120 Volt / Jupiter / Monstrance / Salvation: Great sources of passive damage without disrupting camo.

• Aries: Isaac can run into enemies without disrupting the camouflage.

• Blood Puppy: Like most enemies, a hostile Blood Puppy will not target Isaac while the camo effect is active, but it will still target and attack other enemies.

• Dark Arts: The stealth mode given by Camo Undies won't be removed by activating Dark Arts. However, Dark Arts only gives +0.5 speed while Camo Undies is active.

• Mars: Can be used to deal damage without cancelling the effect.

• Mom's Knife: As long as it's not being charged, the knife can deal damage passively.

• Will not break camouflage while using mouse controls to aim.

• Neptunus: The passive charge of Neptunus does not disrupt Camo, and the initial burst of damage is enhanced by Neptunus.

• Rock Bottom: Temporary tears and damage up do not go away, causing a permanent boost for the rest of the run.

• [Repentance] Tainted Judas: Gets a lot of use out of Camo Undies due to his in-built Dark Arts not disrupting camo. [end edition note] 

• Venus: Charm effect activates while in stealth.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone / Chocolate Milk / Cursed Eye / Monstro's Lung / Spirit Sword / Tech X: Charging ends the camo effect, and the effect doesn't happen when entering a room with a full charge.

• The Ludovico Technique: Camo Undies will remain active until the tear is moved by pressing a button.

• [Before Repentance] Since the tear follows Isaac, he can run around and use the tear to kill enemies.

• • [Repentance] Tear no longer follows Isaac, but will still not remove Camo effect until moved.

• Tainted Forgotten: The item does not affect Tainted Soul, making it useless.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The phrase Camo Kid is a reference to the CAM0 K1DD seed.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Shooting with mouse control enabled will not break the camouflage effect, permanently causing confusion effect on enemies, but without granting the stat bonuses.
Bug note: Triggering Dark Arts while Camo Undies are still active will deactivate Camo Undies for the duration of Dark Arts, after which Camo Undies will reactivate.

fields.description: Isaac becomes camouflaged at the beginning of each room. Until he shoots, all non-boss enemies will be confused. [Repentance] Isaac gains +0.5 Speed while camouflaged, and gains Tears and Damage upon breaking it.

Candy Heart.title: Candy Heart
Candy Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac one of the following stat boosts per half heart healed with Red Heart pickups or when gaining an extra filled heart container:

• +0.02 speed.

• +0.05 tears.

• +0.10 flat damage.

• +0.25 range.

• +0.02 shot speed.

• +0.10 luck.

• Spawns a Red Heart when picked up.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Items/effects that directly heal Isaac (such as Yum Heart, XIX - The Sun, Charm of the Vampire, etc.) do not trigger stat boosts from Candy Heart.

• Healing using Rotten Hearts triggers the stat boosts for Candy Heart.

• Picking up an Eternal Heart while already having one so that a new Red Heart container is formed provides stat boosts.

• The stat boosts are equivalent to picking up a full Red Heart.

• Picking up the first Eternal Heart does not grant stat boosts.

• Adding the second Eternal Heart to Isaac's health directly (e. g. by using Prayer Card) does not give stat boosts.

• This item does not give stats when adding to Tainted Bethany's blood charges.

• This item is useless for characters that can't have red hearts (e.g. The Lost, Keeper, ???, etc.).

• Any healing prior to picking up Candy Heart will not provide stat boosts.

• [Before Repentance+] The stat bonuses are "stored" on the Candy Heart. Dropping or losing it in any way won't immediately revert the bonuses gained, only when Isaac's stats are updated again. The respective stat changed is the one that loses the Candy Heart bonuses.

• The bonus stats will be lost if Isaac's stats are updated by dropping out of the game or if the game crashes.

• The stat bonuses are seeded, meaning the same stat ups will apply in the same order in the same seed.

• Strategy Suggestion: Leaving Soul Hearts on the ground during a level allows the player to force Red Heart damage and still offer Devil/Angel Deal protection for the next floor.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Hypercoagulation:/Tainted Magdalene: Can provide infinite stat boosts, if the dropped hearts are caught in time.

• Maggy's Bow: Increases the stat boosts given by Candy Heart, provided extra Red health was restored.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Apple of Sodom: This doesn't give the stat increases when picking up hearts to make spiders.

• Candy Heart: This item isn't affected by stacking.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is the red heart equivalent to Soul Locket, and gives half as many stats per heart collected, comparatively.

fields.description: Gives Isaac a permanent stat boost whenever he heals with Red Heart pickups.

Car Battery.title: Car Battery
Car Battery.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Causes eligible activated items to activate twice on each use.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Having more than one Car Battery has no effect.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Best Friend: Spawns two decoys on top of each other.

• Blank Card: Uses the card twice. For example, if used with the Two of Hearts/Diamonds/etc. cards it will quadruple whatever amount Isaac has.

• Blank Card + Tarot Cloth: The effect of the active card is quadrupled.

• Broken Shovel 1: Prevents the Mom's Foot from appearing for two rooms (empty or not), or for two waves of a Challenge Room or the Boss Rush, essentially removing the stomping attacks for the entire duration of the Boss Rush.

• D10: Weakens affected enemies twice.

• Isaac's Tears: The damage of tears shot from the active item is doubled.

• Kamikaze!: Now causes smaller explosions in a ring around Isaac.

• Jacob's Ladder / 120 Volt: Electricity deals 75% of Isaac's tear damage if he owns 1 of these items, to 100% if Isaac owns both.

• Crooked Penny: Splits the 50% chance to succeed into a 25% chance to quadruple all items and a 25% chance to duplicate all items while consuming the originals; the latter will make Devil deal and Shop items free.

• [Repentance] The 25% chance to duplicate all items while consuming the originals now generates 2 pennies instead.

• Sulfur: Will count as giving double Brimstone, giving extra damage and a x1.2 damage multiplier for the current room.

• Void: Applies Car Battery's effect on all eligible absorbed active items. Absorbing passives will not give extra stat ups.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Anarchist Cookbook: Spawns 13 Troll Bombs.

• Book of Revelations: Give Isaac 2 soul hearts.

• Converter: Consumes 2 Soul Hearts and produces 2 Red Heart Containers.

• The Bean / Mega Bean / Kidney Bean: Deals double damage, but charms/poisons/petrifies for the same amount of time.

• Berserk!: Will only increase rage duration if no enemies are killed in the first half, effectively only affecting bosses that can't spawn enemies.

• Book of Virtues: Doubles the spawned wisps on activation.

• Book of Secrets: Activates twice, [Before Repentance] but has a chance to uselessly activate the same effect twice.

• Book of Shadows / The Gamekid / My Little Unicorn / Unicorn Stump: Doubles the length of invincibility, but no effect on damage where applicable.

• The Candle / Red Candle: Spawns a second flame that travels a shorter distance.

• Clicker: If the Car Battery is removed by the first activation, a second activation will not happen. Two activations in a row is mostly detrimental, removing two items and possibly cycling through a character that lowers health.

• D infinity: Activates 2 dice. The second activation die cannot be predicted.

• [Repentance] Activates the currently selected die twice.

• D4 / D100: Instantly re-rolls Isaac's items twice, which doubles the speed at which the item pools are exhausted and transformations are achieved.

• [Repentance] As items are returned back into the item pool when re-rolled, the item pools aren't exhausted at all. In addition, you need to actively be holding a transformation's respective items to retain them now, so using the double re-roll to gain multiple transformations is no longer possible.

• The D6 / D8 / D12 / D20: Re-rolls twice instantly without any benefits. The D6 depletes item pools at double the speed, and the D20 may invisibly reroll a trinket, effectively skipping it in the circulation.

• D12: Roughly doubles the rare chance of obstacles being turned into Reward Plates, Killswitches, and very rarely Crawl Spaces, as the D12 can create these but cannot re-roll them.

• D7: Doubles the amount of enemies summoned, but does not give double rewards.

• Dark Arts: Doubles the duration, giving more time to walk through more enemies, if you end the effect before the end of the first second, the item will reactivate itself; allowing to target the same enemies twice.

• Dead Sea Scrolls: Activates 2 random effects.

• Doctor's Remote: Drops an additional missile after the first one.

• Dull Razor: The invulnerability time is not increased, but damage-triggered items will activate twice if applicable.

• Eternal D6: Re-rolls twice like The D6 (see above), but the 30% chance of the item disappearing is increased to 51%.

• Everything Jar: Instead of doubling its effect, Everything Jar will spawn a poop alongside its normal drop.

• Gello: Spawns an additional familiar.

• Guppy's Head: Increases range of flies spawned to 4-7.

• Head of Krampus: Doubles the damage the brimstone beams deal (for a total of [Before Repentance] 880 damage/ [Repentance] 400 damage per use). Doesn't double the brimstone beams' duration.

• The Hourglass: Doubles the length of the effect.

• Mega Blast: Extends the length of the effect from 15 seconds to 23 seconds.

• Mega Mush: Makes the effect twice as long.

• Metronome: Metronome is activated twice at once as expected, but the item chosen for the first activation is shown raised above Isaac's head, instead of the second one that actually remains active.

• Moreover, active item effects chosen by Metronome are only activated once.

• Mine Crafter: Spawns a Movable TNT and instantly detonates it, damaging Isaac.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] This has been changed to spawn two Movable TNT barrels instead, which you can detonate at will.

• Moving Box: Activation swaps the contents of the box with the contents of the room.

• [Repentance] This has been changed to have no effects.

• The Scooper: Will summon 2 peepers in a bifurcated direction.

• Spider Butt: Deals 10 damage to enemies twice but does not increase slow effect.

• Spindown Dice: Lowers ID by 2.

• Stitches: Swaps places with Isaac twice in quick succession, rendering Stitches useless for collecting pickups & items beyond pits, rocks etc.

• However, it can still be used to telefrag enemies.

• Tear Detonator: Multiplies detonated tears, resulting in 6x more tears than normal.

• Telekinesis: Grants 7 seconds of protection, effectively giving Isaac immunity to enemy bullets as long as the item is used immediately upon recharging.

• Ventricle Razor: Places both trapdoors in same location.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Ventricle Razor works normally.

• We Need To Go Deeper! / Mom's Shovel: In most cases, no extra effect. When used near the entrances to a room, the item can occasionally open 2 trapdoors at once, [Before Repentance] increasing the chance of opening a Crawl Space.

sections.text: [achievement text: Extension Cord, Jumper Cables]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:

• [Repentance+] 66 items (38.6%) are not eligible.

sections.heading: Bugs

Card Reading.title: Card Reading
Card Reading.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• At the beginning of each floor, spawns 2 portals that lead to certain special rooms:

• A red portal leading to the Boss Room.

• A yellow portal leading to the Treasure Room.

• A blue portal leading to the Secret Room.

• [Repentance+] A green portal leading to the Shop.

• On floors with no treasure rooms or no secret rooms, only 1 portal will spawn.

• The portals will disappear once the starting room is left, whether a portal was taken or not.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Assuming that each portal has an equal chance of spawning, before chapter 4, each portal has a [Before Repentance+] 2/3 [Repentance+] 1/2 chance to appear. From chapter 4 onward, there's a 1/2 chance of either color spawning.

• In challenges without treasure rooms or without secret rooms, only 1 portal will spawn on each floor.

• No portals will spawn in Home.

• During the Ascent, the portal will spawn in the "starting room" that leads to the next floor.

• Entering the starting room in the Mirrored World will cause the portals to spawn there, leading to the mirror's treasure, secret, boss, [Repentance+] or shop.

• If the run is exited, the portals will not be there upon continuing.

• In The Void the boss portal will lead to a random boss, not necessarily Delirium.

• Entering a portal with [cu: Maze] active on the current floor has a chance of teleporting Isaac to a random room instead.

• The Treasure Room portal will not lead to a Planetarium if available, unlike XVII - The Stars.

• [Repentance+] Card Reading's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bloody Crown: Makes a second portal spawn in Chapter 4.

• Holy Crown/Wicked Crown: Makes a second portal spawn in Chapter 5, if on the respective floor.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Fittingly, this item's sprite is a combination of IV - The Emperor and XVII - The Stars.

• This item may be a reference to the portals in the videogame Wizard of Legend, where four portals appear after clearing the boss room, that teleport you to important locations (shops or the start point) depending on their color (red, green, purple, and turquoise).

• The subtext "A link to your future" is very likely a reference to the game The Legend of Zelda: A Link to The Past.

• Card Reading is twice as unlikely to appear as most other Shop items, and is the only Shop item which acts this way that cannot be obtained from a different item pool.

• Card Reading is tied with Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2 for the item with the most item tags at 6.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: In the first floor of a Victory Lap, the portals will appear but cannot be entered. It will work again from floor 2.
Bug note: Entering one of the portals causes the Found Soul familiar to become invisible until Isaac drops and picks up the trinket again or enters a new floor.
Bug note: Using a portal, then rewinding time with the Glowing Hourglass will not cause the portals to reappear.
Bug note: Portals may on rare occasion appear in Death Certificate rooms, even under item pedestals. Taking the portal will simply teleport Isaac to another room inside the Death Certificate area.

Cards and Runes.title: Cards and Runes
Cards and Runes.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Cards and runes are single-use pickups with a wide variety of effects. They take up the same slot as pills.

Runes and special cards are unlocked by completing challenges.

In the base game, there are 32 cards and 8 runes.

• [Afterbirth onward] The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth adds Get out of Jail Free Card, ? Card, the Blank Rune, and two non-card consumables: Dice Shard and Emergency Contact. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth † adds the Ace cards, Holy Card, and Black Rune, for a total of 39 cards and 10 runes.

• Booster Pack#1 also added three other Magic: The Gathering cards: Huge Growth, Ancient Recall, and Era Walk. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The Binding of Isaac: Repentance adds Reversed Major Arcana Cards, the Queen of Hearts, the Wild Card, Rune Shards, Soul Stones, as well as the Cracked Key, for a grand total of 66 cards, 28 runes and 3 other consumables. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Other
sections.text:
These are items other than cards and runes (and pills) that take up the consumable slot. When on the ground, each of these items are uniquely identifiable by their respective icon. [Repentance] These consumables cannot be replicated by either Blank Card or Clear Rune, and Tarot Cloth has no effect on them, but the D1 will always duplicate these into themselves. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Probabilities
sections.text:
Cards that spawn as random ones, i.e. with a sub-type of 0, have the following probabilities:

• Any tarot card (1-22) - 66.66%

• A specific tarot card - 3.03%

• Any reverse tarot card (56-77) - 11.22%

• A specific reverse tarot card - 0.51%

• Any face card (23-31) - 7.74%

• A specific face card (23-31) - 0.86%

• Queen of Hearts (79) - 0.86% (same as a specific face card)

• Any special card (42-54) - 3.51%

• A specific special card - 0.27%

• Cracked Key (78) - 0.27% (same as a specific special card)

• Wild Card (80) - 0.27% (same as a specific special card)

• Any rune (32-41) - 3.60%

• A specific rune - 0.36%

• Any soul stone (81-97) - 5.95%

• A specific soul stone - 0.35%

• Rune shard (55) - 0.00% (never spawns on a fully completed save file, chosen only as a replacement otherwise)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] The game counts runes as cards for the purposes of Blank Card, and Tarot Cloth.

• [Repentance] Even though runes no longer count as cards as of Repentance, Little Baggy still prevents new runes from appearing except through forced drops (such as from Mom's Ring or Clear Rune). Runes that already existed prior to picking up Little Baggy will not be converted.

• Starter Deck does not prevent runes/soul stones from generating, will sometimes turn pills into either, and allows holding two of them.

• Runes will be replaced with cards if no runes are unlocked.

• [Repentance] However, items that normally spawn runes (e.g. Rune Bag or Clear Rune) can spawn Rune Shards before any runes are unlocked. [end edition note] 

• If alternate versions of consumables have been unlocked (for example, Charged Keys or Mega Chests), any cards that can spawn that type of consumables (for example, Ace of Spades or [Repentance] VIII - Justice?) have a chance of being replaced with those rarer consumables.

• Key Rings are the only exception to this.

• [Repentance] If Tarot Cloth is held, the card will flash, indicating that it will be amplified by Tarot Cloth. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Using any teleport cards while inside of The Beast fight will simply move Isaac instantly to a different spot in the same room. This also includes the Joker card. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The appearance of the tarot cards seems to be based on the Universal Tarot of Marseille deck produced by Lo Scarabeo, most clearly seen with the card backs as well as the splash image that appears when using The Sun.

• The runes and their names ingame are based on the Elder Futhark alphabet system and its reconstructed Proto-Germanic names. In popular culture, runes often signify that something is in some way magical.

• Ancient Recall, Era Walk, Huge Growth, and Chaos Card are all based on cards from Magic: The Gathering.

• A NULL card with ID 0 exists, revealed by the "giveitem k0" Debug Console command. It can't be acquired or used in any way.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Many cards were given new unique back sprites in Booster Pack#5, some originating from Antibirth.

• [Repentance] The Reverse Tarot Cards refer to tarot card readings, where a reversed card has a contrary meaning to its upright variant.

sections.text: Bug note: Any blue flies, blue spiders, [Afterbirth+ onward] friendly enemies, [Afterbirth+ onward] locusts, [Afterbirth+ onward] orbital bones, and [Repentance] wisps created by cards, runes, and soul stones can be multiplied when Glowing Hourglass teleports Isaac in a way that does not move him to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again).

Charger.title: Charger
Charger.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Chargers are a more advanced form of Maggot.

They possess a smiling face of sorts and look quite harmless as they slowly crawl along without attempting to follow Isaac. If a Charger lines up with Isaac vertically or horizontally, however, they will immediately and quickly charge in a straight line towards him. Because they're usually encountered in groups, avoiding them quickly becomes a problem. They are also unusually tanky for enemies encountered so early; the default damage of most characters is 3.5, so without damage upgrades (not especially rare for Chapter 2), they require 6 shots to take down, and can thus easily become overwhelming when combined with other threats. Usage of Bombs or offensive Active Items/Cards may be warranted during those early floors to dispatch them.

sections.heading: Drowned Charger
sections.text:
Drowned Chargers are a drowned variant added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth DLC.

They possess the same behavior of regular Chargers, but have 10% more health. They shoot four diagonal blood shots upon death. They can be spawned by Drowned Boom Fly upon death, as well as (at reduced health) by Drowned Hives.

sections.heading: Dank Charger
sections.text:
Dank Chargers are the dank variants added in Booster Pack #5 of The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth † DLC.

They behave similarly to regular Chargers, but have a much faster dash, bounce off of walls while dashing, and leave a trail of slowing black creep while dashing. When their charge ends, they have a short cooldown period before they start moving again.

sections.heading: Carrion Princess
sections.text:
Carrion Princess is a Carrion Queen-like variation of a Charger added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. They appear exclusively in Ashpit.

They charge diagonally, similar to Carrion Queen. Much like the Carrion Queen, they can only be damaged by hitting their pink tail segments.

[Repentance+] Destroyed by Hagalaz on use. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Level 2 Charger
sections.text:
Level 2 Chargers are stronger variants of Chargers added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC. They are found in Corpse and the ascent to Home.

Upon lining up with Isaac cardinally, Level 2 Chargers will initially charge cardinally towards him but will curve their trajectory towards Isaac's position if attempting to move out of the way. Level 2 Chargers move slightly slower than default Chargers.

sections.heading: Elleech
sections.text:
Elleeches are enemies added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC.

Their behavior is a cross between a Level 2 Charger and Small Leech, moving aimlessly until Isaac lines up with them cardinally. They then will charge indefinitely at Isaac, not stopping at objects.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Chargers first appear in the original Flash version of The Binding of Isaac.

• Chargers are based on Ropes from the Legend of Zelda franchise, since both charge at the player when they are in their sight.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Dank Chargers were created by Kilburn for Booster Pack #5.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The behavior of the Dank Charger resembles that of the Charger from The End is Nigh, another game made by Edmund McMillen.

• [Repentance] Elleeches are the only Ascent enemy without "Tainted" in its name.

• Their name instead is a portmanteau combining the words "Elite" and "Leech", still carrying its elevated status.

• They also take the appearance and behavior of a Small Leech, so in a way, they could be called Tainted Small Leeches.

Mother's Shadow.title: Mother's Shadow
Mother's Shadow.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Mother's Shadow is a mini-boss found in a sub-area of the second floor of Chapter 2.5 (Mines and Ashpit). She spawns on the way back after obtaining the Knife Piece 2. She's completely invincible and only serves as an obstacle in a chase sequence.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Upon entering this area, all passive items, active items, and trinkets will be rendered inactive, and Isaac's Bombs, Penny, and Keys will be set to zero, leaving him similar to his state during the start of the game. He only has his current hearts. He must walk through several empty rooms before reaching the end room containing Knife Piece 2. Picking it up causes the room to shake and summons Mother's Shadow. Mother's Shadow is completely invulnerable and Isaac must escape her by returning to the special area entrance and leaving. On the way back, the path back will be obstructed by various obstacles, such as rocks, Fire Places, spikes, and Poops.

Mother's Shadow, after appearing, begins slowly floating after Isaac. When close enough to him, she stops and then quickly dashes at Isaac, dealing a whole heart of contact damage. Isaac can 'push' Mother's shadow before her charge by walking into her and will not take contact damage. Mother's Shadow can go off-screen with her dash attack or when a door is crossed into a different room. She then resumes following Isaac.

• Mother's Shadow's position at all times is determined by her position relative to the general layout of the floor, meaning she persists in the same location even when Isaac moves through rooms. However, she cannot be left behind and is carried along as the screen moves.

• After encountering Mother's Shadow, the previously empty path back to the main floor map becomes filled with a variety of obstacles, such as poops that must be destroyed, timed spikes, rocks that must be broken by Throwable Bombs from Bomb Grimaces, buttons, and sometimes keys and certain cards that spawn in each room.

As soon as Isaac passes the door leading out of the sub-area, Mother's Shadow screams Isaac's name in defeat and disappears as the sub-area's entrance is blocked by falling rocks. It is no longer possible to access this area again past this point.

sections.heading: Audio
sections.text:
[sound table row: ; The stinger that plays upon picking up Knife Piece 2 as Mom's Shadow appears.] 
[sound table row: ; The laugh the shadow makes upon emerging.] 
[sound table row: ; The laugh the shadow makes upon emerging.] 
[sound table row: ; The shadow calling Isaac's name as she lunges at him.] 
[sound table row: ; The noise Mother's Shadow makes after Isaac successfully escapes.]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Upon acquiring the Knife Piece 2, all Fire Places are extinguished and then re-ignited as red fires as Mother's Shadow appears.

• Fire places can drop their pickups during this scene.

• After Mother's Shadow spawns and the Knife Piece room reopens, Isaac gains 1 charge for his active item.

• New pickups obtained in the area will persist after Isaac leaves.

• Unlike non-story items, which disappear during the sequence, Isaac's health stays the same, and friendly enemies still follow him here.

• Blue Flies, Blue Spiders, Locusts, Big Fan spawned from a Pretty Fly Horse Pill, Cube of Meat spawned from a Potato Peeler, and Wisps spawned from Book of Virtues and Vengeful Spirit persist into this sequence, but have no effect on Mother's Shadow. Blood clots spawned by Sumptorium will also persist and are immune to Mother's Shadow.

• Extra lives granted by items such as Dead Cat or Guppy's Collar do not work, as they are removed from Isaac.

• Lazarus, however, still retains his extra life.

• Items that grant flight are taken away, forcing most characters to traverse the obstacles normally.

• XIX - The Sun? allows any character to fly, despite not having the visual effects of the card's Spirit of the Night visible.

• XV - The Devil? also allows any character to fly. However, the effect is likely to wear off before the end of the chase sequence.

• Esau Jr. works similarly. If Isaac enters the zone with Esau Jr., he is still able to fly without his appearance.

• The active piece of Broken Shovel 1 will still spawn Mom's feet in this area.

• Eve will benefit from her Whore of Babylon if criteria are met but her sprite will remain un-cursed.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
• The key to avoiding damage during the chase sequence is to be patient. Trying to rush to the exit door will often result in unavoidable hits.

• Mother's Shadow will not attack Isaac directly between dashes, only float in his general direction. She will scream right before attacking, and will lock her direction; stay in place until she starts to dash and then swiftly move out of the way to dodge.

• Going back into the previous room doesn't cancel her attacks, but provides more space for avoiding them, as well as invincibility frames.

• Do not stand on one tile-wide paths for too long, because they limit Isaac's ability to move out of the way of her dashes.

• Since Isaac keeps any health he enters the area with, it is wise to stock up on hearts beforehand to minimize chances of death.

• Tainted Eve's Sumptorium should be used before entering to maximize health.

• Azazel, The Lost, Tainted Lost, Tainted Jacob in his Lost form, and Tainted Forgotten can escape with minimal risk, as they can use their inherent flight to fly directly to the exit door.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• If a Crawl Space or Black Market spawns, the player can regain access to their items and cards/pills/runes in that space; however, Mother's Shadow will continue to give chase. If the player progresses to the next floor while in this space, Mother's Shadow dies, letting out the Isaac scream and temporarily locking the doors at the beginning of the next floor.

• Mother's Shadow resembles the face of Mom as she is depicted on the cover art for Repentance.

• Sometimes when charging, Mother's Shadow can yell Isaac's name in a deeper voice.

• The only items that are not taken away from Isaac in this sequence are Knife Piece 1, Key Piece 1, Key Piece 2, and Dogma, although the latter can only be obtained through special means.

• Although Mother's Shadow has 250 health, it can not be damaged or killed, even with Chaos Card.

• Using debug 10 while entering the room containing Knife Piece 2 will kill Mother's Shadow before the chase activates. Picking up Knife Piece 2 will not start the chase if Mother's Shadow has been killed this way.

• Due to how the escape sequence is spawned (one version spawned when you enter for the first time, and one edited version spawned when Mother's Shadow appears after Knife Piece 2 is collected), items relevant to the escape sequence, such as cards used in puzzles like XII - The Hanged Man, will spawn both when the area is entered and when the escape sequence itself begins. Ergo, despite normally being blocked off, if you have some way to collect these items on the way to collect Knife Piece 2 (such as methods either as simple as using a character like Azazel or The Lost and their innate ability to fly, or complex ones such as using the explosive tears made by Wisps spawned from Book of Virtues combined with Bob's Rotten Head to break rocks that prevent items like these from being obtained on the first run through), you can obtain an extra copy of these items, allowing you to 'skip' rooms that may not account for you possessing these items before the escape begins - for example, using the aforementioned XII - The Hanged Man within the room you got it from before Mother's Shadow spawned to simply fly through the room, grab another copy of the same card spawned by Mother's Shadow's appearance before exiting, and then use that copy in another room.

• If Mama Mega! is used prior to entering the sequence, it will destroy all obstacles in every new room entered. However, due to how Mama Mega! works, it will not re-destroy obstacles on the way out, and thus does not aid the player during the chase.

• When Isaac enters the final room that contains Knife Piece 2, Mama Mega will activate, breaking open the exit door. If Isaac takes Knife Piece 2 and leaves before Mother's Shadow activates and charges at Isaac, the exit path of the sub-area will not have completely reset, and the doors will all be locked while Mother's Shadow still continues her activation sequence. This forces the player to re-enter the Knife Piece 2 room, which will start another activation process for Mother's Shadow, but this time, the exit door will lock as normal, preventing the player from leaving early. This results in the player being pursued by 2 Mother's Shadows during the escape sequence.

• The effect of the player's items being disabled whilst in the Mother's Shadow area is known as Curse of the Mist, as seen in the Lua Documentation.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If the game is saved and exited while in the sub-area, when it is continued, Isaac's visual appearance will match his items; however, items will still have no effect. It will revert to his plain appearance after either changing rooms or picking up a Throwable Bomb.
Bug note: Familiars with levels/stages will revert to their base form upon exiting the sub-area as the game does not internally store their levels. This includes, but is not limited to: Bumbo, Guppy's Hairball, etc.
Bug note: If Mother's Shadow kills Issac as he exits the sub-area, after his death animation finishes, the game will crash.

Moving Box.title: Moving Box
Moving Box.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Not to be confused with Box.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• If the box is empty, it picks up items and pickups in a room and stores them.

• [Repentance] Moving Box can carry up to 10 items or pickups at once, randomly picked (i.e. items are not prioritized).

• If the box is not empty, places all stored items and pickups in the current room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] Moving Box can sometimes spawn within the special bedroom created by Lil Portal. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] There is no limit to the number of items and pickups that can be held in the box.

• The best way to utilize Moving Box is often to absorb a large number of weaker items, then place them all into one room, and use a reroll effect to reroll them all at the same time. This is especially effective in Secret Rooms.

• Any stored items and pickups unpacked from Moving Box will remain identical to what was originally packed; pills, cards, and runes will stay the same, Sticky Nickels will remain stuck to the floor, active items keep their charge in the box, and Chests will have the same contents as they would if they had been opened immediately.

• Stealing from Shops and Devil Rooms is not possible; only items on pedestals will be packed up.

• All existing Moving Boxes share their opened/closed state. Therefore, it is not possible to carry a Moving Box that is holding items within another Moving Box as the items must be unpacked first.

• If used in a room with a choice of multiple item pedestals, only one of the choice objects will be packed up and [Before Repentance] the rest will remain and behave normally / [Repentance] the rest will disappear.

• [Before Repentance] Both items presented by There's Options and More Options can be taken.

• [Before Repentance] Both The Polaroid and The Negative can be taken.

• [Before Repentance] If used in the Boss Rush room, one of the objects is packed up but the rush is not started. The remaining item choices start the rush as normal.

• • [Repentance] Using Moving Box to pack items in Boss Rush starts the challenge.

• [Before Repentance] If used in a Challenge Room or Boss Challenge Room the objects within can be packed up without starting the challenge.

• [Repentance] Using Moving Box in these rooms starts the challenge.

• [Repentance] Disappearing pickups that are spawned by Tainted Magdalene / Soul of Magdalene or Tainted Keeper can't be packed into Moving Box.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a box wisp on the middle ring. Moving Box must drop a pickup/item in order for it to spawn wisps. The wisps invoke the effect of The Book of Sin when destroyed.

• Glowing Hourglass: If a charged Glowing Hourglass is stored in the Moving Box, it can be unpacked and used to rewind time and regain some item charges.

• [Before Repentance] Both items regain their charges, essentially allowing unlimited use.

• [Repentance] Moving Box charges are regained, but Glowing Hourglass will lose one charge.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: Activation swaps the contents of the box with the contents of the room.

• [Repentance] No effect.

• Death Certificate: Takes one random item from a Death Certificate room which is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.

• Flip: Moving items that are able to be swapped by Flip will still be able to be swapped after placing them down again. However, empty item pedestals that only contain the "ghostly" item cannot be moved unless flipped.

• Options?: Only one of the choice pickups will be packed up and the other will disappear.

• Void: This item's effect cannot be absorbed by Void. It will be treated as a passive item by the Void.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Moving Box is based on this Steam Workshop item by Tim l'enchanteur.

sections.text:
• Places a large Bomb similar to ones produced by Mr. Mega.

• Despite slightly different appearance, the bomb is functionally identical to a Mr. Mega bomb, being compatible with all bomb modifiers.

• [edition rnr+] This item can be crafted by Bag of Crafting with eight Bombs.

sections.heading: Synergies

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring, looking like bombs. The wisps spawn miniature homing bombs when destroyed. These miniature bombs behave the same as ones created by Scatter Bombs, with the exception that they deal 100 blast damage instead of 50.

• Remote Detonator + Schoolbag: The Mr. Boom bomb is affected by remote detonator.

• Blasting Cap: Mr. Boom bombs can drop extra bomb pickups.

• Mr. Mega: No further improvement in damage or blast radius.

sections.heading: Trivia

Mr. Fred.title: Mr. Fred
Mr. Fred.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the enemy; Fred] 

Mr. Fred is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In the Womb and the Utero.

• [Repentance] In the Womb and the Scarred Womb. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Mr. Fred stays stationary in the middle of a 1x2 or 2x1 room and performs the following attacks:

• Breaks the chain of 1 of the 4 Homunculus that accompany him at the beginning of the fight.

• Unlike other Homounculi, the ones spawned with Mr. Fred can not break free on their own and can only be unleashed by this attack.

• Shoots 4 large long-range blood projectiles in the cardinal directions. These tears leave Red Creep and will burst at the end of their range into a larger pool of Creep.

• Burrows underground briefly and pops back up in his original position, firing eight projectiles in all directions.

• Spawns a Fred on his position, which immediately burrows underground.
Mr. Fred deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mr. Fred is the boss version of the Freds.

• Mr. Fred resembles a large baby with a medical condition Harlequin Ichthyosis. He could, therefore, be a giant Harlequin Baby.

• Mr. Fred may be the inspiration for the Throbbing King's design.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Unlike other bosses, Mr. Fred disappears upon death instead of exploding into blood.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Similar to Delirium's room, if Mr. Fred spawns in The Void, his room will be seen in the map as a 1x1 room. [end edition note] 

• That's why he can't be replaced by a harbinger with Book of Revelations

• Mr. Fred's boss art shows the ground around him to be grey, instead of a fleshy red.

Mr. ME!.title: Mr. ME!
Mr. ME!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Summons a ghost near Isaac that will follow him around, and summons a controllable blue crosshair. After a few seconds, the crosshair disappears, and the ghost will act depending on what the crosshair was targeting:

• Items / Pickups / Trinkets / Chests / Red Chests / Spiked Chests / Mega Chests: Brings it to Isaac.

• • Can steal from Shops, Devil Rooms, and Black Markets, making the item/pickup free. Stealing an item has a 33% chance to fail. If that happens, a buzzer sound will play and the ghost will disappear without doing anything.

• • [Before Repentance] Stealing an item from a Shop will restock it with another item, as if Isaac had Restock. This does not happen in other room types.

• Locked Chests / Eternal Chests / Bomb Chests: Opens the chest for free.

• Pressure Plate/Reward Plate: Presses the button. This includes the wave pause button in Greed Mode.

• Enemies: Attacks the enemy until it dies or can no longer be targeted due to a form change or similar cause. The ghost does 3 damage per tick, for 9 damage per second.

• Doors: Opens the door, even if it is locked. Functions the same as Dad's Key when being used in this way. This includes the door to Mega Satan, exiting Hush's room, and exiting Boss Rush.

• • [Repentance] This does not work on A Strange Door. However, it does work on doors leading to alternate path levels. [end edition note] 

• • [Repentance] This does not work on the flesh door leading to Mom's Heart that appears after defeating Mom in Mausoleum or Gehenna. [end edition note] 

• • [Repentance] This does not work on the hidden closet in Home to unlock the tainted characters. [end edition note] 

• Secret Room entrances: Explodes, opening the entrance.

• Some destructible obstacles, Shopkeepers, Slot Machines, Beggars, and [Before Repentance] angel statues: Explodes and destroys them.

• • Can't target regular rocks, bomb rocks, spiked rocks, fool's gold rocks, blocks, key blocks, normal and red fire places, any poop, or [Repentance] angel statues.

• If the room has nothing to interact with, the ghost will disappear without doing anything.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If the crosshair is not targeting anything when the crosshair disappears, the ghost will interact with the object closest to the crosshair.

• Picking up a stolen Devil deal will not prevent Angel Rooms from appearing. [Repentance] It will also not despawn the other Devil items for characters like The Lost.

• The ghost cannot pick up Sticky Nickels and will disappear upon touching them.

• The ghost can open chests in Challenge Rooms without triggering the room.

• Unlike chests, stealing an item pedestal from a Challenge Room will trigger the waves to spawn upon picking up the stolen item.

• In rooms with multiple pedestal items where only one can be taken, if the ghost is carrying a pedestal while Isaac picks up a different pedestal item, the ghost will disappear. This prevents taking both items for free.

• [Before Repentance] If used in an Angel Room with no item pedestals, Mr. ME! will target the angel statue, blowing it up.

• If used with MouseControl=1 enabled, while pressing mouse left button, the blue crosshair will keep going away from the character, not following the mouse.

• Having Marked make the blue crosshair follow the mouse instead.

• If the ghost is currently out and moving, putting down Mr. ME! by any means will destroy the ghost and consume the charge.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a wisp that looks like a face in the middle ring. The wisp cannot shoot. If the current room is cleared, the wisps automatically move toward and unlock chests (Except for Bomb Chests and Mega Chests) and special room doors, destroying themselves in the process. The wisps can open almost any locked doors, including the ones to Mega Satan, the Ascent, but excluding Corpse.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Does not increase the ghost's damage when attacking enemies.

• Car Battery: May sometimes glitch pedestal items, resulting in Isaac being unable to pick them up without leaving and re-entering the room. Otherwise has no effect.

• Flip: Ghostly items cannot be targeted.

• [Repentance] Restock: Stolen items will not be restocked, even in Greed Mode. [end edition note] 

• Sack Head: If Mr. ME! successfully stole a consumable from the shop, there is a chance he will drop a sack instead.

• Glitched Crown/Binge Eater/Tainted Isaac/Soul of Isaac/Everything Jar: Stealing a cycling item pedestal will give you whichever item is currently present when Mr. ME! picks up the item, making it risky to steal items this way, and entirely unreliable with Glitched Crown

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mr. ME! is based on this Steam Workshop item by Jean-Alphonse, originally known as Mr. Meeseeks.

• Mr. ME! is a reference to Mr. Meeseeks from Rick and Morty, which spawn from a box and stop existing after completing their given task.

• The pickup quote also refers to a catchphrase used by Mr. Meeseeks.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If used while shooting with Marked, the crosshair will continue straight in the first direction Isaac shot at, and cannot be controlled until Marked is deactivated.
Bug note: Mr. ME! is able to damage Mom's doors even when no body part is sticking out of them, Mom's Heart and It Lives! while they're withdrawn, and Isaac and Hornfel while they're off-screen. He never loses them as a valid target, eventually killing the boss.

fields.description: Summons a controllable ghost that can perform various tasks depending on what it targets.

Mr. Maw.title: Mr. Maw
Mr. Maw.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Mr. Maw walks towards Isaac and when in range it will launch its head towards him. It appears to be a Maw attached to a Gusher and will turn into either upon death depending on the killed body segment. It can also randomly separate at will into a Gusher and a Maw.

sections.heading: Mr. Red Maw
sections.text: Mr. Red Maw behaves similarly to Mr. Maw, but moves quicker and has a Red Maw as its head instead of a regular Maw. If the Red Maw segment is killed first, it will release four shots in the cardinal directions like a regular Red Maw. It can also occasionally separate at will.

sections.heading: Mr. Mine
sections.text:
Mr. Mines are chained to pits and will attempt to launch themselves at Isaac if he comes near. They will occasionally burrow and pop up in another pit, often near Isaac. Upon death, they fire six shots in all directions.

[Before Repentance] Since pits have a chance to replace rocks in the Flooded Caves where Mr. Mine resides, this can give them more tiles to utilize.

sections.heading: Swinger
sections.text:
Swingers behave differently to its variants as rather than firing its head, the Swinger's head is constantly detached and spins around its base clockwise in a fixed radius, while slowly sliding towards Isaac. The cord connecting the head and body of a Swinger isn't solid and does not deal damage. If the base is killed, the spinning head turns into a Maw, and if the head is killed, the base turns into a Globin in its goo form which then can reform into a Globin.

When entering a room, their heads will be retracted and slowly rotate outwards until they reach max length. [Afterbirth+ onward] Since Booster Pack #5, Swingers extend their heads at a much slower pace, making it easier to avoid damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mr. Mine and Mr. Red Maw were added in Booster Pack #5.

• Though the Maw appears to have eyes when attached to the Globin, if the Maw survives and spawns upon the Swinger's death, then it will have empty eye sockets.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Mr. Maw makes Gaper noises while chasing Isaac, while Mr. Red Maw makes the Maw noise only if the Red Maw segment dies first.

• Mr. Mine is based on the enemy Crunch from The End is Nigh.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using the D10 on any monster with several pieces will reroll every piece into a monster. For the case of Mr. Maw, his cord dots are considered as pieces, and each will turn into a new monster.
Bug note: If a Swinger's neck touches a red poop, the neck sometimes disappears while the Swinger keeps swinging.
