Little Horn (Item).title: Little Horn (Item)
Little Horn (Item).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the boss; Little Horn]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Adds a chance to fire piercing tears which will instantly kill any non-boss enemy.

• [Repentance] Adds a chance to fire a tear that summons Big Horn's hand. It will grab and crush any non-boss enemy, killing them instantly, and attacks bosses 3 times for 12 damage each hit (even Big Horn himself).

• If the tear kills an enemy, it will be feared for a moment before being crushed.

• Running into enemies deals 3.5 damage to them.

• Damage is dealt up to twice per second per enemy.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Little Horn or Big Horn. [end edition note] 

• The chance to fire special tears depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: min(\frac1 { 20 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor}, 20\%)

• At base luck (0), the chance is 5%, maxing out at 20% at 15 luck.

• The special tears will kill some normally invulnerable monsters, such as Death's Heads, Stoney, and Peep's floating eyeballs.

• [Before Repentance] The special tears can also destroy Blue Fire Places and Purple Fire Places.

• The special tears can destroy the various spiked blocks (Wall Hugger, Slide, and Poky) as well as the variants of Stone Grimace. All of these won't respawn if Isaac leaves and re-enters the room.

• [Before Repentance] The contact damage effect overrides the superior contact damage from Aries, The Gamekid, My Little Unicorn / VII - The Chariot, and The Nail. Only Midas' Touch still works and deals an additional 3.5 damage.

• [Repentance] The contact damage adds to other contact damage sources.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Angelic Prism: Little Horn tears can be split by the prism and will be quadrupled when they pass through it.

• [Repentance] Brimstone/Mom's Knife: Each damage tick may trigger Little Horn's effect.

• Evil Eye: Eyes can fire Little Horn tears. Little Horn tears won't destroy other eyes.

• Jacob's Ladder: Enemies hit by Jacob's Ladder's arcs produced by a Little Horn tear will be hit by Big Horn's hand.

• Kidney Stone: The stone can have the Little Horn effect.

• Soy Milk: Due to its high tear rate, the effect will trigger very often, even with average luck stats.

• Saturnus: Little Horn tears can orbit around Isaac upon entering a room.

• [Repentance] Tech.5/Technology/Tech X: Occasionally fires a Little Horn laser beam.

• [Repentance] Technology 2: The laser can also trigger Little Horn’s effect with the laser’s chance to apply the effect being determined rapidly every tick.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Brimstone/Mom's Knife/Technology/Tech X: Overrides Little Horn’s tear effects.

• [Before Repentance] Dr. Fetus / Epic Fetus: Overrides Little Horn’s tear effects.

• [Repentance] Black-tinted bombs can summon Big Horn's hand to instantly kill non-boss enemies or to deal damage against bosses.

• Lachryphagy: If Little Horn tears are fed, they will burst into split tears with the same effect. If Little Horn tears feed normal tears, however, the effect is lost.

• [Before Repentance] Tech.5/Technology 2: The laser is unaffected by Little Horn.

• Technology Zero: Electricity connected to Little Horn tears will not instantly kill enemies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item might be a reference to Cutaneous horns, unusual keratinous skin tumors with the appearance of horns.

• Little Horn was originally an unofficial item which was supposed to showcase the modding capabilities of Afterbirth+ in the PAX 2016 livestream. However, all items included in the demo were later added to the final game.

• [Repentance] Little Horn's description is a reference to George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four.

• This may imply that the boss Little Horn is the younger brother of Big Horn.

• Little Horn is a reference to the Antichrist in the book of Daniel.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The item's effect cannot be triggered on Mobile Hosts while they walk.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Science!; Repentance: Big brother is watching]
fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Adds a chance to fire a piercing tear that instantly kills any enemy that it touches.
[Repentance] Adds a chance to fire a tear that summons Big Horn's hand to crush the first enemy it hits, instantly killing monsters or greatly damaging bosses.

Little Steven.title: Little Steven
Little Steven.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the familiar item; the boss; Steven; the stat upgrading item; Steven (Item)]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Little Steven having [edition alternatives: baseline: 5th; Repentance+: 7th] priority.

sections.heading: Synergies

sections.heading: Trivia

• In the original Binding of Isaac, Little Steven could only be dropped by Steven, 80% of the time.

Locust of War.title: Locust of War
Locust of War.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Upon entering a room with enemies for the first time, spawns a Red Locust which detonates upon impact with enemies, dealing double tear damage for the impact of the Locust and 60 damage for the explosion.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This trinket has a 1% chance to drop when defeating War. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Explosive locusts have a larger aggro range than all other locusts. They will target an enemy from further away.

• [Before Repentance] This trinket can be dangerous to hold, as the locust will instantly target the nearest enemy as Isaac enters the room, which can be close enough to catch Isaac in its blast radius.

• [Repentance] The explosion from the locust is very small, on scale of a single tile, but can still hurt Isaac.

• The Locust will also spawn each time a wave starts in Boss Rush and [Repentance+] [mode: greed; greedier] Greed Mode.

• The explosion takes most bomb effects from items that Isaac has, with some exceptions.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy will spawn one more locust.

• Bomber Boy: Additional smaller explosions will spawn in a tight cross formation.

• Brimstone Bombs: The locust explosions fires thinner beams, dealing 4.8 damage per tick.

• Glitter Bombs: Locust explosions have a chance to spawn pickups or trinkets.

• Hive Mind: The locusts’ impact damage is doubled and the explosion damage is increased to 85.

• Sad Bombs: A ring of 10 tears is shot outward upon detonation, which are affected by Isaac's tear modifiers, and deal damage equal to 15 + 0.6x, where x is Isaac's Damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bomber Boy: The explosion damage is halved to 30 without additional explosions.

• Ghost Bombs: No ghost is spawned.

• Glitter Bombs: Pickups and trinkets will not spawn from locust explosions.

• Mr. Mega: No additional explosion damage or radius.

• Scatter Bombs: Mini bombs are not spawned.

• Sticky Bombs: No spiders are spawned on enemy death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Before Booster Pack #3, Locust of War was named Locust of Wrath. Unlike other Locusts, the name of Locust of Wrath was from one of seven Deadly Sins instead of four Harbingers. This is why the Steam achievement still reads as such.

fields.name: Locust of War
fields.description: Upon entering a room with enemies for the first time, spawns a Red Locust which detonates upon impact with enemies.

Lodestone.title: Lodestone
Lodestone.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac the chance to fire tears that magnetize enemies they hit, giving them properties similar to tears fired by Isaac when he has Strange Attractor:

• Enemies and pickups that are near magnetized enemies are pulled towards them. This includes live Bombs.

• All tears/enemy shots (from Isaac, his familiars, and all enemies, including the magnetized one) will be strongly pulled towards magnetized enemies.

• • Enemy shots that get pulled in will now also damage enemies other than the ones that fired them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The chance to fire magnetizing tears depends on the luck stat. The activation rate is equal to 1/(6 - Luck). At 0 luck, the chance is 16.67%, maxing out at 100% at 5 luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues: The wisps' tears are attracted to the magnetic enemy, making it much easier to connect all of the wisps' tears on an enemy.

• E. Coli: If an enemy is hit by a lodestone tear perfectly simultaneously with it being turned into poop, the resulting poop will be tinted black and have a lodestone aura that sucks in enemies. This poop will return to normal after a few seconds.

• Pop!: Magnetizing an enemy causes all active eyeball tears to rush to the enemy.

• Rotten Tomato: Enemies affected by Lodestone and Rotten Tomato will be quickly swarmed and killed by other enemies.

• Tech X: Changes the color of rings to gray. They still apply the magnetized effect, but the effect being applied is random for each enemy damaged with the same ring. Has increased chance of magnetizing enemy.

• Tech X + Dr. Fetus: Only the explosions from Dr. Fetus' bombs can magnetize enemies.

• The Ludovico Technique: Isaac's tear has a chance to magnetize and stick to enemies or bosses, making it impossible to move the tear until the enemy dies or until the magnetization effect somehow doesn't get reapplied long enough for the effect to end.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone: Changes the beam to gray, can still apply the magnetized effect. The beams are not attracted to enemies with the magnetized effect.

• Technology: Changes the laser to gray, can still apply the magnetized effect. The lasers are not attracted to enemies with the magnetized effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Lodestone is from the Antibirth mod where it would require 10 Luck to have a 100% chance of activating.

• When used on Dogma or its TV, the respective sprites will get fuzzier, as if the boss/TV is having signal errors.

• A lodestone is a naturally magnetized piece of mineral magnetite.

fields.description: Gives Isaac the chance to fire tears that magnetize enemies they hit, causing them to attract nearby pickups and enemies, as well as tears/shots from all sources.

Loki.title: Loki
Loki.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[distinguish: Lokii] 

Loki is a boss that can appear in all environments of Chapter 3 (Depths, Necropolis, Dank Depths).

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Loki teleports to random locations in the room away from Isaac and has the following attacks:

• Shoots 4 projectiles in the four cardinal directions, followed by the four diagonal directions, and then the cardinal directions once again.

• Spawns a Boom Fly on top of himself. A maximum of 4 Boom Flies can be alive at once.

• Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.
Loki deals a whole heart of contact damage.

A Poky can accompany Loki during the fight, dealing contact damage and blocking Isaac's tears.

[Repentance] Loki can also be accompanied by 4 Stone Grimaces in the corners of the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Using the Meat Cleaver on Loki has a unique interaction, splitting him into Lokii.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Loki appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• Loki has smaller eyes and different horns in his boss portrait.

• The Poky in the room does not damage Loki's Boom Flies as it did in the original game.

• Loki's "mark" (The numbers 666 on his forehead) is more noticeable than his appearance in the original game.

• Lokii is the posthumous version of him.

• Loki is based on the Norse trickster god of the same name.

• Edmund McMillen loved Loki's design so much that he made Little Horn.

• The Horny Boys are a stitched amalgamation of Loki and Hornfel.

• Loki and Hornfel are brothers.

Loki's Horns.title: Loki's Horns
Loki's Horns.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Adds a chance to shoot tears in four cardinal directions, similar to Loki.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Loki. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] The chance to shoot extra tears depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 8 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 12.5%, maxing out at 100% at 7 luck.

• [Repentance] The chance to shoot extra tears depends on the luck stat and is based on this formula: 25\% + (5\% * \mathit{Luck})

• This means that the chance starts at 25% at 0 luck, minimizes at 0% at -5 luck, and maximizes at 100% at 15 luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Mom's Eye: Each time Mom's Eye would activate, Loki's Horns activates instead. If Mom's Eye fails to activate, Loki's Horns' activation rate is still checked for afterwards.

• Eye of the Occult: Extra tears will fire in the same direction.

• Sprinkler: The sprinkler eye turns into four eyes and alternates shots between the cardinal and ordinal directions.

• Technology 2: All additional tears are affected by the item but are replaced with Technology's lasers, effectively dealing 100% of Isaac's damage, and with 16 luck uses 100% of Technology 2's fire rate.

• Tiny Planet: Effectively grants a great tear multiplier, as on item activation the extra tears will follow the trajectory given by the Tiny Planet.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 20/20/The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider: No effect on the tears fired in the other 3 directions. The chance to activate is checked per shot, not for each tear fired.

• Dr. Fetus: Not recommended without immunity. Adds a chance to fire four bombs in cardinal directions.

• Epic Fetus: Adds a chance to spawn four crosshairs in cardinal directions. Isaac controls one and the others will mirror the movement keeping their space.

• Incubus: Not affected by Loki's Horns.

• Ipecac: Adds a chance to fire four explosive shots in cardinal directions. Caution is advised, though it is easier to avoid damage than Dr. Fetus.

• The Ludovico Technique: Adds a chance for 4 piercing + spectral tears to be fired in cardinal directions from the main tear. This chance scales with luck and goes up to 100% at 20 Luck.

• Mom's Knife: Adds four knifes on the cardinal directions around Isaac that can be rotated but all of them will be thrown when four tears would shoot with only Loki's Horns.

• Monstro's Lung: Only one red tear will be fired in the other directions.

• [Repentance] Fires 14 tears in each of the four directions.

• Tech X: Overridden by Tech X.

• [Repentance] The laser rings will only fire forwards and backwards, with 2 stacked on top of each other in both directions, shooting at an angle will shoot the stacked rings at different angles.

• Tractor Beam: Extra tears are not affected by Tractor Beam.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is used in Glass Cannon.

sections.heading: References
sections.text: • The Binding of Isaac Item Trigger Testing

fields.description: Gives a random chance for projectiles to fire in all 4 cardinal directions.

Lokii.title: Lokii
Lokii.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[distinguish: Loki] 

Lokii is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In the Womb and the Utero.

• [Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb). [end edition note] 
Each half of Lokii has 350 HP.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The fight against Lokii resembles fighting two individual Lokis. Each half of Lokii teleports to random locations in the room and has the same attacks which they perform independently of each other:

• Shoots 4 projectiles in the four cardinal directions, followed by the four diagonal directions, and then the cardinal directions once again.

• Spawns a Red Boom Fly on top of himself. Only 1 Red Boom Fly can be alive at once.

• Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.
Lokii deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Loki's Horns, Glass Cannon]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Using the Meat Cleaver on Loki has a unique interaction, splitting him into Lokii.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Lokii was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• They are the posthumous version of Loki.

• Lokii's name is a pun on the Roman numeral for two, II.

• It can also be a reference to the Latin plural suffix "ii" such as in "radii" and "virii" which is not commonly used.

• Lokii's battle sprite is depicted with no arms despite Lokii's sprite in-game having arms. Additionally, the boss's art is missing Lokii's mark on their foreheads.

• Both Lokii halves have the same sprite, just flipped horizontally.

• The only actual difference with Loki is that Lokii spawns Red Boom Flies instead of normal ones.

• Because of this, since Red Boom flies don't explode upon death, Isaac cannot damage Lokii by killing them.

• Lokii's design may be inspired by the Judgement of Solomon, a story from the Hebrew Bible in which King Solomon ruled between two women both claiming to be the mother of a child. King Solomon suggested that the baby should be cut in two, so the women will receive the two halves.

Lost Contact.title: Lost Contact
Lost Contact.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac's tears a shield surrounding them, allowing the player to block enemy shots.

• Isaac's shots are destroyed upon contact with an enemy's shot.

• [Afterbirth only] Affects familiar's tears.

• -0.15 shot speed.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Anti-Gravity: Placing many tears around Isaac creates a safe zone, especially with larger tears.

• Brimstone/Maw Of The Void/Technology/Technology 2: Beam/ring/laser destroys projectiles, although only during its damage tick interval. The projectiles are not instantly destroyed when they touch the beam/ring/laser.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: Split tears will be shielded. The Parasite's split tears will not appear to have shields.

• Eye of Belial: Piercing through a projectile will trigger Eye of Belial's double damage and homing effect. Belial tears will still block shots.

• [Repentance] The Forgotten: Enemy shots may be reflected with melee attacks. The damage of the reflected shots depends on their size and properties, with standard enemy shots dealing 6 damage, champion and homing shots dealing 7 and explosive ones dealing 50.

• Jacob's Ladder: Destroyed tears via shot-blocking will trigger the electric arc effect.

• The Ludovico Technique: Can block an infinite amount of enemy shots if the tear is placed on top of a monster. The projectiles that they attempt to shoot will be immediately destroyed.

• [Before Repentance] Mom's Knife: The knife will destroy projectiles in its path without being affected.

• [Repentance] The knife does not destroy projectiles.

• Piercing tears: The tears can pass through multiple enemy projectiles. This means that one tear can hurt the enemy and block its projectiles.

• Polyphemus: Enemy shots are treated like enemies with 10 health, which are deducted from the Polyphemus tear. If it has strength remaining afterward, it will continue.

• Sinus Infection/Mucormycosis: Tears that stick to enemies will block shots, and will not be destroyed in the process.

• Soy Milk: The constant stream of tears will cut through any complex attack patterns with ease.

• Spirit Sword: Sword swings reflect projectiles.

• Almond Milk: The random tear effects can allow more shots to be blocked, as effects such as Ouroboros Worm, My Reflection, and Tiny Planet can cause tears to wander outside of the main stream of tears. However, this, in combination with the lower fire rate of Almond Milk compared to Soy Milk, makes Almond Milk slightly less effective than Soy Milk at blocking shots in the direction Isaac is shooting.

• Tech X: The rings block enemy shots.

• [Repentance] The rings sometimes block enemy shots. [more testing/debugging required]

• Trisagion: Beams will block shots and continue on.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Dr. Fetus: Bombs will not destroy or block shots. Stat effects apply.

• Epic Fetus: Missiles will not destroy or block shots. Stat effects apply.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Fire Mind: Lost Contact will remove the chance to explode on impact effect.

• God's Flesh: Tears with the shrink effect do not appear to be shielded, but will still block enemy shots.

• Godhead: Auras will not block shots but tears will.

• Haemolacria: Main tears will block shots but burst tears cannot.

• Ipecac: Ipecac shot will explode upon contact with an enemy's shot.

• Lachryphagy: Tears often block shots before they can burst; however, burst tears can also block shots.

• Kidney Stone: The stone will not block shots.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Mysterious Liquid: Overridden by Lost Contact.

• Rubber Cement: Tears will bounce off of enemy tears and destroy them.

• Tough Love: Teeth will not appear to be shielded but will still block enemy shots.

fields.description: Isaac's tears can hit and destroy enemy projectiles. -0.15 shot speed.

Lost Cork.title: Lost Cork
Lost Cork.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Increases the radius of all creep produced by Isaac, his familiars, and friendly enemies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Lost Cork: Each copy further increases creep size. However, having 4+ copies will reset creep to its default size.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Sticky Bombs: No effect on the creep size from the bomb.

• Blood Bombs: No effect on the creep size from the bomb.

fields.name: Lost Cork
fields.description: Increases the radius of any creep produced by Isaac.

Lost Fly.title: Lost Fly
Lost Fly.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a fly familiar that moves in a straight line and attaches itself to the first wall or obstacle it comes into contact within each room.

• The Lost Fly will then move around the room functionally similar to the Guts.

• [Before Repentance] If any enemies walk into its path, it will deal 7 contact damage per tick or 105 damage per second.

• [Repentance] Lost Fly deals 7 contact damage every 7 ticks, or 30 damage per second. Enemies near Lost Fly will target it instead of Isaac.

• Some enemies that do not normally give chase to Isaac, such as Mulligans, will chase after the Lost Fly if nearby it.

• If the obstacle it is attached to is destroyed, then it will continue rolling in the direction it was previously traveling until it meets another wall or obstacle.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The fly will glow slightly in [curse: Darkness] , making its position always visible.

• The name of the item is likely a reference to the maze-solving algorithm called the left-hand rule, which is based on walking forward and turning left as far as possible until you find an exit to the maze.

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Before Afterbirth+: Afterbirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth+]
fields.description: Spawns a fly familiar that moves in a straight line and circles around the first wall or obstacle it hits. [Before Repentance] It deals 105 damage per second on contact. [Repentance] It deals 56 damage per second and forces nearby enemies to attack it.

Eye of Belial.title: Eye of Belial
Eye of Belial.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1.5 range.

• [Before Repentance] +1.0 tear falling speed.

• Grants piercing tears.

• After piercing one enemy, tears will gain double damage, homing, and a 1.3x size multiplier.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] The piercing effect makes placed Bombs, Troll Bombs, and Mega Troll Bombs unable to be pushed around by Isaac's tears.

• Tears will also gain homing and double damage when they pierce bombs and entities the game considers enemies, like Stone Grimaces and Fire Places.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: Tears that pass through enemies will become Belial tears and split into smaller Belial tears. Non-Belial split tears can also turn into Belial tears if they pass through enemies.

• C Section: Fetuses will continue to deal damage per tick after gaining the effect, almost doubling total damage output.

• Godhead: Normal tears and Eye of Belial tears will retain damaging aura.

• Lachryphagy: Eye of Belial tears can still be fed and will burst, and burst Eye of Belial tears will still be homing. Tears from regular bursts can also turn into Eye of Belial tears.

• Lost Contact: Piercing through a projectile triggers the double damage and homing effect.

• Remote Detonator: Placed Bombs won't explode automatically, so they can be placed and have tears fired through them to activate double damage and homing.

• [Repentance] Tiny Planet: After piercing an enemy, tears will continue orbiting rather than homing, but each tear can gain multiple damage and size multipliers. These tears can make quick work of even most bosses.

• [Repentance] Saturnus: When an orbiting tear hits an enemy, it will turn into an Eye of Belial tear. From that point, the tear gets out of Saturnus' orbit every time an enemy is nearby, becomes autonomous and chases every enemy in the room. It won't be destroyed by enemies anymore. When there's no enemy close from it, it comes back into the orbit. As all 7 tears can become Eye of Belial ones, this synergy is significantly powerful. [end edition note] 

• Technology Zero: All tears will be connected with electricity. Electricity will double in damage when the tears change.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
Overrides Eye of Belial:

• Brimstone

• Epic Fetus

• Ipecac

• Mom's Knife

• Technology

• Tech X

• Trisagion

• The Forgotten
Other interactions:

• Diplopia: Only further increases range.

• Dr. Fetus: Piercing effect applies, but homing and doubled damage do not.

• [Repentance] Bombs also deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.

• Haemolacria: If the main tear pierces an enemy, it will turn into a Belial tear, and the burst tears retain the piercing effect and do double damage. If the main tear does not turn into a Belial tear, the burst tears will not be able to turn into Belial tears.

• The Ludovico Technique: Doubled damage does not apply if hitting the same enemy multiple times in a row. The controlled tear will continue to increase in size on every hit up to roughly the width of a single room, and the effect resets on changing rooms.

• Ouija Board: Eye of Belial tears lose their homing ability and fly offscreen.

• Pop!: Homing tears will only damage the enemy once and then just remain fixed above the target for a brief amount of time until disappearing.

• Technology 2/Tech.5: The lasers are not affected by the Eye of Belial; however, the tears apply the effect normally.

• Tractor Beam: May seem to override Eye of Belial but if a homing tear finds a target to seek it will stop midair as if it were fighting its momentum.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Belial is a term from the Hebrew Bible referring to the devil.

fields.description: Grants piercing tears. After piercing one enemy, tears start homing and deal double damage.

Eye of Greed.title: Eye of Greed
Eye of Greed.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a golden tear every 20 tears fired, which causes enemies to turn gold and petrifies them for a few seconds (similar to Midas' Touch) at the cost of one Penny. Golden tears can still be fired if Isaac has no money.

• Unlike other tear effects, golden tears are fired alongside regular tears rather than replacing a regular tear.

• With multi-shot abilities, whichever tear is the 20th since previous will produce the additional golden tear.

• [Before Repentance] The golden tear does 2x normal damage.

• [Repentance] If Isaac has no money, the golden tear does normal tear damage. If Isaac does have money, the golden tear deals 1.5x normal damage +10.

• [Before Repentance] Enemies killed while golden will drop 1-4 coins.

• [Repentance] Enemies killed while golden will drop 1-3 coins.

• [Repentance] If Isaac has money, golden tears that hit enemies will drop a Penny, effectively returning the cost.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tears fired from items that cause multiple tears to be fired at once, e.g. 20/20, Monstro's Lung, etc., are counted separately.

• The gold tear is not duplicated by said items.

• The Forgotten has separate tear counters for The Forgotten and Soul.

• [Repentance] Using this item is an easy way of unlocking Golden Razor after obtaining 99 coins, since it drains them by just shooting and with enough patience it will reduce their count to 0. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Hitting ArmoredTuff Twins or The Shell will turn them into gold, and all armored segments will drop 1-3 coins. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Chocolate Milk: How much the 20th tear was charged determines the size and damage of the golden tear.

• Compound Fracture / Cricket's Body / The Parasite: Golden tears will still look like coins and will still split into other golden coins when hitting obstacles.

• Equality!: The coin lost when firing the tear can be quite useful for equalizing the pickup counter.

• Humbleing Bundle: Affects coins dropped from hitting enemies, allowing Isaac to potentially farm money.

• Lachryphagy: Golden tears can also be fed and will burst into split tears. Burst tears are not golden.

• Piercing tears: The golden tear will petrify all enemies it hits, [Repentance] and will drop a penny for each one.

• Trisagion: Golden tears become blast that constantly drop Pennies on hit.

• Urn of Souls: Golden tears still shoot as normal while using the urn.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Petrified enemies that are turned into pickups don’t also drop coins from the petrification effect.

• [Before Repentance] Brimstone: Overrides Eye of Greed.

• [Repentance] Occasionally fires a coin tear with the beam.

• [Before Repentance] Dr. Fetus: Overrides Eye of Greed.

• [Repentance] A coin shot is fired every 20 shots, but it's very likely to hit the bomb. This makes Eye of Greed drain money over time for no benefit, unless piercing is gained.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Petrified enemies that are turned to poop don't drop coins.

• [Before Repentance] Epic Fetus: Overrides Eye of Greed.

• [Repentance] Occasionally fires a coin tear in the direction of the cross similarly to Marked.

• Fate's Reward: Does not shoot coin tears.

• [Before Repentance] Flat Stone: No effect.

• [Repentance] Freeze Effects: Petrified enemies that are frozen don’t drop coins.

• [Before Repentance] Incubus: Does not shoot coin tears.

• [Repentance] Incubus will fire coin tears in tandem with Isaac. His shot counter is independent of Isaac's. Coin tears still subtract from Isaac's pennies.

• [Before Repentance] Lost Contact: No effect.

• [Before Repentance] The Ludovico Technique: Overrides Eye of Greed.

• [Repentance] Isaac occasionally fires a coin tear towards the controlled tear.

• [Before Repentance] Mom's Knife: Overrides Eye of Greed.

• [Repentance] Occasionally fires a coin tear in addition to the knife.

• [Before Repentance] Technology/Tech X: Overrides Eye of Greed.

• Twisted Pair: The two familiars will also fire coin tears which spend Isaac's coins. Their shot counter are independent from Isaac's.

fields.description: Every 20 tears, Isaac loses 1 Penny and shoots an additional gold tear that petrifies enemies and turns them into gold. Any enemy killed while in this state will drop coins.

Eye of the Occult.title: Eye of the Occult
Eye of the Occult.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Firing in a direction causes all of Isaac's tears to move in that direction. Tears will stay in place if a fire button is not being pressed.

• The flight duration of tears is determined by the range stat.

• +1 damage.

• +2.0 range.

• -0.16 shot speed.

• Contributes to the Leviathan transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Adversary. [end edition note] 

• Items which use charge mechanics (like Chocolate Milk, Cursed Eye or Monstro's Lung) require precise input to be able to both charge the shot and then move the tears, making it significantly harder to control.

• Beams and lasers like Brimstone are unaffected by this.

• This item replaces Isaac's regular white aura with a dimmer purple one which lowers visibility in [curse: darkness] .

• MouseControl=1 enabled via the options.ini file does not allow the player to control the tears by mouse. Synergies which add a crosshair, however, will allow the tears to be controlled by mouse normally. (Further detail on valid synergies below)

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Synergies which cause auto-fire can have the firing stopped by pressing the "drop" key or button. Pressing Fire will resume auto-firing.

• Anti-Gravity + Proptosis: Tears travel and keep their initial size as long as the fire key is held, allowing for massive damage.

• Bob's Rotten Head: Isaac can control the mid-flight direction of the head, however its air-time is not increased.

• Brimstone/Technology: The laser becomes dark purple and automatically fires at a controllable crosshair. The crosshair behaves nearly identically to the one created by Marked (including in its synergies and interactions with other items), but the laser itself always fires in the cardinal directions and bends toward the crosshair rather than directly targeting it.

• Azazel: Like Brimstone, except that his short beam becomes a lasso. The loop starts where the beam would normally end and extends out to the cross-hair.

• Brimstone/Technology + Chocolate Milk: The closer the crosshair is to Isaac, the less charged the laser will be, and vice versa.

• Brimstone/Technology + Incubus/Twisted Pair: The familiars fire a straight laser towards the crosshair.

• Brimstone/Technology + Marked/Analog Stick: The laser more closely follows the crosshair's position relative to Isaac. In Brimstone's case, moving the crosshair while the laser is firing makes the laser bend toward it rather than changing the firing angle of the laser itself.

• Brimstone/Technology + Montezuma's Revenge: The brown beam has a similar interaction as Azazel's beam but cannot create the crosshair on its own. Corn shots are unaffected.

• Brimstone/Technology + Revelation/Tech.5/Technology 2: The Revelation, Tech.5, and Technology 2 lasers are also affected by the crosshair but cannot create the crosshair on their own.

• Cain's Other Eye/Sprinkler: The familiar's and sprinkler's tears travel a very short distance in their original direction and can be controlled afterwards.

• Conjoined/Eye Sore/Loki's Horns/Mom's Eye/The Wiz: Extra tears fly in the same direction making it easier to hit every shot increasing damage substantially.

• Isaac's Tears/Tammy's Head/Tear Detonator/Varicose Veins: Generates a halo of tears that don't break their shape.

• The Ludovico Technique: While holding a direction, the Ludovico tear will constantly shoot out controllable tears in random directions. The air time of these tears scales with the range stat.

• Marked: Turns the Marked crosshair purple. Tears target the crosshair's exact position. Upon reaching it, tears follow and hover on top of the crosshair for their remaining airtime.

• Technology: The laser becomes dark purple and automatically fires at a controllable crosshair. The crosshair behaves nearly identically to the one created by Marked (including in its synergies and interactions with other items) with the exception that lasers often arch towards the crosshair rather than traveling towards it directly and any other projectiles affected by Eye of the Occult that are not lasers (such as from Eye of Greed or Fate's Reward) will chase the crosshair and hover above it for the remainder of their range.

• Technology Zero: Static beams persist between tears while moving.

• Trisagion: The Trisagion beams will fire in the direction of cross-hair and after the fire button is released they stay in place until they fade away.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Anti-Gravity: Overridden by Eye of the Occult. Tears up still applies.

• Brain Worm: Tears will veer slightly towards enemies when travelling by, but will quickly return to player control.

• Brimstone + Twisted Pair: Twisted pair will only fire brimstone when the crosshair is moved.

• Brimstone + Taurus: When Taurus' effect triggers, Isaac will be unable to move the crosshair, but he'll keep firing the Brimstone laser at wherever the crosshair remained before Taurus triggered, effectively circumventing Taurus' penalty of being unable to fire during the invincibility period.

• Chocolate Milk: Not Recommended. Releasing the key to fire tears will stop the tear's movement, making it difficult to shoot enemies.

• C Section/Epic Fetus/Mom's Knife: Overrides Eye of the Occult, stat effects still apply.

• Cursed Eye: The tears stack on top of each other, and only move forward when holding a direction afterwards.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs will now be controlled both in direction and range.

• Evil Eye: Eyes cannot be controlled, but the tears they shoot can be.

• Homing Tears: Tears still home towards enemies, but controlled movement is stronger than the homing effect.

• Immaculate Heart: Extra tears are not affected by Eye of the Occult. Stat changes still apply.

• The Ludovico Technique + Technology: Overrides Eye of the Occult, stat effects still apply.

• My Reflection: Causes the pull to be lessened while actively controlling the tears. Pull returns to normal when not firing.

• Pop!: When being actively moved, tears can stay in the air until the fire button is let go.

• Saturnus: Extra tears are only affected by Eye of the Occult when holding fire while moving between rooms causing some of the orbiting tears' spacing and shot speed to be uneven. Stat changes still apply.

• Sprinkler: Sprinkler's tears travel a very short distance in their original direction and can be controlled afterwards.

• Tech X: Overrides Eye of the Occult; however, the shot speed down is still beneficial for Tech X.

• Tiny Planet: Not Recommended. The tears will stop moving when not shooting in the direction of their orbit, making it nearly impossible to control where they go.

• Tractor Beam: Tears will only move forward while being fired, but control is otherwise overridden.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Eye Of The Occult originates from the Antibirth mod.

• This item's name and visual design originate from a Reddit post on the Binding of Isaac subreddit.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: After the first Brimstone shot, the Twisted Pair familiars will be unable to fire until Isaac moves the crosshair and even then they will often only fire once or not at all. Chocolate Milk fixes this.

fields.quote: DMG up + range up + controlled tears
fields.description: +1 damage, +2 range, -0.16 shot speed. Isaac's tears can be controlled mid-flight with tear controls.

Faceless.title: Faceless
Faceless.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Faceless is a monster added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. It takes on the appearance of a Gaper with most of its head cut off, but with its entire spine still intact. Initially, it wanders around the room aimlessly, occasionally firing out 6 blood shots in a hexagonal shape. Once it takes damage or if Isaac gets close to it, it starts to chase him and fires shots much more frequently. Upon death, it may turn into a Pacer or Gusher but more often the latter.

sections.heading: Tainted Faceless
sections.text:
The Tainted Faceless appears to be a Fatty version of the Faceless, with its lower jaw including teeth still intact.

The Tainted Faceless walks towards Isaac while rapidly releasing volleys of 6 blood shots in a hexagonal shape. It essentially behaves like the Faceless with higher health and faster attack rate.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Faceless originate from the Antibirth mod.

Faded Polaroid.title: Faded Polaroid
Faded Polaroid.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Occasionally causes Isaac to blend into the ground, which briefly confuses all enemies in the room.

• Effect can only trigger every 10 seconds on the timer.

• [Repentance] Can be used to open A Strange Door instead of The Polaroid or The Negative, destroying the trinket in the process. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Confusion is only applied when Isaac begins fading into the background. Any enemy that spawns while Isaac is already faded won't be confused until Isaac fades in, then out again.

• [Repentance] Faded Polaroid has the highest priority to open the Strange Door, and will always be taken first if Isaac is holding multiple items that open it. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Faded Polaroid cannot open the Strange Door if it was consumed by "Gulp!" pill, Marbles, or Smelter. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Faded Polaroid: Each trinket copy stacks, lengthening the duration of the confusion and visual effect per stack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance] Faded Polaroid being used to open the Strange Door is a nod to a mechanic in the original Binding of Isaac: Wrath of The Lamb flash game, where The Polaroid was a trinket in that game and was required to access the Chest after beating Cathedral.

fields.description: Occasionally causes Isaac to blend into the ground, which briefly confuses all enemies in the room. [Repentance] Can be used to open the Strange Door in The Depths. [end edition note]

False PHD.title: False PHD
False PHD.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Identifies all pills upon pickup.

• Spawns a pill.

• Grants one Black Heart on pickup.

• Converts all good pills into their bad counterparts.

• Grants +0.6 damage for each stat down pill and +1.2 damage for each stat down horse pill Isaac has taken, including those taken before acquiring False PHD.

• Using a non-stat down bad pill drops a Black Heart.

| Pill | Changes Into 
| Stat up pill | Stat down pill

| Bad Gas & Friends Till the End! | Health Down

| I can see forever! & Lemon Party | Amnesia

| Explosive Diarrhea & One makes you larger | Range Down

| Bombs are Key & Infested! | Tears Down

| 48 Hour Energy & One makes you small | Speed Down

| Pretty Fly & Infested? | Luck Down

| Balls of Steel, Full Health, & Hematemesis | Bad Trip

| Pheromones | Paralysis

| Telepills | ???

| I'm Drowsy... | I'm Excited!!!

| Percs! | Addicted!

| Feels Like I'm Walking on Sunshine! | Retro Vision

| Power Pill! | R U A Wizard?

| Something's wrong... | X-Lax

| Gulp! & Vurp! | Horf!

| Experimental Pill | Only grants a stat down

| Gold Pill | Only has negative effects

| Neutral pills

| I Found Pills

| Puberty

| Re-Lax

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Bad Trip and Health Down pills will turn into I Found Pills when Isaac is at one heart.

• Neutral pills will not have a secondary effect.

• Telepills will be converted to ??? even if the latter has not yet been unlocked.

• Gulp! and Vurp! will be converted to Horf! even if the latter has not yet been unlocked.

• Pills are only converted while held by a character with False PHD. For example: If playing as Jacob and Esau and Jacob has this item, pills that got converted into 'bad' pills like a Tears Down pill can be given to Esau to convert them back into whatever the pill was originally.

• Losing the item by either dropping it as Tainted Isaac or re-rolling it via D4, etc., causes the damage buffs given to be removed.

• With Little Baggy and False PHD, the Marked Skull in Depths II will drop a ??? pill, making it much harder to open A Strange Door that run.

• This item can be crafted from Bag of Crafting with seven pills and one Black Heart.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Pony/White Pony: Effectively converts all Speed Down pills into Damage Up as long as one of the ponies are being held, since they will always give a minimum of 1.5 speed.

• Black Feather: Counts as an evil item, granting a damage up.

• Lucky Foot / PHD / Virgo: Pills can now be both good and bad again. The other effects of False PHD still apply when taking bad pills.

• Getting multiple of the pill-upgrading items has no effect, bad pills can still appear.

• The Wafer: Using a Bad Trip pill will only deal half a heart of damage and spawn a full Black Heart, resulting in a net gain of health.

• The Wafer + Placebo: Allows for farming infinite health using Bad Trip pills.

• Rock Bottom: Prevents stat-decreasing pills from decreasing your current stats. They still have an effect in the background, making it more difficult to raise that stat in the future.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Libra: The balancing of stats mostly leads to a net decrease between Stat Downs and +0.6 damage up, while Luck Down provides +0.6 damage and -1 luck.

fields.description: Converts good pills into bad pills and identifies all pills. Bad pills now have secondary positive effects. Grants one Black Heart.

Famine.title: Famine
Famine.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Famine is a Harbinger that can appear in all environments of Chapter 1 (Basement, Cellar, Burning Basement).

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
• If Isaac is to the left or right of Famine, he charges horizontally across the screen. He continues this charge off-screen and reappears from the opposite end of the screen.

• Spawns a Pooter with a limit of 2.

• If this limit is reached Famine will move to try to position himself horizontally of Isaac so he can charge at him.

• Any Pooters caught in Famine's charge will be killed.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
When Famine takes a sufficient amount of damage, his body and horse explode and vanish while only his head remains.

• Famine's head behaves similarly to a Maw, slowly moving towards Isaac, and occasionally stops to fire three projectiles in a spread at Isaac.
Famine deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases and during his charge.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 7] : Charges more often and veers towards Isaac (similar to the Dark One). He can do this attack regardless of whether Isaac is to his sides or not. He will shoot six bullets in all directions instead of summoning Pooters. In Phase 2, he will spit out a cluster of bullets instead of a triple shot, similar to Monstro's attack, with a lower shot speed than his non-champion version. Will always drop a Soul Heart upon death.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Revelations, 7 Seals]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Famine appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• Famine is one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse mentioned in the Bible. However, in the Bible, Famine is depicted as riding a black horse rather than the tan horse seen in-game.

• A famine is the scarcity of food over a large area, which can explain Famine's emaciated appearance.

• Famine is shown with pupils in his Rebirth artwork, which is absent in his original artwork. This is slightly averted with his ultra form.

• The Pooters Famine spawns may be a reference to the many insect-caused famines.

• [Repentance] Blue Champion Famine's cleft lip is a reference to Monstro's iconic cleft lip, as he uses a similar projectile cluster attack to Monstro in his second phase.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If phase 2 of Famine is inflicted with fear or confusion, instead of running away from Isaac, it will chase him without attacking.
Bug note: If Famine is stunned at the same time as he tries to shoot Isaac after the effect wears off, his shots will be fired without his corresponding animation.

Fanny Pack.title: Fanny Pack
Fanny Pack.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Grants a 50% chance to drop a random Penny, Bomb, Key, or Red Heart whenever Isaac takes damage.

• The chances of the drops between each category are roughly equal.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Fanny Pack: Having multiples of Fanny Pack neither increases the amount of drops, nor the drop chance.

• Blood Oath: Each half-heart lost has a chance of spawning a pickup from the fanny pack.

• Scapular: Allows for infinite pickups once Isaac is at half a red heart (or full red heart in Chapter 4 onward) by moving between rooms to reset Scapular's effect.

• Placenta: Similar to Scapular, allows for unlimited pickups provided a disregard for time.

• Sharp Plug: Each half a heart lost from the use of sharp plug has a chance of spawning a picking from the fanny pack.

• Spindown Dice + Greed Mode: Turns into Humbleing Bundle when rerolled by Spindown Dice (which is not normally obtainable in Greed Mode) and this allows penny drops from each wave a chance of turning into double pennies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Fanny packs are purses that can be strapped to the stomach, usually carried by mailmen, couriers, tourists etc.

fields.description: Has a chance to drop a random pickup when Isaac takes damage.

Farting Baby.title: Farting Baby
Farting Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and blocks enemy projectiles. Upon blocking a shot, it has a 25% chance of farting. Farting has a cooldown of 210 frames. There are three possible fart effects:

• Charms all nearby enemies.

• Poisons all nearby enemies.

• Knocks back nearby enemies [Repentance] and hostile tears.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Conjoined transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Farting Baby does no contact damage.

• The knockback fart deals no damage.

• [Repentance] The reflected tears deal 6 damage if they would've hurt Isaac for half a heart, and 7 for a full heart.

• The charm fart deals 5 damage.

• The poison fart initially deals 5 damage and the poison deals 3.5.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Farting Baby having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • BFFS!: No effect on damage or blocking radius; only the visual size is changed.

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Before Afterbirth+: Afterbirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth+]
fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac and blocks enemy shots. If a shot hits Farting Baby, it has a chance to fart, which charms, poisons, or knocks back nearby enemies.

Fast Bombs.title: Fast Bombs
Fast Bombs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +7 Bombs.

• Removes the delay between bomb placements, allowing them to be placed rapidly.

• [Repentance] Fast Bombs inflict no knockback on Isaac's bombs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Holding the bomb button will not automatically place them. Each bomb needs to be manually placed.

• On [plat: PC] , it's possible to bind two buttons to lay bombs and use both for even higher rates of bombing.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Remote Detonator: Since bombs can be placed rapidly, this can be used to do lots of damage at once to a boss or enemy.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Bob's Rotten Head: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Unlike other "bomb modifying" items, Fast Bombs grants 7 bombs, instead of 5.

fields.description: +7 Bombs. Removes the delay between bomb placements, allowing them to be placed rapidly. [Repentance] Bombs will no longer knock each other away.

Fate.title: Fate
Fate.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants flight and one Eternal Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Taking this item as Keeper will grant Blue Flies instead of the Eternal Heart.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Fate's name, sprite and presence in the Locked Chest pool are an implication to Isaac's ultimate fate: to lock himself in the chest and become ???. This is likely why Fate was left in the Locked Chest pool even after head-themed items were removed from the pool.

• Isaac's winged form when he picks up Fate is similar in many aspects to the winged forms of both his boss incarnation and that of ???.

• In Wrath of the Lamb, this item was unlocked by default.

fields.description: Grants flight and one Eternal Heart.

Fate's Reward.title: Fate's Reward
Fate's Reward.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that fires tears with the same damage and tear effects as Isaac's tears.

• Fires at half the normal fire rate of a familiar.

• Since the normal fire rate of familiars (such as Little Steven, Robo-Baby or Seraphim) is [Before Repentance] once per second / [Repentance] 1.36 times a second, Fate's Reward shoots [Before Repentance] once every 2 seconds / [Repentance] 0.68 times a second.

• The familiar is not affected by [Before Repentance] range/ [Repentance] tear height; only tear falling speed.

• [Repentance] Since increasing tear height and shot speed lowers tear falling speed in order to adjust Isaac's range, increases to either stat will decrease the familiar's range, and decreases to either stat will increase the familiar's range.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Fate's Reward having [Before Repentance+] 5th / [Repentance+] 7th priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Flat Stone: Familiar's tears will travel very far and then bounce once, traveling up and hitting the nearest wall.

• Haemolacria: Will fire tears that burst into split tears. Does not affect fire rate.

• Ipecac: Will fire explosive tears. Does not affect fire rate.

• Lachryphagy + Brimstone: The tears fired by the familiar will eventually explode in a star-like pattern of Brimstone lasers if they don't hit anything.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Following tear modifiers do not affect Fate's Reward, and the familiar will only fire normal tears:

• Brimstone

• C Section

• Dr. Fetus

• Epic Fetus

• The Ludovico Technique

• Mom's Knife

• Monstro's Lung

• Technology

• Tech X

• 20/20 / The Inner Eye / Mutant Spider: Fate's Reward only fires single tears. The items do not affect the fire rate of Fate's Reward.

• Chocolate Milk: Familiar's tears will turn a brown color but can not be charged.

• [Before Repentance] Marked: Fate's Reward will only fire while the crosshair is being moved, and can only fire in cardinal directions.

• [Repentance] Fate's Reward will aim and fire at the crosshair, wherever it's pointed.

• Soy Milk / Almond Milk / Polyphemus: Does not affect fire rate, but does affect damage.

fields.description: A blue head familiar that will follow Isaac and fire tears copying his tear effects and damage.

Filigree Feather.title: Filigree Feather
Filigree Feather.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Angels drop items from the Angel Room item pool instead of key pieces when defeated.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Items are dropped even if both key pieces are already acquired.

• [Repentance] If one key piece was acquired before picking up Filigree Feather, the next time the angel that normally drops the key piece Isaac currently has is defeated, it will drop the other key piece even with Filigree Feather equipped. (E.g. defeating Uriel while holding Key Piece 1 and Filigree Feather will drop Key Piece 2, but defeating Gabriel with the same items will drop an angel item instead.)

• • [Repentance+] Key Piece drops are prioritized. 

• • 
• For example, after fighting Angels for the first time they will drop Key Pieces. If both pieces are picked up, next time Angels will drop items upon defeat.

• • 
• If only one Key Piece is picked up, an Angel defeated in the next room will drop another Key Piece, and the next Angel in the same room will drop an item. If a remaining Key Piece is not picked up again, an Angel fought in a third room will drop the missing Key Piece again.

• [Before Repentance] If both Angels are fought at the same time, only the last one defeated will drop an item.

• Isaac can drop the Filigree Feather, fight the Angel, then grab the trinket again if a Key Piece is desired.

• Only Angels that would otherwise drop a Key Piece will drop an item. This means that those who spawn during the Mega Satan fight, Boss Rush or those rarely found in closets in the Cathedral do not drop items, but ones found in some Super Secret Rooms and those summoned from Sacrifice Rooms do.

• Considering that Sacrifice Rooms always spawn 2 Angels, and Isaac can get 1 Angel deal each floor, Filigree Feather can potentially generate a ludicrous 3 Angel items per floor.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Defeated angels drop a Half Soul Heart in addition to whatever else they drop.

• Meat Cleaver: Each angel gives an item.

• [Repentance+] Only one item will drop.

• The Stairway: Allows for an extra Angel in the Angel Shop every floor.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Jacob and Esau: Jacob must be the one holding Filigree Feather for the trinket to work properly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Filigree is a type of ornamental art made of carefully shaped thin strips of metal, typically silver.

fields.description: Angels drop Angel Room items instead of key pieces when defeated.

Finger!.title: Finger!
Finger!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Spawns a floating finger familiar that can be aimed with the fire buttons in all directions.

• The finger fires invisible spectral lasers, doing 10% of Isaac's Damage. The lasers fire 10 times per second and are not affected by Isaac's tear rate.

• The lasers have thickness based on Isaac's Damage, making it easier to inflict damage on higher Damage.

• While not being aimed with the fire buttons, the finger points in the direction of movement or downwards if standing still.

• [Before Repentance] The Finger!'s lasers can apply Isaac's Tear effects, which makes status effects trigger very often.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Finger! will fire in the exact direction it's pointed, meaning it can be fired diagonally, or at any angle, if using a controller - the same effect as Analog Stick.

• The beam can be used to destroy TNT (among other destructible obstacles).

• The Finger! does not do contact damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Doubles the finger's damage, but does not affect its lasers' thickness.

• Box of Friends: Adds another finger on top of the previous one, effectively doubling its damage.

• Finger!: Multiple fingers will stack on top of each other and move simultaneously, effectively boosting the damage of the original one.

• Having too many fingers can cause the game to lag.

• Spirit Sword: When doing a spin attack, the familiar will spin with the sword.

• Guppy: Flies are generated from the damage the finger does.

• Ipecac: The finger gains massive damage boost as expected.

• [Before Repentance] The finger can poison enemies.

• Proptosis:

• [Before Repentance] Almost doubles the finger's damage as expected. Has no damage penalty with range.

• [Repentance] Triples the finger's damage, but does not affect its lasers' thickness. Has no penalty with range.

• Sulfuric Acid / Terra: The finger has a chance to destroy rocks when pointing at them.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Godhead: Only increases damage.

• Terra: Causes the finger to constantly destroy obstacles in its line of sight.

• Homing tears: The finger's lasers do not become homing.

• A Lump of Coal: No effect on the finger's damage.

• Marked: While actively aiming, the finger behaves as normal and while fire keys are not pressed, it points towards the targeting crosshair.

• Trinity Shield: When not firing, the finger will point towards the nearest cardinal direction as to where the shield is left. This favors the vertical directions when the shield is at a 45° angle.

• Trisagion: No effect on the finger's damage.

• Angelic Prism: No effect on the finger's fire.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is a reference to Fingered!, one of Edmund's games.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The floating finger familiar is not reflected properly on Chapter 1.5 or other rooms that have water.

fields.description: Spawns a finger familiar that faces in the same direction as Isaac, rapidly damaging enemies it points at for 10% of Isaac's damage.

Finger Bone.title: Finger Bone
Finger Bone.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants a [Before Repentance] 2% / [Repentance] 4% chance to gain a Bone Heart upon taking damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy adds 4% more chance to gain a bone heart upon taking damage.

fields.description: Grants a chance to gain a Bone Heart upon taking damage.

Fire Mind.title: Fire Mind
Fire Mind.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Tears inflict burn to enemies.

• Tears have a chance to explode on impact with an enemy, leaving behind a fire.

• Explosions do Isaac's current tear damage, in addition to the tear's hit.

• [Before Repentance] The fires deal 22 damage per tick.

• [Repentance] Each fire deals up to 4 ticks of damage: 1st tick deals 23 damage, 2nd tick 17.3 damage, and 3rd and 4th tick 11.5 damage.

• • [Repentance] Fires can block projectiles, up to 4 times, each time getting smaller.

• • 
• Isaac cannot take damage from the flame, but can still take damage from the explosion.

• [Afterbirth onward] Isaac gives a wide glow lighting up dark areas, such as those under the effects of the [cu: Darkness] or the Dark One's attacks.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The explosion effect chance depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 10 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.7 \right \rfloor}

• At base Luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 100% at 12.86 Luck.

• [Before Repentance] An exploding tear does not set either the hit enemy or anything in the blast range on fire.

• [Repentance] All enemies hit by the explosion will be set on fire.

• Explosive and burning damage is equal to Isaac's current damage stat.

• The flame will transform certain enemies into their fire-related versions (e. g. Hoppers into Flaming Hoppers).

• Tears can explode upon hitting Bombs of any kind.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Fire Mind it turns into a burning locust that sets enemies on fire but does not explode.

• Bob's Rotten Head: Creates fire when the head lands.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/Haemolacria/The Parasite: Each fractal tear has its own chance to explode. However, if the main tear explodes, all fractal tears explode.

• [Rebirth only] Death's Touch: Adds burn damage to the scythes, but will not cause explosions.

• Dr. Fetus: All Dr. Fetus bombs will leave a flame behind after exploding, similar to the effect of Hot Bombs.

• Epic Fetus: The missile will leave behind a fire.

• Explosivo: Explosivo tears leave a flame behind after exploding.

• Finger!: Finger familiar can set enemies on fire but won't cause explosions.

• Host Hat/Pyromaniac: Makes Isaac immune to explosions caused by flaming tears.

• Ipecac: Every time the tear explodes, it will leave a fire.

• Jacob's Ladder: Sparks can set enemies on fire but won't explode.

• Lost Contact: Tears can explode when they destroy an enemy's tear.

• Piercing tears: Tears will pierce enemies and retain the chance to self-destruct each time it hits an enemy.

• [Repentance] Tears will pierce enemies without exploding, then self-destruct when they hit a wall or fall to the ground.

• [Repentance] Soy Milk: Explosions are smaller (similar to those of Scatter Bombs) and do not reach Isaac as easily.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone: Adds burn damage to the beam, but will not cause explosions.

• The Forgotten: Club turns orange and burns enemies, but doesn't cause explosions.

• The Lost /Tainted Lost: Since you'll likely have Perfection, Fire Mind is an awful item to obtain due to the explosion being based on luck.

• The Ludovico Technique: Tears retain the ability to ignite enemies and explode. Tears will respawn at Isaac's location after the explosion.

• Mom's Knife: Overrides the explosion chance, but the knife can still set enemies on fire.

• Mysterious Liquid: Overrides the explosion chance, but tears can still set enemies on fire.

• [Afterbirth onward] When the Fire Mind tear explodes, a much larger pool of creep is left behind.

• Sinus Infection: Tears will still stick to enemies, but lose the booger appearance. The booger tears will not constantly burn the enemy they are stuck to.

• Technology/Technology 2/Tech.5/Tech X/Technology Zero: Adds burn damage to the beam, but will not cause explosions.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Trisagion: Beams can burn enemies, but won't cause explosions. [end edition note] 

• Rubber Cement: Causes tears that bounce off of enemies after exploding to also explode when the tear lands.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Fires spawned by Angelic Prism will damage Isaac.

fields.description: Grants flaming tears that deal burning damage over time. Tears have a chance to explode on impact with an enemy, which creates a fire at the location of the explosion.

Fish Head.title: Fish Head
Fish Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Spawns 1-2 blue flies every time Isaac takes damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Spawns 2-4 blue flies on hit. Having both increases to 3-6 blue flies per hit.

fields.description: Spawns a Blue Fly every time Isaac takes damage.

Fish Tail.title: Fish Tail
Fish Tail.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Many items and trinkets that generate Blue Flies or Locusts will generate twice as many.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Flies may spawn on top of each other, appearing as a single fly initially.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
Blue Fly / Locust sources that are doubled:

Other notable interactions:

• Compost: Isaac will gain twice as many flies per use, meaning each fly will be tripled.

• Beelzebub: Blue flies generated will be doubled, but charmed flies will not be doubled.

• Rotten Baby: Will spit two flies at a time with one being a copy. Will only spawn more flies when the original fly is destroyed.

• Parasitoid: The duplicated flies will spawn on top of the enemy and deal damage immediately.

• Tainted ??? / IBS: Blue flies created by corny poops will be duplicated when spawned in, but not when the poop is broken.

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper: Blue Flies created from hearts will be doubled.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: If you have either, when blue files are spawned, 20% chance to triple the number spawned.

• [Repentance+] If you have both, 20% chance to quadruple the number spawned.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 7 Seals: No effect.

• Cricket Leg: No effect.

• Soul of Apollyon: No effect.

• Abyss: No effect.

fields.description: Items and trinkets that generate Blue Flies or Locusts will generate twice as many.

Fissure.title: Fissure
Fissure.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Fissure is a monster exclusive to Downpour, resembling a fish wearing a skull on its head. Fissures do not need to be defeated to clear the room, and rather act as a stage hazard, spawning endlessly by jumping out of pits and bouncing off walls until they land in a pit again. They can be damaged normally, despite their vague resemblance to Hosts. If a fissure goes too long without re-entering a pit, it dies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Fissure is based off of the monster of the same name from The End is Nigh.

• Fissure shares its name with a cut enemy in Repentance, Fissure, which appeared in Antibirth.

fields.name: Fissure
fields.environment: Downpour /
fields.behavior: Jumps out of pits and bounces around the room. Spawns endlessly from pits until room clear. Do not need to be killed to clear room.

Exorcist.title: Exorcist
Exorcist.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Exorcists are enemies found exclusively in the fight against The Heretic, and can never be found naturally. They take the appearance of a Gaper with its head's skin rolled down, revealing its skull.

If spawned by itself, it will start to walk towards Isaac, occasionally spawning a single Lil' Haunt. It will try to follow the most recently spawned Lil' Haunt and use it to shield itself, and it will only spawn another Lil' Haunt once the previous one has been killed. It will also run away from Isaac once its designated Lil Haunt has been killed prior to spawning another.

After an enemy dies, it will leave behind a small red spirit, sometimes, an Exorcist will walk over to one of the red spirits and revive it as a Lil' Haunt, similar to Rag Man or a Cultist. These red spirits are the same ones created by Vade Retro and can be blown up as such. All red spirits will disappear once an exorcist dies unless holding Vade Retro.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The only method to kill the shielded Exorcists in The Heretic's fight is with Chaos Card, Little Horn, Euthanasia, or Suplex! as they go through shields.

sections.heading: Fanatic
sections.text:
The Fanatic is a variant of Exorcists, encountered only at the start of the fight with The Heretic.

At the beginning a group of 5 Exorcists are seen on the edges of a large purple pentagram on the floor, chanting and kneeling towards the center as The Heretic emerges. They are shielded until after The Heretic is fully summoned, after which they transform into Fanatics (which appear to be Exorcists with the skull replaced by a purple flame) and begin behave similarly to Faceless, chasing Isaac while occasionally shooting two purple, rotating tears as it does so, like a Ragling.

Upon death, they have a chance to turn into Pacers or Gushers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Exorcists are from the Antibirth mod where they were a common enemy in Mausoleum.

• They could also spawn Wizoobs and Candlers in conjunction with Lil' Haunts.
