AAA Battery.title: AAA Battery
AAA Battery.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • If an activated item would regain its second to last charge upon clearing a room, it is instead fully charged. This effectively reduces its charge time by one bar.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Does not affect items with only one bar of charge or those with automatic recharge.

• Recharging an item by taking damage with Habit, the instant charge given by 9 Volt, or any source of charge other than clearing a room, will not activate the trinket's effect.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Items require one charge unit fewer to get fully charged. [Repentance] This effect stacks up to 3 fewer charges.

• 9 Volt: If active item requires three or more charges, trinket gives an extra charge, effectively utilizing itself with 9 Volt.

• Jacob's Ladder / 120 Volt: Increases the amount of arcs a spark can generate.

• Schoolbag: The trinket activates based on the primary item slot, but it grants an extra point of charge to the second item as well.

• The Battery: If an active item would have at least one level of charge upon clearing a room, an extra point of charge is granted by the trinket.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 4.5 Volt: AAA Battery has no effect after picking up 4.5 Volt.

• Watch Battery: Watch Battery triggering after clearing a room will also trigger AAA Battery, provided the activated item was missing exactly 3 charges prior to clearing the room.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: AAA Battery will not contribute to unlocking Jumper Cables despite having the item tag.

fields.description: Automatically recharges the last energy slot of an activated item, effectively reducing recharge rates by one.

A Missing Page.title: A Missing Page
A Missing Page.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When damaged, grants a chance to activate The Necronomicon effect, dealing 40 damage to enemies in the room.

• [Repentance] Adds +40 damage to The Necronomicon and similar effects, such as Black Hearts. This also includes its own effect.

• Contributes to the Necromancer transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The activation chance depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \min(\frac1 { 20 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.3 \right \rfloor},50\%)

• At base Luck (0), the chance is 5%, maxing out at 50% at 60 Luck.

• If multiple copies of the trinket are obtained, they wont count as a Necromancer's items.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Blood Rights / Dry Baby / The Negative / Heartbreak / XIII - Death / Black Rune: The damage boost is applied to these items. [end edition note] 

• Golden Trinket/Mom's Box/Missing Page 2: Each copy grants +40 damage to The Necronomicon and similar effects.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Necronomicon, A Missing Page, and Missing Page 2 are all references to the Necronomicon and its missing pages appearing in Evil Dead.

• Which, in turn, is a reference to The Necronomicon, a fictional grimoire appearing in the works of horror writer H.P. Lovecraft.

• [Repentance+] This is one of the only three trinkets that count toward a transformation, the other ones are Kid's Drawing and Bob's Bladder.

fields.description: 5% chance to induce The Necronomicon's effect upon taking damage. [Repentance] Adds +40 damage to Black Hearts and The Necromonicon-like effects.

A Pony.title: A Pony
A Pony.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Passively gives flight whether it has charges or not.

• If Isaac's speed is less than 1.5, passively increases his speed to 1.5.

• Upon use, Isaac charges in the direction the pony is facing, giving invincibility during the charge and dealing contact damage to enemies.

• [Before Repentance] The dash deals 40 flat contact damage to enemies.

• Invincibility granted by dashing will not prevent Isaac from being damaged by Blood Donation Machines, Devil Beggars, and similar self-damage active items (when holding Schoolbag).

• [Repentance] The dash deals 4 times Isaac's damage, plus a flat 28 damage.

• [Repentance] Isaac can dash through doors, which means that damage from Curse Room doors can be avoided.

• • The dash persists through rooms, and lasts up to the length of 2 normal rooms unless Isaac collides with a closed door/wall.

• • 
• This allows Isaac to enter and exit curse rooms for free, provided the dash is activated to give invincibility before charging through the exit.

• • 
• Caution should be taken when dashing into rooms that have not been explored, as some room layouts have Blood Donation Machines or Devil Beggars, which Isaac may dash into and get damaged.

• • 
• This is more important to The Lost and Tainted Lost, as Holy Mantle or Holy Card can not prevent damage from them. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• A Pony is only obtainable as a boss drop from Headless Horseman, as a starting item for Eden, by using Spindown Dice on Bomb Bag, or by using Death Certificate.

• The flight and potential speed added by A Pony will be removed if a new activated item is collected.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If Void is used, Isaac will not be granted permanent flight. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring, looking like "A Pony". The wisps charge in the direction Isaac shoots instead of firing tears. While charging, the wisps deal contact damage equal to 40% of Isaac's damage per tick (120% of Isaac's damage per second) and are immune to damage. Wisps must wait 2.5 seconds after hitting a wall before they can charge again. The wisps deal their normal contact damage while not charging.

• Mars: Using A Pony after dashing lowers the dash cooldown to approximately 1 second.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Taurus / Thunder Thighs: The speed decreases from the items can lower Isaac's speed past 1.50 (making the new lower speed limits 1.20 and 1.10, respectively). Having both items can lower the minimum speed to 0.80.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item appears to be a stick horse.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, A Pony's contact damage was weaker and the charge was slower.

fields.description: Passively grants flight and increases speed to 1.5. Upon use, Isaac charges in the direction the pony is facing, giving invulnerability during the charge and dealing damage to enemies hit.

A Pound of Flesh.title: A Pound of Flesh
A Pound of Flesh.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Devil deals and Black Market items can now be paid with Penny.

• Anything that generates Devil Deals (such as Satanic Bible or the special chests in Dark Room) will also create items that cost coins.

• Items in Shops now cost health.

• Consumables in shops have no cost, but are surrounded with Spikes and can't be pushed out with an explosion.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Buying shop items for health does not prevent Angel Rooms from appearing.

• Taking a health consumable surrounded by spikes at a single heart or less will still result in Isaac's death.

• Immunity to spikes or invulnerability of any kind (e.g. via The Gamekid) does not prevent damage when taking consumables in shops.

• Shop consumables cannot be taken during invincibility frames, e.g. from taking another consumable.

• The Lost can take the consumables, without losing his Holy Mantle.

• When transformed into The Lost in Downpour/Dross II with the White Fire Place, shop consumables can be taken for free even without Holy Mantle.

• The item is not available to Keeper and Tainted Keeper normally. If acquired through Spindown Dice, Death Certificate or such, it has no effect.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Binge Eater: All shops become free stat-ups if the food item is chosen.

• Restock: The price never increases, staying at one red heart container/three soul hearts for each item, and one full heart of damage for pickups.

• However, Restock's coin cost increase mechanic is still present, and if Pound of Flesh is lost, the items will have their equivalent coin cost displayed.

• With Binge Eater, this can result in infinite stat gains.

• If a Heart is on sale, Isaac can trigger items that activate upon taking damage indefinitely.

• If a Lil' Battery is on sale, Isaac can buy items indefinitely with certain active items such as Blank Card with XI - Strength or Book of Revelations with Car Battery.

• When transformed into a ghost in Downpour II or as Tainted Jacob, or playing asThe Lost, Isaac can buy items indefinitely.

• Maggy's Bow: Buying a Red Heart will out-heal the damage taken from the spikes if Isaac can survive it.

• The Wafer / Cancer / Percs!: The spikes only deal half a heart damage, allowing Isaac to gain health from buying hearts.

• With Restock, any character except Bethany can buy items indefinitely if a Soul Heart is on sale.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Chaos: Items in Devil Rooms that would otherwise cost two heart containers will only cost one if found in Shops.

• Flat File: No effect. Spikes generated surrounding consumables will not be removed.

• Holy Mantle / Holy Card / Wooden Cross / Blanket / Dogma: Unless Isaac is The Lost, the spikes around consumables will simply break the shield without letting him take them.

• Isaac's Heart: Consumables can no longer be picked up in shops.

• Judas' Tongue: Ensures that items in the Member Card secret shop only cost one heart container, but Devil Deal prices are not reduced, and other shop items already only cost one heart container.

• Keeper's Box: Items and pickups generated outside Devil Rooms will cost health, but items generated inside Devil Rooms will cost coins.

• Keeper's Sack: Because shop items no longer cost coins, stat bonuses are no longer gained from buying shop items, but they are gained from Devil Deals.

• The Lost: Only one item can be picked up from each shop; any other items will vanish. Consumables can be taken for free.

• However, multiple items can be bought from Devil Deals.

• Items will not disappear when taking any consumable.

• With Restock, the Lost can buy items indefinitely.

• Member Card: Items in the secret shop can cost two heart containers.

• Redemption: Doesn't change the conditions to lose or keep the cross even when spending health in shops.

• The Stairway: Affects Angel Shops the same way it does regular shops.

• Steam Sale: Devil Deals will have their price reduced. Shop items will cost the same amount of health.

• Store Credit: Store Credit becomes a useless trinket, as neither Devil Deals nor shop items will become free.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The name of this item is a reference to Shakespeare's play The Merchant of Venice, where the Jewish moneylender Shylock asks the bankrupt Antonio for 'a pound of flesh' in payment for his debt.

• The name of this item matches the description of the Potato Peeler, which also references the play.

• This is the only item with the nokeeper item tag.

fields.description: Devil deals now cost Penny, Shop items now cost health, and consumables in shops are free but surrounded by spikes.

A Quarter.title: A Quarter
A Quarter.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Gives Isaac 25 Penny.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The item has a chance to drop when destroying urns or killing Super Greed.

• [Before Repentance] Super Greed can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. 

• Will not spawn from Urns once picked up.

• Rerolling this item with the  D4,  D100 , Missing No., or a 1 or 6 pip Dice Room will not remove 25 coins.

• [Repentance] Its Quality value is treated as 1 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] When the Shop item pool is depleted, it is possible to find The Quarter for sale in the store for 15 cents. This can also occur in the I AM ERROR room.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, A Quarter was unlocked by beating Mom's Heart four times instead of eight.

• It was also present in the Devil Room item pool in the original game and in the “Antibirth” mod.

• • [Repentance] It is now part of the Devil Room item pool again.

fields.description: Gives Isaac 25 Pennys.

A Snack.title: A Snack
A Snack.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Grants one full Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Binge Eater: When Isaac picks up A Snack it now grants: a permanent +0.2 Shot Speed, +1.0 Luck, -0.03 Speed and a temporary +3.6 Damage (which diminishes to 0 in 30 seconds).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A Snack was the final item added in Rebirth.

• A Snack appears to be a dog treat.

fields.description: Grants one full Red Heart container. [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

Abaddon.title: Abaddon
Abaddon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1.5 damage.

• +0.2 speed

• [Before Repentance] Also affects maximum speed (may never exceed 2.0).

• [Before Repentance] Removes all current Red Heart containers and grants 6 Black Hearts.

• [Repentance] Converts all current Red Heart containers into Black Hearts, and adds 2 additional Black Hearts.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Empties all Bone Hearts without removing them.

• Adds a chance to shoot fear tears.

• Contributes to the Leviathan transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Fear tear effect depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac{15}{100 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor}

• At base Luck (0), the chance is 15%, maxing out at 100% at 85 Luck.

• Dark Matter is significantly better at inflicting fear than Abaddon.

• Does not remove Soul Hearts or Eternal Hearts.

• [Before Repentance] As it removes all Red Heart Containers, other Deals with the Devil can be taken for "free" as long as Abaddon is taken last while still having at least 1 Container.

• Can always be taken as a deal. Even if Isaac only has one or two Soul Hearts, the Black Hearts will be granted after taking the item.

• [Repentance] Emptied Bone Hearts will not be converted to Black Hearts.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Black Feather: Grants a damage boost.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bethany: Leaves her with half a Red Heart with her other Heart Containers removed.

• Greed's Gullet: If heart containers are being granted, removes them as well as 25 cents.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Keeper: Instantly kills him when picked up. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Keeper/Tainted Keeper: Sets Coin Hearts to 1 on pickup. [end edition note] 

• Mom's Perfume: The chance to inflict fear does not stack.

• Tainted Bethany: Does not remove stored Red Hearts nor converts them into Black Hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the Hebrew Bible, the name Abaddon is used as a reference to a bottomless pit, often appearing alongside the place of the dead (which is known as Sheol), meaning the land of the dead. The actual Hebrew word Abaddon (אבדון - pronounced avadon) means "doom".

• Abaddon is the Hebrew equivalent of Apollyon.

• In the New Testament's Book of Revelation, an angel called Abaddon is written as the king of an army of locusts; his name is first transcribed in Greek (Revelation 9:11 – "whose name in Hebrew Abaddon").

• Abaddon also shares its name with a level from Edmund's previous game Super Meat Boy.

• [Repentance] Lil Abaddon resembles this item's costume and shares a similar name, but its effects are closer to Maw Of The Void. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: [Before Afterbirth+] If Keeper picks up Abaddon, it will remove all of his Coin Hearts but will not kill him until he picks up an item.
[Afterbirth+ before Repentance] This still applies if Abaddon is acquired via the Debug Console, but not if the item is picked up normally.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] +1.5 damage, +0.2 speed. Removes all Red Heart containers, grants six Black Hearts, and adds a chance to shoot fear tears.
[Repentance] +1.5 damage, +0.2 speed. Grants two Black Hearts, converts all Red Heart Containers into Black Hearts, and adds a chance to shoot fear tears.

Abel.title: Abel
Abel.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that mirrors Isaac's movements and shoots tears that deal 3.5 damage.

• Abel shoots once per [edition alternatives: baseline: second; Repentance: half-second] .

• [Rebirth only] Abel shoots tears in the opposite direction of Isaac.

• [Afterbirth onward] Abel shoots tears towards Isaac regardless of which direction Isaac is shooting.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Conjoined transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Although it is difficult to hit enemies with Abel, he can be useful in certain situations. Doples and Evil Twins can be easily taken care of without risk of damage using Abel. Abel can also assist in killing slow or stationary monsters that happen to be around the center of the room.

• In symmetrical room layouts Abel can be used to clear away destructible obstacles such as fire places and poops.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Cain / Tainted Cain: Abel's tears are red and deal 7.5 damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• According to the Bible, Abel was one of Adam and Eve's children and was the first human to ever be murdered. He was an opposite to his murderous brother Cain, which may explain the mirrored nature of this item. Also, this item is unlocked by defeating The Lamb with Cain, which makes the connection with the Bible more obvious.

• This item was originally unlocked in Wrath of the Lamb by defeating Isaac as Cain.

fields.description:
[Rebirth only] Spawns a familiar that mirrors Isaac's movements and shoots in the opposite direction.
[Afterbirth onward] Spawns a familiar that mirrors Isaac's movements and shoots towards him. [end edition note]

Abyss.title: Abyss
Abyss.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• On use, destroys all items on item pedestals in the room and gives a unique red locust familiar for each item destroyed.

• These locusts are permanent once created, up to a maximum of 64, after which creating more will replace older locusts.

• This limit is shared with Blue Flies and Spiders.

• The locusts loosely orbit Isaac similarly to regular Blue Flies, charging in the direction Isaac is firing until hitting an enemy, wall, or certain obstacles like key blocks.

• [Before Repentance+] Locusts deal Isaac's damage unless they are a special locust (2-3 times per hit).

• [Repentance+] The damage locusts deal is a multiplier of Isaac's damage and dependent on the quality of the item destroyed (2-3 times per hit):

• Quality 0: 0.5x damage.

• Quality 1: 0.75x damage.

• Quality 2: 1x damage.

• Quality 3: 1.5x damage.

• Quality 4: 2x damage.

• The locusts may gain additional effects depending on the item destroyed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tainted Apollyon starts with this item in the consumable slot.

• [Repentance+] Effects from some special locusts have the following consistent properties:

• Explosions are smaller and deal 20 damage.

• Electricity deals 25% of Isaac's damage per tick. It also does not deal damage to the enemy hit, but arcs to other nearby enemies, similar to 120 Volt

• Crack the Sky beams deal 3x the locust's damage per tick.

• Small poison farts deal 5 damage and poison all enemies caught in it.

• Regular large farts don’t deal damage, but push away other nearby enemies.

• All creep function identically to that from Mysterious Liquid regardless of color.

• Locusts which destroy enemy projectiles will still trigger their effect and block shots while orbiting around Isaac.

• The Necronomicon effect deals 40 damage. This can be affected by the damage increase from A Missing Page or Missing Page 2.

• The Brimstone vortex and subsequent laser each deal 75% of Isaac's damage per tick.

• The Maw Of The Void effect deals Isaac's damage per tick.

• Locusts that destroy rocks can also open regular doors as well as Secret Room entrances.

• Using Abyss in the Shop or the Devil Room will not affect any items that have not been purchased.

• In rooms where there are multiple items to choose from, using Abyss will give only one locust for each item choice/set.

• If already at the maximum amount of locusts and presented with multiple non-choice item pedestals, using Abyss will only consume half of the pedestals.

• If Abyss is used while Isaac is holding an item above his head, it can still consume the item and grant a locust.

• This mechanic can be used to destroy bought items, unwanted blind items as well as familiars given by Soul of Lilith.

• Using Abyss to destroy items in Boss Rush or Challenge Room counts as taking an item and causes waves of bosses or enemies to start spawning.

• Locusts granted by Abyss are not taken away during the sequence to obtain the Knife Piece 2. Mother's Shadow cannot be harmed, but they can help destroy Fire Places blocking the path faster.

• Locusts granted by Abyss are nearly irremovable, only Genesis can completely remove all locusts from a character. Sacrificial Altar and exceeding the familiar limit can remove some locusts. Reroll effects such as D4, Tainted Eden taking damage, Missing No., etc. cannot remove locusts.

• [Repentance+] Locusts that have a chance to explode can extinguish Blue Fire Places.

• In Repentance Co-Op if a player dies, any of the special locusts they have will persist, following and attacking from their ghost.

• Using Abyss will destroy the pedestal and the ghostly item from Flip is not obtainable.

• Passive items can still be consumed while Isacc is holding them above his head without destroying the ghostly item, active items can only be consumed this way while having an empty hand with Schoolbag.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS! / Hive Mind: Increases the locusts' size and damage by 25%.

• These two items don't stack.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring in the form of black-glowing flies with extra HP that do not fire tears.

• Extension Cord: Electricity will flow between Isaac and the locusts.

• Guppy : Damage dealt by locusts can spawn blue flies.

• Tainted Eden: Abyss can be rerolled, but the locusts are permanent.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Baby-Bender / Box of Friends: Does not affect locusts.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Death Certificate: Only allows the consumption of one item per Death Certificate room and the consumed item is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.

• Genesis: The locusts created by Abyss are removed without creating items to replace them.

• Sacrificial Altar: Locusts can be sacrificed for items.

• Void: If Void consumes Abyss, the latter will take priority and using Void to consume another item pedestal will generate a locust. Even consuming active items will generate a locust, and Void will not copy that active item's effect. This essentially causes Void to act identically to Abyss, [Before Repentance+] albeit requiring 2 more charges per use. Stats and effects of the active items absorbed prior to consuming Abyss are kept and will trigger everytime Void will be used.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The way that Abyss works is similar to how it's described in the Book of Revelation, where locusts emerge from the Abyss and are controlled by Apollyon.

• The swirl in Void's appearance is in the opposite direction of Abyss's.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: According to locusts.xml, Ipecac locusts are supposed to explode. This never happens in game; Ipecac only gives a locust that deals slightly more damage and poisons enemies.
Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room than the one he is currently in (such as the starting room of a new floor) will duplicate the locusts.
Bug note: Shard of Glass, Backstabber, Mom's Razor, as well as Abyss' bleed locust appear to have been not updated properly for v1.9.7.9 and do not have the correct color or effect to match with Charm of the Vampire.
Bug note: Mega Mush's damage is inconsistent, sometimes not applying any damage multiplier. It also does not apply the rock-breaking effect which it should have.
Bug note: Punching Bag's projectile destroying ability is not functional.
Bug note: The Maw Of The Void's effect appears to be dealing too much damage: dealing up to 100 damage per single activation on base damage.
Bug note: Blood Bombs is likely meant to spawn red instead of yellow creep, like with Anemic.

fields.description: Destroys all item pedestals in the room and gives Isaac a unique locust familiar for each item destroyed. Locusts fly forwards in the direction Isaac shoots and damage enemies hit. Destroying certain items spawns special locusts with unique effects.

Ace of Clubs.title: Ace of Clubs
Ace of Clubs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Turns all pickups, trinkets and chests in the room into Bombs.

• [Repentance] All non-boss enemies in the room are also transformed into bombs.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Any unlocked bomb variant can appear, including Troll Bombs.

• Troll Bombs are unaffected.

• [Repentance] On-kill effects such as Charm of the Vampire, do not trigger from turning enemies into bombs.

• [Repentance] Friendly enemies will be transformed into bombs.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• Blood Puppy: Using an Ace card on an angry Blood Puppy will create the respective pickup and tame it.

Ace of Spades.title: Ace of Spades
Ace of Spades.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the trinket; the card of the same name; Ace of Spades (Card)]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives a 10% chance of changing the room drop reward to a tarot or playing card.

• Gives a 33% chance of adding a card or rune to the rewards from opening certain Chests, or destroying Tinted Rocks, certain Machines, and certain Beggars.

• Other than Tinted Rocks and Wooden Chests, these can only drop the card if they drop coins, hearts, Bombs, or Keys.

• • Wooden Chests can even drop the card in addition to an item.

• This includes: 

• This excludes:

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases the chance of changing the room drop reward to a tarot or playing card by 20% and increases the chance of adding a card or rune to rewards to 66%. Having both increases these chances to respectively 30% and 100%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Ace of Spades is often seen as the most powerful and highest card in an average 52 card deck.

fields.description: Increases the chance of tarot cards or playing cards dropping after clearing a room, and the chance of finding cards when opening a Chest.

Acid Baby.title: Acid Baby
Acid Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that drops random pills.

• Acid Baby drops a pill every [Before Repentance] 3 / [Repentance] 7 cleared rooms. The first drop happens after [Before Repentance] 2 / [Repentance] 6 rooms.

• Upon using a pill, all enemies in the room will be poisoned.

• [Before Repentance] The poison lasts for 2 ticks.

• • [Repentance] The poison lasts for 6 ticks. Enemies also take 10 additional damage.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Acid Baby having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] BFFS!: The familiar drops pills in a repeating pattern of 2, 2 then 3 rooms. No damage increase on the poison effect.

• [Repentance] Acid Baby drops a pill every 6 cleared rooms.

• Vurp!: If Isaac's last used pill is a Vurp! pill and Isaac finds another Vurp! pill afterward, he can infinitely generate Vurp! pills and repeatedly use them for mass poison damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Second Hand: No effect.

• Starter Deck: All pills dropped by Acid Baby will turn into cards.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that drops a random pill every [Before Repentance] 3 / [Repentance] 7 rooms. Upon using a pill, all enemies in the room are poisoned.

Act of Contrition.title: Act of Contrition
Act of Contrition.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.7 tears up.

• Grants an Eternal Heart.

• Allows Angel Rooms to spawn even after Isaac has taken a Deal with the Devil.

• Mitigates the penalties to the chance for a deal to appear from taking red heart damage.

• Damage during the stage replaces the 99% no-damage bonus with 40% instead of removing it.

• Damage against the boss replaces the 35% no-damage bonus with 15% instead of removing it.

• In practice, this results in a -24% chance instead of -64% for taking damage during the stage, and -44% instead of -99% for taking damage against the boss.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Act of Contrition originates from the Antibirth mod. It originally granted an Immortal Heart instead of an Eternal Heart, a heart type that was not added in Repentance. It also did not have the effect to increase the Devil/Angel chance.

• An act of contrition is a Christian prayer that expresses regret over committing a sin and asks for forgiveness.

fields.description: +0.7 tears, grants an Eternal Heart. Allows Angel Rooms to appear even if a Devil Deal has been taken before. Reduces the Devil/Angel room chance penalty for taking Red heart damage.

Adoption Papers.title: Adoption Papers
Adoption Papers.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Shops and Black Markets now sell familiars instead of the usual item selection.

• The familiars are chosen from the Baby Shop item pool.

• While holding the Adoption Papers, the familiars are discounted to 10 coins. If the papers are dropped, they cost 15 coins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• A shop that has already been entered will not have its item selection changed, nor will dropping the papers revert them to normal.

• In Greed Mode, only the shop pool item is replaced with a familiar and discounted.

• This also applies to all shop pool items when playing as Tainted Keeper. Familiars spawned from the Treasure Room pool remain unaffected.

• Familiars that appear in both the Shop pool and Baby Shop pool (Buddy in a Box, King Baby, etc) will be discounted by Adoption Papers even if the shop was visited before the trinket was held.

• After Baby Shop item pool is exhausted, items from normal shop pool will be generated again in shops.

• Items generated by this will still discount to 10 coins.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Familiars are always on sale. [Repentance+] Shops will also be able to sell Soul of Lilith if isaac has both Golden Trinket and Mom's Box.

• Steam Sale: Both of the discounts stack, selling familiars for 5 cents.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Chaos: Chaos takes priority in item selection. However, items will still be discounted.

• Eden's Soul / Mystery Gift: Ignores the effect of Adoption Papers, spawning items from the Shop pool if used there.

• Flip: The ghostly items will be from the Shop pool.

• Glitched Crown: While one of the items will come from the Baby Shop pool, the other 4 items cycled between will come from the regular Shop pool, all of which still discounted at 10 coins.

• Keeper's Box: Does not affect Keeper's Box' items, meaning both familiars and shop items can be purchased in tandem over the course of a run.

• Member Card / The Stairway: The extra shops are unaffected by Adoption Papers.

fields.description: Shops can sell familiars, which will always be at a discounted price.

Adrenaline.title: Adrenaline
Adrenaline.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac a flat damage up based on how many empty Red Heart containers he has.

• [Before Repentance] The damage up given is 0.2 for each empty Red Heart container Isaac has.

• • [Repentance] The damage up given is ((2 × MissingHearts) ^ 1.6) × 0.1, where MissingHearts is the number of full red hearts of health missing. The amount of damage gained this way is exponential, so each heart lost will provide a bigger bonus than the last.

• Damage ups are only applied for every fully empty heart container.

• Contributes to the Spun transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item has no effect on characters that can't have any Red Heart containers, unless Bone Hearts are collected. If a Bone Heart is gone, so does the Adrenaline damage. This means that Adrenaline is only truly useless on The Lost.

• This item affects both Keeper and Tainted Keeper; empty Coin Hearts increase damage.

• As The Forgotten, empty Bone Hearts increase damage, but if the Bone Hearts are broken, the damage buff is lost.

• [Repentance] The maximum damage bonus from Adrenaline is 14.05 normally, 16.15 with Bone Hearts, and 30.9 for Magdalene with Birthright. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Birthright + Magdalene: Allows Magdalene to gain more damage than the other characters can because of her 6 additional heart containers.

• Blood Oath: Activates the damage up effect of Adrenaline for the resulting empty heart containers at the start of each floor.

• Empty Heart: Activates the damage up effect of Adrenaline if an empty heart container is granted at the beginning of each floor.

• Rock Bottom: Allows Isaac to keep the damage up after refilling hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Before v1.06.0190, Adrenaline was named Adderline.

• Despite having its name changed, Adrenaline's item sprite is named collectibles_493_adderline in the game files.

• Adrenaline is a hormone produced by the body in situations of high stress that increases blood circulation, breathing, and other things in preparation for the natural flight or fight reflex.

• Adrenaline causes characters to have an animation that makes them look like they are breathing rapidly. The more health they're missing, the more exaggerated the animation is.

fields.description: Increases damage based on how many empty Red Heart containers Isaac has.

fields.description: +1 Red Heart container.

Akeldama.title: Akeldama
Akeldama.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• While in a room with enemies, creates a trail of tears that Isaac drags behind him.

• Each tear deals 3.5 damage, regardless of Isaac's damage.

• Tears are spawned at an irregular rate, roughly between once every 0.1 to 1 seconds.

• The tears are spectral.

• Once the room is cleared, the trail will remain but will stop regenerating.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Shell. [end edition note] 

• Another trail of tears may appear if the trail is cut in the middle.

• A maximum of 20 tears can exist at once, shared between all trails.

• The tears cannot push active Bombs and Troll Bombs.

• The tears can extinguish Fire Places and set off TNT.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Angelic Prism: Splits the trail of tears into four multi-colored chains.

• Lachryphagy: Some Akeldama tears will absorb tears shot by Isaac and gain size and damage as expected, but will not burst from being overloaded and can be fed infinite amount of tears. Meaning that each tear, if fed enough, can deal massive amounts of damage.

• Lodestone: Magnetized enemies will attract the tears from Akeldama's trail, making it easier to use.

• Multidimensional Baby: Akeldama tears that passes through Multidimensional baby will be cloned and may also create a separate trail if enough tears are cloned.

• Tear Detonator: Will burst tears generated by Akeldama into Isaac's current tears.

• Technology Zero: Shot tears will create a laser between it and the Akeldama tear closest to Isaac.

• Dead Eye: The tears in the trail will contribute to the damage boost, making it possible to stack damage while having items that do not interact with Dead Eye on their own (such as Brimstone).

• IBS: Holding a White Poop above your head will give Akeldama tears homing.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Anti-Gravity: Akeldama tears are unaffected by Anti-Gravity.

• Brimstone: Akeldama creates normal tears.

• Godhead: Akeldama tears do not have the aura.

• Ipecac: Akeldama creates normal tears.

• Pop!: Akeldama blocks the eyeballs created by Pop!, making it quite difficult to hit enemies.

• Scissors: The trail will follow Isaac's body.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Akeldama originates from the Antibirth mod.

• Akeldama means 'field of blood' in Aramaic, and is thought to be the monastery where Judas Iscariot committed suicide after betraying Christ in the Bible.

• The name comes from a passage from the Gospel of Matthew, where after his betrayal, Judas cast his reward of 30 silver pieces into the temple for the priests. The coins were deemed as 'blood money', so instead of adding them to the treasury, a field was bought to bury foreigners (27:7).

• An alternative naming origin comes from the Acts of the Apostles, where it is stated that Judas "acquired a field with the reward of his unjust deed, and falling headfirst he burst open in the middle and all his intestines gushed out," (Acts 1:18-19). This telling in particular is likely where the item description comes from.

• • However, this is why this item is a Judas unlock.

fields.description: While in an uncleared room, Isaac forms a trail of bloody tears that drags behind him, bursting and dealing damage upon contact with enemies.

Alabaster Box.title: Alabaster Box
Alabaster Box.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• This item starts with no charges. Rather than gaining charges by clearing rooms or picking up batteries, Alabaster Box has to be charged through Soul Heart or Black Heart. Instead of being added to Isaac's health bar, they charge the box at a rate of one charge per half heart.

• Both Soul or Black Hearts that are picked up, or directly added to Isaac's health will count towards Alabaster Box's charges.

• Upon use, Alabaster Box is consumed and vanishes from Isaac's inventory, spawning three Soul Hearts and two items from the Angel Room item pool.

• There's a small chance for each of the spawned Soul Hearts to be replaced with an Eternal Heart.

• If a Devil Deal was taken previously, it spawns only two Soul Hearts and one Angel Room item instead.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Isaac takes a Devil Deal that requires Soul Hearts while holding a charged Alabaster Box, hearts are taken from the box before it takes from Isaac's health.

• [Before Repentance+] If Isaac has a full HP bar, and he has either Soul or Black Hearts in his health pool, picking up Bone Hearts will take away 2 charges from Alabaster Box each, instead of replacing any Soul/Black Hearts as they normally would. Bone Hearts will only replace health if the Alabaster Box has no charges.

• If Isaac picks up a Bone Heart at max HP while the Alabaster Box only has 1 charge, then it will take away both that 1 charge and half of a whole Soul/Black Heart (half hearts are unaffected).

• If The Lost picks up a Black Heart the box will not gain any charges.

• If the box requires two or more charges and Isaac picks up a Black Heart, the box gains charge as for a Soul Heart and the last Soul Heart (or half Soul Heart, if there is one) in Isaac's health becomes black.

• If the box requires only one more charge and Isaac picks up a full Soul Heart or a Black Heart, then the box becomes fully charged and a half heart of the same type is added to Isaac's health.

• If sleeping in a bed would restore Soul Hearts, they are used to charge the Alabaster Box instead. Any excess are added as Soul Hearts as normal.

• This applies to The Lost, who is always in the state to recover Soul Hearts, even if usually without effect.

• Soul hearts from Blended Heart can also be used to charge the box. They are, as usual, used for red health first.

• Bulbs are able to drain charges from Alabaster Box.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• ? Card: Activates Alabaster Box without consuming it, allowing for multiple uses.

• Bethany / Tainted Bethany: Soul/blood charges count as charges for Alabaster Box.

• Book of Belial interaction: Changes the payout to 2 Black Hearts and 1 item from the Devil Room item pool. If a Devil Deal has been taken, the payout is boosted to 3 Black Hearts and 2 Devil items.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns up to 8 normal wisps, filling up the middle ring.

• Found Soul: Found Soul will also activate Alabaster Box when Isaac does, doubling the rewards.

• Guppy's Paw + Schoolbag: Heart containers converted to Soul Hearts contribute to Alabaster Box's charge instead of being added to Isaac's health. This enables a full charge for just two heart containers.

• Metronome: When Metronome chooses Alabaster Box, it will immediately activate without requiring Soul Hearts.

• Void: Can activate Alabaster Box without consuming Soul Hearts. The effect is only used by Void once.

• Wild Card: Allows for multiple uses of Alabaster Box so long as no other activated item, card, pill or rune has been used following the initial activation.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 4.5 Volt / 9 Volt / 48 Hour Energy / The Battery / Battery Pack / Car Battery / Charged Penny / Hairpin / Habit / Jumper Cables : No effect.

• Abaddon: Red Hearts will be converted to Black Hearts, which will be used to charge the box. If Isaac would die as a result of picking up Abaddon (he only has Red health), he is given a Half Soul Heart.

• Battery Bum: No effect, even though there's a cue that the item was charged.

• Converter: Cannot use charges stored in Alabaster Box.

• Devil's Crown / Satanic Bible: The extra Devil items will count as taking a deal, lowering Alabaster Box's payout.

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper: Though Keeper cannot encounter Soul Hearts normally, it is possible to charge the Alabaster Box by having something that adds them directly to health, such as Schoolbag with Book of Revelations or Dream Catcher, purchasing soul hearts spawned by Keeper's Box, or playing in Co-op alongside someone not playing as Keeper.

• Tainted Magdalene: Not recommended. If Tainted Magdalene has any soul hearts as health, then soul hearts will leak from the box, taking priority over soul health.

• The Lost / Tainted Lost: Alabaster Box does not gain charges from Black Hearts. Soul Hearts still function as expected.

• Magic Skin / Sumptorium: Will use Soul Hearts from the box before removing the ones in health.

• Mother's Kiss: Taking this trinket as a character that can't use red hearts grants a Soul/Black Heart instead of giving it to Alabaster Box.

• Schoolbag: Picked up Soul Hearts are consumed by Alabaster Box, even if it's in the second slot.

• Sharp Plug: Takes up to 6 full hearts if possible without giving charge, even when having Soul Hearts.

• XI - Strength and III - The Empress? cards apply a temporary charge on characters that can only use Soul/Black Hearts such as ??? or Tainted Judas.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Alabaster Box originates from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, the item was guaranteed to drop an eternal heart.

• Alabaster Box is one of the three activated items, alongside Eden's Soul and Broken Glass Cannon, that:

• Has no charges upon pickup.

• Needs to be charged and disappears upon use.

• Prior to patch v1.06.J813, an Alabaster Box crafted from Bag of Crafting was immediately fully charged.

• Tainted Eden can reroll into a fully-charged Alabaster Box.

• The item is likely a reference to the anointing of Jesus - while He was in Bethany, a woman came to Him with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume, which she poured on His head as He was reclining at the table.

• In Biblical times, alabaster boxes were made of a rich marble-type stone called alabaster. Much like an alabaster jar or vial of perfume as mentioned in Mark 14, the perfume would be sealed inside. When the owner wished to use it, the seal or neck had to be broken so that it could be used.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Picking up Bone Hearts while at 12 hearts removes charges from the Box.

fields.description: Upon use, spawns three Soul Hearts and two Angel Room items and is consumed. Starts with no charges, and can only be charged by picking up 6 Soul Hearts.

Algiz.title: Algiz
Algiz.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants a shield which lasts for [Before Repentance] 30 / [Repentance] 20 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Subsequent uses of Algiz are additive: if it's used while the shield effect is already active, it will add to the duration of the shield effect.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • The invulnerability effect negates all forms of damage, including health loss from Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars. They can be used for free for the duration of the effect.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Doubles the duration of the shield, making it last a full minute.

• Book of Shadows: The shield effects also stack.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

fields.name: Algiz
fields.description:

[Repentance] Grants a shield which lasts for 20 seconds.

Almond Milk.title: Almond Milk
Almond Milk.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Quadruples fire rate.

• ×0.3 damage multiplier.

• -0.16 tear size.

• Each tear gains the effects of either Flat Worm, Pulse Worm, Wiggle Worm, Hook Worm, Ring Worm, Whip Worm, Lazy Worm, Tape Worm, Ouroboros Worm, Brain Worm, Rubber Cement, My Reflection or Tiny Planet at random.

• Some tears may have multiple effects at once.

• These inherit the movement, shot speed, range, and spectral effects, but not changes to tears or damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brimstone / Azazel / Tainted Azazel: The beam will fire continuously as long as the fire button is held and can be aimed in any direction. It shuffles through the worm effects rapidly.

• Chocolate Milk / Cursed Eye / Monstro's Lung / Tech X: Fires automatically upon reaching full charge.

• Tech X overrides the worm trinket effects.

• Tractor Beam: All tears now travel along the beam, improving overall accuracy and DPS.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Soy Milk: Overridden by Almond Milk (no additional effect on tears or damage).

• The Ludovico Technique: The tear will rapidly teleport in a small area around it, making it difficult to aim.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Almond Milk is from the Antibirth mod.

Analog Stick.title: Analog Stick
Analog Stick.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.35 tears up.

• Allows tears to be fired diagonally.

• With a keyboard or using buttons to fire with a controller, tears can be shot at 45-degree angles by holding two buttons. This is known as eight-directional firing. For example, holding the up button and right button will shoot diagonally towards the upper right-hand corner.

• Using a controller with a physical analog stick, its input is accepted, allowing for tears to be shot in any direction, as it shoots wherever the analog stick is pointing without being limited to 45-degree angles.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Enables full directional firing for keyboard and mouse users with the accessibility option EnableMouseControl enabled.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Abyss: Locusts cannot attack diagonally, and will attack upwards or downwards instead.

• Book of Virtues: Summoned wisps are unable to shoot diagonally, and will shoot upwards or downwards instead.

• Cain's Other Eye: The familiar will fire in completely random directions, not locked to the cardinal ones.

• Compound Fracture: When bone tears are fired diagonally, the bone shards will not always move diagonally.

• Cricket's Body/The Parasite: When tears are fired diagonally, the split tears will also move diagonally.

• Epic Fetus: No effect, as missiles will always be fired towards the landing point.

• Epiphora: Tears fired diagonally can retain the bonus fire rate, as long as Isaac's head continues to face the same direction.

• Incubus: Incubus cannot fire in non-cardinal directions, only tears up applies.

• [Repentance] Incubus can fire diagonally in the same direction Isaac is shooting.

• The Ludovico Technique: No effect; the singular tear already has this ability, being able move in any direction.

• Marked: Overridden by Marked.

• Mom's Knife: Only the tears up applies, since Mom's Knife already has the ability of being able to be pointed in any direction.

• Tiny Planet: Overridden by Tiny Planet.

• Tractor Beam: Overridden by Tractor Beam.

• [Repentance] Tractor Beam can be pointed in any direction.

fields.description: +0.35 tears up. Allows Isaac to fire tears diagonally.

Lost Soul.title: Lost Soul
Lost Soul.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Found Soul; Your Soul]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Creates a ghostly familiar that closely follows behind Isaac. It dies in one hit, respawning at the start of the next floor.

• If Lost Soul survives until the start of the next floor, it rewards Isaac with one of the following:

• 3 Soul Hearts.

• 2 Eternal Hearts.

• A Treasure Room item or an Angel Room item.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Blighted Ovum. [end edition note] 

• Lost Soul hides behind Isaac, opposite to the direction he is firing tears.

• Also, if Isaac is moving to the opposite side he's shooting, then his hitbox will completely absorb Lost Soul's hitbox, making it significantly harder for enemies to hit it.

• Floors completed during the Ascent count.

• Waiting until after the floor is cleared before picking up Lost Soul nearly guarantees a reward payout on the next floor.

• The ghost can take explosive damage from Isaac, e.g. via placing a Bomb.

• Lost Soul's position behind Isaac can overlap with other Familiars.

• Leaving the Mother's Shadow chase sequence respawns Lost Soul.

• Swapping the item as Tainted Isaac and picking it up again respawns Lost Soul.

• Spiked Rocks will kill Lost Soul.

• [Before Repentance+] If Lost Soul is hit, this will invalidate the conditions for spawning Perfection, even if Isaac hasn't been hit.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Gives Lost Soul a once-per-room shield, similar to Holy Mantle.

• If BFFS! is dropped, the shield will still remain active until taking one hit of damage, acting similarly to Holy Card.

• Forget Me Now / R Key: Restarting a floor/run causes Lost Soul to give a reward if it's alive when used.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Box of Friends: Cannot duplicate the ghost and won't spawn a Demon Baby, even when the ghost is dead.

• Bursting Sack / Skatole: Does not provide immunity to contact damage from spiders/flies to Lost Soul.

• Chaos: Items dropped by Lost Soul are drawn from a random pool.

• Child Leash / Duct Tape / Friendship Necklace / King Baby / RC Remote / The Twins: No effect.

• Diplopia / Crooked Penny: Picking up multiple Lost Souls has no effect, even if one died previously.

• Missing No.: If a new floor is entered and Missing No. rerolls into this item, it will immediately give a reward.

• Tainted Forgotten: The ghost follows Tainted Forgotten, making it very difficult to protect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Lost Soul originates from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, multiple copies of the item would grant multiple familiars.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Lost Soul is killed before the segment with Mother's Shadow, it will respawn after Isaac returns to the normal floor.
Bug note: Swapping Lost Soul for another item as Tainted Isaac and picking it back up again will cause it to respawn if it died previously. This can also be accomplished with Butter!.
Bug note: Resuming a Jacob and Esau run with Lost Soul given to Esau will cause it to respawn if it died previously.

fields.description: Creates a ghostly familiar that closely follows behind Isaac. It dies in one hit, but respawns at the start of the next floor. Each time it survives until the next floor, it rewards Isaac with Soul Hearts, Eternal Hearts, or an Item.

Louse.title: Louse
Louse.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Occasionally spawns a Blue Spider.

• Effect only occurs when in an uncleared room.

• After the first spider spawns, there is a 50% chance of one spawning after 30 seconds and a guaranteed spawn a minute later.

• [Repentance+] Spawns a Blue Spider when completing a combat room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Louse : Each copy of the effect will spawn an additional spider every time one is spawned.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The phrase "Itchy, tasty..." is a reference to the Keeper's Diary from Resident Evil. The Diary describes the slow transformation of a researcher into a zombie as his entries become less and less coherent due to neural decay caused by t-Virus infection. His final entry consists of two words: "Itchy. Tasty.".

Luck.title: Luck
Luck.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Luck affects a variety of chance-based effects and is represented by a 3-leaf clover.

The large majority of characters have a base Luck of 0. The following characters are exceptions:

| Character | Luck

| Keeper Dead Tainted Lazarus Tainted Keeper | -2

| Lazarus Esau | -1

| Jacob | 1

• Eden and Tainted Eden: varies between -1 and 1, inclusive (including decimal values).

• Cain's base Luck is technically 0, but he starts with Lucky Foot, increasing his luck to 1.

sections.heading: Effects of Luck
sections.text:
Luck influences many different elements:

• Room drops: For calculating room drops, luck is capped between 0 and 10, with higher luck not only resulting in higher amounts of drops but also higher quality drops such as chests.

• Room drop rates are otherwise identical in Normal and Hard game modes, but Hard mode removes [Before Repentance] 66%/ [Repentance] 33% of heart-type drops, replacing them with nothing.

• [Repentance] If there is more than one playable character on screen (Jacob and Esau, Co-op, using the item Strawman, etc.) the room drop rate depends on the total luck the 2 characters have.

• Tear effect chance: The chance of shooting tears with status effects becomes more likely as Luck goes up. This scales up to 100% chance per tear in most cases with enough Luck.

• Most of the status inflicting effects require high Luck to activate on every tear.

• • Since these effects persist on the enemies for a set amount of time regardless of the Tears stat, a fast rate of fire is often enough to affect an enemy indefinitely.

• Most tear effect chances scale exponentially with luck, while a few others scale linearly with luck, meaning that it can take a lot of luck to notice a significant increase in activation rates in most cases.

• However not all effects scale up to 100%, and some items have the rates capped at a lower percentage. If the maximum activation rate is not 100% for an item, the true maximum rate will be listed instead.

• [anchor: Luck-based tear effects; Tear items affected by Luck] are:

• • Abaddon (Tears cause fear) - 100% at 85 Luck

• • Apple! (Razor tears) - 100% at 14 Luck

• • Ball of Tar (Tears slow enemies) - 100% at 18 Luck

• • Bird's Eye (Fire produced along with tear) - 50% at 10 Luck

• • The Common Cold (Poison tears) - 100% at 12 Luck

• • Dark Matter (Tears cause fear) - 100% at 20 Luck

• • [Repentance] Dr. Fetus has luck based effects with certain bomb items

• • 
• Brimstone Bombs (Bombs create Brimstone beams) - 100% at 29.67 Luck

• • 
• Butt Bombs (Bombs damage and confuse every enemy) - 100% at 27 Luck

• • 
• Hot Bombs (Bombs damage on contact and leave a fire) - 100% at 12.34 Luck

• • 
• Ghost Bombs (Bombs spawn ghosts) - 100% at 8.25 Luck

• • 
• Sad Bombs (Bombs burst into tears) - 100% at 29.67 Luck

• • 
• Scatter Bombs (Bombs explode into smaller bombs) - 100% at 8.25 Luck [end edition note] 

• • Euthanasia (Needle tears) - [Before Repentance] 100% at 14.5 Luck / [Repentance] 25% at 13 Luck

• • Evil Eye (Eye tears) - 10% at 20 Luck

• • Fire Mind (Chance that tears explode) - 100% at 13 Luck

• • Ghost Pepper (Fire produced along with tear) - 50% at 10 Luck

• • Holy Light (Tears inflict Crack the Sky effect) - 50% at 8.89 Luck

• • Iron Bar (Tears confuse enemies) - 100% at 26.95 Luck

• • Knockout Drops (Tears knock back enemies significantly) - 100% at 8.01 Luck

• • Little Horn (Instant death tears) - 20% at 15 Luck

• • Lodestone (Tears cause enemy to become magnetized) - 100% at 5 Luck

• • Loki's Horns (4-way tears) - [Before Repentance] 100% at 7 Luck / [Repentance] 100% at 15 Luck

• • 
• [Afterbirth onward] Loki's Horns + The Ludovico Technique - Maximizes at 20 Luck

• • Mom's Contacts (Tears petrify enemies) - 50% at 20 Luck

• • Mom's Eye (Forwards and backwards tears) - [Before Repentance] 100% at 2 Luck / [Repentance] 100% at 5 Luck

• • 
• [Afterbirth onward] Mom's Eye + The Ludovico Technique - Maximizes at 10 Luck

• • Mom's Eyeshadow (Tears charm enemies) - 100% at 26.95 Luck

• • Mom's Perfume (Tears cause fear) - 100% at 85 Luck

• • Mom's Wig (Spawn blue spiders while shooting) - 100% at 9.5 Luck

• • Ocular Rift (Tears create rifts) - 20% at 15 Luck

• • Parasitoid (Egg tears) - 50% at 5 Luck

• • Rotten Tomato (Tears mark enemies) - 100% at 4.01 Luck

• • Spider Bite (Tears slow enemies) - 100% at 15 Luck

• • Tough Love (Teeth instead of tears) - 100% at 9 Luck

• Trinkets affected by Luck are:

• • Black Tooth (Poisonous double damage tear) - 100% at 32 Luck

• • Cain's Eye (The Compass effect) - 100% at 3 Luck

• • Cartridge (The Gamekid effect when hit) - 100% at 38 Luck

• • Chewed Pen (Tears slow enemies) - 100% at 18 Luck

• • Eve's Bird Foot (Spawn a dead bird on killing an enemy) - 100% at 7.6 Luck

• • Ice Cube (Chance for each enemy to be frozen upon entering a room) - 100% at 40 Luck

• • Isaac's Fork (Heal half a heart on clearing a room) - 100% at 18 Luck

• • Jawbreaker (Chance for tooth shot dealing x3.2 damage) - 100% at 9 Luck

• • A Lighter (Chance for each enemy to be lit on fire upon entering a room) - 100% at 40 Luck

• • A Missing Page (The Necronomicon effect) - 50% at 60 Luck

• • Old Capacitor - 33% at 4.34 Luck

• • Ouroboros Worm (Chance to shoot homing tears) - 100% at 9 Luck

• • Pinky Eye (Poison tears) - 100% at 18 Luck

• • Push Pin (Spectral + Piercing tears) - 100% at 18 Luck

• • Red Patch (+1.8 Damage Up on taking damage) - 100% at 8 Luck

• • Samson's Lock (Chance for +0.5 Damage Up on killing an enemy) - 100% at 9.34 Luck

• Other items affected by Luck include:

• • Athame: Black brimstone circles are created more often with higher luck, up to 100% of the time at 30 Luck.

• • Broken Modem: Higher luck increases the rate of freezing enemies and their shots.

• • Celtic Cross: The Celtic Cross grants its invulnerability more often with higher Luck, topping out at 100% at 26.67 Luck.

• • Gimpy: The Soul Heart drop chance upon taking damage increases with higher Luck, topping out at [Before Repentance] 50% with 20 Luck / [Repentance] 100% at 46 Luck.

• • Midas' Touch: Poops generated by Isaac's actions have a chance to turn into Golden Poop, with the chance depending on the source.

• • 
• A Card Against Humanity: 10% at 0 Luck to 100% at 18 Luck.

• • 
• The Poop: [Before Repentance] 50% at 0 Luck to 100% at 5 Luck. [Repentance] 33% at 0 Luck and 100% at 6.7 Luck.

• • 
• Re-Lax: 25% at 0 Luck to 100% at 7.5 Luck.

• • Mystery Gift: Higher luck results in a lower chance of getting The Poop or A Lump of Coal.

• • Old Bandage: The Red Heart drop chance when you take a hit increases with higher Luck, topping out at [Before Repentance] 50% with 26.67 Luck / [Repentance] 100% at 80 Luck.

• • Virgo: The shield activation chance increases with Luck, topping out at 100% at 10 Luck.

• • Dirty Mind: Rocks can be replaced by poops depending of Luck, capping at 10% with 7.5 Luck.

However, Luck doesn't affect:

• Fortune Telling Machine, Portable Slot, Shell Game, Slot Machine: Their chance of giving a consumable doesn't increase with Luck. Only Lucky Foot increases the winning chances with these machines.

• The activation chance of: Fanny Pack, Dry Baby, The Mulligan, Broken Watch, Infamy, Tech.5, Guppy's Collar, Undefined (for I AM ERROR or Black Market teleports), We Need To Go Deeper! (Crawl Spaces | [Repentance] Only on specific floor tiles), Pandora's Box (as its effects are predetermined depending on which floor it's used on), and Missing Page 2.

• Content from Chests, Pots, Mushrooms, Skulls, Fires, Devil Rooms, and Angel Rooms.

• Beggars, Devil Beggars, Key Masters, and Bomb Bums aren't affected by Luck.

sections.heading: Other
sections.text:
• "Luck Up" pills increase luck by 1, and "Luck Down" pills decrease Luck by 1.

• Putting a coin in the Donation Machine has a 2% chance to increase Luck by 1.

• [Repentance] Having Karma increases this chance.

• [Afterbirth onward] Lucky Penny increase Luck by 1. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth onward] In co-op, Green Baby will occasionally briefly increase Luck by 2. Dark Baby will occasionally briefly increase all stats, including Luck.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Absorbing an item using Black Rune can increase Luck by 1.

• [Repentance] Certain wisps (such as those generated by Fortune Cookie + Book of Virtues synergy) increase Luck by 0.2 per wisp. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Unlike the most common representation, the in-game icon for Luck has 3 leaves instead of 4.

Lucky Foot.title: Lucky Foot
Lucky Foot.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 luck.

• Increases chances of winning at Shell Game, [machine: Hell Game] , Slot Machine, Fortune Telling Machine, and Confessional.

• Increases chances of getting a room-clearing drop (independent from the luck stat).

• Increases the chance of a reward from a Beggars or Devil Beggar after each of their first payouts.

• On Hard mode, reduces the minimum number of donations for each reward to 2 (from 3).

• Does not apply to Key Master, Bomb Bum, Battery Bum, or Rotten Beggar.

• [Repentance] Converts all "bad" pills into their "good" counterparts but doesn't affect neutral ones, like PHD. Pills remain unidentified.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Cain starts with this item by default.

• For Room Clear Awards, the Lucky Foot works by first applying a decimal multiplier to the room-clearing drop RNG, and then by raising its minimum value. All of this happens before the luck stat modifies the RNG's maximum value by adding another random number.

• With zero luck, your chance to get nothing from a room clear is 22%; with Lucky Foot's modifiers (other than luck), it's reduced to around 13.33%. The effect on its own is similar to having 6.5 extra points of luck, though with a much lower likelihood of getting Chests.

• Lucky Foot also slightly increases the likelihood of running into Chests, though this effect is most noticeable if your luck isn't very high.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• False PHD: Pills can both be good or bad again. Taking a bad pill still applies the benefits from False PHD.

• Lucky Toe: The extra luck-independent chance of room clearing drops from Lucky Toe applies only in a diminished form, unless at zero or negative luck. This bonus from Lucky Foot is still retained.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Lucky Foot had the added effect of changing "bad pills" into "good pills".

• [Repentance] This was restored in Repentance.

• [Before Repentance] On the Character Select Screen, this item is mistakenly called the "Luck Foot". This is a carryover from the original The Binding of Isaac.

• The Lucky Foot may be a reference to a rabbit's foot, which is carried as an amulet for good luck.

fields.description: +1 luck. Improves Isaac's chances at various random events (independent from the luck stat). [Repentance] Converts all bad pills into good pills, without identifying them.

Lucky Rock.title: Lucky Rock
Lucky Rock.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Rocks and their variants drop 1 Penny when destroyed.

• [Repentance] Rocks and their variants have a 33% chance to drop 1 Penny when destroyed.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [edition rnr+] Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Chance for rocks to drop pennies is multiplied.

• [Repentance+] Having either has the same chance to drop 2 pennies at once. Having both the same chance to drop 3 pennies at once.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The spawned coin is always a regular penny; it cannot be a (sticky) Nickel, Dime, or Lucky Penny.

• Coins from obstacles are dropped from any source that destroys them, including enemies such as the Roundy.

[Before Repentance] Rocks and their variants drop 1 Penny when destroyed.
[Repentance] Rocks and their variants have a 33% chance to drop 1 Penny when destroyed.

Lucky Sack.title: Lucky Sack
Lucky Sack.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Spawns a Grab Bag upon traveling to the next floor.

sections.heading: Synergies

• Found Soul: An extra sack will spawn next to Found Soul.

• Golden Trinket/Mom's Box: Grants 1 extra sack every floor per copy.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Strawman: Does not spawn an extra sack for the Keeper.

fields.description: Spawns a Grab Bag upon traveling to the next floor.

Lucky Toe.title: Lucky Toe
Lucky Toe.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 Luck.

• Increases chances of getting a room clearing drop (independent of the luck stat).

• 33% chance to drop 1 additional Pickup when opening certain Chests, or destroying Tinted Rocks, certain Machines, and certain Beggars.

• Other than Wooden Chests, these can only drop the additional pickup if they drop coins, hearts, Bombs, or Keys.

• • Wooden Chests can only drop the additional pickup if it drops pills, cards, or runes.

• This includes: 

• This excludes:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• For Room Clear Awards, Lucky Toe does the exact same thing as Lucky Foot, except that it applies after luck has had its chance to modify the RNG. The difference in placement doesn't have much effect at all.

• If you have zero luck, you have a 22% chance to not get a room clear drop without the Lucky Toe; regardless of your luck stat, the Lucky Toe significantly reduces that chance.

• Lucky Toe's effect also very slightly boosts the chance to get Chests from clearing rooms, independent of luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases Luck by 2. Having both by 3.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Lucky Foot: The extra luck-independent chance of room clearing drops from Lucky Foot applies only in a diminished form, unless at zero or negative luck. This bonus from Lucky Toe is still retained.

fields.name: Lucky Toe
fields.description: +1 Luck. Adds a chance to drop an extra pickup when opening a Chest, destroying a machine, or blowing up a tinted rock.

Lump.title: Lump
Lump.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Lumps remain stationary in one spot and shoot a spread of three shots towards Isaac when he comes within range, then they burrow underground and resurface in a different part of the room. If they resurface in range to shoot at Isaac, they will do so incredibly quickly before burrowing underground again.

Lumps will also burrow underground to reappear elsewhere if Isaac doesn't approach them for a short period of time.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • When a Lump is a Green or Purple Champion, it can be seen teleporting around the room while burrowed.

sections.heading: Tar Boy
sections.text:
Tar Boys occasionally fire a short-ranged spray of shots towards Isaac that leaves behind slowing Black Creep. It can also burrow underground and resurface in a different part of the room, much like the Lump. However, it is only able to resurface in areas that have Black Creep and it will prefer to resurface close to Isaac.

If Isaac is standing on Black Creep, Tar Boys can [Before Repentance] launch a fountain of tar shots straight upwards out of the Creep where Isaac is standing/ [Repentance] create a Nerve Ending-like tentacle directly underneath Isaac. This can also occur with Black Creep spawned by other enemies such as Gushes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Tar Boys were added in Booster Pack #4.

• Lumps had a radically different appearance in the original Binding of Isaac.

• [Afterbirth onward] Previously, Lumps appeared as Light Brown in the Scarred Womb. As of Booster Pack #5, Lumps are now red in this environment. [end edition note] 

• Tar Boy is a reference to the Newgrounds animation of the same name.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If you stun a Lump at the same time that it burrows underground, it will cause their sound effect to repeat continuously for a few seconds.
Bug note: If a Lump spawns as a Light White Champion, when the Lump burrows underground, its Eternal Fly will rapidly teleport around the room, potentially resulting in unavoidable damage.

Luna.title: Luna
Luna.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds an extra Secret Room and Super Secret Room to each floor.

• Reveals one random Secret Room on the map on pickup and at the start of each floor.

• Each newly discovered Secret Room has a shining beam of light that will raise tears for the current floor and gives Isaac a Half Soul Heart when walked under.

• The first light gives Isaac +1 tears fired per second, and all subsequent ones give +0.5 tears fired per second.

• This gives a potential +2.5 tears per second for a given floor, on top of 2 soul hearts.

• The tears up breaks the default 5 tears per second cap.

• Once the effect is triggered for the floor, a silver-bluish shine will appear around Isaac. This light will be strengthened for every beam of light "gathered".

• While this effect is mostly cosmetic, it also partially counteracts both the [curse: Darkness] and the "dark rooms" in the Mines/Ashpit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The beams of light appear in both Secret Room types but not in Ultra Secret Rooms.

• The beams of light also appear in Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms that appear as a result of Red Key.

• The beams of light appear even in unopened Secret Rooms on the same floor the item was acquired on.

• The effect can also be obtained in the Mirrored World.

• The tears up bonuses still apply while in the special area of Mines/Ashpit II.

• No new Secret Rooms are added in Greed Mode or Chapter 1 (if it's a starting item for Eden), but the beam of light is still added to current Secret Rooms.

• No new Secret Rooms are added in ???, The Ascent, or Home.

• If kept after using Birthright with Tainted Eden, upon taking damage, the additional tear rate is lost. More beams of light will have to be found or used for the tears to be regained (assuming not all of them were used).

• If playing Co-op or as Jacob and Esau, characters that did not pick up Luna will still gain full benefit from stepping within the beam of light. However, this will only benefit one character.

• Tainted Lazarus: The opposite form of Tainted Lazarus can stand in the beam of light and receive its benefits but the fire rate bonuses are independent of each other and does not carry over between forms. 

• Multiple copies of Luna will not cause additional Secret Rooms or Super Secret Rooms to be generated.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• X-Ray Vision: Opens every Secret Room generated for free, allowing for the maximum tear bonus every floor.

• Fragmented Card: The effects stack, spawning three Secret Rooms on the floor. All three Secret Rooms will contain beams of light.

• Glowing Hourglass: If Glowing Hourglass is used while Isaac touches the beam of light but before the animation where he raises Luna above his head is complete, the bonuses will be granted after time is rewound, allowing the same beam of light to be used multiple times.

• XVIII - The Moon: The Moon will always teleport to an unexplored secret room. If one has already been explored, it will teleport to the other one. If both have been explored, it will teleport randomly in one of the two.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Luna originates from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Luna's effect only provided extra Secret and Super Secret rooms.

• "Luna" is the word for "moon" in Latin and some of its descendant languages, and is sometimes used to distinguish the Earth's Moon from other natural satellites.

fields.quote: The moon's blessing shines upon you
fields.description: Adds an extra Secret Room and Super Secret Room to each floor. Secret Rooms contain a beam of light that increases Fire Rate for the current floor and gives a Half Soul Heart.

Lunch.title: Lunch
Lunch.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the trinket; Bag Lunch]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Grants one full Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item has a 12.6% chance to spawn from paying out a Beggar in addition to being in the Beggar item pool. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method.

• Lunch can also be spawned from Bag Lunch.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Binge Eater: When Isaac picks up Lunch it now grants: a permanent +0.5 Tears and +2.5 Range, a temporary +3.6 Damage (which diminishes to 0 in 30 seconds), heals 1 additional red heart, and takes a permanent -0.03 Speed reduction.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original Binding Of Isaac, the dog bowl had the name "Max" carved on it. This is a reference to a dog that Edmund McMillen wanted as a child but never got, in which he wanted to name the dog Max.

• In the first post-Repentance Lore Stream, Edmund McMillen states that Lunch is probably cat food.

• Lunch’s sprites can be seen as part of Binge Eater.

fields.name: Lunch
fields.description: Grants one full Red Heart container. [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

Lust.title: Lust
Lust.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Lust is a mini-boss and one of the Seven Deadly Sins.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Lust chases Isaac around the room at a fast speed, attempting to do contact damage.

• She builds speed the longer she travels without turning and takes heavily reduced knockback from Isaac's tears.
Lust deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Having high speed will make the fight much easier.

• [Before Repentance] Lust can drop The Virus even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Sin]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Lust is confirmed to be female.

• The Virus gives Isaac a lumpy appearance that looks similar to Lust's appearance.

• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived.

• Lust's sickly appearance and chance to drop The Virus may be a reference to sexually transmitted diseases.

• Lust is a personification of one of the Seven Deadly Sins. Lust is sexual immorality in all its forms. It is believed to lead to impulsivity, dullness in religious thinking, inconstancy, and worldliness — as well as violence and hatred towards God in more extreme forms.
