The Lamb.title: The Lamb
The Lamb.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Lamb is the boss of the Dark Room, and the final boss of Ending 15.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
The Lamb floats towards Isaac and performs the following attacks:

• Fires 6 rings of 10 projectiles outwards with one projectile always aimed in Isaac's direction. The Lamb continues to move towards Isaac but at a very slow pace while performing this attack.

• Shoots rotating waves of 3 projectiles around himself in all directions that split apart once they make contact with any surface, similar to The Parasite.

• Fires 5 rotating lines of projectiles.

• The Lamb occasionally spawns 0-3 Attack Fly during any of the 3 attacks above.

• Fires 2-4 lines of homing projectiles in a spread that rotate to follow Isaac's movements.

• Unleashes a burst of many small Ipecac-like projectiles in random directions.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Once The Lamb reaches 50% HP, his body detaches from his head and falls to the ground. This phase has each part of The Lamb attacking independently of each other.

The head of The Lamb continues to chase Isaac and can still perform most of the attacks from Phase 1. He loses the explosive shot attack and no longer spawns Attack Flies but gains 3 additional attacks:

• Charges extremely quickly directly towards Isaac, stopping at the edge of the room.

• Stops in place and fires four Brimstone beams in the cardinal directions. The beams can rotate 90 degrees either clockwise or counterclockwise.

• Fires a large burst of homing projectiles towards Isaac, similar to the combination of Monstro's Lung and Spoon Bender.

• Defeating the body first has no effect on the head's behavior.

The body of the Lamb remains stationary at the position the Lamb was at the end of Phase 1. The body has one attack which it performs at random intervals but while the head is attacking:

• Fires a large burst of disorganized projectiles in all directions and spawns up to 5 Attack Flies.

• If the head is defeated first, the body can spawn up to 25 Attack Flies.

• When the body is killed, a [cu: darkness] effect is applied for a long period of time.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text:
Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

[Repentance+] The Lamb has damage scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Lamb can be reached before The Negative is unlocked by taking the trapdoor in a Black Market or I AM ERROR room from Sheol if one shows up.

• [Afterbirth onward] The Lamb can be reached before The Negative is unlocked if a Sacrifice Room is used 12 or more times.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Despite Jesus Christ often being referred to as the "Lamb of God" in the Bible in the books of John and Revelation, The Lamb in this scenario most likely refers instead to the ram that was sacrificed in Isaac's place in the story of Abraham and Isaac, which this game is based upon.

• Upon defeating The Lamb, the song that plays in the credits changes to Hush (Jesus loves uke)

• The music that plays during this battle is titled The Fallen Angel.

• The Lamb is likely a reference to the name of the original Binding of Isaac's DLC expansion, Wrath of the Lamb. Due to the absence of any mention of a Lamb in the original game, this may be the character eponymous with Wrath of the Lamb expansion pack.

• The Lamb's battle portrait depicts him with dark grey bones, but in-game the Lamb has white bones.

• The Lamb shares its name with a level from Edmund's previous game Super Meat Boy.

• The Lamb is one of the three bosses that can dim the room (making a temporary [cu: Darkness] effect). The other bosses are Dark One and The Adversary.

• During an AMA stream, Edmund McMillen confirmed that The Lamb is "Isaac, dead, as a demon," and that it represents "his evil side".

• The Lamb is male.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Killing the body in around 5 seconds will make the body stand inside of the chest, making you unable to reach it (and end the game). You can fix this by going in and out of the room.
Bug note: With the special seed BASEMENT and coming with the last sacrifice room reward, opening The Lamb's chest makes the game crash.
Bug note: If the body is hit with Little Horn effect after it is killed, it will be crushed by the Big Horn's hand and "die" again, causing [cu: darkness] effect to be applied a second time. The body is not destroyed by the hand, so this can be repeated indefinitely. Regular tears cannot hit the body after it is defeated, a beam attack such as Brimstone or Technology is needed to cause the bug.

The Left Hand.title: The Left Hand
The Left Hand.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish: Monkey Paw]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Replaces all types of Chests with Red Chests.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Killing Edmund last in an Ultra Pride fight will drop The Left Hand, even if Isaac is already carrying it.

• [Before Repentance] The effect includes Chests already spawned. Entering a room that previously contained other types of Chests while holding The Left Hand will turn them into Red Chests permanently.

• [Repentance] Chests that have already spawned are not converted into Red Chests.

• It is advised to drop The Left Hand (by holding [plat: PC] CTRL key for few seconds / [plat: PS4, Vita] R2 for 3 seconds / [plat: XboxOne] RT for 3 seconds / [plat: 3DS, Switch] ZR for a few seconds) before entering Chest, as non-Red Chests always contain item pedestals on this floor, especially the 4 located in the starting room.

• [Before Repentance] Isaac may prefer Red Chests for their possible Soul Hearts or Red Chest items, at the expense of guaranteed items.

• [Repentance] Locked Chests converted in Chest's starting room will contain Devil Deals, potentially allowing for more powerful items, but at the cost of Hearts.

• • Red Chests found past the starting rooms of either Chest or Dark Room will contain regular Red Chest drops. Dropping the trinket before leaving the starting room is advised.

• [Repentance] Bomb Chests are affected by The Left Hand. Old Chests and Mega Chests are not affected.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Red chests drop an additional pickup. Additionally prevents red chests from dropping enemy spiders if isaac has both Golden Trinket and Mom's Box.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Gilded Key: Overridden by The Left Hand.

• Sharp Key: Enemies killed by keys will only give the contents of red chests allowing items to be obtained through Sharp Key more consistently.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Left Hand is a reference to occult beliefs in which the "The left hand path" is associated to black magic.

• The Left Hand is the only item in the game with 2 separate conditions for unlocking it, being unlocked by killing Ultra Pride, or by defeating ??? in Chest as Judas

The Ludovico Technique.title: The Ludovico Technique
The Ludovico Technique.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Instead of firing tears, Isaac controls one floating tear that hovers over obstacles. This tear deals constant damage when held in place over an enemy.

• [Repentance+] +0.2 shot speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] The Ludovico Technique is a special item.

• Ludovico tear is piercing and spectral by default.

• Ludovico tear movement speed is determined by the shot speed stat.

• Ludovico tear hits per second are determined by the tears stat, maxed out at 30 ticks per second.

• [Before Repentance] When Death uses his The Hourglass attack, the tear is slow to respond, but then moves so quickly that it is nearly impossible to use effectively.

• [Before Repentance] When there are no enemies in a room, the tear slowly floats towards Isaac.

• The Brimstone ring still follows when Isaac is outside of it.

• If multiple Ludovico Techniques are acquired (via Diplopia, Crooked Penny, Bag of Crafting or on a victory lap), then additional smaller tears will orbit the main tear.

• A maximum of 15 smaller tears can orbit the main tear.

• The Ludovico tear is larger than normal, but does not gain size from damage as much as normal tears.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20 / The Inner Eye / Mutant Spider / Conjoined: Smaller tears orbit the main tear.

• Angelic Prism: While the tear is in contact with the prism, it will fire 4 additional tears in cardinal directions at Isaac's tear rate.

• Azazel: The same effect as with Brimstone, but the damage is halved.

• Azazel + Brimstone: Full damage of the laser ring is regained.

• Backstabber: Much easier to inflict bleeding and double damage on most enemies.

• Berserk!: The tear can't be controlled while berserking, but it can be batted around the room until the effect ends.

• Tainted Samson: uses a passive form of Berserk! that works the same way.

• Bookworm: Causes an additional smaller tear to constantly appear and disappear, teleporting from Isaac's location to the main Ludovico tear in a glitchy manner.

• Brimstone: Tear takes the shape of a very large laser ring. [Before Repentance] The shot speed is ignored. The Tears stat is ignored and the damage is dealt very rapidly at a rate equivalent to 1 tear delay. This ring will always be present and doesn't need charging up like normal Brimstone would.

• Brimstone + Incubus: Incubus' Brimstone laser is not affected by Ludovico Technique.

• • [Repentance] Adds a smaller controllable laser ring in addition to the main one.

• Brimstone + Twisted Pair: Similar effects to Incubus.

• [Repentance] Brimstone + Ipecac: +2 damage, beam explodes when colliding with enemies and obstacles.

• Brimstone + A Lump of Coal: The ring increases in diameter, but not the damage, the farther away it gets from Isaac.

• Brimstone + Spoon Bender: The ring reaches out to attack enemies near it, reforming into a ring when no enemies are present.

• Brimstone + Technology: The ring is visually identical to a normal Brimstone ring, but the 1.5x damage multiplier applies.

• Brimstone + 20/20/The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider / Conjoined: no effect.

• Brimstone + Apple! / Holy Light / Other tear effects: no effect.

• Compound Fracture: Turns tear into a large bone, which shoots out smaller tears when attacking/touching an enemy. Scattered tears are spectral and piercing.

• Dead Eye: Damage bonus increases until it hits the max of 2x. Since the controllable tear never hits the ground or wall, the bonus cannot be lost.

• Dr. Fetus: A bomb is shot out at high speed and can be controlled, another bomb cannot be shot until the previously shot bomb has detonated.

• [Repentance] Causes your tears to act like Epic Fetus and now inherits all synergies Epic Fetus has.

• Epiphora: Moving the tear in one direction for an extended time increases your fire rate.

• Explosivo/Nose Goblin/Sinus Infection: Every tick of damage the Ludovico tear deals has a chance to stick a separate Explosivo/booger tear onto the enemy allowing Isaac to continue controlling the Ludovico tear.

• Eye of the Occult: While holding a direction key, the Ludovico tear will constantly shoot out controllable tears in random directions. The air time of these tears scales with the range stat.

• Fate's Reward: The familiar gains spectral and piercing tears.

• Flat Stone: The tear starts bouncing at a rate somewhat below Isaac's fire rate, each bounce dealing splash damage.

• Flat Stone + Ipecac: Causes a poisonous explosion when it bounces instead of plain splash damage, as per normal Ipecac. The first bounce when entering a room does not explode, allowing moving the tear with less risk of self-damage.

• Fruit Cake: The tear will cycle through different effects, based on Isaac's tear rate.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] If Isaac stays in one room long enough the Ludovico tear will often fill the room with many stationary Trisagion tears that last until Isaac leaves the room. This combination can easily clear most rooms.

• The Forgotten: The tear follows the Forgotten when in its skeleton form. It can be hit with its melee attack to propel it, making it do more damage. When switching to the Soul, the tear behaves as normal.

• The Forgotten + Multidimensional Baby: The second tear acts exactly like the first and can also be hit to propel it.

• The Forgotten + Multi-shot: Switching back from the Soul to the Forgotten will only remove the main tear, thus creating infinitely persisting tears on the screen. Repeating this process allows suspending arbitrarily high amount of tears.

• Godhead: The tear homes towards nearby enemies and gains a large damaging aura. However, the aura cannot damage an enemy that is in contact with the actual tear; barring a high tear rate, it may be better to keep the aura on the enemies instead of the tear.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Guppy: A large number of flies is rapidly deployed whilst controlling the Ludovico tear.

• Holy Light: The Ludovico tear will release holy beams on itself periodically while touching an enemy.

• Incubus: Isaac gains a controlled tear while also being able to shoot normally with Incubus. Incubus's tears gain piercing and spectral properties.

• [Repentance] Incubus creates a second smaller Ludovico Technique tear instead, which can both be controlled by Isaac. The second tear is slightly delayed/ outside of the main tear. This may cause it to not hit enemies sometimes.

• [Repentance] Lilith: Lilith's incubus will fire a smaller Ludovico Technique tear. For each doubled incubus caused by Box of Friends, there will be an additional Ludovico Technique tear that spawns on Lilith's location.

• Lead Pencil: The tear blinks red, but the effect is entirely cosmetic.

• [Repentance] Tear barrages are launched in cardinal directions, even when not controlling the tear. Proc rate depends on fire rate.

• Lodestone: The single floating tear will flash grey to indicate that the magnetism might apply on hit. Like Strange Attractor, enemies tagged with magnetism will also draw the floating tear towards said enemy.

• Loki's Horns: The Ludovico tear will sometimes shoot 4 smaller piercing + spectral tears in each cardinal direction. This chance scales with luck and goes up to 100% at 20 Luck.

• Lost Contact: Tear will block enemy tears without disappearing.

• A Lump of Coal: The tear becomes larger the further away it is from Isaac, increasing in damage.

• Mom's Eye: The Ludovico tear has a chance on each damage tick to fire a smaller piercing + spectral tear in a random direction. This chance scales with luck and goes up to 100% at 10 Luck.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Mom's Wig: The item causes spiders to spawn rapidly when moving the tear.

• [Repentance] Causes Spiders to rapidly spawn until the cap of 5 is reached.

• Monstro's Lung: Tear turns red and does more damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] Tear becomes a cluster of variously sized tears spread over a small area. The tears move at the same speed when controlled but constantly move around each other.

• My Reflection: The shot speed multiplier causes the tear to move significantly faster, allowing it to catch up to any fast-moving enemies.

• Mysterious Liquid: Creep continuously oozes from underneath the tear.

• The Parasite: Shoots out smaller tears when attacking an enemy. Scattered tears are spectral and piercing.

• Pause: The tear deals damage, even if the enemies are stopped. Moving the tear unpauses the enemies.

• Strange Attractor: Enemies, items and even most bosses will be sucked to the single floating tear, dealing constant damage while keeping Isaac well away from harm, making this combination extremely effective in almost all scenarios.

• [Repentance] Tainted Azazel: The same effect as Brimstone, dealing full damage (Tainted Azazel's default laser damage is halved unless Hemoptysis is used first). Tainted Azazel can no longer use Hemoptysis. [end edition note] 

• Tear Detonator: The tear explodes into six smaller tears, then reappears next to the player.

• Tech.5: The tear controls as usual, and Isaac fires the laser towards the tear relative to his position, rather than in the direction the player is moving the tear. The laser becomes spectral.

• Technology: The tear becomes a large laser ring, which visually looks like a shot fired by Tech X. Shot speed is ignored. The Tears stat is ignored and the damage is dealt very rapidly at a rate equivalent to 1 tear delay.

• The Wiz: Small tear orbits the main tear. Tear controls rotated 45 degrees clockwise - holding up makes it move northeast and so on.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
Overrides The Ludovico Technique:

• C Section

• Except when combined with Brimstone in which case fetuses cease to spawn.

• Epic Fetus

• Haemolacria, provides piercing tears

• Spirit Sword

• Tech X
Overridden by The Ludovico Technique:

• Chocolate Milk

• Cursed Eye

• Ipecac

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] +2 Damage.

• • [Repentance] +4 Damage.

• Lachryphagy

• Neptunus
Overridden by The Ludovico Technique, other than stat changes:

• Anti-Gravity

• Cricket's Body

• Marked

• Tractor Beam
Other interactions:

• ???'s Only Friend / Robo-Baby 2.0: The tear and familiar(s) travel together, as they are controlled in the same way. Because the familiars' travel speeds are not affected by Isaac's shot speed, they only travel in the same spot when Isaac has exactly the amount of shot speed to sync them up.

• Almond Milk: The tear will rapidly teleport in a small area around it, making it difficult to aim.

• Bag of Crafting: Swiping the bag at the Ludovico tear will bat it in the direction of the knockback.

• Bird's Eye: Isaac will occasionally shoot a flame towards the Ludovico tear.

• Blood Clot / Chemical Peel: The tear steadily cycles between red and "normal," dealing more damage when red.

• Chocolate Milk: The tear can't be charged, but reduces Isaac's tear delay by 20%.

• The Common Cold: The tear pulses green, poisoning enemies.

• Explosivo: Not recommended as the tear will alternate between "normal" and black. If it touches an enemy, it will stick to it, grow in size, then explode. The tear can not damage anything or be controlled when stuck to an enemy.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The tear will grow very quickly when stuck to an enemy and pop without dealing damage, instead of the normal Explosivo delay and explosion.

• Fire Mind: Tears retain the ability to ignite enemies and explode. Tears reappear at Isaac's location after exploding.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Tears do not explode on contact with an enemy.

• Ghost Pepper / Red Candle: Created fires will destroy the tear and cause it to reappear at Isaac's location.

• [Repentance] Fires generated by both items do not interact with the Ludovico tear. However Ghost Pepper will create fires quickly when the Tear is moved.

• Isaac's Tears:

• [Before Repentance] : The item charges based on the tear's movement.

• [Repentance] : The item charges even while the tear is not moving, with the speed based on Isaac's tears stat.

• Homing Tears: The Ludovico tear will slowly move towards an enemy. This can make it harder to control towards a different enemy or for enemies that hide underground.

• Mom's Knife: The tear becomes a controllable knife that deals double Isaac's damage. Effective shot speed is lowered. Tears stat is ignored and the damage is dealt at a rate equivalent to 4 tear delay.

• Mom's Knife + Brimstone / Flat Stone / Monstro's Lung / Technology: The latter items are overridden completely.

• Multishots: Knives orbit the main knife, similarly to Tiny Planet.

• Multidimensional Baby: No effect.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] An additional Ludovico tear is created when it passes through Multidimensional Baby, at the start of every room, and persists like the Ludovico tear itself. However, it cannot be controlled; it instead slowly follows Isaac.

• • [Repentance] The extra tear stays completely still where it appeared.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Nose Goblin/Sinus Infection: Not recommended as the tear can occasionally stick to an enemy. This leaves Isaac defenseless until the enemy dies or a minute has passed causing the tear to pop and a new one to appear.

• Notched Axe: The Ludovico tear cannot be moved while Notched Axe is held up.

• [Repentance] The tear can be moved by swings, without any special effect happening to it.

• Proptosis: The closer the tear floats to Isaac, the larger it is. The farther away, the smaller.

• Pupula Duplex: Decreases the tear size by taking the form of a Pupula Duplex tear; however, it travels faster.

• Sulfuric Acid: The Ludovico tear occasionally becomes acidic and can destroy objects.

• Tainted Lilith: Gello shoots a smaller Ludovico tear which disappears if he retreats back into Lilith. However, the automatic aiming of Gello interacts with the manual control of Ludovico, making the tear uncontrollable while fighting enemies.

• Technology 2: The tear controls as usual, and Isaac fires the laser towards the tear relative to his position, rather than in the direction the player is moving the tear. Technology 2's damage penalty still applies. The laser becomes spectral.

• [Repentance] Technology 2's tears penalty applies instead of damage.

• • Technology 2 + Analog Stick: Laser is fired directly at the tear while it is being moved, instead of being limited to cardinal directions.

• Technology Zero: No effect without additional items. Extra tears orbiting the main one or familiar tears will generate arcs to the controlled tear.

• The Wiz: A smaller Ludovico tear will appear and revolve around the main one. Also, the Ludovico tear moves diagonally, up is up-right, down is down-left, left is left-up, right is right-down. This can be counteracted by holding the keys or d-pad in its associated path (up-right to make it go up and so forth with the other keys).

• Tiny Planet: Tear orbits around Isaac, however, the orbit can be grown or shrunken, sped up or slowed down by using the firing keys.

• Tough Love / Jawbreaker: Tear occasionally flicks to being a tooth, which deals 3.2x Isaac's tear damage, before immediately returning to being a normal tear. The frequency at which the tear very briefly transforms into a tooth increases with Luck, permanently becoming a tooth at 9 Luck. Jawbreaker does not change the tear appearance.

• Trinity Shield: The controls of the tear and the shield overlap, making it impossible to consistently control both.

• Tropicamide: No size increase effect. Ludovico tear size scales with damage, and not with size multipliers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Ludovico Technique is a reference to Anthony Burgess' novel A Clockwork Orange and Stanley Kubrick's film adaptation, where it was referred to as "Ludovico's Technique." The technique involved headgear which forced the patient's eyelids open (hence "Controlled Tears") while watching violent films under nausea-inducing drugs, conditioning them against violence.

• It is possible to control the tear with the mouse; just open the options.ini file in C:\Users\USER\Documents\My Games\Binding of Isaac Repentance and change MouseControl=0 to MouseControl=1.

• The sound of firing a tear with The Ludovico Technique can be heard in the splash screen of a boss room, before it is possible to control your character.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Mom's Knife + Technology: Creates an uncontrollable laser ring centered on Isaac. The knife becomes stuck under Isaac and cannot be fired.
Bug note: With the bookworm transformation, the tear generated by Ludovico Technique will disappear and reappear on top of Isaac occasionally.
Bug note: At exactly 30.00 fire rate, the tear can only tick once on an enemy, potentially causing softlock due to lack of dps.
Bug note: If Isaac is holding fire and has Technology 2 while pulling out Urn of Souls, another Technology 2 laser is created in the direction being fired that persists until the urn is put away or the room is left.

fields.description: Instead of firing tears, Isaac controls one floating tear that hover over obstacles. This tear deals constant damage when held in place over an enemy.

The Mark.title: The Mark
The Mark.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish: Marked]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Grants one Soul Heart.

• [Repentance] Grants one Black Heart.

• +1 damage.

• +0.2 speed.

• Contributes to the Leviathan transformation.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Black Feather: Counts as an evil item, granting a damage up.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Mark refers to the Mark of the Beast in the end of times prophecies (3 6's arranged in a triskelion). Without this mark, one would not be allowed to buy or sell.

• While The Mark's icon shows the 6's facing towards the center, on Isaac's forehead the symbol appears with the 6's facing outwards.

• Loki has the Mark of the Beast on his forehead.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: DMG up; Repentance: DMG + speed up]
fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Grants one Soul Heart, +1 damage, and +0.2 speed.
[Repentance] Grants one Black Heart, +1 damage, and +0.2 speed. [end edition note]

The Mind.title: The Mind
The Mind.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants the combined effects of the Blue Map, Treasure Map, and The Compass, revealing the floor layout and all special rooms, including Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms.

• Picking up this item and then dropping it with Butter! or as Tainted Isaac will not remove the effect.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • [Repentance] Book of Secrets: Immediately gives the X-Ray Vision effect for the floor upon use.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item, along with The Soul and The Body, are references to the Three Primes of Alchemy.

• The designs of these items appear to be that of Triquetra, a Christian symbol of the Trinity.

• The item's description, along with those of The Soul and The Body, are references to the three attributes commonly ascribed to God in Christian theology: omniscience, omnipotence, and omnipresence. For The Mind, it is omniscience, the ability to "know all".

• This item might be referencing Solomon from the Bible, who became unhappy with life after gaining preposterous wisdom - which is why Isaac might look so done with everything in the item sprite.

• [Repentance] The Mind's icon under the minimap overrides the icons of other mapping effects.

fields.description: Reveals the entire map, including all special rooms and Secret Rooms.

The Mulligan.title: The Mulligan
The Mulligan.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the enemy; Mulligan]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Tears have a 16.67% chance of spawning allied Blue Flies when they hit an enemy.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Because the Guppy transformation includes the guaranteed ability to spawn flies on hit, the Mulligan's effect is nullified. This means individual tears cannot spawn more than one fly per hit.

• [Repentance] The 66.67% chance of spawning a fly granted by Guppy will not stack with The Mulligan's 16.67% chance.

• [Repentance] Blue flies will only spawn if Isaac has less than 30 blue flies.

• [Before Repentance] This item does not work for Lilith since the Incubus tears do not count for her tears.

• Items and trinkets that increase tear firing rate synergize well with the Mulligan.

• This item is not affected by luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Azazel/Brimstone: Rapid damage ticks can cause large amounts of blue flies to spawn.

• Chocolate Milk: The Mulligan's ability isn't affected by the charge time, meaning rapidly firing uncharged shots will generate a ton of blue flies.

• Cricket's Body / The Parasite: Has a 16.67% chance to spawn a fly on every hit by a split shot, which boosts the spawning of flies immensely.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs have a chance to spawn blue flies when damaging enemies.

• Finger!: Rapidly spawns blue flies when pointed at an enemy.

• Urn of Souls: Fires have a chance to spawn blue flies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Dr. Fetus: Overrides The Mulligan.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides The Mulligan.

• Mom's Knife: Has a very low chance of spawning flies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in The Host.

• The term "mulligan" means a second chance to perform an action, usually after the first chance went wrong through bad luck or a blunder.

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Before Afterbirth+: Rebirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth+]
fields.description: Tears have a 16.67% chance of spawning allied Blue Flies when they hit an enemy.

The Nail.title: The Nail
The Nail.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Gives one Soul Heart, +0.7 damage, -0.18 speed, and the ability to destroy most obstacles by walking into them. Cannot be stacked in one room.

• Isaac deals 40 contact damage to enemies, once per second. Does not prevent Isaac from taking contact damage.

• [Repentance] Gives half a Black Heart, +2 damage, -0.18 speed and the ability to destroy obstacles for the current room.

• If used multiple times in one room, the speed penalty only applies once, but the damage buff can stack.

• Isaac deals 20 contact damage to enemies, twice per second. Does not prevent Isaac from taking contact damage.

• • If an enemy is at 40 HP or less, the contact damage is increased to 40 for that enemy.

• [Repentance] Isaac's tears become red for the current room.

• Contributes to the Leviathan transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Isaac makes a demon sound when taking damage while this item is in use. This is quieter than Isaac's standard damage sound and is easy to miss.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns black wisps on the inner ring. Wisps shoot nails that deal double damage from standard wisps and have increased knockback, akin to 8 Inch Nails.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item's effect is a reference to the Nail of Vlad item in Castlevania II: Simon's Quest; equipping it would allow Simon to break certain obstacles such as rocks.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, The Nail was unlocked by beating Mom's Heart three times.

• This item has the same pickup quote as Sulfur.

• Biblically, this item likely references the nails used to pin Jesus Christ to the cross.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Gives one Soul Heart. For the current room; +0.7 damage, -0.18 speed, Isaac breaks rocks and deals contact damage. [end edition note] 
[Repentance] Gives half a Black Heart. For the current room; +2 damage, -0.18 speed, Isaac breaks rocks and deals contact damage. [end edition note]

The Necronomicon.title: The Necronomicon
The Necronomicon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, deals 40 damage to every enemy in the room.

• Contributes to the Bookworm transformation.

• Contributes to the Necromancer transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Many collectibles will produce effects similar to the Necronomicon, such as depleting a Black Heart or blocking projectiles with Dry Baby.

• The Necronomicon deals a considerable amount of damage to bosses that have multiple damageable parts, e.g. Larry Jr. and The Hollow.

• This item also does high enough damage to instantly kill most non-boss enemies; however it is not especially useful against most bosses (with the above exceptions), which will only take minor chip damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] Damage from the Necronomicon bypasses damage scaling.

• [Repentance+] With the Necromancer transformation, the Necronomicon gains a unique appearance and 10 free uses per floor. After the free charges are expended, it behaves as normal until the next floor.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Missing Page / Missing Page 2: Necronomicon will deal an additional +40 damage. Effects stack together and with multiple copies.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns black wisps on the inner ring. The wisps deal 40 damage to all enemies in the room when destroyed. This is not boosted by BFFS!, but is boosted by A Missing Page and Missing Page 2.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Necronomicon is a fictional grimoire appearing in the works of horror writer H.P. Lovecraft.

• A Missing Page and Missing Page 2 are both references to missing pages of the Necronomicon appearing in Evil Dead.

• The book seems to be bound in human skin, which explains the face on its cover.

• The face on the cover is another reference to The Evil Dead franchise, which has the same face on its Necronomicon.

• [Repentance+] This item is one of only six in the game that work towards 2 transformations (Bookworm and Necromancer), the other five being Magic Mushroom, The Bible, Hive Mind, Parasitoid, and Skatole.

fields.description: Deals 40 damage to every enemy in the room.

The Negative.title: The Negative
The Negative.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• If the character has half a red heart or no red hearts after taking damage, it triggers The Necronomicon effect, damaging all enemies in the room.

• Allows entrance into the Dark Room after beating Satan in Sheol by touching the chest.

• [Repentance] +1 damage.

• [Repentance] Opens A Strange Door in Depths II and its variants that leads to Mausoleum/Gehenna II.

• Unlike with the Dark Room entrance, The Negative gets consumed by the door and vanishes from Isaac's inventory. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item is a guaranteed drop from Mom, if unlocked. Will drop alongside The Polaroid, provided they are both unlocked. However, they are mutually exclusive: Once one of them is picked up, the other one will disappear.

• With the use of a teleportation item and either a 5 pip Dice Room or a Forget Me Now, a Diplopia, a Crooked Penny, or R Key, both The Polaroid and The Negative or multiple copies of The Polaroid or The Negative can be obtained.

• With Jacob and Esau, proper alignment of both characters can enable picking up both The Polaroid and The Negative.

• With frame-perfect timing and a bomb, it is possible to pick up both The Polaroid and The Negative.

• The Negative always triggers when taking damage as characters who lack Red Heart containers, such as ??? and Tainted ???, Black Judas and Tainted Judas, The Soul, Tainted Forgotten, Tainted Bethany or any other character who has chosen to trade away their heart containers in devil deals, Black Markets, Guppy's Paw or the Potato Peeler.

• The Negative will be the rightmost item after defeating Mom, in case [cu: blind] is active.

• [Before Repentance] It is possible to obtain two Negatives by obtaining one as an Eden starting item.

• Obtaining multiple copies of The Negative does not cause its effect to stack.

• As with all items crucial to story progress (Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2, Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2, Dad's Note, and Dogma), this item has protection from full-run rerolls. It does not, however, share the immunity Dad's Note has to D6-type rerolls and Void.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • A Missing Page / Missing Page 2: Deals an additional +40 damage. Effects stack together and with multiple copies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Negative allows access to the Dark Room, which is also the name of a room used to develop photos (Darkroom).

• A negative is a piece of film with an image imprinted on it and developed, and light can be shone through it to imprint a positive image on photographic paper. A negative has inverted hues and luminosity.

fields.description: If Isaac has half a red heart or no red hearts after taking damage, all enemies in the room take significant damage. Allows entrance into the Dark Room. [Repentance] +1 Damage and also allows access to Home. [end edition note]

The Pact.title: The Pact
The Pact.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Grants two Soul Hearts.

• [Repentance] Grants two Black Hearts.

• +0.5 damage.

• +0.7 tears.

• Contributes to the Leviathan transformation.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Black Feather: Counts as an evil item, granting a damage up.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item appears on the six of hearts in the official Binding of Isaac Tarot Card deck. In this illustration, the pact is titled "Your Soul," and the body of the contract consists of the text from the bridge of the song "Deal with the Devil," by Judas Priest. The pact is signed by "E" and "R.C."

• [Before Repentance] Brimstone has the same appearance of The Pact, but with big, curved horns and slightly less angry eyes.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Grants two Soul Hearts, +0.5 damage, and +0.7 tears.
[Repentance] Grants two Black Hearts, +0.5 damage, and +0.7 tears. [end edition note]

The Parasite.title: The Parasite
The Parasite.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Tears that deal more than 1.0 damage split into two tears with half damage and half remaining range on impact with obstacles or enemies.

• Damage less than 1.0 causes the tears to simply disappear.

• The splitting can keep up as long as the tears have range remaining and the damage of the split tears stays above 0.5.

• Split tears are scaled down by 0.5x from the parent one, ignoring damage based size reduction.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Angelic Prism: All tears split by the prism will burst into split tears when hitting obstacles.

• Azazel: Two beams that deal full damage are fired perpendicular to the main beam at the end of the laser.

• Brimstone: Two beams that deal full damage are fired perpendicular to the main beam at the closest point of intersection with an enemy or obstacle.

• C Section: Fetuses fire short-ranged tears constantly while in contact with an enemy.

• Compound Fracture: Both tear split effects happen simultaneously.

• Cricket's Body: Two groups of this item's four tears, creating eight additional miniature tears on every point of impact instead.

• Flat Stone: Every time tears bounce, burst tears spawn.

• Holy Light / Other similar tear modifiers: As the effect is applied before the split, both split tears will retain it.

• Jacob's Ladder: Split tears can spawn sparks.

• Lachryphagy: Fed tears split into 12 tears. When tears are minimally fed and hit an obstacle, they will split into 5 Lachryphagy burst tears and Parasite burst tears.

• The Ludovico Technique: Repeatedly spawns miniature tears when on top of an enemy, greatly increasing damage.

• Mom's Knife: Knife splits into two smaller, perpendicular knives that deal full damage on hitting an enemy.

• My Reflection: Split tears boomerang back to Isaac, making it easier to hit enemies with them.

• Piercing tears: Split tears form for each hit as the tears pass through the enemies.

• Spectral tears: When tears pass through solid objects, like rocks, they will split, resulting in many tears shooting out from every rock the original tear passed through.

• Technology: Laser splits into two perpendicular beams that deal full damage upon hitting an obstacle or enemy.

• Tiny Planet: The split tears will continue to orbit Isaac, increasing damage potential.

• Tractor Beam: The split tears will be forced directly forward, impacting whatever caused the first tear to split. This increases damage immensely.

• If all shots connect, effective damage will be multiplied by 2 + log2(damage) rounded up, with the maximum increasing as range increases, with a max of 4x at Isaac's base range.

• Trisagion: When beams hit obstacles, the beam will split; the split beams can split again when hitting other obstacles.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Aquarius: Creep trail turns dark orange but doesn't affect the creep itself.

• Bob's Rotten Head: Splits into two explosive shots when it blows up on an obstacle or wall, each dealing half the explosion of the head. Doesn't split on hitting an enemy.

• Brimstone: Overrides The Parasite.

• Diplopia: Additional copies of The Parasite have no effect.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs turn orange and with no other effect.

• [edition anr] Bombs split into two bombs that deal 24 damage each upon detonation.

• [Repentance] Bombs split into two bombs that deal 40 damage each upon detonation.

• • Dr. Fetus + Rocket in a Jar: Rockets split into two bombs (not rockets) upon detonation.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides The Parasite.

• Eye of the Occult: Split tears can be controlled similarly to normal tears, which results in a large amount of floating tears.

• Ipecac: The Ipecac tear will spawn two smaller explosive tears when it collides with a solid object, but not with an enemy. These tears can spawn tears on their own as well, potentially leading to huge chain reactions. Having Host Hat or Pyromaniac is strongly recommended.

• Kidney Stone: Drastically decreases range making it less likely for tears to split. The stone will not split.

• Mom's Knife: Knife turns orange with no other effect.

• Rubber Cement: Tears only split when hitting enemies and no longer off the wall or most obstacles.

• Sharp Key: Split tears from thrown keys are normal tears.

• Soy Milk: Without any damage increases, Soy Milk tears deal under 1.0 damage and cannot split until the situation is rectified with other items.

• Spirit Sword: No effect on swings and spins. Projectiles bursts into 2 small tears.

• Technology: Overrides The Parasite.

• Tech X: Overrides The Parasite. Laser rings become orange.

• [Repentance+] The ring produces small tears in contact with enemies.

fields.description: Isaac's tears split in two when they hit something.

The Peeper.title: The Peeper
The Peeper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that slowly floats diagonally around the room and bounces off walls. The eye blocks enemy shots and deals 8 damage per tick or about 17.1 damage per second to enemies it passes through.

• Gives tears shot from Isaac’s left eye a red appearance.

• [Repentance] All tears shot from the left eye will deal 35% more damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Bloat. [end edition note] 

• The empty eye leaves behind a small blood trail. This doesn't affect anything and is a purely cosmetic effect.

• The Peeper is distinguishable from the eyes emitted from Peep by the size of the pupil, it being noticeably bigger on The Peeper.

• [Repentance] A slightly better Peeper familiar can be spawned by The Scooper. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • The Scooper: When used, causes Isaac's right eye to be scooped out too with the same benefits as the left, effectively granting Isaac a 35% damage boost.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that slowly floats around the room in a zig-zag pattern, damaging enemies it passes through. [Repentance] Increases the damage of tears from Isaac's left eye by 35%.

The Pile.title: The Pile
The Pile.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Pile is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in Necropolis, as well as in the Ashpit in the alternate path.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Pile slowly slides around the room slowly and performs the following attacks:

• Burrows underground, then quickly reemerges elsewhere in the room and fires 5 bone projectiles in a spread towards Isaac. The Pile repeats this attack 3 times in a quick succession. It will generally try to reemerge close to Isaac or directly in his path to cut him off.

• Summons a Bony with a maximum of 2 alive at once.

• Summons spikes in each of its cardinal directions which start at the edges of the room and move towards the Pile.

• Charges in Isaac's direction and continues until it rams into a wall or an obstacle, creating two diagonal lines of rock waves away from the wall and launching a spray of bone projectiles in Isaac's direction. If it runs into an obstacle it also destroys it along with any other obstacles in a small radius.

• The Pile gains dramatically increased knockback resistance while charging.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Callus and Orphan Socks prevent Isaac from taking damage from spikes summoned by The Pile.

• Flat File has no effect on these spikes.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Pile originates from a conceptual Reddit post by NotYourSaggitarius on the Binding of Isaac subreddit in 2015. A few days later it was programmed into Rebirth by Kilburn, before being incorporated into the Antibirth mod.

• In Antibirth, The Pile could appear as a boss in the Mausoleum.

• It is a skeletal variant of Polycephalus and an even further decayed version of The Stain.

• This makes Polycephalus the only boss in the entire game to have more than one posthumous version.

• In its boss art, the rightmost head lacks 2 teeth on the bottom jaw, unlike its enemy sprite.

• The Pile is one of two bosses that can appear in both the main path and the alternate path, appearing in the Necropolis as well, the other being Reap Creep, who can appear in the Depths and Dank Depths.

• Because of this, its battle theme will be different, depending on where it's fought. If it's fought in Necropolis, either Crusade or Cerebrum Dispersio will play, while if it's fought in the Ashpit, Juggernaut will play.

The Pinking Shears.title: The Pinking Shears
The Pinking Shears.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Not to be confused with the Scissors or Safety Scissors.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Separates Isaac's head and body for the current room. Isaac's head, which now has flight, will be under the player's control, while his body will seek out enemies to attack by contact damage.

• The body's movement speed is dependent on Isaac's speed.

• [Before Repentance] The body deals 5.5 damage per tick, or up to 82.5 damage per second.

• [Repentance] The body deals 5.5 damage per tick, or up to 23.6 damage per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The damage of the body familiar is independent of Isaac's stats. [Before Repentance] Its damage per second is the highest of all chasing familiars.

• [Repentance] If Isaac's body is not visible (for example, through the effects of Transcendence or previous uses of the Pinking Shears), the familiar will gain Flight and take upon a ghost-like body, similar to the Lost's body type.

• If used multiple times in the same room (via battery pickups, for example), more instances of the body familiar can be spawned.

• [Before Repentance] If Isaac switches active items while The Pinking Shears is in effect, the body will immediately despawn for the rest of the room.

• The body familiar will avoid creep, and will consequently rarely damage enemies like Brains and Blighted Ovum that leave creep trails as they walk, instead opting to stand right next to them.

• Using The Pinking Shears just above an obstacle results in the body becoming stuck in the terrain, making it useless until the obstacle is destroyed.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Damage dealt by the body is doubled.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps on the inner ring, looking like Isaac's floating head. Wisps fire piercing tears.

• Car Battery: Two bodies are spawned at once.

• Tainted Forgotten: Only the head needs to be moved by the Tainted Soul.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Scissors: If Scissors and Pinking Shears are used together, control is given back to an invisible head with only a shadow visible as both the head and body are mobilized to attack.

• Guillotine: Using The Pinking Shears after picking up Guillotine results in the head revolving around a shadow, making Isaac's hitbox difficult to determine.

• The Intruder: If the familiar is released after Pinking Shears are used, control is given back to an invisible head with only a shadow visible. This is due to both the head (the spider) and the body being mobilized to attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, The Pinking Shears were unlocked by dying 100 times. In Rebirth, this unlocks Scissors instead.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, the familiar of this item had the same instant-kill property on contact with Fly and Pooter variants that an item like Halo of Flies has. This effect is removed in Rebirth.

• Pinking shears are shears with a serrated blade and are used for cutting canvas.

• [Before Repentance] Isaac's headless body looks similar to a Pacer.

• [Repentance] The body shares the same appearance as Isaac's body but with blood gushing from the top, similar to a Gusher.

fields.description: Separates Isaac's head from his body for the current room, granting flight and turning the body into a familiar that chases enemies.

The Polaroid.title: The Polaroid
The Polaroid.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• If the character has half a red heart or no red hearts after taking damage, it triggers the Book of Shadows effect, creating a shield that nullifies all types of damage for 5 seconds.

• Allows entrance into Chest after beating Isaac in the Cathedral by touching the chest.

• [Repentance] Opens A Strange Door in Depths II and its variants that leads to Mausoleum/Gehenna II. [end edition note] 

• Unlike with the Chest entrance, The Polaroid gets consumed by the door and vanishes from Isaac's inventory.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item is a guaranteed drop from Mom, if unlocked. Will drop alongside The Negative, provided they are both unlocked. However, they are mutually exclusive: Once one of them is picked up, the other one will disappear.

• With the use of either a teleportation item and 5 pip Dice Room, a Forget Me Now, a Diplopia, a Crooked Penny, or R Key, both the Polaroid and the Negative or multiple copies of the Polaroid or Negative can be obtained.

• With Jacob and Esau, proper alignment of both characters can enable picking up both The Polaroid and The Negative.

• With frame-perfect timing and a bomb, it is possible to pick up both The Polaroid and the Negative.

• The Polaroid always triggers when taking damage as characters who lack Red Heart containers, such as ??? and Tainted ???, Black Judas and Tainted Judas, The Soul, Tainted Forgotten, Tainted Bethany or any other character who has chosen to trade away their heart containers in devil deals, Black Markets, Guppy's Paw or the Potato Peeler.

• The shield effect provided by The Polaroid can be stacked if the character takes damage multiple times. For example, using IV Bag 2 times provides 10 seconds of shield.

• Although The Lost and Tainted Lost don’t have health, The Polaroid can trigger if they take non-fatal damage (e. g. take damage while Berserk! is active or imitate damage via Dull Razor).

• The Polaroid will be the leftmost item after defeating Mom, in case [cu: Blind] is active.

• [Before Repentance] It is possible to obtain two Polaroids by obtaining one as an Eden starting item.

• Obtaining multiple copies of The Polaroid does not cause its effect to stack.

• As with all items crucial to story progress (Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2, Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2, Dad's Note, and Dogma), this item has protection from full-run rerolls. It does not, however, share the immunity Dad's Note has to D6-type rerolls and Void.

• If Isaac took fatal damage and is revived in the same room, The Polaroid will trigger upon revival.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac flash game, The Polaroid used to be a trinket that Mom would drop in addition to a regular collectible from the boss pool. When it was originally implemented, it was only available in the normal Trinket drop pool and was implemented secretively. Players were frustrated, so, with an update, Edmund made it so it would also only drop if the player took no red heart damage against Mom, similar to the conditions for the Devil Room to open its path. Since players would not always receive the Polaroid and might switch it out with another trinket, Edmund wanted to make the discovery of Chest (and its at-the-time new ending) something special.

• In the game files, the sprite for The Polaroid can still be seen in the trinket sprites folder.

• As soon as The Polaroid or The Negative become available, they will drop in place of the regular Boss Mom would otherwise provide, essentially providing a difficulty increase for Womb and beyond after either has been unlocked.

• They can, however, be re-rolled (or converted into stat increases with Void) at the cost of closing off access to Chapter 6.

fields.description: If Isaac has half a red heart or no red hearts after taking damage, he gains a shield that nullifies all types of damage for 5 seconds. Allows entrance into Chest. [Repentance] Also allows access to Home. [end edition note]

The Poop.title: The Poop
The Poop.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, spawns a pile of Poop where Isaac is standing and knocks back nearby enemies. This pile of poop may yield pickups like regular poop.

• [Afterbirth onward] Also knocks back pickups and enemy shots upon use.

• Contributes to the Oh Crap transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• ??? starts with this item by default.

• In combination with Petrified Poop, this item becomes far more useful. With moderate luck, a poop pile spawned by this item may drop the trinket itself, and with a method of generating unlimited battery charge, it becomes a matter of time. With the trinket, The Poop can easily become a better source of Hearts and money than other items that require more charges, such as Book of Revelations or The Book of Sin.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] This item can spawn as a possible payout of Mystery Gift. Mystery Gift can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] This item can rarely drop from destroying buckets in Dross.

• It can also be spawned by Bumbino if he picks up 12 cents. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Dingle. [end edition note] 

• Poops can bridge gaps when bombed from the opposite side (the same way standard rocks can).

• If used on top of an obstacle while flying, it will only produce its sound effect, but no poop will be spawned.

• [Before Repentance] This also applies to destroyed obstacles.

• If Isaac has Thunder Thighs, Leo, or Stompy, the poop will be destroyed beneath you as soon as it is placed.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] After defeating Ultra Greedier, all remaining piles of poop in the room will be converted into Golden Poops.

• [Repentance] This effect is purely visual; the "golden" poop acts as regular poop despite the recolor. [end edition note] 

• The Poop can be used to permanently destroy Red Poops while they're temporarily disabled. [Repentance] The same is true of retractable spikes while they're retracted.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Bird's Eye / Ghost Pepper: Fire will appear behind Isaac when The Poop is used.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps on the outer ring, looking like miniature Dips. Wisps' tears have a 2.5% chance to apply E. Coli to enemies, turning them to poop.

• Brown Cap: The Poop may be used as a discounted Mine Crafter, both for utility, as well as combat.

• Gigante Bean: Deals 10 flat damage to nearby enemies.

• Hallowed Ground: Using The Poop will always spawn a White Poop.

• Meconium: Using The Poop has chance to spawn a Black Poop.

• Midas' Touch: Using The Poop has a chance to spawn Golden Poop.

• The chance of this effect is 100% at [Before Repentance] 5 Luck / [Repentance] 6.56 Luck

• 9 Volt: Can be used in an incomplete room to repeatedly spawn poop.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Dirty Mind: Allows the creation of extra Dip familiars.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in BRAINS! and Scat Man.

• In the flash version, The Poop was unlocked by defeating Mom's Heart 10 times.

• [Repentance] A rare closet exists in Downpour and Dross with The Poop as a guaranteed item. If Isaac has already found The Poop, the item in the closet does not change. [end edition note]

fields.name: The Poop
fields.description: Spawns a pile of Poop where Isaac is standing and knocks back nearby enemies. It may yield pickups like regular poop.

Isaac's Heart.title: Isaac's Heart
Isaac's Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Isaac's body becomes immune to all damage.

• [Before Repentance] Most enemies now target the heart instead of Isaac. Eyes and other similar enemies, however, will still target Isaac.

• [Repentance] Isaac's body becomes immune to all damage from enemies and the environment. This does not include interactable objects such as Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars.

• A heart familiar appears and closely follows Isaac. If the heart is hurt, Isaac is hurt.

• [Repentance] The heart tries to position itself in the opposite direction of where Isaac is shooting.

• [Repentance] The heart charges up as Isaac fires. At full charge, upon releasing the fire button, it knocks back nearby enemies and tears, creates a small puddle of red creep on the ground, and releases blood shots in 8 directions that deal 8 damage.

• [Repentance] Enemies pushed into walls or obstacles by the knockback blast take 10 + 2 * (floor - 1) damage.

• [Repentance] Enemies that come in contact with Isaac take 2x Isaac's current damage per tick or 4x Isaac's damage per second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars can be used for free.

• During The Guardian, Devil Beggars and Blood Donation Machines deal damage to Isaac.

• Spikes, Curse Room doors and Spiked Chests do no damage. Sacrifice Room spikes still work, though the heart has to go on the spikes instead of Isaac. [Repentance] The door to Mausoleum / Gehenna is not affected. [end edition note] 

• Picking up a non-orbital familiar will cause either Isaac's Heart or the other familiar to be layered over the other's sprite. This is due to the heart not taking up the spot that the other familiar follows in.

• Co-op babies gain the immunity effect without spawning additional hearts.

• [Rebirth only] Enemy Brimstone shots (such as from The Bloat) will not do any damage to the heart.

• [Repentance] Enemy Brimstone shots will now be blocked by the body. This visually resembles the blocking effect of Divine Intervention.

• The tracking lasers from Hush and light pillars from Isaac do not damage the heart.

• Isaac will turn into The Lost form if either he or the heart touches a White Fire Place.

sections.heading: Items / Trinkets
sections.text:
• Items that activate on contact with enemies retain their ability, allowing Isaac to use them without suffering collision damage.

• [Before Repentance] Items that hurt Isaac on activation, such as IV Bag and Blood Rights no longer do so, allowing infinite uses for free.

• [Before Repentance] Get 5 cents as soon as possible so an Arcade can show up, Blood Donation Machines and IV Bag are the best and most common ways to win Isaac's heart run.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If Lucky Penny are unlocked, it may be beneficial to immediately try to gain 10 luck or more via the IV Bag to maximize room drops and enhance tear effects.

• Speed up items are invaluable when having Isaac's heart since the delay between the player moving away and the heart moving as well gets drastically reduced. Avoid speed down items early in the run.

• Orbital familiars are invaluable as Isaac can get extremely close to the enemy without fear of contact damage.

• Flight items are invaluable as the heart can be placed over a rock and Isaac can stick out enough to shoot at enemies without needing spectral tears.

• Angel Rooms are safer bets for items than Devil Rooms.

sections.heading: Combat and Damage
sections.text:
• Hug obstacles to avoid taking damage. Look out for enemies that fly or can jump over rocks, and make sure enemies don't push Isaac far away from his heart to expose it.

• When dodging, Isaac must move in semi-straight lines as the heart only follows Isaac's movements when he is at a certain distance away, for example, moving in a circle would pull the heart in and make it stay in place in the middle of the arc as Isaac would no longer be moving away from the heart. Moving in a triangle formation would allow the heart to move more.

• If dodging requires traversing long distances, it is recommended to shoot in the opposite direction to the movement direction (e. g. shoot left when moving right). This way, the heart will be positioned very close to Isaac, making the process easier.

• Enemies that fly and charge like One Tooth are extremely hard to dodge and should be killed as soon as possible, take caution since they can appear as early as Caves / Catacombs.

• Enemies can be pushed away with Isaac's body, while not recommended, it can be used as a last resort.

• [Repentance] To avoid taking damage from Mega Troll Bombs, push into them while firing at them, instead of running away.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 120 Volt/Monstrance: These items become much safer to use offensively as they are centered around Isaac's body which no longer takes damage.

• Blood Rights: Blood Rights doesn't deal damage to Isaac, allowing repeated usage without penalty. [end edition note] 

• Box of Friends: Box of Friends does not duplicate the heart, making it safe to use.

• Breath of Life: Isaac can be infinitely invulnerable, as invincibility carries out to the heart without hurting the player. Note that the item needs to be activated for longer than one second for the invulnerability to kick in, however.

• [Repentance] Works as normal except for the fact that the damage to the heart must be blocked to spawn the 4 beams.

• Duct Tape: Makes dodging significantly easier.

• E. Coli: Isaac can turn enemies into poop without taking damage.

• Holy Mantle: The shield effect carries over to the heart.

• Gigante Bean: Makes the heart much easier to defend as it increases the knockback amount and radius of the heart when fully charged and the heart makes farting noises when it shoots.

• Items granting invulnerability or a shield: The invincibility carries over to the heart.

• [Repentance] Due to the contact damage, Gnawed Leaf allows Isaac to clear most rooms without moving.

• IV Bag: Can be used without taking damage, resulting in an infinite amount of coins.

• Kamikaze!: As long as the heart is away from the blast radius, no damage is taken. The character must be at high enough speed for this.

• Pyromaniac / Host Hat: Explosion immunity carries over to the heart.

• The heart must be in range of explosion for Pyromaniac to heal Isaac.

• Razor Blade: Isaac cannot take damage from the Razor Blade, allowing for infinite uses of the item.

• Sacrificial Altar: Can remove the Isaac's Heart familiar while the item remains, making Isaac invulnerable.

• [Repentance] Sacrificial Altar now doesn't remove Isaac's Heart.

• Serpent's Kiss: Isaac can poison enemies by contact without taking damage, allowing for free black hearts.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Aries: The invulnerability does not extend to the heart.

• Baby-Bender: The heart's tears do not gain homing.

• BFFS!: Fires additional shots in random directions, and leaves larger puddles of creep.

• Dry Baby: If Isaac has obtained Dry Baby in the first familiar spot before Isaac's Heart, the baby will block enemy tears before they can hit the heart. Enemies touching the heart can still do damage, and picking up the baby after the heart will cause the heart's hitbox to be checked first against shots.

• [Repentance] Isaac's Heart no longer follows Isaac in a way where Dry Baby can constantly block it from tears.

• Farting Baby: If Isaac has obtained Farting Baby in the first familiar spot before Isaac's Heart, the baby will block enemy tears before they can hit the heart. Enemies touching the heart can still do damage, and picking up the baby after the heart will cause the heart's hitbox to be checked first against shots.

• [Repentance] Isaac's Heart no longer follows Isaac in a way where Farting Baby can constantly block it from tears.

• King Baby: The Heart will follow King Baby. This makes it much harder to avoid damage, but also makes other synergies like Kamikaze! much easier to use.

• A Pound of Flesh: Consumables can no longer be picked up in Shops.

• Sharp Plug: Sharp Plug can no longer be used.

• The Soul: Isaac's body repels projectiles, but Isaac's Heart doesn't.

• Tainted Forgotten: The heart follows Tainted Soul.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Isaac's Heart while it's following Isaac fittingly shares the same sprite as Child's Heart.

• The nature of the item is similar to that of a Mask + Heart enemy.

• This item is used in The Guardian.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: When picked up by Tainted Lazarus after picking up Birthright, the character which has Isaac's Heart can be damaged even in ghost form.

fields.description: Isaac himself is now immune to all damage, and a heart familiar follows him. If the heart is hurt, Isaac is hurt. [Repentance] The heart charges up as Isaac shoots, firing 8 blood shots, knocking back enemies, and leaving a puddle of creep when released.

Isaac's Tears.title: Isaac's Tears
Isaac's Tears.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Each tear shot by Isaac increases item charge by one.

• Upon use, fires 8 tears around Isaac, which retain the damage, range, shot speed, and most special tear effects of his tears.

• [Repentance] Tears from this item have a +5 flat damage bonus.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The effect of Tammy's Head is similar to Isaac's Tears, but Isaac's Tears will not benefit from tear-replacing items like Brimstone.

• [Before Afterbirth+] It takes 1.3 seconds to use, during which time Isaac cannot shoot tears normally. Because of this it is only worth it to use Isaac's tears DPS-wise if 4 or more tears successfully land.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] It takes 0.4 seconds to use, during which time Isaac cannot shoot tears normally.

• [Repentance] It takes 0.1 seconds to use, short enough that it usually will not interrupt shooting tears normally.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Fires a ring of 10 tears instead of 8, the tears are piercing and spectral, and the tears deal 1.4 × Judas' damage, plus a flat 5.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Summons six wisps at a time, in the middle ring. Using Isaac's Tears destroys the previous set of wisps. The wisps are automatically destroyed after three seconds.

• Car Battery: The damage of tears from the item is doubled.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Brimstone / Mom's Knife:

• [Before Afterbirth+] The item fires normal tears, although it will charge nearly instantly while the attack charges.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Fires normal tears. Charges at the same rate as Isaac's fire rate while charging Brimstone/Mom's Knife.

• Brimstone + Lachryphagy: When tears burst, they will shoot out Brimstone lasers in a fashion similar to Tammy's Head.

• Brimstone: Adds up to 4 charges for the duration of the laser. (If the player cancels the laser early, less charges will be given)

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Chocolate Milk: The size and damage of tears fired depend on how far Isaac has charged up his shot. For example, if Isaac has completely charged his shot, the tears fired by the item will be fully charged.

• Cursed Eye / Neptunus: Adds one charge per each shot.

• Dr. Fetus: Fires normal tears.

• Epic Fetus:

• [Before Repentance] The item fires normal tears, but charges very quickly as the crosshairs are moved.

• [Repentance] The item charges even while the crosshair is not moving, with the speed based on Isaac's tears stat.

• Eye of the Occult: Makes the tears controllable and able to be made most use of.

• [Repentance] Mom's Knife / Tech X / Chocolate Milk: Adds one charge per shot regardless of how much the tear was charged up.

• The Ludovico Technique:

• [Before Repentance] The item charges based on the tear's movement.

• [Repentance] The item charges even while the tear is not moving, with the speed based on Isaac's tears stat.

• Spirit Sword: The item fires normal tears and can be charged as fast as the sword can be swung. Doing a spin attack will fully charge Isaac's Tears.

• Technology / Technology 2: Fires normal tears.

• Trisagion: Fires Trisagion beams. [Repentance] Does not gain the additional +5 damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Isaac's Tears is unique in that it's the only activated item that charges by simply firing tears.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: With Brimstone and Chocolate Milk, the attack can be charged past the fully charged point, firing massive, extremely damaging tears when Isaac's Tears is used.
Bug note: When Isaac's Tears is in the first active item slot of Schoolbag, the secondary item does not charge upon clearing rooms.

fields.description: Fires 8 tears around Isaac, which use his damage, range, shot speed, and tear effects. Shooting charges this item. [Repentance] Tears from this item have a +5 flat damage.

Isaac's Tomb.title: Isaac's Tomb
Isaac's Tomb.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns an Old Chest at the start of each floor.

• Old Chests are similar in appearance to Locked Chests and likewise require a Key to unlock, but have the color of a normal Chest and a worn-down appearance. When opened, they contain one of the following:

• 1-3 Soul Hearts (43% chance)

• 3 trinkets (42% chance)

• An Old Chest item (10% chance)

• An Angel Room item (5% chance)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The chest also spawns in the mirrored floor of Downpour II and Dross II if picked up before entering.

• During the Ascent, the chest spawns in the original starting room of each floor, right above the beam of light to the floor above.

• The chest does not spawn in Home.

• Does nothing on Tainted Lazarus if the new floor is entered by the character without Isaac's Tomb.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Death Certificate : An Old Chest will appear in the Death Certificate area, unless Death Certificate is used on the floor where Isaac's Tomb was obtained.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Crooked Penny / Diplopia: Additional copies of Isaac's Tomb have no effect. Only one chest is spawned at the start of the floor.

• Gilded Key / The Left Hand / Mom's Key / Poker Chip: No effect.

fields.description: Spawns an Old Chest at the start of each floor.

It Hurts.title: It Hurts
It Hurts.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Taking damage causes Isaac to release a ring of 10 tears and gain tears up for the current room. [Repentance+] For the rest of the room, Isaac's tears, including the initial ring of tears, leave pools of red creep where they land.

• The first hit taken increases Isaac's tears fired per second by 1.2, then by 0.4 for every subsequent hit in the same room. This ignores the tears cap and can stack indefinitely.

• Each tear in the ring deals 10 damage and doesn't use Isaac's tear effects.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Varicose Veins: Two rings of tears are released at once.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It Hurts originates from the Antibirth mod, and by extension, from the Community Remix mod for the flash version.

• In Community Remix, it was a simple stat up and damage multiplier item which multiplied damage by 1.3, added 1.0 damage, and added 0.3 speed.

• The splash text "No it doesn't..." could reference the fact that Isaac has a sewn shut mouth, making him unable to say that it does.

fields.description: Releases a ring of tears and increases fire rate for the current room when Isaac takes damage. [Repentance+] Isaac's tears also leave pools of red creep for the rest of the room.

It Lives!.title: It Lives!
It Lives!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: It Lives! is a boss that can appear on the second floor of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb). It is unlocked by beating Mom's Heart 11 times; after that, it permanently replaces it.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
It Lives! behaves identically to Mom's Heart, with the exceptions of different spawns for its phases:

• In phase 1 its order is now:

• 2 Eyes

• 3 Flesh Mobile Hosts

• Polycephalus

• Fistula

• In phase 2 its order is now:

• 2 Knights

• 4 Walking Boils

• Teratoma

• Chub

• In phase 3 its order is now:

• 3 Lumps

• 3 Globins

• 4 Tumors

• 4 Hearts

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: A Halo, Flooded Caves, Dank Depths, Scarred Womb, Lost Baby, Cute Baby, Glass Baby, Shadow Baby, Dead Baby, Crow Baby, Fighting Baby, Wrapped Baby, Begotten Baby, Glitch Baby, -0- Baby, Goat Head Baby, Super Greed Baby, Smelter, Marrow, Wisp Baby, Double Baby]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Just like Mom and Mom's Heart, using The Bible or XV - The Devil? against It Lives! will kill it instantly.

• [Afterbirth onward] Isaac can encounter It Lives! in the nightmare boss wave of chapter 4 in Greed/Greedier mode even if it has not been unlocked.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It Lives! appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac. Unlike its appearance in Rebirth, It Lives! had opened eyes, a simple poker face, and hung to the ceiling in a sideways position via an umbilical cord.

• The music that plays during this fight is titled Ventricide. Ventricide is a portmanteau formed from the word ventricle (chamber of the heart) and the suffix -cide, which denotes an act of killing. This theme is used in other tracks, such as Matricide, Hericide, and Infanticide.

• Ventricide could also be a junction of the prefix ventr- (from the latin word venter), which could denote "belly", "stomach", "womb" or "fetus", with the suffix -cide.

• It Lives! shares this theme with Mom's Heart, and therefore, both interpretations could co-exist.

• It Lives!, according to the developers, takes the shape of what Isaac looked like as a fetus.

• According to Edmund McMillen, It Lives! supposedly represents Isaac wishing that he were never born.

• It Lives! makes the same sounds as Mom's Heart.

• Like Mom's Heart, if Isaac takes damage from It Lives!' Brimstone attack, Mom's laugh can be heard.

• Despite being a major boss, It Lives! isn't linked to any Ending, instead, it opens up entrances to both Sheol and the Cathedral, as well as ??? if beaten in under 30 minutes.

• The unlock note for It Lives! states "Your futures past awaits.", referencing Time Fcuk, another game by Edmund McMillen.

• [Before Repentance] During the versus screen, It Lives!' enemy/boss-spawning sound can be heard. It Lives! is one of [Before Repentance] seven/ [Repentance] five bosses that can be heard during the versus screen, the other [Before Repentance] six/ [Repentance] four being The Stain, The Forsaken, Big Horn, Mom, [Before Repentance] Mom's Heart and Mother.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Sometimes, if the boss intro is skipped, the game will not teleport Isaac into the center of the bottom of the room, resulting in immediate contact damage with one of the Eyes or It Lives!, depending on the direction of the room's entrance.

sections.heading: Item Weight
sections.text:
• Each item that is in an item pool has a weight associated with it. The weight represents how likely it is for the game to spawn the item. Nearly every item in the game has a weight of 1.

• For example, if there are 200 items in a given item pool, and each item has a weight of 1, that means there is a 1 in 200 (0.5%) chance to get any particular item from that pool.

• However, if an item has a weight of 0.5, that means that item is 50% as likely to spawn compared to an item that has a weight of 1. In a pool of 200 items that has only 2 items with a weight of 0.5, that would result in the total weight being 199. ((198 * 1) + (2 * 0.5) = 199) This means items with a weight of 1 have a 1 in 199 (≈0.5%) chance to spawn, while an item with a weight of 0.5 has a 1 in 398 (≈0.25%) chance to spawn.

• [Before Repentance] Only a few items in the game do not have a weight of 1:

• Bomber Boy has a weight of 0.2 in the Bomb Bum pool, making it 80% less likely to encounter.

• Delirious has a weight of 0.4 in Angel Room pool, making it 60% less likely to encounter.

• Mega Blast has a weight of 0.2 in the Devil Room and Greed Mode Devil Room pools, making it 80% less likely to encounter.

• Plan C has a weight of 0.2 in the Curse Room, Devil Beggar, Devil Room, Greed Mode Shop, Red Chest and Shop pools, making it 80% less likely to encounter.

• [Repentance] Item weights were adjusted more extensively in Repentance and Repentance+.
