sections.heading: Weight Decrementation
sections.text:
• When you see an item spawn, the weight of that item is automatically decremented inside of the respective item pool. However, the amount of the decrementation varies depending on the specific item pool.

• If an item happens to be in more than one item pool, the weight decrementation will also apply to other pools.

• Touching an item will remove it from all item pools.

• If a pedestal cycles between multiple items, such as from Glitched Crown, each item option will count as being seen.

The seen items in the following item pools are decremented by 50% on sight:

• Beggar

• Bomb Bum

• Curse Room and Greed Mode Curse Room

• Devil Beggar

• Key Master

• [Repentance] Battery Bum

• [Before Repentance] Shop and Greed Mode Shop

• [Repentance] Mom's Chest

The seen items in the following item pools are decremented by 40% on sight:

• Golden Chest and Greed Mode Golden Chest

• Red Chest

• [Repentance] Ultra Secret Room

• [Repentance] Old Chest

The seen items in the following item pools are decremented by 10% on sight:

• Library and Greed Mode Library

• [Repentance] Crane Game

All other item pools not listed above are fully decremented on sight, and thus, removed.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.text:
• All items in the Treasure Room pool are completely decremented on sight. Thus, seeing a Notched Axe in the Basement 1 Treasure Room will make it impossible to spawn another Notched Axe in the run. (In this case, players do not have to touch the Notched Axe in order to prevent the game from ever spawning another one.)

• [Before Repentance] All items in the shop pool are decremented by 0.5 on sight. Thus, if you use a Restock Machine to reroll a Treasure Map, you have a chance for another Treasure Map to appear. However, after the Treasure Map has already appeared twice on a run, it is completely decremented from the shop pool and it will never appear again.

• [Repentance] All items in the shop pool are fully decremented on sight. Thus, if you use a Restock Machine to reroll a Treasure Map, it will never appear again for the rest of the run.

• If the player sees Telepathy For Dummies in the Basement 1 Treasure Room, it is completely removed from all other pools for the rest of the run even without touching it. Seeing it in a Library and not touching it, however, allows it still to be encountered as a Treasure item, with slightly lowered weight.

sections.heading: [Before Repentance] Unused Item Pools
sections.text:
In the itempools.xml file, we can see that there are some unused item pools:

• bossrush - Likely intended to be used for the Boss Rush. However, in the actual game, the Boss Rush draws from the Treasure Room pool.

• challenge - Likely intended to be used for Challenge Rooms. However, in the actual game, Challenge Rooms draw from the Treasure Room pool.

• dungeon - Likely intended to be used for the Crawl Spaces. However, in the actual game, Crawl Spaces draw from the Treasure Room pool.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Set Drops
sections.text:
• Some specific collectible items are hard-coded to have a chance to drop from certain special events. These are referred to as "set drops".

• [Before Repentance] Set drops from the Seven Deadly Sins are not affected by item pools. For example, if you touch The Virus in the Treasure Room on Basement 1, and then you fight Lust in the Mini-Boss Room of Basement 2, Lust will still have the normal chance to drop The Virus. If it does, you can take it and have two Viruses.

• Set drops from most Machines can be obtained multiple times.

• With the exception of IV Bag, Redemption, and Skatole.

• Famine, Pestilence, War, and Death will always drop Cube of Meat or Ball of Bandages, even if either was already obtained.

• • [Before Repentance] Respectively, if A Pony or White Pony have been touched, then Headless Horseman and Conquest will drop a Boss Room Item instead.

• [Repentance] Hornfel will drop his items in addition to the boss room item, and will only drop 3 bombs once all his drops are seen. [end edition note] 

• Sacrificial Altar's drops are deceptively not from the Devil Room Pool, and are considered set drops.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Item pools can be exhausted by having the game create every item in that specific pool. Items do not need to be picked up for this to happen, the game simply has to generate them (re-rolling the item with The D6 for example).

• When an item pool is exhausted, the game will generate items from the Treasure Room pool instead.

• If the Treasure Room pool is exhausted, the only item that can be generated from it is Breakfast. This game-state is commonly referred to by players as "Breakfasting".

• Even though you technically cannot see items during [cu: Blind] , their weights are still being reduced upon encountering them.

• [Repentance] The same applies to blind items in alternative chapters.

Item Quality.title: Item Quality
Item Quality.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Item quality is a hidden item mechanic added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance, assigned to all items. The quality ranges from 0 to 4 and causes them to behave differently with certain items or automatically get rerolled if certain conditions are met.

sections.heading: Mechanics Affected
sections.text:
• Bag of Crafting: Determines what kind of item is given by the bag, depending on the pickups put into it.

• Birthright (Tainted Bethany): The Lemegeton wisps spawned by this item are guaranteed to be quality 3 or higher.

• NO!: If multiple copies, Mom's Box, or a golden version of the trinket is held, items with quality 0 are rerolled.

• [Repentance+] Poker Chip: If the chest would contain an item of quality 0-2, it is rerolled to get a +1 quality bonus.

• Sacred Orb: Automatically rerolls items with a quality of 0 or 1, and has a 33% chance to reroll items with a quality of 2.

• Tainted Lost: 20% chance of rerolling items with a quality of 2 or less.

• [Repentance+] Abyss: The damage locusts deal is dependent on the quality of the item destroyed.

Item Tags.title: Item Tags
Item Tags.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Item tags are internal metadata, like Item quality, that were added in Repentance. The tags are used to create groups of items which are used in a few different ways.

sections.heading: Examples
sections.text:

• The Lost's Birthright rerolls items tagged nolostbr.

• Tainted Lost can only find items tagged offensive.

Items.title: Items
Items.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Items are an integral part of the gameplay of The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth. They modify Isaac's attributes, grant or modify tear effects, and much more.

Items are classified into several distinct types and groups. Some items are passive, which add an effect permanently to Isaac, while others only activate when used.

• The original The Binding of Isaac had 196 items.

• Rebirth has a total of 341 items.

• [Afterbirth onward] Afterbirth adds 95 new items, for a total of 436 items.

• Updates to the DLC added or enabled a total of 22 items. On release, the DLC's item count was 73.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Afterbirth † adds 111 new items, for a total of 547 items.

• Booster Packs added a total of 42 items. The DLC's original item count was 69.

• [Repentance] Repentance adds 172 new items, for a total of 719 items.

• An update for Repentance, V1.7.5, added 3 new items. The DLC's original item count was 169.

In Afterbirth † and prior, 13 items are considered special and are less likely to appear if Isaac has already come across other special items. The Repentance expansion removed the Special Item mechanic, replacing it with the item weight and item quality mechanics.

For a list of which items can potentially appear in a given special room or under certain conditions, see item pool and Item Tags.

For the grids of items that appear in the stats menu, see Collection Page.

Not to be confused with cards and runes, pills, and trinkets.

sections.heading: Activated Collectibles
sections.text:
Unless Isaac has Schoolbag, only one activated item can be held at a time, with the old collectible being placed on a pedestal if a new activated item is picked up. Most activated items need to recharge before use, with the recharge bar filling either by clearing rooms or recharging over time. Other activated items do not have a charge bar, and, with a few exceptions (such as How to Jump), will instead either disappear after a single use or require resources such as coins or health. Some activated items will also grant passive effects as long as they are equipped.

[Repentance] In some special circumstances, activated items can be placed in the consumable slot instead of the standard activated item slot. This counts as both an extra activated item slot and an extra consumable slot, meaning other activated items and consumables can be picked up as normal. Items in this slot are used with the consumable key, and can't be lost through any means (unless they're consumed like items from Dice Bag). Otherwise, they function the same as other activated items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Battery Bums and most Batteries charge item(s) in the activated item slot first, then the item in the consumable slot. The exception to this is the Mega Battery, which recharges the items in both slots.

• Most trinkets that work with activated items (e.g. Vibrant Bulb, Panic Button, etc.) ignore items in the consumable slot.

• There are a total of 171 activated items.

sections.heading: Passive Collectibles
sections.text:
Passive collectibles are vast and diverse, varying wildly in effect and strength. Some simply improve Isaac's stats, add health, or provide a familiar. Some completely change the way the run can play.

• Other common effects include:

• Isaac's tears gaining Tear effects or causing Status Effects on hitting enemies.

• Isaac's tears being replaced with a completely different weapon, such as a knife.

• Isaac's bombs gaining new effects, often with a bonus supply of extra bombs.

• Triggering a special effect when Isaac takes damage, or kills an enemy.

• Creating additional pickups, either when first collected, or over time.

• Improving active item cooldowns.

• Granting permanent flight.

An unlimited amount of passive collectibles can be held at a time, and the effects they grant usually last until the end of that run.

• Removing a passive item is only possible in a few rare ways, and usually comes with severe drawbacks, such as D4 and Genesis rerolling all passive items, or Clicker removing the last passive item collected at the cost of changing the active character.

• [Repentance] Tainted Isaac is limited to 8 passive items (12 with Birthright) at a time, and can freely swap out old passive items once his inventory is full.

Nearly all passive collectibles alter Isaac's appearance when collected, with newer items replacing the cosmetic effects of older items.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Wiggle Worm was an item in the original The Binding of Isaac; however, in Rebirth, it was changed into a trinket.

• The Polaroid was a trinket in the original The Binding of Isaac, but was changed into an item. Interestingly, these changes keep the count of items and trinkets from the original game the same.

• There are a total of 170 active items, with 74 in Rebirth, 19 in Afterbirth, 30 in Afterbirth+, and 47 in Repentance. Of those, 138 items possess a charge bar, with 61 items in Rebirth, 16 in Afterbirth, 24 in Afterbirth+, and 37 in Repentance.

• There are a total of 547 passive items, with 267 in Rebirth, 76 in Afterbirth, 81 in Afterbirth+, and 123 in Repentance.

• From Rebirth to Afterbirth+, there has been about a 1:4 ratio of active items to passive items.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Afterbirth+'s original item count was 89. The Booster Packs added 42 items.

Jacob's Ladder.title: Jacob's Ladder
Jacob's Ladder.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the Afterbirth † item granting electric tears; the renamed Antibirth item granting Angel Room shops; The Stairway]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Tears fire 1-2 sparks of electricity in random directions upon hitting an obstacle or enemy.

• [Repentance] Tears fire 1 short-ranged spark of electricity in a random direction upon hitting an obstacle or enemy. When an arc strikes an enemy, it will strike another nearby enemy, chaining up to four times.

• Sparks deal half of the tear's damage.

• Sparks behave like spectral and piercing lasers and will arc to hit enemies that are close enough, even striking multiple ones in a row.

• An enemy can take damage multiple times from sparks of a single chain. If an enemy take damage from a tear, it does not take any damage from the chain which the tear causes.

• Tears that hit the floor due to running out of range do not generate arcs.

• [Repentance] If the floor is wet, such as Downpour, Dross, Flooded Caves, some rooms in Scarred Womb and Corpse, and after using Flush!, the arcing distance is increased. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Multiple battery-themed items have special synergies with the sparks:

• Sharp Plug / Car Battery: Electricity deals 75% of Isaac's tear damage if he owns 1 of these items, and 100% if Isaac owns both.

• 9 Volt / Watch Battery / Hairpin: Increases arcing distance of sparks.

• The Battery / Jumper Cables / AAA Battery: Increases amount of arcs a spark can generate.

• Old Capacitor: Allows sparks to arc on the same enemy multiple times.

• Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Jacob's Ladder it turns into a pale blue locust. 

• [Before Repentance+] The locust can create arcs of electricity dealing 0.1 damage per tick.

• [Repentance+] The locust can create arcs of electricity dealing 25% of Isaac's damage per tick.

• Angelic Prism: All of the split tears will be electrified. [Before Repentance] Also, the sparks that pass through the prism will be split.

• [Repentance] Brimstone / Azazel / Tainted Azazel: The beam gains a light blue tint, spawning sparks at the end of the beam and near enemies hit by the beam.

• C Section: Spawns the sparks for each tick they hit.

• Little Horn: Enemies hit by the sparks also get hit with Big Horn's hand.

• Lost Contact: Tears block enemy shots as normal and will then spawn the sparks where the shot was blocked.

• A Lump of Coal: Sparks deal damage based on the tear's range, increasing with distance. No extra damage is applied by the distance covered by the spark.

• [Repentance] Mom's Knife: The knife will occasionally generate sparks when hitting an enemy.

• Piercing tears: A tear will generate sparks for each enemy it hits.

• Spectral tears: The tears can spawn sparks while passing through obstacles, and a tear can spawn sparks only once in this way.

• Tainted Magdalene: Hugs cause sparks to spawn.

• Tear effects: The tear effects will be applied over the sparks as well.

• Serpent's Kiss: The poison caused by the sparks will not drop black hearts.

• Nose Goblin / Sinus Infection: The boogers do not spawn sparks when directly hit on an enemy, but their sparks spawn the boogers for each enemy hit.

• Euthanasia: The sparks coming off of needle shots also act as needle shots themselves, allowing entire rooms to be killed instantly.

• [Repentance] Tech.5 / Technology / Technology 2 / Tech X: Lasers gain a light blue tint and generate sparks.

• Trisagion: Spawns the sparks for each tick they hit.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Brimstone / Azazel: The beams do not spawn the sparks.

• Backstabber: The sparks cannot hit the enemies' backs for the extra damage and bleeding.

• Compound Fracture / Cricket's Body / The Parasite: Split tears can spawn the sparks.

• Dr. Fetus / Epic Fetus: The bombs do not spawn the sparks.

• Haemolacria:

• [Before Repentance] Only the main tear can spawn the sparks.

• [Repentance] Burst tears can also spawn the sparks.

• Ipecac: The sparks spawn only when they hit a wall.

• The Ludovico Technique: The Ludovico tear spawns a large number of sparks when in contact with an enemy, but not on obstacles.

• Mom's Knife: The knife does not spawn the sparks.

• Proptosis: The sparks will decrease in damage based on how much damage the tear has lost. The spark's damage also dereases by the distance covered by the spark.

• Rubber Cement: Tears will only spawn the sparks when hitting enemies.

• Spirit Sword: Both swing attacks and projectiles can spawn the sparks.

• [Before Repentance] Tech.5 / Technology / Technology 2 / Tech X: The lasers do not spawn the sparks.

• Trisagion: Only spawns the sparks when hitting obstacles.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item refers to high voltage traveling arcs, which are colloquially known as Jacob's ladders. It creates a small electric arc rising between two metal rods, as the item graphic represents.

• The name is a reference to The Book of Genesis from the Old Testament. In Genesis 28:10-19 Jacob rested on his journey and had a dream; in the dream, he saw a ladder that served as the connection between Heaven and Earth.

• [Repentance] This item's new effect closely resembles 120 Volt from Antibirth, which was added to the game with a different effect. [end edition note] 

• The Stairway was originally named Jacob's Ladder in Antibirth. It was renamed when being ported to avoid a naming conflict.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: When using The Forgotten's melee attack with both Jacob's Ladder and Haemolacria, the sparks caused by splattered tears will hurt the player. This does not apply to other tear scattering items.
