• Enemies must be actually killed to add a fly; transformations (such as Gapers turning into Pacers) or knockouts (such as incapacitating a Globin) do not count as kills.

• Destroying a Shopkeeper will count as a kill.

• With items that kill normally unkillable enemies, killing things like Stone Grimaces will add flies to the jar.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Using Jar of Flies summons wisps instead of Blue Flies; the wisps do not summon the flies when destroyed. Up to five flies at a time are consumed to summon one wisp, with stacking health and damage. The damage of the wisps decreases as they take damage. Enemies killed by wisps’ tears will not add flies to the jar.

• Fish Tail: Doubles the number of flies that spawn.

• Hive Mind: Flies are bigger and deal double damage.

• Schoolbag: Flies will be gained even while the Jar of Flies is in the inactive slot.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups do not grant extra flies.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop do not grant extra flies.

• Void: Flies will not collect when absorbed by Void, making the interaction worthless.

• Infestation 2: Blue Spiders spawned by Infestation 2 grant extra flies, and Blue Flies spawned by Jar of Flies spawn Blue Spiders.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] The item's pickup quote references the tagline of the Pokémon games. The quote said "Gotta catch 'em all?".

• The updated quote is also a Pokémon reference, with Bug Catchers being common low-level trainers that appear in foresty areas in most Pokémon games.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] With Booster Pack #2, this item's sprite fills up with more flies depending on how many flies it contains. [Before Repentance] This is based on this Steam Workshop mod by Stewartisme.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The synergy of The Ludovico Technique with Brimstone or Technology will not spawn flies.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Gotta catch 'em all?; Repentance: Bug catcher]
fields.description: Killing an enemy adds a fly to the jar, up to a maximum of 20. On use, releases Blue Flies equal to the number of flies in the jar.

Jar of Wisps.title: Jar of Wisps
Jar of Wisps.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a wisp that orbits Isaac, fires tears, blocks enemy shots, and deals contact damage to enemies, much like the ones spawned by Book of Virtues.

• The jar initially spawns only [Before Repentance+] one / [Repentance+] two wisps, but spawns an additional wisp each time the jar is used, up to a maximum of 12 per use. The number of wisps that will be spawned by the jar is indicated by both a counter and the jar visually filling up with wisps.

• The wisps spawned by the jar can be ones created by any Book of Virtues synergy, although basic wisps are much more common than special variants.

• Isaac can have up to 3 rings of wisps; an inner, counter-clockwise spinning ring of 6 wisps, a center, clockwise-spinning ring of 8 wisps, and an outer, counter-clockwise spinning ring of 12 wisps, for a total of 26.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Will only spawn Satanic Bible wisps that increase Judas' Devil Room chance by 10% for each one he has.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Triples the wisps which are spawned including any special wisps spawned.

• Car Battery: The number of wisps spawned is doubled.

• Car Battery + Book of Virtues: The number of wisps spawned is multiplied by 6.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Void: Will spawn only one wisp per use.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• While most wisps that can be given act similarly to normal wisps, there are some with effects that can potentially harm Isaac.

• Anarchist Cookbook Wisps look like bombs and spawn Troll Bombs when destroyed.

• • Mama Mega! wisps look like gold tinted bombs, and will spawn Golden Troll Bombs.

• • Bomb wisps with a gray tint are not dangerous; Doctor's Remote wisps only invoke their special effect when said item is used.

• Wisps that look like gray cubes will invoke the effect of the D7 when they take damage.

• Teleport!/Teleport 2.0 Wisps fade into and out of existence and have a chance to teleport non-boss enemies to a random spot in the current room when their tears hit them.

• Switching the jar with other active items and then picking it up again does not reset the number of wisps that will be spawned on use.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again) will duplicate the wisps. Any extra wisps created from duplication on a filled ring will appear at the entrance of each room Isaac enters and shoot in the direction Isaac is currently shooting.

fields.description: Spawns random wisps that shoot various tears, block shots, and deal contact damage. The number of wisps spawned increases every time the jar is used.

Jaw Bone.title: Jaw Bone
Jaw Bone.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that fires across the room in the direction of the first tear fired and returns to Isaac when it hits a wall, similar to Little Chubby. Deals a flat 7 damage to enemies that come in contact with it.

• When thrown, the familiar will pierce through some fly enemies, instantly killing them, but will instantly bounce back upon hitting other enemies.

• The familiar can pass through obstacles.

• The familiar can retrieve pickups like The Boomerang.

• Blocks enemy tears when stationary and when thrown.

• After returning to Isaac, it has a short recharge time before it can be fired again.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Just like The Boomerang, Jaw Bone can grab pickups through obstacles and will not grab Troll Bombs.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Jaw Bone having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

• The following types of flies are instantly killed when they come in contact with the familiar:

• Army Fly

• Attack Fly

• Dart Fly

• Fly

• Hush Fly

• Moter

• Pooter

• Ring Fly

• Super Pooter

• Swarm

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Familiar grows in size and does a flat 14 damage to enemies.

• Duct Tape: Jaw Bone will face in the same direction as Isaac and remain stationary as opposed to trailing behind him. Jaw Bone can still be fired.

• King Baby: After being thrown, Jaw Bone will return to Isaac and then reappear behind King Baby.

fields.name: Jaw Bone
fields.description: Spawns a familiar that flies through the room while firing, dealing a flat 7 contact damage to enemies and retrieving pickups.

Jawbreaker.title: Jawbreaker
Jawbreaker.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Adds a chance to shoot a tooth instead of a tear, which deals ×3.2 Isaac's damage.

sections.heading: Notes
Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: At base luck, having either increases the chance to 20% and having both to 33%.

• With one of the two, all tears will become teeth at 4 luck. With both, it requires only 2 luck.

• Tough Love: Activation rates are individually applied to each tear, effectively allowing for higher amounts of teeth.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Jawbreaker originates from the Antibirth mod, and by extension, from the Community Remix mod for the flash version.

• In Community Remix, it was named The Jaw Breaker.

fields.description: Adds the chance to fire teeth that deal 3.2× damage; mechanically identical to the passive item Tough Love.

Jera.title: Jera
Jera.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Duplicates all pickups and chests in the room.

• This includes pickups for sale in the Shop; the duplicates can then be picked up for free.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Cannot duplicate other Jera runes and trinkets.

• Duplicated chests will contain exactly the same type of items: if the original contains a pickup, so will the duplicate.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• If obtained later in the run, it is recommended to keep it for the Chest / Dark Room, as their first rooms always contain 4 chests that can be duplicated.

• [Repentance] If Jera is used in the starting room of the Dark room, the newly spawned Red Chests will contain four additional and distinct devil deals.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Quadruples all pickups and chests in the room.

• Wild Card: Jera can duplicate the Wild card, allowing for infinite duplication on the room's pickups.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• D20: Rerolling duplicated pickups will result in both the original item and the duplicate being rerolled into the exact same pickup.

• Diplopia: Does not duplicate Jera.

• Hypercoagulation: Duplicating temporary hearts makes the duplicates permanent.

• Mom's Chest: Cannot be duplicated by Jera.

fields.name: Jera
fields.description: Duplicates all pickups and chests in the room. Cannot clone other Jera runes and trinkets.

Jesus Juice.title: Jesus Juice
Jesus Juice.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.5 damage.

• [Before Repentance] +0.25 range.

• [Repentance] +1.5 range.

• [Before Repentance] +0.5 tear falling speed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• "Jesus juice" is slang for the red wine used in Holy Communion, which is supposed to signify the blood of Jesus. When children take communion, instead of letting them have wine, most churches will let them have grape juice instead, which is why the item is a box of grape juice.

• According to the Repentance trailer, Jesus Juice contains "less than 1% Blood of Christ".

• According to a 2021 interview with Edmund McMillen hosted by BroskiPlays, the name 'Jesus Juice' is also a reference to the term allegedly used by Michael Jackson when giving wine to minors, adding a layer of dark satire to the item’s religious symbolism.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] +0.5 damage, +0.25 range, +0.5 tear falling speed.
[Repentance] +0.5 damage, +1.5 range.

Joker.title: Joker
Joker.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Teleports Isaac to the Devil Room or Angel Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using the Joker in Womb II / Utero II / Scarred Womb II will teleport Isaac to the Devil Room or Angel Room with a trapdoor leading to Sheol or a light beam leading to the Cathedral (respectively). This can be used to skip Mom's Heart and will not count as a kill.

• [Afterbirth onward] After unlocking It Lives!, Devil or Angel Rooms in Womb / Utero / Scarred Womb II no longer contain trapdoors and instead have their normal contents. [end edition note] 

• Using The Joker card can allow Isaac to encounter Devil Rooms or Angel Rooms on floors they otherwise cannot appear on, such as the first floor, or Corpse II.

• Unlike all teleportation cards, the Joker still works normally when [curse: maze] is active.

• [Before Repentance] The Joker cannot spawn in [mode: greed] Greed mode.

• Using the Joker does not affect the spawn chance of Devil and Angel Rooms.

• [Repentance] This includes the 100% chance of an Angel Room appearing after skipping the first Devil Room. If a Joker card is used to teleport to Angel Room and it has not spawned after defeating the boss, the 100% chance will get carried over to the next floor as usual.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • [Repentance] Touching the White Fire Place in Downpour II / Dross II temporarily turns Isaac into a ghost. Using the Joker allows Isaac to take the devil deals for free, which is normally impossible because beating the boss makes Isaac lose his ghost form before entering the devil room. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Eucharist: Always teleports to an Angel Room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• Duality: Teleportation before defeating the boss and choosing a door will follow the normal rules of Devil/Angel Room generation, instead of a 50/50 chance.

• This means that if Duality was taken as a Devil deal, or any other deal with the Devil was made in the run, teleportation will always lead to the Devil Room.

• The room that was chosen this way will be the only one that opens once the boss is defeated.

• Teleporting after choosing a door will always teleport to the same room.

sections.heading: In-game Footage
sections.text: • TBA

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Joker is a special card from a playing card deck. It belongs to none of the 4 suites and sometimes has a red variant. It is oftentimes used as a highest value card, a trump card or other special roles within a game.

fields.name: Joker
fields.description: Teleports Isaac to the Devil Room or Angel Room.

Judas' Shadow.title: Judas' Shadow
Judas' Shadow.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Upon death, respawns Isaac as Black Judas with two Black Hearts in the previous room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Resurrection items activate in a set order. 

• [Before Repentance] Judas' Shadow is 8th in this order after 1up!, Dead Cat, Lazarus' inherent extra life, Guppy's Collar, Lazarus' Rags, Ankh, and Broken Ankh. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Judas' Shadow is 10th in this order after Soul of Lazarus, 1up!, Lazarus' inherent extra life, Dead Cat, Inner Child, Guppy's Collar, Lazarus' Rags, Ankh, and Broken Ankh. [end edition note] 

• Beating bosses as Black Judas will give Completion Marks for Judas and will unlock the associated items and achievements.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Tainted Judas: Revived as Tainted Judas instead of Black Judas.

fields.description: Upon death, respawns Isaac as Black Judas with two Black Hearts in the previous room.

Judas' Tongue.title: Judas' Tongue
Judas' Tongue.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Devil Deals only cost 1 heart container.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Soul heart trades still cost 3 Soul Hearts, rendering this item useless for characters that can only have soul, black or bone hearts.

• [Repentance] An exception can be made for ??? as the tongue reduces devil deal prices as normal.

• Judas' Tongue can retroactively change the price of devil deals.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• A Pound of Flesh / Keeper's Bargain / Keeper / Tainted Keeper: The tongue provides no discounts for any item costing money.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Also reduces the cost of soul heart items by 1 soul heart. Having both also guarantees Devil Room sacrifice items on the first pay (instead of 50%).

fields.name: Judas' Tongue
fields.description: Devil Deals only cost 1 heart. Soul Heart trades still cost 3 soul hearts.

Juicy Sack.title: Juicy Sack
Juicy Sack.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac, leaving a trail of white creep that slows enemies.

• Spawns 1-2 Blue Spiders after every room.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Spider Baby transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Wretched. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars.

• [Before Repentance+] Juicy Sack has 6th priority.

• [Repentance+] Juicy Sack has 8th priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • BFFS!: Juicy Sack spawns an extra Blue Spider.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac and drips a trail of slow creep, spawning 1-2 Blue Spiders after each room.

Jumper Cables.title: Jumper Cables
Jumper Cables.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Grants an active item charge every 15 enemies killed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Destroying a Shopkeeper will count as an enemy killed.

• Multiple copies of this item do not grant more charges.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Jacob's Ladder / 120 Volt: Increases the amount of arcs a spark can generate.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups don't count towards the kills needed to grant an active item charge.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Turning enemies into poop doesn’t count towards the kills needed to grant an active item charge.

• [Repentance] Freeze Effects: Enemies that die from being frozen don't count towards the kills needed to grant an active item charge.

• [Repentance+] Frozen enemies do contribute to the charge counter.

• Isaac's Tears: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Jumper Cables is based on this Steam Workshop item by Ashkait and Scayze.

fields.description: Grants an active item charge every 15 enemies killed.

Jupiter.title: Jupiter
Jupiter.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance+] Grants two empty Red Heart containers and restores half a red heart.

• [Repentance+] Grants two full Red Heart containers.

• -0.3 Speed.

• Standing still causes Isaac to build up speed at a rate of +0.25 per second, up to a +0.5 speed bonus.

• Isaac charges up while standing still. Moving releases a fart cloud behind Isaac, damaging and inflicting Poison on enemies that pass through it and draining the speed buff at a rate of -0.25 speed per second. The fart clouds are left behind for the duration of the speed buff.

• The fart clouds deal 0.5× Isaac's damage per tick (1.5× Isaac's damage per second), and last ~2.5 seconds.

• Isaac is immune to Poison from enemies, such as Gasbag or Mushrooms.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• As the speed buff requires Isaac to stand still, Jupiter is effectively a speed down.

• The fart clouds are mechanically independent of the speed increase. Even while at max speed, the fart cloud must be charged by standing still.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Camo Undies: Damaging enemies with the fart clouds will not take away Isaac's camouflage.

• Dark Arts: Stays in effect even while using Dark Arts, allowing Isaac to deal more damage to nearby enemies while invulnerable.

• Gigante Bean: Greatly increases size of fart clouds.

• Tainted Forgotten: Gives a flat +0.20 speed boost and +2 soul hearts with no other effects.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Jupiter, as well as Neptunus, was designed for the original Antibirth mod, but never actually implemented until Repentance.

• Jupiter's effects and pickup quote reference the planet Jupiter's nature as a gas giant, being composed mainly of hydrogen and helium in gas and liquid form.

• The item's ability to create fart clouds after standing still and poison immunity could be a reference to Nuclear Throne, where the character Frog has similar abilities.

• [Before Repentance+] Jupiter is the only item that gives a half-full heart container on pickup.

fields.description: +2 red Heart containers, -0.3 speed. Isaac builds speed while standing still, and releases poison gas clouds when he moves afterwards.

Kamikaze!.title: Kamikaze!
Kamikaze!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, creates an explosion on Isaac's position.

• The explosion damages Isaac for half a heart of health (or a full heart in Chapter 4 onward).

• [Before Repentance] The explosion deals 40 damage.

• [Repentance] The size and damage of the Kamikaze! explosion is identical to that of a Mr. Mega bomb, dealing 185 damage in a wide radius.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The explosion will damage Soul Hearts before Red Hearts, unlike most other self-damaging active items.

• Despite the explosion usually damaging Isaac, Kamikaze! is not considered a self-damaging item because it is not the item's use which causes the damage, but rather the resulting explosion. This has a few consequences:

• Kamikaze! does not bypass invincibility, which means items such as Holy Mantle or Tooth and Nail work normally.

• [Before Repentance] Devil Room/Angel Room chance is lowered if red heart damage is taken.

• [Repentance] Devil Room/Angel Room chance will not be lowered if red heart damage is taken.

• Kamikaze!'s cool down length is as long as the invincibility frames Isaac normally gets from being hit. This means that Isaac cannot activate Kamikaze!, and then activate Kamikaze! again before the invincibility frames end.

• Synergizes with many bomb-enhancing items such as Bob's Curse, with exceptions listed in Interactions.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blind Rage: With longer invincibility, Isaac can use Kamikaze! a second time without taking damage.

• Book of Belial interaction: Invokes the effect of The Necronomicon effect along with the original effect.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring that looks like small sticks of dynamite. The wisps fire explosive projectiles and explode when destroyed, dealing 30 damage to enemies that are close to it. This explosion is small enough to not always hit Isaac, although it will hurt him should he get caught in it. All explosions the wisps make are unaffected by BFFS! and bomb synergies. Using Kamikaze! will also trigger an explosion on each dynamite wisp.

• Dark Arts: Kamikaze can be used for free while Dark Arts is active.

• Glitter Bombs: Has a chance to drop a pickup or trinket each time it is used.

• Gnawed Leaf: Activating Kamikaze will cancel out of the statue state, but Isaac will not be damaged by the resulting explosion.

• Host Hat: Allows unlimited uses without consequences.

• Mars: Isaac is invincible during the dash, allowing for unlimited uses with careful timing.

• Nancy Bombs: Gains the effect of a random bomb synergy each time it is used.

• Pyromaniac: Allows unlimited uses and heals without consequences.

• Each use will heal Isaac for [Before Repentance] one full / [Repentance] half a red heart.

• Scapular: Damage from the explosion will trigger Scapular's effect, allowing Isaac to trigger on-damage effects infinitely between rooms.

• Sigil of Baphomet: Isaac can chain-kill enemies without taking explosion damage while the shield is active.

• Schoolbag: The cool down before the player can use Kamikaze! again is eliminated when switching items. Depending on how fast the player can push the buttons, Kamikaze! can be used multiple times during Isaac's invincibility frames.

• Tainted Forgotten: Explodes on Tainted Forgotten’s body, meaning that it is safe to use infinitely, so long as Tainted Soul is not within the blast radius.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• The following items have no effect:

• Blasting Cap

• Bob's Bladder

• Car Battery

• Mr. Mega

• Rocket in a Jar

• Scatter Bombs

• Sticky Bombs

• Panic Button: Isaac will use Kamikaze before taking damage, similarly to Swallowed M80, with the exception that, if Kamikaze triggers on red health, it will not affect devil/angel deal chances, effectively preserving it.

• Jacob and Esau: Jacob will always take damage if he activates the item. Esau will take damage when he uses it, but only if Jacob is not inside the blast radius. If Jacob is within the blast radius, he will take damage despite Esau holding the item, and Esau will not take damage.

• Soul of the Forgotten/Strawman: The Forgotten or Keeper will take damage if they are caught within the blast radius.

• Swallowed M80: The damage received from Kamikaze itself cannot trigger the trinket, and the activation of the trinket applies a cooldown to Kamikaze (as if it was used).

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The term kamikaze comes from the Japanese language (神風, divine wind), and refers to Japanese pilots that would blow up their aircraft and themselves to damage enemy targets during World War II.

• This item is used in Blue Bomber.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, Kamikaze! dealt a full heart of damage instead of half.

fields.description: Creates an explosion around Isaac, damaging him and nearby enemies as well as destroying obstacles.

Karma.title: Karma
Karma.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Donating to a Donation Machine has a chance to do one of the following:

• Heal Isaac for a full Red Heart

• Spawn a Beggar

• Get a Penny back, directly added to Isaac's total

• Increases the chance that donating to a Donation Machine will increase Isaac's luck.

• [Repentance+] Reduces the chance of the Donation Machine jamming.

• [Repentance+] Donating to a Beggar has a chance to do one of the following:

• Get a Penny back, directly added to Isaac's total

• Heal Isaac for a full Red Heart

• Increase Isaac's luck

• [Repentance+] Blood Donation Machines, Devil Beggars, Confessionals, and Hell Games have a chance to do one of the following:

• Heal Isaac for a full Red Heart

• Spawn a Beggar

• Increase Isaac's luck

• [Repentance+] Shop Restock Machines have a chance to increase Isaac's luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Karma / Mom's Box / Golden Trinket: The luck increase granted by Donation Machines grows with each effect/trinket copy stack granting +1 luck per stack up to +5 luck.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] Karma's sprite was changed for Booster Pack #5.

• The trinket's sprite is a Triskelion, also known as a Triskele.

• While there is no connection between the triskelion and the concept of karma itself in any culture, the Celtic Irish considered the triskelion and its three spirals a representation of the cycle of birth, life and death, which could be associated with the karmic cycle.

fields.name: Karma
fields.description: Donating to a Donation Machine, Blood Donation Machine, or Confessional has a chance to heal Isaac for a full Red Heart or spawn a Beggar. Increases the chance that donating to a Donation Machine will increase Isaac's luck. [Repentance+] Reduces the chance of the Donation Machine jamming. Donating to a Beggar has a chance to heal Isaac for a full Red Heart or increase luck.

Keeper.title: Keeper
Keeper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the playable character; the monster; Keeper (Enemy)] 
Keeper is a secret character added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth.

Keeper is unlocked by donating 1000 Penny to the Greed Donation Machine. Keeper starts with 1 Bomb and a triple shot similar to The Inner Eye.

• Keeper starts with Wooden Nickel after defeating Isaac with Keeper.

• Keeper will start with Store Key after defeating Satan with Keeper.

• Keeper will start with 1 coin pickup after defeating Hush with Keeper.

• [Repentance] Keeper will start with 3 Coin Hearts instead of 2 after defeating Hush with Keeper. If Hush has not yet been beaten with him, Keeper can still gain one extra Coin Heart container with a Health Up.

• [Repentance] Instead of using Coin Heart containers to trade for Devil Deal items, they must be bought using coins. 1 Red Heart and 2 Red Heart deals cost 15 and 30 cents, respectively.

• Devil Deals created by Satanic Bible are also paid in coins.

• Paying cents for Devil Deals will remove the Angel room appearance chance as normal.

Unlike other characters, Keeper uses coins as health. He starts with 2 Coin Hearts, loses one every time he is damaged, and heals for one every time he obtains a coin, at the cost of a cent.
If Keeper loses Coin Heart containers (Health Down, [Before Repentance] Devil Deals, etc.), a Health Up will increase his health back up. 

All types of hearts are transformed into blue flies. [Repentance+] Gold Hearts are an exception, and immediately turn into coins when picked up.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Keeper when initially unlocked is one of the game's weakest characters due to his frailty, lack of healing, and slow fire rate and speed. After unlocking the starting Wooden Nickel, he becomes a high-risk, high-reward character who can dominate the late game if played strategically. By beating Hush with him and unlocking his free third Coin Heart, he can enter Curse Rooms without needing a Health Up, and faces less risk when playing Sacrifice Rooms.

• It is recommended that players who struggle with Keeper play in Normal Mode to obtain his key unlocks before attempting the more challenging Hard Mode.

• Keeper can be quite a tedious character to unlock, because the player needs to deposit 1000 Coins to the Greed Donation Machine, which takes multiple good runs and good enough luck for the donation machine to not jam/explode too early.

• [Before Repentance] Keeper cannot have more than 2 Coin Hearts.

• [Repentance] Keeper cannot have more than 3 Coin Hearts. This cap applies even before Hush is defeated.

• The only three exceptions to this are Greed's Gullet, which allows him to have up to [edition alternatives: baseline: 6; Repentance: 7] Coin Hearts, and Birthright and Mother's Kiss, which allow him to have an additional Coin Heart.

• • [Repentance] Greed's Gullet in combination with Deep Pockets can allow Keeper to reach 12 Coin Hearts at 600 coins.

• • 
• It is possible to reach 15 Coin Hearts at 900 coins. Any Coin Heart containers past the max of 12 will appear as an additional row beneath the standard 2 rows of Coin Hearts, similar to Magdalene's Birthright.

• Theoretically, Keeper could gain limitless Coin Hearts by generating and smelting Mother's Kiss, as each copy would grant a heart container, eventually bypassing the 12 heart container cap.

• If the effect of Mother's Kiss is doubled via Mom's Box or a Golden Trinket, Keeper will also receive an extra coin.

• Keeper always takes one full Coin Heart of damage, which means he cannot have half Coin Hearts.

• Effects that regenerate half a Red Heart, such as Charm of the Vampire or Placenta, regenerate a full Coin Heart for Keeper instead.

• Because Keeper can usually not have less than one full heart, items such as Whore of Babylon and Empty Vessel cannot be activated.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The effect of Clicker can allow Keeper to have half Coin Hearts.

• [Repentance] The effect of Clicker will now fill one Coin Heart if Keeper would otherwise have no health.

• The amount of blue flies created from each heart depends on the type of heart.

• Half Red Hearts are transformed into 1 blue fly.

• Full Red Hearts, Blended Hearts, Half Soul Hearts, Rotten Hearts, are transformed into 2 blue flies.

• Full Soul Hearts are transformed into 3 blue flies.

• Black Hearts, Double Hearts, Bone Hearts, are transformed into 4 blue flies.

• Eternal Hearts are transformed into 5 blue flies.

• [Before Repentance+] Gold Hearts are transformed into 6 blue flies.

• Every time Keeper uses a coin to heal himself, that coin is consumed and isn't added to his current coin amount.

• Double Pennies, Nickels, Dimes and items that give money on pickup (such as A Quarter, A Dollar, Piggy Bank, etc.) will give their amount minus the healed HP.

• Using a Lucky Penny to refill health will not give a coin, but will still give +1 Luck.

• 2 of Diamonds can refill Keeper's health at the cost of 1 coin.

• Counterfeit Penny allows the chance for Keeper to gain the full value of a coin while healing.

• Coin Hearts are generally treated as Red Hearts, such as in [Before Repentance] Devil Room /Angel Room chance, [Before Repentance] Devil Deals, Challenge Rooms, Boss Challenge Rooms, health-recovering items and consumables, and items such as Dark Prince's Crown.

• [Before Repentance] Taking a Devil Deal costing 2 Red Hearts will kill Keeper.

• [Repentance] Getting hit will not lower the chance for a Devil Room/Angel room to appear.

• [Before Repentance] If Keeper doesn't have maximum Coin Heart containers, using XI - Strength will give Keeper an additional Coin Heart that does not disappear upon leaving the room.

• IV Bag only gives Keeper 0-1 coins per use (instead of 1-3).

• IV Bag + PHD: IV Bag drops 0-2 coins per use.

• [Repentance] Blood Donation Machine aren't guaranteed to pay Keeper out with a coin.

• Piggy Bank only allows Keeper to drop 0-1 pennies when taking damage (instead of 1-2).

• [Repentance] Having a partner in True Co-Op mode can get around this, as the Co-Op partner will drop pennies normally (as long as they are not Keeper themselves), giving Keeper a reliable source of health (the drawback being that the partner will have normal health mechanics and therefore won't have infinite health this way).

• [Repentance] Swallowed Penny only allows Keeper to drop 0-1 pennies when taking damage (instead of 1).

• Despite having an innate triple shot, Keeper does not start with The Inner Eye. Because of this, the item can still spawn.

• The Inner Eye grants [edition alternatives: baseline: 6; Repentance: 4] shots with a reduced fire rate.

• [Repentance] Health Down pills cannot spawn while playing as Keeper.

• [Repentance] When Keeper is being played in Co-op mode:

• If he dies, his ghost baby will maintain his innate triple shot.

• He will not convert hearts into flies unless he picks up a soul heart or is granted them directly by an item.

• Devil Deals will use coins for all players.

• Because he cannot pick up hearts, he will not pick up eternal hearts when dead for a free revive.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• Changes to the Tears stat are much less effective on fire rate at or below -0.77 Tears (see Tears for the exact calculations), so Keeper will gain very little fire rate from his first 1.13 added Tears. After crossing this threshold, as he fires 3 tears at a time with no multiplicative fire rate penalty, Keeper can gain far more DPS from Tears than other characters.

• For reference, a Tears Up pill gives 0.35 tears. Assuming no other tears modifiers are taken, Keeper will gain 0.08, 0.1, and 0.12 fire rate from his first three Tears Up pills, and 0.47 from his fourth; over 50% more than his first three combined.

• Items that directly increase fire rate are very desirable for Keeper.

• Due to his [edition alternatives: Before Repentance: 2; Repentance: 3] Coin Heart limit, Keeper can easily die due to fast shooting enemies. As all hearts turn into flies, Soul/Black Hearts cannot be found to protect the Keeper's health.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Keeper can take a 2 heart Devil Deal by spawning in a co-op baby, taking the Devil Deal, then quickly getting rid of the co-op baby, which will leave Keeper with one Coin Heart.

• [Before Repentance] Taking Devil Deals that cost 2 Red Hearts will instantly kill him.

• It is strongly recommended to defeat Isaac as soon as possible so that Keeper has the Wooden Nickel, which will vastly improve his survivability.

• Leaving a few coins on the ground when clearing a floor allows Keeper to heal himself if he takes a hit from an enemy.

• Try to bomb as many urns as possible during Chapter 1; Swallowed Penny can drop from urns, which is amazing as Keeper (see Good Items).

• Urns can also appear in an Angel Room, an Arcade, and the Cathedral.

• In Greed Mode, as coins spawn during waves, Keeper can easily heal himself during each wave by leaving some coins on the ground, even if this will decrease the amount of coins he will be able to collect and spend in the Shop. [Afterbirth onward] Ultra Greed attacks make the player lose coins when damaged, which means that Keeper can heal himself as long as he possesses coins.

• [edition alternatives: baseline: Curse Rooms are very risky to enter as Keeper. Entering it through the door will leave the player at 1 health, meaning that if they don't find any coins there, it will end their run. Even with the Wooden Nickel unlocked, it's not guaranteed that they will leave the Curse Room alive.; Repentance: With 3 Coin Hearts, entering a Curse Room and leaving through the door will leave the player at 1 health, meaning that if they get hit by an enemy inside the room, it will end their run. The Wooden Nickel does reduce this risk.] 

• It is possible to enter the Curse Room and remain at full health. This is achieved with a coin in the room right next to the Curse Room's door, most easily achieved with Wooden Nickel. The player can then walk into the Curse Room doorframe to take damage, quickly pick up the coin and heal, then walk through the door into the Curse Room while their invincibility frames are still active.

• [Before Repentance] It is possible to take a 2 Red Heart Devil Deal by using Judas' Tongue, a Health Up pill, or XI - Strength right after paying for the item. This would leave Keeper at 1 Coin Heart (empty if it was recovered using the pill, but he will not be killed), which is quite risky as he will be one hit away from death. However, if the boss item is a normally-useless Health Up, it can make even a 2 heart Devil Deal effectively free if Keeper possess a Strength Card and take the boss item after leaving the Devil Room.

• [Before Repentance] It can be useful for the player to hold onto any Joker cards they find, as they will probably be given an item that increases health at some point in their run; before taking it, they should use Joker to see if any 1 heart Devil Deals are available. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] Keeper's Coin Hearts count as Red Hearts for the purposes of Devil Room and Angel Room spawn chances, making Joker Cards, Goat Head and Eucharist invaluable for getting consistent Devil Rooms and Angel Rooms. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] Pills can be risky to take as Keeper since there are many adverse effects in the pool, which can quickly ruin a run should they happen. Picking up PHD is recommended before trying any pills.

• [Before Repentance] The Hematemesis Pill will reduce the Keeper's health, but in exchange, spawn many flies.

• [Repentance] The Hematemesis Pill will drop many coins on the floor, making it very useful for quick health regeration, and Health Down Pills are excluded from the pill pool when playing as Keeper, making using unknown pills slightly less risky. [end edition note] 

• Co-op babies can be used to exploit a Blood Donation Machine and a Devil Beggar because babies still spawn with a whole heart while Keeper always has a full coin; thus, the baby's health can be replenished by spawning/respawning.

• This doesn't work in Chapter 4 and beyond unless Keeper has The Wafer.

• In fights against Hush and}} Mega Satan, bring X - Wheel of Fortune: they will not attack the Keeper until he gets closer to the center of the room, allowing him to spawn a lot of coins from the Slot Machine for healing in the middle of battle.

• The Keeper can utilize the Sacrifice Room much more reliably and efficiently than other characters. To do this, instead of picking up extra dropped coins, leave them all on the floor. When the player finds a sacrifice room, they can repeatedly step on the spikes for a reward, then go pick up a penny left on the floor, and repeat this process until they are satisfied with their rewards. This process is easier in Repentance, as the player can start with 3 Coin Hearts rather than 2.

• Once unlocked, Rib of Greed is particularly useful for Keeper, since it increases the chances of coins dropping after a room clear in place of hearts. This allows for more opportunities to heal.

sections.heading: Wooden Nickel
sections.text:
After beating Cathedral with Keeper, he will start with Wooden Nickel, giving Keeper a source of potential free coins and health.

• It's usually a good idea to use the Wooden Nickel right after entering a room, so that the coin dropped will also work as emergency healing.

• The Battery, Jumper Cables, 9 Volt, Charged Baby, and Car Battery help to further increase the amount of coins produced. Having Habit will recharge the Wooden Nickel whenever Keeper is hit, allowing him to potentially sustain himself endlessly, as long as the Wooden Nickel pays out. Having Habit and Car Battery increases chances for infinite coins.

• Sacrifice rooms can be used much more with the Wooden Nickel, as the coins gained from it can be spent on them.

• 9 Volt can be used to farm charges infinitely in the room before the boss room or a trap room, as the doors will not automatically open after the normal amount of time. It is easiest if there are any immobile or passive enemies.

sections.heading: Shops
sections.text:
After beating Sheol with Keeper, he will start with Store Key, giving Keeper free access to Shops.

The following shop items are particularly useful for Keeper:

• Hive Mind: Enhances the many blue flies Keeper will naturally produce.

• Piggy Bank: Drops 0-1 coins with Keeper instead of 1-2, but still provides increased survivability.

• [Repentance] In Co-Op, a player not using Keeper can take the Piggy Bank instead for its full benefit and thus supply Keeper with coins when necessary.

• Mom's Box: Can drop Swallowed Penny, and makes Swallowed Penny drop 2 coins instead of one, resulting in infinite money.

• [Repentance] While this no longer results in infinite money, having a Swallowed Penny that's twice as effective will drastically increase survivability.

• Any Battery type items (see above)

• Sharp Plug takes only one HP on use.

sections.heading: Item Interactions
sections.text:
• Birthright: Raises Keeper's HP cap by 1.

• [Repentance] Steam Sale: Applies to the Devil Deals.

sections.heading: Good Items
sections.text:
• Because of Keeper's slow rate of fire, any Tears Up items are a boon to him. His tears stat can be raised higher than the normal Inner Eye cap with enough Tears Up. This is because his low Tears stat is separate from his triple shot effect, allowing him to hit the standard Tears levels while having triple shots.

• Flight is useful in general, and it also lets Keeper enter Curse Rooms with less risk.

• [Repentance] Before Hush is defeated, any health increasing items will grant him a 3rd Coin Heart, greatly increasing his survivability. Once Hush is defeated this no longer applies, as he will start with a 3rd Coin Heart from the beginning of the run from then on, although these items can still heal Keeper if he is missing health.

• Since every heart is changed into flies, items that give extra Heart drops like Gimpy, The Virus, Old Bandage, Fanny Pack, Bloody Penny, Serpent's Kiss, Little C.H.A.D., or The Relic become great sources to generate flies. Having Hive Mind also helps Keeper deal extra damage to enemies.

• [Before Repentance] 1up! / Dead Cat: Allows Keeper to trade all of his Coin Hearts in Devil Deals, reviving him with 1 health for Dead Cat, and 0 Coin Hearts and 1/2 Soul Heart for 1up!. Keeper can later regain lost Coin Hearts with health up items.

• 20/20: Causes Keeper to shoot 5 tears in an arc, without decreasing his fire rate.

• [Repentance] 20/20 grants a similar effect to Odd Mushroom (Thin), giving Keeper a massive Tears Up in exchange for a Damage Down.

• Blind Rage: Has good synergies with money-dropping items. Since coins need to complete their animations before Keeper can collect it, the extra invincibility frames give him a bigger window of opportunity to pick them up.

• Brittle Bones: Picking this item up will give a one-time +0.5 tears up ( [Repentance] +0.4 fire rate) and 24 Blue Flies without removing any health. This bonus is retained even if the item is later lost or rerolled.

• Cursed Eye: Allows him to fire [edition alternatives: baseline: 12; Repentance: 15] tears without an increase in tear delay.

• Charm of the Vampire: Charm of the Vampire works with Coin Hearts, therefore providing a consistent source of healing.

• Dim Bulb: Very useful with the Wooden Nickel, as using it at the start of any room or beforehand will grant a hefty boost to most stats.

• Diplopia / Credit Card: Can be used to take Devil Deals without spending any [edition alternatives: baseline: hearts; Repentance: coins] 

• Glass Cannon: Since Glass Cannon can never reduce Isaac's health to 0 it works well in early game with Keeper for killing bosses and large groups of fast enemies, especially when holding Dark Prince's Crown or Dead Cat. It's also useful for speeding up the run when the player's goal is Boss Rush or Blue Womb.

• Greed's Gullet: Allows Keeper's health to extend past [edition alternatives: baseline: 2; Repentance: 3 or 4 coins with Birthright] . 

• [Before Repentance] Do NOT pick up Dead Cat if Keeper has all hearts available while using Greed's Gullet. This will instantly kill him, and when he is brought back by the Dead Cat, he will only have 1 heart container which he can no longer increase. [end edition note] 

• Head of the Keeper: Very useful since enemies will drop coins when hit, which will help Keeper stay alive.

• When combined with Soy Milk, it practically guarantees a steady stream of coin drops. This makes the Keeper effectively immortal as long as he keeps collecting those coins.

• Holy Mantle: Allows Keeper to enter and leave Curse Rooms with less risk.

• [Before Repentance] The Inner Eye / Mutant Spider: Causes Keeper's fire rate to drop considerably, but in exchange he shoots 6/7 tears, respectively, in an arc, allowing for greater damage output. [end edition note] 

• Lucky Rock: Can allow Keeper to get coins from rocks as long as he has bombs.

• Missing Page 2: Will activate every time Keeper is at one coin Heart, making it an effective replacement to The Negative's The Necronomicon effect.

• Moving Box: Can be used to drop multiple coins in a potentially harder room or boss fight.

• Options?: Hearts spawned will immediately turn into blue flies, giving Keeper both the flies and the other pickup.

• Piggy Bank: Works differently with Keeper and doesn't drop coins every time he takes damage. Still, it allows him to sometimes recover from a hit for free. 

• [Repentance] The same is true for Swallowed Penny. [end edition note] 

• Petrified Poop: Similarly to Lucky Rock, allows for Keeper to acquire coins (and flies) from poops.

• Placenta: Regeneration effect affects the Coin Hearts just like regular red hearts and will allow the Keeper to regenerate 1 Coin Heart every minute. As Keeper does not benefit from items that trigger at half a red heart, this item has no downsides.

• Portable Slot: Can be used to generate coins to heal Keeper during extended fights and in some cases might be better than Wooden Nickel when money is not a concern.

• Pyromaniac: Explosions heal Keeper for a full Coin Heart. Combined with bomb items such as Kamikaze!, Dr. Fetus, Epic Fetus, Ipecac renders Keeper almost unkillable.

• Items that restore red hearts directly such as Leech and Yum Heart will heal Keeper.

• [Before Repentance] Swallowed Penny: Is very powerful as Keeper will always be able to heal himself after taking a hit. This can also grant unlimited money since this will sometimes drop a nickel or a dime. [Before Afterbirth+] However, invincibility after taking damage does not last long enough to pick up the money without risk of death.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The coin dropped on hit can be picked up before Keeper's invincibility frames end, making Swallowed Penny even better for him.

• If Keeper takes damage from entering a Curse Room, the coin will be dropped on the outside and can't be used to heal before leaving.

• • However, if one quickly enters, exits to collect the coin, and re-enters the room before the invulnerability period ends, the Swallowed Penny allows the Curse Room to be traversed with no net loss in life. Just be wary that there may be enemies in the curse room that would lock the door and prevent the player from leaving and collecting the coin outside the curse room.

• Obtaining Swallowed Penny means you can play the Blood Donation Machine, Devil Beggar and Sacrifice Room practically for free until they pay out since each time you donate a coin to them, you get a coin back.

• • [Repentance] You are no longer guaranteed to get a coin back.

• Tech X: Synergizes well with Keeper's triple shot.

• Tractor Beam: Will make all 3 of Keeper's tears travel along the beam, hitting a single target all at the same time and effectively increasing damage output.

• [Repentance] IV Bag + Panic Button: Panic Button will make it so that when Keeper is about to take damage, IV Bag will activate, giving immunity frames to avoid the initial damage and having a chance to heal Keeper right away. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bad Items
sections.text:
• Health Ups are useless when Keeper has maximum health ( [edition alternatives: baseline: 2; Repentance: 3] Coin Hearts). They still heal him if he has unfilled Coin Heart containers.

• [Repentance] This does not apply if Keeper has yet to defeat Hush, as they can grant him a 3rd Coin Heart until that point.

• It is not recommended to take Bum Friend or Bumbo, as they will pick up coins off the floor that could be used as health.

• [Before Repentance] Taking Abaddon will instantly kill Keeper, since it takes away all Red Hearts (which also includes Coin Hearts) and Keeper cannot make use of the Black Hearts given. Amusingly, it will spawn a lot of flies in the process.

• [Repentance] Taking Abaddon will not kill Keeper as in previous versions, but it will reduce his Coin Heart containers to 1.

• Guppy's Paw will remove a Coin Heart and spawn 9 blue flies. 

• [Before Repentance] Removing all Coin Hearts with Guppy's Paw will not kill the Keeper immediately, but he will die upon picking up an item.

• [Repentance] Removing all Coin Hearts will kill the Keeper.

• Maggy's Bow, The Jar, Dark Bum, Immaculate Conception, Candy Heart, Soul Locket, will not provide Keeper any benefit, as all heart pickups turn into flies.

• Maggy's Faith does nothing for Keeper and will not grant 5 blue flies when traveling to the next floor, like it would if an Eternal Heart spawned.

• Monstro's Lung will take a dangerously long time to charge, giving it terrible usability.

• [Repentance] Mutant Spider / The Inner Eye: Shoots 5 / 4 tears at a time with reduced fire rate. The extra tear rarely compensates for the significant fire rate decrease.

• The Polaroid, The Negative ( [Repentance] though the damage up still applies), Empty Vessel or Whore of Babylon cannot be triggered by the Keeper since he can't have half a heart of health. [Before Repentance] An exception is after being revived by Guppy's Collar, which is a Bug.

• The Wafer and Cancer have no effect, as Coin Hearts cannot be Half Red Hearts.

• Alabaster Box can only be charged with items that directly give Soul Hearts to the player, as Soul Hearts spawned on the ground will be converted into blue flies.

• [Repentance] Judas' Tongue is completely useless with Keeper. It won't decrease 30 Cent devil deals to 15 Cents, and does not have any other effect.

• Heartbreak will remove one Coin Heart and replace it by a broken heart upon pickup.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Sticky Nickels, Super Greed Baby, Keeper holds Store Key, Keeper holds Wooden Nickel, Karma, Deep Pockets, Rib of Greed, Eye of Greed, Keeper now holds... A Penny!, Noose Baby, Crooked Penny, Keeper's Sack, Keeper's Box, The Miser, Sale Baby]

sections.heading: Unlockable Starting Items
sections.text:
• [achievement unlock: Keeper holds Wooden Nickel] - Start with Wooden Nickel

• [achievement unlock: Keeper holds Store Key] - Start with Store Key

• [achievement unlock: Keeper now holds... A Penny!] - Start with 1 coin

• [Repentance] [achievement unlock: Keeper now holds... A Penny!] - Start with 3 [heart: coin] Coin Hearts (instead of 2)

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Keeper was publicly revealed to players through an alternate reality game created by the developers; however, files alluding to Keeper's existence already were found after the initial release of Afterbirth. With the conclusion of the ARG, a patch was released to fully add Keeper to the game as a playable character.

• [Before Repentance] In the game's files, there is a character called "Old Man Keeper", which was most likely meant to be the 2nd Afterbirth character instead of Keeper. However, he was replaced with this Keeper. This sprite is used for April Fool's Day's daily run since 2016, as Keeper's sprite is changed to this sprite for the day.

• Keeper's starting health is listed as "II" on the character selection screen, despite having no red hearts. This is unique among such characters, whose health is usually listed as "-I" or "?".

• [Repentance] The starting health will become "III" after defeating Hush with him.

• The Keeper was created for the sake of being "another challenge character" for this game (the other character is The Lost).

• As a secret character, Keeper does not appear on the character select screen until unlocked.

• He shares this trait with ???, The Lost, and The Forgotten.

• Edmund has confirmed that Keeper (and by extension, Shopkeepers) is a mummified version of Isaac from previous runs.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Guppy's Collar respawns Keeper with half a soul heart

Keeper (Enemy).title: Keeper (Enemy)
Keeper (Enemy).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the monster; the playable character; Keeper] 

Keepers (also known as "Greed Heads") are bodiless Hangers, commonly found in Catacombs and the Dank Depths. They can also be spawned by Super Greed and Ultra Greed, or found alongside Hangers. They move like Hoppers and occasionally stop to shoot two projectiles in a V shape towards Isaac. If hit by these projectiles, Isaac will drop or lose coins.

fields.name: Keeper
fields.environment:
Catacombs / 
Depths / Necropolis / Dank Depths / 
Cathedral / 
Chest / 
Ultra Greed / 
challenge / Shop /
fields.behavior: Hops around the room, firing 2 blood shots in a V formation at Isaac. Upon damaging Isaac, Isaac drops 2 coins on the ground but loses 3.

Dry Baby.title: Dry Baby
Dry Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and blocks enemy projectiles. Upon blocking a shot, it has a 25% chance of triggering The Necronomicon effect, dealing 40 damage to all enemies in the room. This effect of the familiar has a cooldown of 150 frames.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Conjoined transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item can rarely drop from destroying skulls.

• The Necronomicon effect can occur multiple times in the same room with a small delay in-between each activation.

• It can be used to block multiple shots if positioned correctly.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars.

• [Before Repentance+] Dry Baby has 4th priority.

• [Repentance+] Dry Baby has 6th priority.

• It is possible to activate The Necronomicon effect in a different room than the one it was hit in if Isaac transitions between them quickly enough.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Missing Page / Missing Page 2: Dry Baby will deal an additional +40 damage. Effects stack together and with multiple copies.

• Duct Tape: Picking up Duct Tape while Dry Baby has the same position as Isaac will result in Dry Baby blocking almost all projectiles that would hit him while holding the trinket.

• This can be achieved by standing in a doorway, dropping Duct Tape, leaving the room, then re-entering the room slowly.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: No effect on damage or blocking radius; only the visual size is changed.

• Isaac's Heart: [edition alternatives: baseline: If Isaac has obtained Dry Baby in the first familiar spot before Isaac's Heart, the baby will block enemy tears before they can hit the heart. Enemies touching the heart can still do damage, and picking up the baby after the heart will cause the heart's hitbox to be checked first against shots.; Repentance: No longer follows Isaac in a way where Dry Baby can constantly block it from tears.]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A baby born 24 hours after a mother's 'water' breaks is referred to as a 'dry birth'.

• Its name and appearance may be a reference to Dry Bones from the Mario franchise, which are immortal skeletal creatures.

• Its design is likely a posthumous version of Farting Baby, as well as serving the same purpose in blocking shots.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and blocks enemy projectiles. Upon blocking a shot, it has a chance of triggering The Necronomicon effect.

Duality.title: Duality
Duality.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Whenever a Devil Room/Angel Room spawns after defeating a boss, the other will also spawn.

• Upon entering one, the other one will disappear.

• Both rooms will spawn even if a devil deal was made before.

• In rooms without enough accessible walls, only one of the two will spawn.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Even with Goat Head or Eucharist, both rooms will not stay open, and entering either of the rooms will make the other disappear.

• Teleportation via a Joker card, a Red Chest, or a Sacrifice Room before defeating the boss and choosing a door will follow the normal rules of Devil/Angel Room generation, instead of a 50/50 chance.

• This means that if Duality was taken as a Devil deal, or any other deal with the Devil was made in the run, teleportation will always lead to the Devil Room.

• The room that was chosen this way will be the only one that opens once the boss is defeated.

• Teleporting after choosing a door will always take you to the same room.

• Gaining Duality during Greed/Greedier Mode will only generate one room as per normal, rendering it normally useless. However, both rooms will generate in the penultimate floor, The Shop.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Goat Head / Eucharist: Guarantees an Angel & Devil room to spawn after every boss.

• Glowing Hourglass: Time can be reversed while inside one deal to go into another.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Duality is one of only five items to appear in both the Angel and Devil item pools, the others being 7 Seals, Lil Delirium, Void, and Purgatory.

• The Duality image appears to be similar in concept to the yin and yang symbol of Ancient Chinese philosophy, as the latter represents the concept of dualism as well. However, they don't quite appear to be exact in terms of the diameter format.

fields.description: Whenever a Devil Room or Angel Room would spawn after defeating a boss, both rooms spawn. Only one can be entered.

Duct Tape.title: Duct Tape
Duct Tape.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Familiars that are bound to Isaac's movement will be stuck in place relative to his position.

• This includes orbital familiars, shooting familiars and [Repentance] mimicking familiars.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Familiars are stopped in the exact position they are when Duct Tape is picked up. Position of familiars can be changed by dropping Duct Tape and picking it up again.

• Blue Flies and familiars that attack nearby enemies such as Gemini will be stuck, but will still target enemies as usual if within range.

• Throwable familiars such as Little Chubby will still charge forward and will also return to the same spot each time.

• By dropping Duct Tape directly outside of a door, then exiting and re-entering through the same door, all familiars will be perfectly centered on Isaac's position.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Tapping the drop button will cycle familiars into various formations.

• Ball of Bandages / Cube of Meat: No effect at level 3 and 4.

• Dry Baby / Farting Baby: If properly positioned, it can greatly protect Isaac from projectiles.

• This same technique can be used with Lilith to shoot with more accuracy.

• Friendship Necklace + Spin to Win: Familiars affected by Friendship Necklace are still considered orbitals regardless of positioning allowing Isaac to use their contact damage without getting close to enemies. Duct Tape also prevents familiars that weren't already orbitals from flashing when Spin to Win is used despite still being affected by the active item.

• Multidimensional Baby: If properly positioned, Isaac's tears will always be doubled.

sections.heading: No Effect
sections.text: The following familiars will not change their behavior:

fields.description: Holds Isaac's familiars in place relative to his position.

Dukie.title: Dukie
Dukie.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Dukie is an enemy added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth. It floats diagonally around the room, occasionally spitting out 1-2 Dart Fly. Dukies do not attack in any other way but can still do contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If there are 6 Dart Fly spawned, Dukies will stop spawning Dart Flies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Dukies were inspired by a video by LeatherIceCream about a miniature Duke Of Flies.

• The Duke of Flies is the boss version of these enemies.

• Despite the fact that the Duke of Flies is a boss found in Chapter 1, Dukies themselves only begin to appear from Chapter 2 onward, or Chapter 1.5 in the alternate path.

Dull Razor.title: Dull Razor
Dull Razor.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Hurts Isaac without taking away health, giving him invincibility frames equal to a full heart damage and activating any items that trigger upon getting hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] The item will cost 10 cents if found in a Shop.

• As using the Dull Razor will grant extra invincibility frames like normal damage, this item can be used to enter Curse Room for free, or, with proper timing, allow Isaac to avoid taking damage from an enemy or obstacle.

• [Before Repentance] The invincibility frames allow Isaac to use [machine: Blood Donation Machine] s and [machine: Devil Beggar] s for free.

• [Repentance] Dull Razor ignores shields granted by Holy Mantle, and similar items.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a grey wisp on the middle ring. The wisp doesn't fire any tears. Whenever Isaac takes damage, there is a chance that the damage is negated and one of the wisps is destroyed instead. "Damage" taken from using Dull Razor does not count for this effect.

• Car Battery: Dull Razor activates twice, triggering on-damage items twice. Invincibility frames are the same.

• Cambion Conception: Allows for free familiar spawns on repeated use.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
For a full list of items that work with Dull Razor, see the list of damage-triggered items. Note that any specific extra conditions the items may have for their activation still apply.

• [Before Repentance] Blanket / Holy Mantle / Wooden Cross: Absorbs the "hit", wasting both items.

• Cone Head / Star of Bethlehem / Aura from White Poops or White Dips: Can block the "hit" Dull Razor inflicts, nullifying the invincibility frames and causing no effect.

• Crown Of Light: Disables the effect for the current room.

• Habit: Will try to charge Dull Razor itself, but fails due to the effect trigger before the charge bar is emptied.

• Habit + The Battery: Will charge Dull Razor itself only when the charge bar is not filled by extra charges.

• • Habit + The Battery + Car Battery: Will fully charge Dull Razor itself, allowing for infinite uses of the item.

• Habit + Schoolbag: The secondary item will be charged.

• • Habit + Schoolbag + 9 Volt: If Dull Razor is copied into the second active item through an effect such as Diplopia or Crooked Penny, the two Dull Razors can be switched between infinitely.

• Isaac's Heart: Completely nullifies the effect of Dull Razor.

• Perfection: Is not destroyed by a use of Dull Razor, as it counts as self-damage.

• Purity: Cancels the current effect of Purity, allowing a different aura to be gained instead.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The item works almost identically to the Voodoo Pin in Antibirth.

fields.description: Hurts Isaac without depleting health, activating any items that trigger upon taking damage.

Dummy.title: Dummy
Dummy.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Dummy is a special enemy available through the Debug Console's spawn command.

It is immobile, harmless, and visually identical to a normal Shopkeeper but has a damage counter overlaid on the face, adding up any and all damage taken. Touching the Dummy will reset the counter to 0.00.

Although the Dummy has the limited amount of 10000 HP, it is nearly impossible to kill as its health refills completely on every internal tick of the game; it must take 10000 damage in one frame to be destroyed.

The game considers the Dummy to be a boss, giving it resistance to status effects, immunity to instant kills from Euthanasia and Little Horn and practical immunity to Eraser. However, this does allow the Dummy to be killed using a Chaos Card.

fields.behavior: Only encounterable through Debug Console, it is immobile, harmless, and used to track Isaac's damage.

Dump.title: Dump
Dump.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Dump is a monster that is exclusive to Dross.

Dump is consistently in a puddle of Brown Creep and leaves a trail while chasing Isaac. When it takes enough damage, its head comes off and flies around the room while its body spews out brown shots like a geyser until it empties and disappears into the ground.

This enemy has 3 different facial expressions, all of which are purely cosmetic and don't affect how its head looks after it detaches.

sections.heading: Dump Head
sections.text:
Dump Head refers to the head of Dump once its body takes enough damage, although it can also spawn naturally in rooms.

It slides towards Isaac and leaves a trail of slippery brown creep. If split as a result of depleting the Dump’s health, it bounces off walls then chases Isaac.

Dust.title: Dust
Dust.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Dust will slowly chase after Isaac and are completely invisible and intangible when far away. They will only fade into view once they are close enough to Isaac, becoming vulnerable to damage once visible. Once visible, they will also rapidly gain speed the closer they are to Isaac. Each time a Dust takes at least around a third of its HP, it will teleport to a random spot in the room, far away from Isaac. They can fly over obstacles and pits.

E. Coli.title: E. Coli
E. Coli.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Enemies that touch Isaac are transformed into Poop.

• All brown Poops, including those created by E.Coli, now have a 6.25% chance to drop a heart if it normally wouldn't drop anything.

• Contributes to the Oh Crap transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Bosses cannot be turned into poop.

• Enemies that are turned into poop do not count towards on kill effects such as health regeneration from Charm of the Vampire or the damage increase from Lusty Blood.

• [Repentance] This is especially detrimental for Tainted Keeper or Tainted Magdalene which depend on pickups generated on enemy kills.

• Poops created by this item are not tiles, but entities. As such, they are not grid-aligned, and behave differently:

• The poops vanish if the room is left and then returned to.

• Things that automatically target enemies, such as Monstro's Tooth and II - The High Priestess, will also target the poops.

• The poops can be slowly moved by pushing them.

• The poops cannot create a bridge if they are bombed near a pit.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The poops will flash red when hit, similar to damaging monsters.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The poops will crumble when hit, identically to regular poops.

• Touching the middle section of a Grub with E. Coli will split it and create a second head (rather than destroying the Grub and spawning Maggots).

• [Before Repentance] Mullibooms can be turned into poop without taking damage.

• Turning Champion versions of a monster into poop will forfeit the chance to get the champion's drop.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brown Cap : The generated poops explode when destroyed.

• Butt Penny / Petrified Poop: Grants poops made from enemies a chance to drop pickups.

• Death's List: Enemies that die by being turned into poop do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into poop still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.

• Dirty Mind: Enemies that are turned into poop generate double the normal amount of Dips.

• Holy Mantle / Isaac's Heart / Invulnerability : The effect can be applied without taking contact damage.

• Lodestone: If an enemy is hit by a lodestone tear perfectly simultaneously with it being turned into poop, the resulting poop will be tinted black and have a lodestone aura that sucks in enemies. This poop will return to normal after a few seconds.

• Midas' Touch: Enemies touched are turned into Golden Poop.

• Oh Crap: Isaac can heal by destroying poops created from enemies.

• Tainted Forgotten: The body will turn enemies into poop on contact.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bob's Brain : Bob's Brain will explode upon hitting an enemy that has been turned into poop.

• Butt Penny / Petrified Poop: Poops made from enemies still do not drop pickups.

• Hallowed Ground / Meconium: The poop colors are not changed.

• Oh Crap: Destroying poops created from enemies do not heal Isaac.

• Serpent's Kiss / The Virus: The poops won't drop Black Hearts, negating the touch effect from these items on non-bosses.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Escherichia coli is a type of intestinal bacteria present naturally in the human intestinal system. However, some harmful strains of E. Coli can cause food poisoning.

• This item is used in High Brow and Scat Man.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Effects like Monstro's Tooth and II - The High Priestess can target poops created by the item.

fields.description: Enemies that touch Isaac are transformed into Poop.

Echo Chamber.title: Echo Chamber
Echo Chamber.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • When Isaac uses a Card, Pill, or Rune, he also uses a copy of the previous three Cards/Pills/Runes he used after picking up Echo Chamber.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Previously used cards, pills, and runes are effectively used again, meaning items that modify the effects of cards, pills, or runes will also modify the effects that Echo Chamber activates.

• As a result, previously taken golden pills and blank runes will activate a random effect each time Echo Chamber activates them.

• If Isaac uses cards that convert/destroy pickups (such as Ace of Spades, Black Rune, IX - The Hermit?, etc.), any other cards Echo Chamber activates that generate pickups have a high chance to have their pickups converted.

• It is advised to avoid using cards that teleport Isaac, as he will be teleported to a specific room the next three times he uses a consumable. This effectively negates any current-room effects from consumables, such as XV - The Devil or Algiz, during that period, as Isaac is teleported after they activate.

• Similarly, it is also advised to avoid using unidentified pills, as Isaac runs the risk of activating either a stat down or Telepills for the next three consumables he uses.

• When obtained on Jacob and Esau / Tainted Lazarus, Echo Chamber will only duplicate the last three cards or pills previously used on the character with Echo Chamber. As a result, the character without Echo Chamber can safely use teleport cards or unidentified pills.

• If this item is somehow removed and reobtained during the run (such as when obtained from Lemegeton or Modeling Clay), the last three consumable types used during the time Isaac had Echo Chamber will be remembered. Genesis and Victory Laps will erase all of the remembered consumable types, however.

• A card, rune, or pill must be consumed for the effect of Echo Chamber to trigger. That means using Blank Card, Placebo, or Clear Rune will not trigger Echo Chamber.

• Consuming XIV - Temperance? will trigger its effect normally. The pills consumed as a result of using the card are not added to Echo Chamber, and any pills in the current run's pool can be picked as normal.

• While Cracked Key will activate the effect of Echo Chamber and trigger the last three consumables used, using a different consumable near a wall that a red room could be created on will not create a red room, even if a Cracked Key has been used before.

• Getting automatically revived by Soul of Lazarus does not add it to the queue, and directly using the soul stone will not allow for automatic revival in the future.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• ? Card + Ancient Recall / Vurp Pill + R Key: The ? Card effect can be used in conjunction with R Key without consuming it, allowing the player to in theory (with the help of Clicker) obtain completion marks for up to four additional routes and characters in a single run.

• Ancient Recall: Can be used to spawn many extra cards.

• False PHD: Taking benign pills (e.g. puberty) will give black hearts or damage ups for each of the pills that are activated. Caution should be exercised when using this synergy, since the last three pills taken will be converted to their bad counterparts, and one stat down can ruin the synergy.

• PHD, Virgo, or Lucky Foot: The last three activated pills are converted to their good counterparts, including pills taken prior to picking up PHD, Virgo, or Lucky Foot.

• R Key: Using the R key does not reset the consumable pool, as such they stay the same in Echo Chamber too.

• Jera: Allows for repeat duplication of consumables in the room, up to 16x if used four times.

• Suicide King + Dead Cat: Can be used to generate many pickups and items at the cost of three extra lives.

• Tarot Cloth: Every activated tarot card will be given a bonus effect.

• Vurp Pill: Can be used to spawn infinite pills.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Genesis: The consumable pool is reset when Genesis is used, so if it's re-obtained after using Genesis, the previously stored consumable types won't be activated.

• Placebo/Blank Card/Clear Rune: Doesn't cause Echo Chamber to activate, or put the pill/card/rune into the queue.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This is possibly a reference to the card Eye of the Storm from Magic: the Gathering, as the item resembles the art of the card and both result in previous effects being reused when a new one is activated.

• This is also possibly a reference to the card Echo Form from 'Slay the Spire', which will duplicate the card effect of the first card played per turn.

• Before the 1.7.7 patch, Echo Chamber was able to copy the effects of all previously used cards and pills, enabling many powerful synergies such as getting infinite cards and pills with Ancient Recall.

• Echo chamber is a term for the act of surrounding yourself with people and media that only support and agree with one's views and excluding any opposing views or criticism.

• Echo Chamber appears to be a Tarot Card and a Playing Card being sucked into some kind of vortex.

fields.quote: I can see see the future future future
