Eden's Blessing.title: Eden's Blessing
Eden's Blessing.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.7 tears up.

• Grants a random item at the start of the next run.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Quest items, such as Key Piece 1, Key Piece 2, Broken Shovel 1, Broken Shovel 2, Mom's Shovel, Knife Piece 1, Knife Piece 2, and Dogma cannot be granted.

• The effect still occurs whether the run was successful or not, even if the run was restarted.

• The effect does not work if Eden's Blessing was obtained on a seeded run, during a Victory Lap, a RERUN, or during a challenge.

• Likewise, Eden's Blessing will not grant a free item at the start of a challenge or RERUN, instead granting the free item on the next valid run started.

• • Interestingly, seeded runs will still gain the benefit of banked Eden's Blessings, without depleting them. This means that it is possible to play an infinite amount of seeded runs, and they all start with a free item until a normal run is started.

• Even if Eden's Blessing is re-rolled, such as with the D4 or D100, a random item will still be granted at the start of the next run.

• If Eden's Blessing is obtained via a re-roll, it will not grant an extra item in the next run.

• Picking up Eden's Blessing and then using Glowing Hourglass to pick it up again will not reward more than one extra item on the next run.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Absorbing Eden's Blessing with Void will not grant an extra item in the next run. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Removing Eden's Blessing as Tainted Isaac or with Genesis will still grant an extra item in the next run. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Obtaining Eden's Blessing temporarily by using Soul of Jacob and Esau will grant an extra item in the next run. [end edition note] 

• Eden's Blessing can choose itself as the free item you gain, but will not give you an item on your next run.

• If more than one Eden's Blessing is acquired in a single run, that quantity of random items will be granted at the start of the next run, [Afterbirth+ onward] although it's capped at [Before Repentance+] ten [Repentance+] two items.

• It is possible to obtain multiple copies of an item at once this way.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If Eden's Blessing effect is obtained through Metronome, no extra item will be given. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] If gained from Lemegeton, it will not grant an item next run. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Taking Eden's Blessing and then starting a run as Jacob and Esau will only give item(s) to Jacob. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] As Tainted Lazarus, the item will be given to his alive form.

• If Tainted Lazarus somehow acquires the item before flipping for the first time of the run, Eden's Blessing will be consumed upon flip and a random item will be granted to Dead Tainted Lazarus. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] If Strawman picks up Eden's Blessing, the item will be granted on the next run whether Strawman Keeper survives or not.

• XVII - The Stars? can't remove the item(s) given by Eden's Blessing and using it will consume the first item(s) acquired after them or do nothing if there are no other items.

• XVII - The Stars? can remove Eden's Blessing and the item will be granted in the next game.

• Eden's Blessing will never attempt to give more than one activated item. Even if there are multiple Blessings and one of them gives Isaac a Schoolbag, only one activated item can be generated.

• From the bugs listed below, one can potentially "soft-lock" the game by overflowing the number of items one gets. This repeats and crashes until it fully loads, which may take several attempts to load. Anywhere over 1000 Eden's Blessings will have an increased chance to permanently soft-lock the game; therefore, these bugs are highly unadvised to abuse.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Up to 10 Eden's Blessing items will be given per run. Any remaining Blessings will continue to be given each run until you have no more left.

• [Repentance] Free items gained from Eden's Blessing do not carry over to subsequent runs and are capped at 10 free items for only the next run.

• [Repentance+] The cap has been reduced to 2 free items for the next run.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Glowing Hourglass: If Isaac starts with this item and immediately uses it in the starting room, the room will be reset, and all starting items and trinkets removed.

• [Repentance] Instead of the starting room being reset, Isaac is taken to the starting room of Home. If used again in this room without having entered any other rooms, the room will be reset, and all starting items and trinkets removed except Glowing Hourglass. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The white eyes given to Isaac by Eden's Blessing first appear during ending 1, when Isaac falls into the chest and transforms into Eden.

• This is the only item with an effect that applies on a future run.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: A bug may occur when the item is picked up, and Glowing Hourglass is used with either ? Card or The Battery to reverse time, out of the room, restoring your ability to get out using either of the two items and the Eden's Blessing pickup. This will allow you to generate an endless amount of Eden's Blessings, which will all carry over to your next run, and may be repeated endlessly.
Bug note: If Clicker turns the player into Jacob and Esau after collecting Eden's Blessing, any items that would have been normally gained at the beginning of the next run are instead given to Jacob and Esau.
Bug note: If the game crashes on the floor where you have taken Eden's Blessing, that counts as +1 item for the next run. If you continue the saved game and you take Eden's Blessing again, you gain an additional +1 item for that run. This process can grant you unlimited items for the next run.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Your future shines brighter; Repentance: Tears up + your future shines brighter]

Eden's Soul.title: Eden's Soul
Eden's Soul.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the item; the soul stone; Soul of Eden] 
[distinguish visual: Star of Bethlehem]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Upon use, spawns two random item pedestals using the item pool of the current room. Eden's Soul is consumed and vanishes from Isaac's inventory.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Starts with no charges when first picked up.

• [Before Repentance] Unlike Mega Blast, this item can be charged with a single Lil' Battery.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• ? Card: Activates the item without consuming it, allowing for potential multiple uses.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a random wisp. For the rest of the run, a random wisp spawns after clearing a room if the one given by the item was destroyed, including the replacement wisps given by this effect.

• Wild Card: Gives the effect of Eden's Soul if it was the last item/card used.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• The Battery: Eden's Soul cannot be activated twice with a double charge.

• Car Battery: Does not affect Eden's Soul. Only two items will spawn upon use.

• Void: If absorbed, Eden's Soul is stored, and allows for a single use in a desired location. Also effectively reduces charge time to [Repentance] 6 / [Repentance+] 4 rooms.

• [Repentance] Car Battery + Void: Eden's Soul is Voided and then immediately consumed, spawning 2 items from the current item pool. This is likely to be the Angel Room as that is where Eden’s Soul is usually found. Effectively removes the charge time of Eden’s Soul.

• • If Car Battery is picked up after Eden's Soul was absorbed, the next Void use will spawn 2 item pedestals and immediately Void them.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Eden's Soul is one of the three activated items, alongside Alabaster Box and Broken Glass Cannon, that:

• Has no charges upon pickup rather than full.

• Needs to be charged AND disappears upon use. [end edition note]

fields.description: Spawns two random items from the current room's Item Pool and then disappears. Starts with no charges.

• This Rune's effect is identical to We Need To Go Deeper!. See the item page for further effect notes.

Embryo.title: Embryo
Embryo.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Embryos are monsters that hop around the room, dealing contact damage. They are relatively harmless as they do not move much from their position and don’t target the player.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] Embryos count as the Blastocyst boss. Blastocyst still splits into Embryos.

• Embryos bear a strong resemblance to Spewer: the star of the game Spewer which was also created by Edmund Mcmillen, the maker of The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, they have health bars (like mini-bosses or bosses have). This is likely because Blastocyst splits into them.

• Embryos can often be seen in rooms with Blood Donation Machines.

• In the Bestiary, Embryos have a unique appearance in which they're smiling.

Emergency Contact.title: Emergency Contact
Emergency Contact.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Emergency Contact is a consumable item added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns up to two of Mom's Hands that fall down onto two random enemies in the room, dealing 40 damage.

• Enemies with more than 40 HP and bosses will be immobilized for 5 seconds, rendering them unable to move and attack.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Despite it not being a card, the Emergency Contact is considered a special card, having a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• [Before Repentance] When used on Hush, damage resistance is briefly lowered. This can be used to deal additional damage to it.

• Grabs mom's parts when they're out of the doors when used on Mom. Does nothing if no part and monsters are visible.

• Isaac, ???, and first phase of Hush will not retaliate with tears while grabbed.

• The consumable will have no effect if used in a room without enemies.

• [Repentance] This consumable cannot be mimicked by Blank Card, and Tarot Cloth has no effect on it. [end edition note]

fields.description: When used, will cause two Mom's Hands to come down and grab two random enemies, dealing damage and, if they have 40 or more HP, immobilizing them temporarily.

Empty Heart.title: Empty Heart
Empty Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • If Isaac has one red heart or less at the beginning of a floor, an empty heart container is added.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Visage. [end edition note] 

• This item will have no effect for characters that cannot have red hearts: Black Judas, ???, The Lost, Keeper, The Forgotten, The Soul, Tainted Judas, Tainted ???, Tainted Lost, Tainted Keeper, Tainted Forgotten and Tainted Bethany.

• The empty heart containers will replace any other heart containers if the maximum has been reached.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Adrenaline: Activates the damage up effect of Adrenaline if conditions are met to grant an empty heart container at the beginning of each floor.

• Crow Heart: If no Devil Beggars or Blood Donation Machines can be found, the Crow Heart trinket is a great way to guarantee red hearts are lost so long as you still have non-red health available.

• Dark Prince's Crown: The heart containers are empty when granted, which allows the crown's buff to stay active when advancing floors.

• Guppy's Paw: The heart containers granted by Empty Heart can be used by Guppy's Paw while staying at or below 1 red heart, granting massively increased survivability.

• Lazarus: The heart containers granted by Empty Heart allows Lazarus to effectively negate the downside that removes a single heart container on death, allowing him to purposefully use his mechanic to get a +0.5 damage up per floor. (As long as he still proceeds at one red heart or less)

• Potato Peeler: The heart containers granted by Empty Heart can be used by Potato Peeler while staying at or below 1 red heart, granting increased damage and a Cube of Meat per floor.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Isaac is operating only on soul hearts and manages to get 12 empty heart containers by using this item, he will die immediately upon leaving the spawn room or picking up an item.
Bug note: Using Glowing Hourglass to go back to the previous floor will keep the new empty hearts that was obtained from Empty Heart.

fields.description: If Isaac has one red heart or fewer at the beginning of a floor, he gains an empty red heart container.

Empty Vessel.title: Empty Vessel
Empty Vessel.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When Isaac has no Red Hearts:

• Grants flight.

• Every 40 seconds since activation or pickup, when the seconds on the timer hit 00, 20, or 40, while in a room with enemies, a shield triggers, nullifying all types of damage for 10 seconds.

• Grants 2 Black Hearts on pickup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Does not affect Keeper/Tainted Keeper.

• [Before Repentance] This item is difficult to use for anyone with red health, as it is impossible to have no red hearts without removing all heart containers (such as through Devil deals). It is best used by characters that cannot gain red health at all, such as ???.

• [Repentance] Characters can now deplete their red health fully through sources like Blood Donation Machines while having other hearts like Soul Hearts. As a result, this item is usable for a wider amount of characters, and has synergies with characters who prefer to have no red health (such as Eve).

• Rotten Hearts also prevent Empty Vessel's effects.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brittle Bones: The empty Bone Hearts will trigger Empty Vessel.

• Gnawed Leaf: If the player has no Red Hearts, they can stand still and wait for the shield to activate, allowing the player to deal damage without leaving invulnerability.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The changed texture of the player's body is the same as The Lost's, but recolored.

• "Empty vessel" is a religious term for having an open mind so God can fill it with His divine wisdom.

fields.description: Grants two Black Hearts. While Isaac has no red hearts, grants flight and periodically grants an invincibility shield for a few seconds.

Endless Nameless.title: Endless Nameless
Endless Nameless.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • When Isaac uses a consumable pickup like a pill or card, there is a 25% chance to spawn another copy of it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Endless Nameless is especially useful when used with item multiplier playing cards.

• The new consumable will spawn before the effect goes through. This means teleportation will leave the new copy in the previous room, [Before Repentance] and item conversion or destruction cards like Ace of Diamonds and Black Rune will consume the new copy [end edition note] .

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Vurp! + D20: Consuming two Vurp! pills consecutively can spawn an infinite amount of Vurp! pills.

• Gold Pill: A new gold pill may be spawned with each use, allowing for very easy exploitation (if Isaac has an item that removes negative effects).

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either of these effects raises the chance to 33%. Having both of them raises the chance to 50%.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Blank Card / Placebo / Clear Rune: Consumable effects activated by the items do not generate copies of it.

• Echo Chamber: Echoed effects do not spawn their corresponding consumable, only the one used will have a chance to reappear.

• XIV - Temperance?: The card may only copy itself, not the pill effects it generates.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] Endless Nameless' sprite was changed for Booster Pack #5.

• Endless Nameless is a reference to the hidden track of the same name on Nirvana's album, Nevermind.

• The Pickup Quote is a reference to Time Fcuk, a 2009 flash game by Edmund McMillen.

fields.description: Has a 25% chance of creating a duplicate of any pill, card, or rune Isaac uses.

Envy.title: Envy
Envy.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Envy is a mini-boss and one of the Seven Deadly Sins.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Envy floats around the room diagonally, bouncing off the walls.

• He splits into 2 medium heads upon death which split into 2 small heads each when destroyed. These small heads split one last time into 2 even smaller heads when destroyed.

• The last head killed drops a Troll Bomb or Shoop da Whoop!.

• The heads increase in speed as they split into smaller versions.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [edition anr] Occasionally, 2 regular Envies appear in a Mini-Boss Room and the boss message will display "Isaac vs. Super Envy".

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Both Envy and Super Envy are extremely vulnerable to Contagion as their relatively low health generally ensures that the poison effect will persist all the way down to the smallest heads. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] Envy can drop Shoop da Whoop! even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Sin]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Envy's expressions are a reference to "rage comic" memes, with the biggest and smallest heads showing a troll face and poker face, respectively.

• Envy and Super Envy have a lower chance of dropping their item than the other sins.

• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived.

• Envy is a personification of one of the Seven Deadly Sins. Envy is described as resentment or sorrow at the success or good fortune of others. It is believed to lead to hatred, slander, and gossip aimed at ruining the reputation of others.

or

Epic Fetus.title: Epic Fetus
Epic Fetus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Dr. Fetus]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac's tears are replaced with guided missiles. Pressing the fire buttons spawns a crosshair that can be moved freely, dropping a missile on its position from above 1.5 seconds later.

• Missiles deal 20 times Isaac's damage.

• Isaac's tear delay determines how quickly a new missile can be fired after the previous one has landed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Epic Fetus is a special item.

• [Before Repentance] Epic Fetus overrides most items in the game and has the highest priority of all tear modifiers, over Brimstone and Mom's Knife.

• Missiles benefit from some bomb modifier items, though at a lesser scale compared to Dr. Fetus.

• Stacking multiple copies of the item causes a barrage of missiles in quick succession without resetting the crosshair's position, up to sixteen at a time.

• Missiles deal a full heart of damage to Isaac if they deal 85 or more damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] 20/20/Conjoined [end edition note] /Bookworm/Mutant Spider/The Inner Eye: Fires a barrage of missiles corresponding with the amount of tears.

• Bomber Boy: Missiles explode in a large cross-shaped blast, with each explosion dealing 0.75x times damage. Unlike with regular bombs, getting hit by every separate explosion from Epic Fetus won't decrease the damage for each successive explosion, drastically increasing damage.

• Blood Bombs: Every missile explosion leaves a large, lasting pool of red creep.

• Blood Clot/Chemical Peel: Each missile has a 50% chance to deal 20 or 40 points more damage, respectively.

• Poison tears: This is guaranteed by Bob's Curse, Ipecac, and Scorpio, and also has a chance to trigger from The Common Cold, Pinky Eye or Serpent's Kiss.

• [Repentance] Explosions leave behind a cloud of poison gas that will poison enemies in contact with it aside from the main target.

• Brimstone: Missile explosions shoot ten blood lasers in all directions.

• Brimstone Bombs: Missile explosions have a chance to shoot four Brimstone lasers in the cardinal directions. The chance scales with Isaac's luck.

• Butt Bombs: Missile explosions will cloud up the screen, briefly confusing and dealing 10 damage to all enemies in the room.

• Eye Sore: More marks appear orbiting around where you're aiming.

• Fire Mind/Hot Bombs: Missile explosions leave behind a fire that damage enemies on contact. Fire Mind's burn effect is overridden.

• The Forgotten: The charge attack is replaced by a missile in the Forgotten's hand and a crosshair that may be moved for an indefinite amount of time. The missile is thrown at the crosshair when all attack buttons are released, with an additional melee swing in the same direction. The melee attack is unaffected.

• Glitter Bombs: Missile explosions have a small chance of spawning pickups.

• [Afterbirth onward] Homing tears: The crosshair slowly slides towards enemies.

• Host Hat/Pyromaniac: Isaac becomes immune to his own airstrikes.

• Incubus: Incubus fires a missile alongside Isaac's.

• [Before Repentance] Ipecac: Missiles have a poison effect, have a larger blast radius and deal drastically increased damage, as the +40 damage from Ipecac is run through the damage multiplier of Epic Fetus.

• [Repentance] Adds flat +2 damage instead of +40. Explosions leave behind a cloud of poison gas that will poison enemies in contact with it aside from the main target.

• Lil Clot / Tainted Eve: The clots have their own targeting reticles and fire simultaneously with Isaac.

• Mom's Knife: Missile explosions shoot a ring of ten knives.

• [Afterbirth onward] With a second Mom's Knife a second missile will be shot similar to 20/20. [end edition note] 

• Monstro's Lung: 2 to 4 additional crosshairs orbit the main crosshair, and missiles are fired onto each crosshair.

• Mysterious Liquid: Every missile explosion leaves a small, lasting pool of creep.

• Nancy Bombs: Explosions have a chance to be affected by any of the bomb-modifier effects that synergize with Epic Fetus.

• Polyphemus: Increased tear delay, but massively increases the missiles' blast radius and damage, as Polyphemus' damage multiplier is run through the damage multiplier of Epic Fetus.

• Sad Bombs: Missile explosions fire ten tears in all directions. The shrapnel's damage is not run through the damage multiplier of Epic Fetus.

• [Repentance] The chance for the effect to proc is dependent of Isaac's luck. Chance goes up to 100% at 30 luck.

• Sticky Bombs: Missile explosions leave a puddle of slowing white creep.

• [Repentance+] Missiles also spawn Blue Spiders and Blue Flies upon damaging an enemy.

• Strange Attractor: Enemies, pickups and trinkets get drawn towards the crosshair.

• Technology: Both fire normally and the missile explosions shoot ten Technology beams in all directions.

• [Repentance] Only Epic Fetus crosshairs are fired, but missile explosions still shoot ten Technology beams in all directions.

• Ipecac: Not recommended. Technology beams explode and may end up catching you off guard.

• Technology 2: Both fire normally.

• [Repentance] Does not reduce missiles' damage, and both fire normally at the cost of a slightly higher delay between each crosshair appearing.

• Tech X: Missile explosions shoot ten Technology beams in all directions.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
Overridden by Epic Fetus:

• Azazel's default attack

• Brimstone

• Chocolate Milk

• C Section, Epic Fetus is the only item in the game that can override it

• Cursed Eye

• Dr. Fetus

• [Repentance] Due to the minimum time delay between missiles, a single copy of Epic Fetus does slightly less DPS than Dr. Fetus, especially with an elevated tears stat. This is only at low-to-moderate damage stats, however, due to a change in Dr. Fetus's damage formula past a certain total.

• Evil Eye

• Godhead

• [Rebirth only] Homing tears

• Jacob's Ladder

• The Ludovico Technique

• Mom's Knife

• Monstro's Lung

• Mucormycosis

• Neptunus

• The Parasite

• Rubber Cement

• Sinus Infection

• Tainted Azazel's default attack

• Technology

• Technology Zero

• Tiny Planet

• Trisagion
Only stat effects are applied; otherwise overridden by Epic Fetus:

• Anti-Gravity

• Eye of the Occult

• Technology 2, not recommended as the damage down multiplier is still applied, massively reducing missile damage
Other interactions:

• 8 Inch Nails: Missile explosions retain the knockback boost, so enemies that survive the blast will be knocked back far.

• Bobby-Bomb/Bomber Boy/Ghost Bombs/Mr. Mega/Scatter Bombs: No effect.

• Chocolate Milk: Reduces Isaac's tear delay by 20%. Missiles can't be charged.

• Godhead: Stat effects apply and the crosshair gains a homing effect, but missiles do not have a damaging aura.

• Incubus: Incubus fires normal tears while the crosshair is being aimed.

• Isaac's Tears:

• [Before Repentance] The item fires normal tears, but charges very quickly as the crosshairs are moved.

• [Repentance] The item charges even while the crosshair is not moving, with the speed based on Isaac's tears stat.

• It Hurts/Tammy's Head/Varicose Veins: Fires only normal tears, not missiles.

• Loki's Horns: Adds a chance to spawn four crosshairs in cardinal directions. Isaac controls one and the others will mirror the movement keeping their space.

• Marked: Continuously fires missiles at the marked spot.

• [Repentance] If the crosshair is dismissed before the next missile is dropped, it still drops in the crosshair’s last position.

• Soy Milk: Not recommended. Damage of missiles is drastically reduced, and unlike normal tears, the fire rate will not significantly increase.

• Spirit Sword: Overrides Epic Fetus, making it the only item in the game that takes priority over Epic Fetus.

• The Wiz: Makes two missiles drop in quick succession, and control of the crosshair is rotated 45 degrees clockwise. Not recommended, as it makes controlling the crosshair harder. However, mouse control is less affected.

• Twisted Pair: Each familiar will fire a missile from a two additional crosshairs. Not Recommended, as the twisted pair crosshairs are not synced to Isaac's crosshair and move at a much slower rate, making self damage much more likely as the additional crosshairs will struggle to make distance from Isaac.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is similar to Doctor's Remote, which fires one missile per use.

• In the original game it was possible to control the crosshair with the mouse. This was removed in Rebirth.

• [Repentance] Mouse control can however be re-enabled by editing the options.ini file in C:\Users\<username>\Documents\My Games\Binding of Isaac Afterbirth/Rebirth and changing the line MouseControl=0 into MouseControl=1. Also useful for The Ludovico Technique.

• The Dr. Fetus and Epic Fetus items are based off of Dr. Fetus, the main antagonist in Super Meat Boy which is a game by Edmund McMillen (the creator of The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth).

• In Wrath of the Lamb, Epic Fetus could be found in both the Secret Room and Treasure Room item pools.

• [Repentance] Epic Fetus was added to the Secret Room item pool.

• This item is used in Glass Cannon.

• In Wrath of the Lamb, this item was originally unlocked by beating a challenge titled, "The Doctor's Revenge!".

fields.description: Instead of tears, firing creates a crosshair which can be moved freely. A missile is dropped in the location after 1.5 seconds, exploding for high damage.

'M.title: 'M
'M.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Using an activated item rerolls it into a different one.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either will give a 10% chance that the rerolled item will be fully charged. Having both will give a 20% chance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The item given by ‘M will always have no charges, regardless of what the previous active item was and whether or not it was overcharged. 

• Rerolling into items counting towards transformations (e.g.Guppy's Paw, Jar of Flies, Bob's Rotten Head, The Bible etc.) will not be counted towards said transformation, regardless if Isaac puts it back down and picks it back up.

• Having the Guppy transformation and rerolling either Guppy's Head orGuppy's Paw will remove the transformation, even if these items were acquired before using ‘M.

• Items that have costs associated with using them (such as Magic Fingers, Potato Peeler, Converter, etc.) can be rerolled even if Isaac doesn't have the resources necessary to use them.

• The only exception is Golden Razor: Isaac must have the 5 cents necessary to use it in order for it to be rerolled.

• The item's charge must be expended for it to be rerolled; items that can be used without spending their charge immediately (such as Bob's Rotten Head, Black Hole, Eraser, Spin to Win, Mom's Bracelet, etc.) must be properly used to have their charge expended.

• ‘M cannot reroll items into Broken Shovel 1, Mom's Shovel, Hold or Recall.

• The items generated are fixed per seed. This means the same active item on the same seed while holding 'M will always reroll into the same other active item every time.

• The items rerolled into will not be removed from their item pools unless Isaac puts them down and picks them up again.

• Items can be generated multiple times, even after they have been removed from their pools.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• Once ‘M gives a good active item, it can be dropped so that it can be continually used without it getting rerolled.

• For this reason, it is recommended to drop 'M when taking unknown pills, in case Gulp! appears, which would prevent Isaac from keeping any active item.

• Some active items have effects that can be harmful to Isaac when used; consider if rerolling the active item is worth the risk of getting an item that can't be rerolled (either at all or without hurting the run).

• Alabaster Box is especially noteworthy, as it cannot be rerolled, and will also prevent Isaac from gaining Soul Hearts until he uses or gets rid of it.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• One-time use items: The item disappears before it can be rerolled.

• Sacrificial Altar: If Isaac has no eligible familiars, the altar can be rerolled without being consumed.

• Book of Virtues: If an active item is combined with the Book, only the active item is rerolled; the Book remains unchanged. If no active item is combined with the Book, the Book will be rerolled on use. ‘M also cannot give Book of Virtues, as it is considered a passive item.

• Breath of Life: Breath of Life is rerolled once the charge is fully expended.

• [Before Repentance+] After one second, Isaac starts getting hurt as if he was still using Breath of Life until he leaves the room.

• Broken Glass Cannon: The item is rerolled instead of turning into Glass Cannon. This item can also be given by ‘M directly.

• This only applies if you manage to obtain a charged and usable Broken Glass Cannon, as it otherwise automatically replaces itself with Glass Cannon once charged.

• Butter!: The active item is rerolled before being dropped.

• Car Battery: The current active item is used twice before it is rerolled.

• Esau Jr.: Isaac will transform into Esau Jr. if ‘M rerolls Isaac’s active item into Esau Jr. However, he will not transform into Esau Jr. if the item itself is used.

• As the original character will be holding ‘M, Esau Jr. must be used twice for it to be rerolled.

• Friendly Ball / Moving Box: As the item must be used twice to have its intended effect, rerolling it on the first use will prevent it from being used to its full effect.

• [Repentance+] The contents of the items contained can be recovered by finding another Friendly Ball or Moving Box and using them.

• Glowing Hourglass: Glowing Hourglass rewinds time before the reroll goes through, preventing it from happening. This is avoided when used during the Beast fight and will be rerolled into another active.

• If Glowing Hourglass rerolls into a rechargeable item(e.g. Spin to Win, The Boomerang), The Glass will have all its charges restored, allowing for infinite rewinding.

• Magic Skin: Items given by Magic Skin cannot be Magic Skin even if it’s rerolled on use. However, as Isaac will not be holding Magic Skin after using it, it will be able to replace future items after being rerolled.

• Notched Axe: The item will be rerolled once it runs out of durability.

• Schoolbag: Only the primary item is rerolled.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• 'M is from the Antibirth mod.

• Like Missing No., the name 'M is a reference to a glitch from the Generation I Pokémon games, often thought of as a counterpart to MissingNo. itself. This is also referenced by its appearance, as random jumbles of pixels is very similar to the corrupted sprites you would see from a sprite error in Generation I Pokémon games.

• The description is a combination of Broken Remote's, Dataminer's and The D6's descriptions, "It's broken", "109", and "Reroll your destiny". This may be because it triggers when an active item is used (like Broken Remote), is a glitch-themed item (Like Dataminer) and it rerolls the active item (like D6).

fields.description: Using an activated item rerolls it.

0 - The Fool.title: 0 - The Fool
0 - The Fool.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Teleports Isaac to the starting room of the current floor.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If the room teleported out of was hostile, it will be reset.

• Previously cleared rooms do not reset.

• If used in the mirror dimension in Downpour or Dross, Isaac will be warped to the starting room of the main floor instead of the mirror world

• [Repentance] A 0 - The Fool is guaranteed to appear on Depths / Necropolis / Dank Depths II in a marked skull after unlocking A Strange Door. [end edition note] 

• When [curse: Maze] is active, using this card can teleport Isaac to a random room instead.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• 0 - The Fool is the only teleportation card that guarantees a teleportation to a safe room:

• IX - The Hermit may teleport Isaac to a Greed fight.

• XVII - The Stars / XVIII - The Moon may teleport Isaac to a Treasure Room / Secret Room containing enemies.

• Joker may teleport Isaac to a Devil Room with enemies or a Krampus fight.

• 0 - The Fool can be used to escape any room that locks down after taking its contents, like Challenge Rooms or Boss Rush, effectively "stealing" its contents without facing the imposed challenge.

• 0 - The Fool can be used to escape any boss fight to recover on the current floor.

• [Repentance] Using 0 - The Fool during the ascent can entirely skip a floor, as the light beam is located in the starting room. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth : No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] 0 - The Fool is the only teleportation card available in Greed mode.

• [Repentance] Two other cards are available in greed mode : XVII - The Stars and Joker.

• The Fool is considered a special trump card, being the last or the first of a Major Arcana set, hence the number 0, or no number at all being attributed to it.

fields.name: 0 - The Fool
fields.description: Teleports Isaac to the starting room of the current floor.

0 - The Fool?.title: 0 - The Fool?
0 - The Fool?.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Drops all hearts, trinkets, and pickups Isaac currently possesses on the ground near him, leaving Isaac at half a heart.

• Pickups will be dropped grouped in their highest possible value:

• Every 25 cents will first be dropped as the A Quarter, then Dimes for every remaining 10 cents, Nickels for every 5 cents, Double Penny for every 2 cents, then finally a Penny if Isaac has 1 remaining cent.

• If Isaac has exactly 99 bombs, they will be dropped as Pyro. If less than 99, then Boom! for every 10 bombs, Double Bombs for every 2 bombs, then finally a Bomb if Isaac has 1 remaining.

• If Isaac has exactly 99 keys, they will be dropped as Skeleton Key. If less than 99, then Key Rings for every 2 Keys, then finally a Key if Isaac has 1 remaining.

• Every 2 full red hearts will first be dropped as Double Hearts, then Red Hearts for every remaining red heart, then finally a Half Red Heart if Isaac has one red heart remaining.

• Soul Hearts, Half Soul Hearts, and Black Hearts will be dropped as usual. If half a Black Heart needs to be dropped, it will drop as a Half Soul Heart. If Isaac only has Soul Hearts, then he will be left at half a Soul Heart. However, if Isaac has only Black Hearts or a mix of Black and Soul Hearts, then he will always be left at half a Black Heart.

• Gold Hearts will be dropped as usual.

• Bone Hearts will also be dropped. If Isaac only has Bone Hearts, then he can go down to one empty Bone Heart.

• A single Rotten Heart will not be dropped, and always stay in the container as the last remaining heart. Any additional Rotten Hearts will be dropped as usual.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The pickups Isaac drops are set and are not affected by replacement effects, i.e. Daemon's Tail.

• If the amount of pickups dropped exceeds the room's allowed space, then extra pickups will be stacked near Isaac's position when he used the item. The player can still move out of the way while using the card to avoid picking them up.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• 0 - The Fool?‘s effect is most useful in generating item pedestals, as long as Isaac has enough pickups to sacrifice. These item pedestals can be then re-rolled through sources such as The D6 or Shop Restock Machines to get better items, or consumed through Black Rune or Abyss for other benefits. 

• As 0 - The Fool? can generate a lot of pickups for Isaac to collect, it can activate effects which require pickup collection. Re-picking up Isaac's dropped hearts can contribute to Candy Heart, Immaculate Conception, Alabaster Box etc., and his dropped coins can contribute to Counterfeit Penny, Blessed Penny, etc..

• 0 - The Fool? also allows Isaac a method to give pickups to Bum Friend, Key Bum, Dark Bum, or Bumbo.

• 0 - The Fool? allows Isaac to manipulate his health without needing to take damage. Its uses include lowering health to access a Boss Challenge Room, dropping Soul Hearts on the ground so as to spend less valuable Red Hearts in Sacrifice Rooms, etc.

• Similarly, it can be used to regain health in scenarios where that health would otherwise be taken away, such as accepting a devil deal or taking Dead Cat.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Deep Pockets: Every 100 cents will first be dropped as A Dollar.

• Tarot Cloth: Drops Isaac's 6 most recently collected items on the floor, alongside pickups. Does not affect quest items (e.g. The Polaroid) or Missing No..

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Only 3 items drop instead of 6; this also applies with Car Battery.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Greed's Gullet: If Isaac only has heart containers granted by Greed's Gullet, then using 0 - The Fool? will kill him. The only exception is if all heart containers are empty and Isaac also has temporary health, in which case the card will leave him at half a Soul/Black Heart

• Little Baggy / Starter Deck / Polydactyly: The second held consumable will also be dropped.

• Mother's Kiss: If Isaac uses 0 - The Fool? while having only one heart container, he will die since dropping the trinket will remove his last health. Similarly, using the card as one of the characters that can't have red health while holding this trinket will kill the player instantly, as it drops the trinket, removing the last half soul heart the character normally would remain with. 

• Tick: Cannot remove the Tick.

• Bethany / Tainted Bethany: Drops Soul Heart and Red Heart charges.

• Tainted ???: Cannot drop his poop pickups.

fields.name: 0 - The Fool?
fields.description: Drops all hearts, trinkets, and pickups Isaac currently possesses on the floor, leaving Isaac at half a heart. Pickups may be dropped as items such as A Quarter and Boom!.

120 Volt.title: 120 Volt
120 Volt.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Repeatedly zaps enemies that are in close proximity to Isaac with electricity beams for light damage.

• Enemies can be zapped up to five times per second, with each zap dealing 0.75× Isaac's damage.

• Each zap can hit up to 4 enemies, if they are sufficiently close to each other.

• If the floor is wet, such as in Downpour, Flooded Caves, some rooms in Dross, Scarred Womb, and Corpse, as well as under the effect of Flush!, the initial distance is unchanged, but enemy-to-enemy arcs reach further.

• Trigger range appears to be approximately two tiles wide — it's possible to zap an enemy standing directly on the other side of a rock.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • This item has a brief targeting delay, such that enemies can close in and touch Isaac before they start getting zapped.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Multiple battery-themed items have special synergies with the zaps:

• Sharp Plug / Car Battery: Electricity deals 100% of Isaac's tear damage if he owns 1 of these items, and 150% if Isaac owns both.

• The Battery / Jumper Cables / AAA Battery: Increases amount of arcs a zap can generate.

• Old Capacitor: Allows zaps to arc on the same enemy multiple times.

• Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb 120 Volt, it turns into a pale blue locust.

• [Before Repentance+] The locust can create arcs of electricity dealing 0.1 damage per tick.

• [Repentance+] The locust can create arcs of electricity dealing 25% of Isaac's damage per tick.

• Camo Undies: Enemies won't target Isaac, thus he can safely zap enemies while standing near them. However, this won't work with bosses.

• Isaac's Heart: 120 Volt becomes much safer to use offensively as Isaac's body no longer takes damage.

• Items granting invulnerability or a shield: 120 Volt zaps enemies while Isaac is invincible.

• This includes Gnawed Leaf, allowing Isaac to clear most rooms without moving.

• Dark Arts: Enemies and bosses will be zapped while Dark Arts' effect is active, allowing Isaac to safely deal damage while invulnerable in this way.

• Pause: Zaps will not stop the pause effect allowing Isaac to kill or chip bosses easily by standing near them for the duration of the pause effect.

• Tainted Forgotten: Tainted Forgotten zaps enemies, allowing Tainted Soul to damage enemies from a safe distance.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Ipecac: The zaps get only a +2 flat damage bonus instead of +40 from Ipecac. The 0.75x-1.5x damage multiplier applies afterwards.

• Libra: The zaps ignore damage modification from Libra, both positive and negative: the actual unbalanced damage value is used.

• Mine Crafter: The TNT is spawned and then instantly detonated by 120 Volt's electric shock, inflicting 1 full heart of damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item originated in the Antibirth mod. It originally had an effect similar to Jacob's Ladder and a different costume.

• The Antibirth item was very similar to the item "Box of Wires" from the Community Remix mod for the original Flash version of Isaac.

• 120 volt is the voltage of standard household circuits in the US.

• In the Chinese translation of Repentance, the item's name is “220伏 (220 Volt)”, referencing the standard household circuit voltage in mainland China.

fields.description: Repeatedly zaps enemies that are close to Isaac.

1up!.title: 1up!
1up!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac an extra life. Upon death, he will respawn in the previous room with full health, after which 1up! will disappear.

• If Isaac has no Red Heart Containers, he'll respawn with a Half Soul Heart instead.

• The 1up! mushroom begins following Isaac like a familiar upon pickup, but doesn't do anything. It disappears when its life is used up.

• Contributes to the Fun Guy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Resurrection items activate in a set order. 1up! is [edition alternatives: baseline: 1st in this order; Repentance: 2nd in this order after Soul of Lazarus] .

• ??? ( [Repentance] Tainted ??? / Tainted Bethany / Tainted Forgotten) will each respawn with 3 Soul Hearts.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Forgotten will respawn with [edition alternatives: baseline: 3; Repentance: 2] filled Bone Hearts and The Soul with whatever Soul and Black Hearts he had on death.

• Dying as The Soul respawns him with [edition alternatives: baseline: a Half Soul Heart; Repentance: 1 Soul Heart] and The Forgotten with whatever Bone Hearts he had on death.

• [Repentance] Black Judas / Tainted Judas will respawn with 2 Black Hearts.

• Tainted Jacob will respawn in his ghost form if he had been turned into his ghost form before dying.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with 1up! having the lowest priority at [edition alternatives: baseline: 6th; Repentance+: 8th] and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This is a reference to the Super Mario franchise, wherein collecting a green mushroom would give the player an extra life.

• 1up!, along with Magic Mushroom, Mini Mush, Super Bandage, and Mega Mush is one of the few items that make a unique sound upon pickup.

fields.description: Gives Isaac an extra life. Upon death, he will respawn in the previous room with full health, after which 1up! will disappear.

20/20.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Isaac fires two tears at once, one from each eye.

• [Repentance] 0.8× damage multiplier.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Unlike other multiple shot items like Mutant Spider or The Inner Eye, 20/20 does not reduce the rate of fire.

• The maximum amount of tears per volley that can be reached by combining and/or duplicating 20/20, The Inner Eye, Mutant Spider, and The Wiz is 16.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Clot / Chemical Peel: Every second row of tears has increased damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] Brimstone: Two Brimstone shots are fired, without an increase in charge time.

• Diplopia: Every additional 20/20 adds 2 more tears in a tight pattern.

• [Repentance] Adds one more tear without further lowering damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] Doctor's Remote / Epic Fetus: Replaces the single missile strike with a barrage of two consecutive missiles.

• [edition anr] The Inner Eye / Mutant Spider: Adds two/three tears to each shot, with no extra fire rate decrease.

• [Repentance] Removes the fire rate penalty while reducing damage to 80%. Additional copies will add one additional tear with no further change to damage/fire rate.

• Keeper: Fires 5 tears with no fire rate decrease.

• [Repentance] Decreases tears' spread. Reduces damage dealt to 80%, but makes his base tear stat equal 2.73. This is a damage per second increase if tear rate before picking up was less than 3.75; otherwise this is a damage per second decrease. This is the same for Tainted Keeper.

• The Ludovico Technique: The Ludovico tear gains one smaller tear orbiting the main one, each dealing the same amount of damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] Monstro's Lung: Adds two tears to the tear barrage, for a total of 16.

• [Repentance] Polyphemus: Grants additional +5 flat damage and removes the fire rate penalty, firing 2 tears per shot.

• Sprinkler: Fires two tears at once that almost completely overlap each other.

• [Afterbirth onward] Technology: Fires two technology shots simultaneously.

• Tractor Beam: Both tears are fired along the beam. Only one tear can be seen, as they overlap each other.

• The Wiz: Two tears are fired in each direction.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] Brimstone: Overrides 20/20.

• [Rebirth only] The Inner Eye: Overrides 20/20.

• Kidney Stone: Increase number of tears in tear barrage; however, only fires one stone.

• Loki's Horns: Only occasionally fires one tear in the other three directions.

• Mom's Eye: Only occasionally fires one tear out of the back of Isaac's head.

• [Rebirth only] Mom's Knife: Overrides 20/20.

• [Rebirth only] Monstro's Lung: Overrides 20/20.

• [Rebirth only] Mutant Spider: Overrides 20/20.

• Sad Bombs: Does not affect the number of tears when bombs explode.

• [Rebirth only] Technology: Overrides 20/20.

• Varicose Veins: No effect on number of tears when taking damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• 20/20 is an idiom that refers to someone with near-perfect vision.

• Despite only having one eye, Cain shoots two tears at once with this item.

• [Repentance] This item is used in Seeing Double. [end edition note]

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Rebirth only: Rebirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth]
fields.description: Isaac fires two tears at once, one from each eye. [Repentance] 0.8× damage multiplier.

2Spooky.title: 2Spooky
2Spooky.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Applies fear to enemies in a small radius around Isaac.

• [Repentance+] +0.5 fire rate.

• [Repentance+] +0.2 shot speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • 2Spooky can be used to manipulate Ultra Greed. Once Greed Gapers spawn and Ultra Greed is in his resistance stance, the gapers will be feared when getting close, leaving the boss unable to move or damage Isaac.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tainted Forgotten: Not recommended, the fear aura makes it more difficult to hit enemies with Tainted Forgotten and does not provide protection to Tainted Soul.

• Venus: Overrides 2Spooky.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• 2Spooky originates from the Antibirth mod, and by extension, from the Community Remix mod for the flash version.

• In Antibirth, it also would cosmetically change Isaac's tears to red.

• In Community Remix, it would instead have a 1/10 chance to trigger a room-wide fear effect after killing an enemy.

• The name and pickup quote are a reference to the "2spooky4me" meme. Isaac's appearance also makes him appear similar to popular internet horror images, such as Squidward's Suicide and Giygas from Earthbound.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: When using D12 to reroll obstacles; any Movable TNT or Fire Places created within the radius will occasionally spawn as feared momentarily with only the purple tint to indicate the status effect. This effect lasts even on the remains of either object after it's destroyed before the fear effect ends. Corn poops created in the radius are unaffected however the Eternal Fly may also become temporarily feared.

fields.description: Enemies near Isaac are afflicted with fear. [Repentance+] Grants +0.5 tears and +0.2 shot speed.

2 of Clubs.title: 2 of Clubs
2 of Clubs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Doubles Isaac's Bombs.

• If Isaac has no bombs, gives 2 bombs instead.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • The bomb counter cannot exceed 99, so the most optimal time to use 2 of Clubs is when Isaac has 49 or 50 bombs.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: Quadruples Isaac's bombs.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• Tainted ???: Does not double the poop count. Gives two blue flies instead.

• It's the Key: Acquiring bombs with 2 of Clubs does not invalidate the achievement condition.

fields.name: 2 of Clubs
fields.description:
Doubles Isaac's Bombs.
If he has no bombs, gives him 2 instead.

2 of Diamonds.title: 2 of Diamonds
2 of Diamonds.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Doubles Isaac's Penny.

• If Isaac has no pennies, gives 2 pennies instead.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• The penny counter cannot exceed 99, so the most optimal time to use 2 of Diamonds is when Isaac has 49 or 50 pennies.

• [Afterbirth onward] [mode: greed] 2 of Diamonds is an excellent way of filling up the Greed Donation Machine:

• It can be used if Isaac has few coins left after defeating Ultra Greed.

• If Isaac has many coins, they can be donated until 49 or 50 coins are left and then doubled for a total of donated coins exceeding 99 coins. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Quadruples Isaac's pennies.

• Deep Pockets: Allows for enormous wealth to be accumulated, as the coin limit is increased to 999.

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper: Can refill coin health at the cost of 1 coin after doubling.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• It's the Key: Acquiring pennies with 2 of Diamonds does not invalidate the achievement condition.

fields.name: 2 of Diamonds
fields.description:
Doubles Isaac's Penny.
If he has no coins, gives him 2 instead.

2 of Hearts.title: 2 of Hearts
2 of Hearts.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Doubles Isaac's Red Hearts.

• If Isaac only has empty Red Heart containers, he is healed for 1 Red Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • 2 of Hearts doesn't add new Red Heart containers, just fills empty ones. Nor does it double any other types of health.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • 2 of Hearts can be used to significantly increase the use of Sacrifice Rooms / Blood Donation Machines / Devil Beggars and any other health-draining object. The more heart containers, the more free hearts can be obtained form one use of the card.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Quadruples Isaac's red hearts.

• Tainted Bethany: Doubles her Blood Charges.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• It's the Key: Acquiring red hearts with 2 of Hearts does not invalidate the achievement condition.

• Bone Heart: Bone hearts are also filled by doubling health.

• Rotten Heart: If only a rotten heart is the only heart filling the otherwise empty heart containers, heals one heart.

• If there are red hearts and rotten hearts, the rotten heart is counted as a full red heart for doubling.

fields.name: 2 of Hearts
fields.description:
Doubles Isaac's current number of Red Hearts.
If Isaac only has empty Red Heart containers, he is healed for 1 Red Heart.

2 of Spades.title: 2 of Spades
2 of Spades.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Doubles Isaac's Key.

• If Isaac has no keys, gives 2 keys instead.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • The key counter cannot exceed 99, so the most optimal time to use 2 of Spades is when Isaac has 49 or 50 keys.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: Quadruples Isaac's keys.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

fields.name: 2 of Spades
fields.description:
Doubles Isaac's Keys.
If he has no keys, gives him 2 instead.

3 Dollar Bill.title: 3 Dollar Bill
3 Dollar Bill.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants Isaac random tear effects. The possible effects are: 

• [Rebirth only] The type of randomized tear is determined upon entering a room.

• [Afterbirth onward] The type of randomized tear changes every 6 seconds. The item appears to select two tear effects at once, perhaps staggering the times at which each of those effects change.

• [Repentance] While not directly a tear effect, 3 Dollar Bill may rotate through Magneto and Lucky Foot, which may be used to take only positive pills.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] If a run is quit, and then continued, 3 Dollar Bill will have a new random tear effect for the current room.

• Items that are required to charge like Brimstone or Monstro's Lung can have their charge amount change when gaining a new tear effect, depending on Isaac's new Tears stat. This can cause fully-charged items to need more charge time.

• [Afterbirth onward] Unlike Fruit Cake, which can only modify individual tears, 3 Dollar Bill can modify stats as well. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to an old expression "queer as a three dollar bill".

• [Afterbirth onward] This item is used in PRIDE DAY!. [end edition note] 

• Visually resembles the money from the popular board game Monopoly

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The Proptosis effect will only fire half the range it would normally (damage is increased normally).

fields.description:
[Rebirth only] Gives Isaac a random tear effect every room.
[Afterbirth onward] Gives Isaac a random tear effect every few seconds.

4.5 Volt.title: 4.5 Volt
4.5 Volt.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Causes Isaac's active item to charge when Isaac deals damage to enemies, rather than when he clears rooms.

• Damage dealt by charmed/friendly enemies, active items, orbitals, and familiars (including blue flies and spiders) works as well.

• Charges are gained at a rate equal to the following formula: (40 + (20 × stage)). For example:

• In Basement I / Downpour I, it takes 60 damage to gain 1 charge.

• In Caves II / Mines II, it takes 120 damage.

• In Womb I / Corpse I, it takes 180 damage.

• In Sheol / Cathedral, it takes 240 damage.

• In Home, it takes 300 damage.

• Ascent floors use the values of their regular floors, meaning the amount of damage 4.5 Volt needs to gain charges steadily decreases during the Ascent sequence until reaching Home.

• Multiple charges cannot be gained at once.

• Overkill damage does not count towards a charge.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tainted characters with active items in their pill/card slot will not have those items charged by 4.5 Volt if their active item isn't already fully charged.

• Lilith can be particularly strong with 4.5 Volt during long fights such as Delirium and Hush if she still has the Box of Friends, as the damage she deals will allow her to repeatedly duplicate her familiars, dealing many times her typical damage during a single fight.

• Bethany will benefit from 4.5 Volt's effect for regular item charges while retaining her ability to use Soul Hearts as item charges. This applies to Tainted Bethany with her Red Heart charges as well.

• Tainted Jacob will gain charges from 4.5 Volt when Dark Esau damages enemies.

• While the two versions of Tainted Lazarus normally charge both their active items at the same time, 4.5 Volt will only charge when the state that holds it deals damage, and will prevent it from being charged when the other clears a room. This makes 4.5 Volt much worse while playing Tainted Lazarus.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Shadows: With sufficient damage, the Book of Shadows can be kept active indefinitely.

• If combined with 9 Volt, it becomes even easier to achieve invincibility.

• Door Stop / Mercurius / any means of room resetting (infinite bombs): Provides infinite charges by clearing some enemies then leaving the room, and repeating.

• Jumper Cables: Increases the rate of charge by appending its 15-kills-per-charge quality on top of 4.5 Volt's damage-based charge.

• Old Capacitor: Since the 4.5 Volt also makes it so that active items don't charge when clearing rooms, this trinket can be picked up with no downside.

• Unicorn Stump + Sacrificial Dagger: In most boss fights, charges are regenerated faster than invincibility wears off.

• White Pony: Since the beam trail from the charge attack deals so much damage, if used on a boss with a high amount of health, 4.5 Volt will often completely recharge the item after each use, allowing for repeated usage while the boss is still alive.

• For the same reason (so much damage against bosses that the active item is recharged from its use), Tammy's Head + Brimstone / Azazel / Tainted Azazel is also a strong synergy.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Does not charge items which gain charge over time by default. (e.g. Sharp Straw, The Candle, Butter Bean etc.)

• Items converted to charge-over-time by 9 Volt are not affected and may gain charge in both ways.

• Alabaster Box: No effect. It still must be charged with Soul Hearts.

• Dim Bulb: Does not deactivate until the first charge bar is completely filled. A partial charge of the first bar will retain Dim Bulb's bonus.

• Schoolbag: The item in the second slot gets charged when the first one is full. Overcharges on the first item also jump to the second one.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The game files name 4.5 Volt's icon as "assaultbattery", which may imply "Assault Battery" was its original name.

• Assault and battery is the combination of two violent crimes in common law: assault (the threat of violence) and battery (physical violence).

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: With 9 Volt and The Battery, the gradual charge of 4.5 Volt is separate from 9 Volt's charge on one-charge items rather than being additive.

fields.quote: Beat the juice out of them!
fields.description: Active items don't charge when clearing rooms. Instead, they're charged by dealing damage to enemies.

7 Seals.title: 7 Seals
7 Seals.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a random Harbinger familiar that changes every 10 seconds. All harbingers deal contact damage to enemies and periodically spawn locusts if Isaac currently doesn't have any, though each harbinger behaves slightly differently:

• Famine wanders around the room, leaves a trail of slowing black creep, deals 0.5 contact damage per tick or 15 damage per second, and spawns yellow locusts every 3 seconds that deal double Isaac's damage and slows enemies.

• Pestilence wanders around the room, leaves a trail of green creep that deals 1 damage per tick or 30 damage per second, deals 0.5 contact damage per tick or 15 damage per second, and spawns green locusts every 3 seconds that deal double Isaac's damage and poisons enemies, which deals double Isaac's damage over time.

• War chases enemies, moves faster than the other Harbingers, deals 1.5 contact damage per tick or 45 damage per second, and spawns red locusts every 5 seconds which detonates upon impact with enemies, dealing double tear damage for the impact of the locust and 60 damage for the explosion. The explosion synergizes with multiple bomb related items.

• Death chases enemies, deals 1.5 contact damage per tick or 45 damage per second, and spawns black locusts every 3 seconds that deal quadruple Isaac's damage, applied as two hits of double damage.

• Conquest wanders around the room, deals 0.5 contact damage per tick or 15 damage per second, and spawns two white locusts at a time every 2 seconds that deal double Isaac's damage.

• • [Before Repentance] Conquest ignores the locust spawn timer.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Explosive locusts have a larger aggro range than all other locusts. They will target an enemy from further away.

• [Before Repentance] If Conquest is on top of an enemy when Isaac has no white locusts, it will spawn locusts at an incredibly high rate and deal a lot of damage.

• If an enemy is large enough to stand on multiple segments of Pestilence's creep trail, the damage from each pool of creep will stack.

• The locusts that War spawns can damage Isaac if they explode near him.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Increases Horsemens' size and doubles their contact damage. Does not affect locusts spawned.

• Bomber Boy: War's locusts explode in a small horizontal cross-shape pattern.

• Box of Friends: Creates another random horseman that can be different from the original.

• This makes it possible to gain multiple varying horsemen and gain all of their locusts at one time.

• Brimstone Bombs: War's locusts will shoot out four brimstone beams in a + formation after hitting an enemy.

• Glitter Bombs: Locust explosions have a chance to spawn pickups or trinkets.

• Hive Mind: Increases locusts' size and doubles their damage.

• Red locusts’ impact damage is doubled and the explosion damage is increased to 85.

• Sad Bombs: War's locusts fire a ring of ten tears outward upon detonation, which are affected by Isaac's tear modifiers, and deal damage equal to 15 + 0.6x, where x is Isaac's Damage.

• King Baby / RC Remote: No effect.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Fish Tail: Despite working with the locust trinkets, it does not double locusts from any of the 7 Seals Horsemen.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• 7 Seals is based on this Steam Workshop item by Ashkait and Scayze.

• In the original mod, Conquest was able to horizontally charge with multiple copies of himself, just like the real boss.

• The 7 Seals is a phrase in the Book of Revelation that refers to the 7 symbolic seals, which explains why it summons miniature Harbingers.

• If all 5 Harbingers were defeated on a save file before Booster Pack #5 was installed, defeating any normal boss will unlock 7 Seals.

• 7 Seals was given a new sprite in Booster Pack #4. The harbinger familiars also got new sprites, based on this Steam Workshop item by Quartz.

• 7 Seals is one of only five items to appear in both the Angel and Devil item pools, the others being Duality, Lil Delirium, Void and Purgatory.

• Although the Headless Horseman is a horseman, it isn't represented in the 7 Seals roster.

• Its achievement popup graphic was changed in v1.7.6; the previous one resembled its Steam Workshop sprite, and the new one resembles its actual in-game appearance after it officially released.

• The mini harbinger familiars use the pre-repentance designs of their boss counterparts.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again) will duplicate the locusts.

fields.description: Spawns a random Harbinger familiar that changes every 10 seconds. Harbingers have different behaviors and spawn themed Locusts.

8 Inch Nails.title: 8 Inch Nails
8 Inch Nails.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1.5 damage.

• Isaac's tears are replaced with nails, which have increased knockback.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Does not grant penetrative shots, despite the appearance of Isaac's tears.

• Any item that normally colors Isaac's tears red will cause the nails to become bloody.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Dr. Fetus / Epic Fetus / Ipecac: Explosions also gain increased knockback.

• Piercing tears: Allows tears to knock enemies back again.

• Brimstone / Tech.5 / Technology / Technology 2 / Tech X / Mom's Knife / Trisagion: They gain knockback. Especially powerful with Tech X, as the knockback helps keeps enemies within the ring for longer.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Blister: The knockback from Blister is stronger than from 8 Inch Nails, and knockback boosts do not stack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item is a reference to the nails used to hang Jesus Christ upon the cross when he was crucified.

• The item's name is also a reference to the band, Nine Inch Nails.

• The visual effect on Isaac may also be a reference to a line in Eminem's "My Name Is", in which he says, "Wanna see me stick Nine Inch Nails through each one of my eyelids?". This line is also a reference to the aforementioned band.

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Before Afterbirth+: Afterbirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth+]
fields.description: +1.5 damage. Replaces Isaac's tears with nails, which have increased knockback.

9 Volt.title: 9 Volt
9 Volt.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Fully charges the currently held active item upon 9 Volt's first pickup.

• If the current active item has a recharge time of more than 1 bar, then it will grant 1 bar of charge whenever the item is activated.

• If the current active item has a recharge time of 1 bar, then it will change the item to have a timed recharge of 15 seconds. The recharging of the item only triggers so long as there are enemies present in the room in any fashion. Empty rooms do not cause recharging to start.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If the current activated item already has a timed recharge, 9 Volt makes it start at half charge when used, effectively halving the time to recharge and allowing quicker reuse.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Enemies generated through a [machine: Slot Machine] , [machine: Shell Game] , [machine: Hell Game] , [machine: Rotten Beggar] or breaking Urns/Skulls will restart the charging process, even though a cleared room still counts as cleared if enemies are spawned in it.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 2-bar items: Fills the entire gauge in a single room, effectively granting the opportunity for the item to be used every room.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] 3-bar items: Quadruple rooms and L-shaped rooms give 2 bars after clearing them, allowing one free use of the item in those rooms if the gauge is full upon entering them. It can also be used at the beginning of a Boss Challenge Room to get the full charges back after beating both bosses.

• AAA Battery + 3-bar items: Same as the 2-bar item synergy without AAA Battery.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] 4-bar items: In a Challenge Room, if the item is used during the first wave, it will get all its charges back at the end.

• AAA Battery + 4-bar items: Same as the 3-bar item synergy without AAA Battery.

• Jacob's Ladder: Increases arcing distance of sparks.

• Keeper: The Wooden Nickel and the 9 Volt allow him to gain health (and money) forever, as long as there is an enemy in the room.

• An enemy spawned in a cleared room will also cause recharging to start.

• Telekinesis: The item can be reactivated the moment the previous charge stops, making it always active.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 9 Volt: No further decrease in charges.

• Alabaster Box: No effect.

• Dim Bulb: Prevents Dim Bulb from working, as minimum charge becomes 1 instead of 0.

• Eraser: No effect.

• Everything Jar / Larynx: The first bar gains an automatic recharge, but the further bars will not be affected.

• Sharp Plug:

• [Before Repentance] Renders the Sharp Plug unusable on 2+ charge items. Sharp Plug can only be used if the item is at 0 charges, but 9 Volt instantly gives +1 charge to the item upon activation.

• [Repentance] Lowers the cost of using Sharp Plug by half a heart on 2+ charge items.

• The Battery: If the effect of 9 Volt would result in the active item having at least 1 full level of charge, 9 Volt has no effect. Otherwise, it functions as usual.

sections.text: • This item is used in When Life Gives You Lemons (challenge #12), Beans! (challenge #13), It's in the Cards (challenge #14), and [Repentance] Scat Man (challenge #36).

???'s Only Friend.title: ???'s Only Friend
???'s Only Friend.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a controllable familiar that damages enemies on touch. It can be moved using the shooting directional keys, similarly to The Ludovico Technique and Robo-Baby 2.0.

• [Before Repentance] ???'s Only Friend deals 2.5 damage per tick, and ticks 15 times a second, dealing a total of 37.5 damage per second.

• [Repentance] ???'s Only Friend deals 3.5 damage per tick, and ticks ~4.3 times per second, dealing a total of 15 damage per second.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Unlike The Ludovico Technique, it cannot be controlled with the mouse, even with mouse control enabled.

• Holding two opposite fire keys (both left and right or both up and down) at the same time will keep the familiar in place, while making Isaac fire in the direction of whichever fire key was pressed second.

• This can help during combats with bosses who do not move a lot, as the familiar can continuously damage the boss when kept stationary.

• On some keyboards, holding opposite fire keys may cause other keys to become unresponsive.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS! / Hive Mind: Double the damage. The items don't stack.

• King Baby / RC Remote: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The sprite for the familiar resembles a Boom Fly, which has been resprited to fit the blue/dead nature of ??? and Hush, similar to the Hush Fly, Blue Gaper, and Fate's Reward

• This item is slightly faster than Robo-Baby 2.0, but is only noticeable when rapid clicking the tear button.

fields.description: Spawns a controllable familiar that deals [edition alternatives: baseline: 37.5; Repentance: 15] damage per second on touch. It can be moved using the shooting directional keys

???'s Soul.title: ???'s Soul
???'s Soul.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the trinket; the soul stone; Soul of ???]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that floats slowly around the room on a zig-zag pattern similar to The Peeper and fires spectral and homing tears that deal 3.5 damage.

• [Before Repentance] The familiar shoots once per second.

• [Repentance] The familiar shoots once every 3/4ths of a second.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Unlike The Peeper, ???'s Soul does no contact damage.

• [Before Repentance] ???'s Soul is unable to shoot while flying over obstacles (which is the same behavior that Ghost Baby has).

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Spawns 1 more familiar, this effect stacks to a maximum of 3 familiars at a time.

• Box of Friends: No effect; does not duplicate.

• Sacrificial Altar: Sacrifices the familiar, destroying the trinket and generating an item normally.

• King Baby / RC Remote: No effect.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that floats slowly around the room on a zig-zag pattern similar to The Peeper and fires spectral and homing tears.

??? (Boss).title: ??? (Boss)
??? (Boss).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss at the end of The Chest; the character; ??? (Character)] 

??? is the boss of the Chest, and the final boss of Ending 14.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
??? lies on the ground in the middle of the room and does not begin attacking until he takes damage.

During all three of ???'s phases, he performs similar attacks to Isaac, but at a faster pace. He also shoots multiple projectiles in the player's direction at fixed intervals. After taking enough damage, he begins to shoot double and triple projectiles.

• Each projectile has a chance of having a homing effect.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
??? remains stationary on the ground and performs the following attacks:

• Shoots 7-8 rapid-fire lines of projectiles in all directions that expand outwards. After taking enough damage, these lines curve while travelling.

• Shoots 8 lines of 2 projectiles in all directions that expand outwards. Each line consists of one normal projectile and one homing projectile. After taking enough damage, these lines curve while travelling.

• After taking enough damage, ??? summons Attack Fly, Moters, or Pooters that orbit around himself.

• Pooters have a farther orbit than the other flies.

• Attack Flies spawned from Moters chase Isaac instead of orbiting ???.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
2 Eternal Fly that can block tears begin to circle ???, who stands up but remains stationary and performs the following attacks:

• Continues to spawn orbiting flies.

• Fires 4 homing projectiles in a lop-sided X pattern.

• Fires 8 homing projectiles in all directions.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text:
??? grows a pair of angelic wings and is no longer stationary, slowly drifting towards Isaac and performing the following attacks:

• Spawning orbiting eternal flies (with increasing frequency compared to the previous phase).

• Teleporting to a position in front of the player - predicting their movements and attempting to cut them off. ??? will teleport directly on top of the player if the player is stationary.

• Shooting 2 projectile patterns from the first phase.
