sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text:
Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

[Repentance+] ??? has damage scaling.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• ??? was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• The music that plays during this boss fight is titled Ascension. The term "ascend" is typically used in religion as the act of one's soul rising to Heaven.

• ???, along with Isaac, flies away upon defeat and does not "die".

• ??? is commonly referred to as the 'blue baby' by the Binding of Isaac community, as well as Steam Achievements.

• [Afterbirth onward] ??? is fought as the first phase of Hush with identical behavior and music, only using a different sprite. The Hush version also has half the HP. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Blighted Ovum, Big Horn, Triachnid, Isaac, and ??? are the only bosses whose portraits were completely changed in Repentance (beyond simply adding more detail). Of these, only Triachnid, Isaac, and ??? didn't receive new sprites. [end edition note] 

• Isaac and ???'s portraits were changed to match the appearance of the characters on the transition screen between levels. This was also the case in the original Flash game.

• [Repentance] ??? has a unique sprite when encountered in the GFVELLLL seed as well as the limited time G Fuel themed daily challenge.

• This sprite was added in celebration of the release of "Isaac's Tears" flavored G Fuel.

? Card.title: ? Card
? Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Replicates the effect of Isaac's activated collectible.

• [Before Repentance] Single-use items, such as Pandora's Box, will not replicate but instead activate and disappear.

• [Repentance] Single-use items do not disappear after using ? Card, allowing for potential multiple uses of the items.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, the ? Card has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• The ID of this card was 43 before the Afterbirth+ expansion.

• [Repentance] Doesn't work with pocket activated items (such as Tainted Bethany's Lemegeton or items given by Dice Bag). [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: Does not influence the card's effect, activating the active item only once.

• Everything Jar / Larynx: The effect will be determined by the number of charges the active item currently has.

• Jar of Flies: Expends both the card and all charges with no additional benefit.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Alabaster Box: Causes the Alabaster Box to yield rewards without destroying the item or depleting any of its current charges.

• Blank Card: Teleports Isaac to the I AM ERROR room of the current floor. This will consume both the Blank Card and the ? Card. If done on Chest or Dark Room, will instead spawn an I AM ERROR shopkeeper.

• Diplopia: Duplicates all pedestal items and pickups in the room, without expending Diplopia.

• If used with another ? Card dropped on the floor in the room, allows for infinite duplication.

• Eden's Soul: Spawns two items without consuming Eden's Soul or depleting its charge.

• Glowing Hourglass: Since the card replicates the effect of moving back one room to the previous state, Isaac keeps the card having not used it as an item until the room later. This effectively gives him charge-free uses of the Glowing Hourglass.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The card is no longer refunded if you enter the room with it in your inventory and use it. [Before Repentance] But if you enter a room, drop it, leave the room, come back, pick it up and use it in that room, you do get a refund as the next time you enter the room the card will be in the floor. This allows for infinite uses.

• • [Repentance] The Glowing Hourglass loses a charge when the card is used.

• Mystery Gift: Grants an item without consuming Mystery Gift.

• Tarot Cloth: ? Card is used twice, giving the active item the same effect as if Isaac had Car Battery. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The interaction with Blank Card presents a paradox, as Blank Card and ? Card try to replicate the effects of each other. This would result in an endless loop, so a special case was put in.

• The Blank Card interaction is one of the four reliable ways to reach the I AM ERROR room in game, alongside Teleport 2.0 in certain circumstances, [Repentance] using Red Key to go beyond the 13x13 level grid, [end edition note] and Undefined.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Before Booster Pack #5, Glowing Hourglass was limited to 5 uses, and uses of the ? Card counted against that limit.

• This was re-implemented in V1.7.8 (although the limit was changed to 3 uses). [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Using ? Card on any activated item that needs a direction, such as Bob's Rotten Head or Gello will still result in the charges being used once a direction is chosen. The ? Card will be used up as well, despite providing no free use of the item.

fields.description: When used, copies the effect of Isaac's currently held activated collectible.

A Bar of Soap.title: A Bar of Soap
A Bar of Soap.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.5 Tears.

• +0.2 Shot Speed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A Bar Of Soap originates from the Antibirth mod, and by extension, from the Community Remix mod for the flash version.

• In Community Remix, it was instead called The Soap, and would give a 0.2 tears up and a 0.16 shot speed up.

• A Bar of Soap could be a reference to the uncommon practice of washing a child's mouth out with soap, most often done as punishment for profanity or verbal disrespect.

A Card Against Humanity.title: A Card Against Humanity
A Card Against Humanity.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Fills the entire room with Poop.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, A Card Against Humanity has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• Poop will not fill tiles with obstacles, even if they have already been destroyed.

• The process is not instant and the room will not get fully filled if Isaac leaves before it's done filling.

• It is more beneficial to use the card in a large-sized room as it will create more poop piles.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Using A Card Against Humanity in the Ultra Greedier fight will result in Golden Poops spawning after defeating the boss.

• [Repentance] Results in Yellow Poops which only have normal drops. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth onward] Using A Card Against Humanity in the Ultra Greed fight can trap the Greed Gapers after Ultra Greed Coin (Key) appear, preventing Ultra Greed from attacking. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Dirty Mind: Each poop spawns 1-4 Dip Familiars when destroyed.

• Meconium: Spawned Poops have a 33% chance to turn into Black Poop.

• [Afterbirth onward] Infested! pill: Every Poop spawns a Blue Spider.

• Lil Larva / [Repentance] ???: Every Poop spawns a Blue Fly.

• Hallowed Ground: Spawned Poops have a 33% chance to turn into White Poop.

• Butt Penny: Spawned Poops drop coins 20% more often.

• Midas' Touch: Spawned Poops have a great chance to turn into Golden Poops. (11% when 0 Luck)

• Petrified Poop: Pickup drop rate set to 50%. It's extremely likely to be obtained when using the card in larger, less obstructed rooms.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brown Cap: All the Poop explodes in a chain reaction once one is destroyed.

• Dr. Fetus/Ipecac: If Isaac has no other means of destroying Poop than his explosive tears, he will have to hurt himself to clear out a path through the Poop unless he has acquired Pyromaniac or Host Hat.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The card is a reference to Cards Against Humanity, a satirical card game whose name in turn references "crimes against humanity". Specifically, it refers to the way the first player is chosen: Whoever was the last to poop goes first.

• This actually contradicts the original card game, as black cards are prompts while the white cards are answers to the prompt.

• In the pop-up (if not disabled) for unlocking this card, the text on it reads "A room full of poop".

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using this card in the TV room in Home will move the sofa and the TV to the nearest empty space (Which would be where Isaac is standing as that's the only space that doesn't get filled with poop). If Isaac tries to approach where they were previously then he will be violently pushed back. Destroying the poop will return them back to normal.
If the poop is not destroyed before sleeping in Mom's bed then Isaac will have to stand below where the TV was teleported to in order to activate the Dogma fight. If Dogma is summoned before destroying the poop then the TV will glitch inside the Dogma fight and push Isaac around, possibly making him touch Dogma and get hit multiple times.

fields.description: Covers the entire room with Poop. The process is not instant, and the room will not get filled if Isaac leaves before it's done filling.

A Lighter.title: A Lighter
A Lighter.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:

sections.heading: Synergies

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This trinket is from the Antibirth mod where it was called Lighter. In Antibirth the trinket would make all farts explode harming both enemies and Isaac alike.

• The description is likely a reference to Alfred's line in The Dark Knight "Some men just want to watch the world burn".

Super Lust.title: Super Lust
Super Lust.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Super Lust is a mini-boss and one of the Seven Super Deadly Sins. She is randomly encountered as an alternate version of Lust.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Super Lust chases Isaac around the room at a very fast speed, leaving a trail of damaging Red Creep behind and attempting to do contact damage.

• She builds up speed the longer she travels without turning and takes heavily reduced knockback from Isaac's tears.
Super Lust deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Super Lust can drop Yum Heart even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. 

• A high speed attribute and/or flight helps with the fight tremendously.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived.

• Super Lust appears to be violently diseased or sick, which could be a reference to sexually transmitted diseases (STDs), which fits Super Lust's sin. Super Lust's maimed appearance could also imply rough or violent sexual acts, which is an extreme act of lust.

• Super Lust is female, like her counterpart Lust.

Super Magnet.title: Super Magnet
Super Magnet.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Pickups and enemies are attracted to Isaac.

• The attraction enables pickups to pass over pits and rocks, but not through Key Blocks.

• Red Heart are only attracted if Isaac could pick them up with his existing heart containers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Does not pull other trinkets, Chests, or Grab Bags.

• [Before Afterbirth+] If Isaac has The Ludovico Technique while also holding the Super Magnet, the speed at which the tear slowly crawls nearer to Isaac is increased.

• One tactic for using the Super Magnet is to drop it in the floor's starting room and come back for it once rooms are cleared. This allows it to be used to attract unreachable pickups without the downside of attracting enemies.

• [Before Afterbirth+] While fighting Ultra Greed, the doors are affected by the magnet as well.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either also pulls trinkets and sacks toward Isaac. Having both also pulls Chests.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] Super Magnet's sprite was changed for Booster Pack #5.

• Super magnets, also known as neodymium magnets, are magnets made of an iron, boron, and neodymium alloy (Nd2Fe14B). They are more powerful compared to the ordinary ferrite magnets, made of iron oxide.

Suplex!.title: Suplex!
Suplex!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac dashes forward a short distance. If Isaac runs into an enemy while dashing, he picks them up and a crosshair spawns under him that can be controlled with tear controls. After one second, Isaac leaps up and slams down on the crosshair with the enemy, dealing damage to them and any enemies he lands on depending on his size. On impact, this move creates circular rock waves that damage nearby enemies and destroy obstacles.

• The damage the slam deals is 50 +/- 10 for each size up/down Isaac has.

• Each spike in the rock wave deals 10 damage, and the range of the rock waves increases/decreases for each size up/down Isaac has.

• Isaac is immune to damage for the duration of the effect, which allows him to use it to get into Curse Rooms, open Spiked Chests, and travel over spikes without taking damage.

• • Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars will still deal damage while Suplex! is active.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• In addition to normal enemies, Isaac is able to suplex:

• Bombs of any kind

• Bosses

• Friendly enemies (this deals no damage to them).

• Shopkeepers

• Poky type enemies

• Movable TNT

• Stationary or mostly stationary enemies such as a Stone Grimace or Slide (they will move back to their original position after the suplex)

• Fires (including Fire Places; if Isaac suplexes a fireplace, it will glitch out and leave an invisible damaging fireplace in its original spot)

• Enemies that are normally invincible, such as the ghost of Blighted Ovum (which deals no damage to it) and The Haunt before it moves to the top of the room.

• Tainted ???'s poops, making it easier to break tinted rocks and open secret rooms. After being suplexed, the broken poop can be repeatedly suplexed as well. The broken poop will block the movement of Isaac and enemies, as it is still technically intact, even though it is visually destroyed. If the broken poop is shot at by Isaac, it will be 'destroyed' and is no longer able to be suplexed.

• Dark Esau if playing as Tainted Jacob, although care should be taken to move away after the suplex attack to avoid touching Dark Esau.

• Furniture on the Home floor.

• If Isaac picks up an enemy and then suffers fear, he cannot move the crosshair.

• Despite the description, Isaac cannot suplex angel statues unless the fight has already been started.

• As this item allows Isaac to leap over gaps and obstacle, the player must be careful not to strand him in an inaccessible place without a means to exit, such as teleportation, flight, or another target to Suplex, as that will effectively softlock the game.

• Using suplex on a bomb in the Crawl Space and positioning the cross hair slightly above Isaac propels Isaac with enough force downward to force through the floor and access the error room. Be cautious about this as there's no way to go back to the floor other than teleporting.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: 3 wisps are spawned where Isaac lands after using Suplex!. The wisps rotate around the spot Isaac landed and fire tears in the same direction Isaac does. The wisps do not persist between rooms.

• Berserk! / Soul of Samson / Tainted Samson: When used near the end of the Berserk state (any time after the second bell ring), Suplex receives a unique visual effect, and will deal massive damage to the target, while setting off a Mama Mega! style explosion, destroying all obstacles in the current room and blowing open all doors. The target being Suplexed, as well as nearby enemies, will receive 300 base damage that scales with Isaac's size. All other enemies receive 200 flat damage. The reason this interaction exists is that prior to a patch, doing this would instantly kill any enemy, including end bosses. It was then nerfed to only produce an explosion.

• Freeze effects: Isaac can suplex frozen enemies.

• Friendly enemies: If Isaac uses Suplex! to dash in a room, he will suplex a friendly enemy upon entering the room. This gives more time to react to danger and allows to deal damage to a group of enemies without risk (since the item gives invincibility during suplexes).

• Panic Button: As long as Suplex! is fully charged and Isaac is moving, Panic Button automatically triggers when about to take damage, avoiding the damage and potentially grabbing an enemy in the process. Allows Isaac to grab an enemy by simply walking into them, provided the item is charged.

• The Virus: The nature of suplexing helps to inherently poison enemies without consequences most of the time.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Tainted Forgotten: Suplex can only be used while carrying the body or throwing the body, and can only control where he lands after being thrown. Tainted Soul gains the temporary damage immunity, including while Tainted Forgotten is suplexing a target. Tainted Forgotten cannot dash, requiring walking into enemies after using Suplex to grab them.

• Safety Scissors: Suplexed Troll Bombs (and their versions) will explode instead of turning into Bomb pickups.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is likely a reference to the biblical story of Jacob wrestling an angel, hence its description.

• It also likely refers to the Suplex ability from Final Fantasy, which is itself somewhat of an internet meme due to it being possible to suplex ridiculous things like trains or the suplexer themselves (when under the confusion status).

• Several games in the Kirby series also feature a functionally identical Suplex ability. Suplex's pickup graphic resembles the ability's icon in Kirby Super Star.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using Suplex! in an room that contains normal floor tiles separated by pits or other obstacles Isaac cannot cross (without flying) and using a consumable to cancel the Suplex!'s jumping back animation may leave Isaac stranded on the other side, effectively softlocking the game and ending the run. Isaac can usually get around this by exiting and resuming the run (returning him to the last door that was entered), but if a Crawl Space was entered first, resuming the run will place you there instead, meaning you're out of luck without using the console.
Bug note: Using Suplex! in combination with Mega Mush makes you grab enemies and move them around until you leave the room. Doing this on any of the Ultra Harbingers or The Beast will make the enemy disappear and render you unable to move at all.
Bug note: Using Suplex! on the White Fire will permanently extinguish it, preventing you from turning into the Lost any further and potentially locking you out of Knife Piece 1.
Bug note: When Isaac leaps with an enemy that has a status effect it creates a visual bug where the effect is displayed over the enemy's head twice with one display following the enemy as Isaac leaps with them and the other display remaining static. This effect goes away once Isaac slams the enemy into the ground.
Bug note: When using Suplex! with Tainted Jacob on Dark Esau, then using a pill while offscreen, it will cause Dark Esau to become fused to your body. He will not be able to hurt you, and he will stay stuck on you permanently until you are put into an animation (on hit, grabbing/using items,going to the next floor, etc;) which ends the bug, reverting him to his normal properties. It can also be used on anything that is or the game considers an enemy, (ex: Mom's Couch, Mom's Dresser, Shopkeepers, etc). It can also be used on bosses as well. Using this on either stage of Dogma will softlock the game.
Bug note: Using a consumable while an enemy is under the effects of Suplex! results in Isaac being unable to move and that enemy not reappearing. This can lead to a softlock if there are no other enemies in the room, which can be fixed by exiting and resuming the run.

fields.description: Isaac dashes forward and picks up the first enemy hit. After a moment, he jumps and slams them into the ground to deal damage and create a circular rock wave.

Supper.title: Supper
Supper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives one full Red Heart container.

• Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Binge Eater: When Isaac picks up Supper it now grants: a permanent +0.5 Tears and +1.0 Luck, a temporary +3.6 Damage (which diminishes to 0 in 30 seconds), heals 1 additional red heart, and takes a permanent -0.03 Speed reduction.

fields.description: Grants one full Red Heart container. Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

Swallowed M80.title: Swallowed M80
Swallowed M80.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac has a 50% chance to explode when he takes damage, similarly to if he used Kamikaze!.

• The explosion deals 185 damage and uses most of Isaac's bomb synergies.

• The explosion does not cause additional damage to Isaac, as the explosion occurs during Isaac's invincibility frames.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Causes [machine: Devil Beggar] and [machine: Hell Game] to become essentially unplayable, as any damage that could trigger Swallowed M80 will likely cause Isaac to explode, killing them.

• [Before Repentance+] Causes [machine: Blood Donation Machine] s and [machine: Confessional] s to act as if they were destroyed from the explosion despite surviving and functioning normally, resulting in extra coin and Red Heart drops.

• The explosion cannot be triggered by Curse Room or Sacrifice Room spikes.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / Swallowed M80: Having either of these effects/another copy of the trinket raises the chance to trigger an explosion to 100%.

• Pyromaniac: Heals half a red heart on triggered explosion, rendering Isaac invincible on earlier stages if combined with the above synergy.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Kamikaze!: The damage received from Kamikaze cannot trigger the trinket, and the activation of the trinket applies a cooldown to Kamikaze (as if it was used).

• Tainted Magdalene: Explosions will kill enemies before Tainted Magdalene's “hug” attack, preventing heart drops from killing enemies on contact from being guaranteed.

sections.heading: No Effect
sections.text:
All bomb upgrades affect Swallowed M80 except the following:

• Bob's Curse

• Fast Bombs

• Ghost Bombs

• Mr. Mega

• Rocket in a Jar

• Scatter Bombs

• Sticky Bombs

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to M-80 firecrackers.

• The inability to properly destroy [machine: Blood Donation Machine] s and [machine: Confessional] s with this trinket was unintended, but kept in as a feature.

fields.description: Isaac explodes upon taking damage.

Swallowed Penny.title: Swallowed Penny
Swallowed Penny.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Spawns one coin of any type upon taking damage.

• [Repentance] When held by Keeper and Tainted Keeper, spawns 0-1 coins.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This trinket can be found by destroying urns, Special Shopkeepers, and [Repentance] buckets in Downpour. [end edition note] 

• Though similar to the Piggy Bank item, the Swallowed Penny is not limited to just pennies.

• [edition anr] Unlike Piggy Bank, playing as Keeper with this trinket always drops a coin, allowing semi-infinite life.

• A trick for farming money when playing as Keeper is to find a room with some static hazard like spikes and taking damage, causing a coin to appear. A penny will only refill life while a nickel will give four cents, and a dime will give nine cents.

• • This trick can also be used to survive multiple uses of a sacrifice room, healing with the dropped coin between each sacrifice.

• [Repentance] As it can now give 0 coins when playing as the Keeper, this no longer works. The Piggy Bank and IV Bag also spawn 0-1 coins when damage is taken; with all three, though money is no longer guaranteed, if a large pool of coins is found it can be used to mitigate streaks of bad luck, allowing Keeper to farm coins almost reliably.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Mom's Box: Spawns two coins on hit, multiple copies don't stack.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy spawns one more coin on getting hit with a limit of 5 coins.

• [Repentance] This does not add another 0-1 chance as Keeper or Tainted Keeper.

fields.name: Swallowed Penny
fields.description: Upon taking damage, Isaac drops a coin.

Swarmer.title: Swarmer
Swarmer.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Swarmers float aimlessly around the room, occasionally spawning Attack Fly. When hit, they will spawn a Pooter, and when destroyed, they will spawn a Boom Fly. Swarmers do not deal contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Skatole will charm a Swarmer. When charmed it won't spawn any Attack Flies until it is damaged. The Attack Flies that spawn will also be charmed.

• The ring of Flies that surround the Swarmer is an indication of how much health it has. The Flies deplete as the Swarmer takes more damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Swarmers are the next and possibly the final stage of the original Gaper.

• As Swarmers have Champion forms it's possible to encounter a White Champion (though extremely rarely). This can be a challenging occurrence as the Swarmer will regain invincibility every time it takes damage due to spawning Pooters.

Sworn Protector.title: Sworn Protector
Sworn Protector.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns an orbital familiar that blocks enemy shots and deals 7 damage per tick or [Before Repentance] 105 / [Repentance] 52.5 damage per second on contact.

• It also attracts enemy shots to itself, making them more likely to be blocked. A shot actively being attracted can no longer damage Isaac and is essentially nullified, but if it slips outside the Protector's range, it can again deal damage.

• Sworn Protector has a chance to drop an Eternal Heart upon blocking 10 shots in one room.

• This can only happen once per room, but leaving and re-entering a room will allow another eternal heart to be dropped.

• [Before Repentance] Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Sworn Protector can be exploited with the help of a Constant Stone Shooter to spawn unlimited eternal hearts.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Friendly enemies: Spawning a friendly enemy that shoots bullets allows Eternal Hearts to be farmed since the friendly enemy will fire at Isaac if no hostile enemies are in the room.

• Sacrificial Altar: This familiar will also reward 2 Black Hearts when sacrificed.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Extension Cord: Familiar and Isaac are occasionally connected by electricity, but it is very hard to notice because Sworn Protector orbits so close to Isaac.

• [Repentance] Friendly enemies: Friendly enemy tears are ignored by Sworn Protector.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Sworn Protector resembles Uriel/Gabriel.

• The name of this item is also the pickup quote for Best Bud.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Sworn Protector is supposed to drop an Eternal Heart after absorbing 10 projectiles, without any randomness. However, enemy shots that hit the familiar are sometimes not registered, so the actual number of intercepted shots before the Eternal Heart is spawned may be larger.

fields.description: Spawns an orbital familiar which does [Before Repentance] 105 / [Repentance] 53 damage per second and attracts and blocks enemy shots. Upon blocking 10 shots in a room, it drops an Eternal Heart.

Synthoil.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 damage.

• [Before Repentance] +5.25 range.

• [Repentance] +2.5 range.

• [Before Repentance] +0.5 tear falling speed.

• Contributes to the Spun transformation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Synthoil, or as it should correctly be spelled as "synthol", is a mixture of oil, lidocaine, and alcohol used to artificially increase muscle volume through scar tissue formation.

TMTRAINER.title: TMTRAINER
TMTRAINER.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When picked up, all future items become "Glitched", causing them to become random combinations of 2-3 effects based on other items as well as effects that are not normally controlled by the player, such as enemy spawning and other behind-the-scenes effects.

• Quest items do not become glitched. This includes: The Polaroid, The Negative, Key Piece 1, Key Piece 2, Knife Piece 1, Knife Piece 2, Dad's Note.

• Additionally, the currently playing music will fade out. The silence will remain until another music track plays.

• Any enemies in the room will also become simultaneously frozen and set on fire.

• "Glitched" items can be passive or active and are completely randomly generated with practically infinite possibilities. There is a 75% chance that the item will be passive.

• Random effects combine effects that exist on other items, and assign them to a random event (e.g. on enemy death, on room clear, on damage taken etc.).

• These effects may also be derived from installed modded items.

• Glitched items sold for money cost a random amount of pennies up to 99 pennies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Once Corrupted Data is unlocked, the TMTRAINER effect may be randomly applied to items found in Secret Rooms and I AM ERROR rooms.

• Items affected by TMTRAINER may take the effect of rerolling all of your items. This includes TMTRAINER itself, meaning any future items you encounter will not be under its effect, nor will the items obtained by rerolling due to the glitched item.

• All glitched items appear as Mega Blast in Isaac's Last Will or the In-game Pause Menu.

• If an item held by Isaac is rerolled into TMTRAINER (Either by D4 or a 1-pip Dice Room), all items after it will be rerolled into glitched items.

• A majority of the random item effects include farts, including active items.

• Due to the sheer randomness of glitched items, some may cause the game to either crash or lag to the point of unplayability.

• However, some may spawn entities that are normally only accessible using the Debug Console, including the Challenge Trophy that spawns at the end of Challenges and the Big Chest that spawns after most major bosses. Touching either of these on a floor that would not normally spawn them will instantly end the run and send the player back to the title screen (unless a challenge is currently being played, in which case the player will receive unlocks as if they had completed the challenge normally). Touching a Big Chest on any floor that can spawn them will NOT give the player the respective completion marks but will still end the run (unless Isaac has either The Polaroid or The Negative and is on either Cathedral or Sheol, respectively.)

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 'M: Rerolls glitched actives into other glitched actives.

• Bag of Crafting: Recipes are not glitched.

• Binge Eater: Functions as intended, cycling pedestals between a glitched item and an HP up item.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Using a glitched active spawns a random wisp.

• Death Certificate: TMTRAINER will not apply to Death Certificate's items.

• Diplopia: Glitched items are copied normally. Pedestals spawned before acquiring TMTRAINER will duplicate into a glitched item.

• Dream Catcher: Cannot identify glitched items.

• Genesis: Removes TMTRAINER's effect and allows items to spawn normally again, including items which appear in the special Bedroom created by Genesis. This also applies to glitched items which invoke Genesis' effect.

• Lemegeton: Spawns wisps of glitched items. All wisps look like The Sad Onion, but this is purely aesthetic. The wisps do not have any items' effects.

• Magic Skin: All summoned items will be glitched. Magic Skin cannot replace future glitched items after being left behind.

• Missing No.: Can reroll TMTRAINER, but not any previously acquired glitched items.

• Modeling Clay: Cannot transform into glitched items. Will visually vanish from sight, but is still held and can be dropped as normal.

• Spindown Dice: Glitch items will disappear if rerolled.

• Tainted Cain: Can craft TMTRAINER but it will have no effect other than giving shop items random prices which are most often overpriced.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The name and description of the item comes from the result of glitches in Pokémon Red and Blue. Certain glitch moves in that game can have names so long they run into the memory, corrupting it and causing glitchy effects, like the opponent's name becoming "TMTRAINER". A certain other glitch (commonly referred to as the ZZAZZ glitch) replaces the letters in the player's name with capital Zs except for every third letter.

• The pickup quote for this item is defined as "Isaac and his mother lived alone in a small house on a hill", but in game it's shown with the pattern of Zs overlaid on top.

• • When viewed in the collection grid, the pickup quote is unobscured, but it's so long it goes off of the screen.

• The music fading out and status effects being applied to enemies upon acquiring the item is another direct reference to the effects of TMTRAINER in Pokémon Red and Blue, which fades the music out upon use until another song is triggered to play (assuming the game survives the effects), as well as applying burn and frozen statuses to enemy pokémon.

• The sprite for TMTRAINER itself is a heavily glitched version of the in-game Isaac's Head's face, affected similarly to the face of Tainted Eden in menus.

• For the TMTRAINER sprite in particular is a reference to how sprites corrupt in Pokémon Red and Blue, especially after encountering glitch Pokémon, by segmenting into strips, then rearranged, usually flipped around.

• The effect of the item is similar to a "Randomizer" for other games.

• The item's effect is a reference to an old randomizer mod that came out before Afterbirth+.

• This item is used in DELETE THIS.

• DELETE THIS will always be unlocked before TMTRAINER on any given file. This item, The Small Rock, Dirty Mind, and Spirit Sword are the only items that appear in challenges before they are unlocked. Small Rock and TMTRAINER are also notable for not being unlocked by beating the challenge they appear in.

• MEAT!, YO LISTEN!, G FUEL!, PHD, BBF, IBS, BFFS! and TMTRAINER are the only items in the game with all capital letters in their names.

• All glitched items have a unique appearance in the pause menu and death screen.

• [Before Repentance+] Most glitched item sprites are shown as Mega Blast in Isaac's last will. Very rarely one will show a glitchy icon.

• [Repentance+] Glitched items appear as a question mark symbol. The description of the glitched item matches what is shown when picked up, and also lists pickup items granted, if any.

• Sounds when picking up glitched items are often changed.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: In Online Mode, glitched active items do not have on-activation effects, but effects gained passively still work.
Bug note: Glitched items can trigger the effect of Wavy Cap, crashing the game.

Mom.title: Mom
Mom.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the transformation; Yes Mother (Transformation); the final boss of Corpse; Mother] 

Mom is the boss that appears on the second floor of Chapter 3 (Depths, Necropolis, Dank Depths). She is the initial final boss of the game, and defeating her for the first time unlocks both the Epilogue ending and Chapter 4 (Womb).

• [Repentance] She also appears as a stronger version on the second floor of Chapter 3.5 (Mausoleum, Gehenna). [end edition note]

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Mom appears in a unique boss room that has a boss door in the center of all sides of the room. Mom can use these doorways to perform various attacks:

• Stomps on Isaac's position, damaging nearby enemies and destroying obstacles. This attack is telegraphed by a growing shadow and her grunting.

• She always begins the fight by stomping in the center of the room.

• [Before Repentance] Stomping is considered as explosion damage.

• • [Repentance] Stomping is now considered as contact damage in Repentance.

• The foot itself does no contact damage.

• • [Repentance] Changed to deal contact damage in Repentance.

• If Isaac is near a door, Mom reaches out from it with her hand, dealing contact damage.

• Sticks out a piece of flesh from a door and spawns a Monster with a maximum of 3 alive at once:
Gusher
Frowning Gaper
Globin
Attack Fly
Pooter
Mulligan
Maggot
Charger
Horf
Maw
Red Maw
Clotty

• Sticks an eye out of a door, which does not attack but can deal contact damage.

• All enemies spawned by Mom die alongside her, except for Globins, which collapse into piles of goo.
Mom deals one heart of contact damage.

Upon defeating Mom, all boss doors in the arena will disappear, trapping Isaac in the room unless he has a collectible or pickup effect that can teleport him out.

sections.heading: [Repentance] Behavior in Mausoleum/Gehenna
sections.text:
A stronger version of Mom can be fought on the second floor of the Mausoleum and Gehenna. This version of Mom has noticeably bluer veins on her leg and stronger variations of her attacks:

• Stomps 3 times on Isaac's position in rapid succession, with the third stomp releasing explosions in the cardinal directions.

• If an eye is already attacking, only 1 stomp will be performed.

• She always begins the fight by stomping once in the center of the room, just like in Chapter 3.

• Sticks an eye out of a door, and if Isaac is in line of sight, it shoots 2 Brimstone beams in a helix pattern towards the door on the opposite side.

• If Mom had already initiated the 3-stomp attack, the eyes opened during it won't fire the beams.

• Sticks out a piece of flesh from a door and spawns a Monster:
Attack Fly
Cursed Globin
Fetal Demon
Rag Man's Ragling
Sucker
Psychic Horf

• Unlike in Chapter 3, Mom never uses her hand attack.

• All enemies spawned by Mom die alongside her, except for Cursed Globins, which collapse into 2 piles of goo.
Mom deals a whole heart of contact damage.
This version of Mom never spawns as a champion.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 7] : Has 793.4 HP (23% more), summons monsters more often, and summons a different variation of enemies that were added in the Wrath of The Lamb expansion of the original game, which are:
Spider
Big Spider
Trite
Buttlicker
Keeper
[bc: 1] : Does not summon monsters at all, and instead repeatedly uses her foot stomp, which has increased speed. Occasionally, she will pause her stomps briefly to use one or both of the following attacks:

• Stick an eye out from one of the doors, which shoots three blood shots in a spread formation at Isaac.

• Reaches in with her hand through one of the doors, dealing contact damage, if Isaac is close enough to one.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Womb, The Harbingers, A Cube of Meat, Purist, XXXXXXXXL, SPEED!, Have a Heart, PRIDE DAY!, Onan's Streak, The Guardian, Aprils fool, A Halo, Item Descriptions]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Defeating Mom for the first time changes the current savefile's image and will allow unlocks to be obtained with mods enabled.

• The 'Stats' section of the menu keeps a tally of "Mom kills". However, this refers to how many times you've defeated Mom completely, as in, how many times you've killed Mom's Heart, not just Mom.

• Using The Bible or XV - The Devil? during the Mom boss fight kills her instantly and unlocks The Halo.

• Using II - The High Priestess during the fight with Mom results in Isaac being targeted instead of the enemy with the highest health. However, the stomp can still damage Mom.

• [Before Repentance] Mom's stomp attack counts as a bomb; this means Isaac can be immune to it with Pyromaniac or Host Hat.

• [Before Repentance] With Pyromaniac, Isaac can be healed when stomped.

• [Before Repentance] Red Champion Mom is greatly negated with Pyromaniac or Host Hat.

• [Repentance] Mom's stomp attack now deals contact damage, causing immunity to explosions to no longer avoid damage from the stomp.

• The Polaroid will always spawn on the left pedestal and The Negative is always on the right.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In Mom's entry in the bestiary, her "kills" value will never increase. It is unclear if this is a lore implication or a bug.

• In The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls rendition of Credit Card, the name "Magdalene O. Moriah" can be seen carved in the credit card. The name was reused on the Four Souls+ rendition of Divorce Papers. Edmund has confirmed that this is indeed Mom's full name.

• The initials spell out "M.O.M.".

• [Repentance] This is further confirmed in-game during the background conversation during the Ascent, where Dad calls Mom "Maggy" as he tells her to shut up.

• The last name "Moriah" is likely a reference to the biblical location of the same name. In the Bible, it is said that Moriah is where Abraham almost sacrificed his son before God sent an angel to stop his hand.

• The playable character Magdalene shares a first name with Mom, but whether or not the two of them have connections remains yet to be known.

• According to Edmund, the occupations of Mom and Dad are stay-at-home mom and handyman respectively.

• Mom is voiced by Carla Kihlstedt.

• The battle theme for this boss is "Matricide", a term for the killing of one's own mother.

• Mom appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original, Mom's voice was provided by Michelle Schroeder-Lowrey, an associate of Jordan Fehr, the sound designer.

• Unlike in Rebirth, Mom would shout "Isaac!" whenever she exposed her eye.

• The battle theme in the original game was "Thine Wrath..."

• Using The Bible and killing Mom instantly is a reference to how a bible hits her head in the epilogue of the game, knocking her out or killing her.

• Mom's eye appearing out of the doors could represent Mom's peeping in Isaac's room to check on him.

• Mom constantly screaming "Isaac" seems to suggest how Mom was desperately trying to find her son.

• Mom is the only final boss that has Champion variants.

• During the versus screen, the "Isaac!" line from Mom can be heard, despite the battle not starting yet. She is one of [Before Repentance] seven/ [Repentance] five bosses that can be heard during the versus screen; the other [Before Repentance] six/ [Repentance] four are Big Horn, The Stain, The Forsaken, [Before Repentance] Mom's Heart, [Before Repentance] It Lives!, and Mother.

• The skirt she wears on her in-game sprite is difficult to see in regular play, as her leg extends past the screen. Using the Dataminer or the Meat Cleaver can make the skirt visible.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Delirium's Mom form appears to wear a pile of flesh and organs rather than a skirt.

• A disembodied version of Mom's leg stomp attack can be summoned as part of the effects of II - The High Priestess, Mom's Toenail, Broken Shovel 1, and II - The High Priestess?.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Prior to Booster Pack #5, Globins spawned by Mom could turn into Dank Globins if she was fought in Dank Depths.

• [Repentance] When she is fought in the Mausoleum, her leg appears to be in a much more sickly state, with many varicose veins lining it. [end edition note] 

• Her hand also has a unique updated sprite, despite the fact that she never uses it in this fight.

• Mother could be considered as her posthumous version.

• Mom later made appearances in The Legend of Bumbo and Mewgenics, two other games by Edmund.

Mom's Bottle of Pills.title: Mom's Bottle of Pills
Mom's Bottle of Pills.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• On use, gives Isaac a random pill.

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] The item will cost 10 cents if found in a Shop

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the inner ring, looking like pills. The wisps spawn pills when destroyed. The wisps come in random colors (Blue, Red, White, Pink, Gray, Light Blue, and Yellow). Each color may fire tears that confuse, poison, petrify, burn, or spawn troll bombs. Each tear effect is assigned to one color of pill wisp based on the current seed. The only color pill wisp without a tear effect also spawns a hostile Spider when destroyed. For the troll bomb effect, the pill itself spawns the troll bomb instead of the tear, and the chance for it to do so is independent of whether or not its tears hit anything.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Starter Deck: Gives cards instead.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • In the original The Binding of Isaac, this item was unlocked by donating to Blood Donation Machines 20 times.

fields.description: Gives Isaac a random pill.

Mom's Box.title: Mom's Box
Mom's Box.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Increases luck by 1 and doubles the effects of certain trinkets while held. When used, drops a random trinket on the ground.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Most trinkets are not affected.

• [Repentance] Of the 188 trinkets in Repentance, only 72 have a doubled effect.

• [Repentance+] All trinkets have some added effect, either simply a doubled effect or a specifically enhanced one.

• [Repentance] This effect stacks additively with Golden Trinkets; holding one with Mom's Box will cause applicable trinkets to have triple the regular effect. [end edition note] 

• Holding a second Mom's Box by using Schoolbag only increases luck, the effects of trinkets are not affected further.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] Gulp! Pill / Marbles / Smelter: Trinket effects are still doubled when permanently applied to Isaac. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Mother's Kiss: Grants double the heart containers but only one of them is filled.

• Void: Passive effects of Mom's Box are lost if absorbed.

• Book of Virtues: Spawns a normal wisp with no unique effect.

The following trinkets have a different benefit than their effect being doubled:

• Broken Remote: Triggers the Teleport 2.0 effect whenever an activated item is used.

• NO!: Prevents items with quality 0 from appearing.

• Rosary Bead: Adds 4 Rosaries to all item pools, 6 if the trinket is golden. Upon picking up a Rosary, the effect ends.

• 'M: The new item has a 10% chance to be fully charged, 20% chance if the trinket is golden.

• Adoption Papers: Familiars are always on sale. Shops are also able to sell Soul of Lilith if the trinket is golden.

• Apple of Sodom: All types of hearts can be converted to spiders. No further benefit if the trinket is golden.

• Baby-Bender: Familiars gain the Brain Worm effect. Familiars gain the Tape Worm effect on top if the trinket is golden.

• Beth's Essence: The wisps spawned by the trinket have a 50% chance to be special wisps, 100% chance if the trinket is golden.

• Blessed Penny: Proc chance increases, but less than 2× or 3× if the trinket is golden.

• Bloody Crown: Treasure rooms in the Womb have an item choice, as if Isaac had More Options. No further benefit if the trinket is golden.

• Bloody Penny: Proc chance increases, but less than 2× or 3× if the trinket is golden.

• Blue Key: Makes the blue rooms drop double rewards when cleared. If the trinket is golden, the reward is tripled.

• Brain Worm: Shots have a 25% chance to be piercing, 50% chance if the trinket is golden. 

• Broken Ankh: Proc chance increases, but less than 2× or 3× if the trinket is golden.

• Broken Padlock: Challenge rooms, arcades and Mega Satan door can be opened with bombs. Boss rooms can be opened with bombs as well if the trinket is golden.

• Callus: Damage from sacrifice spikes is reduced to 1/2 hearts. If the trinket is golden, all damage is reduced to 1/2 hearts

• Crow Heart: Adds a 25% chance that taking red heart damage does not reduce Devil room chances, 50% if the trinket is golden.

• Daemon's Tail: Blue and purple fires drop Black Hearts instead of Soul Heart. No further benefit if the trinket is golden.

• Cursed Skull: Teleports Isaac to a random special room instead of any room. Golden trinket triggers if Isaac has 1 full heart or less after taking damage.

sections.heading: [Before Repentance+] No Effect
sections.text:
These trinkets are not affected by Mom's Box.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Mom's Contact]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item description possibly is a reference to the film Seven (1995) where the climax of the film involves the protagonist asking the question over and over again "What's in the box?".

• [Repentance] The item strongly resembles the chest found in Mom's room in Home. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] This item is used in Pica Run. [end edition note] 

• This item is implied to be made of wood, due to its inclusion in the Wooden Chest.

Mom's Bracelet.title: Mom's Bracelet
Mom's Bracelet.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, picks up the obstacle in front of Isaac. The obstacle can be thrown at enemies, dealing 40 damage and breaking on impact, dropping any contents they may contain.

• Obstacles can be carried between rooms.

• Using it on a Host / Mobile Host will lift the shell off and transform it into a Red Host / Flesh Mobile Host. Isaac can throw the shell after picking it up.

• • The affected hosts will still fire 3 shots instead of 5.

• Isaac can throw bombs using this, either his bombs or Troll Bombs.

• • Golden Troll Bombs grant Isaac unlimited bombs for the floor as they can be carried through rooms this way.

• Tainted Forgotten can be picked up by any other player using it.

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The item will cost 10 cents if found in a Shop.

• Throwing a Throwable Bomb or Poops and bombs created by Tainted ??? and IBS counts as using the bracelet, using up a charge.

• The item's charge will only be depleted once an object is thrown.

• Activating the item again will drop the picked up obstacle where Isaac is standing without consuming a charge. This doesn't damage Isaac directly, but any break effects the obstacle has can still occur.

• • This makes it easy to quickly clear paths through large amounts of rocks.

• • While the dropped obstacle is falling toward the ground, it can be picked up again by activating Mom's Bracelet.

• • 
• Obstacles thrown by enemies, such as Polty, can be caught in the same way.

• Spiked rocks cannot be picked up, even if their spikes are retracted.

• Similarly, Metal Blocks, Key Blocks and Pillars also cannot be picked up.

• Throwing a Giant Poop at an enemy deals 320 damage instead of 40.

• Activating the item while running into a Red Poop will allow Isaac to chuck it and effectively remove it from the room.

• Poops created by Tainted ??? and IBS can be picked up and thrown again freely. You can carry them between rooms and using Mom's Bracelet while holding one will drop them on top of Isaac without destroying them.

• Unlike other obstacles, dropping them under a pit will spawn them to the nearest open space available. 

• Picking up a Corn Poop, will cause the blue flies to follow Isaac, but Corn Poop will not spawn more flies unless the ones around Isaac get used. 

• Rapidly dropping and picking up a Stinky Poop in one spot will create a potent fart cloud, which when detonated deals a lot of damage.

• While carrying a rock, Isaac cannot drop down a trapdoor to the next floor. This can be used as a way to get pickups close to an open trapdoor without accidentally dropping to the next floor.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Best Friend: The explosive decoy can be picked up and thrown.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Three wisps are created where thrown obstacles land; these wisps rotate around where the obstacle was thrown and fire tears in the same direction Isaac does. The wisps do not persist between rooms. Isaac cannot have more than 8 of these wisps at one time, and wisps in Isaac's middle ring count against this limit. Wisps' tears have a 10% chance of inflicting confusion on enemies.

• Cube Baby: Can be picked up and thrown by using the bracelet while trying to kick the Cube Baby. When thrown, Cube Baby deals around the amount of damage as a higher speed kick, but it will also leave the creep that a frozen enemy would create when kicked.

• Dirty Mind / Dingle Berry: Friendly Dips can be picked up and thrown at enemies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Multidimensional Baby: Rocks thrown through the baby will turn into tears, thus removing the possibility to get any rewards from rocks that spawn them.

• Stompy transformation: Isaac will raise his hands, but be unable to pick up any rocks, effectively rendering the bracelet useless. Can still be used on Hosts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mom's Bracelet originated from the Antibirth mod.

• The item's design and mechanics are a direct reference to the Power Bracelet from the "Legend of Zelda" series.

• This item is used in Isaac's Awakening.

• This item can be found as one of the Nintendo-themed Treasure Room items in the 6th of December's Daily Run, which is an homage to the late CEO of Nintendo, Satoru Iwata.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using Mom's Bracelet to throw a tile into Multidimensional Baby will turn the tile into two tears, and any pickups (such as Soul Hearts from Tinted Rocks) will not drop.
Bug note: Infinite skulls can be farmed off of Hosts even though after initially removing the skull, the Host changes into a different variant.

fields.description: Lets Isaac pick up and throw rocks, TNT, Poops, friendly Dips, Bombs, and other obstacles.

Mom's Contacts.title: Mom's Contacts
Mom's Contacts.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a chance to shoot petrifying tears.

• [Before Repentance] +0.25 range. ( [Rebirth only] not applied until the next time Isaac's range stat is updated).

• [Repentance] +1.5 range.

• [Before Repentance] +0.5 tear falling speed. ( [Rebirth only] not applied until the next time Isaac's tear falling speed is updated).

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] This item has a 1% chance to spawn when bombing Mom's Dressing Table. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method. [end edition note] 

• Despite granting the Yes Mother? transformation, duplicated items will not contribute to unlocking Mom's Contacts. Three different items are required to unlock it.

• The chance to fire a petrifying tear depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \min(\frac1 { 5 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.15 \right \rfloor},50\%)

• At base Luck (0), the chance is 20%, maxing out at 50% at 20 Luck.

• Petrifying the Heart of a Mask + Heart also freezes the Mask bound to it.

• Petrifying an enemy with a weak zone (Scolex or Carrion Queen) will make the enemy take damage anywhere while it is petrified, making combat significantly easier.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/Haemolacria/The Parasite: If the main tear causes petrification, split tears will too.

• Finger!: Finger can also apply the petrification effect.

• Lachryphagy: If freezing tears are fed first when they burst, the split tears can also freeze enemies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone: The beam can occasionally freeze enemies with no visual difference.

• Epic Fetus: Occasionally fires missiles that can freeze enemies. No visual difference.

• Technology: Lasers can occasionally freeze enemies with no visual difference.

• Technology Zero: The electricity that is connecting tears has a chance to freeze enemies.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] Mom's Contacts' appearance was changed in Booster Pack #5.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Enemies with multiple segments (Chub, Pin, etc.) can be petrified and have their segments destroyed individually, but continue to live with any remaining health. This can be problematic at times especially with Carrion Queen, as you could destroy the "tail" or center body segment when Carrion Queen is petrified, thus making you have to petrify her again, or use bombs to do damage.

sections.text: • The Binding of Isaac Item Trigger Testing

Mom's Eye.title: Mom's Eye
Mom's Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac a chance to shoot a tear out of an eye on the back of his head.

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] The chance to shoot an extra tear depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 2 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.5 \right \rfloor}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 50%, maxing out at 100% at 2 luck.

• [Repentance] The chance to shoot an extra tear depends on the luck stat and is based on this formula: 50\% + (10\% * \mathit{Luck})

• This means that the chance starts at 50% at 0 luck, minimizes at 0% at -5 luck, and maximizes at 100% at 5 luck.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Continuum: Tears shot out of the back reappear on the opposite side of the screen.

• Eye of the Occult: Mom's Eye tears follow the direction in which Isaac is shooting.

• Loki's Horns: Any time Mom's Eye would activate, Loki's Horns activates instead.

• Rubber Cement: Tears bounce around, making the backward tear more likely to hit enemies.

• Mom's Knife: Another knife is permanently behind Isaac, able to deal contact damage. The fire chance is still affected by luck as usual.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 20/20/The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider: No effect on the tears fired out of the back of Isaac's head. The chance to activate is checked per shot, not for each tear fired.

• Dr. Fetus: Occasionally shoots a bomb backward. Not recommended, as self-damage is likely.

• Doctor's Remote/Epic Fetus: Chance for two airstrikes on opposite sides of Isaac.

• Ipecac: Occasionally shoots an explosive shot backward. Not recommended, as self-damage is likely.

• Incubus: No effect.

• Kidney Stone: Adds a chance for each tear from the barrage to fire from the front and back of Isaac. The kidney stone will only fire from the front of Isaac.

• Lead Pencil: Adds a chance for the tear barrage to be fired behind Isaac instead of in front.

• The Ludovico Technique: Adds a chance for piercing + spectral tears to be fired in random directions from the main tear. This chance scales with luck and goes up to 100% at 10 Luck.

• Monstro's Lung: Occasionally fires one red tear out the back of Isaac's head.

• Tractor Beam: The backward tear is not affected by Tractor Beam.

• The Wiz: The backward tear is not affected by The Wiz.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] Mom's Eye's appearance was changed in Booster Pack #5.

• The item is based on the adage that a mother has an eye on the back of her head, and is thus always able to see what her child is up to.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Having a Mom's Eye, Technology and Technology 2 makes the back laser fire extremely fast.

Mom's Eyeshadow.title: Mom's Eyeshadow
Mom's Eyeshadow.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives a chance to shoot charming tears.

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] This item has a 1% chance to spawn when bombing Mom's Dressing Table. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method. [end edition note] 

• The chance for a tear to be charming depends on the Luck stat. The activation rate is almost equal to 1/(10 - (Luck / 3)). With 0 Luck, the chance is 10%, maxing out at 100% at 26.95 Luck.

• Due to how this formula works, increases in activation rate are only seen with about every 3 points of Luck, as this formula rounds down after dividing Isaac's Luck by 3.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Immaculate Heart: Orbital tears produced by this item can charm.

• Compound Fracture / Cricket's Body / Haemolacria / The Parasite: Split tears will retain the charm effect if main tear had the charm effect.

• Finger!: Finger can also apply the charm effect.

• Lachryphagy: If a charm tear is fed, all burst tears can charm. If a normal tear is fed, the burst tears cannot charm.

fields.description: Tears have a chance to charm enemies.

Mom's Hand.title: Mom's Hand
Mom's Hand.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Mom's Hands are tricky foes. When these enemies spawn (either at the start of a room or in a Challenge Room wave), Mom's laugh can be heard [Afterbirth onward] and the ground may shake [end edition note] . After this, a disembodied hand will come down to try and grab Isaac, pausing in a stunned state for a brief moment before going back up to repeat this. Before coming down, a subtle shadow on the floor will indicate where the hand is going to land. They can spawn in groups of up to six in large rooms.

If Isaac is grabbed, he takes half a heart of damage and is sent back to the spawn room of the floor. Any enemies that Isaac damaged or killed before being grabbed will respawn at full health when Isaac returns to the room. If a black heart is depleted when Isaac is grabbed, he will not be teleported and the hand will die instead.

Charmed Mom's Hands are extremely powerful, as they can potentially kill any monster they attack in a single move if they manage to grab them and pull them up without getting killed in the process. This includes normally invincible enemies such as Stone Grimaces. This can be seen more easily by using the "C0CK FGHT" Special Seed.

sections.heading: Mom's Dead Hand
sections.text: Mom's Dead Hands behave similarly to regular Mom's Hands. When they land, they send out 3-4 lines of rock waves in the cardinal directions that can curve slightly and will destroy most obstacles and damage most monsters in its path. Upon death, they spawn 2-3 Spiders. Unlike normal Mom's Hands, they can't grab and teleport Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The rock waves that Mom's Dead Hands spawn can open Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Hands are likely inspired by Wallmasters from the The Legend of Zelda.

• If Mom's Hand catches Isaac in a Challenge Room, it will teleport him out of the room without having to fight the remaining enemy waves, even if the room is re-entered.

• Mom's Hand is the only enemy in the game that can teleport Isaac to a different room.

• Emergency Contact card spawns two Mom's Hands that grab enemies.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Entering a room with a Mom's Hand/Mom's Dead Hand causes only very minimal screen shake. Spawning them with the debug console will cause a much more noticeable effect.

Mom's Heart.title: Mom's Heart
Mom's Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Mom's Heart is a boss that can appear on the second floor of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero), and is the final boss of Endings 1-11.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Prior to Booster Pack #5, it could also appear in the Scarred Womb.
After being killed 11 times, Mom's Heart is permanently replaced by It Lives!. However, even after being replaced by It Lives!, there are a few circumstances in which Mom's Heart can still be fought:

• [Afterbirth onward] It can still appear in the Nightmare Boss wave of Chapter 4 in [mode: greed; greedier] Greed/Greedier Mode.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] It has a chance to appear in one of the boss rooms in The Void. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] After the defeat of the stronger version of Mom on the second floor of Chapter 3.5 (Mausoleum, Gehenna), a flesh door appears, which can be opened if Isaac has collected both Knife Piece 1 and Knife Piece 2. Behind it, a stronger version of Mom's Heart can be fought. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
At the beginning of the fight, Mom's Heart is always accompanied by 2 Eyes. After a while, Mom's Heart retreats upwards, becoming invulnerable and launching four diagonal lines of red projectiles in a spread that slowly rotates clockwise. When each original Eye is killed, another one spawns in its place near the top of the arena.

• At any point during this sequence, if Mom's Heart's HP is brought below the threshold for her second phase, she will spawn Lumps instead of Eyes.

After the second set of Eyes have been killed, Mom's Heart alternates between two attacks:

• Lowers itself and shoots red projectiles in different patterns:

• 10 projectiles in all directions that expand outwards either continuously or in a pulsating manner.

• 2 streams of projectiles that spiral outwards.

• 2 rings of ten projectiles that pulsate outwards at different intervals.

• 8 slightly curved lines of projectiles that rotate and expand outwards slowly.

• After performing one of these projectile patterns for long enough, Mom's Heart retreats upwards again, shooting the same four slow-moving lines of projectiles, and spawns a number enemies of a singular type:

• 3 Flesh Mobile Hosts

• 3 Globins

• 2 Eyes

• • The type of monsters spawned in each wave is determined always follows the above order.

• • In the same manner as the original Eyes, a copy of each individual monster spawns again following the defeat of the original one.

• After all enemies have been defeated, Mom's Heart lowers itself and repeats the entire process.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After reaching 60% HP, Mom's Heart beats slightly faster and continues the same behavior, but includes new projectile patterns and replaces the types of monsters it spawns.

• Its projectile patterns now include:

• A single line of projectiles that follows Isaac.

• 5 lines of projectiles that mimic Isaac's movements (these lines have no space between projectiles).

• 3 pulsating curved lines of projectiles that rotate and expand outwards. This pattern can occasionally change direction of rotation.

• Its spawned monsters are now:

• 3 Lumps

• 2 Swingers

• 3 Globins

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text:
After reaching 30% HP, Mom's Heart beats much faster and no longer retreats upwards and instead performs projectile attacks and spawns enemies simultaneously. However, after finishing each projectile pattern, if there are any monsters alive, it will not perform another pattern until they are killed. In addition, a second wave of monsters no longer spawns after the first is killed.

• It gains one new projectile pattern:

• 4 curved lines of projectiles that continuously rotate and expand outwards.

• It loses the projectile patterns from the first phase except for the following 2:

• 2 streams of projectiles that spiral outwards.

• 8 slightly curved lines of projectiles that rotate and expand outwards slowly.

• Its spawned monsters are now:

• 4 Walking Boils

• 4 Tumors

• 4 Hearts

sections.heading: Phase 4
sections.text:
After reaching 20% HP, Mom's Heart stops its previous attacks and shoots four diagonal Brimstone lasers that rotate either clockwise or counter-clockwise for a duration before stopping for a moment and then repeating the attack.

• The direction the lasers rotate depends on which is closest to Isaac when they are fired. The closer laser will rotate after Isaac and the rest will follow.

• The duration the beams rotate can be: 1 rotation, 1 and a half rotations, or 2 whole rotations.

• Upon defeat, Mom's Heart fires out a ring of 14 projectiles.

All of Mom's Heart's projectiles deal a whole heart of damage. The heart itself does not deal contact damage.

As most of Mom's Heart's projectile attacks are synced with the rhythm of the heart's beating, as the fight progresses, the speed of each projectile attack increases.

All of Mom's Heart's projectile attacks can hurt and kill spawned monsters.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
The beginning of this fight is similar to one from Chapter 4, as Mom's Heart is always accompanied by two Eyes and retreats upwards after awhile, shooting the same four slow-moving lines of projectiles. However, a second pair of Eyes does not replace the first, and after both initial Eyes are killed, Mom's Heart lowers itself and no longer retreats upwards.

• Mom's Heart begins with 3 projectile patterns it can perform:

• 2 rings of 8 projectiles at different intervals that expand outwards overlapping on each other either continuously or in a pulsating manner.

• 2 streams of projectiles that spiral outwards and gradually increase in density.

• 2 rings of 8 projectiles each ring expanding and alternating between rotating clockwise and counter-clockwise.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After reaching 60% HP, Mom's Heart beats slightly faster and replaces the patterns from its first phase with the following patterns:

• 5 lines of projectiles that rotate and pulsate outwards.

• A combined ring of 2 rings of 8 projectiles that rotate in opposite directions while expanding.

• 16 wavy streams of projectiles that intertwine and create gaps.

• 16 streams of projectiles that curve back towards Mom's Heart and intertwine to create gaps.

• 5 waving lines of projectiles that rotate and expand outwards.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text:
After reaching 30% HP, Mom's Heart beats much faster, keeps the patterns from its previous phase, and gains the following patterns:

• 6 curved lines of projectiles that rotate in opposite directions while expanding — 3 clockwise, 3 counter-clockwise.

• A ring of 12 projectiles that expands outwards, along with 2 rings of 4 projectiles that expand outwards and rotate in opposite directions at a higher speed.
It also regains 2 patterns from its first phase:

• 2 streams of projectiles that spiral outwards and gradually increase in density.

• 2 rings of 8 projectiles, each ring expanding and alternating between rotating clockwise and counter-clockwise.

sections.heading: Phase 4
sections.text:
After reaching 10% HP, Mom's Heart stops its previous projectile attacks and fires 2 Brimstone lasers in opposite directions that slowly rotate either clockwise or counter-clockwise at a steady pace. During this, it also shoots 2 continuous streams of projectiles, one that follows Isaac's movements and the other mirroring the first.

• Upon defeat, Mom's Heart fires out a ring of 14 projectiles and permanently causes the [cu: Darkness] and gray-scale effect for the entire floor. This persists for a brief moment upon entering the Corpse. Additionally it makes all consumables, items, and shops disappear after Mom's Heart is killed.

A majority of Mom's Heart's projectile attacks use large projectiles and deal a whole heart of damage; however, some attacks can be mixed with, or fully use smaller projectiles which only deal half a heart of damage. The heart's Brimstone lasers also only deal half a heart of damage.

As most of Mom's Heart's projectile attacks are synced with the rhythm of the heart's beating, as the fight progresses, the speed of each projectile attack increases.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Everything Is Terrible!!! changes
sections.text:
[hatnote: See also: Everything is Terrible 2!!!] 
After beating Mom's Heart 5 times, the following playthroughs have the following changes:

• Bosses drop 1 less health pickup.

• The chance of a floor receiving a curse increases.

• [Repentance] The Bulb enemy can appear. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Unlocks Half Soul Hearts.

• [Repentance] Unlocks Micro Battery.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Every time Mom's Heart is defeated changes the current savefile's image until It Lives! is unlocked.

• Until It Lives! is unlocked, Mom's Heart cannot be continued past unless a Devil Room or an Angel Room appears, which allows access to Sheol or the Cathedral, respectively.

• Just like Mom, using The Bible or XV - The Devil? against Mom's Heart will kill it instantly.

• If Forget Me Now or a 5 pip Dice Room is used on Womb II / Utero II / Scarred Womb II after defeating Mom's Heart, and Mom's Heart is again defeated on the regenerated floor, it will count as having defeated Mom's Heart 2 separate times, therefore unlocking 2 consequent endings.

• [Repentance] Erasing Mausoleum / Gehenna Mom's Heart with the Eraser will not open the passage to Corpse. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Mom's Heart appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original Binding Of Isaac, the only attack Mom's Heart could perform was spawning 2-4 monsters before disappearing and repeating the same move each time the wave of monsters were killed off.

• The music that plays during this fight is titled Ventricide. Ventricide is a made-up word formed from the word ventricle (one of the two larger chambers of the heart) and the suffix -cide, which denotes an act of killing. This theme is used in other tracks, such as Matricide, Hericide, and Infanticide.

• Ventricide could also be a junction of the prefix ventr- (from the latin word venter), which could denote "belly", "stomach", "womb" or "fetus", with the suffix -cide.

• Mom's Heart shares this theme with It Lives!.

• [Before Repentance] During the versus screen, Mom's Heart's enemy-spawning sound can be heard. Mom's Heart is one of [Before Repentance] seven / [Repentance] five bosses that can be heard during the versus screen, the other [Before Repentance] six / [Repentance] four being The Stain, The Forsaken, Big Horn, Mom, [Before Repentance] It Lives!, and Mother.

• [Repentance] The floor graphic beneath Isaac and Mom's Heart in the boss VS Screen in Mausoleum/Gehenna is of a slightly lighter shade of red than in the Womb.

• In addition to this, despite having a Womb backdrop, Mom's Heart's room in the Mausoleum/Gehenna does not have the red static effect of the Womb.

• Getting killed by the final ring of projectiles released after killing Mom's Heart will play the respective ending if there is one, and will count as a Mom's Heart kill. However, it is still considered a loss and will not count towards a win streak.

• [Repentance] Originally in Antibirth, the Mausoleum version of Mom's Heart could spawn enemies like Bouncers and Blurbs. [end edition note] 

• Isaac consistently killing Mom's Heart, followed by the first appearances of the Ending Chest, could represent how his death hurt his mother. Considering how in the Final Ending after defeating The Beast, Isaac's Mom can be seen heartbroken about her son's demise.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Sometimes, if the boss intro is skipped, the game will not teleport Isaac into the center of the bottom of the room, resulting in immediate contact damage with one of the Eyes or Mom's Heart, depending on the direction of the room's entrance.

Mom's Key.title: Mom's Key
Mom's Key.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac two Keys.

• If a non-Red Chest spawns hearts, coins, Bombs and/or Keys, causes the chest to spawn a second group of said pickups, effectively doubling the average pickup yield.

• Contributes to the Yes Mother? transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Mom's Key cannot change the contents of a chest; it will only cause it to spawn extra pickups.

• All other chest rewards (such as pills, cards, items, etc.) will not cause the chest to spawn additional pickups.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:

• The appearance of Mom's Key is a reference to Bowser's boss key in Super Mario 64 as well as the Boss Key in various Legend of Zelda games.
