Schoolbag.title: Schoolbag
Schoolbag.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Allows Isaac to hold two active items.

• Swap between active items by pressing the [plat: PC] CTRL, [plat: PS4] R2, [plat: XboxOne] RT, or [plat: Switch] ZR.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The button to swap between active items is the same button used to swap between cards and pills.

• Items in the secondary slot will recharge at the same rate as the primary item.

• Items that grant temporary effects for the room, such as The Nail, may deactivate if switched with an item in the secondary slot.

• The ? Card does not activate both active items.

• While holding an active item that grants passive bonuses in the secondary slot, swapping the main slot item with a pedestal item may remove the bonuses. If this happens, Isaac can swap the bonus-granting item to the pedestal and pick it up again to regain them.

• The swap key must be pressed twice if playing as The Forgotten.

• This item cannot be unlocked if the player encounters more than [Before Repentance] one/ [Repentance] two [cu: XL] in Chapters 1-3, except by chance of finding Silver Dollar, Wicked Crown, Holy Crown, Forget Me Now, or a 5-pip Dice Room.

• If one Curse of the Labyrinth is encountered, getting to ??? or Mausoleum/Gehenna II and entering the Shop there will unlock the Schoolbag.

• [Repentance] If Curse of the Labyrinth was encountered twice, entering the shops in both Mausoleum/Gehenna II and ??? will unlock the Schoolbag. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] If Tainted Isaac drops Schoolbag, the 2nd active item in the player's inventory is destroyed. However, a duplicate active item spawns beside Schoolbag. Tainted Isaac's reroll ability applies to this new item, and the player can choose between the original active item or a new item. Picking up the original active item again will count as another item towards any transformation.

• [Repentance] In "True" Co-op, when a player dies with this item, they will drop one of their active items if they have two. It is unknown if this is a bug or intended interaction.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Best Friend/Mr. Boom + Remote Detonator: The active item bombs are affected by Remote Detonator.

• Blood Rights/Razor Blade + Habit: Damage from the item grants a point of charge to Isaac's other held active item.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Glowing Hourglass + Forget Me Now: Using Forget Me Now will fully recharge Glowing Hourglass on the new floor, using Glowing Hourglass after that will take Isaac back to the previous room while also giving back Forget Me Now. This allows for infinite usage of Glowing Hourglass as well as infinite retries of any room as long as Forget Me Now is used before the room is cleared. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Converter + Guppy's Paw : Converter turns one soul heart into 1 red heart, while Guppy's paw turns 1 red heart into 3 soul hearts. This effectively gives you infinite health for the run.

• Kamikaze!: The cooldown before the player can use Kamikaze! again is eliminated when switching items. Depending on how fast the player can push the buttons, Kamikaze! can be used multiple times during Isaac's invincibility frames.

• Mom's Box: If a trinket is picked up while Mom's Box is in the active slot, swapping between active items will not remove the doubled trinket effect.

• A Pony / White Pony: Will continue to grant flight and the speed bonus while held in the secondary slot.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• ? Card: Does not activate both active items.

• My Little Unicorn / The Gamekid / Unicorn Stump: Switching items breaks the invincibility effect. This does not apply to other sources of invincibility.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Schoolbag was based on the Racing+ implementation of the Schoolbag from the Antibirth mod, and it is the only item from Antibirth to be added to the game before Repentance.

• This item is used in Baptism by Fire.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Removing Schoolbag using D100, D4, or through being granted the effect from Metronome and using it again, does not cause the second active item to be removed or dropped into a pedestal; Isaac will still be able to hold his second active item until he picks up another active item, which will then remove the second slot and delete the active item contained.
Bug note: Re-rolling by a Dice Room removes the primary active item but the second one remains unchanged, allowing another active item to be picked up. Picking up another active item after this will result in the previous bug; the second slot is removed and the active item contained is deleted.
Bug note: As of V1.06.J168, the item inside the Schoolbag has a minor graphical glitch when picking up a third active item. For a single frame as the pickup animation ends, the item's "charged glow" status and number of bars will match the item that Isaac is picking up.
Bug note: When Isaac's Tears is in the first active item slot, the secondary item does not charge upon clearing rooms.
Bug note: If a player dies in True Co-op in the boss room, and the schoolbag drops an active item, because of the fact that boss item pedestals will spawn as many items as there are players, picking the active item back will spawn additional items up to 3. If the boss pool is gone through, it will start pulling from the treasure room. Once another Active item appears, any other items that could be gained through this method are (likely, needs more testing) unavailable.

fields.description: Allows Isaac to hold two active items.

Scissors.title: Scissors
Scissors.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; a similar looking item; The Pinking Shears; the trinket; Safety Scissors]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Detaches Isaac's head from his body and turns the head into a stationary familiar that fires tears for the current room.

• The player still controls Isaac's headless body, which also shoots tears.

• • [Repentance] The body constantly spews a controllable fountain of blood shots, dealing about 0.66x-1.01x damage.

• • 
• The blood fountain can be aimed in any direction like Analog Stick.

• [Before Repentance] The tears fired by the head do not scale with Isaac's damage and always do 3.5 damage.

• • [Repentance] The head's tears are affected by Isaac's stats and attack modifiers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Can spawn multiple heads if used in the same room more than once.

• [Repentance] Only the most recent head is able to fire.

• [Before Repentance] Brimstone and Technology are not fired from the stationary head.

• If Isaac has an invisible body due to the cosmetic effect of Transcendence, only a shadow will be seen after using the Scissors.

• [Before Repentance] If Isaac is Blindfolded, the floating head can still fire tears.

• [Repentance] The floating head does nothing as Lilith, Tainted Lilith, and Tainted Forgotten.

• As The Forgotten, the floating head will only fire tears when the Soul is active.

• The floating head will not fire tears as Tainted Samson while he is enraged.

• [edition anr] Each wave of Boss Rush fully recharges the item, allowing many heads to be spawned.

• Only deaths which end runs (i.e. Isaac is not revived by a revival item such as 1up!) count towards unlocking the Scissors.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns red wisps in the middle ring. The wisps fire 2-3 tears at a time, which are inaccurate, travel in an arc, and have variable range.

• [Repentance] Epic Fetus / Marked: Blood fountain from the body will aim at the crosshair.

• [Repentance] The Ludovico Technique: Blood fountain from the body will aim at the controlled tear.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• The Pinking Shears: If Scissors and Pinking Shears are used together, control is given back to an invisible head with only a shadow visible as both the head and body are mobilized to attack.

• BFFS!: The loose head won't become larger, but will deal double damage.

• Box of Friends: No effect.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• C Section: C Section tears are fired from the body instead of the head. This makes the head do nothing, but the item still provides a benefit as the body will fire both the C Section tears and the blood fountain from Scissors.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is very likely a reference to the English idiom "running with scissors", which means to "willfully act in a reckless, foolish, and/or dangerous manner", alluding to the literal act of running with a pair of scissors in one's hand, which can cause severe injury, thus the item's effect and unlock condition.

• In original flash version of The Binding of Isaac, dying 100 times unlocked The Pinking Shears.

fields.name: Scissors
fields.description: Turns Isaac's head into a stationary familiar for the current room which fires tears automatically. [Repentance] Isaac's body also shoots a controllable fountain of blood shots for the room.

Scolex.title: Scolex
Scolex.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Scolex is a boss that can appear in the Womb and the Scarred Womb.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Scolex is only vulnerable in his blinking tail segment. He burrows into the ground before performing the following attacks:

• Jumps out of the ground towards Isaac, burrowing back into the ground at the end of the jump.

• If Scolex is hit by an explosion while mid-air, he will be deflected backwards.

• Partially emerges head-first and shoots out a cluster of projectiles towards Isaac, similar to Monstro, but with a wider spread.

• After performing this attack, Scolex will always jump out of the same spot he entered.

• Partially emerges tail-first and fires cluster of 3 red Ipecac shots towards Isaac.

• After performing this attack, Scolex will always jump out of the same spot he entered.
Scolex deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 18] : Scolex is 15% larger, slower, and has 25% more HP (375).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Sometimes, several Lumps, Guts, Para-Bites, or Round Worms can accompany Scolex at the start of the battle.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Scolex appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• Scolex is the only Boss to have lost access to a Champion variant in an update. Specifically in Repentance, where his dark grey counterpart is inaccessible unless using Console commands to summon it.

• Scolex can be considered an older or younger version of Pin, but not a posthumous one (that title goes to The Frail).

• A scolex is the name of the head of a tapeworm.

• Compared to the original Binding of Isaac, Scolex's head and tail attacks are swapped.

• He also has 3 more body segments than in the original.

• Scolex bears some resemblance to a mythological Mongolian Death Worm, which are described as long, scaly, and blood red. It also raises half its body out of the sand and covers its prey with a lethal acidic substance, which is somewhat similar to Scolex's head attack.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: When Scolex is slowed, some of his body parts may detach or won't even show up - they will only be visible while entering the ground (especially the tail).
Bug note: If the final vulnerable segment of Scolex's tail is destroyed using the Chaos Card, the boss will glitch and become harder to kill. The tail will appear again if his head gets bombed or he hits Isaac.
Bug note: If Scolex is petrified (with Mom's Contacts or other similar items) when it is in mid-air, any segment of its body can be damaged.
Bug note: If Scolex is under the effects of Broken Modem in mid-air, his jump will be stopped and he will fall.
Bug note: If Scolex is frozen with Midas' Touch or Dad's Ring and attacked, he can split into two halves, one with his head and one with his tail.

Scorpio.title: Scorpio
Scorpio.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants poison tears, dealing damage over time when inflicted.

• [Rebirth only] The poison randomly hits either 2 or 3 times, dealing a total of 4 or 6 damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] The poison hits twice, dealing a total of double Isaac's damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item has the same effect as The Common Cold on every shot. As such, all synergies with that item also apply to Scorpio at a 100% chance.

• This includes the same effect when absorbed by Abyss.

sections.heading: Effects

• +0.5 tears.

• +0.2 shot speed.

Head of the Keeper.title: Head of the Keeper
Head of the Keeper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac's tears become coins. Hitting an enemy with tears has a 5% chance to drop a Penny at the point of impact.

• The chance is not affected by Luck.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Head of the Keeper has a 1% chance to drop from destroying normal Shopkeepers.

• [Repentance] The only way of finding Head of the Keeper is from Shopkeepers, using Spindown Dice on Papa Fly, as a starting item with Eden, or by using Death Certificate. [end edition note] 

• Does not produce coins other than Pennies.

• Hitting the front side of enemies such as the Knight will still produce Pennies, even though the enemy does not take damage. This can be exploited to produce an infinite amount of Pennies from a single enemy. This however doesn't work with lowered Hosts.

• Enemies that spawn other enemies, Globins, or enemies that regain health can also be farmed for infinite money.

• [Before Repentance] Head of the Keeper does not work with The Forgotten but will work with The Soul.

• When used against Ultra Greed, the coins are spawned directly in front of him and will heal him very often.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Brimstone/Azazel/Tainted Azazel/Tech X: The laser is yellow and each tick has a chance to drop a penny. [end edition note] 

• Monstro's Lung: Every tear in the burst of tears can spawn coins.

• Nuh Uh!: From Chapter 4 and beyond, any coins spawned will be from the loot table of Nuh Uh! instead, with an occasional harmless black fly spawning.

• Sack Head: Coins spawned from hitting enemies have a chance to become sacks.

• Soy Milk: Due to the Soy Milk's high fire rate and low damage, enemies can be hit many more times than usual, resulting in a larger amount of coins dropping.

• [Repentance] Technology: The laser is yellow and has a chance to drop a penny upon damaging an enemy.

• Technology Zero: Coin tears are connected via electricity. Beams of electricity can cause enemies to drop coins.

• Technology 2: Due to Technology 2's constant fire rate, enemies are hit many more times than usual, resulting in a higher likelihood of coins dropping.

• [Repentance] Trisagion: Each tick that hits an enemy has a chance to spawn a penny. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone/Azazel: Overrides Head of the Keeper.

• Death's Touch: Tears retain Death's Touch's cosmetic effect but both items are fully active.

• Dr. Fetus: Overrides Head of the Keeper.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Head of the Keeper.

• Euthanasia: Main tears can cause enemies to drop Pennies; however, burst tears do not.

• Haemolacria: Only the main tear retains the effect of Head of the Keeper.

• Ipecac: Because Ipecac's high damage will quickly kill enemies, and because enemies will often be hit with explosions rather than tears themselves, Pennies will not drop as frequently.

• Mom's Knife: Overrides Head of the Keeper.

• [Repentance] Knife has a very low chance to drop coins.

• Sulfuric Acid: Tears retain Head of the Keeper's cosmetic effect but both items are fully active. Which tears are acidic can no longer be visually identified.

• Technology: Overrides Head of the Keeper.

• Tech X: Overrides Head of the Keeper.

• Trisagion: Overrides Head of the Keeper. Coin debris will still appear after beams dissipate.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item resembles Ultra Greed's head.

• The coins fired are the same as Ultra Greed's coin projectiles.

• [Repentance] The coins fired now use their own unique sprite, which is significantly smaller than before.

• When picked up as Keeper or Tainted Keeper, they will begin smiling.

fields.description: Isaac's tears become coins. Hitting an enemy has a 5% chance to drop a Penny.

Headless Baby.title: Headless Baby
Headless Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around, leaving a trail of red creep that damages enemies.

• The creep deals 2 damage per tick or 6 damage per second to non-flying enemies.

• [Repentance] The creep deals damage much more rapidly at 20 damage per second.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Headless Baby having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Lost Cork: Creep trail size is bigger.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • BFFS!: Familiar is bigger; however, no effect on creep damage.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac, leaving blood creep on the ground.

Headless Horseman.title: Headless Horseman
Headless Horseman.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Headless Horseman is a Harbinger that can appear in all environments of Chapters 1, 2, 3, and 4; replacing any other Horsemen.

The head has 100 HP. The body's HP scales depending on what Chapter it is encountered, ranging from 60-300 HP.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Headless Horseman consists of two entities: The head and the body. Each performs attacks independently of the other.

The head has the following attacks:

• Shoots 3 projectiles in a spread at Isaac.

• Charges either left or right off-screen and reappears on the opposite end of the screen. He can charge either one, two or three times.

• He performs this attack more often if Isaac is to his left or right.

• This attack deals a full heart of damage.

The body has the following attack:

• Periodically shoots red Ipecac-like shots at Isaac, leaving a large puddle of damaging Red Creep on impact.

• This behavior is similar to Pestilence's second phase.
Both the head and the body deal a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• In several normal rooms, Headless Horseman's head appears on his own without his body.

• Two or three of Headless Horseman's heads can be found in the same normal rooms.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Headless Horseman appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• The Headless Horseman originated from European folklore during the Middle Ages but gained popularity in America with The Legend of Sleepy Hollow, a short story written in 1820 by American author Washington Irving, in which the Headless Horseman was prominently featured.

• The boss art shows the head with both eyes, even though its in-game sprite only has one.

• The boss art shows the horse's head as brown, even though its in-game sprite is black.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Delirium version of Headless Horseman's horse resembles Famine's horse rather than Headless Horseman's.

Health.title: Health
Health.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Health represents the amount of damage the player can take before dying. There are multiple different types of health in the game, each with their own pickups. The health bar is the visual representation of a player's health on the HUD, where hearts are arranged in two rows of six.

• The order in which hearts are placed is, from left to right, Red Hearts (and empty Red Heart containers), [Repentance] Rotten Hearts, then Eternal Hearts, then Soul Hearts, Black Hearts, and [Afterbirth+ onward] Bone Hearts (depending on the order in which they were picked up), then [Repentance] Broken Hearts. The top row is filled before the bottom row.

• Hearts are lost in a certain order, which depends on the damage source.

• The player can only hold a maximum of twelve hearts, and any permutation of the different types can be used. Picking up a Black or Soul Heart will refill a halved Black/Soul Heart (the other half is then placed at its right); Soul Hearts can replenish Black Hearts and vice versa.

• Keeper and Tainted Keeper: only Coin Hearts are available when playing as these characters.

• Obtaining Birthright as Magdalene increases the maximum amount of hearts from twelve to eighteen.

• The exact damage taken by Isaac depends on the item, hazard, or enemy and the specific attack used by the enemy, but in chapters 1 to 3, most sources deal half a heart of damage unless otherwise specified. From Chapter 4 onwards, all half-heart hits deal a full heart of damage (unless Isaac has a form of damage reduction, such as The Wafer).

sections.heading: Damage Order
sections.text: There are two separate damage orders; the game uses these to determine which hearts to take when the player is damaged. In both orders, the bottom row of hearts is taken from first.

sections.heading: Normal Order
sections.text: The first order is simple, and applies to most situations. Hearts are drained from right to left, with [Afterbirth+ onward] Bone Hearts having to be drained before their bone component is destroyed. The bottom row of hearts will always be drained first.

sections.heading: Alternate Order
sections.text:
The alternate order is more complicated and only applies when holding Crow Heart, taking damage from a Blood Donation Machine, Devil Beggar, Confessional, or Hell Game, or using a self-damaging item such as Razor Blade or Blood Rights. This order will drain Red Hearts from their containers before other heart types, [Afterbirth+ onward] including leaving empty Bone Hearts. Once Isaac has no Red Hearts left to drain, normal order is resumed.

[Before Repentance] If Isaac has any Red Heart containers, at least half of a Red Heart must be full at all times. If damage in the alternate order would bring Isaac below one Red Heart, normal order is resumed instead.

Using machines and items will not lower the chance for a Devil Room/Angel Room. However, taking damage from an enemy while holding Crow Heart will.

[Repentance] Rotten Hearts are drained after Red Hearts, but before all other hearts.

[Before Repentance] Eternal Hearts are drained after Red Hearts, but before all other Hearts.

[Repentance] Eternal Hearts will be drained only when they would be the only heart left otherwise. This means that if Isaac has an Eternal Heart and only half a Red / Soul / Black Heart, or only a Rotten Heart / Empty Bone Heart, then the Eternal Heart will be taken instead of the other heart.

sections.heading: Red Heart Containers
sections.text:
[heart: red] [heart: red; half] [heart: red; empty] 

Red Heart containers, or [anchor: Red Heart; Red Hearts] , are the main form of health for the majority of characters. If the player has only Red Hearts, the containers will be unfilled as damage is taken (but the containers themselves remain). Empty Red Heart containers can be refilled with Red Heart pickups. If Isaac takes a heart that would heal him for more than his current maximum health (for example, taking a Red Heart when he is only missing half a Red Heart worth of health), the excessive health will be wasted. The number of Red Heart containers can be increased with multiple items or Health Up pills or decreased with items, Health Down pills, having another player join a game as a baby, or trading them away in a Devil Room or at an underground Black Market.

sections.heading: Soul Hearts
sections.text:
[heart: soul] [heart: soul; half] 

Soul Hearts are blue hearts that are appended to the end of the health bar. Unlike Red Hearts, Soul Hearts do not have containers, so once they're depleted, new ones must replace them. If Isaac has Red Hearts and half a Soul Heart, taking a full heart of damage will not remove any Red Hearts. Losing Soul Hearts does not count as damage for Devil Room or Angel Room appearance chances, but does count as damage taken for the Basement Boy, Spelunker Boy, Dark Boy, Mama's Boy, and Dead Boy achievements.

sections.heading: Black Hearts
sections.text:
[heart: black] [heart: black; half] 

Black Hearts are similar to Soul Hearts in that they are appended to the end of the health bar, are not permanent, and that losing them does not count as damage for Devil or Angel Room chances. However, when a Black Heart is depleted, The Necronomicon effect is triggered, damaging all enemies in the current room. Picking up a Soul Heart while at half a Black Heart will complete the Black Heart and add half a Soul Heart, and vice versa. If Isaac is at his HP cap and any of his hearts are Soul Hearts, the Black Heart will replace the rightmost Soul Heart when picked up.

sections.heading: Eternal Hearts
sections.text:
[heart: red; empty; eternal] 

Eternal Hearts are the rarest variation of a heart. They always appear as half-hearts and, once picked up, can transform into a new Red Heart container in two ways: either by collecting a second Eternal Heart on the same floor or by traveling to the next floor. Eternal Hearts are not permanent, cannot be refilled when lost, and do not count for the limit of twelve hearts, instead overlapping the rightmost Red Heart container. If no Red Heart containers are available, the Eternal Heart will overlap the leftmost Soul Heart or Black Heart. Losing an Eternal Heart will prevent it from becoming a new Red Heart container. If Isaac has 12 Red Heart containers and travels to a new floor with an Eternal Heart, Isaac will heal one Red Heart but will not gain another Heart Container. If Isaac is at full health, the Eternal Heart will simply disappear.

An Eternal Heart will be used up the first time Isaac takes Red Heart damage (but is not lost by taking Red Heart damage if Isaac has no Red Heart containers). Health removal from Devil Room deals will not drain an Eternal Heart; rather, the Eternal Heart is appended onto the end of the next Red Heart. An Eternal Heart cannot keep Isaac alive on its own; making a deal with the Devil which drains all hearts except the Eternal Heart will kill Isaac. [Before Repentance] This also means that using a Blood Donation Machine or activated items like the Razor Blade will drain the Eternal Heart, even if Isaac has full health and Soul Hearts.

[Afterbirth+ onward] Since Bone Hearts are treated as Red Heart containers, Eternal Hearts will be appended to the rightmost Bone Heart even if there are Soul and Black Hearts between it and any Red Hearts.

[Repentance] Blood Donation Machines and other items and devices that take red hearts directly will ignore Eternal Hearts, even if Isaac has no other red hearts left. However, an eternal heart will still be taken if Isaac's only other health is worth one half-heart, meaning that you cannot have just an eternal heart and no other health.

When playing as Tainted Magdalene, Eternal Hearts won't be drained even if there is no other leaking health left.

sections.heading: Gold Hearts [Afterbirth onward]
sections.text:
[heart: red; empty; gold] 

Gold Hearts are unlocked by completing the XXXXXXXXL challenge. Once picked up, the Gold Heart surrounds Isaac's rightmost heart. The Gold Heart does not prevent damage, but when the heart that the Gold Heart surrounds is depleted, several Penny will spawn and nearby enemies will be changed to gold statues that release Pennies upon death, similar to the Midas' Touch effect. Some other methods of losing hearts, such as a non-red heart being "pushed off" the health bar by an HP up or removing hearts via items such as Converter or Potato Peeler, will also trigger the effect. Gaining additional hearts that go after the rightmost heart will move the Gold Heart to the newly rightmost heart.

[Afterbirth+ onward] Gold Hearts that surround Bone Hearts will not be used if the red health inside them is removed, instead triggering on the Bone Heart itself being removed. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Coin Hearts [Afterbirth onward]
sections.text:
[heart: coin] [heart: coin; half] [heart: coin; empty] 

Coin Hearts are a special heart type used exclusively by Keeper and Tainted Keeper. Coin Hearts always take a full heart of damage from all sources, even with The Wafer. They can only be replenished by acquiring money (either through picking up coins or obtaining items such as A Quarter), which will consume one cent from the coin pickup for each heart restored. They are treated as Red Hearts by the effects of all items. [Before Repentance] They can be sold in Devil deals or Black Markets. [Repentance] Taking Coin Heart damage does not reduce the chance to find a Devil Room or Angel Room.

See Keeper Notes for more information.
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Bone Hearts [Afterbirth+ onward]
sections.text:
[heart: bone] [heart: bone; half] [heart: bone; empty] 

Bone Hearts are special Red Heart containers unlocked alongside The Forgotten, and are appended to the end of the health bar. Empty containers can be filled with Red Hearts and filled containers take three hits to deplete (or two hits against sources that deal a full heart of damage), but disappear permanently upon depleting. If a Bone Heart is only filled with half a heart or a [Repentance] Rotten Heart, taking a full heart of damage will only empty it without destroying it. Bone Hearts, empty or full, are considered Red Hearts by most items, [Before Repentance] but cannot be used for Devil deals or Black Markets [end edition note] . Bone Hearts will be emptied when picking up items that remove all Red Hearts, such as Abaddon and Brittle Bones. Losing Bone Hearts or the Red Hearts contained within will not affect the chance to find a Devil Room or Angel Room, with the exception of The Forgotten, who receives a penalty for a Bone Heart breaking. Acquiring an empty Red Heart container while you have a filled Bone Heart will fill the new heart and empty the Bone Heart. Any character with health can pick up bone hearts, but characters who cannot possess Red Heart Containers cannot fill them with Red Hearts. [end edition note] 

Self-damage that prioritize red hearts such as IV Bag and Razor Blade will empty bone hearts in a slightly different way: if the rightmost bone heart is half-filled, only a half heart is removed even if the hit would deal a full heart of damage. Any further bone hearts are allowed to take full hearts of damage, draining past bone heart borders. This can be used to optimize health usage, refilling the rightmost heart with half hearts before applying self-damage.

[Repentance] Bone Hearts can replace the rightmost Soul or Black Hearts if acquired while Isaac is at his HP cap. They can also be filled with Rotten Hearts. Bone Hearts count as Red Heart containers when paying for items with health, unless the character can't have Red Heart containers. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Rotten Hearts [Repentance]
sections.text: Rotten Hearts are special Red Hearts unlocked by entering Corpse for the first time. Rotten Hearts spawn two friendly Blue Flies for each one that Isaac possesses upon clearing a room. They can be used to fill empty Red Heart containers or replace the rightmost Red Heart if there are no empty containers. It is not possible to have half a Rotten Heart; rather, each Rotten Heart is equivalent to half a heart. Normal hits will fully deplete them and hits which would deal a full heart of damage will deplete two Rotten Hearts or, if Isaac has only one Rotten Heart, a Rotten Heart and half a red heart. Losing Rotten Hearts will not affect the chance to find a Devil Room or Angel Room. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Broken Hearts [Repentance]
sections.text: Broken Hearts are special Red Heart containers that only appear when using Magic Skin, Heartbreak, a VI - The Lovers? card or an [Repentance+] Addicted! horse pill. Broken Hearts are considered empty Red Heart containers, but cannot be removed or refilled under normal circumstances. They cannot be used for any Devil Deals, they cannot be refilled with any form of Heart, or replaced by any Heart Container. They are permanently applied to the character for the rest of the run, even after using items that can revive or change the current character. They also do not let you benefit from stat upgrades for having empty red heart containers like Adrenaline. One of the only ways to remove them is to donate to a Confessional, which has a chance to remove them with each donation. The other way is using Genesis. Replacing all 12 Heart Container slots with Broken Hearts will cause Isaac to instantly die, and if revived, Isaac will have 1 of the Broken Hearts removed and have half a Soul Heart take its place. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Magdalene, Lazarus, The Tank, Cursed!]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Upon entering a room with only half a heart left, a small yellow spot, presumably urine, will appear underneath Isaac.

• If Isaac has Kidney Stone, a bloodstain will appear instead of urine.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] As Eve and Tainted Eve, a bloodstain will appear instead of urine.

• [Repentance] Eternal Hearts have a special animation if used by a character who cannot use red hearts, where the animation of the hearts joining together will show their respective heart type.

• There is a half Coin Heart graphic left in the files. To see it, you must have half a Red Heart, use Clicker, and turn into Keeper.

• The most amount of hearts Isaac can have on one heart slot is a Bone, Gold, Eternal, Rotten heart.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: A Gold Heart surrounding a Soul, Black, or empty Bone Heart will be used if a Red Heart is depleted via the alternate order before the rightmost heart is lost.
Bug note: Losing many hearts at once, such as via Dead Cat or a Hematemesis pill, while having a Gold Heart will trigger the Gold Heart loss effect many times at once, showering the player in coins.
Bug note: If the last Rotten Heart is drained when Isaac has an Eternal Heart, the latter will turn into a Half Red Heart. The same will occur if normal damage is taken to a Rotten Heart while Isaac has an Eternal Heart. If in this scenario the Rotten Heart fills the Bone Heart, the Bone Heart will be filled with a Half Red Heart after taking damage even if a full heart worth of damage is taken.

Heartbreak.title: Heartbreak
Heartbreak.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants +0.25 damage for every broken heart Isaac has.

• Immediately grants 3 broken hearts.

• Every otherwise fatal hit will add 2 more, replacing other types of hearts if necessary, and activates The Necronomicon's effect, dealing 40 damage to all enemies in the room.

• Once Isaac has no non-broken hearts left, he dies. Extra lives will apply at this point.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• At the maximum of 11 broken hearts, Isaac gains a total of +2.75 damage.

• The effect does not save Isaac from fatal Devil deals.

• However, while taking an item that costs heart/s and will result in death, if Isaac takes any damage, it will leave him on half a blue heart with taken item and will add 2 broken hearts.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Missing Page / Missing Page 2: Deals an additional +40 damage when Isaac dies. Effects stack together and with multiple copies.

• Found Soul: The ghost gains 2 extra hits per floor, and every hit they take will damage all enemies in a room as well.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Damocles: Heartbreak does not protect Isaac from Damocles.

• Keeper: Keeper will gain 1 broken heart instead of 3. Taking fatal damage will only grant Keeper 1 broken heart.

• Magdalene + Birthright: Can hold up to 17 broken hearts, totaling +4.25 damage instead.

• Plan C / Suicide King: Heartbreak does not protect Isaac from these effects.

• Tainted Eden / Tainted Isaac: The starting broken hearts are removed when Heartbreak is rerolled/dropped. However, any broken hearts gained from lethal damage will persist.

• Tainted Jacob: This effect will save Tainted Jacob while he is in his Lost form, adding two broken hearts to his regular health.

• Tainted Keeper: Tainted Keeper will gain 1 broken heart instead of 3. Taking any damage will kill him, as he will then have 2 broken hearts.

• Mother's Kiss can mitigate this as it gives Tainted Keeper an extra coin heart.

• The Lost / Tainted Lost: The Lost has full benefit of the item. This lets him survive 4 extra hits, each hit adding 1 damage, and the 5th is fatal.

• Tainted Lost can't normally obtain it, as it doesn't have the offensive item tag.

• The Lost / Tainted Lost + Magic Skin / VI - The Lovers?: No broken hearts are added by the item/card, thus having no effect on Heartbreak.

fields.description: Grants 3 broken hearts and +0.25 damage for every broken heart Isaac has. Every otherwise fatal hit will add 2 more until Isaac has nothing but broken hearts.

Hearts.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the pickup]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
More details on these pickups and how they work can be found here.

• Unless an item effect specifically states it, a Red Heart always has the chance to be replaced by a Soul, Black, or Eternal Heart.

• If Heart pickups are created by item, card, or pill effects in certain Super Secret Room layouts, they will be forced to spawn as a specific heart type (e. g. all hearts will be Black Hearts). There are layouts corresponding to Red, Soul, Black, Eternal and Rotten Hearts.

• If Isaac's health bar is filled with Soul Hearts, picking up a Black Heart will replace the topmost Soul Heart.

• If Isaac's health bar is filled up to 11 1/2 (Soul/Black) Hearts with the last one being half a Black Heart, picking up a Black Heart will fill that one and convert a full Soul Heart to a Black Heart (therefore adding half a Black Heart and converting a Soul Heart).

• Collecting a Soul Heart with half a Black Heart left will complete the Black Heart, and add half a Soul Heart. The reverse is also true.

• [Afterbirth onward] If Gold Hearts have not been unlocked yet, they be replaced by random Heart pickups in any room layouts containing them.

• [Repentance] If Rotten Hearts have not been unlocked yet, they will always be replaced by Half Red Hearts (Corpse themed Super Secret Room, etc.). [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Eternal Hearts take half a heart of damage without counting as a hit for Devil Room / Angel Room purposes.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Taking Red Heart damage in a Bone Heart Container does not lower the chance of the Angel Room or Devil Room appearing. Breaking an empty Bone Heart will not either.

• The Forgotten is the only exception, as breaking a Bone Heart while playing as him will affect the chance.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Bone Hearts cannot be broken if filled with at least a Half Red Heart, even if a full heart of damage is taken. This can be abused to repeatedly pay a half-red heart to step on a spike in a Sacrifice Room, for example.

• [Repentance] Rotten Hearts are only donated to the [machine: Blood Donation Machine] after all Red Hearts are depleted.

• [Repentance] Losing Rotten Hearts does not lower the chance of the Angel Room or Devil Room appearing.

• [Repentance] If after clearing a room the number of Blue Flies Isaac has is less than 2× the number of Rotten Hearts in Isaac's health, additional Blue Flies are spawned so that these numbers are equal (e. g. if Isaac has 3 Rotten Hearts and 4 Blue Flies upon clearing a room, 2 Blue Flies will spawn). Otherwise, no Blue Flies will spawn.

• Bag of Crafting will treat double hearts as two heart pickups. Blended Hearts will be treated as a Soul Heart and a Red Heart.

• The probabilities in the table refer to the kind of heart that is generated by the game when a heart is spawned with a subtype of 0 (i.e. a random heart).

• [Repentance+] In Online Co-op, dead ghost characters can pick up an Eternal Heart to instantly revive themselves.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Magdalene, Eve, Lazarus, The Tank, Cursed!, It's the Key, Living on the edge]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• There are unused graphics for Half Soul Hearts and Half Black Hearts that are never seen in-game.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Half Soul Hearts were eventually added to the game as an unlockable.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Booster Pack#5 made Scared Hearts beat faster, making them slightly easier to spot. This was from this Steam Workshop mod by piber20.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Gold Hearts' appearance was changed in Booster Pack#5.

• Most items that grant Black Hearts upon being picked up say "evil up" in their description.

• Immortal Hearts were a heart type present in the original Antibirth mod, but were not added to Repentance.

• Blended hearts were a feature in the Community remix mod for the original The Binding of Isaac.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Gold Hearts actually simply compare Isaac's current heart count to what he had on the previous frame, leading to two bugs. Firstly, it's possible for a Gold Heart to burst when health other than the rightmost heart is lost, such as using up Red Hearts with a Blood Donation Machine. [Before Repentance] Secondly, the "previous frame hearts" value is updated incorrectly; a Gold Heart bursts immediately upon pickup if Isaac had and lost a Gold Heart earlier, and his current heart count is lower than after losing the previous one.

Hemoptysis.title: Hemoptysis
Hemoptysis.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Double-tapping the fire button causes Isaac to sneeze blood, dealing damage to enemies in front of him. The sneeze deals damage equal to 1.5x Isaac's damage, knocking enemies and projectiles back. Knocked back enemies take 10 + 2 * (floor - 1) additional damage if they hit a wall or obstacle, and deal that same damage to other enemies they collide with.

• The sneeze has a cooldown of 1 second.

• The reflected projectiles deal 6 damage to enemies if it would have caused Isaac half a heart of damage, and 7 damage if it would have caused Isaac a full heart damage.

• The sneeze applies a curse to enemies. Enemies under the curse will take more damage from Brimstone-like laser attacks and violently explode on death, damaging and spreading the curse to nearby enemies. Any enemies spawned by those under the curse will also be cursed.

• The following attacks will deal increased damage (2x damage +3 flat damage):

• • Brimstone attacks from Azazel/Tainted Azazel

• • Athame

• • Brimstone

• • Brimstone Bombs

• • Head of Krampus

• • Lil Abaddon

• • Lil Brimstone

• • Maw Of The Void

• • Montezuma's Revenge's brimstone (not tears)

• • Mega Blast

• • Shoop da Whoop!

• • Trisagion

• • Urn of Souls' brimstone (while holding Birthright with Judas or Black Judas)

• The curse lasts for 5 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tainted Azazel begins with an inherent version of Hemoptysis that allows him to deal full damage to cursed enemies.

• The innate sneeze ability is entirely separate from Hemoptysis, and so the sneeze can be triggered twice in quick succession. However, triggering the sneeze from Hemoptysis will cancel Tainted Azazel's brimstone charge, meaning that this item is largely ineffective as this character.

• The sneeze's range is affected by the shot speed stat, and not by the range stat itself.

• The sneeze can push Bombs, pickups and enemy shots.

• The collision damage can be used to damage Hosts while their skulls are lowered.

• Brimstone lasers shot by enemies who are not charmed, such as Monstro II, will also do increased damage to cursed enemies.

• Revelation's charged attack will not deal increased damage to cursed enemies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Fire Mind: The sneeze will still set enemies on fire, but not cause explosions, similar to its interaction with Brimstone.

• Loki's Horns: Chance to sneeze in all cardinal directions.

• Monstro's Lung: Multiple sneezes are applied around the character.

• The Wiz: Shoots two sneezes diagonally instead of one straight forward.

• Ipecac: The sneeze causes an explosion. The explosion deals additional damage equal to 3x Isaac's damage +10 and will not hurt Isaac.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Hemoptysis is the medical term for coughing up blood.

fields.description: Double-tapping a fire button causes Isaac to sneeze blood, dealing damage to enemies in front of him. Affected enemies are cursed and take more damage from Brimstone-like attacks.

Henry.title: Henry
Henry.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Henry is a monster added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC and is exclusively found in Dross.

Henry appears only in a single extremely rare room within the floor. When Isaac enters the room, Henry smiles and then gets flushed down a drain. Isaac can fire tears at him, but due to his high HP he is extremely difficult to kill, and this would be pointless anyway as his only behavior is killing himself.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Friendly Ball can be used to capture Henry, although when released he will still flush himself, doing no damage to enemies. Henry also does not spawn properly if the room lacks a pit.

• Although Henry does not attack Isaac directly, he can still deal contact damage if the player has flight.

• Henry does not have his own kill icon, so if Isaac somehow manages to die from him, the death screen will instead show a bucket as the cause of death.

• Henry does not appear in the game's Bestiary, and as such, does not need to be killed to complete it.

• The room in which Henry spawns has an id of 485 and has a weight of 0.01. The rarity is further compounded by the room requiring a dead end with only a south exit, and as such cannot be generated by Red Key.

• Using Flush! on Henry will not flush him, instead turning him into a poop.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Henry was initially a design by Kilburn, and Edmund McMillen suggested that he do nothing and appear extremely rarely.

fields.name: Henry
fields.environment: Dross /
fields.behavior: Flushes itself away shortly after Isaac enters the room.

Hive Mind.title: Hive Mind
Hive Mind.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Increases the size and doubles the damage of Blue Spiders, Blue Flies and [Afterbirth+ onward] Locusts.

• [Repentance] Fly and spider familiars become stronger, exactly like BFFS!.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Spider Baby transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The size change is only cosmetic, the flies' hitboxes remain the same.

• [Before Repentance] This item does not affect Fly familiars or orbitals.

• No effect on flies made passive by Skatole.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Guppy: Doubles the damage of all Blue Flies spawned greatly increasing damage output.

• Brown Nugget: Turret does 7 damage instead of 3.5

• Mom's Wig: Doubles spider limit of the wig to 10 spiders.

• Plum Flute: Doubles Baby Plum's contact damage, but not projectile damage. Plum is also larger.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Red Locusts: Contact damage is doubled as normal and explosions will deal an additional 25 flat damage.

• Sissy Longlegs: Increases familiar's size. Spiders spawned by Sissy are affected by Hive Mind.

• Abyss: Spawned locusts deal increased damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • [Repentance] BFFS!: Does not give any additional benefit to fly and spider familiars.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Hive mind is the concept of a large number of beings acting in the interest of the survival of the group as a whole, with little to no individuality.

• [Repentance] This item is one of the only five ( [Repentance+] seven) that count towards 2 transformations (Beelzebub and Spider Baby), the other ones being Magic Mushroom, The Bible, Parasitoid, Skatole, [Repentance+] The Necronomicon, and Seraphim.

fields.description: Increases the size of Blue Spiders and Blue Flies and doubles the amount of damage they deal. [Repentance] Also increases the effectiveness of fly and spider familiars.

Hold.title: Hold
Hold.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: It is available solely for Tainted ??? as his starting item.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Removes Tainted ???'s leftmost poop, storing it inside of Hold and cycling to the next poop.

• Using Hold again while a poop is inside it will remove the poop and use it as expected.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The item is unavailable for anyone except Tainted ???.

• It can, however, activate when using Metronome. This does nothing with most characters; however, it will count as a use of the item when activated as Tainted ???.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: No effect.

fields.description: Exclusive to Tainted ???. Allows him to save one poop bomb for later, allowing him to gather more over time.

Hollow Heart.title: Hollow Heart
Hollow Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one Bone Heart container upon entering a new floor.

• If Isaac has 12 heart containers, the added bone heart will replace the rightmost Soul Heart (if any).

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brittle Bones: Allows Isaac to sacrifice a bone heart for a fire rate increase every floor.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Adds 2 bone heart containers instead of one.

fields.description: Grants an empty Bone Heart upon entering a new floor.

Holy Card.title: Holy Card
Holy Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a one-time Holy Mantle effect.

• [Before Repentance] This only applies for the current room.

• [Repentance] The effect lasts until damage is taken.

• [Before Repentance] Has a 25% chance to display the message "You feel blessed!" and spawn another Holy Card.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, the Holy Card has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• The effect cannot be stacked by using multiple Holy Cards.

• Tainted Lost starts with this card. Additionally, all cards that spawn have a 10% chance of being turned into a Holy Card, and the card can be found even if not unlocked.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Blanket: Holy Card's effect takes priority over the shield from Blanket in Boss Rooms.

• [Repentance+] The shield from Blanket now takes priority.

• Holy Mantle: Effect stacks with Holy Card, [Repentance+] with Holy Mantle taking priority.

• Wooden Cross: Stacks with Holy Card depending on the order of use. If Wooden Cross is picked up after Holy Card has been used, their effects don't stack. If Holy Card is used after Wooden Cross has been picked up, they do. The stacking only lasts for the current room.

• [Repentance+] The shield from Wooden Cross always stacks no matter the order of use, and will always take priority.

• Little Baggy: Will make Isaac unable to find Holy Cards, as all cards turn into pills. If Holy Card is dropped after taking Little Baggy, the Holy Card will turn into a random pill.

• Dogma: Effect stacks with Holy Card, with the latter taking priority.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Grants a shield that blocks the next hostile damage that would be taken in the current room. Has a chance to spawn another Holy Card on use.
[Repentance] Grants a shield that blocks the next hostile damage that would be taken.

Holy Crown.title: Holy Crown
Holy Crown.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Causes a Treasure Room and Shop to generate in Cathedral.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Cannot appear in Greed Mode.

• The spawned Treasure Room will have one of 23 unique layouts for the floor.

• Card Reading will spawn a second portal if Isaac has the trinket upon entering Cathedral.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Treasure rooms in the Cathedral have an item choice, as if Isaac had More Options and Shops will be upgraded. Having both reveals the locations of the treasure room and the shop on the map.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This trinket has a demonic counterpart in Wicked Crown.

fields.quote: Walk the path of the saint
fields.description: A Treasure Room and Shop appear in the Cathedral.

Holy Grail.title: Holy Grail
Holy Grail.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants flight and one full Red Heart container.

• Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This is based on the grail Jesus drank out of in the Last Supper, and the myth that says whoever drinks from it will be blessed.

• This item's costume is a combination of Fate's and Mitre's.

• This item is used in The Guardian.

fields.description: Grants flight and one Red Heart container. [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

Holy Light.title: Holy Light
Holy Light.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac has a chance to fire a glowing blue tear that, after colliding with an enemy, spawns a damaging beam of light (similar to Crack the Sky).

• [Before Repentance] Each beam of light deals quadruple (4×) Isaac's tear damage.

• [Repentance] Each beam of light deals triple (3×) Isaac's tear damage.

• The beam of light will damage all enemies in a small radius around it.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The chance to fire a holy tear depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \min(\frac1 { 10 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \times 0.9 \right \rfloor},50\%)

• At base Luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 50% at 8.89 Luck.

• Its damage is multiplied from the tear's damage, not directly from Isaac's Damage.

• This means that, if the tears' damage has been multiplied from effects such as Proptosis or Tough Love, the beam's damage is also multiplied.

• Light beams can destroy Shopkeepers if a holy tear hits an enemy nearby.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb Holy Light it turns into a glowing cyan locust. Every tick of damage it deals has a chance to call down a beam of light dealing triple Isaac’s damage.

• Bob's Rotten Head: Has a chance to throw a Holy Light head that spawns a damaging beam of light dealing ( [Before Repentance] 4×) [Repentance] 3× the explosion damage when it hits an enemy.

• Compound Fracture / Cricket's Body / The Parasite: Holy Light tears will have split tears with Holy Light effect; normal tears will not have split tears with Holy Light effect.

• Lachryphagy: If Holy Light tears feed normal tears, fed normal tears will not gain Holy Light effect; however if normal tears feed Holy Light tears, it will just increase the size of fed Holy Light tears.

• The Ludovico Technique: The controlled tear will sometimes glow and trigger the beam.

• C Section: Glowing shots will rapidly strike light beams on contact, making short work of most enemies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Following items can trigger Holy Light effect:

• Eye of Greed

• Fate's Reward

• Found Soul

• Gello

• Host Hat

• Incubus

• Kidney Stone

• Lead Pencil

• Metal Plate

• Sad Bombs

• Saturnus

• Tammy's Head

• Twisted Pair

• Varicose Veins

• Following items do not trigger Holy Light effect:

• Akeldama

• Athame

• Brimstone Bombs

• Circle of Protection

• Divine Intervention

• It Hurts

• Large Zit

• Maw Of The Void

• Montezuma's Revenge

• Revelation

• Shard of Glass

• Slipped Rib

• Vasculitis

• 20/20 / Keeper and other multi-shot effects: Each shot can have Holy Light effect separately.

• Brimstone / Azazel / Tainted Azazel: [Before Repentance] Overrides Holy Light.

• [Repentance] The Brimstone shot can create beams of light.

• Dr. Fetus: [Before Repentance] Overrides Holy Light.

• [Repentance] The bombs created by Dr. Fetus can create beams of light upon exploding for each enemy hit by the explosion, although there is no visual indication that this will happen. The beams deals a flat 10.5 damage.

• Epic Fetus: [Before Repentance] Overrides Holy Light.

• [Repentance] The rockets created by Epic Fetus can create beams of light upon exploding for each enemy hit by the explosion, although there is no visual indication that this will happen. The beams deals a flat 10.5 damage.

• Euthanasia: Having Holy Light effect on a tear does not affect the burst tears from it. They can have Holy Light effect applied depending on Isaac's Luck.

• Explosivo:

• [Repentance] Explosivo tears can have the Holy Light effect applied to them. These tears spawn beams of light upon exploding for each enemy hit by the explosion. The beams deal a flat 10.5 damage.

• The Forgotten: The melee and ranged attack can create beams of light.

• Haemolacria: Occasionally fires Haemolacria tears with Holy Light effect. Only the main tear will contain the effect and not the burst tears.

• [Repentance] If the main tear has the effect, burst tears also gain the effect.

• Holy Light: Additional copy of this item through Diplopia or Crooked Penny etc. has no effect.

• [Repentance] Additional copy of this item is counted for Seraphim set.

• Ipecac: If the explosives don't kill enemies instantly, explosives with Holy Light will spawn a light beam after the explosion is over.

• [Repentance] A beam of light with a tripled damage spawn on top of the closest enemy from the explosion, and beams with a flat 10.5 damage spawn for each enemy hit by the explosion

• Mom's Knife: [Before Repentance] Overrides Holy Light.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Holy Light can trigger on both held and thrown knives.

• Mucormycosis: The spores with Holy Light effect do not spawn beams of light, including the one from Isaac.

• Multidimensional Baby: Duplicated tears have Holy Light effect if the tear they originated had it.

• Sinus Infection: The boogers with Holy Light effect do not spawn beams of light.

• Spirit Sword: Hitting an enemy with Spirit Sword has a chance to spawn a damaging beam of light.

• Tear Detonator: Having Holy Light effect on a tear does not affect the burst tears from it. They can have Holy Light effect applied depending on Isaac's Luck.

• Teardrop Charm: Activation rate is affected.

• Technology: [Before Repentance] Overrides Holy Light.

• [Repentance] The lasers can create beams of light.

• Technology Zero: Electricity connecting tears with Holy Light tears will not gain Holy Light effect.

• Technology 2: Tears will occasionally have Holy Light effect.

• [Repentance] The lasers can create beams of light.

• Tech X: [Before Repentance] Overrides Holy Light.

• [Repentance] The lasers can create beams of light.

• Trisagion: [Before Repentance] Overrides Holy Light.

• [Repentance] Blasts can apply Holy Light, with a light beam being generated on each damage tick, dealing Isaac's tear damage per beam (three times Trisagion's damage).

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Holy shot!; Repentance: Holy death shot]
fields.description: Adds a chance to fire holy tears, which will create a damaging light beam in the area if they hit an enemy.

Holy Mantle.title: Holy Mantle
Holy Mantle.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a shield that negates the first instance of damage taken from a hostile source in each room.

• Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] When the shield is broken, Isaac gets invincibility frames like he does when he would normally take damage, based on the damage it negated; 1 second for half a heart of damage, 2 seconds for a full heart, and 4 seconds for 2 full hearts. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Holy Mantle breaking grants one second of invincibility frames, regardless of the damage source.

• [Before Repentance] Holy Mantle won't be active when initially appearing in the starting room of a floor if it was lost in the room where Isaac left the previous floor.

• [Repentance] If Holy Mantle's shield is broken prior to using R Key, the shield won't be active in the new starting room initially.

• As the shield gets restored whenever another room is entered, Holy Mantle allows Curse Rooms to be entered and exited without taking damage.

• Holy Mantle does not prevent damage from Blood Donation Machines, Devil Beggars, and Blood Rights.

• [Before Repentance] However, Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars can be played practically for free during the invincibility frames granted when losing the shield, by taking damage from touching a Fire Place, etc.

• Damage from Sacrifice Room spikes can be blocked by Holy Mantle, but no payout is rewarded.

• The blocked hit does not count as damage taken for related achievements and will not trigger items that activate upon taking damage, like Dead Bird.

• The Lost starts with this item after donating 879 coins to the Greed Donation Machine.

• [Repentance] When Holy Mantle's shield is broken, a white cross symbol will briefly appear overlaid on top of Isaac and a smashing sound will play.

• [Repentance] While Holy Mantle is in effect, a blue cross icon appears in the HUD next to Isaac's health.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Belly Jelly / Host Hat / Infamy / Metal Plate: The chance of blocking projectiles is applied before the Holy Mantle, allowing the Holy Mantle shield to be saved.

• Blanket / Dogma / Holy Card / Wooden Cross: All stack with Holy Mantle. [Before Repentance+] Holy Mantle applies last.

• [Repentance+] Shield-type items stack in the following order:

• • Wooden Cross

• • Blanket

• • Holy Mantle

• • Holy Card

• • Dogma

• Blind Rage: Doubles the invincibility frames given when damage is negated.

• Damocles: The nullified first hit does not trigger the chance of the sword falling. It will not, however, protect Isaac from the falling sword.

• E. Coli / Midas' Touch: On-contact effects still apply to enemies if Holy Mantle negates the contact damage taken.

• Isaac's Heart: The shield effect transfers to the heart.

• Stop Watch: If damage is blocked with Holy Mantle, Stop Watch will trigger the slow effect.

• Tainted Lazarus + Greed Mode: The shield regenerates every wave if broken. This allows one form of Tainted Lazarus to press the button for free on every wave.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bad Trip: Damage is blocked by Holy Mantle.

• Dull Razor: Ignores Holy Mantle's shield and works normally.

• IV Bag: IV Bag ignores the shield's protection, resulting in Isaac taking damage regardless.

• Glass Cannon: Holy Mantle's effect will apply after Glass Cannon reduces Isaac's health to half a heart.

• Holy Mantle / The Lost: An extra shield is given in the room it was found in, but the shield is removed when leaving that room and does not reapply.

• Sharp Plug: Holy Mantle blocks the damage from Sharp Plug, but also prevents it from adding charges.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This may be a reference to the card of the same name from Magic: the Gathering, a collectible card game Edmund McMillen played since his childhood.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If the Holy Mantle is removed from Isaac's inventory — for example, when using the D4 — Isaac can still take one damage and it will be negated with Holy Mantle's effect, but only in the room where the items were re-rolled.
Bug note: Activating Soul of Judas at the same time Isaac blocks a hit with Holy Mantle, time will freeze as normal, but Isaac will be allowed to shoot during the duration of the Dark Arts effect.
Bug note: Upon leaving the game and reentering it, if Holy Mantle was broken in the room, it will be restored.

fields.description: Grants a shield that negates the first instance of damage taken from a hostile source once per room.

Holy Water.title: Holy Water
Holy Water.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac. If Isaac takes damage, it will shatter and create a pool of damaging blue creep, similar to Lemon Mishap.

• The pool lasts for ~9 seconds and deals 8 damage per tick to non-flying enemies (24 damage per second).

• After breaking, Holy Water will reappear in the next room.

• [Repentance] Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac and launches itself in the direction Isaac shoots. Upon hitting an enemy, it will deal 7 damage and shatter, creating a pool of damaging blue creep that also petrifies enemies that touch it.

• Once the pool disappears completely, Holy Water will respawn and can be fired again. Holy Water does not immediately respawn upon entering a new room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Holy Water having [edition alternatives: baseline: 5th; Repentance+: 7th] priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Familiar is bigger but no effect on damage.

• [Repentance] Doubles the initial damage and causes it to also spawn a blue flame on point of impact that blocks shots and deals 6 contact damage per tick to enemies (36 damage per second). The fire can hit flying enemies, persists for the same amount of time as the creep, and cannot be destroyed.

• Vasculitis: Upon killing an enemy while they are inside the puddle of holy water, The enemy bursts into a cluster of petrifying tears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item is a reference to the sub-weapon of the same name from the Castlevania series of games.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, holding Holy Water will turn one of your shooting familiars into Brother Bobby, and it will change back when the Holy Water breaks. It will turn back into Brother Bobby after entering the next room.

• The in-game description for Holy Water in the original game was 'Don't Spill It'.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If Isaac has the Extension Cord and Holy Water breaks, the sprite is temporarily stored just off the top-left of the screen, where the yellow beams will still connect to it.

[Repentance] A bottle familiar that flies forward when Isaac shoots. It breaks upon hitting an enemy, leaving a puddle of blue creep that petrifies enemies.

Eye.title: Eye
Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Eyes are immobile and attack by rotating towards Isaac and firing a Technology laser towards his position. Non-Eye enemies hit by the lasers take 8 damage.

The battle against Mom's Heart / It Lives! begins with an Eye on either side of it.

sections.heading: Bloodshot Eye
sections.text: Bloodshot Eyes behave similarly to Eyes but fires a wider Brimstone beam towards Isaac. Non-Eye enemies hit by the beam take 22 damage per tick.

sections.heading: Holy Eye
sections.text:
Holy Eyes are a unique variety of eye added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance. They are only encountered on Cathedral.

The Holy Eye is a stationary enemy, much like other Eyes. Every few seconds, it summons four beams of light (similar to the beams summoned by Crack the Sky) near Isaac's position, with shadows telegraphing where the beams will strike. The first beam strikes where Isaac is, but the others will attempt to predict his movements, striking where Isaac would be if he kept moving in a straight line. Holy Eyes will always attempt to summon beams of light if they take damage and aren't already firing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• When Eyes spawn, they can be briefly seen opening their eyelids before they start turning towards the player.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, Bloodshot Eyes, despite using Brimstone as projectiles, had limited range. This does not apply to Rebirth.

• Eyes may be a reference of Mr. I from Super Mario 64, which is immobile and can rotate, although they shoot pink bubbles from their pupils instead of lasers.

• Afflicting fear to Eyes will cause them to look away from Isaac.

• [Repentance] Holy Eyes, Holy Bony, and Holy Mulligans originated as cards from the card game The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls. [end edition note] 

• They originally went by the card name "Holy Mom's Eye" as the card name for regular Eyes was "Mom's Eye".

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The game will crash if a Bloodshot Eye that is a Dark-Red champion regenerates and attacks.

Black Lipstick.title: Black Lipstick
Black Lipstick.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Increases the chance of Black Hearts appearing by 10%.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases chance of Black Hearts appearing by 20%. Having both by 33%.

• Black Feather: Black Feather grants a damage boost for Black Lipstick, provided that Isaac has an extra trinket slot or has [Afterbirth+ onward] gulped or used Smelter on either of the trinkets.

fields.description: Increases the chance of Black Hearts appearing.

Black Lotus.title: Black Lotus
Black Lotus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Grants a full Red Heart Container, one Soul Heart, and one Black Heart.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This is a reference to the iconic card of the same name from Magic: the Gathering, a collectible card game Edmund McMillen played since his childhood.

• Its powerful effect of producing three Mana of any color is reflected by the ingame item's effect of adding three hearts of different colors to the player's health.

• The fact that it's one of the rarest and most expensive commercially released cards in the game might also be referenced by the fact that it's a relatively hard item to come across, being only a rare find exclusively in Secret Rooms.

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Before Afterbirth+: Rebirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth+]
