Black Powder.title: Black Powder
Black Powder.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Isaac constantly leaves a trail of black powder on the floor. Drawing a circle with it spawns a pentagram symbol on the floor, which deals 10 damage per tick to enemies within it.

• [Before Repentance] This does not affect flying enemies.

• [Repentance+] Grants larger explosions and deal 185 damage instead of 100 similar to Mr. Mega.

• It doesn't stack with Mr. Mega itself though.

• [Repentance+] Destroying Fire Places causes them to explode.

• Explosions from destroyed fire places do not hurt Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The trail of black powder left on the floor will quickly disappear, meaning that there is an effective limit to the size of the pentagram that can be created, though bigger pentagrams can be created if the player has higher movement speed.

• The traced pattern does not have to be perfectly circular; closed shapes such as squares or very narrow crescents will work.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Lost Cork: Although the powder trail is wider in appearance, it has no effect on how easily a valid shape is determined.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Ventricle Razor: When the Ventricle Razor portals are placed on the opposite wall of a room and Isaac goes from one portal to another repeatedly, a pentagram symbol can be created which covers almost the whole room.

• How to Jump: Jumping can create large pentagrams by drawing a rectangle.

• Spin to Win: Faster movement speed while using spin to win allows for larger pentagrams to be created.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The pickup quote may be a reference to the Pearl Jam song of the name "Spin the black circle".

fields.description: Isaac leaves a trail of black powder on the floor. Walking in a circle will spawn a pentagram symbol on the floor, which deals 10 damage per tick to any enemies inside it. [Repentance+] Grants larger explosions and fireplaces will explode when extinguished.

Black Rune.title: Black Rune
Black Rune.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Deals 40 damage to all enemies in the room.

• Turns pickups into Blue Flies and Spiders.

• Absorbs items and turns them into random stat upgrades.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Black Rune's effect is similar to Void.

• Unlike Void, the Black Rune will grant stat ups for sacrificing active items. This makes Black Rune useful even while holding Void, as any active item that would be detrimental to absorb can instead be absorbed by Black Rune.

• Like Void, stats gained by a Black Rune will be removed when Isaac's build is re-rolled (e.g. with D4 or a Dice Room).

• Using a Black Rune to absorb items in Boss Rush or Boss Challenge Rooms counts as taking the items and will cause waves of bosses or enemies to start spawning.

• If Black Runes have not been unlocked, they will be replaced by random Cards of any type, rather than Rune Shards, in any room layouts containing them.

• [Repentance] If Isaac uses the Black Rune to absorb items from a room with choice pedestals, it will only absorb one item, and the other item vanishes. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• [Repentance] If a Black Rune is used while Isaac is holding an item above his head, it will consume the item. This allows him to immediately absorb passive items bought from Devil Rooms, Black Markets, or Shops. This also can be used to give Isaac a chance to see what an unknown item is before deciding if he wants to consume it. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The Black Rune can be used to absorb Knife Piece 1 if Mother isn't the goal of the run. Can also be used to absorb Key Piece 1 or Key Piece 2. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Deals 80 damage.

• A Missing Page / Missing Page 2: Deals +40 damage per copy.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: No effect.

• Death Certificate: Only allows the consumption of one item. The consumed item is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.

• Endless Nameless: The newly spawned Black rune will spawn before the effect goes through, transforming it instantly into blue flies.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Using a Black Rune in a room with exactly one pickup and one item while being near the fly limit won't absorb the item.

fields.name: Black Rune
fields.description: Deals 40 damage to all enemies in the room. Consumes all pickups in the room and turns them into Blue Flies and Spiders. Consumes all pedestal items in the room and turns them into random stat upgrades.

Black Tooth.title: Black Tooth
Black Tooth.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a chance to fire a black tooth that poisons enemies.

• Black teeth deal double Isaac's normal tear damage.

• The chance to shoot teeth depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 33 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor}

• • At base Luck (0), the chance is ~3%, maxing out at 100% at 32 Luck.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either doubles the chance to fire a black tooth. Having both triples the chance.

fields.description: Adds a chance to fire a black tooth that deals double damage and poisons enemies.

Blank Card.title: Blank Card
Blank Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Upon use, copies the effect of the card or rune currently held by Isaac.

• [Repentance] Upon use, copies the effect of the card currently held by Isaac. Blank Card's recharge time changes upon use, depending on the card Isaac was holding when he used it.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [edition anr] Blank card also mimics Dice Shard and Emergency Contact. [end edition note] 

• Using Blank Card does not expend the consumable.

• Using the Blank Card with a consumable that isn't compatible, or no consumable at all, spends the charge with no effect.

• If holding more than one consumable (e.g. Starter Deck, Tainted Characters...), only the consumable that is selected will be used. If one of them isn't a card, they must ensure the card is the one selected when activating Blank Card, otherwise the effect won't be triggered.

sections.heading: [Repentance] Recharge Time
sections.text:
Blank Card's recharge time changes upon use, depending on the card Isaac was holding when he used it (except in the case of using the item with no held card). This is a list of the following recharge times the card can have:

1 room
2 rooms
3 rooms
4 rooms
6 rooms
12 rooms
Single use

• ? Card

• ? Card has a unique interaction with Blank Card, noted in the synergies section. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Butter!: As Blank Card is dropped upon usage, the recharge time for it is reset to 4, allowing to use more expensive cards much more frequently. [end edition note] 

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns card wisps in the middle ring. Enemies killed by the wisps' tears have a 15% chance to drop a card. A wisp is given even if Isaac is not holding a card when the item is used.

• Car Battery: Uses the card twice. For example, if used with the Two of Hearts/Diamonds/etc. cards it will quadruple whatever amount Isaac has.

• Tarot Cloth: Invokes the extra effect when used.

• [Repentance] Only certain cards gain the Tarot Cloth effect with Blank Card.

• Car Battery + Tarot Cloth: The effect of the active card is quadrupled.

• • [Repentance] Only certain Tarot Cloth effects will be doubled again.

• 2 of Diamonds + Restock or in Greed mode:

• [edition anr] Coins can be infinitely generated by buying Lil' Battery. As Lil' Batteries only cost 5 coins (need two lil' batteries to reload blank), as long as Isaac starts with at least 21, the maximum of 99 coins can be quickly reached. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] This cannot be repeated infinitely outside of Greed Mode, as Restock now increases the price of a shop slot each time something is purchased from it. Having 12 coins will very slowly allow Isaac to obtain 99 coins, however.

• • Deep Pockets allows this to once again be repeated infinitely, as the price will cap at 99 coins, while up to 999 coins can be obtained. [end edition note] 

• ? Card: Teleports Isaac to the I AM ERROR room. This will consume both the Blank Card and the ? Card.

• An exception is when they are used on Chest, Dark Room, The Void, Ultra Greed, Mausoleum/Gehenna II leading to Ascent, Corpse II, or Home floors. Using them here consumes both the Blank Card and the ? Card, spawning an I AM ERROR Shopkeeper.

• Jera: Copies pickups with every use. This combination can double Lil' Battery, which can allow for game-breaking combos, due to repeated use of the synergy.

• Spawning too many items will cause objects to despawn. This can even despawn the End Chest after finishing a final boss fight.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Little Baggy: All cards are replaced by pills, rendering Blank Card useless unless Isaac also has Starter Deck.

• Wild Card: Does nothing if used through Blank Card. Wild Card can, however, copy the last card used through Blank Card.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Blinding Baby]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a card counterpart to Placebo and Clear Rune.

• ? Card sending Isaac to the I AM ERROR room and destroying both items is a nod to how the combination acting as expected would create an infinite loop, as the two items would attempt to use each other infinitely.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Copies the effect of the card or rune currently held by Isaac.
[Repentance] Copies the effect of the card currently held by Isaac. The recharge time is based on the power of the card.

Blank Rune.title: Blank Rune
Blank Rune.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish: Clear Rune]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants a random rune effect. 

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Black Rune is excluded. [end edition note] 

• Rune Shard is excluded.

• Has a 25% chance to drop another Blank Rune on the ground upon use.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The random rune effect can be from a rune that hasn't been unlocked yet.

• [Repentance] Blank Rune cannot replicate the effects of Soul Stones.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text: • The two most valuable rune effects from Blank Rune are Perthro, for a re-roll, or Ehwaz, for a Crawl Space which has a high chance of containing a free item. Therefore, the best use of Blank Rune is in a room with an item while also standing over a tile with a special graphic. [Repentance] Using Blank Rune in a room with an item pedestal also has the chance to activate Black Rune, exchanging the item for stats. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: Activates two random rune effects. Attempts to spawn additional Blank Rune twice.

fields.name: Blank Rune
fields.description: Grants a random rune effect and has a 25% chance to drop another Blank Rune on the ground upon use. [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Black Rune is excluded. [end edition note]

Blanket.title: Blanket
Blanket.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Heals one Red Heart.

• Grants one Soul Heart.

• Upon entering a Boss Room, grants a shield that blocks one hit. If the shield is not used by the time the player leaves the room, the shield will disappear.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The shield will be granted regardless of whether the Boss Room is already cleared.

• This item's shield effect has the same synergies and interactions as Holy Mantle with the only difference being that when paired with Holy Mantle or The Lost's innate shield it can still reapply later into the run. For a list of synergies and interactions, visit that page.

• Multiple Blankets will only give 1 shield.

• In Greed Mode, this item grants a shield only for the two boss fights on the final level. The shield does not activate for the regular boss waves on previous floors.

• To quickly unlock this item, keep restarting Greed mode to enter its Curse Room which occasionally contains a bed.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • IV - The Emperor?: A shield is granted upon teleporting to the extra boss room.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Blanket is based on this Steam Workshop item by P.5000 and Ratlah, originally known as Security Blanket.

• A "security blanket" is a common type of childhood comfort object, an item which provides psychological comfort.

• The blanket's appearance (being worn around the neck as a cape) and blue color is similar to the outfit of Pajama Sam, a character who also wears a blanket as a cape. This trait is shared with PJs.

• This item is part of a set of bedtime-themed items, including Binky, Mr. Dolly, Night Light, and PJs.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Blanket doesn't work in Dogma and The Beast boss fights.

fields.description: Grants one Soul Heart. Upon entering a boss room, grants a shield that blocks one hit, then disappears.

Blaster.title: Blaster
Blaster.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Blaster is an enemy that is exclusive to Mines. It is characterized by a large boulder with holes on its upper body and its lack of arms.

Blasters slowly wander around the room, occasionally shooting Fly Bombs at Isaac; the aim of these bombs varies between normal ones aimed directly at Isaac and predictive ones aimed where Isaac is going to be. When it shoots, the boulder on its head forms an opening for the Fly Bomb to be shot out of.

Blasters cannot shoot Fly Bombs if at least 4 Fly Bombs are alive in the current room, regardless of whether or not they were spawned by Blasters.

Blasters take only 25% damage from non-explosive sources. This means they have an effective 80 HP, but can be killed in a single hit by bombs, both ones placed by Isaac and ones created by the Fly Bombs the Blaster spawns.

[Repentance+] Destroyed by Hagalaz on use. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Blaster first appeared in the Antibirth mod.

fields.behavior: Slowly wanders around and occasionally shoots Fly Bombs at Isaac.

Blasting Cap.title: Blasting Cap
Blasting Cap.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Upon exploding, Bombs have a 10% chance to drop a Bomb pickup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The 10% chance to drop a bomb pickup still applies even if Isaac has a Golden Bomb. Because of this, it is trivial to get up to 99 bombs given enough time.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases the chance to 20%. Having both increases the chance to 30%.

• Curse of the Tower / Anarchist Cookbook / XVI - The Tower: Spawned Troll Bombs can drop bomb pickups.

• Ring Cap: The extra bomb also has a chance to drop a bomb pickup.

• Scatter Bombs: Tiny bombs can drop bomb pickups.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bomber Boy: The extra explosions cannot drop bomb pickups.

• Dr. Fetus: Shot bombs cannot drop additional bombs.

• Kamikaze!: Does not drop bomb pickups.

• Mr. Boom's Bomb can drop bomb pickups.

• Rocket in a Jar: Rockets can drop bomb pickups.

• Throwable Bombs from Bomb Grimaces cannot drop bomb pickups.

• Golden Troll Bombs: Do not drop bomb pickups.

fields.description: Exploding Bombs have a chance to drop another Bomb pickup.

Blastocyst.title: Blastocyst
Blastocyst.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Blastocyst is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb).

• [Repentance] Only in the Womb and the Scarred Womb. [end edition note] 
The large Blastocyst has [Before Repentance] 190 HP / [Repentance] 300 HP, the medium forms have 75 HP, and the small forms have 30 HP.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Makes hops towards Isaac and can perform the following attacks:

• If Isaac is close it, hops in place and upon landing:

• [Before Repentance] Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.

• [Repentance] Sends out a burst of large disorganized projectiles in all directions.

• If Isaac is far away it, leaps off-screen and lands on Isaac's position; upon landing:

• [Before Repentance] Shoots 12 small projectiles in all directions.

• [Repentance] Shoots 8 larger projectiles in all directions.

• Once enough health is depleted, it splits into two medium versions of itself that continue to hop after Isaac. Medium Blastocysts only hop after Isaac if he is within a certain distance from them. Otherwise, they hop around randomly.

• Each medium form shoots 6 projectiles in all directions by hopping in place. The orientation of the projectiles depends on Isaac's position.

• Once enough health is depleted, each medium Blastocyst splits into two small versions. Small Blastocysts no longer hop after Isaac and only hop around randomly.

• Each small form shoots 4 projectiles in the cardinal directions after pausing for a moment.

• Each of these small Blastocysts leaves an Embryo behind upon defeat.
Blastocyst's large and medium forms deal a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Blastocyst can be encountered in groups consisting of:

• 1 large Blastocyst and 2 small Blastocysts.

• 1 large Blastocyst and 6 Embryos.

• 2 medium Blastocysts and 2 small Blastocysts.

• The medium and small Blastocysts' projectiles deal full heart damage regardless of chapter.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Blastocyst appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• An embryo is called a blastocyst when the differentiation of cells within a morula finally begins, usually 4–5 days after the fertilization of an embryo.

• It's likely that this boss is a reference to the main character of Viviparous Dumpling, one of Edmund McMillen's older games.

• Blastocyst's behavior is very similar to Monstro's.

• As Blastocyst divides, its positive facial expressions will become less happy, losing its smile entirely when it becomes an Embryo.

• If Blastocyst is killed on spikes, none of the smaller versions will spawn. This can also apply if a very large amount of damage is dealt very quickly to any of the phases.

• [Before Afterbirth+] This can also happen if Blastocyst is killed while still having a debuff that actively harms it (e.g. poison, fire).

• Upon killing Blastocyst, it seems as though, for a split second, an audio clip of someone's voice can be heard. Which can be easier to make out with the music turned off.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] During the Afterbirth+ expansion's release, an unfair room consisting of 8 Blastocysts with a Portal in the middle existed in all environments of Chapter 4 as a result of unintentionally placed full-sized ones rather than small ones. It was acknowledged by Edmund McMillen on Twitter and was fixed shortly after. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Blastocyst's intro animation where it drops in from the ceiling from the original game has been restored and it has new animations for when it divides.

• It is the only boss whose smaller variants can be encountered long before encountering the boss, as small Blastocysts can appear as early as Chapter 1.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Blastocyst will briefly appear as the largest form before splitting into smaller ones, regardless of which form was killed.
