Night Light.title: Night Light
Night Light.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• A cone of light shines from Isaac's chest that slows all enemies and enemy shots.

• The light will face the direction Isaac is moving.

• The light doesn't affect bosses, but it will slow their shots.

• The slow effect will disappear from enemies when the light stops shining on them, but shots will remain slow.

• Removes [curse: darkness] for the current floor.

• Doesn't provide immunity on later floors, but lessens the visual effect significantly, effectively removing the curse.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The light only needs to touch a shot once to slow it permanently.

• Doing a quick circular motion is effective to slow surrounding enemy shots, especially while fighting Hush.

• Overuse of this effect can cause unavoidable patterns, as the slowed shots will often still travel most of their original distance.

• Tainted Forgotten's light will always face right.

• [Repentance] This item is not recommended against The Beast, as the fires spawned by her will be slowed down significantly and pile up quickly, leading to no room to dodge.

• [Repentance] Doesn't remove Curse of Darkness afflicted by XIX - The Sun?, no matter if Night Light was picked up before or after using the card. However, the visual effect is still lessened by the beam of light. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is part of a set of bedtime-themed items, including Binky, Blanket, Mr. Dolly, and PJs.

fields.description: A cone of light shines in the direction Isaac is moving that slows enemies and enemy shots.

No. 2.title: No. 2
No. 2.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Holding any fire button/direction for 2.35 seconds causes Isaac to drop a free Butt Bombs bomb. This includes charging or directly controlled attacks. Only 1 Butt Bomb can be dropped per charging cycle, so it is required to stop firing and then charge again to drop another Butt Bomb. Taking damage will interrupt the cycle.

• [Repentance] There is a visual fart effect whenever a Butt Bomb is placed.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Oh Crap transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Turdlings. [end edition note] 

• Essentially grants unlimited bombs, as the charge time can be repeatedly reset by pressing and releasing the fire button. This allows Isaac to bomb an unlimited amounts of tinted rocks, get into every Secret Room and Super Secret Room, etc.

• Increases difficulty of poop-themed bosses such as Dingle, as Butt Bombs restore 25% of maximum HP to the bosses when they explode.

• The spawned butt bombs will be affected by bomb modifiers, excluding Mr. Mega.

• This item can be great for clearing the early floors of Greed mode, due to the butt bombs dealing room-wide damage every few seconds.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• No. 2, Maw Of The Void, Montezuma's Revenge and Revelation all have the same charge time, allowing Isaac to easily utilize them at same time.

• Bird's Eye/Ghost Pepper: Shoots a flame behind Isaac with each fart.

• Glitter Bombs: The butt bombs have a chance of spawning pickups or trinkets upon exploding.

• Remote Detonator: Bombs placed by No. 2 will not explode until Remote Detonator is activated.

• Ring Cap: Only 1 bomb is placed by No. 2.

• Short Fuse: No effect.

• Tiny Planet: Orbiting tears tend to knock the bomb towards Isaac, making self damage likely.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The item's name is a reference to a well-known euphemism for defecation.

fields.name: No. 2
fields.description: Continuously firing tears for 2.35 seconds causes Isaac to drop a Butt Bombs bomb, which damages and confuses all enemies in the room when it explodes.

Nose Goblin.title: Nose Goblin
Nose Goblin.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a 10% chance to fire a booger tear that sticks to the first enemy that it comes in contact with and deals damage over time.

• Each booger deals damage equal to Isaac's tear damage every second.

• [Before Repentance] The booger lasts for 60 seconds or until the enemy dies.

• • [Repentance] The booger lasts 10 seconds.

• Boogers have a 50% chance of being homing.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Not affected by Luck.

• Booger tears cannot pierce through enemies.

• Multiple boogers can stick to one enemy to deal extra damage.

• Nose Goblin's effect is almost identical to Sinus Infection beyond the added homing effect and having half the chance to trigger. Consequently, all its non-homing synergies apply to Nose Goblin.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Brimstone/The Ludovico Technique/Tech X/Trisagion: Every tick of damage Isaac’s tears deal have a chance to attach a separate booger tear on a hit enemy.

• Cricket's Body: Booger tears will split into split booger tears that can attach to enemies.

• Explosivo: Explosivo tears can also be booger tears which damage the enemy over time while stuck to them before exploding.

• Godhead: Shots retain their aura while stuck to an enemy, but the aura can damage only enemies other than the booger victim. If the enemy dies before the booger’s maximum duration, it will resume homing and will often stick to a second enemy.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either raises the chance to fire a booger tear to 20% chance and to 75% the chance for it to be homing. Having both raises the chance to respectively 30% and 100%.

• Guppy: Damage instances from boogers attached to enemies have a 100% ( [Repentance] 50%) chance to spawn a Blue Fly.

• Lachryphagy: All tears have a chance to burst into boogers. Boogers will always burst into more boogers, though some of the boogers may incorrectly appear to be normal tears. When a booger sticks to an enemy, it will burst into 8 boogers which have a high chance of sticking again to the same enemy.

• Lost Contact: Boogers that stick to enemies will block shots, and will not be destroyed in the process.

• Polyphemus: Booger shots lose the Polyphemus pierce effect, but stick to enemies while dealing the full damage of the Polyphemus shot. Damage does not degrade.

• Sinus Infection: The 50% homing also applies to boogers fired by Sinus Infection.

• Spirit Sword: Swings and projectiles have a chance to apply boogers on enemies.

• Strange Attractor: Attraction effect will remain on the booger shot stuck to an enemy. This can drag the enemy across the whole room until they reach one wall and get stuck on it, effectively disabling their normal movement.

• Tech.5: The laser also has a chance to apply boogers on enemies.

• Technology: Hit enemies have a chance for a booger to be applied to them.

• Technology 2: The laser can also apply boogers with the laser’s chance to apply boogers being determined rapidly every tick.

• Technology Zero: Boogers can be connected with electricity while being attached dealing large amounts of damage to the booger victim.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Brimstone/Technology/Tech X/Trisagion/Ipecac: Overrides Nose Goblin.

• Ipecac: Booger tears will still appear, but will act identically to other Ipecac shots.

• Compound Fracture/The Parasite: Booger tears will not split after killing enemies.

• Dr. Fetus/Epic Fetus/Mom's Knife: Overrides Nose Goblin.

• Holy Light: Holy light strikes do not activate on booger shots.

• Immaculate Heart/Saturnus: Orbiting tears that stick to an enemy will return to the ring if the enemy cannot be stuck to anymore before the tear's duration ends.

• Jacob's Ladder: Lightning strikes do not activate on booger shots.

• [Before Repentance] Tech.5/Technology 2: The laser is unaffected by Nose Goblin.

• [Before Repentance] The Ludovico Technique: The large tear has a chance to stick to enemies. The tear cannot be controlled while it is stuck to an enemy, and cannot be removed until the enemy has died.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The trinket's name and description appear to be a reference to the episode "Nurse Stimpy" from the cartoon "Ren and Stimpy".

fields.name: Nose Goblin
fields.description: Chance to fire a homing booger that sticks to enemies and deals damage over time.

Notched Axe.title: Notched Axe
Notched Axe.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Isaac holds the Notched Axe above his head as long as he is in that room, and can break any obstacles he touches, as well as being able to break through walls that lead into Secret Rooms.

• [Repentance] Isaac stops shooting tears and holds the Notched Axe like The Forgotten's club, and can break obstacles, blow open doors, and hit enemies for 3x damage by swinging it. The Notched Axe has 64 charges. Hitting rocks or opening doors depletes 1 charge for each obstacle destroyed. Hitting enemies depletes 2 charges. Isaac can toggle back and forth between tears and using the Notched Axe by pressing the Active Item button. Once the Notched Axe runs out of charges, it cannot be used for the rest of the floor.

• [Repentance] The charges on Notched Axe cannot be refilled by means other than going to a new floor or picking up Iron Bar. This includes Lil' Battery, Battery Bums, 4.5 Volt, Jumper Cables, etc. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] If Isaac takes damage while using the Notched Axe, his current use of the Axe will end.

• [Before Repentance] Isaac cannot attack or pick up other items while using the Notched Axe.

• [Before Repentance] Activating the item while it is already being used will end the effect. This does not require any charge.

• [Before Repentance] Obstacles destroyed by the Notched Axe will never fill pits.

• [Repentance] The Notched Axe may be used to get access to the Mines. The door will break open with one swing. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Notched Axe shares its synergies with The Forgotten's bone club. See that page for details. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Notched Axe, like The Forgotten's bone club, may be used to pick up items that are just out of reach over a pit or spikes. This does not require any charge. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Notched Axe can open secret rooms, and so it can be used on walls to test for secret rooms without using charge. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Notched Axe cannot free Sticky Nickels. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Notched Axe can provoke an Angel Statue in Angel Rooms, triggering the boss fight. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Notched Axe can be used to destroy the Tuff Twins and The Shell bosses instead of using bombs. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Anti-Gravity: Melee attacks will generate a hovering tear in the shape of the swing of the pickaxe.

• The Battery: Causes remaining charge from the previous floor to carry over to the next one.

• Bethany: Breaking Notched Axe and using a Soul Charge to activate it again will allow for a single use before immediately breaking.

• Book of Belial interaction: The axe receives a purplish glow and receives the following upgrades:

• Increased durability: Each use of the axe has a very high chance not to use a charge.

• Faster usage: The axe can be swung up to four times per second, regardless of Judas' tears stat.

• Higher knockback: Enemies are knocked back when hit, receiving 8 + 0.2 × floor damage if they collide with a wall, obstacle, or other enemies.

• Fire effect: The axe will set enemies on fire. The burn deals damage equal to Judas' damage, and ticks up to 5 times.

• Increased luck: destroying obstacles with the axe has an increased chance to spawn pickups.

• • Destroying Poops will spawn pickups much more frequently. When combined with Petrified Poop, the chance becomes 100% and will often result in multiple pickups from a single poop.

• • Destroying Tinted Rocks will drop more consumables than usual, similarly to Super Special Rocks.

• • Destroying Props (such as Urns, Mushrooms, Skulls, and Polyps) gives the prop an extra chance to drop its rewards. This can result in a single prop giving multiple drops.

• • Destroying Fool's Gold rocks will drop significantly more coins.

• Book of Virtues interaction: When used with the Book of Virtues, breaking obstacles has a chance to generate wisps that have different effects based on the "mineral" mined, from most common to least common:

• Dip wisp (can only be obtained from poop): Fires brown tears that deal 1.5 damage and has extremely low health.

• Black wisp: Fires black tears that have the effect of A Lump of Coal and deal 2.5 damage.

• Silver wisp: Fires metallic tears that have the effect of Iron Bar and deal 4 damage.

• Gold wisp: Fires penny tears that can turn enemies gold similar to Midas' Touch and deal 3.5 damage.

• Red wisp: Fires laser tears similar to the ones fired by Technology and deal 3.5 damage.

• Blue wisp: Fires diamond tears similar to the ones fired by Crown Of Light that deal 7 damage.

• Broken Padlock: Allows the Notched Axe to open locked chests and doors. The opening of chests does not use durability, however it will consume a key if Isaac has any.

• Ipecac: Melee attacks will trigger an explosion when they makes contact with an enemy; unlike with the Forgotten's bone club, Isaac will take damage from these Ipecac explosions.

• Iron Bar: Fully recharges the axe when picked up.

• Technology: Melee attacks will cause a technology laser ring to appear around Isaac, damaging enemies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Found Soul: Found Soul gets a Notched Axe that breaks after a single use. If Notched Axe is dropped and picked up again, Found Soul will be able to use it again.

sections.heading: In Rebirth [Before Repentance]
sections.text: [end edition note]

sections.heading: In Repentance [Repentance]
sections.text: [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to Markus "Notch" Persson, the creator of Minecraft.

• It resembles an Iron Pickaxe, which can be used to mine stones and ores.

• The item durability being 64 could also be a reference the max amount of copies you could hold in a slot for most items in Minecraft.

• The item is also a reference to the Notched Pickaxe from The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, which itself was most likely also a reference to Notch.

• This item got significantly buffed from the original Binding of Isaac, where it could not open up secret rooms and could only break 1 rock for every use, though it did only have a 1 room recharge time.

• [Repentance] The "mineral" wisps that appear when using Book of Virtues with this item follow the same scheme as they do in Minecraft, giving the player black, silver, gold, blue, and red wisps, most likely corresponding to the Minecraft minerals coal, iron, gold, diamond, and redstone respectively.

• [Repentance] The new effect from The Book of Belial resembles an enchanted pickaxe that appears to have the following Minecraft enchantments: Efficiency (quicker usage), Fire Aspect (setting enemies on fire), Fortune (increased amount of drops when destroying obstacles), Knockback (increased knockback) and Unbreaking (increased durability).

• The synergy as a whole references the fact that enchanted books are used to augment tools in Minecraft.

• Using Iron Bar to repair the item is another reference to Minecraft where you can repair Iron Pickaxes using iron and an Anvil.

fields.name: Notched Axe
fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Isaac destroys obstacles and opens Secret Rooms by walking into them, but cannot shoot or pick up items until it's cancelled.
[Repentance] Toggles between tears and the pickaxe, which can be swung to attack and break obstacles. Using it depletes the charge, and it can't be used until next floor once the charge runs out. [end edition note]

Nuh Uh!.title: Nuh Uh!
Nuh Uh!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: NO!]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• On Chapter 4 and beyond, replaces all coin and Key spawns with a random pickup from the table below.

| Pickup | Chance 
| Bomb | 26.6%

| Red Heart | 26.6%

| Pill | 16.6%

| Card | 16.6%

| Trinket | 6.6%

| Lil' Battery | 6.6%

• If the pickup is a coin, it also has a 20% chance to be replaced with a Fly.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• All items, trinkets, cards, machines, etc. that spawn coins and keys synergize with this trinket and will cause a random pickup to be spawned instead.

• The floors during the Ascent are unaffected.

• This trinket has no effect in Greed Mode.

• Coins and keys generated prior to holding Nuh Uh! are unaffected.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
*Any mention of "Random pickups" refers to the above table. "~#" are averages as 20% of coins are flies.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy grants +10% chance to spawn the double variant of pickups.

• Head of the Keeper: Coins generated by Head of the Keeper will be replaced with random pickups.

• Sanguine Bond: 17% of the time, generates ~5 random pickups, often allowing infinite use with red hearts.

• The Sacrifice Room will pay out with ~26 random pickups on it's 10th use 50% of the time.

• Midas' Touch / Eye of Greed: Enemies affected by Midas' touch will drop 1-4 random pickups.

• Because 20% of coins become harmless Fly, 20% of the time you can trigger this effect again by affecting and killing spawned flies.

• Wooden Nickel: Can generate a random pickup ~40% of the time.

• 4.5 Volt: Generate random pickups over the course of a fight.

• Blank Card: Allows repeated use of card effects that synergize with this trinket.

• IX - The Hermit?: Pickups / Items are sold and turned into other random pickups.

• XIV - Temperance: The generated machine now drops random pickups.

• Ace of Diamonds / Ace of Spades: Re-rolls pickups in the room into other random pickups or turns enemies into random pickups.

• XII - The Hanged Man?: Slain enemies drop random pickups.

• A Card Against Humanity: Coins dropped by generated poops become random pickups.

• • Midas' Touch / Petrified Poop: Greatly increases the amount of coins and thus the amount of random pickups.

• Soul of the Keeper: Creates 0-25 random pickups.

• IV Bag / Piggy Bank / Swallowed Penny: Convert health into random pickups.

• Gimpy / Old Bandage / Fanny Pack: Further increase the chance of hearts appearing after use allowing the generation of even more random pickups.

• Tainted Keeper: Coins generated by killing enemies will be replaced by random pickups, however they will still disappear after a short time.

• Lucky Rock: 26.6% of rocks exploded will drop random pickups.

• Guppy's Tail: The keys needed to open gold chests will be converted to other pickups. However, the large quantities of coins generated from chests can be turned into many random pickups. Dropping Nuh Uh! at the start of the floor and then picking it back up to collect random pickups later allows for keys to collected but still gain large quantities of random pickups. Due to the large amount of pills and bombs generated, having the Bombs are Key pill effect in the pool may allow you to turn a surplus of bombs into a surplus of keys as needed.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: No effect.

• Unless dropped or used on pickups spawned prior:

• Blessed Penny / Charged Penny and other penny trinkets can no longer be used.

• Bumbo / Bum Friend / Key Bum: No longer function except for associated transformations. (Super Bum)

• Sharp Key: Can no longer pickup keys to use.

• Keeper andTainted Keeper can no longer pickup coins to heal.

fields.description: Replaces Keys and coins that spawn in Chapter 4 and beyond with more useful pickups.

D8.title: D8
D8.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Re-rolls Isaac's damage, tears, range, and speed.

• Each stat is given a multiplier, ranging from 0.5x to 2.0x, which applies after all other adjustments.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Luck, Shot Speed, and [Before Repentance] Tear Falling Speed are unaffected.

• The Tears multiplier can cause Isaac's tear delay to decrease beyond the normal cap of 5.

• The Speed multiplier cannot cause Isaac's speed to decrease or increase past the normal range of 0.1 to 2.0.

• The multiplier overrides the Speed Up effect of A Pony or White Pony, which normally raise Isaac's Speed to 1.5 if it is below that value.

• [Before Repentance] The hidden maximum Speed value also gets the same multiplier, which may further cap Isaac's Speed.

• The multipliers are chosen in a way that keeps their total product roughly the same; the item will most often increase two and decrease two of Isaac's stats, although it can increase three and decrease one or increase one and decrease three. Larger increases are balanced by larger decreases.

• In the area where you claim Knife Piece 2, the multipliers granted by d8 will remain, when activated using Void (possible bug). This can be detrimental if there are negative multipliers to fire rate or speed.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a black glowing die wisp on the middle ring. Each wisp has a random damage and fire rate assigned to it. Wisp health is not randomized.

• Libra: Libra's balancing applies after the D8 multipliers, making it possible to aim for a high multiplier in the most efficient stats for a large across-the-board boost.

• Rock Bottom: Allows affected stats to reach high multipliers, potentially doubling them if used enough.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: Re-rolls twice instantly without any benefits.

• Rock Bottom: Considers both sets of multipliers, allowing higher stats to be reached faster.

• Jacob and Esau: Only the brother using D8 will get their stats rerolled with the exception of Speed, which is shared between both brothers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The sprite for D8 has an 8 and a 7 below it, but judging by how real 8-sided dice look, the 7 should be a 5 instead.

fields.description: Re-rolls Isaac's damage, tears, range, and speed.

Dad's Key.title: Dad's Key
Dad's Key.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Upon use, opens all doors in the current room in almost all circumstances.

sections.heading: Notes
Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Creates wisps in the middle ring. If the wisps touch Locked Chests, Special Room doors, or uncleared room doors, they will unlock and open them, destroying themselves in the process. These wisps can open any locked door they touch, including the door to the Mega Satan arena, A Strange Door, and the flesh door to Corpse. Bomb Chests and Mega Chests are unaffected. They will also donate to Key Masters on touch, destroying themselves in the process. Opening a chest in a Challenge Room with a wisp will not start the challenge.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in The Family Man and Red Redemption, as well as the June 19th curated daily challenge.

• Dad's Key may be a reference to Isaac's father leaving his mother, as it can be used to escape from almost any conflict.

• In Wrath of the Lamb, this item was unlocked by beating ??? for the first time.

• The function of this item is very similar to the Magical Key from The Legend of Zelda.

fields.description: Opens all doors in the current room in almost all circumstances, including doors which require a Key to open, entrances to Secret Rooms, and the door to Mega Satan.

Dad's Lost Coin.title: Dad's Lost Coin
Dad's Lost Coin.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] +1.5 range.

• [Repentance] +2.5 range.

• [Before Repentance] +1 tear falling speed

• Drops a Lucky Penny.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] Dad's Lost Coin's quality is considered 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item may refer to Sobriety Coins, which are given to members of the Alcoholics Anonymous organization to commemorate how long a member has remained sober.

• This is further supported in the item's The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls rendition, which closely resembles the most common design of Sobriety Coin.

• [Repentance] This is also supported by the dialogue during the Ascent, where at one point Mom mentions that Dad has a drinking problem.

• This was confirmed by Edmund in the Four Souls Isaac lore stream. He went on to say it was inspired by his own father, who is a recovered alcoholic/drug addict, and gave Edmund one of his first sobriety chips as a gift.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] +1.5 range, +1 tear falling speed. Drops a Lucky Penny.
[Repentance] +2.5 range. Drops a Lucky Penny.

Dad's Note.title: Dad's Note
Dad's Note.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Initiates the Ascent sequence.

• Any trinkets left in Treasure Rooms and Boss Rooms will turn into Cracked Keys.

sections.heading: How to Acquire
sections.text:
• Once Mother has been defeated at least once, A Strange Door will appear in the starting room of Depths II and its alts (only Necropolis and Dank Depths, as the door does not appear on Mausoleum or Gehenna). This door can only be opened if Isaac has The Polaroid, The Negative, or Faded Polaroid.

• This can be done by beating Mom then teleporting out of the boss room to anywhere else on the floor, or, alternatively, by inheriting any of the items from a previous run. Helpfully, a marked Skull will always appear somewhere on Depths II which, when destroyed, drops 0 - The Fool. If Isaac has Little Baggy, it will drop a Telepills instead.

• The door can also be opened with Broken Padlock, Cracked Orb, Soul of Cain, or Sharp Key.

• Interacting with this door consumes The Polaroid, The Negative or Faded Polaroid. If multiple are available, Faded Polaroid is preferred, The Negative next, and The Polaroid last.

• The door leads to a special version of Mausoleum/Gehenna II. Instead of a boss, the boss room of this floor contains Dad's Note.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Dad's Note cannot be rerolled or destroyed in most ways, such as with The D6, Void, Abyss, or even Spindown Dice.

• Dad's Note cannot be duplicated via Crooked Penny, even if other items in the same room would be duplicated. Other duplication items such as Diplopia work as normal.

• The boss room containing Dad's Note cannot be exited once entered, similar to the Mom boss fight. The only way to exit is through teleportation.

• The only item that can be taken in the boss room of this special version of Mausoleum/Gehenna is Dad's Note. No other items will be spawned.

• Lemegeton pulls from the Boss Pool when used.

• Treasure Room and Shop will still generate in this special floor as in usual floors, giving Isaac more options.

• If Dad's Note is obtained outside of the special boss room via unintended means (such as using Spindown Dice on Sausage), the music will slowly fade out, but the Ascent will not start.

• Red Room doors cannot appear on the borders of the map, preventing access to the I AM ERROR room and Womb/Utero/Scarred Womb.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The boss room that contains Dad's Note is same boss room that would contain Mom if the player were to have entered Mausoleum/Gehenna normally (by entering the door to Mausoleum/Gehenna I in the boss room of the Depths/Necropolis/Dank Depths I or the Mines/Ashpit II). Whether or not Mom has already been killed in Chapter 3, the boss room reflects the fight's completed state with blood on the floor and no exit door, which would normally be the scenario after defeating Mom.

fields.description: Sends Isaac on an Ascent toward Home.

Dad's Ring.title: Dad's Ring
Dad's Ring.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Creates a ring of light around Isaac that petrifies enemies on contact.

• Normal enemies stay permanently petrified as long as they are within the ring, whereas bosses get a standard petrification effect that stays even outside the ring but isn't permanent.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Dad's Ring has no effect on the Mask of a Mask + Heart.

• [Repentance] Will not affect invincible boss enemies such as Dark Esau or Mother's Shadow. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: This item's visual appearance is overridden by some items, rendering the ring invisible. It will still behave as normal in this state.
Bug note: When Pause is used with Dad's Ring, it creates a second ring of light that stays in place where Isaac used "Pause" which lasts for the active item's duration. The second ring is a visual glitch and does not interact with enemies. Moreover, both rings are flashing for the duration.

fields.description: Creates a ring of light around Isaac that petrifies enemies in contact.

Daddy Long Legs.title: Daddy Long Legs
Daddy Long Legs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the item; Daddy Longlegs] 

Daddy Long Legs is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb).

• [Repentance] Only in the Utero.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Daddy Long Legs' head hangs down stationary and can perform the following attacks:

• Raises his head, making it invulnerable, and stomps the ground in random locations around the room 4 times in quick succession. [Repentance] One of these legs will always stomp on top of Isaac's position.

• The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.

• Lifts his head off-screen and stomps the ground 4 times at regular intervals on top of Isaac's position. At the end of the 4 stomps, he slams his head down quickly, shooting out 8 projectiles in all directions. He can only slam his head down along a horizontal plane across the center of the room and slams it down close to Isaac's position.

• Occasionally performs a fifth stomp before slamming his head down.

• The appendages that he stomps with can be attacked to damage him.

• Spits out 2-3 Spiders.

• These spiders can be killed by Daddy Long Legs' stomps and head slam.
Daddy Long Legs' foot stomp and head slam deal a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The passive item Daddy Longlegs is a familiar form of this boss, stomping enemies to assist Isaac. The familiar will even attack the Daddy Long Legs.

• On rooms where Daddy Long Legs is treated as a degraded Boss, they can be used to blow open doors.

• [Before Repentance] Like Mom's stomp, his stomp deals explosive damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Daddy Long Legs was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original game, Daddy Long Legs could be encountered in Necropolis.

• Daddy Long Legs's appendages consist of 2 hands and 2 legs; he will use each of them once in his stomping attacks.

• Only 3 appendages visually appear to be connected to his head despite him having 4.

• Daddy Long Legs is a colloquialism for various types of arachnids including Opiliones and Pholcidae.

• Triachnid is his alternative version.

• His limbs are also used in the Daddy Longlegs item.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: During the mass-stomp attack, the player will take damage before the animation even begins, making it impossible to dodge.
Bug note: During the mass-stomp attack, if the player deals damage to one of the legs that would normally kill a full health Daddy Long Legs, it will cause the leg to die as a separate Daddy Long Legs. This will not damage the boss at all.
Bug note: If you freeze one of Daddy Long Legs's legs, then kill Daddy Long Legs while a Spider is still alive, then kill the Spider, the boss fight music won't stop. This is fixed if Isaac leaves the room and then re-enters again.

Daddy Longlegs.title: Daddy Longlegs
Daddy Longlegs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the boss; Daddy Long Legs]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Daddy Long Legs' shadow follows Isaac and stomps on enemies for 20 damage per tick, with each stomp capable of hitting a single enemy twice for a total of 40 damage. The delay between stomps is approximately 4 seconds.

• In a room with multiple enemies, Daddy Long Legs will prioritize on monsters with the most health first.

• If all monsters are of the same type, the familiar will attack the closest enemy.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Spider Baby transformation. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Daddy Long Legs. [end edition note] 

• The foot stays down for about 1 second, and enemies who wander into it will also take damage.

• This item deals enough damage to kill most early enemies in one hit and is especially powerful against enemies with multiple segments like Larry Jr.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS! / Hive Mind: Increases the foot's size and doubles its damage. Both items cannot be stacked for an even stronger effect.

• Box of Friends: Spawns an additional foot for the rest of the room.

• Extension Cord: Bolts of electricity will arc between the shadow or the foot and Isaac and his familiars.

• Gnawed Leaf: Allows Isaac to stay invincible while Daddy Longlegs clears the room, granting Isaac a slow but effective way of completely avoiding damage. This combination is especially useful as The Lost and Tainted Lost.

• Spin to Win: Boosts the foot's damage while spinning.

• The Twins: Has a chance to spawn an additional foot when entering a new room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Duct Tape: No effect.

• Forgotten Lullaby: No effect.

• Sacrificial Altar: Daddy Longlegs cannot be sacrificed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • In the original The Binding of Isaac, this item was unlocked by completing Purist.

fields.description: Daddy Long Legs' shadow follows Isaac and occasionally stomps enemies for 40 damage total.

Daemon's Tail.title: Daemon's Tail
Daemon's Tail.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• 80% of heart drops are replaced with Keys.

• All heart drops turn into Black Hearts, if possible. (Sometimes heart types are tied to the room, such as in certain Super Secret Rooms.)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Objects and items such as tinted rocks, Red Chests, Fortune Telling Machines, Little C.H.A.D., Bloody Penny, or Blue Fire Places can't drop Black Hearts. Thus, they will still drop Soul Hearts/Red Hearts with Daemon's Tail.

• Glyph of Balance can still force drops to be Red Hearts if the proper conditions are met.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] All heart drops from Ace of Hearts will be Black Hearts. [end edition note] 

• No effect on Queen of Hearts, V - The Hierophant, V - The Hierophant?, and VI - The Lovers.

• VIII - Justice is affected by the heart pickup reduction, however its Red Heart drop will be replaced if it spawns.

• Sources of heart drops that are reduced include cleared rooms, bosses, Slot Machines, Fortune Telling Machines, Beggars, Fire Places, Chests, Red Chests, Poops, tinted rocks, items (Gimpy, Old Bandage, Fanny Pack), trinkets (Bloody Penny), and familiars (Little C.H.A.D., The Relic, etc).

• Hearts that are present upon entering a room for the first time are unaffected by the reduction (for example, the ones found in Curse Rooms/Devil Rooms/Angel Rooms), but will be converted to Black Hearts.

• • The exceptions to this are particular Super Secret Rooms, which have the effect of forcing all heart drops to be the kind found within them.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The V - The Hierophant and VI - The Lovers tarot cards have a chance to drop one heart instead of two.

• Things that can drop pickups other than hearts will keep the same chance to drop a consumable, but with an increased chance for drops other than hearts and a decreased chance for heart drops. In particular, this increases the chances of acquiring:

• Tarot cards & trinkets from Fortune Telling Machines

• Bombs and Keys from tinted rocks

• Pills and items from Red Chests

• Coins from Poops and Fire Places

• Any pickup from Slot Machines, cleared rooms, Beggars, Chests, and the Fanny Pack.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Blue and purple fires drop Black Hearts instead of Soul Heart.

• Black Feather: Black Feather grants a damage boost for Daemon's Tail, provided Isaac has an extra trinket slot ( [Afterbirth+ onward] or has gulped/smelted either of the trinkets).

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Box: The Red Heart drop will not be reduced and will always be replaced by a Black Heart.

• Crystal Ball: The chance to drop Cards or Runes will change to 90%/10% in favor of cards.

• Squeezy / Mr. Dolly / Marrow: Heart drops are unaffected.

sections.heading: Tips
sections.text:
• Due to its specific mechanic, Daemon's Tail has no synergy with items increasing chances for Soul/Eternal/Black Hearts to drop instead of a Red Heart, like Mitre, Mom's Pearl, or Bible Tract.

• Since the frequency of heart drops is lowered, holding this trinket can be dangerous to Isaac if he has numerous Red Heart containers, as he can easily find himself short on health.

• This trinket is more effective for ???, Tainted ???, [Repentance] Black Judas, Tainted Judas, and Tainted Forgotten because they cannot gain red heart containers or fill their Bone Hearts with red hearts.

• The trinket is also beneficial for The Lost, Tainted Lost, Keeper, and Tainted Keeper since it replaces useless hearts with other pickups.

• Mom's Pearl or Bible Tract are trinkets which only need to be held to be useful, whereas Daemon's Tail is more effective if it is held and dropped at the right times, to get an increased chance for consumables from certain mechanics (to counter a lack of Bombs/Keys/coins, or to get Black Heart protection), and to still get enough heart drops to stay alive at other times (from bosses or familiars).

• This trinket nearly requires this kind of strategy to pay off, making it tough to use as the player will have to sort and remember the moments where they must pick up or drop the trinket, as it interacts with nearly every consumable dropping mechanic.

fields.description: Most non-specific Red Heart drops become Black Hearts, but most heart drops are replaced by Keys.

Damage.title: Damage
Damage.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Damage refers to the amount of damage each tear deals to enemies, and is represented by a sword. As damage increases, the size of the tears increases as well. However, tear size is not always a direct indication of how much damage tears will do; for example, items like Dead Onion and Tropicamide increase tear size without increasing damage. Tears will grow and shrink when damage changes, but tears of a certain size do not have a specific damage value, and two tears of the same size (in two different runs) are likely to have different damage values.

sections.heading: Effective Damage
sections.text:
The formula for damage is: \mathit{EffectiveDamage} = (\mathit{CharBaseDmg} \times \sqrt{\mathit{TotalDmgUps} \times 1.2 + 1} + \mathit{FlatDmgUps}) \times \mathit{Multipliers}

where:

• CharBaseDmg = The character's base damage multiplied by their multiplier,

• TotalDmgUps = the total of all regular damage ups collected (not including special exceptions or damage multipliers),

• FlatDmgUps = the total of all damage ups that are excluded from the above (for example, Curved Horn or Ipecac), and

• EffectiveDmg = the approximate damage that can be expected per tear, or per 'tick' when using Brimstone or Technology 2.

This formula makes most damage upgrades less potent the more that Isaac has. For example, a Pentagram (+1 Damage) on Isaac would make his total damage 3.5 × (1 × 1.2 + 1)^0.5 = 3.5 × 1.48 = 5.19. Another Pentagram (+1+1) increases this to 6.45 (a 1.26 increase instead of a 1.69 increase). The higher a character's base damage, the more effective damage ups will be for that character. Flat damage modifiers and special adjustments like Polyphemus or Sacred Heart happen after the main formula.

sections.heading: Character Modifier
sections.text:
The character base damage is defined by a base number and a multiplier.

• Eve† and Tainted Magdalene: 0.75 × 3.50 = 2.625

• Jacob‡: 1.00 × 3.50 - 0.75 = 2.75

• Isaac, Magdalene, Samson, Lazarus, Lilith, The Lost, Apollyon, The Soul, Bethany, Tainted Isaac, Tainted Judas, Tainted ???, Tainted Samson, Tainted Lazarus, Tainted Lilith, Tainted Keeper, Tainted Apollyon, Tainted Bethany, and Tainted Jacob: 1.00 × 3.50 = 3.50

• Eden and Tainted Eden: 1.00 x 3.50 ± 1.0 = from 2.50 to 4.50

• ???: 1.05 × 3.50 = 3.675

• Esau‡: 1.00 × 3.50 + 0.25 = 3.75

• Keeper, Cain, Tainted Cain, Tainted Eve, and [Before Repentance] Lazarus Risen: 1.20 × 3.50 = 4.20

• Judas: 1.35 × 3.50 = 4.725

• Azazel, The Forgotten, Tainted Azazel, Tainted Forgotten, and Dead Tainted Lazarus: 1.50 × 3.50 = 5.25

• [Repentance] Lazarus Risen: 1.40 × 3.50 = 4.90 (+0.5 damage after each death, 6.20 effective damage on the first death) [end edition note] 

• Tainted Lost: 1.30 × 3.50 = 4.55

• Black Judas: 2 × 3.50 = 7.00

†: Whore of Babylon has the unique effect of increasing Eve's damage modifier from 0.75 to 1.00 when active. This does not apply to other characters, however.

‡: Jacob and Esau have -0.75 and +0.25 flat damage, respectively: their base damage, as far as the damage formula is considered, is still 3.5 with a 1.0 multiplier.

sections.heading: Damage Multipliers
sections.text:
Some items multiply damage rather than simply adding to it. Damage multipliers (not to be confused with the aforementioned character-inherent base multiplier) do not simply multiply the character's damage once; the damage stat is constantly recalculated and the damage multipliers are multiplied with the end result. This means that if a character starts with 3.50 damage and gets a 2× multiplier, their effective damage will be 3.5×2 = 7.00. If an item that grants +1 damage is picked up, the character's effective damage will be 3.5×(1×1.2+1)^0.5×2 = 3.5×(2.2)^0.5×2 = 3.5×1.48×2 = 10.38, and not 7.00 + 1.

Most damage multipliers stack. For example, [Before Repentance] Proptosis and Eve's Mascara both provide a 2× multiplier; picking up both will give a total multiplier of 4×. The exception to this is the 1.5× damage multipliers provided by Cricket's Head, Magic Mushroom, and the combination of Blood of the Martyr and The Book of Belial. These multipliers do not stack; for example, picking up both Cricket's Head and Magic Mushroom will result in an overall 1.5× multiplier rather than the expected 2.25×. Some damage multipliers may be applied to certain flat damage increases, while others will not; see the section on the order in which damage multipliers and flat damage are applied for more information.

sections.heading: Reverse Formula
sections.text:
Consequently, the reverse formula to determine your damage bonuses from the displayed value is \mathit{Bonus} = \frac{1}{1.2}\left[\left(\frac{\mathit{EffectiveDamage}/\mathit{Multipliers} - \mathit{FlatDmgUps}}{\mathit{CharBaseDmg}}\right)^2 - 1\right]
Multipliers is the product of all damage multipliers in effect.

sections.heading: Passive Items
Positive Multiplier
sections.text:
Character-specific damage multipliers:

• Eve + Whore of Babylon - Raises her damage multiplier from 0.75× to 1× while the whore effect is active. (It does not have this effect for any other character.)

• Judas + The Book of Belial + Birthright + Damocles - 1.4× damage multiplier while the Damocles effect is active.

• Dying with Judas' Shadow transforms the player into Black Judas, who has a 2× damage multiplier, which is the highest character-based damage multiplier in the game.

Synergy-specific damage multipliers:

• The Book of Belial + Blood of the Martyr - 1.5× damage multiplier. (The multiplier is shared with Cricket's Head and Magic Mushroom.)

• Brimstone + Brimstone - 1.2× damage multiplier.

• Brimstone + Technology - 1.5× damage multiplier.

sections.heading: Negative Multiplier
sections.text:
[collectible rows: 20/20, Almond Milk, Odd Mushroom (Thin), Soy Milk] 
[collectible rows: Technology 2] 
|}

• Note that Odd Mushroom (Thin) is not a "real" damage multiplier in that it only affects the increases from other items. For example, if you only had Eve's Mascara for a 2× damage multiplier and nothing else, then Odd Mushroom would only grant a flat -0.4 damage (because nothing would be multiplied by 0.9).

Damage Scaling.title: Damage Scaling
Damage Scaling.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to make certain monsters and bosses more challenging. Some specific entities in the game mitigate high-damage attacks, which effectively caps Isaac's damage per second to a maximum amount. The more damage dealt to such an enemy in a short period of time, the more Isaac's damage gets reduced.

The mechanic of damage scaling is conventionally referred to as "armor".

The amount of armor that an entity has corresponds to the "shieldStrength" field in the "entities2.xml" file.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text:
• The armor is based on four different criteria: how much base HP the entity has, how much damage it has taken in the last 4 seconds (120 game logic frames), the value of its armor (every applicable entity has a specific armor value), and their starting armor protection (increases from a value of 0 to 120).

• Every entity in the game is predisposed to make use of this mechanic: in fact, every entity sports a "starting armor protection" counter and an "armor value" field, but few entities actually use it.

sections.heading: How it Works
sections.text:
• When an entity with an armor value spawns, it starts off with a separate instance of armor. This instance of armor starts off by reducing incoming damage by 99% and will steadily decrease over the course of 4 seconds, at which point it is no longer in effect. This value will increase its "armor deployment" each game logic frame going from 0 (fully armored) to 120 (no longer in effect), and use this value to compute a 'static degree' of damage reduction, separate from this starting armor protection.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] In practice, this is only a significant factor in the battle with Delirium, as while it's transformed, its starting armor protection is reapplied. In the cases of all other armored entities, the starting armor protection becomes irrelevant after 4 seconds.

• The entity keeps track of how much unmodified damage it has taken in the last 4 seconds, which combined with the 'static degree', the entity's HP, and armor effectiveness, results in a multiplier to the actual damage dealt, capping out at a multiplier of 0.09× (in other words, Isaac's tears can never deal less than 9% of his Damage stat). This can stack with the starting armor protection to reduce damage even further.

• The entity's base HP is divided by its armor value to create a soft cap on damage per second (DPS). This soft cap serves as a way to equalize damage coming from Isaac; if his DPS is above this cap, it will be lowered, while DPS values below the soft cap are completely unaffected. The higher Isaac's DPS, the more his damage will be decreased.

• Due to the entity keeping track of how much unmodified damage it has taken in the past 4 seconds, Isaac's damage output will gradually decrease until it is equalized to the DPS soft cap, or the damage instance reaches the point that it is reduced to 9% of its original damage.

• Isaac's Damage stat is also taken into consideration, not just his DPS. If an individual damage instance is greater than 4 times the armored entity's DPS soft cap, that damage will be preemptively decreased, so as to prevent Isaac from obliterating entities in one shot, even if the entity has not been attacked in a period of 4 seconds.

• The overall result of this mechanic is that slow, high-powered attacks are less effective than rapid, lower-damage ones; the damage reduction formula has difficulty keeping up with rapid, low-damage attacks while slow, high-powered attacks will preemptively have their damage lowered, allowing for such attacks to have their damage equalized more easily.

• Ultimately this mechanic has its limits, as no matter what, each individual attack cannot have its damage reduced below 9% of its original damage, allowing the armor to be overwhelmed if the outgoing damage per second is large enough.

sections.heading: [Repentance] Bypassing Damage Scaling
sections.text:
• Methods were added to bypass this mechanic, giving Isaac ways to deal full damage by certain means. However, these ways of dealing damage do contribute to Isaac's damage per second, which can cause the damage dealt from his other attacks to be lowered as a result of running into the DPS soft cap. The amount of damage dealt through these methods tends to outweigh the downsides of lowering Isaac's damage in most cases.

• Bomb damage and most explosive damage in general bypasses damage scaling; most non-explosive bomb effects, however, do not (e.g. the tears fired by Sad Bombs, etc).

• • Bomber Boy: The initial explosion bypasses damage scaling, the subsequent explosions do not.

• • Ghost Bombs: The initial explosion bypasses damage scaling, the contact and explosion damage from the ghosts do not.

• • Scatter Bombs: Both the initial and subsequent explosions deal full damage.

• Effects which invoke The Necronomicon (e.g. Black Hearts, XIII - Death, etc), and the damage boosts from A Missing Page and Missing Page 2 bypass damage scaling.

• Strong knockback damage, for example from Butter Bean, Hemoptysis and Knockout Drops bypasses damage scaling.

• Dark Esau (see Tainted Jacob) bypasses damage scaling with his charge attack.

• Tick bypasses damage scaling in all versions of the game.

• The following items that deal explosive damage are exceptions and do not bypass damage scaling:

• Doctor's Remote

• Dr. Fetus

• Epic Fetus

• Explosivo

• Fire Mind

• Ipecac

• Mama Mega!
[end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Delirium only has armor while assuming the form of random bosses. Its armor will start from 0 and increase as damage is taken while transformed; once taking the shape of its true form, it won't have any. Its armor only protects its alternate forms. Every time Delirium transforms, its partial armor will be reapplied, resulting in considerably more damage reduction than the armor value alone.

• Armor is always actively updated, not only when an entity is taking damage.

• It is possible to apply the armor effect to any entity via editing its entry in entities2.xml.

• Ultra Greed, Ultra Greedier, and Delirium do not have corresponding "shieldStrength" values in the "entities2.xml" file. However, they nonetheless have damage scaling, so in these cases the mechanic is likely hard-coded.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Despite the armor attempting to balance damage dealt and keep fights challenging, it's very possible to overwhelm the mechanic and destroy even strong armored enemies like Hush.

• Dark Esau (866.0), Mother's Shadow (867.0), and Dogma's phase 1 angel (950.0) have a "shieldStrength" value in the "entities2.xml" file. However, all of these entities are invulnerable, so it has no effect.

Damocles.title: Damocles
Damocles.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, summons a sword that hangs directly above Isaac. As long as the sword hangs above Isaac, all item pedestals are doubled, spawning an additional free item next to them.

• Items spawned via other means, like Machines, Beggars, and certain items and cards, are also doubled.

• The extra item will be pulled from the current room's item pool, even if the original item is from a different pool (ex. Beggars or items from Alabaster Box).

• After Isaac takes damage (with exceptions, see below) once with the item activated, at any time with only a brief warning, the sword may fall, instantly killing Isaac regardless of his health. The sword has a 1/10000 chance every 4 game ticks (every 0.133 seconds) to fall, so on average, 50% of all Damocles runs will not drop the sword until after at least 15 minutes and 24 seconds have passed.

• Self-damage (such as from a [machine: Blood Donation Machine] , [machine: Devil Beggar] , Curse Room, Sacrifice Room, Spiked Chest, Bad Trip pill, or self-damage Active Items) does not count as damage taken for Damocles, and will not give it the chance to fall.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The chance for the sword to fall does not increase beyond the first hit taken.

• Items from Chests will not be doubled, which greatly limits Damocles' benefit in Chapter 6.

• The exception to this is Mega Chest, which will spawn one extra item alongside the 2 original items for a total of 3 items.

• In scenarios that have multiple items to choose from (such as rare double Treasure Room layouts and Boss Rush), an additional set of items for Isaac to choose from spawns. Only one item from each set can be taken.

• In alternate path treasure rooms, one item from the second set is known.

• Having multiple Damocles active at once does not spawn additional items.

• The only way Isaac can survive the falling sword is if he's invincible at the time it falls or, by technicality, with a respawn item. After the sword falls, extra items will no longer spawn.

• Losing a life before the sword falls does not remove the sword or its threat.

• Items with associated costs, like those in Devil Rooms or Shops, will not create additional items. This severely limits this item's benefit when used as Tainted Keeper, since most items that are normally created as pedestals are instead Shop items.

• This can cause items that are in inaccessible spots in certain room layouts to be moved to a more convenient location due to not having space for two pedestals in that spot. It can also cause items to move to less convenient spots.

• [Repentance+] Damocles' quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: The sword also increases Judas' damage by x1.4 then a flat +1 while it's active.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a wisp on the middle ring, looking like a sword. The wisp's tears look like Spirit Sword's beams, but there are no other effects.

• Blanket / Holy Mantle / Holy Card / Wooden Cross: Damage blocked by the shield doesn't count as damage taken. It will not, however, protect Isaac from the falling sword.

• Book of Shadows / Empty Vessel / Algiz / other items that give shield: Nullifies the instant kill of Damocles if the shield is active when the sword falls.

• Cone Head / Host Hat / Infamy / Metal Plate: Blocked damage does not count as damage and can delay the triggering of Damocles.

• Crooked Penny / Diplopia: An extra item is spawned per each item cloned.

• However, duplicating Damocles itself and activating additional copies has no effect.

• Dark Arts: When in the shadow state, Isaac can survive the instant kill of Damocles, though this requires precise timing and can be impossible if Dark Art's charge is empty as the sword is falling.

• Filigree Feather: Angels spawn 2 items when defeated. However, if a Key Piece spawns, a second pedestal will not appear.

• Genesis: If the player acquires Damocles and uses it before all items have been collected, then each subsequent item spawned after using it will each spawn an extra item. Unlike the Genesis choices, the other extra items will not disappear upon collecting one of them, potentially allowing the player to obtain a much higher amount of items than usual.

• Using Genesis will remove the hanging sword and its effects.

• Gnawed Leaf: If in the form of the statue, Isaac will be immune to the falling sword.

• Tooth and Nail's statue form can also save Isaac, but the statue transformation time lining up with the sword falling is unlikely.

• Lazarus' revival mechanic allows him to continue the run after dying to Damocles.

• This extends to other extra-life items such as 1up! or Dead Cat.

• The Lost / Tainted Lost: Any damage the Lost would take is likely to kill him instantly, meaning that the item's downside is greatly mitigated. Dying and respawning, however, will still trigger the chance of falling.

• Magic Skin: Spawns 2 items on every use instead of 1.

• My Little Unicorn / Unicorn Stump / other items that give invulnerability: If active, will negate the sword's lethal fall, saving Isaac.

• Mega Mush: When activated, protects from falling Damocles.

• Mystery Gift: When Damocles is activated, a second item will be spawned with adherence to the item pool for the current room. Even if Mystery Gift "fails" and spawns either The Poop or A Lump of Coal, a second item from the room's item pool will be rewarded.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: The sword will appear larger, but will gain no actual benefits.

• Blood Oath: Getting stabbed by Blood Oath does not trigger the chance of falling.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Clicker: The sword cannot be removed from Isaac's inventory.

• D4 / D100 / Tainted Eden: The sword does not get rerolled.

• Devil's Crown: The Devil Room items that appear are not doubled.

• Flip: The extra item will not have a "ghost" item to flip to.

• Glitched Crown: Duplicated item pedestals do not reroll.

• Holy Mantle: Does not protect Isaac from death when the sword falls.

• Isaac's Heart: Taking damage still allows it to fall, and the sword will still kill Isaac if it falls.

• Jacob and Esau: The sword only gains the chance to fall if the brother who used it takes damage.

• Metronome: Can invoke the effect of Damocles, which applies permanently.

• Panic Button: Not recommended. Panic Button will activate Damocles right before Isaac takes damage, guaranteeing Damocles will fall later in the run even if Isaac hasn't activated it yet.

• Spirit Shackles: Does not protect Isaac from death when the sword falls.

• Apollyon / Void: Using Void on Damocles will activate the effect and begin hanging the sword above Isaac on the next use of Void. Subsequent uses of Void will do nothing in regards to Damocles.

• If the player has Damocles and Birthright on Apollyon and after using Void, a previously destroyed item appears, Damocles will spawn an additional item.

• Tainted Eden: Taking damage does not reroll an active Damocles.

• Tainted Forgotten: The sword will hang over Tainted Forgotten's body but will still kill the character despite being invincible.

• Tainted Isaac: Damocles does not count toward his passive item count, and cannot be removed.

• Tainted Lazarus / Esau Jr.: The character that used Damocles must be active for double items to spawn.

• In the case of Boss Room, the form of Lazarus that did not use Damocles must fight the boss for it to drop double items.

• If the player has Birthright as Tainted Lazarus and the inactive form has Damocles, the sword can fall on them and kill the player, bypassing the inactive form's immunity to damage.

• XVII - The Stars?: The sword will not be removed from Isaac's inventory.

sections.heading: Survival
sections.text:
Given the 1/10000 chance for the sword to fall every 4 game ticks (0.133 seconds), Isaac has a ~4.4% chance to die for every minute of gameplay that passes after he takes damage with Damocles active. The following is a table for times Isaac could survive to after getting hit, along with the chances of reaching them:

| Time passed | Chance of Survival 
| 2 Minutes 20 seconds | 90%

| 4 Minutes, 57 seconds | 80%

| 7 Minutes, 55 seconds | 70%

| 11 Minutes, 21 seconds | 60%

| 15 Minutes, 24 seconds | 50%

| 20 Minutes, 21 seconds | 40%

| 26 Minutes, 45 seconds | 30%

| 35 Minutes, 40 seconds | 20%

| 51 Minutes, 9 seconds | 10%

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Damocles originates from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, the sources of damage Damocles would ignore was very limited, only being damage that would not lower angel/devil deal chance under any circumstances. The more times Isaac would get hit, the higher the chance of Damocles falling became.

• Damocles' doubling effect would also double all item pedestals including ones from chests, shops, and devil deals with the extra items created by Damocles being free.

• Damocles would also appear in Secret Rooms.

• The item's appearance and effects are a reference to [the] Sword of Damocles, a story in which Damocles frequently praised King Dionysius's life of wealth and luxury, and is offered to switch places with Dionysius on the throne for a day to have a taste of his power. Damocles accepts, only to find that Dionysius had a sword hanging over his throne by a single horse hair to remind Damocles of the never-ending threats to both themselves and their country that a ruler must deal with during their reign, causing Damocles to beg to give the throne back to Dionysius.

• Damocles can be seen hanging over Isaac's head on the Antibirth album cover.

• There are actually two different Damocles items in the game: one (item ID 577) is the active item that Isaac can encounter, and the other (item ID 656) is a hidden passive item that is given when the active Damocles is used and that carries out the item's effects. The passive Damocles cannot be encountered through any normal means, even via Spindown Dice or Death Certificate, nor does it appear in the collection grid. If spawned on a pedestal via the Debug Console, collecting the passive Damocles will immediately put the sword above Isaac's head as if the active Damocles were used.

fields.quote: A king's fortune... but at what cost?
fields.description: Spawns a sword above Isaac's head, which doubles all item pedestals. After Isaac takes damage, the sword can randomly fall at any point, instantly killing him.

Dangle.title: Dangle
Dangle.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Dangle is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth that can appear in the Basement [Repentance] and in the Burning Basement [end edition note] .

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Fires three projectiles towards Isaac.

• Whistles before summoning 1-3 Brownie Corns and then fires 3 projectiles at Isaac.

• Quickly performs 2 long dashes towards Isaac while bouncing off obstacles and walls, after which he pauses to catch his breath. While dashing, he leaves slippery Brown Creep.

• Occasionally spawns a Corn Mine at the start of a dash, which immediately detonates, poisoning Dangle. If he is poisoned while dashing he leaves behind damaging Green Creep instead.

• Brownie Corns caught in his dashes are knocked back a distance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Dangle is much less common than his counterpart, Dingle, spawning only 1/4th as often.

• If a Butt Bombs Bomb goes off in the same room as Dangle, it will heal him.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Butt Bomb effect on Dr. Fetus or Epic Fetus does not heal Dangle.

• Flush! kills Dangle instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 Brownie Corns.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• He is a corny variant of Dingle.

• Upon death, Brownie will turn into a Dangle with lower HP.

• Dangle has the highest health of any boss fought in Chapter 1.

• Dangle looks slightly similar to Honey Buckets from Gish, one of Edmund McMillen's other games.

Dark Arts.title: Dark Arts
Dark Arts.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Tainted Judas starts with this item in his consumable slot.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When used, Isaac gains +1.0 speed and can walk through enemies/bullets for 1 second or until he shoots. If Isaac walks through an enemy or bullet during this time, it freezes until the effect ends, then takes damage equal to 2× Isaac's damage plus a flat 3.5. If there are multiple enemies/projectiles caught in the attack, each consecutive attack deals an additional flat 3.5 damage. At the end of the effect, an area of effect blast is created, dealing more damage the more enemies or bullets were pierced during the effect.

• The damage of the blast at the end of Dark Arts is equal to the sum of all damage dealt while dashing between enemies.

• • Bullets walked through will still count for the final blast damage calculation, even though they can't be damaged.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The invincibility can be canceled early by firing tears (and hence receive the damage bonus early with Tainted Judas or Black Judas).

• If an enemy/bullet Isaac walks through dies or otherwise disappears before Dark Arts deactivates, they will not grant a damage bonus.

• Orbitals that deal contact damage such as Forever alone will still deal damage and potentially kill an enemy, while those that block shots like Pretty Flies will still block and destroy projectiles.

• Dark Arts still works on reflected bullets.

• Explosive projectiles will explode when destroyed by Dark Arts.

• While Dark Arts is active, Isaac:

• Cannot pick up items or donate to Blood Donation Machines or Devil Beggars.

• Cannot open Chests. Standing on Spiked Chests or Mimic Chests when the effect ends will safely open them without taking damage.

• Can pass through Curse Room doors or over spikes.

• Can still press Pressure Plates, including the button in Greed Mode without taking damage.

• Dark Arts will trigger certain tear effects on enemies it damages, such as burning from Fire Mind.

• Invincible enemies such as Stoney and Stone Grimaces can still be affected and used to increase the damage.

• Hosts can be damaged and killed even while they are lowered and invincible.

• Similarly, using Dark Arts on Scolex's invulnerable segments will deal damage.

• If Isaac walks through an enemy/bullet, the blast at the end of Dark Arts can destroy Shopkeepers.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 9 Volt: Halves the time required to charge Dark Arts.

• Backstabber: Tagging an enemy from behind will apply bleeding.

• The Battery: Second charge can be used while Dark Arts is active.

• Book of Belial interaction: Grants temporary damage ups for every enemy/projectile hit by Dark Arts, similarly to Tainted Judas. This stacks with Black Judas' inherent version of this, doubling the amount of damage gained.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns black wisps on the middle ring whenever an enemy is killed with Dark Arts. The wisps do not persist between rooms.

• Camo Undies: The stealth mode given by Camo Undies won't be removed by activating Dark Arts. However, Dark Arts only gives +0.5 speed while Camo Undies is active.

• Car Battery: Dark Arts will last twice as long, totalling at 2 seconds per use.

• Euthanasia: Dark Arts can apply the Euthanasia effect.

• Pause: Activating Dark Arts will not cancel the effect.

• Taurus: Dark Arts' speed increase will contribute towards Taurus' activation.

• Black Judas / Tainted Judas: For every enemy/bullet he walks through, he will gain a temporary +1 damage bonus, which wears off at a rate of -0.25 damage every half second.

• Wisps: Wisps cannot be destroyed while Dark Arts is in effect.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Aries / E. Coli / Midas' Touch / Mom's Heels / Serpent's Kiss / The Virus: On-touch effects won't activate while Dark Arts is active.

• The effects will safely activate if Isaac is touching an enemy when he reappears, as there are a few frames where he is immune to damage but can still collide with enemies.

• Blood Oath: Using Dark Arts will block the damage, preventing Blood Oath from activating.

• Gnawed Leaf: If Isaac is stationary when Dark Arts ends, he will gain invulnerability without any downtime. Dark Arts can also be used from invulnerability without taking damage.

• How to Jump: Can be used while Dark Arts is active.

• Kamikaze!: Can be activated without harm while using Dark Arts.

• Lil Clot / Sumptorium: Clots gain increased speed and are no longer able to fire, but are still vulnerable to damage while Isaac is using Dark Arts.

• Mars: Isaac is able to dash while using Dark Arts.

• Tainted Forgotten: Tainted Soul will gain the speed increase, but the invulnerability & attack portion of the activation will only apply to Tainted Forgotten.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item is a reference to a flash game Edmund McMillen created in 2005 called Grey-Matter. In this game, enemies would be killed in a fashion identical to Dark Arts.

• Before being added in game, Dark Arts was the starting item for Black Judas in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls, a card game created by Edmund McMillen.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using Dark Arts after using Doctor's Remote before the missile hits the ground will trap Isaac in the animation of holding the remote over his head until leaving the room or getting hit, preventing you from firing tears.
Bug note: If tagged during a dash attack, certain enemies and bosses will "dash" without actually moving after Dark Arts end. This is most notable for The Cage - the boss will roll in place for a couple of seconds. If such an enemy gains momentum in any way (e. g. via collision with other enemies, explosions, or knockback from Isaac's tears), it will resume the dash.

fields.description: Briefly grants +1 speed and makes Isaac invulnerable and intangible. When the effect ends, destroys all projectiles and damages all enemies Isaac passed through.

Dark Bum.title: Dark Bum
Dark Bum.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and collects Red Hearts. For every one-and-a-half Red Hearts collected, Dark Bum will generate one of the following:

• [Before Repentance] A single Soul Heart.

• [Repentance] A single Black Heart.

• A hostile Spider.

• A friendly Blue Spider.

• [Repentance] A random pill, card, or rune.

• Contributes to the Super Bum transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Dark Bum enters one of a set of Super Secret Rooms which allow only certain types of hearts to generate in them, he will drop that type of heart instead of what he normally would.

• The one which only allows Red Hearts will cause Dark Bum to consume the Red Hearts on the floor only to generate yet more Red Hearts. Leading Dark Bum around the room to consume the Red Hearts and then leaving the room before he's able to generate anything will avoid this.

• [Afterbirth onward] Dark Bum will only pick up regular Red Hearts (Half Red Hearts, Red Hearts, Double Hearts, Scared Hearts). [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Temporary hearts (such as from Tainted Magdalene, Tainted Eve with Birthright, etc.) can be collected by Dark Bum, which situationally may prove useful or dangerous. [end edition note] 

• This item is very beneficial for characters that can't have Red Heart containers (???, Tainted ???, Black Judas, Tainted Judas, Tainted Forgotten) since they have no use for Red Hearts.

• Alternatively, characters that can't obtain Soul Hearts or Black Hearts for health may gain very little to no advantage from Dark Bum or may even be harmed if they're unable to pick up the Red Hearts before the Bum consumes them.

• Keeper and Tainted Keeper generally have no use for the Dark Bum since all hearts are converted to Blue Flies.

• This is averted if Keeper is in a co-op party with other characters that can utilize hearts.

• Dark Bum may also be picked up by Keeper for the potential transformation.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Scared Hearts will run away from Dark Bum. Pinching them between Dark Bum and Isaac or walls/corners will make them easier for the Bum to collect. [end edition note] 

• [edition anr] From a scoring perspective, hearts that Dark Bum picks up count towards your Schwag bonus on daily runs.

• Dark Bum does not join the line of familiars that follow behind Isaac.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Humbleing Bundle / Equality!: Most Red Heart drops will become Double Red Heart drops. This counts as two full Red Hearts for Dark Bum, essentially doubling the value of it.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: No effect, but familiar is bigger.

• Dark Bum / Cambion Conception: Each Dark Bum tracks the collected hearts separately.

• King Baby / RC Remote: No effect.

• Options?: If one of the options is a Red Heart variant, Dark Bum may collect it, making the other option disappear.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is the Devil Beggar counterpart of Bum Friend and Key Bum.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Activating Glowing Hourglass twice after Dark Bum picked up Red Hearts and before he finishes his animation will save his Red Heart pick up progress while the Red Hearts will stay untouched in the room.

fields.quote: He wants to take your life
fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and collects Red Hearts. For every 1½ Red Hearts collected, Dark Bum will give a reward.

Dark Matter.title: Dark Matter
Dark Matter.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 damage.

• Adds a chance to shoot fear tears, causing enemies to run away from Isaac.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Dark One. [end edition note] 

• Fear tear effect depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 3 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.1 \right \rfloor}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 33.33%, maxing out at 100% at 20 luck.

• This makes Dark Matter significantly better at inflicting fear than Abaddon or Mom's Perfume.

• [Repentance+] Dark Matter's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brimstone: Laser applies fear to enemies more consistently due to its tick rate.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: Chance for tears and split tears to cause fear. If the main tear causes fear, the split tears cause fear too.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Haemolacria: Tear appearance stays the same; only the main tear can cause fear.

• Lachryphagy: If a fear tear is fed, all burst tears cause fear. If a normal tear is fed, the burst tears cannot cause fear.

• The Ludovico Technique: Tear occasionally changes appearance to Dark Matter tears and causes fear.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Darkness Falls.

• Dark Matter is a hypothetical form of matter that is thought to account for over 80% of all the matter in the universe. In media, dark matter is often portrayed as an evil element or demonic power, which explains why this item is found in Devil Rooms.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Fear shot; Repentance: DMG up + fear shot]
fields.description: +1 damage, adds a chance to shoot fear tears.

Dark One.title: Dark One
Dark One.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Dark One is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 2 (Caves, Catacombs, Flooded Caves).

• [Repentance] Only in the Catacombs.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Sends out a ring of 12 projectiles.

• If Isaac is below him, fires a Brimstone laser downwards.

• Charges twice across the screen, veering slowly towards Isaac while charging. When going off-screen, he reappears from the opposite end of the screen. Dark One will do this attack more often if Isaac moves to one of his sides.

• Dims the room, causing the [curse: darkness] effect for a period of time.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: [plat: 3DS] If Dark One dims the room, pause the game and the dim will eventually go away while still in the pause screen.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Adversary is the posthumous version of him.

• [Repentance] One of Dark One's horns is cut off during his death animation, signifying his transformation into The Adversary.

• • The sprite can flip horizontally, making it look like the Dark One lost his right horn, even though the Adversary's left horn is broken

• Dark One is one of the three bosses that can dim the room (a temporary [curse: darkness] effect). The other bosses are The Adversary and The Lamb.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Upon entering the room, if the player goes toward the bottom-center of the screen and The Dark One uses his dashing attack, there is a chance that The Dark One will freeze on his dashing frame and remain in the same state for the remainder of the fight. This bug has been observed when entering from both the left and right sides of the screen.
