Dark Prince's Crown.title: Dark Prince's Crown
Dark Prince's Crown.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When at exactly 1 Red Heart, some of Isaac's stats are increased.

• [Before Repentance] +0.75 tears.

• [Repentance] +2.0 fire rate. The bonus can break the soft tears cap.

• +1.5 range.

• [Before Repentance] +1 tear falling speed.

• +0.2 shot speed.

• The effect is lost any time Isaac gains or loses Red Hearts.

• The crown will glow red while active; if inactive, it will appear black.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Full Bone Heart containers are counted towards the maximum.

• Rotten Hearts count as Red Hearts.

• This item pairs well with Eve, since she starts with Whore of Babylon, and is the only character that can gain Whore of Babylon's effect at 1 heart.

• This item does not affect ???, The Lost, The Soul, [Repentance] Black Judas, Tainted Judas, Tainted ???, Tainted Lost, Tainted Soul, or Tainted Bethany since they cannot gain Red Hearts.

• This item only affects Keeper and Tainted Keeper when he has only one Coin Heart.

• This item only affects The Forgotten when he has one full Bone Heart.

• The effect does not stack with multiple Dark Prince's Crowns.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is the first Afterbirth+ item by ID number.

• This is the demonic counterpart of the Crown Of Light.

• Prior to Repentance, the item's name was Dark Princes Crown, without an apostrophe.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] When at exactly one Red Heart, +0.75 tears, +1.5 range, and +0.2 shot speed.
[Repentance] When at exactly one Red Heart, +2 fire rate, +1.5 range, and +0.2 shot speed.

Dataminer.title: Dataminer
Dataminer.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, rotates every enemy and pickup 90 degrees and moves its sprite up and left for the current room.

• Enemy hitboxes remain the same.

• Increases one of Isaac's stats and decreases another. Possible stat changes include:

• ± 1 flat damage

• [Before Repentance] ±0.5 tears

• [Repentance] ±0.5 fire rate

• ±0.2 speed

• • [Before Repentance] Also affects maximum speed (may never exceed 2.0)

• ±0.2 shot speed

• ±1 luck

• [Before Repentance] ±0.5 range

• [Repentance] ±2.5 range

• Adds random tear effects for the current room.

• Distorts the music for the current room.

• [Repentance+] Rerolls any item in the room to a glitched TMTRAINER item. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a special wisp on the middle ring that is otherwise undistinguishable from a normal wisp. These wisps' tears have a 5% chance of transforming any non-boss enemy into random wisps.

• Rock Bottom: The stats are locked to the highest number achieved, though the lowered stat will still be more difficult to increase.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] If the tears stat reaches a negative number, there will be a wrap-around into the maximum fire rate of 120; if the tears stat is boosted back into a positive number, fire rate will again become low.

• If Rock Bottom is obtained while the tears stat is negative, fire rate will stay at 120 even if boosts are obtained.

• The minimum values for each stat are as follows:

• Damage: 0.5

• Speed: 0.1

• Shot Speed: 0.6

• Range: 1.0

• Further changes to Isaac's stats are still calculated normally behind the scenes, but their effective values cannot go below the minimum. For example, 0.5 Shot Speed will behave as though it were 0.6, but a 0.2 Shot Speed increase would apply to the true stat value of 0.5, meaning the new stat value would be 0.7.

• [Repentance] Using Dataminer during the fight against The Beast is not recommended, as it will distort the stalagmites and stalactites, causing them to be incredibly difficult to dodge. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item name and description are a likely reference to the dataminers who discovered the secret of The Lost, as well as the Keeper ARG's recurring usage of the number 109.

• The item and its pickaxe icon are a play on words on the term data mining, used in the context of gaming communities as extracting data from the game files.

• The item's sprite is a recolor and flipped version of the Notched Axe.

• If used during the Mom fight, a normally hidden part of the leg sprite, revealing a blue skirt with yellow polka dots, will be visible.

• If Dataminer is used right before traveling to the next floor, the music for the transition screen will be affected by it.

• Also affects the music during the Game Over screen (Isaac's last will), if activated before death.

• In a Q&A from Twitter, Edmund McMillen considered Dataminer to be the worst item in The Binding of Isaac.

fields.description: Displaces enemy sprites for the current room and randomly increases one of Isaac's stats while decreasing another. [Repentance+] Turns all items in the room into glitched items with random effects.

Dice Bag.title: Dice Bag
Dice Bag.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Has a 50% chance to give Isaac a one-time use Dice item in a consumable slot when he enters a new room. The dice disappears when he leaves the room, and cannot be dropped.

• This doesn't replace any consumables Isaac already has.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If Isaac leaves and re-enters a room, Dice Bag will not try to give another die when Isaac re-enters it.

• The dice given are determined by the amount of rooms cleared, and are not actually tied to specific rooms.

• This is the opposite of how Modeling Clay works.

• Any die can be given to Isaac, including ones that haven't been unlocked yet.

• Dice Bag cannot give Spindown Dice, D infinity, Cracked Dice, or Dice Shard.

• Dropping the trinket on the ground does not remove dice until Isaac leaves the room.

• This means that the D1 can always be used on the Dice Bag to spawn another trinket.

• If a D4 or D100 die is used, it won't reroll your active item. This is likely because the code for the dice consumable was directly copied from the items themselves, and because the D4 and D100 doesn't reroll your active item (themselves), neither can the dice consumables.

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• Be cautious when carrying cards and/or pills. The die given by Dice Bag will always be first in the consumable queue, so one unaware press of the "use consumable" button can lead to Isaac's build getting fully rerolled.

• Cards, pills, and runes/soul stones can be held until Dice Bag gives a D1 to get a chance at an extra copy of them.

• Cards/items that can spawn items when used (such as XX - Judgement or Mystery Gift) can be held until Dice Bag gives an (Eternal) D6 to reroll the items they give before the die goes away.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: The chance to get a die increases to 100%.

• Book of Virtues: Creates wisps as if the equivalent active item was used.

• Glowing Hourglass: The die given in the room Isaac used Glowing Hourglass in will be granted in the next new room Isaac visits, regardless of what it is. This can be strategically used to get a D6 or Eternal D6 at the optimal moment.

• Moving Box: Can be used to hold undesirable items and pickups until Dice Bag grants a consumable that can reroll them.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• When Dice Bag gives Isaac a die, it can actually be seen in the list of items in the Pause menu, meaning that Dice Bag grants items, not consumables.

• Therefore Dice Bag will add dices in the collection if you have not picked them up before or even unlocked them.

• This trinket resembles a bag from Crown Royal, a popular brand of liquor that comes in a purple sack. In real life, these bags are commonly used as dice bags due to their availability.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Jacob and Esau: Regardless of who is holding the die, it is activated by pressing the consumable key. If Esau is holding an active item, it will be used at the same time as the die. Possibly unintended behavior.

fields.description: When Isaac enters a new room, has a chance to give him a Dice item as a consumable for the current room.

Dice Shard.title: Dice Shard
Dice Shard.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Dice Shard is a consumable item added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Upon use, it:

• rerolls all pedestal items in the room (like The D6)

• rerolls all pickups and trinkets in the room (like the D20)

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Despite it not being a card, the Dice Shard is considered a special card, so it has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• [Before Repentance] Similarly to runes, this item counts as a card and can be used with Blank Card.

• [Repentance] This item cannot be mimicked by either Blank Card or Clear Rune, and Tarot Cloth has no effect on it. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Dice Shard's ID was changed from 44 to 49.

• [Repentance+] Dice Shard can sometimes spawn within the special bedroom created by Lil Portal.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item's appearance is similar to The D6, but broken in half.

• [Repentance] Dice Shard is similar to Cracked Key in that they are both one-use broken versions of an active item. However, Dice Shard has an additional effect that The D6 lacks while Cracked Key simply replicates the use of Red Key. [end edition note] 

• Despite being a dice item, Dice Shard is not an unlock.

• This trait is shared with D10 and D7.

fields.description: Upon use, invokes the effects of The D6 and the D20 at the same time, rerolling all item pedestals and pickups in the room.

Dim Bulb.title: Dim Bulb
Dim Bulb.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Increases all stats while Isaac's active item is completely uncharged:

• +0.50 speed.

• +1.50 range.

• [Before Repentance] +1.00 tear falling speed

• [Before Repentance] +0.40 tears.

• [Repentance] +0.50 tears.

• +0.30 shot speed.

• +1.5 damage.

• +2 luck.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Dim Bulb is more than twice as powerful as Vibrant Bulb; however, its effects are active less frequently.

• However, 1 room charge items can be used at the start of each room to effectively get the Dim Bulb's effects constantly.

• Items that charge automatically will get only a tiny moment of benefit from the Dim Bulb before they gain more charge again.

• [Before Repentance] Items with no charge bar like How to Jump will activate Dim Bulb's effects permanently as long as the item is held.

• Dim Bulb has no effect when no active item is held.

• If Isaac has 2 items (via Schoolbag), [Before Repentance+] both of them need to be empty to receive the benefits / [Repentance+] only the currently held item needs to be empty to receive the benefits.

• [Before Repentance] However, if one of the two active items has no charge bar (e.g. Remote Detonator), it can be swapped to, preserving the Bulb's effect.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 4.5 Volt: Dim Bulb will be active for as long as the active item has less than one bar of charge.

• Bethany / Tainted Bethany: The effect remains active with both soul and blood charges.

• If the active item is fully charged only with soul/blood charges and no regular charges, Vibrant Bulb can be active simultaneously with Dim Bulb.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either doubles the stat increases. Having both triples them.

• Old Capacitor: As long as the active item uses charges, Dim Bulb can be held active indefinitely.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 9 Volt: Renders Dim Bulb useless, save for 1 charge items.

• [Repentance] Dim Bulb produces no effect with active items in consumable slots, such as Tainted Apollyon's Abyss, Tainted Bethany's Lemegeton or Tainted Magdalene's Yum Heart.

fields.description: Provides a boost to all stats when Isaac's active item is completely uncharged.

Dingle.title: Dingle
Dingle.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Dingle is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] Only in the Basement.

• [Repentance] In the Basement and the Burning Basement. [end edition note] 
He is the boss version of the Dips.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Dingle remains stationary and performs the following attacks:

• Fires 3 projectiles towards Isaac.

• Whistles before summoning 1-3 Dips and then fires 3 projectiles at Isaac.

• Quickly performs 3 long dashes towards Isaac while bouncing off obstacles and walls, after which he pauses to catch his breath.

• Dips caught in his dashes are knocked back a distance.

• Occasionally, Dingle will leave behind a Poop while using this attack.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 18] : Dingle summons Spiders instead of Dips and fires eight shots in all directions instead of spitting three at Isaac. He also dashes much faster, but will only dash one time instead of three.
[bc: 1] : Dingle creates a Red Poop instead of summoning Dips. He also dashes four times instead of three, though the dashes are shorter and slower. [Repentance] He also fires blood projectiles instead of poop projectiles, though this is a purely cosmetic effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Flush! kills Dingle instantly and causes him to leave behind 6 Dips.

• If a Bomb from Butt Bombs goes off in the same room as Dingle, it will heal him. [Afterbirth onward] This is especially bad if Isaac happens to have No. 2, which causes him to drop butt bombs while firing tears. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Butt Bombs fired by Dr. Fetus and Epic Fetus do not heal Dingle.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] Dangle and Brownie are related to Dingle. [end edition note] 

• The name 'Dingle' derives from the crude term, "dingleberry".

• Dingle was the first new boss to be shown by Edmund.

• Dingle is referred to as male by Edmund.

• There are three other poop monsters: Dinga, Squirt, and Dip.

• [Afterbirth onward] Two more poop monsters (Corn and Dank Squirt) and three poop bosses (Brownie, Dangle, and the Turdlings) were added. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Four more poop monsters (Big Corn, Drip, Splurt, and Hardy) and three poop bosses (Clog, Colostomia, and Turdlet) were added. [end edition note] 

• The Black Champion Version of Dingle acts slightly similar to the Dank Squirt and appears to be a "dank" or meconium version of Dingle.

• [Repentance] Prior to Repentance, all versions of Dingle could fire blood projectiles instead of just the Red Champion variant.

Dingle Berry.title: Dingle Berry
Dingle Berry.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a random friendly Dip upon clearing a room.

• Spawns a random friendly Dip upon starting a new wave in Greed Mode.

• Turns enemy Dips into friendly Dips, similar to Dirty Mind.

• Dips come in Poops variants rather than Dip variants. Golden variants drop coins on being damaged and can turn enemies into gold. Red variants do extra damage. Rainbow variants turn into a heart upon death. White variants are harder to kill. Black and Corny variants have had no extra visible effects.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket/Mom's Box: Grants 1 extra dip per copy. Also, dip enemies become friendly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Dingle Berry might be a reference to Dingle, as both are poop themed and Dingle's name is thought to come from the word "dingleberry", which means a small ball of feces clinging to an animal.

fields.description: Spawns a Dip Familiar upon clearing a room.

Dinner.title: Dinner
Dinner.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one full Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • This item has a 12.6% chance to spawn from paying out a Beggar in addition to being in the Beggar item pool. Multiple copies can be obtained through this method.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Binge Eater: When Isaac picks up Dinner it now grants: a permanent +0.5 Tears and +0.2 Shot Speed, a temporary +3.6 Damage (which diminishes to 0 in 30 seconds), heals 1 additional red heart, and takes a permanent -0.03 Speed reduction.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance] Dinner’s sprites can be seen as part of Binge Eater. [end edition note]

fields.description: Grants one full Red Heart container. [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

Diplopia.title: Diplopia
Diplopia.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Instantly spawns a copy of all pickups and pedestal items on the floor in the current room, then disappears.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If used in a room with anything that has a cost to obtain, including a Shop, Devil Room or the Black Market, the duplicated items and pickups will spawn without a cost attached and can be taken for free. 

• The original items will remain unchanged, and Deal with the Devil precedent will not be set by collecting the free copies. 

• If an item pedestal that is duplicated is visible as "?" (for example with the [cu: Blind] ), duplicate will be visible as "?" until taken, just like the original item pedestal.

• Diplopia cannot be copied with another copy of Diplopia or any duplication that mimics the effect. Other forms of item duplication, such as Crooked Penny work as normal. 

• [Before Repentance] Using Diplopia on a trinket will spawn another random trinket instead of duplicating the trinket.

• [Repentance] Using Diplopia on a trinket does nothing.

• [Repentance] Does not duplicate Jera.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Using Diplopia on an empty item pedestal will spawn another random item.

• [Before Repentance] Picking up multiple copies of items that can cause Isaac to transform will not count towards transformation progress.

• [Repentance] Multiple copies of the same item do count towards transformations.

• [Before Repentance] If Diplopia is used in a room that offers a choice between multiple items, all of the duplicated items can be taken. The original items will still behave as normal: once an item is chosen, the others will disappear, but the duplicates will remain. This also includes Boss Rush (though taking any duplicate will still start the Boss Rush)

• [Repentance] Only one duplicate can be taken. This affects Treasure Room on the alternate path, Angel Room that has multiple item pedestals, the The Polaroid and The Negative after defeating Mom, the item More Options, Boss Rush, etc.

• Jacob and Esau can use this item to duplicate an active item to each have the same active item.

• Tear-boosting items, if stacked, cap at shooting 16 tears at once.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Most passive item stats bonuses stack normally when duplicated. 

• Active item copies do not share charges, and appear with a full charge (unless the item normally spawns empty of charges). 

• 20/20: Isaac fires 3 tightly-packed tears with no increase in tear delay.

• [Repentance] Damage down does not stack.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a special Diplopia wisp on the middle ring. The wisp fires two tears at a time (similar to 20/20) and has very high HP. Also duplicates all of Isaac's other wisps.

• Additional copies of Book of Virtues do not have any effect. 

• Brimstone: Isaac fires two lasers simultaneously.

• [Repentance] Isaac gains a powered-up version of Brimstone with a unique costume that deals 1.2x damage and has +1 damage. Further copies will add another +1 damage.

• Contract From Below: Triples the drops upon clearing a room.

• Damocles: Spawns an extra item for each item cloned.

• Dr. Fetus: Isaac fires two bombs simultaneously.

• Eden's Blessing: Tears upgrades stack and Isaac gains two items at the start of the next run. Stacks up to [Before Repentance+] 10 / [Repentance+] 2 times.

• Epic Fetus: Two missiles drop, one after the other.

• The Inner Eye: Isaac fires 6 tears. Tears down stat does not stack.

• [Repentance] Isaac fires an additional tear. Tears down stat does not stack.

• The Ludovico Technique: A smaller tear orbits the main tear.

• Maw Of The Void: Increased damage for tears and ring.

• Mom's Knife: Isaac fires two knives simultaneously.

• Monstro's Lung: The tear burst gains another [Before Repentance] 10 tears/ [Repentance] 12 tears, nearly doubling in size. Stacks up to 4 times.

• Mutant Spider: Isaac fires 8 tears. Tears down stat does not stack.

• [Repentance] Isaac fires 2 additional tears. Tear down stat does not stack.

• The Relic: An extra soul heart is given for each relic familiar.

• Schoolbag + any active item: While there is no use in duplicating the Schoolbag, it gives Isaac a use for duplicating an active item.

• Steam Sale: All items in Shops become free. With Restock, items can be infinitely bought for free.

• [Repentance] Each additional Steam Sale will further halve the price. Items cannot be reduced below 1 cent.

• Technology: Isaac fires two lasers simultaneously.

• Tech X: Isaac fires two laser rings simultaneously.

• Twisted Pair: Adds two more familiars that float further away from either side of Isaac.

• Wild Card: Allows infinite uses of Diplopia. This can be done by dropping the card, using Diplopia, then picking up the copied card and using it. This results in everything in the room being copied, including the first wild card. This can be repeated infinitely as long as Diplopia was the last item used.

• The Wiz: Isaac fires 4 tears diagonally.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Isaac fires 3 tears, one straight ahead and two diagonally.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• ? Card: Expends both the card and the item with no additional benefit.

• [Repentance] Now expends the card without consuming Diplopia, allowing for potential multiple uses.

• • If 2 ? Cards are gathered in the same room, one can be used to duplicate the other, allowing for infinite duplication of everything else in that room.

• • If 3 ? Cards are gathered in the same room, one of them can be used to duplicate infinite ? Cards as well.

• Compound Fracture: Range increases twice. No effect on how many bone tears are fired or how many bone shards are fired.

• Continuum: Only increases range further.

• Cricket's Head: Damage multiplier doesn't stack.

• Crown Of Light: Only further decreases shot speed and increases range.

• Dead Eye: The damage multiplier increases twice as fast, but still caps at double damage.

• Eden's Soul / Alabaster Box: All copies of these items starts with no charge.

• Eve's Mascara: The damage and tear multipliers do not stack. The shot speed does stack.

• Eye of Belial: Only further increases range.

• Finger!: Spawns two familiars completely overlapping each other.

• Godhead: Only stat ups and downs compound, but the aura gains no bonus.

• Guillotine: Isaac will have two orbital heads, but only one will fire tears.

• Holy Mantle: An extra effect is added in the room it was found in, but only a single effect will be given in future rooms.

• Iron Bar: Increases damage but not chance of concussive tears being fired.

• Key Piece 1, Key Piece 2: Spawns a copy of the same Key Piece. The copy does not increase the chance for an Angel Room.

• Kidney Stone: Only further decreases speed.

• Little Baggy / Polydactyly / Starter Deck / Deep Pockets: Does not allow more than two pills or cards to be held at once.

• Lost Contact: Only further decreases shot speed.

• Magic Mushroom: Increases all stats twice, but damage significantly less the second time as the 1.5x multipliers do not stack.

• Marked: Only increases range and firerate.

• Mom's Contacts: Only increases range.

• Mom's Purse / Belly Button: Does not allow more than two trinkets to be held at once.

• My Reflection: Only increases range.

• Piggy Bank: Only grants 3 more coins. Does not drop more pennies when taking damage.

• Placenta: Only increases HP with no change to the regeneration effect.

• Pointy Rib: Spawns two familiars that completely overlap each other.

• Purity: No effect. Aura changes after a second pickup.

• Quints: Increases maximum familiar count by 5.

• Revelation: Only adds soul hearts with no addition effect on the beam.

• Sacred Heart: Further decreases tears and shot speed with no increase in damage.

• Stop Watch: Further increases speed with no further effect on movement speed or shot speed of enemies.

• Sulfuric Acid: Only further increases damage.

• Tractor Beam: Further increases shot speed, fire rate, and range with no other effects.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This is the first Afterbirth item by ID number.

• Diplopia is the simultaneous perception of two images of a single object, commonly referred to as double vision.

• This item's appearance is similar to Pupula Duplex.

fields.description: Duplicates all pickups and item pedestals in the current room.

Dirty Mind.title: Dirty Mind
Dirty Mind.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Converts all enemy Dips and Drips into Dip Familiars.

• Rocks have a chance to be replaced with poop when generated.

• The formula to calculate the chance is: \mathit{Chance} = \mathit{Luck} \times 0.5 + 6.25, capped at 10% at 7.5 Luck.

• Destroying Poops spawn 1-4 Dip Familiars, which loosely follow Isaac around, block enemy shots, and deal contact damage to enemies.

• Dips deal contact damage to enemies equal to the damage Isaac had at the time it spawned, and can deal up to 2 ticks of contact damage and/or block 2 shots before dying.

• Destroying different types of poop will spawn special Dips:

• Corny Poops create Corny Dips that spawn 1 Blue Fly on death.

• • Brownie Dips spawned by Brownie and Dangle have the same behavior.

• Red Poops create Red Dips that deal twice as much damage and autonomously charge at enemies, but automatically die after 15 seconds.

• Golden Poops create Gold Dips that have a chance to inflict the Midas' Touch effect on enemies they hit. They can also take 5 hits before being destroyed, at which point they will drop 2-3 random coins.

• Rainbow Poops create Rainbow Dips that charm enemies they hit and have a chance to drop a Half Red Heart on death.

• Black Poops create Black Dips that leave a trail of slowing creep.

• White Poops create White Dips that recreate the effect of Hallowed Ground and can take 3 hits before being destroyed.

• Poops unique to Tainted ??? and IBS also spawn Dips with special effects:

• Stone Poops create Rock Dips that deal an additional 3.5 damage per hit and can take 6 hits before dying instead of 2.

• Stinky Poops create Stinky Dips that release toxic gas as they move and a larger cloud of toxic gas when they die.

• • The toxic gas does 0.5x Isaac's damage per tick (~1.2x Isaac's damage per second) and poisons enemies; clouds left behind while alive last 1.5 seconds and the cloud created on death lasts 8 seconds.

• Fire Poops create Flaming Dips that burn enemies they hit and leave behind a fire when they die.

• • The burn deals 3.5 damage up to 6 times, and the fire deals 8 damage at full durability, 6 after taking 1 hit, and 4 otherwise, for a maximum of 22 damage.

• Contributes to the Oh Crap transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Brownie. [end edition note] 

• The familiars are destroyed by Bombs, making them very easy to destroy when trying to blow up walls or rocks.

• Familiars remain if this item is lost (re-rolled, etc.).

• Enemies that charge towards Isaac, such as Gurdy Jr., can deflect off of friendly Dips in unpredictable directions.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Doubles damage dealt and halves damage taken by Dips, as well as increasing their size.

• Butt Penny: Grants a chance to spawn a Dip each time a coin is picked up.

• A Card Against Humanity: Allows Isaac to obtain a large number of Dips.

• E. Coli / Flush!: Poops generated by these items spawn double the normal amount of Dips.

• Mom's Bracelet: Friendly Dips can be picked up and thrown.

• Mysterious Candy: Allows a steady supply of Dips, with time. Useful for later chapters.

• The Poop: Allows generation of extra Dips after every room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Compost: Compost does not multiply Dips.

• Sacrificial Altar: All Dips are sacrificed and a coin is spawned for each Dip sacrificed. The Dips do not count towards the 2 familiar limit of Sacrificial Altar.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Dirty Mind is from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, Dirty Mind could also turn Angel and Devil statues into poop.

• This item is used in Scat Man.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again) will duplicate Dip Familiars.

fields.description: Destroying poop spawns Dip Familiars that follow Isaac and damage enemies. Destroying different types of poop spawns different Dips with special effects.

Distant Admiration.title: Distant Admiration
Distant Admiration.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a red attack fly that circles around Isaac, and deals 5 damage per tick or 75 damage per second on contact.

• The fly circles farther out than regular orbitals, but closer than Forever alone.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • While most orbital familiars orbit Isaac counter-clockwise, Distant Admiration orbits clockwise. It shares this orbit ring, speed, and pattern with Bot Fly.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Solar System.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, this item had the same instant-kill property on contact with Fly and Pooter variants that an item like Halo of Flies has. This effect is removed in Rebirth.

fields.description: Spawns an attack fly that circles further out than Halo of Flies, but closer than Forever alone, dealing 75 damage per second.

Divine Intervention.title: Divine Intervention
Divine Intervention.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Double tapping a fire key creates a Divine Shield that slowly moves in the chosen direction.

• The Divine Shield has a variety of effects.

• Enemies are pushed back in the opposite direction, completely reversing their trajectory with some added momentum.

• • Enemies pushed into walls or obstacles take 10 + 2 * (floor - 1) damage and deal that same damage to other enemies they collide with.

• Enemy tears are reflected, dealing damage back to enemies depending on the source of the tear.

• • The reflected projectiles deal 6 damage if they would've hurt Isaac for half a heart, and 7 for a full heart.

• • Reflected projectiles do not gain Tear effects from Isaac.

• • 
• Explosive projectiles (e.g. from Gurgle) explode as normal, dealing as much damage as they would have.

• • 
• Projectiles that create other projectiles (e.g. Shady) can harm Isaac and be reflected.

• • 
• Homing projectiles (e.g. from Psychic Horf) do not retain their homing effect after being reflected.

• • Can reflect:

• • 
• Fire projectiles (e.g. from Mega Satan).

• • 
• Obstacles thrown by Polty or Kineti, dealing a flat 35 damage.

• • Does not reflect:

• • 
• Lines of fire (e.g. from Dragon Fly), but can reflect fireballs (e.g. from Crackle) and their lines of fire do not harm Isaac.

• • 
• Projectiles from Big Bony, Coal Boy, Danny.

• Enemy Brimstone lasers are reflected, dealing 7 damage per tick (105 damage per second) to enemies hit by the reflection. It can even deflect the colossal brimstone laser fired by The Beast.

• • White beams, such as those used by Dogma in its second phase, are reflected into Revelation beams.

• The shield lasts 1 second and has a cooldown of 3 seconds.

• Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If any charged item is obtained along with Divine Intervention e.g. Brimstone or Revelation, a different fire key may be pressed to put out the shield without forfeiting the charge of said item.

• The Blindfolded status from certain challenges disables the ability to fire, which also disables the ability to double tap to fire Divine Shields.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Divine Intervention: Multiple copies of this item (from effects such as Diplopia or Crooked Penny) have no effect aside from being counted for Seraphim.

fields.description: Double tapping a fire key creates a shield that pushes away enemies and reflects enemy projectiles and lasers.

Divorce Papers.title: Divorce Papers
Divorce Papers.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants one Bone Heart.

• +0.7 tears.

• Spawns Mysterious Paper if it has been unlocked and not previously encountered during the run.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The existence of this item suggests that the way Isaac’s father left his Mom as seen in Chest's ending (Ending 14) could have been through a divorce.

• A more detailed rendition of Divorce Papers can be found in The Binding of Isaac: Four Souls Card Game. The papers are signed by Isaac's mother, but not his father, implying that a divorce was filed but the process was left incomplete.

• • [Repentance] The details of the split can be discerned via the dialogue that plays during Ascent, as well as Ending 22.

fields.description: Grants one Bone Heart, +0.7 tears, spawns a Mysterious Paper.

Doctor's Remote.title: Doctor's Remote
Doctor's Remote.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon activation, a large red crosshair will appear on the ground. The crosshair can be moved using tear controls.

• After approximately 2 seconds, a large missile will land on the red marker. The missile acts like a large bomb explosion, dealing 20 times Isaac's damage (the same as Epic Fetus).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The red marker works different from Epic Fetus' marker when controlled with the mouse: While pressing mouse left button, it keeps going away from Isaac, not following the mouse.

• Activating the item again while the crosshair is on the ground will cancel the animation of Isaac holding up the remote and allow him to shoot tears sooner.

• Activating the item again while having full charge (e.g. with The Battery) will also deplete the charge, wasting it.

• [Before Repentance] Taking damage also cancels the animation.

• [Before Repentance] The missile will still drop on the crosshair, which can no longer be controlled.

• [Repentance] This will cancel the missile drop and remove the crosshair.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• This item shares many of the synergies and interactions with Epic Fetus.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns grey bomb-like wisps in the middle ring. When Doctor's Remote is used, the wisps fire two inaccurate, explosive tears at the crosshair in an arc that deal 14 damage (28 with BFFS!).

• Car Battery: Drops an additional missile after the first one.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Tainted Azazel: Shoots thin Brimstone beams when rocket explodes. This behavior is not shared with Epic Fetus, which produces no brimstone lasers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to the remote Dr. Fetus uses several times throughout Super Meat Boy.

• Epic Fetus is the endless version of this Item and, as such, uses the same attack animation.

• The sprite of this item is identical to Teleport! and Teleport 2.0, but with a different color.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, this item was used in the challenge "The Doctor's Revenge".

fields.description: Creates a crosshair on the ground that can be aimed with tear controls. A missile strikes the spot after 2 seconds, creating a heavy damage explosion.

Dog Tooth.title: Dog Tooth
Dog Tooth.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.3 damage.

• +0.1 speed.

• [Before Repentance] Also affects maximum speed (may never exceed 2.0).

• When entering a room connected to an undiscovered Secret Room or Super Secret Room, a howl sound effect will play.

• A barking sound will play if there is an undiscovered Crawl Space in the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• A sound won't play in the first room of a new floor until you re-enter the room.

• An extra Crawl Space added by Stud Finder will not trigger the sound.

sections.heading: Sounds
Trivia
sections.text:
• The pickup quote appears to refer to the way the game associates Moon with secrets, with XVIII - The Moon teleporting to secret rooms and Fragmented Card being a torn Moon card that spawns extra secret rooms.

• "Bark at the moon!" could also be a reference to the song and album made by Ozzy Osbourne.

fields.description: +0.3 damage, +0.1 speed. Plays a howl or bark sound when entering a room with undiscovered Secret Rooms or Crawl Spaces.

Dogma.title: Dogma
Dogma.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the boss; the item; Dogma (Item)] 

Dogma is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance and is the first boss of Home.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
In its first phase, Dogma is attached to a television. Damage can only be dealt to Dogma by damaging the television in the center of the room. Any attacks towards Dogma itself causes a shield to briefly appear and block the attack. Dogma moves slowly towards Isaac, leaving a trail of damaging Static Creep and has a variety of attacks:

• Fires three consecutive radial bursts of 8 Godhead projectiles. If Isaac stands within the projectiles' auras for long enough, a Crack the Sky beam hits Isaac from above.

• Fires four consecutive bursts of projectiles in groups of 1, 2, 3, and 4 in each of the cardinal directions, with the overall pattern resembling a star.

• Occasionally after firing the 4th burst, Dogma greatly slows down all the projectiles mid-flight, leaving them to float around slowly for a moment before vanishing.

• • Dogma starts using this variant after losing around 60% of its HP, and performs it more frequently the lower its HP is.

• Fires 3 consecutive waves of 3 to 4 projectiles each in random directions. When these projectiles land, it creates thin, harmless rays that point towards Isaac and become damaging lasers after a few seconds.

• Fires a static Brimstone beam that bends towards Isaac. This beam is always fired in the closest cardinal direction to Isaac and switches if Isaac moves closer to a different cardinal direction.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After destroying the television, Dogma falls apart into a puddle of static, before rising out of it as an orb and growing two pairs of wings resembling a Seraph. During this phase, Dogma continues to chase Isaac between attacks, but becomes vulnerable and has completely different attacks:

• Fires a spread of disorganized feather projectiles towards Isaac if he's to its left or right.

• Summons a ball of light overhead which creates 16 to 18 harmless rays of light that point outwards and spin around the ball in random directions. After a few seconds, the rays stop moving and become damaging thin beams, similar to the ones used by the Angels. This pattern is repeated three times, then Dogma throws it, firing one last wave of 8 wider beams in the cardinal and ordinal directions before dissipating.

• If the thrown ball of beams is slowed (by Stop Watch for instance), the 8 beams fire before being properly aligned.

• Turns into a winged wheel resembling an Ophanim and floats off-screen before charging back towards Isaac, continuing off-screen releasing a radial burst with three layers of feather projectiles with 12 feathers each near the end of the dash. It repeats this attack a total of 6 times.

As Dogma takes more and more damage during this phase, its Seraph form will occasionally flicker into various other forms; these include Isaac's head, a lamb's skull with a serpent in its eye, a fly, and a troll face with horns (each of which represents one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse). This is a purely visual effect.

When Dogma's HP reaches zero for the second time, it is destroyed as the whole screen fades to white before turning off like an old TV. Then Isaac is automatically given Dogma as the cutscene that introduces The Beast is played.

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to the players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• After the beginning cutscene, Dogma appears very close to Isaac, making it easy to immediately take damage.

• Having a high speed is highly recommended for the second phase, as the charge attack can be almost unavoidable with low speed.

• Censer makes the second phase more difficult by reducing the space between feathers during Dogma's charging attack while not slowing Dogma itself. It is not recommended for this fight.

• If a Godhead-like projectile is "caught" with Telekinesis, it will be impossible to avoid the projectile's aura. As a result, taking damage is unavoidable.

• As the Dogma room is not counted as a Boss room, effects like Blanket will not occur in this fight.

• If Isaac has triggered the beginning cutscene, re-entering the room by any means (such as being revived outside the room as ??? with Ankh) will trigger the Dogma fight immediately.

• Before beginning the fight, going out and back into the living-room repeatedly while holding a trinket like Liberty Cap guarantees to get the best possible effect sooner or later, which can greatly help during the fight.

• Evil Charm will prevent Isaac from being affected by Dogma's Godhead aura projectile attack in its first phase.

• Any effect that lasts for one room won't remain after the fight and won't carry over to the Ultra Harbingers and The Beast fight.

• Perfection will spawn after defeating Dogma if the correct conditions are met, however, the trinket will be left behind when Isaac arrives to fight the Ultra Harbingers and The Beast.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A "dogma" is most commonly defined as "A set of rules, beliefs, or opinions laid down by a group, the members of which unquestionably follow".

• Dogma's portrayal as a being made of static tied to a television heavily implies that it represents the "Christian broadcasts" that Isaac's mother watches. This is further evidenced by the level transition that plays, showing Isaac watching the broadcasts with his mother.

• Dogma could be interpreted as the Third Beast: The Beast from the Earth. A popular interpretation of this beast is the "False Prophet".

• Dogma's theme is called "Living in the Light", and is taken directly from one of the many Bible quotes heard during the fight's second phase.

• The vocals in "Living in the Light" are performed by Matthias Bossi and Jon Evans.

• The OST version of "Living in the Light" plays unique vocals before playing the vocals from the in-game version.

• The composition of the "Living in the Light" is very similar to Matricide, and shares motifs with tracks Genesis 22:10 and Crusade.

• The vocals from "Living in the Light" can also be heard in the cutscene that plays prior to fighting The Beast.

• The majority of Dogma's sprites are actually blue in the files.

• This is because the blue is used to indicate areas that the game should apply the static effect to. This was likely done to avoid making the sprite file animated, instead simply letting the game apply the effect to designated areas when the time comes to use them. This also results in the static effect being randomized, instead of following a repeating pattern. This same trick is also what the Dogma item uses.

• This is also the case with the flickering eyes in its first phase, which are actually colored green. The flickering itself is done at random every frame in the game's code.

• During Dogma's first phase, a quiet recording of Psalm 23:1-4 can be heard. At the beginning of most of Dogma's attacks, this recording is temporarily made much louder.

• Dogma is one of the two bosses that have a unique health bar, the other one being Great Gideon.

• Dogma is the only boss to have a unique level transition and a unique Versus screen sound.

• If the player uses Lodestone to magnetize Dogma or its TV, the respective sprite will become fuzzy, as if it's having a signal error.

• Salvation will also distort Dogma's sprite while the beam of light is charging.

• The same can be accomplished with Hemoptysis.

• Using XI - Strength? will cause the distortion as well.

• If a player defeats Dogma but dies during the Beast fight on the first time fighting Dogma, a unique save file state will appear, showing a Cross similar to the one in the cutscene between the two bosses.

• [Repentance+] Another way to do this is by defeating the Beast in the Daily Run before doing so in a regular run.

• According to one of the Repentance developers, Dogma's static Brimstone attack is heavily inspired by the "Brimsnapping" bug from the Flash version of the game.

• Dogma has two unused attacks in the games files. One would have summoned an enemy similar to Angelic Baby and the other an effect similar to Black Hole.

• During the Repentance DLC's early development, Isaac was meant to fight a demonic doppelgänger of himself, who would grow larger and stronger from every hit. This boss was scrapped and replaced by Dogma.

• Ridiculon, the composers of Dogma's theme, has stated that one of Dogma's quote can both be heard as "anger" and "angel" of God.

• Edmund McMillen noted that Dogma, along with the Tainted Characters and The Beast sequence, were initially reserved for a possible Isaac sequel.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If the player dies at the same time as killing Dogma's second phase and has extra lives that make him respawn outside of the room, the fight will reset to the start when entering the room again. The static transitioning effect that starts at the end of the fight will remain on the screen after reviving, making it very difficult to see anything during the rematch.
Bug note: If the player has extra lives and dies during a specific frame of the transition cutscene to The Beast (i. e. II - The High Priestess?, Broken Shovel 1 or being in Astral Projection form while having no life), Dogma's room will be cleared and the player will respawn in the previous room, leading to a softlock.

Dogma (Item).title: Dogma (Item)
Dogma (Item).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the item; the boss; Dogma] 
[distinguish visual: The Relic] 

It is automatically given to Isaac after defeating Dogma; the only ways to acquire it on a pedestal are either through the Death Certificate or by using Spindown Dice on Purgatory.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants flight.

• Grants a one-time Holy Mantle-like effect. This effect wears off upon leaving the room.

• Prevents Isaac's speed from going under 1.1.

• +2 damage.

• If Isaac has fewer than six full hearts of health, Isaac is given enough hearts to get to six full hearts, first by restoring empty red heart containers, and then by granting soul hearts if that isn't enough.

• Does not affect The Lost or Tainted Lost normally.

• Keeper and Tainted Keeper's coin heart containers are affected by the red heart healing, but they will gain Blue Flies instead of soul hearts.

• The Forgotten will have all his bone hearts replenished, and any soul hearts earned will go to The Soul.

• Bethany will gain soul charges instead of soul hearts.

• Tainted Lazarus will receive the flight and stat bonuses for both forms. Since defeating Dogma will swap between forms, the active character before the cutscene will not receive the healing and shield effect, which will instead be given to the form present after the cutscene.

• Alabaster Box will take the soul hearts before they're given to Isaac, like normal.

• [mode: normal] On Normal mode, grants The Wafer effect, reducing all damage taken to half a heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• As with all items crucial to story progress (The Polaroid, The Negative, Key Piece 1, Key Piece 2, Knife Piece 1, Knife Piece 2, and Dad's Note), this item:

• Cannot be rerolled once picked up.

• Does not take up an item slot for Tainted Isaac.

• Still grants flight while acquiring Knife Piece 2, as it isn't removed (possible when carried over in a RERUN, using R Key, using Death Certificate, or using Spindown Dice on Purgatory).

• [Before Repentance+] Dogma's Holy Mantle effect does not stack with an actual Holy Mantle, but it does stack with a Holy Card effect.

• [Repentance+] All shield-type items now stack in the following order:

• • Wooden Cross

• • Blanket

• • Holy Mantle

• • Holy Card

• • Dogma

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Dogma's in-game appearance is actually TV static, much like the boss, instead of being blue.

• This is because the blue is used to indicate areas that the game should apply the static effect to. This was likely done to avoid making the sprite file animated, instead simply letting the game apply the effect to designated areas when the time comes to use them. This also results in the static effect being randomized, instead of following a repeating pattern. This same trick is also what Dogma uses.

fields.description: Grants flight, +2 damage, and increases speed to 1.1. Grants enough health to have 6 full hearts, if possible. Grants the Holy Mantle effect for the room it was obtained in. Automatically given to Isaac after defeating Dogma.

Door Stop.title: Door Stop
Door Stop.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• While held, the last door Isaac went through stays open, allowing him to leave the room even if enemies are in it.

• Does not prevent doors from closing while Isaac is within the room, e.g. triggering a Challenge Room or awaking an Angel in an Angel Room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Does not work in Greed Mode.

• [Repentance] Cannot spawn in Greed Mode.

• This trinket allows Isaac to leave rooms, including boss rooms, if the fight goes poorly.

• This becomes particularly useful in The Void, as it allows to escape the Delirium fight if encountered.

• Leaving immediately after enemies have spawned gives the player information on the fight, potentially improving decision making.

• If a Devil Room has a Krampus fight in it, Isaac may choose not to fight him and leave.

• If Greed / Super Greed is found in a Shop, one can kill it and leave the room while summoned monsters are still alive to respawn the boss and farm its loot infinitely.

• If Sloth / Super Sloth is found, one can kill it and leave the room while summoned monsters are still alive to respawn the boss, allowing one to farm cards indefinitely. 

• Does not affect Mom's and Mega Satan's boss room as the access door itself disappears.

• [Before Repentance] If a room contained champion enemies, upon leaving and re-entering the room, all previous champion enemies will have turned to regular enemies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Boss Rush exit remains open.

• 4.5 Volt / Jumper Cables: Provides infinite charges by clearing some enemies then leaving the room, and repeating.

• Charm of the Vampire / Gimpy: Allows the possibility to generate unlimited Hearts.

• Head of the Keeper: With enough patience, Coins can be gathered infinitely.

• Holy Mantle: Can be used to reset the shield at will.

• Tainted Keeper: Leaving and re-entering the room allows for limited coin farming; however, enemies in rooms Tainted Keeper has already visited will eventually stop dropping coins.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Door Stop is based on this Steam Workshop trinket by Strawrat and CupertinoEffect - which in turn is based on this Steam Workshop trinket by Lord Pigfoot Nosebeggar XVII.

• Before Repentance+, the pickup quote included an exclamation point.

• The pickup quote may be a reference to the Game of Thrones episode The Door where the same quote is repeatedly exclaimed.

fields.description: The last door Isaac went through stays open, allowing him to leave the room even if enemies are in it.

Dople.title: Dople
Dople.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Doples mirror Isaac's movements exactly. They attack by firing projectiles but only when Isaac fires tears, and these shots are fired at the same frequency as Isaac's tears.

sections.heading: Evil Twin
sections.text: Evil Twins shoot three spread blood shots instead of one but have a reduced fire rate. Also, due to the fact that they have flight, they cannot be hurt by spikes.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Doples often appear in rooms that have hazards, such as Spikes. It is possible to kill a Dople by maneuvering Isaac in such a way that the Dople walks onto a hazard, though these spots are often blocked by obstacles such as rocks, key blocks, or Hosts.

• Doples and Evil Twins do not deal contact damage, allowing Isaac to utilize contact items like Mom's Heels against them without risk.

• If Isaac attacks with an item that replaces regular tears with a charged attack such as Brimstone, Doples and Evil Twins will only attack when the beam first starts to charge up.

• If Isaac is blindfolded, Doples and Evil Twins will not attack.

• If Isaac has low tear delay, the Dople (but not the Evil Twin) will fire very rapidly at the same rate as Isaac, making it very dangerous.

• The Dople, despite mirroring Isaac's movements exactly, do not mimic his range. As a result, they can be significantly easier if Isaac has a higher range and attacks from as much of a distance as possible.

• [Before Afterbirth+] If you are to charm a Dople/Evil Twin in a room with other enemies, the Dople/Evil Twin will try to copy the movement of every other enemy in the room, resulting in teleportation all around the room at very high speeds.

• [Repentance] When playing with multiple characters, such as Jacob and Esau or when using Soul of the Forgotten, Doples/Evil Twins will mimic only one of them. Multiple Doples/Evil Twins will mimic different characters. [end edition note] 

• If a temporary character dies, their Dople/Evil Twin will also die.

• Doples and Evil Twins can press buttons.

• If multiple Doples are in the room at once, all of them will be killed except one. This is done because multiple doples mimicing the same character at once would cause all of them to overlap and be in the same position at once.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Evil Twins appear to have The Inner Eye ability, given the fact that it has a spread of 3 shots and a slower fire rate compared to Doples.

• Doples and Evil Twins are based on the term doppelganger, which means a double of a living person.

• Doples are a reference to Doppelgängers from the game Tomb Raider. It's a replica of Lara Croft, the protagonist of the video game, and can be found in The Great Pyramid. It's a skinless creature that would mirror the player's movements and could be tricked into jumping into a pit of molten lava.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Maximum mirroring tear rate of a Dople is 15. From 15 to 30 they will fire slower like from 15 to 0 and above 30 they will only fire one tear.
