Dr. Fetus.title: Dr. Fetus
Dr. Fetus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Epic Fetus]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Tears are replaced with Bombs that explode approximately one second after being fired.

• [Rebirth only] Each bomb deals 3 times the character's normal tear damage.

• [edition anr] Each bomb deals 5 times the character's normal tear damage plus a flat 30 damage. The flat 30 is not affected by damage multipliers.

• [Repentance] Dr. Fetus has two formulas for calculating the damage it does. At first, each bomb deals 10 times the character's normal tear damage. If the previous formula would lead to the bombs doing more than 60 damage, the bombs instead deal 5 times the character's normal tear damage plus a 30 flat damage. The flat 30 is not affected by damage multipliers.

• Tears down: [Before Repentance] Tear Delay × 2.5 / [Repentance] Fire Rate ÷ 2.5.

• [Before Repentance] The range and shot speed stats both affect the velocity at which the bombs are fired out. Delay before the explosion is not affected by either.

• • [Repentance] Bomb velocity formula has not been updated to account for the new range stat so it uses tear height for calculation (and not the actual range stat), resulting in the range stat effectively not working for Dr. Fetus with exceptions being Number One, Kidney Stone, Pluto, and Inner Child's revive, which make velocity absurdly low. Shot speed still increases bomb velocity. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Bombs grow larger or smaller with tear size modifiers and deal no knockback to each other.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Dr. Fetus is a special item.

• Dr. Fetus overrides multiple tear effect items, but benefit some/ [Afterbirth onward] all bomb-enhancing effects like Mr. Mega.

• Dr. Fetus bombs deal half a heart of damage to Isaac. Other explosion damage is not affected.

• Self-damage is increased to a full heart if the bomb would deal 85 damage or more. This includes effects from bomb modifiers, not just raw base damage.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Apple! / Euthanasia / Tough Love: Damage multiplier may be applied to the non-flat damage without a visual difference.

• [Before Repentance] Euthanasia bombs do not retain the instant kill ability.

• [Repentance] Euthanasia bombs retain the instant kill ability.

• Bob's Bladder: Bombs from Dr. Fetus leave creep, allowing for extra damage.

• Bobby-Bomb / [Afterbirth onward] Homing Tears: Bombs home in on enemies.

• Bomber Boy: Bombs explode in a large cross-shaped pattern.

• Bomber Boy + Cricket's Body / The Parasite / Polyphemus / Scatter Bombs: The subsequent bomb or bombs explode in a cross-shaped pattern.

• Blood Bombs: Bombs leave behind a pool of red creep.

• Brimstone / Mom's Knife: Isaac continuously fires bombs while charging the beam/knife.

• Brimstone Bombs: The activation rate of the Brimstone lasers is random and dependent on Luck. The chance is 11% at 0 Luck, increasing by 3% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 29.67 luck and minimizes at 0% at -3.67 luck. The beams of Brimstone Bombs can push fired bombs, making this item powerful but hazardous.

• Butt Bombs: Bombs inherit the Butt Bomb effects.

• [Repentance] The activation rate is random and dependent on luck. The chance is 20% at 0 Luck, increasing by 3% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 26.67 luck and minimizes at 0% at -6.67 luck.

• [Afterbirth onward] Unlike normal Butt Bombs, this synergy cannot heal Brownie, Clog, Colostomia, Dangle, or Dingle. Both the explosion and the cloud effect deal full damage. [end edition note] 

• Poisonous Tears : Fires Bob's Curse bombs.

• Cricket's Body: The bombs split outwards into 4 tiny bombs, which detonate almost immediately.

• The split bombs deal a flat [Before Repentance] 21 damage / [Repentance] 35 damage.

• [Repentance] Increases range instead of decreasing it.

• Cricket's Body + The Parasite: Bombs split outwards into 4 Cricket bombs and 2 Parasite bombs, which detonate and split a second time into the other type, for a total of 23 explosions.

• C Section: C Section has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. The fetuses drop small bombs when they touch an enemy. The bomb's damage follows Dr. Fetus' damage calculation, based on half of the fetuses damage. A fetus can drop only one bomb.

• The fetuses' bombs do not benefit from Isaac's bomb effects such as Hot Bombs or Bobby-Bomb. However, they do benefit from Isaac's tear effects and have appearance of the corresponding bombs. For example, Hot Bombs from Fire Mind, Bobby-Bomb from Homing Tears. As such, Cricket's Body, The Parasite and Polyphemus leave a subsequent bomb or bombs, and Mysterious Liquid leaves a creep.

• C Section + Ipecac: The fetuses explode before dropping any bomb.

• Dr. Fetus: Each additional copy of this item, such as from Diplopia / Crooked Penny, causes Isaac to fire one additional bomb in a side by side spread up to a maximum of 16 bombs. This maximum can’t be surpassed by other multi-shot effects such as 20/20.

• Eye of Belial: Bombs get piercing. No more further effect.

• [Repentance] Bombs deal 2.5x piercing damage.

• Fire Mind / Hot Bombs: The bombs leave behind a fire that damages enemies on contact after exploding, and bombs themselves deal [edition anr] 1 / [Repentance] points of 16 damage on contact.

• [Repentance] For Hot Bombs, the activation rate of the fire is dependent on luck. The chance is 26% at 0 Luck, increasing by 6% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 12.34 luck and minimizes at 0% at -4.34 luck.

• [Before Repentance] Fire Mind + Cricket's Body / Scatter Bombs: The fire spawned from split bombs can damage Isaac.

• [Repentance] Ghost Bombs: Bombs gain spectral and create ghosts when they explode. The activation rate of the ghosts is dependent on luck. The chance is 34% at 0 Luck, increasing by 8% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 8.25 luck and minimizes at 0% at -4.25 luck.

• Ghost Bombs + Almond Milk / Haemolacria / Monstro's Lung / Scatter Bombs / Soy Milk: While the bombs are mini, any created ghosts are smaller too and instantly launch themselves at enemies and explode, destroying nearby enemy tears, similar to Purgatory. They each deal 2x Isaac's damage, up to 4 times. [end edition note] 

• Godhead: Does not give bombs the damaging aura, but does give them the homing effect.

• [Repentance] Guppy/The Mulligan: Explosions can spawn flies.

• Haemolacria: Haemolacria has priority. Applies +10 Tear Delay after Haemolacria tears down, instead of Dr. Fetus tears down. The main tear is reminiscent of a bomb and scatters into 3-5 bombs that explode simultaneously. The split bombs deal half of Dr. Fetus' damage calculation based on the main tear's damage.

• Haemolacria + Sad Bombs: Sad bombs from Haemolacria tears shoot 10 Haemolacria tears, which then scatters into bombs without Sad Bombs' property.

• Ipecac: The bombs become Bob's Curse bombs. Isaac is immune to his bomb shots (not explosives or placed bombs). Shots will also explode immediately on impact with enemies, rocks, Poops, angel statues, devil statues, or walls. Does not apply Ipecac's tears down.

• [Before Repentance] The damage is massively increased, as the +40 damage from Ipecac is run through the damage multiplier of Dr. Fetus.

• [Repentance] The effect on damage becomes a flat +2 bonus instead of +40. Bombs leave behind a cloud of poison gas that will poison enemies in contact with it.

• [Before Repentance] Ipecac + Cricket's Body / The Parasite / Polyphemus / Sad Bombs / Scatter Bombs: Isaac is immune to the main bomb shot, but not to the explosive shrapnel.

• • [Repentance] Isaac is immune to the shrapnel bombs left by Cricket's Body, The Parasite, Polyphemus, and Scatter Bombs. Isaac is not immune to Ipecac shots from Sad Bombs.

• Ipecac + Monstro's Lung: Isaac is no longer immune to his own bombs, and since they explode as soon as they make contact, it makes self-damage very likely. [Repentance] The flat damage bonus is increased to +40.

• Ipecac + Tech X: Isaac is immune to the main bomb shot, but not the explosions created by the laser ring.

• Little Horn: Black-tinted bombs can summon Big Horn's hand to instantly kill non-boss enemies or to deal damage against bosses.

• Monstro's Lung: Monstro's Lung has priority. Does not apply Dr. Fetus' tears down. Fires 6 bombs which detonate [edition anr] simultaneously / [Repentance] at different times.

• Multi-shot effects add 1 bomb to the barrage, up to 21 bombs.

• Mr. Mega: Adds 25 flat damage to bomb explosions.

• [Repentance] The bonus damage is only applied if the bombs are visually Mr. Mega bombs, which means items like Soy Milk won't get the bonus damage.

• Mysterious Liquid: Exploding bombs leave behind a large pool of creep.

• The Parasite: Upon exploding, bombs split into two other bombs, which explode almost immediately.

• The split bombs deal a flat [Before Repentance] 24 damage/ [Repentance] 40 damage.

• [Repentance] Piercing tears: Bombs deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.

• Poison tears: This is guaranteed by Bob's Curse, Ipecac, and Scorpio, and also has a chance to trigger from The Common Cold, Black Tooth, Pinky Eye or Serpent's Kiss.

• [Repentance] Poison bombs leave behind a cloud of toxic gas that will poison enemies in contact with it aside from the main target.

• Polyphemus: The bombs increase in size and do increased damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] The bombs become Mr. Mega bombs. After they detonate, they leave behind a regular-sized bomb that deals a flat [Before Repentance] 60 damage/ [Repentance] 100 damage, much like a standard bomb.

• Proptosis: Distance penalty does not apply.

• The non-flat damage for Dr. Fetus' damage calculation is [Before Repentance] doubled / [Repentance] tripled.

• Pyromaniac: Explosions heal Isaac, essentially making him invincible as long as he has at least one red heart container.

• Remote Detonator: The bombs can be detonated on command, making it easier to hit moving enemies. Unlike placed bombs, they will eventually detonate on their own.

• Rocket in a Jar: Shoots rockets.

• Piercing tears: Rockets do not pierce through enemies. However, they deal both piercing damage and explosion damage on impact with an enemy.

• Rocket in a Jar + Polyphemus: Rockets will “bounce” off of enemies, rocks, and walls, detonating twice. This is easily observable by firing parallel to a wall while moving towards it.

• Sad Bombs: Fires tears as normally placed Sad Bombs would.

• [Repentance] The activation rate is random and dependent on luck. The chance is 11% at 0 Luck, increasing by 3% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 29.67 luck and minimizes at 0% at -3.67 luck.

• Scatter Bombs: The bombs split into [Before Repentance] 2-4/ [Repentance] 4-5 tiny bombs. The bombs deal half damage of the bomb it came from.

• [Repentance] The activation rate is random and dependent on luck. The chance is 34% at 0 Luck, increasing by 8% per luck. This maximizes at 100% at 8.25 luck and minimizes at 0% at -4.25 luck.

• Stye: The bombs have a 50% chance of gaining Stye's damage boost but not its range upgrade/shot speed downgrade. Affected bombs and their explosions are tinted a pale blue.

• The damage boost is applied to Isaac's base tear damage and does not affect any other aspect of Dr. Fetus's damage calculation.

• Technology: Both fire normally.

• Tech X: Dr. Fetus has priority. The bombs have a laser ring around them.

• Tech X + Cricket's Body / The Parasite / Polyphemus / Scatter Bombs: The subsequent bomb or bombs do not have the laser ring.

• Uranus: The bombs freeze enemies upon killing them.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
Overridden by Dr. Fetus:

• R U A Wizard? pill

• Azazel's default attack

• Tainted Azazel's default attack

• Brain Worm

• Brimstone

• Chocolate Milk

• Cursed Eye

• Guppy

• Jacob's Ladder

• Lachryphagy

• Lead Pencil

• Little Horn

• A Lump of Coal

• Mucormycosis

• The Mulligan

• Neptunus

• Ocular Rift

• The Parasite

• Parasitoid

• Pop!

• Sinus Infection

• Technology

• Trisagion
Only stat effects are applied; otherwise overridden by Dr. Fetus:

• Anti-Gravity

• Compound Fracture

• Cricket's Body, greatly decreases range

• Marked
Other interactions:

• Blasting Cap: Shot bombs cannot drop additional bombs.

• Chocolate Milk: The bombs can't be charged, but reduces Isaac's tear delay by 20%.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Dr. Fetus.

• Explosivo: The bombs have a chance of sticking to an enemy. These bombs have the same appearance as Sticky Bombs, but do not spawn spiders or slowing white creep.

• Eye Sore: When Isaac shoots, he has a chance to fire 1-3 additional bombs in random directions.

• The Forgotten/Tainted Forgotten: A live bomb will spawn on top of The Forgotten when he starts charging his attack. The Forgotten will toss bombs after releasing the charge; airborne bombs deal 1.5x his damage if they collide with an enemy with enough speed. Max distance is obtained with minimal charge. If the bomb explodes while charging, a normal ranged bone attack happens after releasing it. The melee attack is unaffected.

• Isaac's Tears: Fires normal tears.

• Immaculate Heart: Orbital tears are unaffected by Dr. Fetus and act normally.

• [Repentance] Kidney Stone / Number One / Pluto / Inner Child's revive: The bombs lose almost all of their range, and cannot be improved by range ups. Shot speed and tear height ups can be used to mitigate this downside. [end edition note] 

• Kidney Stone: The range decrease applies, but since the tear falling speed stat doesn't affect Dr. Fetus' bombs, they spawn directly in front of Isaac, making self-damage very likely. The effect can be mitigated with range ups.

• Lead Pencil: Every fifteenth shot will cause a barrage of short-ranged tears, which blocks the path of the bomb and can harm Isaac as the result.

• The Ludovico Technique: The bomb can be controlled before exploding, similar to Epic Fetus. Isaac does not shoot bombs while controlling it.

• The Ludovico Technique + Almond Milk / Soy Milk: Since Isaac can't shoot bombs before they explode, this results in a damage down with no effective fire rate increase.

• Marked: Isaac continuously fires bombs at the crosshair.

• Monstro's Lung: Same effect as 20/20, except retains fire rate.

• Mom's Eye: Grants a chance to shoot an extra bomb from the back of Isaac's head.

• Mom's Eye + Eye of the Occult: Bombs that spawn from Mom's Eye will try to move to where you're shooting making it very difficult to not get hit by your own explosions.

• Mom's Knife: Overrides Dr. Fetus.

• My Reflection: The bombs lose momentum and slide back towards Isaac, making self-damage very likely.

• Ouroboros Worm: Does not affect the trajectory of the bombs. Turns some bombs into homing bombs, similar to Bobby-Bomb.

• Parasitoid: Bomb explosions have a chance of leaving the slowing creep in a larger pool than egg sack tears, [Before Repentance+] however the egg sack bombs can't spawn Blue Flies/Blue Spiders.

• [Before Repentance] Piercing tears: The bombs pierce through enemies, which makes killing them more difficult.

• Soy Milk: Rapidly shoots very low damage bombs. Can create a line of bombs which can knock each other back, which can be difficult to avoid taking damage from.

• [edition anr] Rapidly shoots medium damage bombs. Can create a line of bombs which can knock each other back, which can be difficult to avoid taking damage from.

• [Repentance] Rapidly shoots low damage mini-bombs. Bombs don't knock each other back.

• Spectral tears: The bombs can pierce through the obstacles. If a bomb is fired inside an obstacle, the bomb collides against it, but not against others.

• Spirit Sword: Overrides Dr. Fetus.

• Spirit Sword + Haemolacria: The split bombs can appear from Spirit Sword's projectiles.

• Sticky Bombs: The bombs stick to enemies ( [Before Repentance] unless Isaac has piercing), but enemies killed by the bomb will not spawn Blue Spiders.

• [Repentance] The bombs always spawn slowing white creep after exploding.

• Tear Detonator: No effect on bombs.

• [Repentance] Tear height ups such as Tape Worm, Jupiter, Telepathy For Dummies, I - The Magician, and Huge Growth: Improves the effective range of the bombs. [end edition note] 

• Technology 2: The bombs are pushed forward by the laser.

• Technology Zero: Dr. Fetus bombs do not generate electricity. Tears from other sources such as Sad Bombs can still generate electricity.

• The Wiz: Causes Isaac to fire two bombs instead of one in diagonal directions.

• Tiny Planet: The bombs fly uncontrollably around the player, making self-damage very likely.

• Tractor Beam: After firing a bomb and moving, the bomb will have a homing-style effect towards the beam, but will not stay directly on the beam. Not recommended, as changing directions while firing will cause the bomb to reel back to Isaac at high speed, making self-damage very likely.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Dr. Fetus and Epic Fetus items are based on Dr. Fetus, the main villain in Super Meat Boy, which is a game by Edmund McMillen (the creator of The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth).

• This is also the reason why taking the item replaces tears with bombs (Dr. Fetus fires rockets in chapter 6's bossfight in Super Meat Boy), and gives Isaac a top hat and a monocle (Dr. Fetus has a top hat and a monocle in Super Meat Boy).

• This item is used in Demo Man.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, Dr. Fetus was unlocked by beating Mom's Heart five times instead of nine.

• When the player unlocks Dr. Fetus, the item is labeled as "Fetus in a Jar" on the unlock screen.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: The black ring generated from the synergy of Dr. Fetus and Tech X behaves as a Maw Of The Void ring and may cause Black Hearts to drop.
Bug note: Even though having spectral tears will make bombs not collide with obstacles, if Isaac shoots a bomb while on top of an obstacle, the bomb will collide with it, making it possible to take damage.

fields.description: Tears are replaced by Bombs that benefit from bomb-enhancing effects and slide for a fixed time after being fired.

Dream Catcher.title: Dream Catcher
Dream Catcher.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• During the transition between floors, Isaac's nightmare shows the item that will be found in the Treasure Room and what Boss will be at the end of the floor.

• [cu: Blind] items will be revealed, as well as the hidden second item on the alternate floors (Downpour, etc.)

• Grants a Half Soul Heart upon entering a new floor (this includes each floor of the Ascent).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• On [cu: XL] floors, both items and bosses are shown.

• If the floor Isaac is going to has no Treasure Rooms, Dream Catcher will simply show the floor's boss. If there are no Treasure Rooms or bosses on the floor (i.e. in The Shop, Ultra Greed, and Home), the dream will instantly be skipped.

• Dream Catcher cannot show glitched items generated by TMTRAINER. Instead, it will just show The Sad Onion.

• Dream Catcher will show a poop in the Treasure Room if there are no item pedestals in the room.

• On Corpse II, the boss will appear as a blank space; on the special Mausoleum/Gehenna II floor that leads to Home, it will appear as Mom.

• On The Void, the Dream Catcher will show all the bosses that can be found in the various boss rooms, starting with Delirium.

• [Repentance+] When holding Dream Catcher, the dream sequence is unskippable, except when entering The Void.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Revelations: If the floor boss is revealed to be one of the horsemen, therefore Book of Revelations can be used early, as the downside is no longer relevant.

• Satanic Bible: If the floor boss is revealed to be one of the horsemen, and if the player has no interest in the Cube of Meat or doesn't mind paying health for it, Satanic Bible can be used early.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Devil's Crown: Dream Catcher will show what the Treasure Room will have if Isaac chooses to enter the room without the crown.

• Found Soul: The soul will receive half a soul heart for every new floor he follows Isaac to, allowing him to survive multiple hits and gather up to a maximum of 12 soul hearts. His health resets when the trinket is dropped.

• More Options + Downpour / Dross, etc.: Dream Catcher will not show the third item if going to the alternate floors.

• Red Key: When on alt path, if a bonus Treasure Room is encountered before the regular Treasure Room, the left item showed in the dream sequence will appear in that red Treasure Room, but the right item showed in the dream sequence will still be in the regular Treasure Room.

• Tarot Cloth + XVII - The Stars: The boosted reverse Stars card converting a Treasure Room into a double choice treasure room will make Dream Catcher's prediction inaccurate, neither of the items offered is likely to be the one displayed.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Dream Catcher will not show the correct items in Greed Mode.
Bug note: Dream Catcher will not show the correct items when combined with Broken Glasses.

fields.description: During the transition between floors, Isaac's nightmare shows the contents of the upcoming floor's Treasure Room, as well as the floor's boss. Grants a Half Soul Heart when entering a new floor.

Carrion Queen.title: Carrion Queen
Carrion Queen.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Carrion Queen is a boss that can appear in the Catacombs.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
Carrion Queen is only vulnerable in the flesh segment of her behind. She moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:

• Carrion Queen charges at Isaac whenever he lines up with one of her cardinal directions.

• Like Chub, Carrion Queen eats any Bombs dropped in her path; stunning her for a moment before dealing considerable damage.

• Spawns a damaging Red Poop, up to a maximum of 5.

• She damages and destroys Red Poop she charges into.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
• When below half health, Carrion Queen begins to move diagonally, similar to The Hollow, but without flight. She no longer performs her previous attacks from Phase 1.

• She will bounce off of obstacles and her own Red Poop damaging it and destroying it in the process.
Carrion Queen deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 20] : Carrion Queen moves slightly quicker, has 100% more HP (700), and spawns small Mask + Heart instead of Red Poop. The hearts have 28 HP and killing them deals 40 damage to Carrion Queen. She does not bounce diagonally around the room when below half health.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Piercing tears make the fight much easier, as tears can pass through Carrion Queen's invulnerable segments and hit her vulnerable segment.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Carrion Queen was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the flash version, the Carrion Queen could also be encountered in Necropolis.

• She is the posthumous version of Chub.

• Since the Carrion Queen is a posthumous version of Chub, and both appear in Chapter 2, this makes Chub one of four bosses to have its poshumous version in the same chapter the others being Gemini having Blighted Ovum in Chapter 1, Polycephalus having The Stain in Chapter 2 and the Tuff Twins having The Shell in Chapter 2.5.

• • However, Chub and the Carrion Queen don't share the same environment, as Chub can appear in The Caves and The Flooded Caves, while the Carrion Queen can only appear in The Catacombs, where Chub cannot.

• [Repentance] She is the boss version of the Carrion Princess. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] Despite the Princess being destroyed by Hagalaz, it has no effect on Carrion Queen.

• Carrion is another word for the rotting flesh of a dead animal, often eaten by scavengers like vultures, coyotes, maggots, etc.

• The name "Carrion Queen" could be inspired by a level of Super Meat Boy under the name "King Carrion".

• Despite the Carrion Queen being an invertebrate, or an animal lacking a skeleton of bones, she has a skeletal appearance.

• [Before Repentance] During the death animation, Carrion Queen's head doesn't burst into blood. Instead, it flattens and instantly disappears.

• In the Bestiary, she is referred to as "The Carrion Queen".

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Sometimes when entering the boss room and skipping the cut scene, Carrion Queen will spawn in the door, dealing damage to the player.
Bug note: While petrified, her entire body can be damaged.
Bug note: Each of the three segments of Carrion Queen will drop a heart instead of just one.
Bug note: Carrion Queen's last segment can be temporarily disconnected with Anima Sola.

• Unlike in Rebirth, in the original game, Cat-o-nine-tails was merely a shot speed up and was widely considered by the community to be one of the worst items in the game.

Celtic Cross.title: Celtic Cross
Celtic Cross.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Grants a chance to trigger the Book of Shadows effect upon taking damage, creating a shield that nullifies all types of damage for 7 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The base chance of creating the protective shield is 20%.

• The activation chance of this item depends on the Luck stat and goes up to 100% at 27 Luck.

• The shield negates health loss from Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars.

• Does not prevent Heart Container loss from Health Down pills or Devil Room Deals.

• Does not prevent damage from IV Bag.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • [Repentance] The Polaroid, Virgo: Can trigger at the same time as The Polaroid or Virgo, cumulating to up to 22 seconds of shield.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In Galicia, Celtic crosses are usually found on top of granaries as a protective measure against any kind of evil. They are also commonly found among Celtic nations today and historically.

• This item is functionally almost identical to Virgo, minus the pill conversion effect.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: You feel blessed; Repentance: Blessing of protection]

Censer.title: Censer
Censer.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Spawns a familiar projecting a circular aura that slows enemies and enemy shots within its radius and for a short period once they exit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The aura does not affect bosses but slows down their shots.

• Bosses that use tight volleys of projectiles are extremely difficult to avoid without additional items to block, remove, or redirect those shots, as the slowing effect will cause their attacks to clump together.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Censer having [Before Repentance+] 4th / [Repentance+] 6th priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] 2Spooky / Venus: The slowing aura mitigates the delay between fast enemies that charge Isaac and the status effect, making it much harder for Isaac to take contact damage. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Bot Fly / Psy Fly: The slowing aura allows these items to deal with the incoming projectiles more reliably. [end edition note] 

• The Soul: The slowing aura allows incoming enemies and shots to be more reliably deflected.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• BFFS!: The aura does not slow things from further away despite increased visual size.

• Montezuma's Revenge: The corn shots are slowed by the aura.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• A censer is a container used to burn incense.

• This item shares its pickup quote with Eucharist.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar which creates a circular aura that slows down enemies and enemy shots inside.

Ceremonial Robes.title: Ceremonial Robes
Ceremonial Robes.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants 3 Black Hearts.

• +1 damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Heretic. [end edition note] 

• When purchased at a Devil Room by ??? (or another character who has lost all Red Heart containers), this item effectively converts 3 Soul Hearts into 3 Black Hearts, increasing damage at no downside.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Black Feather: Ceremonial Robes counts as an 'evil' item, granting a damage boost.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Despite this, the item has always functioned exactly the same since its initial implementation in Rebirth. Previously, the damage increase went unmentioned in-game.

• The change from 'sin up' to 'evil up' made the item consistent with others that grant Black Hearts — two examples being Match Book and Abaddon.

Champion Belt.title: Champion Belt
Champion Belt.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 damage.

• Increases the chance for champion enemies to appear by 15%.

• Without any other champion enemy appearance modifiers the chance increases from 5% to 20% ( [Before Repentance] 20% to 35% in hard mode).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• While more champions likely mean a tougher run, players will also profit from a higher amount of pickups available to them, thanks to many champions dropping items upon death.

• Champion enemies don't drop consumables while playing Greedier mode, making Champion Belt significantly worse in that mode.

• The belt does not affect the appearance rate of champion bosses.

• This is one of the only raw DMG up's in the shop item pool.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The chance for champions to appear does not increase in The Void. It has a fixed 75% chance. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] Champion Belt's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Purple Heart: Champion Belt's increased chance is also doubled.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The item resembles a championship belt in wrestling, MMA, boxing, and other similar commercialized fighting competitions.

fields.description: +1 damage. Increases the chance of champion enemies appearing by 15%.

Champions.title: Champions
Champions.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
Some monsters can spawn as a Champion which deviates in coloration and size. The champion's coloration/size denotes which peculiar behaviors and traits it will exhibit. Champions will generally drop a pickup (coinciding with the color of the champion) when killed on normal difficulty. However, in hard mode, the drop rate is reduced to 33%, while in Greed mode, champions won't drop pickups at all.

Most champions have a visual 15% size increase, inflict full heart damage regardless of chapter, and have double the health of a normal monster. Champions are generally regarded as more dangerous than common monsters.

[Before Afterbirth+] Champions always deal contact damage, regardless of what monster they are (e.g. a common Mulligan will not deal contact damage, but champion versions will).

sections.text:
The following enemies are able to spawn as Champions

The following enemies cannot spawn as Champions under any circumstances

sections.heading: Champion Bosses
sections.text:
Bosses are also capable of being champions, but these work much differently from regular monsters as champions. Every champion boss is unique, with individualized adjustments to the attacks and AI of the boss in question, usually specializing in certain aspects of the boss's repertoire to make them harder to deal with. A champion boss may or may not have increased or decreased health, speed, and/or size in comparison to the default version of the boss, depending on the champion in question. Champion bosses are usually not strictly stronger than the default versions of the bosses, having trade-offs with certain stats being lowered and/or certain attacks being weaker or outright inaccessible in exchange for other stats and/or attacks being stronger.

Because every champion boss is unique, the following table contains a brief summation of how they differ from the default bosses. Additional details (including any changes to the differences in versions prior to Repentance) can be found in the pages for each individual boss.

• Does not use The Hourglass.

The following bosses have no Champion versions and cannot spawn as Champions under any circumstances

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: The Frail's black champion is intended to spawn in the second phase with 30% more HP (390), but the second phase is coded to always spawn at 66.6% HP (200) total.

Chaos.title: Chaos
Chaos.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Drops 1-6 random pickups around Isaac.

• Causes items to be chosen from random item pools.

• Fixed item drops that ignore the current room's item pool will not be replaced. Examples include Cube of Meat after defeating one of The Harbingers as a floor boss, or The Small Rock after breaking a Tinted Rock.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• When playing Greed mode, items that are available only in the normal game will still not appear despite Chaos; the modes' different item pools stay separate.

• As the item does not mix or combine item pools, it is possible to deplete smaller item pools and end up with Breakfast before all items in the game have been taken.

• Thus, if Chaos tries to pull from an item pool that is already depleted, it will not pull from a different pool and instead give Isaac Breakfast.

• • As many Greed mode item pools are small, Chaos tends to result in Breakfast more often during Greed mode.

• [Before Repentance] Chaos will draw items even from item pools that are not used in the game, but defined in the game's files. The unused pools are bossrush containing nearly all bomb related items, challenge with a smaller selection of bomb items and dungeon containing several Mom related items and food items.

• [Before Repentance] Since all item pools have the same probability of being selected, bomb-related items are much more common due to the Bomb Bum, bossrush and challenge item pools.

• [Repentance] Each pool has a weight based on the number of items in the pool. Items from large pools such as Treasure Room, Shop, and Boss are very likely, while items from small pools like Bomb Bum and Planetarium are more rare.

• If an item outside of the Devil Room pool appears as a Devil Deal, it will always cost 1 Red Heart Container (or 3 Soul Hearts should Isaac have no Red Hearts).

• [Repentance] If an item from the Angel Room pool appears as a Devil deal, it will cost 2 Red Hearts if it would cost 30 cents in the Angel Shop generated by The Stairway, and 1 Red Heart if it would cost 15 cents in the Angel Shop.

• • Similarly, if an item from the Devil Room pool appears in an Angel Shop generated by The Stairway, it will cost 30 cents if it would cost 2 Red Hearts as a Devil Deal, and 15 cents if it would cost 1 Red Heart as a Devil Deal. [end edition note] 

• If an item that grants an Eternal Heart is taken in a devil deal, the eternal heart will not keep Isaac alive if he has no other hearts.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Bosses defeated in The Void drop items as if Chaos was active. Rerolling the items uses the Boss Room pool as normal. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item's sprite is a Symbol of Chaos.

• The character costume is similar to the "Trollface" internet meme.

• Keeper's Chaos costume resembles the "Forever Alone" internet meme instead.

fields.description: Drops 1-6 random pickups on the floor. Causes items to be chosen from random item pools.

Chaos Card.title: Chaos Card
Chaos Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon activation, Isaac throws the card in front of himself.

• The card is thrown in the direction Isaac's body is facing, meaning the card will be thrown in the direction Isaac is moving. If he is stationary, it will be thrown in the last direction that Isaac moved.

• The thrown card kills anything in its path (including end-game bosses like ??? and otherwise indestructible entities like Stone Grimaces and Wall Huggers) and gets stuck in the ground/wall after being thrown.

• The only exceptions to this are Delirium, The Beast, Mother's Shadow and Dark Esau.

• The card can open doors as if a Bomb had exploded them, although it cannot open any locked doors or open the big door in the starting room of Dark Room and Chest.

• The card can extinguish fires, break rocks, and open secret rooms.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, the Chaos Card has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• Using it on multi-phase bosses like Isaac, ??? and The Lamb will instantly end the boss fight.

• Using it on Satan during his first form will end the fight, despite him having multiple forms and health bars. Using it on The Fallen instead of Satan himself will not end the fight.

• • However, using it on Mega Satan will only skip one phase.

• [Afterbirth onward] It will only kill one phase of Hush [Before Repentance] unless Isaac throws it from the bottom side, such that after killing the first phase, the card can still catch up with Hush's true form as he pops out at the top of the room. However, this method can fail depending on the timing and the position of the first phase. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth+ onward] It will only kill one phase of Ultra Greed in Greedier mode. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] It will only kill one phase of Mother and Dogma. [end edition note] 

• To aim the card correctly, make sure to move/shoot in the direction that it needs to be thrown.

• Does not kill Beggars or Shopkeepers.

• Can kill normally indestructible enemies like the Masks of Mask + Hearts (though this will not kill the heart), Hosts while they're invulnerable, the little chubs in Chubbers, and Death's Heads. It can also be used to kill things typically not considered alive like Wall Huggers and Stone Grimaces.

• If used on Pin or The Frail segments can be cut off causing both bosses to lose length like Larry Jr..

• Using it on an Angel Statue will reveal an Angel and kill them instantly.

• Great Gideon has a special death animation if killed using it, which also reveals a Crawl Space under him containing several Chests and items.

• [Repentance] Mother's Shadow cannot be killed with Chaos Card, though it is normally impossible to get one in the abandoned area of Mines/ Ashpit II. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Tainted Forgotten does not throw the card in the direction that Tainted Soul is moving if Tainted Forgotten is held. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Angelic Prism: If the Chaos Card passes through the prism, it will replicate the Chaos Card four times each in their respective colors.

• Blank Card: Allows for an easy run by allowing repeated use of the card.

• Items such as Habit, 9 Volt, and Charged Baby give more opportunities to use the card since all these items decrease the charge time of Blank Card.

• The Battery allows Blank Card to be used twice in a room, allowing multi-phase bosses to be killed instantly.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Tarot Cloth: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The icon, name and functionality are all a reference to the Magic: The Gathering card Chaos Orb. This card is famous for its unusual effect: the card is flipped from a height of over one foot above the board and all cards it touches as it lands are destroyed.

• [Repentance] There is one room in the game (in Mines) that contains a guaranteed Chaos Card (see Gallery). [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If used against Scolex while he's jumping, Chaos Card will not instantly kill him and will instead cut off the bottom of his tail, dealing some damage. Although his weak point will no longer be visible, its hitbox will be and can still be damaged as normal.

fields.description: Throws the card in the direction Isaac is moving, which opens doors, breaks obstacles, and instantly kills any enemy in its path.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the main player character; the additional multiplayer characters; Babies; non-player characters; NPCs] 

There are 34 playable characters in The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, with 11 available in the base game and 23 available in the DLCs. Five of these characters (Isaac, Magdalene, Cain, Judas, and ???) came with the original The Binding of Isaac, while two additional characters (Eve and Samson) were added later. Eve was added in The Binding of Isaac's Halloween Update, while Samson was added in the Wrath of the Lamb expansion. Rebirth contains four new characters (Azazel, Lazarus, Eden, and The Lost).

[Afterbirth onward] The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth adds one new character (Lilith), plus one more character via an update (Keeper).

[Afterbirth+ onward] The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth † adds one character (Apollyon), plus one more secret character (The Forgotten) added via a Booster Pack.

[Repentance] The Binding of Isaac: Repentance adds two characters: Bethany and Jacob and Esau.

Repentance also adds alternate Tainted versions of all 17 characters. Tainted characters have their own set of completion marks and corresponding unlocks, however they only have a single unlock for completing both Boss Rush and Hush, and one altogether for beating Isaac, ???, Satan, and The Lamb. [end edition note] 

Each character's progress can be gauged by checking their completion marks.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• One common theory (which was confirmed by Edmund) is that all characters are different forms of Isaac himself. This theory suggests that every character is a creation of Isaac's imagination which he assumes the personality and appearance of when playing as them. Most characters represent different issues that Isaac believes he has, while ??? is Isaac after dying by suffocation inside The Chest, Azazel is who Isaac sees himself as, and The Lost is Isaac's wandering soul (which can be seen upon dying).

• [Afterbirth onward] Additionally, Keeper is Isaac's desiccated corpse, as evidenced by Ending 18.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Forgotten could be Isaac's skeleton shown in Ending 17 and Ending 20.

• [Repentance] This theory is also confirmed by the cutscene before fighting The Beast, in which Isaac briefly turns into The Lost, The Forgotten, and ??? as he grows angel wings.

• The original 4 characters were based on D&D classes and tarot suits, being:

• Isaac = fighter / swords

• Cain = thief / pentacles 

• Judas = wizard / rods

• Maggy = cleric / cups

• Samson was also loosely based on a Brezerker and Eve on a Druid.

• [Repentance] While on the character selection screen for the tainted characters, a male voice sings instead of the normal female voice, and the song is distorted. The same is true when loading into the game after selecting a tainted character.

• Also, when a tainted character is selected or being selected, the taskbar icon of the game changes to look like Tainted Isaac.

• In the Requiem expansion for the Four Souls card game, the tainted characters have their achievement names (e.g. "The Broken" instead of "Tainted Isaac") unlike in the video game. This was decided in a poll made by Edmund via twitter.

• Before that, Edmund had posted an image of Isaac's alternate version being referred to as "Tainted Isaac".

• When switching back and forth between the tainted and normal characters, you can see Isaac's face behind the Who Am I? note, which either appears as Normal or Tainted Isaac depending on which side you switch to.

• The closet you find any tainted character in is the same closet you see during Ending 21. This is reflected in how the characters you find inside the closet are usually hurt or damaged in some way, like how a child might look after being forced into a closet.

• Most of the tainted character's Delirium unlocks are their starting ability. Exceptions to this are Tainted Isaac, Tainted Lost, Tainted Keeper and Tainted Eden.

• Many, if not all, of the tainted characters have similar abilities to their non-tainted variants, with them having a "twist" on the original character that alters the playstyle in significant ways. An example of this is Isaac and Tainted Isaac, where the former uses D6 to reroll unfavorable items, and the latter automatically is presented with 2 options each pedestal, at the cost of an inventory allowing only 8 passive items at a time.

Charged Baby.title: Charged Baby
Charged Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a battery familiar that, while Isaac is in an uncleared room, every 30 seconds, starting from the moment it has been picked up, does one of the following:

• Spawns a Lil' Battery. It does this a maximum of 2 times per room.

• • [Repentance] Can also spawn a Micro Battery or Mega Battery instead.

• Adds a charge to Isaac's activated item. It does this a maximum of 2 times per room.

• Petrifies all enemies for 1.3 seconds.

• Nothing.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Charged Baby becomes very powerful as Lilith in Greed mode, as the duplicates will continue to spawn Lil' Batteries, leading to a huge chain of familiars.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Charged Baby having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

• In an uncleared room, if Charged Baby familiar has reached the maximum of spawned batteries and/or added activated item charges, Isaac may re-enter the room (e.g. by bombing a closed door, having Door Stop or Mercurius) to reset Charged Baby's effect limits.

• This effectively allows farming for batteries and activated item charges, given the player's patience, ability to avoid enemies present in the room, and a way to re-enter the room indefinitely.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • BFFS!: Familiar is bigger and drops Lil' Batteries more often. No effect on its other abilities.

fields.description: Spawns a familiar that occasionally drops a Lil' Battery, gives an active item charge, or petrifies all enemies in the room.

Charged Penny.title: Charged Penny
Charged Penny.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Picking up coins has a chance to add one charge to Isaac's currently held Active Item.

• This chance is equal to 1/6th of the value of the coin, and cannot activate more than once per coin collected.

| +Chance per Coin | Coin | Value | Chance 
| Penny | 1 | 16-17%

| Double Penny | 2 | 33%

| Nickel | 5 | 83%

| Dime | 10 | ~99%

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy adds one more charge to Isaac's active item.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This trinket used to be called Electric Penny in Antibirth, and had a different sprite. In Antibirth, it was always unlocked and nickels and dimes would proc the charge chance 5 and 10 times respectively.

fields.description: Picking up coins has a chance to give an Active Item charge.

Charm of the Vampire.title: Charm of the Vampire
Charm of the Vampire.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Restores a Half Red Heart for every 13 enemies killed.

• [Repentance] +0.3 damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• As Keeper and Tainted Keeper, Coin Hearts can be restored with this item.

• The healing effect is useless for characters that cannot use Red hearts.

• [Repentance] Tainted Bethany will gain one blood charge when it activates. [end edition note] 

• Destroyed Shopkeepers contribute to the counter.

• The healing counter also applies to enemies killed by familiars.

• If a room is cleared save for one enemy, it can be reset if the games is quit and resumed. The counter for Charm of the Vampire is saved along with the game, meaning the same room can be farmed for Red Hearts.

• The Door Stop trinket can be used to achieve this without having to save and quit the game. Simply leaving the room will reset the room.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Turning enemies into pickups doesn't count towards the healing counter.

• E. Coli / Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop don't count towards the healing counter.

• [Repentance] Freeze Effects: Enemies that die from being frozen don't count towards the healing counter.

• [Repentance+] Frozen enemies do count for the healing effect.

• Maggy's Bow: No effect.

• My Reflection: Despite vampires having no reflection, Charm of the Vampire does not remove the effect of My Reflection.

• Tainted Magdalene: Restores a full Red Heart instead.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] This item is used in Have a Heart. [end edition note] 

• A vampire is a being from folklore who subsists by feeding on the life essence (generally in the form of blood) of the living.

• In folklore, a vampire leaves no reflection because it has no soul. [Repentance] This is why Charm of the Vampire removes Isaac's reflections in the water/blood visible in some floors.

• If an enemy dies while Isaac is dying, Charm of the Vampire can still heal him, leaving him dead with half a Red Heart.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Kills heal; Repentance: DMG up + kills heal]
fields.description: Heals Isaac for a Half Red Heart for every 13 enemies killed. [Repentance] +0.3 damage.

Chemical Peel.title: Chemical Peel
Chemical Peel.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • +2 flat damage to tears fired from Isaac's left eye.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The damage bonus is unaffected by both positive and negative damage multipliers.

• Cain has a 50% chance of firing a shot with the effects of Chemical Peel whenever he fires.

• Blood Clot applies to the same eye and the effects stack.

• Generally every interaction and synergy that applies to Chemical Peel also applies to Blood Clot. See its page for any differences to what is listed here.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20/The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider: Every other set of tears has the Chemical Peel effect.

• Brimstone: The entire laser has a high chance to have the Chemical Peel effect, with no visual difference.

• Dr. Fetus: The damage bonus applies to every bomb, with no visual difference.

• Epic Fetus: The missiles have a high chance to deal 40 points extra damage, with no visual difference.

• Lead Pencil: All tears in the tear barrage will gain the Chemical Peel effect.

• The Ludovico Technique: The tear flashes between normal and the higher-damaging Chemical Peel tear.

• Mom's Knife: Each tick of the Knife's damage has a high chance to gain the bonus, with no visual difference.

• Soy Milk / Almond Milk: Chemical Peel is unaffected by the damage down modifier, greatly increasing DPS.

• Tech.5: Chemical Peel has a chance to apply to the laser, with no visual difference.

• Technology: Lasers have a high chance to gain extra damage, with no visual difference.

• Technology 2: Every tear fired has Chemical Peel applied to it, but the laser is unaffected.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Diplopia: No effect from additional copies.

• Incubus: Has a 50% chance of firing a shot with the Chemical Peel effect.

• Sad Bombs: The last type of tear fired is used for the burst.

• Stapler: Gives a 50% chance of firing a Chemical Peel shot, similar to Cain.

• Tech X: Overrides Chemical Peel.

• Varicose Veins: The last type of tear fired is used for the burst.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Isaac's face looks similar to a Dople when this item is obtained.

• Chemical Peel may be a reference to the DC Comics character Two-Face, who had the left side of his face burned by a chemical product in a way similar to the item costume effect.

fields.description: Tears fired from the left eye have +2 flat damage.

Chewed Pen.title: Chewed Pen
Chewed Pen.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Adds a chance to fire tears that slow enemies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The chance to fire a slowing tear depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 10 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.5 \right \rfloor}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 100% at 18 luck.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: At base luck, having either increases the chance to 20% and having both to 30%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Chewed Pen originates from the Antibirth mod, and by extension, from the Community Remix mod for the flash version.

• In Community Remix, it was named The Pen.

• This trinket is extremely similar to the Game Squid trinket found in the eternal edition of the original The Binding of Isaac, which was never added to Rebirth.

fields.description: Adds a chance to fire tears that slow enemies.

Child's Heart.title: Child's Heart
Child's Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives a 10% chance of changing the room drop reward to a Red Heart.

• Gives a 33% chance of adding a heart to the rewards from opening certain Chests, or destroying Tinted Rocks, certain Machines, and certain Beggars.

• Other than Tinted Rocks, these can only drop the heart if they drop coins, hearts, Bombs, or Keys.

• This includes: 

• This excludes:

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases the chance of changing the room drop reward to a Red Heart to 20% and increases the chance of adding a heart to rewards to 66%. Having both increases these chances to respectively 30% and 100%.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Upon using a Blood Donation Machine, there is a chance for the Child's Heart to spawn.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Samson will start with Child's Heart after completing Ultra Hard.

• Since the increase of heart drops come at the expense of other pickups, if Isaac is short on pickups such as keys and bombs, dropping the trinket by holding the 'Drop' key (default: control) may be beneficial.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This trinket is used in Cursed! (challenge #10) and [Repentance] Bloody Mary (challenge #37).

fields.quote: It calls out to its brothers
fields.description: Increases the chance of a Red Heart dropping after clearing a room, and the chance of finding a heart when opening a Chest.

Child Leash.title: Child Leash
Child Leash.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Causes Isaac's familiars to stay closer to Isaac.

• [Repentance+] Increases damage and size of all familiars by 25%.

• Size increase doesn't stack with such from BFFS!, but damage multiplier does, resulting in 2.25x damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Afterbirth+ onward] This trinket affects the same familiars King Baby effects. For a list of the familiars unaffected by this trinket, visit King Baby's page. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either now increases the damage of all familiars by 50%. Having both by 75%.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Friendship Necklace: Familiars orbit much closer to Isaac.

• King Baby: Familiars stay closer to King Baby while Isaac is firing.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The pickup quote is a reference to the saying "Keep your friends close, and your enemies closer".

sections.heading: Bugs

XXI - The World.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

XX - Judgement.title: XX - Judgement
XX - Judgement.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Spawns a Beggar near Isaac.

• The beggar can sometimes be a Devil Beggar and rarely a Key Master, Bomb Bum, Battery Bum, or Rotten Beggar instead.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The probabilities for each type of beggar to spawn are as follows:

• If Rotten Beggar is unlocked:

• • 61.50% Beggar

• • 33.33% Devil Beggar

• • 1.33% Battery Bum

• • 1.31% Rotten Beggar

• • 1.28% Key Master

• • 1.24% Bomb Bum

• If Rotten Beggar is not unlocked:

• • 62.75% Beggar

• • 33.33% Devil Beggar

• • 1.33% Battery Bum

• • 1.31% Key Master

• • 1.28% Bomb Bum

sections.heading: Strategy
sections.text:
• Even if Isaac is short on pickups to give to the beggars, they can still be blown up for more pickups and increased Devil Room / Angel Room chance.

• To save on bombs, it is recommended to use XX - Judgement near a tinted rock or a Secret Room's entrance, so that they can both be blown up by the same bomb.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth: Spawns two beggars. Each beggar can be any of type.

• Tarot Cloth + Blank Card: Only spawns one beggar when used with blank card.

sections.heading: Trivia

fields.name: XX - Judgement
fields.description: Spawns a Beggar near Isaac. The beggar can sometimes be a Devil Beggar and rarely a Battery Bum, Rotten Beggar, Key Master, or Bomb Bum instead.

sections.heading: Synergies

YO LISTEN!.title: YO LISTEN!
YO LISTEN!.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 luck.

• Spawns a familiar that sporadically moves around the room.

• Upon entering a room with a Secret Room/Super Secret Room entrance, tinted rock, or a rock with a Crawl Space underneath, it will fly towards it.

• If there are multiple secrets, then it will fly from one to the other.

• [Repentance] Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The familiar will sometimes hover over a pit or a Poop, indicating that an unreachable crawl space has been generated there.

• [Before Repentance] Although it might seem intuitive to dig the spot open with We Need To Go Deeper! or Ehwaz, their chance of spawning a crawl space is independent and not guaranteed to work.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a reference to the fairy Navi in the The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, who guides the player during the game with the catchphrase, "HEY, LISTEN."

• The item name and description both being “Yo listen!” is a joke about how frequently Navi interrupts the player, to the point of annoyance.

• MEAT!, YO LISTEN!, PHD, G FUEL! and TMTRAINER are the only ALL CAPS items in the game.

fields.name: YO LISTEN!
fields.description: +1 luck. Spawns a fairy familiar that points out Secret Rooms, Crawl Space entrances, and tinted rocks.

Your Soul.title: Your Soul
Your Soul.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Found Soul; Lost Soul]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants 1 free Devil Deal item in exchange for the trinket. 

• After a Devil Deal has been taken, the trinket is removed from Isaac's inventory.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Your Soul has no effect on Devil Deals that cost money instead of health, such as from Keeper's Bargain, or playing Keeper and Tainted Keeper.

• [edition rnr+] Using Your Soul as The Lost / Tainted Lost grants the possibility of taking two items from the Devil Deal instead of only one.

Yuck Heart.title: Yuck Heart

fields.description: Grants Isaac a Rotten Heart.

Yum Heart.title: Yum Heart
Yum Heart.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:

• Magdalene / Tainted Magdalene starts with this item by default.

• This item is used in The Tank and Cursed!.

Zodiac.title: Zodiac

sections.text: For a list of all zodiac signs, see Signs of the Zodiac.

• This item's appearance is a reference to the Zodiac Killer, who used the symbol as his signature.

fields.description: Gives Isaac a random zodiac item effect that changes every floor.

The Beast.title: The Beast
The Beast.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Beast is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance DLC. She appears in Home and is the final boss of Ending 22, as well as The Binding of Isaac as a whole.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
After defeating Dogma, Isaac is given Dogma, granting him flight and allowing him to traverse The Beast's 2D Crawl Space-like arena. Dogma also grants a one-time Holy Mantle shield, the effect of The Wafer (if playing in Normal Mode), prevents Isaac's speed from going under 1.1, and +2 damage, and heals him up to 6 hearts with Red Heart Containers and Soul Hearts.

At the start of the fight, The Beast sits inactive in the background. Flying around The Beast are four Ultra Harbingers, which attack Isaac one at a time in the order of Ultra Famine, Ultra Pestilence, Ultra War, and Ultra Death. Once they have all been defeated, The Beast lets out a roar, submerges into the lava, then reemerges on the right side of the screen, beginning her fight.

sections.heading: [Before Repentance+] Phase 1
sections.text:
During her first phase, The Beast uses the following sequence of attacks, repeating indefinitely:

• Charges towards Isaac, forcing the screen to scroll while harmful, destructible stalagmites and stalactites move towards Isaac.

• The screen scrolls along with The Beast, meaning that she will not get closer to Isaac even if he doesn't move; this attack only brings the stalagmites and stalactites on-screen.

• At the end of the charge, The Beast begins to inhale large rings of fire which have one small gap that Isaac can fit through.

• Any remaining stalagmites or stalactites on-screen are destroyed at the start of this attack.

• After inhaling 8 rings of fire, The Beast stops and fires a colossal Brimstone-like beam that covers the bottom and middle portions of the screen.

• After this attack, she performs a quick charge across the screen before repeating the initial charge in the opposite direction. Similar to the Brimstone-like beam directly before, she covers a large portion of the bottom and middle parts of the screen.
Even if The Beast's HP drops below the threshold for her second phase, this will always still be the first attack she performs every single time.

sections.heading: [Before Repentance+] Phase 2
sections.text:
The Beast enters her second phase below 6660 HP and loses her inhaling attack, but gains 2 new ones. Additionally, during the charging attack, there are more rocky obstacles and some stalactites are cracked and fall when Isaac passes underneath. (As before, the screen scrolls while The Beast charges, with Isaac's position on the screen being maintained.)

At the end of a charge, The Beast performs one of two attacks:

• Opens her mouth and fires 3 radial waves of slow-moving fire, then fires 6 radial strings of fast-moving projectiles which travel through the gaps left between each fire.

• Roars and spawns 4 Beast Souls which chase Isaac and charge at him, trying to predict his movements, before dissipating.

• Any remaining stalagmites or stalactites on-screen are destroyed at the start of this attack.

After using either of these attacks, The Beast submerges into the lava and causes glowing orange lines to appear beneath Isaac and in other random areas. The glow of these lines increases in intensity over time before launching out a large fiery projectile that flies up and falls back into the lava. The Beast gradually increases the rate at which projectiles are launched before eventually reemerging from the lava on the opposite end of the screen and launching a small burst of large fiery projectiles arcing in all directions.

• Any remaining stalagmites or stalactites on-screen are destroyed at the start of this attack.

sections.heading: [Repentance+] Phases 1&2
sections.text: In The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+, previous attacks from phase 1 and 2 are mixed together and not tied to HP. Phase 3 is still triggering at 33% HP.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text:
The Beast enters her third phase at 33% HP and is indicated by a burst of blood. The Beast is forced to submerge into the lava and reappear on the other side of the screen, then begins charging towards Isaac indefinitely while more stalagmites and stalactites spawn behind him. (As before, the screen scrolls while The Beast charges, with Isaac's position on the screen being maintained.) Cracked stalactites do not appear during this phase.

Once The Beast's HP reaches 2000, her horns crack and her body ruptures in boils. She degrades through two more stages: losing 2 horns and an eye upon reaching 1000 HP, and losing another eye, another horn, all of her teeth, and generally having a melted look upon reaching 500 HP. Upon defeat, a large light ray comes from above and strikes her down, followed immediately by Ending 22.

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text: Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to the players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high-damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Phase 2's narrow activation period (from 50% to 33% health) means it will often be skipped, typically if enough damage is done during the long-duration fire rings attack.

• Censer / Night Light is not recommended for this boss battle, as it can cause flames to pile up unavoidably during the Beast's fire ring inhalation attack.

• Chaos Card doesn't work on The Beast.

• If the fight is entered with a Chaos Card it will be converted to a Full Health pill

• Era Walk, "I'm Drowsy..." pill, etc. works for the duration of the fight, and makes for an easy battle.

• Sprinkler will float in the air for the duration of the flight and remains in place during the chase sequence, providing constant extra damage.

• Plan C works and will kill The Beast before dying, triggering Ending 22. It must be used after all four Ultra Harbingers are defeated, or else it will only kill the current Ultra Harbinger.

• However, if the "I'm Drowsy..." pill was used in the boss room, using Plan C would kill Isaac right before the Beast's death animation's end.

• All teleportation items/cards cannot be used to escape the fight; instead, Isaac will be teleported to a random spot on the screen. Similarly, any respawn items will respawn Isaac immediately, without restarting the fight. Essentially, there is no way to leave the fight after it has begun, outside of R Key and Forget Me Now.

• [Before Repentance+] Lil Portal is capable of creating a portal in the fight if it consumes enough pickups. Going into the portal will return Isaac to an unexplored room in Home and softlock the run as it is not possible to return to the boss fight.

• Ipecac and Haemolacria travel in an arc, similar to Ultra Pestilence's shots, and are extremely hard to aim. If Isaac has high range when firing left or right, the projectiles will go up and off-screen.

• Most non-flying familiars, such as Super Meat Boy, Leech, or Blue Spiders, are almost completely useless against the Ultra Harbingers, as the familiars will stay stuck in the lava on the bottom of the arena. However, they can damage Ultra War if his movement pattern takes him close enough to the bottom of the screen, and The Beast as she is half-submerged in lava.

• Any item that gives an effect for the room, such as Box of Friends or The Book of Belial, will work for the entire fight, starting with Ultra Famine.

• Broken Watch can affect this fight. However, it only activates for 1 unvisited room out of 4. Finishing the fight with Dogma and beginning the fight against the Ultra Harbingers counts as a new visited room. Hence, to have the effect against The Beast, the last visited room in Home must be the 3rd after the effect was triggered for the last time.

• Gnawed Leaf works as normal in this fight — as long as Isaac stays still and has some way of dealing damage without moving or firing, such as an enemy-chasing familiar. He will eventually kill The Beast with enough patience.

• Flat Stone makes tears travel straight down, as there is no ground they can skip on.

• Like Flat Stone, bombs fired with Dr. Fetus will be fired in a downward arch since there's no ground for them to slide on, making it a difficult item to use in the fight without bomb immunity items such as Pyromaniac or Host Hat.

• Defeating each Ultra Harbinger will grant Isaac's active item 2 charges, similar to Boss Rush.

• The Soul is capable of dragging The Forgotten with him as he moves. This means he can move anywhere on the screen, but at a much slower rate. Tainted Forgotten flies during this battle and stays where he ends up when thrown (in mid-air), meaning that if you throw him at the Beast you can constantly attack its during the chase scenes.

• The hitboxes of stalactites, stalagmites, and the lava persist during The Beast's death animation.

• Despite not being able to fly or go over gaps in its final form, Bumbo will be able to "fly" around the arena and deal damage without sinking in the lava. Bombs placed by Bumbo still behave normally and fall.

• Bombs are affected by gravity and are hard to hit the Ultra Harbingers with, but can easily be used against The Beast, especially during chase sequences. As such, it is a great strategy to continuously use all of your bombs during this sequence, as there is no longer any other need for them. This also makes Curse of the Tower and Anarchist Cookbook safe to use as long as Isaac does not move too close to the bottom of the screen.

• Because there are no walls or floors for tears to collide with in this fight, the damage boost from Dead Eye will not fade away.

• Items that place Poops, such as The Poop or Hallowed Ground, cannot place poops during the fight.

• However, poops will spawn if enemies are turned into poops (e. g. by E. Coli).

• The lava projectiles from both the lava and when The Beast rises afterward can be slowed and knocked down with certain slowing items such as Censer and high knockback tears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Beast is heavily based on the first Beast described in the Book of Revelation.

• The Beast's theme is called "Revelations 13-1", referencing the section in the Book of Revelation describing the first Beast.

• • A narration performed by Matthias Bossi reads the second verse of this passage during the cutscene before The Beast's fight. This narration says, "And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion: and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority."

• The Beast appears to be wearing a tattered version of Mom's dress, suggesting that it is yet another interpretation of Mom from Isaac's perspective.

• The Beast is the only boss to be preceded by an introductory cutscene rather than a VS screen.

• The cutscene depicts Isaac being crushed by a giant static cross that rises from the remains of Dogma, which turns his tears into static. Following this, the room begins collapsing, revealing a hellish cavern while Isaac sprouts a pair of wings and flickers between resembling ???, The Forgotten, and The Lost. Isaac then flies up to face The Beast rising from the lava.

• • Isaac's flickering between ???, the Forgotten, and the Lost is a reference to the events of Ending 20.

• The Beast is one of the only 2 bosses to take place in a Crawlspace-like side-scrolling environment, the other being Rotgut.

• At the end of the fight, Isaac's father refers to The Beast as "the Mother of Harlots."

• When using the "I'm Drowsy..." pill during the battle with the Ultra Harbingers, there is one extra slow sign in the position of where The Beast will be, indicating that The Beast is actually "hidden" below the lava before the Ultra Harbingers are defeated.

• Revelations 13-1 is the longest track in the entire Rebirth OST, sitting at 7 minutes and 53 seconds. This makes sense, as the theme is highly dynamic, changing depending on where the player is in the fight.

• During the section that plays while fighting The Beast, Latin chanting can be heard in the background sometimes. The chanting is "mori bestia, cum nostra lucis", which is a mistranslation of "die, Beast, to our light". A more accurate translation would be "Mori, bestia, per luce nostra".

• In Revelation, it is said that the Lord is the one who defeats The Beast, which may explain the beam of light that comes down to kill The Beast.

• In the fight's background, each of the four Harbingers can be seen doing a small animation before they fly into the foreground. Ultra Famine chuckles, Ultra Pestilence raises his fists in the air, Ultra War becomes enraged, and Ultra Death facepalms before brandishing his scythe.

• They can also be seen doing a small animation whenever Isaac takes a hit. Ultra Pestilence waves his arms and grins, Ultra War raises his arms and then "slams" them down, and Ultra Death laughs. Ultra Famine doesn't have one because he is the first Ultra Harbinger to come into battle.

• According to the game files, The Beast's boss fight takes place in Hell itself.

• Despite being in a standard fire-and-brimstone depiction of Hell, Isaac's last will still retains Home's "familiar place" location line, suggesting some level of allusion to the events of The Beast.

• Edmund McMillen has referred to the place as the Lake of Fire on Twitter.

• The Beast is confirmed to be female.

• The Beast was teased initially in a post made to Steam by Edmund 5 days before Repentance's release, which included an artwork that featured its faint silhouette in the background

• The skull of The Beast can be seen in the icon for the Dead God achievement.

• Edmund McMillen noted that the Beast sequence, along with the Tainted Characters and Dogma, was initially reserved for a possible Isaac sequel.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If the player has Knockout Drops, a sufficiently high amount of luck, and an item that fires multiple tears at once (such as Monstro's Lung), they will be capable of knocking the Ultra Harbingers far off the screen during The Beast's fight. This also occurs if the player has Strange Attractor and enough sources of tears being fired. Ocular Rift and Lodestone can provide similar effects.
Bug note: II - The High Priestess will always summon the foot on the right side of the screen, trying to target The Beast even during the fight with Ultra Harbingers. This will not deal damage to her, but can still hit enemies if they are close to the foot. Monstro's Tooth, however, works normally.
Bug note: If you get too close to The Beast during the inhaling attack, you won't be able to get out and will be stuck for the rest of the attack. This can be detrimental if you're playing Tainted Samson or The Forgotten, as The Beast will continuously deal contact damage.

The Scourge.title: The Scourge
The Scourge.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Scourge is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Corpse.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Scourge floats quickly around the room, attempting to get above Isaac's position. It can perform the following attacks:

• Shoots a large, fast cluster projectile out of its hood that homes in slightly on Isaac. When it hits a wall, it explodes into a spray of projectiles, leaving behind damaging Green Creep and a cluster of Small Maggots.

• If The Scourge is below half health, it instead shoots out three slower, smaller cluster projectiles from out of its hood that create fewer projectiles on impact.

• Launches one of its tendrils towards Isaac and embeds it in a wall. It then drags the tendril along the wall, causing projectiles, creep, and Small Maggots to shoot out from the wall.

• Launches two tendrils and embeds them into the wall, one directly at Isaac and one in the cardinal/ordinal direction opposite of him. It then starts rotating its arms around while shooting two rings of 12 projectiles outwards.

• Launches two tendrils to either side of Isaac, embedding them into the wall and trapping him in a triangle-shaped area. It will then perform one of two attacks:

• Fires walls of tight projectiles with gaps to pass through from its body. It follows up each wave with an additional, faster projectile aimed directly at Isaac.

• Fires horizontally travelling projectiles randomly out from both its left and right tendrils.

• If Isaac gets caught out of this triangle space for any reason, The Scourge will cancel this attack.

• • The three previous attacks end if The Scourge or its tendrils take enough damage. Each tendril has a total HP of 400.

• • The Scourge takes damage equal to 25% of the damage its tendrils take.

• • The tendrils passively take heavy damage if they're dragged along a wall, dealing a total of 50 damage to The Scourge for each tendril dragged.

• • The tendrils kill Small Maggots they are dragged into.

• Moves to the center of the room and begins sucking in 2 tight streams of projectiles towards it in a spiral pattern. This spiral pattern can randomly switch directions during the attack. Additional random projectiles can appear in the gap between the two streams, further limiting the space.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The Scourge is instantly killed by Meat Cleaver.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Scourge gets its name from a type of whip.

• The Scourge resembles the Snapper monster, as they both attack using long, tendril-like whips, have a bottom row of teeth, and have an eye in the middle of their mouth.

• It also resembles the Cultist monster, in terms of appearance.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Tendrils are made out of many separate entities resulting in items that activate upon enemies dying, such as Hungry Soul or Infestation 2, to trigger multiple times at once.
