Rotten Tomato.title: Rotten Tomato
Rotten Tomato.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a chance to fire tears that mark enemies with the Bait status effect. Enemies marked as bait will move slower and be attacked by other enemies until it is killed or the effect wears off.

• Tears that apply the effect are red.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The chance to fire marking tears depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \frac1 { 6 - \left \lceil \mathit{Luck} \right \rceil}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 16.67%, maxing out at 100% at 4.01 luck.

• Causes pathing issues with segmented bosses, as they attempt to attack their own segments.

• Most enemies will ignore Isaac in order to attack a baited enemy, making Rotten Tomato an item with both offensive and defensive applications.

• With a high enough luck stat and piercing effects, the uptime of the bait effect can be enough to render some bosses harmless, such as Ultra Pestilence or The Duke of Flies who spawn a multitude of flies that it will then focus on.

• This item is very effective during Boss Rush. Boss enemies affected by this item will deal massive amounts of damage to each other and Isaac will be less likely to get hurt by their attacks.

• Due to the nature of Mother's hitbox, the bait effect will cause Mother to often shoot herself in her second phase causing a lot of her attacks to be nullified.

• Enemies and entities normally non-affected by status effects like the Stone Grimace or Red Fire Place will target the baited enemies.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Brimstone: Firing can mark enemies as bait.

• Dr. Fetus: Fired bombs can mark enemies as bait.

• Jacob's Ladder: Chaining electricity arcs can mark enemies as bait.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Rotten Tomato is from the Antibirth mod.

• It is likely a reference to the act of throwing rotten tomatoes at a bad performance.

• Rotten Tomato is the only item that grants the bait status effect reliably, even if it can also be obtained by rainbow tears items like Playdough Cookie

• The bait effect is the inverse of the charmed effect; a charmed enemy would seek to target any other enemies, a baited enemy will be targeted by all other enemies.

• The tomato dripping from Isaac's mouth with this item's costume will leave red stains on the ground. This is entirely visual; it does not create Creep.

fields.description: Adds a chance to fire tears that mark enemies with the Bait status effect. Enemies marked as bait are attacked by other enemies.

Rubber Cement.title: Rubber Cement
Rubber Cement.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Ipecac]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Makes tears bounce off walls, enemies and environmental objects.

• Tears that bounce off of enemies bounce in random directions, whereas tears that bounce off of walls and other objects bounce directly back.

• When tears bounce from enemies, they become able to hit the same enemy again should they bounce off of another enemy or obstacle.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Tears bounce off bombs and are unable to push them, making Troll Bombs more difficult to deal with.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Tears will bounce off of walls while fighting The Beast, despite the lack of visible walls.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] Brimstone: The blood laser bounces off of walls, creating a second beam that deals half damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] Azazel's Brimstone laser becomes a full length laser after bouncing, but will deal half of the damage.

• • [Afterbirth+ onward] Azazel's Brimstone no longer becomes a full length laser after bouncing, and instead bounce as a regular mini-Brimstone.

• A Lump of Coal: Both effects stack, with tears that bounce off of enemies being able to hit others for more damage.

• The Parasite: Tears will bounce off of walls without splitting, but split and bounce when hitting enemies. The split tears and the original one will bounce off everything.

• Pop!: Significantly increases the uptime of tears, since they are not limited by range and each tear will bounce off of each other. Continuously firing tears will eventually create a positive feedback loop, as the tears will keep bouncing faster and faster while not dropping to the floor.

• Pop! + A Lump of Coal: Extremely powerful combination; Lump of Coal's tear size increase will make it much easier for tears to bounce off of each other, while they increase in damage very rapidly. Given some time and enough tears, this can kill even final bosses such as Hush and Delirium quickly.

• [Afterbirth onward] Technology / Technology 2 / Tech.5: Laser bounces off walls, creating a second beam that does half damage.

• Tech X: The laser rings bounce off walls.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Rebirth only] Brimstone: Overrides Rubber Cement.

• Bob's Rotten Head: The bomb bounces back upon hitting an obstacle, and will not explode until it runs out of air time. Not recommended, as it can make self-damage more likely in small rooms.

• Continuum: Overridden by Rubber Cement; tears will still bounce off of walls and obstacles.

• Dr. Fetus: Overrides Rubber Cement.

• Epic Fetus: Overrides Rubber Cement.

• The Forgotten: No effect on the skeleton form's attacks.

• Homing tears: Tears will bounce off enemies and home back in, but to deal damage to that enemy again they must bounce off a different object.

• Ipecac: Tears will bounce off of obstacles, but not enemies.

• Jacob's Ladder: Tears don't generate arcs when hitting obstacles.

• Lost Contact: Tears will bounce off of enemy tears. Not recommended unless the player's fire rate is high, as it can prove detrimental when trying to hit a shooting enemy.

• The Ludovico Technique: Overrides Rubber Cement.

• Mom's Knife: Overrides Rubber Cement.

• Piercing tears: Tears that don't destroy enemies will bounce off of them instead of going straight through them. Tears can still damage enemies such as Knights that are normally invulnerable from the front.

• [Repentance] Tears regain the ability to push bombs.

• Sinus Infection: Boogers stick to enemies, but otherwise they bounce normally.

• Spectral tears: Overridden by Rubber Cement.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Tears pass through obstacles but bounce off walls.

• Sulfuric Acid: Overridden by Rubber Cement.

• [Rebirth only] Technology / Technology 2: Overrides Rubber Cement.

• Tiny Planet: Tears no longer fly over obstacles but instead bounce very quickly along with them, appearing to "vibrate".

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Tears pass through obstacles but coast along walls, trying to maintain the circular trajectory.

• Trisagion: Tears no longer bounce off of enemies but will still bounce off of walls and obstacles.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The item's appearance is loosely based off Elmer's Glue brand Rubber Cement.

Rules Card.title: Rules Card
Rules Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon activation, displays one of the following messages:

| CHUB DISLIKES SMOKE! | Referencing the trick in which Isaac can drop a Bomb in front of a charging Chub to have her swallow it. Reference to Zelda 1 and 'DODONGO DISLIKES SMOKE'. 
| A PIECE OF PAPER IS YOUR GUIDE | Possibly refers to the Missing Poster or, the choice between The Polaroid and The Negative after defeating Mom or the card itself.

| THE WALLS WILL HARDEN OVER TIME. TIME IS THE ESSENCE | Presumably referencing the Boss Rush that occurs if Mom is beaten in under 20 minutes, and/or the Hush fight that is accessible if Mom's Heart or It Lives! is beaten in under 30 minutes.

| A DARK MARKET LIES UNDER YOUR FEET | Presumably referencing the secret trapdoors occasionally under rocks and the Crawl Space that leads Isaac to the Black Market, a room which sells Shop items for Hearts rather than Coins.

| SOME DOORS REQUIRE A BLESSING. CARRY THEM WITH YOU | Refers to how to open the large golden door on Chest and the Dark Room and fight Mega Satan, by gathering two Key Pieces from the Angels.

| DENY HIS GIFTS TO ATTAIN YOUR REWARD | References how skipping a Devil Room gives the chance to gain access to the Angel Room.

| SLEEPING GATEKEEPERS WILL NEED TO BE AWOKEN WITH A LOUD SOUND | Possibly referencing how Isaac can use bombs on the Angel statues in order to awaken them. Reference to Zelda 1.

| ROOMS MAY YIELD MORE THAN YOU EXPECT. EXPERIMENTATION IS KEY | Unknown, possibly referencing Secret Rooms or the trapdoor and bed in Isaac's room, or tinted rocks and other breakable objects.

One of the following Seeds may also be displayed:

Rune Bag.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Rune Bag having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

sections.heading: Synergies

Rune Shard.title: Rune Shard
Rune Shard.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Activates a random, weakened rune effect:

• Algiz grants a 3 second shield.

• Ansuz reveals the map up to 3 rooms away (including Ultra Secret Room).

• Berkano:

• • [Before Repentance+] Gives 1 blue fly and spider.

• • [Repentance+] Gives 1 standard Abyss locust for the room.

• Dagaz gives a Half Soul Heart.

• Ehwaz makes a trapdoor.

• Hagalaz destroys some rocks.

• Jera duplicates one pickup.

• Perthro rerolls one item.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Rune shard is a placeholder for rune spawns on a save file that doesn't have all runes unlocked yet. Once 6 runes of any kind (including soul stones) are available, Rune Shards cease to spawn.

• Before Repentance, unlocking only one rune would make all runes the same one. This exploit that incentivized against completion was fixed with the rune shard.

• The Jera effect activated by Rune Shards is similar to D1 - it can create a variant of the pickup rather than its exact copy.

• The Perthro effect from Rune Shards has a chance to reroll an item into The Poop (ignoring item pools).

• The Ehwaz effect can still create Crawl Space entrances if used on a floor element.

• The three most valuable rune effects from Blank Rune are Perthro, for a re-roll, Jera for copying one drop, or Ehwaz for a Crawl Space which has a high chance of containing a free item. Therefore, the best use of Blank Rune is in a room with an item, after dropping a Trinket, Rune or Card on the floor, while standing over a tile with a special graphic.

fields.name: Rune Shard

Sack Head.title: Sack Head
Sack Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Pennys have a 10% chance to be replaced with Grab Bags. Bombs, Keys, Cards, Runes, and Lil' Battery have a 20% chance.

• This includes pickups spawned by most sources: room rewards, chests, slot machines, special shopkeepers, Greed Mode waves, etc.

• [Repentance] Coins bombed out of a Donation Machine can become sacks.

• The exception to this are pickups spawned by Isaac himself directly, e.g. with the likes of IV Bag or Fanny Pack, and contents of other sacks.

• Spawns a sack upon pickup.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The item does not replace hearts, pills and chests.

• The item can also replace Troll Bombs and Mega Troll Bombs that are not used as attacks, i.e. generated as room rewards, chest contents and such.

• The pickup replacement is applied retroactively when the item is collected: any appropriate pickup already existing on the current level may be replaced by a sack.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Sacks on each floor tend to have the same contents, which can be taken advantage of if cards are involved.

• [Repentance] Picking up a Golden Penny may spawn a sack instead of another Golden Penny.

• Cracked Key in the Ascent can be replaced by a sack, thus it is not recommended to take the item if you're going to unlock a tainted character.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Equality!: Sacks may drop new sacks while Equality! is active, potentially resulting in massive amounts of resources from a single sack.

• Head of the Keeper: Coins spawned from hitting enemies have a chance to become sacks.

• Tainted Keeper: The coins dropped from killing enemies have a chance to be sacks instead. The sacks do not flash and disappear.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The appearance given by the item is most likely based on one of the trailers for Rebirth, where several naked people are wearing sacks with crying eyes, strikingly similar to Sack Head.

• May also reference the character Sack Boy from the Little Big Planet game series.

fields.description: Spawns a Grab Bag on pickup. Pennys, Bombs, Keys, cards, runes and batteries have a chance to become Grab Bags.

The Scooper.title: The Scooper
The Scooper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Summons The Peeper for the current room, which also leaves a trail of red creep.

• The Peeper deals 12 contact damage per tick (36 per second) and the creep it trails deals 2 damage per tick (20 per second).

• The Peeper can block enemy shots.

• All tears shot from the right eye will deal 35% more damage, same as with The Peeper affecting the left eye.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns white-glowing eyeball wisps on the middle ring. They function the same as normal wisps.

• Car Battery: Will summon 2 peepers in a bifurcated direction.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Scooper originates from the Antibirth mod where it acts similarly but doesn't grant damage to all tears shot from the right eye.

• The pickup quote for The Scooper is the same as the one for The Peeper.

fields.description: Summons The Peeper for the current room, which leaves a trail of red creep.

The Shell.title: The Shell
The Shell.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Shell is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in the Ashpit.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Shell always spawns in a pair consisting of 4 body segments and a head segment each. They are always fought in a double-sized room.

• Flies around the room diagonally, bouncing off of walls while dealing contact damage; behaving identically to The Hollow.

• Unlike the Hollow, however, if Isaac is close to the vicinity of its head, it veers slightly in Isaac's direction.

• Normally invincible, but bombs and explosives can destroy its bony exterior (after 15 damage per segment), making its segments vulnerable. There are always one or two Bomb Grimaces that dispense Throwable Bombs for Isaac to use against The Shell.

• When the armor on their body is destroyed, the exposed flesh segments lose the ability to fly, and will spawn Fly Bombs if the segment is at the very end, or shoot a volley of three shots at Isaac if the segment is in the middle.

• The Shell moves slower if there are exposed flesh segments attached to its head.

• If a group of conjoined flesh segments have been detached from the head, they chase directly after Isaac at a very slow pace and continue to attack normally.

• If a single flesh segment has been completely detached, it becomes stationary but continues to spawn Fly Bombs.

• The Shell cannot split into smaller copies; when split down the middle, the side containing 3 segments with at least one of end segments having armor turns into a new copy of the boss with one of the armored body segments turning into a head segment.

• Flesh body segments on the shorter side detach and behave normally but armored body segments are automatically destroyed.

• The Shell's head cannot be damaged or destroyed and dies once it loses all its segments.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Terra can destroy the The Shells' armor, along with any items that create rock waves like Mega Bean and Wait What?.

• [Repentance+] Hagalaz will also remove their armor on use.

• Sulfuric Acid tears cannot destroy their armor.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• They appear to be a bony variation of The Hollow.

• They appear to be the posthumous version of the Tuff Twins. This makes them one of four boss pairs to have their regular and posthumous version in the same chapter, the others being Gemini having Blighted Ovum in Chapter 1, Chub having Carrion Queen in Chapter 2 and Polycephalus having The Stain in Chapter 2.

The Small Rock.title: The Small Rock
The Small Rock.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 damage.

• -0.2 speed ( [Before Afterbirth+] not applied until the next time Isaac's speed stat is updated or upon taking damage).

• [Before Repentance] -0.2 maximum speed.

• +0.2 tears ( [Before Afterbirth+] not applied until the next time Isaac's tears stat is updated or upon taking damage).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Has a small chance to be dropped from a destroyed tinted rock.

• Normally only appears once per run, but can appear again if Isaac's items are re-rolled with D4, D100, or a Dice Room.

• [Before Repentance] Always has a chance to spawn as long as Isaac does not currently have it. This includes the possibility of spawning and obtaining multiple copies of The Small Rock on the same floor if not picked up the first time.

• Taking the rock in the Boss Rush from a tinted rock in the room will count as taking an item and consequently trigger Boss Rush. The other items do not disappear and will stay until one is picked up.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Diplopia/Crooked Penny: Additional copies grant an additional tears up and speed down with no further increase in damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is likely a reference to the biblical story of David and Goliath, where David kills the giant known as Goliath with a small rock.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, Isaac's tears would take on a grey color after Small Rock has been picked up. In Rebirth, however, the tears are red.

• However, before the Halloween Update, the player’s tears were blood tears. The reasoning for the change from blood to grey is unknown.

• This item is used in Head Trauma.

• Head Trauma is unlocked by default, despite the fact that Small Rock isn't.

The Soul.title: The Soul
The Soul.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the character; The Soul (character)]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants two Soul Hearts.

• Isaac gains a pulsing blue aura that repels enemies and projectiles.

• The power of the repel force alternates in strength at random, sometimes strong enough to counter a projectile well before it hits Isaac, sometimes only strong enough to slow it down.

• Ground-based enemies will overcome the counterforce easier than flying enemies and projectiles.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] A stronger effect of this item is given temporarily by I - The Magician?.

• [Repentance] When playing as Tainted Forgotten, this item works only on the Forgotten's body and not the soul.

• [Repentance] When playing as Tainted Jacob, Dark Esau is unaffected by this item's repelling properties.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item, along with The Body and The Mind, are references to the Three Primes of Alchemy.

• The designs of these items appear to be that of Triquetra, a Christian symbol of the Trinity.

• The item's description, along with those of The Body and The Mind, are references to the three attributes commonly ascribed to God in Christian theology: omniscience, omnipotence, and omnipresence. For The Soul, it is omnipotence, the ability to do anything, which follows naturally from the ability to "be all".

fields.description: Grants two Soul Hearts. Isaac gains a pulsing aura that repels enemies and projectiles.

The Stain.title: The Stain
The Stain.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Stain is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 2 (Caves, Catacombs, Flooded Caves).

• [Repentance] Only in the Caves and the Flooded Caves. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Stain burrows underground when Isaac is not within range. While burrowed it becomes invincible and follows Isaac's movements. When close to Isaac, it pops out and performs one of the following attacks:

• Sends out 2 patterns of numerous projectiles in all directions. The first barrage consists of fast-moving bullets that slow down. The second barrage consists of slow-moving bullets that speed up.

• Sends out tendrils to its left and right leaving small puddles of damaging Red Creep directly around The Stain and to its either side.

• Spawns 2 Chargers and can have a maximum of 3.
It will stay vulnerable for a brief moment after performing an attack before quickly burrowing underground again.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 2] : Continuously spawns 2 Round Worms instead of Chargers, with a maximum of 3 at any time. Never fires barrages of bullets.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It is the posthumous version of Polycephalus. It appears that the top heads have been stripped of their skin, while the bottom head only lacks its first skin layer.

• Unlike its alive counterpart, the lower head has closed eyes and eyelids.

• As of Repentance, the Stain is more common in terms of floor variants than Polycephalus, since it can appear in the Caves and the Flooded Caves, whereas Polycephalus can only appear in the Catacombs. This means that the player is more likely to encounter the Stain than Polycephalus, despite the Stain being a posthumous version of it.

• The Stain has an alternative more degraded variation known as The Pile.

• A third head can be seen in the background in The Stain's boss art.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Prior to Booster Pack #5, The Stain could spawn Drowned Chargers if it was fought in the Flooded Caves.

• During the versus screen, The Stain's popping out sound can be heard. The Stain is one of [Before Repentance] seven/ [Repentance] five bosses that can be heard in the versus screen; the other are The Forsaken, Big Horn, Mom, [Before Repentance] Mom's Heart, [Before Repentance] It Lives!, and Mother.

The Stairway.title: The Stairway
The Stairway.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• At the start of every floor, generates a ladder which leads to a special Angel Room Shop, regardless of whether a devil deal has been taken. These angel shops always contain the following:

• Three items/pickups for sale. These items/pickups can be on sale, just like with normal Shops.

• • An item from the Angel Room Item Pool for 15 or 30 pennies.

• • An Eternal Heart for 5 pennies.

• • A Soul Heart for 5 pennies.

• • A Key for 5 pennies.

• • A Holy Card for 5 pennies.

• An Angel statue. The Angel can be fought for a Key Piece like normal.

• A normal [machine: Beggar] or [machine: Rotten Beggar] next to the entrance.

• A [machine: Confessional] , if it has been unlocked.

• The ladder to the angel room disappears if Isaac leaves the starting room, regardless of whether Isaac has climbed it or not.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Layouts can be found here.

• The following items cost 30 coins to purchase:

• The ladder disappears after save-quitting.

• Weight decrementation in the generated shops is the same as in regular Angel Rooms, so if an item is seen in the special shop, it won't be encountered regularly again for the rest of the run.

• During the Ascent, ladders will generate in the "starting rooms" (where light beams are located) on every floor.

• The same does not apply during Backasswards, in which the item simply has no effect.

• The ladder will appear in the Mirrored World in the starting room, and will lead to the same shop.

• Rerolled items in the room will be taken from the Angel Room pool.

• Since a beggar always spawns immediately to the right of the entrance way, caution should be taken to avoid accidental donation.

• If a run is started with The Stairway, i.e. playing as Eden or having collected Eden's Blessing, the ladder will not appear on the first floor.

• In Greed mode, the ladder does not go away when pressing the button to start the waves. This means money can be gathered from the waves before entering the Stairway shop.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Adoption Papers: Does not affect the Angel shop.

• Coupon / Credit Card / Mr. ME!: Can be used to obtain items for free.

• Death Certificate: An additional ladder will spawn in one room of the Death Certificate area. This ladder leads to the same Angel Shop as the one in the starting room of the floor. Purchasing an item will remove Isaac from the Death Certificate area as though he had collected an item normally. Sometimes, the ladder will spawn directly on top of an item pedestal, making the Angel Shop impossible to enter without collecting that item and subsequently being removed from the area.

• Keeper's Sack: Buying items grants stats, same as with other shops.

• A Pound of Flesh: Makes Angel Shops cost health just like regular Shops.

• Restock / Store Credit: No effect in the Angel shop.

• Steam Sale: Reduces the prices of the items on offer.

• Glowing Hourglass: When used in the Angel shop, uses all three charges and removes the ladder.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item was originally called Jacob's Ladder in the Antibirth mod but was changed to avoid confusion between this item and the existing Jacob's Ladder. In Antibirth, the ladder would take Isaac to a regular Angel Room instead of a unique Angel Shop, however using the ladder prevented an Angel or Devil Room from appearing after fighting the boss. The ladder would also not disappear when Isaac left the starting room.

• The name is a reference to The Book of Genesis from the Old Testament. In Genesis 28:10-19 Jacob rested on his journey and had a dream; in the dream, he saw a ladder that served as the connection between Heaven and Earth.

• This item's name and its flavor text are a reference to the Led Zeppelin song "Stairway to Heaven."

fields.quote: May you get what you came for
fields.description: Generates a ladder at the start of every floor that leads to a unique Angel Room shop.

The Swarm.title: The Swarm
The Swarm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives eight orbital flies when picked up.

• Each time a fly blocks a projectile, it will turn into a blue fly.

• Each time a room is cleared, spawns an orbital fly.

• The maximum number of orbital flies Isaac can have is 16.

• Contributes to the Beelzebub transformation.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room from the one he is currently in (such as by teleporting to the previous room then using it again) will duplicate orbital flies. Obtaining orbital flies by duplicating them can surpass the item's normal orbital limit.

fields.description: Spawns eight orbital flies, which turn into Blue Flies after they block a shot. Each time a room is cleared, spawns another orbital fly.

The Twins.title: The Twins
The Twins.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a 50% chance to duplicate one of Isaac's familiars when entering a new room.

• If Isaac has no familiars, spawns Brother Bobby or Sister Maggy instead.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This trinket has a 1% chance to drop when defeating The Horny Boys. [end edition note] 

• The following items/trinkets cannot be duplicated:

• ???'s Soul

• [Repentance+] 1up!

• Abyss / Apollyon's Best Friend’s unique attack locusts

• Dead Bird

• Dead Cat

• The Intruder

• Isaac's Head

• Isaac's Heart

• Giant Cell

• Halo of Flies / Pretty Flies

• Lost Soul

• Milk!

• Quints

• Spin to Win

• Stitches

• The Swarm

• Umbilical Cord

• Vanishing Twin

• Any temporary familiars, including those from Monster Manual

• The duplication chance reoccurs when starting a room, even when starting a room by exiting to the main menu and re-entering.

• This allows quitting to the menu to be an effective method to cycle for a specific duplicated familiar.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box / The Twins: Each copy grants an additional 50% chance to trigger the effect again. This results in another familiar doubling. This can be the same familiar that was doubled originally. The duplication chance of three or more stacks can go above 100% allowing for even more duplicate familiars or Brother Bobbys/Sister Maggys to be created.

• Sacrificial Altar: Both the duplicated familiar (if one is available) and Brother Bobby/Sister Maggy (if not available) can be sacrificed for an item reward. This does not remove the trinket, and fully retains its effect.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Movement-mimicking familiars: Duplicated familiars will follow the original on the same delay.

• In the case of Shade, a copy of the familiar will spawn even if Shade was already absorbed by Isaac.

• Pickup-generating familiars: If they remain duplicated for enough consecutive rooms, they will give a pickup as normal. The following familiars have to be duplicated for the following number of consecutive room clears to give pickups:

• Sack of Pennies: 1 room (will give a coin every time it’s duplicated)

• Bomb Bag / Little C.H.A.D.: 2 rooms

• Mystery Sack / Rune Bag / Sack of Sacks: 5 rooms

• Acid Baby: 6 rooms

• The Relic: 7 rooms

• • Because Lil Chest and Charged Baby’s chances to spawn pickups are independent from the total number of rooms cleared with them, they have an extra chance to pay out in any room they’re duplicated in.

• [Before Repentance+] 1up!: Despite the fact that it can be duplicated, Isaac will not keep the 1up if he dies while it's duplicated.

• [Repentance+] No longer attempts to duplicate 1up!.

• Bum Friend / Bumbo / Dark Bum / Key Bum / Lil Portal: The pickup count of duplicated familiars is not remembered when they go away.

• Ball of Bandages / Cube of Meat: Upgrades the familiar instead of duplicating it.

• Best Bud / Bird Cage: If the trinket tries to duplicate it, it will instead immediately activate. Taking damage does not spawn another familiar.

• If this happens to Bird Cage as Isaac walks into a room with enemies, Bird Cage will also leap onto the enemies.

• Blood Puppy / Bumbo / Guppy's Hairball: The duplicate will always be at its first stage.

• Buddy in a Box: The duplicated familiar will be randomly generated instead of copying the original.

• Cambion Conception / Immaculate Conception: Familiars given by these items can be duplicated as normal.

• GB Bug: The familiar can be duplicated even if it hasn’t respawned; by constantly moving to new rooms, GB Bug can constantly respawn, allowing pickups to be rerolled indefinitely.

• Guillotine: The head can be duplicated, and will give an extra damage and tears up if it is. The extra head will be unable to fire tears.

• Hallowed Ground: Duplicate poops will also drop when Isaac takes damage. The bonuses from standing in the aura of multiple white poops does not stack.

• [Before Repentance+] Lost Soul / Star of Bethlehem / Strawman: The trinket can try to make a duplicate of the familiar, but it will always fail. This reduces the odds of the trinket giving copies of other familiars or prevents it from giving Brother Bobby or Sister Maggy if Isaac has no other familiars.

• [Repentance+] The trinket will not attempt to duplicate these familiars, and will correctly spawn the default Brother Bobby/Sister Maggy if Isaac does not have other familiars.

• Mystery Egg: The friendly the duplicated egg spawns depends on how many consecutive rooms cleared the duplicate persisted for.

• Succubus: The damage multiplier from standing in the aura of multiple Succubi multiplicatively stacks.

• YO LISTEN!: An extra +1 luck will be given for every duplicate.

sections.text: • The Binding of Isaac Item Trigger Testing

The Virus.title: The Virus
The Virus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Inflicts poison on enemies who make contact with Isaac.

• [Rebirth only] The poison deals 2 damage per tick (3 damage per second) and lasts for 2-3 ticks.

• [Afterbirth only] The poison deals Isaac's damage per tick (1.5x Isaac's damage per second) and lasts for 2-3 ticks.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The poison deals Isaac's damage per tick (1.5x Isaac's damage per second) and lasts for 6 ticks for normal enemies and 3 ticks for bosses.

• [Repentance] The poison lasts for 6-7 ticks and deals damage equal to (0.2*HeartContainers^2) + 2, where HeartContainers is the total number of heart containers and Bone Hearts Isaac has. [end edition note] 

• • The poison can be continuously applied to bosses, which normally are immune to status effects for a brief time after being inflicted with one.

• [Repentance] Lets Isaac deal 12 contact damage per tick on top of applying poison (24 damage per second).

• [edition anr] Enemies who are killed after they have been inflicted with this type of poison have a 20% chance to drop Black Hearts.

• [Before Repentance] -0.1 speed down.

• [Rebirth only] This is not applied until the next time Isaac's speed stat is updated.

• [Repentance] +0.2 speed up.

• Contributes to the Spun transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item can drop from killing Lust. [Before Repentance] Lust can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. 

• Taking another copy of The Virus:

• [Rebirth only] results in a speed down with no benefit.

• [Afterbirth onward] does not affect Isaac.

• [Repentance] counts as two items towards the Spun transformation.

• [edition anr] The black heart is only dropped if the poison was caused by The Virus. The item's effect doesn't extend to poison tears.

• [edition anr] If an enemy doesn't do contact damage, The Virus can safely be applied to it for more chances at black hearts. Fly, Mulligans, and Hosts are the most common enemies this can be applied to.

• [edition anr] With Skatole, Hives and Swarmers will constantly spawn normal Flies, meaning they can be endless sources of Black Hearts.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Although Stoney and Shopkeepers can't be visibly poisoned, they still can drop Black Hearts if destroyed after being touched.

• Enemies won't start taking poison damage if they are pushing up against Isaac; The Virus will be constantly trying to apply poison and refreshing the ticks where poison damage would occur.

• [edition anr] Gnawed Leaf and The Virus can still work if Isaac has a short-range orbital such as Cube of Meat or Ball of Bandages, as it will kill enemies pushing against Isaac that are not taking poison damage while still dropping Black Hearts.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb The Virus it turns into a green locust that poisons enemies.

• Invulnerability: Contact while invincible poisons enemies.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • [Before Repentance] Odd Mushroom (Large): The speed down from the Virus does not stack with the Odd Mushroom; if both are collected, only a total of -0.1 applies.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Little Baggy]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Upon picking up The Virus, Isaac looks very similar to Lust, which is fitting since Lust also drops The Virus.

• As such, The Virus may be a reference to an STI.

fields.description: Isaac poisons enemies on contact. [Before Repentance] -0.1 speed. [Repentance] +0.2 speed. [edition anr] Poisoned enemies have a chance to drop a black heart when killed.

The Visage.title: The Visage
The Visage.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Visage is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Repentance that can appear in Gehenna.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
The Visage is bound together by a chain and cannot be damaged; the chain must first be destroyed to progress the fight, and has 150 HP. During this phase, it only has one attack:

• The heart slowly wanders around the room, and the mask attempts to move toward Isaac, constrained by the length of its chain (which reaches up to 4 tiles outward). Occasionally, the mask charges at Isaac when he approaches it from any cardinal direction, predicting his movements. Upon colliding with a wall, the mask launches out a spray of rock projectiles before being pulled back to the heart.

• The mask cannot charge if it’s close to Isaac.

• The chain only extends for this attack, it's normally rigid and constrains the mask and the heart to a specific length.

• If the mask hasn’t charged in a while, it starts pulling the heart with it in its attempt to reach Isaac.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Once the chain is broken, the mask and heart are unbound from each other and their behavior changes:

• The mask freely moves around the room, briefly speeding up and chasing Isaac if it sees him in a cardinal direction.

• The mask has 100 HP, and can be damaged by explosions, piercing shots, or by being shot in its open back. Upon death it deactivates, which stops it from moving, dealing contact damage to Isaac, or from firing certain projectiles when used by the heart. However, it can still block Isaac's tears.

• The heart now actively avoids Isaac, but also uses a chain to perform a variety of attacks in conjunction with the mask:

• Launches a chain to the mask. Once attached, it directly pulls the mask in and fires a horizontal helix of Brimstone lasers that pushes both backwards into a wall.

• • The lasers and pushback don’t happen if the mask is deactivated.

• Launches a chain to the mask. Once attached, it swings the mask around in a spiral while also bringing the two closer. The mask fires red projectiles outward while being reeled in. If the mask collides with wall before it unites with the heart, it creates rock projectiles on impact and is then pulled directly to the heart.

• • The mask doesn’t fire projectiles while being reeled in if it’s deactivated.

• Launches a chain to the mask. Once attached, it directly pulls the mask in and then jumps onto Isaac's position, creating a burst of rock projectiles as well as 4 rock waves in the diagonal directions upon landing.

• Launches a chain at Isaac. If the chain hits him, it pulls him into the heart, causing him to take contact damage. If the chain misses, it pulls the heart into the wall it hits, creating a burst of rocks and red projectiles. This attack can only be used if the mask is deactivated, and takes higher priority once it becomes available.

• • Unlike all other attacks, the chain directly hitting Isaac doesn’t deal damage, only him being pulled into the heart does.

• • If the chain hits a bomb while being launched, the bomb instantly explodes and the attack is cancelled.

sections.heading: Phase 3
sections.text:
When the heart drops to half HP, its visual outer shell breaks, exposing the heart. The Heart's movement becomes quicker and more erratic along with an attack change:

• Launches a large, slow-moving energy ball known as Visage Plasma in a diagonal direction that bounces off of walls. If this projectile touches the mask, it fires a Brimstone laser out its back, rapidly propelling it in the direction it was facing and creating rock projectiles and a radial burst of 8 projectiles upon collision with a wall.

• If the mask is deactivated, Visage Plasma will automatically travel towards it, reviving it as well as causing its normal effect.

• Visage Plasma have 50 HP, and can be destroyed by Isaac.

• The heart always begins the phase with this attack.

• Briefly stops moving and fires out a ring of 16 red projectiles.

• If there are 3 Visage Plasma floating around the room, the heart sucks them in, drawing in Isaac in the process. Each Visage Plasma absorbed heals the heart a small portion of HP. After absorbing all 3, it fires out 4 tight rings of fire along with 4 short-range diagonal Brimstone lasers.

• The mask deactivates during this attack, regardless of its HP. Unless the heart is on a far side of the room and Isaac is far away enough, Isaac must hide behind the mask to dodge this attack, as the rings of fire are too dense to weave through.
Once the heart has been killed, the mask permanently deactivates.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The Visage's deactivated mask can be still targeted by effects such as Anima Sola.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Visage started as a boss versus screen mockup by Antibirth artist NotYourSagittarius in January 2015, alongside Reap Creep and a scrapped posthumous version of Dingle known as "The Mass".

• The Visage appears to be a fiery variation of the Mask of Infamy.

• In a way, it can be seen as the posthumous version of the Mask of Infamy.

• The Visage in Antibirth bore a grey and purple color palette better suited for the Mausoleum, while the Visage in Repentance has been recolored black and red to match the Gehenna floor.

• Prior to patch V1.7.5, many of its attacks were still purple.

• The back of the mask shows many small children being burned while the mask is alive.

• This is probably a reference to the fact that in Gehenna, some kings of Judah sacrificed their children by fire.

• In Antibirth, instead of many children, there was a singular Isaac head in the back of the mask.

• This is a reference to the original Mask of Infamy from the Wrath Of The Lamb DLC of the original flash game, as it had a small head peeking through the crack behind the boss.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using the console to spawn the mask by itself (id 903.1) will crash the game. All other parts of the Visage can be spawned safely.
Bug note: If a slash from Dark Arts / Soul of Judas reduces the mask's hp to 0, it will die and despawn instead of deactivating, leaving only the heart to be fought.
Bug note: If The Visage's mask is chained by Anima Sola down when it runs out of HP, it will outright die instead of becoming temporarily inactive, leaving only the heart to be fought.
Bug note: If The Visage's mask is defeated by knockback damage from Hemoptysis or Knockout Drops, it will outright die instead of becoming temporarily inactive.

The Wafer.title: The Wafer
The Wafer.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Most damage taken is reduced to half a heart.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The damage reduction includes most sources in the game that would cause more than half a heart of damage:

• Bombs.

• Most Champions.

• • The exceptions being the skull and large champions - damage from them is reduced from two full hearts to one.

• Sacrifice Rooms.

• Environmental hazards such as Spikes.

• Most self-inflicting damage items (exceptions are noted).

• Every source of damage in Womb/Utero/Scarred Womb and beyond, including all enemies, Curse Rooms, Blood Donation Machines, and Devil Beggars.

• The "HARD HARD" special seed.

• [Repentance] The Wafer does not reduce damage from opening the door to Mausoleum / Gehenna. [end edition note] 

• Despite The Wafer reducing damage to 1/2 a heart, this does not change the amount of invincibility frames granted from full/two heart damage sources.

• The Wafer is substantially less useful in Greed Mode, since Chapter 4 and beyond does not increase damage taken like usual.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Blood Oath: Does not reduce the damage taken.

• [Repentance] Glass Cannon: The extra damage taken when the cannon breaks is not reduced. [end edition note] 

• Sharp Plug: [edition alternatives: baseline: Damage taken is reduced to half a heart.; Repentance: Does not reduce the damage taken.] 

• Keeper / Tainted Keeper: No effect as Coin Hearts cannot be reduced to half.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, "resistance" in the pickup quote was misspelled as "resistence". This was corrected in Rebirth.

• A wafer is a thin cake made of flour and is used in Christianity for various purposes, including the sacrament of the Eucharist, in which believers consume the body (represented by sacramental bread) and blood (represented by sacramental wine) of Jesus Christ.

• In the original The Binding of Isaac, The Wafer required an unlock, by beating Mom's Heart seven times.

fields.description: Most sources of damage that would cause more than one-half heart of damage are reduced to one-half heart instead.

The Wiz.title: The Wiz
The Wiz.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac fires tears from both eyes at the same time.

• Isaac's tears are fired diagonally outwards, similar to the effect of the R U a Wizard? pill.

• Isaac's tears become spectral.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Reap Creep. [end edition note] 

• The maximum amount of tears per volley that can be reached by combining and/or duplicating 20/20, The Inner Eye, Mutant Spider and The Wiz is 16.

• [Repentance] The Wiz's quality is considered 1 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 20/20 / Conjoined: Fires 2 tears in both diagonal directions.

• [Before Repentance] Diplopia/Crooked Penny: Each additional copy of The Wiz will make Isaac fire two more tears in a wider diagonal layout.

• [Repentance] Each additional copy of The Wiz will make Isaac fire one extra tear, starting with one tear fired forwards.

• Eye of the Occult: Both tears shoot much closer together and can be controlled, creating for a better double shot similar to what Tractor Beam would grant.

• The Inner Eye/Keeper: Fires 2 tears to both diagonal directions with a wider spread.

• Mutant Spider /Tainted Keeper: Fires 3 tears to both diagonal directions.

• Spirit Sword: Beams and sword swings are fired forwards instead of diagonally. Isaac spins an additional time when doing a charged attack.

• Technology Zero: Electricity arcs between both tears, damaging enemies between them.

• Tractor Beam: Both tears will follow the beam, making it easier to hit enemies with them.

• Tractor Beam + Mom's Knife: Knives ignore the path of the beam and remain flying diagonally.

• Tiny Planet: Each shot fires two tears in opposing orbital directions. The orbit can be controlled as normal.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Analog Stick: Will make one tear go forwards and the other tear fire at a 90-degree angle to the other tear.

• Azazel/Brimstone/Tainted Azazel: Fires two Brimstone beams diagonally. Beams remain diagonal even if Isaac has Tractor Beam.

• [Before Repentance] Azazel + Anti-Gravity: Overrides The Wiz. 

• Cain / Tainted Cain: Makes Cain fire in the two diagonal directions instead of just his right eye as the R U a Wizard? pill does.

• Epic Fetus: The crosshair is controlled diagonally as if rotated 45 degrees clockwise from usual (i.e.: the up arrow will move it in a northeast direction), and two missiles are fired, similar to the effect of 20/20. The crosshair can be moved in the cardinal directions by pressing two arrow keys at once (e.g.: pressing the up and right arrows will move the crosshair right).

• Homing tears: Tears are more likely to home in on enemies if enemies are coming towards Isaac diagonally. With big enough tears or a big enough enemy, homing tears are very powerful with The Wiz.

• The Ludovico Technique: Small tear orbits the main tear. Tear controls rotated 45 degrees clockwise - holding up makes it move northeast and so on.

• Marked: Fires two shots aimed diagonally from the crosshair.

• Monstro's Lung: 7-8 tears are fired at each diagonal direction instead of a full burst.

• R U a Wizard? pill: Makes Isaac fire forward with a normal fire rate and 90 degrees outwards with half fire rate.

• Sad Bombs: Does not affect the number of tears when bombs explode.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is possibly a reference to Nethack, where an unidentified "conical hat" can be either a cornuthaum (i.e. a "wizard hat") or a cursed dunce cap. Equipping the conical hat will identify it, but if it's a cursed dunce cap it will lower your intelligence and be difficult to remove. The Wiz has the word "DUNCE" printed in the image but is officially named after wizardry. This confusion alludes to the ambiguous identity of the conical hat.

• This item shares its name with a 1978 musical based on The Wizard Of Oz.

fields.description: Grants spectral tears. Tears simultaneously fire out of both eyes diagonally, similar to the effect of the R U a Wizard? pill.

The Wretched.title: The Wretched
The Wretched.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Wretched is a boss that can appear in the Catacombs.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Wretched's behavior is similar to Widow's: making large leaps towards Isaac, and can perform the following attacks after landing:

• Leaves a puddle of White Creep that is slightly larger than Widow's, and shoots 8 white projectiles outwards.

• Spits out 2 Spiders, a Big Spider, or a Trite.

• The Wretched can kill her own summons if she jumps on top of them.

• [Repentance] Spawns 3 Spiders upon death.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Wretched was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original game, The Wretched could also appear in Necropolis.

• She is the posthumous version of Widow.

• The word Wretched means to be in an unfortunate state, which may refer to The Wretched's stitched upper mouth, and multiple bumps on her face.

• [Repentance] Widow's and Wretched's animations and behavior have been sped up to more closely resemble their Flash counterparts.
