There's Options.title: There's Options
There's Options.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: an item affecting Boss rewards; a similar item affecting room clear rewards; Options?; a similar item affecting Treasure Rooms; More Options]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Two items appear after defeating a Boss. Only one can be taken; the other will disappear.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If the boss has a fixed item drop such as The Harbingers, the other item will be selected from the normal Boss.

• Two items appear after clearing Boss Rush.

• Both items that appear after defeating a Boss in The Void are from random item pools. Likewise, both items that appear after defeating The Fallen are Devil Room.

• There is no effect on items dropped by Mini-Bosses.

• There is no effect on what appears after defeating Mom, even if The Polaroid / The Negative have not unlocked (in which case only 1 Boss will appear).

• Does not retroactively affect Boss Rooms that had already been cleared prior to picking it up.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Revelations: Defeating a Harbinger will spawn both a regular Boss and either Ball of Bandages or Cube of Meat.

• [Repentance] Crooked Penny / Diplopia: Both items are copied, allowing Isaac to take both copied items without the other disappearing. The original pedestals will function as normal, removing the other if one is collected. [end edition note] 

• IV - The Emperor?: The extra boss room's rewards will be two choice pedestals.

• Jacob and Esau: Both brothers can take one item each if they are lined up properly.

• Satanic Bible: Both items will be Devil Room; only one can be bought.

• Vanishing Twin: The item which appears after defeating the copied boss is also affected.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • [Repentance] More Options' description is "There's options". It's the other way around for this item. [end edition note]

fields.description: Two items appear after defeating a Boss. Only one can be taken; the other will disappear.

Thunder Thighs.title: Thunder Thighs
Thunder Thighs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Not to be confused with Bucket of Lard.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1 Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Heals 1 additional Red Heart.

• -0.4 speed down.

• [Before Repentance] Also affects maximum speed.

• Isaac gains the ability to destroy obstacles by walking into them.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Mega Fatty. [end edition note] 

• Holes in the ground can be filled if Isaac walks into adjacent rocks from the right direction, similar to bombs.

• Avoid walking over Mushrooms and Bomb Rocks, as they can damage Isaac upon destruction.

• With this item, Isaac can walk over and destroy Red Poop and Spiked Rocks without taking damage. He will still be damaged if he's above the destroyed Red Poop when it reforms.

• Walking over an Angel Statue in the Angel Room will trigger the boss fight, and the Angel will spawn on top of Isaac. It is possible to avoid taking contact damage by walking away from the statue immediately after touching it.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • A Pony/White Pony: The lower limit for Isaac's speed is decreased from 1.50 to 1.10.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in The Tank, BRAINS!, and Scat Man.

• The item's sprite is a bucket of nacho cheese.

fields.quote: HP up + speed down + you feel stompy
fields.description: Destroys rocks upon contact with Isaac. Adds one Red Heart container and lowers Speed.

Tick.title: Tick
Tick.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Removes 15% of any enemy's health if they have 60 HP or higher.

• Gives Isaac one Red Heart if he enters an unexplored Boss Room.

• Once picked up, Tick can't be dropped or replaced with another trinket.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Only works on the first stage of multistage bosses.

• [Afterbirth onward] Friendly enemies are also affected by the health removal when above 60 hp.

• [edition anr] This trinket's effect can be multiplied to a maximum of x2 through any combination of multiple copies and Mom's Box. This also includes multiplying the healing effect when entering a Boss Room. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] This trinket's effect can be stacked via any combination of multiple copies, golden variants, and Mom's Box with enough stacks causing any enemy above 60 hp to have the lowest amount of health possible with any amount of damage killing them. This also includes stacking the healing effect when entering a Boss Room. The HP removal stacking effect is equal to 0.85 ^ Number of Tick Instances, with golden trinkets adding on 2 to this. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Has no effect on Mega Satan.

• [Repentance] Has no effect on the Ultra Harbingers. Works on both phases of Dogma. [end edition note] 

• Losing Mom's Purse or Belly Button (such as from an item re-roll) will drop Tick if it's in the second trinket slot.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket: The golden version can be freely dropped or replaced by another trinket.

• Golden Trinket/Mom's Box: Having either heals Isaac for 2 hearts when entering an unexplored Boss Room. Having both heals Isaac for 3 hearts.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Marbles / Smelter / Gulp!: Absorbs the trinket, allowing Isaac to pick another trinket up. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth onward] Match Stick / [Repentance+] A Lighter [end edition note] : Tick can be removed by picking up these trinkets.

• [Before Repentance+] Match Stick + Mom's Purse / Belly Button: Match Stick can no longer remove Tick, instead moving to the second trinket slot even if Isaac already holds two trinkets. [end edition note] 

• Mom's Box: Reduces enemy's health by 30%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth onward] Being able to replace the Tick with Match Stick is a reference to how one can remove a tick that has latched onto their skin in real life with a heated tip of a match stick; however, removing a tick like this can expose oneself to disease-causing bacteria present in the tick. It is also a feature that was carried over from the original The Binding of Isaac, though it's unclear why it wasn't originally added in Rebirth.

• The Tick is the only trinket that passively changes Isaac's appearance.

• The Tick bears similarity to a real-life deer tick.

• This trinket is used in The Host (challenge #18).

fields.description: Drains 15% health from enemies with more than 60 HP. Restores one Red Heart when entering an uncleared Boss Room. The Tick cannot be dropped or swapped for another trinket.

Gemini (Item).title: Gemini (Item)
Gemini (Item).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the zodiac item; the boss; Gemini]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Spawns a conjoined familiar, much like Gemini's small twin, Suture. It chases enemies close to Isaac, dealing 3 damage per tick (~6.43 damage per second).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Gemini. [end edition note] 

• Despite its appearance and description, Gemini does not count towards the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Interaction
sections.text:
• Duct Tape: The familiar will stay in place relative to Isaac, but the effect of chasing enemies persists.

• King Baby: Suture will rest near King Baby if there are no enemies near Isaac, but will snap towards the enemy once one gets close enough to Isaac. Otherwise, no functional difference.

• RC Remote: The familiar can be extended way past its attack range, and will still do contact damage, but will only chase when an enemy enters the usual aggro distance.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Gemini familiar is now animated, turning red and chasing enemies, similar to how Suture chases the player after Contusion is killed, based on this Steam Workshop mod by piber20.

• Gemini's item ID is 318, putting it outside the range of other Zodiac items that are 299 to 309.

fields.description: Spawns a conjoined familiar which chases enemies close to Isaac, dealing ~6.43 damage per second.

Genesis.title: Genesis
Genesis.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• On use, Isaac is teleported to a unique Clean Bedroom that acts like an I AM ERROR room. It has a Bed, two random Chests, two Grab Bags, and a random Trinket. The only way out is through the beam of light, which teleports Isaac to the next floor (with some exceptions, seen below).

• Isaac loses all items and is reset to a state exactly like if he started a new run, though keeping quest items to not block progression. All stats, consumables, trinkets, and all items except for starting items and quest items, are removed. Isaac gains back all of his starting trinkets and consumables. 

• For every item removed using Genesis, there will be a set of three items from the removed item's pool to choose from, each set appearing one after the other at the bottom of the room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• If used on one of the final floors of the game, such as Chest, Dark Room, The Void, or Corpse II, the beam of light will be replaced with a Crawl Space that leads Isaac back to the starting room of the floor he used it on. In addition, on Chest or Dark Room the aforementioned chests will include items. These items will not disappear along the "choice" pedestals.

• [Before Repentance+] If used in the final floor of Greedier mode, the beam of light will instead be replaced with a normal trap door that leads Isaac to a brand new Ultra Greed floor, forcing him to repeat the boss fight.

• • [Repentance+] The trapdoor now leads to the starting room of the floor, without resetting it.

• If used in Womb II, Utero II, or ???, the beam will always teleport Isaac to Cathedral.

• Crawl Spaces can be generated and entered inside the Genesis room, but upon leaving them, Isaac will be returned to the floor Genesis was used on instead of returning to the room.

• Similarly, Joker can teleport Isaac to a Devil Room or Angel Room, and leaving will return Isaac to the room Genesis was used in, instead of the Genesis room.

• Other cards, such as 0 - The Fool, can be used to directly teleport to one of the rooms in the current floor, successfully escaping as well. Cards can be obtained by opening a Chest, whose contents could be a Locked Chest, whose contents could be a Card.

• Item Pools will not be reset, however any lost items can be obtained again if they spawn.

• Transformations are also removed.

• Does not work during The Beast's fight, instead merely teleporting Isaac to a random location in the room. No items will be removed.

• Take caution; choosing an active item while holding another one will not drop the previous item to the ground, but replace it.

• Genesis will remove all currently active curses, meaning [cu: Blind] will not affect the item pedestals present inside the room (except during the Ultra Hard challenge).

• Trinkets absorbed using a Gulp! pill or an item such as Smelter will simply be removed with no extra pedestals granted for them.

• If used as Jacob and Esau, both characters' items are removed to offer choices, but Jacob and Esau cannot take two items at once from the choices. Both characters' items are considered in the amount of choices offered.

• Tainted Cain will be able to pick up the items that appear normally, one of the few times he is able to do so (along with quest items and items in the Death Certificate area).

• If used as Tainted Lazarus, both forms' items are removed and offer the equivalent number of choices, while his initial Flip is granted infinite charges and can be used freely in the special room.

• Bethany will lose all existing wisps and reset the soul charge count to its default of 4 on use, but will gain 3 default wisps upon appearing in the Genesis room.

• Tainted Bethany will lose all of her Lemegeton wisps and reset the blood charge count to its default of 6 on use. She does not gain extra wisps back.

• If used as Eden or Tainted Eden, a new set of items and stats will be generated. The first random passive item Eden starts with is rerolled immediately with no choice of three.

• If Isaac uses Genesis while in Downpour II / Mines II / Mausoleum II or their variants, the beam of light will send him back to the regular floors. However, after using Genesis on Downpour I / Mines I / Mausoleum I / Corpse I, it sends Isaac to the respective second part of the stage.

• Since Genesis resets Isaac's health, it is one way to remove Broken Hearts.

• Using Genesis removes the schwag bonus and [Before Repentance+] damage penalty on Daily Challenges and outside.

• [Repentance+] Genesis' quality is treated as 3 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Grants a free Pentagram that will not be removed by Genesis.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Replaces all of Isaac's wisps with 3 normal wisps. Unlike other reroll items, Isaac does not keep Book of Virtues.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• ? Card: If ? Card is used in place of Genesis, Genesis will be counted as an extra item for the choice set.

• Abyss: The locusts created by Abyss are removed without creating items to replace them making Genesis one of the few effects that can remove them.

• Azazel / Tainted Azazel: Both have the ability to return to the floor Genesis was used on, due to them starting with a 0 - The Fool card.

• Book of Revelations/Satanic Bible: Effects on the Boss Room and boss item still apply to the floor even after using Genesis.

• Brittle Bones: Genesis removes the fire rate upgrades upon use.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Crooked Penny: Using it on the choice pedestals has the 50/50 chance of duplicating them as normal, or make them disappear, in which case no new ones will spawn.

• Damocles / Missing No.: Genesis removes these items as well, making it the only item or effect that can remove them besides Butter!.

• Death Certificate: After taking an item in the Death Certificate area, Isaac will return to the Genesis room and the current 3 item pedestals can all be taken, with the next set spawning on top of them.

• Echo Chamber: The consumable pool is reset when Genesis is used, so if it's re-obtained after using Genesis, the previously stored consumable types won't be activated.

• Eden's Blessing: Eden's Blessing will be consumed, and the next run Isaac starts will begin with a random item.

• Esau Jr.: Using Genesis as Esau Jr. will revert back to the original character.

• Lazarus' Rags / Ankh / Clicker: Using Genesis after Lazarus' Rags, Ankh or Clicker activates will continue as the new character.

• Glowing Hourglass: Using it works as intended and will give back all previous stats, items, pickups, and health.

• Magic Skin: Genesis does NOT remove the downside of Magic Skin; any of the choice pedestals can be replaced by Magic Skin.

• Sacred Orb: Will affect future items while inside the Genesis Room.

• Teleport! / Teleport 2.0 / Telepills / Teleport Cards: Should such items/consumables be obtained in the Genesis room, they can be used to circumvent the forced floor skip.

• In the case of pills, unidentified pills should only be consumed after taking all of the items in case telepills is rolled, for the Genesis room cannot be returned to after leaving.

• Void: All effects granted by absorbed items including stat ups and activated item abilities Void takes are removed without creating items to replace them. Since Void is stripped of any active item abilities it would have gained, any other Void found will also have no other active effects stored in it.

• Void's active effects are reset even if Isaac is currently not holding it.

• Wild Card: Can't activate Genesis.

• Tainted Lost: Will lose his Holy Mantle shield on use but will gain a new Holy Card.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Genesis refers to the first book in the Bible, and is an Ancient Greek term for "birth". The item description refers to the very first words in the Book of Genesis.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using Genesis immediately after taking Dad's Note will teleport Isaac to the Genesis room, then to the start of the ascent with no items except those that cannot be removed (Dad's Note, Key Pieces, etc.).
Bug note: Genesis removes wisps created by Lemegeton but not the item effects associated with them. These remain permanently active until Lemegeton is used again.

fields.description: Removes all of Isaac's items and pickups and takes him to a unique Clean Bedroom with some pickups and Chests and a passage to the next floor. For every item Isaac lost, he gets to take an item from a set of three.

Get out of Jail Free Card.title: Get out of Jail Free Card
Get out of Jail Free Card.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Opens all doors in the current room, just like Dad's Key.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Being a special card, the Get out of Jail Free Card has a significantly lower chance of appearing compared to other cards.

• Get out of Jail Free Card can open:

• [Repentance] The door of a Challenge Room after the fight has started.

• The door to the Mega Satan boss fight. The door will remain open after leaving the room.

• The fight in Boss Rush to leave early, but cannot be used to get into the Boss Rush room if the time limit has already passed.

• Get out of Jail Free Card cannot open:

• [Before Repentance] The door of a Challenge Room after the fight has started.

• The door to ???.

• A Strange Door.

• [Repentance] The flesh door to the Mom's Heart boss fight in Mausoleum II / Gehenna II. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • "Get out of Jail Free" is a card found in the board game Monopoly, allowing its user to escape jail early. The phrase has since spread and a "Get out of Jail Free Card" is also an idiomatic expression for something that would alleviate an undesirable situation.

fields.description: Upon use, opens all doors in the current room, exactly like Dad's Key.
fields.unlocked by: Get out of Jail Free Card

boxes.name: Get out of Jail Free Card

Ghost Baby.title: Ghost Baby
Ghost Baby.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and fires spectral tears that deal 3.5 damage each.

• [Before Repentance] Ghost Baby shoots once per second.

• [Repentance] Ghost Baby shoots 1.36 times a second.

• Contributes to the Conjoined transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item can rarely drop from destroying skulls.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Ghost Baby having [Before Repentance+] 5th / [Repentance+] 7th priority.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Mongo Baby: Will copy Ghost Baby’s tears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • There was a bug in the original game where picking up Ghost Baby for the first time could grant you the Platinum God achievement, even if you lacked other items on the collection page.

fields.image name: * [edition alternatives: Before Afterbirth+: Rebirth; Before Repentance: Afterbirth+]
fields.description: Spawns a familiar that follows Isaac around and fires spectral tears.

Ghost Bombs.title: Ghost Bombs
Ghost Bombs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac 5 Bombs.

• Isaac's bombs create ghosts when they explode, which rapidly chase and deal contact damage to enemies.

• The ghost deals contact damage equal to half of Isaac's damage per tick (2× Isaac's damage per second).

• After 10 seconds, the ghost explodes, dealing 7 damage to nearby enemies up to 3 times and destroying nearby projectiles. Isaac does not take damage from the explosion.

• If there are no enemies in the room, the ghost follows Isaac. However, it cannot follow Isaac between rooms.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Friendly enemies can be killed by the ghosts.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Dr. Fetus: Has a chance to shoot a Ghost Bomb that also has spectral properties and can travel through objects.

• Scatter Bombs: Split bombs create ghosts that instantly launch themselves at enemies and explode, similar to Purgatory. They each deal 2× Isaac's damage, up to 4 times.

• Mr. Mega: Ghosts appear larger and do extra damage only upon exploding.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Doctor's Remote/Epic Fetus: No effect.

• Ipecac: The ghosts get only +1 flat damage from Ipecac, not the expected +20.

• Libra: The ghosts ignore damage modification from Libra, both positive and negative: the actual unbalanced damage value is used.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Defeating Delirium as most tainted characters will unlock their gameplay characteristic. Interestingly, Tainted Lost's passive ability to reroll low quality items (Sacred Orb) is unlocked through defeating The Beast instead.

• This item may be a reference to "Super Ghost Kamikaze Attack" from Dragon Ball Z.

fields.description: +5 Bombs. Bombs become spectral and spawn ghosts that deal contact damage to enemies and explode after 10 seconds.

Ghost Pepper.title: Ghost Pepper
Ghost Pepper.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Shooting tears sometimes spawns a fire similar to Red Candle, damaging enemies and destroying shots it comes into contact with. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Shooting tears sometimes spawns a blue fire similar to The Candle, damaging enemies and destroying shots it comes into contact with. It lasts on the ground for a limited time and can pass through obstacles. [end edition note] 

• The fire deals 6× Isaac's damage at base, gradually fading to 3× damage with the size of the flame.

• Creating farts through items/pills such as Re-Lax, The Poop, Butter Bean, and etc. causes fire to shoot out alongside the fart.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The only exception to this is the farts generated by Butt Penny.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] The chance of spawning fires is not affected by luck.

• [Repentance] The chance to shoot fires depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \min(\frac1 { 12 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor},50\%)

• At base luck (0), the chance is 8.33%, maxing out at 50% at 10 luck.

• The fire can destroy Shopkeepers.

• [Before Repentance] Enemies with fire variants will change to their flaming variants when they get hit with the flame.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Bird's Eye: Changes the activation rate to \frac1 { 8 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} \right \rfloor}

• At base luck (0), the chance is 12.5%, maxing out at 100% at 7 luck. Only one type of fire can be spawned at a time; however, each flame has an equal chance of being launched.

• Brimstone: The flames can still shoot from Isaac while holding the fire button.

• [Repentance] Occasionally emits a flame while the beam is firing.

• Butter Bean, Mega Bean, The Black Bean, Wait What?: Will spawn fires upon use/activation.

• Dr. Fetus: Fires can be spawned while firing bombs.

• Epic Fetus: Fires can be spawned while moving the crosshair.

• Farting Baby: The familiar has a chance to spawn a flame upon farting.

• Ipecac: Fires are spawned as normal and can be hit by Ipecac tears, making this especially dangerous with a multi-shot ability.

• Mom's Knife: The flames can still shoot from Isaac while holding the fire button.

• [Repentance] Occasionally spawns a fire when thrown.

• Monstro's Lung: The flames can still be shot from Isaac while holding the fire button.

• [Repentance] Occasionally fires a barrage of flames along with the blast. The trajectory of the flames is unaffected, making them stack on top of each other.

• The Poop: Fire will appear behind Isaac.

• Pupula Duplex: The fires gain a large size and duration increase.

• Technology/Tech X: Will occasionally spawn a fire while firing lasers. The lasers will not douse the flames.

• Trisagion: Will occasionally spawn a fire while firing beams. [Before Repentance] Fires' damage is not reduced.

• Urn of Souls: Causes the Urn to emit Ghost Pepper's flames in addition to its regular flames.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• 20/20/The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider: Will only spawn one fire.

• Anti-Gravity: When holding down the fire button, when the fire spawns, it will be almost immediately put out by the clumps of tears.

• Blood Clot: No effect.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: Fires cannot split.

• Ghost Pepper: No effect. Extra copies will not boost the chances of shooting out a fire like with Bird's Eye.

• Homing tears: Flames will not be homing.

• IBS: Not recommended. IBS can trigger farts that automatically release a flame, which detonate the toxic cloud left behind and hurt Isaac, unless he has explosion immunity. While less of a risk than Bird's Eye, the flames spawned by Ghost Pepper can detonate stinky poops held by Isaac when IBS activates.

• Contagion: Has a chance to make Isaac shoot a fire in a random direction after killing an enemy affected by Contagion.

• Tear-copying Familiars like Incubus/Lil Clot/Evil Eye: Any fires that would be spawned from the familiars will be shot from Isaac instead.

• Lachryphagy: Feeding tears will quickly douse the flames.

• Lilith: Spawns fire from her mouth.

• The Ludovico Technique: Fires created from Ghost Pepper will destroy the tear and cause it to respawn on Isaac.

• [Repentance] Isaac now periodically creates fires that shoot towards the Ludovico Technique tear.

• A Lump of Coal: No effect.

• Pop!: Eyeball tears quickly douse flames.

• Proptosis: Flames will not lose damage or shrink as they travel.

• [Repentance] Flame damage is tripled at base, follows Ghost Pepper's damage decay formula instead of the one from Proptosis.

• Soy Milk: No effect on frequency or damage of flames.

• Sprinkler: The sprinkler will not spawn flames.

• Jupiter: No effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• "Ghost pepper" is an alternate name for the bhut jolokia, which is arguably one of the world's hottest peppers.

• [Repentance] After Repentance, this item is essentially a The Candle variant of Bird's Eye. It was likely reworked instead of the new item since the "ghost" thematic fits blue fires better. [end edition note]

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Gives a chance to shoot fires alongside tears that block enemy shots and deal damage to enemies that touch them.
[Repentance] Gives a chance to shoot blue fires alongside tears that become smaller as they travel.

Giant Cell.title: Giant Cell
Giant Cell.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish visual: Eye Sore]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Whenever Isaac takes damage, he summons a micro-Isaac familiar, known as Minisaac, that chases nearby enemies and attacks on its own.

• Minisaacs deal 1.35 base damage that scales with +0.15 per floor: damage = 1.35 + 0.15 * (floor - 1)

• Minisaacs shoot 3 tears per second and their tear delay is not affected by Isaac's stats.

• Minisaacs persists between rooms and floors.

• Each Minisaac is spawned with 15 health points that are constantly drained with a rate of 0.4 per second. The draining stops when they reach 0.8 HP.

• • They are healed back to full HP whenever Isaac takes damage, even when the familiars cap is reached.

• Enemies can damage Minisaacs by shooting projectiles at them or dealing contact damage.

• • Isaac's bomb explosions will also damage the familiars.

• • Minisaacs are immune to spikes and lasers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Polycephalus. [end edition note] 

• The familiar cap for Giant Cell is 16, after which taking damage will not spawn a new Minisaac.

• Minisaacs will change their skin color based on the character that they were spawned from.

• Certain items that change skin color can also affect the familiars' appearance.

• When playing as The Forgotten, the familiars take the style as either The Soul or The Forgotten, depending on who gets hit.

• If the familiar takes the style of The Forgotten, it will also inherit its bone club attack, dealing 8.1 base damage that scales with +0.9 per floor. It will swing its bone club 1.5 times per second. It can also interact with pickups using the bone club.

• Minisaacs for Tainted Forgotten will spawn from The Forgotten's body and inherit its skin color but they will shoot regular tears.

• Familiars spawned for Azazel or Tainted Azazel will not inherit the Brimstone laser and will fire regular tears.

• If Isaac has any form of flight, the Minisaacs will receive wings and will be able to fly as well.

• Minisaacs spawned before flight was acquired will not get upgraded, unless the flight is acquired by killing Dogma and starting The Beast fight in which case they will get upgraded.

• Minisaacs that acquire temporary flight (e.g. from The Bible) will remain permanently upgraded until they die, even after the effect of The Bible expires.

• If being hit makes Isaac become the Whore of Babylon, a Shadow-like Minisaac will spawn instead of a regular one.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• BFFS!: Increases damage dealt by the familiars by 40%.

• Dull Razor: Provides a penalty-free way of spawning Minisaacs and/or healing existing ones.

• Glowing Hourglass: Each use of Glowing Hourglass that does not move Isaac to a different room than the one he is currently in (such as the starting room of a new floor) will duplicate the Minisaacs. (This is possibly a bug)

• Sacrificial Altar: Converts all Minisaacs into 1 Penny each upon use.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Many familiar-modifying items and trinkets do not affect the Minisaacs. These include:

• Box of Friends

• [Before Repentance+] Child Leash [end edition note] 

• Duct Tape

• Extension Cord

• Forgotten Lullaby

• Friendship Necklace

• King Baby

• [Before Repentance+] RC Remote [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • A Minisaac spawned by Giant Cell will not only attack Dummy on screen, but will prioritize attacking the Dummy over any other enemies.

fields.description: Causes Isaac to spawn Minisaac familiars when he takes damage, which chase and shoot at nearby enemies.

Gigante Bean.title: Gigante Bean
Gigante Bean.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Makes farts (e.g. Butter Bean) significantly larger.

• [Before Repentance+] Also affects enemy farts.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either makes all farts gain knockback. Having both makes all farts gain knockback and inflict confusion.

• Contagion: All enemies killed while infected produce a much larger gas cloud, making the spread much more effective.

• Isaac's Heart: Increases the knockback amount and radius of the heart when fully charged and the heart makes farting noises when it shoots.

• Jupiter: Affects all gas clouds produced, increases them in size drastically.

• Linger Bean: The clouds will be larger, increasing the range drastically. The damage is unaffected.

• Mucormycosis: Spore explosions count as farts, and increase in size.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This trinket originated in Antibirth, where it was originally called Giant Bean and had the additional effect of stunning enemies.

fields.description: Increases the size of Isaac's farts.

Gilded Key.title: Gilded Key
Gilded Key.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Replaces all new chests with Locked Chest.

• Old Chests and Mega Chests are not replaced.

• Causes Golden Chests to either grant an item or multiple random pickups. This modifies the contents of Golden Chests to be able to give one or even multiple cards, runes, and trinkets from a single chest alongside normal pickups when it doesn't reward an item.

• This includes one or more Lil' Battery and pill pickups allowing Golden Chests to drop these pickups.

• Gives Isaac one Key when picked up for the first time in a run.

sections.heading: Gilded Key's Changes To Golden Chest Rewards
sections.text:
| Reward | % Chance | Gilded Key

| 1 Item | 20% | 20%

| 2-6 Random Pickups (see table below) | 58% | 80%

| 1 Trinket | 10% | 0%

| 1 Chest | 1% | 0%

| 1 Locked Chest | 1% | 0%

| 1 Card or Rune | 10% | 0%

sections.heading: Random pickup changes
sections.text:
| Reward | Base % | Gilded Key | Gilded Key + Daemon's Tail

| 1-3 Coins | 35% | 25% | 29.7%

| 1 Heart | 20% | 20% | 4%

| 1 Key | 15% | 10% | 11.9%

| 1 Bomb | 30% | 20% | 23.8%

| 1 Pill | 0% | 5% | 5.9%

| 1 Card or Rune | 0% | 5% | 5.9%

| 1 Rune | 0% | 5% | 5.9%

| 1 Trinket | 0% | 5% | 5.9%

| 1 Lil' Battery | 0% | 5% | 5.9%

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The contents of Golden Chests can be changed retroactively by picking up/dropping Gilded Key. This can even be observed if Isaac has Guppy's Eye, allowing him to see what the chest would have if he did(n't) have the key and choose which payout he wants.

• This also applies to chests that use Golden Chests' loot systems, such as Bomb Chests and Eternal Chests.

• Mega Chests will also have their contents modified if they didn't contain items.

• The difference in contents between the two chest payouts are independent from each other; regardless of if the original chest had an item, card, trinket, or pickups, the modified chest can have any combination of them.

• • Modified chests are still unable to spawn pickups alongside items.

• Gilded Key does not retroactively change chests that have already spawned into Golden Chests, or change their contents.

• Golden Chests in Chest will still spawn items.

• The unique Red Chests in the beginning room of the Dark Room will be replaced with golden chests, allowing Isaac to take 4 treasure room items for free instead of Devil Deal items.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: +10% chance for chests as room rewards per copy.

• If Isaac has both a golden trinket and the Box, the chance is increased by +20%.

• Paper Clip: Allows all Golden Chests spawned to be opened without a key.

• Sharp Key: Enemies killed by keys will only give the contents of locked chests allowing items to be obtained through Sharp Key more consistently. The pickups they can drop will also include runes and Lil' Battery.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • The Left Hand: Overrides Gilded Key.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gilded Key is the only trinket in the game to grant a consumable upon pickup.

• The pickup text "Less is more" is a reference to Mom's Key's old pickup text "less is now more +2 keys"

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Picking up a golden Gilded Key does not give a key.

fields.description: Replaces all new chests, except Mega Chests and Old Chests, with Locked Chests. Grants one Key on pickup.

Gimpy.title: Gimpy
Gimpy.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• When Isaac takes damage, there is a chance that a Soul Heart may spawn.

• Monsters have a chance to drop a Half Red Heart after being killed. Chance depends on killed monster's base health.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Sisters Vis. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] The chance for Gimpy to spawn a Soul Heart depends on the luck stat, and the formula used to determine the chance is: \min(\frac1 { 10 - \left \lfloor \mathit{Luck} * 0.4 \right \rfloor},50\%)

• At base luck (0), the chance is 10%, maxing out at 50% at 20 luck.

• [Repentance] The chance for Gimpy to spawn a Soul Heart depends on the luck stat and is based on this formula: 8\% + (2\% * \mathit{Luck})

• This means that the chance starts at 8% at 0 luck, minimizes at 0% at -4 luck, and maximizes at 100% at 46 luck.

• Monsters that have less than 10 HP have a 1% chance to drop a Half Red Heart.

• Monsters that have 10 to 29 HP have a 5% chance to drop a Half Red Heart.

• Monsters that have more than 30 HP have a 10% chance to drop a Half Red Heart.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood Oath: For each half heart damaged by Blood Oath, Gimpy has a chance to drop a soul heart. Synergy further improves with luck.

• Dark Bum: Dark Bum can collect the Half Red Hearts that enemies drop, which when combined with the chance to drop Soul Hearts when damaged, is a good way to generate Soul and Black Hearts as well as other pickups.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups can't drop hearts.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into poop can't drop hearts.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The "Sweet Suffering" flavor text is a reference to BDSM. Specifically, it references masochism, which is when sexual pleasure is derived from pain.

• Much like Gish and Sisters Vis, this item could be a reference to the "Gimp" enemy in Gish, who wears a BDSM mask.

• Gimpy is a possible reference to "the gimp" a minor character of the movie "Pulp fiction" of Quentin Tarantino

fields.description: Gives chance of spawning a Soul Heart when taking damage. Enemies have a chance to drop a Half Red Heart after being killed.

Gish.title: Gish
Gish.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Gish is a boss that can appear in the Depths and the Dank Depths.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Makes short hops towards Isaac, similar to Monstro.

• Fires a black Ipecac shot towards Isaac, leaving a large puddle of Black Creep on impact.

• Leaps off-screen and lands on Isaac's position twice in a row, similar to Monstro II.

• Leaves a large puddle of Black Creep on his first landing.

• • The Black Creep spawned by Gish's first jump will remain for the entire battle until Gish is killed.

• Spawns two Clots on his second landing.

• • There is a maximum of 2 Clots alive at once.

• • Gish deals a full heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance] While just as common as other bosses in the Dank Depths' boss pool, Gish is only 1/4th as common as other Boss Room bosses in The Depths.

• Gish is the only boss to have more than 1 boss weight besides The Matriarch.

• Gish will often be accompanied by Clots.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gish appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• He is a rare alternative to Monstro II.

• The item Ball of Tar gives Isaac a Gish-like appearance.

• The enemy Clots are tiny Gishes.

• Gish is the protagonist of the 2004 PC game Gish, created by Edmund McMillen.

• Gish is the only boss to be an alternate version of a posthumous boss, being Monstro II's alternative.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Gish can be found in The Void, even before being unlocked. [end edition note]

Glass Cannon.title: Glass Cannon
Glass Cannon.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the challenge; Glass Cannon (Challenge)]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Fires a single high-damage piercing tear which can travel over obstacles.

• The damage dealt by this tear is ten times Isaac's damage, plus a flat 10 damage.

• The shot has an additional 1.5x size multiplier on top of damage-increased size.

• [Before Repentance] Sets Isaac's health to half a heart with each use (half a Soul Heart if these are present but there are no Red Heart containers). This also removes any other Soul Hearts or Black Hearts, but not Eternal Hearts.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] If Isaac has no Red Hearts and at least one Bone Heart, only an empty Bone Heart remains. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Upon taking damage, this item turns into Broken Glass Cannon, and Isaac will lose an additional 2 hearts of health on top of the damage he already took. Isaac gains 1.5 range and leaves a trail of red creep behind him for the rest of the current room, identical to the effects of Anemic.

• If the damage from breaking Glass Cannon would result in death, Isaac will remain at half a heart, gaining half a soul heart if necessary. This does not apply if the damage Isaac took would be lethal before the extra damage is taken.

• The damage from breaking Glass Cannon does not count as self-damage and will result in losing Angel/Devil Room chance if it is taken to Red Hearts.

• Self-damage (e.g. from [machine: Blood Donation Machine] s or Sacrifice Rooms) will not break Glass Cannon. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Glass Cannon can be fired diagonally, [Afterbirth+ onward] even without Analog Stick [end edition note] .

• Shooting the Glass Cannon gives a slight knockback effect to Isaac, which can be dangerous in rooms with obstacles like spikes or Fire Places.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Grants Judas +2.67 damage up while Glass Cannon is broken.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns white wisps on the middle ring. The wisps shatter in one hit and their tears deal 8 damage per shot, but if one of the wisps is destroyed, all the others are also destroyed. Does not affect wisps other than ones made by this item. Despite Glass Cannon having a timed charge, the wisps persist between rooms.

• Chocolate Milk: The current charge of Chocolate Milk affects Glass Cannon.

• Compound Fracture / Cricket's Body / The Parasite: Tears fired by Glass Cannon will split.

• Godhead: Creates a giant aura around Glass Cannon tears that almost fills up normal sized rooms.

• Lachryphagy: Glass Cannon will fire giant Lachryphagy tears. Tears are harder to feed as they will burst very quickly but they can be fed if you fire tears beforehand and then fire Glass Cannon into those tears.

• Multidimensional Baby: The Glass Cannon tears will be doubled by Multidimensional Baby.

• Mysterious Liquid: Creates a large pool of creep when tears land.

• Tiny Planet: Tears produced by Glass Cannon will orbit Isaac.

• Lost Contact: The Glass Cannon tears can block enemy shots.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Anti-Gravity, Car Battery, The Inner Eye, Mutant Spider, Brimstone, Dr. Fetus, Epic Fetus, The Ludovico Technique, Marked, Mom's Knife, Monstro's Lung, Technology, Tech X, 9 Volt, and 20/20: No effect, Glass Cannon fires a normal tear.

• 9 Volt: Reduces charge time to 2 seconds.

• 20/20: Gives a 25% damage down, hurting Glass Cannon's performance.

• Eye of the Occult: Cannon shot can be controlled. If a synergy is given a crosshair (e.g. Brimstone, Technology etc.), the tear will follow wherever it's pointed.

• [Repentance] Habit: Upon taking damage, Broken Glass Cannon will be half-charged. However, taking damage before the last charge will break the cannon again. [end edition note] 

• Items that trigger upon taking damage (such as It Hurts and Swallowed Penny) will activate 3 times when the Glass Cannon breaks.

• Holy Mantle: Doesn't prevent damage done by Glass Cannon, but will protect against other types of damage.

• Ipecac: As the Glass Cannon tears are so large, even a modest damage increase or a single tear size increasing item is likely to render the tear unable to damage enemies, their explosions too far from them.

• Pluto: Allows Isaac to cross small gaps using the knockback of Glass Cannon.

• Schoolbag: The cannon will break on damage, regardless if it or another active is on hand.

• Schoolbag + Tear Detonator: Glass Cannon shots will detonate into normal tears. The tears don't inherit spectral or piercing.

• Soy Milk: Reduces damage of shots, no effect on charge time.

• Trisagion: Fires normal Trisagion beams that do not have increased damage.

• The Wafer: Doesn't reduce the damage from breaking the Glass Cannon.

• Stye and Blood Clot: Copies the eye used most recently.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Glass Cannon is a term used in video games for a character or entity that deals high amounts of damage but has very low defense.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Glass Cannon can be used to steal Devil Room items by using it to set your health to [Before Afterbirth+] half of a Soul Heart or [Afterbirth+ onward] no health at all before you die. In the latter case, picking up any item that isn't a health upgrade will kill Isaac.
Bug note: If Tainted Forgotten takes damage with the cannon held above his head, he will be unable to fire and unable to attack. Exiting and continuing will fix this.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Fires a high-damage piercing spectral tear, but lowers Isaac's health to half a heart.
[Repentance] Fires a high-damage piercing spectral tear. If Isaac takes damage while holding this, he takes extra damage and it becomes Broken Glass Cannon.

Glass Eye.title: Glass Eye
Glass Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +0.75 damage

• +1 luck.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Glass Eye: Picking up a second copy of the item gives Isaac a unique costume with both eyes replaced. The damage up and luck up stack as expected.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Glass Eye is one of the few items that will give Isaac a unique costume when two copies are acquired, along with Brimstone and Guppy's Eye.

fields.description: +0.75 damage, +1 luck.

Glaucoma.title: Glaucoma
Glaucoma.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a 5% chance to shoot concussive tears, causing enemies to walk around randomly.

• The confusion caused by Glaucoma tears is effectively permanent for normal enemies, and a very long duration compared to most status effects for bosses.

• Makes the screen darker.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Not affected by Luck.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that result in damage to the optic nerve and vision loss.

• However, the item's sprite and Isaac's appearance when he obtains the item resemble Leucoma.

• This item bears a strong resemblance to Cain's Other Eye.

fields.description: Adds a chance to shoot tears that confuse enemies for an extremely long time.

Glitched Crown.title: Glitched Crown
Glitched Crown.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• New item pedestals cycle very quickly between 5 random items.

• The 5 items will cycle in the same order every loop.

• Items are rerolled at a rate of once every 0.2 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Plot-related items (i.e The Polaroid/The Negative, Broken Shovel 1/Broken Shovel 2, Knife Piece 1/Knife Piece 2,Key Piece 1,Key Piece 2 etc.) are unaffected by Glitched Crown.

• One of the items will be the initial one spawned/rerolled, while the other four will be from the item pool of the room the item is in.

• [Before Repentance+] Items spawned from Chest normally have a small delay between when they spawn and when Isaac can pick them up; if Isaac has Glitched Crown, this delay is removed and he can pick up the item the moment it spawns, effectively forcing him to get a random item.

• Chests have to be lightly tapped and immediately walked away from to avoid accidentally picking up the item so Glitched Crown can be used properly.

• Isaac's Birthright effect and Tainted Isaac's inherent ability are overridden by this effect.

• All five options will have their weight decremented on sight like usual.

• A good strategy to get a specific item is to remember the one that comes before it in the cycle. Stand as close to the pedestal as possible and move towards the pedestal when the item that comes before the desired one appears.

• [Before Repentance+] Pausing the game between each roll can make this substantially easier.

• • [Repentance+] Pausing the game does not pause the rotation of items. Instead, its cycling speed increases to one per frame, returning to normal once the game is unpaused.

• Due to Glitched Crown's indiscriminate cycling of items, anything that turns item pedestals into blind item pedestals, such as Curse of the Blind, or traveling to a floor that offers blind items such as Downpour, renders Glitched Crown's effect useless or even detrimental, as there is a chance of missing out on desirable items permanently among the blind choices.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Spindown Dice: Rerolling a cycling item will reduce the ID number of the displayed item by 1 and randomize the other 4 options.

• This allows Spindown Dice to mimic The D6's rerolling effect on 4/5 of Glitched crown's displayed items.

• The D6: All 5 items will be re-rolled.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Binge Eater: Adds a random food item to the cycle, for a total of 6 items on the cycling pedestal. Only the pedestals generated after picking up Binge Eater will be affected.

• Damocles: Extra item pedestals do not reroll.

• Diplopia: The items on-screen at the moment of activation will be duplicated, but the pedestal will also cycle through four new items.

• Genesis: If Glitched Crown is picked up during the item sequence, the effect will start on the second item after grabbing Glitched Crown.

• 0 - The Fool?: Items spawned using the card such as Boom! will not generate a cycling pedestal.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is a stronger version of the item cycling mechanic of Tainted Isaac. Its unlock method is unusual, as most other tainted characters have items based on their mechanics unlocked by defeating Delirium instead of The Beast.

• The Glitched Crown is a nod to a visual glitch in Super Mario Bros. where if the player has more than 99 lives, often achieved by the Koopa shell infinite 1up trick, the lives counter shown at the start of each stage shows a crown.

• There are five question marks in the item description, a nod to the five options that the item gives.

• The crown's glitched appearance looks to be a sprite error, a bug that messes with video game sprites by making their sprites either devolve into unintelligible pixels like in the bottom right quarter of the crown, or renders the sprite incorrectly, like the flipped effect of the top right quarter of the sprite.

• This causes it to look like an item afflicted by TMTRAINER, an item whose icon features similar glitchy distortions.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Glitched Crown still attempts to create 4 extra items when a quest item is generated (such as Key Piece 1), but because quest items cannot be rerolled, it will delete 4 items from that room's item pool.

fields.description: Item pedestals cycle between 5 random items before being picked up.

Glitter Bombs.title: Glitter Bombs
Glitter Bombs.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants 5 Bombs.

• Isaac's bombs have a 25% chance to spawn a pickup or trinket when they explode including other bombs.

• [Repentance] Isaac's bombs have a 63% chance to spawn a pickup or trinket when they explode, but the chance for either to generate decreases by 1% for each spawn until Isaac enters a new floor. This is to prevent items such as Dr. Fetus or a Golden Bomb from providing unlimited resources. This means that the maximum spawns per floor is 63, although the final generation of a pickup or trinket will have a 1% chance to occur.

• Isaac's bombs have a 15% chance to charm random enemies in the room when they explode.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Picking up a Golden Bomb, Dr. Fetus, Epic Fetus, or No. 2 with Glitter Bombs allows infinite pickup generation.

• [Before Repentance] In Greed Mode, Glitter Bombs cannot generate coins. Infinite pickup generation that isn't coins is still possible, however, so this can be worked around if Isaac has the Swallowed Penny or Piggy Bank, since it does still produce health.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Anarchist Cookbook/Curse of the Tower/XVI - The Tower: Each Troll Bomb has a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket including a Lil' Battery or Red Heart which can be taken advantage of for repeated uses of Anarchist Cookbook or Curse of the Tower respectively.

• Best Friend/Bob's Rotten Head/Mr. Boom/BBF/Bob's Brain/Kamikaze!: Has a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket when exploding.

• Bomber Boy: Each additional explosion created has a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket.

• Doctor's Remote/Epic Fetus: Missiles have a chance of spawning a pickup or trinket upon exploding.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs have a chance of spawning pickups or trinkets upon exploding.

• Everything Jar: At eleven charges guarantees a golden bomb.

• No. 2: The butt bombs have a chance of spawning pickups or trinkets upon exploding.

• [Repentance] Red Locusts: Red locust explosions have a chance to spawn a pickup or trinket.

• Scatter Bombs: Each smaller bomb also has a chance of dropping a pickup or trinket.

• Swallowed M80: Swallowed M80 explosions have a chance of spawning pickups or trinkets.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Bomber Boy: Extra explosions are unaffected by Glitter Bombs.

• Ipecac: No effect on shots.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Red Locusts: No effect on red locust explosions.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The act of glitter bombing refers to showering individuals with containers of glitter.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The limit of generated pickups is reset when exiting and reentering the game.

fields.description: +5 Bombs. Bombs have a chance to drop random pickups or charm enemies when they explode.

Glowing Hourglass.title: Glowing Hourglass
Glowing Hourglass.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the glowing hourglass; the normal version of this item; The Hourglass]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• On use, Isaac will be returned to the previous room and everything that happened in the current room will be undone.

• Health, bombs, coins, keys, cards / runes / pills, items, and trinkets, gained or lost, will be restored to their state before having entered the room.

• Time spent and score gained or lost within the room are reverted.

• • [Before Repentance] About one second will be spent during the animation after use.

• Most permanent unlocks will be reverted (see below).

• [Repentance] Can only be used 3 times on each floor, after which it functions like The Hourglass until a new floor is entered.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Glowing Hourglass is very useful for finding out hidden information. For example:

• Every pill on the floor can be accumulated and used in the same room, the pills' effects can be noted and reverted if unwanted.

• Isaac can bomb walls with potential secret rooms, then go back in time if he fails to find one.

• If Isaac has [cu: Blind] , Glowing Hourglass can be used to pick up or purchase an unknown item to see what it is, then decide whether or not to undo picking it up.

• It can be even be used in extremely creative ways, such as using XXI - The World and screenshotting the map, then going back in time to get the card back.

• Does not affect the chance for a Devil Room, Angel Room, or a portal to The Void to spawn (it will not spawn if it didn’t initially).

• If used in a Devil Room or Angel Room, the door to it has its normal chance to close.

• If used on the Boss Rush after the time limit expires, the door will not remain open when sent back to the boss room.

• If Isaac goes into a Devil / Angel room, sees undesirable items, activates the Glowing Hourglass, and the Devil / Angel door doesn't stay open, then the game will think that Isaac missed the Devil / Angel deal on the floor, and will thus increase the chance of getting one on the next floor.

• However, if it's the first Devil Deal, and the door doesn't stay open, then you'll still get an Angel deal on the next floor.

• • By combining these two bugged interactions, Isaac can get a Devil Deal on Basement 2, bomb himself to reduce your deal chance to 1%, then go into the Devil Deal, and use the Glowing Hourglass. You then have a 100% Angel Deal chance on Caves 1.

• Finding the Glowing Hourglass in a room and using it to undo picking up Glowing Hourglass will preserve its charges, allowing for infinite resets for that room.

• This effect can also be achieved by replacing the Glowing Hourglass with a different active item, exiting the room, then re-entering and using the Glowing Hourglass.

• [Before Repentance] Doing this will remove the charges of the returned active item.

• [Before Repentance] If there is a Lil' Battery in a Shop, the Glowing Hourglass can be used infinitely, by entering the Shop without a charge and using the Lil' Battery to recharge and exit the shop. This is useful for duplicating temporary familiars or filling up the Donation Machine, among other uses.

• The delayed effect of the I'm Excited pill will still occur after rewinding.

• [Before Repentance] The Retro Vision Pill will continue to affect the game even after using the Glowing Hourglass.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Does not turn a character back into another should they have been revived by Ankh, Lazarus' Rags, or Judas' Shadow.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Character changes are reverted by Glowing Hourglass.

• [Before Repentance] Does not return keys or health used to enter special rooms.

• If a bomb is used to enter a Secret Room, the Secret Room is entered, and the Glowing Hourglass is used, the Secret Room door will stay open and the bomb will not be refunded.

• [Before Repentance] Does not return extra lives.

• [Before Repentance] Using any teleportation card and then the Glowing Hourglass to return to the previous room does not refund the used card.

• [Repentance] Teleport cards like Joker can be refunded. However, if used on the first room on the floor, the Glowing Hourglass will be uncharged when returning.

• [Repentance] Using the Glowing Hourglass after entering a new floor will teleport Isaac back to the room in which the trapdoor was entered on the previous floor.

• Going back to the previous floor will transform Glowing Hourglass into The Hourglass for the rest of that previous floor. Going back to the new floor recharges the Glowing Hourglass, which allows for infinite usage of Glowing Hourglass on the starting room of a new floor.

• • If the Glowing Hourglass is held in the secondary slot of Schoolbag when entering the room with the trapdoor, the Glowing Hourglass will not be transformed into The Hourglass after returning to the previous floor.

• After returning to the previous floor, most changes in the room with the trapdoor will be undone. However, enemies / bosses will not be revived.

• [Repentance] Bethany's soul heart counter does not get reset upon activating this item.

• [Repentance] If Tainted Jacob is hit by Esau, using the Glowing Hourglass will return him to normal form in the previous room.

• [Repentance] The guaranteed angel room chance can be preserved if the item is used after entering the first devil room.

• [Repentance] When Isaac enters The Beast fight, Glowing Hourglass will transform into a fully charged The Hourglass.

• [Repentance] May be helpful for finding Planetariums, as it lets the player effectively skip item rooms while also seeing if what's inside them is worth taking. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] If Isaac enters a Planetarium for the first time and then uses Glowing Hourglass to leave, the chance of a Planetarium generating on future floors can be preserved, effectively allowing Isaac to reroll his Planetarium until a desired item is found. The likelihood of this being useful is rather low, however, due to Planetariums being rather rare. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The Boss Challenge Room re-rolls bosses on using the Glowing Hourglass.

• Perfection is still able to drop if the Glowing Hourglass is used to reset damage, and will be brought back by the Glowing Hourglass if used to reset a damage taken while holding it.

• [Repentance] If used in the starting room of Basement I without having entered any other rooms, Isaac is taken to the first room of Home. If used again in this room without having entered any other rooms, the room will be rewound to when it was first entered. In a normal game, this is only possible by getting the item as a starting item from Eden / Tainted Eden, or from Eden's Blessing. Having Schoolbag and obtaining R Key and resetting the run also makes this possible. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] Doing the same in [mode: greed] Greed Mode will teleport Isaac to the I AM ERROR room.

• The Glowing Hourglass affects permanent unlocks, event counters, boss kills, etc. differently depending on what is being reset:

• Completion marks earned in the room will be removed.

• [Before Afterbirth+] Donations to the Donation Machine or Greed Donation Machine are not reverted, and they can be reset into a working state once jammed.

• • [Afterbirth+ onward] Event counters will get restored (including Donation Machines, Greed Donation Machines, and Eden's Blessing).

• • Other counters not tied to the specific run, such as Slot Machines or Tinted Rocks destroyed, continue to accumulate, allowing easy unlocking of secrets such as the Counterfeit Penny, the D4, and Conquest if one has have access to infinite uses of the Glowing Hourglass (see the Synergies section).

• Does not remove collection page entries if it undoes collecting an item for the first time.

• No Damage Achievements are still available if the Glowing Hourglass is used to reset damage.

• • If a hit is taken, then reversed, Samson can still be unlocked.

• [Before Repentance] Can be used to unlock multiple achievements tied to the killing of certain bosses such as Mom's Heart / It Lives!.

• [Before Repentance] Using the Glowing Hourglass right after beating Mom's Heart / It Lives! / Ultra Greed allows additional Eden tokens to be obtained.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Any reroll item/collectible: Items in the room can be rerolled, and if the result is undesirable, then Isaac can go back in time to save whatever was used to reroll. However, note that activating the reroll on the same items again will result in the same items being generated as the first time. Rerolling different items from the same type of room (such as going to a different Shop) will result in the reroll effect creating new and different items. This technique is useful for saving charges on items like The D6, or getting multiple options with consumables like the Perthro.

• Anything that spawns an item such as Mystery Gift / XVII - The Stars?: After the player activates them, they can then go back in time if the item is undesirable. However, unlike reroll effects, using something that spawns an item/collectible will always generate that same item, dependent on the room type, even if the player goes to a different one in the future. For example, activating XVII - The Stars? in a Secret Room will create two items from the Secret Room item pool, and even if the player goes to the next floor and uses it again in a new Secret Room, the same exact items will be generated. So, the best way to use something that spawns an item is to activate it in rooms with different item pools (Secret, Devil/Angel, Treasure, Shop, etc.) and see which item would be the best before accepting it.

• [Before Afterbirth+] ? Card: Allows for infinite usage as the ? Card gets refunded upon usage.

• [Before Repentance] 9 Volt: Clearing any room is enough to instantly recharge the hourglass, allowing infinite tries for the best outcome.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The Battery: When the item is double charged and used, it will also refund the used extra charge bar, making it possible to use it endlessly.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] 48 Hour Energy pill: Allows for infinite usage as the pill gets refunded upon use.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Sharp Plug: Allows for infinite usage as long as you have more than 2 full hearts as the hearts used to charge will be refunded upon use.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Habit: Allows rooms to be repeated infinitely as long as Isaac has enough health to take two hits, which are refunded on use.

• Hairpin: If Hairpin is held while entering any Boss Room for the first time, Glowing Hourglass may be used indefinitely on said room to repeat the fight until you beat it.

• Moving Box: Using the Glowing Hourglass after retrieving it from Moving Box will not deplete its charge.

• Curse of the Tower: If used quickly after taking damage, Troll bombs will spawn in the previous room. If you have the Safety Scissors, these can be harvested as normal.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] Crooked Penny + Schoolbag: If there is a battery and an item in the same room, you can multiply items an infinite number of times. Every time you fail the Crooked Penny flip, you can activate the Glowing Hourglass, go back in, grab a battery, then try again. Every time you succeed a flip, you must leave the room and enter it again to "save" your progress. [end edition note] 

• [edition rnr+] More Options: If used after entering the Treasure Room in an Alt-Path floor, the items in the room will change.

• [Repentance] If Tainted Eden's active item re-rolls into Glowing Hourglass, it can be used immediately to return Tainted Eden to their previous state. This allows the player to have practically infinite attempts to keep their loadout of passive items as long as they travel back in time before being hit again.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Any wisps lost in the previous room will be restored, and an additional Glowing Hourglass wisp will be added on the middle ring. This wisp's tears have a 30% chance to petrify enemies.

• While playing as Tainted Eden and rerolling an active item into the Glowing Hourglass, you can infinitely spawn wisps as much as possible until you reroll it again.

• Duality: The doors to the Devil Room and Angel Room can stay open if you use the Glowing Hourglass inside their rooms, so Duality lets you check the items of both of them before deciding which room to use, provided two charges are still available by the end of the floor.

• [Repentance] Forget Me Now + Schoolbag: Using Forget Me Now will fully recharge Glowing Hourglass on the new floor, using Glowing Hourglass after that will take Isaac back to the previous room while also giving back Forget Me Now. This allows for infinite usage of Glowing Hourglass as well as infinite retries of any room as long as Forget Me Now is used before the room is cleared. [end edition note] 

• Saturnus: Using the Glowing Hourglass will activate the effect of Saturnus again, essentially allowing for double the amount of orbiting tears, if the player returns to a room, where the tears created by Saturnus were not destroyed.

• [Repentance] If activated while under the effect of Soul of Azazel, as long as you had the consumable in the previously visited room, you will keep the Megablast effect while having another copy of the soul in your inventory.

• Schoolbag + Mega Blast + Glowing Hourglass: Works the same way

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• ? Card: The Glowing Hourglass loses a charge when the card is used.

• Bag of Crafting: The bag's contents will be reverted to its previous state. Additionally, Bag of Crafting cannot be used to create Glowing Hourglass.

• The Battery: Glowing Hourglass will receive a maximum of two full charges as normal, however, using the item twice consecutively will not result in the player being teleported two rooms previous, only one. This means that if Glowing Hourglass is used twice in succession, they will rewind as normal with the first use to the previous room, then, upon second use, everything will be rewound, but the player will not be teleported to the room previous to the one they just teleported to and will instead find themselves teleported to the room they are currently in. Rewinding works as normal, but teleportation is limited to the last room visited.

• [Repentance] The battery has no effect on Glowing Hourglass when it is not in The Hourglass form.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Schoolbag: Losing your Schoolbag while Glowing Hourglass is in your second active slot will drop it on the ground fully charged.

• Tainted Jacob: Using this item in a room where Dark Esau has spawned will cause him to remain with the player after teleporting, but once enough time has passed, he will suddenly disappear and respawn elsewhere. This may be a bug.

• Void: It is impossible to absorb a Glowing Hourglass pedestal without using the item and preventing it from having been absorbed.

• [Repentance] The Glowing Hourglass is absorbed like normal. Subsequent uses of Void send Isaac back to the previous room, reverting most changes, nullifying many other effects that Void may have absorbed. This will prevent you from consuming any further powers, as you will instead reset the room. This effectively turns Void into a charged version of Glowing Hourglass, allowing potential infinite uses with items like 48 Hour Energy pills, Sharp Plug, Habit, Hairpin, 4.5 Volt, or a room with a Lil' Battery. [end edition note] 

• The Stairway: Using the Glowing Hourglass whilst in the Angel shop will consume all three charges and remove the ladder.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Prior to Afterbirth+ Booster Pack 5, Glowing Hourglass would turn into The Hourglass after being used 5 times.

• Prior to Repentance V1.7.9a, Glowing Hourglass was called "Glowing Hour Glass".

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Using Glowing Hourglass on the first room of the first floor of Ascent will take Isaac to the room containing Dad's Note. However, Dad's Note will be missing, and Glowing Hourglass will be in The Hourglass state, causing a softlock unless Isaac can teleport.
Bug note: Having Error will make familiars respawn each time Glowing Hourglass is used, which leads for some interesting interactions. For example, Buddy in a Box and 7 Seals will change their forms each time leap, and the Star of Bethlehem will change its position to the previous room, allowing strategic repositioning of the star.
Bug note: Rewinding time will add one more copy of each familiar that were created by Monster Manual for the duration of the room Isaac is teleported into, regardless if in possession or not of Monster Manual. Exiting this room and using Glowing Hourglass again will add another copy for each use of the item. The familiars disappear upon exiting the room.
Bug note: Going back to the starting room will undo some map-revealing effects, such as The Compass.
Bug note: Isaac's temporary familiars (Blue Flies and Spiders) duplicate when using the Glowing Hourglass.
Bug note: If a new game is started and Eden begins with this item, using it in the first room will remove Eden's starting items.
Bug note: Playing as Tainted Lazarus, if one form has Mega Mush, Mega Blast, A Pony, White Pony, or Berserk!'s effects active before flipping to the other form and using Glowing Hourglass, the form that holds Glowing Hourglass will gain the effects of that item.

fields.description: Rewinds time, putting Isaac back in the previous room and undoing anything that happened in the current room. [Repentance] Can only be used three times per floor, after which it functions like The Hourglass until the next floor.

Gluttony.title: Gluttony
Gluttony.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Gluttony is a mini-boss and one of the Seven Deadly Sins.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Gluttony wanders randomly around the room and performs one of two attacks:

• Shoots 8 projectiles in all directions.

• Fires a Brimstone laser from his belly towards Isaac if he is aligned in a cardinal direction.
Gluttony deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [edition anr] Occasionally, 2 regular Gluttonies appear in a Mini-Boss Room and the boss message will display "Isaac vs Super Gluttony".

• [Before Repentance] Gluttony can drop <3 even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Sin]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Gluttony is essentially a Vis with an attached head. The same applies to Super Gluttony, except his body is that of a Double Vis.

• The Seven Deadly Sins that these mini-bosses are based upon are, in Christian teachings, a classification of vices from which all others are derived from.

• Gluttony is a personification of one of the Seven Deadly Sins. Gluttony is the distorted desire to experience pleasures related to eating and drinking. It is a type of hedonism that could involve things such as over-eating, excessively unhealthy eating, alcohol abuse, and spending excessive amounts of money of luxurious foods, among other things. Gluttony is believed to open up a person to impulsivity, dullness in religious thought, as well as other kinds of hedonism such as lust.

Glyph of Balance.title: Glyph of Balance
Glyph of Balance.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants 2 Soul Hearts.

• Modifies drops from Champion enemies depending on certain conditions.

• [Repentance] Also modifies room clear drops.

• [Repentance] Every room is guaranteed to drop a reward.

• The priorities of the drops, in order, are as follows:

• Soul Hearts: When Isaac has no Red Heart containers and less than 2 Soul Hearts.

• Red Hearts: While at 0.5 Red Hearts.

• Keys: When Isaac has no keys. 

• Bombs: When Isaac has no bombs.

• Red Hearts: When Isaac has at least half a Red Heart container empty.

• • Tainted Bethany will always get this drop until she reaches 12 "blood charges".

• Penny: While Isaac has less than 15 pennies.

• Keys: When Isaac has less than 5 keys. 

• Bombs: When Isaac has less than 5 bombs.

• Trinkets: If Isaac has no trinkets and there are no trinkets on the ground in the room.

• Soul Hearts: When Isaac has less than 6 total Heart containers of any kind.

• • Bethany will only get this drop until she reaches 12 "soul charges". 

• • Tainted Bethany changes blue heart drop to red heart drop until she reaches 12 "blood charges", thus she is unable to receive any blue hearts.

• If none of the above conditions are true, items dropped will be rolled as normal.

• [Repentance] Chest drops override the Glyph of Balance.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• When the conditions for specific drop is met, you can intentionally not pick up the drop to guarantee that same drop (or a chest) every room.

• [Repentance] Staying at low luck is recommended to take full advantage of Glyph of Balance, as higher luck will make chest drops more common and override the effect of the Glyph.

• The Glyph has no effect in Greed Mode or Greedier Mode aside from the Soul Hearts granted upon pickup; champions still never drop anything.

• [Before Repentance] Because of how the item works in the priorities listed above, this item is not recommended for The Lost (except in combination with Immaculate Conception) as he is always considered to be at half a Soul Heart, and all drops from champions are replaced with Soul Hearts.

• [Repentance] The Lost and Tainted Lost ignore both rules for Soul Heart generation. This prevents the item from generating mostly useless Soul Hearts. [end edition note] 

• When playing as The Forgotten, the priority of the drops is based on the active form's health: for example, if The Forgotten has half a red heart or less, but The Soul was active right before the pickup drop and it had more than 2 soul hearts, the Glyph will skip over the full red heart drops to the next condition. Also if The Forgotten is full on pickups and health, has a trinket but has less than 6 bone hearts, the Glyph will always drop soul hearts unless The Soul is active at the moment of the drop.

• [Repentance] When playing as Jacob and Esau / Tainted Lazarus, the priority of the drops is based on the health of the character that has the Glyph. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] When playing as Tainted Lazarus, the room drop will be modified when the character switches to the character that has the item on room clear. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] When playing as characters incapable of having red heart containers such as ???, the Glyph will skip soul heart and red heart generation.

• While empty room drops are replaced by Glyph of Balance drops, if you get a heart drop in [mode: hard] Hard mode, there is a separate chance of it being replaced with an empty drop.

• It is still possible to get hearts if none of the other conditions are true.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Options?: Only one of the options will be modified by the Glyph.

• Perfection: Chest spawns are prioritized over Glyph of Balance, meaning it will be very hard to use the Glyph effectively.

fields.description: Grants 2 Soul Hearts and modifies drops from Champion monsters based on certain conditions. [Repentance] Also modifies room clear drops.

Gnawed Leaf.title: Gnawed Leaf
Gnawed Leaf.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• After standing still and not pressing the move or attack buttons for one second, Isaac will turn into an invulnerable statue.

• Using bombs and active items will remove the invincibility state.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Great Gideon. [end edition note] 

• [Afterbirth onward] While invulnerable, Little Horn’s pitfall still affects Isaac and will teleport him throughout the room; however, the damage is not dealt. [end edition note] 

• With items like Cube of Meat, Isaac can easily, but slowly, kill most enemies and bosses without taking any damage.

• Bombs can be placed while stationary and safely be stood on until they blow up if no other inputs are done after placing the bomb, as the invincibility state will be activated before the bomb explodes.
