The Battery.title: The Battery
The Battery.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the item; the pickup; Batteries]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Activated items can be overcharged, allowing them to store up to one extra use.

• Extra charges appear in yellow over the normal charge meter.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Afterbirth+] The Battery does not affect self-recharging activated items.

• [Before Repentance] Picking up a Lil' Battery while the held activated item's main charge bar isn't full will only fill the main charge bar without adding overcharge.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 48 Hour Energy pill: A fully discharged item will be doubly charged, along with spawning 1 or 2 Lil' Battery.

• AAA Battery: If Isaac's active item would have at least one full charge upon clearing a room, it gains two charges.

• Friendly Ball: Walking over a captured enemy will double charge the ball, allowing the enemy to be released, and allowing to catch a new one in the same room, and the process repeats. Trying to catch a new enemy while the old one hasn't spawned yet will have no effect.

• [Repentance] Jacob's Ladder / 120 Volt: Increases the amount of arcs a spark can generate. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Notched Axe: Causes remaining charge from the previous floor to carry over to the next one. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Extension Cord, Jumper Cables]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in It's in the Cards.

• The screws that appear in Isaac's head may be a reference to Frankenstein's Monster.

• The effect of this item was completely changed from the original Binding of Isaac. It's old effect gave Isaac an extra charge for his Activated Item every 15 seconds per room, up to a maximum of three charges. This was likely changed to prevent the boring, but optimal strategy of waiting in every room for 45 seconds for your active item to recharge.

fields.description: Activated items can be overcharged, allowing them to store up to one extra use.

The Bean.title: The Bean
The Bean.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [disambig msg: the activated item; challenge #13; Beans!; the activated item which knocks back enemies; Butter Bean; the passive item; The Black Bean]

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac farts, dealing 5 damage and poisoning any enemies within close range for 6 ticks.

• [Rebirth only] The poison deals 3.5 damage per tick.

• [Afterbirth onward] The poison deals Isaac's tear damage.

• The area of effect is 2 tiles in all directions.

• [Repentance] The fart also has knockback and deflects enemy projectiles with deflected projectiles dealing 6 damage if they would've hurt Isaac for half a heart, and 7 for a full heart.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Bird's Eye/Ghost Pepper: Poison farts shoot a fire behind Isaac. Two flames will be shot if Isaac also has Car Battery.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps surrounded by green stink clouds on the outer ring. The wisps deal 5 damage and poison nearby enemies when destroyed.

• Car Battery: Deals double damage, but the status effect lasts for the same amount of time.

• Gigante Bean: The fart deals 10 additional damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Second Hand: The poison duration is not affected.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is used in Beans!.

fields.description: Isaac farts, damaging and poisoning any enemy in close range.

The Belt.title: The Belt
The Belt.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • +0.3 speed.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In his first post-Repentance Lore Stream, Edmund McMillen revealed that The Belt is inspired by a real belt that his step-father would crack menacingly to threaten him with.

• The Belt granting a speed up is a nod to the act of running faster out of fear of being hit.

• In this way, The Belt is a counterpart to Wooden Spoon, which is also a speed-up item based on a specific object used by McMillen's parents to abuse him.

fields.description: +0.3 speed.

The Bible.title: The Bible
The Bible.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac flight for the current room.

• Instantly kills Mom, Mom's Heart, It Lives!, and their Mausoleum / Gehenna variants upon use.

• Kills Isaac instantly when used on Satan.

• Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

• Contributes to the Bookworm transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Using The Bible on Isaac, ???, The Lamb, Hush, Mega Satan, Delirium, Dogma, The Beast or Mother has no special effect and does not kill Isaac.

• Will not affect Delirium even if it is transformed into a relevant boss.

• Switching active items while The Bible is active does not remove the flight, allowing continued flight until the room is exited.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns white wisps in the middle ring. Wisps' tears have 0.75 shot speed and homing, and deal 6 damage +0.1 per floor.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: No effect.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: A Halo]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Bible is a set of Christian scriptures, consisting of 73 books of the Old and New Testaments (66 in Protestant Bibles).

• The Bible item instantly killing Mom, Mom's Heart, and It Lives!, is a reference to the epilogue of The Binding of Isaac when the Bible hits Mom's head, knocking out or killing her.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, using The Bible on Isaac or ??? would kill the player.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] This item is one of the only two ( [Repentance] five/ [Repentance+] six) in the game that work toward 2 transformations (Bookworm and Seraphim) and is the only activated item to. The other ones are Magic Mushroom, Hive Mind, Parasitoid, Skatole, [Repentance+] and The Necronomicon.

• With an ID of 33, The Bible is the very first active item on the ordered ID list, likely due to its plot relevance.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If The Bible is used on Mom with the Broken Remote trinket, it will not kill Mom and will instead teleport Isaac randomly to another room. However, this still unlocks The Halo as if Mom was killed with the Bible.

fields.description: Grants flight for the current room. Instantly kills Mom, Mom's Heart, and It Lives! when activated, but kills Isaac when used on Satan.

The Black Bean.title: The Black Bean
The Black Bean.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] When taking damage, Isaac farts, applying poison to all enemies in range.

• [Repentance] When taking damage, Isaac farts 5 times in quick succession. The farts poison and knock back enemies and projectiles, and leave lingering poison clouds. Deflected projectiles deal 7 damage.

• [Rebirth only] Farts deal 5 damage and the poison deals 21 damage over time.

• [Afterbirth onward] Farts deal 5 damage and the poison deals Isaac's tear damage for 6 ticks.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Ghost Pepper/Bird's Eye: Shoots a flame behind Isaac when he farts.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Second Hand: The poison duration is not increased.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is used in Beans!.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] When taking damage, Isaac farts, poisoning enemies in range.
[Repentance] When taking damage, Isaac farts five times, poisoning and knocking back nearby enemies and leaving lingering poison clouds.

The Bloat.title: The Bloat
The Bloat.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Bloat is a boss that can appear in Necropolis and:

• [Before Repentance] All environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb).

• [Repentance] The Utero.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Unlike Peep, The Bloat's eyes are dislocated at the start of the fight.

• The Bloat Eye float diagonally, bouncing off of walls, and do not take damage. They block Isaac's tears and inflict contact damage.

• Performs a small jump in place and fires eight projectiles in all directions.

• Unlike Peep's, The Bloat's projectiles are always shot in the same orientation.

• Creates large puddles of Red Creep.

• Jumps into the air and travels a moderate distance in Isaac's direction, leaving a small puddle of Red Creep and sending out a ring of eight projectiles upon landing.

• Fires 2 Brimstone lasers from his eye sockets, aiming below him or to both sides of him, depending on Isaac's location. This attack is not telegraphed and fires near-instantly, although it can be deliberately triggered by standing beside or above The Bloat's head.

• He can not perform this attack upwards.
The Bloat deals a whole heart of contact damage.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 5] : Fires 2 [Before Repentance] greenish-red/ [Repentance] green Ipecac projectiles instead of blood shots when performing a small jump, and 3 when jumping off-screen. Spawns 2 Chargers whenever he creates large puddles of Creep. [Repentance] Creates Green Creep instead of Red Creep.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The Bloat's eyes can be destroyed with Chaos Card, Euthanasia, God's Flesh, or Little Horn.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Bloat was added in the Wrath of the Lamb DLC for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• He is the posthumous version of Peep.

• Bloating is a medical condition in which the stomach becomes overstretched by excessive gas content.

• Corpses also bloat during decomposition due to the excessive build-up of gas-releasing bacteria.

• [Before Repentance] The Bloat's eyeballs look slightly different than Peep's.

• [Repentance] The Bloat's eyeballs are now very different than Peep's.

• Aprils Fool replaces all bosses with The Bloat as a reference to the exceptional hatred some fans express towards this boss.

• The Bloat cameos in Mewgenics, Edmund McMillen's latest game, as a miniboss.

• His eyes function more similar to Peep's in this appearance.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The Bloat's eyes have the same collision radius as The Bloat himself, which results in the eyes being difficult to dodge since the hitbox doesn't match up with the eyes' visual size.

The Body.title: The Body
The Body.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Adds three full Red Heart Containers.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item, along with The Mind and The Soul, are references to the Three Primes of Alchemy.

• The designs of these items appear to be that of Triquetra, a Christian symbol of the Trinity.

• The item's description, along with those of The Mind and The Soul, are references to the three attributes commonly ascribed to God in Christian theology: omniscience, omnipotence, and omnipresence. For The Body, it is omnipresence, the ability to be everywhere, thus to "feel all".

• By itself (without other items/pickups), the Body grants the most amount of Red Heart Containers out of all items in the game, and is the only one that grants three Red Heart Containers.

• Between this item, The Mind, and The Soul, The Body is the only one that cannot be summoned via the Lemegeton.

fields.description: Adds 3 Red Heart Containers.

The Book of Belial.title: The Book of Belial
The Book of Belial.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Not to be confused with Satanic Bible.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Gives +2 damage for the current room.

• [Rebirth only] Guarantees the Devil Room or Angel Room to spawn after killing a boss while holding it.

• [Afterbirth onward] Increases the chance to open the Devil Room or Angel Room after killing a boss by 12.5% while holding it.

• Contributes to the Bookworm transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Judas starts with this item by default.

• [Before Repentance] While activated, switching items will end the bonus damage effect.

• [Before Repentance] If the Schoolbag and a second activated item are held, the book must be equipped in the primary slot to receive the Devil Room / Angel Room bonus.

• [Rebirth only] Only guarantees Devil/Angel Rooms on floors that they can normally appear on, and, unlike Goat Head, picking up The Book of Belial after killing the boss will not open the Devil/Angel Room door.

• [Before Repentance] The damage bonus does not stack with multiple uses in the same room or with XV - The Devil.

• [Repentance] Additional uses in the same room or combined with XV - The Devil give +1 damage per use.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Blood of the Martyr: Causes The Book of Belial to apply a 1.5× damage multiplier on top of its normal effect. This multiplier cannot stack with multipliers from Cricket's Head or Magic Mushroom.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns black and red wisps in the middle ring. Wisps deal double damage compared to normal wisps.

• Car Battery: Gives +3 damage for the current room.

sections.heading: [Repentance] Judas' Birthright Combinations
sections.text:
While holding Birthright with Judas or Black Judas, The Book of Belial is able to be held alongside another active item, similarly to Book of Virtues. The book provides +0.66 damage for each charge of the held item. Items that do not require charges to use do not grant a damage bonus unless there is an exception listed below.

Certain active items also gain additional effects, which are noted below; any items not listed have their standard effects aside from the temporary damage up Birthright gives them.

[end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item can also increase the odds of getting an Angel Room, despite being a Satanic book.

• It is one of the four books in the Satanic Bible.

• Belial is a name used for Satan in some Jewish and Christian texts.

• [Repentance] This item is used in Bloody Mary (Challenge #37).

• [Repentance] The previously unused item ID 59 is now occupied by the active/passive version of The Book of Belial, which is obtained when Judas or Black Judas has Birthright.

• Despite this, this version of the item is not obtainable by other characters. If you use Spindown Dice on an item pedestal of item ID 60, The Ladder, it'll skip to Book of Shadows.

• [Repentance] The effect of Notched Axe with Judas' andBlack Judas' Birthright is a reference to Minecraft's enchanting mechanic.

• All of its upgrades are based on existing Minecraft enchantments — Unbreaking, Fire Aspect, Knockback, Efficiency, and Fortune.

• However, Fire Aspect and Knockback normally cannot be applied to pickaxes in Minecraft.

fields.description:
[Rebirth only] +2 damage for the current room. Passively guarantees a Devil Room or Angel Room will appear while held. [end edition note] 
[Afterbirth onward] +2 damage for the current room. Passively increases the chance of finding a Devil Room or Angel Room while held. [end edition note]

The Book of Sin.title: The Book of Sin
The Book of Sin.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• On use, spawns a random coin, heart, bomb, key, battery, pill or card near Isaac.

• Contributes to the Bookworm transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Hearts are proportionally more likely to be generated, with Red Hearts, Soul Hearts and Black Hearts each having a 1/9 chance of being chosen, the other 6/9 being distributed among the other categories.

• [Repentance] Each category has a 1/7 chance of being chosen.

• The card category includes runes, Dice Shard, Emergency Contact and Cracked Key.

• [Repentance] The heart category has the following distribution:
{| class="wikitable"
! Type !! Chance
|-
| Red Heart || 48.3%
|-
| Soul Heart || 16.1%
|-
| Black Heart || 16.1%
|-
| Bone Heart || 6.4%
|-
| Rotten Heart || 6.4%
|-
| Eternal Heart || 3.2%
|-
| Gold Heart || 3.2%
|}

• Half Red Hearts, Half Soul Hearts and Blended Hearts cannot be generated. [end edition note] 

• Penny can be of any type, with higher value coins, including Lucky Penny, and Sticky Nickel, being rarer.

• Bombs and Keys will always be singular (unless Isaac has BOGO Bombs and/or Humbleing Bundle).

• [Repentance] The Book of Sin cannot generate a Micro Battery.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Grants a random wisp based on one of the Seven Deadly Sins. The wisp spawned isn't linked to the pickup dropped.

• Pride: a blue bomb wisp in the middle ring. When destroyed, a small homing bomb that deals normal troll bomb damage is spawned.

• Greed: 3 yellow coin wisps in the outer ring. Their tears may petrify enemies like Midas' Touch.

• Wrath: an orange bomb wisp in the middle ring, which fire flaming tears. They drop troll bombs when continuously firing, and leave a bomb pickup when they die.

• Envy: a white face-like wisp in the outer ring.

• Lust: a randomly colored pill wisp in the inner ring, with effects that are the same as Mom's Bottle of Pills wisps.

• Gluttony: a heart wisp in the middle ring, with effects that are the same as Yum Heart wisps.

• Sloth: a Bob's Head wisp in the middle ring. Their tears travel in an arc like Ipecac but don't always explode on impact. There is a small chance for an exploding tear.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Book of Sin is a reference to the Seven Deadly Sins. Unlike other Book items, The Book of Sin doesn't appear to be based on a real book or scripture.

fields.name: The Book of Sin
fields.description: Spawns a random coin, heart, bomb, key, battery, pill or card near Isaac.

The Boomerang.title: The Boomerang
The Boomerang.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• On use, Isaac readies the Boomerang. Pressing a fire key will throw it in the chosen direction, and it will return shortly afterward.

• Any pickups hit will return to Isaac with the Boomerang.

• Enemies hit by it will take double Isaac's current damage and are petrified for about 2 seconds.

• [Repentance] Boomerang pierces enemies it hits.

• The Boomerang will only hit a given enemy once during its travel time.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The Boomerang starts to recharge only after it has returned to Isaac.

• The Boomerang can grab pickups from afar, even over obstacles.

• The Boomerang can be used to destroy any Shopkeepers.

• If Isaac has low damage, the shopkeeper won’t get destroyed and will instead flash red as if taking damage.

• The Boomerang can damage Host and Mobile Host enemies even while under their shells.

• [Before Repentance] The Boomerang's range scales with Isaac's range stat.

• [Repentance] The Boomerang's range scales with Isaac's tear height.

• The Boomerang can hit and stun The Haunt or Lil' Haunts even when they are invincible.

• The Boomerang is unable to pick up Sticky Nickels, or Chests.

• With enough speed, it is possible to have two Boomerangs in the air at the same time.

• [Before Afterbirth+] The Boomerang can grab troll bombs.

• [Repentance] The item only costs 10 coins when found in a Shop.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the middle ring. Wisps' tears have the My Reflection effect and do not persist between rooms.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• Angelic Prism: No effect on the Boomerang's attack.

• [Repentance] Kidney Stone / Number One / Pluto / Inner Child's revive: The Boomerang loses almost all of its range, and can only be improved with tear height ups. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Boomerang is a recurring item in The Legend of Zelda series. The icon used is inspired by The Magic Boomerangs appearance in the firstThe Legend of Zelda game.

• [Afterbirth onward] This item is used in I RULE!.

• This item can be found as one of the Nintendo-themed Treasure Room items in the 6th of December's Daily Run, which is an homage to the late CEO of Nintendo, Satoru Iwata.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: The Boomerang can collide with The Ladder when deployed, causing it to immediately return to Isaac when thrown. It doesn't always happen.

fields.description: Throws a boomerang which retrieves pickups, as well as damages and petrifies enemies hit for 2 seconds. [Repentance] Pierces through enemies.

The Cage.title: The Cage
The Cage.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Cage is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] Only in the Depths.

• [Repentance] In the Depths and the Dank Depths.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Leaps off-screen and tries to land in Isaac's path, predicting his movement. Leaves a small puddle of damaging Grey Creep and sends out 4-5 lines of rock waves upon landing.

• Quickly shoots 6 streams of 3-7 projectiles in a spiral pattern, similar to Mom's Heart/It Lives!.

• Curls up in a ball and rolls towards Isaac, bouncing off walls and obstacles around the room.

• Spawns a grey-coloured Vis that shoots a brown-coloured Brimstone laser.

• The different colours are purely cosmetic, and it behaves exactly like a normal Vis.

• Any Vis caught in The Cage's rolling attack will be killed.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 5] : Periodically leaves puddles of Green Creep and doesn't spawn any Vis.
[bc: 20] : Two Cages, each with 50% HP (400), replace the normal Cage. They never perform their jump attack. [Repentance] Both Cages are ~50% smaller.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Host Hat and Pyromaniac make Isaac immune to The Cage's rock waves, since it is considered to be the same as explosions by the game.

• When The Cage jumps, there is a delay to his falling animation, causing Isaac to be hurt before The Cage falls back down.

• If Isaac is flying on Pits, The Cage can hit Isaac if it jumps towards him, and it will then be pushed back to the ground.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It has the highest health of any boss fought before Mom's Heart.

• Despite being a possible encounter before Mom, The Cage has more HP than her.

• It is the posthumous version of Mega Fatty. It appears to have lost its head.

• Although The Cage is a dead version of Mega Fatty, it also bears a lot of resemblances to a giant Vis as well, since it is a fat headless body with a giant cut in its belly. Another slight nod to their resemblance is The Cage's ability to spawn Vis with a Grey color palette and a Brown Brimstone laser.

• The stitches on the Cage's body resemble Y-shaped incisions commonly made at the start of an autopsy.

The Candle.title: The Candle
The Candle.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, Isaac raises the candle above his head. On pressing a fire button, a blue flame, similar to a Blue Fire Place, will fire in the chosen direction, extinguishing itself after a fixed time of approximately two seconds.

• [Before Repentance] The flame deals 23 damage per damage tick.

• [Before Repentance] The maximum damage dealt by a single flame is around 276, dealing damage roughly 6 times per second.

• [Repentance] The flame decreases in damage over time, starting at 23 per tick at max size, until it scales down to 11.5 per tick at minimum size.

• [Repentance] The maximum damage dealt by a single flame is around 160, dealing damage roughly 6 times per second.

• The flame also destroys enemy shots it comes into contact with.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] While Isaac holds the candle above his head, his movement speed is reduced.

• [Before Repentance] Will block Isaac's tears, unlike Red Candle and won't burn him.

• Flames do not drop any collectibles when doused.

• The flame can destroy Shopkeepers.

• The flame projectile can pass over Pits, but can not travel through Rocks or Poop.

• The flames from this item can put out Fire Places.

• [Repentance] The flame can ignite gas clouds such as ones found in Dross. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns blue wisps on the middle ring. The wisps do not persist between rooms.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• [Repentance+] Spawns a second flame that travels a shorter distance.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Legend of Zelda, a major inspiration for The Binding of Isaac, also has a blue candle item that can be activated once per room to create flames for burning enemies and bushes, as well as lighting dark rooms. Unlike in Isaac however, the red candle is an upgrade of the blue one, which can be activated any number of times per room.

• The Red Candle is a variation of this item unlocked after donating 400 coins, diminishing on damage dealt instead of time.

• The Candle was an item in The Binding of Isaac: Wrath of the Lamb where it used to be the only auto-recharging item.

• In the Wrath of the Lamb DLC, this item was originally unlocked by beating a challenge titled, "Dark was the Night".

• Although this item is normally only available in the Shop, it can be found as one of the Nintendo-themed Treasure Room items in the 6th of December's Daily Run, which is an homage to the late CEO of Nintendo, Satoru Iwata.

fields.name: The Candle
fields.description: Throws out a blue flame that damages everything in its path, diminishing in size as it travels.

The Common Cold.title: The Common Cold
The Common Cold.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Adds a chance to shoot poison tears, dealing damage over time when inflicted.

• [Rebirth only] The poison randomly hits either 2 or 3 times, dealing a total of 4 or 6 damage.

• [Afterbirth onward] The poison hits 2 times, dealing a total of 2x Isaac's damage.

sections.heading: Notes
Synergies
sections.text:
• Abyss: When Isaac uses Abyss to absorb The Common Cold it turns into a green locust that poisons enemies.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/Haemolacria/The Parasite: Chance for tears and split tears to be poisonous. If the main tear is poisonous, the split tears are too.

• Dr. Fetus/Epic Fetus: Chance for bombs/explosions to become poisonous like Bob's Curse.

• Finger!: Finger can also apply the poison effect.

• Lachryphagy: If a poison tear is fed, all burst tears are poisonous. If a normal tear is fed, the burst tears are not poisonous.

• The Ludovico Technique: The tear flickers green, capable of poisoning enemies when it does.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Ipecac/Scorpio: Overrides The Common Cold.

• Serpent's Kiss: Both poison effects work, but poison caused by Common Cold will not cause Black Heart drops. There is no way to tell which poison is applied.

• Pinky Eye: Activation rates are individually applied to each tear, effectively allowing for higher amounts of poison tears. However at 12 Luck, the trinket will not do anything for Isaac as The Common Cold is guaranteed to make every tear poisoned at that point.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• In the original The Binding of Isaac, this item also belonged to the Devil Room pool.

• In the original game, this item was unlocked by collecting two of the following items in one run: Roid Rage, The Virus, Growth Hormones

sections.heading: References
sections.text: • The Binding of Isaac Item Trigger Testing

fields.description: Adds a chance to shoot poison tears, dealing damage over time when inflicted.

The Compass.title: The Compass
The Compass.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text: • Reveals the locations and types of all special rooms on the map, except Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The following rooms will be revealed if they exist:

• When combined with Blue Map and Treasure Map, the entire floor is revealed, identical to the effect of The Mind.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Secrets: It is easier to gain X-Ray Vision as Book of Secrets cannot give a mapping effect Isaac already has.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The compass icon is the same as the one from the the game The Legend of Zelda.

• This item is used in Cursed!.

• [Repentance] Under the minimap, The Mind's icon will override the icon of this item.

• This item can be found as one of the Nintendo-themed Treasure Room items in the 6th of December's Daily Run, which is an homage to the late CEO of Nintendo, Satoru Iwata.

fields.description: Reveals the locations and types of all special rooms on the map, except Secret Rooms and Super Secret Rooms.

The D6.title: The D6
The D6.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: • Upon use, replaces every item in the current room (not pickups or trinkets) with other random items corresponding to the current room's item pool.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] The D6 is a special item.

• Isaac starts with this item once it is unlocked.

• Since it re-rolls every item in the room, it can be more efficient to use it in rooms where multiple items are in the same room. For instance:

• In the Shop, when multiple items are available for purchase.

• In the Devil Room, when there are multiple deals offered.

• In the Boss Room after the Mom fight, where both The Polaroid and The Negative can be rerolled, at the cost of the opportunity to go to the Chest/Dark Room. Once one item is picked up the other will disappear.

• In the Angel Room, when there is a choice between multiple items.

• In the Boss Rush Room, where all items can be rerolled at once.

• When There's Options or More Options spawn two items.

• Items from Chests can be rerolled.

• When an item from a chest is rerolled, the item is rolled from the current room's item pool, and not the chest's

• When an item pool is exhausted, the pool will start to use the Treasure Room.

• When the Treasure Room is exhausted, every item in it will be rerolled to Breakfast.

• With Chaos, every fully depleted item pool will only contain Breakfast.

• [Rebirth only] If Isaac runs out of red hearts in the Devil Room, then rerolls, the prices of the items switch over to soul hearts.

• [Before Repentance] Using the D6 on an active item yields different rerolls depending on whether you picked up the active item first.

• Using the D6 to reroll items duplicated with Diplopia will reroll all the items into different items. The copied item will not be rerolled into the same one as the original item.

• Be careful when rerolling, as it will replace the item with another item from the current room's item pool, even if the item came from a different pool, or is a set drop. This can be used as an advantage in various ways; for example, after defeating The Fallen, the item will be drawn from the Devil Room, so Isaac can safely roll the item into another from that pool. This behavior can also be an advantage in Angel Rooms since Key Piece 1 and Key Piece 2 can be rerolled to get a free Angel Room item.

• Normal rooms use the Treasure Room.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns a D6 wisp in the middle ring. An extra wisp is spawned per item rerolled.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: Re-rolls twice instantly without any benefits, doubling the speed of depleting item pools.

• Glitched Crown: When the D6 is used, all 5 items will be re-rolled.

• Soul of Isaac: Using the D6 re-rolls the current item and cancels alternation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Although the D6 is considered a Special Item, it will only count as a special item if found naturally during gameplay. Starting with the D6 as Isaac will not cause fewer special items to appear later on. This fact also extends to Eden's starting items: if Eden starts with a special item, that item will not count toward the special item total.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, the D6 had a recharge time of 3 instead of 6.

• The D6 could not reroll special boss items in the original game, such as Little C.H.A.D. and Little Steven.

• In the Eternal Edition of the original Binding of Isaac, The D6 has a chance to delete the item instead of rerolling it when playing in hard mode.

• [Repentance] The Eternal D6 has the same effect but with a 2 room charge.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, this item was called "The Dice".

• Like the other dice items, the D6 uses the naming scheme of dice for tabletop RPGs like Dungeons & Dragons, which were associated with devil worship during the Satanic Panic.

• The D7, D8, D12, D20, D100, Spindown Dice, and D infinity has the sides displayed with numbers, while D1, D4, The D6, and the Eternal D6 has sides displayed with pips.

• The D6 is the only dice item that includes ‘The’ in its name.

• This may be because it is ‘The’ quintessential dice item; being the first added to the game, arguably the most iconic, and the only one featured as a starting item - for Isaac himself, no less.

fields.name: The D6
fields.description: Re-rolls all items in the current room into other items, depending on the current room's item pool.

The Duke of Flies.title: The Duke of Flies
The Duke of Flies.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: The Duke of Flies is a boss that can appear in all environments of Chapter 1 (Basement, Cellar, Burning Basement).

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
The Duke of Flies constantly floats around the room in diagonal directions. Knockback from tears and other sources can cause him to change travel direction. He has three attacks that he can perform while he floats:

• Spawns 3 Attack Fly that will orbit around him, blocking shots.

• Spawns a larger Attack Fly that will chase Isaac.

• Sends any orbital Flies outward to chase Isaac.

• He can only perform this attack if he has 5-6 orbiting Flies.

• • If he has 4 orbiting Flies, he cannot perform this attack nor can he spawn more as it would exceed his limit resulting in him only spawning the larger Attack Flies.

• The Duke of Flies will never spawn Flies if 12 already exist.

• Upon death, all orbiting Flies will be free to chase Isaac.

• [Repentance] Spawns 6 random Fly or Attack Flies upon death.

• Unlike regular Attack Flies, the ones spawned by The Duke of Flies can be killed if Isaac walks into them, though they will still deal contact damage before dying.

• [Repentance] This does not include the Attack Flies spawned on death.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 5] : Spawns Moters instead of the large Attack Flies and shoots blood shots in eight directions when spreading the orbiting flies. He can spread the Attack Flies at any moment instead of only performing it when having enough of them orbiting him, similar to The Husk.
[bc: 6] : 15% larger than normal with 25% more HP (137.5) and spawns Suckers instead of the large Attack Flies.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • If Isaac has the Beelzebub transformation, the Attack Flies that The Duke of Flies spawns will instantly turn into blue flies which damage him.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Duke of Flies appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• In the original Binding of Isaac, the flies in the Duke's mouth were animated; this was removed in Rebirth but re-added in Repentance.

• The Duke seems to be a human corpse in the bloating stage of decomposition, filled to the brim with flies. The Duke has bloated to the point that he has lost his once-human silhouette, becoming nothing more than a sphere with dangling nubs that used to be its appendages.

• Any enemy summoned by the Duke dies immediately upon making contact with Isaac.

• [Afterbirth onward] He is the boss version of the Dukies.

• The Husk is his posthumous version.

• The stitching under The Duke of Flies' mouth is an autopsy stitch, an incision in the shape of a Y. The incision allows passage to the cadaver's insides; when the autopsy is complete, it is stitched back up.

• The name "Duke of Flies" is a reference to the demon Beelzebub, and an alternate name for the devil who is known by the title "Lord of the Flies".

• The name could also be a reference to the book "Lord of the Flies", specifically the character named Lord of the Flies — a severed pig's head mounted on a pike, swarming with flies.

• [Before Repentance] When under the effects of Curse of Darkness, a brief flash of light is seen when The Duke of Flies summons flies.

• Edmund McMillen has confirmed The Duke Of Flies to be his favorite boss design in The Binding Of Isaac in an AMA thread.

• In another AMA for the Binding of Isaac subreddit, Edmund had also confirmed The Duke Of Flies to be a super old design, before Meat Boy in 2007. However, he never used the design until developing The Binding Of Isaac.

• The Duke of Flies additionally returns in the Binding of Isaac spinoff, The Legend of Bum-bo, under the simpler name of "The Duke", which further concretes him as being special to Edmund.

• [Repentance] In Repentance, The Duke Of Flies resembles his sprite from the original Binding of Isaac.

• [Repentance] Although it is difficult to tell, the Green Champion Duke of Flies visually has a Moter within his mouth, reflecting his behavior.

• The Duke of Flies, along with Mom's Knife and Isaac himself, were chosen to appear in Fortnite. The Duke himself is an emote.

The Fallen.title: The Fallen
The Fallen.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Fallen is a boss that can appear on any main path Chapter, with the prerequisite that Isaac has entered (not just encountered) a Devil Room through any methods, and with the following exceptions:

• It cannot appear on floors with predetermined bosses such as Mom, Mom's Heart, Isaac, etc.

• [Repentance] It also cannot appear on any of the alternate Chapters added in Repentance.
It is also encountered as the first phase of the Satan battle.

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
The Fallen moves randomly around the room in cardinal directions and can perform the following attacks:

• Fires 3 projectiles in a spread followed by 4 projectiles in a spread in succession towards Isaac.

• Increases its speed and chases Isaac. After taking a certain amount of damage, it halts and fires a Brimstone laser in each cardinal direction.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
• At 50% health, The Fallen splits into two smaller versions of itself. The two clones have identical behaviour.

• It is possible to avoid the split if the Fallen takes a single hit doing more than 50% damage that causes poisoning or burning as the final one.
The Fallen deals a whole heart of contact damage in both phases.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Unlike other bosses, the item pool of the Fallen room is the Devil Room item pool.

• [Rebirth only] Leaving and re-entering the room will change the item pool to the normal Boss Room item pool.

• The Fallen can appear on the first floor during a Victory Lap if a Devil Room was entered during the previous lap. Even more rarely, it is possible to encounter him on a normal run if the first level was rerolled with Forget Me Now or a 5-pip Dice Room after visiting the Devil Room by teleporting with a Joker card, a Red Chest, or similar methods.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Fallen appeared in the Halloween Update for the original The Binding of Isaac.

• Under normal circumstances, the Fallen is one of six bosses (the other five being Conquest, Headless Horseman, Krampus, Baby Plum if spared, and Bumbino if he picks up enough coins) who drop or can drop active items upon defeat.

• The Fallen is both visually and behaviorally similar to Krampus.

• [Before Repentance] Despite the first phase of The Fallen having a death animation before splitting into clones, the clones themselves don't have a death animation. [Repentance] The clones now have a death animation, like the main Fallen.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Previously, only Crusade would play when The Fallen appeared as Satan's first phase. As of Booster Pack #5, Cerebrum Dispersio also has a chance to play in this situation.

• This also applies to when the Angels are fought normally (by bombing the Angel statues).

• The Boss might represent Satan or another fallen angel who fell from grace and became evil.

• The Fallen is tied with Krampus as having the highest Stage HP among all entities in the game.

• Double Trouble Fallen encounters in The Womb/Utero do not require the player to have entered a Devil Room before. Upon defeat, they will still drop a Devil Room item.

• The Fallen could appear in the alternative chapters in Antibirth.

The Forsaken.title: The Forsaken
The Forsaken.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Forsaken is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 2 (Caves, Catacombs, Flooded Caves).

• [Repentance] Only in the Catacombs and the Flooded Caves. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
• Spawns a Bony.

• While at least one Bony is still alive, the Forsaken becomes incorporeal and floats erratically around the room staying away from Isaac and very occasionally drifts towards Isaac attempting to pass through him.

• Every tear shot towards the Forsaken during this phase passes through it.

• When at around 30% HP, it spawns 2 Bonies instead.

• When all Bonies are killed, The Forsaken moves close to the center of the room before reappearing and firing 3 Brimstone lasers in triangular directions with one laser always shooting in the opposite direction of Isaac. These lasers then rotate just over 180 degrees in either direction.

• Afterwards it stays vulnerable for a few moments before spawning another Bony and repeating the process.

• Unlike its counterparts, The Haunt and The Heretic, The Forsaken does not deal contact damage while incorporeal. Rather, if Isaac walks through The Forsaken, it spawns another Bony, briefly becoming vulnerable while doing so.

• If this is repeated without killing any Bonies until there are 4 alive on-screen, the next time Isaac walks through The Forsaken, it performs a modified version of its Brimstone attack with greatly increased speed and duration, killing off all Bonies.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 18] : Spawns Black Bony instead of regular Bonies. The Spinning Brimstone attack is replaced with The Forsaken spawning 4 Dank Death's Heads and resuming invincibility for 1 second if there are no other Dank Death's Heads alive. It can not spawn any Dank Death's Heads if there is at least 1 other alive and will instead remain vulnerable for a duration before spawning another Black Bony.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • The Forsaken can be instantly killed with Vade Retro if it is at 50% health or below.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It is the posthumous version of The Haunt.

• When The Forsaken disappears, it covers its eyesockets with its arm-like bones. This is most likely a reference to Boos from the Mario franchise.

• The Forsaken appears to be The Haunt without its ghostly exterior.

• During the versus screen, the Forsaken's Bony-spawning sound can be heard.

• The Forsaken is one of [Before Repentance] seven/ [Repentance] five bosses that can be heard during the versus screen, the other [Before Repentance] six/ [Repentance] four being The Stain, Big Horn, Mom, [Before Repentance] Mom's Heart, [Before Repentance] It Lives!, and Mother.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Forsaken can be found in The Void, even before being unlocked. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] The Forsaken has an alternative resurrected variation known as The Heretic.

The Frail.title: The Frail
The Frail.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Frail is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In all environments of Chapter 2 (Caves, Catacombs, Flooded Caves).

• [Repentance] Only in the Catacombs and the Flooded Caves. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text: The Frail in its first phase has 100 HP like Pin and behaves identically, with the only difference that The Frail is less accurate in its jumps and generally overshoots or undershoots Isaac.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
Upon its HP being depleted, The Frail's appearance becomes skeletal. It now has 200 HP and performs the following attacks:

• Jumps out of the ground towards Isaac, firing 4 diagonal projectiles from the last section of its body that each split into 4 more projectiles in either cardinal or diagonal directions.

• [Repentance] Whether it fires projectiles depends on the length of its jump: does not fire projectiles on short jumps, fires projectiles shortly upon exiting the jump on regular/medium jumps, and fires projectiles both shortly upon exiting and after a few moments airborne on long jumps.

• Partially emerges head-first and:

• Fires a Brimstone laser at Isaac, rotating to follow his movements.

• Fires a quick, non-moving Brimstone laser at Isaac 2 times before stopping.

• After performing any of these attacks, The Frail will always jump out of the same spot it entered.

• Partially emerges tail-first and fires a burst of white projectiles in all directions which leave small puddles of slowing White Creep where they land.

• After performing this attack, The Frail will always jump or appear head-first out of the same spot it entered.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 18] : Starts in its second phase, with only 66.6% HP (200) total.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It is the posthumous version of Pin.

• The definition of the word frail is weak and delicate, which explains its rotting body and depressed look in The Frail's first phase.

• The main body of The Frail's battle sprite is heavily based on Larry Jr.'s battle sprite.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Frail can be found in The Void, even before being unlocked.

• The name is possibly a reference to the Nine Inch Nails song of the same name.

• It is the boss version of the Pasty.

• Even if it is the boss version of Pasties, it precedes their addition.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: The Black Champion is intended to spawn in the second phase with 30% more HP (390), but the second phase is coded to always spawn at 66.6% HP (200) total. 
Bug note: If The Frail is under the effects of Broken Modem in mid-air, its jump will be stopped and it will fall.

The Gamekid.title: The Gamekid
The Gamekid.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, transforms Isaac into a Pac-Man-like creature for 6.5 seconds and provides the following effects:

• Gives invulnerability.

• Inflicts fear on all enemies.

• Removes the ability to shoot tears.

• [Before Repentance] Allows Isaac to deal 40 contact damage to enemies, at the rate of 1 hit per second per enemy.

• [Repentance] Allows Isaac to deal 20 contact damage to enemies, at the rate of 2 hits per second per enemy.

• • If an enemy is at 40 HP or less, the contact damage is increased to 40 for that enemy.

• Each enemy that dies during the duration has a chance to replenish a Half Red Heart even if they weren't killed by Isaac's contact damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The invulnerability effect negates almost all forms of damage, including health loss from Blood Donation Machines and Devil Beggars.

• This also negates damage from entering or exiting a Curse Room, but the effect is immediately removed upon walking through the door.

• Does not prevent damage from the door to the Mausoleum / Gehenna.

• Does not prevent Red Heart container loss from Health Down pills or Devil deals.

• This item is very similar to My Little Unicorn, trading the extra speed for the ability to gain health from killing enemies.

• Power Pill! has the same effect as The Gamekid, same goes with Cartridge on getting hit.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• 4.5 Volt: With some damage source while this item is active, it can be permanently invulnerable inside the room while you have enemies.

• If combined with 9 Volt, it will be easier to achieve invincibility.

• ???'s Only Friend: The fly can still be controlled while invincible.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps in the inner ring, looking like little Pac-Men. Wisps' tears have the Anti-Gravity effect and can inflict fear on enemies.

• Car Battery: Doubles the length of invincibility, but no effect on damage.

• Mom's Knife does contact damage in the same direction it was being held at the time of using it, giving a massive amount of free damage by ramming into an enemy.

• If you have the Yes Mother? Transformation, you can basically do the same thing using this item.

• Damage on contact items (Aries, The Virus, etc.) and Orbital Familiars (Cube of Meat, Sacrificial Dagger, etc.): Deals damage on top of The Gamekid's damage and invincibility.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that are turned into pickups don’t have a chance to heal Isaac.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that are turned into Poop don’t have a chance to heal Isaac.

• E. Coli Usually turns non-boss enemies into poop when Isaac attempts to deal contact damage making heals off of contact damage kills much harder.

• [edition rnr+] Freeze Effects: Effects that can still freeze enemies while the item is active do not grant the chance to heal Isaac.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Beating the game whilst under the effects of The Gamekid, Unicorn Stump, My Little Unicorn or the Power Pill will cause the credits music and ending animation to be sped up dramatically.

• This item's name and appearance are references to the Nintendo Game Boy.

• The pickup quote and Isaac's appearance while under the effects of The Gamekid are references to Pac-Man.

• Tetris appears to be the game being played on The Gamekid. Tetris was also the launch title for the Nintendo Game Boy.

fields.description: Transforms Isaac into a rainbow-colored chomping creature for 6.5 seconds. Grants invulnerability, inflicts fear on all enemies, and has a chance of replenishing a Half Red Heart every time an enemy is killed.

The Gate.title: The Gate
The Gate.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The Gate is a boss that can appear:

• [Before Repentance] In the Depths and Necropolis.

• [Repentance] In the Depths and the Dank Depths.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Like Mega Maw, The Gate is stationary and will perform the following attacks:

• Spawns a Leaper into the air. It can land anywhere in the room while releasing its projectile attack immediately.

• There is a maximum of 4 Leapers alive at once.

• The Gate cannot perform other attacks if there are no Leapers alive. As such, it will also always perform this attack first.

• Shoots a ring of 9 projectiles that can rotate in either direction while expanding outwards.

• Shoots two rings of 6 projectiles which expand outwards and rotate in opposite directions.

• Shoots a ring of 11 straight projectiles in all directions.

• The Gate's projectiles can damage its Leapers.

• If there are 2-3 Leapers alive, it charges up and fires a Brimstone laser that curves to connect to all Leapers that are not off-screen.

• This kills any Leapers hit.

• If faced alongside other enemies or bosses, such as in Boss Rush, the laser connects to them, damaging them as well.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text:
[bc: 18] : Has 25% more HP (625) and spawns Big Spiders instead of Leapers. The Big Spiders are tossed directly towards Isaac instead of landing randomly in the room, and can be damaged by The Gate's blood shots, like the Leapers. It does not perform the Brimstone attack.
[bc: 1] : Does not spawn any enemies and has a completely different set of attacks, including:
Fires 5 lines of 2-3 slow-moving homing purple shots.
Fires 8 lines of 9 blood shots that spiral outwards.
Fires 7 lines of 9 blood shots that pulsate outwards.
Fires 8 lines of 9 blood shots that move outwards in a zigzag pattern.
All the attacks of the Red version do 1 heart of damage.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Using the Eraser to remove Leapers causes The Gate to be stuck attempting to spawn them infinitely, as it cannot perform other attacks without any Leapers alive.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It is the posthumous version of Mega Maw.

• Despite being a posthumous version of Mega Maw, The Gate physically resembles a giant Host.

• It's also larger than Mega Maw.

• Upon death, a small Isaac head can be seen poking out of its corpse before it explodes.

• Two glowing white eyes can be seen in its mouth throughout the fight, which may also be the Isaac head.

• [Repentance] The Red Champion Gate's death animation reveals a small demon instead, whose glowing red eyes can also be seen in its mouth during the fight.

Tammy's Head.title: Tammy's Head
Tammy's Head.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Shoots 10 tears in a circle around Isaac.

• The tears retain the range, shot speed, and special effects (such as poison) of Isaac's tears.

• Each tear will do Isaac's current damage and a flat +25 damage bonus on top.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: The effect of Tammy's Head is similar to Isaac's Tears, but Tammy's Head will benefit from tear-replacing items like Brimstone, unlike Isaac's Tears.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Azazel / Brimstone: Isaac will fire Brimstone lasers in all directions. [Before Repentance] Each laser is given bonus damage.

• This will deal a substantial amount of damage near the center of the effect due to how lasers overlap the closer you get to Isaac.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns pale wisps in the outer ring. The wisps' tears deal 1.5 damage, but fire twice as fast as standard wisps. Tears are inaccurate and fire in a spread.

• Car Battery: Shoots 20 tears in a circle around Isaac.

• [Before Repentance] Chocolate Milk: The size and damage of tears shot depends on how far Chocolate Milk is charged.

• Tainted Azazel: Although Tainted Azazel's Brimstone beams do not have a damage bonus, they also do not have the normal damage penalty and still deal double damage to enemies that have been sneezed on.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Dr. Fetus / Ipecac: Tears are replaced by bombs or exploding shots, which may result in self-damage.

• Epic Fetus: Fires only normal tears.

• Eye of the Occult: The tears quickly lose their outward momentum and can now be controlled all at once, making it easy to make the tears hit enemies.

• Mom's Knife: The tears are replaced with knives that deal double Isaac's damage, but move very quickly, have a small hitbox, and don't return to Isaac.

• Trisagion: Shoots Trisagion blasts without any increase to their damage.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Parasite]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Tammy's Head is named after one of Edmund McMillen's cats.

• When Repentance released, this item was removed from Golden Chests, but it wasn't added into any other item pool besides the Crane Game, effectively making it impossible to find normally. This was later rectified.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: With the Mom's Knife synergy, the Blindfolded condition prevents Tammy's Head from shooting knives and makes the item useless.

fields.name: Tammy's Head
fields.description: Shoots 10 tears in a circle around Isaac, which retain the damage, range, shot speed, and special effects (such as poison) of Isaac's tears. Tears from this item have a +25 flat damage bonus.

Tape Worm.title: Tape Worm
Tape Worm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] x2 range.

• [Repentance] +3 range.

• [Before Repentance] x0.5 tear falling speed.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance+] This trinket has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Pin, Larry Jr., The Hollow or Scolex. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Mom's Box: Quadruples the range.

• Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Having either increases range by 6. Having both by 9.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Azazel: Increases the laser's range, but doesn't double it.

• Dr. Fetus: Shot bombs are very fast.

• Incubus / Fate's Reward: Only tear falling speed affects their shots, usually lowering effective range.

• Ipecac: Reduces the effective range of shots, as they fall faster.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The Tapeworm is a well-known species of Cestoda, a class of parasitic flatworms of the phylum Platyhelminthes, who can reach many meters of length within their host's intestines.

fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Doubles Isaac's range and halves his tear falling speed.
[Repentance] +3 range.

Tarot Cloth.title: Tarot Cloth
Tarot Cloth.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Drops a random tarot card on pickup.

• [Before Repentance] Adds an extra effect to a card, rune, or other card-like pickup.

• [Repentance] Adds an extra effect to certain tarot cards.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
Items not listed do not benefit from Tarot Cloth.

• [Repentance] I - The Magician: Gives The Book of Belial effect on top of homing.

• [Repentance] II - The High Priestess: Another foot strikes down shortly after the first.

• III - The Empress: Doubles the speed increase and quadruples the damage increase.

• [Repentance] IV - The Emperor: If the boss has not yet been defeated, grants a Soul Heart on top of teleporting Isaac.

• V - The Hierophant: Spawns [Before Repentance] four or [Repentance] three Soul Hearts.

• VI - The Lovers: Spawns [Before Repentance] four or [Repentance] three Red Hearts.

• VII - The Chariot: Doubles the duration of the invulnerability.

• VIII - Justice: Spawns twice as many pickups.

• [Repentance] IX - The Hermit: Prevents Greed/Super Greed from spawning in the shop. If the shop was already entered and Greed/Super Greed was fought, using the card turns it into a normal shop. (Does not create a working shop in the Mirrored World.)

• X - Wheel of Fortune: Spawns two Slot Machines.

• XI - Strength: Doubles the stat increases, but the damage multiplier applies only once.

• XIII - Death: Deals 80 damage to all enemies in the room.

• XIV - Temperance: Spawns two Blood Donation Machines.

• [Repentance] XV - The Devil: Damage increase is doubled.

• XVI - The Tower: Spawns 13 Troll Bombs. 

• [Repentance] XVII - The Stars: If the treasure room was not entered before, it will have two items to choose from, as if More Options was active. This will not work if the card teleports you to a Planetarium. [end edition note] 

• XIX - The Sun: Deals [Before Repentance] 200 damage or [Repentance] 400 damage to all enemies in the room.

• XX - Judgement: Spawns two Beggars.

• [Before Repentance] 2 of Clubs: Quadruples Isaac's Bombs.

• [Before Repentance] 2 of Diamonds: Quadruples Isaac's Penny.

• [Before Repentance] 2 of Spades: Quadruples Isaac's Keys.

• [Before Repentance] 2 of Hearts: Quadruples Isaac's Red Hearts.

• [Before Repentance] Suicide King: Spawns twice as many pickups/items/Chests.

• [Before Repentance] ? Card: Activates the effect of Isaac's active item twice.

• [Before Repentance] Ancient Recall: Spawns 6 cards.

• [Before Repentance] Algiz: Doubles the duration of the shield, making it last a full minute.

• [Before Repentance] Berkano: Spawns 6 Blue Flies and 6 Blue Spiders.

• [Before Repentance] Dagaz: Removes any curses from the current floor and grants two Soul Hearts.

• [Before Repentance] Jera: Quadruples all pickups and chests in the room.

• [Before Repentance] Perthro: Instantly re-rolls items twice, essentially removing an extra item from the item pool.

• [Before Repentance] Blank Rune: Activates two random rune effects. Attempts to spawn additional Blank Rune twice.

• [Before Repentance] Black Rune: Deals 80 damage to all enemies in the room. Other effects are unchanged.

• 0 - The Fool?: Drops Isaac's 6 most recently collected items on the floor, alongside pickups. Does not affect quest items (e.g. The Polaroid) or Missing No..

• III - The Empress?: Adds a total of three temporary heart containers.

• V - The Hierophant?: Spawns 3 Bone Hearts.

• VI - The Lovers?: Removes 2 heart containers or 4 Soul Hearts, adds 2 broken hearts and spawns 2 items.

• VIII - Justice?: Spawns 4-14 Locked Chests.

• IX - The Hermit?: Spawns 1 additional Penny.

• X - Wheel of Fortune?: Invokes an additional Dice Room effect.

• XII - The Hanged Man?: Doubles the effect's duration.

• XIV - Temperance?: Forces Isaac to eat 10 pills.

• XVI - The Tower?: Spawns 14 rock clusters.

• XVII - The Stars?: Removes 2 items and spawns 4.

• XX - Judgement?: Spawns two Shop Restock Machines.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Tarot Cloth's effect also applies to card effects used through Blank Card.

• [Repentance] Only certain cards gain the Tarot Cloth effect with Blank Card, which include: I - The Magician, II - The High Priestess, III - The Empress, IV - The Emperor, V - The Hierophant, VI - The Lovers, VII - The Chariot, VIII - Justice, IX - The Hermit, XVII - The Stars, XIX - The Sun, 0 - The Fool?, III - The Empress?, V - The Hierophant?, VI - The Lovers?, VIII - Justice?, and XIV - Temperance?

• • Three of these cards will have diminished Tarot Cloth effects:

• • 
• XIX - The Sun: Only 200 damage is dealt.

• • 
• 0 - The Fool?: Only 3 items drop instead of 6; this also applies with Car Battery.

• • 
• VIII - Justice?: Only 2-7 chests spawn.

• As a result, using the Blank Card in conjunction with the Car Battery will cause the effect of the active card to quadruple, instead of double.

• • [Repentance] Only certain effects will be doubled again, which include: I - The Magician (only the damage up), III - The Empress, IV - The Emperor (only the soul hearts), V - The Hierophant, VI - The Lovers, VII - The Chariot, VIII - Justice, V - The Hierophant?, VI - The Lovers?, and XIV - Temperance?.

• [Repentance] The enhanced effect of The Fool? can't drop starting items in challenges on the ground.

• [Repentance] With a IX - The Hermit card, it is usually best to walk into the shop first. If Greed is there, he can be fought for money, and then the card can be used to restock the shop.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • A tarot cloth is a particular type of tablecloth used to cover tables during tarot card readings.

fields.description: Drops a random tarot card. [Before Repentance] Doubles the effects of most cards and runes. [Repentance] Doubles the effects of tarot cards.

Taurus.title: Taurus
Taurus.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• -0.3 speed.

• [Before Repentance] -0.3 maximum speed.

• When in a room with enemies, Isaac gradually gains speed at a rate of +0.065 per tick.

• [Before Repentance] This speed boost will be able to go past the lowered maximum.

• Once Isaac's speed reaches 2.0, he gains the My Little Unicorn effect for 5 seconds, becoming invulnerable, and loses the speed bonus from Taurus afterward.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Isaac slowly gains a red tint that becomes more intense as he gains speed.

• The speed boost and invulnerability effect activate only once per room.

• The higher Isaac's base speed, the quicker the effect activates. It can activate immediately upon entering a room if his base speed is already 2.0.

• If Isaac's base speed is 2.0, the effect will activate upon entering any room (including rooms with no enemies such as Sacrifice Rooms) for the first time.

• If Isaac's speed is decreased during the My Little Unicorn effect (e. g. by using a Speed Down pill), Isaac will continue to gain speed while the effect is active.

• The item doesn't trigger when enemies are spawned, even if the room did not have enemies when first entered. This includes Challenge Rooms, Sacrifice Rooms when spawning Uriel or Gabriel, and the Boss Rush room.

• [Repentance] [mode: greed; greedier] Taurus will trigger each time the button is pressed to start a new Greed or Greedier wave. Since the invincibility allows pressing the button to stop waves for free, it can be used repeatedly without leaving the arena.

• The item doesn't trigger in trap rooms which only contain Poky enemies.

• If Isaac gets teleported out of the room by any source, the My Little Unicorn effect won't trigger if the room is re-entered.

• Bombs can be placed during the charge.

• [Repentance] When playing as Jacob and Esau, the speed changes apply for both, but only the character that is holding Taurus gains invincibility.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Blood Rights: While Isaac is invincible, Blood Rights can be freely used without taking damage. This trivializes many rooms, and since Taurus can activate every room, this combination can be game-changing, especially if Isaac has high base speed.

• [Repentance] Isaac will still take damage from Blood Rights during the invincibility.

• Camo Undies: Isaac will be able to move around unnoticed, letting Taurus charge up.

• Dark Arts: Using Dark Arts provides a temporary +1.0 speed boost, allowing Isaac to activate Taurus earlier.

• Gnawed Leaf: Isaac's speed will still increase while he is invincible from Gnawed Leaf, allowing Taurus to activate with only a very small period of vulnerability when first entering a room.

• Rock Bottom: Isaac keeps the maximum speed boost after reaching it once.

• Serpent's Kiss/The Virus: Isaac will poison enemies in addition to dealing damage to them on contact.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Libra: Isaac's damage and range increases as speed increases. However, if Isaac's base speed is not high enough, the invincibility never activates.

• [Repentance] Damage, Range, and Tear delay increase as speed increases. Speed increases much slower than normal.

• The Ludovico Technique: Isaac cannot control the tear while invincible, but any enemies touching it will still take damage from it.

• A Pony/White Pony: The lower limit for Isaac's speed is lowered from 1.50 to 1.20.

• [Repentance] Strawman: Taurus will not affect Isaac's speed if it's held by the Strawman Keeper, effectively rendering the item useless until Isaac is at 2.00 speed naturally.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Touching the chest after the ??? fight while the invulnerability is active will speed up the music during the credits. The music during Ending 14 and its "The End" screen will play as normal, however (This has not been confirmed for other endings or items that cause music to distort).

fields.description: -0.3 Speed. Isaac builds speed while in a room with enemies. At max speed, he gains the My Little Unicorn effect for 5 seconds.

Tear Detonator.title: Tear Detonator
Tear Detonator.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Once activated, all tears in the air split into 6 more tears in all directions, which retain their damage and shot speed.

• Luck-based effects from items such as Tough Love or Holy Light are applied individually to each tear.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] The item only costs 10 coins when found in a Shop.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Akeldama: Will bust tears generated by Akeldama into Isaac's current tears.

• Angelic Prism: Tears that are split by the prism can be split again by Tear Detonator.

• Anti-Gravity: All tears currently floating in the air will be multiplied, resulting in a massive amount of tears.

• Bethany/Tainted Bethany: Bethany can use Tear Detonator multiple times in rapid succession at the cost of one Soul/Blood Charge per use, allowing for a huge area of effect that wipes out most rooms.

• Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns wisps on the middle ring. The wisps' tears are also detonated into 6 tears; the resulting tears are based on Isaac's own, rather than the wisps'. Created wisps trigger Tear Detonator's effect when destroyed. Despite Tear Detonator having a timed recharge, the wisps persist between rooms.

• Car Battery: Splits tears twice, creating 36 tears for every tear currently airborne.

• The Battery: Allows for multiple uses, creating tear counts in the hundreds.

• Circle of Protection / Metal Plate: Reflected tears can be split.

• Compound Fracture/Cricket's Body/The Parasite: Tears that are split can split again into burst tears.

• Eye of the Occult: Split tears form a circle around the original tear's position, and can be controlled as normal.

• Haemolacria: Splits tears into 6 Haemolacria tears that burst into split tears. If split tears are burst, all of them will split into 6 Haemolacria tears creating an enormous amount of tears when the main tear splits again.

• Hushy: All 8 projectiles shot by Hushy will split and become Isaac's tears, gaining their effects.

• Ipecac: All tears will split into 6 explosive tears, making it very powerful (but also dangerous unless Isaac has Host Hat or Pyromaniac).

• Lachryphagy: Similar to the Haemolacria synergy, if the main tear splits, 6 tears will spawn that can be fed. However, if burst tears are split, all burst tears will split into 6 tears resulting in an enormous amount of tears that are likely to feed each other.

• Lead Pencil: Each of the tears explodes into 6 smaller tears.

• The Ludovico Technique: The tear explodes into six smaller tears, then reappears next to the player.

• My Reflection: The shrapnel tears will curve back to the location of the original detonated tear.

• Sad Bombs: Bomb tears are multiplied.

• Saturnus: Orbiting tears can be split, including enemy tears caught in the orbit.

• Shooting familiars: Shooting familiars' tears explode into Isaac's tears, with his actual damage and effects.

• Technology Zero: Tears generated by Tear Detonator can be connected with electric charges.

• Technology Zero + Mucormycosis / Sinus Infection: Spores/Boogers generated by Tear Detonator can be connected with electric charges.

• Tiny Planet: Tears split, and then orbit around where the tear was originally from, three spinning clockwise, three counterclockwise.

• Trisagion: Tears split into six beams.

• Uranus: Tears shot out from frozen enemies when they are destroyed can be split.

• Urn of Souls: Each flame splits into six tears, unlike other fire effects.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• C Section: Fetuses split into normal tears.

• [Before Repentance] Chocolate Milk: No matter how charged the tears are, split tears always deal a tiny amount of damage.

• [Repentance] Split tears always deal Isaac's damage.

• Explosivo: Tears that are stuck to enemies will not deal explosion damage; tears released by it may be sticky tears that immediately stick back onto the enemy.

sections.heading: No Effect
sections.text:
Tear Detonator becomes useless with the following, barring other sources of tears:

• Azazel

• Blindfolded

• Brimstone

• Dr. Fetus

• Epic Fetus

• Mom's Knife

• Tech X

• Technology

• Technology 2 (laser only)

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Tear Detonator has the same sprite as Remote Detonator, but colored blue.

• [Before Repentance] Tear Detonator's sprite, in comparison to Remote Detonator's, is 1 pixel to the right.

fields.description: Splits all of Isaac's tears that are currently in the air into 6 tears that fire in all directions, which retain their damage and shot speed.

Tear Effects.title: Tear Effects
Tear Effects.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: Isaac's primary weapon; the attribute of the same name that governs the rate of fire; Tears; debuffs that can be inflicted on monsters; Status Effects] 

Tear Effects modify Isaac's primary weapon — tears. A few of the most common tear effects are listed below.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
| Effect | Appearance | Description 
| Homing | | Completely diverts from their original path to seek nearby enemies. The distance homing tears can travel is determined by the range stat. [Before Repentance] The friction of Sacred Heart's and Seraphim's homing effects have a lower value than other sources of homing, meaning the tears won't go as far.

| Piercing | | Can travel through enemies (but not obstacles) without breaking on impact. Once a single target or a segment of an enemy has been hit by a piercing tear, it can no longer take damage from that tear.
[Before Repentance] However, piercing effects also remove knockback.

| Spectral | | Can travel through obstacles (but not enemies) without breaking on impact. Spectral tears can be used to safely dispatch most types of monsters from behind obstacles, or over them in combination with flying.
Allows tears to pass through both enemies and obstacles if combined with Piercing.

| Bouncing | | Makes tears bounce off walls, enemies and environmental objects. Tears that bounce off of enemies bounce in random directions, whereas tears that bounce off of walls and other objects bounce directly back. When tears bounce from enemies, they become able to hit the same enemy again should they bounce off of another enemy or obstacle.

Teardrop Charm.title: Teardrop Charm
Teardrop Charm.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Luck-based tear effects (i.e. status-inflicting tears or other effects, such as Euthanasia) have a higher chance of occurring.

• The bonus is equivalent to +4 Luck, but the other benefits of Luck do not apply.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Because the bonus is a flat +4 Luck, this trinket works best on items that require a low luck stat to trigger most often.

• These items include Ghost Pepper, Bird's Eye, Holy Light, Knockout Drops, Lodestone, Mom's Eye, Parasitoid, Rotten Tomato, and Tough Love

• The bonus only affects Isaac's tears, the familiars that copy Isaac's tear effects (such as Incubus) do not benefit from the trinket.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Golden Trinket / Mom's Box: Each copy gives an additional +2 Luck flat to the trinket.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Teardrop Charm is from the Antibirth mod. In Antibirth, the bonus was equivalent to +3 Luck.

fields.description: Luck-based tear effects have a higher chance of occurring.

Tech.5.title: Tech.5
Tech.5.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: For all Tech items, check Tech (Disambiguation)

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants an unlimited range piercing laser with random rate of fire that does not replace tears.

• The laser has a 1/6 chance to fire every ~0.07 seconds (4 frames), firing at an average rate of 2.5 times per second.

• [Before Repentance] The laser occasionally fires with the effect of the listed items or trinkets, randomly:

• Hook Worm

• Spoon Bender

• Tiny Planet

• [Afterbirth onward] Mysterious Liquid

• [Afterbirth onward] Rubber Cement

• [Repentance+] The laser has a 5% chance of firing with a Fruit Cake effect.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The damage of the laser scales directly with Isaac's damage.

• Unlike Technology or Technology 2, Isaac can still fire tears from both eyes in addition to firing the laser.

• The laser can be fired independently from tears by slightly tilting the right analog stick, just like shooting familiars.

• [Repentance] Unlike Technology, Tech.5 Lasers do not have momentum, and fire exclusively in the cardinal directions unless Isaac has an item like Analog Stick, Eye of the Occult or Marked.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Anti-Gravity: Creates floating laser balls that will all fire simultaneously when the fire button is released.

• Brimstone: Tech.5 does not fire. However, it will still fire when playing as Azazel with his short-ranged Brimstone. Since the laser scales with player damage, this can be a devastating combination.

• [Afterbirth onward] Tech.5 fires normally while Brimstone laser is charging.

• [Before Repentance] Cricket's Body: Tear delay down as expected, but no benefit from the splash effect.

• [Repentance] Releases a 4-way spread of tears whenever the laser hits a wall or an enemy.

• Eye of the Occult: Only affects the laser's color.

• Eye of the Occult + Brimstone/Technology: The Tech.5 laser also automatically fires at the crosshair.

• Gello: Laser only fires from Isaac.

• Lilith: No effect, as Lilith is inherently Blindfolded.

• [Repentance] Lilith fires the Tech.5 laser from her forehead as expected, though the costume doesn't appear.

• The Ludovico Technique: Laser is fired in the same direction that the controlled tear is moving and the laser becomes spectral.

• Ipecac: Laser explodes and poisons enemies on contact.

• The Parasite: Laser splits into two perpendicular beams upon hitting an obstacle.

• [Repentance+] Also spawn small split tears.

• [Afterbirth onward] Rubber Cement: Laser will bounce in angle depending on the obstacle hit.

• Sprinkler: No effect.

• Urn of Souls: Isaac can still fire the laser as normal while using the urn.
