sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Polyphemus, Mutant Spider, and Inner Eye's fire rate delay formulas do not stack with each other, meaning that there is no downside to taking another after you have already taken one. This fire rate delay is negated with 20/20.

• [Before Repentance] Charge-bar items like Monstro's Lung or Brimstone stop working at 30 tears per second.

• [Repentance] Eye drops x1.2 multiplier only applies over Tears Delay-gained Fire Rate.

• Dr Fetus, Brimstone, Ipecac, and Monstro's Lung fire rate delay formulas do not (always) stack with each other, following a priority list:
- Dr Fetus + Monstro's Lung + X = x1/4.3
- Dr Fetus + X (but no Monstro's Lung) = x0.4
- No Dr Fetus + Brimstone + X = x1/3
- Monstro's Lung and Ipecac DO stack with each other if no Brimstone and Dr Fetus.

• Haemolacria has very complex interactions with other fire rate items, almost resulting in an overhaul of the formulas.
- For Tear Delay (TD) = TD_preHeamolacria * 2 + 11
- Fire rate is first calculated 'normal' for Tear Delay and Fire rate additions. This Fire rate is turned back into Tear Delay via (30 / FR) - 1. This Tear Delay is put into the above formula.

sections.heading: Other
sections.text:
• Tears up pills increase tears by 0.35 and tears down pills decrease tears by 0.28.

• The Conjoined transformation decreases tears by 0.3.

• [Afterbirth onward] In co-op, Cry Baby will occasionally briefly increase tears. Dark Baby will occasionally briefly increase all stats, including tears. Buddy Baby will occasionally briefly grant the Guillotine effect, which increases tears.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Absorbing an item using Black Rune can increase fire rate by 0.5.

• III - The Empress? increases fire rate by 1.5 for the duration of its effect.

• VII - The Chariot? greatly increases fire rate for the duration of its effect.

• XII - The Hanged Man? grants triple shot and reduces fire rate (similar to The Inner Eye) for the duration of its effect.

• [Repentance] Standing near a White Poop or White Dip will greatly increase fire rate.

• [Repentance] Standing on brown creep produced by IBS or Tainted ??? will increase fire rate by 1.5.

• Soul of Samson activates the Berserk! effect, which increases tears.

• [Repentance] Judas + The Book of Belial + Birthright + Decap Attack: Grants Judas ×3 fire rate while his head is detached from his body. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If your tear rate is decreased into a negative number, then it will flip back to 120 tears per second.

Dead Bird.title: Dead Bird
Dead Bird.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Taking damage summons a bird familiar that chases enemies for the remainder of the current room, dealing 2 damage per tick (~4.3 damage per second).

• [Repentance+] As long as Isaac's HP is at one half heart ( no matter the type of heart), Dead Bird will remain active between rooms. Upon entering a new floor, Dead Bird will be inactive, and a hit must be taken to activate it again.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Eve starts with this item by default.

• [Repentance+] Additionally, Dead Bird will remain active between rooms at a total HP of one heart or less.

• The following types of flies are instantly killed when they come in contact with the familiar:

• Army Fly

• Attack Fly

• Dart Fly

• Fly

• Hush Fly

• Moter

• Pooter

• Ring Fly

• Super Pooter

• Swarm

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Birthright + Eve: Dead Bird will be active at all times.

• [Repentance+] The Lost / Tainted Lost: Dead Bird is active at all times. [end edition note] 

• Box of Friends: Does not double Dead Bird, even if Isaac has taken damage before use.

• Sacrificial Altar: The familiar can only be sacrificed while it is active.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• This item is used in Darkness Falls.

• This item is a reference to an old series of comics Edmund McMillen drew called Thicker Than Water, where the Dead Bird is said to represent his inner doubts and self-destructive nature.

sections.heading: Bug
sections.text: Bug note: When using Extension Cord with Dead Bird, if Isaac and the bird are both moving sometimes the electricity does not always fully connect.

fields.description: After Isaac takes damage, spawns a flying familiar that chases enemies for the current room, dealing ~4 damage per second. [Repentance+] As long as Isaac's HP is at one half heart ( no matter the type of heart), Dead Bird will remain active between rooms.

Dead Cat.title: Dead Cat
Dead Cat.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Sets Isaac's Red Heart containers to 1 when being picked up.

• Does not remove Soul Hearts or Black Hearts unless picked up as ???, The Soul, [Repentance] Black Judas, Tainted Judas, Tainted ???, Tainted Forgotten, or Tainted Bethany.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] Does not remove Bone Hearts unless picked up as The Forgotten.

• • Can be picked up as The Soul half of The Forgotten to remove all but 1 Soul heart and keep all Bone Hearts.

• Grants 9 extra lives.

• Upon death, Isaac respawns with 1 Red Heart container, typically in the previous room. 

• The head of Guppy begins following Isaac like a familiar upon pickup but doesn't do anything.

• When Isaac has lost all of the lives provided by this item, the Guppy familiar will disappear.

• Contributes to the Guppy transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• This item can drop from killing Super Pride. [Before Repentance] Super Pride can drop this item even if Isaac has already encountered/possessed it. 

• Resurrection items activate in a set order. Dead Cat is [Before Repentance] 2nd / [Repentance] 4th in this order after Soul of Lazarus, 1up!, and Lazarus' inherent extra life.

• [Rebirth only] Picking this item up as The Lost does not show the number of lives remaining, but still functions normally.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] If picked up as The Forgotten, his Bone Hearts are reduced to 1 but The Soul's Soul Hearts remain unaffected; It is also true the other way. [end edition note] 

• The lives are added after the "picking up an item" animation has ended, so characters that die while the animation is playing will not be revived by this item.

• [Before Repentance] The effects of the D4, D100, Missing No., or a 1- or 6-pip Dice Room will not remove the lives granted by this item.

• Additional Dead Cats can be picked up during a run, increasing lives well past 9. [Before Repentance] Only the first dead cat counts toward becoming Guppy.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] This item counts as 9 items, so if Isaac is trying for an early portal to The Void after beating Mom, this will significantly boost the progress closer to 20 items.

• [Repentance] If Jacob and Esau take the item, only the brother who takes it will be set to one Red Heart Container on pickup. But if they die, both are resurrected with one Red Heart Container. [end edition note] 

• If both brothers take the item (via Diplopia or Birthright), resurrections will be subtracted from Jacob before Esau, regardless of which brother actually died.

• Tainted Jacob's health will still be reduced to 1 Red Heart Container if he takes this item after being touched by Dark Esau or if he dies in his Lost form.

• [Repentance] Familiars that follow behind Isaac have a certain priority in how close their position is to him over other familiars, with Dead Cat having the lowest priority at [Before Repentance+] 6th / [Repentance+] 8th and thus being farther from Isaac than familiars of different priorities.

• If Isaac somehow obtains Dead Cat in the starting room of Chapter 1 and dies before ever leaving it, he will respawn in that same room.

• [Repentance] Similarly, during the fight against The Beast, Isaac will respawn in the same room on the spot and can continue the battle.

• [Repentance] Despite the life counter being shown during the Mother's Shadow chase, the item is inactive like all other items and will not provide extra lives.

• [Repentance] If all 9 lives are used, Dead Cat disappears from Isaac's inventory. If Isaac only has three Guppy items prior to losing Dead Cat, then its disappearance will cause the Guppy transformation to be lost.

• [Repentance+] Dead Cat's quality is treated as 2 for the purposes of Bag of Crafting. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
• In the context of a Devil Room:

• Taking Dead Cat with 1 or 2 Heart Containers won't kill Isaac because it will set his number of Heart Containers to 1 immediately, saving him from the death that would have resulted from having no Heart Containers. [Before Repentance] Buying Dead Cat when at 1 Heart Container essentially obtains the item for free.

• Because Dead Cat sets Isaac's Heart Containers to 1, if it's found alongside other devil deals and Isaac has enough Heart Containers, it's possible to essentally take those other deals for free if they're taken before Dead Cat.

• Other Devil Room items can be bought without the necessary number of Heart Containers at the cost of one of the many lives Dead Cat provides.

• To take multiple Devil Deals, buy a Devil deal item then quickly leave the room before the "item get" animation finishes. This will result in Dead Cat reviving Isaac back inside the Devil Room.

• [Afterbirth onward] Taking Dead Cat as Keeper or Tainted Keeper will reduce their total number of Coin Hearts to one, meaning they will die upon taking any damage at all. Unless either of them have immediate access to an HP Up item, such as from the Boss Item Drop, taking Dead Cat is usually detrimental.

• [Repentance] Dead Cat no longer allows Keeper to spend his lives for Devil Deals like others characters due to his Devil Deal purchasing mechanic. As he no longer needs heart containers to purchase Devil Deals, it is more likely he will have extra heart containers around that can be used to mitigate Dead Cat's penalty.

• [Repentance] Holding onto a XIX - The Sun? can be beneficial if at high HP. Using it prior to taking Dead Cat will convert all red heart containers to Bone Hearts for the floor. The bone hearts do not disappear when taking Dead Cat and will all revert back to normal red-heart containers on the next floor (and stay filled if the bone hearts were filled).

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Gold Hearts: Gives Isaac many coins when picked up, due to the amount of hearts lost.

• Guppy's Paw: In addition to contributing to the transformation, converting the Red Heart Container obtained after revival into three Soul Hearts effectively triples Isaac's HP.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Parasite]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The 9 lives gained by the item is a reference to a myth that cats have 9 lives.

• The item Guppy's Tail and the transformation Guppy implies that Guppy has a white fur on it's tip of the tail while the sprite for Dead Cat does not.

• The Dead Cat shares the same tuxedo type bicolor fur with Guppy.

• Despite not having Guppy in its name, this item counts for the Guppy transformation which may imply that Dead Cat is Guppy, or at least was what Guppy looked like at some point.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If picked up as ???, Black Judas, Tainted Judas, Tainted ???, Tainted Forgotten, or Tainted Bethany while in possession of Bone Hearts, the health bar may become glitched. The actual health amount is correctly set to 1 Soul Heart/Black Heart + all Bone Hearts, but some of the Bone Hearts are incorrectly displayed as half Soul Hearts depending on the situation before picking up Dead Cat. This can mess with the order of Soul Hearts and Bone Hearts after taking damage or gaining health. The glitch will resolve itself after taking damage, picking up health or touching an item.

fields.description: Sets Isaac's Red Heart Containers to 1, but grants 9 extra lives. After dying, Isaac respawns with 1 Red Heart Container in the previous room.

Dead Dove.title: Dead Dove
Dead Dove.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants spectral tears and flight.

• Contributes to the Seraphim transformation.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • Because the boosts provided by Dead Dove are already innate to The Lost and Azazel, this item grants no real benefits when playing as the characters in question other than its contribution to the seraphim transformation.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• It is the Angel Room equivalent of Spirit of the Night.

• This item's appearance has the same body as The Lost.

• In most Christian denominations, a dove is often used as symbolism for the Holy Spirit, the third divine Person of the Trinity. In this case, a "dead dove" could imply a dead or otherwise damaged/weakeaned God.

• The item's name may also reference an Archive of Our Own tagging convention in which works with particularly objectionable content are tagged "Dead Dove, Do Not Eat", which is in turn a reference to the TV show Arrested Development.

fields.description: Grants spectral tears and flight.

Dead Eye.title: Dead Eye
Dead Eye.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Isaac's damage increases for each successive tear hit on enemies.

• The multiplier increases by 0.25x for each hit, going up to a maximum of 2x after 4 successive hits.

• If a tear misses and hits nothing (wall/floor), there is a chance for the multiplier to be reset back to 1.

• • The chance is 20% for the first miss, 33% for the second miss, and 50% for the third miss and beyond.

• As the multiplier increases, Isaac's tears glow red and increase in size.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• The effect is triggered by many entities aside from enemies. Shooting [Before Repentance] Fire Places, Poop, Wall Huggers, and Stone Grimaces will count towards the multiplier. This can be used to preemptively increase damage before entering a new room.

• [Before Repentance] Because blue fires do not deteriorate when shot at with tears, maximum damage can always be achieved as long as the fire is not destroyed by an explosion.

• Shooting Hosts will increase the damage multiplier even if their skull is lowered down.

• If Dead Eye is removed by re-rolling it with D4, D100, or a 1 or 6 pip Dice Room, the damage multiplier will be removed, but the tears will continue to glow red.

• Tears do not have to be landed on only one enemy to build the multiplier; as long as they do not miss, Isaac gains damage.

• [Repentance] Because there are no walls or floors for tears to collide with in the fight with The Beast, the damage boost will not fade away.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Compound Fracture/Haemolacria/Lachryphagy: Main tears and burst tears will contribute to damage multiplier.

• Lachryphagy Firing into the floating tear won't reset the multiplier unless it hits a wall. The burst tears never reset the multiplier.

• Dark Arts: Hitting enemies/bullets successfully with Dark Arts contributes to Dead Eye's damage multiplier.

• The Ludovico Technique: Damage bonus increases until it hits the max of 2x. Since the controllable tear never hits the ground or wall, the bonus cannot be lost.

• Petrification/Slow items: Enemies will be petrified or slowed, making them easier to hit without missing.

• Pop!: Tears that miss an enemy and do not hit a wall or obstacle will not fall to the ground immediately, allowing many damage-amplified tears to be fired before the damage boost is lost.

• Proptosis: Tears are larger and easier to hit with at a low range. Additionally, if the tear fades out of existence instead of running out of range or hitting a wall/obstacle, it does not count as a miss.

• Spirit Sword: Dead Eye will increase the damage every slash until it hits the max of 2x. The bonus can be lost if a sword projectile doesn't hit anything.

• Tiny Planet: Isaac's tears no longer hit walls and stay in the air for longer, allowing many damage-amplified tears to be fired before the damage boost is lost.

• Akeldama: The tears in the trail will contribute to the damage boost, making it possible to stack damage while having items that do not interact with Dead Eye on their own (such as Brimstone).

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone / Dr. Fetus / Epic Fetus / Mom's Knife / Technology / Tech X: Will not increase or decrease Dead Eye's bonus, resulting in it remaining as it was prior to their pickup.

• 20/20/The Inner Eye/Mutant Spider/Cursed Eye: If all tears hit, they all contribute to the damage multiplier. However, the spread shot granted by The Inner Eye and Mutant Spider may make it hard to retain the damage multiplier.

• Azazel: Gains no benefit by picking up Dead Eye unless his tear effect has been replaced.

• Cricket's Body/The Parasite: Split tears that do not hit enemies are considered misses, nearly guaranteeing the chance of losing the multiplier.

• Flat Stone: Each skip counts as missing.

• [Afterbirth+ onward] The Forgotten: The Forgotten's swing increases the multiplier when successfully hitting enemies, making it much easier to maintain the damage buff. Resets the multiplier upon swinging and missing. The multiplier changes normally when firing tears as The Soul, and the two forms share the same multiplier.

• The Forgotten + Soy Milk: Damage multiplier will not reset as long as the fire key is held, and will quickly build up to the maximum value of x2. The multiplier will only reset if, upon releasing the fire button, the thrown bone does not hit any enemy.

• Rock Bottom The damage multiplier stays, even if you reset the item bonus.

• Host Hat: Tears fired by the Host are affected by Dead Eye.

• Immaculate Heart: The tears from Immaculate Heart can add to the damage multiplier and cannot lower it by missing. This can be particularly useful with items that normally prevent the damage multiplier from increasing, such as Brimstone.

• Incubus: Incubus's tears do not affect the multiplier, but Incubus can gain damage from Isaac's normal tears increasing the multiplier. The familiar's tears do not reset the multiplier if they miss, either.

• [Before Repentance] Lilith's Incubus doesn't work with Dead Eye.

• Incubus + Monstro's Lung: Tears fired by Incubus are now affected by Dead Eye.

• Isaac's Tears: If the tears fired by Isaac's tears miss, they cause the multiplier to reset.

• Jacob's Ladder: Electricity sparks do not contribute to damage multiplier.

• Marked: Damage buff often lost quickly because of the constantly firing tears.

• Piercing tears: Damage buff is halved, .125x, reaching the 2x multiplier with 8 successive hits.

• Rubber Cement: Tears that hit enemies may bounce off and still count as misses.

• Sad Bombs: Tears spawned by sad bombs that miss will reset the multiplier.

• Saturnus: Tears spawned when entering the room and enemy tears collected by the ring can add to the damage multiplier and cannot lower it by missing. This can be particularly useful with items that normally prevent the damage multiplier from increasing, such as Brimstone.

• Technology 2: No effect from the laser itself, but the tears fired from the second eye are affected by Dead Eye.

• Technology Zero: Electricity connecting tears will not increase the damage multiplier.

• Trisagion: Cannot increase Dead Eye's bonus, but can lose it.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: When picking up Brimstone, Technology, Dr. Fetus, Epic Fetus, or Mom's Knife, the damage multiplier that was gained before picking them up will now be permanent. However, saving and quitting the run will result in this damage multiplier being permanently lost.

fields.description: Isaac's damage increases each time an enemy is hit. Damage is reset upon missing a shot.

Dead Onion.title: Dead Onion
Dead Onion.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: [distinguish: The Sad Onion]

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Grants piercing and spectral tears.

• [Before Repentance] +0.25 range.

• [Repentance] -1.5 range.

• -0.4 shot speed. 

• [Before Repentance] -0.5 tear falling speed.

• [Before Repentance] Tear size multiplier: 1.5x.

• [Repentance] +0.22 tear size.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Although the description says "Toxic aura tears", the tears do not inflict poison damage.

• Due to the spectral tears, tears will go through walls and the floor in a Crawl Space.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Incubus: Does not affect shot speed or tear size, but still gives the piercing effect.

• [Repentance] : Shot speed, range, and tear size will be affected.

• Lost Contact: Tears will destroy enemy projectiles without being destroyed in the process.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Azazel: Range penalty is the only effect.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs are slow to fire and will pass through enemies, making it far more difficult to hit them with explosions.

• [Repentance] Bombs also deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.

• Epic Fetus / Brimstone: Overrides Dead Onion, although stat effects apply.

• The Ludovico Technique: Tear moves very slowly making it hard to kill mobile enemies.

• Mom's Knife: Overrides Dead Onion.

• Monstro's Lung: Fires a barrage of large tears that disappear at close range. Spectral and piercing effects make it very effective at close range.

• My Reflection: Tears will travel a very short distance before they return to Isaac and eventually disappear.

• Proptosis: While tears do massive damage at short range, it makes it a lot easier to be damaged by explosive enemies or enemies that do contact damage.

• Rubber Cement: Edges of tears retain both piercing and spectral effects; however, the center of the tear will lose them and bounce.

• Sulfuric Acid: Acid Tears no longer impact objects and can no longer open Secret Rooms.

• [Repentance] Acid Tears can break objects.

• Technology: Laser size is increased.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • Dead Onion has the most stat downs out of any other item if tear falling speed is counted as a stat.

fields.description: Grants piercing and spectral tears. Increases tear size (without increasing damage) while greatly reducing range and shot speed.

Dead Sea Scrolls.title: Dead Sea Scrolls
Dead Sea Scrolls.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: When used, a random activated item effect will be activated from the following:

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• When Bob's Rotten Head or Shoop da Whoop! is chosen, Dead Sea Scrolls will not lose its charge until said item is thrown or released.

• This allows Isaac to press Spacebar again if need be to skip over said items in the rotation while keeping full charge, allowing it to be used again for a different effect.

• • This doesn't work if Bethany has Soul Charges and Book of Virtues.

• It may be helpful to use Dead Sea Scrolls upon entering an enemy room, as many of its effects such as The Gamekid and Tammy's Head are helpful in combat.

• As many of Dead Sea Scrolls effects involve explosions, using it near Tinted Rocks or potential Secret Room entrances can potentially be helpful when low on bombs.

• While Anarchist Cookbook and Kamikaze! can hurt the player, effects such as Book of Revelations, The Nail, Crystal Ball and Prayer Card will pay out with more health than is lost long-term.

• [Repentance] Since We Need To Go Deeper! guarantees a crawlspace if used on special tiles, it may be helpful to use Dead Sea Scrolls on such tiles whenever possible.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Each wisp spawned has the attributes of the active item that was triggered.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text: • Car Battery: Two effects are activated, with only one being named on screen.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The Dead Sea Scrolls are a collection of 981 Hellenistic-period manuscripts found within caves on the north shore of the Dead Sea.

• The pickup quote "It's a mystery" references the item's effect, as well as the fact that the real Dead Sea Scrolls are so tattered and eroded that reading them can prove impossible.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: If an effect triggers and adds to the character's appearance while being held (Monstro's Tooth or Kamikaze! for example), the additional visual effects will remain for the rest of the game or until they are replaced.

fields.description: Triggers the effect of a random activated item from a list of possible options (not every activated item is included).

Dead Tooth.title: Dead Tooth
Dead Tooth.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• While firing, creates an aura around Isaac that poisons any nearby enemies for 2 ticks.

• The poison may stack up to 6 ticks at a time.

• The aura range is approximately two tiles.

• Poison damage is equal to Isaac's damage stat.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • [Repentance] This item can be spawned by Bumbino if he picks up 12 cents. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Azazel/Brimstone/Chocolate Milk/Mom's Knife/Monstro's Lung/Tech X: The green aura only activates when Isaac's attack is charging.

• Diplopia: No effect.

• Epic Fetus/The Ludovico Technique/Marked: The green aura only activates when pressing the attack buttons.

• The Forgotten: The green aura will activate when using melee and charging throw attack.

• Lilith: No effect.

• Mega Blast: The green aura will not activate while the beam is firing.

• Sprinkler: Green aura will not activate if only the sprinkler is firing, and the sprinkler does not get its own green aura.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Halitosis; Repentance: Toxic breath]
fields.description: While firing, Isaac gains a green aura that poisons nearby enemies.

Death.title: Death
Death.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
[disambig msg: the conditions that will kill Isaac; the Death tarot card; XIII - Death; the boss; Death (Boss)] 

Death occurs when Isaac runs out of health, or more rarely, by some effect regardless of health remaining. There are multiple ways to cause this.

• Damage from monsters

• Damage from bosses

• Damage from obstacles

• Damage from bombs

• Damage from a [machine: Blood Donation Machine] 

• Damage from Curse Rooms

• Trading your last bit of health when making a deal with the Devil unless that item provides any hearts in return, such as the Ceremonial Robes

• Using The Bible against Satan

• Using the Suicide King card

• ... and more.

sections.heading: Extra Lives
sections.text: Typically, when Isaac dies, the game over screen appears; however, there are certain revival items, characters, and abilities that can resurrect Isaac after death. It is possible to obtain extra lives throughout a run by picking up various items. When Isaac dies with one (on most occasions), he will be revived in the previous room under the new life. Below is a list of these items and special death / extra life conditions that they bestow; take note that reviving as a different character than your current one gives any further Completion Marks to the new one, and the transformation may change stats if the new character has different base values. The order of revives is independent of order of item pickup, determined by the list below from highest to lowest placing:

sections.heading: Soul of Lazarus
sections.text: When a Soul of Lazarus is used, Isaac immediately dies and is revived in the same room at half a heart and given some invincibility time. If Isaac dies while holding the stone, it is automatically used upon taking the fatal hit, acting as another life (with the same effect as if it was used manually). If used manually, it does not count as taking damage, so any positive or negative effects associated with taking damage are not triggered.

sections.heading: 1up!
sections.text: Isaac will be revived with full Red Heart containers. If he lacks any, he will revive with one Half Soul Heart, unless he is a character that can't use Red hearts, in which case he will respawn with 3 of their respective heart type (Soul Hearts for ???, The Soul, Tainted ???, Tainted Soul, and Tainted Bethany, Black Hearts for Black Judas and Tainted Judas, and Bone Hearts for The Forgotten).

sections.heading: Lazarus and Lazarus' Rags
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Upon death while holding Lazarus' Rags or playing as Lazarus, the player will be revived in the same room as Lazarus Risen with 1 Red Heart container.

• [Repentance] Upon death while holding Lazarus' Rags or playing as Lazarus, the player will be revived in the same room as Lazarus Risen with one less Red Heart container (but no less than one).

sections.heading: Dead Cat
sections.text: Dead Cat grants Isaac nine extra lives. Isaac will be revived with one Red Heart container unless playing as ??? or Tainted Judas, where he will be revived with one soul heart/black heart.

sections.heading: Inner Child
sections.text: Isaac respawns in the same room with half a heart left, a massive size down, and +0.2 speed. If Isaac has any heart containers, he will respawn with half a heart container filled; otherwise, he will respawn with half a soul heart.

sections.heading: Guppy's Collar
sections.text: Guppy's Collar grants Isaac a 50% chance to be revived with one Red Heart container half-filled. If he lacks any, he will be revived at half a Soul Heart instead. If the collar fails to activate, any other items after Guppy's Collar will be checked. The revives from Guppy's Collar are seeded per death.

sections.heading: Ankh
sections.text: Isaac revives as ??? with 3 Soul Hearts.

sections.heading: Broken Ankh
sections.text: Broken Ankh has a 2/9 chance to resurrect Isaac as ??? with 3 Soul Hearts. The revives from Broken Ankh are seeded per death.

sections.heading: Judas' Shadow
sections.text: Judas' Shadow revives Isaac as Black Judas with 2 Black Hearts.

sections.heading: Missing Poster
sections.text: Isaac will be revived as The Lost and Missing Poster will be removed. If already playing as The Lost or Tainted Lost, Isaac will respawn as normal in the previous room.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Scissors, The Lost, Lil Spewer]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Quitting the game before the death animation is completed does not allow the player to continue the run, but does not add a death on the stats screen.

Death's List.title: Death's List
Death's List.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon entering a room, a skull appears over an enemy's head.

• The marked enemy will have a bigger shadow.

• Killing the marked enemy will cause the skull to move to a different enemy.

• If all enemies in the room are cleared in the order they are marked, Isaac gains one of the following rewards at random:

• • A Soul Heart, a pill, a Key, a Bomb, or a Nickel.

• • +0.2 speed, +0.5 range, [Before Repentance] +0.5 tears, [Repentance] +0.5 fire rate, +0.2 shot speed, +1 flat damage, or +1 luck.

• If a non-marked enemy is killed, the skull will disappear and no bonuses will be granted for that room.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Losing this item will not remove stat rewards.

• As long as the room is not cleared, Isaac can re-attempt a Death's List by leaving and re-entering.

• The marked enemies are chosen in the same order in a given room, starting from the top-left corner with enemies that are vulnerable at their spawn time (from top to bottom, then from left to right). If new enemies are spawned via Portals or on death, they are added to the end of the marked queue.

• The marked Army Fly will always be the last one in the line of Army Flies.

• Bishops can shield the marked enemy unless frozen or petrified beforehand.

• Killing all piles of a Cursed Globins counts as one kill.

• A room with no enemies that instead requires Pressure Plates to be pressed will also give a reward when cleared.

• If a reward stat is chosen that is already at maximum, the sound effect and Isaac's thumbs up animation will play, but there is no other effect.

• Bosses may also be marked.

• If a Portal is marked and despawns, no other enemy will be marked and the bonus is lost.

• Enemies that are not spawned when the room is entered (such as Angels from bombed Angel Statues and enemies in Challenge Rooms, Greed Mode, and Boss Rush) will not be marked.

• In the Mom boss fight, each of Mom's body parts (eyes, foot, and hands) is considered as a different enemy, and Isaac has to kill the foot to get the bonus.

• If the doors open automatically due to spending a long enough time in the room, any existing mark will disappear.

• Familiars, especially ones that passively or actively damage enemies of their own accord, may make killing enemies in order difficult, if not impossible.

• Ace cards will kill the enemies in the correct order when possible.

• If a Mr. Maw is marked, killing either part of its body will not forfeit Death's List, as the remaining enemy of said Mr. Maw will still be marked.

• This item has little to no effect in Greed Mode.

• Waiting for the Room Anti-softlock to trigger will always grant a reward from Death's List.

• Friendly enemies cannot be marked, and their deaths do not cause the mark to disappear.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Ace Cards: Enemies that die by being turned into pickups don't disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into pickups still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.

• Door Stop: If Isaac has failed Death's List but hasn't cleared the room, leaving and re-entering will reset the list.

• E. Coli/Flush!: Enemies that die by being turned into poop do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by turning all its enemies into poop still grants Isaac the Death's List reward.

• Eraser: Erasing enemies makes it easier to complete the list as erased enemies do not disrupt the Death's List chain and rooms cleared by Eraser's effect will also reward the bonus.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• [Repentance] Freezing attacks: Enemies that die by freezing do not disrupt the Death's List chain and clearing a room by freezing its enemies still grants Isaac the Death's List reward, though the shards caused by them breaking do.

• [Repentance+] Frozen enemies do disrupt Death's List's chain.

• Toxic Shock: Not recommended. If multiple enemies are killed by Toxic Shock at the same time, the mark will disappear and no reward will be given, even if the enemy next in line to be marked was killed at the same time as the marked one.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Death's List is based on this Steam Workshop item by x Wyvern x, Ashkal, and Merlo.

• [Repentance+] Death's List is the only non-quest item to have the item tag lazarusshared.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: Swarmers will lose the mark and no reward will be granted.
Bug note: Multisegmented enemies such as Mr. Maw and Pin may be impossible to kill in the correct order, as each segment is considered a separate entity and are destroyed as the enemy on the whole dies.
Bug note: Other multisegmented enemies such as Larry Jr. can have their segments destroyed in a proper order, but the skull marker is displayed on the wrong segment.

fields.description: Grants a pickup or stat upgrade if all enemies in a room are killed in the order they are marked.

Death's Touch.title: Death's Touch
Death's Touch.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• +1.5 damage

• -0.3 tears

• Grants piercing tears.

• Tear size multiplier: 2x.

• Tears are replaced by Death's scythes.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Brimstone / Azazel / Tainted Azazel: Overrides Death's Touch. Only stat changes apply.

• Dr. Fetus: Bombs travel through enemies. When combined with Ipecac, bombs do not explode upon hitting enemies.

• [Repentance] Bombs also deal 2.5x Isaac's damage to enemies when passing through them.

• Haemolacria: Stat effects apply. Fired tears will retain piercing effect; however, burst tears will not. All other effects do not apply.

• Ipecac: Tears explode at their center, not where they touch the enemy, which means the very large size from Death's Touch may be detrimental. Piercing effect does not apply.

• Trisagion: Overrides Death's Touch. Only stat changes apply.

• Spirit Sword Overrides the scythe visual including the ranged attack.

• Tech X: Overrides Death's Touch. Only stat changes apply.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The sound effect of the scythes hitting the ground is the same that was used in Super Meat Boy.

• The sound effect was originally used when shooting sawblades were hitting the walls.

• Isaac's face resembles Death's when holding this item.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: Penetrative shot; Repentance: Piercing shots] + DMG up
fields.description: +1.5 damage, -0.3 tears. Tears are replaced with large piercing scythes.

Death (Boss).title: Death (Boss)
Death (Boss).attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Death is a Harbinger that can appear in all environments of Chapter 4 (Womb, Utero, Scarred Womb).

sections.heading: Phase 1
sections.text:
• Spawns four Death Scythes along the walls of the room, aligned with Isaac in the cardinal directions. After a few seconds, they will accelerate towards Isaac.

• If Isaac is close to a wall, the scythe that would normally be spawned on that wall does not spawn.

• Spawns two Death Scythes in random positions around the room that constantly home in on Isaac until they are destroyed.

• Uses The Hourglass to slow Isaac down.

sections.heading: Phase 2
sections.text:
After enough damage is dealt, Death will dismount from his horse. The horse has 150 HP, but it will also lose health when Death is damaged. Attacking the horse does not damage Death.

• Death occasionally spawns two Knights and can have a maximum of two.

• Death's horse continuously flies horizontally across the room going off-screen and continuing on from the opposite end of the screen.

• Its charging patterns occur along 3 paths, starting with an upper charge into a middle charge a short distance below and finally a lower charge an identical distance below the middle path. It then restarts this process and can perform its upper charge in a new position in the room.

• • Its first charge will always leave room below it to allow for the lower second and third charges.

• The horse continues to charge even after Death has been defeated.

• It deals heavy damage to any enemy it runs into, except Death.
Both Death and his horse deal a whole heart of contact damage in both phases.

sections.heading: Champion Versions
sections.text: [bc: 18] : 15% larger with 25% more HP (562.5). In his first phase, he summons Kamikaze Leech instead of homing Death Scythes and does not use the Hourglass. He spawns Red Maws rather than Knights after he dismounts from his horse.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: The Book of Revelations, 7 Seals]

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: • When Death uses The Hourglass, The Ludovico Technique's tear is slow to respond and has a higher maximum speed, becoming difficult to control.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Death appeared in the original The Binding of Isaac.

• Conquest is the alternate version of him.

• Death is one of the Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse.

• Death's scythe attack is a homage to Castlevania's recurring boss, Death. Both summon four scythes that stay put for a few seconds, then home in on the player.

• Death's horse shares a visual similarity to a scythe, with the head's shape mimicking that of the tool's curved blade. 

• [Before Repentance] Death is currently the only enemy in-game that can use a status effect against Isaac.

• [Repentance] Death is redrawn to resemble his sprite from the Flash Binding of Isaac, which, in turn, resembles the "planet face" of Chapter 6: The End in Super Meat Boy, another game by Edmund McMillen.

• The redraw also makes the visual similarity of Death's horse to a scythe more apparent. However the changed texture of the handle now no longer matches those of the summoned Death Scythes.

Death Certificate.title: Death Certificate
Death Certificate.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Upon use, transports Isaac to an abandoned and expanded version of Home, which has one copy of almost every item the player has unlocked on that save file on pedestals. After taking an item from a pedestal, Isaac returns to the room he used Death Certificate in.

• There are also several pickups and Chest in the area. Picking them up/opening them will not cause Isaac to leave the area.

• • If a chest in the area contains an item, picking it up will not cause Isaac to leave the area.

• • Items spawned through the use of pre-obtained items brought into the area, such as Eden's Soul or Mystery Gift, will also not cause Isaac to leave the area.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Items that have not been unlocked will not show up in this unique location.

• If Death Certificate is used on a floor while [curse: blind] is active, the area will not be affected by the curse, meaning all items will be revealed. Chaos doesn't affect the area either.

• Items that are typically only granted under special circumstances like Dogma and Mom's Shovel are present.

• The layout of the area is randomly generated, and items will show up in order of lowest ID number to highest (starting at items in the original Flash version and working up to the Repentance items).

• A new Death Certificate area is randomly generated on the next floor.

• If more items are added to the game through modding, the area will expand to include them, ordered after the Repentance items.

• The only items that do not show up in the Death Certificate area are Dad's Note, hidden items (Recall, Hold, passive Damocles, passive The Book of Belial), Death Certificate itself, and G FUEL!.

• During a Challenge, Daily Challenge, or playing Greed Mode their respective banned items will not appear.

• Using Death Certificate while in the area that generates from using it consumes the item without doing anything.

• Using this item multiple times in the same floor will always teleport to the same areas, without respawning the items that were taken or destroyed.

• If an item is taken, it will only destroy the other ones in the current room or any other room Isaac travels to after taking an item, meaning other items present in the remaining rooms will still be available.

• The player can be softlocked by using Death Certificate while having already taken/destroyed all items that were in the area.

• Using this item during the fight against The Beast resets the fight after Isaac leaves the special area.

• Using this item while in the Genesis room will teleport Isaac back into the Genesis room after taking an item.

• Doing this will turn the current 3 choice pedestals into permanent ones and spawn the next set right on top of them.

• This item can be crafted from Bag of Crafting with eight Bone Hearts.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• ? Card: Mimics the effect of Death Certificate without consuming it.

• Diplopia: Has no use inside of the Home area, as Isaac can only take 1 item. However, it can be used to duplicate the Death Certificate item, allowing Isaac to enter the area twice.

• Jacob and Esau: Both characters can take an item from any given room if they're lined up correctly and take them at the same time. This can be very powerful in the case of Brimstone and Mom's Knife, as they are both close together.

• Red Key: Using the Red Key in this area has a chance of spawning rooms with many items from the Treasure Room pool in them, all of which can be taken without being returned back to the floor. It can also spawn special rooms from Home. If Mom's bedroom is spawned and Isaac sleeps in the bed, it will behave like a normal bed, but can be slept in while at full health.

• Schoolbag: Allows Isaac to hold another Active item in the area along with Death Certificate.

• Tainted Cain: Unlike his modified pedestal behavior in the rest of the run, Tainted Cain can pick up an item like normal in this area, effectively allowing him to craft any specific item for the cost of 8 bone hearts (the guaranteed recipe for Death Certificate in the Bag of Crafting).

• Wild Card: Will use Death Certificate if it was the item/card Isaac most recently used.

• Metronome: Can invoke the effect of Death Certificate as normal, even if it is not unlocked.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Abyss / Black Rune / Void: Only allows the consumption of one item per room and the consumed item is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.

• Binge Eater/Glitched Crown: No effect; items will not cycle through multiple items.

• Car Battery: No effect.

• Moving Box: Takes one random item which is treated as if it was picked up causing all other items in the room to disappear and forcing Isaac to leave the area.

• Book of Virtues: Spawns a single, regular wisp with no special properties.

• Damocles: No effect; Damocles doesn't duplicate the item pedestals in any room.

• NO!: causes Death Certificate to no longer spawn. inside Death Certificate floor Ignores changes to item availability.

• Sacred Orb / Tainted Lost / The Lost's Birthright: Ignores changes to item availability caused by characters/items.

• IX - The Hermit?: When used with items present no coins are spawned and the floor exit sequence is triggered as if Isaac had taken an item.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• The item's name is likely alluding to Isaac being dead, something that is heavily implied through the game's cutscenes and confirmed by Edmund McMillen in a tweet.

• This item is arguably the best in the game due to the fact that it gives any other item.

• Death Certificate's effect could be a reference to developer rooms, which are spaces created by game developers that contain every item in the game for testing.

• Death Certificate used to not limit the amount of items in its rooms which certain effects would interact with. This included the items Abyss, Void, and the pickup Black Rune which used to consume multiple items in a room without forcing Isaac to leave the area which had allowed him to amass a large quantity of locusts/stat upgrades. Another was Moving Box which had allowed an additional 10 items to be taken without forcing Isaac to leave the area.

• NO!, Sacred Orb, and Tainted Lost used to have the ability to change item availability in Death Certificate rooms.

• Rerolling items used to allow Isaac to take every rerolled item without being sent out of the area.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Breaking the mirror in Downpour / Dross II, will cause Isaac to die of suffocation in the Death Certificate area.

fields.description: Transports Isaac to an abandoned and expanded version of Home, which contains one copy of every item in the game. After taking an item, Isaac returns to the room he used Death Certificate in.

Death Scythe.title: Death Scythe
Death Scythe.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Death Scythes are enemies spawned by Death that either stay stationary for a few seconds before accelerating toward Isaac or immediately home in on him. They have 50 HP in total, but spawn with only 15 HP. They deal 1 full heart of damage. If Death is killed, any Death Scythes he summoned are immediately destroyed.

sections.heading: Ultra Death Scythe
sections.text:
Ultra Death Scythes are enemies spawned by Ultra Death; they are larger than regular Death Scythes and travel in one direction towards Ultra Death's position a brief moment after spawning, continuing until they travel off-screen or are killed. Unlike regular Death Scythes, they only deal half a heart of damage.

When spawned in manually they remain stationary and only deal contact damage if walked into.

Decap Attack.title: Decap Attack
Decap Attack.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effects
sections.text:
• Throws Isaac's head while allowing to shoot from the spot it lands, blocking enemy shots as well as dealing contact damage to nearby enemies. Meanwhile, Isaac's body can no longer shoot tears.

• The head does 24 damage on impact and 4 damage per tick (12 damage per second) on contact when it's on the ground.

• The head can return by picking it up with the body, or by using the item again without requiring charges. Both the throwing and retaking of the head can deal damage to enemies passing through.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] This item has a 1% chance to drop when defeating Chimera. [end edition note] 

• This item acts similarly to Tainted Forgotten's birthright.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Belial interaction: Grants Judas +2 damage and ×3 tears fired per second while his head is detached from his body.

• Book of Virtues interaction: A stationary wisp spawns where Isaac was when he threw his head that fires tears in the same direction Isaac does. The wisps do not persist between rooms.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Car Battery: No effect.

• The Forgotten: The head changes in sync when switching between The Forgotten and The Soul. The Forgotten's bone attack still belongs to the body, while The Soul's tear attack belongs to the head as expected.

• Tainted Forgotten: Throws the head of Tainted Forgotten, but the bone attack still remains on his body. The head can only be recalled by reactivating the item or having the body touch the head.

• Transcendence/The Pinking Shears: Isaac is invisible apart from his shadow while both items are active.

• Mom's Knife: The knife still follows and shoots from the body, the head doesn't shoot tears.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • The name, description, effect and sprite of this item is a reference to the Sega Genesis game of the same name from 1991.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: Playing as Tainted Lazarus, flipping while the head is detached and leaving the room will cause the tears from the form holding Decap Attack to still be detached. This can also happen to the form not holding Decap Attack, by flipping twice in the same room while the head is detached, then returning the head.

fields.description: Throws Isaac's head, which is still able to fire tears at the spot it lands. Reactivating the item or stepping on the head reattaches it.

Deck of Cards.title: Deck of Cards
Deck of Cards.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Gives Isaac a random card.

• If all of Isaac's card slots are full, the card given by the Deck of Cards is placed in the first slot, dropping the card that was in it on the ground.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [edition anr] Dice Shard is technically a card, but cannot be generated by the Deck of Cards. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Dice Shard, Emergency Contact, and Cracked Key can be found in the Deck, albeit extremely rarely. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] This item can be crafted from Bag of Crafting with eight cards.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text: • Book of Virtues interaction: Spawns card-like wisps on the inner ring which spawn a card when destroyed.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Little Baggy: Gives pills instead. Deck of Cards have then the same effect as Mom's Bottle of Pills.

• [Before Repentance] Picking up Starter Deck will nullify this effect but pills are only transformed into cards when they are dropped on the ground.

• [Repentance] Picking up Starter Deck will nullify this effect.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item is used in It's in the Cards.

fields.description: Gives Isaac a random card.

Deep Pockets.title: Deep Pockets
Deep Pockets.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] Allows Isaac to carry two cards or pills (or a combination of both) at the same time.

• [Repentance] Increases the coin cap to 999.

• [Repentance] If a room would otherwise yield no reward, 1-3 random coins will spawn.

• All coins spawned will be of the same type.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Before Repentance] This item has the same effects as Little Baggy and Starter Deck, but without removing pills/cards from the game.

• [Afterbirth+ before Repentance] This item has the same effect as Polydactyly.

• [Repentance] Has no effect on spawning coins in Greed mode, including the trapdoor/exit room.

• [Repentance] Losing this item while holding more than 99 coins will reduce coin count to 99. Picking it back up again (if playing asTainted Isaac, for example) will not restore lost coins.

• [Before Repentance+] This includes going for Knife Piece 2 in Mines.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• A Dollar: Allows Isaac to gain the full 100 coins when picking this up.

• Contract From Below / Guppy's Tail: If the room clear reward is removed, spawns 1-3 random coins. Allows Deep Pockets to remain useful at high luck.

• Greed's Gullet: After exceeding 100 coins, Isaac gains an extra Heart Container for every 100 coins instead of every 25.

• Keeper/Tainted Keeper: The limit of 12 heart containers can be bypassed, allowing for up to 15 coin hearts at 999 coins. Additional coin hearts past 12 are not displayed.

• Money Power: Increases maximum damage bonus. The damage caps at +39.96 damage with 999 coins.

• Midas' Touch: Increases maximum contact damage. The damage caps at 203.3 damage with 999 coins.

• Options?: A pickup, card, pill, trinket, or Chest will accompany each coin.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Diplopia: No effect, only two pills or cards can be held.

• [Repentance] No effect. Only 999 coins can be held.

• Perfection: Possibly detrimental. Since room clear rewards become very common at high luck, the 1-3 coin drop will rarely occur.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text: Bug note: While holding Esau Jr., swapping to the character without Deep Pockets then collecting or spending coins will cap the number of coins at 99.

fields.quote: [edition alternatives: baseline: More stuff to carry!; Repentance: More money!]
fields.description:
[Before Repentance] Allows Isaac to carry two cards or pills (or a combination of both) at the same time.
[Repentance] Increases the coin cap to 999. If a room would otherwise yield no reward, 1-3 coins will spawn.

Delirious.title: Delirious
Delirious.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text:
• Upon use, spawns Delirium in a form of a friendly boss.

• [Before Repentance+] The boss lasts for the current room, or until killed.

• [Repentance+] The boss persists between rooms until killed. Using the item again will kill the current summoned boss if it is still alive. Any friendly monsters spawned by the previous boss will also be killed. Their health will deteriorate steadily and their color will slowly turn more gray until they reach 1 health.

• • If used on a boss that has a phase change which requires the boss to die, the boss will still persist in its new phase (i.e. The Frail or Fistula). (This may be a bug as some bosses, such as Blastocyst, are unaffected)

• Changes the appearance of the current room so it looks like a different chapter.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• [Repentance+] Hush has an extremely low chance of spawning.

• [Before Repentance+] Sometimes bosses don't spawn because of grid entities getting in the way. When this happens, the upper door appears to have friendly particles.

• [Before Repentance] Unlike Mega Blast, this item can be charged with a single Lil' Battery.

• Lil' Battery gives 6 charges.

• Delirious has a 60% decreased item pool weight, making it less likely to appear than other collectibles.

• Using Delirious in the Delirium fight is ill-advised, as it can be confusing which Delirium is the right one to attack.

• Some bosses leave fires on the ground, such as the orange champion Little Horn, which can still hurt Isaac.

sections.heading: Synergies
sections.text:
• Book of Virtues interaction: Generates a white wisp that resembles one random boss from this list:

• Monstro: Fires an inaccurate spray of 6-10 tears, similar to Lil Monstro but without the charge time.

• The Duke of Flies: Creates Blue Flies instead of firing tears. Each wisp can have a maximum of 3 flies at a time.

• Loki: Fires four tears that alternate between cardinal and ordinal directions.

• The Haunt: Fires Brimstone lasers. The laser does not need to be charged to be fired, and can tick up to 8 times for a total of 8 damage.

sections.heading: Interactions
sections.text:
• Blood Puppy: Either angry version of Blood Puppy will target friendly bosses as well and can drag them along with it when it charges them. Blood Puppy cannot damage friendly bosses; however, friendly bosses can damage Blood Puppy despite not targeting it outright.

• Broken Modem: Broken Modem also affects friendly bosses and projectiles created by them.

• Eraser: The thrown Eraser can’t hit friendly bosses; however, if it erases their hostile variant, they too are erased. If Delirious attempts to spawn an erased boss, it will fail to do so, wasting a use.

• [Repentance] Ghost Bombs / Hungry Soul / Purgatory / Vade Retro: Explosions from ghosts can harm friendly bosses. [end edition note] 

• Tick: Friendly bosses start with less health if they have over 60HP.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text: • This item was most likely intended to be the "ultimate item" of Afterbirth †, similar to Mega Blast of the Afterbirth DLC.

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Lokii is spawned by the item, one will have the Delirium skin and the other will have the normal Lokii skin.
Bug note: If Pink Champion Polycephalus / Pink Champion The Cage is spawned by the item, one will have the Delirium skin and the other will have the normal skin.
Bug note: Using Delirious can sometimes spawn a boss without its Delirium skin.
Bug note: If a Mega Fatty is spawned by the item during The Beast fight, when the Mega Fatty inhales, it will move the sprites of the bosses in the background.
Bug note: Friendly Blue Gapers spawned by Hush may rarely get stuck in their spawn fade-in state, unable to either take or deal damage, and follow enemies or Isaac around endlessly.

fields.description: Spawns Delirium as a random friendly boss that fights for Isaac. [Before Repentance+] The boss lasts the for the current room. [Repentance+] The boss persists between rooms. The charge time is based on the power of the boss summoned.

Delirium.title: Delirium
Delirium.attribution: The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth Wiki contributors

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text: Delirium is a boss added in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth †. It is the main boss of The Void and the final boss of Ending 20.

sections.heading: Behavior
sections.text:
Delirium's main form is stationary but teleports erratically around the room and performs the following attacks:

• Continuously sends out various overlapping patterns of white projectiles for the entire duration of the fight:

• 20 projectiles that slowly rotate clockwise or counterclockwise while expanding.

• 16 projectiles outwards in all directions.

• 14 projectiles that rotate clockwise, counterclockwise, or back and forth while expanding.

• 10 projectiles that fluctuate in and out while expanding.

• 8 slow-moving green-tinted Ipecac projectiles in all directions.

• 6 projectiles that travel outwards in a zig-zag pattern.

• 4 projectiles outwards in a lop-sided cross.

• 4 lines of 3 projectiles that spiral outwards.

• A spread of 5 projectiles in Isaac's direction.

• A burst of projectiles that travel outwards in random directions.

• A stray short-range projectile in a random direction.

• • The projectile size per each attack is random and varies from very small to moderately large.

• Transforms into bosses previously encountered during the run, which can include major bosses such as Mom or It Lives!.

• When it transforms into a boss, Delirium retains its own health, not the health of the boss it transformed into.

• When transforming into certain multi-phase bosses, such as Isaac, Delirium copies the phase that that boss would be at, given its current health percentage.

• When transforming into a segmented boss, only the first two segments share Delirium's hp; the other segments have separately generated hp and can be defeated separately.

• In rare occasions, it can transform into two or even three bosses at once.

• In rare occasions, it spawns a separate copy of the boss it transformed into.

• Whether it turns into a Champion variant or a regular variant is random and does not depend on which variant was previously defeated.

• [Before Repentance] It is unable to properly transform into Hush's true form. In order for this to happen, very few bosses must be encountered in the run. Additionally, many of Hush's attacks do not work properly and the sprite is also unfinished.

• [Repentance] Can transform into Baby Plum, Bumbino, and The Pile, but only Baby Plum has a unique sprite. Cannot transform into any other Repentance bosses. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] Cannot transform into Mega Satan, rendering its unique sprite unused.

• Occasionally, it returns to its main form to perform projectile attacks at a faster pace.

• As it takes damage, it becomes more aggressive: moving, teleporting, transforming, and attacking at a faster rate.

• [Repentance+] Mom and Satan's second phase are exempt from the faster attack speed, instead attacking at a fixed speed.

• It also takes on a reddish hue to signify this change.

• Destroying non-Delirium segments when it transforms into segmented bosses can also temporarily trigger this effect.

• If Delirium is being dealt damage at a significantly high rate from multiple tear sources, it will attack, teleport, and transform at extreme speeds.

Upon defeat, the screen starts to glitch, fills with static, and the room switches between different environments, while short scenes from the current run are played ending with Delirium screaming and bursting into a small puddle of blood.

sections.heading: Unlockable Achievements
sections.text: [achievement text: Delirious, Lil Delirium, D infinity, Eucharist, Silver Dollar, Shade, King Baby, Dull Razor, Bloody Crown, Dark Prince's Crown, Compound Fracture, Eden's Soul, Holy Card, Godhead, Euthanasia, Crooked Penny, Void, Book of the Dead, Star of Bethlehem, Suplex!, Spindown Dice, Hypercoagulation, Bag of Crafting, Dark Arts, IBS, Sumptorium, Berserk!, Hemoptysis, Flip, Corrupted Data, Ghost Bombs, Gello, Keeper's Kin, Abyss, Decap Attack, Lemegeton, Anima Sola]

sections.heading: Damage Scaling
sections.text:
Damage scaling is a mechanic introduced in The Binding of Isaac: Afterbirth to provide a more challenging experience to the players, enabling some enemies to retaliate against high damage attacks by deploying an "armor" of a sort to greatly reduce the amount of damage taken. Further details and an in-depth explanation may be found here.

Delirium only has damage scaling while transformed, not while in its main form.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text:
• Delirium is immune to Chaos Card.

• Upon defeating Delirium, Isaac gains 2 charges for his active item.

• Plan C can be used to kill Delirium. After Plan C is used against Delirium, when pausing in the instant of each flash from Delirium's death animation, the animation can be skipped before the death from Plan C's 3 seconds delay; this works because each flash from Delirium's death animation is still played when the game is paused. It is also recommended to position Isaac on the chest spawn location before Plan C's death occurs.

• It works with Lazarus' Rags, as it revives Isaac on the spot. However, the Completion Mark will go towards Lazarus, not the character originally selected.

• [Repentance] Soul of Lazarus and Inner Child revive Isaac in the same room he died in, and the Completion Mark goes toward the selected/current character. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance] While playing as Tainted Lost, Birthright revives him inside Delirium's room without transforming himself into another character. [end edition note] 

• [Repentance+] This is no longer necessary, as Plan C will kill Isaac in 10 seconds after being used inside Delirium's room, which is enough time to let its death animation finish, and reward the completion mark for the current character before Isaac's Last Will pops up.

• Most entities that are considered to be bosses by the game (usually identified by ones that add the boss health bar to the screen, though there are exceptions) are marked as bosses that Delirium can transform into.

• Delirium's transformations have a huge amount of quirks and odd mechanics, and as such are practically impossible to fully document. A good amount of these quirks are documented below.

• Delirium can transform into either form of Satan.

• When transformed into the Gurglings or the Turdlings, it only appears as one instead of two.

• When transformed into Headless Horseman, it transforms into either the head or the body, but it doesn't transform into both at the same time.

• If Delirium transforms into Isaac and Delirium's health is low enough, it will attempt to perform Isaac's Crack the Sky attack. However, because Delirium's boss arena is a quadruple-sized room, the attack will cover half of the arena, making it extremely deadly.

• Each size of Fistula and Teratoma count as a separate boss, which Delirium can transform into just like any other boss.

• This also results in many bugs due to unaccounted for transformations. These can be viewed in the bugs section of this page.

• When transformed into two instances of the same boss (like Lokii or Sisters Vis), one of them can be killed but the other cannot (until Delirium's hp fully runs out).

• • If Delirium transforms into Pink Champion Monstro, it only takes the form of one and summons an extra Pink Champion Monstro.

• • 
• This is also true for Pink Champion Polycephalus and Pink Champion The Cage.

• • If Delirium transforms into The Lamb's second phase then undergoes another transformation, the body doesn't disappear and can be killed, just like the original Lamb's body.

• • 
• Killing this body will cause the screen to become darker for a period of time, just like when you kill the original Lamb's body.

• • 
• Delirium can also transform into the Lamb's body on its own. If this happens, the body disappears when Delirium transforms again.

• When transformed into a boss that has multiple segments, the extra segments can be killed. The head, however, cannot.

• • This also applies to Gemini — Suture can be killed but Contusion cannot.

• • 
• If Delirium transforms into Gemini, then undergoes another transformation, Suture doesn't disappear. Instead, he continues to chase Isaac as if Contusion was killed in the original fight.

• Delirium's Mom form only stomps and does not spawn enemies.

• [Repentance] If a segmented worm-boss such as Larry Jr. or Scolex is removed via Eraser, Delirium will disappear if it attempts to turn into that boss. This will spawn the ending chest and count as having defeated Delirium. Other multipart bosses' erased pieces may be unable to spawn, but do not kill Delirium entirely. [end edition note] 

• [Before Repentance] If Delirium transforms into Mega Satan, the boss maintains the ability to spawn the Harbingers, the Super Sins, and the Fallen Angels, and can do so in quick succession depending on Delirium's health. This can make the fight much longer, as attacking the bosses spawned by Delirium will have no effect on Delirium's actual health.

• Delirium can transform into Fallen Uriel and Fallen Gabriel but they don't have unique Delirium skins.

• Each time Delirium transforms, its Status Effect timer resets, allowing for useful effects to be active for a large portion of the fight if re-inflicted frequently enough.

• This quirk is especially useful in conjunction with the petrification from Mom's Contacts, as it can hold Delirium in place each time it is petrified, making it a much easier target to hit.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.text:
• Just like with Hush, effects that cause long-lasting mass slowdown such as Stop Watch or the I'm Drowsy pill are very valuable, aiding the player's ability to dodge the complex tear patterns and deal with the massive spawns of enemies, which can happen in quick succession.

• [Repentance] Broken Modem can also remove a lot of bullets, making it a must-have against Delirium.

• Delirium's main form lacks any damage scaling or armor, allowing the opportunity to deal high damage attacks against its massive base HP. Be wary that dealing significant bursts of damage against Delirium will also quickly increase its aggressiveness.

• One may wish to save this fight with Tainted Eden for the last mark of a file, as Corrupted Data can make I AM ERROR and Secret Rooms worse.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.text:
• Delirium is Isaac's manifestation of the "white light at the end of the tunnel" where the entire history of his life flashes before his eyes, moments before Isaac's death.

• This is reflected by Delirium's death animation and its ability to shapeshift into previously encountered bosses.

• "Delirium" is the state of mental confusion of a person who is delirious. Symptoms include restlessness, illusions, and incoherence.

• The arena can randomly change themes during the fight and is purely visual.

• After Delirium finishes his death animation, the arena will change into the theme of Chest.

• Delirium is one of only two enemies immune to Chaos Card, [Repentance] the other being The Beast [end edition note] .

• Killing Delirium in a daily challenge counts as winning it. [Before Repentance+] However, this does not reward any unique bonus points.

• [Repentance+] Delirium can be a goal and grants unique bonus points.

• Unlike other completion marks, defeating Delirium does not add a mark to the post-it note. Instead, the note will become tattered (with blood on Hard mode).

• If no other bosses have been encountered during the run, Delirium is unable to transform.

• This is normally impossible, as Mom must always be defeated in order to even have access to The Void on any run.

• [Repentance] We Need To Go Deeper! can be used to access Dark Room, then create an Crawl Space there. Entering the Crawl Space and leaving it through an unintended direction will lead Isaac to an I AM ERROR room, allowing access to The Void, all without fighting any bosses. [end edition note] 

• Every time Delirium transforms into another boss, it adds onto the encounters counter in the Bestiary.

• If Delirium transforms into Mom as soon as the battle starts, it stomps in the center of the room regardless of Isaac's position, similar to how the original Mom always starts her battle by stomping in the center of the room.

• Similarly, If Delirium transforms into Mom's Heart/It Lives! as soon as the battle starts, it is accompanied by two Eyes in the same position as they are when they accompany the original Mom's Heart/It Lives! at the start of its battle.

• Prior to Booster Pack#5, Delirium could turn into a Lil' Haunt.

• Also, if it transformed into Black Champion Brownie when at low health, it would spawn two Dank Squirts like the original boss would and die before the health bar actually fully depleted, without playing its death animation. This no longer happens because Delirium's Brownie form (normal and Black Champion) no longer transitions into the second phase (turning into a weakened Dangle or leaving two Dank Squirts, respectively).

• Delirium uses the exact same sprite for both its Dingle and Dangle forms.

• [Repentance] Delirium's sprite for its Steven form is based on Ash from The End Is Nigh.

• If Delirium transforms into Mega Fatty and performs the vomit attack, it attracts its White and Green projectiles towards it.

• The only bosses Delirium can't normally transform are Ultra Greed, Ultra Greedier, and any other Repentance boss except for most of those that can appear on the "main" route: Baby Plum, Bumbino, and The Pile.

• Technically speaking, Delirium can transform into Ultra Greed and Ultra Greedier, but they lack unique sprites. This will never happen in a normal playthrough, as the bosses exist in different game modes.

• [Before Repentance] Delirium's Hush form can be summoned with Delirious, but it has to be used many times in quick succession in the same room, which is only possible via cheats or the Debug Console.

• • [Repentance+] Delirious has a very low chance to spawn the Hush form.

• Delirium can even transform into the hidden incomplete Skinless Hush boss, which does not move and performs basic projectile attacks. This is despite the fact that Skinless Hush does not have any AI by itself and cannot be encountered without manually spawning it in.

• [Repentance] Delirium can transform into a dummy spawned by the spawn dummy command in the Debug Console, and when they do, a functioning endgame chest spawns instantly, which ends the fight and triggers the ending regardless of Delirium's health.

• There are a couple items themed around Delirium that play off of its ever-changing form — those being Lil Delirium, Delirious, and D infinity.

• [Repentance] Delirium's unlocks for Tainted characters mostly reflect the special ability of that character. For example, beating Delirium as Tainted Azazel unlocks Hemoptysis, which gives Isaac the sneeze ability of Tainted Azazel.

• The only exceptions to this are Tainted Isaac, who instead unlocks Spindown Dice, Tainted Lost, who instead unlocks Ghost Bombs, and Tainted Keeper, who instead unlocks Keeper's Kin.

• The item that most mimics Tainted Isaac's starting ability, Glitched Crown, is instead unlocked by defeating The Beast.

• The item that most mimics Tainted Lost's starting ability, Sacred Orb, is instead unlocked by defeating The Beast.

• The item that most mimics a Tainted Keeper property is Keeper's Bargain, unlocked by Satan, The Lamb, Isaac and ???'s completion marks together. [end edition note]

sections.heading: Bugs
sections.text:
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into an enemy like Chub with multiple hitboxes, the game may crash if one of the secondary hitboxes is hit by Chaos Card.
Bug note: Delirium can be killed by a Chaos Card if shot in the black segment in Carrion Queen form.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into Mega Satan, the sprites will bug out. It can attack normally, but the sprite may not be visible/half-visible/only showing the hands.
Bug note: On Isaac's last will, Delirium will be shown in its current form rather than its main one. Sometimes it will show his main form, even if Isaac is killed by a different form.
Bug note: Delirium can sometimes deal unavoidable damage. For example, when transformed into Mom, the boss will constantly target Isaac until it stomps down. If Delirium changes during this targeting phase, it can teleport into Isaac, instantly damaging him.
Bug note: Sometimes, when Delirium transforms into a segmented boss, its health will appear to be lower than it is. This is usually purely visual and returns to normal whenever it transforms again.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into Blue Champion Larry Jr., it will, due to how Blue Champion Larry Jr.'s HP works, effectively lose a large portion of HP as its total HP will get divided into however many segments it transforms into. It will not receive the lost HP back after transforming again.
Bug note: If Delirious is used to spawn Hush, Delirium will be able to transform into Hush.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into Gemini, Suture will stay in its enraged form separated from Contusion when Delirium transforms again.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into Blighted Ovum, Suture will keep its usual sprite instead of using its special sprite for Delirium.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into the Mask of Infamy, it will only transform into the heart.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into The Frail, it will always transform into the first phase, regardless of how much hp it has left (unless it's the Black Champion version).
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into Lokii, it will only transform into one Lokii half.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into War's second phase, the body will be invisible (except for when it does its sobbing animation). This also applies to Blighted Ovum's Contusion.
Bug note: As of patch V1.7.8, if Delirium transforms into a champion boss, it will retain its normal appearance and color, but its attacks (and size in the case of some forms) will be those of the champion.
Bug note: If Delirium transforms into Bumbino and there are coins on the floor of its boss room, it will move toward the coins but cannot pick them up, causing it to get stuck until it transforms again.
